# Siva Purana. Chapter 2

## Section 2 - Rudra-saṃhitā (1): Sṛṣṭi-khaṇḍa

## Chapter 1 - The inquiry of the sages

## \|\| 2.1.1 \|\|

*viśvodbhavasthitilayādiṣu hetumekaṃ gaurīpartividitatattvamanantakīrtim \|\| māyāśrayamvigatamāyamaciṃtyarūpambodhasvarūpamamalaṃ hi śivannamāmi \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. I bow to Śiva the consort of Gaurī, the sole cause of the origin, sustenance, dissolution of the universe, who has understood the reality, who is of endless renown, who is the support of Māyā but is free from its influence, whose form is incomprehensible, who is unsullied and who is perfect knowledge itself.

## \|\| 2.1.2 \|\|

*vande śivantamprakṛteranādimpraśāntamekampuruṣottamaṃ hi \|*  
*svamāyayā kṛtsnamidaṃ hi sṛṣṭvā nabhovadantarbahirāsthito yaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. I salute Śiva who is prior to Prakṛti, who is calm and tranquil, the only excellent Puruṣa, who has created this visible universe and who stays both within and without like ether.

## \|\| 2.1.3 \|\|

*vandetarasthaṃ nijagūḍharūpaṃ śivaṃsvatassraṣṭumidamvicaṣṭe \|*  
*jaganti nityamparito bhramaṃti yatsannidhau cumbakalohavattam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. I salute Śiva, of unmanifest form, who having extended himself by way of creation stands in the middle of it while the worlds move around him like iron filings round the magnet.

## \|\| 2.1.4 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*jagataḥ pitaraṃ śambhuñjagato mātaraṃ śivām \|*  
*tatputraśca gaṇādhīśannatvaitadvarṇayāmahe \|\| 4 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:—

4\. I describe this after bowing to Śambhu, the father of the universe, Śivā the mother of the universe and Gaṇādhīśa their son.

## \|\| 2.1.5 \|\|

*ekadā munayassarve naimiṣāraṇya vāsinaḥ \|*  
*papracchurvarayā bhaktyā sūtante śaunakādayaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Once Śaunaka and other sages living in Naimiṣa forest asked Sūta with full devotion.

## \|\| 2.1.6 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*vidyeśvarasaṃhitāyāḥ śrutā sā satkathā śubhā \|*  
*sādhyasādhanakhaṃḍā khyā ramyādyā bhaktavatsalā \|\| 6 \|\|*

The sages said:—

6\. The good and auspicious story of Vidyeśvarasaṃhitā has been heard by us. This first delightful compendium, “On the achievable and the means of achievement” is lovingly disposed to the devotees.

## \|\| 2.1.7 \|\|

*sūta sūta mahābhāga cirañjīva sukhī bhava \|*  
*yacchrāvayasi nastāta śāṃkarīṃ paramāṃ kathām \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Sūta, O blessed Sūta, live long. Be happy. You will please narrate to us, O dear, the great anecdotes of Śiva.

## \|\| 2.1.8 \|\|

*pibantastvanmukhāmbhojacyutaṃ jñānāmṛtamvayam \|*  
*avitṛptāḥ punaḥ kiṃcitpraṣṭumicchāmahe'nagha \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. O sinless one, drinking the nectar of knowledge poured out from your lotus-mouth we are never satiated. Hence we would like to inquire of you something more.

## \|\| 2.1.9 \|\|

*vyāsaprasādātsarvajño prāpto'si kṛtakṛtyatām \|*  
*nājñātamvidyate kiṃcidbhūtaṃ bhabyaṃ bhavacca yat \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. O omniscient one, by the favour of Vyāsa you have realised contentment. There is nothing not known to you whether of the past, present or future.

## \|\| 2.1.10 \|\|

*gurorvyāsasya sadbhaktyā samāsādya kṛpāṃ parām \|*  
*sarvaṃ jñātaṃ viśeṣeṇa sarvaṃ sārthaṃ kṛtaṃ januḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. In return for your excellent devotion you have gained the great favour of your preceptor Vyāsa. You have understood everything. You have made your life highly noble and purposeful.

## \|\| 2.1.11 \|\|

*idānīṃ kathaya prājña śivarūpamanuttamam \|*  
*divyāni vai caritrāṇi śivayorapyaśeṣataḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Now, O wise one, please explain the excellent form of Śiva. Please narrate the divine anecdote of Śiva and Pārvatī without omitting anything.

## \|\| 2.1.12 \|\|

*aguṇo guṇatāṃ yāti kathaṃ loke maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*śivatattvaṃ vayaṃ sarve na jānīmo vicārataḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Maheśvara is Aguṇa (free from attributes). How does He take up the Saguṇa from in the world? We do not know the true nature of Śiva, despite our great deliberation.

## \|\| 2.1.13 \|\|

*sṛṣṭeḥ pūrvaṃ kathaṃ śaṃbhussvarūpeṇāvatiṣṭhate \|*  
*sṛṣṭimadhye sa hi kathaṃ krīḍansaṃvarttate prabhuḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Before the origin of creation how does lord Śiva maintain His form? In the midst of creation how does He maintain His sport?

## \|\| 2.1.14 \|\|

*tadante ca kathandevassa tiṣṭhati maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*kathamprasannatāṃ yāti śaṃkaro lokaśaṃkaraḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. How does lord Maheśvara stand at the moment of dissolution? How is Śañkara who blesses the world with happiness propitiated?

## \|\| 2.1.15 \|\|

*sa prasanno maheśānaḥ kiṃ prayacchati satphalam \|*  
*svabhaktebhyaḥ parebhyaśca tatsarvaṃ kathayasva naḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. What benefit does the great Lord confer when He is pleased with His own devotees and others? Please tell us.

## \|\| 2.1.16 \|\|

*sadyaḥ prasanno bhagavānbhavatītyanuśaśruma \|*  
*bhaktaprayāsaṃ sa mahānna paśyati dayāparaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. We have heard that the lord becomes pleased instantaneously. The merciful lord is unable to bear the stress and strain that His devotee undergoes.

## \|\| 2.1.17 \|\|

*brahmāviṣṇurmaheśaśca trayo devāśśivāṃgajāḥ \|*  
*maheśastatra pūrṇāṃśassvayameva śivo'paraḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The three deities Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Maheśa are born of Śiva. Among them Maheśa when he has all the substrata of elements is Śiva himself as distinct from Maheśa.

## \|\| 2.1.18 \|\|

*tasyāvirbhāvamākhyāhi caritāni viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*umāvirbhāvamākhyāhi tadvivāhaṃ tathā prabho \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Please explain His manifestation and tell us about His various activities. Please tell us about the birth of Umā and her marriage too, O lord.

## \|\| 2.1.19 \|\|

*tadgārhasthyaṃ viśeṣeṇa tathā līlāḥ parā api \|*  
*etatsarvaṃ tadanyacca kathanīyaṃ tvayā'nagha \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Their domestic life and their divine sports shall also be narrated to us. O sinless one, please tell us all about it and anything else that shall be told.

## \|\| 2.1.20 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*iti pṛṣṭastadā taistu sūto harṣasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*smṛtvā śaṃbhupadāṃbhojampratyuvāca munīśvarān \|\| 20 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:—

20\. Being thus requested Sūta was delighted. Remembering the lotus-like feet of Śiva he replied to the sages.

## \|\| 2.1.21 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*samyakpṛṣṭaṃ bhavadbhiśca dhanyā yūyaṃ munīśvarāḥ \|*  
*sadāśivakathāyāṃ vo yajjātā naiṣṭhikī matiḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

Sūta said:—

21\. O lordly sages, what you have asked for is very nice. You are all blessed inasmuch as your minds are drawn towards Sadāśiva’s anecdotes.

## \|\| 2.1.22 \|\|

*sadāśivakathāpraśnaḥ puruṣāṃstrīnpunāti hi \|*  
*vaktāraṃ pṛcchakaṃ śrotṝñjāhnavīsalilaṃ yathā \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Like the holy waters of the Gaṅgā the inquiry into the anecdotes of Sadāśiva sanctifies the three persons: the narrator, the inquirer and the hearer.

## \|\| 2.1.23 \|\|

*śaṃbhorguṇānuvādātko virajyeta pumāndvijāḥ \|*  
*vinā paśughnaṃ trividhajanānandakarātsadā \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. O brahmins, except for the slayer of animals, who can be averse to hear the narrative of the attributes of Śiva, that highly delights three types of people always?

## \|\| 2.1.24 \|\|

*gīyamāno vitṛṣṇaiśca bhavarogauṣadho'pi hi \|*  
*manaḥśrotrābhirāmaśca yattassarvārthadassa vai \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. When it is being recited by persons who have no attachment or desire, it is verily an antidote for all ailments of worldly existence, for it is highly delightful to the ear and the heart while at the same time it bestows all objects.

## \|\| 2.1.25 \|\|

*kathayāmi yathābuddhi bhavatpraśnānusārataḥ \|*  
*śivalīlāṃ prayatnena dvijāstāṃ śṛṇutādarāt \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. O brahmins, I shall explain Śiva’s sports in the light of your enquiry as far as my intelligence enables me to do so. Please listen respectfully.

## \|\| 2.1.26 \|\|

*bhavadbhiḥ pṛcchyate yadvattattathā nāradena vai \|*  
*pṛṣṭaṃ pitre preritena hariṇā śivarūpiṇā \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Induced by lord Viṣṇu, a manifestation of Śiva, Nārada had also put the same question to his father Brahmā as you are asking me now.

## \|\| 2.1.27 \|\|

*brahmā śrutvā sutavacaśśivabhaktaḥ prasannadhīḥ \|*  
*jagau śivayaśaḥ prītyā harṣayanmunisattamam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. On hearing the words of his son, Brahmā, a devotee of Śiva, was delighted in his mind. Out of love he sang the glory of Śiva heightening the pleasure of the excellent sage (Nārada).

## \|\| 2.1.28 \|\|

*vyāsa \|*  
*sūtoktamiti tadvākyamākarṇya dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*papracchustatsusaṃvādaṃ kutūhalasamanvitāḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:—

28\. The learned brahmins, on hearing the words of Sūta became eager to know more of that conversation and so asked him.

## \|\| 2.1.29 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*sūta sūta mahābhāga śaivottama mahāmate \|*  
*śrutvā tava vaco ramyaṃ ceto nassakutūhalam \|\| 29 \|\|*

The sages said:—

29\. O Sūta, O blessed Sūta, of great intellect and foremost among the devotees of Śiva, on hearing your most delightful words our minds have become very eager to know more.

## \|\| 2.1.30-31 \|\|

*kadā babhūva sukhakṛdvidhināradayormahān \|*  
*saṃvādo yatra giriśasu līlā bhavamocinī \|\| 30 \|\|*

*vidhināradasaṃvādapūrvakaṃ śāṃkaraṃ yaśaḥ \|*  
*brūhi nastāta tatprītyā tattatpraśnānusārataḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

30-31. Dear one, please tell us lovingly when this highly pleasant conversation between Brahmā and Nārada took place, wherein Śiva’s glory was sung and the divine sport of Lord Śiva, destructive of worldly existence, had been discussed. What were the questions and how were they answered, please explain.

## \|\| 2.1.32 \|\|

*ityākarṇya vacasteṣāṃ munīnāṃ bhāvitātmanām \|*  
*sūtaḥ provāca suprītastatsaṃvādānusārataḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. On hearing these words of the sages of noble mind Sūta was pleased much and narrated everything pertaining to the conversation referred to.

## Chapter 2 - Indra sends Kāmadeva to disturb the penance of Nārada

## \|\| 2.2.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*etasminsamaye viprā nārado munisattamaḥ \|*  
*brahmaputro vinītātmā taporthaṃ mana ādadhe \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sūta said:—

1\. O brahmins, once Nārada the excellent sage, son of Brahmā was inclined to perform penance controlling himself very much.

## \|\| 2.2.2 \|\|

*himaśailaguhā kācidekā paramaśobhanā \|*  
*yatsamīpe suranadī sadā vahati vegataḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. There is a very beautiful cave in the Himālaya mountain near which the celestial river flows rapidly.

## \|\| 2.2.3 \|\|

*tatrāśramo mahādivyo nānāśobhāsamanvitaḥ \|*  
*taporthaṃ sa yayau tatra nārado divyadarśanaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. There was a great hermitage of divine splendour which was resplendent in many ways. Nārada endowed with divine vision went there to perform the penance.

## \|\| 2.2.4 \|\|

*tāṃ dṛṣṭvā muniśārdūlastepe sa suciraṃ tapaḥ \|*  
*badhvāsanaṃ dṛḍhaṃ maunī prāṇānāyamya śuddhadhīḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. On seeing the hermitage (very convenient for penance) the leading sage performed the penance for a long time, seated firmly and steadily, keeping silent, controlling the breath and retaining the purity of the intellect.

## \|\| 2.2.5 \|\|

*cakre munissamādhiṃ tamahambrahmeti yatra ha \|*  
*vijñānaṃ bhavati brahmasākṣātkārakaraṃ dvijāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. O brahmins, the sage performed meditation and contemplation wherein the realisation “I am Brahman” is generated leading to the direct perception of Brahman.

## \|\| 2.2.6 \|\|

*itthaṃ tapati tasminvai nārade munisattame \|*  
*cakaṃpe'tha śunāsīro manassaṃtāpavihvalaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. When the great sage Nārada was thus performing penance, the mind of Indra became excessively agitated and he trembled.

## \|\| 2.2.7 \|\|

*manasīti viciṃtyāsau munirme rājyamicchati \|*  
*tadvighnakaraṇārthaṃ hi hariryatnamiyeṣa saḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Thinking “This sage is yearning for my kingdom” Indra wanted to spoil it.

## \|\| 2.2.8 \|\|

*sasmāra smaraṃ śakraścetasā devanāyakaḥ \|*  
*ājagāma drutaṃ kāmassamadhīrmahiṣīsutaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Indra, the leader of Devas, remembered Kāmadeva (Cupid) who arrived there immediately, accompanied by his Queen (Rati) and spring (his friend).

## \|\| 2.2.9 \|\|

*athāgataṃ smaraṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃbodhya surarāṭ prabhuḥ \|*  
*uvāca taṃ prapaśyāśu svārthe kuṭilaśemuṣiḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The king of Devas, endowed with crooked intelligence to achieve his interests, saw that Kāma had arrived and addressed him thus.

## \|\| 2.2.10 \|\|

*indra uvāca \|*  
*mitravaryya mahāvīra sarvadā hitakāraka \|*  
*śṛṇu prītyā vaco me tvaṃ kuru sāhāyyamātmanā \|\| 10 \|\|*

Indra said:—

10\. O friend, of great prowess, always doing what is beneficent to me, please hear lovingly what I am going to say. Render me your help.

## \|\| 2.2.11 \|\|

*tvadbalānme bahūnāñca tapogarvo vināśitaḥ \|*  
*madrājyasthiratā mitra tvadanugrahatassadā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Strongly supported by you I have destroyed the pride of many ascetics O friend, the stability of my kingdom is always due to your blessing.

## \|\| 2.2.12 \|\|

*himaśailaguhāyāṃ hi munistapati nāradaḥ \|*  
*manasoddiśya viśveśaṃ mahāsaṃyamavāndṛḍhaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Nārada, the sage, is performing a penance in the Himalaya mountain directing his mind towards the Lord of the universe with great mental control and firm resolve.

## \|\| 2.2.13 \|\|

*yācenna vidhito rājyaṃ sa mameti viśaṃkitaḥ \|*  
*adyaiva gaccha tatra tvaṃ tattapovighnamācara \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. I now fear lest he should beg of Brahmā my kingdom. You must go there now itself and hinder his penance.

## \|\| 2.2.14 \|\|

*ityājñapto mahendreṇa sa kāmassamadhu priyaḥ \|*  
*jagāma tatsthalaṃ garvādupāyaṃ svañcakāra ha \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Being thus commanded by Indra, Kāmadeva, accompanied by his wife (Rati) and Madhu, his friend, went haughtily to that place. He then prepared his own means of attack.

## \|\| 2.2.15 \|\|

*racayāmāsa tatrāśu svakalāssakalā api \|*  
*vasaṃtopi svaprabhāvaṃ cakāra vividhaṃ madāt \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. He employed all his arts there immediately. Spring too haughtily spread his prowess of diverse nature.

## \|\| 2.2.16 \|\|

*na babhūva muneśceto vikṛtaṃ munisattamāḥ \|*  
*bhraṣṭo babhūva tadgarvo maheśānugraheṇa ha \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. O great sages, the mind of the sage (Nārada) did not waver. Only the arrogance of these fellows suffered a setback and that too by the favour of Maheśa.

## \|\| 2.2.17 \|\|

*śṛṇutādaratastatra kāraṇaṃ śaunakādayaḥ \|*  
*īśvarānugraheṇātra na prabhāvaḥ smarasya hi \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Please listen to the reason thereof, O Śaunaka and other sages! By the controlling power of the lord, Kāma could not exercise any influence.

## \|\| 2.2.18 \|\|

*atraiva śambhunā'kāri sutapaśca smarāriṇā \|*  
*atraiva dagdhastenāśu kāmo munitapopahaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. It was in this very place that Śiva, the indefatigable enemy of Kāma, had formerly performed a great penance. It was here that Kāma was reduced to ashes—Kāma who used to spoil the penances of sages.

## \|\| 2.2.19 \|\|

*kāmajīvanahetorhi ratyā saṃprārthitaissuraiḥ \|*  
*samprārthita uvācedaṃ śaṃkaro lokaśaṃkaraḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Rati wanted the resuscitation of Kāma and requested the Devas. They appealed to lord Śiva, the benefactor of the whole world who said thus:

## \|\| 2.2.20 \|\|

*kaṃcitsamayamāsādya jīviṣyati surāḥ smaraḥ \|*  
*paraṃ tviha smaropāyaścariṣyati na kaścana \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. “O Gods, after some time Kāma will come to life again. But none of his tricks will succeed here.

## \|\| 2.2.21 \|\|

*iha yāvaddṛśyate bhūrjanaiḥ sthitvā'marāssadā \|*  
*kāmabāṇaprabhāvotra na caliṣyatyasaṃśayam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Whatever space all round this spot is visible to persons here, will be out of the influence of Kāma for ever, O Devas.

## \|\| 2.2.22 \|\|

*iti śaṃbhūktitaḥ kāmo mithyātmagatikastadā \|*  
*nārade sa jagāmāśu divamindrasamīpataḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. It was due to this statement of Śiva that Kāma’s viles did not prevail upon Nārada. From Śiva’s abode he went to Indra.

## \|\| 2.2.23 \|\|

*ācakhyau sarvavṛttāṃtaṃ prabhāvaṃ ca muneḥ smaraḥ \|*  
*tadājñayā yayau sthānaṃ svakīyaṃ sa madhupriyaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Kāma then narrated everything about the sage and commended his power. At Indra’s bidding Kāma returned to his own place.

## \|\| 2.2.24 \|\|

*vismitobhūtsurādhīśaḥ praśaśaṃsātha nāradam \|*  
*tadvṛttāṃtānabhijño hi mohitaśśivamāyayā \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Deluded by Śiva’s Māyā (power of illusion) Indra was unaware of the true facts and was greatly surprised and he admired Nārada.

## \|\| 2.2.25 \|\|

*durjñeyā śāṃbhavī māyā sarveṣāṃ prāṇināmiha \|*  
*bhaktaṃ vinārpitātmānaṃ tayā saṃmohyate jagat \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Śiva’s Māyā is incomprehensible to all. The whole universe is deluded by it. Only the true devotees of dedicated souls escape.

## \|\| 2.2.26 \|\|

*nārado'pi ciraṃ tasthau tatreśānugraheṇa ha \|*  
*pūrṇaṃ matvā tapastatsvaṃ virarāma tato muniḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Backed by Śiva’s blessings Nārada stayed in the hermitage for. a long time. Then realising that his penance was complete, the sage concluded the same.

## \|\| 2.2.27 \|\|

*kāmopyajeyaṃ nijaṃ matvā garvito'bhūnmunīśvaraḥ \|*  
*vṛthaiva vigatajñānaśśivamāyāvimohitaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Thinking that he had conquered Kāma he was puffed with pride. He was devoid of true knowledge and deluded by Śiva’s Māyā.

## \|\| 2.2.28 \|\|

*dhanyā dhanyā mahāmāyā śāṃbhavī munisattamāḥ \|*  
*tadgatiṃ na hi paśyaṃti viṣṇubrahmādayopi hi \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. O great sages, blessed and very blessed is Śiva’s Māyā. Even Viṣṇu, Brahmā and others do not know the the turn it takes.

## \|\| 2.2.29 \|\|

*tayā saṃmohitotīva nārado munisattamaḥ \|*  
*kailāsaṃ prayayau śīghraṃ svavṛttaṃ gadituṃ madī \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. In that state of delusion and puffed up arrogance, the great sage Nārada went to Kailāsa to expatiate on his own achievement.

## \|\| 2.2.30 \|\|

*rudraṃ natvābravītsarvaṃ svavṛttaṅgarvavānmuniḥ \|*  
*matvātmānaṃ mahātmānaṃ svaprabhuñca smarañjayam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Bowing down to Rudra, the sage arrogantly spoke of his exploits with the conviction that he was equal to the noble-souled lord, the conqueror of Kāma, i.e., Siva.

## \|\| 2.2.31 \|\|

*tacchrutvā śaṃkaraḥ prāha nāradaṃ bhaktavatsalaḥ \|*  
*svamāyāmohitaṃ hetvanabhijñaṃ bhraṣṭacetasam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. On hearing it, Śiva who is favourably disposed to His devotees, advised Nārada who was ignorant of the real cause, whose mind had strayed and who had been deluded by His (Śiva’s) Māyā.

## \|\| 2.2.32 \|\|

*rudra uvāca \|*  
*he tāta nārada prājña dhanyastvaṃ śṛṇu madvacaḥ \|*  
*vācyamevaṃ na kutrāpi hareragre viśeṣataḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

Rudra said:—

32\. “Dear Nārada, O wise sage, you are blessed. But please listen to me. Never speak like this anywhere else, especially in the presence of Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 2.2.33 \|\|

*pṛcchamāno'pi na brūyāḥ svavṛttaṃ me yaduktavān \|*  
*gopyaṃ gopyaṃ sarvathā hi naiva vācyaṃ kadācana \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Even when you are asked you should not mention your achievements as you have done just now. These should be guarded as close secrets and should never be expressed.

## \|\| 2.2.34 \|\|

*śāsmyahaṃ tvāṃ viśeṣeṇa mama priyatamo bhavān \|*  
*viṣṇubhakto yatastvaṃ hi tadbhaktotīva me'nugaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. I bid you specifically like this because you are a great favourite of mine. Since you are a devotee of Viṣṇu you are my follower as all his devotees are.”

## \|\| 2.2.35 \|\|

*śāstismetthañca bahuśo rudrassūtikaraḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*nārado na hitaṃ mene śivamāyāvimohitaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

Sūta said:—

35\. Lord Rudra, the cause of creation, advised him in many ways like this. But Nārada who was still under the influence of Śiva’s Māyā did not take up this wholesome advice.

## \|\| 2.2.36 \|\|

*prabalā bhāvinī karma gatirjñeyā vicakṣaṇaiḥ \|*  
*na nivāryā janaiḥ kaiścidapīcchā saiva śāṃkarī \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. The future course of actions shall be considered inevitable by sensible persons. The will of Śiva cannot be warded off by any one.

## \|\| 2.2.37 \|\|

*tatassa munivaryo hi brahmalokaṃ jagāma ha \|*  
*vidhiṃ natvā'bravītkāmajayaṃ svasya tapobalāt \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Then the great sage went to Brahmā’s world. After saluting Brahmā he told him about his conquest of Kāma as a result of his penance.

## \|\| 2.2.38 \|\|

*tadākarṇya vidhissotha smṛtvā śambhupadāmbujam \|*  
*jñātvā sarvaṃ kāraṇaṃ tanniṣiṣedha sutaṃ tadā \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. On hearing that, Brahmā remembered the lotuslike feet of Śiva and knew thereby the true cause. He then forbade his son.

## \|\| 2.2.39 \|\|

*mene hitanna vidhyuktaṃ nārado jñānisattamaḥ \|*  
*śivamāyāmohitaśca rūḍhacittamadāṃkuraḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Although foremost among the wise, Nārada did not take up the advice of Brahmā as he had been deluded by Śiva’s Māyā. The sprout of arrogance had been so fixed in his mind.

## \|\| 2.2.40 \|\|

*śivecchā yādṛśī loke bhavatyeva hi sā tadā \|*  
*tadadhīnaṃ jagatsarvaṃ vacastaṃtyāṃta sthitaṃ yataḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Everything will take place in the world in the manner Śiva wills. It is true that the entire universe is dependent on His will.

## \|\| 2.2.41 \|\|

*nārado'tha yayau śīghraṃ viṣṇulokaṃ vinaṣṭadhīḥ \|*  
*madāṃkuramanā vṛttaṃ gadituṃ svaṃ tadagrataḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Nārada hastened to Viṣṇuloka in the same state of senseless arrogance, to boast of his exploits in the presence of Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 2.2.42 \|\|

*āgacchaṃtaṃ munindṛṣṭvā nāradaṃ viṣṇurādarāt \|*  
*utthitvāgre gato'raṃ taṃ śiśleṣajñātahetukaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. When Viṣṇu saw Nārada approaching, he could guess the purpose of his visit. He stood up and received him cordially. He walked forward and embraced him lovingly.

## \|\| 2.2.43 \|\|

*svāsane samupāveśya smṛtvā śivapadāmbujam \|*  
*hariḥ prāha vacastathyaṃ nāradaṃ madanāśanam \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. He made Nārada sit comfortably. After remembering the lotus-like feet of Śiva, He frankly uttered these words intended to quell the arrogance of Nārada.

## \|\| 2.2.44 \|\|

*viṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*kuta āgamyate tāta kimarthamiha cāgataḥ \|*  
*dhanyastvaṃ muniśārdūla tīrtho'haṃ tu tavāgamāt \|\| 44 \|\|*

Viṣṇu said:—

44\. “O dear Nārada, foremost among sages, you are blessed. I am sanctified by your visit. May I know where you come from and why you have come?”

## \|\| 2.2.45 \|\|

*viṣṇuvākyamiti śrutvā nārado garvito muniḥ \|*  
*svavṛttaṃ sarvamācaṣṭa samadaṃ madamohitaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. On hearing these words of Viṣṇu, the sage Nārada felt elated. He narrated his story in the same haughty manner.

## \|\| 2.2.46 \|\|

*śrutvā munivaco viṣṇussamadaṃ kāraṇaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*jñātavānakhilaṃ smṛtvā śivapādāmbujaṃ hṛdi \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. On hearing the arrogant words of the sage, Viṣṇu remembered the lotus-like feet of Śiva again and understood the true cause.

## \|\| 2.2.47 \|\|

*tuṣṭāva giriśaṃ bhaktyā śivātmā śaivarāḍ hariḥ \|*  
*sāṃjalirvisudhīrnamramastakaḥ parameśvaram \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Viṣṇu, a leading devotee of Śiva, with his soul dedicated to Śiva, bowed his head and eulogised Parameśvara, the lord of the holy mountain, with his palms joined in reverence.

## \|\| 2.2.48 \|\|

*viṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*devadeva mahādeva prasīda parameśvara \|*  
*dhanyastvaṃ śiva dhanyā te māyā sarva vimohinī \|\| 48 \|\|*

Viṣṇu said:—

48\. “O Lord, O Lord Mahādeva, Parameśvara, be pleased. O Śiva thou art blessed. Thy Māyā enchants everyone.”

## \|\| 2.2.49 \|\|

*ityādi sa stutiṃ kṛtvā śivasya paramātmanaḥ \|*  
*nimīlya nayane dhyātvā virarāma padāmbujam \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Having thus chanted the prayer to Śiva, the supreme Ātman, he closed his eyes and meditated on His lotus-like feet and stopped.

## \|\| 2.2.50 \|\|

*yatkartavyaṃ śaṃkarasya sa jñātvā viśvapālakaḥ \|*  
*śivaśāsanataḥ prāha hṛdātha munisattamam \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. On coming to know what Śiva was about to do, through Śiva’s bidding, he addressed the great sage pleasantly.

## \|\| 2.2.51 \|\|

*viṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*dhanyastvaṃ muniśārdūla taponidhirudāradhīḥ \|*  
*bhaktitrikaṃ na yasyāsti kāmamohādayo mune \|\| 51 \|\|*

Viṣṇu said:—

51\. O foremost among sages, you are blessed. You are the storehouse of austerities and large-hearted. O sage, lust and delusion rise only in the heart of that man who is devoid of the three types of devotion.

## \|\| 2.2.52 \|\|

*vikārāstasya sadyo vai bhavaṃtyakhiladuḥkhadāḥ \|*  
*naiṣṭhiko brahmacārī tvaṃ jñānavairāgyavānsadā \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Base passions that bring in their wake all sorts of miseries crop up in him instantly. But you are vowed to perpetual celibacy. You are ever endowed with knowledge and devoted to non-attachment.

## \|\| 2.2.53-55 \|\|

*kathaṃ kāmavikārī syā janmanā vikṛtassudhīḥ \|*  
*ityādyuktaṃ vaco bhūri śrutvā sa munisattamaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

*vijahāsa hṛdā natvā pratyuvāca vaco harim \|*  
*nārada uvāca \|*  
*kiṃ prabhāvaḥ smaraḥ svāminkṛpā yadyasti te mayi \|\| 54 \|\|*

*ityuktvā harimānamya yayau yādṛcchiko muniḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

53-55. Unaffected by passion and highly intelligent by nature how can you be swayed by lust?”

On hearing words like these, the great sage laughed within himself but spoke to Viṣṇu humbly.

## Chapter 3 - Nārada attends the Svayaṃvara of a virgin and is discomfited

## \|\| 2.3.1-2 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*sūtasūta mahābhāga vyāsaśiṣya namo'stu te \|*  
*adbhuteyaṃ kathā tāta varṇitā kṛpayā hi naḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*munau gate haristāta kiṃ cakāra tataḥ param \|*  
*nāradopi gataḥ kutra tanme vyākhyātumarhasi \|\| 2 \|\|*

The sages said:——

1-2. Sūta, O blessed Sūta, the disciple of Vyāsa, our obeisance to thee. It is due to thy grace that this wonderful story has been narrated to us, O dear one.

Now tell us in detail what Viṣṇu did after Nārada had left the place? And where did Nārada go?

## \|\| 2.3.3 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya vacasteṣāṃ sūtaḥ paurāṇikottamaḥ \|*  
*pratyuvāca śivaṃ smṛtvā nānāsūtikaraṃ budhaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:—

3\. On hearing these words of the sages, Sūta the wise and excellent scholar of Purāṇas remembered Śiva, the cause of different kinds of creation and replied.

## \|\| 2.3.4 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*munau yadṛcchayā viṣṇurgate tasminhi nārade \|*  
*śivecchayā cakārāśu māyā māyāviśāradaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

Sūta said:—

4\. When Nārada went away casually Viṣṇu, skilful in wielding his Māyā, spread his Māyā, as Śiva had willed.

## \|\| 2.3.5 \|\|

*munimārgasya madhye tu virece nagaraṃ mahat \|*  
*śatayojanavistāramadbhutaṃ sumanoharam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. On the path taken by the sage He created a big wonderful city. It was a hundred Yojanas in extent and surprisingly beautiful.

## \|\| 2.3.6 \|\|

*svalokādadhikaṃ ramyaṃ nānāvastuvirājitam \|*  
*naranārīvihārāḍhyaṃ caturvarṇākulaṃ param \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. It was far more beautiful than heaven. Many articles were displayed there. Men and women of all the four castes stayed there.

## \|\| 2.3.7 \|\|

*tatra rājā śīlanirdhirnāmaiśvaryasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*sutāsvayamvarodyukto mahotsavasamanvitaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The wealthy and prosperous king of that city named Śīlanidhi was preparing for the gorgeous celebration of the voluntary wooing (Svayaṃvara) of his daughter.

## \|\| 2.3.8 \|\|

*caturdigbhyaḥ samāyātaissaṃyutaṃ nṛpanandataiḥ \|*  
*nānāveṣaissuśobhaiśca tatkanyāvaraṇotsukaiḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Brilliant princes coming from all the four quarters eager to court the princess had thronged there dressed in diverse ways.

## \|\| 2.3.9 \|\|

*etādṛśampuraṃ dṛṣṭvā mohamprāpto'tha nāradaḥ \|*  
*kautukī tannṛpadvāraṃ jagāma madanedhitaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. On seeing such a splendid city Nārada was enchanted. With his love kindled, he eagerly went to the palace threshold.

## \|\| 2.3.10 \|\|

*āgataṃ munivaryaṃ taṃ dṛṣṭvā śīlanidhirnṛpaḥ \|*  
*upaveśyārcayāṃcakre ratnasiṃhāsane vare \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. When the sage reached the palace the king Śīlanidhi adored him, having offered him a seat on the splendid throne studded with precious gems.

## \|\| 2.3.11 \|\|

*atha rājā svatanayāṃ nāmataśśrīmatīṃ varām \|*  
*samānīya nāradasya pādayossamapātayat \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. He called his daughter Śrīmatī and asked her to kneel down at the feet of Nārada.

## \|\| 2.3.12 \|\|

*tatkanyāṃ prekṣya sa munirnāradaḥ prāha vismitaḥ \|*  
*keyaṃ rājanmahābhāgā kanyā surasutopamā \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Being struck with wonder on seeing the girl, Nārada said—“O king, who is this lovely girl comparable to celestial damsels?”

## \|\| 2.3.13 \|\|

*tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā rājā prāha kṛtāṃjaliḥ \|*  
*duhiteyaṃ mama mune śrīmatī nāma nāmataḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. On hearing the words of the sage, the king replied with his palms joined in reverence—“O sage, this is my daughter Śrīmatī.

## \|\| 2.3.14 \|\|

*pradānasamayaṃ prāptā varamanveṣatī śubham \|*  
*sā svayaṃvarasaṃprāptā sarvalakṣaṇalakṣitā \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. She has attained the marriageable age. She is in search of a qualified bridegroom. She has all charms and accomplishments and her Svayaṃvara is imminent.

## \|\| 2.3.15 \|\|

*asyā bhāgyaṃ vada mune sarvaṃ jātakamādarāt \|*  
*kīdṛśaṃ tanayeyaṃ me varamāpsyati tadvada \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. O sage, kindly foretell her destiny, everything that is in her horoscope. Please tell me what sort of a husband she will get.”

## \|\| 2.3.16 \|\|

*ityukto muniśārdūlastāmicchuḥ kāmavihvalaḥ \|*  
*samābhāṣya sa rājānaṃ nārado vākyamabravīt \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. By the time these words were spoken Nārada had become an agitated victim of love and desired her. Addressing the king, he said thus:—

## \|\| 2.3.17 \|\|

*suteyaṃ tava bhūpāla sarvalakṣaṇalakṣitā \|*  
*mahābhāgyavatī dhanyā lakṣmīriva guṇālayā \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. “O great king, this daughter of yours is endowed with all characteristics: She is highly fortunate and blessed like Lakṣmī. She is an abode of all qualities.

## \|\| 2.3.18 \|\|

*sarveśvaro'jito vīro girīśasadṛśo vibhuḥ \|*  
*asyāḥ patirdhruvaṃ bhāvī kāmajitsurasattamaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Her future husband will certainly be a splendid God, lord of all, unvanquished, heroic, on a par with Śiva, and Vying with Kāmadeva”.

## \|\| 2.3.19 \|\|

*ityuktvā nṛpamāmaṃtrya yayau yādṛcchiko muniḥ \|*  
*babhūva kāmavivaśaśśivamāyā vimohitaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Having said this, the casual visitor Nārada took leave of the king. Deluded by Śiva’s Māyā he was extremely oppressed by love.

## \|\| 2.3.20 \|\|

*citte vicintya sa munirāpnuyāṃ kathamenakām \|*  
*svayaṃvare nṛpālānāmekaṃ māṃ vṛṇuyātkatham \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. The sage began to muse—“How shall I get her? How shall she woo me amongst the princes in the Svayaṃvara hall.

## \|\| 2.3.21 \|\|

*saundaryaṃ sarvanārīṇāṃ priyaṃ bhavati sarvathā \|*  
*taddṛṣṭvaiva prasannā sā svavaśā nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. A comely appearance appeals to all women in every respect. Only by seeing a charming personality will she become enamoured.

## \|\| 2.3.22 \|\|

*vidhāyetthaṃ viṣṇurūpaṃ grahītuṃ munisattamaḥ \|*  
*viṣṇulokaṃ jagāmāśu nāradaḥ smaravihvalaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Thinking thus, Nārada who was agitated by love, went to Viṣṇuloka somehow to acquire Viṣṇu’s form to captivate her.

## \|\| 2.3.23 \|\|

*praṇipatya hṛṣīkeśaṃ vākyametaduvāca ha \|*  
*rahasi tvāṃ pravakṣyāmi svavṛttāntamaśeṣataḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. He saluted Viṣṇu and said—“I shall tell you secretly my affairs entirely.”

## \|\| 2.3.24 \|\|

*tathetyukte tathā bhūte śivecchā kāryakarta hi \|*  
*brūhītyuktavati śrīśe munirāha ca keśavam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. When Viṣṇu who did everything according to Śiva’s wish agreed and asked him to narrate, the sage said:—

## \|\| 2.3.25 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*tvadīyo bhūpatiḥ śīlanidhissa vṛṣatatparaḥ \|*  
*tasya kanyā viśālākṣī śrīmatīvaravarṇinī \|\| 25 \|\|*

Nārada said:—

25\. The king Śīlanidhi is one of your devotees. He is a righteous king. His daughter Śrīmatī is a maiden of very fair complexion and wide eyes.

## \|\| 2.3.26 \|\|

*jaganmohinyabhikhyātā trailokyepyati sundarī \|*  
*pariṇetumahaṃ viṣṇo tāmicchāmyadya mā ciram \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. She has the lustre of Jaganmohinī (enchantress of the universe—a manifestation of Viṣṇu) and is the most beautiful woman in all the three worlds. O Viṣṇu, I wish to marry her without delay.

## \|\| 2.3.27 \|\|

*svayaṃvaraṃ cakarāsau bhūpatistanayecchayā \|*  
*caturdigbhyaḥ samāyātā rājaputrāssahasraśaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. The king at the request of the princess has arranged for a Svayaṃvara. Thousands of Princes have come from all the four quarters.

## \|\| 2.3.28 \|\|

*yadi dāsyasi rūpaṃ me tadā tāṃ prāpnuyāṃ dhruvam \|*  
*tvadrūpaṃ sā vinā kaṃṭhe jayamālāṃ na dhāsyati \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. If you can favour me with a splendid form I shall be able to gain her certainly. She will not put the wedding garland round my neck without your splendid form.

## \|\| 2.3.29 \|\|

*svarūpaṃ dehi me nātha sevako'haṃ priyastava \|*  
*vṛṇuyānmāṃ yathā sā vai śrīmatī kṣitipātmajā \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. O lord! give me your form. I am your servant and favourite. Give me your beautiful form so that the princess Śrīmatī may choose me.

## \|\| 2.3.30 \|\|

*suta uvāca \|\| vacaḥ śrutvā muneritthaṃ vihasya madhusūdanaḥ \|*  
*śāṃkarīṃ prabhutāṃ buddhvā pratyuvāca dayāparaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

Sūta said:—

30\. On hearing these words of the sage Viṣṇu, the slayer of Madhu demon laughed and sympathetically replied, bearing in mind the overwhelming power of Śiva.

## \|\| 2.3.31 \|\|

*viṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*sveṣṭadeśaṃ mune gaccha kariṣyāmi hitaṃ tava \|*  
*bhiṣagvaro yathārttasya yataḥ priyataro'si me \|\| 31 \|\|*

Viṣṇu said:—

31\. “O sage, you can go to the place where you wish. I shall do what is beneficent to you in the manner of a physician doing what is good to the patient, since you are a great favourite of mine.”

## \|\| 2.3.32 \|\|

*ityuktvā munaye tasmai dadau viṣṇurmukhaṃ hare \|*  
*svarūpamanugṛhyāsya tirodhānaṃ jagāma saḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. After saying thus, Viṣṇu blessed the sage with a form like his own and the face of Hari (i.e. the monkey since the word Hari means a monkey also). The lord then vanished.

## \|\| 2.3.33 \|\|

*evamukto munirhṛṣṭaḥ svarūpaṃ prāpya vai hareḥ \|*  
*mene kṛtārthamātmānaṃ tadyatnaṃ na bubodha saḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The sage thus consoled became highly delighted on receiving Hari’s form. He was contented but did not know the scheme behind the scene.

## \|\| 2.3.34 \|\|

*atha tatra gataḥ śīghrannārado munisattamaḥ \|*  
*cakre svayamvaraṃ yatra rājaputraissamākulam \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. The great sage Nārada hastened to the place where Svayaṃvara was to be held and where the princes had assembled.

## \|\| 2.3.35 \|\|

*svayamvarasabhā divyā rājaputrasamāvṛtā \|*  
*śuśubhe'tīva viprendrā yathā śakrasa bhā parā \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. O great brahmins, the Svayaṃvara hall splendidly decorated and graced by so many princes shone like another council-chamber of Indra.

## \|\| 2.3.36 \|\|

*tasyāṃ nṛpasabhāyāṃ vai nāradaḥ samupāviśat \|*  
*sthitvā tatra vicintyeti prītiyuktena cetasā \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Nārada too went in and sat down in the hall of his king. With his mind surging with love he began to think like this.

## \|\| 2.3.37 \|\|

*māṃ variṣyati nānyaṃ sā viṣṇurūpadharandhruvam \|*  
*ānanasya kurūpatvaṃ na veda munisattamaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. “She will choose only me since I am in Viṣṇu’s form”. The poor sage did not know the ugly character of his face.

## \|\| 2.3.38 \|\|

*pūrvarūpaṃ muniṃ sarve dadṛśu'statra mānavāḥ \|*  
*tadbhedaṃ bubudhuste na rājaputrādayo dvijāḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. The men assembled there saw the sage only in his old form. O brahmins, the princes and others did not know the difference created therein.

## \|\| 2.3.39 \|\|

*tatra rudragaṇau dvau tadrakṣaṇārthaṃ samāgatau \|*  
*viprarūpadharau gūḍhau tatredaṃ jajñatuḥ param \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Two of the attendants of Rudra knew this difference. They had come there in the guise of brahmins in order to protect him.

## \|\| 2.3.40 \|\|

*mūḍha matvā muniṃ tau tannikaṭaṃ jagmaturgaṇau \|*  
*kurutastatprahāsaṃ vai bhāṣamāṇau parasparam \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Considering the sage a fool, the two attendants sat near the sage and began to mock at him seemingly conversing between themselves.

## \|\| 2.3.41 \|\|

*paśya nārada rūpaṃ hi viṣṇoriva mahottamam \|*  
*mukhaṃ tu vānarasyeva vikaṭaṃ ca bhayaṃkaram \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. “See Nārada’s features as splendid as Viṣṇu’s, but the face as that of a monkey deformed and awful.

## \|\| 2.3.42 \|\|

*icchatyayaṃ nṛpasutā vṛthaiva smaramohitaḥ \|*  
*ityuktvā sacchalaṃ vākyamupahāsaṃ pracakratuḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Being deluded by Kāma he wishes to marry the Princess”. With these and other veiled remarks they mocked at him.

## \|\| 2.3.43 \|\|

*na śuśrāva yathārthaṃ tu tadvākyaṃ smaravihvalaḥ \|*  
*paryaikṣacchrīmatīṃ tāṃ vai tallipsurmohito muniḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. The sage overwhelmed by love did not heed their whisper. He went on gazing at the princess Śrīmatī and was eager to get her.

## \|\| 2.3.44 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare bhūpakanyā cāṃtaḥpurāttu sā \|*  
*strībhissamāvṛtā tatrājagāma varavarṇinī \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. In the meantime, the princess had come out of the harem surrounded by ladies in waiting. The comely maiden came to the hall.

## \|\| 2.3.45 \|\|

*mālāṃ hiraṇmayīṃ ramyāmādāya śubha kṣaṇā \|*  
*tatra svayambare reje sthitā madhye rameva sā \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. With the beautiful golden garland in her hands, the princess of auspicious features, shone in the middle of the Svayaṃvara hall like Goddess Lakṣmī.

## \|\| 2.3.46 \|\|

*babhrāma sā sabhāṃ sarvāṃ mālāmādāya suvratā \|*  
*varamanveṣatī tatra svātmābhīṣṭaṃ nṛpātmajā \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. The princess in search of a suitable bridegroom went round the hall with the garland in her hands.

## \|\| 2.3.47 \|\|

*vānarāsyaṃ viṣṇutanuṃ muniṃ dṛṣṭvā cukopa sā \|*  
*dṛṣṭiṃ nivārya ca tataḥ prasthitā prītamānasā \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. On seeing the sage with the face of a monkey and the body of Viṣṇu she was infuriated. Averting her eyes she went elsewhere being distressed in her mind.

## \|\| 2.3.48 \|\|

*na dṛṣṭvā svavaraṃ tatra trastāsīnmanasepsitam \|*  
*aṃtassabhāsthitā kasminnarpayāmāsa na srajam \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Failing to find a bridegroom of her choice she was afraid. She remained in the middle of the hall and did not put the garland round the neck of any one.

## \|\| 2.3.49 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare viṣṇurājagāma nṛpākṛtiḥ \|*  
*na dṛṣṭaḥ kaiścidaparaiḥ kevalaṃ sā dadarśa hi \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Meanwhile Viṣṇu came there in the guise of a king. He was not seen by anyone. Only the princess saw him.

## \|\| 2.3.50 \|\|

*atha sā taṃ samālokya prasannavadanāmbujā \|*  
*arpayāmāsa tatkaṇṭhe tāṃ mālāṃ varavarṇinī \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Then on seeing Viṣṇu, her lotus-like face beamed. The comely lady put the garland round his neck.

## \|\| 2.3.51 \|\|

*tāmādāya tato viṣṇū rājarūpadharaḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*aṃtardhānamagātsadyassvasthānaṃ prayayau kila \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Lord Viṣṇu in the guise of a king took her with him and vanished from there immediately back to his own abode.

## \|\| 2.3.52 \|\|

*sarve rājakumārāśca nirāśāḥ śrīmatīmprati \|*  
*munistu vihvalo'tīva babhūva madanāturaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. The assembled princes lost their hope of getting Śrīmatī. The sage oppressed by love became excessively agitated.

## \|\| 2.3.53 \|\|

*tadā tāvūcatussadyo nāradaṃ svaravihvalam \|*  
*viprarūpadharau rudragaṇau jñānaviśāradau \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Immediately the two attendants of Rudra, of perfect wisdom, disguised as brahmins spoke to Nārada.

## \|\| 2.3.54 \|\|

*gaṇāvūcatuḥ \|*  
*he nāradamune tvaṃ hi vṛthā madanamohitaḥ \|*  
*tallipsussvamukhaṃ paśya vānarasyeva garhitam \|\| 54 \|\|*

The attendants said:—

54\. O sage Nārada, being deluded by love, you are desirous of getting her. Your effort is in vain. See, your face is as despicable as that of a monkey.

## \|\| 2.3.55 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya tayorvākyaṃ nārado vismito'bhavat \|*  
*mukhaṃ dadarśa mukure śivamāyāvimohitaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

Sūta said:—

55\. On hearing their words Nārada was surprised. Deluded by Śiva’s māyā he looked into a mirror.

## \|\| 2.3.56 \|\|

*svamukhaṃ vānarasyeva dṛṣṭvā cukrodha satvaram \|*  
*śāpandadau tayostatra gaṇayormohito muniḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. On seeing his face like that of a monkey he became infuriated. The deluded sage cursed the two attendants.

## \|\| 2.3.57 \|\|

*yuvāṃ mamopahāsaṃ vai cakraturbrāhmaṇasya hi \|*  
*bhavetāṃ rākṣasau vipravīryajau vai tadākṛtī \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Since you had mocked at me, you will become demons born of brahminical semen and of that form.

## \|\| 2.3.58-59 \|\|

*śrutvā haragaṇāvitthaṃ svaśāpaṃ jñānisattamau \|*  
*na kiṃcidūcatustau hi munimājñāya mohitam \|\| 58 \|\|*

*svasthānaṃ jagmaturviprā udāsīnau śivastutim \|*  
*cakraturmanyamānau vai śivecchāṃ sakalāṃ sadā \|\| 59 \|\|*

58-59. On hearing the curse, the two attendants of perfect wisdom remained silent because they knew that the sage was deluded. O brahmins, they returned to their abode and sitting there quietly went on eulogising Śiva. They considered everything as Śiva’s will.

## Chapter 4 - Nārada goes to Vaikuṇṭha and curses Viṣṇu there

## \|\| 2.4.3-5 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*vimohito munirdattvā tayośśāpaṃ yathocitam \|*  
*jale mukhaṃ nirīkṣyātha svarūpaṃ giriśecchayā \|\| 3 \|\|*

*śivecchayā na prabuddhaḥ smṛtvā harikṛtacchalam \|*  
*krodhaṃ durviṣahaṃ kṛtvā viṣṇulokaṃ jagāma ha \|\| 4 \|\|*

*uvāca vacanaṃ kuddhassamiddha iva pāvakaḥ \|*  
*duruktigarbhitaṃ vyaṅgaḥ naṣṭajñānaśśivecchayā \|\| 5 \|\|*

The sages said:—

l-2. Sūta, O Sūta of great intellect, a wonderful tale has been narrated by you. Blessed indeed is the Māyā of Śiva. All mobile and immobile things depend upon it. When the two attendants of lord Rudra had left at their own will what did the infuriated Nārada, the sage disquieted by Kāmadeva, do?

Sūta said:—

3-5. After cursing the two attendants of Śiva suitably, the sage still under the earlier delusion looked into the water and saw that his face was quite normal. It was also due to Śiva’s will. He did not wake from the delusion still again due to Śiva’s will. Thereupon recollecting that it might have been a deception of Hari, he became unbearably infuriated and went to Viṣṇuloka. There he angrily poured abusive words blazing like kindled fire since his wisdom had vanished due to Śiva’s will.

## \|\| 2.4.6 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*he hare tvaṃ mahāduṣṭaḥ kapaṭī viśvamohanaḥ \|*  
*parotsāhaṃ na sahase māyāvī malināśayaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

Nārada said:—

6\. O Viṣṇu, you are extremely wicked, deceptive enchanter of the world. You are unable to brook others’ enthusiastic success. You dabble in illusory tactics and your intentions are always dirty.

## \|\| 2.4.7 \|\|

*mohinīrūpamādāya kapaṭaṃ kṛtavānpurā \|*  
*asurebhyo'pāyayastvaṃ vāruṇīmamṛtaṃ na hi \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Formerly you assumed the form of an enchantress and showed your deceptive power. You made the demons drink liquor and not the nectar.

## \|\| 2.4.8 \|\|

*cetpibenna viṣaṃ rudro dayāṃ kṛtvā maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*bhavennaṣṭā'khilā māyā tava vyājarate hare \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. If out of pity Śiva had not drunk poison, O Viṣṇu, all your illusory tactics would have been quelled since you take pleasure only in deception.

## \|\| 2.4.9 \|\|

*gatissa kapaṭā te'tipriyā viṣṇo viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*sādhusvabhāvo na bhavānsvataṃtraḥ prabhuṇā kṛtaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. O Viṣṇu, a deceptive path is extremely attractive to you. You had never been of saintly nature, but the lord made you free from control.

## \|\| 2.4.10-11 \|\|

*kṛtaṃ samucitannaiva śivena paramātmanā \|*  
*tatprabhāvabalaṃ dhyātvā svataṃtrakṛtikārakaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*tvadgatiṃ susamājñāya paścāttāpamavāpa saḥ \|*  
*vipraṃ sarvopari prāha svoktaveda pramāṇakṛt \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. What is done by Śiva the supreme Ātman does not seem proper. Thinking of your influence and strength when you act independently and seeing the way you go He has now repented. He has announced that a brahmin is superior to all, thereby making the Vedas pronounced by Him authoritative.

## \|\| 2.4.12 \|\|

*tajjñātvāhaṃ hare tvādya śikṣayiṣyāmi tadbalāt \|*  
*yathā na kuryāḥ kutrāpīdṛśaṃ karma kadācana \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. O Viṣṇu, knowing that, I shall now teach you through that power so that hereafter you will never do such things.

## \|\| 2.4.13 \|\|

*adyāpi nirbhayastvaṃ hi saṃgaṃ nāpastarasvinā \|*  
*idānīṃ lapsyase viṣṇo phalaṃ svakṛtakarmaṇaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. You are fearless because till now you have not come into clash with an equally powerful person. Now you will derive, O Viṣṇu, the fruit of your own “deeds”.

## \|\| 2.4.14 \|\|

*itthamuktvā hariṃ sotha munirmāyā vimohitaḥ \|*  
*śaśāpa krodhanirviṇṇo brahmatejaḥ pradarśayan \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. After saying this, the sage still under the influence of Māyā furiouly cursed Viṣṇu, thereby exhibiting the superiority of his brahminical power.

## \|\| 2.4.15-16 \|\|

*strīkṛte vyākulaṃ viṣṇo māmakārṣīrvimohakaḥ \|*  
*anvakārṣīssvarūpeṇa yena kāpaṭyakāryakṛt \|\| 15 \|\|*

*tadrūpeṇa manuṣyastvaṃ bhava tadduḥkhabhugghare \|*  
*yanmukhaṃ kṛtavānme tvaṃ te bhavaṃtu sahāyinaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. O Viṣṇu, the enchanter that you are, you made me distressed for the sake of woman. O Hari, you shall experience misery in that human form which you imitated while proceeding with your deceptive tactics. Your allies will be those whose face you assigned to me.

## \|\| 2.4.17 \|\|

*tvaṃ strīviyogajaṃ duḥkhaṃ labhasva paraduḥkhadaḥ \|*  
*manuṣyagatikaḥ prāyo bhavājñānavimohitaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. O inflictor of miseries upon others, you shall get the misery of separation from a woman. You shall have the travails of a human being deluded by ignorance.”

## \|\| 2.4.18 \|\|

*iti śaptvā hariṃ mohānnārado'jñānamohitaḥ \|*  
*viṣṇurjagrāha taṃ śāpaṃ praśaṃsañśāṃbhavīmajām \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Thus Nārada, deluded himself by ignorance, cursed Hari. Viṣṇu quietly accepted the cause praising the Māyā of Sambhu.

## \|\| 2.4.19 \|\|

*atha śaṃbhurmahālīlo niścakarṣa vimohinīma \|*  
*svamāyāṃ mohito jñānī nāradopyabhavadyayā \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Thereafter Śiva, of great divine sport withdrew his enchanting Māyā whereby Nārada became wise (as before) and free from delusion.

## \|\| 2.4.20-21 \|\|

*aṃtarhitāyāṃ māyāyāṃ pūrvavanmatimānabhūt \|*  
*nārado vismitamanāḥ prāptabodho nirākulaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*paścāttāpamavāpyāti nininda svaṃ muhurmuhuḥ \|*  
*praśaśaṃsa tadā māyāṃ śāṃbhavīṃ jñānimohinīm \|\| 21 \|\|*

20-21. When the Māyā vanished he became as intelligent as before regaining perfect knowledge and becoming free from distress. He was surprised (at his own action in the meantime). He cursed himself after repenting again and again. He praised the Māyā of Śiva which could enchant even wise people.

## \|\| 2.4.22 \|\|

*atha jñātvā munissarvaṃ māyāvibhramamātmanaḥ \|*  
*apatatpādayorviṣṇornārado vaiṣṇavottamaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. On realising his mistakes due to illusion, Nārada, the most excellent of the devotees of Viṣṇu, fell at his feet.

## \|\| 2.4.23 \|\|

*haryyupasthāpitaḥ prāha vacanaṃ naṣṭa durmatiḥ \|*  
*mayā duraktayaḥ proktā mohitena kubuddhinā \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Consoled by Hari and freed from wicked ideas he said—“Being deluded and evil-minded I have spoken many wicked words to you.

## \|\| 2.4.24 \|\|

*dattaśśāpo'pi tenātha vitathaṃ kuru taṃ prabho \|*  
*mahatpāpamakārṣaṃ hi yāsyāmi nirayaṃ dhuvam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. O lord, I heaped curses on you. O master, please make them ineffective. I have committed a great sin. Certainly I will be falling into a hell.

## \|\| 2.4.25 \|\|

*kamupāyaṃ hare kuryāṃ dāso'haṃ te tamādiśa \|*  
*yena pāpakulaṃ naśyennirayo na bhavenmama \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. O Hari, I am your slave. Please direct me what to do whereby I may destroy my sins and prevent my downfall into hell.”

## \|\| 2.4.26 \|\|

*ityuktvā sa punarviṣṇoḥ pādayormunisattamaḥ \|*  
*papāta sumatirbhaktyā paścāttāpamupāgataḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Saying thus, the excellent sage once again fell at Viṣṇu’s feet and with the mind purified repented sincerely.

## \|\| 2.4.27 \|\|

*atha viṣṇustamutthāpya babhāṣe sūnṛtaṃ vacaḥ \|*  
*viṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*na khedaṃ kuru me bhakta varastvaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Thereupon Viṣṇu lifted him up and spoke affably and courteously.

## \|\| 2.4.28 \|\|

*śṛṇu tāta pravakṣyāmi suhitaṃ tava niścayāt \|*  
*nirayaste na bhavitā śivaśśaṃ te vidhāsyati \|\| 28 \|\|*

Viṣṇu said:—

“Do not be sorry too much. Undoubtedly you are my true devotee.

28\. Dear sage, now listen. I shall tell you what is certainly beneficial to you. You will not fall into hell. Śiva will make you happy.

## \|\| 2.4.29 \|\|

*yadakārṣīśśivavaco vitathaṃ madamohitaḥ \|*  
*sa dattavānīdṛśaṃ te phalaṃ karma phalapradaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Deluded by your haughtiness you disobeyed the instructions of Śiva. The true bestower of fruits according to the actions, He has given you this result.

## \|\| 2.4.30 \|\|

*śivecchā'khilaṃ jātaṃ kurvitthaṃ niścitāṃ matim \|*  
*garvāpahartā sa svāmī śaṃkaraḥ parameśvaraḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Be sure in your mind that everything has happened in accordance with Śiva’s wish. That lord Śiva, the supreme lord, removes haughtiness.

## \|\| 2.4.31 \|\|

*paraṃ brahma parātmā sa saccidānaṃdabodhanaḥ \|*  
*nirguṇo nirvikāro ca rajassatvatamaḥpara \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. He is the supreme Brahman; the supreme Ātman, Existence, Knowledge and Bliss. He is free from the three Guṇas, changes and deviations. He is beyond Rajas, Sattva and Tamas.

## \|\| 2.4.32 \|\|

*sa evamādāya māyāṃ svāṃ tridhā bhavati rūpataḥ \|*  
*brahmaviṣṇumaheśātmā nirguṇo'nirguṇo'pi saḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. He is both Saguṇa and Nirguṇa (with and without attributes). He Himself availing of his own Māyā manifests into three forms—Brahma, Viṣṇu, and Maheśa.

## \|\| 2.4.33 \|\|

*nirguṇatve śivāhvo hi paramātmā maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*paraṃ brahmāvyayo'naṃto mahādeveti gīyate \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. In his attributeless pure form He is glorified as Śiva, the supreme Ātman, Maheśvara, the supreme Brahman, the undecaying, the endless, and Mahādeva.

## \|\| 2.4.34 \|\|

*tatsevayā vidhissraṣṭā pālako jagatāmaham \|*  
*svayaṃ sarvasya saṃhārī rudrarūpeṇa sarvadā \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Serving him, Brahmā becomes the creator and I the sustainer of the worlds. He himself in the manifestation as Rudra is the annihilator always.

## \|\| 2.4.35 \|\|

*sākṣī śivasvarūpeṇa māyābhinnassa nirguṇaḥ \|*  
*svecchācārī saṃvihārī bhaktānugrahakārakaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Different from Māyā, the pure Being in the form of Śiva is the Sākṣin (cosmic witness) and moving about according to His Will and indulging in divine sport He blesses his devotees.

## \|\| 2.4.36 \|\|

*śṛṇu tvaṃ nārada mune sadupāyaṃ sukhapradam \|*  
*sarvapāpāpaharttāraṃ bhuktimuktipradaṃ sadā \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. O sage Nārada, please listen to a good remedy that bestows happiness, removes all sins and yields worldly pleasures and salvation.

## \|\| 2.4.37 \|\|

*ityuktvāstvasaṃśayaṃ sarvaṃ śaṃkarasadyaśaḥ \|*  
*śatanāmaśivastotraṃ sadānanyamatirjapa \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Cast off all your doubts. Sing the songs of noble glory of Śiva. With your mind not turning to anything else, always repeat the hundred names of Śiva and his hymns.

## \|\| 2.4.38 \|\|

*yajjapitvā drutaṃ sarvaṃ tava pāpaṃ vinaśyati \|*  
*ityuktvā nāradaṃ viṣṇuḥ punaḥ prāha dayānvitaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. By his Japa all of your sins will perish instantaneously. After saying this to Nārada, Viṣṇu continued mercifully.

## \|\| 2.4.39 \|\|

*mune na kuru śokaṃ tvaṃ tvayā kiṃcitkṛtaṃ nahi \|*  
*svecchayā kṛtavānśaṃbhuridaṃ sarvaṃ na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. “O sage, do not be grief-striken. Nothing has been perpetrated by you. It was Śiva who did everything. There is no doubt in this.

## \|\| 2.4.40 \|\|

*ahārṣittvanmatiṃ divyāṃ kāma kleśamadātsa te \|*  
*tvanmukhāddāpayāṃcakre śāpaṃ me sa maheśvaraḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. It was lord Maheśvara who deluded your splendid intellect and made you suffer on account of love. It was he who made you His mouthpiece and cursed me.

## \|\| 2.4.41 \|\|

*itthaṃ svacaritaṃ loke prakaṭīkṛtavān svayam \|*  
*mṛtyuṃjayaḥ kālakālo bhaktoddhāraparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. In this manner the great Conqueror of Death, Kāla of Kāla, always devoted to the uplift of his devotees, made His own conduct of life manifest in the world.

## \|\| 2.4.42 \|\|

*na me śivasamānosti priyaḥ svāmī sukhapradaḥ \|*  
*sarvaśaktiprado me'sti sa eva parameśvaraḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. There is no other lord and master so loving and pleasure-inspiring unto me as Śiva. The same Parameśvara bestows all power on me.

## \|\| 2.4.43 \|\|

*tasyopāsyāṃ kuru mune tameva satataṃ bhaja \|*  
*tadyaśaḥ śṛṇu gāya tvaṃ kuru nityaṃ tadarcanam \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. O sage, perform His adoration. Worship him always. Hear and sing his glory. Perpetually pay Him homage.

## \|\| 2.4.44 \|\|

*kāyena manasā vācā yaśśaṃkaramupaiti bho \|*  
*sa paṇḍita iti jñeyassa jīvanmukta ucyate \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. He who approaches Śiva by means of his body, mind and speech is a great scholar. He is called a living liberated soul.

## \|\| 2.4.45 \|\|

*śiveti nāmadāvāgnermahāpātakapa rvatāḥ \|*  
*bhasmībhavantyanāyāsātsatyaṃ satyaṃ na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. The name Śiva blazing like the forest conflagration reduces mountainous heaps of great sins to ashes without any difficulty. True, it is undoubtedly true.

## \|\| 2.4.46 \|\|

*pāpamūlāni duḥkhāni vividhānyapi tānyataḥ \|*  
*śivārcanaikanaśyāni nānya naśyāni sarvathā \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. The different kinds of miseries arising from sins shall be destroyed only through the worship of Śiva, and not through other means.

## \|\| 2.4.47 \|\|

*sa vaidikasya puṇyātmā sa dhanyassa budho mune \|*  
*yassadā kāyavākcittaiśśaraṇaṃ yāti śaṃkaram \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. He who always seeks refuge in Śiva, O sage, is the real follower of the Vedas, a meritorious soul and a blessed scholar. He must resort to Him by means of his body, speech and mind for ever.

## \|\| 2.4.48 \|\|

*bhavaṃti vividhā dharmā yeṣāṃ sadyaḥphalonmukhāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ bhavati viśvāsastripurāṃtakapūjane \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. The different sacred rites of those who have full faith in the worship of Śiva, the destroyer of Tripura become fruitful instantaneously.

## \|\| 2.4.49 \|\|

*pātakāni vinaśyaṃti yāvaṃti śivapūjayā \|*  
*bhuvi tāvaṃti pāpāni na saṃtyeva mahāmune \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. O great sage, there are not so many sins in the world as the worship of Śiva is capable of destroying.

## \|\| 2.4.50 \|\|

*brahmahatyādipāpānāṃ rāśayopyamitā mune \|*  
*śivasmṛtyā vinaśyaṃti satyaṃsatyaṃ vadāmyaham \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Innumerable heaps of sins like that of the slaughter of a brahmin perish by remembering Śiva. Truth, I am telling you the truth.

## \|\| 2.4.51 \|\|

*śivanāmatarīṃ prāpya saṃsārābdhiṃ taraṃti te \|*  
*saṃsāramūlapāpāni tasya naśyaṃtyasaṃśayam \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. The sins (that usually cause worldly existence) relating to persons who cross the ocean of worldly existence in the raft of Śiva’s names, perish undoubtedly.

## \|\| 2.4.52 \|\|

*saṃsāramūlabhūtānāṃ pātakānāṃ mahāmune \|*  
*śivanāmakuṭhāreṇa vināśo jāyate dhruvam \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. The sins which are at the root of worldly existence are destroyed certainly by the axe of Śiva’s name.

## \|\| 2.4.53 \|\|

*śivanāmāmṛtaṃ peyaṃ pāpadāvānalārditaiḥ \|*  
*pāpadāvāgnitaptānāṃ śāṃtistena vinā na hi \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Persons scorched and distressed by the conflagration of sins must drink the nectar of Śiva’s names. Without that there is no peace and tranquillity to those who are scorched and distressed by the sins’ wild fire.

## \|\| 2.4.54 \|\|

*śiveti nāmapīyūṣavarṣadhārāpariplutaḥ \|*  
*saṃsāradavamadhyapi na śocati na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Those who are drenched by the downpour of the nectarine names of Śiva are not distressed in the midst of the conflagration of worldly existence. There is no doubt in this.

## \|\| 2.4.55-56 \|\|

*na bhaktiśśaṃkare puṃsāṃ rāgadveṣaratātmanām \|*  
*tadvidhānāṃ hi sahasā muktirbhavati sarvathā \|\| 55 \|\|*

*anaṃtajanmabhiryena tapastaptaṃ bhaviṣyati \|*  
*tasyaiva bhaktirbhavati bhavānī prāṇavallabhe \|\| 56 \|\|*

55-56. Immediate salvation can be achieved only by the people who have performed penance in various lives. They alone will have devotion for Śiva the cherished consort of Pārvatī. Men who frequently indulge in passions of love and hatred will never have devotion for Śiva.

## \|\| 2.4.57 \|\|

*jātāpi śaṃkare bhaktiranyasādhāraṇī vṛthā \|*  
*paraṃ tvavyabhicāreṇa śivabhaktirapekṣitā \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. The devotion for Śiva that extends to other deities is futile. It is necessary to be exclusively devoted to Śiva.

## \|\| 2.4.58 \|\|

*yasyā sādhāraṇī śaṃbhau bhaktiravyabhicāriṇī \|*  
*tasyaiva mokṣassulabho nāsyetinya matirmama \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. It is my conviction that salvation is easy of access only to the person who has exclusive and unflinching devotion for Śiva and not for any other.

## \|\| 2.4.59 \|\|

*kṛtvāpyanaṃtapāpāni yadi bhaktirmaheśvare \|*  
*sarvapāpavinirmukto bhavatyeva na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Even if he commits endless sins, he will be freed from them all, if he has true devotion for Śiva. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 2.4.60 \|\|

*bhavaṃti bhasmasādvṛkṣādavadagdhā yathā vane \|*  
*tathā bhavaṃti dagdhāni śāṃkarāṇāmaghānyapi \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Just as trees in the forest are reduced to ashes in the wild fire so also the sins of the devotees of Śiva are burnt away in the fire of Śiva’s name.

## \|\| 2.4.61 \|\|

*yo nityaṃ bhasmapūtāṃgo śivapūjonmukho bhavet \|*  
*sa taratyeva saṃsāramapāramatidāruṇam \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. He who is ever devoted to the worship of Śiva with his body purified by the ash, definitely crosses the terrible and endless expanse of the ocean of worldly existence.

## \|\| 2.4.62 \|\|

*brahmasvaharaṇaṃ kṛtvā hatvāpi brāhmaṇānbahūn \|*  
*lipyate naraḥ pāpairvirūpākṣasya sevakaḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. A man serving the three-eyed Śiva is never sullied by sins even if he misappropriates a brahmin’s wealth or kills many brahmins.

## \|\| 2.4.63 \|\|

*vilokya vedānakhilāñchivasyaivārcanamparam \|*  
*saṃsāranāśanopāya iti pūrvairviniścitam \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. After going through all the Vedas this has been definitely concluded by ancestors that the sole means of destroying worldly existence is the worship of Siva.

## \|\| 2.4.64 \|\|

*adyaprabhṛti yatnena sāvadhāno yathāvidhi \|*  
*sāmbaṃ sadāśivaṃ bhaktyā bhaja nityaṃ maheśvaram \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. From now onwards you shall always worship lord Śiva who is Sāmba and Sadāśiva, with care, effort and due observance of the rules of procedure.

## \|\| 2.4.65 \|\|

*āpādamastakaṃ samyak bhasmanoddhūlya sādaram \|*  
*sarvaśrutiśrutaṃ śaivammaṃtrañjapa ṣaḍakṣaram \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Dusting profusely and carefully your body from head to foot with the particles of ashes, you shall perform the Japa of the six-syllabled mantra of Śiva, well-known in all the Vedas.

## \|\| 2.4.66 \|\|

*savārṅgeṣu prayatnena rudrākṣāñchivavallabhān \|*  
*dhārayasvātisadbhaktyā samantramvidhipūrvakam \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. You shall wear on the different parts of your body Rudrākṣa beads pleasing to Śiva, repeating the respective mantras with devotion and observing the rules of procedure.

## \|\| 2.4.67 \|\|

*śṛṇu śaivīṃ kathāṃ nityaṃ vada śaivīṃ kathāṃ sadā \|*  
*pūjayasvātiyatnena śivabhaktānpunaḥ punaḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Listen to Śiva’s anecdotes for ever. Narrate the stories of Śiva always. Strenuously worship the devotees of Śiva again and again.

## \|\| 2.4.68 \|\|

*apramādena satataṃ śivaikaśaraṇo bhava \|*  
*śivārcanena satatamānandaḥ prāpyate yataḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Without blundering ever seek refuge in Śiva, be cause a perpetual worship of Śiva bestows bliss.

## \|\| 2.4.69 \|\|

*urasyādhāya viśade śivasya caraṇāmbujau \|*  
*śivatīrthāni vicara prathamaṃ munisattama \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. Bearing the lotus-like feet of Śiva within your pure heart, carry on at first the pilgrimage to various holy centres of Śiva, O excellent sage.

## \|\| 2.4.70 \|\|

*paśyanmāhātmyamatulaṃ śaṃkarasya parātmanaḥ \|*  
*gacchānandavanaṃ paścācchaṃbhupriyatamaṃ mune \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Observing the unrivalled greatness of Śiva, the supreme Ātman, O sage, you must next go to Ānandavana which is a great favourite of Siva.

## \|\| 2.4.71 \|\|

*tatra viśveśvaraṃ dṛṣṭvā pūjanaṃ kuru bhaktitaḥ \|*  
*natvā stutvā viśeṣeṇa nirvikalpo bhaviṣyasi \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. Seeing Śiva, the lord of the universe there, worship Him with devotion. After bowing to him and eulogising Him you will become free from all doubts.

## \|\| 2.4.72 \|\|

*tataśca bhavatā nūnaṃ vidheyaṃ gamanaṃ mune \|*  
*brahmaloke svakāmārthaṃ śāsanānmama bhaktitaḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. Thereafter you must go to Brahmaloka, O sage, to achieve your wishes. That is my command to you out of love.

## \|\| 2.4.73 \|\|

*natvā stutvā viśeṣeṇa vidhiṃ svajanakaṃ mune \|*  
*praṣṭavyaṃ śivamāhātmyaṃ bahuśaḥ prītacetasā \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. O sage, after bowing to and specifically eulogising your father Brahma, you shall ask him many points regarding Śiva’s greatness with an endearing mind.

## \|\| 2.4.74 \|\|

*sa śaivapravaro brahmā māhātmyaṃ śaṃkarasya te \|*  
*śrāvayiṣyati suprītyā śatanāmastavaṃ ca hi \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. Brahma, the foremost among the devotees of Śiva, will narrate to you the greatness of Śiva as well as the hymn of hundred names, out of love.

## \|\| 2.4.75 \|\|

*adyatastvaṃ bhava mune śaivaśśivaparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*muktibhāgī viśeṣeṇa śivaste śaṃ vidhāsyati \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. O sage, from now onwards become a devotee of Śiva, solely devoted to Śiva. You will be liberated. Śiva will grant you his special blessings”.

## \|\| 2.4.76 \|\|

*itthaṃ viṣṇurmuniṃ prītyā hyupadiśya prasannadhīḥ \|*  
*smṛtvā nutvā śivaṃ stutvā tatastvaṃtaradhīyata \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. After advising the sage thus, Viṣṇu was pleased. Remembering, saluting and eulogising Śiva he vanished from that place.

## Chapter 5 - Nārada goes to Kāśī

## \|\| 2.5.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*aṃtarhite harau viprā nārado munisattamaḥ \|*  
*vicacāra mahīṃ paśyañchivaliṃgāni bhaktitaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sūta said:—

1\. O brahmins, when Viṣṇu vanished, the excellent sage Nārada roamed over the Earth seeing Śiva Liṅgas (in the various holy centres) with piety.

## \|\| 2.5.2 \|\|

*pṛthivyā aṭanaṃ kṛtvā śivarūpāṇyanekaśaḥ \|*  
*dadarśa prītito viprā bhuktimuktipradāni saḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. In the course of his wanderings over the Earth, O brahmins, with his mind full of devotional pleasure he saw many forms of Śiva that confer worldly pleasures and salvation on the devotees.

## \|\| 2.5.3 \|\|

*atha taṃ vicaraṃtaṃ kau nāradaṃ divyadarśanam \|*  
*jñātvā śaṃbhugaṇau tau tu sucittamupajagmatuḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. On knowing that Nārada of divine vision was wandering over the Earth, the two attendants of Śiva approached him who by that time had become pure in mind.

## \|\| 2.5.4 \|\|

*śirasā supraṇamyāśu gaṇāvūcaturādarāt \|*  
*gṛhītvā caraṇau tasya śāpoddhārecchayā ca tau \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. They bowed to him and touched his feet. With a desire to secure release from the curse they spoke to him respectfully.

## \|\| 2.5.5 \|\|

*śivagaṇāvūcatuḥ \|*  
*brahmaputra surarṣe hi śṛṇu prītyā vayorvacaḥ \|*  
*tavāparādhakartārāvāvāṃ viprau na vastutaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

The attendants of Śiva said:—

5\. O celestial sage, son of Brahmā, please hear our words. We who formerly offended you are really not brahmins.

## \|\| 2.5.6-7 \|\|

*āvāṃ haragaṇau vipra tavāgaskāriṇau mune \|*  
*svayambare rājaputryā māyāmohitacetasā \|\| 6 \|\|*

*tvayā dattaśca nau śāpaḥ pareśapreritena ha \|*  
*jñātvā kusamayaṃ tatra maunameva hi jīvanam \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. O brahminical sage, we, your former offenders, are the attendants of Śiva. Induced by Śiva you had cursed us when your mind was deluded by the illusory infatuation for the princess at the Svayaṃvara. Realising that the occasion was inopportune we kept quiet then.

## \|\| 2.5.8 \|\|

*svakarmaṇaḥ phalaṃ prāptaṃ kasyāpi na hi dūṣaṇam \|*  
*suprasanno bhava vibho kurvanugrahamadya nau \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. We reaped the fruit of our own action. No one is to be blamed for it. O lord, be pleased. Bless us now.

## \|\| 2.5.9 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*vaca ākarṇya gaṇayoriti bhaktyuktamādarāt \|*  
*pratyuvāca muniḥ prītyā paścāttāpamavāpya saḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

Sūta said:—

9\. On hearing the words of the attendants uttered with devotion and respect, the sage replied lovingly, repenting (for his previous fury).

## \|\| 2.5.10 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇutaṃ me mahādeva gaṇā mānyatamau satām \|*  
*vacanaṃ sukhadaṃ mohanirmuktaṃ ca yathārthakam\|\| \|\| 10 \|\|*

Nārada said:—

10\. O attendants of Lord Śiva, most worthy of the respect of good people, please listen to my words now free from delusion. They are true and shall make you happy.

## \|\| 2.5.11 \|\|

*purā mama matirbhraṣṭāsīcchivecchāvaśāt yuvam \|*  
*sarvathā mohamāpannaśśaptavānvāṃ kuśemuṣiḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Formerly my mind had been depraved. Certainly it was Śiva’s will. In that state of delusion and crookedness of the mind I had unfortunately cursed both of you.

## \|\| 2.5.12 \|\|

*yaduktaṃ tattathā bhāvi tathāpi śṛṇutāṃ gaṇau \|*  
*śāpoddhāramahaṃ vacmi kṣamathā maghamadya me \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. What I have said is bound to happen. Still, O Gaṇas (attendants) listen. I shall tell you the way of redemption from the curse. Please forgive my sin now.

## \|\| 2.5.13-14 \|\|

*vīryānmunivarasyāptvā rākṣaseśatvamādiśam \|*  
*syātāṃ vibhavasaṃyuktau balino supratāpinau \|\| 13 \|\|*

*sarvabrahmāṃḍarājānau śivabhaktau jitendriyau \|*  
*śivāparatanormṛtyuṃ prāpya svaṃ padamāpsyathaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. You will be born as demons from the semen virile of a great sage and due to his power you will secure the commanding position of the king of demons endowed with prosperity, strength and valorous exploits. You will rule over whole of the universe as devotees of Śiva with your sense conquered. You will gain your former position after courting death at the hands of a manifestation of Siva.

## \|\| 2.5.15 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya munervākyaṃ nāradasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*ubhau haragaṇau prītau svaṃ padaṃ jagmaturmudā \|\| 15 \|\|*

Sūta said:—

15\. On hearing these words of the noble-souled Nārada, the two attendants of Śiva became delighted and went back to their abode joyfully.

## \|\| 2.5.16 \|\|

*nārado'pi paraṃ prīto dhyāyañchivamananyadhīḥ \|*  
*vicacāra mahīṃ paśyañchivatīrthānyabhīkṣṇaśaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Nārada too was delighted. Meditating exclusively on Śiva he continued his wanderings over the Earth seeing the various holy centres of Śiva personally.

## \|\| 2.5.17-18 \|\|

*kāśīṃ prāpyātha sa muniḥ sarvopari virājitām \|*  
*śivapriyāṃ śaṃbhusukhapradāṃ śambhusvarūpiṇīm \|\| 17 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭvā kāśīṃ kṛtā'rthobhūtkāśīnāthaṃ dadarśa ha \|*  
*ānarca parama prītyā paramānandasaṃyutaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. Reaching Kāśī that excelled all other cities in holiness, which is a favourite resort of Śiva, which easily bestows the favour of Śiva and which is identical with Śiva, the sage became contented. He saw Śiva, the lord of Kāśī and worshipped Him with very great pleasure and love.

## \|\| 2.5.19 \|\|

*sa mudaḥ sevyatāṃ kāśīṃ kṛtārtho munisattamaḥ \|*  
*namansaṃvarṇayanbhaktyā saṃsmaranpremavihvalaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. While staying at Kāśī, the excellent sage became contented; he bowed to the lord, described his glory piously, and remembered him with the flutter of love.

## \|\| 2.5.20 \|\|

*brahmalokaṃ jagāmātha śivasmaraṇasanmatiḥ \|*  
*śivatattvaṃ viśeṣeṇa jñātumicchussa nāradaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Nārada then went to the region of Brahmā, his mind being highly purified by remembering Śiva. He was eager to know further the principles of Śiva.

## \|\| 2.5.21 \|\|

*natvā tatra vidhiṃ bhaktyā stutvā ca vividhaistavaiḥ \|*  
*papraccha śivattatvaṃ śivasaṃbhaktamānasaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. There he bowed to Brahmā with devotion and eulogised him with various prayers. With his mind riveted to Śiva he asked him the good principles of Śiva.

## \|\| 2.5.22-23 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*brahmanbrahmasvarūpajña pitāmaha jagatprabho \|*  
*tvatprasādānmayā sarvaṃ viṣṇormāhātmyamuttamam \|\| 22 \|\|*

*bhaktimārgaṃ jñānamārgaṃ tapomārgaṃ sudustaram \|*  
*dānamārgañca tīrthānāṃ mārgaṃ ca śrutavānaham \|\| 23 \|\|*

Nārada said:—

22-23. O Brahmā, knower of the form of Brahman, O Pitāmaha, the lord of the universe, by your grace I have heard the greatness of Viṣṇu entirely and also the path of devotion, of knowledge, of austere penance, of charitable gifts and of holy centres.

## \|\| 2.5.24 \|\|

*na jñātaṃ śivatattvaṃ ca pūjāvidhimataḥ kramāt \|*  
*caritraṃ vividhaṃ tasya nivedaya mama prabho \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. But I have not understood the principle of Śiva. Hence, O lord, please explain the rules of His worship and also the various activities of the lord.

## \|\| 2.5.25 \|\|

*nirguṇo'pi śivastāta saguṇaśśaṃkaraḥ katham \|*  
*śivatattvaṃ na jānāmi mohitaśśivamāyayā \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. O dear sage, how can Śiva who is free form \[from?\] attributes become full of attributes? Since I am deluded by Śiva’s Māyā, I do not know the principle of Śiva.

## \|\| 2.5.26 \|\|

*sṛṣṭeḥ pūrvaṃ kathaṃ śaṃbhussvarūpeṇa pratiṣṭhitaḥ \|*  
*sṛṣṭimadhye sa hi kathaṃ krīḍansaṃvartate prabhuḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. How did Śiva remain in His pure form before Creation? In the middle of creation how does He sport about?

## \|\| 2.5.27 \|\|

*tadante ca kathaṃ devassa tiṣṭhati maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*kathaṃ prasannatāṃ yāti śaṃkaro lokaśaṃkaraḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. At the time of dissolution how does He remain? How is He, the benefactor of the world, propitiated?

## \|\| 2.5.28 \|\|

*saṃtuṣṭaśca svabhaktebhyaḥ parebhyaśca maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*kiṃ phalaṃ yacchati vidhe tatsarvaṃ kathayasva me \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. O Brahmā, when propitiated what benefit does He bestow on His devotees and on others? Please satisfy me on all these enquiries

## \|\| 2.5.29 \|\|

*sadyaḥ prasanno bhagavānbhavatītyanusaṃśrutam \|*  
*bhaktaprayāsaṃ sa mahānna paśyati dayāparaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. I have heard that the lord becomes delighted immediately. The merciful Great God cannot bear the stress and strain of His devotees.

## \|\| 2.5.30 \|\|

*brahmā viṣṇurmaheśaśca trayo devāśśivāṃśajāḥ \|*  
*maheśastatra pūrṇāṃśassvayameva śivaḥ paraḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. The three deities Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Maheśa are born as parts of Śiva. Maheśa, having all the parts of Śiva, is Śiva Himself.

## \|\| 2.5.31 \|\|

*tasyāvirbhāvamākhyāhi caritāni viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*umāvirbhāvamākhyāhi tadvivāhaṃ tathā vibho \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Please tell me all about His manifestation and especially His exploits. O lord, please narrate the manifestation of Umā and her marriage.

## \|\| 2.5.32 \|\|

*tadgārhasthyaṃ viśeṣeṇa tathā līlāḥ parā api \|*  
*etatsarvaṃ tathānyacca kathanīyaṃ tvayānagha \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Their domestic life, especially their great divine sports and other things which are worthy of mention should be narrated to me, O sinless one.

## \|\| 2.5.33 \|\|

*tadutpattiṃ vivāhaṃ ca śivāyāstu viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*prabrūhi me prajānātha guhajanma tathaiva ca \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Pārvatī’s birth and her marriage as well as Guha’s birth shall be narrated in detail, O lord of people.

## \|\| 2.5.34 \|\|

*bahubhyaśca śrutaṃ pūrvaṃ na tṛpto'smi jagatprabho \|*  
*atastvāṃ śaraṇaṃ prāptaḥ kṛpāṃ kuru mamopari \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. O lord of universe, this I have heard from many, before, but I am not satisfied. Hence I have sought refuge in you. Please have mercy on me.

## \|\| 2.5.35 \|\|

*iti śrutvā vacastasya nāradasyāṃgajasya hi \|*  
*uvāca vacanaṃ tatra brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. On hearing these words of Nārada his own son, Brahmā, the grandfather of the world, said this.

## Chapter 6 - Description of the nature of Mahāpralaya and the origin of Viṣṇu

## \|\| 2.6.1 \|\|

*\|\|brahmovāca \|*  
*bho brahmansādhu pṛṣṭo'haṃ tvayā vibudhasattama \|*  
*lokopakāriṇā nityaṃ lokānāṃ hitakāmyayā \|\| 1 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

1\. O Brahmin, foremost among the celestial beings, a good matter has been enquired into by you rendering service to the worlds and desiring their benefit.

## \|\| 2.6.2 \|\|

*yacchrutvā sarvalokānāṃ sarvapāpakṣayo bhavet \|*  
*tadahaṃ te pravakṣyāmi śivatattvamanāmayam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. I shall explain to you the wholesome and salutary principles of Śiva on hearing which the various sins of the people are destroyed.

## \|\| 2.6.3 \|\|

*śivatattvaṃ mayā naiva viṣṇunāpi yathārthataḥ \|*  
*jñātaśca paramaṃ rūpamadbhutaṃ ca pareṇa na \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Neither the principles of Śiva nor His supreme wonderful forms have been understood by me or by Viṣṇu or by any one else.

## \|\| 2.6.4 \|\|

*mahāpralayakāle ca naṣṭe sthāvarajaṃgame \|*  
*āsīttamomayaṃ sarvamanarkagrahatārakam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. At the time of Great Dissolution when all the mobile and immobile objects of the world are dissolved everything gets enveloped in darkness, without the sun, planets and stars.

## \|\| 2.6.5 \|\|

*acandramanahorātramanagnyanilabhūjalam \|*  
*apradhānaṃ viyacchūnyamanyatejovivarjitam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. There is no moon. The day and the night are not demarcated. There is no fire, no wind, no earth and no water. There is no unmanifest primordial being. The whole firmament is one complete void, devoid of all Tejas elements.

## \|\| 2.6.6 \|\|

*adṛṣṭatvādirahitaṃ śabdasparśasamujjhitam \|*  
*avyaktagaṃdharūpaṃ ca rasatyaktamadiṅmukham \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. There is no Dharma or Adharma, no sound, no touch. Smell and colour are not manifest. There is no taste. The face of the quarters is not demarcated.

## \|\| 2.6.7 \|\|

*itthaṃ satyaṃdhatamase sūcībhedyaṃ niraṃtare \|*  
*tatsadbrahmeti yacchrutvā sadekaṃ pratipadyate \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Thus when there is pitch darkness that cannot be pierced with a needle and what is mentioned in the Vedas as “The Existent and the Brahman” is alone present.

## \|\| 2.6.8 \|\|

*itīdṛśaṃ yadā nāsīdyattatsadasadātmakam \|*  
*yoginoṃtarhitākāśe yatpaśyaṃti niraṃtaram \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. When the present visible world is not in existence, the Sat Brahman alone is present which Yogins observe perpetually in the inner Soul, the inner Firmament.

## \|\| 2.6.9 \|\|

*amanogocaramvācāṃ viṣayanna kadācana \|*  
*anāmarūpavarṇaṃ ca na ca sthūlaṃ na yatkṛśam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. It is incomprehensible to the mind. It cannot at all be expressed by words. It has neither name nor colour. It is neither thick nor thin.

## \|\| 2.6.10 \|\|

*ahrasvadīrghamalaghugurutvaparivarjitam \|*  
*na yatropacayaḥ kaścittathā nāpacayo'pi ca \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. It is neither short nor long. It is neither light nor heavy. There is neither increase nor decrease in it.

## \|\| 2.6.11 \|\|

*abhidhatte sa cakitaṃ yadastīti śrutiḥ punaḥ \|*  
*satyaṃ jñānamanaṃtaṃ ca parānaṃdamparammahaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The Veda says that it envelops whatever is in a surprising way. It is the splendour, the truth, the knowledge, the eternal and the great Bliss.

## \|\| 2.6.12 \|\|

*aprameyamanādhāramavikāramanākṛti \|*  
*nirguṇaṃ yogigamyañca sarvavyāpyekakārakam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. It is immeasurable, propless, changeless, formless, attributeless, perceptible to the Yogins, all-pervasive and the sole cause of the universe.

## \|\| 2.6.13 \|\|

*nirvikalpaṃ nirāraṃbhaṃ nirmāyaṃ nirupadravam \|*  
*advitīyamanādyantamavikāśaṃ cidātmakam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. It is free from alternatives. It has no beginning. It is free from illusion and its harassment. It has no second. It has neither beginning nor end. It has no development. It is in the form of pure knowledge.

## \|\| 2.6.14 \|\|

*yasyetthaṃ saṃvikalpaṃte saṃjñāsaṃjñoktitaḥ sma vai \|*  
*kiyatā caiva kālena dvitīyecchā'bhavatkila \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. People have doubts about giving it a name. That Being, then after sometime, it is said, wished for a second.

## \|\| 2.6.15 \|\|

*amūrtena svamūrtiśca tenākalpi svalīlayā \|*  
*sarvaiśvaryaguṇopetā sarvajñānamayī śubhā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The Being, having no form of its own, wished to create, in the course of its own sport, an auspicious form of its own endowed with all power, qualities and knowledge.

## \|\| 2.6.16-18 \|\|

*sarvagā sarvarūpā ca sarvadṛksarvakāriṇī \|*  
*sarvekavaṃdyā sarvādyā sarvadā sarvasaṃskṛtiḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*parikalyeti tāṃ mūrtimaiśvarīṃ śuddharūpiṇīm \|*  
*advitīyamanādyaṃtaṃ sarvābhāsaṃ cidātmakam \|*  
*aṃtardadhe parākhyaṃ yadbrahma sarvagamavyayam \|\| 17 \|\|*

*amūrte yatparākhyaṃ vai tasya mūrtissadāśivaḥ \|*  
*arvācīnāḥ parācīnā īśvaraṃ taṃ jagurbudhāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

16-18. A form that goes everywhere, that has all forms, that sees all, that is the cause of all, that should be respected by all, that is at the beginning of all, that bestows everything, and that sanctifies everything should be created (So it wished) and hence created that form of Īśvara of pure nature. The original Being without a second, with neither beginning nor end, that illuminates everything, that is in the form of Cit (pure knowledge), that which is termed Supreme Brahman, the all-pervasive and undecaying, vanished, The manifest form of the formless Being is Sadāśiva. Scholars of the ancient and succeeding ages have sung of it as Īśvara.

## \|\| 2.6.19 \|\|

*śaktistadaikalenāpi svairaṃ viharatā tanuḥ \|*  
*svavigrahātsvayaṃ sṛṣṭā svaśarīrānapāyinī \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Īśvara though alone, then created the physical form Śakti from his body. This Śakti did not affect his body in any way.

## \|\| 2.6.20 \|\|

*pradhānaṃ prakṛti tāṃ ca māyāṃ guṇavatīṃ parām \|*  
*buddhitattvasya jananīmāhurvikṛtivarjitām \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. This Śakti is called by various names. Pradhāna, Prakṛti, Māyā, Guṇavatī, Parā. The mother of Buddhi Tattva (The cosmic Intelligence), Vikṛtivarjitā (without modification).

## \|\| 2.6.21 \|\|

*sā śaktirambikā proktā prakṛtissakaleśvarī \|*  
*tridevajananī nityā mūlakāraṇamityuta \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. That Śakti is Ambikā, Prakṛti and the goddess of all. She is the prime cause and the mother of the three deities.

## \|\| 2.6.22 \|\|

*asyā aṣṭau bhujāścāsanvicitravadanā śubhā \|*  
*rākācandrasahasrasya vadane bhāśca nityaśaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. She has eight arms. Her face wears a peculiar splendour, the splendour of a thousand moons. Thousands of stars perpetually sparkle round her face.

## \|\| 2.6.23 \|\|

*nānābharaṇasaṃyuktā nānāgatisamanvitā \|*  
*nānāyudhadharā devī phullapaṃkajalocanā \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. She is bedecked in various ornaments. She has various weapons. She is capable of various movements. Her eyes beam like a full blown lotus.

## \|\| 2.6.24 \|\|

*aciṃtyatejasā yuktā sarvayonissamudyatā \|*  
*ekākinī yadā māyā saṃyogāccāpyanekikā \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. She has a brilliance which could hardly be conceived. She is the generating cause of all. She sprang up singly as Māyā. In her union she manifested in various forms.

## \|\| 2.6.25 \|\|

*paraḥ pumānīśvarassa śivaśśaṃbhuranīśvaraḥ \|*  
*śīrṣe mandākinīdhārī bhālacandrastrilocanaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The supreme Puruṣa is Śiva. He is called Śambhu. He has no other lord over Him. He holds the Mandākinī (Gaṅgā) on His head, and the crescent moon on His forehead. He has three eyes.

## \|\| 2.6.26 \|\|

*paṃcavaktraḥ prasannātmā daśabāhustriśūladhṛk \|*  
*karpūragaurasusito bhasmoddhūlitavigrahaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. He has five faces. He is always joyful. He has ten arms. He holds the trident. He is as pure and white as camphor. His body is entirely dusted with the ash.

## \|\| 2.6.27 \|\|

*yugapacca tayā śaktyā sākaṃ kālasvarūpiṇā \|*  
*śivalokābhidhaṃ kṣetraṃ nirmitaṃ tena brahmaṇā \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. That Brahman of the form of Kāla (Time) together with Śakti, simultaneouly created the holy centre called Śivaloka.

## \|\| 2.6.28 \|\|

*tadeva kāśiketyetatprocyate kṣetramuttamam \|*  
*paraṃ nirvāṇasaṃkhyānaṃ sarvopari virājitam \|\| 28 \|\|*
