67\. After performing the regular worship of Śiva, with great devotion in accordance with prescribed rules, the devotees shall pour water in a continuous stream.

## \|\| 2.14.68-70 \|\|

*jvarapralāpaśāṃtyarthaṃ jala dhārā śubhāvahā \|*  
*śatarudriyamaṃtreṇa rudrasyaikādaśena tu \|\| 68 \|\|*

*rudrajāpyena vā tatra sūkten pauruṣeṇa vā \|*  
*ṣaḍaṃgenātha vā tatra mahāmṛtyuṃjayena ca \|\| 69 \|\|*

*gāyatryā vā namoṃtaiśca nāmabhiḥ praṇavādibhiḥ \|*  
*maṃtraivāthāgamoktaiśca jaladhārādikaṃ tathā \|\| 70 \|\|*

68-70. This Dhārā worship is very efficacious in delirium due to fever. At that time Śatarudriya\[1\] mantra, Rudraikādaśa mantra, Rudrajāpya mantra, Puruṣa Sūkta,\[2\] Ṣaḍaṅga mantra, Mahāmṛtyuñjaya mantra, Gāyatrī, names ending with Namaḥ and beginning with Praṇava or Āgama mantra shall be repeated.

## \|\| 2.14.71 \|\|

*sukhasaṃtānavṛddhyarthaṃ dhārāpūjanamuttamam \|*  
*nānādravyaiḥ śubhairdivyaiḥ prītyā sadbhasmadhāriṇā \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. The Dhārā worship is very excellent in regard to flourishing series of pleasures. Different types of auspicious materials of worship shall be added to the water.

## \|\| 2.14.72 \|\|

*ghṛtadhārā śive kāryā yāvanmaṃtrasahasrakam \|*  
*tadā vaṃśasya vistāro jāyate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. IfDhārā worship is performed with ghee continuously while a thousand mantras are repeated, the family will undoubtedly flourish.

## \|\| 2.14.73 \|\|

*evaṃ maduktamaṃtreṇa kāryaṃ vai śivapūjanam \|*  
*brahmabhojyaṃ tathā proktaṃ prājāpatyaṃ munīśvaraiḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. Thus the worship of Śiva shall be performed with the mantras mentioned by me. Sages have held that brahmins shall be fed and Prājāpatya rite shall be performed.

## \|\| 2.14.74 \|\|

*kevalaṃ dugdhadhārā ca tadā kāryā viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*śarkarāmiśritā tatra yadā buddhijaḍo bhavet \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. Milk without sugar is usually taken for the Dhārā. If the devotee is deficient in intellect and yearns for the same, sugar shall be added to milk for the sake of Dhārā.

## \|\| 2.14.75 \|\|

*tasyā saṃjāyate jīvasadṛśī buddhiruttamā \|*  
*yāvanmaṃtrāyutaṃ na syāttāvaddhārāprapūjanam \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. His intellect will become as keen as that of Bṛhaspati. The Dhārā shall be continued till ten thousand mantras are completely repeated.

## \|\| 2.14.76-77 \|\|

*yadā coccāṭanaṃ dehe jāyate kāraṇaṃ vinā \|*  
*yatra kutrāpi vā prema duḥkhaṃ ca parivarddhitam \|\| 76 \|\|*

*svagṛhe kalaho nityaṃ yadā caiva prajāyate \|*  
*taddhārāyāṃ kṛtāyāṃ vai sarvaṃ duḥkhaṃ vilīyate \|\| 77 \|\|*

76-77. If there is any crack or laceration in the body without an apparent cause, if there is any uncommon increase of love or misery anywhere, or if there be very frequent quarrels in the house, miseries will perish when the Dhārā worship is performed.

## \|\| 2.14.78 \|\|

*śatrūṇāṃ tāpanārthaṃ vai tailadhārā śivopari \|*  
*kartavyā suprayatnena kāryasiddhirdhuvaṃ bhavet \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. Oil-Dhārā shall be performed on Śivaliṅga for harassing enemies. Success in the enterprise is certain.

## \|\| 2.14.79 \|\|

*māsi tenaiva tailena bhogavṛddhiḥ prajāyate \|*  
*sārṣapenaiva tailena śatrunāśobhaveddhruvam \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. If scented oil is used, worldly pleasures will be increased. If mustard oil is used, enemies will be exterminated undoubtedly.

## \|\| 2.14.80 \|\|

*madhunā yakṣarājo vai gacchecca śivapūjanāta \|*  
*dhārā cekṣurasasyāpi sarvānandakarī śive \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. If honey is used, the devotee will become Kubera (God of wealth). The Dhārā of sugarcane juice is conducive to all pleasures.

## \|\| 2.14.81-82 \|\|

*dhārā gaṃgājalasyaiva bhuktimuktiphalapradā \|*  
*etāssarvāśca yāḥ proktā mṛtyaṃjayasamudbhavāḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

*tatrā'yutapramāṇaṃ hi kartavyaṃ tadvidhānataḥ \|*  
*kartavyaṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ ca bhojyaṃ vai rudrasaṃkhyayā \|\| 82 \|\|*

81-82. The Dhārā of Gaṅgā water yields worldly pleasures and salvation. In all these Dhārās Mṛtyuñjaya mantra shall be muttered ten thousand times. Eleven brahmins shall be fed.

## \|\| 2.14.83 \|\|

*etatte sarvamākhyātaṃ yatpṛṣṭo'haṃ munīśvara \|*  
*etadvai saphalaṃ loke sarvakāmahitāvaham \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. O lordly saint, what I have been asked I have now explained to you completely. This will be fruitful in the world and will contribute to the achievement of all desires.

## \|\| 2.14.84 \|\|

*skaṃdomāsahitaṃ śaṃbhuṃ saṃpūjya vidhinā saha \|*  
*yatphalaṃ labhate bhaktyā tadvadāmi yathāśrutam \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. I shall now tell you, as I have heard, the benefit accruing from the due worship of Śiva in the company of Skanda and Umā.

## \|\| 2.14.85-87 \|\|

*atra bhuktvākhilaṃ saukhyaṃ putrapautrādibhiḥ śubham \|*  
*tato yāti maheśasya lokaṃ sarvasukhāvaham \|\| 85 \|\|*

*sūryakoṭipratīkāśairvimānaiḥ sarvakāmagaiḥ \|*  
*rudrakanyāsamākīrṇairgeyavādyasamanvitaiḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

*krīḍate śivabhūtaśca yāvadābhūtasaṃplavam \|*  
*tato mokṣamavāpnoti vijñānaṃ prāpya cāvyayam \|\| 87 \|\|*

85-87. He will enjoy in this world all kinds of auspicious pleasures with sons and grandsons. Then he will go to the region of Śiva that is conducive to all happiness. He will enjoy happy sports with Śiva’s attendants, move about in aerial chariots that can go anywhere they pleased and that shine like ten million suns and will be served by Rudra’s maidens with songs and instrumental music, till the time of Dissolution. Then he will attain perfect knowledge and ultimately salvation.

## Chapter 15 - The manifestation of Rudra

## \|\| 2.15.1 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*vidhe vidhe mahābhāga dhanyastvaṃ surasattama \|*  
*śrāvitādyādbhutā śaivakathā paramapāvanī \|\| 1 \|\|*

Nārada said:—

1\. O creator, O Brahmā the fortunate, you are blessed O foremost among Devas. A wonderfully sanctifying story of Śiva has been narrated by you, today.

## \|\| 2.15.2 \|\|

*tatrādbhutā mahādivyā liṃgotpattiḥ śrutā śubhā \|*  
*śrutvā yasyāḥ prabhāvaṃ ca duḥkhanāśo bhavediha \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. I have heard the wonderfully divine story of the origin of the Liṅga, the auspicious hearing of the efficacy of which destroys all miseries here.

## \|\| 2.15.3 \|\|

*anaṃtaraṃ ca yajjātaṃ māhātmyaṃ caritaṃ tathā \|*  
*sṛṣṭeścaiva prakāraṃ ca kathaya tvaṃ viśeṣataḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Please narrate what transpired thereafter, the grandeur of the created things and particularly the mode of creation.

## \|\| 2.15.4 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*samyak pṛṣṭe ca bhavatā yajjātaṃ tadanaṃtaram \|*  
*kathayiṣyāmi saṃkṣepādyathā pūrvaṃ śrutaṃ mayā \|\| 4 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

4\. You have requested very pertinently. I shall briefly narrate what transpired later as I have heard before.

## \|\| 2.15.5-6 \|\|

*aṃtarhite tadā deve śivarūpe sanātane \|*  
*ahaṃ viṣṇuśca viprendra adhikaṃ sukhamāptavān \|\| 5 \|\|*

*mayā ca viṣṇunā rūpaṃ haṃsavārāhayostadā \|*  
*saṃvṛtaṃ tu tatastābhyāṃ lokasargāvanecchayā \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. When the eternal lord Śiva vanished, O chief of brahmins, Viṣṇu and I in a very happy mood withdrew our forms of Swan and Boar and wished for creation and sustenance of the worlds.

## \|\| 2.15.7 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*vidhe brahman mahāprājña saṃśayo hṛdi me mahān \|*  
*kṛpāṃ kṛtvātulāṃ śīghraṃ taṃ nāśayitumarhasi \|\| 7 \|\|*

Nārada said:—

7\. O Vidhi, O Brahmā, O wise one, I have a great doubt. Please remove the same.

## \|\| 2.15.8 \|\|

*haṃsavārāhayo rūpaṃ yuvābhyāṃ ca dhṛtaṃ katham \|*  
*anyadrūpaṃ vihāyaiva kimatra vada kāraṇam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. How is it that both of you assumed the forms of Swan and Boar instead of other forms? Please tell me the reason for the same.

## \|\| 2.15.9 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*ityetadvacanaṃ śrutvā nāradasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*smṛtvā śivapadāṃbhojaṃ brahmā sādaramabravīt \|\| 9 \|\|*

Sūta said:—

9\. On hearing these words of the noble-souled Nārada, Brahmā spoke after remembering the lotus-like feet of Śiva.

## \|\| 2.15.10 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*haṃsasya corddhvagamane gatirbhavati niścalā \|*  
*tattvātattvaviveko'sti jaladugdhavibhāgavat \|\| 10 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

10\. The swan has the power of going up steadily. It has the power of discriminating between the real and the unreal as in separating milk from water.

## \|\| 2.15.11 \|\|

*ajñānajñānayostattvaṃ vivecayati haṃsakaḥ \|*  
*haṃsarūpaṃ dhṛtaṃ tena brahmaṇā sṛṣṭikāriṇā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The swan understands the distinction between ignorance and knowledge. Hence I (Brahmā) the Creator, assumed the form of Swan.

## \|\| 2.15.12 \|\|

*viveko naiva labdhaśca yato haṃso vyalīyata \|*  
*śivasvarūpatattvasya jyotirūpasya nārada \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. O Nārada! But I failed to cognize the refulgent form of Śiva and therefore could not exercise my power of discrimination.

## \|\| 2.15.13 \|\|

*sṛṣṭipravṛttikāmasya kathaṃ jñānaṃ prajāyate \|*  
*yato labdho viveko'pi na mayā haṃsarūpiṇā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. How can real knowledge dawn on one who is engaged in activities of creation? Hence though in the form of Swan I could not attain the power of discrimination.

## \|\| 2.15.14 \|\|

*gamane'dho varāhasya gatirbhavati niścalā \|*  
*dhṛtaṃ vārāharūpaṃ hi viṣṇunā vanacāriṇā \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. A boar has the power of steadily going deep below. Hence Viṣṇu, the wanderer in the forest, assumed the form of the boar.

## \|\| 2.15.15 \|\|

*athavā bhavakalpārthaṃ tadrūpaṃ hi prakalpitam \|*  
*viṣṇunā ca varāhasya bhuvanāvanakāriṇā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Or Viṣṇu, the protector of all the worlds assumed the form of a Boar to start a new Kalpa (Aeon).

## \|\| 2.15.16 \|\|

*yaddinaṃ hi samārabhya tadrūpaṃ dhṛtavānhariḥ \|*  
*taddinaṃ prati kalpo'sau kalpo vārāhasaṃjñakaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Since the day he assumed the form of a Boar, the aeon by the title of Vārāha has started.

## \|\| 2.15.17 \|\|

*tadicchā vā yadā jātā tābhyāṃ rūpaṃ hi dhāraṇe \|*  
*taddinaṃ pratikalpo'sau kalpo vārāhasaṃjñak \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Or the Vārāhakalpa can be considered to have started since the day we two decided to assume these forms.

## \|\| 2.15.18 \|\|

*iti praśnottaraṃ dattaṃ prastutaṃ śṛṇu nārada \|*  
*smṛtvā śivapadāṃbhojaṃ vakṣye sṛṣṭividhiṃ mune \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. O Nārada, thus I have answered your relevant question. O sage, now listen. I shall resume the context. Remembering the lotus-like feet of Śiva I shall explain to you the mode of Creation.

## \|\| 2.15.19 \|\|

*aṃtarhite mahādeve tvahaṃ lokapitāmahaḥ \|*  
*tadīyaṃ vacanaṃ kartumadhyāyandhyānatatparaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. When God Śiva vanished, I, Pitāmaha (grandfather) of the worlds fell into contemplation pondering on the means of carrying out His words of direction.

## \|\| 2.15.20 \|\|

*namaskṛtya tadā śaṃbhuṃ jñānaṃ prāpya harestadā \|*  
*ānaṃdaṃ paramaṃ gatvā sṛṣṭiṃ kartuṃ mano dadhe \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Then after bowing down to Śiva, getting knowledge from Viṣṇu and attaining the highest bliss, I decided to start the work of creation.

## \|\| 2.15.21 \|\|

*viṣṇuścāpi tadā tatra praṇipatya sadāśivam \|*  
*upadiśya ca māṃ tāta hyaṃtardhānamupāgataḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. After bowing to Śiva and instructing me, O dear one, Viṣṇu too vanished.

## \|\| 2.15.22 \|\|

*brahmāṇḍācca bahirgatvā prāpya śambhoranugraham \|*  
*vaikuṃṭhanagaraṃ gatvā tatrovāsa harissadā \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. After getting the blessings of Śiva and going out of the cosmic egg, Viṣṇu made Vaikuṇṭha his permanent abode.

## \|\| 2.15.23 \|\|

*ahaṃ smṛtvā śivaṃ tatra viṣṇuṃ vai sṛṣṭikāmyayā \|*  
*pūrvaṃ sṛṣṭaṃ jalaṃ yacca tatrāṃjalimudākṣipam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Desiring to create, I remembered Śiva and Viṣṇu. In the waters that had already been created I offered handfuls of water as libation.

## \|\| 2.15.24 \|\|

*ato'ṇḍamabhavattatra caturviṃśatisaṃjña kam \|*  
*virāḍrūpamabhūdvipra jalarūpamapaśyataḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Then the cosmic egg arose consisting of twenty-four Principles. O brahmin, then a splendid, huge form Virāṭ appeared and the form of waters was not seen.

## \|\| 2.15.25 \|\|

*tatassaṃśayamāpannastapastepe sudāruṇam \|*  
*dvādaśābdamahaṃ tatra viṣṇudhyānaparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Confusion arose in my mind and I performed a severe penance for twelve years meditating on Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 2.15.26 \|\|

*tasmiṃśca samaye tāta prādurbhūto harissvayam \|*  
*māmuvāca mahāprītyā madaṃgaṃ saṃspṛśanmudā \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. At that time, Viṣṇu appeared before me and touching my body lovingly and joyously he told me.

## \|\| 2.15.27 \|\|

*\|\| viṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*varaṃ brūhi prasanno'smi nādeyo vidyate tava \|*  
*brahmañchaṃbhuprasādena sarvaṃ dātuṃ samarthakaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

Viṣṇu said:—

27\. O Brahmā, thanks to the favour of Śiva, I am capable of giving you everything. There is nothing which cannot be given to you. I am delighted. Tell me the boon (you wish to have).

## \|\| 2.15.28 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*yuktametanmahābhāga datto'haṃ śaṃbhunā ca te \|*  
*taduktaṃ yācate me'dya dehi viṣṇo namo'stu te \|\| 28 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

28\. O Viṣṇu, the fortunate one, I have been entrusted to you by Śiva. Hence it is but proper that I should request you. Please give me who request you what He has told you (to give me). Obeisance be to you.

## \|\| 2.15.29 \|\|

*virāḍrūpamidaṃ hyaṃḍaṃ caturviṃśatisaṃjñakam \|*  
*na caitanyaṃ bhavatyādau jaḍībhūtaṃ pradṛśyate \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. This Virāṭ form of the cosmic egg consists of twenty-four principles. There is no sentience in it. It is insentient.

## \|\| 2.15.30 \|\|

*prādurbhūto bhavānadya śivānugrahato hare \|*  
*prāptaṃ śaṃkarasaṃbhūtyā hyaṇḍaṃ caitanyamāvaha \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. O Viṣṇu, you have now appeared before me; thanks to the blessings of Śiva. Confer sentience on this cosmic egg originating from Śiva’s power.

## \|\| 2.15.31 \|\|

*ityukte ca mahāviṣṇuśśaṃbhorājñāparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*anaṃtarūpamāsthāya praviveśa tadaṃḍakam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. When I said this, the great Viṣṇu adhering strictly to the directives of Śiva assumed infinite forms and entered the cosmic egg.

## \|\| 2.15.32 \|\|

*sahasraśīrṣā puruṣassahasrākṣaḥ sahasrapāt \|*  
*sa bhūmiṃ sarvataspṛtvā tadaṇḍaṃ vyāptavāniti \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Viṣṇu with a thousand heads, a thousand eyes and a thousand feet encompassed the cosmic egg touching the earth everywhere.

## \|\| 2.15.33 \|\|

*praviṣṭe viṣṇunā tasminnaṇḍe samyakstutena me \|*  
*sacetanamabhūdaṇḍaṃ caturviṃśatisaṃjñakam \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. When Viṣṇu who was properly eulogised by me entered it, the cosmic egg consisting of the twenty-four principles became sentient.

## \|\| 2.15.34 \|\|

*pātālādi samārabhya saptalokādhipaḥ svayam \|*  
*rājate sma haristatra vairājaḥ puruṣaḥ prabhuḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Viṣṇu shone as the great Being, the lord of the seven worlds beginning with Pātāla.

## \|\| 2.15.35 \|\|

*kailāsanagaraṃ ramyaṃ sarvopari virājitam \|*  
*nivāsārthaṃ nijasyaiva paṃcavaktra ścakāra ha \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. The five-faced lord Śiva created for His residence the beautiful city of Kailāsa that shone above all.

## \|\| 2.15.36 \|\|

*brahmāṃḍasya tathā nāśe vaikuṇṭhasya ca tasya ca \|*  
*kadācideva devarṣe nāśo nāsti tayoriha \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. O celestial sage, Kailāsa and Vaikuṇṭha will never be destroyed even if the whole cosmic egg is destroyed.

## \|\| 2.15.37 \|\|

*satyaṃ padamupāśritya sthito'haṃ munisattama \|*  
*sṛṣṭikāmo'bhavaṃ tāta mahādevājñayā hyaham \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. O foremost among sages, I am staying in Satyaloka. O dear one, I desired the activity of creation at the bidding of Siva.

## \|\| 2.15.38 \|\|

*sisṛkṣoratha me prādurabhavatpāpasargakaḥ \|*  
*avidyāpaṃcakastāta buddhipūrvastamopamaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Even as I stood desirous of creation, the Evil creation, viz. the set of five Illusions appeared before me. It was of the nature of darkness endowed with knowledge.

## \|\| 2.15.39 \|\|

*tataḥ prasannacitto'hamasṛjaṃ sthāvarābhidham \|*  
*mukhyasargaṃ ca nissaṃgamadhyāyaṃ śaṃbhuśāsanāt \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Then I created the chief creation consisting of immobile beings with a delightful mind. At the bidding of Śiva, I continued my meditation in a detached spirit.

## \|\| 2.15.40 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā me sisṛkṣośca jñātvā sādhakamātmanaḥ \|*  
*sargo'vartata duḥkhāḍhyastiryaksrotā na sādhakaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. While creating it I had thought it would be an aspirant after the Ātman. But the creation Tiryaksrotas turned out to be full of misery. And it was not an aspirant.

## \|\| 2.15.41-42 \|\|

*taṃ cāsādhakamājñāya punaściṃtayataśca me \|*  
*abhavatsāttvikassarga ūrdhvasrotā iti drutam \|\| 41 \|\|*

*devasargaḥ pratikhyātassatyo'tīva sukhāvahaḥ \|*  
*tamapyasādhakaṃ matvā'ciṃtayaṃ prabhumātmanaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

41-42. Realising that it was not an aspirant I began to ponder over the matter. Then the Sāttvika Sarga otherwise known as Ūrdhvasrotas and Devasarga (Divine creation) took shape. It was really charming. But considering that it too was not aspirant I meditated on my lord.

## \|\| 2.15.43 \|\|

*prādurāsīttatassargo rājasaḥ śaṃkarājñayā \|*  
*avāksrotā iti khyāto mānuṣaḥ parasādhakaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Then the Rājasasarga, otherwise known as Arvāksrotas—the human creation which was a great aspirant, appeared at the bidding of Lord Śiva.

## \|\| 2.15.44 \|\|

*mahādevājñayā sargastato bhūtādiko'bhavat \|*  
*iti paṃcavidhā sṛṣṭiḥ pravṛttā vai kṛtā mayā \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Then again at the bidding of Lord Śiva the Bhūtādika Sarga (creation of the elements etc.) appeared. Thus five types of creation collectively called Vaikṛta were set in motion by me.

## \|\| 2.15.45-46 \|\|

*trayassargāḥ prakṛtyāśca brahmaṇaḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|*  
*tatrādyo mahatassargo dvitīyaḥ sūkṣmabhautikaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

*vaikārikastṛtīyaśca ityete prakṛtāstrayaḥ \|*  
*evaṃ cāṣṭavidhāssargāḥ prakṛtervekṛtaiḥ saha \|\| 46 \|\|*

45-46. Brahmā evolved three types of creation from Prakṛti. The first one was the creation of Mahat (the cosmic principle of intellect.) The second was that of the subtle elements. The third was Vaikārika of the nature of transformations and ramifications). Thus with five Vaikṛta types and three later Prākṛtas there were eight types of creation.

## \|\| 2.15.47 \|\|

*kaumāro navamaḥ proktaḥ prākṛto vaikṛtaśca saḥ \|*  
*eṣāmavāṃtaro bhedo mayā vaktuṃ na śakyate \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. The Kaumāra Sarga was the ninth. It was both Prākṛta and Vaikṛta. I cannot adequately describe the divisions and sub-divisions of all these types of creation.

## \|\| 2.15.48 \|\|

*alpatvādupayogasya vacmi sargaṃ dvijātmakam \|*  
*kaumāraḥ sanakādīnāṃ yatra sargo mahānabhūt \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Last of all, I shall mention the brahminical creation which is of very little utility. It is here that the great creation of Sanaka and others, referred to above as Kaumāra Sarga, took shape.

## \|\| 2.15.49 \|\|

*sanakādyāḥ sutā me hi mānasā brahmasaṃmitāḥ \|*  
*mahāvairāgyasaṃpannā abhavanpaṃca suvratāḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Sanaka and others, my mental sons, were five in number. They were all on a par with Brahman, of good rites and averse to worldly attachment.

## \|\| 2.15.50 \|\|

*mayājñaptā api ca te saṃsāravimukhā budhāḥ \|*  
*śivadhyānaikamanaso na sṛṣṭau cakrire matim \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Despite my command they were not inclined to carry on the activities of creation; those scholarly sons turned their attention from worldly activities and were devoted to the exclusive meditation on Śiva.

## \|\| 2.15.51 \|\|

*pratyuttaraṃ ca tadanu śrutvāhaṃ munisattama \|*  
*akārṣaṃ krodhamatyugraṃ mohamāptaśca nārada \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. O Nārada, they were bold enough to retort to me whereat I became very furious and nearly senseless.

## \|\| 2.15.52 \|\|

*kuddhasya mohitasyātha vihvalasya mune mama \|*  
*krodhena khalu netrābhyāṃ prāpatannaśrubiṃdavaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. When I became nearly unconscious on account of excessive fury and agitation, drops of tears fell from my eyes.

## \|\| 2.15.53 \|\|

*tasminnavasare tatra smṛtena manasā mayā \|*  
*prabodhitohaṃ tvaritamāgatenā hi viṣṇunā \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. At that time, on being mentally meditated upon, Viṣṇu came there hurriedly and enlightened me.

## \|\| 2.15.54 \|\|

*tapaḥ kuru śivasyeti hariṇā śikṣito'pyaham \|*  
*tapokārī mahadghoraṃ paramaṃ munisattama \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. O foremost among sages, I was instructed by Viṣṇu to perform the penance of Śiva. Accordingly I performed a severe penance.

## \|\| 2.15.55-56 \|\|

*tapasyataśca sṛṣṭyarthaṃ bhruvorghrāṇasya madhyataḥ \|*  
*avimuktābhidhāddeśātsvakīyānme viśeṣataḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

*trimūrtīnāṃ maheśasya prādurāsīdghṛṇānidhiḥ \|*  
*ārddhanārīśvaro bhūtvā pūrṇāśassakaleśvaraḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

55-56. While I was performing penance for creation, the merciful lord Śiva of Trinity, came out of the spot called Avimukta between the eyebrows and the nose. He manifested himself as Half woman and Half man in full potency.

## \|\| 2.15.57-58 \|\|

*tamajaṃ śaṃkaraṃ sākṣāttejorāśimumāpatim \|*  
*sarvajñaṃ sarvakartāraṃ nīlalohitasaṃjñakam \|\| 57 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭvā natvā mahābhaktyā stutvāhaṃ tu praharṣitaḥ \|*  
*avocaṃ devadeveśaṃ sṛja tvaṃ vividhāḥ prajāḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

57-58. On seeing the unborn lord Śiva, a mass of refulgence, the consort of Umā, the omniscent, the creator of everything, famous as Nīlalohita, straight in front of me I saluted him with great devotion and was highly delighted. I told the lord “Please create various subjects.”

## \|\| 2.15.59 \|\|

*śrutvā mama vacassotha devadevo maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*sasarja svātmanastulyānrudro rudragaṇānbahūna \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. On hearing my words, the lord of lords, Rudra, created many Gaṇas identical with Himself.

## \|\| 2.15.60 \|\|

*avocaṃ punareveśaṃ mahārudraṃ maheśvaram \|*  
*janmamṛtyubhayāviṣṭāssṛja deva prajā iti \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. I again told the great lord Rudra—“O lord, please create those subjects, tormented by the fear of birth and death”.

## \|\| 2.15.61 \|\|

*evaṃ śrutvā mahādevo madvacaḥ karuṇānidhiḥ \|*  
*prahasyovāca māṃ sadyaḥ prahasya munisattama \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. O foremost among sages! on hearing my words the merciful lord Rudra laughed and said thus.

## \|\| 2.15.62 \|\|

*mahādeva uvāca \|*  
*janmamṛtyubhayāviṣṭā nāhaṃ srakṣye prajā vidhe \|*  
*aśobhanāḥ karmavaśā vimagnā duḥkhavāridhau \|\| 62 \|\|*

Lord Rudra said:—

62\. O Brahmā, I shall not create the subjects tormented by the fear of birth and death. The inauspicious beings are immersed in the ocean of distress by their own actions.

## \|\| 2.15.63 \|\|

*ahaṃ duḥkhodadhau magnā uddhariṣyāmi ca prajāḥ \|*  
*samyakjñānapradānena gurumūrtiparigrahaḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. In my manifestation in the form of preceptor I shall lift up these beings immersed in the ocean of distress by conferring on them perfect knowledge.

## \|\| 2.15.64 \|\|

*tvameva sṛja duḥkhāḍhyāḥ prajāssarvāḥ prajāpate \|*  
*madājñayā na baddhastvaṃ māyayā saṃbhaviṣyasi \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. You alone, create all the miserable subjects, O Lord! At my bidding, you will not be bound by illusion.

## \|\| 2.15.65 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityuktvā māṃ sa bhagavānsuśrīmānnīlalohitaḥ \|*  
*sagaṇaḥ paśyato me hi drutamaṃtardadhe haraḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

65\. Saying this, the lord, the glorious Śiva vanished along with His attendants even as I was watching.

## Chapter 16 - Description of the Creation

## \|\| 2.16.1-2 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*śabdādīni ca bhūtāni paṃcīkṛtvāhamātmanā \|*  
*tebhyaḥ sthūlaṃ nabho vāyuṃ vahniṃ caiva jalaṃ mahīm \|\| 1 \|\|*

*parvatāṃśca samudrāṃśca vṛkṣādīnapi nārada \|*  
*kalādiyugaparyetānkālānanyānavāsṛjam \|\| 2 \|\|*

Brahmā said:

1-2. O Nārada, after performing the Pentuplication of the Bhūtas, elements and their attributes sound etc., I evolved the gross Ether, wind, fire, water and the Earth out of them and created mountains, seas, trees etc. and the periods of time ending with Kali and other ages.

## \|\| 2.16.3 \|\|

*sṛṣṭyaṃtānaparāṃścāpi nāhaṃ tuṣṭo'bhava nmune \|*  
*tato dhyātvā śivaṃ sāmbaṃ sādhakānasṛjaṃ mune \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. I created many other things as well, but O sage, I was not satisfied. Then O sage, I meditated on Śiva and his consort Ambā and created aspirants.

## \|\| 2.16.4-7 \|\|

*marīciṃ ca svanetrābhyāṃ hṛdayādbhṛgumeva ca \|*  
*śiraso'girasaṃ vyānātpulahaṃ munisattamam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*udānācca pulastyaṃ hi vasiṣṭhañca samānataḥ \|*  
*kratuṃ tvapānācchrotrābhyāmatriṃ dakṣaṃ ca prāṇataḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*asṛjaṃ tvāṃ tadotsaṃgācchāyāyāḥ kardamaṃ munim \|*  
*saṃkalpādasṛjaṃ dharmaṃ sarvasādhanasādhanam \|\| 6 \|\|*

*evametānahaṃ sṛṣṭvā kṛtārthassādhakottamān \|*  
*abhavaṃ muniśārdūla mahādevaprasādataḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

4-7. I created Marīci from my eyes, Bhṛgu from my heart; Aṅgiras from the head and the great sage Pulaha from the vital breath Vyāna. I created Pulastya from Udāna; Vasiṣṭha from Samāna; Kratu from Apāna; Atri from the ears and Dakṣa from the Prāṇa. I then created you from my lap and the sage Kardama from my shadow. Finally, I created, out of my conception, Dharma which is the means for the achievement of everything. O foremost among sages, creating thus, thanks to the favour of Mahādeva, these excellent Sādhakas I became contented.

## \|\| 2.16.8 \|\|

*tato madājñayā tāta dharmaḥ saṃkalpasaṃbhavaḥ \|*  
*mānavaṃ rūpamāpannassādhakaistu pravartitaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Then, O dear one, Dharma, born out of my conception assumed the form of Manu at my bidding and was engaged in activity by the aspirants.

## \|\| 2.16.9 \|\|

*tato'sṛjaṃ svagātrebhyo vividhebhyo'mitānsutān \|*  
*surāsurādikāṃstebhyo dattvā tāṃ tāṃ tanuṃ mune \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Then I created from the different parts of my body innumerable sons, Suras (devas) and Asuras (demons) and many others after assigning them different bodies, O sage.

## \|\| 2.16.10 \|\|

*tato'haṃ śaṃkareṇātha preritoṃ'targatena ha \|*  
*dvidhā kṛtvātmano dehaṃ dvirūpaścābhavaṃ mune \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. I was then prompted by Śiva present within me and hence, O sage, I split myself into two having assumed two forms.

## \|\| 2.16.11 \|\|

*arddhena nārī puruṣaścārddhena saṃtato mune \|*  
*sa tasyāmasṛjaddvaṃdvaṃ sarvasādhanamuttamam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. One half had the form of a woman and the other half that of a man. He then created in her a couple, the means of excellent nature.

## \|\| 2.16.12 \|\|

*svāyaṃbhuvo manustatra puruṣaḥ parasādhanam \|*  
*śatarūpābhidhā nārī yoginī sā tapasvinī \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The man was Svāyambhuva Manu, the greatest of the means (of creation). The woman was Śatarūpā, a yoginī, an ascetic woman.

## \|\| 2.16.13 \|\|

*sā punarmanunā tena gṛhītātīva śobhanā \|*  
*vivāhavidhinā tātā'sṛjatsargaṃ samaithunam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The auspicious lady was accepted by Manu with due matrimonial rites, O dear one, he created beings through her by the process of sexual intercourse.

## \|\| 2.16.14-16 \|\|

*tasyāṃ tena samutpannastanayaśca priyavrataḥ \|*  
*tathaivottānapādaśca tathā kanyātrayaṃ punaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*ākūtirdevahūtiśca prasūtiriti viśrutāḥ \|*  
*ākūtiṃ rucaye prādātkardamāya tu madhyamām \|\| 15 \|\|*

*dadau prasūtiṃ dakṣāyottānapādānujāṃ sutāḥ \|*  
*tāsāṃ prasūtiprasavaissarvaṃ vyāptaṃ carācaram \|\| 16 \|\|*

14-16. He begot of her two sons Priyavrata and Uttānapāda and three daughters Ākūti, Devahūti and Prasūti, all of them very famous. He gave Ākūti in marriage to Ruci and the middle one to Kardama. He gave Prasūti the younger sister of Uttānapāda in marriage to Dakṣa. Their sons and progeny are spread over the world both mobile and immobile.

## \|\| 2.16.17 \|\|

*ākūtyāṃ ca ruceścābhūdvaṃdvaṃ yajñaśca dakṣiṇā \|*  
*yajñasya jajñire putrā dakṣiṇāyāṃ ca dvādaśa \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Ruci begot of Ākūti the couple Yajña and Dakṣiṇā. Twelve sons were born of Yajña and Dakṣiṇā.

## \|\| 2.16.18 \|\|

*devahūtyāṃ kardamācca bahvyo jātāssutā mune \|*  
*daśājjātāścatasraśca tathā putryaśca viṃśatiḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. O sage, Kardama begot of Devahūti many daughters. Dakṣa begot twenty-four daughters.

## \|\| 2.16.19 \|\|

*dharmāya dattā dakṣeṇa śraddhādyāstu trayodaśa \|*  
*śṛṇu tāsāṃ ca nāmāni dharmastrīṇāṃ munīśvara \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Thirteen daughters Śraddhā etc. were given to Dharma in marriage by Dakṣa. O lordly sage, listen to the names of Dharma’s wives.

## \|\| 2.16.20 \|\|

*śraddhā lakṣmīrdhṛtistuṣṭiḥ puṣṭirmedhā tathā kriyā \|*  
*vasuḥrbuddhi lajjā śāṃtiḥ siddhiḥ kīrtistrayodaśa \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Their names are Śraddhā (faith), Lakṣmī (fortune), Dhṛti (fortitude), Tuṣṭi (satiety), Puṣṭi (nourishment), Medhā (intelligence), Kriyā (rite, activity), Buddhi (intellect, wisdom), Lajjā (Bashfulness), Vasu (wealth), Śānti (peace, calmness), Siddhi (achievement, accomplishment) and the thirteenth is Kīrti (fame).

## \|\| 2.16.21-23 \|\|

*tābhyāṃ śiṣṭā yavīyasya ekādaśa sulocanāḥ \|*  
*khyātissatpathasaṃbhūtiḥ smṛtiḥ prītiḥ kṣamā tathā \|\| 21 \|\|*

*sannatiścānurūpā ca ūrjā svāhā svadhā tathā \|*  
*bhṛgurbhavo marīciśca tathā caivāṃgirā muniḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*pulastyaḥ pulahaścaiva kratuścarṣivarastathā \|*  
*atrirvāsiṣṭho vahniśca pitaraśca yathākramam \|\| 23 \|\|*

21-23. The eleven younger daughters were Khyāti, Satī, Sambhūti, Smṛti, Prīti, Kṣamā, Sannati, Anurūpā, Ūrjā, Svāhā and Svadhā who were respectively married by Bhṛgu, Bhava (Śiva), Marīci, the sage Aṅgiras, Pulastya, Pulaha, the excellent sage Kratu, Atri, Vasiṣṭha, the fire-god and the Pitṛs (manes).

## \|\| 2.16.24 \|\|

*khyātāstā jagṛhuḥ kanyā bhṛgvādyāssādhakā varāḥ \|*  
*tatassaṃpūritaṃ sarvaṃ trailokyaṃ sacarācaram \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. The great aspirants Bhṛgu and others took the hands of these famous daughters. Thereupon the entire universe consisting of three worlds, mobile and immobile was filled (with progeny).

## \|\| 2.16.25 \|\|

*evaṃ karmānurūpeṇa praṇināmaṃbikāpate \|*  
*ājñayā bahavo jātā asaṃkhyātā dvijarṣabhāḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Thus according to their own actions and at the bidding of Śiva innumerable famous brahmins were born out of the various living beings.

## \|\| 2.16.26-28 \|\|

*kalpabhedena dakṣasya ṣaṣṭiḥ kanyāḥ prakīrtitāḥ \|*  
*tāsāṃ daśa ca dharmāya śaśine saptaviṃśatim \|\| 26 \|\|*

*vidhinā dattavāndakṣaḥ kaśyapāya trayodaśa \|*  
*catasraḥ pararūpāya dadau tārkṣyāya nārada \|\| 27 \|\|*

*bhṛgvaṃgiraḥ kṛśāśvebhyo dve dve kanye ca dattavān \|*  
*tābhyastebhyastu saṃjātā bahvī sṛṣṭiścarācarā \|\| 28 \|\|*

26-28. In another Kalpa, Dakṣa had sixty daughters. Of them ten were given to Dharma, twenty-seven to the Moon, thirteen to Kaśyapa. O Nārada, he gave four to Garuḍa of excellent form. Two to each of these—Bhṛgu, Aṅgiras and Kṛśāśva. Born of them are many children in the world of mobile and immobile.

## \|\| 2.16.29-30 \|\|

*trayodaśamitāstasmai kaśyapāya mahātmane \|*  
*dattā dakṣeṇa yāḥ kanyā vidhivanmunisattama \|\| 29 \|\|*

*tāsāṃ prasūtibhirvyāptaṃ trailokyaṃ sacarācaram \|*  
*sthāvaraṃ jaṃgamaṃ caiva śūnya naiva tu kiṃcana \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. O foremost among the sages, the children of the thirteen daughters given to the noble-souled Kaśyapa by Dakṣa spread over the three worlds. Mobile or immobile nothing was void.

## \|\| 2.16.31-32 \|\|

*devāśca ṛṣayaścaiva daityāścaiva prajajñire \|*  
*vṛkṣāśca pakṣiṇaścaiva sarve parvatavīrudhaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*dakṣakanyāprasūtaiśca vyāptamevaṃ carācaram \|*  
*pātālatalamārabhya satyalokāvadhi dhruvam \|\| 32 \|\|*

31-32. Devas, sages, demons, trees, birds and mountain-creepers born of the daughters of Dakṣa filled the entire space between Pātāla and Satyaloka.

## \|\| 2.16.33 \|\|

*brahmāṃḍaṃ sakalaṃ vyāptaṃ śūnyaṃ naiva kadācana \|*  
*evaṃ sṛṣṭiḥ kṛtā samyagbrahmaṇā śaṃbhuśāsanāt \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The whole cosmic egg was filled. Never was it a void. Thus, at the bidding of Śiva, the creation was perfectly accomplished by Brahmā.

## \|\| 2.16.34-35 \|\|

*satī nāma triśūlāgre sadā rudreṇa rakṣitā \|*  
*taporthaṃ nirmitā pūrvaṃ śaṃbhunā sarvaviṣṇunā \|\| 34 \|\|*

*saiva dakṣātsamudbhūtā lokakāryārthameva ca \|*  
*līlāṃ cakāra bahuśo bhaktoddharaṇahetave \|\| 35 \|\|*

34-35. Dakṣa’s daughter Satī was perfectly guarded by Rudra at the tip of His Trident, for the sake of penance. Śiva had created her himself and later for the activities of the world she was born of Dakṣa. In order to uplift the devotees, the lord indulged himself in many divine sports.

## \|\| 2.16.36 \|\|

*vāmāṃgo yasya vaikuṃṭho dakṣiṇāṃgo'hameva ca \|*  
*rudro hṛdayajo yasya trividhastu śivaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Śiva manifested himself in three ways in the form of Vaikuṇṭha (Viṣṇu) born of the left limb, in my form (of Brahmā) born of the right limb and in the form of Rudra born of the heart.

## \|\| 2.16.37 \|\|

*ahaṃ viṣṇuśca rudraśca guṇāstraya udāhṛtāḥ \|*  
*svayaṃ sadā nirguṇaśca parabrahmāvyayaśśivaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Viṣṇu, Rudra and I represent the three Guṇas. Śiva is free from Guṇas. He is the supreme Brahman, the undecaying.

## \|\| 2.16.38 \|\|

*viṣṇussattvaṃ rajo'haṃ ca tamo rudra udāhṛtaḥ \|*  
*lokācārata ityevaṃ nāmato vastuto'nyathā \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Viṣṇu is of Sattva attribute, I (Brahmā) am of Rajas attribute and Rudra is of Tamas attribute. This is only in view of the activities in the world. But in fact and in name it is otherwise.

## \|\| 2.16.39 \|\|

*aṃtastamo bahissattvo viṣṇūrudrastathā mataḥ \|*  
*aṃtassattvastamobāhyo rajohaṃ sarvethā mune \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Viṣṇu is of Tāmasika nature within but externally Sāttvika; Rudra is of Sāttvika nature within but of Tāmasic nature outside, I am of Rājasic nature throughout.

## \|\| 2.16.40 \|\|

*rājasī ca surā devī sattvarūpāttu sā satī \|*  
*lakṣmīstamomayī jñeyā virūpā ca śivā parā \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. The goddess of speech is of Rājasic nature; Satī is of the Sāttvika nature and Lakṣmī is of Tamasic nature; the great goddess Śivā is of the three natures.

## \|\| 2.16.41 \|\|

*evaṃ śivā satī bhūtvā śaṃkareṇa vivāhitā \|*  
*pituryajñe tanuṃ tyaktvā nādāttāṃ svapadaṃ yayau \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Śivā became Satī and Śiva married her. At the sacrifice of her father she cast off her body which she did not take again and went back to her own region.

## \|\| 2.16.42 \|\|

*punaśca pārvatī jātā devaprārthanayā śivā \|*  
*tapaḥ kṛtvā suvipulaṃ punaśśivamupāgatā \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Śivā incarnated as Pārvatī at the request of the devas. It was after performing a severe penance that she could attain Śiva again.

## \|\| 2.16.43-45 \|\|

*tasyā nāmānyanekāni jātāni ca munīśvara \|*  
*kālikā caṃḍikā bhadrā cāmuṃḍā vijayā jayā \|\| 43 \|\|*

*jayaṃtī bhadrakālī ca durgā bhagavatīti ca \|*  
*kāmākhyā kāmadā hyambā mṛḍānī sarvamaṃgalā \|\| 44 \|\|*

*nāmadheyānyanekāni bhuktimuktipradāni ca \|*  
*guṇakarmānurūpāṇi prāyaśastatra pārvatī \|\| 45 \|\|*

43-45. O lordly sage, she came to be called by various names such as Kālī, Caṇḍikā, Cāmuṇḍā, Vijayā, Jayā, Jayantī, Bhadrakālī, Durgā, Bhagavatī, Kāmākhyā, Kāmadā, Ambā, Mṛḍānī and Sarvamaṅgalā. These various names confer worldly pleasures and salvation according to qualities and action. The name Pārvatī is very common.

## \|\| 2.16.46 \|\|

*guṇamayyastathā devyo devā guṇamayāstrayaḥ \|*  
*militvā vividhaṃ sṛṣṭeścakruste kāryamuttamam \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. The goddesses of various attributes and the three deities of various attributes performed the diverse excellent activities of creation in mutual collaboration.

## \|\| 2.16.47 \|\|

*evaṃ sṛṣṭiprakāraste varṇito munisattama \|*  
*śivājñayā viracito brahmāṃḍasya mayā'khilaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. O excellent among sages, I have thus explained the mode of creation to you. The entire cosmic egg was created by me at the bidding of Śiva.

## \|\| 2.16.48 \|\|

*paraṃ brahma śivaḥ proktastasya rūpāstrayaḥ surāḥ \|*  
*ahaṃ viṣṇuśca rudraśca guṇabhedānurūpataḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Śiva is the Supreme Brahman. The three deities, Viṣṇu, I and Rudra are His manifestations according to the difference in the attributes.

## \|\| 2.16.49 \|\|

*śivayā ramate svairaṃ śivaloke manorame \|*  
*svataṃtraḥ paramātmā hi nirguṇassaguṇo'pi vai \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. The independent Supreme Ātman, who is both Nirguṇa and Saguṇa sports with Śivā in the beautiful Śivaloka.

## \|\| 2.16.50 \|\|

*tasya pūrṇavatāro hiṃ rudrassākṣācchivaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*kailāse bhavanaṃ ramyaṃ paṃcavaktraścakāra ha \|*  
*brahmāṃḍasya tathā nāśe tasya nāśosti vai na hi \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. His perfect and complete incarnation is Rudra. He is Śiva himself. The five-faced lord has made His beautiful mansion in Kailāsa. Even if the whole Brahmāṇḍa were destroyed, it knows no destruction.

## Chapter 17 - The Story of Guṇanidhi

## \|\| 2.17.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya vacastasya brahmaṇassa tu nāradaḥ \|*  
*punaḥ papraccha taṃ natvā vinayena munīśvarāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sūta said:—

1\. O great sages, after hearing these words of Brahmā, Nārada once again bowed to him and asked humbly.

## \|\| 2.17.2-3 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*kadāgato hi kailāsaṃ śaṃkaro bhaktavatsalaḥ \|*  
*kva vā sakhitvaṃ tasyāsītkubereṇa mahātmanā \|\| 2 \|\|*

*kiṃ cakāra harastatra paripūrṇaḥ śivākṛtiḥ \|*  
*etatsarvaṃ samācakṣva paraṃ kautūhalaṃ mama \|\| 3 \|\|*

Nārada said:—

2-3. When did Śiva favourably disposed to His devotees go to Kailāsa? Where did he have the intimate acquaintance with Kubera of great and noble soul? What did Śiva of auspicious form do there? Please narrate all these things to me. I am deeply interested in it.

## \|\| 2.17.4 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*śṛṇu nārada vakṣyāmi caritaṃ śaśimaulinaḥ \|*  
*yathā jagāma kailāsaṃ sakhitvaṃ dhanadasya ca \|\| 4 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

4\. O Nārada, listen. I shall tell you the story of the moon-crested lord, how he went to Kailāsa and how he contracted friendship of Kubera.

## \|\| 2.17.5 \|\|

*asītkāṃpilyanagare somayājikulodbhavaḥ \|*  
*dīkṣito yajñadattākhyo yajñavidyāviśāradaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. In the city of Kāmpilya there was a sacrificer named Yajñadatta. Born of Somayāji family he was an adept in the performance of sacrifice.

## \|\| 2.17.6 \|\|

*vedavedāṃgavitprājño vedāntādiṣu dakṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*rājamānyo'tha bahudhā vadānyaḥ kīrtibhājanaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. He knew Vedas and Vedāṅgas. He was a great scholar of Vedānta etc. He was honoured by the king. He was a liberal-minded donor and as such his fame had spread far and wide.

## \|\| 2.17.7-8 \|\|

*agniśuśrūṣaṇarato vedādhyayanatatparaḥ \|*  
*sundaro ramaṇīyāṃgaścandrabiṃbasamākṛtiḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*āsīdguṇanidhirnāma dīkṣitasyāsya vai sutaḥ \|*  
*kṛtopanayanassoṣṭau vidyā jagrāha bhūriśaḥ \|*  
*atha pitrānabhijñāto yūtakarmarato'bhavat \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. He assiduously maintained the sacrificial fire and was devoted to the study of the Vedas. His son (Guṇanidhi) was of a very handsome complexion and shone like the moon’s disc. After the investiture with the sacred thread he learned all the eight lores over and over again. Yet, unknown to his father he indulged in gambling.

## \|\| 2.17.9 \|\|

*ādāyādāya bahuśo dhanaṃ mātussakāśataḥ \|*  
*samadādyūtakārebhyo maitrīṃ taiśca cakāra saḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Ever and anon he took plenty of sums from his mother and gave them over to other gamblers with whom he contracted great intimacy.

## \|\| 2.17.10 \|\|

*saṃtyaktabrāhmaṇācāraḥ saṃdhyāsnānaparāṅmukhaḥ \|*  
*niṃdako vedaśāstrāṇāṃ devabrāhmaṇaniṃdakaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. He eschewed all brahminical ways and conduct of life. He was averse to the performance of Sandhyā prayers and ceremonial ablutions. He began to speak ill of the Vedas, sacred texts, devas and brahmins.

## \|\| 2.17.11 \|\|

*smṛtyācāravihīnastu gītavādyavinodabhāk \|*  
*naṭapākhaṃḍabhāṇḍaistu baddhapremaparaṃparaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. He did not follow the conventions and injunctions of the Smṛti code, He indulged in singing and playing. Actors, heretics etc. were his beloved friends.

## \|\| 2.17.12-15 \|\|

*prerito'pi jananyā sa na yayau pituraṃtikam \|*  
*gṛhakāryāṃtaravyāpto dīkṣito dīkṣitāyinīm \|\| 12 \|\|*

*yadā yadaiva tāṃ pṛcchedaye guṇanidhissutaḥ \|*  
*na dṛśyate mayā gehe kalyāṇi vidadhāti kim \|\| 13 \|\|*

*tadā tadeti sā brūyādidānīṃ sa bahirgataḥ \|*  
*snātvā samarcya vai devānetāvaṃtamanehasam \|\| 14 \|\|*

*adhītyādhyayanārthaṃ sa dvijairmitraissamaṃ yayau \|*  
*ekaputreti tanmātā pratārayati dīkṣitam \|\| 15 \|\|*

12-15. Although his mother wanted him to meet his father now and then, he never went near his father. Engaged in extra-domestic activities Yajñadatta used to ask his wife “Dear good woman, what is our son Guṇanidhi doing? He is not at home.” Then the woman used to say, “He has gone out just now. So long he had been taking his bath and worshipping the deities. He has finished his Vedic studies and has just gone out in the company of two or three friends for the purpose of learning somewhere”. The poor woman in view of the fact that she had only one son deceived her husband thus.

## \|\| 2.17.16 \|\|

*na tatkarma ca tadvṛttaṃ kiṃcidvetti sa dīkṣitaḥ \|*  
*sarvaṃ keśāṃtakarmāsya cakre varṣe'tha ṣoḍaśe \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The simple husband did not know anything about the nefarious activities of his son or his bad conduct. All sacred rites ending with Keśa Karma were performed in the sixteenth year of the son.

## \|\| 2.17.17 \|\|

*atho sa dīkṣito yajñadattaḥ putrasya tasya ca \|*  
*gṛhyoktena vidhānena pāṇigrāhamakārayam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Thereafter Yajñadatta performed the marriage rite of the son in accordance with the rules prescribed in the Gṛhya Sūtras.

## \|\| 2.17.18 \|\|

*pratyahaṃ tasya jananī sutaṃ guṇanidhiṃ mṛdu \|*  
*śāsti snehārdrahṛdayā hyupaveśya sma nārada \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. O Nārada, every day the woman with her heart melting with motherly affection used to make her son sit up and gently upbraid him.

## \|\| 2.17.19 \|\|

*krodhanaste'sti tanaya sa mahātmā pitetyalam \|*  
*yadi jñāsyati te vṛttaṃ tvāṃ ca māṃ tāḍayiṣyati \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. “Dear son, your father is surely a great man, but he is of rash temperament. If he comes to know of your activities he will beat you and will not spare me too.

## \|\| 2.17.20 \|\|

*ācchādayāmi te nityaṃ pituragre kuceṣṭitam \|*  
*lokamānyo'sti te tātassadācārairna vai dhanaiḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. I conceal your nefarious activities from your father every day. Due to his good conduct and his affluent circumstances he is honoured by all the people.

## \|\| 2.17.21 \|\|

*brāhmaṇānāṃ dhanaṃ tāta sadvidyā sādhusaṃgamaḥ \|*  
*kimarthaṃ na karoṣi tvaṃ suruciṃ prītamānasaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Dear child, a good learning and association with men of saintly character constitute a great asset for brahmins. How is it that you do not gladly take interest in such things?

## \|\| 2.17.22 \|\|

*sacchrotriyāste'nūcānā dīkṣitāssomayājinaḥ \|*  
*iti rūḍhimiha prāptāstava pūrvapitāmahāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Your ancestors and grandfathers had all earned the reputation of being good Vedic scholars, well learned in Śāstras, and performers of sacrifices, especially Somayāgas.

## \|\| 2.17.23 \|\|

*tyaktvā durvṛttasaṃsargaṃ sādhusaṃgarato bhava \|*  
*sadvidyāsu mano dhehi brāhmaṇācāramācara \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Shun the company of the wicked people, associate with good men, turn your attention to good learning and strictly adhere to brahminical conventions.

## \|\| 2.17.24 \|\|

*tātānurūpo rūpeṇa yaśasā kulaśīlataḥ \|*  
*tato na trapase kinnastyaja durvṛttatāṃ svakām \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Emulate your father in form, fame and traditional activity. Why don’t you feel ashamed? Cast off your wickedness.

## \|\| 2.17.25 \|\|

*ūnaviṃśatiko'si tvameṣā ṣoḍaśavārṣikī \|*  
*etāṃ saṃvṛṇu sadvṛttāṃ pitṛbhaktiyuto bhava \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. You are nineteen now. This girl is sixteen years old. She is a good girl. Take her. Protect her. Above all be devoted to your father.

## \|\| 2.17.26 \|\|

*śvaśuro'pi hi te mānyassarvatra guṇaśīlataḥ \|*  
*tato na trapase kinnastyaja durvṛttatāṃ suta \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. You shall respect your father-in-law also, in view of his good qualities and conduct. How is it that you do not feel ashamed of wickedness?

## \|\| 2.17.27 \|\|

*mātulāste'tulāḥ putra vidyāśīlakulādibhiḥ \|*  
*tebhyo'pi na bibheṣi tvaṃ śuddho'syubhayavaṃśataḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Dear son, your maternal uncles too are matchless in learning, conduct and pedigree and other things. You are not afraid even of them. Your paternal and maternal lineages are equally pure.

## \|\| 2.17.28 \|\|

*paśyaitānprati veśmasthānbrāhmaṇānāṃ kumārakān \|*  
*gṛhe'pi śiṣyānpaśyaitānpituste vinayocitān \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. See the brahmin boys of your neighbourhood. Even in our house see the disciples of your father. How humbly do they behave?

## \|\| 2.17.29 \|\|

*rājāpi śroṣyati yadā tava duśceṣṭitaṃ suta \|*  
*śraddhāṃ vihāya te tāte vṛttilopaṃ kariṣyati \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Dear son, if the king hears of your evil propensities, he will cease to respect your father and may even suspend the regular maintenance allowance.

## \|\| 2.17.30 \|\|

*bālaceṣṭitamevaitadvadaṃtyadyāpi te janāḥ \|*  
*anaṃtaraṃ hariṣyaṃti yuktāṃ dīkṣitatāmiha \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Till now people used to call your activities the foolish blunders of an ignorant boy. Hereafter they may take away the traditional title of Dīkṣita.

## \|\| 2.17.31 \|\|

*sarvepyākṣārayiṣyaṃti tava tātaṃ ca māmapi \|*  
*mātuścaritraṃ tanayo dhatte durbhāṣaṇairiti \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. People will curse and cavil at your father and me saying such evil words as “The son has adopted the wickedness of the mother.”

## \|\| 2.17.32 \|\|

*pitāpi te na pāpīyāñchrutismṛtipathānugaḥ \|*  
*tadaṃghrilīnamanaso mama sākṣī maheśvaraḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Your father has never been a sinner. He strictly follows the path of the Vedas and Smṛtis. Lord Śiva is my witness for the purity of my mind that is riveted to his feet.

## \|\| 2.17.33 \|\|

*na cartusnātayayāpīha mukhaṃ duṣṭasya vīkṣitam \|*  
*aho balīyānsa vidhiryena jāto bhavāniti \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. I have not seen the face of any wicked man after my menstrual bath. Powerful indeed is Fate whence a boy like you is born of my womb!”

## \|\| 2.17.34 \|\|

*pratikṣaṇaṃ jananyeti śikṣyamāṇotidurmatiḥ \|\| \|*  
*na tatyāja ca taddharmaṃ durbodho vyasanī yataḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Although constantly advised thus by his mother, the wicked boy did not abandon his evil ways. For, an idiot indulging in vice is beyond redemption.

## \|\| 2.17.35 \|\|

*mṛgayāmadyapaiśunyānṛtacauryadurodaraiḥ \|*  
*sa vāradārairvyasanairebhiḥ ko'tra na khaṃḍitaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Who is he that is not broken up by the evil influences of hunting, wine, slander, untruth, theft, gambling and prostitutes?

## \|\| 2.17.36 \|\|

*yadyanmadhyagṛhe paśyettattannītvā sudurmatiḥ \|*  
*arpayeddyūtakārāṇāṃ sakupyaṃ vasanādikam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. The wicked fellow (Guṇanidhi) used to lay his hands on whatever he could see in the house, a cloth, a base metal etc. and take it to the gambling den, there to lose the same to his brother gamblers.

## \|\| 2.17.37 \|\|

*nyastāṃ ratnamayīṃ gehe karasya piturūrmikām \|*  
*corayitvaikadādāya durodarakare'rpayat \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Once he stole a very valuable ring of his father set with precious stones and gave it to one the of gamblers.

## \|\| 2.17.38 \|\|

*dīkṣitena parijñāto daivāddyūtakṛtaḥ kare \|*  
*uvāca dīkṣitastaṃ ca kuto labdhā tvayormikā \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. It chanced that one day the Dīkṣita saw it in the hand of the gambler. He asked the fellow—“Where did you get this ring from?”

## \|\| 2.17.39-40 \|\|

*pṛṣṭastenātha nirbaṃdhādasakṛttamuvāca saḥ \|*  
*māmākṣipasi viproccaiḥ kiṃ mayā cauryakarmaṇā \|\| 39 \|\|*

*labdhā mudrā tvadīyena putreṇaiva samarpitā \|*  
*mama māturhi pūrvedyurjitvā nīto hi śāṭakaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

39-40. First the gambler did not say anything. When repeatedly asked he said—“O brahmin, you are unnecessarily accusing me of theft. It was your son who gave it to me. On the previous day I had won his mother’s upper garment.

## \|\| 2.17.41 \|\|

*na kevalaṃ mamaivaitadaṃgulīyaṃ samarpitam \|*  
*anyeṣāṃ dyūtakartṝṇāṃ bhūri tenārpitaṃ vasu \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Do not think that I alone was the winner of this ring. He has lost many costly things to other gamblers as well.

## \|\| 2.17.42 \|\|

*ratnakupyadukūlāni śṛṃgāraprabhṛtīni ca \|*  
*bhājanāni vicitrāṇi kāṃsyatāmramayāni ca \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. He has thus given gems, metals, silk garments, vessels, golden vases, and different sorts of copper and bell metal pots.

## \|\| 2.17.43 \|\|

*nagnīkṛtya pratidinaṃ badhyate dyūtakāribhiḥ \|*  
*na tena sadṛśaḥ kaścidākṣiko bhūmimaṃḍale \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Everyday he is being bound stark naked by the gamblers. In the whole world you cannot see such a useless poor gambler as he (your son).

## \|\| 2.17.44 \|\|

*adyāvadhi tvayā vipra durodara śiromaṇiḥ \|*  
*kathaṃ nājñāyi tanayo'vinayānayakovidaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. How is it that till now, O brahmin, you have not realised that your son is a ring leader of base gamblers, very clever in misdemeanour and unfair means?

## \|\| 2.17.45 \|\|

*iti śrutvā trapābhāravinamratarakaṃdharaḥ \|*  
*prāvṛtya vāsasā mauliṃ prāviśannijamandiram \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. On hearing these words, the poor Dīkṣita’s head bent down with shame. He covered his face and head with a cloth and quietly slipped back into his house.

## \|\| 2.17.46 \|\|

*mahāpativratāmasya patnī provāca tāmatha \|*  
*sa dīkṣito yajñadattaḥ śrautakarmaparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Yajñadatta, the sacrificer, well versed in Vedic rites spoke thus to his wife who was a very chaste lady.

## \|\| 2.17.47-48 \|\|

*yajñadatta uvāca \|*  
*dīkṣitāyani kutrāsti dhūrte guṇanidhissutaḥ \|*  
*atha tiṣṭhatu kiṃ tena kva sā mama śubhormikā \|\| 47 \|\|*

*aṃgodvartanakāle yā tvayā me'ṅgulito hṛtā \|*  
*sā tvaṃ ratnamayī śīghraṃ tāmānīya prayaccha me \|\| 48 \|\|*

Yajñadatta said:—

47-48. O mistress! where is that gambling rogue of a son, Guṇanidhi? Or let it be. Why should I ask for him? Where is that auspicious ring which you took off at the time of applying unguents on my body? Bring it quickly and give it to me.

## \|\| 2.17.49-51 \|\|

*iti śrutvātha tadvākyaṃ bhītā sā dīkṣitāyanī \|*  
*provāca snānamadhyāhnīṃ kriyāṃ niṣpādayatyatha \|\| 49 \|\|*

*vyagrāsmi devapūjārthamupahārādikarmaṇi \|*  
*samayo'yamatikrāmedatithīnāṃ priyātithe \|\| 50 \|\|*

*idānīmeva pakvānnakāraṇavyagrayā mayā \|*  
*sthāpitā bhājane kvāpi vismṛteti na vedmyaham \|\| 51 \|\|*

49-51. The mistress was frightened at these words. While she was engaged in arranging for bath and midday sacred rites she replied—“O lord, I am busy arranging the various articles of offerings for worship. O lord, fond of guests, the guests may be unnecessarily detained. While I was busy cooking the pudding I kept the ring somewhere in some vessel just now. What a pity! I have forgotten it. I do not know where it has been kept.

## \|\| 2.17.52-53 \|\|

*dīkṣita uvāca \|*  
*haṃ he'satputrajanani nityaṃ satyaprabhāṣiṇi \|*  
*yadā yadā tvāṃ saṃpṛche tanayaḥ kva gatastviti \|\| 52 \|\|*

*tadātadeti tvaṃ brūyānnathedānīṃ sa nirgataḥ \|*  
*adhītyādhyayanārthaṃ ca dvitrairmitraissayugbahiḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

Dīkṣita said:—

52-53. O truthful lady who has given birth to a base boy, whenever I asked “Where has the son gone?” you used to say, “Dear lord, just now he has gone out after finishing his lesson of the Vedas, in the company of two or three friends for revision of the lesson”.

## \|\| 2.17.54 \|\|

*kutaste śāṭakaḥ patni māṃjiṣṭho yo mayārpitaḥ \|*  
*labhate yo'niśaṃ dhāmni tathyaṃ brūhi bhayaṃ tyaja \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Where is your silk saree red like madder which I had presented to you and which used to hang down here in the house always? Tell me the truth. Do not be afraid.

## \|\| 2.17.55 \|\|

*sāṃprataṃ nekṣyate so'pi bhṛṃgāro maṇimaṃḍitaḥ \|*  
*paṭṭasūtramayī sāpi tripaṭī yā mayārpitā \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. That gem-set golden vase which I had given you is also missing. That tripod with a velvet cushion which I had given you is nowhere to be seen.

## \|\| 2.17.56 \|\|

*kva dākṣiṇātyaṃ tatkāṃsyaṃ gauḍī tāmraghaṭī kva sā \|*  
*nāgadaṃtamayī sā kva sukhakautuka maṃcikā \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Where is that bell metal pot made in the South? Where is that copper pot made in Bengal? Where is that ivory casket intended for curios and trinkets?

## \|\| 2.17.57 \|\|

*kva sā parvatadeśīyā candrakāṃtirivādbhutā \|*  
*dīpakavyagrahastāgrālaṃkṛtā śālabhañjikā \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Where is that wonderfully fine statuette of a lady lighting a lamp, shining like the moon, and brought from the hilly province?

## \|\| 2.17.58 \|\|

*kiṃ bahūktena kulaje tubhyaṃ kupyāmyahaṃ vṛthā \|*  
*tadābhyavahāriṣyehamupayaṃsyāmyahaṃ yadā \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Why should I unnecessarily speak much? O lady of a noble family, it is futile to be angry with you. I shall take food -only after I marry again!

## \|\| 2.17.59 \|\|

*anapatyo'smi tenāhaṃ duṣṭena kuladūṣiṇā \|*  
*uttiṣṭhānaya pāthastvaṃ tasmai dadyāstilāṃjalim \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. I am childless now since that wicked fellow has defiled the whole family. Get up and fetch me some water. Let me offer libations to him with gingelly seeds.

## \|\| 2.17.60 \|\|

*aputratvaṃ varaṃ nṝṇāṃ kuputrātkulapāṃsanāt \|*  
*tyajedekaṃ kulasyārthe nītireṣā sanātanī \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Better to be issueless than have a wicked son who defiles the entire family. It is the traditional policy to abandon one to save the family.

## \|\| 2.17.61 \|\|

*snātvā nityavidhiṃ kṛtvā tasminnevāhni kasyacit \|*  
*śrotriyasya sutāṃ prāpya pāṇiṃ jagrāha dīkṣitaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. The Brāhmaṇa took his bath, performed his daily rites and married the daughter of a Vedic scholar the same day.

## Chapter 18 - The Redemption of Guṇanidhi

## \|\| 2.18.1-2 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*śrutvā tathā sa vṛttāṃtaṃ prāktanaṃ svaṃ viniṃdya ca \|*  
*kāṃciddiśaṃ samālokya niryayau dīkṣitāṃgajaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*kiyacciraṃ tato gatvā yajñadattātmajassa hi \|*  
*duṣṭo guṇanidhistasthau gatotsāho visarjitaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

1-2. Guṇanidhi, the son of the Dīkṣita Yajñadatta, came to know of this. Regretfully he cursed himself and set off from that place. After wandering aimlessly for a long time, he, the wicked fellow, felt the abandonment keenly and losing all hopes halted at a place.

## \|\| 2.18.3-7 \|\|

*ciṃtāmavāpa mahatīṃ kva yāmi karavāṇi kim \|*  
*nāhamabhyastavidyo'smi na caivātidhano'smyaham \|\| 3 \|\|*

*deśāṃtare yasya dhanaṃ sa sadyassukhamedhate \|*  
*bhayamasti dhane caurātsa vighnassarvatobhavaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*yājakasya kule janma kathaṃ me vyasanaṃ mahat \|*  
*aho balīyānhi vidhirbhāvikarmānusaṃdhayet \|\| 5 \|\|*

*bhikṣitunnādhigacchāmi na me paricitiḥ kvacit \|*  
*na ca pārśve dhanaṃ kiñcitkimatra śaraṇaṃ bhavet \|\| 6 \|\|*

*sadānabhyudite bhānau prasūrme miṣṭabhojanam \|*  
*dadyādadyātra kaṃ yāce na ceha jananī mama \|\| 7 \|\|*

3-7. He thought to himself: “Where am I to go? What shall I do? I have not studied much, nor am I rich enough. Only a wealthy man can be happy in a foreign land, although he has to face the fear of thieves there. Of course this fear is present everywhere. I am born in the family of priests officiating in sacrifices. Why am I reduced to this wretched plight? Fate is powerful indeed, controlling all our future actions. I cannot even beg as I have no acquaintance, no money. Where shall I seek refuge? Everyday, even before sunrise, my mother used to feed me with sweet pudding. Today whom shall I beg? My mother too is away from me.”

## \|\| 2.18.8 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*iti ciṃtayatastasya bahuśastatra nārada \|*  
*ati dīnaṃ tarormūle bhānurastācalaṃ gataḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. O Nārada, even as he was musing like this woefully, sitting at the foot of a tree, the sun set.

## \|\| 2.18.9 \|\|

*etasminneva samaye kaścinmāheśvaro naraḥ \|*  
*sahopahārānādāya nagarādbahirabhyagāt \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. In the meantime a certain devotee of Lord Śiva came out of the city taking with him various articles of offering.

## \|\| 2.18.10 \|\|

*nānāvidhānmahādivyānsvajanaiḥ parivāritaḥ \|*  
*samabhyarcitumīśānaṃ śivarātrāvupoṣitaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. He had observed fast on the Śivarātri day. In order to worship lord Śiva, he was on his way, along with his kinsmen and was carrying different sorts of delightful offerings.

## \|\| 2.18.11 \|\|

*śivālayaṃ praviśyātha sa bhaktaśśivasaktadhīḥ \|*  
*yathocitaṃ sucittena pūjayāmāsa śaṃkaram \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The devotee entered the temple of Śiva where he worshipped Him in the prescribed manner with sincere devotion.

## \|\| 2.18.12 \|\|

*pakvānnagaṃdhamāghrāya yajñadattātmajo dvijaḥ \|*  
*pitṛtyakto mātṛhīnaḥ kṣudhitaḥ sa tamanvagāt \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The brahmin boy, son of Yajñadatta, devoid of his mother and dismissed by his father, was very hungry by this time. He inhaled the sweet fragrance of the sweet puddings and followed the devotee.

## \|\| 2.18.13 \|\|

*idamannaṃ mayā grāhyaṃ śivāyopakṛtaṃ niśi \|*  
*supte śaivajane daivātsarvasminvividhaṃ mahat \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. “If fortunately these devotees of Śiva go to sleep after offering the eatables to Śiva, I shall eat these vast varieties of puddings and sweets in the night”.

## \|\| 2.18.14 \|\|

*ityāśāmavalambyātha dvāri śaṃbhorupāviśat \|*  
*dadarśa ca mahāpūjāṃ tena bhaktena nirmitām \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. With this hope he sat at the threshold of the temple of Śiva watching the great worship by the devotee.

## \|\| 2.18.15 \|\|

*vidhāya nṛtyagītādi bhaktāssuptāḥ kṣaṇe yadā \|*  
*naivedyaṃ sa tadādātuṃ bhargāgāraṃ viveśa ha \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. When the worship was over, the songs and dances of prayer were duly concluded, the devotees lay down and began to sleep. Immediately the young man entered the sanctum sanctorum of Śiva in order to steal the eatables left there.

## \|\| 2.18.16 \|\|

*dīpaṃ maṃdaprabhaṃ dṛṣṭvā pakvānnavīkṣaṇāya saḥ \|*  
*nijacailāṃjalādvartiṃ kṛtvā dīpaṃ prakāśya ca \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The lamp was burning very dimly. Hence in order to see the puddings clearly he tore a piece of cloth from his lower garment and put that piece in the lamp as a wick thus making the lamp give a good light.

## \|\| 2.18.17 \|\|

*yajñadattātmajasso'tha śivanaivedyamādarāt \|*  
*jagrāha sahasā prītyā pakvānna vahuśastataḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Yajñadatta’s son gleefully took plenty of the sweets offered as eatables to Lord Śiva by the devotees.

## \|\| 2.18.18 \|\|

*tataḥ pakvānnamādāya tvaritaṃ gacchato bahiḥ \|*  
*tasya pādatalāghātātprasuptaḥ kopyabudhyata \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. With sweets in his hands he came out hurriedly. In his hurry he stamped on some person lying there who woke up immediately.

## \|\| 2.18.19 \|\|

*ko'yaṃ ko'yaṃ tvarāpanno gṛhyatāṃ gṛhyatā masau \|*  
*iti cukrośa sa jano girā bhayamahoccayā \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. “Who is that? Who is running away so fast? Catch him.” So shouted the man who woke up in a voice hoarse with fear.

## \|\| 2.18.20 \|\|

*yāvadbhayātsamāgatya tāvatsa purarakṣakaiḥ \|*  
*palāyamāno nihataḥ kṣaṇādaṃdhatvamāgataḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. The brahmin boy (Guṇanidhi) who ran for life became blind. So he was caught and killed by the watchmen on duty.

## \|\| 2.18.21 \|\|

*abhakṣayacca naivedyaṃ yajñadattātmajo mune \|*  
*śivānugrahato nūnaṃ bhāvipuṇyabalānna saḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. O sage, by the favour of Śiva or by the power of accumulated merit, the son of Yajñadatta could not partake of the offerings of eatables made to Lord Śiva.

## \|\| 2.18.22 \|\|

*atha baddhassamāgatya pāśamudgarapāṇibhiḥ \|*  
*ninīṣubhiḥ saṃyamanīṃ yāmyaissa vikaṭairbhaṭaiḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The terrible soldiers of Yama who desired to take him to Saṃyamani (the abode of Yama), approached him with nooses and clubs in their hands and bound him.

## \|\| 2.18.23 \|\|

*tāvatpāriṣadāḥ prāptāḥ kiṃki ṇījālamālinaḥ \|*  
*divyaṃ vimānamādāya taṃ netuṃ śūlapāṇayaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. In the meantime the attendants of Śiva with tridents in their hands and tinkling anklets on their arms reached the spot in an aerial chariot in order to take him to Śivaloka.

## \|\| 2.18.24 \|\|

*śivagaṇā ūcuḥ \|*  
*muṃcatainaṃ dvijaṃ yāmyā gaṇāḥ parama dhārmikam \|*  
*daṇḍayogyo na vipro'sau dagdhasarvāghasaṃcayaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

Śivagaṇas said:—

24\. “O attendants of Yama, leave this righteous brahmin alone. He cannot be punished since his sins have been burnt off.”

## \|\| 2.18.25-27 \|\|

*ityākarṇya vacaste hi yamarājagaṇāstataḥ \|*  
*mahādevagaṇānāhurbabhūvuścakitā bhṛśam \|\| 25 \|\|*

*śaṃbhorgaṇānathālokya bhītaistairyamakiṃkaraiḥ \|*  
*avādi praṇatairitthaṃ durvṛtto'yaṃ gaṇā dvijaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*yamagaṇā ūcuḥ \|*  
*kulācāraṃ pratīryyaiṣa pitrorvākyaparāṅmukhaḥ \|*  
*satyaśaucaparibhraṣṭassaṃdhyāsnānavivarjitaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

25-27. On hearing these words of Śiva’s attendants, the attendants of Yama became terrified and addressed the attendants of Śiva:

## \|\| 2.18.28 \|\|

*āstāṃ dūresya karmānyacchivanirmālyalaṃghakaḥ \|*  
*pratyakṣato'tra vīkṣadhvamaspṛśyo'yaṃ bhavādṛśām \|\| 28 \|\|*

Yamagaṇas said:—

“O Gaṇas, this is a wicked brahmin who has broken the traditions and conventions of his family. He has disobeyed his father’s directions and has forsaken truthfulness or purity. He does not offer his Sandhyā prayers. He does not take his ceremonial baths regularly.

28\. Leave aside his other activities. He has now transgressed and outraged the offerings of eatables made to Śiva. You can see this personally. In fact he is not worthy of even being touched by people like you.

## \|\| 2.18.29 \|\|

*śivanirmālyabhoktāraśśivanirmmālyalaṃghakāḥ \|*  
*śivanirmālyadātāraḥ sparśasteṣāṃ hyapuṇyakṛt \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Those who consume or outrage the offerings of eatables made to Śiva and those who offer these to others, the mere touch of these persons, it is said, is sinful.

## \|\| 2.18.30 \|\|

*viṣamālokya vā peyaṃ śreyo vā sparśanaṃ param \|*  
*sevitavyaṃ śivasvaṃ na prāṇaḥ kaṇṭhagatairapi \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Even poison is not so dangerous when drunk. Never shall a person make use of Śiva’s property even if he were to die.

## \|\| 2.18.31 \|\|

*yūyaṃ pramāṇaṃ dharmeṣu yathā na ca tathā vayam \|*  
*asti ceddharmaleśosya gaṇāstaṃ śṛṇumo vayam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. It is granted that you are an authority on virtue. We are not. But O Gaṇas, if this fellow has at least a bit of virtue to his credit, please let us hear the same”.

## \|\| 2.18.32 \|\|

*itthaṃ tadvākyamākarṇya yāmānāṃ śivakiṃkarāḥ \|*  
*smṛtvā śivapadāmbhojaṃ procuḥ pāriṣadāstu tān \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. On hearing these words of Yama’s attendants, the attendants of Śiva remembered the lotus-like feet of Śiva and spoke to them thus:—

## \|\| 2.18.33 \|\|

*śivakiṃkarā ūcuḥ \|*  
*kiṃkarāśśivadharmā ye sūkṣmāste tu bhavādṛśaiḥ \|*  
*sthūlalakṣyaiḥ kathaṃ lakṣyā lakṣyā ye sūkṣmadṛṣṭibhiḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

Śiva’s attendants said:—

33\. “O Attendants of Yama, Śiva’s ideas of Dharma are very subtle. They can be observed only by persons of subtle and keen vision, not by people like you whose aim is only the gross exterior.

## \|\| 2.18.34 \|\|

*anenānenasā karma yatkṛtaṃ śṛṇuteha tat \|*  
*yajñadattātmajenātha sāvadhānatayā gaṇāḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. O Gaṇas, hear attentively what this son of Yajñadatta has done which has freed him from sins.

## \|\| 2.18.35 \|\|

*pataṃtī liṃgaśirasi dīpacchāyā nivāritā \|*  
*svacailāṃcalato'nena dattvā dīpadaśāṃ niśi \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. The shadow of the lamp was falling on the top of the liṅga and this brahmin prevented it by adding a wick to the lamp at night, cutting a piece from his lower cloth.

## \|\| 2.18.36 \|\|

*aparopi paro dharmo jātastatrāsya kiṃkaraḥ \|*  
*śṛṇvataḥ śivanāmāni prasaṃgādapi gṛhṇatām \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Another great merit he derived from listening to the names of Śiva, though casually, O attendants.

## \|\| 2.18.37 \|\|

*bhaktena vidhinā pūjā kriyamāṇā nirīkṣitā \|*  
*upoṣitena bhūtāyāmanenāsthitacetasā \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. He witnessed the worship that was being performed duly by a devotee. He was observing a fast and his mind was concentrated too.

## \|\| 2.18.38 \|\|

*śivalokamayaṃ hyadya gaṃtāsmābhissahaiva tu \|*  
*kaṃcitkālaṃ mahābhogānkariṣyati śivānugaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Let him go to Śivaloka along with us. As Śiva’s follower let him enjoy great pleasures there for sometime.

## \|\| 2.18.39 \|\|

*kaliṃgarājo bhavitā tato nirdhūtakalmaṣaḥ \|*  
*eṣa dvijavaro nūnaṃ śivapriyataro yataḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Then he will shake off his sins and become the king of Kaliṅga since he has indeed become a great favourite of Śiva.

## \|\| 2.18.40 \|\|

*anyatkiṃcinna vaktavyaṃ yūyaṃ yāta yathāgatam \|*  
*yamadūtāssvalokaṃ tu suprasannena cetasā \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Nothing else need be mentioned now. Let all of you, emissaries of Yama, return to your own world with contented minds.”

## \|\| 2.18.41 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya vacasteṣāṃ yamadūtā munīśvara \|*  
*yathāgataṃ yayussarve yamalokaṃ parāṅmukhāḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

41\. O lordly sage, on hearing these words of Śiva’s attendants, the emissaries of Yama returned to Yama’s abode.

## \|\| 2.18.42 \|\|

*sarvaṃ nivedayāmāsuśśamanāya gaṇā mune \|*  
*tadvṛttamāditaḥ proktaṃ śaṃbhudūtaiśca dharmataḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. O sage, they narrated everything to Yama whatever the messengers of Śiva told them about Dharma etc.

## \|\| 2.18.43 \|\|

*\|\| dharmarāja uvāca \|*  
*sarve śṛṇuta madvākyaṃ sāvadhānatayā gaṇāḥ \|*  
*tadeva prītyā kuruta macchāsanapurassaram \|\| 43 \|\|*

Dharmarāja said:—

43\. “O Gaṇas, listen attentively to what I say. Whatever I direct you to do, you shall do with loving devotion.

## \|\| 2.18.44 \|\|

*ye tripuṇḍradharā loke vibhūtyā sitayā gaṇāḥ \|*  
*te sarve parihartavyā nānetavyāḥ kadācana \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. O Gaṇas, you shall avoid those persons who bear on their forehead the mark of Tripuṇḍra besmeared with white ashes. Never shall they be brought here.

## \|\| 2.18.45 \|\|

*uddhūlanakarā ye hi vibhūtyā sitayā gaṇāḥ \|*  
*te sarve parihartavyā nānetavyāḥ kadācana \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. O Gaṇas, you shall avoid those persons who regularly dust their body with white ashes. Never shall they be brought here.

## \|\| 2.18.46 \|\|

*śivaveṣatayā loke yena kenāpi hetunā \|*  
*te sarve parihartavyā nānetavyāḥ kadācana \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. You shall avoid all those persons who assume the garb and features of Śiva whatever their reason may be. Never shall they be brought here.

## \|\| 2.18.47 \|\|

*ye rudrākṣadharā loke jaṭādhāriṇa eva ye \|*  
*te save parihartavyā nānetavyāḥ kadācana \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. You shall avoid those persons who wear Rudrākṣas and keep matted hair. Never shall they be brought here.

## \|\| 2.18.48 \|\|

*upajīvanahetośca śivaveṣadharā hi ye \|*  
*te sarve parihartavyā nānetavyāḥ kadācana \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. You shall avoid those persons who imitate the dress or the features of Śiva, even for their livelihood. Never shall they be brought here.

## \|\| 2.18.49 \|\|

*daṃbhenāpi cchalenāpi śivaveṣadharā hi ye \|*  
*te sarve parihartavyā nānetavyāḥ kadācana \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. You shall avoid those persons who imitate the dress and features of Śiva even for the purpose of deception. Never shall they be brought here.”

## \|\| 2.18.50 \|\|

*evamājñāpayāmāsa sa yamo nija kiṃkarān \|*  
*tatheti matvā te sarve tūṣṇīmāsañchucismitāḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Yama thus commanded his servants. They too agreed to follow his command and remained silent with the flickering smile on their lips.

## \|\| 2.18.51 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*pārṣadairyamadūtebhyo mocitastviti sa dvijaḥ \|*  
*śivalokaṃ jagāmāśu tairgaṇaiśśucimānasaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

51\. Thus freed from the emissaries of Yama, the brahmin boy became pure-minded and went to Śivaloka along with the attendants of Śiva.

## \|\| 2.18.52 \|\|

*tatra bhuktvākhilānbhogānsaṃsevya ca śivāśivau \|*  
*ariṃdamasya tanayaḥ kaliṃgādhipaterabhūt \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. There he served Śiva and Śivā (Pārvatī) and enjoyed all sorts of pleasures. Afterwards he was born as the son of Arindama, the king of Kaliṅga.

## \|\| 2.18.53 \|\|

*dama ityabhidhāno'bhūcchivasevāparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*bālo'pi śiśubhiḥ sākaṃ śivabhaktiṃ cakāra saḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Known as Dama he was devoted to the service of Śiva. Even as a boy he carried on many acts of devotion to Śiva in the company of other children.

## \|\| 2.18.54 \|\|

*kramādrājyamavāpātha pitaryuparate yuvā \|*  
*prītyā pravartayāmāsa śivadharmāṃśca sarvaśaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. When his father passed away he became the king in the prime of his youth. In his kingdom he spread the ideals and tenets of Śiva lovingly.

## \|\| 2.18.55 \|\|

*nānyaṃ dharmaṃ sa jānāti durdamo bhūpatirdamaḥ \|*  
*śivālayeṣu sarveṣu dīpadānādṛte dvijaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. The king Dama was unconquerable. O brahmin, he did not stress any act of piety other than furnishing temples of Śiva with lamps in plenty.

## \|\| 2.18.56 \|\|

*grāmādhīśānsamāhūya sarvānsa viṣayasthitān \|*  
*itthamājñāpayāmāsa dīpā deyāśśivālaye \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. He called headmen of the villages in his kingdom and asked them to furnish all temples of Śiva with lamps.

## \|\| 2.18.57 \|\|

*anyathā satyamevedaṃ sa me daṇḍyo bhaviṣyati \|*  
*dīpa dānācchivastuṣṭo bhavatīti śrutīritam \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. He warned them that if they defaulted they would be punished. It is declared in the Vedas that Śiva is delighted at the gift of a lamp to his temples.

## \|\| 2.18.58 \|\|

*yasyayasyābhito grāmaṃ yāvataśca śivālayāḥ \|*  
*tatratatra sadā dīpo dyotanīyo'vicāritam \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. “Therefore, you headmen shall see that the temples of Śiva in your jurisdiction are properly illuminated with lamps. There is no question of hesitation in this matter.

## \|\| 2.18.59 \|\|

*mamājñābhaṃgadoṣeṇa śiraśchetsyāmyasaṃśayam \|*  
*iti tadbhayato dīpā dīptāḥ pratiśivālayam \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. “Undoubtedly I shall get the defaulter beheaded.” Thus for fear of him every temple was duly illuminated.

## \|\| 2.18.60 \|\|

*anenaiva sa dharmeṇa yāvajjīvaṃ damo nṛpaḥ \|*  
*dharmarddhiṃ mahatīṃ prāpya kāladharmavaśaṃ gataḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. With this act of piety alone, as long as he lived, the king Dama acquired ample prosperity. Finally he passed away.

## \|\| 2.18.61 \|\|

*sa dīpavāsanāyogādbahūndīpānpradīpya vai \|*  
*alakāyāḥ patirabhūdratnadīpaśikhāśrayaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. The impression of lamps persisted in his mind. He caused many lamps to be lighted. Finally he became the lord of Alakā with gem-set lamps to his credit.

## \|\| 2.18.62 \|\|

*evaṃ phalati kālena śive'lpamapi yatkṛtam \|*  
*iti jñātvā śive kāryaṃ bhajanaṃ susukhārthibhiḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Thus even the smallest service rendered to Śiva bears rich fruit in time. Let all persons seeking happiness realise this and continue the worship of Śiva.

## \|\| 2.18.63-65 \|\|

*kva sa dīkṣitadāyādaḥ sarvadharmāratiḥ sadā \|*  
*śivālaye daivayogādyātaścorayituṃ vasu \|*  
*svārthadīpadaśodyotaliṃgamaulitamoharaḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

*kaliṃgaviṣaye rājyaṃ prāpto dharmaratiṃ sadā \|*  
*śivālaye samuddīpya dīpānprāgvāsanodayāt \|\| 64 \|\|*

*kaiṣā dikpālapadavī munīśvara vilokaya \|*  
*manuṣyadharmiṇānena sāṃprataṃ yeha bhujyate \|\| 65 \|\|*

63-65. That son of Dīkṣita never cared for any act of piety. It was to steal that he had entered the temple of Śiva. To serve his own end he had brightened the lamp there, thereby dispelling the shadow of darkness on the top of the liṅga. Then he became the virtuous king of Kaliṅga. O foremost of the sages where the wicked son of the Dīkṣita, and where the guardian of a quarter? Although he had been simply a man, he became the guardian of a quarter.

## \|\| 2.18.66 \|\|

*iti proktaṃ guṇanidheryajñadattātmajasya hi \|*  
*caritaṃ śivasaṃtoṣaṃ śṛṇvatāṃ sarvakāmadam \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Thus I have narrated the story of Guṇanidhi, the son of Yajñadatta. The story is pleasing to Śiva. Besides, it grants all desires of the listening devotees.

## \|\| 2.18.67 \|\|

*sarvadevaśivenāsau sakhitvaṃ ca yatheyivān \|*  
*tadapyekamanā bhūtvā śṛṇu tāta bravīmi te \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. O dear one, I shall tell you how he became the close friend of Śiva. Listen attentively.

## Chapter 19 - The friendship of Śiva and Kubera

## \|\| 2.19.1 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*pādme kalpe mama surā brahmaṇo mānasātsutāt \|*  
*pulastyādviśravā jajñe tasya vaiśravaṇassutaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

1\. In the Kalpa called Pādma, I created my mental son Pulastya whose son Viśravas begot the son Vaiśravaṇa.

## \|\| 2.19.2 \|\|

*teneyamalakā bhuktā purī viśvakṛtā kṛtā \|*  
*ārādhya tryaṃbakaṃ devamatyugratapasā purā \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. He propitiated the three-eyed God Śiva, with a very severe penance and enjoyed the city of Alakā built by Viśvakṛt.

## \|\| 2.19.3 \|\|

*vyatīte tatra kalpe vai pravṛtte meghavāhane \|*  
*yājñadattirasau śrīdastapastepe sudussaham \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. When that Kalpa was over and the Meghavāhana Kalpa had started, the son of Yajñadatta, Śrīda, performed a severe penance.

## \|\| 2.19.4-8 \|\|

*bhakti prabhāvaṃ vijñāya śaṃbhostaddīpamātrataḥ \|*  
*purā purāressaṃprāpya kāśikāṃ citprakāśikām \|\| 4 \|\|*

*śivaikādaśamudbodhya cittaratnapradīpakaiḥ \|*  
*ananyabhaktisnehāḍhyastanmayo dhyānaniścalaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*śivaikyaṃ sumahāpātraṃ tapogniparibṛṃhitam \|*  
*kāmakrodhamahāvighnapataṃgāghāta varjitam \|\| 6 \|\|*

*prāṇasaṃrodhanirvātaṃ nirmalaṃ nirmalekṣaṇāt \|*  
*saṃsthāpya śāṃbhavaṃ liṃgaṃ sadbhāvakusumārcitam \|\| 7 \|\|*

*tāvattatāpa sa tapastvagasthipariśeṣitam \|*  
*yāvadbabhūva tadvarṇaṃ varṣāṇāmayutaṃ śatam \|\| 8 \|\|*

4-8. Realising the efficacy of devotion to Śiva accruing from the mere illumination (of his temple) with lamps, he reached Kāśī for the illumination of his thought. Under the lustre of the gems of the mind, he repeated the mantras of eleven Rudras with loyal devotion and unswerving concentration of the mind. He could realise his identity with Śiva. Then he performed very severe penance for two hundred thousand years—a penance which was enhanced by the fire of austerity, was free from incroachment of the firefly in the form of interference from lust and anger, was windless inasmuch as the breath was curbed and was pure in form with pure vision. He set up the liṅga of Śiva and worshipped it with flowers of good ideas and feelings. The penance was so severe that his body was reduced to skin and bones.

## \|\| 2.19.9-10 \|\|

*tatassaha viśālākṣyā devo viśveśvararasvayam \|*  
*alakāpatimālokya prasannenāṃtarātmanā \|\| 9 \|\|*

*liṃge manassamādhāya sthitaṃ sthāṇusvarūpiṇam \|*  
*uvāca varado'smīti tadācakṣvālakāpate \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. Then in the company of the Goddess Pārvatī, the lord Viśveśvara Himself addressed the devotee, the lord of Alakā, with a pleasant mind—the devotee who stood as a stump with mind concentrated on the liṅga:—“I am ready to grant you a boon. Choose it, O lord of Alakā”.

## \|\| 2.19.11-13 \|\|

*unmīlya nayane yāvatsa paśyati tapodhanaḥ \|*  
*tāvadudyatsahasrāṃśu sahasrādhikatejasam \|\| 11 \|\|*

*puro dadarśa śrīkaṃṭhaṃ candracūḍamumādhavam \|*  
*tattejaḥ paribhūtākṣitejāḥ saṃmīlya locane \|\| 12 \|\|*

*uvāca devadeveśaṃ manorathapadātigam \|*  
*nijāṃghridarśane nātha dṛksāmarthyaṃ prayaccha me \|\| 13 \|\|*

11-13. The devotee opened his eyes and gazed at lord Śiva, the moon-crested consort of Umā who was shining with a brilliance that excelled thousands of rising suns. Dazzled by the brilliance, he closed his eyes and addressed the lord of lords who is beyond the reach of mental conception. “O lord, please give my eyes the power to see your feet.”

## \|\| 2.19.14 \|\|

*ayameva varo nātha yattvaṃ sākṣānnirīkṣyase \|*  
*kimanyena vareṇeśa namaste śaśiśekhara \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. This itself is a great boon, O lord, that I see you present. O lord, O moon-crested God, obeisance be to you. Of what avail are other boons?

## \|\| 2.19.15 \|\|

*iti tadvacanaṃ śrutvā devadeva umāpatiḥ \|*  
*dadau darśanasāmarthyaṃ spṛṣṭvā pāṇitalena tam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. On hearing his words, the lord of devas, Umā’s consort touched him with his palm and gave him the requisite of Vision.

## \|\| 2.19.16 \|\|

*prasārya nayane pūrvamumāmeva vyalokayat \|*  
*to'sau yājñadattistu tatsāmarthyamavāpya ca \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Then on securing the power, Yajñadatta’s son opened his eyes and saw Umā alone at first.

## \|\| 2.19.17 \|\|

*śaṃbhossamīpe kā yoṣideṣā sarvāṃgasundarī \|*  
*anayā kiṃ tapastaptaṃ mamāpi tapaso'dhikam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. “Who is this lady beautiful in person, near Śiva the Lord? What penance did she perform more difficult than mine?

## \|\| 2.19.18 \|\|

*aho rūpamaho prema saubhāgyaṃ śrīraho bhṛśam \|*  
*ityavādīdasau putro muhurmuhuratīva hi \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. “What a form! What a love! What a good luck! What a fine glory!” He repeated these words several times.

## \|\| 2.19.19 \|\|

*krūra dṛgvīkṣate yāvatpunaḥpunaridaṃ vadan \|*  
*tāvatpusphoṭa tannetraṃ vārāṃ vāmāvilokanāt \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. While he was doing this and glancing cruelly at Umā, his left eye as a result of seeing the lady, burst.

## \|\| 2.19.20-21 \|\|

*atha devyabravīddeva kimasau duṣṭatāpasaḥ \|*  
*asakṛdvīkṣya māṃ vakti kuru tvaṃ me tapaḥprabhām \|\| 20 \|\|*

*asakṛddakṣiṇenākṣṇā punarmāmeva paśyati \|*  
*asūyamāno me rūpaprema saubhāgyasaṃpada \|\| 21 \|\|*

20-21. Then the Goddess told Śiva—why does this wicked ascetic look at me often and say “You make my penance shine!” and seeing me with his right eye jealously why does he marvel at my beauty, love and good luck.

## \|\| 2.19.22-23 \|\|

*iti devīgiraṃ śrutvā prahasya prāha tāṃ prabhuḥ \|*  
*ume tvadīyaḥ putro'yaṃ na ca krūreṇa cakṣuṣā \|\| 22 \|\|*

*saṃpaśyati tapolakṣmīṃ tava kiṃ tvadhivarṇayet \|*  
*iti devīṃ samābhāṣya tamīśaḥ punarabravīt \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. On hearing the words of the Goddess, lord Śiva laughed and said “O Umā, he is your son. He does not look at you angrily or jealously. He is describing your glory of penance.” After saying this to the Goddess Īśa told him again.

## \|\| 2.19.24 \|\|

*varāndadāmi te vatsa tapasānena toṣitaḥ \|*  
*nidhīnāmatha nāthastvaṃ guhyakānāṃ bhaveśvaraḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. “Dear son, I am delighted at your penance. I shall give you the boon you desire. You will be the lord of treasures and the lord of Guhyakas.

## \|\| 2.19.25 \|\|

*yakṣāṇāṃ kinnarāṇāṃ ca rājñāṃ rāja ca suvrataḥ \|*  
*patiḥ puṇyajanānāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ dhanado bhava \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. You will be the king of Yakṣas\[3\], Kinnaras and rulers. You will be the leader of Puṇyajanas and the bestower of wealth to all.

## \|\| 2.19.26 \|\|

*mayā sakhyaṃ ca te nityaṃ vatsyāmi ca tavāṃtike \|*  
*alakāṃ nikaṣā mitra tava prītivivṛddhaye \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. My friendship with you shall remain for ever. I shall stay near you, very near Alakā, dear friend, in order to increase your love.

## \|\| 2.19.27 \|\|

*āgaccha pādayorasyāḥ pata te jananī tviyam \|*  
*yājñadatte mahābhakta suprasannena cetasā \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. O son of Yajñadatta, great devotee, come on. This is your mother. Fall at her feet with delighted heart.

## \|\| 2.19.28 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*iti dattvā varāndevaḥ punarāha śivāṃ śivaḥ \|*  
*prasādaṃ kuru deveśi tapasvinyaṃgaje'tra vai \|\| 28 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

28\. After granting him boons, Lord Śiva told Umā, “O Goddess, be pleased with him. This ascetic is your own son.”

## \|\| 2.19.29 \|\|

*ityākarṇya vacaśśaṃbhoḥ pārvatī jagadambikā \|*  
*abravīdyājñadattiṃ taṃ suprasannena cetasā \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. On hearing these words of Śiva, Pārvatī, the mother of the universe said to the son of Yajñadatta with a delighted mind.

## \|\| 2.19.30 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*vatsa te nirmalā bhaktirbhave bhavatu sarvadā \|*  
*bhavaikapiṃgo netreṇa vāmena sphuṭitena ha \|\| 30 \|\|*

The Goddess said:—

30\. Dear son, may your pure devotion to Śiva remain for ever. With your left eye burst you will be Ekapiṅga, (having a yellow mark in place of an eye).

## \|\| 2.19.31 \|\|

*devena dattā ye tubhyaṃ varāssaṃtu tathaiva te \|*  
*kubero bhava nāmnā tvaṃ mama rūperṣyayā suta \|\| 31 \|\|*
