31\. May all the boons granted to you by the lord fructify. You shall be called Kubera (lit. possessed of ill-shaped body), O son, since you jealously looked at me.

## \|\| 2.19.32 \|\|

*iti dattvā varāndevo devyā saha maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*dhanadāyāviveśātha dhāma vaiśveśvarābhidham \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. After granting these boons to Kubera, lord Maheśvara, in the company of the Goddess Pārvatī, entered his Viśveśvara abode.

## \|\| 2.19.33 \|\|

*itthaṃ sakhitvaṃ śrīśaṃbhoḥ prāpaiṣa dhanadaḥ puram \|*  
*alakānnikaṣā cāsītkailāsaśśaṃkarālayaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Thus Kubera attained the friendship of Śiva. Very near his city Alakā was Kailāsa, the abode of Śiva.

## Chapter 20 - Śiva goes to Kailāsa

## \|\| 2.20.1 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*nārada tvaṃ śṛṇu mune śivāgamanasattamam \|*  
*kailāse parvataśreṣṭhe kuberasya tapobalāt \|\| 1 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

1\. O Nārada, hear the story of Śiva’s arrival at Kailāsa, the best of mountains, thanks to the power of penance of Kubera.

## \|\| 2.20.2 \|\|

*nidhipatva varaṃ dattvā gatvā svasthānamuttamam \|*  
*vicintya hṛdi viśveśaḥ kuberavaradāyakaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. “The lord of the Universe, after bestowing the boon of lordship of treasures upon Kubera, returned to His excellent abode and thought within Himself thus.

## \|\| 2.20.3 \|\|

*vidhyaṃgajassvarūpo me pūrṇaḥ pralayakāryakṛt \|*  
*tadrūpeṇa gamiṣyāmi kailāsaṃ guhyakālayam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. My complete manifestation, born of Brahmā can look after the activity of Dissolution. Now, assuming that form I shall go to Kailāsa, the residence of Guhyakas.

## \|\| 2.20.4 \|\|

*rudro hṛdayajo me hi pūrṇāṃśo brahmaniṣphalaḥ \|*  
*hari brahmādibhissevyo madabhinno niraṃjana \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Rudra, born of my heart, my perfect manifestation is the Single Supreme Brahman. He is worthy of being served by Viṣṇu, Brahmā and others. He is not different from me. He is unsullied.

## \|\| 2.20.5 \|\|

*tatsvarūpeṇa tatraiva suhṛdbhūvā vilāsyaham \|*  
*kuberasya ca vatsyāmi kariṣyāmi tapo mahat \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. In that form I shall become that friend of Kubera, shall remain near him and perform great penance.”

## \|\| 2.20.6 \|\|

*iti saṃciṃtya rudro'sau śivecchāṃ gaṃtumutsukaḥ \|*  
*nanāda tatra ḍhakkāṃ svāṃ sugatiṃ nādarūpiṇīm \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Thinking thus, Rudra, desirous of carrying out the wish of Śiva (the supreme Brahman) sounded his drum that gave out the divine Nāda.

## \|\| 2.20.7 \|\|

*trailokyāmānaśe tasyā dhvanirutsāhakārakaḥ \|*  
*āhvānagatisaṃyukto vicitraḥ sāṃdraśabdakaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Its resonant, reverberating sound pervaded the three worlds heightening enthusiasm and called upon everyone in diverse ways.

## \|\| 2.20.8 \|\|

*tacchrutvā viṣṇubrahmādyāḥ surāśca munayastathā \|*  
*āgamā nigamāmūrtāssiddhā jagmuśca tatra vai \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. On hearing that, Viṣṇu, Brahmā and other deities, sages, the persons well-versed in Āgamas, Nigamas and Siddhas.

## \|\| 2.20.9 \|\|

*surāsurādyāssakalāstatra jagmuśca sotsavāḥ \|*  
*sarve'pi pramathā jagmuryatra kutrāpi saṃsthitāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Devas and Asuras came there with great delight. The Pramathas too reached that place from different quarters.

## \|\| 2.20.10 \|\|

*gaṇapāśca mahābhāgāssarvaloka namaskṛtāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ saṃkhyāmahaṃ vacmi sāvadhānatayā śṛṇu \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The leaders of Gaṇas revered by the whole world and of high fortune arrived there. I shall mention to you their number. Listen attentively.

## \|\| 2.20.11 \|\|

*abhyayācchaṃkhakarṇaśca gaṇakoṭyā gaṇeśvaraḥ \|*  
*daśabhiḥ kekarākṣaśca vikṛto'ṣṭābhireva ca \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The leader of the Gaṇas, Śaṅkhakarṇa came there with a crore of his Gaṇas; Kekarākṣa with ten crores and Vikṛta with eight crores.

## \|\| 2.20.12 \|\|

*catuḥṣaṣṭyā viśākhaśca navabhiḥ pāriyātrakaḥ \|*  
*ṣaḍbhiḥ sarvāntakaḥ śrīmāndundubho'ṣṭābhireva ca \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Viśākha with sixty-four crores; Pāriyātraka with nine crores, Sarvāntaka with six crores and the glorious Dunduma with eight crores.

## \|\| 2.20.13 \|\|

*jālaṃko hi dvādaśabhiḥ koṭibhirgaṇapuṃgavaḥ \|*  
*saptabhissamadaḥ śrīmāṃstathaiva vikṛtānanaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Jālaṅka, the chief leader of Gaṇas, with twelve crores; the glorious Madana and Vikṛtānana with seven crores each.

## \|\| 2.20.14 \|\|

*paṃcabhiśca kapālī hi ṣaḍbhiḥ sandārakaśśubhaḥ \|*  
*koṭikoṭibhireveha kaṇḍukaḥ kuṇḍakastathā \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Kapālin with five crores, the auspicious Sandāraka with six crores and Kaṇḍuka and Kuṇḍaka each with a crore.

## \|\| 2.20.15-16 \|\|

*viṣṭaṃbho'ṣṭābhiragamadaṣṭabhiścandratāpanaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*mahākeśassahasreṇa koṭīnāṃ gaṇapo vṛtaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. Viṣṭambha and Candratāpana each with eight crores, the leader of Gaṇas Mahākeśa with a thousand crores.

I 7. Kuṇḍin, Vāha and the auspicious Parvataka with twelve crores each, Kāla, Kālaka and Mahākāla each with a hundred crores.

## \|\| 2.20.18 \|\|

*agnikaśśatakoṭyā vai koṭyābhimukha eva ca \|*  
*ādityamūrddhā koṭyā ca tathā caiva dhanāvahaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Agnika with a hundred crores, Abhimukha with a crore, Ādityamūrdhā and Dhanāvaha each with a crore.

## \|\| 2.20.19 \|\|

*sannāhaśca śatenaiva kumudaḥ koṭibhistathā \|*  
*amoghaḥ kokilaścaiva koṭikoṭyā sumaṃtrakaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Sannāha and Kumuda with a hundred crores, Amogha, Kokila and Sumantraka each with a crore.

## \|\| 2.20.20 \|\|

*kākapādo'paraḥ ṣaṣṭyā ṣaṣṭyā saṃtānakaḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*mahābalaśca navabhirmadhu piṃgaśca piṃgalaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Another (leader of Gaṇas) Kākapāda with six crores and the lord Santānaka with six crores, Mahābala, Madhupiṅga and Piṅgala each with nine crores.

## \|\| 2.20.21 \|\|

*nīlo navatyā deveśaṃ pūrṇabhadrastathaiva ca \|*  
*koṭīnāṃ caiva saptānāṃ caturvaktro mahābalaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Nīla, Deveśa and Pūrṇabhadra each with ninety crores and the strong Caturvaktra with seven crores.

## \|\| 2.20.22 \|\|

*koṭikoṭisahasrāṇāṃ śatairviṃśatibhirvṛtaḥ \|*  
*tatrājagāma sarveśaḥ kailāsagamanāya vai \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The lord of all (Śiva) reached there ready to go to Kailāsa surrounded by groups of crores, thousands, hundreds and twenties.

## \|\| 2.20.23 \|\|

*kāṣṭhāgūḍhaścatuṣṣaṣṭyā sukeśo vṛṣabhastathā \|*  
*koṭibhissaptabhiścaitro nakulīśastvayaṃ prabhuḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Kāṣṭhāgūḍha, Sukeśa and Vṛṣabha each with sixty-four crores. Caitra, Nakulīśa and Svayamprabhu each with seven crores.

## \|\| 2.20.24-25 \|\|

*lokāṃtakaśca dīptātmā tathā daityāṃtakaḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*devo bhṛṃgī riṭiḥ śrīmāndevadevapriyastathā \|\| 24 \|\|*

*aśanirbhānukaścaiva catuṣṣaṣṭyā sanātanaḥ \|*  
*naṃdīśvaro gaṇādhīśaḥ śatakoṭyā mahābalaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. Lokāntaka, Dīptātmā and the lord Daityāntaka, lord Bhṛṅgīriṭi and the glorious Devadevapriya, Aśani, Bhānuka and Sanātana each with sixty-four crores; Nandīśvara the supreme chief of Gaṇas, and Mahābala each with hundred crores.

## \|\| 2.20.26 \|\|

*ete cānye ca gaṇapā asaṃkhyātā mahābalaḥ \|*  
*sarve sahasrahastāśca jaṭāmukuṭadhāriṇaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. These and other leaders of Gaṇas were all powerful and innumerable. They had thousand hands, matted hair, crown etc.

## \|\| 2.20.27 \|\|

*sarve caṃdrāvataṃsāśca nīlakaṇṭhāstrilocanāḥ \|*  
*hārakuṇḍalakeyūramukuṭādyairalaṃkṛtāḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. They had crescent moon as their embellishing decoration; they were blue-necked, three-eyed, adorned with necklaces, earings, crowns and other ornaments.

## \|\| 2.20.28 \|\|

*brahmendraviṣṇusaṃkāśā aṇimādi gaṇairvṛtāḥ \|*  
*sūryakoṭipratīkāśāstatrājagmurgaṇeśvarāḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Lord of Gaṇas emulating Brahmā, Indra and Viṣṇu and shining with the brilliance of crores of suns and possessed of Aṇimā etc. reached there.

## \|\| 2.20.29 \|\|

*ete gaṇādhipāścānye mahānmāno'malaprabhāḥ \|*  
*jagmustatra mahāprītyā śivadarśanalālasāḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. The Gaṇa chiefs and other noble souls of spotless splendour eagerly reached there desirous of seeing Śiva.

## \|\| 2.20.30 \|\|

*gatvā tatra śivaṃ dṛṣṭvā natvā cakruḥ parāṃ nutim \|*  
*sarve sāñjalayo viṣṇupramukhā natamastakāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Reaching the spot they saw Śiva, bowed to and eulogised him. Viṣṇu and others bent their heads and joined their palms in reverence.

## \|\| 2.20.31 \|\|

*iti viṣṇvādibhissārddhaṃ maheśaḥ parameśvaraḥ \|*  
*kailāsamagamatprītyā kuberasya mahātmanaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Then Lord Śiva, Viṣṇu and others, went to Kailāsa, the residence of Kubera lovingly.

## \|\| 2.20.32 \|\|

*kuberopyāgataṃ śaṃbhuṃ pūjayāmāsa sādaram \|*  
*bhaktyā nānopahāraiśca parivārasamanvitaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Kubera and his attendants received the distinguished guest with great respect and worshipped him with devotion offering him various presents.

## \|\| 2.20.33 \|\|

*tato viṣṇvādikāndevāngaṇāṃścānyānapi dhruvam \|*  
*śivānugānsamānarca śivatoṣaṇahetave \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. In order to please Śiva, he worshipped Viṣṇu and other Devas, the Gaṇas and the followers of Siva.

## \|\| 2.20.34 \|\|

*atha śambhustamāliṃgya kuberaṃ prītamānasaḥ \|*  
*mūrdhniṃ cāghrāya saṃtasthāvalakāṃ nikaṣākhilaiḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Śiva was highly delighted and He embraced Kubera and kissed him on the head. With all his followers He stayed near Alakā.

## \|\| 2.20.35 \|\|

*śaśāsa viśvakarmāṇaṃ nirmāṇārthaṃ girau prabhuḥ \|*  
*nānābhaktairnivāsāya svapareṣāṃ yathocitam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. The lord commanded Viśvakarmā to erect buildings on the mountain for His own residence and that of his devotees and others suitably.

## \|\| 2.20.36 \|\|

*viśvakarmā tato gatvā tatra nānāvidhāṃ mune \|*  
*racanāṃ racayāmāsa drutaṃ śambhoranujñayā \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. At the bidding of Śiva, O sage, Viśvakarmā immediately reached the spot and made all suitable arrangements.

## \|\| 2.20.37-38 \|\|

*atha śambhuḥ pramudito hariprārthanayā tadā \|\| 37 \|\|*

*kuberānugrahaṃ kṛtvā yayau kailāsaparvatam \|*  
*sumuhūrte praviśyāsau svasthānaṃ parameśvaraḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

37-38. Then at the request of Viṣṇu, lord Śiva who was highly delighted at the arrangements went to Kailāsa after blessing Kubera and entered his residence in an auspicious hour.

## \|\| 2.20.39 \|\|

*akarodakhilānprītyā sanāthānbhaktavatsalaḥ \|*  
*atha sarve pramuditā viṣṇuprabhṛtayassurāḥ \|*  
*munayaścāpare siddhā abhyaṣiṃcanmudā śivam \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. The lord being favourably disposed to His devotees delighted everyone. Then Viṣṇu and other devas, the sages and the Siddhas celebrated the coronation of Śiva.

## \|\| 2.20.40 \|\|

*samānarcuḥ kramātsarve nānopāyanapāṇayaḥ \|*  
*nīrājanaṃ samākārṣurmahotsavapurassaram \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. With various kinds of presents in their hands they approached him. With very great festivities they performed the rite of waving lights in adoration.

## \|\| 2.20.41 \|\|

*tadāsītsumanovṛṣṭirmaṃgalāyatanā mune \|*  
*suprītā nanṛtustatrāpsaraso gānatatparāḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. O sage, there was an auspicious shower of flowers. The delighted celestial damsels sang and danced in joy.

## \|\| 2.20.42 \|\|

*jayaśabdo namaśśabdastatrāsītsarvasaṃskṛtaḥ \|*  
*tadotsāho mahānāsītsarveṣāṃ sukhavardhanaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Everywhere loud shouts of “victory; victory”, “obeisance, obeisance” were raised. Every one’s enthusiasm was great. Everyone’s happiness was boundless.

## \|\| 2.20.43 \|\|

*sthitvā siṃhāsane śaṃbhurvirājādhikaṃ tadā \|*  
*sarvaissaṃsevito'bhīkṣṇaṃ viṣṇvādyaiśca yathocitam \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Seated in His throne, Śiva then shone all the more. He was duly served by everyone, Lord Viṣṇu and others.

## \|\| 2.20.44 \|\|

*atha sarve surādyāśca tuṣṭuvustaṃ pṛthakpṛthak \|*  
*arthyābhirvāgbhiriṣṭābhiśśakaraṃ lokaśaṃkaram \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. All the devas eulogised Śiva, the benefactor of the world, with words pleasing of nature and pregnant with meaning.

## \|\| 2.20.45 \|\|

*prasannātmā stutiṃ śrutvā teṣāṃ kāmāndadau śivaḥ \|*  
*manobhilaṣitānprītyā varānsarveśvaraḥ prabhuḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. On hearing their hymns of praise Śiva was highly delighted and granted their wishes. He, the lord of all, lovingly fulfilled their cherished desires.

## \|\| 2.20.46-47 \|\|

*śivājñayātha te sarve svaṃsvaṃ dhāma yayurmune \|*  
*prāptakāmāḥ pramuditā ahaṃ ca viṣṇunā saha \|\| 46 \|\|*

*upaveśyāsane viṣṇuṃ māñca śambhuruvāca ha \|*  
*bahu sambodhya suprītyānugṛhya parameśvaraḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

46-47. O sage, at the bidding of Śiva they returned to their abodes. They were highly delighted since their desires were fulfilled. Then lord Śiva asked me and Viṣṇu to sit down. Then He lovingly blessed us and said:—

Śiva said.:—

## \|\| 2.20.48 \|\|

*śiva uvāca \|*  
*he hare he vidhe tātau yuvāṃ priyatarau mama \|*  
*surottamau trijagato'vanasargakarau sadā \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. “Dear Sons, O Viṣṇu, Brahmā, you are great favourites of mine, entrusted with the work of creation and sustenance of the three worlds. You are the best of the Devas.

## \|\| 2.20.49 \|\|

*gacchataṃ nirbhayannityaṃ svasthānaśca madājñayā \|*  
*sukhapradātāhaṃ vai vāmviśeṣātprekṣakassadā \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Go back to your abodes without any fear. I shall always provide you with happiness. I shall particularly look after you both”.

## \|\| 2.20.50 \|\|

*ityākarṇya vacaśśambhossupraṇamya tadājñayā \|*  
*ahaṃ hariśca svaṃ dhāmāgamāva prītamānasau \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. On hearing the words of Śiva, Viṣṇu and I duly bowed to him and though not delighted (in leaving him) returned to our abodes.

## \|\| 2.20.51 \|\|

*tadānīmeva suprītaśśaṃkaro nidhipammudā \|*  
*upaveśya gṛhītvā taṃ kara āha śubhaṃ vacaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. At the same time Śiva delightfully made the lord of treasures sit down and holding his hands with his own said the auspicious words.

## \|\| 2.20.52 \|\|

*\|\| śiva uvāca \|*  
*tava premṇā vaśībhūto mitratāgamanaṃ sakhe \|*  
*svasthānaṅgaccha vibhayassahāyohaṃ sadānagha \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Dear friend, I am charmed by your love. I have become your friend. Go to your place fearlessly. O sincere friend, I shall always assist you.

## \|\| 2.20.53 \|\|

*ityākarṇya vacaśśambhoḥ kuberaḥ prītamānasaḥ \|*  
*tadājñayā svakaṃ dhāma jagāma pramudānvitaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. On hearing these words of Śiva, Kubera was highly delighted. At His bidding he returned to his abode.

## \|\| 2.20.54 \|\|

*sa uvāca girau śambhuḥ kailāse parvatottame \|*  
*sagaṇo yoganiratassvacchando dhyāna tatparaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Śiva stayed on Kailāsa, the best of all mountains, along with his Gaṇas, practising Yoga and meditation at his own sweet will.

## \|\| 2.20.55 \|\|

*kvaciddadhyau svamātmānaṃ kvacidyogarato'bhavat \|*  
*itihāsagaṇānprītyāvādītsvacchandamānasaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. In some places he meditated upon his own soul. In some places he practised Yoga. At times, of his own accord, he gave discourses on ancient historical tales.

## \|\| 2.20.56 \|\|

*kvacitkailāsa kudharasusthāneṣu maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*vijahāra gaṇaiḥ prītyā vividheṣu vihāravit \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. He, being an expert in divine sports, sported with his Gaṇas in the different regions of the Kailāsa hill.

## \|\| 2.20.57 \|\|

*itthaṃ rudrasvarūpo'sau śaṃkaraḥ parameśvaraḥ \|*  
*akārṣītsvagirau līlā nānā yogivaro'pi yaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Thus lord Śiva who had assumed the form of Rudra performed divine sports on the mount Kailāsa though he was foremost among Yogins.

## \|\| 2.20.58 \|\|

*nītvā kālaṃ kiyantaṃ so'patnīkaḥ parameśvaraḥ \|*  
*paścādavāpa svāmpatnīndakṣapatnīsamudbhavām \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Thus lord Śiva spent some time without his divine consort. After some time He married Satī, the daughter of Dakṣa Prajāpati.

## \|\| 2.20.59 \|\|

*vijahāra tayā satyā dakṣaputryā maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*sukhī babhūva devarṣe lokācāraparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Lord Śiva sported with her. Following the conventions of the world, O celestial sage, he became happy.

## \|\| 2.20.60 \|\|

*itthaṃ rudrāvatāraste varṇito'yaṃ munīśvara \|*  
*kailāsāgamanañcāsya sakhitvānnidhipasya hi \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. O sage, thus I have explained to you the manifestation of Śiva in the form of Rudra, his arrival at Kailāsa and his friendship of Kubera, the lord of treasures.

## \|\| 2.20.61 \|\|

*tadantargatalīlāpi varṇitā jñānavardhinī \|*  
*ihāmutra ca yā nityaṃ sarvakāmaphalapradā \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Thus I have explained the inner sport also which increases perfect knowledge and which confers the fulfilment of desires here and hereafter.

## \|\| 2.20.62 \|\|

*imāṃ kathāmpaṭhedyastu śṛṇuyādvā samāhitaḥ \|*  
*iha bhuktiṃ samāsādya labhenmuktimparatra saḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. He who reads or listens to this story attentively will enjoy all worldly pleasures here and attain salvation hearafter.

## Section 3 - Rudra-saṃhitā (2): Satī-khaṇḍa

## Chapter 1 - Summary of Satī’s life

## \|\| 3.1.1 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*vidhe sarvaṃ vijānāsi kṛpayā śaṃkarasya ca \|*  
*tvayādbhutā hi kathitāḥ kathā me śivayośśubhāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Nārada said:—

1\. O Brahmā, thanks to Śiva’s favour, you know everything. You have narrated to me the wonderful stories of Śiva and Pārvatī.

## \|\| 3.1.2 \|\|

*tvanmukhāṃbhojasaṃvṛttāṃ śrutvā śivakathāṃ parām \|*  
*atṛpto hi punastāṃ vai śrotumicchāmyahaṃ prabho \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. O lord, I am never fully satiated by hearing the great story of Śiva from your lotus-like face. I wish to hear further the same.

## \|\| 3.1.3-7 \|\|

*pūrṇāṃśaśśaṃkarasyaiva yo rudro varṇitaḥ purā \|*  
*vidhe tvayā maheśānaḥ kailāsanilayo vaśī \|\| 3 \|\|*

*sa yogī sarvaviṣṇvādisurase vyassatāṃ gatiḥ \|*  
*nirdvaṃdvaḥ krīḍati sadā nirvikārī mahāprabhuḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*so'bhūtpunargṛhasthaśca vivāhya paramāṃ striyam \|*  
*hariprārthanayā prītyā maṃgalāṃ svatapasvinīm \|\| 5 \|\|*

*prathamaṃ dakṣaputrī sā paścātsā parvatātmajā \|*  
*kathamekaśarīreṇa dvayorapyātmajā matā \|\| 6 \|\|*

*kathaṃ satī pārvatī sā punaśśivamupāgatā \|*  
*etatsarvaṃ tathānyacca brahman gaditumarhasi \|\| 7 \|\|*

3-7. As explained by you, Rudra is the complete manifestation of Śiva. He is the great Lord whose abode is Kailāsa. He is a yogin of perfect control. He is worthy of being propitiated by all devas, Viṣṇu and others. He is the final goal of all good men. He is free from Dvandvas (mutually clashing opposites). The great lord never undergoes any change yet indulges in His divine sports. He became a householder again after marrying the noble lady Maṅgalā at the request of Viṣṇu when she performed penance. At first she was born of Dakṣa and later of Himālaya. How could she be the daughter of both with the same body? How did Satī become Pārvatī and attain Śiva again? O Brahmā, please explain all these and other points relating to His episode.

## \|\| 3.1.8 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*iti tasya vacaḥ śrutvā surarṣeḥ śaṃkarātmanaḥ \|*  
*prasannamānaso bhūtvā brahmā vacanamabravīt \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. On hearing these words of the celestial sage devoted to Śiva, Brahmā became delighted and said again.

## \|\| 3.1.9 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*śṛṇu tāta muniśreṣṭha kathayāmi kathāṃ śubhām \|*  
*yāṃ śrutvā saphalaṃ janma bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

9\. O best of sages, dear one, listen. I shall narrate the auspicious story on hearing which undoubtedly the life will become fruitful.

## \|\| 3.1.10 \|\|

*purāhaṃ svasutāṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃdhyāhvāṃ tanayaissaha \|*  
*abhavaṃ vikṛtastāta kāmabāṇaprapīḍitaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Formerly, on seeing my daughter Sandhyā in the company of my sons I was afflicted by the arrows of the cupid and much upset.

## \|\| 3.1.11 \|\|

*dharmaḥ smṛtastadā rudro mahāyogī paraḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*dhikkṛtya māṃ sutaistāta svasthānaṃ gatavānayam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. When remembered by Dharma, Rudra, the highest lord and the greatest yogin came there. He reproached me as well as my sons and went back to His abode.

## \|\| 3.1.12 \|\|

*yanmāyāmohitaścāhaṃ vedavaktā ca mūḍhadhīḥ \|*  
*tenākārṣaṃ sahākārya parameśena śaṃbhunā \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. A serious offence was committed by me against Śiva the great lord, by whose Māyā I was subjected to great delusion despite my being the reciter of the Vedas.

## \|\| 3.1.13 \|\|

*tadīrṣayāhamākārṣaṃ bahūpāyānsutaiḥ saha \|*  
*kartuṃ tanmohanaṃ mūḍhaḥ śivamāyā vimohitaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Under great delusion and goaded by the envious feelings towards the lord I conspired with my sons to find out ways and means to delude the lord Himself. Here again I was deluded by Śiva’s Māyā..

## \|\| 3.1.14 \|\|

*abhavaṃste'tha vai sarve tasmiñ śaṃbho paraprabho \|*  
*upāyā niṣphalāsteṣāṃ mama cāpi munīśvara \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. O great sage, in Śiva the great lord, all those ways and means pursued by me and my sons became ineffective.

## \|\| 3.1.15 \|\|

*tadā'smaraṃ rameśānaṃ vyathopāyastutaissaha \|*  
*abodhayatsa āgatya śivabhaktiratassudhīḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. When my strategy failed I remembered the lord of Lakṣmī (Viṣṇu) in the company of my sons. The intelligent lord (Viṣṇu) devoted to Śiva came there and advised me.

## \|\| 3.1.16 \|\|

*prabodhito rameśena śivatattvapradarśinā \|*  
*tadīrṣāmatyajaṃ sohaṃ taṃ haṭhaṃ na vimohitaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Instructed by Viṣṇu who demonstrated Śiva’s principles, I cast off my envy no doubt, but since I still was under delusion I did not eschew my stubbornness.

## \|\| 3.1.17 \|\|

*śaktiṃ saṃsevya tatprītyotpādayāmāsa tāṃ tadā \|*  
*dakṣādaśiknyāṃ vīriṇyāṃ svaputrāddharamohane \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. I humbly served Śakti and when she was pleased I created her as the daughter of Dakṣa and Asiknī (Dakṣa’s wife). Dakṣa, you remember, was my son. This was my endeavour to make Hara enamoured of her.

## \|\| 3.1.18 \|\|

*somā bhūtvā dakṣasutā tapaḥ kṛtvā tu dussaham \|*  
*rudrapatnyabhavadbhaktyā svabhaktahitakāriṇī \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The goddess Umā became Dakṣa’s daughter, performed a severe penance and thanks to her great devotion became Rudra’s wife. The goddess indeed is a benefactress of her devotees.

## \|\| 3.1.19 \|\|

*somo rudro gṛhī bhūtvā'kārṣīllīlāṃ parāṃ prabhuḥ \|*  
*mohayitvātha māṃ tatra svavivāhe'vikāradhīḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. In the company of Umā, Rudra became a householder and the great lord performed divine sports. He of undecaying intellect deluded me even at the time of his marriage.

## \|\| 3.1.20 \|\|

*vivāhya tāṃ sa āgatya svagirau sūtikṛttayā \|*  
*reme bahuvimoho hi svataṃtrassvāttavigrahaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. The independent lord assuming his own body married her and returned to his mountain. In her company he sported much, deluding many.

## \|\| 3.1.21 \|\|

*tayā viharatastasya vyātīyāya mahān mune \|*  
*kālassukhakaraśśabhornirvikārasya sadrateḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. O sage, much time was happily spent by Śiva free from all depraved feelings and indulging in noble dalliance with her.

## \|\| 3.1.22-23 \|\|

*tato rudrasya dakṣeṇa sparddhā jātā nijecchayā \|*  
*mahāmūḍhasya tanmāyāmohitasya sugarviṇaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*tatprabhāvāddharaṃ dakṣo mahāgarvī vimūḍhadhīḥ \|*  
*mahāśāṃtaṃ nirvikāraṃ nini da bahumohitaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. Then a feeling of rivalry arose between Dakṣa and Rudra; Dakṣa was excessively deluded by Śiva’s illusion and so becoming extremely haughty he censured the quiet Śiva who was free from all depraved feelings.

## \|\| 3.1.24 \|\|

*tato dakṣaḥ svayaṃ yajñaṃ kṛtavāngarvito'haram \|*  
*sarvānāhūya devādīn viṣṇuṃ māṃ cākhilādhipaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Then Dakṣa the haughty, performed a sacrifice without Śiva, although he had invited Viṣṇu, me and all other devas.

## \|\| 3.1.25 \|\|

*nājuhāva tathābhūto rudraṃ roṣasamākulaḥ \|*  
*tathā tatra satīṃ nāmnā svaputrīṃ vidhimohitaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Since he was in delusion he was very furious. So he did not invite Rudra and his own daughter Satī. He was greatly deluded by his own fate.

## \|\| 3.1.26 \|\|

*yadā nākāritā pitrā māyāmohita cetasā \|*  
*līlāṃ cakāra sujñānā mahāsādhvī śivā tadā \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. When she was not invited by her father whose mind was deluded by illusion, Śivā (Satī) of perfect knowledge and purest chastity played a divine sport.

## \|\| 3.1.27 \|\|

*athāgatā satī tatra śivājñāmadhigamya sā \|*  
*anāhūtāpi dakṣeṇa garviṇā svapiturgṛham \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Though not invited by her haughty father she did go to her father’s house securing the reluctant permission of Śiva.

## \|\| 3.1.28 \|\|

*vilokya rudrabhāgaṃ no prāpyāvajñāṃ ca tātataḥ \|*  
*viniṃdya tatra tānsarvāndehatyāgamathākarot \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Seeing no share of Rudra set apart and being slighted by her father, she reproached all those who were present there and cast off her body.

## \|\| 3.1.29 \|\|

*tacchutvā deva deveśaḥ krodhaṃ kṛtvā tu dussaham \|*  
*jaṭāmutkṛtya mahatīṃ vīrabhadramajījanat \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. On hearing that, lord Śiva became unbearably furious and pulling at his matted hair he created Vīrabhadra.

## \|\| 3.1.30 \|\|

*sagaṇaṃ taṃ samutpādya kiṃ kuryyā miti vādinam \|*  
*sarvāpamānapūrvaṃ hi yajñadhvaṃsaṃ dideśa ha \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. When he was created along with attendants he began asking “What shall I do?”. The entire annihilation of Dakṣa’s sacrifice and the disgrace of every one present there was the order issued by Śiva.

## \|\| 3.1.31 \|\|

*tadājñāṃ prāpya sa gaṇādhīśo bahubalānvitaḥ \|*  
*gato'raṃ tatra sahasā mahābalaparākramaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. The lord of the Gaṇas (Vīrabhadra) accompanied by his soldiers reached the place immediately after receiving the orders.

## \|\| 3.1.32 \|\|

*mahopadravamācerurgaṇāstatra tadājñayā \|*  
*sarvānsa daṃḍayāmāsa na kaścidavaśeṣitaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. They worked a great havoc there. Vīrabhadra chastised everyone and spared none.

## \|\| 3.1.33 \|\|

*viṣṇuṃ saṃjitya yatnena sāmaraṃ gaṇasattamaḥ \|*  
*cakre dakṣaśiraśchedaṃ tacchirognau juhāva ca \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. After defeating Viṣṇu and the Devas with strenuous effort, the chief of Gaṇas cut off the head of Dakṣa and consigned it to the sacrificial fire.

## \|\| 3.1.34 \|\|

*yajñadhvaṃsaṃ cakārāśu mahopadravamācaran \|*  
*tato jagāma svagiriṃ praṇanāma prabhuṃ śivam \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Working great havoc he destroyed the sacrifice. Then he came back to the mountain and bowed to Lord Śiva.

## \|\| 3.1.35 \|\|

*yajñadhvaṃso'bhavaccetthaṃ devaloke hi paśyati \|*  
*rudrasyānucaraistatra vīrabhadrādibhiḥ kṛtaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Even as the whole of the world of Devas was witnessing, the process of destruction of the sacrifice was carried out by Vīrabhadra and others, the followers of Rudra.

## \|\| 3.1.36 \|\|

*mune nītiriyaṃ jñeyā śrutismṛtiṣu saṃmatā \|*  
*rudre ruṣṭe kathaṃ loke sukhaṃ bhavati suprabho \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. The policy in agreement with what is laid down in the Vedas and Smṛtis is this, O Sage, which you must note. When lord Rudra is angry, how can there be happiness in the world?

## \|\| 3.1.37 \|\|

*tato rudraḥ prasannobhūtstutimākarṇya tāṃ parām \|*  
*vijñaptiṃ saphalāṃ cakre sarveṣāṃ dīnavatsalaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. On hearing his song of praise Rudra relented. Favourably disposed to the miserable that he was, he granted their request.

## \|\| 3.1.38 \|\|

*pūrvavacca kṛtaṃ tena kṛpālutvaṃ mahātmanā \|*  
*śaṃkareṇa maheśena nānālīlāvi hāriṇā \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Śiva, the great lord, indulging in different sorts of divine sports, became sympathetic and merciful as before.

## \|\| 3.1.39 \|\|

*jīvitastena dakṣo hi tatra sarve hi satkṛtāḥ \|*  
*punassa kārito yajñaḥ śaṃkareṇa kṛpālunā \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Dakṣa was resuscitated. The whole sacrifice was renewed under the instruction of the merciful Lord Śiva. All those present were honoured in due manner.

## \|\| 3.1.40 \|\|

*rudraśca pūjitastatra sarvairdevairviśeṣataḥ \|*  
*yajñe viśvādibhirbhaktyā suprasannātmabhirvane \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. O sage, in that sacrifice Rudra was honoured by all the Gods with due devotion. They were highly delighted.

## \|\| 3.1.41 \|\|

*satīdehasamutpannā jvālā lokasukhāvahā \|*  
*patitā parvate tatra pūjitā sukhadāyinī \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. The flame of fire arising from the body of Satī and delighting the whole world fell on that mountain and it was duly worshipped.

## \|\| 3.1.42 \|\|

*jvālāmukhīti vikhyātā sarvakāmaphalapradā \|*  
*babhūva paramā devī darśanātpāpahāriṇī \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. The deity became famous as Jvālāmukhī yielding fruits of cherished desires. Even her very vision quells all sins.

## \|\| 3.1.43 \|\|

*idānīṃ pūjyate loke sarvakāmaphalāptaye \|*  
*saṃvidhābhiranekābhirmahotsavaparasparam \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Even now she is worshipped with due festivities for the acquisition of all desires, observing all stipulated modes of procedure.

## \|\| 3.1.44 \|\|

*tataśca sā satī devī himālayasutā 'bhavat \|*  
*tasyāśca pārvatīnāma prasiddhamabhavattadā \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. The Goddess Satī became the daughter of Himālaya. As such she became famous as Pārvatī.

## \|\| 3.1.45 \|\|

*sā punaśca samārādhya tapasā kaṭhinena vai \|*  
*tameva parameśānaṃ bharttāraṃ samupāśritā \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. She propitiated lord Śiva with a rigorous penance and attained him as her husband.

## \|\| 3.1.46 \|\|

*etatsarvaṃ samākhyātaṃ yatpṛṣṭohaṃ munīśvara \|*  
*yacchrutvā sarvapāpebhyo mucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. O great sage, I have narrated to you all that you asked me. Whoever hears this narrative will no doubt be freed from all sins.

## Chapter 2 - The appearance of Cupid (Kāma)

## \|\| 3.2.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya vacastasya nemiṣāraṇyavāsinaḥ \|*  
*papraccha ca muniśreṣṭhaḥ kathāṃ pāpapraṇāśinīm \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sūta said:—

1\. O residents of Naimiṣa forest, after hearing his words, the excellent sage further requested him for more such stories that quell sins.

## \|\| 3.2.2 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*vidhevidhe mahā bhāga kathāṃ śaṃbhośśubhāvahām \|*  
*śṛṇvan bhavanmukhāṃbhojānna tṛptosmi mahāprabho \|\| 2 \|\|*

Nārada said:—

2\. O Brahmā, O great lord, though continuously hearing the auspicious story of Śiva from your lotus-face I am never satiated.

## \|\| 3.2.3 \|\|

*ataḥ kathaya tatsarvaṃ śivasya caritaṃ śubham \|*  
*satīkīrtyanvitaṃ divyaṃ śrotumicchāmi viśvakṛt \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Please further narrate the auspicious story of Śiva entirely. I wish to hear that story in which Satī is glorified, O Brahman.

## \|\| 3.2.4 \|\|

*satī hi kathamutpannā dakṣadāreṣu śobhanā \|*  
*kathaṃ haro manaścakre dārāharaṇakarmaṇi \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. How was the auspicious Satī born of Dakṣa’s wife? How did Śiva become inclined to marry her?

## \|\| 3.2.5 \|\|

*kathaṃ vā dakṣakopena tyaktadehā satī purā \|*  
*himavattanayā jātā bhūyo vākāśamāgatā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. How did she cast off her body formerly, due to her rage with Dakṣa? How was she born as the daughter of Himālaya and how did she reach heaven again?

## \|\| 3.2.6 \|\|

*pārvatyāśca tapo'tyugraṃ vivāhaśca kathaṃ tvabhūt \|*  
*kathamarddhaśarīrasthā babhūva smaranāśinaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. How was her rigorous penance performed? How was her marriage celebrated? How did she happen to share half the body of Siva.

## \|\| 3.2.7 \|\|

*etatsarvaṃ samācakṣva vistareṇa mahāmate \|*  
*nānyosti saṃśayacchettā tvatsamo na bhaviṣyati \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Please explain all these points in detail, O intelligent one. There is none else to remove my doubts and none shall ever be like you.

## \|\| 3.2.8 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*śṛṇu tvaṃ ca mune sarvaṃ satīśivayaśaśśubham \|*  
*pāvanaṃ paramaṃ divyaṃ guhyādguhyatamaṃ param \|\| 8 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

8\. O sage, listen to the auspicious glory of Satī and Śiva entirely. It is extremely sanctifying, divine and the greatest secret of all secrets.

## \|\| 3.2.9 \|\|

*etacchaṃbhuḥ purovāca bhaktavaryāya viṣṇave \|*  
*pṛṣṭastena mahābhaktyā paropakṛtaye mune \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. O sage, Śiva himself narrated this formerly to Viṣṇu, the greatest of devotees for helping others, when requested by him.

## \|\| 3.2.10 \|\|

*tatassopi mayā pṛṣṭo viṣṇuśśaivavarassudhīḥ \|*  
*prītyā mahyaṃ samācakhyau vistarānmunisattama \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Viṣṇu, the intelligent and the greatest of Śiva’s devotees was asked by me and O great sage, he told me everything lovingly.

## \|\| 3.2.11 \|\|

*ahaṃ tatkathayiṣyāmi kathāmetāṃ purātanīm \|*  
*śivāśivayaśoyuktāṃ sarvakāmaphalapradām \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Therefore I shall narrate this ancient story that confers the fulfilment of all desires since it glorifies Satī and Śiva.

## \|\| 3.2.12 \|\|

*purā yadā śivo devo nirguṇo nirvikalpakaḥ \|*  
*arūpaśśaktirahitaścinmātrassadasatparaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Originally when Śiva was separated from Śakti and was pure consciousness alone, He was attributeless, free from alternatives, devoid of forms and beyond the existent and non-existent.

## \|\| 3.2.13 \|\|

*abhavatsaguṇassopi dvirūpaśśaktimānprabhuḥ \|*  
*somo divyākṛtirvipra nirvi kārī parātparaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. He, the greatest of the great and of changeless form when united with Śakti, was filled with attributes and had specific forms and divine features. O brahmin, He was accompanied by Umā.

## \|\| 3.2.14 \|\|

*tasya vāmāṃgajo viṣṇurbrahmāhaṃ dakṣiṇāṃgajaḥ \|*  
*rudro hṛdayato jāto'bhavacca munisattama \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Viṣṇu was born of His left and I, Brahmā, of his right side, O great sage, Rudra was born of his heart.

## \|\| 3.2.15 \|\|

*sṛṣṭikartābhavaṃ brahmā viṣṇuḥ pālanakārakaḥ \|*  
*layakartā svayaṃ rudrastridhābhūtassadāśivaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. I became the creator (Brahmā); Viṣṇu the cause of sustenance; Rudra the author of dissolution. Thus Sadāśiva, manifested himself in three forms.

## \|\| 3.2.16 \|\|

*tamevāhaṃ samārādhya brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ \|*  
*prajā sasarja sarvāstāssurāsuranarādikāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. It was after worshipping Him that I, Brahmā, the grand-father of all the worlds, began the creation of all subjects including Devas, Asuras, human beings etc.

## \|\| 3.2.17 \|\|

*sṛṣṭvā prajāpatīn dakṣapramukhānsurasattamān \|*  
*amanyaṃ suprasannohaṃ nijaṃ sarvamahonnatam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. After creating the guardians of the subjects, Prajāpatis, Dakṣa and other Devas, I considered myself loftier than others and was delighted.

## \|\| 3.2.18-19 \|\|

*marīcimatriṃ pulahaṃ pulastyāṃgirasau kratum \|*  
*vasiṣṭhaṃ nāradaṃ dakṣaṃ bhṛguṃ ceti mahāprabhūn \|\| 18 \|\|*

*brahmāhaṃ mānasānputrānasarjaṃ ca yadā mune \|*  
*tadā manmanaso jātā cārurūpā varāṃganā \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. O sage, when I created Marīci, Atri, Pulaha, Pulastya, Aṅgiras, Kratu, Vasiṣṭha, Nārada, Dakṣa and Bhṛgu, my mental sons of lordly stature, a beautiful woman of handsome features was born of my mind.

## \|\| 3.2.20 \|\|

*nāmnā saṃdhyā divakṣāṃtā sāyaṃ saṃdhyā japaṃtikā \|*  
*atīva sundarī subhrūrmunicetovimohinī \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. She was variously called Sandhyā, Divakṣāntā, Sāyaṃ Sandhyā and Jayantikā, She was very beautiful with finely-shaped eyebrows capable of captivating the minds of even sages.

## \|\| 3.2.21 \|\|

*na tādṛśī devaloke na martye na rasātale \|*  
*kālatrayepi vai nārī sampūrṇaguṇaśālinī \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Neither in human world nor in that of the Devas was there such a woman of complete perfection in all qualities. Nor was there such a woman in nether worlds in all the three times (past, present and future).

## \|\| 3.2.22 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvāhaṃ tāṃ samutthāya cintayanhṛdi hṛdgatam \|*  
*dakṣādayaśca sraṣṭāro marīcyādyāśca matsutāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. On seeing her I involuntarily got up. Various thoughts rose. up in my heart. Dakṣa and others—the Prajāpatis, Marīci and others—all my sons, felt similarly.

## \|\| 3.2.23 \|\|

*evaṃ ciṃtayato me hi brahmaṇo munisattama \|*  
*mānasaḥ puruṣo maṃjurāvirbhūto mahādbhutaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. O best of sages, when I Brahmā, thought like this, a wonderfully Beautiful Being appeared as my mental creation.

## \|\| 3.2.24-29 \|\|

*kāṃcanīkṛtajātābhaḥ pīnoraskassunāsikaḥ \|*  
*suvṛttorukaṭījaṃgho nīlavelitakesaraḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*lagnabhrūyugalo lolaḥ pūrṇacandranibhānanaḥ \|*  
*kapāṭāyatasadvakṣo romarājīvarājitaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*abhramātaṃgakākāraḥ pīno nīlasuvāsakaḥ \|*  
*āraktapāṇinayanamukhapādakarodbhavaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*kṣīṇamadhyaścārudantaḥ pramattagajagaṃdhanaḥ \|*  
*praphullapadmapatrākṣaḥ kesaraghrāṇatarpaṇaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*kaṃbugrīvo mīnaketuḥ prāṃśurmakaravāhanaḥ \|*  
*paṃcapuṣpāyudho vegī puṣpakodaṃḍamaṃḍitaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*kāṃtaḥ kaṭākṣapātena bhrāmayannayanadvayam \|*  
*sugaṃdhimāruto tāta śṛṃgārarasasevitaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

24-29. He had a golden complexion. His chest was stout and firm. His nose was fine. His thigh, hips and calves were round and plump. He had blue wavelets of hair. His eyebrows were thickset and tremulous. His face shone like the full moon. His hairy chest was broad like a door. He was as huge as the celestial elephant Airāvata. He was wearing a blue cloth. His hands, eyes, face, legs and fingers were red in colour. He had a slender waist. His teeth were fine. He smelt like an elephant in its rut. His eyes were like the petals of a full-bown lotus. He was fragrant like the filaments. His neck was like the conch. He had the emblem of a fish. He was tall. He had the Makara fish for his vehicle. He was armed with a bow and five flowers for his arrows. His loving glance was very attractive as he rolled his eyes here and there. O dear one, his very breath was a fragrant wind. He was accompanied by the sentiment of love.

## \|\| 3.2.30 \|\|

*taṃ vīkṣya puruṣaṃ sarve dakṣādyā matsutāśca te \|*  
*autsukyaṃ paramaṃ jagmurvismayāviṣṭamānasāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. On seeing that Being, my sons, Dakṣa and others, were struck with wonder and became eager and inquisitive.

## \|\| 3.2.31 \|\|

*abhavadvikṛtaṃ teṣāṃ matsutānāṃ mano drutam \|*  
*dhairyaṃ naivālabhattāta kāmākulitacetasām \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Their mind became deformed and confused immediately. Smitten with love they lost their mental courage.

## \|\| 3.2.32 \|\|

*māṃ sopi vedhasaṃ vīkṣya sraṣṭāraṃ jagatāṃ patim \|*  
*praṇamya puruṣaḥ prāha vinayānatakaṃdharaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. On seeing me the creator and the lord of the worlds, the person bowed down with his shoulders stooping by humility and said.

## \|\| 3.2.33-34 \|\|

*puruṣa uvāca \|*  
*kiṃ kariṣyāmyahaṃ karma brahmaṃstatra niyojaya \|*  
*mānyodya puruṣo yasmāducitaḥ śobhito vidhe \|\| 33 \|\|*

*abhimānaṃ ca yogyaṃ ca sthānaṃ patnī ca yā mama \|*  
*tanme vada trilokeśa tvaṃ sraṣṭā jagatāṃ patiḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

The person said:—

33-34. “O Brahmā, what is the work I am to do? Please assign me an honourable task, O Brahmā, suitable to and becoming me, O lord of the three worlds, you are - the creator and hence the lord of all the worlds. Please tell me. What is my honourable and suitable place? Who is going to be my wife?”

## \|\| 3.2.35-36 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*evaṃ tasya vacaḥ śrutvā puruṣasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*kṣaṇaṃ na kiṃcitprāvocatsa sraṣṭā cātivismitaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*ato manassusaṃyamya samyagutsṛjya vismayam \|*  
*avocatpuruṣaṃ brahmā tatkāmaṃ ca samāvahan \|\| 36 \|\|*

Sūta said:—

35-36. On hearing the words of the noble-souled person Kāma, the creator did not say anything for a short while in his surprised predicament. Then steadying his mind and abandoning his surprised look, Brahmā, already a victim of Kāma, spoke to the person thus:—

## \|\| 3.2.37 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*anena tvaṃ svarūpeṇa puṣpabāṇaiśca paṃcabhiḥ \|*  
*mohayan puruṣān strīśca kuru sṛṣṭiṃ sanātanīm \|\| 37 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

37\. In this form and with your five flower-arrows you can enamour and captivate men and women and carry on the eternal task of creation.

## \|\| 3.2.38 \|\|

*asmiñjīvāśca devādyāstrailokye sacarācare \|*  
*ete sarve bhaviṣyanti na kṣamāstyavalaṃbane \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. In this universe consisting of three worlds, mobile and immobile beings, none of the living beings including the Devas will be competent to defy you.

## \|\| 3.2.39 \|\|

*ahaṃ vā vāsudevo vā sthāṇurvā puruṣottamaḥ \|*  
*bhaviṣyāmastava vaśe kimanye prāṇadhārakāḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. O best of beings, not to speak of ordinary living beings even I Brahmā, Vāsudeva and Śiva will be in your control.

## \|\| 3.2.40 \|\|

*pracchannarūpo jaṃtūnāṃ praviśanhṛdayaṃ sadā \|*  
*sukhahetuḥ svayaṃ bhūtvā sṛṣṭiṃ kuru sanātanīm \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Invisibly you enter the hearts of living beings, excite thrilling feelings of pleasure and carry on the activities of creation that is to last for ever.

## \|\| 3.2.41 \|\|

*tvatpuṣpabāṇasya sadā sukhalakṣyaṃ manodbhutam \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ prāṇināṃ nityaṃ sadā madakaro bhavān \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. The minds of all living beings will become an easy target of your five-flower arrows. You will be the cause of their elation.

## \|\| 3.2.42 \|\|

*iti te karma kathitaṃ sṛṣṭiprāvartakaṃ punaḥ \|*  
*nāmānyete vadiṣyaṃti sutā me tava tattvataḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Thus I have assigned you the task of facilitating creation. These sons of mine will confer names and titles on you.

Brahmā said

## \|\| 3.2.43 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityuktvāhaṃ suraśreṣṭha svasutānāṃ mukhāni ca \|*  
*ālokya svāsane pādme propaviṣṭo'bhavaṃ kṣaṇam \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. O best of the celestials, after saying this and casting a meaningful glance at my sons I resumed my lotus-seat immediately.

## Chapter 3 - Kāma is cursed but blessed later

## \|\| 3.3.1 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*tataste munayaḥ sarve tadābhiprāyavedinaḥ \|*  
*cakrustaducitaṃ nāma marīcipramukhāssutāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

1\. Then those sages, my sons—Marīci and others who understood my view, gave him suitable names.

## \|\| 3.3.2 \|\|

*mukhāvalokanādeva jñātvā vṛttāṃtamanyataḥ \|*  
*dakṣādayaśca sraṣṭāraḥ sthānaṃ patnīṃ ca te daduḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Dakṣa and others who understood other facts on seeing my face gave him a suitable place and a wife.

## \|\| 3.3.3 \|\|

*tato niścitya nāmāni marīcipramukhā dvijāḥ \|*  
*ūcussaṃgatametasmai puruṣāya mamātmajāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The brahmins Marīci and others, my sons, decided on suitable names for the Being and said thus.

## \|\| 3.3.4 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*yasmātpramathase tattvaṃ jātosmākaṃ yathā vidheḥ \|*  
*tasmānmanmathanāmā tvaṃ loke khyāto bhaviṣyasi \|\| 4 \|\|*

The sages said:—

4\. Since at your nativity itself you have begun to torment and bedevil our minds and that of Brahmā too, you will be famous in the world as Manmatha.

## \|\| 3.3.5 \|\|

*jagatsu kāmarūpastvaṃ tvatsamo na hi vidyate \|*  
*atastvaṃ kāmanāmāpi khyāto bhava manobhava \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. You will be able to assume any form you wish. Hence, O mind-born God, you will be known as Kāma too. There is no one equal to you.

## \|\| 3.3.6 \|\|

*madanānmadanākhyastvaṃ jāto darpātsadarpakaḥ \|*  
*tasmātkaṃdarpanāmāpi loke khyāto bhaviṣyasi \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Causing elation in others you will be known as Madana. Since you were haughty even as you were born you will be Darpaka and your name Kandarpa will also become popular in the world.

## \|\| 3.3.7 \|\|

*tvatsamaṃ sarvadevānāṃ yadvīryaṃ na bhaviṣyati \|*  
*tataḥ sthānāni sarvāṇi sarvavyāpī bhavāṃstataḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The collective power of all the Devas will not be equal to yours. Therefore you will have any station as yours and you will be omnipresent too.

## \|\| 3.3.8 \|\|

*dakṣoyaṃ bhavate patnī svayaṃ dāsyati kāminīm \|*  
*ādyaḥ prajāpatiryo hi yatheṣṭaṃ puruṣottamaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Dakṣa here, the first Prajāpati, will give you a suitable wife, O best of men, as you please.

## \|\| 3.3.9 \|\|

*eṣā ca kanyakā cārurūpā brahmamanobhavā \|*  
*saṃdhyā nāmneti vikhyātā sarvaloke bhaviṣyati \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. This girl of handsome features, born of Brahmā’s mind, shall become famous in the world as Sandhyā.

## \|\| 3.3.10 \|\|

*brahmaṇo dhyāyato yasmātsamyagjātā varāṃganā \|*  
*atassaṃdhyeti vikhyātā krāṃtābhā tulyamallikā \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Since she was born when Brahmā was deeply contemplating, the woman of lovely features will be famous as Sandhyā. She will be as lustrous as the jasmine flower.

## \|\| 3.3.11 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*kausumāni tathāstrāṇi paṃcādāya manobhavaḥ \|*  
*pracchannarūpī tatraiva ciṃtayāmāsa niścayam \|\| 11 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

11\. Taking his five flower-arrows, Kāma decided on his future course remaining invisible in form.

## \|\| 3.3.12 \|\|

*harṣaṇaṃ rocanākhyaṃ ca mohanaṃ śoṣaṇaṃ tathā \|*  
*māraṇaṃ ceti proktāni munermohakarāṇyapi \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. His five arrows are respectively Harṣaṇa (delighting), Rocana (appealing), Mohana (deluding), Śoṣaṇa (withering) and Māraṇa (killing). Even sages could be deluded and tormented by them.

## \|\| 3.3.13-15 \|\|

*brahmaṇā mama yatkarma samuddiṣṭaṃ sanātanam \|*  
*tadihaiva kariṣyāmi munīnāṃ sannidhau vidhe \|\| 13 \|\|*

*tiṣṭhaṃti munayaścātra svayaṃ cāpi prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*eteṣāṃ sākṣibhūtaṃ me bhaviṣyaṃtyadya niścayam \|\| 14 \|\|*

*saṃdhyāpi brahmaṇā proktā cedānīṃ preṣayedvacaḥ \|*  
*iha karma parīkṣyaiva prayogānmohayāmyaham \|\| 15 \|\|*

13-15. (Kāma thought like this:—) I shall make a beginning of my career as assigned by Brahmā himself as my eternal task, here itself in the presence of the sages and Brahmā. All the sages and Brahmā are present here. They shall witness my resolution and performance. Sandhyā who was referred to by Brahmā is also present here. She shall be my mouth-piece. I shall test my power here and then only carry on my work elsewhere.

## \|\| 3.3.16 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*iti saṃcitya manasā niścitya ca manobhavaḥ \|*  
*puṣpajaṃ puṣpajātasya yojayāmāsa mārgaṇaiḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. After thinking like this and deciding on his further activity, Kāma fitted his flower-arrows.

## \|\| 3.3.17 \|\|

*ālīḍhasthānamāsādya dhanurākṛṣya yatnataḥ \|*  
*cakāra valayākāraṃ kāmo dhanvivarastadā \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Kāma, the foremost of archers, stood steady in the posture of Ālīḍha (the posture for shooting, the right knee advanced and the left leg retracted), bent his bow almost into a circle and was ready to shoot.

## \|\| 3.3.18 \|\|

*saṃhite tena kodaṃḍe mārutāśca sugaṃdhayaḥ \|*  
*vavustatra muniśreṣṭha samyagāhlādakāriṇaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. O excellent sage, when the bow was kept ready by him, fragrant winds delighting everyone blew there.

## \|\| 3.3.19 \|\|

*tatastānapi dhātrādīn sarvāneva ca mānasān \|*  
*pṛthak puṣpaśaraistīkṣṇairmohayāmāsa mohanaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The enchanter then charmed Brahmā and others, the mental sons with several sharp flower-arrows.

## \|\| 3.3.20 \|\|

*tataste munayassarve mohitāścāpyahaṃ mune \|*  
*sahito manasā kaṃcidvikāraṃ prāpurāditaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. O sage, the sages and I were thus enamoured and we felt very great change in our mental feelings.

## \|\| 3.3.21 \|\|

*saṃdhyāṃ sarve nirīkṣaṃtassavikāraṃ muhurmuhuḥ \|*  
*āsan pravṛddhamadanāḥ strī yasmānmadanaidhinī \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. We began to stare at Sandhyā frequently, passion depraving our minds. Our lust was heightened. Truly a woman is one who increases passionate feelings.

## \|\| 3.3.22 \|\|

*tataḥ sarvānsa madano mohayitvā punaḥpunaḥ \|*  
*yathendriyavikāraṃ ta prāpustānakarottathā \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Making all of us thoroughly enchanted thus, he did not stop till all of us lost control over our sense-organs.

## \|\| 3.3.23 \|\|

*udīriteṃdriyo dhātā vīkṣyāhaṃ sa yadā ca tām \|*  
*tadaiva conapaṃcāśadbhāvā jātāśśarīrataḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. When on seeing her, my vital elements became displaced, forty-nine animal instincts Bhāvas came, out of my body.

## \|\| 3.3.24 \|\|

*sāpi tairvīkṣyamāṇātha kaṃdarpaśarapātanāt \|*  
*cakre muhurmuhurbhāvānkaṭākṣāvaraṇādikān \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. She too began to manifest the instinctive gestures of side-glances, pretences of concealing feelings etc. as a result of being hit by Kāma’s arrows when she was being stared at by them.

## \|\| 3.3.25 \|\|

*nisargasuṃdarī saṃdhyā tānbhāvān mānasodbhavān \|*  
*kurvaṃtyatitarāṃ reje svarṇadīva tanūrmibhiḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Profusely exhibiting these emotions, the naturally beautiful Sandhyā shone brilliantly like the celestial river producing gentle ripples.

## \|\| 3.3.26 \|\|

*atha bhāvayutāṃ saṃdhyāṃ vīkṣyākārṣaṃ prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*dharmābhipūrita tanurabhilāṣamahaṃ mune \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. O sage, on seeing her emotionally excited I loved her all the more despite the fact that I was the creator and my body was filled with Dharmic features.

## \|\| 3.3.27 \|\|

*tataste munayassarve marīcyatrimukhā api \|*  
*dakṣādyāśca dvijaśreṣṭha prāpurvekārikendriyam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. All the sages, Marīci, Atri, Dakṣa and others, O foremost among brahmins, attained the state of sensuous excitement.

## \|\| 3.3.28 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā tathāvidhā dakṣamarīcipramukhāśca mām \|*  
*saṃdhyāṃ ca karmaṇi nije śraddadhe madanastadā \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Seeing me as well as Dakṣa, Marici and others in such a situation and seeing Sandhyā engaged in her affairs, Madana continued to concentrate his attention on his activity.

## \|\| 3.3.29 \|\|

*yadidaṃ brahmaṇā karma mamoddiṣṭaṃ mayāpi tat \|*  
*kartuṃ śakyamiti hyaddhā bhāvitaṃ svabhuvā tadā \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. “The work entrusted to me by Brahmā can easily be performed by me” so thought Kāma justifiably.

## \|\| 3.3.30 \|\|

*itthaṃ pāpagatiṃ vīkṣya bhrātṝṇāṃ ca pitustathā \|*  
*dharmassasmāra śaṃbhuṃ vai tadā dharmāvanaṃ prabhum \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. On seeing the sinful proclivities of his brothers and father, Dharma remembered Lord Śiva, the lord protector of virtue.

## \|\| 3.3.31 \|\|

*saṃsmaranmanasā dharmaṃ śaṃkaraṃ dharmapālakam \|*  
*tuṣṭāva vividhairvākyairdīno bhūtvājasaṃbhavaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Mentally meditating on Śiva, the protector of virtue, Dharma, the son of Brahmā eulogised Śiva with different prayers in his state of sorrow.

## \|\| 3.3.32 \|\|

*dharma uvāca \|*  
*devadeva mahādeva dharmapāla namostu te \|*  
*sṛṣṭisthitivināśānāṃ kartā śaṃbho tvameva hi \|\| 32 \|\|*

Dharma said:—

32\. O Mahādeva, lord of Devas, protector of virtues, obeisance be to Thee. O Śiva, Thou alone art the author of creation, sustenance and dissolution.

## \|\| 3.3.33 \|\|

*sṛṣṭau brahmā sthitau viṣṇuḥ pralaye hararūpadhṛk \|*  
*rajassattvatamobhiśca triguṇairaguṇaḥ prabho \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. By virtue of three Guṇas, Rajas, Sattva and Tamas, Thou assumest the form of Brahmā at the time of creation, that of Viṣṇu at the time of sustenance and that of Rudra at the time of dissolution. Yet, O lord, Thou art devoid of attributes.

## \|\| 3.3.34 \|\|

*nistraiguṇyaḥ śivaḥ sākṣātturyaśca prakṛteḥ paraḥ \|*  
*nirguṇo nirvikārī tvaṃ nānālīlāviśāradaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Thou art Śiva free from the influence of the three Guṇas, the fourth Being. Thou art beyond Prakṛti. Thou art expert in various divine sports, yet without attributes and free from deformities and decays.

## \|\| 3.3.35 \|\|

*rakṣarakṣa mahādeva pāpānmāṃ dustarāditaḥ \|*  
*matpitāyaṃ tathā ceme bhrātaraḥ pāpabuddhayaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Great Lord! save me from this impassable ocean of sin. My father and my brothers are now sinfully inclined towards me.

## \|\| 3.3.36 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*iti stuto maheśāno dharmeṇaiva paraḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*tatrājagāma śīghraṃ vai rakṣituṃ dharmamātmabhūḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

36\. Thus eulogised by Dharma, the great lord, selfborn Śiva came there immediately in order to protect Dharma.

## \|\| 3.3.37 \|\|

*jāto viyadgataśśaṃbhurvidhiṃ dṛṣṭvā tathāvidham \|*  
*māṃ dakṣādyāṃśca manasā jahāsopajahāsa ca \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Stationed in the ether, Śiva saw me, Brahman, Dakṣa and others in such a mental state and so laughed mockingly.

## \|\| 3.3.38 \|\|

*sa sādhuvādaṃ tān sarvānvihasya ca punaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*uvācedaṃ muniśreṣṭha lajjayan vṛṣabhadhvajaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. O best of sages, in the midst of his intermittent laughter making all blush with shame, the full-emblemed deity spoke these consoling words.

## \|\| 3.3.39 \|\|

*śiva uvāca \|*  
*aho brahmaṃstava kathaṃ kāmabhāvassamudgataḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā ca tanayāṃ naiva yogyaṃ vedānusāriṇām \|\| 39 \|\|*

Śiva said:—

39\. Alas! O Brahmā, how is it that you were overwhelmed with lustful feelings on seeing your own daughter? This is highly improper for those who walk on the line of the Vedas.

## \|\| 3.3.40 \|\|

*yathā mātā ca bhaginī bhrātṛpatnī tathā sutā \|*  
*etaḥ kudṛṣṭyā draṣṭavyā na kadāpi vipaścitā \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Sister, brother’s wife and daughter are like one’s mother. A sensible man shall never look at them with a reprehensible vision.

## \|\| 3.3.41 \|\|

*eṣa vai vedamārgasya niścayastvanmukhe sthitaḥ \|*  
*kathaṃ tu kāmamātreṇa sa te vismārito vidhe \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. The conclusion of the path of the Vedas is present in your mouth. O Brahmā, how is it that you forgot that under the influence of momentary passion?

## \|\| 3.3.42 \|\|

*dhairye jāgaritaṃ brahmanmanaste caturānana \|*  
*kathaṃ kṣudreṇa kāmena raṃtuṃ vigaṭitaṃ vidhe \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. O, four-faced deity Brahmā, your mind shall always remain alert in fortitude. How did you undo it for the sake of dalliance in love?

## \|\| 3.3.43 \|\|

*ekāṃtayoginastasmātsarvadādityadarśinaḥ \|*  
*kathaṃ dakṣamarīcyādyā lolupāḥ strīṣu mānasāḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. How is it that your mental sons, Dakṣa, Marīci and others who practise yoga in isolation and see the inner light for ever have become enamoured of woman?

## \|\| 3.3.44 \|\|

*kathaṃ kāmopi maṃdātmā prābalyātsodhunaiva hi \|*  
*vikṛtānbāṇaiḥ kṛtavānakālajñolpacetanaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. This Kāma is a fool, deficient in sense and ignorant of proper occasion. How is it that he has begun to torment them with excessive power?

## \|\| 3.3.45 \|\|

*dhiktaṃ śrutaṃ sadā tasya yasya kāṃtā manoharat \|*  
*dhairyādākṛṣya laulyeṣu majjayatyapi mānasam \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Fie upon the learning of that person whose wife draws his mind inordinately from steadiness and courage and immerses it in fickle revelries.

## \|\| 3.3.46 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*iti tasya vacaḥ śrutvā loke sohaṃ śivasya ca \|*  
*vrīḍayā dviguṇībhūtassvedārdrastvabhavaṃ kṣaṇāt \|\| 46 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

46\. On hearing these words of Śiva, I, the lord of the world, perspired profusely in an instant, on account of shame.

## \|\| 3.3.47 \|\|

*tato nigṛhyaiṃdriyakaṃ vikāraṃ cātyajaṃ mune \|*  
*jighṛkṣurapi tadbhītyā tāṃ saṃdhyāṃ kāmarūpiṇīm \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Although the desire to seize Sandhyā of wishful features still lingered, O sage, I curbed the upset senses, fearing him (Śiva).

## \|\| 3.3.48-49 \|\|

*maccharīrāttu gharmāṃbho yatpapāta dvijottama \|\| dharmāṃbho \|*  
*agniṣvāttāḥ pitṛgaṇā jātāḥ pitṛgaṇāstataḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

*bhinnāṃjananibhāssarve phullarājīvalocanāḥ \|*  
*nitāṃtayatayaḥ puṇyāssaṃsāravimukhāḥ pare \|\| 49 \|\|*

48-49. O excellent brahmin, from the drops of sweat that fell from my body rose the manes who did not perform the sacrifices while they were living on earth, who shone like split collyrium, had eyes resembling the full-bown lotus, were meritorious ascetics and were averse to worldly activities.

## \|\| 3.3.50 \|\|

*sahasrāṇāṃ catuḥṣaṣṭiragniṣvāttāḥ prakīrtitā \|*  
*ṣaḍaśītisahasrāṇi tathā barhiṣado mune \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. These were sixty-four thousand in number, O sage, and the manes called Barhiṣads, lit. seated on grass, were eighty-six thousand.

## \|\| 3.3.51 \|\|

*gharmāṃbhaḥ patitaṃ bhūmau tadā dakṣaśarīrataḥ \|*  
*samastaguṇasaṃpannā tasmājjātā varāṃganā \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. From the drops of sweat that fell from Dakṣa’s body, a splendid woman endowed with good qualities was born.

## \|\| 3.3.52-53 \|\|

*tanvaṃgī samamadhyā ca tanuromāvalī śrutā \|*  
*mṛdvaṃgī cārudaśanā navakāṃcanasuprabhā \|\| 52 \|\|*

*sarvāvayavaramyā ca pūrṇacandrānanāmbujā \|*  
*nāmnā ratiriti khyātā munīnāmapi mohinī \|\| 53 \|\|*

52-53. She was of slender body with symmetrical hips. Her waist was well-shaped; small curly hairs embellished it. She was soft in body with fine teeth. She had a shining golden complexion. In her body, she was perfect. Her face shone like the full moon and full-blown lotus. Her name was Rati. She was capable of captivating even the sages.

## \|\| 3.3.54 \|\|

*marīcipramukhā ṣaḍ vai nigṛhītendriyakriyāḥ \|*  
*ṛte kratuṃ vasiṣṭhaṃ ca pulastyāṃgirasau tathā \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Excepting Kratu, Vasiṣṭha, Pulastya and Aṅgiras, the six viz. Marīci and others successfully curbed their senses and their activities.

## \|\| 3.3.55 \|\|

*kratvādīnāṃ caturṇāṃ ca bījaṃ bhūmau papāta ca \|*  
*tebhyaḥ pitṛgaṇā jātā apare munisattama \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. O excellent sage, the semen virile of the four—Kratu and others—fell on the ground from which other types of manes were born.

## \|\| 3.3.56 \|\|

*somapā ājyapā nāmnā tathaivānye sukālinaḥ \|*  
*haviṣmaṃtastu tāssarve kavyavāhāḥ prakīrtitāḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. They were Somapās, Ājyapās, Kālins and Haviṣmantas. They are all termed Kavyavāhas also. They are their sons.

## \|\| 3.3.57 \|\|

*kratostu somapāḥ putrā vasiṣṭhātkālinastathā \|*  
*ājyapākhyāḥ pulastyasya haviṣmaṃtoṃgirassutāḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. The Somapās are the sons of Kratu, Kālins of Vasiṣṭha, Ājyapās of Pulastya and Haviṣmantas of Aṅgiras.

## \|\| 3.3.58 \|\|

*jāteṣu teṣu viprendra agniṣvāttādikeṣvatha \|*  
*lokānāṃ pitṛvargeṣu kavyavāha sa samaṃtataḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. O excellent brahmin, when the manes Agniṣvāttas and others were born, they were assigned the task of Kavyavāhas (taking the oblations and offering) among the manes.

## \|\| 3.3.59 \|\|

*saṃdhyā pitṛprasūrbhūtvā taduddeśayutā'bhavat \|*  
*nirdoṣā śaṃbhusaṃdṛṣṭā dharmakarmaparāyaṇā \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Sandhyā who thus became the mother of the Pitṛs served the same purpose as theirs. Since she has been glanced at kindly by Śiva she became free from defects and devoted herself to virtuous rites.

## \|\| 3.3.60 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare śambhuranugṛhyākhilāndvijān \|*  
*dharmaṃ saṃrakṣya vidhivadaṃtardhānaṃ gato drutam \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. In the meantime after blessing all the brahmins and protecting virtue duly Śiva vanished suddenly.

## \|\| 3.3.61 \|\|

*atha śaṃkaravākyena lajjitohaṃ pitāmahaḥ \|*  
*kaṃdarppāyākopiṃta hi bhrukuṭīkuṭilānanaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. I, the grandfather of the world, snubbed and put to shame by Śiva’s words, turned my anger against Kāma with a frowning face and knit eyebrows.

## \|\| 3.3.62 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā mukhamabhiprāyaṃ viditvā sopi manmathaḥ \|*  
*svabāṇānsaṃjahārāśu bhītaḥ paśupatermune \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. O sage, seeing my face and realising my hint, Kāma withdrew his arrows. He was so terribly afraid of Siva.

## \|\| 3.3.63 \|\|

*tataḥ kopasamāyuktaḥ padmayonirahaṃ mune \|*  
*ajvalaṃ cātibalavān didhakṣuriva pāvakaḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. O sage, then I, the lotus-born, became very furious like the strong blazing fire seeking to consume everything.

## \|\| 3.3.64-65 \|\|

*bhavanetrāgninirdagdhaḥ kaṃdarpo darpamohitaḥ \|*  
*bhaviṣyati mahādeve kṛtvā karmaṃ suduṣkaram \|\| 64 \|\|*

*iti vedhāstvahaṃ kāmamakṣayaṃ dvijasattama \|*  
*samakṣaṃ pitṛsaṃghasya munīnāṃ ca yatātmanām \|\| 65 \|\|*

64-65. I, Brahmā, then said:—“After playing this same trick on Śiva, Kāma will be consumed in the fire of Śiva’s eye and freed of his arrogance.” O excellent brahmin, it was in the presence of the manes and the sages of perfect control that I spoke to Kāma in this way.

## \|\| 3.3.66 \|\|

*iti bhīto ratipatistatkṣaṇāttyaktamārgaṇaḥ \|*  
*prādurbabhūva pratyakṣaṃ śāpaṃ śrutvātidāruṇam \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. On hearing this curse of terrible nature, Rati’s husband was frightened. He abandoned his arrows and became visible.

## \|\| 3.3.67 \|\|

*brahmāṇaṃ māmuvācedaṃ sa dakṣādisutaṃ mune \|*  
*śṛṇvatāṃ pitṛsaṃghānāṃ saṃdhyāyāśca vigarvadhīḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. O sage, he spoke to me (i.e. Brahmā) and my sons Dakṣa and others even as the Pitṛs and Sandhyā stood there listening. By this time his arrogance had disappeared.

## \|\| 3.3.68 \|\|

*kāma uvāca \|*  
*kimarthaṃ bhavatā brahmañ śaptohamiti dāruṇam \|*  
*anāgāstava lokeśa nyāyyamārgānusāriṇaḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Kāma said:—“O Brahmā, why have I been so terribly cursed by you? O lord of worlds, I have not committed any sin against you who are reputed to follow justiciable path.

## \|\| 3.3.69 \|\|

*tvayā coktaṃ nu matkarma yattadbrahman kṛtaṃ mayā \|*  
*tatra yogyo na śāpo me yato nānyatkṛtaṃ mayā \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. O Brahmā, you have assigned me my task. I have only carried it out. Hence this curse is not proper. I have not done anything else.

## \|\| 3.3.70 \|\|

*ahaṃ viṣṇustathā śaṃbhuḥ sarve tvaccha ragocarāḥ \|*  
*iti yadbhavatā proktaṃ tanmayāpi parīkṣitam \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. You had said:—“All of us, I, Viṣṇu and Śiva are targets of your arrows.” I only tested your statement.

## \|\| 3.3.71 \|\|

*nāparādho mamāpyatra brahman mayi nirāgasi \|*  
*dāruṇaḥ samayaścaiva śāpo deva jagatpate \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. I am not guilty in this respect. O Brahmā I being innocent, this conditional curse, O lord of universe, is very terrible.

## \|\| 3.3.72 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*iti tasya vacaḥ śrutvā brahmāhaṃ jagatāṃ patiḥ \|*  
*pratyavocaṃ yatātmānaṃ madanaṃ damayanmuhuḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. On hearing his words, I, Brahmā, the lord of the universe, replied to Madana who had controlled himself, trying to suppress him further.

## \|\| 3.3.73 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ātmajā mama saṃdhyeyaṃ yasmādetatsa kāmataḥ \|*  
*lakṣyīkṛtohaṃ bhavatā tataśśāpo mayā kṛtaḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

73\. I cursed you because you have aimed at us—this Sandhyā who is my daughter and me her father.

## \|\| 3.3.74 \|\|

*adhunā śāṃtaroṣohaṃ tvāṃ vadāmi manobhava \|*  
*śṛṇuṣva gatasaṃdehassukhī bhava bhayaṃ tyaja \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. But now I am free from anger. In this state I tell you O Kāma, do not be under any suspicion. Listen. Cast off your fear. Be happy.

## \|\| 3.3.75 \|\|

*tvaṃ bhasma bhūtvā madana bhargalocanavahninā \|*  
*tathaivāśu samaṃ paścāccharīraṃ prāpayiṣyasi \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. O Kāma, he will reduce you to ashes in the fire of his eye. But he will give you another similar body afterwards.

## \|\| 3.3.76 \|\|

*yadā kariṣyati haroṃjasā dāraparigraham \|*  
*tadā sa eva bhavataśśarīraṃ prāpayiṣyati \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. When Śiva takes to a wife He Himself will get you another body.

## \|\| 3.3.77 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*evamuktvātha madanamahaṃ lokapitāmahaḥ \|*  
*aṃtargato munīndrāṇāṃ mānasānāṃ prapaśyatām \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. After speaking thus to Kāma, I the grandfather of the world, vanished from there even as the sages, my mental sons, were watching.

## \|\| 3.3.78 \|\|

*ityevaṃ me vacaśśrutvā madanastepi mānasāḥ \|*  
*saṃbabhūvussutāssarve sukhino'raṃ gṛhaṃ gatāḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. On hearing these words of mine, Kāma and the mental sons of mine became happy and returned quickly to their abodes.

## Chapter 4 - Kāma’s marriage

## \|\| 3.4.1 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*viṣṇuśiṣya mahāprājña vidhe lokakara prabho \|*  
*adbhuteyaṃ kathā proktā śivalīlāmṛtānvitā \|\| 1 \|\|*

Nārada said:—

1\. O lord Brahmā, O Viṣṇu’s disciple of great intellect, O creator of the world, you have narrated a wonderful story consisting of the nector of Śiva’s divine sports.

## \|\| 3.4.2 \|\|

*tataḥ kimabhavattāta caritaṃ tadvadādhunā \|*  
*ahaṃ śraddhānvitaḥ śrotuṃ yadi śambhukathāśrayam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. O dear one, what happened thereafter, please tell me now. I am all attention to a narrative based on Śiva’s life.

## \|\| 3.4.3 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*śaṃbhau gate nijasthāne vedhasyaṃtarhite mayi \|*  
*dakṣa prāhātha kaṃdarpaṃ saṃsmaran mama tadvacaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

3\. When Śiva had gone back to His place and I, Brahmā had vanished from the scene, Dakṣa remembered my words and spoke to Kāma.

## \|\| 3.4.4 \|\|

*dakṣa uvāca \|*  
*maddehajeyaṃ kaṃdarpa sadrūpaguṇasaṃyutā \|*  
*enāṃ gṛhṇīṣva bhāryārthaṃ bhavatassadṛśīṃ guṇaiḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

Dakṣa said:—

4\. “O Kāma, this girl is born of my body. She is endowed with beauty and good qualities. She fits you admirably. Take her as your wife.

## \|\| 3.4.5 \|\|

*eṣā tava mahā tejāssarvadā sahacāriṇī \|*  
*bhaviṣyati yathākāmaṃ dharmato vaśavartinī \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. This powerful girl shall ever be under your righteous control and shall be your constant companion as long as you wish.”

## \|\| 3.4.6 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityuktvā pradadau tasyai dehasvedāṃbusambhavām \|*  
*kaṃdarppāyāgrataḥ kṛtvā nāma kṛtvā ratīti tām \|\| 6 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

6\. Saying so, he presented to him the girl born of his sweat after naming her Rati.

## \|\| 3.4.7 \|\|

*vivāhya tāṃ smarassopi mumodātīva nārada \|*  
*dakṣajāṃ tanayāṃ ramyāṃ munīnāmapi mohinīm \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. O Nārada, after marrying the beautiful daughter of Dakṣa who could enchant even sages, Kāma rejoiced much.

## \|\| 3.4.8 \|\|

*atha tāṃ vīkṣya madano ratyākhyāṃ svastriyaṃ śubhām \|*  
*ātmā guṇena viddhosau mumoha ratiraṃjitaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. On seeing his auspicious wife, Rati, Kāma was pierced by his own arrows and was overpowered by the pleasure of dalliance.

## \|\| 3.4.9 \|\|

*kṣaṇapradā'bhavatkāṃtā gaurī mṛgadṛśī mudā \|*  
*lolāpāṃgyatha tasyaiva bhāryā ca sadṛśī ratau \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. His wife of fair complexion, tremulous side-glances and fawn-eyes, admirably suited to his love of pleasure offered him ample sports.

## \|\| 3.4.10 \|\|

*tasyā bhrūyugalaṃ vīkṣya saṃśayaṃ madanokarot \|*  
*utsādanaṃ matkodaṇḍaṃ vidhātrāsyāṃ niveśitam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. On seeing her eyebrows the doubt arose in the mind of Kāma.—“These two have been fitted to her to excel my bow, by Brahmā who wants to undo it!”

## \|\| 3.4.11 \|\|

*kaṭākṣāṇāmāśugatiṃ dṛṣṭvā tasyā dvijottama \|*  
*āśu gantuṃ nijāstrāṇāṃ śraddadhe na ca cārutām \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. O best of Brahmins, On seeing her rapid-roving glances he did not retain his faith in his arrows in the matter of swift action.

## \|\| 3.4.12 \|\|

*tasyāḥ svabhāvasurabhidhīraśvāsānilaṃ tathā \|*  
*āghrāya madanaḥ śraddhāṃ tyaktavān malayāṃtike \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Inhaling the naturally sweet fragrance of her steady breath Kāma abandoned his faith in the Malaya breeze.

## \|\| 3.4.13 \|\|

*pūrṇendusadṛśaṃ vaktraṃ dṛṣṭvā lakṣmasulakṣitam \|*  
*na niścikāya madano bhedaṃ tanmukhacandrayoḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Seeing her face resembling the full moon with all characteristic marks, Kāma was unable to find any difference between her face and the moon.

## \|\| 3.4.14 \|\|

*suvarṇa padmakalikātulyaṃ tasyāḥ kucadvayam \|*  
*reje cūcukayugmena bhramareṇeva veṣṭitam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Her pair of breasts resembled the buds of golden lotus with nipples shining like bees hovering round them.

## \|\| 3.4.15-16 \|\|

*dṛḍhapīnonnataṃ tasyāstanamadhyaṃ vilaṃbinīm \|*  
*ānābhipratalaṃ mālāṃ tanvīṃ candrāyitāṃ śubhām \|\| 15 \|\|*

*jyāṃ puṣpadhanuṣaḥ kāmaḥ ṣaṭpadāvalisaṃbhramām \|*  
*visasmāra ca yasmāttāṃ visṛjyaināṃ nirīkṣate \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. Certainly Kāma had set aside and forgotten the string of his flowery bow with tumultuous buzzing hums of bees because his eyes were riveted to the auspicious necklace with eyelets of peacock’s tail suspended over her firm protruding plump breasts down to her umbilical part.

## \|\| 3.4.17 \|\|

*gambhīranābhiraṃdhrāṃtaścatuḥpārśvatvagādṛtam \|*  
*ānanābje'kṣaṇadvaṃdvamāraktakaphalaṃ yathā \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. His eyes covering the skin with their glances around her deep navel shone like red plums.

## \|\| 3.4.18 \|\|

*madhyena vapuṣā nisargāṣṭāpadaprabhā \|*  
*rukmavedīva dadṛśe kāmena ramaṇī hi sā \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. That lovely woman of slender waist with a natural golden complexion appeared like a golden platform to Kāma.

## \|\| 3.4.19 \|\|

*raṃbhāstaṃbhāyataṃ snigdhaṃ yadūruyugalaṃ mṛdu \|*  
*nijaśaktisamaṃ kāmo vīkṣāṃcakre manoharam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Kāma looked at her thighs lovely like the stump of a plantain as though they were his javelin.

## \|\| 3.4.20 \|\|

*āraktapārṣṇipādāgraprāṃtabhāgaṃ padadvayam \|*  
*anurāgamivā'nena mitraṃ tasyā manobhavaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. The heels, the tips and the sides of her feet were reddish in tinge. With them she looked as the comrade of the Cupid.

## \|\| 3.4.21 \|\|

*tasyāḥ karayugaṃ raktaṃ nakharaiḥ kiṃśukopamaiḥ \|*  
*vṛttābhiraṃgulībhiśca sūkṣmāgrābhirmanoharam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Her red hands with nails like Kiṃśuka flowers and with well-rounded tapering fingers were very beautiful.

## \|\| 3.4.22 \|\|

*tadbāhuyugulaṃ kāṃtaṃ mṛṇālayugalāyatam \|*  
*mṛdu snigdhaṃ ciraṃ rājatkāṃtilohapravālavat \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Her arms were fine like the lotus-stalk. They were glossy and soft. They resembled corals putting forth beams of splendour.

## \|\| 3.4.23 \|\|

*nīlanīradasaṃkāśaḥ keśapāśo manoharaḥ \|*  
*camarīvāla bharavadvibhāti sma smarapriyaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Her glossy hair resembled the blue cloud and the fluffy tail of the Camarī dear. Thus shone the wife of Kāma.

## \|\| 3.4.24-27 \|\|

*etādṛśīṃ ratiṃ nāmnā prāleyādrisamudbhavām \|*  
*gaṃgāmiva mahādevo jagrāhotphullalocanaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*cakrapadmāṃ cārubāhuṃ mṛṇālaśakalānvitām \|*  
*bhrūyugmavibhramavrātatanūrmiparirājitām \|\| 25 \|\|*

*kaṭākṣapātatuṃgaughāṃ svīyanetrotpalānvitām \|*  
*tanulomāṃbuśaivālāṃ manodrumavilāsinīm \|\| 26 \|\|*

*nimnanābhihradāṃ kṣāmāṃ sarvāṃgaramaṇīyikām \|*  
*sarvalāvaṇyasadanāṃ śobhamānāṃ ramāmiva \|\| 27 \|\|*

24-27. Just as Lord Śiva accepted Gaṅgā oozing from the snowy mountain, Kāma married her. She carried a discus and a lotus in her hand. She had arms fine as the lotus-stalk. She had wavelets of her eyebows. Her side-glances rose up and down like gentle tides. She had eyes resembling a blue lotus. The curly locks of hair on her body were like the mossy growth in the river. She shone with her mind expanded like the tree. Her deep navel resembled the deep eddy. Thus shone Rati with her beautiful body. In fact she appeared to be the abode of beauty itself like Ramā (Goddess Lakṣmī).

## \|\| 3.4.28 \|\|

*dvādaśābharaṇairyuktāṃ śṛṃgāraiḥ ṣoḍaśairyutām \|*  
*mohanīṃ sarvalokānāṃ bhāsayaṃtīṃ diśo daśa \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. She had twelve varieties of ornaments. She was an expert in the sixteen types of amorous gestures. She was capable of charming the whole world. She illuminated all the ten quarters.

## \|\| 3.4.29 \|\|

*iti tāṃ madano vīkṣya ratiṃ jagrāha sotsukaḥ \|*  
*rāgādupasthitāṃ lakṣmīṃ hṛṣīkeśa ivottamām \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Seeing Rati like this, Kāma eagerly accepted her just as Viṣṇu accepted Lakṣmī who approached him with love.

## \|\| 3.4.30 \|\|

*novāca ca tadā dakṣaṃ kāmo modabhavāttataḥ \|*  
*vismṛtya dāruṇaṃ śāpaṃ vidhidattaṃ vimohitaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. In his height of joy, the deluded Kāma forgot the terrible curse of Brahmā and so he had no occasion to mention about it to Dakṣa.

## \|\| 3.4.31 \|\|

*tadā mahotsavastāta babhūva sukhavarddhanaḥ \|*  
*dakṣaḥ prītataraścāsīnmumude tanayā mama \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Great festivities heightening the pleasure of everyone ensued, O dear one. My son Dakṣa was more delighted than everyone else. He rejoiced.

## \|\| 3.4.32-34 \|\|

*kāmotīva sukhaṃ prāpya sarvaduḥkhakṣayaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*dakṣajāpi ratiḥ kāmaṃ prāpya cāpi jaharṣa ha \|\| 32 \|\|*

*rarāja cetayāsārddhaṃ bhinnaścāruvacaḥ smaraḥ \|*  
*jīmūta iva saṃdhyāyāṃ saudāmanyā manojñayā \|\| 33 \|\|*

*iti ratipatiruccairmohayukto ratiṃ tāṃ hṛdupari jagṛhe vai yogadarśīva vidyām \|*  
*ratirapi patimagryaṃ prāpya sā cāpi reje harimiva kamalā vai pūrṇacandropamāsyā \|\| 34 \|\|*

32-34. Having reached the acme of happiness Kāma thought all miseries were at an end. Dakṣa’s daughter Rati was highly delighted on getting Kāma as her husband. The sweet-voiced Kāma rejoiced with her like the cloud at sunset mingled with sparkling lightning. Thus Kāma took Rati to his chest in his happy delusion like the Yogin his knowledge. Having secured a fine husband, Rati with face shining like the full moon shone like Lakṣmi having secured Hari.

## Chapter 5 - The story of Sandhyā

## \|\| 3.5.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya vacastasya brahmaṇo munisattamaḥ \|*  
*sa mudovāca saṃsmṛtya śaṃkaraṃ prītamānasaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. On hearing these words of Brahmā, the excellent sage remembered Śiva with a delighted heart and spoke joyfully.

## \|\| 3.5.2 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*brahman vidhe mahābhāga viṣṇuśiṣya mahāmate \|*  
*adbhutā kathitā līlā tvayā ca śaśimaulinaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

Nārada said:—

2\. O Brahmā, the fortunate disciple of Viṣṇu, O intelligent one, you have narrated the wonderful divine sports of the moon-crested lord.

## \|\| 3.5.3-4 \|\|

*gṛhītadāre madane hṛṣṭe hi svagṛhe gate \|*  
*dakṣe ca svagṛhaṃ yāte tathā hi tvayi kartari \|\| 3 \|\|*

*mānaseṣu ca putreṣu gateṣu svasvadhāmasu \|*  
*saṃdhyā kutra gatā sā ca brahmaputrī pitṛprasūḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. After Kāma had married and gone to his residence when all of you, i.e. you the creator, Dakṣa and the mental sons, had all gone to your respective abodes, where did Sandhyā, the daughter of Brahmā and the mother of the Pitṛs go?

## \|\| 3.5.5 \|\|

*kiṃ cakāra ca kenaiva puruṣeṇa vivāhitā \|*  
*etatsarvaṃ viśeṣeṇa saṃdhyāyāścaritaṃ vada \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. What did she do? Who married her? Please tell me all about it and particularly the account related to Sandhyā.

## \|\| 3.5.6 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya vacastasya brahmaputraśca dhīmataḥ \|*  
*saṃsmṛtya śaṃkaraṃ saktyā brahmā provāca tattvavit \|\| 6 \|\|*

Sūta said:—

6\. On hearing these words of his intelligent son, Brahmā, who knew the real situation, remembered Śiva and said:—

## \|\| 3.5.7 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*śṛṇu tvaṃ ca mune sarvaṃ saṃdhyāyāścaritaṃ śubham \|*  
*yacchrutvā sarvakāminyassādhvyassyussarvadā mune \|\| 7 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

7\. O sage, listen to the auspicious story of Sandhyā, on hearing which ladies do always become chaste.

## \|\| 3.5.8 \|\|

*sā ca saṃdhyā sutā me hi manojātā purā' bhavat \|*  
*tapastaptvā tanuṃ tyaktvā saiva jātā tvaruṃdhatī \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. That Sandhyā was my daughter mentally created by me formerly. She performed a penance, cast off her body and was reborn as Arundhatī.

## \|\| 3.5.9-10 \|\|

*medhātithessutā bhūtvā muniśreṣṭhasya dhīmatī \|*  
*brahmaviṣṇumaheśānavacanāccaritavratā \|\| 9 \|\|*

*vavre patiṃ mahātmānaṃ vasiṣṭhaṃ śaṃsitavratam \|*  
*pativratā ca mukhyā'bhūdvaṃdyā pūjyā tvabhīṣaṇā \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. She was born as the intelligent daughter of the excellent sage Medhātithi, performed sacred rites at the bidding of Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva and chose as her husband the noble-souled Vasiṣṭha of praiseworthy rites. She of auspicious countenance became the foremost of chaste ladies and deserved honour and respect from everyone,

## \|\| 3.5.11 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*kathaṃ tayā tapastaptaṃ kimarthaṃ kutra saṃdhyayā \|*  
*kathaṃ śarīraṃ sā tyaktvā'bhavanmedhātitheḥ sutā\|\| \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. How did she perform penance? Why and where? How did she cast off her body and become the daughter of Medhātithi?

## \|\| 3.5.12 \|\|

*kathaṃ vā vihitaṃ devairbrahmaviṣṇuśivaiḥ patim \|*  
*vasiṣṭhaṃ tu mahātmānaṃ saṃvavre śaṃsitavratam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. What did the deities Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva command her to do? and how did she choose the noble-souled Vasiṣṭha of praiseworthy rites as her husband?

## \|\| 3.5.13 \|\|

*etanme śroṣyamāṇāya vistareṇa pitāmaha \|*  
*kautūhalamaruṃdhatyāścaritaṃ brūhi tattvataḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. I am eager to hear all these things. O Grand Father, tell me in detail the story of Sandhyā precisely.

## \|\| 3.5.14 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ahaṃ svatanayāṃ saṃdhyāṃ dṛṣṭvā pūrvamathātmanaḥ \|*  
*kāmāyāśu mano'kārṣaṃ tyaktvā śivabhayācca sā \|\| 14 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

14\. Formerly on seeing Sandhyā, my daughter, I cherished a love for her, which, being afraid of Śiva, I forsook.

## \|\| 3.5.15 \|\|

*saṃdhyāyāścalitaṃ cittaṃ kāmabāṇaviloḍitam \|*  
*ṛṣīṇāmapi saṃruddhamānasānāṃ mahātmanām \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Sandhyā’s mind too was shaken on being stirred by Kāma’s arrows. The same had happened with the mind of the noble-souled sages who had so far curbed their minds.

## \|\| 3.5.16-17 \|\|

*bhargasya vacanaṃ śrutvā sopahāsaṃ ca māṃ prati \|*  
*ātmanaścalitatvaṃ vai hyamaryādamṛṣīnprati \|\| 16 \|\|*

*kāmasya tādṛśaṃ bhāvaṃ munimohakaraṃ muhuḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā saṃdhyā svayaṃ tatropayamāyātiduḥkhitā \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. She had heard the words of Śiva to me couched in mocking terms. She had realised that her mental aberration in regard to the sages was beyond decency. She had seen the attitude of Kāma culminating in the delusion of the sages, frequently. Hence Sandhyā was excessively distressed with respect to her marriage.

## \|\| 3.5.18-19 \|\|

*tatastu brahmaṇā śapte madane ca mayā mune \|*  
*aṃtarbhūte mayi śive gate cāpi nijāspade \|\| 18 \|\|*

*āmarṣavaśamāpannā sā saṃdhyā munisattama \|*  
*mama putrī vicāryaivaṃ tadā dhyānaparā'bhavat \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. O sage, then I cursed Kāma. Śiva left the place and I too disappeared. Thus her support was lost. So, O excellent sage, Sandhyā became furious. Then, my daughter considered all these things and meditated.

## \|\| 3.5.20 \|\|

*dhyāyaṃtī kṣaṇamevāśu pūrvaṃ vṛttaṃ manasvinī \|*  
*idaṃ vimamṛśe saṃdhyā tasminkāle yathocitam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Meditating on the recent events, she of great fortitude mused what befitted the situation.

## \|\| 3.5.21 \|\|

*saṃdhyovāca \|*  
*utpannamātrāṃ māṃ dṛṣṭvā yuvatīṃ madaneritaḥ \|*  
*akārṣitsānurāgoyamabhilāṣaṃ pitā mama \|\| 21 \|\|*

Sandhyā said:—

21\. Seeing me as a lady in the prime of my youth even at my nativity, my father, prompted by Kāma, cherished a lustful desire for me.

## \|\| 3.5.22 \|\|

*paśyatāṃ mānasānāṃ ca munīnāṃ bhāvitātmanām \|*  
*dṛṣṭvaiva māmamaryādaṃ sakāmamabhavanmanaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The minds of the sages, the mental sons, reputed to be pure in mind, on seeing me became lustful breaking the conventions.

## \|\| 3.5.23 \|\|

*mamāpi mathitaṃ cittaṃ madanena durātmanā \|*  
*yena dṛṣṭvā munīnsarvāṃścalitaṃ manmano bhṛśam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. My mind too was excessively stirred up by the wicked Kāma, as a result of which, on seeing those sages it too became excessively shaken.

## \|\| 3.5.24 \|\|

*phalametasya pāpasya madanassvayamāptavān \|*  
*yastaṃ śaśāpa kupitaḥ śaṃbhoragre pitāmahaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Of course Kāma reaped the fruits of his sinful misdeeds, for Brahmā became angry and cursed him in the presence of Śiva.

## \|\| 3.5.25 \|\|

*prāpnuyāṃ phalametasya pāpasya svaghakāriṇī \|*  
*tacchodhanaphalamahamāśu necchāmi sādhanam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. I too shall have to reap the fruits of my sin. I have committed a great sin. I wish to have a means for making amends.

## \|\| 3.5.26 \|\|

*yanmāṃ pitā bhrātaraśca sakāmamaparokṣataḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā cakrusspṛhāṃ tasmānna mattaḥ pāpakṛtparā \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Directly perceiving that I too had lustful feelings, the brothers and my father had a similar desire. Hence I am the worst sinner.

## \|\| 3.5.27 \|\|

*mamāpi kāmabhāvobhūdamaryādaṃ samīkṣya tān \|*  
*patyā iva svaketāte sarveṣu sahajeṣvaṣi \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. I too had the unconventional lustful feelings on seeing them, towards my own father and brothers as towards a husband.

## \|\| 3.5.28 \|\|

*kariṣyāramyasya pāpasya prāyaścittamahaṃ svayam \|*  
*ātmānamagnau hoṣyāmi vedamārgānusārata \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. I shall perform expiatory rites myself for my sin. Following the Vedic injunctions I shall consign myself to the fire.

## \|\| 3.5.29 \|\|

*kiṃ tvekāṃ sthāpayiṣyāmi maryādāmiha bhūtale \|*  
*utpannamātrā na yathā sakāmāssyuśśarīriṇaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. But I shall set up the new limits in the world. No person shall be so lustful at the time of birth.

## \|\| 3.5.30 \|\|

*etadarthamahaṃ kṛtvā tapaḥ parama dāruṇam \|*  
*maryādāṃ sthāpayiṣyāmi paścāttyakṣāmi jīvitam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. For this purpose I shall perform a severe penance. Then I shall establish the new limits and afterwards I shall abandon this life.

## \|\| 3.5.31 \|\|

*yasmiñccharīre pitrā me hyabhilāṣassvayaṃ kṛtaḥ \|*  
*bhātṛbhistena kāyena kiṃcinnāsti prayojanam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. No purpose will be served with this body for which love was cherished by my father and brothers.

## \|\| 3.5.32 \|\|

*mayā yena śarīreṇa tāteṣu sahajeṣu ca \|*
