*udbhāvitaḥ kāmabhāvo na tatsukṛtasādhanam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. This body cannot be the means for achieving merit, for, it was through this body that lustful feelings were generated in my father and brothers.

## \|\| 3.5.33 \|\|

*iti saṃcitya manasā saṃdhyā śailavaraṃ tataḥ \|*  
*jagāma candrabhāgākhyaṃ candrabhāgāpagā yataḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Thinking thus in her mind, Sandhyā went to the mountain Candrabhāga from which the river Candrabhāgā flows.

## \|\| 3.5.34-35 \|\|

*atha tatra gatāṃ jñātvā saṃdhyāṃ girivaraṃ prati \|*  
*tapase niyatātmānaṃ brahmāvocamahaṃ sutam \|\| 34 \|\|*

*vaśiṣṭhaṃ saṃyatātmānaṃ sarvajñaṃ jñānayoginam \|*  
*samīpe sve samāsīnaṃ vedavedāṅgapāragam \|\| 35 \|\|*

34-35. On coming to know that she had gone to the mountain, I, Brahmā, told my son Vasiṣṭha, the omniscient, of purified mind due to penance, who had acquired spiritual knowledge who was seated near me and who had mastered the Vedas and the Vedāṅgas.

## \|\| 3.5.36 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*vasiṣṭha putra gaccha tvaṃ saṃdhyāṃ jātāṃ manasvinīm \|*  
*tapase dhṛtakāmāṃ ca dīkṣasvaināṃ yathā vidhi \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. “O son Vasiṣṭha, approach Sandhyā, my daughter of great fortitude. She is desirous of performing a penance. Initiate her duly in the procedure of that.

## \|\| 3.5.37 \|\|

*maṃdākṣamabhavattasyāḥ purā dṛṣṭvaiva kāmukān \|*  
*yuṣmānmāṃ ca tathātmānaṃ sakāmāṃ munisattama \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. O great sage, formerly seeing you all and me as her lovers and realising her own lustful feelings she had blushed.

## \|\| 3.5.38 \|\|

*abhūtapūrvaṃ tatkarma pūrva mṛtyuṃ vimṛśya sā \|*  
*yuṣmākamātmanaścāpi prāṇānsaṃtyaktumicchati \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Though not expressed and though not personified, your action then is considered by her as her first death. Now she wishes to put an end to her life.

## \|\| 3.5.39 \|\|

*samaryādeṣu maryādāṃ tapasā sthāpayiṣyati \|*  
*tapaḥ kartuṃ gatā sādhvī candrabhāgākhyabhūdhare \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Among those who observe limits and conventions she wants to lay down a limitation. The chaste lady has gone to the mountain Candrabhāga for performing the penance.

## \|\| 3.5.40 \|\|

*na bhāvaṃ tapasastāta sānujānāti kaṃcana \|*  
*tasmādyathopadeśātsā prāpnotviṣṭaṃ tathā kuru \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. She does not know the procedure of performing a penance. O dear, see that she realises her desire by means of your instructions.

## \|\| 3.5.41 \|\|

*idaṃ rūpaṃ parityajya nijaṃ rūpāṃtaraṃ mune \|*  
*parigṛhyāṃtike tasyāstapaścaryāṃ nidarśayan \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. O sage, abandon this form of yours. Disguise yourself and approach her to demonstrate the mode of penance.

## \|\| 3.5.42 \|\|

*idaṃ svarūpaṃ bhavato dṛṣṭvā pūrvaṃ yathātra vām \|*  
*nāpnuyātsā'tha kiṃcidvai tato rūpāṃtaraṃ kuru \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. You shall assume another form lest she should be embarrassed as before on seeing your natural form and features”.

## \|\| 3.5.43 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|\|nāradetthaṃ vasiṣṭho me samājñapto dayāvatā \|*  
*yathā'sviti ca māṃ procya yayau saṃdhyāṃtikaṃ muniḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. O Nārada, Vasiṣṭha was thus ordered by me out of pity. The sage too told me “so be it” and approached Sandhyā.

## \|\| 3.5.44 \|\|

*tatra devasaraḥ pūrṇaṃ guṇairmānasasaṃmitam \|*  
*dadarśa sa vasiṣṭotha saṃdhyāṃ tattīragāmapi \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Vasiṣṭha saw the celestial lake full of Gaṇas and resembling the Mānasa lake. He saw Sandhyā too on its bank.

## \|\| 3.5.45 \|\|

*tīrasthayā tayā reje tatsaraḥ kamalojjvalam \|*  
*udyadiṃdusunakṣatra pradoṣe gaganaṃ yathā \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. With her seated on its bank, the lake, full of splendid lotuses, appeared like the sky in the dusk with the moon rising and the stars twinkling.

## \|\| 3.5.46 \|\|

*munirdṛṣṭvātha tāṃ tatra susaṃbhāvāṃ sa kautukī \|*  
*vīkṣāṃcakre sarastatra bṛhallohitasaṃjñakam \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. On seeing her there full of noble feelings, the sage eagerly looked at the lake called Bṛhallohita.

## \|\| 3.5.47 \|\|

*candrabhāgā nadī tasmātprākārāddakṣiṇāṃbudhim \|*  
*yāṃtī sā caiva dadṛśe tena sānugirermahat \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. From the ridges of that big mountain which appeared like a big fort wall, the river Candrabhāgā rose and flowed towards the Southern sea. The sage saw that too.

## \|\| 3.5.48 \|\|

*nirbhidya paścimaṃ sā tu candrabhāgasya sā nadī \|*  
*yathā himavato gaṃgā tathā gacchati sāgaram \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. That river breaks the western wing of the mountain Candrabhāga even as Gaṅgā of the mountain Himālaya and flows towards the sea.

## \|\| 3.5.49 \|\|

*tasmin girau candrabhāge bṛhallohitatīragām \|*  
*saṃdhyāṃ dṛṣṭvātha papraccha vasiṣṭhassādaraṃ tadā \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Seeing Sandhyā on the bank of the lake Bṛhallohita on that mountain Candrabhāga, Vasiṣṭha asked her respectfully.

## \|\| 3.5.50 \|\|

*vaśiṣṭha uvāca \|*  
*kimarthamāgatā bhadre nirjanaṃ tvaṃ mahīdharam \|*  
*kasya vā tanayā kiṃ vā bhavatyāpi cikīrṣitam \|\| 50 \|\|*

Vasiṣṭha said:—

50\. “O good lady, why have you come to this mountain devoid of men? Whose daughter are you? What is it that you intend to do?

## \|\| 3.5.51 \|\|

*etadicchāmyahaṃ śrotuṃ vada guhyaṃ na cedbhavet \|*  
*vadanaṃ pūrṇacandrābhaṃ niśceṣṭaṃ vā kathaṃ tava \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. I wish to know this if it is not a secret. How is it that your face resembling the full moon is expressionless and inactive?”

## \|\| 3.5.52-53 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*tacchrutvā vacanaṃ tasya vaśiṣṭhasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā ca taṃ mahātmānaṃ jvalaṃtamiva pāvakam \|\| 52 \|\|*

*śarīradhṛgbrahmacaryaṃ vilasaṃtaṃ jaṭādharam \|*  
*sādaraṃ praṇipatyātha saṃdhyovāca tapodhanam \|\| 53 \|\|*

52-53. On hearing the words of the noble-souled Vasiṣṭha and seeing him blazing like fire, shining like Brahmacarya (Celibacy) personified, Sandhyā bowed to the sage wearing matted hair and spoke to him respectfully.

## \|\| 3.5.54 \|\|

*saṃdhyovāca \|*  
*yadarthamāgatā śailaṃ siddhaṃ tanme nibodha ha \|*  
*tava darśanamātreṇa yanme setsyati vā vibho \|\| 54 \|\|*

Sandhyā said:—

54\. “O fearless (sage), know that the purpose for which I came to this mountain has already been achieved or rather will be achieved by your very sight.

## \|\| 3.5.55 \|\|

*tapaścartumahaṃ brahmannirjanaṃ śailamāgatā \|*  
*brahmaṇohaṃ sutā jātā nāmnā saṃdhyeti viśrutā \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. O sage, I came to this mountain devoid of men to perform penance. I am the daughter of Brahmā and am known as Sandhyā.

## \|\| 3.5.56 \|\|

*yadi te yujyate sahyaṃ māṃ tvaṃ samupadeśaya \|*  
*etaccikīrṣitaṃ guhyaṃ nānyaiḥ kiṃcana vidyate \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. If it be proper and not inconvenient for you please instruct me. This is what I expect of you. There is nothing to be kept secret in this.

## \|\| 3.5.57 \|\|

*ajñātvā tapaso bhāvaṃ tapovanamupāśritā \|*  
*ciṃtayā pariśuṣyehaṃ vepate hi mano mama \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Without knowing the procedure of penance I have come to this penance grove. Due to this worry I am perplexed and my heart trembles”.

## \|\| 3.5.58 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ākarṇya tasyā vacanaṃ vasiṣṭho brahmavittamaḥ \|*  
*svayaṃ ca sarvakṛtyajño nānyatkiṃcana pṛṣṭavān \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. On hearing her words, Vasiṣṭha, the most excellent among the knowers of Brahman, well-versed in every rite did not ask anything further.

## \|\| 3.5.59 \|\|

*atha tāṃ niyatātmānaṃ tapaseti dhṛtodyamām \|*  
*provāca manasā smṛtvā śaṃkaraṃ bhaktavatsalam \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. After remembering Śiva favourably disposed to the devotees he addressed the lady who had controlled herself and was preparing for the penance.

## \|\| 3.5.60 \|\|

*vasiṣṭha uvāca \|*  
*paramaṃ yo mahattejaḥ paramaṃ yo mahattapaḥ \|*  
*paramaḥ paramārādhyaḥ śambhurmanasi dhāryatām \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. He who is the supreme brilliance, He who is the greatest austerity, He who is the worthiest of worship—let that Śiva be meditated upon.

## \|\| 3.5.61 \|\|

*dharmārthakāmamokṣāṇāṃ ya ekastvādikāraṇam \|*  
*tamekaṃ jagatāmādyaṃ bhajasva puruṣottamam \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Worship Him who is the most excellent of all Beings, the sole first cause of all the worlds and the principal cause of virtue, wealth, love and salvation.

## \|\| 3.5.62 \|\|

*maṃtreṇānena deveśaṃ śambhuṃ bhaja śubhānane \|*  
*tena te sakalā vāptirbhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. O lady, worship lord Śiva, the lord of all Devas with the following mantra. By that, certainly you will achieve everything.

## \|\| 3.5.63 \|\|

*oṃ namaśśaṃkarāyeti oṃmityaṃtena santatam \|*  
*maunatapasyāprāraṃmbhaṃ tanme nigadataḥ śṛṇu \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. “Oṃ Namaḥ Śaṃkarāya Oṃ” “Oṃ obeisance to Śiva Oṃ.” With this mantra the penance is pervaded. The whole penance begins with silence. I shall explain it. Listen.

## \|\| 3.5.64 \|\|

*snānaṃ maunena kartavyaṃ maunena harapūjanam \|*  
*dvayoḥ pūrṇajalāhāraṃ prathamaṃ ṣaṣṭhakālayoḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. The ceremonial bath shall be taken silently. The worship of Śiva shall be performed silently. The food taken in shall solely consist of water in the first and second Ṣaṣṭakālas (a period ⅙ of the day=4 hrs.)

## \|\| 3.5.65 \|\|

*tṛtīye ṣaṣṭhakāle tu hyupavāsaparo bhavet \|*  
*evaṃ tapassamāptau vā ṣaṣṭhe kāle kriyā bhavet \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. On the third Ṣaṣṭhakāla you shall observe complete fast \[without even taking water\]. This shall continue till the conclusion of the penance. The rites shall be performed at the end of each Ṣaṣṭhakāla.

## \|\| 3.5.66 \|\|

*evaṃ maunatapasyākhyā brahmacaryaphalapradā \|*  
*sarvābhīṣṭapradā devi satyaṃsatyaṃ na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. This is called the penance of silence. It yields all the benefits of celibate life. O lady, it confers all cherished desires. True, it is certainly true.

## \|\| 3.5.67 \|\|

*evaṃ citte samuddiśya kāmaṃ ciṃtaya śaṃkaram \|*  
*sa te prasanna iṣṭārthamacirādeva dāsyati \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Thinking thus in your mind, O lady, you meditate on Śiva. If He is pleased He will confer on you all you wish, ere long.

## \|\| 3.5.68 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*upaviśya vasiṣṭhotha saṃdhyāyai tapasaḥ kriyām \|*  
*tāmābhāṣya yathānyāyaṃ tatraivāṃtardadhe muniḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Vasiṣṭha then sat and explained to Sandhyā the rites of the penance. The sage then vanished from the scene.

## Chapter 6 - Sandhyā granted a boon by Śiva

## \|\| 3.6.1 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*sutavarya mahāprājña śṛṇu saṃdhyātapo mahat \|*  
*yacchrutvā naśyate pāpasamūhastatkṣaṇāddhruvam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

1\. O best of my sons, O intelligent one, listen to the description of the great penance of Sandhyā on hearing which sins are quelled instantly.

## \|\| 3.6.2 \|\|

*upaviśya tapobhāvaṃ vasiṣṭhe svagṛhaṃ gate \|*  
*saṃdhyāpi tapaso bhāvaṃ jñātvā modamavāpa ha \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. When Vasiṣṭha went back to his abode after instructing her in the rites of penance, Sandhyā was greatly pleased on learning the procedure of penance.

## \|\| 3.6.3 \|\|

*tatassānaṃdamanaso veṣaṃ kṛtvā tu yādṛśam \|*  
*tapaścartuṃ samārebhe bṛhallohitatīragā \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. On the bank of the lake Bṛhallohita she began to perform penance after she had put on the dress of a person of blissful mind.

## \|\| 3.6.4 \|\|

*yathoktaṃ tu vaśiṣṭhena maṃtraṃ tapasi sādhanam \|*  
*maṃtreṇa tena sadbhaktyā pūjayāmāsa śaṃkaram \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. She worshipped Śiva with the mantra taught by Vasiṣṭha as the adjunct of penance in the manner explained by him.

## \|\| 3.6.5 \|\|

*ekāntamanasastasyāḥ kurvaṃtyā sumahattapaḥ \|*  
*śaṃbhau vinyastacittāyā gatamekaṃ caturyugam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. A period of four Yugas elapsed during which she continued her great penance with mind fixed and duly concentrated on Śiva.

## \|\| 3.6.6 \|\|

*prasannobhūttadā śaṃbhustapasā tena toṣitaḥ \|*  
*aṃtarbahistathākāśe darśayitvā nijaṃ vapuḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Propitiated by her penance Śiva was greatly delighted. He revealed Himself to her within and without as well as in the heaven.

## \|\| 3.6.7 \|\|

*yadrūpaṃ ciṃtayaṃtī sā tena pratyakṣatāṃ gataḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Śiva became visible to her in the form in which she was meditating upon him.

## \|\| 3.6.8 \|\|

*atha sā purato dṛṣṭvā manasā ciṃtitaṃ prabhum \|*  
*prasannavadanaṃ śāṃtaṃ mumodātīva śaṃkaram \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. She rejoiced much on seeing in front of her, the lord Śiva with face beaming with delight, in the same form as she was meditating on.

## \|\| 3.6.9 \|\|

*sasādhvasamahaṃ vakṣye kiṃ kathaṃ staumi vā haram \|*  
*iti ciṃtāparā bhūtvā nyamīlayata cakṣuṣī \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. “What shall I say? How shall I eulogise?” in this agitation she closed her eyes with fear.

## \|\| 3.6.10 \|\|

*nimīlitākṣyāstasyāstu praviśya hṛdayaṃ haraḥ \|*  
*divyaṃ jñānaṃ dadau tasyai vācaṃ divye ca cakṣuṣī \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. As she remained with eyes shut, Śiva entered her heart and blessed her with divine wisdom, divine speech and divine eyes.

## \|\| 3.6.11 \|\|

*divyajñānaṃ divyacakṣurdivyā vācamavāpa sā \|*  
*pratyakṣaṃ vīkṣya durgeśaṃ tuṣṭāva jagatāṃ patim \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. She thus acquired divine wisdom, divine eyes and divine speech. Directly pereciving the lord of Durgā she eulogised the lord of the worlds.

## \|\| 3.6.12 \|\|

*saṃdhyovāca \|*  
*nirākāraṃ jñānagamyaṃ paraṃ yannaiva sthūlaṃ nāpi sūkṣmaṃ na coccam \|*  
*aṃtaściṃtyaṃ yogibhistasya rūpaṃ tasmai tubhyaṃ lokakartre namostu \|\| 12 \|\|*

Sandhyā said:—

12\. That which has no specific form, that which can be known through perfect knowledge; that which is neither gross, nor subtle, nor high; that which is to be meditated upon by Yogins within themselves—obeisance be to Thee who art of this sort and the creator of the worlds.

## \|\| 3.6.13 \|\|

*sarvaṃ śāṃtaṃ nirmalaṃ nirvikāraṃ jñānāgamyaṃ svaprakāśe'vikāram \|*  
*khādhvaprakhyaṃ dhvāṃtamārgātparastadrūpaṃ yasya tvāṃ namāmi prasannam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. I bow to Thee, lord Śiva, whose form is like a road to heaven, beyond the path of darkness, and who art calm, pure, changeless incomprehensible through worldly knowledge, self-illuminated and unaltered.

## \|\| 3.6.14 \|\|

*ekaṃ śuddhaṃ dīpyamānaṃ tathājaṃ cidānaṃdaṃ sahajaṃ cāvikāri \|*  
*nityānaṃdaṃ satyabhūtiprasannaṃ yasya śrīdaṃ rūpamasmai namaste \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Obeisance to Thee whose form is solitary, pure, luminous, free from illusion, knowledge-cum-bliss, naturally undecaying, eternal bliss, delighted at the outcome of truth and prosperity and productive of glory.

## \|\| 3.6.15 \|\|

*vidyākārodbhāvanīyaṃ prabhinnaṃ sattvacchaṃdaṃ dhyeyamātmasvarūpam \|*  
*sāraṃ pāraṃ pāvanānāṃ pavitraṃ tasmai rūpaṃ yasya caivaṃ namaste \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Obeisance to Thee whose form can be imagined in the nature of Vidyā (Perfect Knowledge), which is different from insentient things, Sāttvika in will, that which should be meditated on as the form of Ātman, which is the utmost essence and which is the holiest of all sanctifying objects.

## \|\| 3.6.16 \|\|

*yattvākāraṃ śuddharūpaṃ manojñaṃ ratnākalpaṃ svacchakarpūragauram \|*  
*iṣṭābhītī śūlamuṃḍe dadhānaṃ hastairnamo yogayuktāya tubhyam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Obeisance to Thee, the Yogin whose Saguṇa form is pure, lovely, bedecked in jewels, as white and clean as camphor and which holds in its hand the desired boon, fearlessness, the trident and the scalp.

## \|\| 3.6.17 \|\|

*gaganaṃ bhūrdiśaścaiva salilaṃ jyotireva ca \|*  
*punaḥ kālaśca rūpāṇi yasya tubhyaṃ namostu te \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Obeisance to Thee whose forms are the sky, the earth, the quarters, the waters, the fire and the Eternal time.

## \|\| 3.6.18 \|\|

*pradhānapuruṣau yasya kāyatvena vinirgatau \|*  
*tasmādavyaktarūpāya śaṃkarāya namonamaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Obeisance, obeisance to Śiva of unmanifest form from whom unmanifest primordial nature and Puruṣa issued forth as its effect.

## \|\| 3.6.19 \|\|

*yo brahmā kurute sṛṣṭiṃ yo viṣṇuḥ kurute sthitim \|*  
*saṃhariṣyati yo rudrastasmai tubhyaṃ namonamaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Obeisance, obeisance to Thee who createst this universe in the form of Brahmā, who sustainest it in the form of Viṣṇu and who destroyest it in the form of Rudra.

## \|\| 3.6.20 \|\|

*namonamaḥ kāraṇakāraṇāya divyāmṛtajñānavibhūtidāya \|*  
*samastalokāṃtarabhūtidāya prakāśarūpāya parātparāya \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Obeisance, obeisance to the cause of causes, to the bestower of divine nectar, wisdom and prosperity; to the best-ower of the prosperity of all other worlds, and the luminous greatest of the great.

## \|\| 3.6.21 \|\|

*yasyā'paraṃ no jagaducyate padāt kṣitirdiśassūrya iṃdurmanaujaḥ \|*  
*barhirmukhā nābhitaścāntarikṣaṃ tasmai tubhyaṃ śaṃbhave me namostu \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Obeisance to Thee, Śiva, beyond whose region no other world exists; from whose umbilical region arose the earth, the quarters, the sun, the moon, the cupid, the devas and the ether.

## \|\| 3.6.22 \|\|

*tvaṃ paraḥ paramātmā ca tvaṃ vidyā vividhā haraḥ \|*  
*sadbrahma ca paraṃ brahma vicāraṇaparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Thou art, the greatest supreme soul. Thou art Śiva, the various lores, the pure Brahman, the supreme Brahman and the utmost object of deliberation.

## \|\| 3.6.23 \|\|

*yasya nādirna madhyaṃ ca nāṃtamasti jagadyataḥ \|*  
*kathaṃ stoṣyāmi taṃ devaṃ vāṅmanogocaraṃ haram \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. How can I adequately eulogise lord Śiva who is inexpressible by words, is incomprehensible to the mind, is the cause of the world and has no beginning, no middle, no end.

## \|\| 3.6.24 \|\|

*yasya brahmādayo deva munayaśca tapodhanāḥ \|*  
*na vipraṇvaṃti rūpāṇi varṇanīyaḥ kathaṃ sa me \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. How can he be described by me, whose forms even Brahmā and other Gods or sages of great austerity cannot describe.

## \|\| 3.6.25 \|\|

*striyā mayā te kiṃ jñeyā nirguṇasya guṇāḥ prabho \|*  
*naiva jānaṃti yadrūpaṃ sendrā api surāsurāḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. O lord, Thou art attributeless. How can Thy attributes be known to me, a mere woman? Even the Gods including Indra and Asuras do not know it.

## \|\| 3.6.26 \|\|

*namastubhyaṃ maheśāna namastubhyaṃ tamomaya \|*  
*prasīda śaṃbho deveśa bhūyobhūyo namostu te \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Obeisance to Thee, O Lord Śiva, obeisance to Thee, O personification of penance; O Śiva, lord of the Gods, be pleased, obeisance be to Thee again and again.

## \|\| 3.6.27 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya vacastasyāssaṃstutaḥ parameśvaraḥ \|*  
*suprasannataraścābhūcchaṃkaro bhaktavatsalaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

2 7. Being thus eulogised and having heard her words Śiva favourably disposed to the devotees became highly pleased.

## \|\| 3.6.28-29 \|\|

*atha tasyāśśarīraṃ tu valkalājinasaṃyutam \|*  
*paricchannaṃ jaṭāvrātaiḥ pavitre mūrdhni rājitaiḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*himānītarjitāṃbhojasadṛśaṃ vadanaṃ tadā \|*  
*nirīkṣya kṛpayāviṣṭo haraḥ provāca tāmidam \|\| 29 \|\|*

28-29. Her body originally clad in barks of trees and deer-hide had by this time been completely covered by clusters of matted hair hanging down from the head and her face appeared like a lotus threatened by frost. On seeing her Śiva melted with pity and said to her.

## \|\| 3.6.30 \|\|

*maheśvara uvāca \|*  
*prītosmi tapasā bhadre bhavatyāḥ parameṇa vai \|*  
*stavena ca śubhaprājñe varaṃ varaya sāṃpratam \|\| 30 \|\|*

Śiva said:—

30\. O gentle lady, I am delighted by your great penance and this eulogy. O auspiciously intelligent woman, you can choose your boon.

## \|\| 3.6.31 \|\|

*yena te vidyate kāryaṃ vareṇāsminmanogatam \|*  
*tatkariṣye ca bhadraṃ te prasannohaṃ tava vrataiḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Whatever boon seems to be useful to you and is desired by you I shall grant it to you. I am delighted by your rites.”

## \|\| 3.6.32 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*iti śrutvā maheśasya prasannamanasastadā \|*  
*saṃdhyovāca suprasannā praṇamya ca muhurmuhuḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

32\. On hearing these words of Śiva who was delighted, Sandhyā was highly pleased and she said after repeated obeisance.

## \|\| 3.6.33-34 \|\|

*saṃdhyovāca \|*  
*yadi deyo varaḥ prītyā varayogyāsmyahaṃ yadi \|*  
*yadi śuddhāsmyahaṃ jātā tasmātpāpānmaheśvara \|\| 33 \|\|*

*yadi deva prasavro'si tapasā mama sāṃpratam \|*  
*vṛtastadāyaṃ prathamo varo mama vidhīyatām \|\| 34 \|\|*

Sandhyā said:—

33-34. O Lord Śiva, if I am to be favoured with the boon, if I am considered worthy of receiving a boon, if I am purified of that sin, if the lord is delighted with my penance, let the first boon chosen by me be granted.

## \|\| 3.6.35 \|\|

*utpannamātrā deveśa prāṇinosminnabhaḥ sthale \|*  
*na bhavaṃtu samenaiva sakāmāssaṃbhavaṃtu vai \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Let no living being, O lord of the Gods, born in this atmosphere be full of lust at the time of its nativity.

## \|\| 3.6.36 \|\|

*yaddhi vṛttā hi lokeṣu triṣvapi prathitā yathā \|*  
*bhaviṣyāmi tathā nānyā vara eko vṛto mayā \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. This is another boon chosen by me that no other woman shall become so famous in the three worlds as I have become or shall become.

## \|\| 3.6.37 \|\|

*sakāmā mama sṛṣṭistu kutracinna patiṣyati \|*  
*yo me patirbhavennātha sopi me'tisuhṛcca vai \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. No creation of mine shall become lustful or fall anywhere degraded. He who becomes my husband shall be my intimate friend of pure mind.

## \|\| 3.6.38 \|\|

*yo drakṣyati sakāmo māṃ puruṣastasya pauruṣam \|*  
*nāśaṃ gamiṣyati tadā sa ca klībo bhaviṣyati \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Any person who looks at me with lustful eyes shall lose his manliness and become a eunuch.

## \|\| 3.6.39 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*iti śrutvā vacastasyaśśaṃkaro bhaktavatsalaḥ \|*  
*uvāca suprasannātmā niṣpāpāyāstayerite \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. On hearing the words of that woman who had become freed of sin Śiva who is favourably disposed to His devotees and who was delighted at what she had said, spoke as follows.

## \|\| 3.6.40 \|\|

*maheśvara uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu devi ca saṃdhye tvaṃ tvatpāpaṃ bhasmatāṃ gatam \|*  
*tvayi tyakto mayā krodhaḥ śuddhā jātā tapaḥkarāt \|\| 40 \|\|*

\[Śiva said:—\]

40\. O lady Sandhyā, listen. Your sin has been reduced to ashes. I have abandoned my anger towards you. By this penance you have become pure.

## \|\| 3.6.41 \|\|

*yadyadvṛtaṃ tvayā bhadre dattaṃ tadakhilaṃ mayā \|*  
*suprasannena tapasā tava saṃdhye vareṇa hi \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. O gentle lady Sandhyā, whatever you have asked I grant you entirely. I am delighted by this excellent penance of yours.

## \|\| 3.6.42 \|\|

*prathamaṃ śaiśavo bhāvaḥ kaumārākhyo dvitīyakaḥ \|*  
*tṛtīyo yauvano bhāvaścaturtho vārddhakastathā \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. (In all living beings) the first stage shall be infancy, the second childhood, the third youth and the fourth stage shall be old age.

## \|\| 3.6.43 \|\|

*tṛtīye tvatha saṃprāpte vayobhāge śarīriṇaḥ \|*  
*sakāmāssyurdvitīyāṃto bhaviṣyati kvacit kvacit \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. When the third stage in life is reached, the living beings shall become lustful. In some cases it shall be at the end of the second stage.

## \|\| 3.6.44 \|\|

*tapasā tava maryādā jagati sthāpitā mayā \|*  
*utpannamātrā na yathā sakāmāssyuśśarīriṇaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. This new limitation is imposed by me as a result of your penance. No living being shall be lustful at the time of its nativity.

## \|\| 3.6.45 \|\|

*tvaṃ ca loke satībhāvaṃ tādṛśaṃ samavāpnuhi \|*  
*triṣu lokeṣu nānyasyā yādṛśaṃ saṃbhaviṣyati \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. You will attain such a pure chastity as will not be attained by any other woman in the three worlds.

## \|\| 3.6.46 \|\|

*yaḥ paśyati sakāmastvāṃ pāṇigrāhamṛte tava \|*  
*sa sadyaḥ klībatāṃ prāpya durbalatvaṃ gamiṣyati \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Excepting your husband whoever looks at you with lustful eyes shall immediately become impotent and weak.

## \|\| 3.6.47 \|\|

*patistava mahābhāgastaporūpasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*saptakalpāṃtajīvī ca bhaviṣyati saha tvayā \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Your husband shall be one endowed with great fortune, penance and comely features. He shall live for a period of seven Kalpas along with you.

## \|\| 3.6.48 \|\|

*iti te ye varā mattaḥ prārthitāste kṛtā mayā \|*  
*anyacca te vadiṣyāmi pūrvajanmani saṃsthitam \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Thus I have granted you all the boons requested by you. I shall tell you another incident that transpired in the previous birth.

## \|\| 3.6.49 \|\|

*agnau śarītyāgaste pūrvameva pratiśrutaḥ \|*  
*tadupāyaṃ vadāmi tvāṃ tatkuruṣva na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. That you would cast off your body in the fire has been foretold. I shall tell you the means thereof. You will certainly carry it out.

## \|\| 3.6.50 \|\|

*sa ca medhātithiryajñe mune dvādaśavārṣike \|*  
*kṛtsnaprajvalite vahnāvacirāt kriyatāṃ tvayā \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Let that be performed by you at the twelve-year-sacrifice of the sage Medhātithi in the blazing sacrificial fire ere long.

## \|\| 3.6.51 \|\|

*etacchailopatyakāyāṃ caṃdrabhāgānadītaṭe \|*  
*medhātithirmahāyajñaṃ kurute tāpasāśrame \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. In the ridge of this mountain, on the banks of this river Candrabhāgā, Medhātithi is performing a great penance in his hermitage.

## \|\| 3.6.52 \|\|

*tatra gatvā svayaṃ chaṃdaṃ munibhirnnopalakṣitā \|*  
*matprasādādvahnijātā tasya putrī bhaviṣyasi \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. You go there unobserved by the sages. Thanks to my favour, you will become his fire-born daughter.

## \|\| 3.6.53 \|\|

*yaste varo vāñchanīyaḥ svāmī manasi kaścana \|*  
*taṃ nidhāya nijasvāṃte tyaja vahnau vapuḥ svakam \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. If you have chosen in your mind a desirable bridegroom as your husband, you shall think of him while you consign your body into the fire.

## \|\| 3.6.54-55 \|\|

*yadā tvaṃ dāruṇaṃ saṃdhye tapaścarasi parvate \|*  
*yāvaccaturyugaṃ tasya vyatīte tu kṛte yuge \|\| 54 \|\|*

*tretāyāḥ prathame bhāge jātā dakṣasya kanyakā \|*  
*vākpāśśīlasamāpannā yathā yogyaṃ vivāhitāḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

54-55. O Sandhyā, while you were performing severe penance—which had lasted for four yugas—in the earlier part of Tretā Yuga, after the Kṛta Yuga had elapsed, Dakṣa had begotten many chaste daughters who were also duly married.

## \|\| 3.6.56 \|\|

*tanmadhye sa dadau kanyā vidhave saptaviṃśatiḥ \|*  
*candro'nyāssaṃparityajya rohiṇyāṃ prītimānabhūt \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. He gave twenty seven of his daughters to the moon in marriage. But the moon had a special liking for only Rohiṇī and he neglected others.

## \|\| 3.6.57-59 \|\|

*taddhetorhi yadā candraśśapto dakṣeṇa kopinā \|*  
*tadā bhavatyā nikaṭe sarve devāssamāgatāḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

*na dṛṣṭāśca tvayā saṃdhye te devā brahmaṇā saha \|*  
*mayi vinyastamanasā khaṃ ca dṛṣṭvā labhetpunaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

*caṃdrasya śāpamokṣārthaṃ jātā caṃdranadī tadā \|*  
*sṛṣṭā dhātrā tadaivātra medhātithirupasthitaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

57-59. Hence, the moon was cursed by Dakṣa, the redemption being, when he sees the Ether he would find her there. At that time the Gods had come near you but since you were having your mind fixed in me, the Gods in the company of Brahmā were not seen by you. The river Candrabhāgā arose being created by Brahmā for the redemption of the moon from the curse. It was then that Medhātithi arrived here.

## \|\| 3.6.60 \|\|

*tapasā satsamo nāsti na bhūto na bhaviṣyati \|*  
*yena yajñassamārabdho jyotiṣṭomo mahāvidhiḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. There is none equal to him in penance. There has never been such a person, nor will there ever be one. He has now started the sacrifice of Jyotiṣṭoma of many great rites.

## \|\| 3.6.61 \|\|

*tatra prajvalito vahnistasmintyaja vapuḥ svakam \|*  
*supavitrā tvamidānīṃ saṃpūrṇostu paṇastava \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. In that blazing sacrificial fire you shall cast off your body. You are pure now. May your other desires be also fulfilled.

## \|\| 3.6.62 \|\|

*etanmayā sthāpitante kāryārthaṃ bho tapasvini \|*  
*tatkuruṣva mahābhāge yāhi yajñe mahāmuneḥ \|*  
*tasyāhitaṃ ca deveśastatraivāṃtaradhīyata \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. O Hermitess, these things have been ordained by me for my own end. O fortunate woman, do as I instruct you. Go to the sacrifice of that sage.

Thus after instructing her for her welfare the lord vanished from the scene.

## Chapter 7 - Sandhyā gets the name Arundhatī and marries Vasiṣṭha

## \|\| 3.7.1 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*varaṃ dattvā mune tasmin śaṃbhāvaṃtarhite tadā \|*  
*saṃdhyāpyagacchattatraiva yatra medhātithirmuniḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

1\. O sage, when Śiva vanished after granting her the boons, Sandhyā too went to the place where Medhātithi was performing sacrifice.

## \|\| 3.7.2 \|\|

*tatra śaṃbhoḥ prasādena na kenāpyupalakṣitā \|*  
*sasmāra varṇinaṃ taṃ vai svopadeśakaraṃ tapaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. She entered the sacrificial hall without being observed by anyone, thanks to Śiva’s favour. She recalled to her memory the brahmin boy who had instructed her in the procedure of penance.

## \|\| 3.7.3 \|\|

*vasiṣṭhena purā sā tu varṇībhūtvā mahāmune \|*  
*upadiṣṭā tapaścartuṃ vacanātparameṣṭhinaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. O great sage, at the bidding of Brahmā, Vasiṣṭha had assumed the guise of a brahmin boy and instructed her in the rites of penance.

## \|\| 3.7.4-5 \|\|

*tameva kṛtvā manasā tapaścaryopadeśakam \|*  
*patitvena tadā saṃdhyā brāhmaṇaṃ brahmacāriṇam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*samiddhegnau mahāyajñe munibhirnopalakṣitā \|*  
*dṛṣṭā śaṃbhuprasādena sā viveśa vidheḥ sutā \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. Meditating on that Brahmacārin, her tutor in the mode of austerities, Sandhyā thought of him as her future husband, and entered the blazing sacrificial fire unobserved by the sages. She was delighted that it was by Śiva’s favour that she could enter the sacrificial fire.

## \|\| 3.7.6 \|\|

*tasyāḥ puroḍāśamayaṃ śarīraṃ tatkṣaṇāttataḥ \|*  
*dagdhaṃ puroḍāśagaṃdhaṃ tastāra yadalakṣitam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Her body itself had become sacrificial offering in that sacrifice. When it was burnt it could not be distinguished from the ordinary Puroḍāśā since it too had the same fragrance.

## \|\| 3.7.7 \|\|

*vahnistasyāḥ śarīraṃ tu dagdhvā sūryasya maṃḍalam \|*  
*śuddhaṃ praveśayāmāsa śaṃbhorevājñayā punaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. At the bidding of Śiva, the god of fire sent forth her body to the pure zone of the sun.

## \|\| 3.7.8 \|\|

*sūryo tryarthaṃ vibhajyātha taccharīraṃ tadā rathe \|*  
*svakeśaṃ sthāpayāmāsa prītaye pitṛdevayoḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The sun severed her body into two halves and placed the same on his own chariot for the propitiation of the Pitṛs and the Devas.

## \|\| 3.7.9-10 \|\|

*tadūrddhvabhāgastasyāstu śarīrasya munīśvara \|*  
*prātassaṃdhyābhavatsā tu ahorātrādimadhyagā \|\| 9 \|\|*

*taccheṣabhāgastasyāstu ahorātrāṃtamadhyagā \|*  
*sā sāyamabhavatsaṃdhyā pitṛprītipradā sadā \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. O great sage, the upper half of her body became the Prātaḥ Sandhyā (dawn) which is at the beginning or in the middle of a day and night. The lower half of her body became the Sāyaṃsandhyā (dusk) which is in the middle of a day and night. The period is always pleasing to the manes.

## \|\| 3.7.11 \|\|

*sūryodayāttu prathamaṃ yadā syādaruṇodayaḥ \|*  
*prātassaṃdhyā tadodeti devānāṃ prītikāriṇī \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Before the sunrise, when the day breaks, the period is called Prātaḥsandhyā. It delights the Gods.

## \|\| 3.7.12 \|\|

*astaṃ gate tataḥ sūryye śoṇapadmanibhe sadā \|*  
*udeti sāyaṃ saṃdhyāpi pitṝṇāṃ modakāriṇī \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. When the sun has set and assumed the hue of a red lotus, the period of Sāyaṃsandhyā sets in. It is delightful to the manes.

## \|\| 3.7.13 \|\|

*tasyāḥ prāṇāstu manasā śaṃbhunātha dayālunā \|*  
*divyena tu śarīreṇa cakrire hi śarīriṇaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Śiva the merciful, created embodied beings with her vital airs, mind and the divine body.

## \|\| 3.7.14 \|\|

*muneryajñāvasāne tu saṃprāpte muninā tu sā \|*  
*prāptā putrī vahnimadhye taptakāṃcanasuprabhā \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. At the end of the sacrifice, the sage found his daughter in the sacrificial pit shining lustrously like heated gold.

## \|\| 3.7.15 \|\|

*tāṃ jagrāha tadā putrīṃ munurāmodasaṃyutaḥ \|*  
*yajñārthaṃ tāntu saṃsnāpya nijakroḍe dadhau mune \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. With very great delight the sage took up the daughter, O sage, as though she were a sacrificial article. He bathed her and kept her on his lap.

## \|\| 3.7.16 \|\|

*aruṃdhatī tu tasyāstu nāma cakre mahāmuniḥ \|*  
*śiṣyaiḥ parivṛtastatra mahāmodamavāpa ha \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The great sage gave her the name Arundhatī. Surrounded by his disciples he celebrated the event joyously.

## \|\| 3.7.17 \|\|

*viruṇaddhi yato dharmaṃ sā kasmādapi kāraṇāt \|*  
*atastriloke viditaṃ nāma saṃprāpa tatsvayam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The word Arundhatī means “one who does not hinder sacred rites in any manner whatsoever”. She acquired this name which later on became well-known in the three worlds.

## \|\| 3.7.18 \|\|

*yajñaṃ samāpya sa muniḥ kṛtakṛtyabhāvamāsādya saṃpadayutastanayā pralaṃbhāt \|*  
*tasminnijāśramapade saha śiṣyavargaistāmeva satatamasau dayite surarṣe \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. O celestial sage, that sage concluded the sacrifice with great contentment and was delighted at the acquisition of a daughter. He spent his days in the same hermitage along with his disciples, tending the daughter, mercifully.

## \|\| 3.7.19 \|\|

*atha sā vavṛdhe devī tasminmunivarāśrame \|*  
*candrabhāgānadītīre tāpasāraṇyasaṃjñake \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The divine lady grew up in the hermitage, Tāpasāraṇya, on the banks of the river—Candrabhāgā.

## \|\| 3.7.20 \|\|

*saṃprāpte pañcame varṣe candrabhāgāṃ tadā guṇaiḥ \|*  
*tāpasāraṇyamapi sā pavitramakarotsatī \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. When she reached her fifth year, the chaste lady sanctified the environs of the Tāpasāraṇya and the river Candrabhāgā, by virtue of her good qualities.

## \|\| 3.7.21 \|\|

*vivāhaṃ kārayāmāsustasyā brahmasutena vai \|*  
*vasiṣṭhena hyaruṃdhatyā brahmaviṣṇumaheśvarāḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva got her marriage celebrated with Vasiṣṭha, the son of Brahmā.

## \|\| 3.7.22 \|\|

*tadvivāhe mahotsāho vabhūva sukhavarddhanaḥ \|*  
*sarve surāśca munayassukhamāpuḥ paraṃ muno \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. O sage, great festivities in the marriage ceremony increased happiness. The sages and the Gods were very happy on that account.

## \|\| 3.7.23 \|\|

*brahmaviṣṇumaheśānāṃ karanissṛtatoyataḥ \|*  
*saptanadyassamutpannāśśiprādyāssupavitrakāḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. From the water oozing from the hands of Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva, the seven holy rivers Śiprā and others rose and flowed.

## \|\| 3.7.24 \|\|

*aruṃdhatī mahāsādhvī sādhvīnāṃ pravarottamā \|*  
*vasiṣṭhaṃ prāpya saṃreje medhātithisutā mune \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. O sage, Arundhatī, the daughter of Medhātithi, the greatest of all chaste ladies shone all the more on attaining Vasiṣṭha.

## \|\| 3.7.25 \|\|

*yasyāḥ putrāssamutpannāḥ śreṣṭhāśśaktyādayaśśubhāḥ \|*  
*vasiṣṭhaṃ prāpya taṃ kāṃtaṃ saṃreje munisattamāḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. O excellent sage, she secured Vasiṣṭha and bore the auspicious sons Śakti etc.

## \|\| 3.7.26-27 \|\|

*evaṃ saṃdhyācaritraṃ te kathitaṃ munisattama \|*  
*pavitraṃ pāvanaṃ divyaṃ sarvakāmaphalapradam \|\| 26 \|\|*

*ya idaṃ śṛṇuyānnārī puruṣo vā śubhavrataḥ \|*  
*sarvānkāmānavāpnoti nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. O excellent sage, I have narrated to you the story of Sandhyā. It is holy, sanctifying, divine and bestower of all benefits. He or she who hears this story accompanied by auspicious rites attains all cherished desires. There is no doubt about it.

## Chapter 8 - The description of the form and features of Vasanta

## \|\| 3.8.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya vacastasya brahmaṇo hi prajāpateḥ \|*  
*prasannamānaso bhūtvā taṃ provāca sa nāradaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sūta Said:—

1\. After hearing the words of Brahmā, Prajāpati, Nārada became delighted in his mind and spoke these words.

## \|\| 3.8.2 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*brahman vidhe mahābhāga viṣṇuśiṣya mahāmate \|*  
*dhanyastvaṃ śivabhakto hi paratattvapradarśakaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

Nārada said:—

2\. O Brahmā, the great disciple of Viṣṇu, endowed with great intellect, you are a blessed devotee of Śiva and a guide to the understanding of the great principle.

## \|\| 3.8.3 \|\|

*śrāvitā sukathā divyā śivabhaktivivarddhinī \|*  
*aruṃdhatyāstathā tasyāḥ svarūpāyāḥ pare bhave \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. You have narrated the divine story of Arundhatī and her previous form. It increases our devotion to Śiva.

## \|\| 3.8.4 \|\|

*idānīṃ brūhi dharmajña pavitraṃ caritaṃ param \|*  
*śivasya parapāpaghnaṃ maṃgalapradamuttamam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Now, O knower of virtue, please tell me the excellent story of Śiva, that quells all sins and is very excellent bestower of all auspicious benefits.

## \|\| 3.8.5 \|\|

*gṛhītadāre kāme ca dṛṣṭe teṣu gateṣu ca \|*  
*saṃdhyāyāṃ kiṃ tapastaptuṃ gatāyāmabhavattataḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. When Kāma was delighted after taking a wife to himself, when Sandhyā had gone to perform penance and when others had also left, what happened?

## \|\| 3.8.6 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*iti śrutvā vacastasya ṛṣervai bhāvitātmanaḥ \|*  
*suprasannataro bhūtvā brahmā vacanamabravīt \|\| 6 \|\|*

Sūta said:—

6\. On hearing the words of that sage of magnanimous soul, Brahmā became more pleased and spoke as follows:

## \|\| 3.8.7 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*śṛṇu nārada viprendra tadaiva caritaṃ śubham \|*  
*śivalīlānvitaṃ bhaktyā dhanyastvaṃ śivasevakaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

7\. O great brahmin, Nārada, listen with devotion to the auspicious story of Śiva’s divine sports. You are a blessed devotee of Śiva.

## \|\| 3.8.8 \|\|

*ahaṃ vimohitastāta yadaivāṃtarhitaḥ purā \|*  
*aciṃtayaṃ sadāhaṃ tacchaṃbhuvākyaviṣārditaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. O dear one, since I vanished from that place highly distressed by the poisonous words of Śiva, I had been thinking about that alone, since I had been in delusion still.

## \|\| 3.8.9 \|\|

*ciṃtayitvā ciraṃ citte śivamāyāvimohitaḥ \|*  
*śive cerṣyāmakārṣaṃ hi tacchृvṛṇuṣva vadāmi te \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. After thinking about it for a long time I began to nurse malicious grudge against Śiva, here again being deluded by Śiva’s Māyā. I shall explain it to you. Listen.

## \|\| 3.8.10 \|\|

*athāhamagamaṃ tatra yatra dakṣādayaḥ sthitāḥ \|*  
*saratiṃ madanaṃ dṛṣṭvā samadoha hi kiñcana \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Then I went to the place where Dakṣa and others were present. On seeing Kāma in the company of Rati I was a little elated.

## \|\| 3.8.11 \|\|

*dakṣamābhāṣya suprītyā parānputrāṃśca nārada \|*  
*avocaṃ vacanaṃ sohaṃ śivamāyāvimohitaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. O Nārada, addressing Dakṣa and the other sons I spoke these words, deluded by Śiva’s illusion.

## \|\| 3.8.12 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*he dakṣa he marīcyādyāssutāḥ śṛṇuta madvacaḥ \|*  
*śrutvopāyaṃ vidheyaṃ hi mama kaṣṭāpanuttaye \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. “O Dakṣa, O Marīci and others, my sons, listen to my words. After hearing you shall all find out a remedy for dispelling my distress.

## \|\| 3.8.13 \|\|

*kāṃtābhilāṣamātraṃ me dṛṣṭvā śambhuragarhayat \|*  
*māṃ ca yuṣmānmahāyogī dhikkāraṃ kṛtavānbahu \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Taking into consideration the only fact of harbouring a desire for woman Śiva despised me and you. It is because He is a great Yogin that He reproached us much.

## \|\| 3.8.14 \|\|

*tena duḥkhābhitaptohaṃ labhehaṃ śarma na kvacit \|*  
*yathā gṛhṇātu kāṃtāṃ sa sa yatnaḥ kārya eva hi \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Hence I am greatly distressed and I do not get mental peace at all. Such an effort must definitely be made as would make Him take a wife unto Himself.

## \|\| 3.8.15 \|\|

*yathā gṛhṇātu kāṃtāṃ sa sukhī syāṃ duḥkhavarjitaḥ \|*  
*durlabhasya tu kāmo me paraṃ manye vicārataḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. I shall become happy and be free from misery when He takes a wife unto Himself. But on reflection I feel that it is impossible to realise the accomplishment of this desire.

## \|\| 3.8.16 \|\|

*kāṃtābhilāṣamātraṃ me dṛṣṭvā śaṃbhuragarhayat \|*  
*munīnāṃ purataḥ kasmātsa kāṃtāṃ saṃgrahīṣyati \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Taking into consideration the only fact that I harboured a desire for woman, Śiva rebuked me in the presence of sages. How will He then take a wife unto Himself?

## \|\| 3.8.17 \|\|

*kā vā nārī trilokesmin yā bhavettanmanāḥ sthitā \|*  
*yogamārgamavajñāpya tasya mohaṃ kariṣyati \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Who can be that woman in the three worlds who will ever haunt his mind, make him neglect the path of Yoga and delude him?

## \|\| 3.8.18 \|\|

*manmathopi samartho no bhaviṣyatyasya mohane \|*  
*nitāṃtayogī rāmāṇāṃ nāmāpi sahate na saḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Even Kāma will not be competent to delude Him. He is a Yogin of great perfection and He does not brook even the name of women.

## \|\| 3.8.19 \|\|

*agṛhīteṣuṇā caiva hareṇa kathamādinā \|*  
*madhyamā ca bhavetsṛṣṭistadvācā nānyavāritā \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Unless the primordial Being Śiva indulges in sexual sport, the creation would continue to be mediocre, its course being unchecked as the Lord himself has stated.

## \|\| 3.8.20 \|\|

*bhuvi kecidbhaviṣyaṃti māyābaddhā mahāsurāḥ \|*  
*baddhā keciddharernūnaṃ kecicchaṃbhorupāyataḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. On the earth there may be great Asuras bound by illusion. Some are bound by the illusion of Viṣṇu and others by the illusion of Śiva.

## \|\| 3.8.21 \|\|

*saṃsāravimukhe śaṃbhau tathaikāṃtavirāgiṇi \|*  
*asmādṛte na karmānyat kariṣyati na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. In regard to Śiva who has turned away from the world and who is extremely detached, nothing else except the endeavour of Kāma will be effective. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 3.8.22 \|\|

*ityuktvā tanayāṃścāhaṃ dakṣādīn sunirīkṣya ca \|*  
*saratiṃ madanaṃ tatra sānaṃdamagadaṃ tataḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. After saying this and casting meaningful glances at Dakṣa and other sons, I addressed Kāma and Rati with great pleasure.

## \|\| 3.8.23 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*matputra vara kāma tvaṃ sarvathā sukhadāyakaḥ \|*  
*madvacaśśṛṇu suprītyā svapatnyā pitṛvatsala \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. O Kāma, foremost among my sons, you are the bestower of happiness in every respect. Listen to my words with great attention in the company of your wife, O son of great filial affection.

## \|\| 3.8.24 \|\|

*anayā sahacāriṇyā rājase tvaṃ manobhava \|*  
*eṣā ca bhavatā patyā yuktā saṃśobhate bhṛśam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. O Kāma, you shine well with this life-companion of yours. She too shines well with you as her husband.

## \|\| 3.8.25-26 \|\|

*yathā striyā hṛṣīkeśo hariṇā sā yathā ramā \|*  
*kṣaṇadā vidhunā yuktā tayā yukto yathā vidhuḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*tathaiva yuvayośśobhā dāṃpatyaṃ ca puraskṛtam \|*  
*atastvaṃ jagataḥ keturviśvaketurbhaviṣyasi \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. Just as Viṣṇu with Lakṣmī and Lakṣmī with Viṣṇu, just as the night with the moon and the moon with the night, so you two mutually illuminate each other and tend your matrimonial life. Hence you will be the banner of the universe, nay the banner of the whole cosmos.

## \|\| 3.8.27 \|\|

*jagaddhitāya vatsa tvaṃ mohayasva pinākinam \|*  
*yathāśu sumanaśśaṃbhuḥ kuryyāddārapratigraham \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. O dear one, you shall enchant Śiva for the benefit of the universe so that Śiva may be included to take a wife unto Himself.

## \|\| 3.8.28-29 \|\|

*vijane snigdhadeśe tu parvateṣu sarassu ca \|*  
*yatrayatra prayātīśastatra tatrānayā saha \|\| 28 \|\|*

*mohaya tvaṃ yatātmānaṃ vanitāvimukhaṃ haram \|*  
*tvadṛte vidyate nānyaḥ kaścidasya vimohakaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

28-29. In a secluded or in a crowded place, on mountains or in lakes, wherever Śiva goes, you shall follow Him along with your mistress and charm him who has controlled Himself and who is averse to women. Excepting you there is no one to delude Him.243

## \|\| 3.8.30 \|\|

*bhūte hare sānurāge bhavatopi manobhava \|*  
*śāpopaśāṃtirbhavitā tasmādātmahitaṃ kuru \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. O Kāma, it is only when Śiva falls in love that you will get redemption from the course. Hence do what is good for you.

## \|\| 3.8.31-32 \|\|

*sānurāgo varārohāṃ yadīcchati maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*tadā bhavopi yogyāryastvāṃ ca saṃtārayiṣyati \|\| 31 \|\|*

*tasmājjāyādvitīyastvaṃ yatasva haramohane \|*  
*viśvasya bhava ketustvaṃ mohayitvā maheśvaram \|\| 32 \|\|*

31-32. Lord Śiva as a noble Being shall save you only when he falls in love and aspires for a wife. Hence with your wife to help you, strive to captivate Śiva. Earn the laurels of the universe after charming Him.

## \|\| 3.8.33 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*iti śrutvā vaco me hi janakasya jagatprabhoḥ \|*  
*uvāca manmathastathyaṃ tadā māṃ jagatāṃ patim \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. On hearing these words of mine, who am his father and the lord of the universe, Kāma spoke these words to me, the lord of all the worlds.

## \|\| 3.8.34 \|\|

*manmatha uvāca \|*  
*kariṣyehaṃ tava vibho vacanācchaṃbhumohanam \|*  
*kiṃ tu yoṣinmahāstraṃ me tatkāṃtāṃ bhagavan sṛja \|\| 34 \|\|*

Kāma said:—

34\. O lord, I shall cause the delusion of Śiva at your bidding; but my prime weapon is a woman. Hence O lord, you shall create a comely maiden.

## \|\| 3.8.35 \|\|

*mayā saṃmohite śaṃbho yayā tasyānumohanam \|*  
*kartavyamadhunā dhātastatropāyaṃ paraṃ kuru \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. O creator, arrange for the way how Śiva has to be further enchanted after He has been deluded by me.

## \|\| 3.8.36 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*evaṃvādini kaṃdarpe dhātāhaṃ sa prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*kayā saṃmohanīyosāviti ciṃtāmayāmaham \|\| 36 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

36\. When Kāma put forward this suggestion I, the creator, and the Prajāpati (Dakṣa) considered the matter: “By whom is he to be enamoured?”

## \|\| 3.8.37 \|\|

*ciṃtāviṣṭasya me tasya niḥśvāso yo vinissṛtaḥ \|*  
*tasmādvasaṃtassaṃjātaḥ puṣpavrātavibhūṣitaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. While I was agitated with this thought, I heaved a deep sigh from which Spring cropped fully bedecked with clusters of flowers.

## \|\| 3.8.38 \|\|

*śoṇarājīvasaṃkāśaḥ phullatāmarasekṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*saṃdhyoditākhaṃḍaśaśipratimāsyassunāsikaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. He was like a red lotus. His eyes resembled the full blown lotus. His face shone like the full moon rising at dusk. His nose was well-shapped.

## \|\| 3.8.39 \|\|

*śārṅgavaccaraṇāvarttaśśyāmakuṃcitamūrddhajaḥ \|*  
*saṃdhyāṃśumālisadṛśaḥ kuḍaladvayamaṃḍitaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. His feet were arched like a bow. His hair was dark and curly. He was decorated with two ear-rings. He looked bright as the morning sun.

## \|\| 3.8.40 \|\|

*pramattebhagatiḥ pīnāyatadorunnatāṃsakaḥ \|*  
*kaṃbugrīvassuvistīrṇahṛdayaḥ pīnasanmukhaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. His gait was majestic like that of an elephant in its rut. His arms were long and stout. His shoulders were raised. His neck resembled the conch-shell. His chest was very broad. His face was plump and finely shaped.

## \|\| 3.8.41 \|\|

*sarvāṃgasundaraḥ śyāmassampūrṇassarvalakṣaṇaiḥ \|*  
*darśanīyatamassarvamohanaḥ kāmavarddhanaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. He was comely in appearance, dark-complexioned and endowed with all characteristic marks. He was very handsome to look at, capable of enchanting everyone and of heightening feelings of love.

## \|\| 3.8.42 \|\|

*etādṛśe samutpanne vasaṃte kusumākare \|*  
*vavau vāyussusurabhiḥ pādapā api puṣpitāḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. When spring, the storehouse of flowers, endowed with these features was born, there blew a very fragrant wind. All the trees put forth blossoms.

## \|\| 3.8.43 \|\|

*pikā vineduśśataśaḥ paṃcamaṃ madhurasvanāḥ \|*  
*praphullapadmā abhavansarasyaḥ svacchapuṣkarāḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Hundreds of sweet-throated cuckoos cooed the note of Pañcama sweetly. The clean and clear lakes abounded in full-blown lotuses.

## \|\| 3.8.44 \|\|

*tamutpannamahaṃ vīkṣya tadā tādṛśamuttamam \|*  
*hiraṇyagarbho madanamagadaṃ madhuraṃ vacaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. On seeing such an excellent Being born thus, I, Brahmā (Hiraṇyagarbha) spoke these sweet words to Kāma.

## \|\| 3.8.45 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|\| evaṃ sa manmathanibhassadā sahacarobhavat \|*  
*ānukūlyaṃ tava kṛtaḥ sarvaṃ deva kariṣyati \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. O God, thus a constant companion for you has come to exist. He too resembles you. He will render favourable service unto you.

## \|\| 3.8.46 \|\|

*yathāgneḥ pavano mitraṃ sarvatropakariṣyati \|*  
*tathāyaṃ bhavato mitraṃ sadā tvāmanuyāsyati \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Just as the wind, the friend of fire, helps it everywhere, so also this spring will always help you.

## \|\| 3.8.47 \|\|

*vasaṃteraṃtahetutvādvasaṃtākhyo bhavatvayam \|*  
*tavānugamanaṃ karma tathā lokānurañjanam \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Since he is the final cause for a permanent abode (after marriage) let him be known as Vasanta. His duty is to follow you and to delight all people.

## \|\| 3.8.48 \|\|

*asau vasaṃtaśṛṃgāro vāsaṃto malayānilaḥ \|*  
*bhavettu suhṛdo bhāvassadā tvadvaśavarttinaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Let the Malaya breeze, the elegance of your person, be your constant companion as he remains under your control.

## \|\| 3.8.49 \|\|

*viṣvokādyāstathā hāvāścatuṣṣaṣṭikalāstathā \|*  
*ratyāḥ kurvaṃtu sauhṛdyaṃ suhṛdaste yathā tava \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. The feminine coquettish gestures like the affected indifference in amorous dalliance and the sixty-four fine arts shall be the friends of your wife Rati in the some manner as there are your friends.

## \|\| 3.8.50 \|\|

*ebhissahacaraiḥ kāma vasaṃta pramukhairbhavān \|*  
*mohayasva mahādevaṃ ratyā saha mahodyataḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. O Kāma, in the company of Rati and these companions, Vasanta and others, you shall exert yourself in charming Lord Śiva.

## \|\| 3.8.51 \|\|

*ahaṃ tāṃ kāminīṃ tāta bhāvayiṣyāmi yatnataḥ \|*  
*manasā suvicāryaiva yā haraṃ mohayiṣyati \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. O dear one, I shall conceive and create that lovely woman who will finally captivate.

## \|\| 3.8.52 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*evamukto mayā kāmaḥ surajyeṣṭhena harṣitaḥ \|*  
*nanāma caraṇau me'pi sa patnī sahitastadā \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. When Kāma was thus addressed by me (Brahmā), he was delighted and he fell at my feet along with his wife and offered obeisance.

## \|\| 3.8.53 \|\|

*dakṣaṃ praṇamya tān sarvānmānasānabhivādya ca \|*  
*yatrātmā gatavāñśaṃbhustatsthānaṃ manmatho yayau \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. He bowed to Dakṣa and paid respects to my mental sons. He then went to the place where Śiva, the supreme Soul had gone.

## Chapter 9 - The power of Kāma and the birth of his attendants

## \|\| 3.9.1 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*tasmin gate sānucare śivasthānaṃ ca manmathe \|*  
*caritramabhavaccitraṃ tacchṛṇuṣva munīśvara \|\| 1 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

1\. O great sage, when Kāma went to Śiva’s abode along with his attendants an adversely surprising incident occurred to which listen please.

## \|\| 3.9.2 \|\|

*gatvā tatra mahāvīro manmatho mohakārakaḥ \|*  
*svaprabhāvaṃ tatānāśu mohayāmāsa prāṇinaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. After going there, the heroic Kāma competent to enchant others spread all his wiles and charmed all living beings.

## \|\| 3.9.3 \|\|

*vasaṃtopi prabhāvaṃ svaṃ cakāra haramohanam \|*  
*sarve vṛkṣā ekadaiva praphullā abhavanmune \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. O sage, spring too showed his prowess in order to delude Śiva. All the trees simultaneously bloomed.

## \|\| 3.9.4 \|\|

*vividhānkṛtavānyatnān ratyā saha manobhavaḥ \|*  
*jīvāssarve vaśaṃ yātāssagaṇeśaśśivo na hi \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Kāma and Rati played many a trick. All living beings fell victims of their wiles but not Śiva, the lord of Gaṇas.

## \|\| 3.9.5 \|\|

*samadhormadanasyāsanprayāsā nipphalā mune \|*  
*jagāma sa mama sthānaṃ nivṛttya vimadastadā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. O sage, the efforts of Kāma who was accompanied by spring were futile. He returned to his residence being cured of his arrogance.

## \|\| 3.9.6 \|\|

*kṛtvā praṇāmaṃ vidhaye mahyaṃ gadgadayā girā \|*  
*uvāca madano māṃ codāsīno vimado mune \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. O sage, Kāma saluted me, and bereft of arrogance and completely despondent he told me in faltering voice.

## \|\| 3.9.7 \|\|

*kāma uvāca \|*  
*brahman śaṃbhurmohanīyo na vai yogaparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*na śaktirmama nānyasya tasya śaṃbhorhi mohane \|\| 7 \|\|*

Kāma said:—

7\. O Brahmā, Śiva, an expert in Yogic practices cannot be charmed. Neither I nor anyone else has the power to enchant Siva.

## \|\| 3.9.8 \|\|

*samitreṇa mayā brahmannupāyā vividhāḥ kṛtāḥ \|*  
*ratyā sahākhilāste ca niṣphalā abhavañcchive \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. O Brahmā, different tricks were tried by me and my friends as well as by Rati. All those became futile in regard to Śiva.

## \|\| 3.9.9 \|\|

*śṛṇu brahmanyathā'smābhiḥ kṛtāṃ hi haramohane \|*  
*prayāsā vividhāstāta gadatastānmune mama \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. O Brahmā, listen to the different kinds of efforts undertaken by us in trying to enchant Him and the manner we did them I shall explain, O sage.

## \|\| 3.9.10-11 \|\|

*yadā samādhimāśritya sthitaśśaṃbhurniyaṃtritaḥ \|*  
*tadā sugaṃdhivātena śītalenātiveginā \|\| 10 \|\|*

*udvījayāmi rudraṃ sma nityaṃ mohanakāriṇā \|*  
*prayatnato mahādevaṃ samādhisthaṃ trilocanam \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. When Śiva was in the state of trance with full control of senses, I tried to agitate him—the three-eyed lord Śiva, through the fragrant cool breeze that blew with force and that usually thrilled everyone.

## \|\| 3.9.12 \|\|

*svasāyakāṃstathā paṃca samādāya śarāsanam \|*  
*tasyābhito bhramaṃtastu mohayaṃstadga ṇānaham \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. I lifted up my bow and fitted my reputed five arrows. Going round him I tried to enchant him.

## \|\| 3.9.13 \|\|

*mama praveśamātreṇa suvaśyāssarvajaṃtavaḥ \|*  
*abhavadvikṛto naiva śaṃkarassagaṇaḥ prabhuḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Even as I entered the zone, the living beings fell into my power but lord Śiva and his Gaṇas were not moved at all.

## \|\| 3.9.14 \|\|

*yadā himavataḥ prasthaṃ sa gataḥ pramathādhipaḥ \|*  
*tatrāgatastadaivāhaṃ saratissamadhurvidhe \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. O Brahmā, when Śiva went to the Himālayan ridge, Rati, Spring and I reached the place.

## \|\| 3.9.15 \|\|

*yadā meruṃ gato rudro yadā vā nāgakeśaram \|*  
*kailāsaṃ vā yadā yātastatrāhaṃ gatavāṃstadā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Wherever He went whether on Meru\[1\] Nāgakeśara or Kailāsa, I too went there immediately.

## \|\| 3.9.16 \|\|

*yadā tyaktasamādhistu harastasthau kadācana \|*  
*tadā tasya puraścakrayugaṃ racitavānaham \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Whenever Śiva was out of Samādhi I used to place a pair of Cakravāka birds in front of Him.

## \|\| 3.9.17 \|\|

*tacca bhrūyugalaṃ brahman hāvabhāvayutaṃ muhuḥ \|*  
*nānābhāvānakārṣīcca dāṃpatyakramamuttamam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. O Brahmā, those birds exhibited diverse gestures of amorous dalliance with brows and other limbs.

## \|\| 3.9.18 \|\|

*nīlakaṃṭhaṃ mahādevaṃ sagaṇaṃ tatpuraḥsthitāḥ \|*  
*akārṣumohitaṃ bhāvaṃ mṛgāśca pakṣiṇastathā \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Many pairs of deer and birds, playing about in front of the great lord Śiva, indeed exhibited many gestures of love to excite Him.

## \|\| 3.9.19 \|\|

*mayūramithunaṃ tatrākārṣīdbhāvaṃ rasotsukam \|*  
*vividhāṃ gatimāśritya pārśve tasya purastathā \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Pairs of peacocks exhibited various gestures of pleasing eagerness with their gambolling tricks at His sides and in front of Him.

## \|\| 3.9.20 \|\|

*nālabhadvivaraṃ tasmin kadācidapi maccharaḥ \|*  
*satyaṃ bravīmi lokeśa mama śaktirna mohane \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Never did my arrow find any vulnerable point in him. O lord of the worlds, I tell you the truth. I am incompetent to enthral Him.

## \|\| 3.9.21 \|\|

*madhurapyakarotkarma yuktaṃ yattasya mohane \|*  
*tacchṛṇuṣva mahābhāga satyaṃ satyaṃ vadāmyaham \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Spring too did the needful in enchanting Him. O, listen to it, O fortunate Being. I tell you the truth, the truth alone.

## \|\| 3.9.22-23 \|\|

*caṃpakānkeśarānvālānkāraṇānpāṭalāṃstathā \|*  
*nāgakeśarapunnāgānkiṃśukānketakānkarān \|\| 22 \|\|*

*māgaṃdhimallikāparṇabharānkuravakāṃstathā \|*  
*utphullayati tatra sma yatra tiṣṭhati vai haraḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. He caused the various kinds of flowers to bloom in the place where Śiva was stationed—flowers such as Campakas, Keśaras, Punnāgas, Ketakas, Mallikās, Kurabakas etc. etc.

## \|\| 3.9.24 \|\|

*sarāṃsyutphullapadmāni vījayan malayānilaiḥ \|*  
*yatnātsugaṃdhīnyakarodatīva giriśāśrame \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. He made the lakes abounding in full-blown lotuses in the hermitage of Śiva, very fragrant by causing Malaya breezes to blow.

## \|\| 3.9.25 \|\|

*latāssarvāssumanaso dadhuraṃkurasaṃcayān \|*  
*vṛkṣāṃkaṃ cirabhāvena veṣṭayaṃti sma tatra ca \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. He made creepers full of flowers twine round trees as if resting on their laps with great attachment—Seedlings of Dhattūra were scattered to beautify the place.

## \|\| 3.9.26 \|\|

*tānvṛkṣāṃśca supuṣpaughān taiḥ sugaṃdhisamīraṇaiḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā kāmavaśaṃ yātā munayopi pare kimu \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. On seeing the trees abounding in beautiful flowers rustling in the fragrant breeze, even the sages became slaves of Kāma, then what about other (ordinary mortals)?

## \|\| 3.9.27 \|\|

*evaṃ satyapi śaṃbhorna dṛṣṭaṃ mohasya kāraṇam \|*  
*bhāvamātramakārṣīnno kopo mayyapi śaṃkaraḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. In spite of all these, no cause of deflection from steadiness was seen in Śiva who did not evince any sentimental feeling, not even anger towards me.

## \|\| 3.9.28 \|\|

*iti sarvamahaṃ dṛṣṭvā jñātvā tasya ca bhāvanām \|*  
*vimukhohaṃ śaṃbhumohānniyataṃ te vadāmyaham \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. On seeing these and realising His ideal conception I am averse to any further attempt at deluding Śiva. This is my firm opinion that I tell you.

## \|\| 3.9.29 \|\|

*tasya tyaktasamādhestu kṣaṇaṃ no dṛṣṭigocare \|*  
*śaknuyāmo vayaṃ sthātuṃ taṃ rudraṃ ko vimohayet \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. When he finally eschews Samādhi we cannot even stand in His presence, within sight. Who can think of charming Him?

## \|\| 3.9.30 \|\|

*jvaladagniprakāśākṣaṃ jaṭṭārāśikarālinam \|*  
*śṛṃgiṇaṃ vīkṣya kassthātuṃ brahman śaknoti tatpuraḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. O Brahmā, who can stand facing Him with eyes blazing like fire and as fearful as flocks of large alligators or a horned animal.

## \|\| 3.9.31 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*mano bhavavacaścetthaṃ śrutvāhaṃ caturānanaḥ \|*  
*vivakṣurapi nāvocaṃ ciṃtāviṣṭo'bhavaṃ tadā \|\| 31 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

31\. On hearing these words of Kāma I, the four-faced lord, though desirous of saying something did not say anything and was agitated with anxious thoughts.

## \|\| 3.9.32 \|\|

*mohanehaṃ samartho na harasyeti manobhavaḥ \|*  
*vacaḥ śrutvā mahāduḥkhānniraśvasamahaṃ mune \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. On hearing the words of Kāma—“I am incompetent to enchant Śiva”,O sage, I heaved a deep sigh due to extreme sorrow.

## \|\| 3.9.33 \|\|

*niśśvāsamārutā me hi nānā rūpamahābalaḥ \|*  
*jātā gatā lolajihvā lolāścātibhayaṃkarāḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The gusts of wind generated by my deep sighs were of various forms and very violent. They were tremulous and terrible and appeared to have shaking tongues (of flames).

## \|\| 3.9.34 \|\|

*avādayaṃta te sarve nānāvādyānasaṃkhyakān \|*  
*paṭahādigaṇāstāṃstān vikarālānmahāravān \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. They played on different musical instruments, drums etc. of terrible nature and of loud sound.

## \|\| 3.9.35 \|\|

*atha te mama niśśvāsasaṃbhavāśca mahāgaṇāḥ \|*  
*mārayacchedayetyūcurbrahmaṇo me puraḥ sthitāḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. The groups of beings issuing forth from my deep breaths stood in front of me, Brahmā shouting “Kill!—Cut!”

## \|\| 3.9.36 \|\|

*teṣāṃ tu vadatāṃ tatra mārayacchedayeti mām \|*  
*vacaḥ śrutvā vidhiṃ kāmaḥ pravaktumupacakrame \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. While they were shouting “Kill—Cut”, Kāma heard those words and began to speak to me.

## \|\| 3.9.37 \|\|

*mune'tha māṃ samābhāṣya tān dṛṣṭvā madano gaṇān \|*  
*uvāca vārayan brahmangaṇānāmagrataḥ smaraḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. O Brahminical sage, on seeing the groups of beings Kāma stopped them and on their presence, said.

## \|\| 3.9.38 \|\|

*kāma uvāca \|*  
*he brahman he prajānātha sarvasṛṣṭipravartaka \|*  
*utpannāḥ ka ime vīrā vikarālā bhayaṃkarāḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

Kāma said:—

38\. O Brahmā, O lord of subjects, O initiator of all creations, who are these terrible, awful heroes?

## \|\| 3.9.39 \|\|

*kiṃ karmaite kariṣyaṃti kutra sthāsyaṃti vā vidhe \|*  
*kinnāmadheyā ete tadvada tatra niyojaya \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. O Brahmā what is the work that these will be doing? Tell me. where will they be staying? Please employ them there.

## \|\| 3.9.40 \|\|

*niyojya tānnije kṛtye sthānaṃ dattvā ca nāma ca \|*  
*māmājñāpaya deveśa kṛpāṃ kṛtvā yathocitām \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. O lord of Gods, after employing them in their task and assigning them proper names and places, be pleased to assign me my future course of action.

## \|\| 3.9.41 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*iti tadvākyamākarṇya mune'haṃ lokakārakaḥ \|*  
*tamavocaṃ ha madanaṃ teṣāṃ karmādikaṃ diśan \|\| 41 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

41\. O sage, on hearing the words of Kāma, I, the creator of the universe, spoke to him showing him the task of the Gaṇas.

## \|\| 3.9.42 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*eta utpannamātrā hi mārayetyavadan vacaḥ \|*  
*muhurmuhuratomīṣāṃ nāma māreti jāyatām \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Even as they were born they shouted “Māraya” “Kill”, very frequently. Hence let their names be “Māras.”

## \|\| 3.9.43 \|\|

*sadaiva vighnaṃ jaṃtūnāṃ kariṣyanti gaṇā ime \|*  
*vinā nijārcanaṃ kāma nānā kāmaratātmanām \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. These groups of beings will hinder the activities of all creatures, O Kāma, except Your Worship as they are engaged in various avocations of love.

## \|\| 3.9.44 \|\|

*tavānugamane karma mukhyameṣāṃ manobhava \|*  
*sahāyino bhaviṣyaṃti sadā tava na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. O Kāma, their chief occupation will be to follow you. There is no doubt that they will assist you always.

## \|\| 3.9.45 \|\|

*yatrayatra bhavān yātā svakarmārthaṃ yadā yadā \|*  
*gaṃtā sa tatratatraite sahāyārthaṃ tadātadā \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Wherever you go for fulfilling your duty, whenever it be, they will invariably follow you and render assistance.

## \|\| 3.9.46 \|\|

*cittabhrāṃtiṃ kariṣyaṃti tvadastravaśavartinām \|*  
*jñānināṃ jñānamārgaṃ ca vighnayiṣyaṃti sarvathā \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. They will create confusion in the minds of those who fall as victims to your weapons. They will hinder wise people in the path of knowledge in all possible ways.

## \|\| 3.9.47 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya vaco me hi saratissamahānugaḥ \|*  
*kiṃcitprasannavadano babhūva munisattama \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. O excellent sage, on hearing these words of mine, Kāma along with his mistress Rati and his comrade spring delighted a little.

## \|\| 3.9.48 \|\|

*śrutvā tepi gaṇāssarve madanaṃ māṃ ca sarvataḥ \|*  
*parivāryya yathākāmaṃ tasthustatra nijākṛtim \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. The groups of beings too, after hearing this surrounded me and Kāma and stood in their own shape.

## \|\| 3.9.49 \|\|

*atha brahmā smaraṃ prītyā'gadanme kuru śāsanam \|*  
*ebhissahaiva gaccha tvaṃ punaśca haramohane \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Then I, Brahmā, spoke to Kāma lovingly—“Do my bidding. Let these beings accompany you. You shall go again to enthral śiva.

## \|\| 3.9.50 \|\|

*mana ādhāya yavāddhi kuru māragaṇaissaha \|*  
*moho bhavedyathā śaṃbhordāragrahaṇahetave \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. With full attention you put forth further efforts so that Śiva may suffer delusion and take a wife unto Himself.

## \|\| 3.9.51 \|\|

*ityākarṇya vacaḥ kāmaḥ provāca vacanaṃ punaḥ \|*  
*devarṣe gauravaṃ matvā praṇamya vinayena mām \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. O celestial sage, on hearing these words, Kāma humbly paid homage to me and considering the gravity of the matter spoke to me again.

## \|\| 3.9.52 \|\|

*kāma uvāca \|*  
*mayā samyak kṛtaṃ karma mohane tasya yatnataḥ \|*  
*tanmoho nābhavattāta na bhaviṣyati nādhunā \|\| 52 \|\|*

Kāma said:—

52\. I have already made sufficient efforts in this matter of enchanting Him. The delusion could not be effected. Nor it is going to take place now. Nor will it ever take place.

## \|\| 3.9.53 \|\|

*tava vāggauravaṃ matvā dṛṣṭvā māragaṇānapi \|*  
*gamiṣyāmi punastatra sadārohaṃ tvadājñayā \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Acting on your directive after giving it the due honour and after visiting my troops I shall go again with all pomp and show.

## \|\| 3.9.54 \|\|

*mano niścitametaddhi tanmoho na bhaviṣyati \|*  
*bhasma kuryānna me dehamiti śaṃkāsti me vidhe \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. But I am certain that He will not be deluded. O Brahmā I have fears that He may reduce me to ashes.

## \|\| 3.9.55 \|\|

*ityuktvā samadhuḥ kāmassaratissabhayastadā \|*  
*yayau māragaṇaiḥ sārddhaṃ śivasthānaṃ munīśvara \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. O great sage, after saying thus Kāma, accompanied by Vasanta and Rati started with his troops to the abode of Śiva, despite the fear lurking in his mind.

## \|\| 3.9.56 \|\|

*pūrvavat svaprabhāvaṃ ca cakre manasijastadā \|*  
*bahūpāyaṃ sa hi madhurvividhāṃ buddhimāvahan \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Kāma employed all his wiles as before. Vasanta too employed various means racking his brain in diverse ways.

## \|\| 3.9.57 \|\|

*upāyaṃ sa cakārāti tatra māragaṇo'pi ca \|*  
*mohobhavanna vai śaṃbhorapi kaścitparātmanaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. He used many tactics. His troops too tried their best. But Śiva, the Great Soul, was not afflicted the least.

## \|\| 3.9.58 \|\|

*nivṛttya punarāyāto mama sthānaṃ smarastadā \|*  
*āsīnmāragaṇo'garvo'harṣo mepi purasthitaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Kāma then returned to my abode. I had great pride in his troops but now distress and discomfit stood facing me.

## \|\| 3.9.59 \|\|

*kāmaḥ provāca māṃ tāta praṇamya ca nirutsavaḥ \|*  
*sthitvā mama puro'garvo māraiśca madhunā tadā \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. O dear, bowing to me with despair and dejection while standing before me without pride and arrogance, along with his troops and Vasanta, Kāma spoke to me in these words.

## \|\| 3.9.60 \|\|

*kṛtaṃ pūrvādadhikataḥ karma tanmohane vidhe \|*  
*nābhavattasya mohopi kaściddhyānaratātmanaḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. O Brahmā, more efforts were put by us to enthral Him, but they all went in vain as He was absorbed in deep meditation.

## \|\| 3.9.61 \|\|

*na dagdhā me tanuścaiva tatra tena dayālunā \|*  
*kāraṇaṃ pūrvapuṇyaṃ ca nirvikārī sa vai prabhuḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. There my body was not reduced to ashes because He is merciful. My previous merits too may have been the cause. As for the lord there is no affectation or change in Him.

## \|\| 3.9.62 \|\|

*cedvaraste haro bhāryāṃ gṛhṇīyāditi padmaja \|*  
*paropāyaṃ kuru tadā vigarva iti me matiḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. O Brahmā, if you desire that Śiva should take a wife unto Himself, you should employ some means with modesty. This is what I think proper in the circumstances.

## \|\| 3.9.63 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityuktvā saparīvāro yayau kāmassvamāśramam \|*  
*praṇamya māṃ smaran śaṃbhuṃ garvadaṃ dīnavatsalam \|\| 63 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

63\. Saying this, Kāma returned to his abode along with his followers after saluting me and remembering Śiva, the destroyer of arrogance and the favourite of His devotees.

## Chapter 10 - Brahmā-Viṣṇu dialogue

## \|\| 3.10.1 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*brahman vidhe mahābhāga dhanyastvaṃ śivasaktadhīḥ \|*  
*kathitaṃ sucaritraṃ te śaṃkarasya parātmanaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Nārada said:—

1\. O Brahmā, the fortunate, the dispenser of the fruits of our actions, you are a blessed devotee of Śiva, as your mind is fixed in him. You have narrated to me the good story of Śiva, the great soul.

## \|\| 3.10.2 \|\|

*nijāśrame gate kāme sagaṇe saratau tataḥ \|*  
*kimāsītkimakārṣīstvaṃ taścaritraṃ vadādhunā \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. When Kāma returned to his hermitage with Rati and his followers what happened and what steps you took? Please narrate that now.

## \|\| 3.10.3 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*śṛṇu nārada suprītyā caritraṃ śaśimaulinaḥ \|*  
*yasya śravaṇamātreṇa nirvikāro bhavennaraḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

3\. O Nārada listen lovingly to the story of the moon-crested lord, a mere listening to which makes a man free from depravity and decay.

## \|\| 3.10.4 \|\|

*nijāśramaṃ gate kāme parivārasamanvite \|*  
*yadbabhūva tadā jātaṃ taccaritraṃ nibodha me \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. When Kāma returned to his abode with Rati and his followers what happened next, you can hear from me in full detail.

## \|\| 3.10.5 \|\|

*naṣṭobhūnnārada mado vismayo'bhūcca me hṛdi \|*  
*nirānaṃdasya ca mune'pūrṇo nijamanorathe \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. O sage Nārada, my arrogance was quashed when my desire remained unrealised. And surprise filled my dissatisfied and distressed heart.

## \|\| 3.10.6 \|\|

*aśocaṃ bahudhā citte gṛhṇīyātsa kathaṃ striyam \|*  
*nirvikārī jitātmā sa śaṃkaro yogatatparaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. How will Śiva who is free from depravity, who has conquered himself and who is devoted to Yogic practices take up a wife unto himself? Thinking thus I bewailed a lot.

## \|\| 3.10.7 \|\|

*itthaṃ vicārya bahudhā tadāhaṃ vimado mune \|*  
*hariṃ taṃ so'smaraṃ bhaktyā śivātmānaṃ svadehadam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Anxiously thinking all this about, O sage, I became free from haughtiness. I remembered Viṣṇu who is identical with Śiva and who is the cause of my origin.

## \|\| 3.10.8 \|\|

*astavaṃ ca śubhastotrairdīnavākyasamanvitaiḥ \|*  
*tacchrutvā bhagavānāśu babhūvāvirhi me purā \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. I eulogised Him with auspicious hymns supplemented by statements of my miserable predicament on hearing which the lord appeared before me immediately.

## \|\| 3.10.9 \|\|

*caturbhujoraviṃdākṣaḥ śaṃravavārja gadādharaḥ \|*  
*lasatpīta paṭaśśyāmatanurbhaktapriyo hariḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The lord Viṣṇu with four arms, lotus-like eyes, holding conch, lotus and mace in his hands and wearing the refulgent yellow robe, dark-complexioned and the beloved of the devotees.

## \|\| 3.10.10 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā tādṛśamahaṃ suśaraṇyaṃ muhurmuhuḥ \|*  
*astavaṃ ca punaḥ premṇā bāṣpagadgadayā girā \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. On seeing him in that form I eulogised him again with devotion and words choked with tears. I considered him as my sole refuge.

## \|\| 3.10.11 \|\|

*harirākarṇya tatstotraṃ suprasanna uvāca mām \|*  
*duḥkhahā nijabhaktānāṃ brahmāṇaṃ śaraṇaṃ gatam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. On hearing this psalm of prayer, Viṣṇu, the destroyer of the miseries of his devotees, became delighted and spoke to me who sought refuge in him.

## \|\| 3.10.12 \|\|

*hariruvāca \|*  
*vidhe brahman mahāprājña dhanyastvaṃ lokakāraka \|*  
*kimarthaṃ smaraṇaṃ me'dya kṛtaṃ ca kriyate nutiḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

Viṣṇu said:—

12\. “O Brahmā of great intellect, you are the blessed creator of the world. Why did you remember me? Why do you laud me?

## \|\| 3.10.13 \|\|

*kiṃ jātaṃ te mahadduḥkhaṃ madagre tadvadādhunā \|*  
*śamayiṣyāmi tatsarvaṃ nātra kāryyā vicāraṇā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. What great misery has befallen you? Tell me now. I shall quell it entirely. You need not entertain any doubt in this respect.”

## \|\| 3.10.14 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*iti viṣṇorvacaśśrutvā kiṃciducchavasitānanaḥ \|*  
*avoca vacanaṃ viṣṇuṃ praṇamya sukṛtāṃjaliḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

14\. On hearing the words of Viṣṇu I heaved a sigh of relief and raised my face. I spoke to Viṣṇu with due salutations and palms joined in reverence.

## \|\| 3.10.15 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*devadeva ramānātha madvārtāṃ śṛṇu mānada \|*  
*śrutvā ca karuṇāṃ kṛtvā hara duḥkhaṃ kamāvaha \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. O lord of Lakṣmī, lord of Gods, please listen to my submission, O bestower of Honour. On hearing it please take pity, remove my misery and bestow happiness on me.

## \|\| 3.10.16 \|\|

*rudrasaṃmohanārthaṃ hi kāmaṃ preṣitavānaham \|*  
*parivārayutaṃ viṣṇo samāramadhubāṃdhavam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. O Viṣṇu, I sent Kāma with his followers, Māras, Spring and others in order to fascinate Rudra.

## \|\| 3.10.17 \|\|

*cakruste vividhopāyān niṣphalā abhavaṃśca te \|*  
*abhavattasya saṃmoho yoginassamadarśinaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. They employed various means but in vain. He, the ascetic of equanimity, was not moved at all.

## \|\| 3.10.18 \|\|

*ityākarṇya vaco me sa harirmāṃ prāha vismitaḥ \|*  
*vijñātākhiladajñānī śivatattvaviśāradaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. On hearing these words of mine Viṣṇu the omniscient who is conversant in the principles of Śiva-cult was surprised and spoke to me thus.

## \|\| 3.10.19 \|\|

*\|\| viṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*kasmāddhetoriti matistava jātā pitāmaha \|*  
*sarvaṃ vicārya sudhiyā brahman satyaṃ hi tadvada \|\| 19 \|\|*

Viṣṇu said:—

19\. O Brahmā, how is it that such an idea entered into your mind? Considering everything sensibly tell me the truth.

## \|\| 3.10.20 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*śṛṇu tāta caritraṃ tat tava māyā vimohinī \|*  
*tadadhīnaṃ jagatsarvaṃ sukhaduḥkhāditatparam \|\| 20 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

20\. Dear lord, hear the story. Your magic is very fascinating. The world is attracted by it. Happiness and misery are based on the same.

## \|\| 3.10.21 \|\|

*yayaiva preṣitaścāhaṃ pāpaṃ kartuṃ samudyataḥ \|*  
*āsaṃ tacchṛṇu deveśa vadāmi tava śāsanāt \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Induced by that I resolved on committing the sin. Please listen. At your bidding I shall narrate it in detail.

## \|\| 3.10.22 \|\|

*sṛṣṭiprāraṃbhasamaye daśa putrā hi jajñire \|*  
*dakṣādyāstanayā caikā vāgbhavāpyatisundarī \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. At the beginning of the creation ten sons were born to me together with a very beautiful daughter originating from my speech.

## \|\| 3.10.23 \|\|

*dharmo vakṣaḥsthalātkāmo manasonyopi dehataḥ \|*  
*jātāstatra sutāṃ dṛṣṭvā mama moho bhavaddhare \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Dharma originated from the heart and Kāma from the various parts of my body. O Viṣṇu, on seeing my daughter I was highly fascinated.

## \|\| 3.10.24 \|\|

*kudṛṣṭyā tāṃ samadrākṣa tava māyāvimohitaḥ \|*  
*tatkṣaṇāddhara āgatya māmanindatsutānapi \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. I looked at her with a distorted vision since I had been deluded by your Māyā. Immediately Śiva came there and reproached me and my sons too.

## \|\| 3.10.25 \|\|

*dhikkāraṃ kṛtavān sarvānnijaṃ matvā paraprabhum \|*  
*jñāninaṃ yoginaṃ nāthābhoginaṃ vijitendriyam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. He rebuked us considering Himself the sole lord, possessed of supreme knowledge and adept in Yogic practices and an enjoyer with full control over all sense-organs.

## \|\| 3.10.26 \|\|

*putro bhūtvā mama hare'nindanmāṃ ca samakṣataḥ \|*  
*iti duḥkhaṃ mahanme hi taduktaṃ tava sannidhau \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. O Viṣṇu, my sorrow is that even after manifesting Himself as my son He reproached me face to face. I have mentioned it to you now.

## \|\| 3.10.27 \|\|

*gṛhṇīyādyadi patnīṃ sa syāṃ sukhī naṣṭaduḥkhadhī \|*  
*etadarthaṃ samāyātuśśaraṇaṃ tava keśava \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. If He were to take a wife unto Himself I shall become happy and forget all my miseries. O Keśava, it is for this purpose that I have sought refuge in you.

## \|\| 3.10.28 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya vaco me hi brahmaṇo madhusūdanaḥ \|*  
*vihasya māṃ drutaṃ prāha harṣayanbhavakārakam \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. On hearing these words of mine, Viṣṇu laughed and spoke immediately delighting me, the cause of entire creation.

## \|\| 3.10.29 \|\|

*viṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*vidhe śṛṇu hi madvākyaṃ sarvaṃ bhramanivāraṇam \|*  
*sarvaṃ vedāgamādīnāṃ saṃmataṃ paramārthataḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

Viṣṇu said:—

29\. O Brahmā listen to my words in full. It will eradicate your frustration. It will be consistent with what is said in the Vedas and Āgamas and what is in conformity with reality.

## \|\| 3.10.30 \|\|

*mahāmūḍhamatiścādya saṃjātosi kathaṃ vidhe \|*  
*vedavaktāpi nikhilalokakarttā hi durmatiḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. O Brahmā, how is it that you became so utterly confused in the mind? It is improper for the reciter of the Vedas and the creator of the universe to be so wicked.

## \|\| 3.10.31 \|\|

*jaḍatāṃ tyaja mandātman kuru tvaṃ nedṛśīṃ matim \|*  
*kiṃ bruvaṃtyakhilā vedāḥ stutyā tatsmara saddhiyā \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. O slow-witted one, cast-off this sluggishness. Do not indulge in such foolish thoughts hereafter. What is it that the Vedas say by means of their hymns? Think on it with a pure mind.

## \|\| 3.10.32 \|\|

*rudraṃ jānāsi durbuddhe svasutaṃ parameśvaram \|*  
*vedavaktāpi vijñānaṃ vismṛtaṃ tekhilaṃ vidhe \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. You foolishly think of Rudra, the great lord as your son. O Brahman, though the reciter of the Vedas you have forgotten all true knowledge.

## \|\| 3.10.33 \|\|

*śaṃkaraṃ surasāmānyaṃ matvā drohaṃ karoṣi hi \|*  
*subuddhirvigatā tedyāvirbhūtā kumatistathā \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Considering Śiva on a par with ordinary Gods you are maliciously disposed towards Him. Your good intents have vanished and evil ones have cropped up.

## \|\| 3.10.34 \|\|

*tattvasiddhāṃtamākhyātaṃ śṛṇu sadbuddhimāvaha \|*  
*yathārthaṃ nigamākhyātaṃ nirṇīya bhavakārakam \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Listen to the first principle that had been narrated of old. Have clean conscience. It is the true Being that is glorified as the cause of all Creation. This is decisive.

## \|\| 3.10.35 \|\|

*śivassarvasvakartā hi bhartā hartā parātparaḥ \|*  
*parabrahma pareśaśca nirguṇo nitya eva ca \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Śiva is the creator of everything, the sustainer and destroyer. He is greater than the great. He is the supreme Brahman, the greatest lord, the attributeless, the eternal.

## \|\| 3.10.36 \|\|

*anirdeśyo nirvikārī paramātmā'dvayo'cyutaḥ \|*  
*anaṃtoṃtakaraḥ svāmī vyāpakaḥ parameśvaraḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. He cannot be defined. He is not subject to deterioration or decay. He is the supreme soul, without a second, unswerving and endless. He is the cause of dissolution, all-pervasive and great lord.

## \|\| 3.10.37 \|\|

*sṛṣṭisthitivināśānāṃ karttā triguṇabhāgvibhuḥ \|*  
*brahmaviṣṇumaheśākhyo rajassattva tamaḥparaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. He is all-pervasive, possessed of three guṇas, for the causation of creation, sustenance and dissolution in the name of Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Maheśa but really beyond Rajas, Śattva and Tamas—the three attributes.

## \|\| 3.10.38 \|\|

*māyābhinno nirīhaśca māyo māyāviśāradaḥ \|*  
*saguṇopi svataṃtraśca nijānaṃdo vikalpakaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. He is distinct from illusion. He is free from desires. He is the creator of illusion yet uninfluenced by illusion. He is an adept. He is possessed of attributes yet independent of them. He is blissful in Himself. He is free from suspicions and alternatives.

## \|\| 3.10.39 \|\|

*ātmā rāmo hi nirdvandvo bhaktādhīnassuvigrahaḥ \|*  
*yogī yogarato nityaṃ yogamārgapradarśakaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. He rests and relaxes in His own soul. He is free from the pair of opposites, such as happiness and unhappiness. He is subservient to His devotees in a fine physical body. He is a yogin devoted always to the practice of Yogas. He is guide to the path of Yoga.

## \|\| 3.10.40 \|\|

*garvāpahārī lokeśassarvadā dīnavatsalaḥ \|*  
*etādṛśo hi yaḥ svāmī svaputraṃ manyase hi tam \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. He is the lord of the worlds and the destroyer of arrogance. He is favourably disposed to the miserable. Such is the lord, our master whom you consider your son!

## \|\| 3.10.41 \|\|

*īdṛśaṃ tyaja kujñānaṃ śaraṇaṃ vraja tasya vai \|*  
*bhaja sarvātmanā śambhuṃ santuṣṭaśśaṃ vidhāsyati \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Cast-off all these stupid notions. Seek refuge in Him. Worship Him exclusively. When He is propitiated He will bestow on you all that is auspicious and beneficent.

## \|\| 3.10.42 \|\|

*gṛhṇīyācchaṃkaraḥ patnīṃ vicāro hṛdi cettava \|*  
*śivāmuddiśya sutapaḥ kuru brahman śivaṃ smaran \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. O Brahmā, if a thought surges in your heart that Śiva should take a wife unto Himself, you must perform penance directed to Śiva and think upon Śiva.

## \|\| 3.10.43 \|\|

*kuru dhyānaṃ śivāyātsvaṃ kāmamuddiśya taṃ hṛdi \|*  
*sā cetprasannā deveśī sarvaṃ kāryaṃ vidhāsyati \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Meditate upon Śiva with that desire cherished in your heart. If that Goddess is propitiated she will do everything.

## \|\| 3.10.44 \|\|

*kṛtvāvatāraṃ saguṇā yadi syānmānuṣī śivā \|*  
*kasyacittanayā loke sā tatpatnī bhaveddhruvam \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. If Śivā takes an incarnation as a human being in Her attributive aspect, as the daughter of a person in the world, She will definitely become His wife.

## \|\| 3.10.45 \|\|

*dakṣamājñāpaya brahman tapaḥ kuryyātprayatnataḥ \|*  
*tāmutpādayituṃ patnīṃ śivārthaṃ bhaktitatsvataḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*
