45\. O Brahmā, command Dakṣa. Let him carry out a penance strenuously with a great devotion to beget her to be given as a wife unto Śiva.

## \|\| 3.10.46 \|\|

*bhaktādhīnau ca tau tāta suvijñeyau śivāśivau \|*  
*svecchayā saguṇau jātau parabrahmasvarūpiṇau \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. O dear, Śivā and Śiva are subservient to their devotees. This must be realised. Both of them being intrinsically the supreme Brahman can readily assume attributive form out of their own free will.

## \|\| 3.10.47 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityuktvā tatkṣaṇaṃ meśaśśivaṃ sasmāra svaprabhum \|*  
*kṛpayā tasya saṃprāpya jñānamūce ca māṃ tataḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

47\. After saying so, the lord of Lakṣmī thought upon his lord Śiva. Thanks to His favour, he received the real knowledge and spoke to me again.

## \|\| 3.10.48 \|\|

*viṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*vidhe smara puroktaṃ yadvacanaṃ śaṃkareṇa ca \|*  
*prārthitena yadāvābhyāmutpannābhyāṃ tadicchayā \|\| 48 \|\|*

Viṣṇu said:—

48\. O Brahmā remember the words spoken by Śiva formerly when requested, due to His own will, by us at the time of our nativity.

## \|\| 3.10.49 \|\|

*vismṛtaṃ tava tatsarvaṃ dhanyā yā śāṃbhavī parā \|*  
*tayā saṃmohitaṃ sarvaṃ durvijñeyā śivaṃ vinā \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Everything has been forgotten by you. Blessed indeed is the great illusion of Śiva which deludes everything. It is incomprehensible to all except Śiva.

## \|\| 3.10.50-51 \|\|

*yadā hi saguṇo jātassvecchayā nirguṇaśśivaḥ \|*  
*māmutpādya tatastvāṃ ca svaśaktyā suvihārakṛt \|\| 50 \|\|*

*upādideśa tvāṃ śambhussṛṣṭikāryaṃ tadā prabhuḥ \|*  
*tatpālanaṃ ca māṃ brahman somassūtikaro'vyayaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

50-51. When Śiva devoid of attributes became, out of His own accord, full of attributes, He created me first and then you with His own power in the course of His divine sport. The lord Śiva assigned to you the work of creation. O Brahman, the imperishable Śiva, the cause of creation, entrusted me with the task of sustaining it.

## \|\| 3.10.52-53 \|\|

*tadā vāṃ veśma saṃprāptau sāṃjalī natamastakau \|*  
*bhava tvamapi sarveśo'vatārī guṇarūpadhṛk \|\| 52 \|\|*

*ityuktaḥ prāha sa svāmī vihasya karuṇānvitaḥ \|*  
*divamudvīkṣya suprītyā nānālīlāviśāradaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

52-53. Then we requested Him “O Śiva, the lord of all, be pleased to take an incarnation with all your attributes.” Thus requested He laughed and spoke sympathetically, with his eyes raised to Heaven. Verily He is an adept in divine sports.

## \|\| 3.10.54 \|\|

*madrūpaṃ paramaṃ viṣṇo īdṛśaṃ hyaṃgato vidheḥ \|*  
*prakaṭībhavitā loke nāmnā rudraḥ prakīrtitaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. O Viṣṇu, a form of mine like this shall be manifested through my limbs and shall be glorified as Rudra in the world.

## \|\| 3.10.55 \|\|

*pūrṇarūpassa me pūjyassadā vāṃ sarvakāmakṛt \|*  
*layakarttā guṇādhyakṣo nirviśeṣaḥ suyogakṛt \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. He is my full form and perfect manifestation. He is worthy of being worshipped by both of you. He shall fulfil your desires entirely. He is the cause of dissolution, the presiding deity of attributes, the practitioner of perfect Yoga without anyone to exceed.

## \|\| 3.10.56 \|\|

*tridevā api me rūpaṃ haraḥ pūrṇo viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*umāyā api rūpāṇi bhaviṣyaṃti tridhā sutāḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. All the three deities are my forms. But Śiva is particularly my full manifestation O sons, Śivā’s forms too shall be three.

## \|\| 3.10.57 \|\|

*lakṣmīrnāma hareḥ patnī brahmapatnī sarasvatī \|*  
*pūrṇarūpā satī nāma rudrapatnī bhaviṣyati \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. The form Lakṣmī is Viṣṇu’s wife; Brahmā’s wife is Sarasvatī. The perfect form Satī shall become Rudra’s wife.

## \|\| 3.10.58 \|\|

*viṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*ityuktvāṃtarhito jātaḥ kṛpāṃ kṛtvā maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*abhūtāṃ sukhināvāvāṃ svasvakāryaparāyaṇau \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. After saying this, the great lord blessed us and vanished. We bent our heads and joined our palms in reverence and returned to our respective abodes. Engaged in our own tasks we were very happy.

## \|\| 3.10.59 \|\|

*samayaṃ prāpya sastrīkāvāvāṃ brahmanna śaṃkaraḥ \|*  
*avatīrṇassvayaṃ rudranāmā kailāsasaṃśrayaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. In due course we secured our wives. Śiva incarnated as Rudra at Kailāsa, His residence.

## \|\| 3.10.60 \|\|

*avatīrṇā śivā syātsā satīnāma prajeśvara \|*  
*tadutpādanahetorhi yatnotaḥ kārya eva vai \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. O lord of subjects, Śivā too shall incarnate as Satī. An effort shall be made for Her future incarnation.

## \|\| 3.10.61 \|\|

*ityuktvāṃtardadhe viṣṇuḥ kṛtvā sa karuṇāṃ param \|*  
*prāpnuvaṃ pramudaṃ cātha hyadhikaṃ gatamatsaraḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. After saying this, Viṣṇu blessed me and vanished. I rejoiced much and my jealousy disappeared altogether.

## Chapter 11 - Hymn to Durgā; Brahmā granted a boon

## \|\| 3.11.1 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*brahman tāta mahāprājña vada no vadatāṃ vara \|*  
*gate viṣṇau kimabhavadakārṣītkiṃ vidhe bhavān \|\| 1 \|\|*

Nārada said:—

1\. O Brahmā, dear, of great intellect, please tell me, O most eloquent one. When Viṣṇu went away what happened? O what did you do?

## \|\| 3.11.2 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*vipranandanavarya tvaṃ sāvadhānatayā śṛṇu \|*  
*viṣṇau gate bhagavati yadakārṣamahaṃ khalu \|\| 2 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

2\. O Brahmin, best of my sons, listen attentively to what I did when the lord Viṣṇu went away.

## \|\| 3.11.3 \|\|

*vidyāvidyātmikāṃ śuddhāṃ parabrahmasvarūpiṇīm \|*  
*staumi deva jagaddhātrīṃ durgāṃ śambhupriyāṃ sadā \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. I began a continuous laudatory prayer of the Goddess Durgā, the beloved of Śiva, the creator of the universe, of the nature of Vidyā and Avidyā and identical with the pure supreme Brahman.

## \|\| 3.11.4 \|\|

*sarvatra vyāpinīṃ nityāṃ nirālaṃbāṃ nirākulām \|*  
*tridevajananīṃ vaṃde sthūlasthūlāmarūpiṇīm \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. I salute the Goddess who is omnipresent, eternal, for whom there is no support, who is never distressed, who is the mother of the three deities, who is the grossest of the gross and yet has no form.

## \|\| 3.11.5 \|\|

*tvaṃ citiḥ paramānaṃdā paramātmasvarūpiṇī \|*  
*prasannā bhava deveśi matkāryaṃ kuru te namaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. O Goddess of the devas, you are Perfect knowledge, Supreme Bliss, identical with the supreme Soul. Be pleased. Grant me the fulfilment of my task. Obeisance to you.

## \|\| 3.11.6 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*evaṃ saṃstūyamānā sā yoganidrā mayā mune \|*  
*āvirbabhūva pratyakṣaṃ devarṣe caṃḍikā mama \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. O celestial sage, on being thus lauded Caṇḍikā, the mystic slumber, appeared before me.

## \|\| 3.11.7 \|\|

*snigdhāṃjanadyutiścārurūpā divyacaturbhujā \|*  
*siṃhasthā varahastā ca muktāmaṇikacotkaṭā \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Her complexion had the glossy hue of collyrium. She had comely features. She had four divine arms. She was seated on a lion. She showed the mystic gesture of granting boons by one of her hands, and pearls adorned her dishevelled hair.

## \|\| 3.11.8 \|\|

*śaradiṃdvānanā śubhracandrabhālā trilocanā \|*  
*sarvāvayavaramyā ca kamalāṃghrinakhadyutiḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Her face shone like the autumnal moon, the crescent moon bedecked her forehead. She had three eyes, looked beautiful and the nails of her lotus-like feet glistened.

## \|\| 3.11.9 \|\|

*samakṣaṃ tāmumāṃ vīkṣya mune śaktiṃ śivasya hi \|*  
*bhaktyā vinatatuṃgāṃśaḥ prāstavaṃ supraṇamya vai \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. O sage, seeing her who was Śiva’s Energy herself, directly in front of me, my lofty shoulders bent down with devotion and I eulogised her after due obeisance.

## \|\| 3.11.10 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*namo namaste jagataḥpravṛttinivṛtirūpe sthitisargarūpe \|*  
*carācarāṇāṃ bhavatī suśaktissanātanī sarvavimohanīti \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Obeisance, obeisence, to Thee, who art in the form of Pravṛtti (Action) and Nivṛtti (Abstinence); who art in the form of creation and sustenance of the universe. Thou art the eternal Energy of the movable and the immovable beings capable of enchanting everyone.

## \|\| 3.11.11 \|\|

*yā śrīḥ sadā keśavamūrtimālā viśvaṃbharā yā sakalaṃ bibharti \|*  
*yā tvaṃ purā sṛṣṭikarī maheśī hartrī trilokasya parā guṇebhya \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Thou hast manifested thyself as Śrī, a garland round Keśava’s form, who in the form of Earth holdest everything within, who art of yore the great Goddess causing creation and the destruction of the three worlds and art beyond the three Guṇas.

## \|\| 3.11.12 \|\|

*yā yogināṃ vai mahitā manojñā sā tvaṃ na te paramāṇusāre \|*  
*yamādipūte hṛdi yogināṃ yā yā yogināṃ dhyānapathe pratītā \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Thou art present in everything even in the essential atom and who art charmingly honoured by Yogins; who art perceivable in the hearts of the Yogins purified by restraints, as well as in the path of their meditation.

## \|\| 3.11.13 \|\|

*prakāśaśuddhyādiyutā virāgā sā tvaṃ hi vidyā vividhāvalaṃbā \|*  
*kūṭasthamavyaktamanaṃtarūpaṃ tvaṃ bibhratī kālamayī jagaṃti \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Thou art the Vidyā of diverse sorts. Thou art endowed with illumination, purity and detachment. Thou assumest Kūṭastha (perpetually immovable), Avyakta (unmanifest) and Ananta (infinite) form and Thou art the eternal time holding all the worlds.

## \|\| 3.11.14 \|\|

*vikārabījaṃ prakaropi nityaṃ guṇānvitā sarvajaneṣu nūnam \|*  
*tvaṃ vai guṇānāṃ ca śive trayāṇāṃ nidānabhūtā ca tataḥ parāsi \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. O Śivā, Thou art the prime cause of the three Guṇas and art still beyond them. But in conjunction with the Guṇas, Thou certainly infusest the seed of change in every matter.

## \|\| 3.11.15 \|\|

*satvaṃ rajastāmasa ityamīṣāṃ vikārahīnā samu vastitīryā \|*  
*sā tvaṃ guṇānāṃ jagadekahetuṃ brahmāṃtarāraṃbhasi cātsi pāsi \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Thou art the fourth to the three Guṇas viz. Sattva, Rajas and Tamas; but devoid of their depravity though these originate from Thee; Thou createst, protectest and devourest the whole universe within and without having three Guṇas as its only cause.

## \|\| 3.11.16 \|\|

*aśeṣajagatāṃ bīje jñeyajñānasvarūpiṇi \|*  
*jagaddhitāya satataṃ śivapatni namostu te \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. I pay my homage to Thee, O Śiva’s consort, for the eternal welfare of the universe. O seed of all the worlds, Thou art knowable as well as knowledge Thyself.

## \|\| 3.11.17 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya vacaḥ sā me kālī loka vibhāvinī \|*  
*prītyā māṃ jagatāmūce sraṣṭāraṃ janaśabdavat \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. On hearing these words of mine uttered like the words of ordinary people, Kālī, the conceiver of the worlds, told me, the creator of the worlds, in words full of love.

## \|\| 3.11.18 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*brahmankimarthaṃ bhavatā stutāhamavadhāraya \|*  
*ucyatāṃ yadi dhṛṣyosi tacchīghraṃ purato mama \|\| 18 \|\|*

The Goddess said:—

18\. O Brahman, why was I lauded by you? If you have been slighted by any one, please mention it quickly to me.

## \|\| 3.11.19 \|\|

*pratyakṣamapi jātāyāṃ siddhiḥ kāryasya niścitā \|*  
*tasmāttvaṃ vāṃchitaṃ brūhi yā kariṣyāmi bhāvitā \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. When I have personally appeared, the realisation of your desires is certain. Hence let me know your desires. I shall certainly fulfil them.

## \|\| 3.11.20 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*śṛṇu devi maheśāni kṛpāṃ kṛtvā mamopari \|*  
*manorathasthaṃ sarvajñe pravadāmi tvadājñayā \|\| 20 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

20\. O Goddess, be pleased with me and listen. O omniscient Goddess, I speak out my mind only since you have commanded me thus.

## \|\| 3.11.21 \|\|

*yaḥ patistava deveśi lalāṭānme'bhavatpurā \|*  
*śivo rudrākhyayā yogī sa vai kailāsamāsthitaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. O Goddess of devas, Śiva the Yogin, who is your husband and who as Rudra manifested Himself formerly through my forehead has now occupied Kailāsa.

## \|\| 3.11.22 \|\|

*tapaścarati bhūteśa eka evāvikalpakaḥ \|*  
*apatnīko nirvikāro na dvitīyāṃ samīhate \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The lord of Goblins is performing penance all alone. Since He does not desire a wife He is without a wife. He is free from mental aberrations.

## \|\| 3.11.23 \|\|

*taṃ mohaya yathā cānyāṃ dvitīyāṃ sati vīkṣate \|*  
*tvadṛte tasya no kācidbhaviṣyati manoharā \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. O Satī, fascinate Him lest He should cast His glance on another lady. Excepting you none will be able to capture His mind.

## \|\| 3.11.24 \|\|

*tasmāttvameva rūpeṇa bhavasva haramohinī \|*  
*sutā bhūtvā ca dakṣasya rudrapatnī śive bhava \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Hence, you alone should fascinate Śiva through your beauty. O Śivā, being born as Dakṣa’s daughter you should become Rudra’s wife.

## \|\| 3.11.25 \|\|

*yathā dhṛtaśarīrā tvaṃ lakṣmīrūpeṇa keśavam \|*  
*āmodayasi viśvasya hitāyaitaṃ tathā kuru \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Just as assuming the physical form of Lakṣmī you delight Viṣṇu, so act similarly to Rudra for the benefit of the universe.

## \|\| 3.11.26 \|\|

*kāṃtābhilāṣamātraṃ me dṛṣṭvā'niṃdadvṛṣadhvajaḥ \|*  
*sa kathaṃ vanitāṃ devī svecchayā saṃgrahīṣyati \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The bull-emblemed deity rebuked me merely for my feelings of love for a woman. How can He take a wife unto Himself, O Goddess, on His own accord?

## \|\| 3.11.27 \|\|

*hare gṛhītakāṃte tu kathaṃ sṛṣṭiśśubhāvahā \|*  
*ādyaṃtamadhye caitasya hetau tasminvirāgiṇi \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Śiva is the cause of this universe in the beginning, middle and end. If He remains detached and refuses to take a wife, how can auspicious creation come into being?

## \|\| 3.11.28 \|\|

*iti ciṃtāparo nāhaṃ tvadanyaṃ śaraṇaṃ hitam \|*  
*kṛcchravāṃstena viśvasya hitāyaitatkuruṣva me \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. This thought has tormented me. It was not conducive to any benefit to seek another shelter. So I request you for the benefit of the universe to accomplish the undertaking.

## \|\| 3.11.29 \|\|

*na viṣṇustasya mohāya na lakṣmīrna manobhavaḥ \|*  
*na cāpyahaṃ jaganmātarnānyastvāṃ kopi vai vinā \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. O mother of the universe, Viṣṇu is not competent to enthral Him, nor Lakṣmī, nor Kāma, nor I; in fact no one other than you.

## \|\| 3.11.30 \|\|

*tasmāttvaṃ dakṣajā bhūtvā divyarūpā maheśvarī \|*  
*tatpatnī bhava madbhaktyā yoginaṃ mohayeśvaram \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Hence be born as Dakṣa’s daughter, the great Goddess of celestial beauty. Inspired by my devotion, be pleased to become His wife and fascinate the lord who at present is detached from the world.

## \|\| 3.11.31 \|\|

*dakṣastapati deveśi kṣīrodottaratīragaḥ \|*  
*tvāmuddiśya samādhāya manastvayi dṛḍhavrataḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. O Goddess of devas, Dakṣa is performing a penance on the north of the milky ocean\* with his mind controlled and directed towards you. He is steady in performing the rite.

## \|\| 3.11.32 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya vacassā ciṃtāmāpa śivā tadā \|*  
*uvāca ca svamanasi vismitā jagadambikā \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. On hearing my words Śivā began to reflect then. The mother of the universe, surprised in her mind, spoke these words.

## \|\| 3.11.33 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*aho sumahadāścaryaṃ vedavaktāpi viśvakṛt \|*  
*mahājñānaparo bhūtvā vidhātā kiṃ vadatyayam \|\| 33 \|\|*

The Goddess said:—

33\. O this is an extremely wonderful thing. He is the reciter of the Vedas and the creator of the universe. He is endowed with great knowledge. Yet what is this that He says?

## \|\| 3.11.34 \|\|

*vidheścetasi saṃjāto mahāmoho'sukhāvahaḥ \|*  
*yadvaraṃ nirvikāraṃ taṃ saṃmohayitumicchati \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. A great delusion has beset His mind that makes him unhappy. That is why he desires to cause the fascination of Śiva who is free from mental aberration.

## \|\| 3.11.35 \|\|

*haramohavaraṃ mattassamicchati vidhistvayam \|*  
*ko lābhosyātra sa vibhurnirmoho nirvikalpakaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. This Brahmā desires the favour of power from me to enchant Śiva. What does he gain thereby? The great lord is free from delusion and mental aberrations.

## \|\| 3.11.36 \|\|

*parabrahmākhyo yaśśaṃbhurnirguṇo nirvikāravān \|*  
*tasyāhaṃ sarvadā dāsī tadājñāvaśagā sadā \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Always subservient to his bidding, I am a mere slave of Śiva, the supreme Brahman, the attributeless God who is free from depravity.

## \|\| 3.11.37 \|\|

*sa eva pūrṇarūpeṇa rudranāmābhavacchivaḥ \|*  
*bhaktoddhāraṇahetorhi svataṃtraḥ parameśvaraḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Śiva who is Parabrahman has become Rudra in a perfect and full-fledged incarnation and manifestation. It is to lift up His devotees that the independant lord has manifested like this.

## \|\| 3.11.38 \|\|

*harervidheśca sa svāmī śivānnyūno na karhicit \|*  
*yogādaro hyamāyastho māyeśaḥ parataḥ paraḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Since He is the lord Viṣṇu and Brahmā, He can never be inferior to Śiva. He is respectfully adhering to Yoga practice. He is the lord of illusion but is not absorbed in it. He is the greatest of the great.

## \|\| 3.11.39 \|\|

*matvā tamātmajaṃ brahmā sāmānyasurasaṃnibham \|*  
*icchatyayaṃ mohayitumato'jñānavimohitaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. This Brahmā considers Him his son and on a par with ordinary devas. Hence, deluded by ignorance, he desires to delude Him.

## \|\| 3.11.40 \|\|

*na dadyāṃ cedvaraṃ vedanītirbhraṣṭā bhavediti \|*  
*kiṃ kuryāṃ yena na vibhuḥ kruddhassyānme maheśvaraḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. If I do not grant him the boon, the convention established in the Vedas would be violated. Then what shall I do to prevent the great lord being angry with me.

## \|\| 3.11.41 \|\|

*brahmo vāca \|*  
*vicāryyetthaṃ maheśaṃ taṃ sasmāra manasā śivā \|*  
*prāpānujñāṃ śivasyāthovāca durgā ca māṃ tadā \|\| 41 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

41\. After pondering thus Śivā thought of Śiva. After getting the permission of Śiva, she said to me:—

## \|\| 3.11.42 \|\|

*\|\| durgovāca \|*  
*yaduktaṃ bhavatā brahman samastaṃ satyameva tat \|*  
*madṛte mohayitrīha śaṃkarasya na vidyate \|\| 42 \|\|*

Durgā said:—

42\. O Brahmā, what you said is entirely true. There is no other lady to fascinate Śiva.

## \|\| 3.11.43 \|\|

*hare'gṛhītadāre tu sṛṣṭinaiṣā sanātanī \|*  
*bhaviṣyatīti tatsatyaṃ bhavatā pratipāditam \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. A great truth has been pointed out by you that if Śiva does not take a wife unto Himself, the creation cannot continue long.

## \|\| 3.11.44 \|\|

*mamāpi mohane yanno vidyatesya mahāprabhoḥ \|*  
*tvadvākyādviguṇo medya prayatno'bhūtsa nirbharaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. I too had been endeavouring to enchant this great lord. After your request my efforts shall be redoubled.

## \|\| 3.11.45 \|\|

*ahaṃ tathā yatiṣyāmi yathā dāraparigraham \|*  
*haraḥ kariṣyati vidhe svayameva vimohitaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. I shall so endeavour that Śiva should take a wife unto Himself, being thus deluded Himself, O Brahmā.

## \|\| 3.11.46 \|\|

*satīmūrtimahaṃ dhṛtvā tasyaiva vaśavartinī \|*  
*bhaviṣyāmi mahābhāgā lakṣmīrviṣṇoryathā priyā \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. I shall take up the body of Satī and be subservient to Him even as Lakṣmī the Goddess of Fortune is the beloved of Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 3.11.47 \|\|

*yathā sopi mayaiveya vaśavartī sadā bhavet \|*  
*tathā yatnaṃ kariṣyāmi tasyaiva kṛpayā vidhe \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. O Brahmā thanks to His own favour I shall so endeavour as to make Him subservient to me always.

## \|\| 3.11.48 \|\|

*utpannā dakṣajāyāyāṃ satīrūpeṇa śaṃkaram \|*  
*ahaṃ sabhājayiṣyāmi līlayā taṃ pitāmaha \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. O Brahmā, being born of Dakṣa’s wife in the from of Satī, I shall duly honour Śiva with my sports.

## \|\| 3.11.49 \|\|

*yathānyajaṃturavanau vartate vanitāvaśe \|*  
*madbhaktyā sa haro vāmāvaśavartī bhaviṣyati \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Just as ordinary mortals on the earth are subservient to their women-folk so also Śiva shall be subservient to a woman due to my ardent devotion.

## \|\| 3.11.50 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*mahyamitthaṃ samābhāṣya śivā sā jagadambikā \|*  
*vīkṣyamāṇā mayā tāta tatraivāṃtardadhe tataḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

50\. After addressing me thus, Śiva, the mother of the universe, vanished from the scene even as I was watching her.

## \|\| 3.11.51 \|\|

*tasyāmaṃtarhitāyāṃ tu sohaṃ lokapitāmahaḥ \|*  
*agamaṃ yatra svasutāstebhyassarvamavarṇayam \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. When she had vanished, I, the grandfather of the worlds, went to my sons and narrated to them everything.

## Chapter 12 - Dakṣa granted the boon

## \|\| 3.12.1 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*brahman śaṃbhuvara prājña samyaguktaṃ tvayānagha \|*  
*śivāśivacaritraṃ ca pāvitaṃ janma me hitam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Nārada said:—

1\. O Brahmā, the sinless and the intelligent one, you have splendidly narrated the story of Śivā and Śiva. My life has been sanctified. This is conducive to my benefit.

## \|\| 3.12.2 \|\|

*idānīṃ vada dakṣastu tapaḥ kṛtvā dṛḍhavrataḥ \|*  
*kaṃ varaṃ prāpa devyāstu kathaṃ sā dakṣajā'bhavat \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Now please tell me, what the boon was that Dakṣa, with steady sacred rites and austere penance, secured from the Goddess, and how she became Dakṣa’s daughter.

## \|\| 3.12.3 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*śṛṇu nārada dhanyastvaṃ munibhirbhaktitokhilaiḥ \|*  
*yathā tepe tapo dakṣo varaṃ prāpa ca suvrataḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

3\. O Nārada, listen. You are blessed. You are revered by all sages with devotion. Hear how with good sacred rites, Dakṣa performed penance and secured boons.

## \|\| 3.12.4 \|\|

*madājñaptassudhīrdakṣassamādhāya mahādhipaḥ \|*  
*apādyaṣṭuṃ ca tāṃ devīṃ tatkāmo jagadaṃbikām \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. At my bidding, the intelligent Dakṣa the great chief controlled his mind and went to worship the Goddess, the mother of the universe, with that cherished desire.

## \|\| 3.12.5 \|\|

*kṣīrodottaratīrasthāṃ tāṃ kṛtvā hṛdayasthitām \|*  
*tapastaptuṃ samārebhe druṣṭuṃ pratyakṣatombikām \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. He went to the northern shore of the ocean of milk and began to perform the penance, keeping the mother of the universe in his heart. He wished to see the Goddess in person.

## \|\| 3.12.6 \|\|

*divyavarṣeṇa dakṣastu sahasrāṇāṃ trayaṃ samāḥ \|*  
*tapaścacāra niyatassaṃ yatātmā dṛḍhavrataḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. For three thousand divine years he performed the penance with good sacred rites, controlling his mind and keeping himself pure.

## \|\| 3.12.7 \|\|

*mārutāśī nirāhāro jalāhārī ca parṇabhuk \|*  
*evaṃ nināya taṃ kālaṃ ciṃtayantāṃ jaganmayīm \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. For some years, he sustained himself on taking in only air, abstaining from food, for some years taking only water and for some years taking only leaves as food. Thus he spent the time meditating upon the Goddess in cosmic form.

## \|\| 3.12.8 \|\|

*durgādhyānasamāsaktaściraṃ kālaṃ taporataḥ \|*  
*niyamairbahubhirdevīmārādhayati suvrataḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. He was intensively devoted to the meditation of the Goddess. He was engaged in the penance for a long time. With sacred rites and various restraints he worshipped the Goddess.

## \|\| 3.12.9 \|\|

*tato yamādiyuktasya dakṣasya munisattama \|*  
*jagadambā pūjayataḥ pratyakṣamabhavacchivā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. O excellent sage, then Śivā appeared in person to Dakṣa who maintained all restraints, Yama etc. and worshipped the mother of the universe.

## \|\| 3.12.10 \|\|

*tataḥ pratyakṣato dṛṣṭvā jagadambāṃ jaganmayīm \|*  
*kṛtakṛtyamathātmānaṃ mene dakṣaḥ prajāpatiḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. On seeing the mother of the universe cosmic in form, Dakṣa the lord of the subjects considered himself well rewarded.

## \|\| 3.12.11-12 \|\|

*siṃhasthāṃ kālikāṃ kṛṣṇāṃ cāruvaktrāṃ caturbhujām \|*  
*varadābhayanīlābjakhaḍgahastāṃ manoharām \|\| 11 \|\|*

*āraktanayanāṃ cārumuktakeśīṃ jagatprasūm \|*  
*tuṣṭāva vāgbhiścitrābhiḥ supraṇamyātha suprabhām \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. With various sorts of prayer he eulogised and bowed to the Goddess mother of the universe, Kālikā seated on a lion, dark-complexioned, with four arms and beautiful face, the bestower of the boon, the abode of safety, holding a blue lotus and the sword in her hands, comely with reddish eyes and with beautiful dishevelled hair.

## \|\| 3.12.13 \|\|

*dakṣa uvāca \|*  
*jagadeva mahāmāye jagadīśe maheśvari \|*  
*kṛpāṃ kṛtvā namastestu darśitaṃ svavapurmama \|\| 13 \|\|*

Dakṣa said:—

13\. Obeisance to Thee, O great Goddess, mother of the universe, wielding the great illusion, the ruler of the universe. It is with great favour that Thou showed Thy own body to me.

## \|\| 3.12.14 \|\|

*prasīda bhagavatyādye prasīda śivarūpiṇam \|*  
*prasīda bhaktavarade jaganmāye namostu te \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Be pleased, O primordial Goddess, be pleased, O Goddess in the form of Śiva; be pleased, O bestower of boons to the devotees; obeisance be to Thee, O wielder of illusion over the universe.

## \|\| 3.12.15 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*iti stutā maheśānī dakṣeṇa prayatātmanā \|*  
*uvāca dakṣaṃ jñātvāpi svayaṃ tasyepsitaṃ mune \|\| 15 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

15\. O sage, thus eulogised by Dakṣa of purified soul, the Goddess spoke to Dakṣa, although she knew what his desire was.

## \|\| 3.12.16 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*tuṣṭāhaṃ dakṣa bhavatassadbhaktyā hyanayā bhṛśam \|*  
*varaṃ vṛṇīṣva svābhīṣṭaṃ nādeyaṃ vidyate tava \|\| 16 \|\|*

The Goddess said:—

16\. O Dakṣa I am very much delighted by your great devotion. Choose a boon according to your desire. There is nothing which shall not be granted to you.

## \|\| 3.12.17 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*jagadambāvacaśśrutvā tato dakṣaḥ prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*suprahṛṣṭataraḥ prāha nāmaṃ nāmaṃ ca tāṃ śivām \|\| 17 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

17\. On hearing the words of the mother of the universe, Dakṣa Prajāpati was very happy and he said to Śivā after bowing to her frequently.

## \|\| 3.12.18 \|\|

*dakṣa uvāca \|*  
*jagadambā mahāmāye yadi tvaṃ varadā mama \|*  
*madvacaḥ śṛṇu suprītyā mama kāmaṃ prapūraya \|\| 18 \|\|*

Dakṣa said:—

18\. O wielder of great illusion, O mother of the universe, if you wish to grant me any boon please listen to my words with pleasure. Be pleased to fulfil my desire.

## \|\| 3.12.19 \|\|

*mama svāmī śivo yo hi sa jāto brahmaṇastutaḥ \|*  
*rudranāmā pūrṇarūpāvatāraḥ paramātmanaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. My lord and master Śiva has manifested Himself as Brahmā’s son in the name of Rudra. He is the perfect and full-fledged incarnation of the supreme soul.

## \|\| 3.12.20 \|\|

*tavāvatāro no jātaḥ kā tatpatnī bhavedataḥ \|*  
*taṃ mohaya maheśānamavatīrya kṣitau śive \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. You have not so far incarnated. Who will be His wife? Hence O Śivā, take an incarnation on the Earth and fascinate the great lord.

## \|\| 3.12.21 \|\|

*tvadṛte tasya mohāya na śaktānyā kadācana \|*  
*tasmānmama sutā bhūtvā harajāyābhavā'dhunā \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Excepting you, no other lady will ever be competent to enthral Him. Hence be born as my daughter and become Śiva’s consort.

## \|\| 3.12.22 \|\|

*itthaṃ kṛtvā sulīlā ca bhava tvaṃ hara mohinī \|*  
*mamaivaiṣa varo devi satyamuktaṃ tavāgrataḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Exhibiting your divine sports as this, O Goddess, you be the enchantress of Śiva, this is the only boon I crave of you. I speak out the truth to you.

## \|\| 3.12.23 \|\|

*kevalaṃ svārthamiti ca sarveṣāṃ jagatāmapi \|*  
*brahmaviṣṇuśivānāṃ ca brahmaṇā prerito hyaham \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. This fulfils my own interests. Indeed it fulfils the interests of all the worlds as well as those of Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva. Hence I have been induced by Brahmā in this direction.

## \|\| 3.12.24 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya prajeśasya vacanaṃ jagadambikā \|*  
*pratyuvāca vihasyeti smṛtvā taṃ manasā śivam \|\| 24 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

24\. On hearing these words of Dakṣa the mother of the universe replied smilingly after thinking on Śiva.

## \|\| 3.12.25 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*tāta prajāpate dakṣa śṛṇu me paramaṃ vacaḥ \|*  
*satyaṃ bravīmi tvadbhaktyā suprasannākhilapradā \|\| 25 \|\|*

The Goddess said:—

25\. Dear one, O Dakṣa Prajāpati, listen to my weighty words. I tell you the truth. I am much delighted by your devotion. I shall bestow everything.

## \|\| 3.12.26 \|\|

*ahaṃ tava sutā dakṣa tvajjāyāyāṃ maheśvarī \|*  
*bhaviṣyāmi na saṃdehastvadbhaktivaśavartinī \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Subservient to your devotion, O Dakṣa, I, the great Goddess, shall be born of your wife as your daughter. There is no doubt in this.

## \|\| 3.12.27 \|\|

*tathā yatnaṃ kariṣyāmi tapaḥ kṛtvā sudussaham \|*  
*harajāyā bhaviṣyāmi tadvaraṃ prāpya cānagha \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. O sinless one, I shall perform a penance strenuously and shall become Śiva’s wife, after I have secured a boon from Him to that effect.

## \|\| 3.12.28 \|\|

*nānyathā kāryasiddhirhi nirvikārī ca sa prabhuḥ \|*  
*vidherviṣṇośca saṃsevyaḥ pūrṇa eva sadāśivaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Otherwise there is no chance of the fulfilment of the object. The lord is free from all aberrations. He is the full incarnation of Sadāśiva, worthy of being served by Brahmā and Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 3.12.29 \|\|

*ahaṃ tasya sadā dāsī priyā janmani janmani \|*  
*mama svāmī sa vai śaṃbhurnānārūpadharopi ha \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. I am His slave for ever, His beloved in every birth (incarnation). Śiva who manifests Himself in many forms is indeed my master.

## \|\| 3.12.30 \|\|

*varaprabhāvādbhrukuṭeravatīrṇo vidhesma ca \|*  
*ahaṃ tadvaratopīhāvatariṣye tadājñayā \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. It was by His favour that He manifested through the eyebrows of Brahmā. I too shall incarnate by His favour and at His bidding.

## \|\| 3.12.31 \|\|

*gaccha svabhavanaṃ tāta mayā jñātā tu dūtikā \|*  
*harajāyā bhaviṣyāmi bhūtā te tanayācirāt \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. O dear one, go back to your residence. I have known my mission. Born as your daughter, ere long I shall be Śiva’s wife.

## \|\| 3.12.32 \|\|

*ityuktvā sadvaco dakṣaṃ śivājñāṃ prāpya cetasi \|*  
*punaḥ provāca sā devī smṛtvā śivapadāmbujam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Having spoken these splendid words, She sought and obtained Śiva’s permission through mental communion. While thinking on Śiva’s lotus-like feet, the Goddess spoke as follows:—

## \|\| 3.12.33 \|\|

*parantu paṇa ādheyo manasā te prajāpate \|*  
*śrāvayiṣyāmi te taṃ vai satyaṃ jānīhi no mṛṣā \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. But O Prajāpati, you have to take a vow. It is a precondition. I shall tell you. It is true, never false, please understand.

## \|\| 3.12.34 \|\|

*yadā bhavān mayi punarbhavenmaṃdādarastapā \|*  
*dehaṃ tyakṣye nijaṃ satyaṃ svātmanyasmyatha vetaram \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. If in future you were to be less respectful to me I will cast off my body. I shall withdraw myself to my soul or take to another form. It is true.

## \|\| 3.12.35 \|\|

*eṣa dattastava varaḥ pratisargaṃ prajāpate \|*  
*ahaṃ tava sutā bhūtvā bhaviṣyāmi harapriyā \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. O Dakṣa, this boon has been granted to you. At every creation I shall be born as your daughter and become the beloved of Śiva.

## \|\| 3.12.36 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|\| evamuktvā maheśānī dakṣaṃ mukhyaprajāpatim \|*  
*aṃtardadhe drutaṃ tatra samyag dakṣasya paśyataḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

36\. After speaking thus to Dakṣa the chief Prajāpati, the great Goddess immediately vanished even as Dakṣa was watching.

## \|\| 3.12.37 \|\|

*aṃtarhitāyāṃ durgāyāṃ sa dakṣopi nijāśramam \|*  
*jagāma ca mudaṃ lebhe bhaviṣyati suteti sā \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. When she had vanished, Dakṣa returned to his hermitage. He rejoiced because he knew that the great Goddess would become his daughter.

## Chapter 13 - Nārada is cursed by Dakṣa

## \|\| 3.13.1 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*brahmanvidhe mahā prājña vada no vadatāṃ vara \|*  
*dakṣe gṛhaṃ gate prītyā kimabhūttadanaṃtaram \|\| 1 \|\|*

Nārada said:—

1\. O Brahmā of great intelligence, O eloquent one, please tell us what happened after Dakṣa went home with great delight?

## \|\| 3.13.2 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*dakṣaḥ prajāpatirgatvā svāśramaṃ hṛṣṭamānasaḥ \|*  
*sargaṃ cakāra bahudhā mānasaṃ mama cājñayā \|\| 2 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

2\. Dakṣa Prajāpati returned with pleasure to his hermitage and began mental creations at my bidding.

## \|\| 3.13.3 \|\|

*tamabṛṃhitamālokya prajāsargaṃ prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*dakṣo nivedayāmāsa brahmaṇe janakāya me \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. On seeing the creation, not increasing in size, Dakṣa Prajāpati informed me his father, Brahmā.

## \|\| 3.13.4 \|\|

*dakṣa uvāca \|*  
*brahmaṃstāta prajānātha varddhante na prajāḥ prabho \|*  
*mayā viracitāssarvāstāvatyo hi sthitāḥ khalu \|\| 4 \|\|*

Dakṣa said:—

4\. O Brahmā, lord of subjects, these subjects are not flourishing. They are conceived by me but they remain stationary.

## \|\| 3.13.5 \|\|

*kiṃ karomi prajānātha varddheyuḥ kathamātmanā \|*  
*tadupāyaṃ samācakṣva prajāḥ kuryāṃ na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. O lord of subjects what shall I do? How can they flourish themselves? Please instruct me in the means thereof. I shall certainly create subjects.

## \|\| 3.13.6 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*dakṣa prajāpate tāta śṛṇu me paramaṃ vacaḥ \|*  
*tatkuruṣva suraśreṣṭha śivaste śaṃ kariṣyati \|\| 6 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

6\. O Dakṣa Prajāpati, listen to my weighty words and carry out the direction. Śiva will bless you with welfare.

## \|\| 3.13.7 \|\|

*yā ca pañcajanasyāṃga sutā ramyā prajāpateḥ \|*  
*asiknī nāma patnītve prajeśa pratigṛhyatām \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. O lord of subjects, let Asiknī, the beautiful daughter of Pañcajana, the lord of five tribes, be taken by you as your consort.

## \|\| 3.13.8 \|\|

*vāmavyavāyadharmastvaṃ prajāsargamimaṃ punaḥ \|*  
*tadvidhāyāṃ ca kāminyāṃ bhūriśo bhāvayiṣyasi \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Indulging in sexual intercourse you can create subjects many in number in a beautiful woman like her.

## \|\| 3.13.9 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*tatassamutpādayituṃ prajā maithunadharmataḥ \|*  
*upayeme vīraṇasya nideśānme sutāṃ tataḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Then, in order to procreate subjects by way of coitus he married the daughter of Vīraṇa at my bidding.

## \|\| 3.13.10 \|\|

*atha tasyāṃ svapatnyāṃ ca vīriṇyāṃ sa prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*haryaśvasaṃjñānayutaṃ dakṣaḥ putrānajījanat \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Then in his wife Vīriṇī, Dakṣa Prajāpati begot sons named Haryaśvas.

## \|\| 3.13.11 \|\|

*apṛthagdharmaśīlāste sarva āsan sutā mune \|*  
*pitṛbhaktiratā nityaṃ vedamārgaparāyaṇāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. O sage, all those sons were devoted to their father and followed the Vedic path. They did not have separate virtues and practices.

## \|\| 3.13.12 \|\|

*pitṛproktāḥ prajāsargakaraṇārthaṃ yayurdiśam \|*  
*pratīcīṃ tapase tāta sarve dākṣāyaṇāssutāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Advised by their father, O dear one, the sons of Dakṣa went in the western direction for penance in order to create subjects (progeny).

## \|\| 3.13.13 \|\|

*tatra nārāyaṇasarastīrthaṃ paramapāvanam \|*  
*gamo yatra saṃjāto divyasindhusamudrayoḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. There they came to the holy lake Nārāyaṇa where the celestial Sindhu has its confluence with the ocean.

## \|\| 3.13.14 \|\|

*tadupasparśanādeva protpannamatayo' bhavan \|*  
*dharme pāramahaṃse ca vinirddhūtamalāśayāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. On touching the holy water, their intellect was sharpened. The Dharma of holy ascetics eradicated all their impurities.

## \|\| 3.13.15 \|\|

*prajāvivṛddhaye te vai tepira tatra sattamāḥ \|*  
*dākṣāyaṇā dṛḍhātmānaḥ pitrādeśa suyaṃtritāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. For making progenies flourish, the excellent sons of Dakṣa, fettered by the command of their father began to perform Tapas with steady resolve.

## \|\| 3.13.16 \|\|

*tvaṃ ca tān nārada jñātvā tapatassṛṣṭi hetave \|*  
*agamastatra bhūrīṇi hārdamājñāya māpateḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. O Nārada, you came to know that they were performing penance for the sake of creation. You realised the intention of Viṣṇu and went there.

## \|\| 3.13.17 \|\|

*adṛṣṭvā taṃ bhuvassṛṣṭi kathaṃ kartuṃ samudyatāḥ \|*  
*haryaśvā dakṣatanayā ityavocastamādarāt \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. “O Haryaśvas, sons of Dakṣa, how is it that you have begun your attempts at creation without seeing the end of the earth?” So you asked them with respect.

## \|\| 3.13.18 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*tanniśamyātha haryaśvāste tvaduktamataṃdritāḥ \|*  
*autpattikadhiyassarve svayaṃ vimamṛśurbhṛśam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. They heard what you said eagerly. With their minds fixed on creation they deliberated on the proposal.

## \|\| 3.13.19 \|\|

*suśāstrajanakādeśaṃ yo na veda nivartakam \|*  
*sa kathaṃ guṇaviśraṃbhī kartuṃ sargamupakramet \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. How can a person begin the work of creation putting faith in the Guṇas alone if he does not know the command of the father of Sacred Texts (which implies) turning back?

## \|\| 3.13.20 \|\|

*iti niścitya te putrāssudhiyaścaikacetasaḥ \|*  
*praṇamya taṃ parikramyāyurmārgamanivartakam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Having made up their minds unanimously, the intelligent sons bowed to you and circumambulated. They then proceeded ahead on a path never to turn back.

## \|\| 3.13.21 \|\|

*nārada tvaṃ manaśśaṃbhorloṃkānanyacaro mune \|*  
*nirvikāro maheśānamanovṛttikarastadā \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. O sage Nārada, with your mind fixed on Śiva, and desirous of carrying out His orders you went to various worlds without any mental aberration.

## \|\| 3.13.22 \|\|

*kāle gate bahutare mama putraḥ prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*nāśaṃ niśamya putrāṇāṃ nāradādanvatapyata \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. When much time elapsed, my son Prajāpati heard that the extinction of his sons was due to Nārada and became distressed.

## \|\| 3.13.23 \|\|

*muhurmuhuruvāceti suprajātvaṃ śucāṃ padam \|*  
*śuśoca bahuśo dakṣaśśivamāyāvimohitaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. He frequently mused like this—“A multitude of sons brings only disaster”. Dakṣa who was deluded by Śiva’s illusion bewailed thus in many ways.

## \|\| 3.13.24 \|\|

*ahamāgatya suprītyā sāṃtvayaṃ dakṣamātmajam \|*  
*śāṃtibhāvaṃ pradarśyaiva devaṃ prabalamityuta \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. I went over to him and consoled my son Dakṣa out of love and reminded him that fate is all powerful. I pointed out the way to calmness.

## \|\| 3.13.25 \|\|

*atha dakṣaḥ paṃcajanyā mayā sa parisāṃtvitaḥ \|*  
*sabalāśvābhidhān् putrān sahasraṃ cāpyajījanat \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. On being consoled by me, Dakṣa begot a thousand sons named Sabalāśvas in the daughter of Pañcajana.

## \|\| 3.13.26 \|\|

*tepi jagmustatra sutāḥ pitrādiṣṭā dṛḍhavratāḥ \|*  
*prajāsarge atra siddhāssvapūrvabhrātaro yayuḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. At the bidding of their father, they too reached the place where their elder brothers, the Siddhas, had gone with the same steady resolve in the creation of subjects.

## \|\| 3.13.27 \|\|

*tadupasparśanādeva naṣṭāghā vimalāśayāḥ \|*  
*tepurmahattapastatra japanto brahma suvratāḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. At the very touch of waters of the Nārāyaṇa lake they too had their sins quelled and became purified. They performed penance, strenuously repeating many mantras and performing sacred rites.

## \|\| 3.13.28 \|\|

*prajāsargodyatāṃstān vai jñātvā gatveti nārada \|*  
*pūrvavaccāgado vākyaṃ saṃsmarannaiśvarīṃ gatim \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. O Nārada, you came to know that they too were attempting the creation of subjects and you told them as before, mindful of the way of Śiva.

## \|\| 3.13.29 \|\|

*bhrātṛpaṃthānamādiśya tvaṃ mune moghadarśanaḥ \|*  
*ayāścorddhvagatiṃ te'pi bhrātṛmārgaṃ yayussutāḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. O sage, of beneficient sight, you showed, them the path followed by their brothers. You went upto heaven and the sons of Dakṣa went the way of their brothers.

## \|\| 3.13.30 \|\|

*utpātān bahuśo'paśyattadaiva sa prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*vismitobhūtsa me putro dakṣo manasi duḥkhitaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. At the very same time, my son Dakṣa Prajāpati saw many an ill omen. He was disagreeably surprised and felt distressed.

## \|\| 3.13.31 \|\|

*pūrvavattvatkṛtaṃ dakṣaśśuśrāva cakito bhṛśam \|*  
*putranāśaṃ śuśocāti putraśoka vimūrchitaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. As before, Dakṣa heard that the disappearance of his sons was brought about by you. He bewailed a lot. He was stunned, grief-stricken at the loss of his sons.

## \|\| 3.13.32 \|\|

*cukrodha tubhyaṃ dakṣosau duṣṭoyamiti cābravīt \|*  
*āgatastatra daivāttvamanugrahakarastadā \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Dakṣa was furious. He called you a wicked fellow. Fate caused you to go there at the psychological moment in the guise of one who wanted to bless him.

## \|\| 3.13.33 \|\|

*śokāviṣṭassa dakṣo hi roṣavisphuritādharaḥ \|*  
*upalabhya tamāhatya dhigdhik procya vigarhayan \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The grief-stricken Dakṣa approached you with his lips throbbing with fury, taunted you and reproached you saying “Fie, Fie” and spoke to you.

## \|\| 3.13.34 \|\|

*dakṣa uvāca \|*  
*kiṃ kṛtaṃ te'dhamaśreṣṭha sādhūnāṃ sādhuliṃgataḥ \|*  
*bhikṣomārgo'rbhakānāṃ vai darśitassādhukāri no \|\| 34 \|\|*

Dakṣa said:—

34\. O foremost among the base, disguised in the garb of a saint, what is it that you have done to those good people—my sons? To those engaged in good actions the accursed path of a mendicant has been pointed out by you.

## \|\| 3.13.35 \|\|

*ṛṇaistribhiramuktānāṃ lokayorubhayoḥ kṛtaḥ \|*  
*vighātaśśreyaso'mīṣāṃ nirdayena śaṭhena te \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Ruthless rogue that you are, even when they were not free from the three debts you put obstacles in the path of their progress both here as well as hereafter.

## \|\| 3.13.36 \|\|

*ṛṇāni trīṇyapākṛtya yo gṛhātpravrajetpumān \|*  
*mātaraṃ pitaraṃ tyaktvā mokṣamicchanvrajatyadhaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. He who renounces the world desiring salvation, without repaying the three debts and departs from the house forsaking his parents surely courts downfall.

## \|\| 3.13.37 \|\|

*nirdayastvaṃ sunirlajjaśśiśudhībhidyaśo'pahā \|*  
*hareḥ pārṣadamadhye hi vṛthā carasi mūḍhadhīḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. You are unkind, shameless, distorter of the tender intellect of children, and a destroyer of fame. Why do you, a foolish fellow, move about among the attendants of Viṣṇu in vain?

## \|\| 3.13.38 \|\|

*muhurmuhurabhadraṃ tvamacaro me'dhamā 'dhama \|*  
*vibhavedbhramataste'taḥ padaṃ lokeṣu sthiram \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Frequently you have committed offences against me, O basest of the base. Hence roaming ever in the worlds your feet will never be steady anywhere.

## \|\| 3.13.39-40 \|\|

*śaśāpeti śucā dakṣastvāṃ tadā sādhusaṃmatam \|*  
*bubodha neśvarecchāṃ sa śivamāyāvimohitaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*śāpaṃ pratyagrahīśca tvaṃ sa mune nirvikāradhīḥ \|*  
*eṣa eva brahmasādho sahate sopi ca svayam \|\| 40 \|\|*

39-40. Grief-stricken Dakṣa cursed you thus, you who are honoured by saints. It was Śiva’s power of delusion that prevented him from understanding the will of Īśvara. Without your mind being affected the least, you accepted the curse. All saintly Brahminical saints forbear thus.

## Chapter 14 - The birth of Satī and her childish sports

## \|\| 3.14.1 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*etasminnantare devamune lokapitāmaha \|*  
*tatrāgamamahaṃ prītyā jñātvā taccaritaṃ drutam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

1\. In the mean time, O celestial sage I, the grandfather of the worlds, came there, on hearing the incident.

## \|\| 3.14.2 \|\|

*asāṃtvayamahaṃ dakṣaṃ pūrvavatsuvicakṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*akārṣaṃ tena susnehaṃ tava suprītimāvahan \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. I consoled Dakṣa as before. Clever that I was I made him friendly with you.

## \|\| 3.14.3 \|\|

*svātmajaṃ munivaryaṃ tvāṃ suprītyā devavallabham \|*  
*samāśvāsya samādāya pratyapadye svadhāma ha \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. O best of sages, I consoled you—my own son, beloved of the Devas, and taking you with love effected conciliation.

## \|\| 3.14.4 \|\|

*tataḥ prajāpatirdakṣo'nunīto me nijastriyām \|*  
*janayāmāsa duhitṝssubhagāḥ ṣaṣṭisaṃmitāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Then Dakṣa, consoled by me, begot of his wife sixty comely daughters.

## \|\| 3.14.5 \|\|

*tāsāṃ vivāhakṛtavāndharmādibhirataṃdritaḥ \|*  
*tadeva śṛṇu suprītyā pravadāmi munīśvara \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Without any lassitude he performed their marriages with Dharma and others. O excellent sage, listen to that with pleasure.

## \|\| 3.14.6 \|\|

*dadau daśa sutā dakṣo dharmāya vidhivanmune \|*  
*trayodaśa kaśyapāya munaye trinaveṃdave \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Dakṣa gave ten of his daughters duly in marriage to Dharma, thirteen to Kaśyapa the sage, and twenty seven to the moon.

## \|\| 3.14.7-8 \|\|

*bhūtāṃgiraḥ kṛśāśvebhyo dvedve putrī pradattavān \|*  
*tārkṣyāya cāparaḥ kanyā prasūtiprasavairyataḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*trilokāḥ pūritāstanno varṇyate vyāsato bhayāt \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. He gave two daughters each to Bhṛgu, Aṅgiras and Kṛśāśva. The other daughters were given to Tārkṣya. The sons and grandsons and descendants of these filled the three worlds. A detailed narration is not attempted here.

## \|\| 3.14.9 \|\|

*kecidvadaṃti tāṃ jyeṣṭhāṃ madhyamāṃ cāpare śivām \|*  
*sarvānantarajāṃ kecitkalpabhedāttrayaṃ ca sata \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Some say that Śivā was the eldest of his daughters, some say that she was the middle and some say that she was the youngest. All the three opinions are correct in different Kalpas.

## \|\| 3.14.10 \|\|

*anaṃtaraṃ sutotpatteḥ sapatnīkaḥ prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*dakṣo dadhau suprītmā tāṃ manasā jagadambikām \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. After the birth of his daughter, Dakṣa Prajāpati and his wife meditated on the mother of the universe with pleasure.

## \|\| 3.14.11 \|\|

*ataḥ premṇā ca tuṣṭāva girā gadgadayā hi saḥ \|*  
*bhūyobhūyo namaskṛtya sāṃjalirvinayānvitaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Then he lovingly eulogised her with words choked at the throat and repeatedly paid respects to her humbly joining the palms in reverence.

## \|\| 3.14.12 \|\|

*santuṣṭā sā tadā devī vicāraṃ manasīti ca \|*  
*cakre'vatāraṃ vīriṇyāṃ kuryāṃ paṇavipūrtaye \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The Goddess, who was highly delighted, thought within himself. “I shall incarnate in Vīriṇī in order to keep my word”.

## \|\| 3.14.13 \|\|

*atha sovāsa manasi dakṣasya jagadambikā \|*  
*vilalāsa tadātīva sa dakṣo munisattama \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. O excellent sage, then the mother of the universe spoke to Dakṣa in mind. Then Dakṣa shone forth splendidly.

## \|\| 3.14.14 \|\|

*sumuhūrtenātha dakṣo'pi svapatnyāṃ nidadhe mudā \|*  
*dakṣapatnyāstadā citte śivovāsa dayānvitā \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. In an auspicious hour he deposited his semen in his wife. Thus full of compassion, Śivā began to reside in the womb of Dakṣa’s consort.

## \|\| 3.14.15 \|\|

*āvirbabhūvuścihnāni dohadasyākhilāni vai \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. All the characteristic signs of pregnancy appeared in her.

## \|\| 3.14.16 \|\|

*vireje vīriṇī tāta hṛṣṭacittādhikā ca sā \|*  
*śivāvāsaprabhāvāttu mahāmaṃgala rūpiṇī \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Dear one, thanks to the power of the presence of Śivā, Vīriṇī had an auspicious appearance and shone all the more with mental pleasure.

## \|\| 3.14.17 \|\|

*kulasya saṃpadaścaiva śruteścittasamunnateḥ \|*  
*vyadhatta sukriyā dakṣaḥ prītyā puṃsavanādikāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. As befitting the loftiness of his mind, customs and manners current in his family and the injunctions of the Vedas, Dakṣa performed the rites of Puṃsavana etc. out of affection.

## \|\| 3.14.18 \|\|

*utsavotīva saṃjātastadā teṣu ca karmasu \|*  
*vittaṃ dadau dvijātibhyo yathākāmaṃ prajāpatiḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Great festivities accompanied those rites. Dakṣa presented liberal sums of money to the brahmins.

## \|\| 3.14.19 \|\|

*atha tasminnavasare sarve haryādayassurāḥ \|*  
*jñātvā garbhagatāṃ devīṃ vīriṇyāste mudaṃ yayuḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. On coming to know that the Goddess had come to the womb of Vīriṇī, Viṣṇu and other Devas became very gay.

## \|\| 3.14.20 \|\|

*tatrāgatya ca sarve te tuṣṭuvurjagadambikām \|*  
*lokopakārakariṇīṃ praṇamya ca muhurmuhuḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. They all approached her and paid frequent respects to the benefactress of the worlds, eulogising the mother of the universe.

## \|\| 3.14.21 \|\|

*kṛtvā tataste bahudhā praśaṃsāṃ hṛṣṭamānasāḥ \|*  
*dakṣaprajāpateścaiva vīriṇyāssvagṛhaṃ yayuḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Delighted in their hearts they praised Dakṣa and Vīriṇī in various ways and went to their respective abodes.

## \|\| 3.14.22-23 \|\|

*gateṣu navamāseṣu kārayitvā ca laukikīm \|*  
*gatiṃ śivā ca pūrṇe sā daśame māsi nārada \|\| 22 \|\|*

*āvirbabhūva purato mātussadyastadā mune \|*  
*muhūrte sukhade candragrahatārānukūlake \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. O Nārada, nine months had passed with due observance of worldly conventions. In the tenth month, in an auspicious happy hour, when the moon, the stars and the planets were favourably disposed, Śivā suddenly appeared, O sage, in front of her mother.

## \|\| 3.14.24 \|\|

*tasyāṃ tu jātamātrāyāṃ suprīto'sau prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*saiva devīti tāṃ mene dṛṣṭvā tāṃ tejasolbaṇām \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. As soon as she was born, Dakṣa was highly pleased. On seeing her extremely brilliant he was convinced that she was the Goddess Śivā herself.

## \|\| 3.14.25 \|\|

*tadābhūtpuṣpasadvṛṣṭirmeghāśca vavṛṣurjalam \|*  
*diśaśśāṃtā drutaṃ tasyāṃ jātāyāṃ ca munīśvara \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. O excellent sage, when she was born there was a gentle shower from the clouds accompanied by that of flowers. The quarters became tranquil immediately.

## \|\| 3.14.26 \|\|

*avādayaṃta tridaśāśśubhavādyāni khe gatāḥ \|*  
*jajjvaluścāgnayaśśāṃtāḥ sarvamāsītsumaṃgalam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The devas gathered in the sky and played on musical instruments; sacrificial fires kindled calmly; everything indicated auspiciousness.

## \|\| 3.14.27 \|\|

*vīriṇosaṃbhavāṃ dṛṣṭvā dakṣastāṃ jagadambikām \|*  
*namaskṛtya karau baddhvā bahu tuṣṭāva bhaktitaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. On seeing the mother of the universe born of Vīriṇī, Dakṣa joined his palms in reverence, paid respects to her and eulogised her.

## \|\| 3.14.28 \|\|

*dakṣa uvāca \|*  
*maheśāni namastubhyaṃ jagadambe sanātani \|*  
*kṛpāṃ kuru mahādevi satye satyasvarūpiṇi \|\| 28 \|\|*

Dakṣa said:—

28\. O Goddess, the eternal mother of the universe, obeisance to Thee. O great Goddess, the Truthful and truth-featured, be pleased.

## \|\| 3.14.29 \|\|

*śivā śāṃtā mahāmāyā yoganidrā jaganmayī \|*  
*yā procyate vedavidbhirnamāmi tvāṃ hitāvahām \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. I bow to Thee, the bestower of benefits, Thee who art auspicious, calm, great illusion, mystic slumber and identical with the universe.

## \|\| 3.14.30 \|\|

*yayā dhātā jagatsṛṣṭau niyuktastāṃ purākarot \|*  
*tāṃ tvāṃ namāmi paramāṃ jagaddhātrīṃ maheśvarīm \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. I bow to Thee, the great mother of the universe, the great Goddess, by whom formerly Brahmā had been directed to create the worlds which he carried out.

## \|\| 3.14.31 \|\|

*yayā viṣṇurjagatsthityai niyuktastāṃ sadākarot \|*  
*tāṃ tvāṃ namāmi paramāṃ jagaddhātrīṃ maheśvarīm \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. I bow to Thee, great support of the universe, the great Goddess, by whom formerly Viṣṇu had been directed to sustain the universe which he has been doing always.

## \|\| 3.14.32 \|\|

*yayā rudro jagannāśe niyuktastāṃ sadākarot \|*  
*tāṃ tvāṃ namāmi paramāṃ jagaddhātrīṃ maheśvarīm \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. I bow to Thee the great mother of the universe, the great Goddess, by whom formerly Rudra had been directed to annihilate the universe which he has been doing always.

## \|\| 3.14.33 \|\|

*rajassattvatamorūpāṃ sarvakāryakarīṃ sadā \|*  
*tridevajananīṃ devīṃ tvāṃ namāmi ca tāṃ śivām \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. I bow to Thee, Śivā, of Rājasika Sāttvika, and Tāmasika forms, performing every thing always, and the Goddess mother of the three deities.

## \|\| 3.14.34 \|\|

*yastvāṃ viciṃtayeddevīṃ vidyāvidyātmikāṃ parām \|*  
*tasya bhuktiśca muktiśca sadā karatale sthitā \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. O Goddess, enjoyment of worldly pleasures and salvation are always within the reach of that person who meditates on thee in the form of Vidyā and Avidyā, every day.

## \|\| 3.14.35 \|\|

*yastvāṃ pratyakṣato devi śivāṃ paśyati pāvanīm \|*  
*tasyāvaśyaṃ bhavenmuktirvidyāvidyāprakāśikā \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. O Goddess, he who directly perceives Thee, the sanctifying deity, will certainly attain salvation with the discrimination of Vidyā and Avidyā.

## \|\| 3.14.36 \|\|

*ye stuvaṃti jaganmātarbhavānīmaṃbiketi ca \|*  
*jaganmayīti durgeti sarvaṃ teṣāṃ bhaviṣyati \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. O mother of the universe, those who eulogise Thee with the names of Bhavānī, Ambikā, Jaganmāyā and Durgā will have everything.

## \|\| 3.14.37 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*iti stutā jaganmātā śivā dakṣeṇa dhīmatā \|*  
*tathovāca tadā dakṣaṃ yathā mātā śṛṇoti na \|\| 37 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

37\. Śivā, the mother of the universe, eulogised by Dakṣa the intelligent, said to Dakṣa without making it heard by her mother.

## \|\| 3.14.38 \|\|

*sarvaṃ mumoha tathyaṃ ca tathā dakṣaḥ śṛṇotu tat \|*  
*nānyastathā śivā prāha nānotiḥ parameśvarī \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Śivā, the great Goddess and the source of future creation, made everyone deluded and said in such a manner that Dakṣa heard the truth and not anyone else.

## \|\| 3.14.39 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*ahamārādhitā pūrvaṃ sutārthaṃ te prajāpate \|*  
*īpsitaṃ tava siddhaṃ tu tapo dhāraya saṃprati \|\| 39 \|\|*

The Goddess said:—

39\. O Prajāpati, I had been propitiated formerly for becoming your daughter. Your wish has been fulfilled now. You can carry on your activities of penance.

## \|\| 3.14.40 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*evamuktvā tadā devī dakṣaṃ ca nijamāyayā \|*  
*āsthāya śaiśavaṃ bhāvaṃ jananyaṃte ruroda sā \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Having spoken thus to Dakṣa, the Goddess assumed infancy through her illusory power and began to cry near her mother.

## \|\| 3.14.41 \|\|

*atha tadrodanaṃ śrutvā striyo vākyaṃ sasaṃbhramāḥ \|*  
*āgatāstatra suprītyā dāsyopi ca sasaṃbhramāḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. On heaving the cry, the woman spoke in agitation. The servant-maids too became pleasantly agitated.

## \|\| 3.14.42 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvāsiknīsutārūpaṃ nanandussarvayoṣitaḥ \|*  
*sarve paurajanāścāpi cakrurjayaravaṃ tadā \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. On seeing the comely form of Asiknī’s daughter, the women rejoiced. The citizens raised shouts of Victory then.

## \|\| 3.14.43 \|\|

*utsavaśca mahānāsīdgānavādyapurassaram \|*  
*dakṣosiknī mudaṃ lebhe śubhaṃ dṛṣṭvā sutānanam \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. There were great festivities with songs and musical instruments. On seeing the unearthly face of their daughter the pleasure of Dakṣa and Asiknī knew no bounds.

## \|\| 3.14.44 \|\|

*dakṣaḥ śrutikulācāraṃ cakre ca vidhivattadā \|*  
*dānaṃ dadau dvijātibhyonyebhyaśca draviṇaṃ tathā \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Dakṣa duly performed all the conventional ceremonies and the rites of the Vedas. He gave various gifts to the brahmins and money to others.

## \|\| 3.14.45 \|\|

*babhūva sarvato gānaṃ nartanaṃ ca yathocitam \|*  
*nedurvādyāni bahuśassumaṃgalapurassaram \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Songs and dances were performed everywhere in a befitting manner. Musical instruments played auspicious songs repeatedly.

## \|\| 3.14.46 \|\|

*atha haryādayo devāssarve sānucarāstadā \|*  
*munivṛndaiḥ samāgatyotsavaṃ cakruryathāvidhi \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Hari and other Gods came with their attendants, along with the sages and joined the festivities.

## \|\| 3.14.47 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā dakṣasutāmaṃbāṃ jagataḥ parameśvarīm \|*  
*nemuḥ savinayāssarve tuṣṭuvuśca śubhaistavaiḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. On seeing the daughter of Dakṣa, the Goddess mother of the universe, they bowed and eulogised her with auspicious hymns.

## \|\| 3.14.48 \|\|

*ūcussarve pramuditā giraṃ jayajayātmikām \|*  
*praśaśaṃsurmudā dakṣaṃ vīriṇīṃ ca viśeṣataḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. In their great delight they shouted cries of victory. They praised Dakṣa and Vīriṇī in particular.

## \|\| 3.14.49 \|\|

*tadometi nāma cakre tasyā dakṣastadājñayā \|*  
*praśastāyāssarvaguṇasattvādapi mudānvitaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Then at their bidding, the delighted Dakṣa named her Umā since she inherited good qualities and was greatly admired.

## \|\| 3.14.50 \|\|

*nāmānyanyāni tasyāstu paścājjātāni lokataḥ \|*  
*mahāmaṃgaladānyeva duḥkhaghnāni viśeṣataḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Her other names in the world were assigned afterwards. They are auspicious and quell miseries in particular.

## \|\| 3.14.51 \|\|

*dakṣastadā hariṃ natvā māṃ sarvānamarānapi \|*  
*munīnapi karau baddhvā stutvā cānarca bhaktitaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. With palms joined in reverence Dakṣa bowed to Hari, me, devas and sages. He eulogised and worshipped all.

## \|\| 3.14.52 \|\|

*atha viṣṇvādayassarve supraśasyājanaṃdanam \|*  
*prītyā yayusvadhāmāni saṃsmaran saśivaṃ śivam \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Then Viṣṇu and others praised Dakṣa and in joyous mood returned to their respective abodes remembering Śiva accompanied by Śivā.

## \|\| 3.14.53 \|\|

*atastāṃ ca sutāṃ mātā susaṃskṛtya yathocitam \|*  
*śiśupānena vidhinā tasyai stanyādikaṃ dadau \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Consecrating the daughter in a befitting manner, the mother fed her with fresh milk in the usual manner of feeding infants.

## \|\| 3.14.54 \|\|

*pālitā sātha vīriṇyā dakṣeṇa ca mahātmanā \|*  
*vavṛdhe śuklapakṣasya yathā śaśikalānvaham \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Duly nurtured by Vīriṇī and the noble-souled Dakṣa, she flourished every day like the digit of the moon in the bright half of a month.

## \|\| 3.14.55 \|\|

*tasyāṃ tu sadguṇāssarve viviśurdvijasattama \|*  
*śaiśavepi yathā candre kalāssarvā manoharāḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. O excellent brahmin, even in her infancy, the good qualities entered her like all the beautiful digits entering the moon.

## \|\| 3.14.56 \|\|

*ācarannijabhāvena sakhīmadhyagatā yadā \|*  
*tadā lilekha bhargasya pratimāmanvahaṃ muhuḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. While she was engaged in various sports in the midst of her girl friends, she used to draw pictures of Śiva everyday.

## \|\| 3.14.57 \|\|

*yadā jagau sugītāni śivā bālyocitāni sā \|*  
*tadā sthāṇuṃ haraṃ rudraṃ sasmāra smaraśāsanam \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Whenever she sang sweet songs as is usual in childhood, she remembered Sthāṇu, Rudra, the suppressor of Kāma.

## \|\| 3.14.58 \|\|

*vavṛdhetīva daṃpatyoḥ pratyahaṃ karuṇātulā \|*  
*tasyā bālyepi bhaktāyāstayornityaṃ muhurmuhuḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. The Couple (Dakṣa and his wife) found her unrivalled mercy increase, even as she had been a great devotee in childhood itself.

## \|\| 3.14.59 \|\|

*sarvabālāguṇā krāṃtāṃ sadā svālayakāriṇīm \|*  
*toṣayāmāsa pitarau nityaṃnityaṃ muhurmuhuḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Endowed with qualities of childhood and making her own residence flourish she delighted her parents for ever.

## Chapter 15 - The Sacred rites of Nandā and Hymn to Śiva

## \|\| 3.15.1 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*athaikadā pituḥ pārśve tiṣṭhaṃtīṃ tāṃ satīmaham \|*  
*tvayā saha munedrākṣaṃ sārabhūtāṃ trilokake \|\| 1 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

1\. O sage, once I saw Satī standing near her father along with you. She is, as it were, the essence of the three worlds.

## \|\| 3.15.2 \|\|

*pitrā namaskṛtaṃ vīkṣya satkṛtaṃ tvāṃ ca māṃ satī \|*  
*praṇanāma mudā bhaktyā lokalīlānusāriṇī \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. When she saw both of us honoured and bowed to by her father, Satī following the conventions of the world, saluted us with joy and reverence.

## \|\| 3.15.3 \|\|

*praṇāmāṃte satīṃ vīkṣya dakṣadattaśubhāsane \|*  
*sthitohaṃ nārada tvaṃ ca vinatāmahamāgadam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. At the end of obeisance, O Nārada, you and I sat in the fine seat provided by Dakṣa. When she humbly bowed again, I spoke to her.

## \|\| 3.15.4 \|\|

*tvāmeva yaḥ kāmayate yantu kāmayase sati \|*  
*tamāpnuhi patiṃ devaṃ sarvajñaṃ jagadīśvaram \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. O Satī, secure, as your husband, the lord of the universe, (the omniscient Śiva) who desires only you and whom you too desire.

## \|\| 3.15.5 \|\|

*yo nānyāṃ jagṛhe nāpi gṛhṇāti na grahīṣyati \|*  
*jāyāṃ sa te patirbhūyādananyasadṛśaśśubhe \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. O auspicious lady, you shall secure, as your husband, the person who has not taken, does not take, and will not be taking another wife. He will be unlike others.

## \|\| 3.15.6 \|\|

*ityuktvā suciraṃ tāṃ vai sthitvā dakṣālaye punaḥ \|*  
*visṛṣṭau tena saṃyātau svasthānaṃ tau ca nārada \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. O Nārada, after saying this to Satī we stayed in Dakṣa’s abode for a long time. We were bidden farewell by him and we went to our respective places.

## \|\| 3.15.7 \|\|

*dakṣobhavacca suprītaḥ tadākarṇya gatajvaraḥ \|*  
*ādade tanayāṃ svāṃ tāṃ matvā hi parameśvarīm \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. On hearing that, Dakṣa became delighted and free from all worries. Thinking that she was a great Goddess, he took her with him.

## \|\| 3.15.8 \|\|

*itthaṃ vihārai ruciraiḥ kaumārairbhaktavatsalā \|*  
*jahāvavasthāṃ kaumārīṃ svecchādhṛtanarākṛtiḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Thus with various charming girlish sports the Goddess who is favourably disposed to her devotees and who had assumed human form out of her own will passed the state of girlhood.

## \|\| 3.15.9 \|\|

*bālyaṃ vyatītya sā prāpa kiñcidyauvanatāṃ satī \|*  
*atīva tapasāṃgena sarvāṃgeṣu manoharā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. After passing her girlhood and reaching the state of early youth she attained beauty in every limb which blazed forth brilliantly.

## \|\| 3.15.10 \|\|

*dakṣastāṃ vīkṣya lokeśaḥ prodbhinnāṃtarvayasthitām \|*  
*ciṃtayāmāsa bhargāya kathaṃ dāsya imāṃ sutām \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Dakṣa, the lord of worlds, on seeing her blooming in the proper age thought within—“How shall I give my daughter to Śiva?”

## \|\| 3.15.11 \|\|

*atha sāpi svayaṃ bhargaṃ prāptumaicchattadānvaham \|*  
*piturmanogatiṃ jñātvā māturnikaṭamāgamat \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. She too desired to attain Śiva. Her desire grew every day. After knowing her father’s idea, she approached her mother.

## \|\| 3.15.12 \|\|

*papracchājñāṃ tapohetośśaṃkarasya vinītadhīḥ \|*  
*mātuśśivātha vairiṇyāssā sakhī parameśvarī \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Satī, the great Goddess of wide intellect, sought the permission of her mother to perform the penance with Śiva as the goal, for the happiness of her mother Vīriṇī.

## \|\| 3.15.13 \|\|

*tatassatī maheśānaṃ patiṃ prāptuṃ dṛḍhavratā \|*  
*sā tamārādhayāmāsa gṛhe māturanujñayā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Firmly resolved in her desire to secure Śiva as her husband, she propitiated him in her own house with the permission of her mother.

## \|\| 3.15.14 \|\|

*āśvine māsi nandāyāṃ tithāvānarca bhaktitaḥ \|*  
*guḍaudanaissalavaṇairharaṃ natvā nināya tam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. In the month of Āśvina, (September-October), on Nandā Tithis (i.e. first, sixth and eleventh days of lunar fortnight) she worshipped Śiva with great devotion, offering cooked rice with jaggery and salt. She spent a month like that.

## \|\| 3.15.15 \|\|

*kārtikasya caturdaśyāmapūpaiḥ pāyasairapi \|*  
*samākīrṇaissamārādhya sasmāra parameśvaram \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. On the Caturdaśī (14th day) of the month of Kārttika (October-November), she worshipped and meditated on Lord Śiva, offering sweet pies and puddings.

## \|\| 3.15.16 \|\|

*mārgaśīrṣe'sitāṣṭamyāṃ satilaissayavaudanaiḥ \|*  
*pūjayitvā haraṃ kīlairnināya divasān satī \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. On the eighth day in the dark half of Mārgaśīrṣa (November-December), Satī worshipped Śiva with cooked barley and gingelly seeds and spent the other days (in devotion).

## \|\| 3.15.17 \|\|

*pauṣe tu śuklasaptamyāṃ kṛtvā jāgaraṇaṃ niśi \|*  
*apūjayacchivaṃ prātaḥ kṛśarānnena sā satī \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. On the seventh day in the bright half of Pauṣa (December-January) Satī spent the night in keeping awake and worshipped Śiva in the morning with cooked rice and Kṛśara (jaggery mixed with gingelly seeds).

## \|\| 3.15.18 \|\|

*māghe tu paurṇamāsyāṃ sa kṛtvā jāgaraṇaṃ niśi \|*  
*ārdravastrā nadītīre'karocchaṃkarapūjanam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. She kept awake in the full-moon night of Māgha (January-February) and worshipped Śiva on the banks of the river wearing wet clothes.

## \|\| 3.15.19 \|\|

*tapasyasitabhūtāyāṃ kṛtvā jāgaraṇaṃ niśi\|\| \|*  
*viśeṣatassamānarca śailūṣaissarvayāmasu \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. On the fourteenth day of the dark half of Phālguna (February-March), she kept awake in the night and performed special worship of Śiva with Bilva fruits and leaves in every period of three hours.

## \|\| 3.15.20 \|\|

*caitre śuklacaturdaśyāṃ palāśairdamanaiśśivam \|*  
*apūjayaddivārātrau saṃsmaran sā nināya tam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. On the Caturdaśī day of the bright half of Caitra (March-April) she worshipped Śiva with Palāśa and Damana flowers day and night. She spent (the rest of) the month remembering Him.

## \|\| 3.15.21 \|\|

*rādhaśuklatṛtīyāyāṃ tilāhārayavaudanaiḥ \|*  
*pūjayitvā satī rudraṃ navyairmāsaṃ nināya tam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. After worshipping Him with cooked barley and gingelly seeds on the third day of the bright half of Māgha (January-February), she spent the month on the products of milk obtained from a cow.

## \|\| 3.15.22 \|\|

*jyeṣṭhasya pūrṇimāyāṃ vai rātrai saṃpūjya śaṃkaram \|*  
*vasanairbṛhatīpuṣpairnirāhārā nināya tam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. After worshipping Him with the offerings of cloths and Bṛhatī flowers on the full-moon night of Jyeṣṭha (May-June) she spent the whole month observing fast.

## \|\| 3.15.23 \|\|

*āṣāḍhasya caturdaśyāṃ śuklāyāṃ kṛṣṇavāsasā \|*  
*bṛhatīkusumaiḥ pūjā rudrasyākāri vai tayā \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. On the Caturdaśī day in the bright half of Āṣāḍha (June-July) wearing a black cloth, she worshipped Rudra with Bṛhatī flowers.

## \|\| 3.15.24 \|\|

*śrāvaṇasya sitāṣṭamyāṃ caturdaśyāṃ ca sā śivam \|*  
*yajñopavītairvāsobhiḥ pavitrairapyapūjayat \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. On the eighth and fourteenth days in the bright half of Śrāvaṇa (July-August), she worshipped Śiva with holy sacred threads and cloths.

## \|\| 3.15.25 \|\|

*bhādre kṛṣṇatrayodaśyāṃ puṣpairnānāvidhaiḥ phalaiḥ \|*  
*saṃpūjya ca caturdaśyāṃ cakāra jalabho janam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. After worshipping Śiva with various fruits and flowers on the thirteenth day in the dark half of Bhādra (August-September) she took only water on the fourteenth day.

## \|\| 3.15.26 \|\|

*nānāvidhaiḥ phalaiḥ puṣpaissasyaistatkālasaṃbhavaiḥ \|*  
*cakre suniyatāhārā japanmāse śivārcanam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Keeping strict control over her diet and repeating various mantras she worshipped Śiva with different fruits, flowers and leaves fresh and readily available.

## \|\| 3.15.27 \|\|

*sarvamāse sarvadine śivārcanaratā satī \|*  
*dṛḍhavratābhavaddevī svecchādhṛtanarākṛtiḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. The Goddess Satī who had assumed human form out of her will, became firmly devoted to the worship of Śiva on every day and month.

## \|\| 3.15.28 \|\|

*itthaṃ naṃdāvrataṃ kṛtsnaṃ samāpya susamāhitā \|*  
*dadhyau śivaṃ satī premṇā niścalābhūdananyadhīḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Concluding all the sacred rites of Nandā, Satī began to meditate on Śiva with concentrated devotion. She was steady and she never thought of any one else.

## \|\| 3.15.29 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare devā munayaścākhilā mune \|*  
*viṣṇuṃ māṃ ca puraskṛtya yayurdraṣṭuṃ satītapaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. In the meantime, O sage, devas and sages with Viṣṇu and me at their head came to see the penance of Satī.

## \|\| 3.15.30 \|\|

*dṛṣṭāgatya satī devairmūrtā siddhirivāparā \|*  
*śivadhyānamahāmagnā siddhāvasthāṃ gatā tadā \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. On arrival, Satī was seen by the devas as an achievement in embodied form or as success incarnate. She was completely engrossed in meditating on Śiva. She had reached the stage of the enlightened seers.

## \|\| 3.15.31 \|\|

*cakruḥ sarve surāssatye mudā sāṃjalayo natim \|*  
*munayaśca nataskaṃdhā viṣṇvādyāḥ prītamānasāḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. With palms joined in reverence, the devas paid respects to Satī joyfully. The sages bent down their shoulders in respect. Viṣṇu and others became delighted.

## \|\| 3.15.32 \|\|

*atha sarve suprasannā viṣṇvādyāśca surarṣayaḥ \|*  
*praśaśaṃsustapastasyāssatyāstasmātsavismayāḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Viṣṇu and others and the celestial sages joyously praised Satī’s penance. They were even surprised at that.

## \|\| 3.15.33 \|\|

*tataḥ praṇamya tāṃ devīṃ punaste munayassurāḥ \|*  
*jagmurgirivaraṃ sadyaḥ kailāsaṃ śivavallabham \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Bowing again to the Goddess, the sages and devas went immediately to Kailāsa, the great mountain dear to Śiva.

## \|\| 3.15.34 \|\|

*sāvitrīsahitaścāhaṃ saha lakṣmyā mudānvitaḥ \|*  
*vāsudevopi bhagavāñjagāmātha harāṃtikam \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. The lord Viṣṇu approached Śiva with great joy, accompanied by Lakṣmī and I too along with Śāvitrī, the Goddess of speech.

## \|\| 3.15.35 \|\|

*gatvā tatra prabhuṃ dṛṣṭvā supraṇamya susaṃbhramāḥ \|*  
*tuṣṭuvurvividhaiḥ stotraiḥ karau baddhvā vinamrakāḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. On arrival there, after paying respects to the lord with great excitement we lauded Him with various hymns with palms joined in reverence.

## \|\| 3.15.36 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*namo bhagavate tubhyaṃ yata etaccarācaram \|*  
*puruṣāya maheśāya pareśāya mahātmane \|\| 36 \|\|*

The Devas said:—

36\. Obeisance to Thee, O lord, from whom the mobile and the immobile beings have originated. Obeisance to the great Puruṣa, Maheśa, the supreme Īśa and the great Ātman.

## \|\| 3.15.37 \|\|

*ādibījāya sarveṣāṃ cidrūpāya parāya ca \|*  
*brahmaṇe nirvikārāya prakṛteḥ puruṣasya ca \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Obeisance to the primordial seed of every one, the Cidrūpa (one possessed of the form of consciousness), the Puruṣa beyond Prakṛti.

## \|\| 3.15.38 \|\|

*ya idaṃ pratipaṃcyedaṃ yenedaṃ vicakāsti hi \|*  
*yasmādidaṃ yataścedaṃ yasyedaṃ tvaṃ ca yatnataḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Obeisance to Thee who createst this world, by whom this is illuminated, from whom this originated, by whom this is sustained, to whom this belongs and by whom everything is kept under control.

## \|\| 3.15.39 \|\|

*yosmātparasmācca paro nirvikārī mahāprabhuḥ \|*  
*īkṣate yassvātmanīdaṃ taṃ natāḥ sma svayaṃbhuvam \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. We bow to that self-born deity who is beyond this and everything that is great, who is the undepraved great lord, who sees these within Himself.

## \|\| 3.15.40 \|\|

*aviddhadṛk paraḥ sākṣī sarvātmā 'nekarūpadhṛk \|*  
*ātmabhūtaḥ parabrahma tapaṃtaṃ śaraṇaṃ gatāḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. We have sought refuge at His feet who is the supreme Brahman, who is the soul of everyone, who is the greatest witness with unbarred vision and who assumes various forms.

## \|\| 3.15.41 \|\|

*na yasya devā ṛṣayaḥ siddhāśca na viduḥ padam \|*  
*kaḥ punarjaṃturaparo jñātumarhati veditum \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Obeisance to Him whose region is not known by devas, sages or Siddhas. How then can other creatures realise it or express it?

## \|\| 3.15.42 \|\|

*didṛkṣavo yasya padaṃ muktasaṃgāssusādhavaḥ \|*  
*caritaṃ sugatirnastvaṃ salokavratamavraṇam \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. He is our goal supreme, seeking to see whose region great saints free from attachment perform unmutilated vow of Release.

## \|\| 3.15.43 \|\|

*tvajjanmādivikārā no vidyaṃte kepi duḥkhadā \|*  
*tathāpi māyayā tvaṃ hi gṛhṇāsi kṛpayā ca tān \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Thou hast no change like death, birth etc. that yields misery, yet by means of āyā thou assumest all these.

## \|\| 3.15.44 \|\|

*tasmai namaḥ pareśāya tubhyamāścaryakarmaṇe \|*  
*namo girāṃ vidūrāya brahmaṇe paramātmane \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Obeisance to Thee who art the great Īśa and the performer of miracles. Obeisance to Brahman, the great soul who is far removed from words.

## \|\| 3.15.45 \|\|

*arūpāyorurūpāya parāyānaṃtaśaktaye \|*  
*trilokapataye sarvasākṣiṇe sarvagāya ca \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Obeisance to the formless Being of immense form, the great, of unlimited power, the lord of the three worlds, the witness of all and all-pervasive.

## \|\| 3.15.46 \|\|

*nama ātmapradīpāya nirvāṇasukhasaṃpade \|*  
*jñānātmane namaste'stu vyāpakāyeśvarāya ca \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Obeisance to the light of Ātman, richly endowed with the happiness of liberation, of the form of knowledge. Obeisance to Thee, the all-pervasive Lord.

## \|\| 3.15.47 \|\|

*naiṣkarmyeṇa sulabhyāya kaivalyapataye namaḥ \|*  
*puruṣāya pareśāya namaste sarvadāya ca \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Obeisance to the lord of salvation who is accessible only through the cessation of worldly activities. Obeisance to Thee the great Puruṣa, the great lord, the bestower of all.

## \|\| 3.15.48 \|\|

*kṣetrajñāyātmarūpāya sarvapratyayahetave \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Obeisance to conscious principle in the corporal frame, identical with Ātman, the cause of all perception.

## \|\| 3.15.49 \|\|

*sarvādhyakṣāya mahate mūlaprakṛtaye namaḥ \|*  
*puruṣāya pareśāya namaste sarvadāya ca \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Obeisance to the original Prakṛti, the great presiding deity of everything. Obeisance to Thee the great Puruṣa, the great lord, the bestower of all.

## \|\| 3.15.50 \|\|

*trinetrāyeṣuvaktrāya sadābhāsāya te namaḥ \|*  
*sarvendriyaguṇadraṣṭre niṣkāraṇa namostu te \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Obeisance to Thee, the three-eyed, the five-faced and the ever-luminous. Obeisance to Thee who hast no cause and who seest all the qualities of the sense-organs.

## \|\| 3.15.51 \|\|

*trilokakāraṇāyāthāpavargāya namonamaḥ \|*  
*apavargapradāyāśu śaraṇāgatatāriṇe \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Obeisance, obeisance to Thee, the cause of the three worlds and salvation. Obeisance to the quick bestower of liberation, and deliverer of those who seek refuge.

## \|\| 3.15.52 \|\|

*sarvāmnāyāgamānāṃ codadhaye parameṣṭhine \|*  
*parāyaṇāya bhaktānāṃ guṇānāṃ ca namostu te \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Obeisance to Thee, the ocean of the knowledge of Vedic texts. Obeisance to Thee, the great lord and the ultimate goal of devotees and possessed of three attributes.

## \|\| 3.15.53 \|\|

*namo guṇāraṇicchanna cidūṣmāya maheśvara \|*  
*mūḍhaduṣprāptarūpāya jñānihṛdvāsine sadā \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Obeisance to Thee, O great lord whose fiery heat of knowledge is latent in the sacrificial churning rod for the production of fire of three attributes. Obeisance to Thee whose form is beyond the reach of fools and who livest for ever in the heart of the wise.

## \|\| 3.15.54 \|\|

*paśupāśavimokṣāya bhaktasanmuktidāya ca \|*  
*svaprakāśāya nityāyā'vyayāyājasrasaṃvide \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Obeisance to the liberator of the individual soul from the noose; to the bestower of salvation to the devotee, to the self-luminous, the eternal, the unwasting, the incessant knowledge.

## \|\| 3.15.55 \|\|

*pratyagdraṣṭrai'vikārāya paramaiśvarya dhāriṇe \|*  
*yaṃ bhajanti caturvarge kāmayaṃtīṣṭasadgatim \|*  
*so'bhūdakaruṇastvaṃ naḥ prasanno bhava te namaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Obeisance to Thee, the self-contemplator, the unchanging, the holder of great suzerainty and glory. Never be ruthless unto them who resort to the four aims of life and desire the cherished final goal. Obeisance to Thee O Siva.

## \|\| 3.15.56 \|\|

*ekāṃtinaḥ kaṃcanārthaṃ bhaktā vāṃchaṃti yasya na \|*  
*kevalaṃ caritaṃ te te gāyaṃti paramaṃgalam \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Thy devotees never desire anything solely to themselves. They sing the auspicious glory of Thy life.

## \|\| 3.15.57 \|\|

*akṣaraṃ paramaṃ brahmatamavyaktākṛtiṃ vibhum \|*  
*adhyātmayogagamyaṃ tvāṃ paripūrṇaṃ stumo vayam \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. We eulogise Thee, the imperishable supreme Brahman, the omnipresent whose features are unmanifest, who can be attained by the Yoga of the Soul and is complete.

## \|\| 3.15.58 \|\|

*atīṃdriyamanādhāraṃ sarvādhāramahetukam \|*  
*anaṃtamādyaṃ sūkṣmaṃ tvāṃ praṇamāmo'khileśvaram \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. O lord of everything, we bow to Thee who art beyond the perception of the sense-organs; who hast no support; who art the support of all; who hast no cause; who art endless; the primordial and the subtle.

## \|\| 3.15.59 \|\|

*haryādayo'khilā devāstathā lokāścarācarāḥ \|*  
*nāmarūpavibhedena phalgvyā ca kalayā kṛtāḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. All the devas, Viṣṇu and others, and the world of mobile and immobile Beings are created by deficient digit with the difference of name and form.

## \|\| 3.15.60 \|\|

*yathārciṣognessavituryāṃti niryāṃti vāsakṛt \|*  
*gabhastayastathāyaṃ vai pravāho gauṇa ucyate \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Just as the flames of fire and the rays of the sun emerge and submerge so also this current of creation and dissolution.

## \|\| 3.15.61 \|\|

*na tvaṃ devo 'suro martyo na tiryaṅ na dvijaḥ prabho \|*  
*na strī na ṣaṃḍho na pumānsadasanna ca kiṃcana \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Thou art neither a deva nor an Asura, nor a man nor a brute, nor a brahmin, O lord. Thou art neither a woman nor a man, nor a eunuch. Thou makest nothing either the existent or the non-existent.

## \|\| 3.15.62 \|\|

*niṣedhaśeṣassarvaṃ tvaṃ viśvakṛdviśva pālakaḥ \|*  
*viśvalayakṛdviśvātmā praṇatāssmastamīśvaram \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. After all negations whatever remains thou art that. Thou art the maker, the sustainer and the destroyer of the universe; Thou art the soul of the universe. We bow to that lord Śiva.

## \|\| 3.15.63 \|\|

*yogaraṃdhitakarmāṇo yaṃ prapaśyanti yoginaḥ \|*  
*yogasaṃbhāvite citte yogeśaṃ tvāṃ natā vayam \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. We bow to Thee, the lord of Yoga, whom the Yogins who have destroyed all their actions by means of Yoga, are able to realise in their minds purified by Yoga.

## \|\| 3.15.64 \|\|

*namostu te'sahyavega śaktitraya trayīmaya \|*  
*namaḥ prasannapālāya namaste bhūriśaktaye \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Obeisance to Thee whose velocity is unbearable, who hast three Śaktis, who art identical with the three Vedas; Obeisance to Thee the delighted protector of immense potentiality.

## \|\| 3.15.65 \|\|

*kadiṃdriyāṇāṃ durgeśānavāpya paravartmane \|*  
*bhaktoddhāraratāyātha namaste gūḍhavarcase \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. O lord, Thou art impenetrable to the wicked sense-organs; worldly lords cannot reach Thee who art beyond all paths; Obeisance to Thee whose splendour is mystically hidden and who art always engaged in the uplift of the devotees.

## \|\| 3.15.66 \|\|

*yacchaktyāhaṃ dhiyātmānaṃ haṃta veda na mūḍhadhī \|*  
*taṃ duratyayamāhātmyaṃ tvāṃ nataḥ smo mahāprabhum \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. We bow to Thee, the great lord, whose greatness cannot be surpassed; whose power the confounded fool with egotistic mind can never realise.

## \|\| 3.15.67 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*iti stutvā mahādevaṃ sarve viṣṇvādikāssurāḥ \|*  
*tūṣṇīmāsanprabhoragre sadbhaktinatakaṃdharāḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

67\. After eulogising the great lord, all the Devas, Viṣṇu and others, stood silently in front of the lord with their shoulders stooping down with great devotion.

## Chapter 16 - Prayer to Śiva offered by Brahmā and Viṣṇu

## \|\| 3.16.1 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*iti stutiṃ ca haryādikṛtāmākarṇya śaṃkaraḥ \|*  
*babhūvātiprasanno hi vijahāsa ca sūtikṛt \|\| 1 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

1\. On hearing the song of praise offered by Viṣṇu and others, Śiva, the cause of protection and enjoyment became delighted and smiled broadly.

## \|\| 3.16.2 \|\|

*brahmaviṣṇū tu dṛṣṭvā tau sastrīkau saṃgatau haraḥ \|*  
*yathocitaṃ samābhāṣya papracchāgamanaṃ tayoḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. On seeing Brahmā and Viṣṇu in the company of their consorts, Śiva addressed them suitably and asked them the purpose of their visit.

## \|\| 3.16.3 \|\|

*rudra uvāca \|*  
*hahara hāvadha devā munayaścādya nirbhayāḥ \|*  
*nijāgamanahetuṃ hi kathayasva sutattvataḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

Śiva said:—

3\. O Viṣṇu, O Brahmā, O devas and sages please tell me precisely and without fear the purpose of your visit.

## \|\| 3.16.4 \|\|

*kimarthamāgatā yūyaṃ kiṃ kāryaṃ ceha vidyate \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ śrotumicchāmi bhavatstutyā prasannadhīḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. I am delighted at the hymn sung by you all. I wish to hear why you have all come here and what is the work to be done here.

## \|\| 3.16.5 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*iti pṛṣṭe hareṇāhaṃ sarvalokapitāmahaḥ \|*  
*mune'vocaṃ mahādevaṃ viṣṇunā paricoditaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

5\. O sage, when we were asked by Śiva thus, I, the grandfather of the worlds, spoke to Lord Śiva on being prompted by Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 3.16.6 \|\|

*devadeva mahādeva karuṇāsāgara prabho \|*  
*yadarthamāgatāvāvāṃ tacchṛṇu tvaṃ surarṣibhiḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. O great lord, lord of Devas, O lord, the ocean of mercy, please listen why we both have come here in the company of devas and sages.

## \|\| 3.16.7 \|\|

*viśeṣatastavaivārthamāgatā vṛpabhadhvaja \|*  
*sahārthinassadāyogyamanyathā na jagadbhavet \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. O bull-emblemed deity, we have come here particularly for your sake, along with these suppliants. Otherwise the universe would not be in a proper state always.

## \|\| 3.16.8 \|\|

*kecidbhaviṣyaṃtyasurā mama vadhyā maheśvara \|*  
*harervadhyāstathā kecidbhavaṃtaścāpi kecana \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. O great lord, some demons are to be killed by me, some by Viṣṇu and some by you.

## \|\| 3.16.9 \|\|
