*kecittvadvīryajātasya tanayasya mahāprabho \|*  
*māyāvadhyāḥ prabho kecidbhaviṣyaṃtyasurāssadā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. O great lord, some of them would be killed by your son and some will be killed by me.

## \|\| 3.16.10 \|\|

*tavaiva kṛpayā śaṃbhossurāṇāṃ sukhamuttamam \|*  
*nāśayitvā'surān ghorāñjagatsvāsthyaṃ sadābhayam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The devas attain happiness only by your favour. The universe can attain peace and fearlessness only after destroying the demons.

## \|\| 3.16.11 \|\|

*yogayukte tvayi sadā rāga dveṣavivarjite \|*  
*dayāpātraikanirate na vadhyā hyathavā tava \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Or they cannot be killed by you in as much as you are always merciful, free from love and hate and engaged in Yoga.

## \|\| 3.16.12 \|\|

*arādhiteṣu teṣvīśa kathaṃ sṛṣṭistathā sthitiḥ \|*  
*ataśca bhavitā yuktaṃ nityaṃnityaṃ vṛṣadhvaja \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. O lord, Vṛṣadhvaja, how can the activities of creation, sustenance and dissolution be carried on properly for ever, if they are not killed?

## \|\| 3.16.13 \|\|

*sṛṣṭisthityaṃtakarmāṇi na kāryāṇi yadā tadā \|*  
*śarīrabhedaścāsmākaṃ māyāyāśca na yujyate \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The activities of creation, sustenance and dissolution are to be persued by us now and then. The difference in our bodies is perceptible only through illusion.

## \|\| 3.16.14 \|\|

*ekasvarūpā hi vayaṃ bhinnāḥ kāryasya bhedataḥ \|*  
*kāryabhedo na siddhaścedrūpabhedā'prayojanaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Though our real form is one, we are different in as much as our activities are different. If there is no functional difference, the difference in forms is meaningless.

## \|\| 3.16.15 \|\|

*eka eva tridhā bhinnaḥ paramātmā maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*māyāsvākāraṇādeva svataṃtro līlayā prabhuḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The same supreme Ātman, lord Śiva manifests in three different ways due to Māyā. The lord is independent in his divine sports.

## \|\| 3.16.16 \|\|

*vāmāṅgajo haristasya dakṣiṇāṃgabhavo hyaham \|*  
*śivasya hṛdayājjātastvaṃ hi pūrṇatanuśśivaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Viṣṇu is born of his left limb. I am born of the right limb. You are born of the heart of Śiva and are his full-fledged incarnation.

## \|\| 3.16.17 \|\|

*itthaṃ vayaṃ tridhā bhūtāḥ prabhābhinnasvarūpiṇaḥ \|*  
*śivāśivasutāstattvaṃ hṛdā viddhi sanātana \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Thus, O lord, we have become three, with different forms. We are the sons of Śivā and Śiva which, O eternal one, you must note.

## \|\| 3.16.18 \|\|

*ahaṃ viṣṇuśca sastrīkau saṃjātau kāryahetutaḥ \|*  
*lokakāryakarau prītyā tava śāsanataḥ prabho \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Viṣṇu and I have become united with our wives for the performance of our function. O lord, with great pleasure we carry on our activities in the world at your bidding.

## \|\| 3.16.19 \|\|

*tasmādviśvahitārthāya surāṇāṃ sukhahetave \|*  
*parigṛhṇīṣva bhāryārthe rāmāmekāṃ suśobhanām \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Hence, for the benefit of the universe, for the happiness of the devas, you must accept an auspicious lady as your wife.

## \|\| 3.16.20 \|\|

*anyacchṛṇu maheśāna pūrvavṛttaṃ smṛtaṃ mayā \|*  
*yannau puraḥpurā proktaṃ tvayaiva śivarūpiṇā \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. O great lord, please listen to another incident of bygone days, just recollected by me. You yourself as Śiva mentioned this to us formerly.

## \|\| 3.16.21 \|\|

*madrūpaṃ paramaṃ brahmannīdṛśaṃ bhavadaṃgataḥ \|*  
*prakaṭī bhavitā loke nāmnā rudraḥ prakīrtitaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. “O Brahmā, this my great form, exactly as this, will be manifested through your limb. He will be known as Rudra in the world.

## \|\| 3.16.22 \|\|

*sṛṣṭikartā'bhavadbrahmā hariḥ pālanakārakaḥ \|*  
*layakārī bhaviṣyāmi rudrarūpo guṇākṛtiḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Brahmā is the cause of creation, Viṣṇu is sustainer.

I shall be the cause of dissolution in the form of Rudra, a Saguṇa form.

## \|\| 3.16.23 \|\|

*striyaṃ vivāhya lokasya kariṣye kāryamuttamam \|*  
*iti saṃsmṛtya svaproktaṃ pūrṇaṃ kuru nijaṃ paṇam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. I shall marry a woman and perform the excellent function.” These are your words. Remembering these words please fulfil your promise.

## \|\| 3.16.24 \|\|

*nideśastava ca svāminnahaṃ sṛṣṭikaro hariḥ \|*  
*pālako layahetustvamāvirbhūtassvayaṃ śivaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. O lord, this is your own directive that I be the creator and Viṣṇu the protector. Śiva Himself has manifested in your form as the cause of dissolution.

## \|\| 3.16.25 \|\|

*tvāṃ vinā na samarthau hi āvāṃ ca svasvakarmaṇi \|*  
*lokakāryarato tasmādekāṃ gṛhṇīṣva kāminīm \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. We two are unable to perform our duties without you. Hence take up a beloved consort who too will be engaged in the activities of creation.

## \|\| 3.16.26 \|\|

*yathā padmālayā viṣṇossāvitrī ca yathā mama \|*  
*tathā sahacarīṃ śaṃbho kāṃtāṃ gṛhṇīṣva saṃprati \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. O Śiva, accept a beloved wife as a life companion in the same manner as Viṣṇu has taken the Goddess of the lotus (Lakṣmī) and I have taken the goddess of speech.

## \|\| 3.16.27 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*iti śrutvā vaco me hi brahmaṇaḥ purato hareḥ \|*  
*sa māṃ jagāda lokeśaḥ smerānanamukho haraḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. On hearing these words of mine—of Brahmā—in the presence of Viṣṇu, Śiva, the lord of worlds spoke to me with his face beaming with a smile.

## \|\| 3.16.28 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*he brahman he hare me hi yuvāṃ priyatarau sadā \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā tvāṃ ca mamānaṃdo bhavatyatitarāṃ khalu \|\| 28 \|\|*

Śiva said:—

28\. O Brahmā, O Viṣṇu, both of you are always dear to me. On seeing you both, my delight is enhanced indeed.

## \|\| 3.16.29 \|\|

*yuvāṃ suraviśiṣṭau hi tribhava svāminau kila \|*  
*kathanaṃ vāṃ gariṣṭheti bhavakāryaratātmanoḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. You two are the best among the devas. You are the masters of three worlds. What you say is indeed weighty since you two are engaged in Śiva’s work.

## \|\| 3.16.30 \|\|

*ucitaṃ na suraśreṣṭhau vivāhakaraṇaṃ mama \|*  
*taporataviraktasya sadā viditayoginaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. O best of Devas, it is not proper for me to marry as I am detached from the world and engaged in penance. I always practise Yoga.

## \|\| 3.16.31-32 \|\|

*yo nivṛttisumārgasthaḥ svātmārāmo niraṃjanaḥ \|*  
*avadhūtatanurjñānī svadraṣṭā kāmavarjitaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*avikārī hyabhogī ca sadāśuciramaṃgalaḥ \|*  
*tasya prayojanaṃ loke kāminyā kiṃ vadādhunā \|\| 32 \|\|*

31-32. Of what avail is a beloved to me in this world since I am in the path of abstinence delighting myself in my own soul, freed of attachment, unsullied, with the body of an ascetic, possessed of knowledge, seeing himself, free from aberrations and a non-reveller. Besides I am always unclean and inauspicious. Hence say now what can I do with a loving wife?

## \|\| 3.16.33-34 \|\|

*kevalaṃ yogalagnasya mamānaṃdassadāsti vai \|*  
*jñānahīnastu puruṣo manute bahu kāmakam \|\| 33 \|\|*

*vivāhakaraṇaṃ loke vijñeyaṃ parabaṃdhanam \|*  
*tasmāttasya rucirno me satyaṃ satyaṃ vadāmyaham \|\| 34 \|\|*

33-34. Even as I am engaged in Yoga, I experience the mystic Bliss. Only a man devoid of perfect knowledge will make much of marriage and desire it. Actually it is a great bondage. Hence I am not interested in it. This is truth. I am telling you the truth.

## \|\| 3.16.35 \|\|

*na svārthaṃ me pravṛttirhi samyaksvārthaviciṃtanāt \|*  
*tathāpi tatkariṣyāmi bhavaduktaṃ jagaddhitam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. None of my activities is pursued with self-interest. Yet I shall carry out what you have suggested for the benefit of the universe.

## \|\| 3.16.36 \|\|

*mattvā vaco gariṣṭhaṃ vā niyoktiparipūrttaye \|*  
*kariṣyāmi vivāhaṃ vai bhaktavaśyassadā hyaham \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Considering your weighty words for the fulfilment of my promise and the goal of my task, I shall marry. I am always subservient to my devotees.

## \|\| 3.16.37 \|\|

*paraṃtu yādṛśīṃ kāṃtāṃ grahīṣyāmi tathāpaṇam \|*  
*tacchṛṇuṣva hare brahman yuktameva vaco mama \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. O Viṣṇu, O Brahmā, you must hear what sort of a wife I will be taking in accordance with that promise. What I say is indeed proper.

## \|\| 3.16.38 \|\|

*yā me tejassamarthā hi grahītuṃ syādvibhāgaśaḥ \|*  
*tāṃ nideśaya bhāryārthe yoginīṃ kāmarūpiṇīm \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Suggest a woman of comely features and Yogic practice who will be able to receive my semen virile in parts.

## \|\| 3.16.39 \|\|

*yogayukte mayi tathā yoginyeva bhaviṣyati \|*  
*kāmāsakte mayi tathā kāminyeva bhaviṣyati \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. She must be a Yoginī when I practise Yoga and a loving woman when I indulge in love.

## \|\| 3.16.40-41 \|\|

*yamakṣaraṃ vedavido nigadaṃti manīṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*jyotīrūpaṃ śivaṃ te ca ciṃtayiṣye sanātanam \|\| 40 \|\|*

*tacciṃtāyāṃ yadā sakto brahman gacchāmi bhāvinīm \|*  
*tatra yā vighnajananī na bhavitrī hatāstu me \|\| 41 \|\|*

40-41. Sometimes I will be thinking about Śiva, my own form of splendour, the eternal principle which the scholars well versed in the Vedas call Imperishable. When I go in trance, O Brahmā, in that meditation, damned be she who causes an impediment therein.

## \|\| 3.16.42 \|\|

*tvaṃ vā viṣṇurahaṃ vāpi śivasya brahmarūpiṇaḥ \|*  
*aṃśabhūtā mahābhāgā yogyaṃ tadanuciṃtanam \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. You, Viṣṇu and I are the parts exceedingly of Brahman. So we are exceedingly fortunate. It is but proper to think about Him.

## \|\| 3.16.43 \|\|

*tacciṃtayā vinodvāhaṃ sthāsyāmi kamalāsana \|*  
*tasmājjāyāṃ prādiśa tvaṃ matkarmānugatāṃ sadā \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. It is this worry that kept me unmarried, O lotus-seated (Brahmā). Hence, get me a wife who will follow my activities ever.

## \|\| 3.16.44 \|\|

*tatrāpyekaṃ paṇaṃ me tvaṃ vṛṇu brahmaṃśca māṃ prati \|*  
*aviśvāso madukte cenmayā tyaktā bhaviṣyati \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. There is another condition to which please also listen, O Brahmā. If she evinces a disbelief in me or in what I say, I shall abandon her.

## \|\| 3.16.45 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*iti tasya vacaśśrutvāhaṃ sa viṣṇurharasya ca \|*  
*sasmitaṃ moditamano'vocaṃ ceti vinamrakaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

45\. On hearing these words of Śiva in the presence of Viṣṇu, smilingly and joyously I spoke thus in humble spirits.

## \|\| 3.16.46 \|\|

*śṛṇu nātha maheśāna mārgitā yādṛśī tvayā \|*  
*nivedayāmi suprītyā tāṃ striyaṃ tādṛśīṃ prabho \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. O lord Śiva, I shall suggest such a woman as you desire for yourself,

## \|\| 3.16.47 \|\|

*umā sā bhinnarūpeṇa saṃjātā kāryasādhinī \|*  
*sarasvatī tathā lakṣmīrdvidhā rūpā purā prabho \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. She is Umā, O lord. Formerly she manifested herself in the forms of Sarasvatī and Lakṣmī in order to fulfil her task.

## \|\| 3.16.48 \|\|

*pādmā kāṃtā'bhavadviṣṇostathā mama sarasvatī \|*  
*tṛtīyarūpā sā nābhūllokakāryahitaiṣiṇī \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Lakṣmī became the wife of Viṣṇu and Sarasvatī mine. From her desire for the welfare of the world she has taken a third form.

## \|\| 3.16.49 \|\|

*dakṣasya tanayā yābhūtsatī nāmnā tu sā vibho \|*  
*saivedṛśī bhavedbhāryā bhaveddhi hitakāriṇī \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. She is born now as Dakṣa’s daughter in the name of Satī. O lord, she will be an ideal wife rendering wholesome service.

## \|\| 3.16.50 \|\|

*sā tapasyati deveśa tvadarthaṃ hi dṛḍhavratā \|*  
*tvāṃ patiṃ prāptukāmā vai mahātejovatī satī \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. O lord of devas, at present she is performing penance for securing you. She is firm in her austere rites. She desires you as her husband. Indeed she is highly brilliant.

## \|\| 3.16.51 \|\|

*dātuṃ gaccha varaṃ tasyai kṛpāṃ kuru maheśvara \|*  
*tāṃ vivāhaya suprītyā varaṃ dattvā ca tādṛśam \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. O Lord Śiva, be merciful to her. Grant her the desired boon. Then lovingly marry her.

## \|\| 3.16.52 \|\|

*harermama ca devānāmiyaṃ vāñchāsti śaṃkara \|*  
*paripūraya saddṛṣṭyā paśyāmotsavamādarāt \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. O Śiva, this is the desire of Viṣṇu, the devas and mine too. With a benignant look fulfil our desire. Let us see the wedding festivities with devotion.

## \|\| 3.16.53 \|\|

*maṅgalaṃ paramaṃ bhūyāttrilokeṣu sukhāvaham \|*  
*sarvajvaro vinaśyedvai sarveṣāṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Let there be a happy and auspicious occasion (for that) in the three worlds. Let all ailments vanish. Let there be no doubt about it.

## \|\| 3.16.54 \|\|

*athavāsmadvacaśśeṣe vadaṃta madhusūdanaḥ \|*  
*līlājākṛtimīśānaṃ bhaktavatsalamacyutaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Then at the conclusion of my speech, Viṣṇu, the slayer of Madhu demon, spoke to Śiva who assumes various forms during His divine sports and who is favourably disposed to his devotees.

## \|\| 3.16.55 \|\|

*viṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*devadeva mahādeva karuṇākara śaṃkara \|*  
*yaduktaṃ brahmaṇā sarvaṃ maduktaṃ tanna saṃśayaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

Viṣṇu said:—

55\. O great lord, the lord of devas, O Śiva the merciful, there is no doubt in this that what Brahmā has said constitutes what I have to say.

## \|\| 3.16.56 \|\|

*tatkuruṣva maheśāna kṛpāṃ kṛtvā mamopari \|*  
*sanāthaṃ kuru saddṛṣṭyā trilokaṃ suvivāhyatām \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Hence, O great lord be merciful to me and carry out this request. Marrying her please make the three worlds blessed with a leader with benignant look.

## \|\| 3.16.57 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityuktvā bhagavān viṣṇustūṣṇīmāsa mune sudhīḥ \|*  
*tathā stutiṃ vihasyāha sa prabhurbhaktavatsalaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

57\. O sage, after saying this, the intelligent lord Viṣṇu kept silent. The great lord Rudra, favourably disposed to His devotees, smilingly said, “So be it.”

## \|\| 3.16.58 \|\|

*tatastvāvāṃ ca saṃprāpya cājñāṃ sa munibhissuraiḥ \|*  
*agacchāvasveṣṭadeśaṃ sastrīkau paraharṣitau \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Then both of us took leave of him and in a cheerful mood returned to our respective abodes along with our wives, the sages and the devas.

## Chapter 17 - Satī granted the boon

## \|\| 3.17.1 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityuktvā sarvadevaiśca kṛtā śaṃbhornutiḥ parā \|*  
*śivācca sā varaṃ prāptā śṛṇu hyādarato mune \|\| 1 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

1\. O sage, thus I have told you about the prayer to Śiva offered by all the devas. How Satī obtained a boon from Śiva, you shall now listen with respect.

## \|\| 3.17.2 \|\|

*atho satī punaḥ śuklapakṣe'ṣṭamyāmupoṣitā \|*  
*āśvine māsi sarveśaṃ pūjayāmāsa bhaktitaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Then, in the month of Āśvina (September-October), Satī observed a fast on the eighth day of the bright half and worshipped Śiva with great devotion.

## \|\| 3.17.3 \|\|

*iti naṃdāvrate pūrṇe navamyāṃ dinabhāgataḥ \|*  
*tasyāstu dhyānamagnāyāḥ pratyakṣamabhavaddharaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. When her Nandā rites were concluded on the ninth day (Navamī), while she was engrossed in meditation, Śiva became visible to her.

## \|\| 3.17.4-6 \|\|

*sarvāṅgasundaro gauraḥ paṃcavaktrastrilocanaḥ \|*  
*caṃdrabhālaḥ prasannātmā śitikaṃṭhaścaturbhuja \|\| 4 \|\|*

*triśūlabrahmakavarābhayadhṛgbhasmabhāsvaraḥ \|*  
*svardhunyā vilasacchīrṣassakalāṅgamanoharaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*mahālāvaṇyadhāmā ca koṭicandrasamānanaḥ \|*  
*koṭismarasamākāṃtissarvathā strīpriyākṛtiḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

4-6. He was fair-complexioned, handsome in appearance, had five faces\[1\] and three eyes\[2\]. The crescent moon adorned His forehead. He was in a joyous mood. He had four arms and His neck was blue in colour. He was holding trident and an amulet (Brahmakavaca) for protection. He was brilliant with dust. His head was comely with the celestial river Gaṅgā. He was gay in all parts of his body. He was the abode of great beauty. His face shone with the brilliance of ten million moons. His lustre matched that of ten million cupids. In every respect His features were such as appeal to all women.

## \|\| 3.17.7 \|\|

*pratyakṣato haraṃ vīkṣya satī sedṛvidhaṃ prabhum \|*  
*vavande caraṇau tasya sulajjāvanatānanā \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. On seeing Śiva directly in such a form she bent her head from shyness and she knelt at his feet.

## \|\| 3.17.8 \|\|

*atha prāha mahādevassatīṃ sadvratadhāriṇīm \|*  
*tāmicchannapi bhāryārthaṃ tapaścaryāphalapradaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Although He desired her to be his wife He wished to bestow on her the fruit of her penance. Thus He spoke to her in the state of her penance.

## \|\| 3.17.9 \|\|

*mahādeva uvāca \|*  
*dakṣanaṃdini prītosmi vratenānena suvrate \|*  
*varaṃ varaya saṃdāsye yattavābhimataṃ bhavet \|\| 9 \|\|*

Śiva said:—

9\. O daughter of Dakṣa, of good rites, I am delighted by these rites you have observed. Choose a boon. I shall grant it whatever it may be.

## \|\| 3.17.10 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*jānannapīha tadbhāvaṃ mahādevo jagatpatiḥ \|*  
*jagau varaṃ vṛṇīṣveti tadvākyaśravaṇecchayā \|\| 10 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

10\. Although Śiva, the lord of the universe, knew her desire, he said—“Choose a boon.” It was because He desired to hear her speak.

## \|\| 3.17.11 \|\|

*sāpi trapāvaśā yuktā vaktuṃ no hṛdi yatsthitam \|*  
*śaśāka sā tvabhīṣṭaṃ yattallajjācchāditaṃ punaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. She too, who was highly bashful, could not speak out her mind as it was covered up by bashfulness.

## \|\| 3.17.12 \|\|

*premamagnā'bhavatsāti śrutvā śivavacaḥ priyam \|*  
*tajjñātvā suprasannobhūcchaṃkaro bhaktavatsalaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. On realising that she was fully immersed in love on hearing Śiva’s pleasing words, Śaṅkara who was favourably disposed to His devotees was highly pleased.

## \|\| 3.17.13 \|\|

*varaṃ brūhi varaṃ brūhi prāheti sa punardrutam \|*  
*satībhaktivaśaśśaṃbhuraṃtaryāmī satāṃ gatiḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. He repeatedly urged her “Speak out the boon you wish to choose, speak out the boon.” Śiva, the immanent lord, the goal of the good was drawn to Satī by her devotion.

## \|\| 3.17.14-15 \|\|

*atha trapāṃ svāṃ saṃdhāya yadā prāha haraṃ satī \|*  
*yatheṣṭaṃ dehi varada varamityanivārakam \|\| 14 \|\|*

*tadā vākyasyāvasānamanavekṣya vṛṣadhvajaḥ \|*  
*bhava tvaṃ mama bhāryeti prāha tāṃ bhaktavatsalaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. Somehow suppressing her bashfulness when Satī spoke “As you please give unto me, O bestower of boons, the desired boon or the bridegroom of my desire, without any hindrance,” the full-emblemed deity Śiva who is favourably disposed to his devotees, did not wait for the completion of her request and said—“you be my wife.”

## \|\| 3.17.16 \|\|

*etacchrutvā vacastasya sābhīṣṭaphala bhāvanam \|*  
*tūṣṇīṃ tasthau pramuditā varaṃ prāpya manogatam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. On hearing his words embracing the fruits of her cherished desire she kept silent. She was highly delighted on obtaining the boon (or bridegroom) stationed in her mind.

## \|\| 3.17.17 \|\|

*sakāmasya harasyāgre sthitā sā cāruhāsinī \|*  
*akaronnijabhāvāṃśca hāvānkāmavivarddhanān \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. She stood smiling sweetly before Śiva who was full of love. She opened her inmost feelings through various subtle gestures that increased notions of love.

## \|\| 3.17.18 \|\|

*tato bhāvānsamādāya śṛṃgārākhyo rasastadā \|*  
*tayościtte viveśāśu kalā hāvā yathoditam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Taking up these notions, gestures and feelings, the flavour of love called Śṛṅgāra entered their hearts.

## \|\| 3.17.19 \|\|

*tatpraveśāttu devarṣe lokalīlānusāriṇoḥ \|*  
*kāpyabhikhyā tayorāsīccitrā candramasoryathā \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. O celestial sage, by the advent of the flavour of love, a peculiar glow, in the usual manner of worldly sports, was manifest in them as in the star Citrā and the moon.

## \|\| 3.17.20 \|\|

*reje satī haraṃ prāpya snigdhabhinnāṃjanaprabhā \|*  
*candrābhyāśe'bhralekheva sphaṭikojjvalavarṣmaṇaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. In the presence of Śiva whose body shone with the brilliance of crystal, Satī who had the glossy brilliance of split collyrium, shone like a line of cloud near the moon.

## \|\| 3.17.21 \|\|

*atha sā tamuvācedaṃ haraṃ dākṣāyaṇī muhuḥ \|*  
*suprasannā karau baddhvā natakā bhaktavatsalam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. The delighted daughter of Dakṣa with her palms joined frequently in reverence, joyfully spoke to Śiva who is favourably disposed to His devotees.

## \|\| 3.17.22 \|\|

*satyuvāca \|*  
*devadeva mahādeva vivāha vidhinā prabhau \|*  
*piturme gocarīkṛtya māṃ gṛhāṇa jagatpate \|\| 22 \|\|*

Satī said:—

22\. O great lord of Devas, lord of the universe, please take me with due marital rites in the presence of my father.

## \|\| 3.17.23 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*evaṃ satīvacaḥ śrutvā maheśo bhaktavatsalaḥ \|*  
*tathāstviti vacaḥ prāha nirīkṣya premataśca tām \|\| 23 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

23\. On hearing these words of Satī, Śiva, favourably disposed to His devotees, glanced lovingly at her and said—“So be it.”

## \|\| 3.17.24 \|\|

*dākṣāyaṇyapi taṃ natvā śaṃbhuṃ vijñāpya bhaktitaḥ \|*  
*prāptājñā māturabhyāśamagānmohamudānvitā \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. The daughter of Dakṣa bowed to Śiva with devotion, sought and received His consent and returned to her mother with a fascinating gaiety.

## \|\| 3.17.25 \|\|

*haropi himavatprasthaṃ praviśya ca nijāśramam \|*  
*dākṣāyaṇīviyogādvai kṛcchradhyānaparo'bhavat \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Śiva returned to His hermitage on the ridges of the Himālayas and began meditations though with difficulty, as He still felt the pangs of love in separation from Satī, the daughter of Dakṣa.

## \|\| 3.17.26 \|\|

*samādhāya manaḥ śaṃbhurlaukikīṃ gatimāśritaḥ \|*  
*ciṃtayāmāsa devarṣe manasā māṃ vṛṣadhvajaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Calming his mind somehow, O celestial sage, Śiva, the bull-emblemed deity, thought of me in the usual conventions of the world.

## \|\| 3.17.27 \|\|

*tatassaṃciṃtyamānohaṃ maheśena triśūlrinā \|*  
*purastātprāviśaṃ tūrṇaṃ harasiddhipracoditaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Being thus thought of by the trident-bearing Śiva, I approached Him immediately prodded by Śiva’s power of meditation.

## \|\| 3.17.28 \|\|

*yatrāsau himavatprasthe tadviyogī haraḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*sarasvatīyutastāta tatraiva samupasthitaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Accompanied by Sarasvatī I reached that place on the Himālayan ridge where Śiva stayed pining in the anguish of love for Satī.

## \|\| 3.17.29 \|\|

*sarasvatīyutaṃ māṃ ca devarṣe vīkṣya sa prabhuḥ \|*  
*utsukaḥ premabaddhaśca satyā śaṃbhuruvāca ha \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. O celestial sage, seeing me in the company of Sarasvatī, lord Śiva who was entangled in the clutches of Satī’s love said thus:—

## \|\| 3.17.30 \|\|

*śaṃbhuruvāca \|*  
*ahaṃ brahmansvārthaparaḥ parigrahakṛtau ca yat \|*  
*tadā svatvamivasvārthe pratibhāti mamādhunā \|\| 30 \|\|*

Śiva said:—

30\. O Brahmā, since, in the matter of accepting a wife I showed a little selfishness, I have a feeling of possession in everything connected with self-interest.

## \|\| 3.17.31 \|\|

*ahamārādhitassatyāddākṣāyaṇyātha bhaktitaḥ \|*  
*tasyai varo mayā datto naṃdāvrataprabhāvataḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. I have been propitiated by Satī, the daughter of Dakṣa with devotion. Thanks to the sacred Nandā rites, I have given her a boon.

## \|\| 3.17.32 \|\|

*bhartā bhaveti ca tayā matto brahman varo vṛtaḥ \|*  
*mama bhāryā bhavetyuktaṃ mayā tuṣṭena sarvathā \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. O Brahmā, the boon “O be my husband” was sought of me by her. Glad at heart in every respect I had told her “Be my wife.”

## \|\| 3.17.33 \|\|

*athāvadattadā māṃ sā satī dākṣāyaṇī tviti \|*  
*piturme gocarīkṛtya māṃ gṛhāṇa jagatpate \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Then Satī, the daughter of Dakṣa told me like this—“O lord of the universe, please accept me in the presence of my father.”

## \|\| 3.17.34 \|\|

*tadapyaṃgīkṛtaṃ brahmanmayā tadbhakti tuṣṭitaḥ \|*  
*sā gatā bhavanaṃ māturahamatrāgato vidhe \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. O Brahmā, that too I granted her as I was satisfied with her devotion, She returned to her mother’s house, O Brahmā and I returned here.

## \|\| 3.17.35 \|\|

*tasmāttvaṃ gaccha bhavanaṃ dakṣasya mama śāsanāt \|*  
*tāṃ dakṣopi yathā kanyāṃ dadyānme'raṃ tathā vada \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. At my bidding you must approach Dakṣa. Speak to him so that he shall give his daughter in marriage to me at once.

## \|\| 3.17.36 \|\|

*satīviyogabhaṃgassyādyathā me tvaṃ tathā kuru \|*  
*samāśvāsaya taṃ dakṣaṃ sarvavidyāviśāradaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Exploit all means to cut short her days of separation. O adept in every lore, console Dakṣa.

## \|\| 3.17.37 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*ityudīrya mahādevassakāśe me prajāpateḥ \|*  
*sarasvatīṃ vilokyāśu viyogavaśagobhavat \|\| 37 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

37\. Saying thus in my presence Lord Śiva looked at Sarasvatī and evinced pangs of separation.

## \|\| 3.17.38 \|\|

*tenāhamapi cājñaptaḥ kṛtakṛtyo mudānvitaḥ \|*  
*prāvocaṃ ceti jagatāṃ nāthaṃ taṃ bhaktavatsalam \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Being thus commanded by him I became contented and delighted. I said this to the lord of worlds who is favourably disposed to his devotees.

## \|\| 3.17.39 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*yadāttha bhagavañśambho tadvicārya suniścitam \|*  
*devānāṃ mukhyassvārtho hi mamāpi vṛṣabhadhvaja \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. O lord Śiva, on considering what you say, this is certain, O bull-emblemed deity, that the chief self-interest of the devas is my interest too.

## \|\| 3.17.40 \|\|

*dakṣastubhyaṃ sutāṃ svāṃ ca svayameva pradāsyati \|*  
*ahaṃ cāpi vadiṣyāmi tvadvākyaṃ tatsamakṣataḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Dakṣa himself will offer you his daughter. I too shall mention your desire in his presence.

## \|\| 3.17.41 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityudīryya mahādevamahaṃ sarveśvaraṃ prabhum \|*  
*agamaṃ dakṣanilayaṃ syaṃdanenātiveginā \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. After saying this to the great lord I went to Dakṣa’s residence by a speedy flight.

## \|\| 3.17.42 \|\|

*\|\| nārada uvāca \|*  
*vidhe prājña mahābhāga vada no vadatāṃ vara \|*  
*satyai gṛhāgatāyai sa dakṣaḥ kimakarottataḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

Nārada said:—

42\. O Brahmā, of great fortune and intellect, O eloquent one, please tell me. When Satī returned to the house what did Dakṣa do thereafter?

## \|\| 3.17.43 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*tapastaptvā varaṃ prāpya manobhilaṣitaṃ satī \|*  
*gṛhaṃ gatvā piturmātuḥ praṇāmamakarottadā \|\| 43 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

43\. Having concluded the austerities, and secured what she desired as a boon, Satī went home and made obeisance to her father and mother.

## \|\| 3.17.44 \|\|

*mātre pitre'tha tatsarvaṃ samācakhyau maheśvarāt \|*  
*varaprāptiḥ svasakhyā vai satyāstuṣṭastu bhaktitaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Her girl friends informed her mother and father about the acquisition of boon by their friend Satī from lord Śiva who was glad at her devotion.

## \|\| 3.17.45 \|\|

*mātā pitā ca vṛttāṃtaṃ sarvaṃ śrutvā sakhīmukhāt \|*  
*ānandaṃ paramaṃ lebhe cakre ca paramotsavam \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. The parents who obtained the news through her friends were very glad and celebrated a great festival.

## \|\| 3.17.46 \|\|

*dravyaṃ dadau dvijātibhyo yathābhīṣṭamudāradhīḥ \|*  
*anyebhyaścāṃdhadīnebhyo vīriṇī ca mahāmanāḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. The noble Dakṣa gave as much wealth to brahmins as they desired. The noble Vīriṇī gave similar gifts to the blind, the poor and the needy.

## \|\| 3.17.47 \|\|

*vīriṇī tāṃ samāliṃgya svasutāṃ prītivarddhinīm \|*  
*mūrdhnyupāghrāya muditā praśaśaṃsa muhurmuhuḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Vīriṇī embraced her daughter on the head and delightfully praised her frequently.

## \|\| 3.17.48 \|\|

*atha dakṣaḥ kiyatkāle vyatīte dharmavittamaḥ \|*  
*ciṃtayāmāsa deyeyaṃ svasutā śambhave katham \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. After some time had elapsed, Dakṣa, the foremost of those who knew Dharma, thought of the procedure of handing over his daughter to Śiva.

## \|\| 3.17.49 \|\|

*āgatopi mahādevaḥ prasannassa jagāma ha \|*  
*punareva kathaṃ sopi sutārthe'trāgamiṣyati \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. The great Lord Śiva had come here himself out of his sheer delight. But he has gone back. How will he come again to woo my daughter?

## \|\| 3.17.50 \|\|

*prāsthāpyotha mayā kaścicchaṃbhornikaṭamaṃjasā \|*  
*naitadyogyaṃ nigṛhṇīyādyadyevaṃ viphalārdanā \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Can a person be sent to Śiva immediately? No, this is not proper. If he spurns the offer it will be a fruitless torment.

## \|\| 3.17.51-52 \|\|

*athavā pūjayiṣyāmi tameva vṛṣabhadhvajam \|*  
*madīyatanayā bhaktyā svayameva yathā bhavet \|\| 51 \|\|*

*tathaiva pūjitassopi vāṃchatyāryaprayatnataḥ \|*  
*śaṃbhurbhavatu madbharttetyevaṃ dattavareṇatat \|\| 52 \|\|*

51-52. Or shall I worship the same bull-emblemed deity? He has already granted the boon to her that He, the lord Himself, shall be her husband. Even if He is delighted at my worship, as at my daughter’s devotion, he may like everything to be done through some noble mediator.

## \|\| 3.17.53 \|\|

*iti ciṃtayatastasya dakṣasya purato'nvaham \|*  
*upasthitohaṃ sahasā sarasvatyanvitastadā \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Even as Dakṣa was constantly thinking like this, I suddenly appeared before him along with Sarasvatī.

## \|\| 3.17.54 \|\|

*māṃ dṛṣṭvā pitaraṃ dakṣaḥ praṇamyāvanataḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*āsanaṃ ca dadau mahyaṃ svabhavāya yathocitam \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. On seeing me Dakṣa, my son, paid due respects and stood waiting. He gave me a fitting seat to sit on.

## \|\| 3.17.55 \|\|

*tato māṃ sarvalokeśaṃ tatrāgamana kāraṇam \|*  
*dakṣaḥ papraccha sa kṣipraṃ ciṃtāviṣṭopi harṣitaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Dakṣa was worried with thoughts. But he became greatly delighted at my sight. He asked me the purpose of my visit.

## \|\| 3.17.56 \|\|

*dakṣa uvāca \|*  
*tavātrāgamane hetuḥ kaḥ praveśe sa sṛṣṭikṛt \|*  
*mamopari suprasādaṃ kṛtvācakṣva jagadguro \|\| 56 \|\|*

Dakṣa said:—

56\. O creator, preceptor of the universe, be kind and tell me the purpose of your visit to me?

## \|\| 3.17.57 \|\|

*putrasnehātkāryavaśādatha vā lokakāraka \|*  
*mamāśramaṃ samāyāto hṛṣṭasya tava darśanāt \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. O creator of worlds, is your visit prompted by your love for your son or for any special task that you have come to my hermitage? I am delighted on seeing you.

## \|\| 3.17.58 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*iti pṛṣṭassvaputreṇa dakṣeṇa munisattama \|*  
*vihasannabruvaṃ vākyaṃ modayaṃstaṃ prajāpatim \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. O excellent sage, being asked thus by my son Dakṣa, I spoke with a smile thereby delighting Dakṣa, the lord of the subjects.

## \|\| 3.17.59 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*śṛṇu dakṣa yadarthaṃ tvatsamīpamahamāgataḥ \|*  
*tvattokasya hitaṃ mepi bhavatopi tadīpsitam \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. O Dakṣa, listen. I shall tell you why I have come here. The wholesome benefit of your progeny is what I desire and what you must also desire.

## \|\| 3.17.60 \|\|

*tava putrī samārādhya mahādevaṃ jagatpatim \|*  
*yo varaḥ prārthitastasya samayoyamupāgataḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Your daughter has propitiated Śiva, the lord of the universe and has secured a boon. The opportune moment for the same has arrived now.

## \|\| 3.17.61 \|\|

*śaṃbhunā tava putryarthaṃ tvatsakāśamahaṃ dhuvam \|*  
*prasthāpitosmi yatkṛtyaṃ śreya stadavadhāraya \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. It is certainly for your daughter that I have been sent to you by Śiva. Listen attentively to your duty conducive to your benefit.

## \|\| 3.17.62 \|\|

*varaṃ dattvā gato rudrastāvatprabhṛti śaṃkaraḥ \|*  
*tvatsutāyā viyogena na śarma labhateṃjasā \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. After granting the boon, Śiva returned. But, ever since, he has not had any mental peace due to separation from your daughter.

## \|\| 3.17.63-64 \|\|

*alabdhacchidramadano jigāya giriśaṃ na yam \|*  
*sarvaiḥ puṣpamayairbāṇairyatnaṃ kṛtvāpi bhūriśaḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

*sa kāmabāṇaviddhopi parityajyātma ciṃtanam \|*  
*satīṃ viciṃtayannāste vyākulaḥ prākṛto yathā \|\| 64 \|\|*

63-64. Kāma could not conquer Śiva as he did not hit at any vulnerable point although he tried it by means of his flower-arrows. But He, without being hit by Kāma’s arrows, has now abandoned meditation on Ātman and begun to think of Satī. He is as excited as any other ordinary man.

## \|\| 3.17.65 \|\|

*vismṛtya praśrutāṃ vāṇīṃ gaṇāgre viprayogataḥ \|*  
*kva satītyevamabhito bhāṣate nikṛtāvapi \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. He asks His attendants “where is Satī?”, as He suffers from the pang of separation. When they say “No”, He hears the words but soon forgets them and repeats the question.

## \|\| 3.17.66 \|\|

*mayā yadvāṃchitaṃ pūrvaṃ tvayā ca madanena ca \|*  
*marīcyādyaimunivaraistatsiddhamadhunā suta \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. O son, what has been desired by me before, by you, by Kāma and the sages—Marīci and others, has been achieved now.

## \|\| 3.17.67 \|\|

*tvatputryārādhitaśśaṃbhussopi tasyā viciṃtanāt \|*  
*anuśodhayituṃ prepsurvarttate himavadgirau \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Śiva was propitiated by your daughter. He now stays in the Himālayan mountains thinking about her and desirous of getting her in order to console her.

## \|\| 3.17.68 \|\|

*yathā nānāvidhairbhāvaissattvāttena vratena ca \|*  
*śaṃbhurārādhitastena tathaivārādhyate satī \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Just as Śiva has been worshipped by her by performing different rites with Sāttvic feelings, so also Satī is being worshipped by Him.

## \|\| 3.17.69 \|\|

*tasmāttu dakṣatanayāṃ śaṃbhvarthaṃ parikalpitām \|*  
*tasmai dehyavilaṃbena kṛtā te kṛtakṛtyatā \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. Hence, O Dakṣa, offer immediately your daughter to Śiva for whom she has been intended. Thereby you will get contentment and relief.

## \|\| 3.17.70 \|\|

*ahaṃ tamānayiṣyāmi nāradena tvadālayam \|*  
*tasmai tvamenāṃ saṃyaccha tadarthe parikalpitām \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Through Nārada I shall bring Him here. Give her to Him for whom she has been intended.

## \|\| 3.17.71 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*śrutvā mama vacaśceti sa me putrotiharṣitaḥ \|*  
*evamevetimāṃ dakṣa uvāca pariharṣitaḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. On hearing these words of mine, my son Dakṣa was highly delighted. He said delightfully. “It is so. It is so.”

## \|\| 3.17.72 \|\|

*tatassohaṃ mune tatrāgamamatyaṃtaharṣitaḥ \|*  
*utsuko lokanirato giriśo yatra saṃsthitaḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. O sage, I too delightfully went to the place where Śiva was eagerly waiting.

## \|\| 3.17.73 \|\|

*gate nārada dakṣopi sadāra tanayo hyapi \|*  
*abhavatpūrṇakāmastu pīyūṣairiva pūritaḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. At my departure Dakṣa, along his wife and daughter, felt contented as if he had been filled with nectar.

## Chapter 18 - Marriage of Śiva and Satī

## \|\| 3.18.1 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*rudrapārśve tvayi gate kimabhūccaritaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*kā vārtā hyabhavattāta kiṃ cakāra haraḥ svayam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Nārada said:—

1\. When you approached Śiva, what was it that transpired? What were the events? What did Śiva Himself do?

## \|\| 3.18.2 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*athāhaṃ śivamānetuṃ prasannaḥ parameśvaram \|*  
*āsadaṃ hi mahādevaṃ himavadgirisaṃsthitam \|\| 2 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

2\. I approached lord Śiva who was staying in the Himālayan mountains in order to bring Him (to the house of Dakṣa). I was in a joyous mood.

## \|\| 3.18.3 \|\|

*māṃ vīkṣya lokasraṣṭāramāyāṃtaṃ vṛṣabhadhvajaḥ \|*  
*manasā saṃśayaṃ cakre satīprāptau muhurmuhuḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. On seeing me, the creator of the world, approaching, the bull-emblemed Śiva had doubts about the acquisition of Satī.

## \|\| 3.18.4 \|\|

*atha prītyā haro loka gatimāśritya līlayā \|*  
*satyā bhaktyā ca māṃ kṣipramuvāca prākṛto yathā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Due to His real affection or as a part of His divine sports in conformity with the conventions of the world or due to the devotion of Satī, Śiva immediately spoke to me like an ordinary man.

## \|\| 3.18.5 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*kimakārṣītsurajyeṣṭha satyarthe tvatsutassa mām \|*  
*kathayasva yathā svāṃtaṃ na dīrye manmathena hi \|\| 5 \|\|*

Śiva said:—

5\. O eldest of devas, what did your son (Daṣka) do in the matter of Satī. Tell me lest my heart should be severed by the cupid.

## \|\| 3.18.6 \|\|

*dhāvamāno viprayogo māmeva ca satīṃ prati \|*  
*abhihaṃti surajyeṣṭha tyaktvānyāṃ prāṇadhāriṇīm \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. This anxiety of separation, O eldest of devas, running between Satī and me attacks only me, leaving the other, the woman, who very well sustains her life.

## \|\| 3.18.7 \|\|

*satīti satataṃ brahman vada kāryaṃ karomyaham \|*  
*abhedānmama sā prāpyā tadvidhe kriyatāṃ tathā \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. O Brahmā, respect the name Satī. Let me do what shall be done. She is not different from me. She has to be attained by me. O Brahmā, act accordingly.

## \|\| 3.18.8 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*iti rudroktavacanaṃ lokācārasugarbhitam \|*  
*śrutvāhaṃ nāradamune sāṃtvayannagadaṃ śivam \|\| 8 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

8\. O sage Nārada, on hearing the words of Śiva best speaking of His strict adherence to the conventions of the world I told Śiva, consoling Him.

## \|\| 3.18.9 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*satyarthaṃ yanmama suto vadati sma vṛṣadhvaja \|*  
*tacchraṇuṣva nijāsādhya siddhamityavadhāraya \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. O bull-emblemed God, hear what my son told me regarding Satī. Rest assured that what you wanted to achieve has been achieved.

## \|\| 3.18.10 \|\|

*deyā tasmai mayā putrī tadarthaṃ parikalpitā \|*  
*mamābhīṣṭamidaṃ kāryaṃ tvadvākyādadhikaṃ punaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Dakṣa has said “My daughter shall go to Him. She has been intended for Him. This has been my desire.” Now that you also say, it is all the more necessary that it shall be carried out.

## \|\| 3.18.11 \|\|

*matputryārādhitaśśaṃbhuretadarthaṃ svayaṃ punaḥ \|*  
*sopyanviṣyati māṃ yasmāttadā deyā mayā hare \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. For this purpose Śiva had been propitiated by my daughter. Now He too seeks her. Hence She has to be offered to Him by me.

## \|\| 3.18.12 \|\|

*śubhe lagna sumuhūrte samāgacchatu soṃtikam \|*  
*tadā dāsyāmi tanayāṃ bhikṣārthaṃ śaṃbhave vidhe \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Let Him come to me in an auspicious conjunction of stars. Then, O Brahmā, I shall offer my daughter to Him in the form of Alms.

## \|\| 3.18.13 \|\|

*ityuvāca sa māṃ dakṣastasmāttvaṃ vṛṣabhadhvaja \|*  
*śubhe muhūrte tadveśma gaccha tāmānayasva ca \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. O bull-emblemed God, Dakṣa has told me so. Go to his house in an auspicious hour and bring her here.

## \|\| 3.18.14 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*iti śrutvā mama vaco laukikī gatimāśritaḥ \|*  
*uvāca vihasanrudro mune māṃ bhaktavatsalaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. O sage, on hearing these words of mine, Rudra, who is favourably disposed to His devotees, spoke with a smile, strictly adhering to the conventions of the world.

## \|\| 3.18.15 \|\|

*rudra uvāca \|*  
*gamiṣye bhavatā sārddhaṃ nāradena ca tadgṛham \|*  
*ahameva jagatsraṣṭastasmāttvaṃ nāradaṃ smara \|\| 15 \|\|*

Śiva said:—

15\. I shall go to his house accompanied by you and Nārada. Hence, O creator of the universe, you remember Nārada.

## \|\| 3.18.16 \|\|

*marīcyādīn svaputrāṃśca mānasānapi saṃsmara \|*  
*taiḥ sārddhaṃ dakṣanilayaṃ gamiṣye sagaṇo vidhe \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Remember your mental as well as physical sons—Marīci and others. O Brahmā, with all my attendants and with them I shall go to Dakṣa’s house.

## \|\| 3.18.17 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityājñaptohamīśena lokācārapareṇa ha \|*  
*saṃsmaraṃ nāradaṃ tvāṃ ca marīcyadīnsutāṃstathā \|\| 17 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

17\. Thus commanded by Śiva following the conventions of the world, I remembered you, Nārada and the other sons—Marīci etc.

## \|\| 3.18.18 \|\|

*tatassamāgatāssarve mānasāstanayāstvayā \|*  
*mama smaraṇamātreṇa hṛṣṭāste drutamādarāt \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Immediately after I remembered them, all of my mental sons and you arrived in a happy mood.

## \|\| 3.18.19 \|\|

*viṣṇussamāgatastūrṇaṃ smṛto rudreṇa śaivarāṭ \|*  
*sasvasainyaḥ kamalayā garuḍārūḍhaṃ eva ca \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Remembered by Śiva, Viṣṇu, the foremost of Śiva’s devotees, came there along with the Goddess Lakṣmī seated on Garuḍa and accompanied by his army.

## \|\| 3.18.20 \|\|

*adha caitrasite pakṣe nakṣatre bhagadaivate \|*  
*trayodaśyāṃ dine bhānau nigacchatsa maheśvaraḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. In the bright half of the month of Caitra (March-April) on the thirteenth day when the star was Uttarā Phalguni on a Sunday, lord Śiva started.

## \|\| 3.18.21 \|\|

*sarvaissuragaṇaissārddhaṃ brahmaviṣṇu purassaraiḥ \|*  
*tathā tairmunibhirgacchan sa babhau pathi śaṃkaraḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Going ahead, with all the devas, led by Brahmā and Viṣṇu and accompanied by the sages, Śiva shone brilliantly.

## \|\| 3.18.22 \|\|

*mārge samutsavo jāto devādīnāṃ ca gacchatām \|*  
*tathā haragaṇānāṃ ca sānaṃdamanasāmati \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Great festivities were arranged by Devas and the attendants of Śiva who were in the happiest mood, on their way.

## \|\| 3.18.23 \|\|

*gajagovyāghrasarpāśca jaṭā caṃdrakalā tathā \|*  
*jagmuḥ sarve bhūṣaṇatvaṃ yathāyogyaṃ śivecchayā \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. The hides of elephant and tiger, the serpents, the crescent moon and the matted hair, all became fitting ornaments and embellishments at Śiva’s will.

## \|\| 3.18.24 \|\|

*tataḥ kṣaṇena balinā balīvardena yoginā \|*  
*sa viṣṇupramukhaḥ prītyā prāpa dakṣālayaṃ haraḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Then in a trice, Śiva reached Dakṣa’s abode seated on his speedy bull and along with Viṣṇu and others.

## \|\| 3.18.25 \|\|

*tato dakṣo vinītātmā saṃprahṛṣṭatanūruhaḥ \|*  
*prayayau sanmukhaṃ tasya saṃyuktassakalairnijaiḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. With great humility and boundless joy, Dakṣa along with his people welcomed Him.

## \|\| 3.18.26 \|\|

*sarve suragaṇāstatra svayaṃ dakṣeṇa satkṛtāḥ \|*  
*pārśve śreṣṭhaṃ ca munibhirupaviṣṭā yathākramam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The Devas and their attendants were honoured by Dakṣa. The sages were seated in their due order.

## \|\| 3.18.27 \|\|

*parivāryākhilāndevāngaṇāṃśca munibhiryathā \|*  
*dakṣassamānayāmāsa gṛhābhyaṃtarataśśivam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Then Dakṣa took Śiva within the house along with the devas and the sages.

## \|\| 3.18.28 \|\|

*atha dakṣaḥ prasannātmā svayaṃ sarveśvaraṃ haram \|*  
*samānarca vidhānena dattvāsanamanuttamam \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. The delighted Dakṣa worshipped lord Śiva, after offering him an excellent seat.

## \|\| 3.18.29 \|\|

*tato viṣṇuṃ ca māṃ viprānsurānsarvāngaṇāṃstathā \|*  
*pūjayāmāsa sadbhaktyā yathocitavidhānataḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. He worshipped Viṣṇu, me, the brahmins, devas and the Gaṇas of Śiva, with great devotion and in a fitting manner.

## \|\| 3.18.30 \|\|

*kṛtvā yathocitāṃ pūjāṃ teṣāṃ pūjyādibhistathā \|*  
*cakāra saṃvidaṃ dakṣo munibhirmānasaiḥ punaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. After performing the suitable worship, Dakṣa in the presence of respectable sages announced the marriage agreement.

## \|\| 3.18.31 \|\|

*tato māṃ pitaraṃ prāha dakṣaḥ prītyā hi matsutaḥ \|*  
*praṇipatya tvayā karma kāryaṃ vaivāhikaṃ vibho \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Then Dakṣa, my son, knelt before me, his father, with pleasure and said—“O lord, the marriage rites shall be performed by you.”

## \|\| 3.18.32 \|\|

*bāḍhamityahamapyuktvā prahṛṣṭaināṃtarātmanā \|*  
*samutthāya tato'kārṣaṃ tatkāryamakhilaṃ tathā \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Saying ‘Amen’ I got up with a delightful heart and performed the preliminary rites.

## \|\| 3.18.33 \|\|

*tataśśubhe muhūrte hi lagne grahabalānvite \|*  
*satī nijasutāṃ dakṣo dadau harṣeṇa śaṃbhave \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Then in an auspicious conjunction of stars with the planets in a propitious position, Dakṣa joyfully gave his daughter Satī to Siva.

## \|\| 3.18.34 \|\|

*udvāhavidhinā sopi pāṇiṃ jagrāha harṣitaḥ \|*  
*dākṣāyaṇyā varatanostadānīṃ vṛṣabhadhvajaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. As a part of the rites of marriage the delighted Śiva grasped the hand of Satī of comely appearance.

## \|\| 3.18.35 \|\|

*ahaṃ haristvadādyā vai munayaśca surā gaṇāḥ \|*  
*nemussarve saṃstutibhi stoṣayāmāsurīśvaram \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. We all, Viṣṇu, I, you and other sages, bowed to Śiva and delighted Him with laudatory hymns.

## \|\| 3.18.36 \|\|

*samutsavo mahānāsīnnṛtyagānapurassaraḥ \|*  
*ānandaṃ paramaṃ jagmussarve munigaṇāḥ surāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. There were great festivities with songs and dances. The sages and the devas were in a gay mood.

## \|\| 3.18.37 \|\|

*kanyā dattvā kṛttārtho'bhūttadā dakṣo hi matsutaḥ \|*  
*śivāśivau prasannau ca nikhilaṃ maṃgalālayam \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. After offering his daughter, Dakṣa, my son, was extremely satisfied, Satī and Śiva were in happy mood. Everything concluded auspiciously.

## Chapter 19 - Description of Śiva’s sports

## \|\| 3.19.1 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*kṛtvā dakṣastutādānaṃ yautakaṃ vividhaṃ dadau \|*  
*harāya suprasannaśca dvijebhyo vividhaṃ dhanam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

1\. After giving his daughter in marriage, Dakṣa gave her different articles in the form of dowry. Many gifts were given to Śiva. Dakṣa gave monetary gifts to the brahmins with great delight.

## \|\| 3.19.2 \|\|

*atha śaṃbhu mudāgatya samutthāya kṛtāṃjaliḥ \|*  
*sārddhaṃ kamalayā cedamuvāca garuḍadhvajaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Then Viṣṇu stood up. Approaching Śiva with palms joined in reverence and accompanied by Lakṣmī, the Garuḍa-vehicled God Viṣṇu spoke thus.

## \|\| 3.19.3 \|\|

*\|\| viṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*devadeva mahādeva karuṇāsāgara prabho \|*  
*tvaṃ pitā jagatāṃ tāta satī mātākhilasya ca \|\| 3 \|\|*

Viṣṇu said:—

3\. O great lord, O ocean of mercy, lord of devas, O dear one, you are the father and Satī is the mother of the world.

## \|\| 3.19.4 \|\|

*yuvāṃ līlāvatārau dve satāṃ kṣemāya sarvadā \|*  
*khalānāṃ nigrahārthāya śrutireṣā sanātanī \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. You have taken incarnation out of sheer sport for the welfare of the good and suppression of the wicked—so says the eternal scripture.

## \|\| 3.19.5 \|\|

*snigdhanīlāṃjanaśyāmaśobhayā śobhase hara \|*  
*dākṣāyaṇyā yathā cāhaṃ pratilomena padmayā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. You are fair-complexioned and Satī has the blue lustre of the glossy collyrium. I on the other hand am blue in hue and Lakṣmī is fair-complexioned. You two shine in juxtaposition with us two.

## \|\| 3.19.6 \|\|

*devānāṃ vā nṛṇāṃ rakṣāṃ kuru satyā'nayā satām \|*  
*saṃsārasāriṇāṃ śambho maṃgalaṃ sarvadā tathā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. O Śiva, along with this Satī, protect the good people and the devas. Similarly always bestow auspicious goodness upon the people of this world.

## \|\| 3.19.7 \|\|

*ya enāṃ sābhilāṣo vai dṛṣṭvā śrutvāthavā bhavet \|*  
*taṃ hanyāssarvabhūteśa vijñaptiriti me prabho \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. O lord of living beings, this is my humble submission. you shall kill the man, whoever it may be, who sees or hears her with lust in his mind.

## \|\| 3.19.9 \|\|

*svasthānaṃ harirāgatya sthita āsīnmunīśvara \|*  
*utsavaṃ kārayāmāsa jugopa caritaṃ ca tat \|\| 9 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

On hearing these words of Viṣṇu, lord Śiva laughed. The omniscient lord told the slayer of Madhu, “Be it so.”

9\. O great sage, after this, Viṣṇu returned to his abode. He kept the incident quite secret but asked the people to continue the festivities.

## \|\| 3.19.10 \|\|

*ahaṃ devīṃ samāgatya gṛhyoktavidhinā'khilam \|*  
*agnikāryaṃ yathoddiṣṭamakārṣaṃ ca suvistaram \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. I approached the Goddess (Satī) and performed in detail all the sacrificial rites as laid down in the Gṛhyasūtras.

## \|\| 3.19.11 \|\|

*tataśśivā śivaścaiva yathāvidhi prahṛṣṭavat \|*  
*agneḥ pradakṣiṇaṃ cakre madācāryadvijājñayā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Then at my bidding in the capacity of the main priest, Śivā and Śiva duly and with great delight performed the circumambulation of the sacred fire.

## \|\| 3.19.12 \|\|

*tadā mahotsavastatrādbhutobhūddvijasattama \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ sukhadaṃ vādyaṃ gītanṛtyapurassaram \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. O excellent brahmin, then wonderfully great festivities were conducted with beatings of drums and playings on musical instruments accompanied by songs and dances pleasing everyone.

## \|\| 3.19.13 \|\|

*tadānīmadbhutaṃ tatra caritaṃ samabhūdati \|*  
*suvismayakaraṃ tāta tacchṛṇu tvaṃ vadāmi te \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Then a surprisingly strange- event occurred there. Dear one, listen to it. I shall tell you.

## \|\| 3.19.14 \|\|

*durjñeyā śāṃbhavī māyā tayā saṃmohitaṃ jagat \|*  
*sacarācaramatyaṃtaṃ sadevāsuramānuṣam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Śiva’s power of illusion is inscrutable. The whole universe, the mobile or immobile, is deluded by it, Devas and Asuras.

## \|\| 3.19.15 \|\|

*yo'haṃ śaṃbhuṃ mohayituṃ puraicchaṃ kapaṭena ha \|*  
*māṃ ca taṃ śaṃkarastāta mohayāmāsa līlayā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Formerly I wished to delude Śiva by deceitful means. But now Śiva Himself has deluded me by means of His divine sports.

## \|\| 3.19.16 \|\|

*icchetparāpakāraṃ yassa tasyaiva bhaveddhruvam \|*  
*iti matvā'pakāraṃ no kuryādanyasya pūruṣaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. If a man wishes evil of others, he himself becomes the victim of the same. There is no doubt about it. Realising this, no man shall wish evil of anyone else.

## \|\| 3.19.17 \|\|

*pradakṣiṇāṃ prakurvaṃtyā vahnessatyāḥ padadvayam \|*  
*āvirbabhūva vasanāttadadrākṣamahaṃ mune \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. O sage, while going round the fire, the feet of Satī protruded out of the cloth that covered them. I looked at them.

## \|\| 3.19.18 \|\|

*madanāviṣṭacetāśca bhūtvāṃgāni vyalokayam \|*  
*ahaṃ satyā dvijaśreṣṭha śivamāyāvimohitaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. My mind being afflicted by love I stared at the limbs of Satī. O excellent brahmin, I was deluded by Śiva’s Māyā.

## \|\| 3.19.19 \|\|

*yathā yathāhaṃ ramyāṇi vyaikṣamaṃgāni kautukāt \|*  
*satyā babhūva saṃhṛṣṭaḥ kāmārto hi tathā tathā \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The more I stared at the beautiful limbs of Satī eagerly the more I became thrilled like a love-afflicted man.

## \|\| 3.19.20 \|\|

*ahamevaṃ tathā dṛṣṭvā dakṣajāṃ ca pativratām \|*  
*smarāviṣṭamanā vaktraṃ draṣṭukāmobhavaṃ mune \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Staring thus at the chaste daughter of Dakṣa and being afflicted by the cupid, O sage, I craved to see her face.

## \|\| 3.19.21 \|\|

*na śaṃbhorlajjayā vaktraṃ pratyakṣaṃ ca vilokitam \|*  
*na ca sā lajjayāviṣṭā karoti pragaṭaṃ mukham \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Since she was bashful in the presence of Śiva I could not see her face. She did not show out her face on account of shyness.

## \|\| 3.19.22 \|\|

*tatastaddarśanārthāya sadupāyaṃ vicārayan \|*  
*dhūmraghoreṇa kāmārto'kārṣaṃ tacca tataḥ param \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Then I began to consider proper means whereby I could see the face. Afflicted much by the cupid, I pitched upon the production of airful smoke as the means thereof.

## \|\| 3.19.23-24 \|\|

*ārdreṃdhanāni bhūrīṇi kṣiptvā tatra vibhāvasau \|*  
*svalpājyāhutivinyāsādārdradravyodbhavastathā \|\| 23 \|\|*

*prādurbhūtastato dhūmo bhūyāṃstatra samaṃtataḥ \|*  
*tādṛg yena tamo bhūtaṃ vedībhūmivinirmitam \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. I put many wet twigs into the fire. Only very little ghee did I pour into the fire. Much smoke arose out of the fire from the wet twigs, so much so that darkness enveloped the whole altar ground (and the neighbourhood).

## \|\| 3.19.25 \|\|

*tato dhūmākule netre maheśaḥ parameśvaraḥ \|*  
*hastābhyāṃ chādayāmāsa bahulīlākaraḥ prabhuḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Then lord Śiva, the supreme God, indulged in many sports, covered his eyes (apparently) afflicted by smoke.

## \|\| 3.19.26 \|\|

*tato vastraṃ samutkṣipya satīvaktramahaṃ mune \|*  
*avekṣaṃ kila kāmārtaḥ prahṛṣṭenāṃtarātmanā \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Then, O sage, afflicted by the cupid and delighted in the heart of hearts, I lifted her veil and stared into the face of Satī.

## \|\| 3.19.27 \|\|

*muhurmuhurahaṃ tāta paśyāmi sma satīmukham \|*  
*athendriyavikāraṃ ca prāptavānasmi so'vaśaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. I looked at the face of Satī many a time. I was helpless in curbing the onset of a sensuous organism.

## \|\| 3.19.28 \|\|

*mama retaḥ pracaskaṃda tatastadvīkṣaṇāddrutam \|*  
*caturbindumita bhūmau tuṣāracayasaṃnibham \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Four drops of my semen virile got displaced and fell on the ground like drops of dew as a result of staring into her face.

## \|\| 3.19.29 \|\|

*tatohaṃ śaṃkito maunī tatkṣaṇaṃ vismito mune \|*  
*ācchādayesma tadreto yathā kaścidbubodha na \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. O sage, then I was stunned into silence. I was surprised. I became suspicious. I covered up the semen drops lest anyone should see them.

## \|\| 3.19.30 \|\|

*atha tadbhagavāñchaṃbhurjñātvā divyena cakṣuṣā \|*  
*retovaskaṃdanāttasya kopādetaduvāca ha \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. But the lord Śiva saw it by His divine vision. The trickling down of the semen excited His fury and He said—

## \|\| 3.19.31 \|\|

*rudra uvāca \|*  
*kimetadvihitaṃ pāpa tvayā karma vigarhitam \|*  
*vivāhe mama kāṃtāyā vaktraṃ dṛṣṭaṃ na rāgataḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

Śiva said:—

31\. “O sinful wretch, what a despicable mess you have perpetrated? At the time of her marriage you have passionately gazed at the face of my beloved.

## \|\| 3.19.32 \|\|

*tvaṃ vetsi śaṃkareṇaitatkarma jñātaṃ na kiṃcana \|*  
*trailokyepi na me'jñātaṃ gūḍhaṃ tasmātkathaṃ vidhe \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. You think that this blunder has not been known by me at all. There is nothing that is unknown to me in the three worlds. O Brahman, how can it then remain hidden?

## \|\| 3.19.33 \|\|

*yatkiṃcittriṣu lokeṣu jaṃgamaṃ sthāvaraṃ tathā \|*  
*tasyāhaṃ madhyago mūḍha tailaṃ yadvattilāṃti kam \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. O foolish fellow, just as the oil is latent in the gingelly seed so also I am present within everything in the three worlds whether mobile or immobile.”

## \|\| 3.19.34 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityuktvā priya viṣṇurmāṃ tadā viṣṇuvacaḥ smaran \|*  
*iyeṣa haṃtuṃ brahmāṇaṃ śūlamudyamya śaṃkaraḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

34\. Saying thus, and remembering the words of Viṣṇu, Śiva who dearly loved Viṣṇu lifted His trident and wished to kill me.

## \|\| 3.19.35 \|\|

*śabhuṃnodyamite śūle māṃ ca haṃtuṃ dvijottama \|*  
*marīcipramukhāste vai hāhākāraṃ ca cakrire \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. O excellent brahmin, when the trident was lifted up by Him to kill me, Marīci and others raised a hue and cry.

## \|\| 3.19.36 \|\|

*tato devagaṇāssarve munayaścākhilāstathā \|*  
*tuṣṭuvuśśaṃkaraṃ tatra prajvalaṃtaṃ bhayāturāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Then all the devas and the sages, extremely terrified, began to eulogise Him who was blazing there.

## \|\| 3.19.37 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*deva deva mahādeva śaraṇāgatavatsala \|*  
*brahmāṇaṃ rakṣa rakṣeśa kṛpāṃ kuru maheśvara \|\| 37 \|\|*

Devas said:—

37\. O lord, O great lord, favourably disposed to those who seek refuge, O Śiva, save me. O lord Śiva, be pleased.

## \|\| 3.19.38 \|\|

*jagatpitā maheśa tvaṃ jaganmātā satī matā \|*  
*haribrahmādayassarve tava dāsāssuraprabho \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. O great lord, you are the father of the universe. Satī is the mother of the universe. O lord of Devas, Viṣṇu, Brahmā and others are all your slaves.

## \|\| 3.19.39 \|\|

*adbhutākṛtilīlastvaṃ tava māyādbhutā prabho \|*  
*tayā vimohitaṃ sarvaṃ vinā tvadbhaktimīśvara \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Mysterious is your form, O lord, and mysterious are your divine sports. Your Māyā is enigmatic and complex. Everything and everyone except your devotee is deluded by it, O Lord.

## \|\| 3.19.40 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*itthaṃ bahutaraṃ dīnā nirjarā munayaśca te \|*  
*tuṣṭuvurdevadeveśaṃ krodhāviṣṭaṃ maheśvaram \|\| 40 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

40\. Thus in many ways, the timid and frightened devas and the sages eulogised the lord of devas who was furious.

## \|\| 3.19.41 \|\|

*dakṣo maivaṃ maivamiti pāṇimudyamya śaṃkitaḥ \|*  
*vārayāmāsa bhūteśaṃ kṣiprametya purogataḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Suspecting some terrible disaster, Dakṣa raised his hand and rushed at Śiva, preventing Him with shouts of “O don’t do this, O don’t do this”.

## \|\| 3.19.42 \|\|

*athāgre saṃgataṃ vīkṣya tadā dakṣaṃ maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*pratyuvācāpriyamidaṃ saṃsmaranprārthanāṃ hareḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Seeing Dakṣa in front of Him in a state of excited suspicion, and remembering the request of Viṣṇu, lord Śiva spoke these displeasing words:—

## \|\| 3.19.43 \|\|

*maheśvara uvāca \|*  
*viṣṇunā metibhaktena yadidānīmudīritam \|*  
*mayāpyaṃgīkṛtaṃ kartuṃ tadihaiva prajāpate \|\| 43 \|\|*

Lord Śiva said:—

43\. O patriarch Dakṣa what has just been requested by Viṣṇu my great devotee and agreed to by me shall be done here.

## \|\| 3.19.44 \|\|

*satīṃ yasyābhilāṣassan vīkṣeta vadha taṃ prabho \|*  
*iti viṣṇuvacassatyaṃ vidhiṃ hatvā karomyaham \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. “O lord, whoever stares at Satī lustfully shall be killed by you.” I shall make these words of Viṣṇu true by killing Brahmā.

## \|\| 3.19.45 \|\|

*sābhilāṣaḥ kathaṃ brahmā satīṃ samavalokayat \|*  
*abhavattyaktaretāstu tato hanmi kṛtāgasam \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Why did Brahmā stare at Satī lustfully? Moreover he has committed a sin by discharging his semen. Hence I shall kill him.

## \|\| 3.19.46 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityuktavati deveśa maheśe krodhasaṃkule \|*  
*cakaṃpire janāḥ sarve sadevamunimānuṣāḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. When the lord of Devas spoke thus furiously, all the people including Devas, sages and human beings trembled.

## \|\| 3.19.47 \|\|

*hāhākāro mahānāsīdaudāsīnyaṃ ca sarvaśaḥ \|*  
*abhūvambikalo'tīva tadāhaṃ tadvimohakaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. There was a piteous cry of distress. Everywhere tense suspense prevailed. Then I who wanted to delude Him was myself deluded.

## \|\| 3.19.48 \|\|

*atha viṣṇurmaheśātipriyaḥ kāryavicakṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*tamevaṃvādinaṃ rudraṃ tuṣṭāva praṇatassudhīḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Then the intelligent Viṣṇu, the great favourite of Śiva and very clever in managing all affairs bowed down and lauded Rudra who spoke as before.

## \|\| 3.19.49 \|\|

*stutvā ca vividhaiḥ stotraiśśaṃkaraṃ bhaktavatsalam \|*  
*idamūce vārayaṃstaṃ kṣipraṃ bhūtvā purassaraḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Standing in front of Him and singing various songs of praise to Śiva who is favourably disposed towards His devotees He prevented Him and said thus:

## \|\| 3.19.50 \|\|

*viṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*vidhinna jahi bhūteśa sraṣṭāraṃ jagatāṃ prabhum \|*  
*ayaṃ śaraṇagastedya śaraṇāgatavatsalaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

Viṣṇu said:—

50\. O lord Śiva, do not kill Brahmā, the creator and lord of the worlds. He has sought refuge in you and you are reputed to be favourably disposed to those who seek refuge in you.

## \|\| 3.19.51 \|\|

*ahaṃ te'tipriyo bhakto bhaktarāja itīritaḥ \|*  
*vijñaptiṃ hṛdi me mattvā kṛpāṃ kuru mamopari \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. O lord, I am a great favourite of yours and am called the chief of Devotees. Keeping my submission in mind be merciful towards me.

## \|\| 3.19.52 \|\|

*anyacca śṛṇu me nātha vacanaṃ hetugarbhitam \|*  
*tanmanuṣva maheśāna kṛpāṃ kṛtvā mamopari \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. O lord, please hear another statement of mine of very great significance. You must consider it, O lord Śiva, being merciful to me.

## \|\| 3.19.53 \|\|

*prajāssraṣṭumayaṃ śaṃbho prādurbhūtaścaturmukhaḥ \|*  
*asminhate prajāsraṣṭā nāstyanyaḥ prākṛto'dhunā \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. O Śiva, this four-faced deity has manifested himself to create the subjects. If he were killed, there will be none to create the subjects.

## \|\| 3.19.54 \|\|

*sṛṣṭisthityaṃtakarmāṇi kariṣyāmaḥ punaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*trayo devā vayaṃ nātha śivarūpa tvadājñayā \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. O lord, we three are carrying out the functions of creation, sustenance and dissolution repeatedly as you bid us in the form of Siva.

## \|\| 3.19.55 \|\|

*etasminnihate śambho kastvatkarma kariṣyati \|*  
*tasmānna vadhyo bhavatā sṛṣṭikṛllayakṛdvibho \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. O Śiva, if he is killed who will carry out your directives? Hence O lord, the annihilator, you shall not kill this creator.

## \|\| 3.19.56 \|\|

*anenaiva satī kanyā dakṣasya ca śivā vibho \|*  
*sadupāyena vai bhāryā bhavadarthe prakalpitā \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. O lord, it was by him that Satī the daughter of Dakṣa was fixed up as your wife by good means.

## \|\| 3.19.57 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya maheśastu vijñaptiṃ viṣṇunā kṛtām \|*  
*pratyuvācākhilāṃstāṃśca śrāvayaṃśca dṛḍhavrataḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

57\. On hearing this entreaty of Viṣṇu, Śiva of steady resolve proclaimed in reply making everyone hear.

## \|\| 3.19.58 \|\|

*maheśa uvāca \|*  
*deva deva rameśāna viṣṇo matprāṇavallabha \|*  
*na nivāraya māṃ tāta vadhādasya khalastvayam \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. O Viṣṇu, Lord of devas and as dear to me as my vital airs, do not prevent me from killing him. He is a rogue.

## \|\| 3.19.59 \|\|

*pūrayiṣyāmi vijñaptiṃ pūrvānteṃgīkṛtāṃ mayā \|*  
*mahāpāpakaraṃ duṣṭaṃ hanmyenaṃ caturānanam \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. I shall fulfil your first entreaty already accepted by me. I shall kill this wicked four-faced one who has committed a great sin.

## \|\| 3.19.60 \|\|

*ahameva prajāssrakṣye sarvāḥ sthiracarā api \|*  
*anyaṃ srakṣye sṛṣṭikaramathavāhaṃ svatejasā \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. I shall myself create all living beings—mobile and immobile. Or by my splendid power I shall create another creator.

## \|\| 3.19.61 \|\|

*hatvainaṃ vidhimevāhaṃ svapaṇaṃ pūrayan kṛtam \|*  
*sraṣṭāramekaṃ srakṣyāmi na nivāraya meśa mām \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Killing this Brahmā and keeping up my plighted word, I shall create another creator. Excuse me. Do not prevent me.

## \|\| 3.19.62 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*iti tasya vacaśśrutvā girīśa syāha cācyutaḥ \|*  
*smitaprabhinnahṛdayaḥ punarmaivamitīrayan \|\| 62 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

62\. On hearing these words of Śiva, Viṣṇu spoke again smiling to himself and saying “O don’t do this.”

## \|\| 3.19.63 \|\|

*acyuta uvāca \|*  
*pratijñāpūraṇaṃ yogyaṃ parasminpuruṣesti vai \|*  
*vicārayasva vadhyeśa bhavatyātmani na prabho \|\| 63 \|\|*

Viṣṇu said:—

63\. Fulfilling the promise is but proper in you, the great Being. But consider, O lord, the desire to kill cannot be directed to one’s own Self.

## \|\| 3.19.64 \|\|

*trayo devā vayaṃ śaṃbho tvadātmānaḥ parā nahi \|*  
*ekarūpā na bhinnāśca tattvatassuvicāraya \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. We three, O Śiva, are your own selves. We are not different. We are of the same form. Think over the exact state.

## \|\| 3.19.65 \|\|

*tatastadvacanaṃ śrutvā viṣṇossvātipriyasya saḥ \|*  
*śaṃbhurūce punastaṃ vai khyāpayannātmano gatim \|\| 65 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

65\. Then on hearing the words of Viṣṇu a great favourite, Śiva spoke again announcing His own special pursuit.

## \|\| 3.19.66 \|\|

*\|\| śambhuruvāca \|*  
*he viṣṇo sarvabhakteśa kathamātmā vidhirmama \|*  
*lakṣyate bhinna evāyaṃ pratyakṣeṇāgrataḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

Śiva said:—

66\. O Viṣṇu, lord of all devotees, how can this Brahmā be my own self? He is observed as different, standing before me.

## \|\| 3.19.67 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*ityājñapto maheśena sarveṣāṃ puratastadā \|*  
*idamūce mahādevaṃ toṣayan garuḍadhvajaḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

67\. Thus commanded by Śiva in the presence of all, Viṣṇu spoke thus propitiating the great lord.

## \|\| 3.19.68 \|\|

*viṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*na brahmā bhavato bhinno na tvaṃ tasmātsadāśiva \|*  
*na vāhaṃ bhavato bhinno na mattvaṃ parameśvara \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. O Sadāśiva, Brahmā is not different from you, nor are you different from him. I am not different from you, O great lord, nor are you different from me.

## \|\| 3.19.69 \|\|

*sarvaṃ jānāsi sarvajña parameśa sadāśiva \|*  
*manmukhādakhilānsarvaṃ saṃśrāvayitumicchasi \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. O omniscient, great lord, Sadāśiva, you know all. But you wish to make it all heard through my oral explanation.

## \|\| 3.19.70 \|\|

*tvadājñayā vadāmīśa śṛṇvaṃtu nikhilāssurāḥ \|*  
*munayaścāpare śaivaṃ tattvaṃ saṃdhārya svaṃ manaḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. O Śiva I say at your bidding. May all the devas, the sages and others hear after retaining the principles of Śaiva cult in their mind.

## \|\| 3.19.71 \|\|

*pradhānasyā'pradhānasya bhāgābhāgasya rūpiṇaḥ \|*  
*jyotirmayasya bhāgāste vayaṃ devāḥ prabhostrayaḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. O lord, of thee, the manifest and unmanifest, divisible and indivisible, possessed of form or of formless brilliance, we three are the parts.

## \|\| 3.19.72 \|\|

*kastvaṃ kohaṃ ca ko brahmā tavaiva paramātmanaḥ \|*  
*aṃśatrayamidaṃ bhinnaṃ sṛṣṭisthityaṃtakāraṇam \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. Who are you? Who am I? Who is Brahmā? Your own three parts—you being the supreme soul. They are different only as the cause of creation, sustenance and dissolution.

## \|\| 3.19.73 \|\|

*ciṃtayasvātmanātmānaṃ svalīlādhṛtavigrahaḥ \|*  
*ekastvaṃ brahma saguṇo hyaṃśabhūtā vayaṃ trayaḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. You shall think of yourself through your own self. O divine one, taking up a physical body by your own sports, you are the sole Brahman, while we three in attributive forms are your very parts.

## \|\| 3.19.74 \|\|

*śirogrīvādibhedena yathaikasyaiva varṣmaṇaḥ \|*  
*aṃgāni te tatheśasya tasya bhagatrayaṃ hara \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. O Śiva, just as the selfsame body has the parts of head, neck, etc. so also we are the three parts of Śiva.

## \|\| 3.19.75 \|\|

*yajjyotirabhraṃ svapuraṃ purāṇaṃ kūṭasthamavyaktamanaṃtarūpam \|*  
*nityaṃ ca dīrghādiviśeṣaṇādyairhīnaṃ śivastvaṃ tata eva sarvam \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. O Śiva, you are the supreme brilliance, the firmament, having your own abode. You are the primordial Being, the immovable, the unmanifest, of endless forms, the eternal and devoid of attributes—length etc. From this form alone everything has emanated.

## \|\| 3.19.76 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|\| etacchrutvā vacastasya mahādevo munīśvara \|*  
*babhūva suprasannaśca na jaghāna sa māṃ tataḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

76\. O excellent sage, on hearing these words the great lord Śiva was delighted. He did not slay me.

## Chapter 20 - Satī’s marriage festival

## \|\| 3.20.3 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*nivṛtte śaṃkare cāsmadvadhādbhaktānukaṃpini \|*  
*abhavannirbhayāssarve sukhinastu prasannakāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

Nārada said:—

l-2. O lord Brahmā, the fortunate one, foremost of Śiva’s devotees, you have narrated the wonderfully auspicious story of Śiva. O dear one, what happened after that? Please continue to narrate the story of the moon-crested Śiva and Satī, the wonderful story that quells all sins.

Brahmā said:—

3\. When Śiva who is sympathetic towards His devotees, desisted from killing me, all became fearless, happy and pleased.

## \|\| 3.20.4 \|\|

*nataskaṃdhāssāṃjalayaḥ praṇemurnikhilāśca te \|*  
*tuṣṭuvuśśaṃkaraṃ bhaktyā cakrurjayaravaṃ mudā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. All of them bowed with stooping shoulders, and palms joined in reverence. They lauded Śiva with devotion. They shouted cries of victory with pleasure.

## \|\| 3.20.5 \|\|

*tasminneva kāle'haṃ prasanno nirbhayo mune \|*  
*astavaṃ śaṃkaraṃ bhaktyā vividhaiśca śubhastavaiḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. At the same time, delighted and fearless, O sage, I eulogised Śiva with devotion by means of auspicious prayers.

## \|\| 3.20.6 \|\|

*tatastuṣṭamanāśśaṃbhurbahulīlākaraḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*mune māṃ samuvācedaṃ sarveṣāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ tadā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. O sage, the lord Śiva who was delighted in His mind and who is an adept in many a divine sport spoke to me within the hearing of all.

## \|\| 3.20.7 \|\|

*\|\| rudra uvāca \|*  
*brahman tāta prasannohaṃ nirbhayastvaṃ bhavādhunā \|*  
*svaśīrṣaṃ spṛśa hastena madājñāṃ kurvasaṃśayam \|\| 7 \|\|*

Rudra said:—

7\. “Dear Brahmā, I am glad. You can be free from fear. You touch your head with your hand. Unhesitatingly carry out my behest.”

## \|\| 3.20.8 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya vacaśśambhorbahulīlākṛtaḥ prabhoḥ \|*  
*spṛśan svaṃ kaṃ tathā bhūtvā prāṇamaṃ vṛṣabhadhvajam \|\| 8 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

8\. On hearing these words of Lord Śiva adept in divine sports I touched my head and in the same manner bowed to Śiva.

## \|\| 3.20.9 \|\|

*yāvadevamahaṃ svaṃ kaṃ spṛśāmi nijapāṇinā \|*  
*tāvattatra sthitaṃ sadyastadrūpavṛṣavāhanam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. When I thus touched my head I assumed the shape of his vehicle, the bull.

## \|\| 3.20.10 \|\|

*tato lajjāparītāṃgassthitaścāhamadhomukhaḥ \|*  
*indrādyairamaraissarvaissudṛṣṭassarvatassthitaiḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Then I was too much ashamed. I stood with my head bent down. Indra and other devas standing around saw me in that plight.

## \|\| 3.20.11 \|\|

*athāhaṃ lajjayāviṣṭaḥ praṇipatya maheśvaram \|*  
*pravocaṃ saṃstutiṃ kṛtvā kṣamyatāṃ kṣamyatāmiti \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Ashamed that I was, I repeatedly bowed to Him and after offering prayers spoke to Him again: “I may be excused. I may be excused.”

## \|\| 3.20.12 \|\|

*asya pāpasya śudhyarthaṃ prāyaścittaṃ vada prabho \|*  
*nigrahaṃ ca tathānyāyaṃ yena pāpaṃ prayātu me \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. “O lord, tell me the mode of atonement for my sin. Even killing is justifiable. May my sin be removed thereby.”

## \|\| 3.20.13 \|\|

*ityuktastu mayā śaṃbhuruvāca praṇataṃ hi tam \|*  
*suprasannataro bhūtvā sarveśo bhaktavatsalaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Thus addressed by me, Śiva, the lord of all, who is favourable, delightedly told me as I stood bowing to Him.

## \|\| 3.20.14 \|\|

*śaṃbhuruvāca \|*  
*anenaiva svarūpeṇa madadhiṣṭhitakena hi \|*  
*tapaḥ kuru prasannātmā madārādhanatatparaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

Śiva said:—

14\. In this very form (of a bull) whereon I sit, you shall perform penance with pleasure in your heart and desire for propitiating me.

## \|\| 3.20.15 \|\|

*khyātiṃ yāsyasi sarvatra nāmnā rudraśiraḥ kṣitau \|*  
*sādhakaḥ sarvakṛtyānāṃ tejobhājāṃ dvijanmanām \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. You will acquire the glory of being called “The head of Rudra” in the world. You will be the accomplisher of rites for brahmins of great repute.

## \|\| 3.20.16 \|\|

*manuṣyāṇāmidaṃ kṛtyaṃ yasmādvīryyaṃ tvayā'dhunā \|*  
*tasmāttvaṃ mānuṣo bhūtvā vicariṣyasi bhūtale \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Discharge of semen is the act of human beings and as you have done the same, you will be born as a man and be roaming over the earth.

## \|\| 3.20.17-18 \|\|

*yastvāṃ cānena rūpeṇa dṛṣṭvā kau vicariṣyati \|*  
*kimetadbrahmaṇo mūrdhni vadanniti purāntakaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*tataste ceṣṭitaṃ sarvaṃ kautukācchroṣyatīti yaḥ \|*  
*paradārakṛtāttyāgānmuktiṃ sadyassa yāsyati \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. When you wander over the earth in this form, people will be asking, “What is there on the head of Brahmā?” and you shall reply “Śiva”. Any body who has committed the sin of outraging the modesty of another man’s wife will be free from that sin if he eagerly hears your story.

## \|\| 3.20.19 \|\|

*yathā yathā janaścaitatkṛtyante kīrtayiṣyati \|*  
*tathā tathā viśuddhiste pāpasyāsya bhaviṣyati \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Whenever people thus repeat your wicked action your sin will gradually subside and you will become pure.

## \|\| 3.20.20 \|\|

*etadeva hi te brahman prāyaścittaṃ mayeritam \|*  
*janahāsyakaraṃ loke tava garhākaraṃ param \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. O Brahmā, this is the atonement I lay down for you, being laughed at by the people and ridiculed by them.

## \|\| 3.20.21 \|\|

*etacca tava vīryyaṃ hi patitaṃ vedimadhyagam \|*  
*kāmārtasya mayā dṛṣṭaṃ naitaddhāryaṃ bhaviṣyati \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. The semen drops that fell in the middle of the altar-ground from you when you were excited by lust and seen by me will not be retained by any one.

## \|\| 3.20.22 \|\|

*caturbindumitaṃ retaḥ patitaṃ yatkṣitau tava \|*  
*tanmitāstoyadā vyomni bhaveyuḥ pralayaṃkarāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Four drops of your semen fell on the ground. Hence so many terrible clouds causing dissolution shall rise up in the sky.

## \|\| 3.20.23 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare tatra devarṣīṇāṃ puro drutam \|*  
*tadretasassamabhavaṃstanmitāśca balāhakā \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. In the meantime, (when Śiva said so) in front of the devas and the sages, so many clouds emanated from the semen drops.

## \|\| 3.20.24 \|\|

*saṃvartakastathāvarttaḥ puṣkaro droṇa eva ca \|*  
*ete caturvidhāstāta mahāmeghā layaṃkarāḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. O dear one, four types of great clouds that caused destruction are the Saṃvartaka, the Āvarta, the Puṣkara and the Droṇa.

## \|\| 3.20.25 \|\|

*garjaṃtaścātha mucaṃtastoyānīṣacchivecchayā \|*  
*phelurvyomni muniśreṣṭha toyadāste kadāravāḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. O excellent sage, those clouds rumbling and roaring with hideous sounds dropping showers at the slightest wish of Śiva burst asunder in the sky.

## \|\| 3.20.26 \|\|

*taistu saṃchādite vyomni sugarjadbhiśca śaṃkaraḥ \|*  
*praśāndākṣāyaṇī devī bhṛśaṃ śāṃto'bhavaddrutam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. When the sky was covered by those roaring clouds, Śiva and the Goddess Śivā were quite calm.

## \|\| 3.20.27 \|\|

*atha cāhaṃ vītabhayaśśaṃkarasyā jñayā tadā \|*  
*śeṣaṃ vaivāhikaṃ karma samāptimanayaṃ mune \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. O sage, thereafter becoming fearless, I concluded the remaining rites of the marriage at the bidding of Śiva.

## \|\| 3.20.28 \|\|

*papāta puṣpavṛṣṭiśca śivāśivaśiraskayoḥ \|*  
*sarvatra ca muniśreṣṭha mudā devagaṇojjhitā \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. O excellent sage, a shower of flowers dropped by the devas with great pleasure fell on the heads of Śivā and Śiva and also on all their sides.

## \|\| 3.20.29-30 \|\|

*vādyamāneṣu vādyeṣu gāyamāneṣu teṣu ca \|*  
*paṭhatsu vipravaryeṣu vādān bhaktyānviteṣu ca \|\| 29 \|\|*

*raṃbhādiṣu puraṃdhrīṣu nṛtyamānāsu sādaram \|*  
*mahotsavo mahānāsīddevapatnīṣu nārada \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. O Nārada, great festivities were conducted by the wives of the devas. Musical instruments were played, songs were sung, Vedic hymns were recited devoutly by groups of brahmins. The celestial damsels Rambhā and others danced zealously.

## \|\| 3.20.31 \|\|

*atha karmavitāneśaḥ prasannaḥ parameśvaraḥ \|*  
*prāha māṃ prāṃjaliṃ prītyā laukikīṃ gatimāśritaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Then the delightful lord, the lord of sacrificial rites, following the conventions of the world, spoke to me as I was standing with palms joined in reverence.

## \|\| 3.20.32 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*he brahman sukṛtaṃ karma sarvaṃ vaivāhikaṃ ca yat \|*  
*prasannosmi tvamācāryo dadyāṃ te dakṣiṇāṃ ca kām \|\| 32 \|\|*

Śiva said:—

32\. O Brahmā, all the rites of marriage have been performed extremely well. I am pleased. You officiated as the priest. What shall I give you as the nuptial fee?

## \|\| 3.20.33 \|\|

*yācasva tāṃ surajyeṣṭha yadyapi syātsudurlabhā \|*  
*brūhi śīghraṃ mahābhāga nādeyaṃ vidyate mama \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. O eldest of devas, you can demand it even if it be hard to get. Tell me quickly, O fortunate one. For there is nothing which cannot be granted by me.

## \|\| 3.20.34 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya vacassohaṃ śaṃkarasya kṛtāṃjaliḥ \|*  
*mune'vocaṃ vinītātmā praṇamyeśaṃ muhurmuhuḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

34\. O sage, on hearing these words of Śiva I humbly bowed to Him repeatedly with palms joined in reverence and said:—

## \|\| 3.20.35 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*yadi prasanno deveśa varayogyosmyahaṃ yadi \|*  
*tatkuru tvaṃ maheśāna suprītyā yadvadāmyaham \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. “O lord of Devas, if you are pleased, if I deserve your blessings, O lord, please do as I request you with pleasure.

## \|\| 3.20.36 \|\|

*anenaiva tu rūpeṇa vedyāmasyāṃ maheśvara \|*  
*tvayā stheyaṃ sadaivātra nṛṇāṃ pāpaviśuddhaye \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. O lord Śiva, for the purification of men from sins you will please stay for ever in this altar in this self-same form.

## \|\| 3.20.37 \|\|

*yenāsya saṃnidhau kṛtvā svāśramaṃ śaśi śekhara \|*  
*tapaḥ kuryā vināśāya svapāpasyāsya śaṃkara \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. O moon-crested God, I shall make my hermitage in its vicinity and perform penance to destroy my sin.

## \|\| 3.20.38-39 \|\|

*caitraśuklatrayodaśyāṃ nakṣatre bhagadaivate \|*  
*sūryavāre ca yo bhaktyā vīkṣeta bhuvi mānavaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*tadaiva tasya pāpāni prayāṃtu hara saṃkṣayam \|*  
*varddhate vipulaṃ puṇyaṃ rogā naśyaṃtu sarvaśaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

38-39. If anyone visits this holy site on the thirteenth day in the bright half of Caitra (March-April) when the star is Uttarāphālgunī and the day is Sunday, may all his sins be quelled O Śiva; may his merits increase and may his ailments disappear.

## \|\| 3.20.40 \|\|

*yā nārī durbhagā vaṃdhyā kāṇā rūpavivarjitā \|*  
*sāpi tvaddarśanādeva nirdoṣā saṃbhaveddhruvam \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. If a woman who is barren, one-eyed, ugly or unfortunate, visits this place she shall be freed from all these defects.”

## \|\| 3.20.41 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya vaco me hi svātmasarvasukhāvaham \|*  
*tathā'stviti śivaḥ prāha suprasannena cetasā \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. On hearing these words of mine, Śiva was pleased and He said “Let it be so”. This made me very happy.

## \|\| 3.20.42 \|\|

*śiva uvāca \|*  
*hitāya sarvalokasya vedyāṃ tasyāṃ vyavasthitaḥ \|*  
*sthāsyāmi sahitaḥ patnyā satyā tvadvacanādvidhe \|\| 42 \|\|*

Śiva said:—

42\. O, for the benefits of the people, I shall stay in this altar, with my wife Satī, in accordance with your words of request.

## \|\| 3.20.43 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*ityuktvā bhagavāṃstatra sabhāryo vṛṣabhadhvajaḥ \|*  
*uvāca vedimadhyastho mūrtiṃ kṛtvāṃśarūpiṇīm \|\| 43 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

43\. After saying this, the lord Śiva in the company of his wife stayed in the middle of the altar creating a partial image of Himself.

## \|\| 3.20.44 \|\|

*tato dakṣaṃ samāmaṃtrya śaṃkaraḥ parameśvaraḥ \|*  
*patnyā satyā gaṃtumanā abhūtsvajanavatsalaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Taking leave of Dakṣa, Śiva, the great lord, desired to depart along with his wife Satī. He was so fond of His own men.

## \|\| 3.20.45 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare dakṣo vinayāvanatassudhīḥ \|*  
*sāṃjalirnatakaḥ prītyā tuṣṭāva vṛṣabhadhvajam \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. In the meantime, the intelligent Dakṣa bowed humbly with palms joined in reverence and eulogised Śiva with devotion.

## \|\| 3.20.46 \|\|

*viṣṇvādayassurāssarve munayaśca gaṇāstadā \|*  
*natvā saṃstūya vividhaṃ cakrurjayaravaṃ mudā \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Viṣṇu, the gods and the Gaṇas bowed to and lauded Him shouting cries of victory with pleasure.

## \|\| 3.20.47 \|\|

*āropya vṛṣabhe śaṃbhussatīṃ dakṣājñayā mudā \|*  
*jagāma himavatprasthaṃ vṛṣabhasthassvayaṃ prabhuḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. With the joyous consent of Dakṣa, Śiva seated Satī on the bull and then sitting Himself on it went to the Himālayan ridges.

## \|\| 3.20.48 \|\|

*atha sā śaṃkarābhyāse sudatī cāruhāsinī \|*  
*vireje vṛṣabhasthā vai candrāṃte kālikā yathā \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Seated on the bull along with Śiva, the sweet smiling Satī of fine teeth shone like a black cloud near the moon.

## \|\| 3.20.49 \|\|

*viṣṇvādayassurāssarve marīcyādyāstatharṣayaḥ \|*  
*dakṣopi mohitaścāsīttathānye niścalā janāḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Viṣṇu and other devas, Marīci and other sages, Dakṣa and the other people were all in a state of pleasant steady senselessness.

## \|\| 3.20.50 \|\|

*kecidvādyānvādayanto gāyaṃtassusvaraṃ pare \|*  
*śivaṃ śivayaśaśśuddhamanujagmuḥ śivaṃ mudā \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Some played on musical instruments, others sang sweetly the lustrous glory of Śiva. They all followed Śiva joyously.

## \|\| 3.20.51 \|\|

*madhyamārgādvisṛṣṭo hi dakṣaḥ prītyātha śambhunā \|*  
*vadhāma prāpa sagaṇaḥ śambhuḥ premasamākulaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Half the way Śiva took leave of Dakṣa with pleasure. Along with his followers Dakṣa returned to his abode thrilled by Śiva’s love.

## \|\| 3.20.52 \|\|

*visṛṣṭā api viṣṇvādyāśśambhunā punareva te \|*  
*anujagmuśśivaṃ bhaktyā surāḥ paramayā mudā \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Viṣṇu and other Devas, though permitted to go, followed Śiva with devotion and great joy.

## \|\| 3.20.53 \|\|

*taissarvaissagaṇaiśśaṃbhussatyaḥ ca svastriyā yutaḥ \|*  
*prāpa svaṃ dhāma saṃhṛṣṭo himavadgiri śobhitam \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. With these, his wife and his attendants Śiva reached his abode in the beauteous surroundings of the Himālayas with very great delight.

## \|\| 3.20.54 \|\|

*tatra gatvākhilāndevānmunīnapi parāṃstathā \|*  
*mudā visarjayāmāsa bahu sammānya sādaram \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. After reaching his abode Śiva honoured the devas and the great sages and then bade farewell to them with respect.

## \|\| 3.20.55 \|\|

*śaṃbhumābhāṣya te sarve viṣṇvādyā muditānanā \|*  
*svaṃsvaṃ dhāma yayurnatvā stutvā ca munayassurāḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Taking leave of Śiva eulogising and bowing to Him, Viṣṇu, as also the Gods and sages with joyful beaming faces returned to their respective abodes.

## \|\| 3.20.56 \|\|

*śivopi muditotyarthaṃ svapatnyā dakṣakanyayā \|*  
*himavatprasthasaṃstho hi vijahāra bhavānugaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Śiva with boundless pleasure in the company of his wife—the daughter of Dakṣa, sported in the Himālayan region following the conventions of the world.

## \|\| 3.20.57 \|\|

*tatassa śaṃkarassatyā sagaṇassūtikṛnmune \|*  
*prāpa svaṃ dhāma saṃhṛṣṭaḥ kailāśaṃ parvatottamam \|\| 57 \|\|*
