57\. Then O sage, Śiva, the primordial creation, entered His residence in Kailāsa the best of mountains along with Satī and his attendants.

## \|\| 3.20.58 \|\|

*etadvassarvamākhyātaṃ yathā tasya purā'bhavat \|*  
*vivāho vṛṣayānasya manusvāyaṃbhuvāntaka \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Thus I have narrated to you all how the marriage of the bull-vehicled lord took place formerly in the Manvantara of Svāyambhuva Manu.

## \|\| 3.20.59-60 \|\|

*vivāhasamaye yajñe prāraṃbhe vā śṛṇoti yaḥ \|*  
*etadākhyānamavyagrassaṃpūjya vṛṣabhadhvajam \|\| 59 \|\|*

*tasyā'vighnaṃ bhavetsarvaṃ karma vaivāhikaṃ ca yat \|*  
*śubhākhyamaparaṃ karma nirvighnaṃ sarvadā bhavet \|\| 60 \|\|*

59-60. If any one hears this narrative with concentrated attention after worshipping Śiva at marriages, sacrifices or other auspicious undertakings, all the rites—of marriage or other auspicious undertaking—will always conclude without obstacles.

## \|\| 3.20.61 \|\|

*kanyā ca sukhasaubhaṇyaśīlācāraguṇānvitā \|*  
*sādhvī syātputriṇī prītyā śrutvākhyānamidaṃ śubham \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. The bride will be blessed with happiness, good fortune, good conduct, and good qualities. She will be chaste and produce sons on hearing this auspicious narration.

## Chapter 21 - The Dalliance of Satī and Śiva

## \|\| 3.21.1 \|\|

*\|\| nārada uvāca \|*  
*samīcīnaṃ vacastāta sarvajñasya tavā'nagha \|*  
*mahādbhutaṃ śrutaṃ no vai caritaṃ śivayośśubham \|\| 1 \|\|*

Nārada said:—

1\. O dear, your words are perfect inasmuch as you are omniscient, sinless one. The wonderfully auspicious story of Śivā and Śiva has been heard by us.

## \|\| 3.21.2 \|\|

*vivāhaśca śrutassamyak sarvamohāpahārakaḥ \|*  
*paramajñānasaṃpanno maṃgalālaya uttamaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. We have heard the detailed account of their marriage that destroys delusions, makes one endowed with true knowledge and which is excellently auspicious.

## \|\| 3.21.3 \|\|

*bhūya eva vivitsā me caritaṃ śivayośśubham \|*  
*tadvarṇaya mahāprājña kṛpāṃ kṛtvā'tulāmaram \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. I wish to know more of the auspicious story of Śivā and Śiva. Hence having unequalled consideration for me, O intelligent one, please narrate the same.

## \|\| 3.21.4 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*samyakkāruṇikasyaiva mune te vicikitsitam \|*  
*yadahaṃ noditassaumya śivalīlānuvarṇane \|\| 4 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

4\. Your enquiries for the history of the merciful lord are pursued well, since you have prompted me to narrate the divine sports of Siva.

## \|\| 3.21.5 \|\|

*vivāhya dakṣajāṃ devīṃ satīṃ trailokyamātaram \|*  
*gatvā svadhāma suprītyā yadakārṣīnnibodha me \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Know from me what Śiva did with pleasure on reaching His abode after His marriage with goddess Satī, Dakṣa’s daughter and the mother of the three worlds.

## \|\| 3.21.6 \|\|

*tato harassa svagaṇassvasthānaṃ prāpya modanama \|*  
*devarṣe tatra vṛṣabhādavātaradatipriyāt \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. O celestial sage, after reaching His gay abode along with His Gaṇas, Śiva descended from His Bull with great pleasure.

## \|\| 3.21.7 \|\|

*yathāyogyaṃ nijasthānaṃ praviśya sa satīsakhaḥ \|*  
*mumude'tīva devarṣe bhavācārakaraśśivaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. O celestial sage, entering His apartment in a befitting manner, along with Satī, Śiva assuming worldly conventions rejoiced very much.

## \|\| 3.21.8 \|\|

*tato virūpākṣa imāṃ prāpya dākṣāyaṇīṃ gaṇān \|*  
*svīyāniryāpayāmāsa nadyādīn girikaṃdarāt \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Then after approaching Satī, Śiva sent out His attendants—Nandin and others, from the cave in the mountain.

## \|\| 3.21.9 \|\|

*uvāca caitāstān sarvānnaṃdyādīnatisūnṛtam \|*  
*laukikīṃ rītimāśritya karuṇāsāgaraḥ prabhuḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Following the manner of the people of the world, the merciful lord spoke these affable and courteous words to Nandin and others.

## \|\| 3.21.10 \|\|

*maheśa uvāca \|*  
*yadāhaṃ ca smarāmyatra smaraṇādaramānasāḥ \|*  
*samāgamiṣyatha tadā matpārśvaṃ me gaṇā drutam \|\| 10 \|\|*

Lord Śiva said:—

10\. O my attendants, with minds respectfully concentrated in thinking upon me, you shall come to me only when I remember you.

## \|\| 3.21.11 \|\|

*ityukte vāmadevena nadyādyāssvagaṇāśca te \|*  
*mahāvegā mahāvīrā nānāsthāneṣu saṃyayuḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. When Śiva said like this, Nandin and others who constituted the powerful set of attendants of quick speed left for different places.

## \|\| 3.21.12 \|\|

*īśvaropi tayā sārddhaṃ teṣu yāteṣu vibhramī \|*  
*dākṣāyaṇyā samaṃ reme rahasye mudito bhṛśam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. When they went away and He was left alone with Satī, Śiva rejoiced much and sported with her.

## \|\| 3.21.13 \|\|

*kadācidvanya puṣpāṇi samāhṛtya manoharām \|*  
*mālāṃ vidhāya satyāstu hārasthāne sa yojayat \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Sometimes He gathered some sylvan flowers and wreathed a fine garland out of them which he put round her neck in the place of the necklace.

## \|\| 3.21.14 \|\|

*kadāciddarpaṇe caiva vīkṣatīmātmanassatīm \|*  
*anugamya haro vaktram svīyamapyavalokayata \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. While Satī was admiring at the reflection of her face in the mirror, Śiva came behind and peeped into the reflection of His own face.

## \|\| 3.21.15 \|\|

*kadācitkuṃḍalaṃ tasyā ullāsyollāsya saṃgataḥ \|*  
*badhnāti mocayatyeva sā svayaṃ mārjayatyapi \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Sometimes He would be sporting with her ear-rings, tying and untying and scrubbing them Himself.

## \|\| 3.21.16 \|\|

*sarāgau caraṇāvasyāḥ pāvakenojjvalena ca \|*  
*nisargaraktau kurute pūrṇarāgau vṛṣadhvajaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Sometimes by the application of red dye Śiva made her naturally red feet completely red.

## \|\| 3.21.17 \|\|

*uccairapi yadākhyeyamanyeṣāṃ purato bahu \|*  
*tata karṇe kathayattyasyāharo draṣṭuṃ tadānanam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Many things which could be said aloud even in the presence of many, Śiva whispered into her ears in order to see her face.

## \|\| 3.21.18 \|\|

*na dūramapi gantāsau samāgatya prayatnataḥ \|*  
*anubadhnāti nāmākṣī pṛṣṭhadeśenyamānasām \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. He would not go far from her, (if at all he went) he would return suddenly and close her eyes from behind and while she was thinking about something else he would ask her his name.

## \|\| 3.21.19 \|\|

*aṃtarhitastu tatraiva māyayā vṛṣabhadhvajaḥ \|*  
*tāmāliliṃga bhītyā svaṃ cakitā vyākulā'bhavat \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Sometimes Śiva would become invisible through His Māyā and suddenly embrace her when she would become terrified and agitated.

## \|\| 3.21.20 \|\|

*sauvarṇapadmakalikātulye tasyā kucadvaye \|*  
*cakāra bhramarākāraṃ mṛganābhiviśeṣakam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Sometimes with musk He would make marks like bees on her breasts that resembled the buds of a golden lotus.

## \|\| 3.21.21 \|\|

*hāramasyāḥ kucayugādviyojya sahasā haraḥ \|*  
*nyayojayacca tatraiva svakarasparśanaṃ muhuḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Sometimes he would take the necklace off her breasts and press them with his hands.

## \|\| 3.21.22 \|\|

*aṃgadānvalayānūrmānviśleṣya ca punaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*tatsthānātpunarevāsau tatsthāne pratyayojayat \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Sometimes he would remove the bracelets, bangles, rings from their places and fix them again one by one.

## \|\| 3.21.23 \|\|

*kāliketi samāyāti savarṇā te sakhī tvimām \|*  
*yāsyatvasyāstathekṣaṃtyāḥ prottuṃgau sāhasaṃ kucau \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Even as she was looking on, sometimes he would come to her lofty breasts saying with laughter, this dark spot “Kālikā” on your breasts is your companion of the same colour as it contains the same letters as are found in your name “Kālikā”.

## \|\| 3.21.24 \|\|

*kadācinmadanonmādacetanaḥ pramathādhipaḥ \|*  
*cakāra narma śarmāṇi tathākṛtpriyayā mudā \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Sometimes when he was too much excited with love he would exchange pleasantries with his beloved.

## \|\| 3.21.25 \|\|

*āhṛtya padmapuṣpāṇi ramyapuṣpāṇi śaṃkaraḥ \|*  
*sarvāṃgeṣu karoti sma puṣpābharaṇamādarāt \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Sometimes he would gather lotuses and other beautiful flowers and decorate her with them as though with ornaments.

## \|\| 3.21.26 \|\|

*girikuṃjeṣu ramyeṣu satyā saha maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*vijahāra samasteṣu priyayā bhaktavatsalaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. In the company of his beloved Śivā, Śiva who is favourably disposed to His devotees, sported about among the mountain hedges.

## \|\| 3.21.27 \|\|

*tayā vinā sma no yāti nāsthito na sma ceṣṭate \|*  
*tayā vinā kṣamamapi śarma lebhe na śaṃkaraḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Without her, he did not move anywhere, he did not stay anywhere, he did not carry on any activity without her company. Śiva was not happy without her even for a moment.

## \|\| 3.21.28 \|\|

*vihṛtya suciraṃ kālaṃ kailāsagirikuṃjare \|*  
*agamaddhimavatprasthaṃ sasmāra svecchayā smaran \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. After dallying among the hedges and grottos in the Kailāsa mountain for a long time he went to the Himālayan ridges where he remembered Kāma out of his own accord.

## \|\| 3.21.29 \|\|

*tasminpraviṣṭe kāme tu vasaṃtaśśaṃkarāṃtike \|*  
*vitastāra nijaṃ bhāvaṃ hārdaṃ vijñāya yatprabho \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. When Kāma reached the vicinity of Śiva, Spring spread all his splendour in accord with the inclination of the lord.

## \|\| 3.21.30 \|\|

*sarve ca puṣpitā vṛkṣā latāścānyāśca puṣpitāḥ \|*  
*aṃbhāṃsi phullapadmāni padmāssabhramarāstathā \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. The trees and creepers blossomed and bloomed. Waters were covered with full blown lotuses. Bees hovered round the lotuses.

## \|\| 3.21.31 \|\|

*praviṣṭe tatra sadṛtau vavau sa malayo marut \|*  
*sugaṃdhigaṃdhapuṣpeṇa modakaśca sugaṃdhiyuk \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. When that excellent season set in, the gentle Malaya breeze fragrant and delightful due to sweet smelling flowers blew all round.

## \|\| 3.21.32 \|\|

*saṃdhyārdracandrasaṃkāśāḥ palāśāśca virejire \|*  
*kāmāstravatsumanasaḥ pramodātpādapādharaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. The Palāśa flowers resembling the hue of the twilight and shaped like the crescent moon shone like the flowery arrows of Kāma at the feet of trees.

## \|\| 3.21.33 \|\|

*babhuḥ paṃkajapuṣpāṇi sarassu saṃkalāñjanān \|*  
*saṃmohayitumudyuktā sumukhī vāyudevatā \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The lotus flowers shone in the lakes. The goddess wind endeavoured to fascinate people with her sweet face.

## \|\| 3.21.34 \|\|

*nāgakeśaravṛkṣāśca svarṇavarṇaiḥ prasūnakaiḥ \|*  
*babhurmadanaketvābhā manojñāśśaṃkarāṃtike \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. With their flowers golden in hue, the Nāgakesara trees shone beautifully like the banners of Kāma.

## \|\| 3.21.35 \|\|

*lavaṃgavallīsurabhigaṃdhenodvāsya mārutam \|*  
*mohayāmāsa cetāṃsi bhṛśaṃ kāmijane purā \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Rendering the breeze fragrant with its smell the clove creeper fascinated the minds of passionate people with its sweetness.

## \|\| 3.21.36 \|\|

*cāru pāvakacarcitsu susvarāścūtaśālinaḥ \|*  
*babhurmadanabāṇaughaparyaṃkamadanāvṛtāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. The mango trees and the Śāli plants shining like mild fire shone like the open couches for the flowery arrows of Kāma.

## \|\| 3.21.37 \|\|

*aṃbhāṃsi malahīnāni rejuḥ phullakuśāśayāḥ \|*  
*munīnāmiva cetāṃsi pravyaktajyotirudgamam \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. With full-blown lotuses, the pure waters of the lakes shone like the minds of sages wherein the supreme splendour—Ātman is clearly reflected.

## \|\| 3.21.38 \|\|

*tuṣārāssūryaraśmīnāṃ saṃgamādagaman bahiḥ \|*  
*pramatvānīkṣyatekṣāśca salilīhṛdayāstadā \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. The dew-drops as they came in contact with the rays of the sun turned in vapours like the hearts of the people turning pure in association with the good.

## \|\| 3.21.39 \|\|

*prasannāssaha candreṇa naniṣārāstadā'bhavan \|*  
*vibhāvaryaḥ priyeṇaivaṃ kāminyastu manoharāḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. The nights became bright with the moon devoid of mist. Lovely women shone beautifully in the company of their lovers.

## \|\| 3.21.40 \|\|

*tasminkāle mahādevassaha satyā dharottame \|*  
*reme sa suciraṃ chandaṃ nikuṃjeṣu nadīṣu ca \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. In this atmosphere, on that excellent mountain, Lord Śiva sported about for a long time among the groves, hedges and streams in the company of Satī.

## \|\| 3.21.41 \|\|

*tathā tena samaṃ reje tadā dākṣāyiṇi mune \|*  
*yathā haraḥ kṣaṇamapi śāṃtimāpa tayā vinā \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. O sage, then Satī so exercised her splendid influence on Śiva that he did not have mental peace without her even for a moment.

## \|\| 3.21.42 \|\|

*saṃbhogaviṣaye devī satī tasya manaḥ priyā \|*  
*viśatīva harasyāṃge pāyayanniva tadrasam \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. The goddess satisfied his mind in fulness in the matter of intercourse. She seemed to enter his body. He made her drink that juice.

## \|\| 3.21.43 \|\|

*tasyā kusumamālābhirbhūṣayansakalāṃ tanum \|*  
*svahastaracitābhistu navaśarmākarocca saḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. With garlands of flowers wreathed by himself he decorated her person and felt new pleasures.

## \|\| 3.21.44 \|\|

*ālāpairvīkṣitairhāsyaistathā saṃbhāṣaṇairharaḥ \|*  
*tasyādideśa girijāṃ sapatīvātmasaṃvidam \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. With diverse conversations, glances, joking remarks and exchanges of pleasantries he instructed Śiva in the knowledge of Self.

## \|\| 3.21.45 \|\|

*tadvaktracaṃdra pīyūṣapānasthiratanurharaḥ \|*  
*nānāvaiśeṣikīṃ tanvīmavasthāṃ sa kadācana \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Drinking the nectar from her moon-face, Śiva stabilised his body. Sometimes he experienced exhilarating and particularly pleasing state.

## \|\| 3.21.46 \|\|

*tadvaktrāmbujavāsena tatsaundaryyaiśca narmabhiḥ \|*  
*guṇairiva mahādaṃtī baddho nānyaviceṣṭitaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Just as a huge elephant that is bound with ropes cannot have any other activity. He was also bound by the sweet fragrance of her lotus-like face, her beauty and her jocular pleasantries.

## \|\| 3.21.47 \|\|

*iti himagirikuṃjaprasthabhāge darīṣu pratidinamabhireme dakṣaputryā maheśaḥ \|*  
*kratubhujaparimāṇaiḥ krīḍatastasya jātā daśa daśa ca surarṣe vatsarāḥ paṃca cānye \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Thus in the ridges and caverns of the Himālayan mountains, the lord sported about in the company of Satī every day. According to the calculation of the devas twenty five years elapsed, O celestial sage, during which he dallied thus.

## Chapter 22 - The dalliance of Śivā and Śiva on the Himālayas

## \|\| 3.22.1 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*kadācidatha dakṣasya tanayā jaladāgame \|*  
*kailāsakṣmābhṛtaḥ prāha prasthasthaṃ vṛṣabhadhvajam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

1\. Once at the advent of clouds, Dakṣa’s daughter said to Śiva who was halting on the ridge of Kailāsa mountain.

## \|\| 3.22.2 \|\|

*satyuvāca \|*  
*deva deva mahādeva śaṃbho matprāṇavallabha \|*  
*śṛṇu me vacanaṃ nātha śrutvā tatkuru mānada \|\| 2 \|\|*

Satī said:—

2\. O lord of devas, O Śiva my dear husband, please hear my words and do accordingly, O bestower of honour.

## \|\| 3.22.3 \|\|

*ghanāgamoyaṃ saṃprāptaḥ kālaḥ paramadussahaḥ \|*  
*anekavarṇameghaughāssaṃgītāṃbaradikcayāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The most unbearable season of the advent of clouds has arrived with clusters of clouds of diverse hues, and their music reverberating in the sky and the various quarters.

## \|\| 3.22.4 \|\|

*vivāṃti vātā hṛdayaṃ hārayaṃtīta veginaḥ \|*  
*kadaṃbarajasā dhautāḥ pāthobinduvikarṣaṇāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The speedy gusts of wind scattering sprays of water mingled with nectarine drops from the Kadamba flowers captivate the heart as they blow.

## \|\| 3.22.5 \|\|

*meghānāṃ garjitairuccairdhārāsāraṃ vimuṃcatām \|*  
*vidyutpatākināṃ tīvraḥ kṣubdhaṃ syātkasya no manaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Whose mind will not be agitated by the loud and forceful rumblings of the clouds that release a heavy downpour and have the beams of lightning for their ensign?

## \|\| 3.22.6 \|\|

*na sūryo dṛśyate nāpi meghacchanno niśāpatiḥ \|*  
*divāpi rātrivadbhāti virahi vyasanākaraḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Covered by the clouds neither the sun nor the moon is visible. Even the day appears like the night and it distresses those who are separated from their lovers.

## \|\| 3.22.7 \|\|

*meghānaikatra tiṣṭhaṃto dhvananta pavaneritāḥ \|*  
*pataṃta iva lokānāṃ dṛśyaṃte mūrdhni śaṃkara \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. O Śiva, tossed about by the gusts of wind the clouds do not remain steady in any place, they rumble and appear as if they would fall on the heads of the people.

## \|\| 3.22.8 \|\|

*vātāhatā mahāvṛkṣā nartaṃta iva cāṃbare \|*  
*dṛśyaṃte hara bhīrūṇāṃ trāsadāḥ kāmukepsitā \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Huge trees struck down by the wind appear to dance in the sky, terrifying the cowards and delighting the lover, O Śiva.

## \|\| 3.22.9 \|\|

*snigdhanīlāṃjanasyāśu sadivaughasya pṛṣṭhataḥ \|*  
*balākarājī vātyuccairyamunāpṛṣṭhaphenavat \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Flocks of cranes above the clouds glossy and blue like the collyrium shine like foams on the surface of Yamunā.

## \|\| 3.22.10 \|\|

*kṣapākṣayeṣavalayaṃ dṛśyate kālikāgatā \|*  
*aṃbudhāviva saṃdīptapāvako vaḍavāmukhaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. During the close of the nights the circle of lightning appears like the blazing submarine fire in the ocean.

## \|\| 3.22.11 \|\|

*prārohaṃtīha sasyāni maṃdiraṃ prāṅgaṇeṣvapi \|*  
*kimanyatra virūpākṣa sasyaudbhūtiṃ vadāmyaham \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. O odd-eyed Śiva, here even in the courtyards of the temples, plants grow; need I mention the growth of plants elsewhere?

## \|\| 3.22.12 \|\|

*śyāmalai rājatairaktairviśadoyaṃ himācalaḥ \|*  
*maṃdarāśrayameghaughaḥ patrairdugdhāṃbudhiryathā \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. With the clusters of clouds dark, silvery and red in colour clinging to the Mandara mountain (peak), Himālaya appears as the ocean of milk with the birds of diverse colours.

## \|\| 3.22.13 \|\|

*asamaśrīśca kuṭilaṃ bheje yasyātha kiṃśukān \|*  
*uccāvacān kalau lakṣmīrgantā saṃtyajya sajjanān \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Unrivalled splendour has resorted to the Kiṃśuka flowers devoid of odour, as Lakṣmī (the Goddess of fortune) abandons good people and resorts to the crooked, whether of high or low birth.

## \|\| 3.22.14 \|\|

*maṃdārastana pīlūnāṃ śabdena hṛṣitā muhuḥ \|*  
*kekāyaṃte prativane satataṃ pṛṣṭhasūcakam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The peacocks are delighted at the sound of the cloud over the Mandara mountain. Their gleeful cackles and out-stretched tails indicate the incessant pleasure of their heart.

## \|\| 3.22.15 \|\|

*meghotsukānāṃ madhuraścātakānāṃ manoharaḥ \|*  
*dhārāsāraśaraistāpaṃ petuḥ pratipathodgatam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The sweet and delightful sounds of the Cātaka birds that are fond of clouds fall upon the way-farers like the arrows of rain-showers causing incessant pain.

## \|\| 3.22.16 \|\|

*meghānāṃ paśya maddehe durnayaṃ karakotkaraiḥ \|*  
*ye chādayaṃtyanugate mayūrāṃścātakāṃstathā \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. See the wickedness perpetrated by the clouds on my body. They are pelting it with hailstones. But they cover and protect the peacocks and Cātakas who are their followers.

## \|\| 3.22.17 \|\|

*śikhasāraṃgayordṛṣṭvā mitrādapi parābhavam \|*  
*harṣaṃ gacchaṃti giriśaṃ vidūramapi mānasam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. On seeing the distress of peacocks and deer from even their friend (sun), the swans go even to the distant Mānasa lake on the top of the mountain.

## \|\| 3.22.18 \|\|

*etasminviṣame kāle nīlaṃ kākāścakorakāḥ \|*  
*kurvaṃti tvāṃ vinā gehān kathaṃ śāṃtimavāpsyasi \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. In this troublesome time, even crows and Cakora birds build their nests. But you don’t. Without a home how will you be happy?

## \|\| 3.22.19 \|\|

*mahatīvādya no bhītirmā meghotthā pinākadhṛk \|*  
*yatasva yasmādvāsāya māciraṃ vacanānmama \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. O Pināka-bearer Śiva, let not the great fear originating from clouds befall us. Hence endeavour for a residence. Do not delay. Heed my words.

## \|\| 3.22.20 \|\|

*kailāse vā himādrau vā mahākāśyāmatha kṣitau \|*  
*tatropayogyaṃ saṃvāsaṃ kuru tvaṃ vṛṣabhadhvaja \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. O bull-emblemed God, either in Kailāsa or in the Himālayas or in Mahākāśī on the earth you make a befitting habitation.

## \|\| 3.22.21 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*evamuktastayā śaṃbhurdākṣāyaṇyā tathā'sakṛta \|*  
*saṃjahāsa ca śīrṣasthacandraraśmismitālayam \|\| 21 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

21\. Thus advised by Satī frequently Śiva laughed provoking a smile from the moon on his head by way of its beams.

## \|\| 3.22.22 \|\|

*athovāca satīṃ devīṃ smitabhinnauṣṭhasaṃpuṭaḥ \|\| \|*  
*mahātmā sarvatattvajñastoṣayanparameśvaraḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Then the high-souled lord Śiva who knew all the principles spoke to Satī with a smile breaking his lips asunder and consoling her.

## \|\| 3.22.23 \|\|

*īśvaraḥ uvāca \|*  
*yatra prītyai mayā kāryo vāsastava manohare \|*  
*meghāstatra na gaṃtāraḥ kadācidapi matpriye \|\| 23 \|\|*

Śiva said:—

23\. “O my beloved, beautiful woman, clouds will not reach the place where I have to make an abode for you.

## \|\| 3.22.24 \|\|

*meghā nitaṃbaparyaṃtaṃ saṃcaraṃti mahībhṛtaḥ \|*  
*sadā prāleyasānostu varṣāsvapi manohare \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. O comely lass! even in the rainy seasons the clouds move about in the side ridges alone of the Himālayas.

## \|\| 3.22.25 \|\|

*kailāsasya tathā devi pādagāḥ prāyaśo ghanāḥ \|*  
*saṃcaraṃti na gacchaṃti tata ūrddhvaṃ kadācana \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. O gentle lady, the clouds usually come only upto the foot of Kailāsa. They never go above it.

## \|\| 3.22.26 \|\|

*sumerorvā girerūrddhvaṃ na gacchaṃti balāhakāḥ \|*  
*jambūmūlaṃ samāsādya puṣkarāvartakādayaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The clouds never go above the mountain Sumeru. The clouds Puṣkara, Āvartaka etc. reach the foot of Jambu (and return).

## \|\| 3.22.27 \|\|

*ityukteṣu girīndreṣu yasyopari bhaveddhi te \|*  
*manorucirnivāsāya tamācakṣva drutaṃ hi me \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Of these mountains I have mentioned you can choose one for residence as you desire. Please tell me quickly where you wish to reside.

## \|\| 3.22.28 \|\|

*svecchāvihāraistava kautukāni suvarṇapakṣānilavṛndavṛndaiḥ \|*  
*śabdottaraṃgairmadhurasvanaistairmudopageyāni girau himotthe \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. On the Himālayan mountains, songs exciting your curiosity and enthusiastic gaiety shall be sung by clusters and swarms of bees with sweet humming sounds as they play about as they please.

## \|\| 3.22.29 \|\|

*siddhāṅganāste racitāsanā bhuvamicchaṃti caivopahṛtaṃ sakautukam \|*  
*svecchāvihāre maṇikuṭṭime girau kurvanti ceṣyaṃti phalādidānakaiḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. On that mountain at the time when you wish to sport about, the Siddha women will gaily offer you a seat on the jewel-studded platform and gladly present you with fruits and other gifts.

## \|\| 3.22.30 \|\|

*phaṇīndrakanyā girikanyakāśca yā nāgakanyāśca turaṃgamukhyāḥ \|*  
*sarvāstu tāste satataṃ sahāyatāṃ samācariṣyaṃtyanumodavibhramaiḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. The daughters of the king of serpents, the mountain damsels, the Nāga ladies and the Turaṅga-Mukhīs will assist you in their excited flutter in congratulating you.

## \|\| 3.22.31 \|\|

*rūpaṃ tadevamatulaṃ vadanaṃ sucāru dṛṣṭvāṃganā nijavapurnijakāṃtisahyam \|*  
*helā nije vapuṣi rūpagaṇeṣu nityaṃ kartāra ityanimiṣekṣaṇacārurūpāḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Seeing your face of unequalled splendour and beauty and your body of uncommon lustre, the celestial ladies there, despising their own beauty and lacking in interest in their own qualities will begin to stare at you with winkless eyes.

## \|\| 3.22.32 \|\|

*yā menakā parvatarāja jāyā rūpairguṇaiḥ khyātavatī triloke \|*  
*sā cāpi te tatra manonumodaṃ nityaṃ kariṣyatyanunāthanādyaiḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Menakā, the wife of the king of mountains famous in the three worlds for her beauty and good qualities will delight you very much through words of entreaties.

## \|\| 3.22.33 \|\|

*puraṃ hi vargairgiṃrirājavaṃdyaiḥ prītiṃ vicinvadbhirudārarūpā \|*  
*śikṣā sadā te khalu śocitāpi kāryā'nvahaṃ prītiyutā guṇādyaiḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The honourable ladies of Himālaya’s harem will cause immense pleasure to your gracious Self. They will impart you useful instruction, though you need none, with pleasure every day.

## \|\| 3.22.34-35 \|\|

*vicitraiḥ kokilālāpamodaiḥ kuṃjagaṇāvṛtam \|*  
*sadā vasaṃtaprabhavaṃ gaṃtumicchasi kiṃ priye \|\| 34 \|\|*

*nānābahujalāpūrṇasaraśśīta samāvṛtam \|*  
*padminīśataśoyuktamacalendraṃ himālayam \|\| 35 \|\|*

34-35. O beloved, do you wish to go to the Himālayas, the king of mountains wherein there is spring for ever, which abounds in hedges and groves where the cuckoos coo in diverse pleasing ways and which contains many lakes filled with cool water and hundreds of lotuses.

## \|\| 3.22.36 \|\|

*sarvakāmapradairvṛkṣaiśśādvalaiḥ kalpasaṃjñakaiḥ \|*  
*sakṣaṇaṃ paśya kusumānyathāśvakari govraje \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. It is of full grassy plains and trees that yield everything one desires and hence on a par with Kalpa trees. You can see plenty of flowers, horses, elephants and cows there.

## \|\| 3.22.37 \|\|

*praśāṃtaśvāpadagaṇaṃ munibhiryatibhirvṛtam \|*  
*devālayaṃ mahāmāye nānāmṛgagaṇairyutam \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. There in the Himālayas even the beasts of prey are calm. It is the abode of many sages and ascetics. It is an abode of devas and many deer move about in it.

## \|\| 3.22.38 \|\|

*sphaṭika svarṇavaprādyai rājataiśca virājitam \|*  
*mānasādisaroraṃgairabhitaḥ pariśobhitam \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. It shines with ramparts of crystals, gold and silver. It is lustrous with the lakes—Mānasa and others.

## \|\| 3.22.39 \|\|

*hiraṇmayai ratnanālaiḥ paṃkajairmukulairvṛtam \|*  
*śiśumāraistathāsaṃkhyaiḥ kacchapairmakaraiḥ karaiḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. It abounds in buds and full-blown lotuses with golden stalks studded with gems. Crocodiles, sharks and tortoises abound in the lakes.

## \|\| 3.22.40-41 \|\|

*niṣevitaṃ maṃjulaiśca tathā nīlotpalādibhiḥ \|*  
*deveśi tasmānmuktaiśca sarvagaṃdhaiśca kuṃkumaiḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*lasadgaṃdhajalaiḥ śubhrairāpūrṇaiḥ svacchakāṃtibhiḥ \|*  
*śādvalaistaruṇaistuṃgaistīrasthairupaśobhitam \|\| 41 \|\|*

40-41. O Goddess of devas, there are many beautiful blue lotuses emitting sweet fragrance. On the banks there are many grass lands, small and big trees and the saffron flowers increasing the fragrance of the waters with which the lakes are full.

## \|\| 3.22.42 \|\|

*nṛtyadbhiriva śākhoṭairvarjayaṃtaṃ svasaṃbhavam \|*  
*kāmadevaissārasaiśca mattacakrāṃgaśobhitaiḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. The Apricot tree seems to dance with their oscillating branches. They seem to be fanning the self-born god of love. There are Sārasa birds and the intoxicated Cakravāka birds heightening its beauty.

## \|\| 3.22.43-45 \|\|

*madhurārāvibhirmodakāribhirbhramarādibhiḥ \|*  
*śabdāyamānaṃ ca mudā kāmoddīpanakārakam \|\| 43 \|\|*

*vāsavasya kuberasya yamasya varuṇasya ca \|*  
*agneḥ koṇaparājasya mārutasya parasya ca \|\| 44 \|\|*

*purībhiśśobhiśikharaṃ meroruccaissurālayam \|*  
*raṃbhāśacīmenakādiraṃbhorugaṇasevitam \|\| 45 \|\|*

43-45. The different parts of the mountain Meru seem to be echoing the pleasing sweet sounds of bees etc. which cause the incitement of love of the guardians of the quarters viz. Indra, Kubera, Yama, Varuṇa, Agni, Nirṛti, Marut (Wind)\[5\] and the Supreme lord (Īśa). Heaven, the abode of the Devas is stationed on the summits of the Meru wherein the cities of the guardians of the quarters are also situated. They are brilliant. Beautiful celestial damsels, Rambhā, Śacī, Menakā and others heighten their glory.

## \|\| 3.22.46 \|\|

*kiṃ tvamicchasi sarveṣāṃ parvatānāṃ hi bhūbhṛtām \|*  
*sārabhūte mahāramye saṃvihartuṃ mahāgirau \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Do you wish to sport about on this great mountain which is very beautiful and which appears to contain the essence of all mountains?

## \|\| 3.22.47 \|\|

*tatra devī sakhiyutā sāpsarogaṇamaṃḍitā \|*  
*nityaṃ kariṣyati śacī tava yogyāṃ sahāyatām \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. There, the Queen Śacī attended by her chaperons and celestial damsels will assist you always.

## \|\| 3.22.48 \|\|

*athavā mama kailāse parvateṃdre sadāśraye \|*  
*sthānamicchasi vitteśapurīparivirājite \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Or do you wish to have an abode in my own Kailāsa, the great mountain affording shelter to the good and enhanced in beauty by the luminous city of Kubera?

## \|\| 3.22.49-51 \|\|

*gaṃgājalaughaprayate pūrṇacandrasamaprabhe \|*  
*darīṣu sānuṣu sadā brahmakanyābhyudīrite \|\| 49 \|\|*

*nānāmṛgagaṇairyukte padmākaraśatāvṛte \|*  
*sarvairguṇaiśca sadvastusumerorapi suṃdari \|\| 50 \|\|*

*sthāneṣveteṣu yatrāpi tavāṃtaḥkaraṇe spṛhā \|*  
*taṃ drutaṃ me samācakṣva vāsakartāsmi tatra te \|\| 51 \|\|*

49-51. O beautiful lady, tell me quickly where do you wish to stay among these places, whether in Kailāsa which is pure and holy by virtue of the river Gaṅgā lustrous like the full moon or in the beautiful mountain Meru wherein the maidens of the sages recite and chant hymns in the caves and ridges or in places full of various deer and hundreds of lotus lakes. I shall make arrangements for your residence.

## \|\| 3.22.52 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*itīrite śaṃkareṇa tadā dākṣāyaṇī śanaiḥ \|*  
*idamāha mahādevaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ svaprakāśanam \|\| 52 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

52\. When Śiva said thus, Satī slowly told lord Śiva revealing her desire.

## \|\| 3.22.53 \|\|

*\|\| satyuvāca \|*  
*himādrāveva vasitumahamicche tvayā saha \|*  
*na cirātkuru saṃvāsaṃ tasminneva mahāgirau \|\| 53 \|\|*

Satī said:—

53\. I wish to stay only on the Himālayas along with you. You please make arrangements for a residence on that mountain at once.

## \|\| 3.22.54 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*atha tadvākyamākarṇya haraḥ paramamohitaḥ \|*  
*himādriśikharaṃ tuṃgaṃ dākṣāyaṇyā samaṃ yayau \|\| 54 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

54\. On hearing her words, Śiva was fascinated and he went to the summit of the Himālayas along with her.

## \|\| 3.22.55 \|\|

*siddhāṃganāgaṇayutamagamyaṃ caiva pakṣibhiḥ \|*  
*agamacchikharaṃ ramyaṃ sarasīvanarājitam \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. He reached the beautiful summit where the Siddha ladies resided, which could not be reached by birds and which shone with lakes and forests.

## \|\| 3.22.56 \|\|

*vicitrarūpaiḥ kamalaiḥ śikharaṃ ratnakarburam \|*  
*bālārkasadṛśaṃ śaṃbhurāsasāda satīsakhaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. The top was of variegated colours as of various gems, embellished by lotuses of diverse forms, shapes and lustre. Śiva in the company of Satī reached that top which shone like the rising sun.

## \|\| 3.22.57-64 \|\|

*sphaṭikābhramaye tasmin śādavaladrumarājite \|*  
*vicitrapuṣpāvalibhissarasobhiśca saṃyute \|\| 57 \|\|*

*praphullataruśākhāgraṃ guṃjadbhramarasevitam \|*  
*paṃkeruhaiḥ praphullaiśca nīlotpalacayaistathā \|\| 58 \|\|*

*śobhitaṃ cakravākādyaiḥ kādaṃbairhaṃsaśaṃkubhiḥ \|*  
*pramattasārasaiḥ krauṃcairnīlaskaṃdhaiśca śabditaiḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

*puṃskokilānāṃ ninadairmadhurairgaṇasevitaiḥ \|*  
*turaṃgavadanaissiddhairapsarobhiśca guhyakaiḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

*vidyādharībhirdevībhiḥ kinnarībhirvihāritam \|*  
*puraṃdhrībhiḥ pārvatībhiḥ kanyābhirabhisaṃgatam \|\| 61 \|\|*

*vipaṃcītāṃtrikāmattamṛdaṃgapaṭahasvanaiḥ \|*  
*nṛtyadbhirapsarobhiśca kautukotthaiśca śobhitam \|\| 62 \|\|*

*devikābhirdīrghikābhirgaṃdhibhissusamāvṛtam \|*  
*praphullakusumairnityaṃ sakuṃjairupaśobhitam \|\| 63 \|\|*

*śailarājapurābhyarṇe śikhare vṛṣabhadhvajaḥ \|*  
*saha satyā ciraṃ reme evaṃbhūteṣu śobhanam \|\| 64 \|\|*

57-64. On the top of the mountain near the city of Himālaya, Śiva sported about for a long time in the company of Satī. It was a very beautiful place which abounded in crystalline clouds. It shone with grassy plains and plenty of trees. There were various flowers in abundance. It had many lakes. The boughs of the full-blown and blossomed trees were surrounded by humming bees. Lotuses and blue lilies were in full bloom. Different kinds of birds flew there, such as—Cakravāka Kādamba, swans, geese, the intoxicated Sārasas, cranes, the peacocks etc. The sweet note of the male cuckoo reverberated there. Many kinds of semidivine beings the Aśvamukhas, the Siddhas, the Apsaras, the Guhyakas, etc. roamed there. Their women-folk, the Vidyādharīs, the Kinnarīs and the mountain lasses played about here and there. The celestial damsels played on their lutes, tabours and drums and danced with enthusiasm. Thus the top of the mountain abounded in beautiful women, beautiful lakes, fragrant flowers and groves of full-blown flowers.

## \|\| 3.22.65 \|\|

*tasminsvargasame sthāne divyamānena śaṃkaraḥ \|*  
*daśavarṣasahasrāṇi reme satyā samaṃ mudā \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. In that heaven-like spot Śiva sported about with Satī for ten thousand years according to divine calculation.

## \|\| 3.22.66-67 \|\|

*sa kadācittatassthānādanyadyāti sthalaṃ haraḥ \|*  
*kadācinmeruśikharaṃ devī devavṛtaṃ sadā \|\| 66 \|\|*

*dvīpānnānā tathodyānavanāni vasudhātalam \|*  
*gatvāgatvā punastatrābhyetya reme satīsukham \|\| 67 \|\|*

66-67. Śiva went from place to place. Sometimes He went to the top of Meru wherein Gods and Goddesses resided. He went to different continents, parks and forests on the earth. After visiting the different places He returned home and lived with Satī.

## \|\| 3.22.68-70 \|\|

*na jajñe sa divā rātrau na brahmaṇi tapassamam \|*  
*satyāṃ hi manasā śaṃbhuḥ prītimeva cakāra ha \|\| 68 \|\|*

*evaṃ mahādevamukhaṃ satyapaśyatsma sarvadā \|*  
*mahādevo'pi sarvatra sadādrākṣītsatīmukham \|\| 69 \|\|*

*evamanyonyasaṃsargādanurāgamahīruham \|*  
*varddhayāmāsatuḥ kālīśivau bhāvāṃbusecanaiḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

68-70. Śiva found place and pleasure only with Satī. He found no pleasure in sacrifices or the Vedas or penances. Day and night Satī stared into the face of Śiva and He, the great lord, stared into the face of Satī. Thus by their mutual association Kālī and Śiva nurtured the tree of love, sprinkling it with waters of emotion.

## Chapter 23 - Description of the Power of Devotion

## \|\| 3.23.1 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*evaṃ kṛtvā vihāraṃ vai śaṃkareṇa ca sā satī \|*  
*saṃtuṣṭā sābhavaccāti virāgā samajāyata \|\| 1 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

1\. After sporting about like this till satiety with Śiva, Satī became less attached.

## \|\| 3.23.2-3 \|\|

*ekasmindivase devī satī rahasi saṃgatā \|*  
*śivaṃ praṇamya sadbhaktyā nyasyoccaiḥ sukṛtāṃjaliḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*suprasannaṃ prabhuṃ natvā sā dakṣatanayā satī \|*  
*uvāca sāṃjalirbhaktyā vinayāvanatā tataḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. One day after delighting the lord with her devotion and obeisance Satī, the daughter of Dakṣa, spoke thus to Śiva.

## \|\| 3.23.4 \|\|

*satyuvāca \|*  
*devadeva mahādeva karuṇā sāgara prabho \|*  
*dīnoddhara mahāyogin kṛpāṃ kuru mamopari \|\| 4 \|\|*

Satī said:—

4\. O great lord, lord of lords and ocean of mercy, O great Yogin, the uplifter of the distressed, take pity on me.

## \|\| 3.23.5 \|\|

*tvaṃ paraḥ puruṣassvāmī rajassattvatamaḥ paraḥ \|*  
*nirguṇassaguṇassākṣī nirvikārī mahāprabhuḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. You are a great Puruṣa, the lord, beyond Sattva, Rajas and Tamas. You are both Saguṇa and Nirguṇa. You are a great lord, a cosmic witness, and free from aberration.

## \|\| 3.23.6 \|\|

*dhanyāhaṃ te priyā jātā kāminī suvihāriṇī \|*  
*jātastvaṃ me patissvāminbhaktivātsalyato hara \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. I am blessed since I became your beloved wife sporting with you. O lord, you became my husband because of your love for your devotees.

## \|\| 3.23.7 \|\|

*kṛto bahusamā nātha vihāraḥ paramastvayā \|*  
*saṃtuṣṭāhaṃ maheśāna nivṛttaṃ me manastataḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. O lord, after sporting with you for many years I have become fully satiated and now my mind is turned away from it.

## \|\| 3.23.8 \|\|

*jñātumicchāmi deveśa paraṃ tattvaṃ sukhāvaham \|*  
*yaṃ na saṃsāraduḥkhādvai tarejjīvoṃjasā hara \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. O lord of gods, I wish to know the great pleasing principle whereby O, Śiva, all living beings surmount worldly miseries in a trice.,

## \|\| 3.23.9 \|\|

*yatkṛtvā viṣayī jīvassa labhetparamaṃ padam \|*  
*saṃsārī na bhavennātha tattvaṃ vada kṛpāṃ kuru \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. O lord, please explain that activity which enables people, to obtain the supreme region and free themselves from worldly bondage.

## \|\| 3.23.10 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityapṛcchatsma sadbhaktyā śaṃkaraṃ sā satī mune \|*  
*ādiśaktirmaheśānī jīvoddhārāya kevalam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. O sage, the primordial Goddess asked Śiva thus only for the sake of uplifting worldly creatures.

## \|\| 3.23.11 \|\|

*ākarṇya tacchivaḥ svāmī svecchayopāttavigrahaḥ \|*  
*avocatparamaprītassatīṃ yogaviraktadhīḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. On hearing that, lord Śiva whose mind is engrossed in the practice of Yoga and who assumes physical bodies out of his own accord, spoke to Satī.

## \|\| 3.23.12 \|\|

*\|\| śiva uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu devi pravakṣyāmi dākṣāyaṇi maheśvari \|*  
*paraṃ tattvaṃ tadevānuśayī mukto bhavedyataḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

Śiva said:—

12\. O Goddess Satī, listen, I shall explain the great principle whereby the remorseful creature becomes a liberated soul.

## \|\| 3.23.13 \|\|

*paratattvaṃ vijānīhi vijñānaṃ parameśvarī \|*  
*dvitīyaṃ smaraṇaṃ yatra nāhaṃ brahmeti śuddhadhīḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. O great Goddess, know that the perfect knowledge is the great principle—the consciousness that “I am Brahman” in the perfect intellect where nothing else is remembered.

## \|\| 3.23.14 \|\|

*taddurlabhaṃ trilokesmiṃstajjñātā viralaḥ priye \|*  
*yādṛśo yassadāsohaṃ brahmasākṣātparātparaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. This consciousness is very rare in the three worlds. O beloved, I am Brahman, the greatest of the great and very few are those who know my real nature.

## \|\| 3.23.15 \|\|

*tanmātā mama bhaktiśca bhuktimuktiphalapradā \|*  
*sulabhā matprasādāddhi navadhā sā prakīrtitā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Devotion to me is considered as the bestower of worldly pleasures and salvation. It is achievable only by my grace. It is nine-fold.

## \|\| 3.23.16 \|\|

*bhaktau jñāne na bhedo hi tatkartussarvadā sukham \|*  
*vijñānaṃ na bhavatyeva sati bhaktivirodhinaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. There is no difference between devotion and perfect knowledge. A person who is engrossed in devotion enjoys perpetual happiness. Perfect knowledge never descends in a vicious person averse to devotion.

## \|\| 3.23.17 \|\|

*bhaktyā hīnassadāhaṃ vai tatprabhāvādgṛheṣvapi \|*  
*nīcānāṃ jātihīnānāṃ yāmi devi na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Attracted by devotion and as a result of its influence, O Goddess, I go even to the houses of the base-born and outcastes. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 3.23.18-20 \|\|

*sā bhaktirdvividhā devi saguṇā nirguṇā matā \|*  
*vaidhī svābhāvikī yā yā varā sā tvavarā smṛtā \|\| 18 \|\|*

*naiṣṭhikyā naiṣṭhikī bhedāddvividhe dvividhe hi te \|*  
*ṣaḍvidhā naiṣṭhikī jñeyā dvitīyaikavidhā smṛtā \|\| 19 \|\|*

*vihitāvihitābhedāttāmanekāṃ vidurbudhāḥ \|*  
*tayorbahuvidhatvācca tattvaṃ tvanyatra varṇitam \|\| 20 \|\|*

18-20. Devotion is variously classified as attributive and attributeless, as conventional and natural, greater and lesser, perpetual and non-perpetual. There are six further subdivisions of the perpetual devotion. Scholars further classify it into enjoined and non-enjoined. Thus devotions are manifold which have been explained elsewhere.

## \|\| 3.23.21 \|\|

*te navāṃge ubhe jñeye varṇite munibhiḥ priye \|*  
*varṇayāmi navāṃgāni premataḥ śṛṇu dakṣaje \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. O beloved, sages have explained that the different kinds of devotion have nine ancillary adjuncts. O daughter of Dakṣa, I shall narrate them to which you listen with love.

## \|\| 3.23.22-23 \|\|

*śravaṇaṃ kīrtanaṃ caiva smaraṇaṃ sevanaṃ tathā \|*  
*dāsyaṃ tathārcanaṃ devi vaṃdanaṃ mama sarvadā \|\| 22 \|\|*

*sakhyamātmārpaṇaṃ ceti navāṃgāni vidurbudhāḥ \|*  
*upāṃgāni śive tasyā bahūni kathitāni vai \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. According to scholars O Goddess, the nine ancillary adjuncts are:—listening, eulogising, remembering, serving, surrendering, worshipping, saluting, friendliness and dedication. O Śiva, its further subdivisions too have been explained.

## \|\| 3.23.24-25 \|\|

*śṛṇu devi navāṃgānāṃ lakṣaṇāni pṛthakpṛthak \|*  
*mama bhaktermano dattvā bhakti muktipradāni hi \|\| 24 \|\|*

*kathādernityasammānaṃ kurvandehādibhirmudā \|*  
*sthirāsanena tatpānaṃ yattacchravaṇamucyate \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. O Goddess, listen to the characteristics of these nine adjuncts separately. By listening is meant the imbibing of my stories that bestow worldly pleasures and salvation, with great devotion, in steady posture.

## \|\| 3.23.26 \|\|

*hṛdākāśena saṃpaśyañ janmakarmāṇi vai mama \|*  
*prītyācoccāraṇaṃ teṣāmetatkīrtanamucyate \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. After conceiving in the mind the details of my manifestations and activities, loudly and cheerfully, proclaiming the same in order to eulogise me is what is called eulogising.

## \|\| 3.23.27 \|\|

*vyāpakaṃ devi māṃ dṛṣṭvā nityaṃ sarvatra sarvadā \|*  
*nirbhayatvaṃ sadā loke smaraṇaṃ tadudāhṛtam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. O Goddess, after realising me to be all-pervading a feeling of fearlessness is what is called remembering.

## \|\| 3.23.28 \|\|

*aruṇodayamārabhya sevākāleṃcitā hṛdā \|*  
*nirbhayatvaṃ sadā loke smaraṇaṃ tadudāhṛtam \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. The service rendered to the godhead commencing at the early dawn, with mind, speech, hands and feet is what is called serving.

## \|\| 3.23.29 \|\|

*sadā sevyānukūlyena sevanaṃ taddhi gogaṇaiḥ \|*  
*hṛdayāmṛtabhogena priyaṃ dāsyamudāhṛtam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Surrendering oneself in the service of the godhead who is worthy of being served and serving with all the sense-organs feeling hearty sense of elation is what is called surrendering.

## \|\| 3.23.30 \|\|

*sadā bhṛtyānukūlyena vidhinā me parātmane \|*  
*arpaṇaṃ ṣoḍaśānāṃ vai pādyādīnāṃ tadarcanam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Offering sixteen types of service to me, the supreme soul, in accordance with one’s capacity is called worshipping. The sixteen types of service are Pādya etc.

## \|\| 3.23.31 \|\|

*maṃtroccāraṇadhyānābhyāṃ manasā vacasā kramāt \|*  
*yadaṣṭāṃgena bhūsparśaṃ tadvai vaṃdanamucyate \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Meditating in the mind, repeating the mantras and touching the ground with eight limbs is called saluting.

## \|\| 3.23.32 \|\|

*maṃgalāmaṃgalaṃ yadyatkarotītīśvaro hi me \|*  
*sarvaṃ tanmaṃgalāyeti viśvāsaḥ sakhyalakṣaṇam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. The belief—“Whatever god bestows on me, good or bad, is for my welfare”—is the characteristic sign of friendliness.

## \|\| 3.23.33 \|\|

*kṛtvā dehādikaṃ tasya prītyai sarvaṃ tadarpaṇam \|*  
*nirvāhāya ca śūnyatvaṃ yattadātmasamarpaṇam \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Dedicating everything, the body and other possessions, for the propitiation of the godhead and retaining nothing for oneself is called dedication.

## \|\| 3.23.34 \|\|

*navāṃgānīti madbhakterbhuktimuktipradāni ca \|*  
*mama priyāṇi cātīva jñānotpattikarāṇi ca \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. These nine adjuncts to the devotion to me, cause perfect knowledge, bestow wordly pleasures and salvation and are pleasing to me.

## \|\| 3.23.35 \|\|

*upāṃgāni ca madbhakterbahūni kathitāni vai \|*  
*bilvādisevanādīni samū hyāni vicārataḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. The further subdivisions in the adjuncts are numerous. Nurturing the Bilva tree etc. can be included therein. They shall be thought of by the devotee himself.

## \|\| 3.23.36 \|\|

*itthaṃ sāṃgopāṃgabhaktirmama sarvottamā priye \|*  
*jñānavairāgyajananī muktidāsī virājate \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. O beloved, thus my devotion with various adjuncts and ancillaries, is contributory to salvation since it is productive of perfect Knowledge and Detachment. It is the most excellent path.

## \|\| 3.23.37 \|\|

*sarvakarmaphalotpattissarvadā tvatsamapriyā \|*  
*yaccitte sā sthitā nityaṃ sarvadā soti matpriyaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. A true devotion is as endearing to me as to you. It is productive of the fruits of all rites for ever. He who has it in his mind is a great favourite of mine.

## \|\| 3.23.38 \|\|

*trailokye bhaktisadṛśaḥ paṃthā nāsti sukhāvahaḥ \|*  
*caturyugeṣu deveśi kalau tu suviśeṣataḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. There is no other path as easy and pleasing as devotion in the three worlds, O goddess of devas, in all the four Yugas generally and in the Kaliyuga particularly.

## \|\| 3.23.39 \|\|

*kalau tu jñānavairāgo vṛddharūpau nirutsavau \|*  
*grāhakābhāvato devi jātau jarjara tāmati \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Knowledge (Jñāna) and Detachment (Vairāgya) have grown old and have lost their lustre in the Kali Age. They have become decayed and worn-out as the people who can grasp them are rare.

## \|\| 3.23.40 \|\|

*kalau pratyakṣaphaladā bhaktissarvayugeṣvapi \|*  
*tatprabhāvādahaṃ nityaṃ tadvaśo nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. In the Kali age as in all the four Yugas there is immediate and visible benefit in devotion. I am subservient to a devotee in view of the power of devotion.

## \|\| 3.23.41 \|\|

*yo bhaktimānpumāṃlloke sadāhaṃ tatsahāyakṛt \|*  
*vighnahartā ripustasya daṃḍyo nātra ca saṃśayaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. I always assist a man endowed with devotion and remove his obstacles. A person devoid of devotion is worthy of being punished. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 3.23.42 \|\|

*bhaktahetorahaṃ devi kālaṃ krodhapariplutaḥ \|*  
*adahaṃ vahninā netrabhavena nijarakṣakaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. I am the protector of my devotees. For the protection of a devotee of mine I burnt the God of death, O goddess, in the fire emerging from my eyes.

## \|\| 3.23.43 \|\|

*bhaktahetorahaṃ devi ravyuparyabhavaṃ kila \|*  
*atikrodhānvitaḥ śūlaṃ gṛhītvā'nvajayaṃ purā \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. For the sake of a devotee of mine I became very furious with the sun formerly. I over-powered him with my trident.

## \|\| 3.23.44 \|\|

*bhaktahetorahaṃ devi rāvaṇaṃ sagaṇaṃ krudhā \|*  
*tyajati sma kṛto naiva pakṣapāto hi tasya vai \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. I was not a party to the evil actions of Rāvaṇa (though he was my devotee). For the sake of another devotee I discarded Rāvaṇa with all his followers.

## \|\| 3.23.45 \|\|

*bhaktahetorahaṃ devi vyāsaṃ hi kumatigraham \|*  
*kāśyā nyasārayat krodhāddaṇḍayitvā ca naṃdinā \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. O goddess, for the sake of a devotee, I angrily expelled Vyāsa when he had a vicious thought, from Kāśī after punishing him duly through Nandin.

## \|\| 3.23.46 \|\|

*kiṃ bahūktena deveśi bhaktyādhīnassadā hyaham \|*  
*tatkartuṃ puruṣasyātivaśago nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Why shall I say more, O Goddess? I am always subservient to a devotee, always under the control of a person who practises devotion. There is no doubt in this.

## \|\| 3.23.47 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*itthamākarṇya bhaktestu mahattvaṃ dakṣajā satī \|*  
*jaharṣātīva manasi praṇanāma śivaṃ mudā \|\| 47 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

47\. On hearing this greatness of devotion, Satī, the daughter of Dakṣa, was delighted much and bowed to Śiva with pleasure.

## \|\| 3.23.48 \|\|

*punaḥ papraccha sadbhaktyā tatkāṇḍaviṣayaṃ mune \|*  
*śāstraṃ sukhakaraṃ loke jīvoddhāraparāyaṇam \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. O sage, again she asked with great devotion more about the subject as explained in the Śāstras which is pleasing and conducive to the uplift of all creatures.

## \|\| 3.23.49 \|\|

*sayaṃtramaṃtraśāstraṃ ca tanmāhātmyaṃ viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*anyāni dharmavastūni jīvoddhārakarāṇi hi \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. She enquired about topics on virtue and righteous living, uplighting the creatures and the sacred lore on Yantras and Mantras together with their greatness.

## \|\| 3.23.50 \|\|

*śaṃkaropi tadākarṇya satīṃ praśnaṃ prahṛṣṭadhīḥ \|*  
*varṇayāmāsa suprītyā jīvoddhārāya kṛtsnaśaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. On hearing the enquiry of Satī Śiva was delighted and He narrated them with pleasure in their entirety for raising the worldly creatures.

## \|\| 3.23.51 \|\|

*tatra śāstraṃ sayaṃtraṃ hi sapaṃcāṅgaṃ maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*babhāṣe mahimānaṃ ca tattaddaivavarasya vai \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. The sacred lore bearing on the subject, the glory and greatness of the illustrious lord, Śiva explained Himself with Yantras, with their five adjuncts.

## \|\| 3.23.52 \|\|

*setihāsakathaṃ teṣāṃ bhaktamāhātmyameva ca \|*  
*savarṇāśramadharmāṃśca nṛpadharmān munīśvara \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. He told her legendary stories, the greatness of the votaries, the norms of peoples of different castes and stages in life and the duties of kings, O great sage.

## \|\| 3.23.53 \|\|

*sutastrīdharmamāhātmyaṃ varṇāśramamanaśvaram \|*  
*vaidyaśāstraṃ tathā jyotiśśāstraṃ jīvasukhāvaham \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. The duties of sons, wives etc. and their greatness, the imperishable system of Varṇas and Āśramas, the medical lore, and the astral lore, all beneficent to worldly creatures were explained by him.

## \|\| 3.23.54 \|\|

*sāmudrikaṃ paraṃ śāstramanyacchāstrāṇi bhūriśaḥ \|*  
*kṛpāṃ kṛtvā mahe śāno varṇayāmāsa tattvataḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Out of compassion for her, the great lord explained the science of palmistry and similar other lores to her.

## \|\| 3.23.55-56 \|\|

*itthaṃ trilokasukhadau sarvajñau ca satīśivau \|*  
*lokopakārakaraṇadhṛtasadguṇavigrahau \|\| 55 \|\|*

*cikrīḍāte bahuvidhe kailāse himavadgirau \|*  
*anyasthaleṣu ca tadā parabrahmasvarūpiṇau \|\| 56 \|\|*

55-56. Thus Satī and Śiva who are intrinsically the Supreme Brahman, who are the bestowers of happiness on the three worlds. who are omniscient, who are bent upon rendering help to the people, who appear as the personification of good qualities sported about in Kailāsa, in the Himālayas and other places.

## Chapter 24 - Satī’s test of Rāma’s divinity

## \|\| 3.24.3 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*satīśivacaritraṃ ca śṛṇu me premato mune \|*  
*laukikīṃ gatimāśritya cikrīḍāte sadānvaham \|\| 3 \|\|*

Nārada said:—

l-2. “O Brahmā, lord of subjects, of great mercy and lofty intellect, you have narrated the benevolent glory of Satī and Śiva. Now, please tell me more of their glory. What did the couple Śiva and Śivā do further, stationed on that (mountain)?

Brahmā said:—

3\. O sage, listen to the story of Satī and Śiva. Having resorted to worldly conventions they continued their sports every day.

## \|\| 3.24.4 \|\|

*tatassatī mahādevī viyogamalabhanmune \|*  
*svapataśśaṃkarasyeti vadaṃtyeke subuddhayaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Thereafter, according to a tradition, it is said that the great Goddess Satī was separated from her husband Śiva.

## \|\| 3.24.5 \|\|

*vāgarthāviva saṃpṛktau śaktośau sarvadā citau \|*  
*kathaṃ ghaṭeta ca tayorviyogastattvato mune \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Śakti and Īśa are united for ever like a word and its meaning. O sage, how can a real separation of the two occur?

## \|\| 3.24.6 \|\|

*līlārucitvādatha vā saṃghaṭetā'khilaṃ ca tat \|*  
*kurute yadyadīśaśca satī ca bhavarītigau \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Or inasmuch as Satī and Śiva have sportive interest, whatever they do is proper. For, they follow the conventions of the world.

## \|\| 3.24.7 \|\|

*sā tyaktā dakṣajā dṛṣṭvā patinā janakādhvare \|*  
*śaṃbhoranādarāttatra dehaṃ tatyāja saṃgatā \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. She was forsaken by her husband at the time of her father’s sacrifice. In view of the disrespect shown to Śiva she cast-off her body there.

## \|\| 3.24.8 \|\|

*punarhimālaye saivāvirbhūtā nāmatassatī \|*  
*pārvatīti śivaṃ prāpa taptvā bhūri vivāhataḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. She was born again as Pārvatī, daughter of the Himālayas. She performed penance for several years and attained Śiva as her husband.

## \|\| 3.24.9 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya vacastasya brahmaṇassa tu nāradaḥ \|*  
*papraccha ca vidhātāraṃ śivāśivamahadyaśaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

Sūta said:—

9\. After hearing these words of Brahmā, Nārada asked the Creator about the glory of Śivā and Śiva.

## \|\| 3.24.10 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*viṣṇuśiṣya mahābhāga vidhe me vada vistarāt \|*  
*śivāśivacaritraṃ tadbhavācāraparānugam \|\| 10 \|\|*

Nārada said:—

10\. O Brahmā, disciple of Viṣṇu, of great fortune, please explain in detail the story of Śivā and Śiva who followed the conventions of the world.

## \|\| 3.24.11 \|\|

*kimarthaṃ śaṃkaro jāyāṃ tatyāja prāṇataḥ priyām \|*  
*tasmādācakṣva me tāta vicitramiti manmahe \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. O dear, why did Śiva abandon His wife who was to Him dearer than his life? It looks rather strange. Hence please explain.

## \|\| 3.24.12 \|\|

*kuto'hyadhvarajaḥ putrāṃ nādarobhūcchivasya te \|*  
*kathaṃ tatyāja sā dehaṃ gatvā tatra pitṛkratau \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Wherefore did your son Dakṣa disrespect Śiva at the time of sacrifice? How did she abandon her body at the sacrifice of her father?

## \|\| 3.24.13 \|\|

*tataḥ kimabhavattatra kimakārṣīnmaheśvaraḥ \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ me samācakṣva śraddhāyuk tacchutāvaham \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. What happened after that? What did Śiva do? Please explain everything to me. I am eager to listen to it.

## \|\| 3.24.14 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*śṛṇu tāta paraprītyā munibhissaha nārada \|*  
*sutavarya mahāprājña caritaṃ śaśimaulinaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

14\. O dear Nārada, of great intellect, the most excellent of my sons, listen with pleasure, along with the sages, to the story of the moon-crested lord.

## \|\| 3.24.15 \|\|

*namaskṛtya maheśānaṃ haryādisurasevitam \|*  
*parabrahma pravakṣyāmi taccaritraṃ mahādbhutam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. After bowing to lord Śiva who is the supreme Brahman and who is served by Viṣṇu and others, I begin to explain and narrate His story of wonderful significance.

## \|\| 3.24.16 \|\|

*sarveyaṃ śivalīlā hi bahulīlākaraḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*svataṃtro nirvikārī ca satī sāpi hi tadvidhā \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Everything is a sport of Śiva. The lord indulges in many divine sports. He is independent and undecaying. Satī too is like that.

## \|\| 3.24.17-18 \|\|

*anyathā kassamartho hi tatkarmakaraṇe mune \|*  
*paramātmā parabrahma sa eva parameśvaraḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*yaṃ sadā bhajate śrīśo'haṃ cāpi sakalāḥ surāḥ \|*  
*munayaśca mahātmānaḥ siddhāśca sanakādayaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. Otherwise, O sage, who can perform such wonderful deeds? Lord Śiva alone is the Supreme soul and the Supreme Brahman whom we all worship—I, Viṣṇu, all the devas, sages, the noble-souled Siddhas like Sanaka and others.

## \|\| 3.24.19 \|\|

*śeṣassadā yaśo yasya mudā gāyati nityaśaḥ \|*  
*pāraṃ na labhate tāta sa prabhuśśaṃkaraḥ śivaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. O dear one, Śiva is that lord whose glory is sung for ever by Śeṣa with great pleasure but is never exhausted.

## \|\| 3.24.20 \|\|

*tasyaiva līlayā sarvoyamiti tattvavibhramaḥ \|*  
*tatra doṣo na kasyāpi sarvavyāpī sa prerakaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. The erroneous perception of this visible world is due to His own sports. There none can be blamed. The all-pervasive lord is the inducer.

## \|\| 3.24.21 \|\|

*ekasminsamaye rudrassatyā tribhuvane bhavaḥ \|*  
*vṛṣamāruhya paryāṭadrasāṃ līlāviśāradaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Once Śiva accompanied by Satī and seated on His Bull wandered over the Earth, in one of his sportive activities.

## \|\| 3.24.22 \|\|

*āgatya daṇḍakāraṇyaṃ paryaṭan sāgarāṃbarām \|*  
*darśayan tatra gāṃ śobhāṃ satyai satyapaṇaḥ prabhuḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Wandering over the ocean-girt Earth He reached Daṇḍaka forest where the lord of truthful stake and transaction pointed to Satī the beauty of the surrounding nature.

## \|\| 3.24.23 \|\|

*tatra rāmaṃ dadarśāsau lakṣmaṇenānvitaṃ haraḥ \|*  
*anviṣyaṃtaṃ priyāṃ sītāṃ rāvaṇena hṛtā chalāt \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. There Śiva saw Rāma who was searching for Sitā who was deceitfully abducted by Rāvaṇa. Lakṣmaṇa too was there.

## \|\| 3.24.24 \|\|

*hā sīteti proccaraṃtaṃ virahāviṣṭamānasam \|*  
*yatastataśca paśyaṃtaṃ rudaṃtaṃ hi muhurmuhuḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Due to the pangs of separation Rāma was crying out “Alas Sītā.” He was pitiably lamenting and glancing here and there.

## \|\| 3.24.25 \|\|

*samicchaṃtaṃ ca tatprāptiṃ pṛcchaṃtaṃ tadgatiṃ hṛdā \|*  
*kujādibhyo naṣṭadhiyamatrapaṃ śokavihvalam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Rāma was yearning for her redemption. He was musing over her whereabouts. Due to adverse position of planets like Mars etc. he had become forlorn and shamelessly grief-stricken.

## \|\| 3.24.26 \|\|

*sūryavaṃśodbhavaṃ vīraṃ bhūpaṃ daśarathātmajam \|*  
*bharatāgrajamānaṃdarahitaṃ vigataprabham \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. He was a heroic king of the solar race, son of Daśaratha, elder brother of Bharata. He had become cheerless and devoid of lustre.

## \|\| 3.24.27 \|\|

*pūrṇakāmo varādhīnaṃ prāṇamatsma mudā haraḥ \|*  
*rāmaṃ bhramantaṃ vipine salakṣmaṇamudāradhīḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. The great liberal-minded lord Śiva who is Pūrṇakāma (one whose ambitions are fully realised) delightfully bowed to Rāma who was wandering in the forest in the company of Lakṣmaṇa and was in need of a favour.

## \|\| 3.24.28 \|\|

*jayetyuktvā'nyato gacchannadāttasmai svadarśanam \|*  
*rāmāya vipine tasmicchaṃkaro bhaktavatsalaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. “Be victorious” said Śiva who is favourably disposed to His devotees. While He was going elsewhere in the forest He revealed Himself to Rāma.

## \|\| 3.24.29 \|\|

*itīdṛśīṃ satīṃ dṛṣṭvā śivalīlāṃ vimohanīm \|*  
*suvismitā śivaṃ prāha śivamāyāvimohitā \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Satī was surprised at this charmingly strange sport of Śiva. She was deluded by Śiva’s Māyā and spoke to Him.

## \|\| 3.24.30 \|\|

*satyuvāca \|*  
*deva deva parabrahma sarveśa parameśvara \|*  
*sevaṃte tvāṃ sadā sarve haribrahmādayassurāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

Satī said:—

30\. O lord, the lord of all, the Supreme Brahman, all the devas, Viṣṇu, Brahmā and others serve Thee always.

## \|\| 3.24.31 \|\|

*tvaṃ praṇamyo hi sarveṣāṃ sevyo dhyeyaśca sarvadā \|*  
*vedāṃtavedyo yatnena nirvikārī paraprabhuḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Thou art worthy of being served and bowed to. Thou art worthy of being meditated upon always. Thou art known and realised only through the science of Metaphysics, after strenuous efforts. Thou art the great lord, the undecaying.

## \|\| 3.24.32 \|\|

*kāvimau puruṣau nātha virahavyākulākṛtī \|*  
*vicaraṃtau vane kliṣṭau dīnau vīrau dhanurdharau \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. O lord, who are these two persons apparently grief-stricken from pangs of separation? Though heroic archers they are greatly distressed. They seem to be roaming about in the forest.

## \|\| 3.24.33 \|\|

*tayorjyeṣṭhaṃ kaṃjaśyāmaṃ dṛṣṭvā vai kena hetunā \|*  
*suditassuprasannātmā'bhavo bhakta ivā'dhunā \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. How is it that Thou becomest highly delighted and behavest like a devotee on seeing the elder of the two who resembles a blue lotus (in complexion)?

## \|\| 3.24.34 \|\|

*iti me saṃśayaṃ svāmiñśaṃkara chettumarhasi \|*  
*sevyasya sevakenaiva ghaṭate praṇatiḥ prabho \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. O lord Śiva, may this doubt of mine be kindly heard. O lord, the kneeling down of the master at the feet of a servant is not quite befitting.

## \|\| 3.24.35 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ādiśaktissatī devī śivā sā parameśvarī \|*  
*śivamāyāvaśībhūtvā papracchetthaṃ śivaṃ prabhum \|\| 35 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

35\. The great Goddess Satī the primordial Sakti, put this question to Śiva on being deluded by Śiva’s illusion.

## \|\| 3.24.36 \|\|

*tadākarṇya vacassatyāśśaṃkaraḥ parameśvaraḥ \|*  
*tadā vihasya sa prāha satīṃ līlāviśāradaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. On hearing these words of Satī, lord Śiva laughed and said to Satī. He was shrewd in his divine sports.

## \|\| 3.24.37 \|\|

*parameśvara uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu devi sati prītyā yathārthaṃ vacmi nacchalam \|*  
*varadānaprabhāvāttu praṇāmaṃ caivamādarāt \|\| 37 \|\|*

Lord Śiva said:

37\. “O Goddess Satī, listen with pleasure. I shall truly explain it. There is no deception. I bowed thus with respect due to the power of the boon (granted by me).

## \|\| 3.24.38 \|\|

*rāmalakṣmaṇanāmānau bhrātarau vīrasammatau \|*  
*sūryavaṃśodbhavau devi prājñau daśarathātmajau \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. O Goddess, they are two brothers Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa. They are heroic, intelligent sons of Daśaratha, born of the solar dynasty.

## \|\| 3.24.39 \|\|

*gauravarṇau laghurbaṃdhuśśeṣeśo lakṣmaṇābhidhaḥ \|*  
*jyeṣṭho rāmābhidho viṣṇuḥ pūrṇāṃśo nirupadravaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. The fair-complexioned one is the younger brother Lakṣmaṇa. He is the partial incarnation of Śeṣa. The elder one is the complete incarnation of Viṣṇu. He is called Rāma. He is incapable of being harassed.

## \|\| 3.24.40 \|\|

*avatīrṇaṃ kṣitau sādhurakṣaṇāya bhavāya naḥ \|*  
*ityuktvā virarāmā'sau śaṃbhusmṛtikaraḥ prabhuḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. The lord has incarnated on the Earth for our welfare and the protection of the good.” Saying thus Śiva, the lord, who causes prosperity to his votaries stopped.

## \|\| 3.24.41 \|\|

*śrutvāpītthaṃ vacaśśambhorna viśaśvāsa tanmanaḥ \|*  
*śivamāyā balavatī saiva trailokyamohinī \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Even after hearing these words of Śiva, her mind was not convinced. Powerful indeed is Śiva’s Māyā capable of deluding even the three worlds.

## \|\| 3.24.42 \|\|

*aviśvastaṃ mano jñātvā tasyāśśaṃbhussanātanaḥ \|*  
*avocadvacanaṃ ceti prabhulīlāviśāradaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. On realising that her mind was not convinced, Śiva, the eternal lord, who is shrewd in the divine sports which He indulges in, spoke these words:—

## \|\| 3.24.43 \|\|

*śiva uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu madvacanaṃ devi na viśvasiti cenmanaḥ \|*  
*tava rāmaparikṣāṃ hi kuru tatra svayā dhiyā \|\| 43 \|\|*

Śiva said:

43\. O Goddess, if your mind is not convinced, listen to my words. You can test the divinity of Rāma yourself, using your own intelligence.

## \|\| 3.24.44 \|\|

*vinaśyati yathā mohastatkuru tvaṃ sati priye \|*  
*gatvā tatra sthitastāvadvaṭe bhava parīkṣikā \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. O beloved Satī, he is standing there beneath the Vaṭa tree. You can test him and proceed until your delusion is quelled.

## \|\| 3.24.45 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*śivājñayā satī tatra gatvāciṃtayadīśvarī \|*  
*kuryāṃ parīkṣāṃ ca kathaṃ rāmasya vanacāriṇaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

45\. Going there at Śiva’s bidding, Satī the Goddess thought—“How shall I test Rāma the forest-roamer.

## \|\| 3.24.46 \|\|

*sītārūpamahaṃ dhṛtvā gaccheyaṃ rāmasannidhau \|*  
*yadi rāmo harissarvaṃ vijñāsyati na cānyathā \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. I shall assume the form of Sītā and shall go to him. If Rāma is Viṣṇu, he will know it and otherwise not.

## \|\| 3.24.47 \|\|

*itthaṃ vicārya sītā sā bhūtvā rāmasamīpataḥ \|*  
*āgamattatparīkṣārthaṃ satī mohaparāyaṇā \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Deciding like this she who was deluded by Śiva became Sītā and went there to test him.

## \|\| 3.24.48 \|\|

*sītārūpāṃ satīṃ dṛṣṭvā japannāma śiveti ca \|*  
*vihasya tatpravijñāya natvāvocadraghūdvahaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. On seeing Satī, in the guise of Sītā, Rāma the scion of Raghu’s race repeated the name Śiva, realised the truth and laughed. He bowed to her and said.

## \|\| 3.24.49 \|\|

*rāma uvāca \|*  
*prematastvaṃ sati brūhi kva śaṃbhuste namogataḥ \|*  
*ekā hi vipine kasmādāgatā patinā vinā \|\| 49 \|\|*

Rāma said:—

49\. “O Satī, Obeisance to you. Where has Śiva gone? Please tell me affably. How is it that you have come here alone without your husband?

## \|\| 3.24.50 \|\|

*tyaktvā svarūpaṃ kasmātte dhṛtaṃ rūpamidaṃ sati \|*  
*brūhi tatkāraṇaṃ devi kṛpāṃ kṛtvā mamopari \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. O goddess Satī, why have you cast off your own form and assumed this guise? Take pity on me and tell me the reason thereof.”

## \|\| 3.24.51 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*iti rāmavacaḥ śrutvā cakitāsītsatī tadā \|*  
*smṛtvā śivoktaṃ matvā cāvitathaṃ lajjitā bhṛśam \|\| 51 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

51\. On hearing these words of Rāma, Satī was stunned. Remembering Śiva’s words and realising the truth of the same she felt ashamed.

## \|\| 3.24.52 \|\|

*rāmaṃ vijñāya viṣṇuṃ taṃ svarūpaṃ saṃvidhāya ca \|*  
*smṛtvā śivapadaṃ citte satyuvāca prasannadhīḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Realising Rāma to be Viṣṇu she re-assumed her own original form. Remembering Śiva’s feet in her heart Satī spoke delightedly:—

## \|\| 3.24.53 \|\|

*śivo mayā gaṇaiścaiva paryaṭan vasudhāṃ prabhuḥ \|*  
*ihāgacchacca vipine svataṃtraḥ parameśvaraḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Wandering over the earth along with me in the company of his attendants, the great lord Śiva came here in the forest.

## \|\| 3.24.54 \|\|

*apaśyadatra sa tvāṃ hi sītānveṣaṇatatparam \|*  
*salakṣmaṇaṃ virahiṇaṃ sītayā śliṣṭamānasam \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Here he saw you searching for Sītā in the company of Lakṣmaṇa. You were highly distressed on account of separation from Śītā.

## \|\| 3.24.55 \|\|

*natvā tvāṃ sa gato mūle vaṭasya sthita eva hi \|*  
*praśaṃsan mahimānaṃ te vaiṣṇavaṃ paramaṃ mudā \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. At the root of the Vaṭa he came and bowed to you glorifying your greatness with pleasure.

## \|\| 3.24.56 \|\|

*caturbhujaṃ hariṃ tvāṃ no dṛṣṭveva mudito'bhavat \|*  
*yathedaṃ rūpamamalaṃ paśyannānaṃdamāptavān \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. He was not so happy on seeing the four-armed Viṣṇu as on seeing this simple pure form of yours.

## \|\| 3.24.57 \|\|

*tacchrutvā vacanaṃ śaṃbhaurbhramamānīya cetasi \|*  
*tadājñayā parīkṣāṃ te kṛtavatya smi rāghava \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. O Rāma, on hearing those words of Śiva, my mind became suspicious and at his bidding I desired to test your divinity.

## \|\| 3.24.58 \|\|

*jñātaṃ me rāma viṣṇustvaṃ dṛṣṭā te prabhutā'khilā \|*  
*niḥsaśaṃyā tadāpi tacchṛṇu tvaṃ ca mahāmate \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. O Rāma, I have realised your Viṣṇuism. I have seen your over-all lordship. I am now free from doubts. But, still, O intelligent one, please listen to this.

## \|\| 3.24.59 \|\|

*kathaṃ praṇamyastvaṃ tasya satyaṃ brūhi mamāgrataḥ \|*  
*kuru nissaṃśayāṃ tvaṃ māṃ śamalaṃ prāpnuhi drutam \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. How is it that you became worthy of being saluted by him? Please tell me the truth. Make me free from doubt. Thus you shall be happy.

## \|\| 3.24.60 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya vacastasyā rāmaścotphullalocanaḥ \|*  
*asmaratsvaṃ prabhuṃ śaṃbhuṃ premābhūddhṛdi cādhikam \|\| 60 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

60\. On hearing her words Rāma became happy, his eyes shining with brilliance. He thought upon his lord Śiva. Emotions of love swelled in his heart.

## \|\| 3.24.61 \|\|

*satyā vinājñayā śaṃbhusamīpaṃ nāgamanmune \|*  
*saṃvarṇya mahimānaṃ ca prāvocadrāghavassatīm \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. O sage, without the specific permission of Śatī \[Satī?\] he did not go near Śiva. Describing his greatness Rāma spoke to Satī again.

## Chapter 25 - Separation of Satī and Śiva

## \|\| 3.25.1-2 \|\|

*rāma uvāca \|*  
*ekadā hi purā devi śaṃbhuḥ paramasūtikṛt \|*  
*viśvakarmāṇamāhūya svaloke parataḥ pare \|\| 1 \|\|*

*svadhenuśālāyāṃ ramyaṃ kārayāmāsa tena ca \|*  
*bhavanaṃ vistṛtaṃ samyak tatra siṃhāsanaṃ varam \|\| 2 \|\|*

Rāma said:—

1-2. O Goddess, formerly once, Śiva, the creator supreme, called Viśvakarman to His highest region. He made him erect a large hall of great beauty in His cowshed, and an exquisite throne there.

## \|\| 3.25.3 \|\|

*tatracchatraṃ mahādivyaṃ sarvadādbhuta muttamam \|*  
*kārayāmāsa vighnārthaṃ śaṃkaro viśvakarmaṇā \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Śiva, caused Viśvakarman to make an excellent, divine, wonderful umbrella for warding off obstacles.

## \|\| 3.25.4-5 \|\|

*śakrādīnāṃ juhāvāśu samastāndevatāgaṇān \|*  
*siddhagaṃdharvanāgānupade śāṃśca kṛtsnaśaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*devān sarvānāgamāṃśca vidhiṃ putrairmunīnapi \|*  
*devīḥ sarvā apsarobhirnānāvastusamanvitāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. He invited Indra and other gods, the Siddhas, Gandharvas, Nāgas, Upadeśas and Āgamas, Brahmā with his sons, the sages and the celestial goddesses and nymphs who came there with various articles.

## \|\| 3.25.6 \|\|

*devānāṃ ca tatharṣīṇāṃ siddhānāṃ phaṇināmapi \|*  
*ānayanmaṃgalakarāḥ kanyāḥ ṣoḍaśaṣoḍaśa \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Sixteen virgins each of devas, sages, Siddhas and serpents were brought for the auspicious ceremony.

## \|\| 3.25.7 \|\|

*vīṇāmṛdaṃgapramukhavādyānnānāvidhānmune \|*  
*utsavaṃ kārayāmāsa vādayitvā sugāyanaiḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. O sages, different musical instruments like lutes, tabours etc. were played and songs sung. Thus there was great pomp and ceremony.

## \|\| 3.25.8 \|\|

*rājābhiṣekayogyāni dravyāṇi sakalauṣadhaiḥ \|*  
*pratyakṣatīrthapāthobhiḥ paṃcakubhāṃśca pūritān \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Articles necessary for a coronation including herbs were brought. Five pots were filled with the sacred waters from all flowing holy rivers.

## \|\| 3.25.9 \|\|

*tathānyāssaṃvidhā divyā ānayatsvagaṇaistadā \|*  
*brahmaghoṣaṃ mahārāvaṃ kārayāmāsa śaṃkaraḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. All other divine arrangements were made by His attendants. Śiva caused them to recite Vedic mantras loudly.

## \|\| 3.25.10 \|\|

*atho hariṃ samāhūya vaikuṃṭhātprītamānasaḥ \|*  
*tadbhaktyā pūrṇayā devi modatisma maheśvaraḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. With a delightful mind He called Viṣṇu from Vaikuṇṭha. O Goddess, Śiva rejoiced at the perfect devotion of Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 3.25.11 \|\|

*sumuhūrte mahādevastatra siṃhāsane vare \|*  
*upaveśya hariṃ prītyā bhūṣayāmāsa sarvaśaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. In an auspicious hour, the great lord made Viṣṇu sit on the exquisite throne and delightedly decorated him in every way.

## \|\| 3.25.12 \|\|

*ābaddharamyamukuṭaṃ kṛtakautukamaṃgalam \|*  
*abhyaṣiṃcanmaheśastu svayaṃ brahmāṃḍamaṃḍape \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. A beautiful coronet was fixed on Viṣṇu and the auspicious holy thread was tied to his waist. He was then coronated by lord Śiva in the Cosmic Hall.

## \|\| 3.25.13 \|\|

*dattavānnikhilaiśvaryaṃ yannaijaṃ nānyagāmi yat \|*  
*tatastuṣṭāva taṃ śaṃbhussvataṃtro bhaktavatsalaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. What was His own and even non-transferable, Śiva the independent and favourably disposed to His devotees, conferred on Viṣṇu and eulogised him.

## \|\| 3.25.14 \|\|

*brahmāṇaṃ lokakartāramavocadvacanaṃ tvidam \|*  
*vyāpayansvaṃ varādhīnaṃ svataṃtraṃ bhaktavatsalaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The lord who is favourably disposed to His devotees, revealing Himself independent but subservient to the boons granted by Him, spoke these words to Brahmā the creator of all worlds.

## \|\| 3.25.15-16 \|\|

*maheśa uvāca \|*  
*ataḥ prabhṛti lokeśa mannideśādayaṃ hariḥ \|*  
*mama vaṃdya svayaṃ viṣṇurjātassarvaśśṛṇoti hi \|\| 15 \|\|*

*sarvairdevādibhistāta praṇamatvamamuṃ harim \|*  
*varṇayaṃtu hariṃ vedā mamaite māmivājñayā \|\| 16 \|\|*

Lord Śiva said:—

15-16. Lord, may you all hear. From now onwards, at my bidding, this Viṣṇu has become worthy of my respect and that of all devas. Dear one, you too bow to him. May all the Vedas extol him at my bidding as they extol me.

## \|\| 3.25.17 \|\|

*rāma uvāca \|*  
*ityuktvātha svayaṃ rudro'namadvai garuḍadhvajam \|*  
*viṣṇubhaktiprasannātmā varado bhaktavatsalaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

Rāma said:—

17\. So saying, Rudra, Himself bowed to Garuḍa-bannered Viṣṇu. The bestower of boons, He who is favourably disposed to His devotees, felt delighted by his devotion to Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 3.25.18 \|\|

*tato brahmādibhirdevaiḥ sarvarūpasuraistathā \|*  
*munisiddhādibhiścaivaṃ vaṃditobhūddharistadā \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Then Viṣṇu was duly revered by Brahmā followed by devas, sages, Siddhas and others.

## \|\| 3.25.19 \|\|

*tato maheśo harayeśaṃsaddiviṣadāṃ tadā \|*  
*mahāvarān suprasanno dhṛtavānbhaktavatsalaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Then the delighted Lord Śiva, favourably disposed towards his devotees, bestowed great boons on Viṣṇu and the other devas.

## \|\| 3.25.20 \|\|

*maheśa uvāca \|*  
*tvaṃ kartā sarvalokānāṃ bhartā hartā madājñayā \|*  
*dātā dharmārthakāmānāṃ śāstā durnayakāriṇām \|\| 20 \|\|*

Lord Śiva said:—

20\. At my bidding you are now the creator, sustainer and destroyer of all the worlds. You are the bestower of virtue, wealth and love and the chastiser of people of evil predilection.

## \|\| 3.25.21 \|\|

*jagadīśo jagatpūjyo mahābalaparākramaḥ \|*  
*ajeyastvaṃ raṇe kvāpi mamāpi hi bhaviṣyasi \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. You are the lord of the universe. You are worthy of the worship of the universe. You will be invincible in battle anywhere even against me. You will be endowed with great strength and valour.

## \|\| 3.25.22 \|\|

*śaktitrayaṃ gṛhāṇa tvamicchādi prāpitaṃ mayā \|*  
*nānālīlāprabhāvatvaṃ svataṃtratvaṃ bhavatraye \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. You take three Śaktis—will etc. conferred by me. You can have the power of exhibiting diverse sports and independence in the three worlds.

## \|\| 3.25.23 \|\|

*tvaddveṣṭāro hare nūnaṃ mayā śāsyāḥ prayatnataḥ \|*  
*tvadbhaktānāṃ mayā viṣṇo deyaṃ nirvāṇamuttamam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. O Viṣṇu, persons who hate you shall indeed be chastised and curbed by me with strenuous efforts. Salvation shall be given by me, O Viṣṇu, to your devotees.

## \|\| 3.25.24 \|\|

*māyāṃ cāpi gṛhāṇemāṃ duḥpraṇodyāṃ surādibhiḥ \|*  
*yayā saṃmohitaṃ viśvamacidrūpaṃ bhaviṣyati \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Accept this Māyā too which cannot be withstood by devas and others and by which the entire universe will be deluded and made insentient as it were.

## \|\| 3.25.25 \|\|

*mama bāhurmadīyastaṃ dakṣiṇo'sau vidhirhare \|*  
*asyāpi hi vidheḥ pātā janitāpi bhaviṣyasi \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. O Viṣṇu, you are my left hand, as Brahmā is my right hand. You shall be his progenitor and sustainer too.

## \|\| 3.25.26 \|\|

*hṛdayaṃ mama yo rudrassa evāhaṃ na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*pūjyastava sadā sopi brahmādīnāmapi dhruvam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Undoubtedly I myself am Rudra who is my heart. He is worthy of your respect as well as that of Brahmā and others too, of course.

## \|\| 3.25.27 \|\|

*atra sthitvā jagatsarvaṃ pālaya tvaṃ viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*nānāvatārabhedaiśca sadā nānoti kartṛbhiḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. While stationed here you protect the entire universe taking different incarnations and diverse ways of protection.

## \|\| 3.25.28 \|\|

*mama loke tavedaṃ va sthānaṃ ca paramarddhimat \|*  
*goloka iti vikhyātaṃ bhaviṣyati mahojjvalam \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. This place of great prosperity and glory in my own world shall be famous as Goloka. It will be very brilliant.

## \|\| 3.25.29 \|\|

*bhaviṣyaṃti hare ye te'vatārā bhuvi rakṣakāḥ \|*  
*madbhaktāstān dhruvaṃ drakṣye prītānatha nijādvarāta \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. O Viṣṇu, I shall certainly see the various incarnations of yours on the earth and shall be delighted by your devotion to me.

## \|\| 3.25.30 \|\|

*rāma uvāca \|*  
*akhaṃḍaiśvaryamāsādya hareritthaṃ harassvayam \|*  
*kailāse svagaṇaistasmin svairaṃ krīḍatyumāpatiḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

Rāma said:—

30\. After conferring thus unlimited prosperity on Viṣṇu, Śiva, the consort of Śivā, freely sported about at Kailāsa along with His attendants.

## \|\| 3.25.31 \|\|

*tadāprabhṛti lakṣmīśo gopaveṣobhavattathā \|*  
*ayāsīttatra suprītyā gopagopogavāṃ patiḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Thenceforth lord of Lakṣmī assumed the guise of a cowherd. The lord of cowherds, cowherdesses and the cows wandered there with pleasure.

## \|\| 3.25.32 \|\|

*sopi viṣṇuḥ prasannātmā jugopa nikhilaṃ jagat \|*  
*nānāvatārassaṃdhartā vanakartā śivājñayā \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. The delightful Viṣṇu protected the universe taking up various incarnations and sustaining it at the bidding of Siva.

## \|\| 3.25.33 \|\|

*idānīṃ sa caturddhātrāvātaracchaṃkarājñayā \|*  
*rāmohaṃ tatra bharato lakṣmaṇaśśatruheti ca \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Now He has taken a fourfold incarnation at the bidding of Śiva. I who am Rāma, and my brothers Bharata, Lakṣmaṇa and Śatrughna are His incarnations.

## \|\| 3.25.34 \|\|

*atha pitrājñayā devi sasītālakṣmaṇassati \|*  
*āgatohaṃ vane cādya duḥkhitau daivato 'bhavam \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. O Goddess Satī, at the bidding of my father I have come to the forest. Unfortunately I have fallen in deep distress.

## \|\| 3.25.35 \|\|

*niśācareṇa me jāyā hṛtā sīteti kenacit \|*  
*anveṣyāmi priyāṃ cātra virahī baṃdhunā vane \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. My wife Sītā has been abducted by a demon. I am now seeking my beloved, separated from her and devoid of my kinsmen.

## \|\| 3.25.36 \|\|

*darśanaṃ te yadi prāptaṃ sarvathā kuśalaṃ mama \|*  
*bhaviṣyati na saṃdeho mātaste kṛpayā sati \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. O mother Satī, since I have the good fortune of seeing you, there is no doubt that everything will be well with me by your favour.

## \|\| 3.25.37 \|\|

*sītāprāptivaro devi bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*taṃ hatvā duḥkhadaṃ pāpaṃ rākṣasaṃ tvadanugrahāt \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. By your blessings I shall have the fortune of acquiring Sītā after killing the demon of evil intention who is the cause of trouble.

## \|\| 3.25.38 \|\|

*mahadbhāgyaṃ mamādyaiva yadyakārṣṭāṃ kṛpāṃ yuvām \|*  
*yasmin sakaruṇau syātāṃ sa dhanyaḥ puruṣo varaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. It is my good fortune that both of you have taken pity on me. That man who is the object of your mercy is the best of blessed people.

## \|\| 3.25.39 \|\|

*itthamābhāṣya bahudhā supraṇamya satīṃ śivām \|*  
*tadājñayā vane tasmin vicacāra raghūdvahaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. After speaking thus and bowing in diverse ways to Satī, Rāma, the scion of the family of Raghu roamed in the forest with her permission.

## \|\| 3.25.40 \|\|

*athākarṇya satī vākyaṃ rāmasya prayatātmanaḥ \|*  
*hṛṣṭābhūtsā praśaṃsantī śivabhaktirataṃ hṛdi \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. On hearing these words of Rāma of pious rites, Satī was delighted. She praised him in her heart for his devotion to Śiva.

## \|\| 3.25.41 \|\|

*smṛtvā svakarma manasākārṣīcchokaṃ suvistaram \|*  
*pratyāgacchadudāsīnā vivarṇā śivasannidhau \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Remembering her own action she was much distressed. She returned to Śiva, pale in face and gloomy in spirit.

## \|\| 3.25.42 \|\|

*aciṃtayatpathi sā devī saṃcalaṃtī punaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*nāṃgīkṛtaṃ śivoktaṃ me rāmaṃ prati kudhīḥ kṛtā \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. While returning, the Goddess frequently mused—“I did not accept Śiva’s explanation. I entertained a senseless thought against Rāma.

## \|\| 3.25.43 \|\|

*kimuttaramahaṃ dāsye gatvā śaṃkarasannidhau \|*  
*iti saṃciṃtya bahudhā paścāttāpo'bhavattadā \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. After going to Śiva what reply shall I give?” Thinking thus, she began to repent in many ways.

## \|\| 3.25.44 \|\|

*gatvā śaṃbhusamīpaṃ ca praṇanāma śivaṃ hṛdā \|*  
*viṣaṇṇavadanā śokavyākulā vigataprabhā \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Approaching Śiva she mentally bowed to Him, with a pallid face and stricken with grief.

## \|\| 3.25.45 \|\|

*atha tāṃ duḥkhitāṃ dṛṣṭvā papraccha kuśalaṃ haraḥ \|*  
*provāca vacanaṃ prītyā tatparīkṣā kṛtā katham \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. On seeing her distressed, Śiva enquired of her health and asked—“O, have you finished your test”?

## \|\| 3.25.46 \|\|

*śrutvā śivavaco nāhaṃ kimapi praṇatānanā \|*  
*satī śokaviṣaṇṇā sā tasthau tatra samīpataḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. On hearing Śiva’s words she bent her head as a mark of respect but did not say anything. Agitated with grief she stood aghast.

## \|\| 3.25.47 \|\|

*atha dhyātvā maheśastu bubodha caritaṃ hṛdā \|*  
*dakṣajāyā mahāyogī nānālīlā viśāradaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. On meditating for a while, Śiva, the great Yogin, adept in diverse divine sports, could understand everything about Śatī, the daughter of Dakṣa.

## \|\| 3.25.48-49 \|\|

*sasmāra svapaṇaṃ pūrvaṃ yatkṛtaṃ harikopataḥ \|*  
*tatprārthitotha rudrosau maryādā pratipālakaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

*viṣādobhūtprabhostatra manasyevamuvāca ha \|*  
*dharmavaktā dharmakarttā dharmāvanakarassadā \|\| 49 \|\|*

48-49. He remembered the promise that He Himself had made on being requested by Viṣṇu when He was angry with the latter. Śiva who keeps the bounds of righteousness intact was distressed. The lord, the propounder, the activator and the protector of righteousness, thought within himself.

## \|\| 3.25.50 \|\|

*śiva uvāca \|*  
*kuryāṃ ceddakṣajāyāṃ hi snehaṃ pūrvaṃ yathā mahān \|*  
*naśyenmama paṇaḥ śuddho lokalīlānusāriṇaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. “If I were to maintain my love towards Satī at the level as before, my promise will be broken—even if I follow the conventions of the world”.

## \|\| 3.25.51 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*itthaṃ vicārya bahudhā hṛdā tāmatyajatsatīm \|*  
*paṇaṃ na nāśayāmāsa vedadharmaprapālakaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

51\. Thus pondering within himself in diverse ways He mentally discarded Satī but did not break his promise as the protector of Vedic Virtue.

## \|\| 3.25.52 \|\|

*tato vihāya manasā satīṃ tāṃ parameśvaraḥ \|*  
*jagāma svagiri bhedaṃ jagāvaddhā sa hi prabhuḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Then after forsaking Satī mentally, the lord returned to His abode. He did not at all reveal the promise.

## \|\| 3.25.53 \|\|

*calaṃtaṃ pathi taṃ vyomavāṇyuvāca maheśvaram \|*
