*sarvān saṃśrāvayan tatra dakṣajāṃ ca viśeṣataḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. While they were on their way, an unembodied speech rose in the sky telling Him within the hearing of everyone particularly of Satī, Dakṣa’s daughter.

## \|\| 3.25.54 \|\|

*vyomavāṇyuvāca \|*  
*dhanyastvaṃ parameśāna tvattsamodya tathā paṇaḥ \|*  
*na kopyanyastrilokesmin mahāyogī mahāprabhuḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

The celestial voice said:—

54\. O great Lord, you are blessed indeed. There is no other great Yogin or great lord in the three worlds, on a par with you. No one else can maintain that promise.

## \|\| 3.25.55 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*śrutvā vyomavaco devī śivaṃ papraccha viprabhā \|*  
*kaṃ paṇaṃ kṛtavānnātha brūhi me parameśvara \|\| 55 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

55\. On hearing the celestial voice, the goddess, utterly lustreless asked Śiva—“O lord, please tell me, what is the promise that you made?”

## \|\| 3.25.56 \|\|

*iti pṛṣṭopi giriśassatyā hitakaraḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*nodvāhe svapaṇaṃ tasyai kaharyagre'karotpurā \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Even when asked, the lord who was benevolent to Satī did not reveal the vow which he took in the presence of Viṣṇu formerly.

## \|\| 3.25.57 \|\|

*tadā satī śivaṃ dhyātvā svapatiṃ prāṇavallabham \|*  
*sarvaṃ bubodha hetuṃ taṃ priyatyāgamayaṃ mune \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Then O sage, meditating on Śiva, her own beloved husband, Satī understood the matter which meant the abandonment of her own self.

## \|\| 3.25.58 \|\|

*tato'tīva śuśocāśu budhvā sā tyāgamātmanaḥ \|*  
*śaṃbhunā dakṣajā tasmānniśvasaṃtī muhurmuhuḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. After realising the abandonment of herself by Him, the daughter of Dakṣa was grieved much and began to heave sighs frequently.

## \|\| 3.25.59 \|\|

*śivastasyāḥ samājñāya guptaṃ cakre manobhavam \|*  
*satye paṇaṃ svakīyaṃ hi kathā bahvīrvadanprabhuḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. But the lord Śiva kept the fact of His vow a secret from her and narrated many a tale to her.

## \|\| 3.25.60 \|\|

*satyā prāpa sa kailāsaṃ kathayan vividhāḥ kathā \|*  
*vare sthitvā nijaṃ rūpaṃ dadhau yogī samādhibhṛt \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Thus, narrating tales to her on the way He reached Kailāsa along with her. There Śiva, the Yogin, entered a trance and meditated upon His real form.

## \|\| 3.25.61 \|\|

*tatra tasthau satī dhāmni mahāviṣaṇṇamānasā \|*  
*na bubodha caritraṃ tatkaścicca śivayormune \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Satī stayed in the abode, overwhelmed by grief. But O sage, no one could guess the conduct of Śiva and Śivā.

## \|\| 3.25.62 \|\|

*mahānkālo vyatīyāya tayoritthaṃ mahāmune \|*  
*svopāttadehayoḥ prabhvorlokalīlānusāriṇoḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. O sage, great time elapsed even as the lord and the Goddess followed the conventions of the world through the physical bodies taken up by themselves.

## \|\| 3.25.63 \|\|

*dhyānaṃ tatyāja giriśastatassa paramārtihṛt \|*  
*tajjñātvā jagadaṃbā hi satī tatrājagāma sā \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Then Śiva the great enjoyer and protector stopped His meditation. On coming to know of it Satī, the mother of the universe, came there.

## \|\| 3.25.64 \|\|

*nanāmātha śivaṃ devī hṛdayena vidūyatā \|*  
*āsanaṃ dattavāñśaṃbhuḥ svasanmukha udāradhīḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. The Goddess bowed to Him with a moaning heart. The benevolent Śiva offered her a seat in front of Himself.

## \|\| 3.25.65 \|\|

*kathayāmāsa suprītyā kathā bahvīrmanoramāḥ \|*  
*niśśokā kṛtavānsadyo līlāṃ kṛtvā ca tādṛśīm \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. He narrated several interesting tales to her. By these divine sports He tried to entertain her and make her mind free from grief.

## \|\| 3.25.66 \|\|

*pūrvavatsā sukhaṃ lebhe tatyāja svapaṇaṃ na saḥ \|*  
*netyāścaryaṃ śive tāta maṃtavyaṃ parameśvare \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. She regained her previous happiness. He too did not forsake His vow. O dear, this need not be considered wonderful in the benign great lord Śiva.

## \|\| 3.25.67 \|\|

*itthaṃ śivāśivakathāṃ vadanti munayo mune \|*  
*kila kecidavidvāṃso viyogaśca kathaṃ tayoḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. But O sage, some ignorant Pandits thus narrate the story of Śivā and Śiva and their separation. But how can there be a real separation between the two?

## \|\| 3.25.68 \|\|

*śivāśivacaritraṃ ko jānāti paramārthataḥ \|*  
*svecchayā krīḍatasto hi caritaṃ kurutassadā \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Who knows the true life and conduct of Śivā and Śiva. They sport about of their own accord and make their own lives for ever.

## \|\| 3.25.69 \|\|

*vāgarthāviva saṃpṛktau sadā khalu satīśivau \|*  
*tayorviyogassaṃbhāvyassaṃbhavedicchayā tayoḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. Śatī and Śiva are united together like words and their meanings. Only if they wish, can their separation be even imagined.

## Chapter 26 - The cause of estrangement between Dakṣa and Śiva

## \|\| 3.26.1 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*purābhavacca sarveṣāmadhvaro vidhinā mahān \|*  
*prayāge samavetānāṃ munīnāṃ ca mahā tmanām \|\| 1 \|\|*

Brahmā said:

1\. Formerly, a great sacrifice was performed by the sages and noble souls who assembled at Prayāga.

## \|\| 3.26.2 \|\|

*tatra siddhāssamāyātāssanakādyāssurarṣayaḥ \|*  
*saprajāpatayo devā jñānino brahmadarśinaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Siddhas, Sanaka and others, the celestial sages, devas with Prajāpatis and men of perfect knowledge who had realised the Brahman attended the function.

## \|\| 3.26.3 \|\|

*ahaṃ samāgatastatra parivārasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*nigamairāgamairyukto mūrtimadbhirmahāprabhaiḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. I too attended the same along with my followers. All the Āgamas and Nigamas in brilliant embodied forms were present with me.

## \|\| 3.26.4 \|\|

*samājobhūdvicitro hi teṣāmutsavasaṃyuḥ \|*  
*jñānavādo'bhavattatra nānāśāstrasa mudbhavaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The assembly was variegated and of diverse character. They conducted discussions on epistemology from different sacred texts with great festivities.

## \|\| 3.26.5 \|\|

*tasminnavasare rudrassabhavānīgaṇaḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*trilokahitakṛtsvāmī tatrāgātsūktikṛnmune \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. O sage, in the meantime, lord Śiva, accompanied by His attendants and Satī came there, the lord conferring benefit on the three worlds and affording them protection.

## \|\| 3.26.6 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā śivaṃ surāssarve siddhāśca munayastathā \|*  
*anamaṃstaṃ prabhuṃ bhaktyā tuṣṭuvuśca tathā hyaham \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. On seeing the lord, devas, Siddhas and sages bowed to and eulogised Him with great devotion. I too joined them.

## \|\| 3.26.7 \|\|

*tasthuśśivājñayā sarve yathāsthānaṃ mudānvitāḥ \|*  
*prabhudarśanasaṃtuṣṭāḥ varṇayanto nijaṃ vidhim \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. At the bidding of Śiva they sat in their respective places. They were excessively delighted on seeing the lord. They explained to Him the various activities they were engaged in.

## \|\| 3.26.8 \|\|

*tasminnavasare dakṣaḥ prajāpatipatiḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*āgamattatra suprītassuvarcasvī yadṛcchayā \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. In the meantime, the lord Dakṣa, the lord of Prajāpatis, came there delighted by shedding lustre everywhere in the course of a casual visit.

## \|\| 3.26.9 \|\|

*māṃ praṇamya sa dakṣo hi nyuṣṭastatra madājñayā \|*  
*brahmāṇḍādhipatirmānyo mānī tattvabahirmukhaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. After saluting me, Dakṣa sat there with my consent. Dakṣa, the lord of the universe, was a bit arrogant though worthy of honour, as he had no deep insight into Reality.

## \|\| 3.26.10 \|\|

*stutibhiḥ praṇipātaiśca dakṣassarvaissurarṣibhiḥ \|*  
*pūjito varatejasvī karau badhvā vinamrakaiḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Dakṣa, of great splendour was honoured by the humble celestial sages with laudatory songs, obeisance, and the joining of palms in great reverence.

## \|\| 3.26.11 \|\|

*nānāvihārakṛnnāthassvataṃtra paramotikṛt \|*  
*nānāmattaṃ tadā dakṣaṃ svāsanastho maheśvaraḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. But lord Śiva who indulges in diverse sports, sat firmly and did not bow to Him. Naturally the lord who is the cause of protection is independent.

## \|\| 3.26.12 \|\|

*dṛṣṭā'nataṃ haraṃ tatra sa me putro'prasannadhīḥ \|*  
*akupatsahasā rudre tadā dakṣaḥ prajāpatiḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Seeing Śiva not bowing to him, my son became displeased. Dakṣa, the patriarch, was furious with Śiva.

## \|\| 3.26.13 \|\|

*krūradṛṣṭyā mahāgarvo dṛṣṭvā rudraṃ mahāprabhum \|*  
*sarvānsaṃśrāvayannuccairavocajjñānavarjitaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Haughty and devoid of perfect knowledge, Dakṣa looked cruelly at Śiva and spoke aloud within the hearing of all present.

## \|\| 3.26.14 \|\|

*ete hi sarve ca surāsurā bhṛśaṃ namaṃti māṃ vipravarāstatharṣayaḥ \|*  
*kathaṃ hyasau durjanavanmahāmanāstvabhūttu yaḥ pretapiśācasaṃvṛtaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

Dakṣa said:—

14\. “All these Suras and Asuras, brahmins and sages bow to me. How is it that this gentleman who is always surrounded by goblins and ghosts behaves like a wicked man?

## \|\| 3.26.15 \|\|

*śmaśānavāsī nirapatrapo hyayaṃ kathaṃ praṇāmaṃ na karoti me'dhunā \|*  
*luptakriyo bhūtapiśācasevito matto'vidho nītividūṣakassadā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. “How is it that this shameless frequenter of cremation grounds does not bow to me now? He is devoid of rites. He has cast off religious practices. He is surrounded by spirits and ghosts. He is elated and he spoils good policies and conventions.

## \|\| 3.26.16 \|\|

*pākhaṃḍino durjanapāpa śīlā dṛṣṭvā dvijaṃ proddhataniṃdakāśca \|*  
*vadhvāṃ sadāsaktaratipravīṇastasmādamuṃ śaptumahaṃ pravṛttaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Heretics, wicked persons, who behave arrogantly on seeing a brahmin and despise him are on a par with one another. Besides, this person is always engrossed in the love of his wife. Hence I am going to curse him”.

## \|\| 3.26.17 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityevamuktvā sa mahākhalastadā ruṣānvito rudramidaṃ hyavocat \|*  
*śṛṇvaṃtvamī vipravarāstathā surā vadhyaṃ hi me cārhatha kartumetam \|\| 17 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

17\. After saying thus the furious rogue spoke to Śiva thus.

## \|\| 3.26.18 \|\|

*dakṣa uvāca \|*  
*rudro hyayaṃ yajñabahiṣkṛto me varṇeṣvatītotha vivarṇarūpaḥ \|*  
*devairna bhāgaṃ labhatāṃ sahaiva śmaśānavāsī kulajanma hīnaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

Dakṣa said:—

May all these brahmins and devas listen. May all of you deem him worthy of being killed by me.

18\. Let not this Śiva, a resident of cremation grounds, lacking in nobility of birth and pedigree, expelled by me from sacrifices, an outcaste and ugly-shaped, obtain his share along with the devas”.

## \|\| 3.26.19-20 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*iti dakṣoktamākarṇya bhṛgvādyā bahavo janāḥ \|*  
*agarhayan duṣṭasattvaṃ rudraṃ mattvāmaraissamam \|\| 19 \|\|*

*nandī niśamya tadvākyaṃ lālākṣotiruṣānvitaḥ \|*  
*abravīttvaritaṃ dakṣaṃ śāpaṃ dātumanā gaṇaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

19-20. On hearing these words of Dakṣa, Bhṛgu and others reproached Śiva. After duly saluting Śiva along with the devas, Nandin, the attendant of Śiva who had heard the words of Dakṣa, was very furious and rolled his eyes. With an intention to curse him, he immediately spoke to Dakṣa.

## \|\| 3.26.21 \|\|

*nandīśvara uvāca \|*  
*rere śaṭha mahā mūḍha dakṣa duṣṭamate tvayā \|*  
*yajñabāhyo hi me svāmī maheśo hi kṛtaḥ katham \|\| 21 \|\|*

Nandīśvara said:—

21\. “O foolish Dakṣa, of roguish and wicked intention, how is it that you have expelled my lord Śiva from sacrifice?

## \|\| 3.26.22 \|\|

*yasya smaraṇamātreṇa bhavaṃti saphalā makhāḥ \|*  
*tīrthāni ca pavitrāṇi soyaṃ śapto haraḥ katham \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. How is it that you cursed him whose thought makes all sacrifices fruitful and all sacred places holy?

## \|\| 3.26.23 \|\|

*vṛthā te brahmacāpalyācchaptoyaṃ dakṣa durmate \|*  
*vṛthopahasitaścaivāduṣṭo rudro mahā prabhuḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. O Dakṣa, of wicked intentions, in vain did you curse him by your inconsiderate rashness as a brahmin. The great lord Śiva who is free from defects, has in vain been ridiculed by you.

## \|\| 3.26.24 \|\|

*yenedaṃ pālyate viśvaṃ sṛṣṭamaṃte vināśitam \|*  
*śaptoyaṃ sa kathaṃ rudro maheśo brāhmaṇādhama \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. O vile brahmin, how is it that you cursed Śiva the great lord, by whom this universe is created, sustained and destroyed in the end?”

## \|\| 3.26.25 \|\|

*evaṃ nirbhatsitastena nandinā hi prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*nandinaṃ ca śaśāpātha dakṣo roṣasamanvitaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Censured and rebuked thus by Nandin, Dakṣa the patriarch who was still furious cursed Nandin too.

## \|\| 3.26.26 \|\|

*dakṣa uvāca \|*  
*yūyaṃ sarve rudragaṇā vedabāhyā bhavaṃtu vai \|*  
*vedamārgaparityaktāstathā tyaktā maharṣibhiḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

Dakṣa said:—

26\. “You all, the attendants of Śiva, are expelled from Vedic rites. You will be abandoned by the followers of the Vedic path as well as by great sages.

## \|\| 3.26.27 \|\|

*pākhaṃḍavādaniratāḥ śiṣṭācārabahiṣkṛtāḥ \|*  
*madirāpānaniratā jaṭā bhasmāsthidhāriṇaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. “You all will be confirmed heretics, out of the conventions of society. You will indulge in drinking wine. Matted hair, ashes and bones will be your embellishments”.

## \|\| 3.26.28 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*iti śaptāstathā tena dakṣeṇa śivakiṃkarāḥ \|*  
*tacchrutvātiruṣāviṣṭobhavannaṃdī śivapriyaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

28\. Thus Śiva’s attendants were cursed by Dakṣa. On hearing that, Nandin the favourite of Śiva became furious.

## \|\| 3.26.29 \|\|

*pratyuvāca drutaṃ pakṣaṃ garvitaṃ taṃ mahākhalam \|*  
*śilādatanayo naṃdī tejasvī śivavallabhaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Nandin, the brilliant son of Śilāda and favourite of Śiva, spoke immediately to Dakṣa who was excessively roguish and haughty.

## \|\| 3.26.30 \|\|

*nandīśvara uvāca \|*  
*re dakṣa śaṭha durbuddhe vṛthaiva śivakiṃkarāḥ \|*  
*śaptāste brahmacāpalyācchivatattvamajānatā \|\| 30 \|\|*

Nandīśvara said:—

30\. O roguish wicked Dakṣa, in vain did you curse Śiva’s attendants, you who do not know Śiva’s principles. You have exercised your indiscreet rashness on being a brahmin.

## \|\| 3.26.31 \|\|

*bhṛgvādyairduṣṭacittaiśca mūḍhaissa upahāsitaḥ \|*  
*mahā prabhurmaheśāno brāhmaṇatvādahaṃmate \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. The great lord Śiva is ridiculed by the evil-minded fools Bhṛgu and others apparently due to their egotism in being brahmins.

## \|\| 3.26.32 \|\|

*ye rudravimukhāścātra brāhmaṇāstvādṛśāḥ khalāḥ \|*  
*rudratejaḥprabhāvatvātteṣāṃ śāpaṃ dadāmyaham \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. With the power of Śiva (backing me) I now heap curses on these brahmins here who are against Śiva and hence wicked like you.

## \|\| 3.26.33 \|\|

*vedavādaratā yūyaṃ vedatattvabahirmukhāḥ \|*  
*bhavaṃtu satataṃ viprā nānyadastīti vādinaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. You are engaged in discussing Vedas but you will be ignorant of Vedic principles. May these brahmins prattle that there is nothing else.

## \|\| 3.26.34 \|\|

*kāmātmānarssvargaparāḥ krodhalobhamadānvitāḥ \|*  
*bhavaṃtu satataṃ viprā bhikṣukā nirapatrapāḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. May these brahmins indulging in lust, heavenly pleasures, anger, covetousness and pride be shameless beggars.

## \|\| 3.26.35 \|\|

*vedamārgaṃ puraskṛtya brāhmaṇāśśūdrayājinaḥ \|*  
*daridrā vai bhaviṣyaṃti pratigraharatā ssadā \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. These brahmins will be officiating in the sacrifices of Śūdras, following the Vedic path. They will be perpetually poor and eager to receive monetary gifts.

## \|\| 3.26.36 \|\|

*asatpratigrahāścaiva sarve nirayagāminaḥ \|*  
*bhaviṣyaṃti sadā dakṣa kecidvai brahmarākṣasāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Due to their acceptance of monetary gifts from undeserving persons they will fall into hell. O Dakṣa, some of them will become brahminical Rākṣasas.

## \|\| 3.26.37 \|\|

*yaśśivaṃ surasāmānyamuddiśya parameśvaram \|*  
*druhyatyajo duṣṭamatistattvato vimukho bhavet \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Brahmā who rivals with Lord Śiva, considering him on a par with ordinary devas and who has evil intentions too, will become averse to the true principles of Śaiva cult.

## \|\| 3.26.38-39 \|\|

*kūṭadharmeṣu geheṣu sadā grāmyasukhecchayā \|*  
*karmataṃtraṃ vitanutā vedavādaṃ ca śāśvatam \|\| 38 \|\|*

*vinaṣṭānaṃdakamukho vismṛtātmagatiḥ paśuḥ \|*  
*bhraṣṭakarmānayasadā dakṣo bastamukho'cirāt \|\| 39 \|\|*

38-39. Dakṣa will become goat-faced ere long. He will be indulging in vulgar worldly lustful pleasures, and evil strategies. He will be laying down rules for rituals and perpetually discussing Vedic passages. His bright pleasing face will disappear. He will become individual soul strayed from his ultimate goal. He will fall from his holy rites and indulge in wicked deeds.

## \|\| 3.26.40 \|\|

*śaptāste kopinā tatra naṃdinā brāhmaṇā yadā \|*  
*hāhākāro mahānāsīcchapto dakṣeṇa ceśvaraḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. When the brahmins were cursed by the furious Nandin and Śiva was cursed by Dakṣa there was a great hue and cry.

## \|\| 3.26.41 \|\|

*tadākarṇyāmahatyaṃtamaniṃdaṃtaṃ muhurmuhuḥ \|*  
*bhṛgvādīnapi viprāṃśca vedasṛṭ śiva tattvavit \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. On hearing that, I, the creator of the Vedas and the knower of the principles of Śiva rebuked him frequently and also the brahmins Bhṛgu and others.

## \|\| 3.26.42 \|\|

*īśvaropi vacaḥ śrutvā naṃdinaḥ prahasanniva \|*  
*uvāca madhuraṃ vākyaṃ bodhayaṃstaṃ sadāśivaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. On hearing the words of Nandin, the lord Sadāsiva laughed and spoke sweetly to him enlightening him further.

## \|\| 3.26.43 \|\|

*sadāśiva uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu naṃdin mahāprājña na kartuṃ krodhamarhasi \|*  
*vṛthā śapto brahmakulo matvā śaptaṃ ca māṃ bhramāt \|\| 43 \|\|*

Sadāśiva said:—

43\. “O Nandin of great intellect, listen. Do not get angry. You have cursed the brahmins in vain, erroneously thinking that I have been cursed.

## \|\| 3.26.44 \|\|

*vedo maṃtrākṣaramayassākṣātsūktamayo bhṛśam \|*  
*sūkte pratiṣṭhito hyātmā sarveṣāmapi dehinām \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Vedas are in the form of syllables of verses and hymns. The Self is established in the Sūkta, whomsoever it may belong to.

## \|\| 3.26.45 \|\|

*tasmādātmavido nityaṃ tvaṃ mā śapa ruṣānvitaḥ \|*  
*śapyā na vedāḥ kenāpi durddhiyāpi kadācana \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Hence do not angrily curse the knowers of the Self. The Vedas shall not be cursed by anyone, not even by the evil-minded.

## \|\| 3.26.46 \|\|

*ahaṃ śapto na cedānīṃ tattvato boddhumarhasi \|*  
*śānto bhava mahādhīmansanakādivibodhakaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. I have not been cursed now. You please understand the factual position. O intelligent one, be calm, enlighten Sanaka and others.

## \|\| 3.26.47 \|\|

*yajñohaṃ yajñakarmāhaṃ yajñāṃgāni ca sarvaśaḥ \|*  
*yatātmā yajñanirato yajñabāhyohameva vai \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. I am the sacrifice, the sacrificial rite, the ancillary adjuncts of the sacrifice, the Self of sacrifice and one engrossed in sacrifice. I am out of sacrifice too.

## \|\| 3.26.48 \|\|

*koyaṃ kastvamime ke hi sarvohamapi tattvataḥ \|*  
*iti buddhyā hi vimṛśa vṛthā śaptāstvayā dvijāḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Who is this? Who are you? Who are these? In reality I am all. Consider everything in this light. In vain did you curse the brahmins.

## \|\| 3.26.49 \|\|

*tattvajñānena nirhṛtya prapaṃcaracano bhava \|*  
*budhassvastho mahābuddhe nandin krodhādivarjitaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Extracting the fundamental basis of the construction of the universe through the knowledge of reality, be enlightened and self-assured, O intelligent one. Be free from anger and other emotions”.

## \|\| 3.26.50 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*evaṃ prabodhitastena śambhunā nandikeśvaraḥ \|*  
*vivekaparamo bhūtvā śāṃto'bhūtkrodhavarjitaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

50\. Thus exhorted by Śiva, Nandikeśvara became calm and free from anger and took up discrimination as the ultimate aim.

## \|\| 3.26.51 \|\|

*śivopi taṃ prabodhyāśu svagaṇaṃ prāṇavallabham \|*  
*sagaṇassa yayau tasmātsvasthānaṃ pramudānvitaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. After enlightening him and also his favourite Gaṇas, Śiva returned to His abode accompanied by his Gaṇas with great delight.

## \|\| 3.26.52 \|\|

*dakṣopi sa ruṣāviṣṭastairddhijaiḥ parivāritaḥ \|*  
*svasthānaṃ ca yayau citte śivadro haparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Seething with fury and malice against Śiva, Dakṣa went to his abode along with the brahmins.

## \|\| 3.26.53 \|\|

*rudraṃ tadānīṃ pariśapyamānaṃ saṃsmṛtya dakṣaḥ parayā ruṣānvitaḥ \|*  
*śraddhāṃ vihāyaiva sa mūḍhabuddhirniṃdāparobhūcchivapūjakānām \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Remembering the situation in which Śiva had been cursed and still furious against him, Dakṣa of confounded intellect forsook his faith and entertained enmity and disgust against the worshippers of Śiva.

## \|\| 3.26.54 \|\|

*ityukto dakṣadurbuddhiśśaṃbhunā paramātmanā \|*  
*parāṃ durdhiṣaṇāṃ tasya śṛṇu tāta vadāmyaham \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Thus I have narrated the crooked intellect of Dakṣa in regard to Śiva the great Self. O dear one, hear about his evil intention and thought. I shall tell you further.

## Chapter 27 - The inauguration of Dakṣa’s sacrifice

## \|\| 3.27.1-2 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*ekadā tu mune tena yajñaḥ prāraṃbhito mahān \|*  
*tatrāhūtāstadā sarve dīkṣitena surarṣayaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*maharṣayo'khilāstatra nirjarāśca samāgatāḥ \|*  
*yadyajñakaraṇārthaṃ hi śivamāyāvimohitaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

1-2. Once a great sacrifice was started by Dakṣa, O sage. To partake in that sacrifice, the celestial and terrestrial sages and devas were invited by Śiva and they reached the place being deluded by Śiva’s Māyā.

## \|\| 3.27.3-5 \|\|

*agastyaḥ kaśyapotriśca vāmadevastathā bhṛguḥ \|*  
*dadhīcirbhagavān vyāso bhāradvājo'tha gautamaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*pailaḥ parāśaro gargo bhārgavaḥ kakupassitaḥ \|*  
*sumaṃtutrikakaṃkāśca vaiśaṃpāyana eva ca \|\| 4 \|\|*

*ete cānye ca bahavo munayo harṣitā yayu \|*  
*mama putrasya dakṣasya sadārāssasutā makham \|\| 5 \|\|*

3-5. Agastya, Kaśyapa, Atri, Vāmadeva, Bhṛgu, Dadhīci, the revered Vyāsa, Bharadvāja, Gautama, Paila, Parāśara, Garga, Bhārgava, Kakubha, Sita, Sumantu, Trika, Kaṅka, Vaiśampāyana and many others along with their sons and wives arrived at the sacrifice of Dakṣa—my son.

## \|\| 3.27.6 \|\|

*tathā sarve suragaṇā lokapālā mahodayāḥ \|*  
*tathopanirjarāssarve svāpakārabalānvitāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. All the devas, the guardians of the quarters of rising fortune, the subordinate devas with their offers of help and service attended the sacrifice.

## \|\| 3.27.7 \|\|

*satyalokātsamānīto nutohaṃ viśvakārakaḥ \|*  
*sasutassa parīvāro mūrtavedāpisaṃyutaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. From Satyaloka, I, the creator of the universe, was duly lauded and taken there along with my sons, followers and the embodied forms of the Vedas etc.

## \|\| 3.27.8 \|\|

*vaikuṃṭhācca tathā viṣṇussaṃprārthya vividhādarāt \|*  
*sapārṣadaparīvārassamānīto makhaṃ prati \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Viṣṇu was duly requested, respected and brought to the place of sacrifice from Vaikuṇṭha along with his aide-decamp and followers.

## \|\| 3.27.9 \|\|

*evamanye samāyātā dakṣayajñaṃ vimohitāḥ \|*  
*satkṛtāstena dakṣena sarve te hi durātmanā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Similarly others too, equally deluded, came to the sacrifice. Then Dakṣa who was ill disposed towards Śiva received them hospitably.

## \|\| 3.27.10 \|\|

*bhavanāni mahārhāṇi suprabhāṇi mahāṃti ca \|*  
*tvaṣṭrā kṛtāni divyāni tebhyo dattāni tena vai \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Large divine mansions of great value and brilliant lustre were erected by Tvaṣṭṛ and assigned to them by Dakṣa.

## \|\| 3.27.11 \|\|

*teṣu sarveṣu dhiṣṇyeṣu yathāyogyaṃ ca saṃsthitāḥ \|*  
*sanmānitā arājaṃste sakalā viṣṇunā mayā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. In all those places they stationed themselves in a befitting manner after being duly honoured. They shone along with Viṣṇu and me.

## \|\| 3.27.12 \|\|

*varttamāne mahāyajñe tīrthe kanakhale tadā \|*  
*ṛtvijaśca kṛtāstena bhṛgvādyāśca tapodhanāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. In that sacrifice that was being performed in that holy place of Kanakhala, Bhṛgu and other sages were made Ṛtviks by him (Dakṣa).

## \|\| 3.27.13 \|\|

*adhiṣṭhātā svayaṃ viṣṇussaha sarvamarudgaṇaiḥ \|*  
*ahaṃ tatrā'bhavaṃ brahmā trayīvidhinidarśakaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Viṣṇu himself was the presiding officer along with the Maruts. I was the Brahmā (a special officiating deity) the director and guide for Vedic rituals.

## \|\| 3.27.14 \|\|

*tathaiva sarvadikpālā dvārapālāśca rakṣakāḥ \|*  
*sāyudhāssaparīvārāḥ kutūhalakarāssadā \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The guardians of the quarters became the gatekeepers and watchmen. They were well-equipped in arms and had many attendants to assist them. They were very enthusiastic.

## \|\| 3.27.15 \|\|

*upatasthe svayaṃ yajñassurūpastasya cādhvare \|*  
*sarve mahāmuniśreṣṭhāḥ svayaṃ vedadharā'bhavan \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. In that altar, sacrifice itself was present in its beautiful embodied form. The excellent sages became the holders of the Vedas.

## \|\| 3.27.16 \|\|

*tanūnapādapi nijaṃ cakre rūpaṃ sahasraśaḥ \|*  
*haviṣā grahaṇāyāśu tasmin yajñe mahotsave \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The sacrificial fire evinced its diverse forms in a thousand ways, during the sacrificial festivities, in order to receive the sacrificial offerings of Dakṣa.

## \|\| 3.27.17-18 \|\|

*aṣṭāśītisahasrāṇi juhvati saha ṛtvijaḥ \|*  
*udgātāraścatuṣaṣṭi sahasrāṇi surarṣayaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*adhvaryavotha hotārastāvanto nāradādayaḥ \|*  
*saptarṣayassamā gāthāḥ kurvaṃti sma pṛthakpṛthak \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. There were eighty-six thousand Ṛtviks\[4\] in the performance of the sacrifice and sixty-four thousand Udgātṛs. The celestial sages Nārada and others acted as Adhvaryus and Hotṛs. They too were as many. The seven sages (jointly and) severally repeated the Sāman hymns.

## \|\| 3.27.19 \|\|

*gaṃdharvavidyādharasiddhasaṃghānādityasaṃghān sagaṇān sayajñān \|*  
*saṃkhyāvarānnāgacarān samastān vavre sa dakṣo hi mahādhvare sve \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. In his great sacrifice Dakṣa extended his invitation to Gandharvas, Vidyādharas, Siddhas, Ādityas, all the innumerable Nāgas along with their followers and sacrificial ritualists.

## \|\| 3.27.20 \|\|

*dvijarṣirājarṣisurarṣisaṃghā nṛpāssamitrāḥ sacivāssa sainyāḥ \|*  
*vasupramukhyā gaṇadevatāśca sarve vṛtāstena makhopavettrāḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Brahminical, Royal and celestial sages, kings, with their friends, ministers, armies etc, Vasus and other chief Gaṇadevatas—all of them were invited by him in the sacrifice.

## \|\| 3.27.21 \|\|

*dīkṣāyuktastadā dakṣaḥ kṛtakautukamaṃgalaḥ \|*  
*bhāryayā sahito reje kṛtasvastyayano bhṛśam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. With the proper initiation, tying of the holy thread round his wrist and Svastyayana rites duly performed, Dakṣa along with his wife, shone well.

## \|\| 3.27.22 \|\|

*tasmin yajñe vṛtaśśaṃbhurna dakṣeṇa durātmanā \|*  
*kapālīti viniścitya tasya yajñārhatā na hi \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Dakṣa, the evil-minded, did not invite Śiva for that sacrifice, deciding that He was not worthy of taking part in the sacrifice because He was a Kapālin.

## \|\| 3.27.23 \|\|

*kapālibhāryeti satī dayitā svasutāpi ca \|*  
*nāhūtā yajñaviṣaye dakṣeṇāguṇadarśinā \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. In view of the fact that Satī was the wife of Kapālin, she was not invited, though she was his beloved daughter, by Dakṣa who was blind to her qualities.

## \|\| 3.27.24 \|\|

*evaṃ pravartamāne hi dakṣayajñe mahotsave \|*  
*svakāryalagnāstatrāsan sarve te'dhvarasaṃmatāḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. While the great festivities in the sacrifice of Dakṣa were being celebrated those who had assembled for the same were engrossed in their respective activities.

## \|\| 3.27.25 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare'dṛṣṭvā tatra vai śaṃkaraṃ prabhum \|*  
*prodvignamānasaśśaivo dadhīco vākyamabravīt \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. In the meantime, Dadhīci a devotee of Śiva, realising that lord Śiva was not there became dispirited and spoke thus.

## \|\| 3.27.26 \|\|

*dadhīca uvāca \|*  
*sarve śṛṇuta madvākyaṃ devarṣipramukhā mudā \|*  
*kasmānnaivāgataśśaṃbhurasmin yajñe mahotsave \|\| 26 \|\|*

Dadhīci said:—

26\. O ye all! celestial sages and others, pay heed to my words. Why has not Śiva taken part in the festivities of this sacrifice?

## \|\| 3.27.27 \|\|

*ete sureśā munayo mahattarāssalokapālāśca samāgatā hi \|*  
*tathāpi yajñastu na śobhate bhṛśaṃ pinākinā tena mahātmanā vinā \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Of course, the chiefs of devas, the great sages and the guardians of the quarters have all come. Yet the sacrifice cannot be perfect and complete without the noble-souled, trident-holder Śiva.

## \|\| 3.27.28 \|\|

*yenaiva sarvāṇyapi maṃgalāni bhavaṃti śaṃsanti mahāvipaścitaḥ \|*  
*so'sau na dṛṣṭo'tra pumān purāṇo vṛṣadhvajo nīlagalaḥ pareśaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. The bull-bannered, blue-necked eternal Puruṣa the great Īśa is not seen here. Great scholars have affirmed, that all auspicious results happen due to Him alone.

## \|\| 3.27.29 \|\|

*amaṃgalānyeva ca maṃgalāni bhavaṃti yenādhigatāni dakṣaḥ \|*  
*tripaṃcakenāpyatha maṃgalāni bhavaṃti sadyaḥ parataḥ purāṇi \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. O Dakṣa, if accepted by Triyambaka all inauspicious things become auspicious and fresh auspicious things take shape which will be greater than the greatest in a trice.

## \|\| 3.27.30 \|\|

*tasmāttvayaiva kartavyamāhvānaṃ parameśituḥ \|*  
*tvaritaṃ brahmaṇā vāpi viṣṇunā prabhuviṣṇunā \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Hence the invitation to the great Śiva shall be extended by you yourself immediately or by Brahmā or by Viṣṇu the lord.

## \|\| 3.27.31 \|\|

*indreṇa lokapālaiśca dvijaissiddhaissahādhunā \|*  
*sarvathā''nayanīyosau śaṃkaro yajñapūrttaye \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. By all means Śiva shall be brought here by you along with Indra, the guardians of the quarters, the brahmins and the Siddhas in order to make the sacrifice complete and perfect.

## \|\| 3.27.32 \|\|

*sarvairbhavadbhirgaṃtavyaṃ yatra devo maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*dākṣāyaṇyā samaṃ śambhumānayadhvaṃ tvarānvitāḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. All of you shall go where He is stationed. Immediately bring Śiva along with Satī.

## \|\| 3.27.33 \|\|

*tena sarvaṃ pavitraṃ syācchambhunā paramātmanā \|*  
*atrāgatena deveśāssāṃbena paramātmanā \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. O lords of Devas, everything shall be sanctified through Śiva, the supreme Self. If the consort of Śivā, the great Being, comes here, everything will be all right.

## \|\| 3.27.34 \|\|

*yasya smṛtyā ca nāmoktyā samagraṃ sukṛtaṃ bhavet \|*  
*tasmātsarvaprayatnena hyānetavyo vṛṣadhvajaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Since all merits accrue from thinking upon Him and repeating His names, the bull-bannered deity shall be brought with all efforts.

## \|\| 3.27.35 \|\|

*samāgate śaṃkare'tra pāvano hi bhavenmakhaḥ \|*  
*bhaviṣyatyanyathā'pūrṇaḥ satyametadbravīmyaham \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. If Śiva comes here, the sacrifice will become sanctified, or it will remain incomplete and imperfect. I am telling you the truth.

## \|\| 3.27.36 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā dakṣo roṣasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*uvāca tvaritaṃ mūḍhaḥ prahasanniva duṣṭadhīḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. On hearing his words, the foolish and evil-minded Dakṣa became furious in a trice and said mockingly.

## \|\| 3.27.37 \|\|

*mūlaṃ viṣṇurdevatānāṃ yatra dharmassanātanaḥ \|*  
*samānīto mayā samyak kimūnaṃ yajñakarmaṇi \|\| 37 \|\|*

Dakṣa said:—

37\. Viṣṇu who is the prime cause of all deities and in whom the eternal virtue resides has been invoked here by me. What is it that the sacrificial rite lacks in?

## \|\| 3.27.38 \|\|

*yasminvedāśca yajñāśca karmāṇi vividhāni ca \|*  
*pratiṣṭhitāni sarvāṇi so'sau viṣṇurihāgataḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Viṣṇu in whom all the Vedas, sacrifices and the different rites are founded has graced this place by his presence.

## \|\| 3.27.39 \|\|

*satyalokātsamāyāto brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ \|*  
*vedaissopaniṣadbhiśca vividhairāgamaissaha \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Brahmā, the grandfather of the worlds, has come here from Satyaloka along with the Vedas, Upaniṣads and the Āgamas.

## \|\| 3.27.40 \|\|

*tathā suragaṇaissākamāgatassurarāṭ svayam \|*  
*tathā yūyaṃ samāyātā ṛṣayo vītakalmaṣāḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Similarly, the king of devas himself has come along with all the devas. You too, the sages free from sins, have come.

## \|\| 3.27.41 \|\|

*yeye yajñocitāśśāṃtāḥ pātrabhūtāssamāgatāḥ \|*  
*vedavedārthatattvajñāssarve yūyaṃ dṛḍhavratāḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Whoever is worthy of being included in the sacrifice and deserves honour has come. You all know the Vedic texts and their meanings. You all are steady in your rites.

## \|\| 3.27.42 \|\|

*atraiva ca kimasmākaṃ rudreṇāpi prayojanam \|*  
*kanyā dattā mayā vipra brahmaṇā noditena hi \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Of what avail is Śiva to us in this place? O brahmin, of course I have given my daughter to Him but that was because I was persuaded by Brahmā.

## \|\| 3.27.43 \|\|

*haro'kulīnosau vipra pitṛmātṛvivarjitaḥ \|*  
*bhūtapretapiśācānāṃ patireko duratyayaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. O brahmin, this Śiva is not a man of nobility. He has neither father nor mother. He is the lord of goblins, ghosts and spirits and is incorrigible.

## \|\| 3.27.44 \|\|

*ātmasaṃbhāvito mūḍha stabdho maunī samatsaraḥ \|*  
*karmaṇyasminna yogyosau nānīto hi mayā'dhunā \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. He is a haughty self-conceited fool with false prestige and hostility. He is unworthy of this sacred rite. Hence he is not invited by me.

## \|\| 3.27.45 \|\|

*tasmāttvamīdṛśaṃ vākyaṃ punarvācyaṃ na hi kvacit \|*  
*sarverbhavadbhiḥ kartavyo yajño me saphalo mahān \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Therefore you shall never make such statements as these henceforth. My great sacrifice has to be made fruitful by all of you.

## \|\| 3.27.46 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*etacchrutvā vacastasya dadhīco vākyamabravīt \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ devamunīnāṃ sārasaṃ yutam \|\| 46 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

46\. On hearing those words, Dadhīci spoke aloud within the hearing of devas and sages. His words were pregnant with meaning.

## \|\| 3.27.47 \|\|

*dadhīca uvāca \|*  
*ayajñoyaṃ mahājāto vinā tena śivena hi \|*  
*vināśopi viśeṣeṇa hyatra te hi bhaviṣyati \|\| 47 \|\|*

Dadhīci said:—

47\. This sacrifice has become “Non-sacrifice” without the presence of Śiva. Indeed your destruction is imminent in this very sacrifice.

## \|\| 3.27.48 \|\|

*evamuktvā dadhīcosāveka eva vinirgataḥ \|*  
*yajñavāṭācca dakṣasya tvaritaḥ svāśramaṃ yayau \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Saying this, Dadhīci walked out of the sacrifice of Dakṣa and immediately returned to his hermitage.

## \|\| 3.27.49 \|\|

*tatonye śāṃkarā ye ca mukhyāśśivamatānugāḥ \|*  
*niryayussvāśramān sadyaśśāpaṃ dattvā tathaiva ca \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Then some important devotees of Śiva who were initiated in the Śaiva cult cursed Dakṣa and returned to their respective abodes.

## \|\| 3.27.50 \|\|

*munau vinirgate tasmin makhādanyeṣu duṣṭadhīḥ \|*  
*śivadrohī munīn dakṣaḥ prahasannidamabravīt \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. When the sage Dadhīci and others staged a walkout, the evil-minded Dakṣa, inimical to Śiva, said mocking at them.

## \|\| 3.27.51 \|\|

*\|\| dakṣa uvāca \|*  
*gataḥ śivapriyo vipro dadhīco nāma nāmataḥ \|*  
*anye tathāvidhā ye ca gatāste mama cādhvarāt \|\| 51 \|\|*

Dakṣa said:—

51\. Gone is that brahmin favourite of Śiva named Dadhīci and others too of his ilk have gone out of my sacrifice.

## \|\| 3.27.52 \|\|

*etacchubhataraṃ jātaṃ saṃmataṃ me hi sarvathā \|*  
*satyaṃ bravīmi deveśa surāśca munayastathā \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. This has become good. I approve of this always. O Indra, devas and sages, I am telling you the truth.

## \|\| 3.27.53 \|\|

*vinaṣṭacittā maṃdāśca mithyāvādaratāḥ khalāḥ \|*  
*vedabāhyā durācārāstyājyāste makhakarmaṇi \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. They are slow-witted and senseless. They are rogues indulging in false deliberations and discussions. They are out of the Vedic circle. These men of evil conduct shall be eschewed from sacrificial rites.

## \|\| 3.27.54 \|\|

*vedavādaratā yūyaṃ sarve viṣṇupurogamāḥ \|*  
*yajñaṃ me saphalaṃ viprāssurāḥ kurvaṃtu mā'ciram \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. You all, brahmins, sages and devas with Viṣṇu at the head shall make my sacrifice fruitful.

## \|\| 3.27.55-56 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya vacastasya śivamāyāvimohitāḥ \|*  
*yanmakhe devayajanaṃ cakrussarve surarṣayaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

*iti tanmakhaśāpo hi varṇito me munīśvara \|*  
*yajñavidhvaṃsayogopi procyate śṛṇu sādaram \|\| 56 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

55-56. On hearing these words, the celestial sages deluded by Śiva’s Māyā performed the worship of the deities in that sacrifice. O great sage, I have thus explained how the sacrifice had been cursed. Now I shall explain how the sacrifice was destroyed.

## Chapter 28 - Satī’s Journey

## \|\| 3.28.1-2 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*yadā yayurdakṣamakhamutsavena surarṣayaḥ \|*  
*tasminnaivāṃtare devo parvate gaṃdhamādane \|\| 1 \|\|*

*dhārāgṛhe vitānena sakhībhiḥ parivāritā \|*  
*dākṣāyaṇī mahākrīḍāścakāra vividhāssatī \|\| 2 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

1-2. In the meantime when the celestial sages were on their way to Dakṣa’s sacrifice, with great eclat Satī the daughter of Dakṣa was engrossed in diverse sports, surrounded by her friends under the canopy of the fountain house on the mountain Gandhamādana.

## \|\| 3.28.3-4 \|\|

*krīḍāsaktā tadā devī dadarśātha mudā satī \|*  
*dakṣayajñe prayāṃtaṃ ca rohiṇyā pṛcchya satvaram \|\| 3 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭvā sīmaṃtayā bhūtāṃ vijayāṃ prāha sā satī \|*  
*svasakhīṃ pravarāṃ prāṇapriyāṃ sā hi hitāvahām \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. While she was thus gaily sportive, Satī saw the moon in the company of Rohiṇī going to the sacrifice of Dakṣa. Satī asked Vijayā her maiden-in-chief, her beloved friend, wishing her all welfare.

## \|\| 3.28.5 \|\|

*\|\| satyuvāca \|*  
*he sakhīpravare prāṇapriye tvaṃ vijaye mama \|*  
*kva gamiṣyati candroyaṃ rohiṇyāpṛcchya satvaram \|\| 5 \|\|*

Satī said:—

5\. O beloved friend Vijayā, where does this moon go now in a hurry in the company of Rohiṇī after taking leave of us?

## \|\| 3.28.6 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*tathoktā vijayā satyā gatvā tatsannidhau drutam \|*  
*kva gacchasīti papraccha śaśinaṃ taṃ yathocitam \|\| 6 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

6\. When Satī thus asked her, Vijayā went near the moon and asked him “Where are you going?”

## \|\| 3.28.7 \|\|

*vijayoktamathākarṇya svayātrāṃ pūrvamādarāt \|*  
*kathitaṃ tena tatsarvaṃ dakṣayajñotsavādikam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. On hearing what Vijayā said, the moon mentioned everything about the sacrificial festival of Dakṣa, with great respect.

## \|\| 3.28.8 \|\|

*tacchrutvā vijayā devīṃ tvaritā jātasaṃbhramā \|*  
*kathayāmāsa tatsarvaṃ yaduktaṃ śaśinā satīm \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. On hearing what the moon told her, Vijayā was greatly agitated and mentioned it immediately to goddess Satī.

## \|\| 3.28.9 \|\|

*tacchrutvā kālikā devī vismitābhūtsatī tadā \|*  
*vimṛśya kāraṇaṃ tatrājñātvā cetasyaciṃtayat \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. On hearing it, Satī, the goddess Kālikā, was surprised. She thought over the possible reason, but not knowing it she mused like this.

## \|\| 3.28.10 \|\|

*dakṣaḥ pitā me mātā ca vīriṇī nau kutassatī \|*  
*āhvānaṃ na karoti sma vismṛtā māṃ priyāṃ sutām \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. “Dakṣa is my father. Vīriṇī is my mother. I am their beloved daughter Satī. Why did they not invite me? Have they forgotten their own beloved daughter?

## \|\| 3.28.11 \|\|

*pṛccheyaṃ śaṃkaraṃ tatra kāraṇaṃ sarvamādarāt \|*  
*ciṃtayitveti sāsīdvai tatra gaṃtuṃ suniścayā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. I shall ask Śiva respectfully the reason for the same”. Thinking thus she decided to go to Him.

## \|\| 3.28.12 \|\|

*atha dākṣāyaṇī devī vijayāṃ pravarāṃ sakhīm \|*  
*sthāpayitvā drutaṃ tatra samagacchacchivāṃtikam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Making her maiden-in-chief Vijayā wait there, Satī immediately went near Śiva.

## \|\| 3.28.13 \|\|

*dadarśa taṃ sabhāmadhye saṃsthitaṃ bahubhirgaṇaiḥ \|*  
*naṃdyādibhirmahāvīraiḥ pravarairyūthayūthapai \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. She saw Him in the middle of the council-chamber surrounded by hosts of his attendants—Nandin and others of great valour.

## \|\| 3.28.14 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā taṃ prabhumīśānaṃ svapatiṃ sātha dakṣajā \|*  
*praṣṭuṃ tatkāraṇaṃ śīghraṃ prāpa śaṃkarasaṃnidhim \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. After seeing her husband, the lord Śiva, the daughter of Dakṣa came near Him quickly in order to ask Him the reason.

## \|\| 3.28.15 \|\|

*śivena sthāpitā svāṃke prītiyuktena svapriyā \|*  
*pramoditā vacobhissā bahumānapurassaram \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Lovingly Śiva took his beloved on his lap and delighted her with pleasing words.

## \|\| 3.28.16 \|\|

*atha śaṃbhurmahālīlassarveśassukhadassatām \|*  
*satīmuvāca tvaritaṃ gaṇamadhyastha ādarāt \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Then Śiva, the lord of all, the bestower of happiness on the good, seated in the midst of his attendants told Satī indulging (as usual) in his great divine sports.

## \|\| 3.28.17 \|\|

*śaṃbhuruvāca \|*  
*kimarthamāgatātra tvaṃ sabhāmadhye savismayā \|*  
*kāraṇaṃ tasya suprītyā śīghraṃ vada sumadhyame \|\| 17 \|\|*

Śiva said:—

17\. “O slender-waisted lady, why did you come here in the council-chamber and that too in a state of surprise? Please tell me the reason.”

Brahmā continues the story—

## \|\| 3.28.18 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*evamuktā tadā tena maheśena munīśvara \|*  
*sāṃjalissupraṇamyāśu satyuvāca prabhuṃ śivā \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. O great sages, Satī on thus being addressed by Śiva, bowed to the lord with palms joined in reverence and said:—

## \|\| 3.28.19 \|\|

*satyuvāca \|*  
*piturmama mahān yajño bhavatīti mayā śrutam \|*  
*tatrotsavo mahānasti samavetāssurarṣayaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

Satī said:—

19\. I have heard that my father is performing a great sacrifice. Great festivities are being conducted there. The celestial sages have assembled too.

## \|\| 3.28.20 \|\|

*piturmama mahāyajñe kasmāttava na rocate \|*  
*gamanaṃ devadeveśa tatsarvaṃ kathaya prabho \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. O lord of devas, how is it that a visit to my father’s great sacrifice does not appeal to you? Please explain to me fully, O lord.

## \|\| 3.28.21 \|\|

*suhṛdāmeṣa vai dharmassuhṛdbhissaha saṃgatiḥ \|*  
*kurvaṃti yanmahādeva suhṛdaḥ prītivarddhinīm \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. This is the duty of friends that they shall frequently associate with their friends. O great lord, friends always do what increases the pleasures of their friends.

## \|\| 3.28.22 \|\|

*tasmātsarvaprayatnena mayāgaccha saha prabho \|*  
*yajñavāṭaṃ piturmedya svāmin prārthanayā mama \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. O lord, please come to my father’s Sacrificial Hall along with me. O lord, let it be at my request.

## \|\| 3.28.23 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*tasyāstadvacanaṃ śrutvā satyā devo maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*dakṣa vāgiṣuhṛdviddho babhāṣe sūnṛtaṃ vacaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

23\. On hearing these words of Satī, lord Śiva, wounded in the heart by the words of Dakṣa piercing like a dart, spoke these courteous and pleasing words.

## \|\| 3.28.24 \|\|

*maheśvara uvāca \|*  
*dakṣastava pitā devī mama drohī viśeṣataḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

Lord Śiva said:—

24\. Dakṣa is very well your father, dear. But he is my particular enemy.

## \|\| 3.28.25 \|\|

*yasya ye māninassarve sasurarṣimukhāḥ pare \|*  
*te mūḍhā yajanaṃ prāptāḥ pituste jñānavarjitāḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. But the celestial sages who usually honour me have become confused now. Being devoid of true knowledge they are attending the sacrifice of your father.

## \|\| 3.28.26 \|\|

*anāhūtāśca ye devī gacchaṃti paramaṃdiram \|*  
*avamānaṃ prāpnuvaṃti maraṇādadhikaṃ tathā \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. O gentle lady, those who go to another man’s house without being invited attain disrespect which is more serious than even death.

## \|\| 3.28.27 \|\|

*parālayaṃ gatopīṃdro laghurbhavati tadvidhaḥ \|*  
*kā kathā ca pareṣāṃ vai rīḍhā yātrā hi tadvidhā \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Even the prosperous Indra and people like him going to another man’s house in such a context become worthless. What then about others? A journey of such a nature is futile.

## \|\| 3.28.28 \|\|

*tasmāttvayā mayā cāpi dakṣasya yajanaṃ prati \|*  
*na gaṃtavyaṃ viśeṣeṇa satyamuktaṃ mayā priyaṃ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Hence you and I particularly shall not go to Dakṣa’s sacrifice. O beloved, I have told you the truth.

## \|\| 3.28.29 \|\|

*tathāribhirna vyathate hyarditopi śarairjanaḥ \|*  
*svānāṃduruktibhirmarmatāḍitassa yathā mataḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. People wounded with arrows by enemies are not so pained as when their vulnerable points are hit by the taunting words of kinsmen.

## \|\| 3.28.30 \|\|

*vidyādibhirguṇaiḥ ṣaḍbhirasadanyaissatāṃ smṛtau \|*  
*hatāyāṃ bhūyasāṃ dhāma na paśyaṃti khalāḥ priye \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. O beloved, the wicked people do not observe that their own status is being hit when they attack good men endowed with the six qualities of learning.”

## \|\| 3.28.31 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*evamuktā satī tena maheśena mahātmanā \|*  
*uvāca roṣasaṃyuktā śivaṃ vākyavidāṃ varam \|\| 31 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

31\. Thus advised by the noble-souled Śiva, Satī was angry and spoke thus to Śiva, the foremost of fluent speakers.

## \|\| 3.28.32 \|\|

*satyuvāca \|*  
*yajñassyātsaphalo yena sa tvaṃ śaṃbhokhileśvara \|*  
*anāhūtosi tenādya pitrā me duṣṭakāriṇā \|\| 32 \|\|*

Satī said:—

32\. O Śiva, lord of all, you by whom sacrifice becomes fruitful have not been invited by my father, thus he has committed a foul deed.

## \|\| 3.28.33 \|\|

*tatsarvaṃ jñātumicchāmi bhava bhāvaṃ durātmanaḥ \|*  
*surarṣīṇāṃ ca sarveṣāmāgatānāṃ durātmanām \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Hence, O Śiva, I wish to know the trend of thought of that evil-minded person as well as that of the celestial sages and all other wicked persons assembled there.

## \|\| 3.28.34 \|\|

*tasmāccādyaiva gacchāmi svapituryajanaṃ prabho \|*  
*anujñāṃ dehi me nātha tatra gaṃtuṃ maheśvara \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Hence O lord, I wish to go to the sacrifice of my father. O lord Śiva, please grant me permission to go there.

## \|\| 3.28.35 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*ityuktau bhagavān rudrastayā devyā śivassvayam \|*  
*vijñātākhiladṛk draṣṭā satīṃ sūtikaro'bravīt \|\| 35 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

35\. Lord Śiva, possessed of the perfect vision, realising everything and seeing all, and the cause of protection, being requested by the Goddess, spoke to her.

## \|\| 3.28.36 \|\|

*\|\| śiva uvāca \|*  
*yadyevaṃ te rucirdevi tatra gaṃtumavaśyakam \|*  
*suvrate vacanānme tvaṃ gaccha śīghraṃ piturmakham \|\| 36 \|\|*

Śiva said:—

36\. “O goddess, if this is what you wish, if you think it needful to go, O righteous one, you can immediately start for your father’s sacrifice with my willing permission.

## \|\| 3.28.37 \|\|

*etaṃ naṃdinamāruhya vṛṣabhaṃ sajjamādarāt \|*  
*mahārājopacārāṇi kṛtvā bahuguṇānvitā \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. You can go in royal splendour mounting this bull richly caparisoned.”

## \|\| 3.28.38 \|\|

*bhūṣitaṃ vṛṣamārohetyuktā rudreṇa sā satī \|*  
*subhūṣitā satī yuktā hyagamatpitumaṃdiram \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Satī thus commanded to mount the decorated bull, bedecked herself and started for her father’s abode.

## \|\| 3.28.39 \|\|

*mahārājopacārāṇi dattāni paramātmanā \|*  
*succhatracāmarādīni sadvastrābharaṇāni ca \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. The royal paraphernalia like the umbrella, chowries, silken clothes and ornaments were given to her by (Śiva) the great lord.

## \|\| 3.28.40 \|\|

*gaṇāḥ ṣaṣṭisahasrāṇi raudrā jagmuśśivājñayā \|*  
*kutūhalayutāḥ prītā mahotsavasamanvitāḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Sixty thousand of the attendants of Śiva lovingly and enthusiastically went with her with great festivities.

## \|\| 3.28.41 \|\|

*tadotsavo mahānāsīdyajane tatra sarvataḥ \|*  
*satyāśśivapriyāyāstu vāmadevagaṇaiḥ kṛtaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. The festivities performed by the attendants of Śiva to Satī, Śiva’s beloved, were indeed very great.

## \|\| 3.28.42-43 \|\|

*kutūhalaṃ gaṇāścakruśśivayoryaśa ujjaguḥ \|*  
*bālāṃtaḥ pupluvuḥ prītyā mahāvīrāśśivapriyāḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

*sarvathāsīnmahāśobhā gamane jāgadambike \|*  
*sukhārāvassaṃbabhūva pūritaṃ bhuvanatrayam \|\| 43 \|\|*

42-43. The heroic attendants, favourites of Śiva sang songs of praise of Śiva and Śivā and jumped in their joy with hearts of childish innocence. In every respect the departure of the mother of the universe was very glorious. The three worlds became filled with pleasing sounds.

## Chapter 29 - Satī’s statement

## \|\| 3.29.1 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*dākṣāyaṇī gatā tatra tatra yajño mahāprabhaḥ \|*  
*surāsuramunīndrādikutūhalasamanvitaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

1\. Satī reached the place where the colourful sacrifice accompanied by the enthusiasm of devas, asuras, great sages etc. was in progress.

## \|\| 3.29.2 \|\|

*svapiturbhavanaṃ tatra nānāścaryasamanvitam \|*  
*dadarśa suprabhaṃ cāru surarṣigaṇa saṃyutam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. She saw her father’s mansion abounding in wondrous things lustrous and beautiful as well as the groups of devas and sages.

## \|\| 3.29.3 \|\|

*dvāri sthitā tadā devī hyavaruhya nijāsanāt \|*  
*nandino'bhyaṃtaraṃ śīghramekaivāgacchadadhvaram \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The Goddess stopped at the gate and descended from Nandin, the bull. She went all alone inside the place of sacrifice.

## \|\| 3.29.4 \|\|

*āgatāṃ ca satīṃ dṛṣṭvā'siknī mātā yaśasvinī \|*  
*akarodādaraṃ tasyā bhaginyaśca yathocitam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. On seeing Satī, her glorious mother Asiknī and her sisters received her respectfully.

## \|\| 3.29.5 \|\|

*nākarodādaraṃ dakṣo dṛṣṭvā tāmapi kiṃcana \|*  
*nānyopi tadbhayāttatra śivamāyāvimohitaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Even after seeing her, Dakṣa did not show any sign or gesture of love or respect. The others too deluded by Śiva’s Māyā did not receive her out of fear of Dakṣa.

## \|\| 3.29.6 \|\|

*atha sā mātaraṃ devī pitaraṃ ca satī mune \|*  
*anamadvismitātyaṃtaṃ sarvaloka parābhavāt \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Satī then bowed to her parents, O sage. In her surprise (at the cool reception) she gazed at every one.

## \|\| 3.29.7 \|\|

*bhāgānapaśyaddevānāṃ haryādīnāṃ tadadhvare \|*  
*na śaṃbhubhāgamakarot krodhaṃ durviṣahaṃ satī \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. In that sacrifice, Satī saw the shares allotted to the deities, Viṣṇu, and others but not to Śiva. She then fell into a great fury.

## \|\| 3.29.8 \|\|

*satyuvāca \|*  
*tadā dakṣaṃ dahantīva ruṣā pūrṇā satī bhṛśam \|*  
*krūradṛṣṭyā vilokyaiva sarvānapyapamānitā \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Slighted thus and hence very furious at everyone she directed her burning fiery look at Dakṣa and every one present there.

## \|\| 3.29.9 \|\|

*satyuvāca \|*  
*anāhūtastvayā kasmācchaṃbhuḥ paramaśobhanaḥ \|*  
*yena pūtamidaṃ viśvaṃ samagraṃ sacarācaram \|\| 9 \|\|*

Satī said:—

9\. How is it that Śiva who is highly auspicious and by whom the entire universe of the mobile and the immobile is sanctified, has not been invited by you?

## \|\| 3.29.10 \|\|

*yajño yajñavidāṃ śreṣṭho yajñāṃgo yajñadakṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*yajñakartā ca yaśśaṃbhustaṃ vinā ca kathaṃ makhaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. What is that sacrifice without Śiva who is sacrifice Himself, the performer of sacrifice, the fee of sacrifice, the adjunct of sacrifice and the foremost of those who know sacrifice itself.

## \|\| 3.29.11 \|\|

*yasya smaraṇamātreṇa sarvaṃ pūtaṃ bhavatyaho \|*  
*vinā tena kṛtaṃ sarvamapavitraṃ bhaviṣyati \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Every rite performed without Him will be impure but with Him or by the mere remembrance of Him becomes pure.

## \|\| 3.29.12 \|\|

*dravyamaṃtrādikaṃ sarvaṃ havyaṃ kavyaṃ ca yanmayam \|*  
*śaṃbhunā hi vinā tena kathaṃ yajñaḥ pravartitaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The articles of offerings, the mantra, the Havya and Kavya, everything is identical with Śiva. How is it that the sacrifice is being performed without Him?

## \|\| 3.29.13 \|\|

*kiṃ śivaṃ surasāmānyaṃ matyākārṣīranādaram \|*  
*bhraṣṭabuddhirbhavānadya jātosi janakādhama \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Did you disrespect Him, considering Him on a par with ordinary devas? You have become senseless and mean though you are my father.

## \|\| 3.29.14 \|\|

*viṣṇubrahmādayo devā yaṃ saṃsevya maheśvaram \|*  
*prāptāḥ svapadavīṃ sarve taṃ na jānāsi re haram \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Ha, you do not know Śiva the great lord by serving whom Viṣṇu Brahmā and other devas have attained their position and status.

## \|\| 3.29.15 \|\|

*ete kathaṃ samāyātā viṣṇubrahmādayassurāḥ \|*  
*tava yajñe vinā śaṃbhuṃ svaprabhuṃ munayastathā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. How did Viṣṇu, Brahmā, other devas and the sages happen to be present at your sacrifice without their lord Śiva?”

## \|\| 3.29.16 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*ityuktvā parameśānī viṣṇvādīnsakalān prati \|*  
*pṛthakpṛthagavocatsā bhartsayaṃtī bhavātmikā \|\| 16 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

16\. After saying this, Satī addressed Viṣṇu and others severally, taunting them.

## \|\| 3.29.17 \|\|

*satyuvāca \|*  
*he viṣṇo tvaṃ mahādevaṃ kiṃ na jānāsi tattvataḥ \|*  
*saguṇaṃ nirguṇaṃ cāpi śrutayo yaṃ vadaṃti ha \|\| 17 \|\|*

Satī said:—

17\. “O Viṣṇu, don’t you know the real nature of Śiva whom the Vedas speak of as both full or devoid of attributes?

## \|\| 3.29.18-19 \|\|

*yadyapi tvāṃ karaṃ dattvā bahuvāraṃ maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*aśikṣayatpurā śālvapramukhākṛtibhirhare \|\| 18 \|\|*

*tadapi jñānamāyātaṃ na te cetasi durmate \|*  
*bhāgārthī dakṣayajñesmin śivaṃ svasvāminaṃ vinā \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. Although as the chieftain of king Śālva, Śiva had caught hold of your hand and set you aright many a time, that admonition has not entered your brain, now that you have evinced a desire to partake of your share in Dakṣa’s sacrifice without inviting lord Śiva.

## \|\| 3.29.20 \|\|

*purā paṃcamukho bhūtvā garvito'si sadāśivam \|*  
*kṛtaścaturmukhastena vismṛtosi tadadbhutam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. O Brahmā, you had five faces formerly. When you exhibited your haughtiness against Śiva, He made you four-faced. It is surprising that you have forgotten it.

## \|\| 3.29.21 \|\|

*indra tvaṃ kiṃ na jānāsi mahādevasya vikramam \|*  
*bhasmī kṛtaḥ paviste hi hareṇa krūrakarmaṇā \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. O Indra, don’t you know the valour of the great lord? Śiva had once ruthlessly reduced your thunderbolt to ashes.

## \|\| 3.29.22 \|\|

*he surāḥ kinna jānītha mahādevasya vikramam \|*  
*atre vasiṣṭha munayo yuṣmābhiḥ kiṃ kṛtaṃ tviha \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. O devas, don’t you know the valour of Mahādeva, O Atri, O Vasiṣṭha, O, sages what have you all done here?

## \|\| 3.29.23-24 \|\|

*bhikṣāṭanaṃ ca kṛtavān purā dāruvane vibhuḥ \|*  
*śapto yadbhikṣuko rudro bhavadbhirmunibhistadā \|\| 23 \|\|*

*śaptenāpi ca rudreṇa yatkṛtaṃ vismṛtaṃ katham \|*  
*talliṃgenākhilaṃ dagdhaṃ bhuvanaṃ sacarācaram \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. Once the lord wandered (begging for alms) in Dāruvana. You, sages, cursed him in the guise of a mendicant. How is it that you have now forgotten what Śiva did on being cursed by you? The entire universe of the mobile and immobile was burnt by His Liṅga.

## \|\| 3.29.25 \|\|

*sarve mūḍhāśca saṃjātā viṣṇubrahmādayassurāḥ \|*  
*munayo'nye vinā śaṃbhumāgatā yadihādhvare \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. All of you, Viṣṇu, Brahmā, gods, sages and others have turned foolish since you have assembled here without Śiva.

## \|\| 3.29.26 \|\|

*sarve vedāśca saṃbhūtāḥ sāṃgāśśāstrāṇi vāgyataḥ \|*  
*yosau vedāṃtagaśśambhuḥ kaiścijjñātuṃ na pāryate \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Śiva of controlled speech, knowable only through self-realisation cannot be understood by anyone with the help of only Vedas with their ancillary adjuncts and other sacred texts.

## \|\| 3.29.27 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*ityanekavidhā vāṇīragadajjagadambikā \|*  
*kopānvitā satī tatra hṛdayena vidūyatā \|\| 27 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

27\. Thus the infuriated Satī, the mother of the universe spoke many words with her heart in distress.

## \|\| 3.29.28 \|\|

*viṣṇvādayokhilā devā munayo ye ca tadvacaḥ \|*  
*maunībhūtāstadākarṇya bhayavyākulamānasāḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Viṣṇu, gods, and sages kept silent on hearing her words, though their minds were distressed on account of Śiva.

## \|\| 3.29.29 \|\|

*atha dakṣassamākarṇya svaputryāstādṛśaṃ vacaḥ \|*  
*vilokya krūradṛṣṭyā tāṃ satīṃ kuddho'bravīdvacaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. But Dakṣa on hearing those words of his daughter looked at Satī cruelly and said thus to her.

## \|\| 3.29.30 \|\|

*dakṣa uvāca \|*  
*tava kiṃ bahunoktena kāryaṃ nāstīha sāṃpratam \|*  
*gaccha vā tiṣṭha vā bhadre kasmāttvaṃ hi samāgatā \|\| 30 \|\|*

Dakṣa said:—

30\. Gentle lady, nothing shall be gained by your speaking so much here. You can go or stay. Why at all did you come?

## \|\| 3.29.31 \|\|

*amaṃgalastu te bhartā śivosau gamyate budhaiḥ \|*  
*akulīko vedabāhyo bhūtapretapiśācarāṭ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Your husband Śiva is known to the wise as inauspicious. He is not of a noble lineage. He is the king of goblins, ghosts and spirits. He is excluded from Vedic rites.

## \|\| 3.29.32 \|\|

*tasmānnāhvārito rudro yajñārthaṃ sukuveṣabhṛt \|*  
*devarṣisaṃsadi mayā jñātvā putri vipaścitā \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Knowing Śiva to be of indecent dress and features, my dear daughter I did not invite him to the sacrifice in the presence of gods and sages.

## \|\| 3.29.33 \|\|

*vidhinā preritena tvaṃ dattā maṃdena pāpinā \|*  
*rudrāyāviditārthāya coddhatāya durātmane \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Induced by Brahmā I gave you in marriage to the wicked haughty Śiva who does not know customs. I have been a sinner and slow-witted.

## \|\| 3.29.34 \|\|

*tasmātkopaṃ parityajya svasthā bhava śucismite \|*  
*yadyāgatāsi yajñesmin dāyaṃ gṛhṇīṣva cātmanā \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Hence leave off your anger. Calm yourself. (Let us see) you smile sweetly. Having come (all the way) to this sacrifice you can take your own share.

## \|\| 3.29.35 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*dakṣeṇokteti sā putrī satī trailokyapū jitā \|*  
*niṃdāyuktaṃ svapitaraṃ dṛṣṭvāsīdruṣitā bhṛśam \|\| 35 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

35\. The daughter Satī honoured in the three worlds, on being addressed thus, became very angry to see her father full of contempt.

## \|\| 3.29.36 \|\|

*arcitayattadā seti kathaṃ yāsyāmi śaṃkaram \|*  
*śaṃkaraṃ draṣṭukāmāhaṃ pṛṣṭā vakṣye kimuttaram \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. She mused to herself—“How can I return to Śiva?” Of course I am desirous of seeing Śiva but what reply shall I give when He were to ask me?

## \|\| 3.29.37 \|\|

*atha provāca pitaraṃ dakṣaṃ taṃ duṣṭamānasam \|*  
*niśśvasaṃtī ruṣāviṣṭā sā satī trijagatprasūḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Satī, the mother of the three worlds, heaving sighs of wrath told her father Dakṣa, the evil-minded.

## \|\| 3.29.38 \|\|

*satyuvāca \|*  
*yo niṃdati mahādevaṃ niṃdyamānaṃ śṛṇoti vā \|*  
*tāvubhau narakaṃ yātau yāvaccandradivākarau \|\| 38 \|\|*

Satī said:—

38\. “He who reproaches Śiva and he who hears such reproaches, both of them go hell and stay there as long as the moon and the sun exist.

## \|\| 3.29.39 \|\|

*tasmāttyakṣyāmyahaṃ devaṃ pravekṣyāmi hutāśanam \|*  
*kiṃ jīvitena me tāta śṛṇvaṃtyānādaraṃ prabhoḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Hence I shall cast off my body and enter the fire. O father, of what avail is this life unto me who am unfortunate enough to hear contemptuous remarks about my lord?

## \|\| 3.29.40 \|\|

*yadi śaktassvayaṃ śaṃbhorniṃdakasya viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*chiṃdyāt prasahya rasanāṃ tadā śuddhyenna saṃśayaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. If a powerful person cuts off the tongue of the man who makes such disrespectful remarks about Śiva both of them will be absolved of sins.

## \|\| 3.29.41 \|\|

*yadyaśakto janastatra nirayātsupidhāya vai \|*  
*karṇau dhīmān tataśśuddhyedvadaṃtīdaṃ budhānvarān \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. If he is not powerful enough let the sensible man close his ears and quit the place—He shall then be pure—so say the learned persons.”

## \|\| 3.29.42 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*itthamuktvā dharmanītiṃ paścāttāpamavāpa sā \|*  
*asmaracchāṃkaraṃ vākyaṃ dūyamānena cetasā \|\| 42 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

42\. After stating the dictum of virtue thus, she remembered the advice of Śiva and repented (her hasty arrival) with a grief-stricken heart.

## \|\| 3.29.43 \|\|

*tatassaṃkuddhya sā dakṣaṃ niśśaṃkaṃ prāha tānapi \|*  
*sarvānviṣṇvādikāndevānmunīnapi satī dhruvam \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Then inciting the fury of Dakṣa further, she said to Viṣṇu and all other devas and sages unhesitatingly.

## \|\| 3.29.44 \|\|

*satyuvāca \|*  
*tāta tvaṃ niṃdakaśśaṃbhoḥ paścāttāpaṃ gamiṣyasi \|*  
*iha bhuktvā mahāduḥkhamaṃte yāsyasi yātanām \|\| 44 \|\|*

Satī said:—

44\. Dear father, hating Śiva now you are sure to repent later. After experiencing a lot of agony here, you are sure to experience further torture.

## \|\| 3.29.45 \|\|

*yasya loke'priyo nāsti priyaścaiva parātmanaḥ \|*  
*tasminnavaire śarvesmin tvāṃ vinā kaḥ pratīpakaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Excepting you, can there be a person who is adversely inclined and disposed towards Śiva who is free from inimical feelings, who is the great Self and who does not hate or love anyone in the world?

## \|\| 3.29.46 \|\|

*mahadviniṃdā nāścaryaṃ sarvadā'satsu serṣyakam \|*  
*mahadaṃghrirajo dhvastatamassu saiva śobhanā \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Contempt of the great is infused with rivalry in the bad people but in regard to those whose Tāmasika quality is quelled by the dust of the feet of the great, it is auspicious.

## \|\| 3.29.47 \|\|

*śiveti dvyakṣaraṃ yasya nṛṇāṃ nāma gireritam \|*  
*sakṛtprasaṃgātsakalamaghamāśu vihaṃti tat \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. The syllables Śi and Va even uttered once casually can quell all sins.

## \|\| 3.29.48 \|\|

*pavitrakīrtitamalaṃ bhavān dveṣṭi śivetaraḥ \|*  
*alaṃghyaśāsanaṃ śaṃbhumaho sarveśvaraṃ khalaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. It is surprising that you are so wicked as to harbour ill feelings against Śiva who is the lord of all, whose dictum is untransgressable and who is the holiest of the holy. You are certainly enemy of Śiva.

## \|\| 3.29.49-50 \|\|

*yatpādapadmaṃ mahatāṃ mano'lisuniṣevitam \|*  
*sarvārthadaṃ brahmarasaiḥ sarvārthibhirathādarāt \|\| 49 \|\|*

*yadvarṣatyarthinaśśīghraṃ lokasya śivaādarāt \|*  
*bhavān druhyati mūrkhatvāttasmai cāśeṣabaṃdhave \|\| 50 \|\|*

49-50. It is a pity that out of foolishness you hold malice towards Śiva, the benefactor of everyone, whose lotuslike feet are always resorted to by the bees in the form of the minds of lofty-natured persons, who confers all blessings even that of realising the Self.

## \|\| 3.29.51 \|\|

*kiṃvā śivākhyamaśivaṃ tvadanye na vidurbudhāḥ \|*  
*brahmādayastaṃ munayassanakādyāstathāpare \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Have the scholarly persons, Brahmā and others, Śanaka and sages, except you, considered Śiva unholy?

## \|\| 3.29.52-53 \|\|

*avakīrya jaṭābhūtaiśśmaśāne sa kapāladhṛk \|*  
*tanmālyabhasma vā jñātvā prītyāvasadudāradhīḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

*ye mūrddhabhirdadhati taccaraṇotsṛṣṭamārād \|*  
*nirmālyaṃ munayo devāssa śivaḥ parameśvaraḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

52-53. Śiva who holds the skull in his hands resides in the cremation ground in the company of goblins. He wears matted hair. But sages and devas keep on their heads the dust from His feet. Such is the nature of lord Śiva, the great God.

## \|\| 3.29.54-55 \|\|

*pravṛttaṃ ca nivṛttaṃ ca dvividhaṃ karmacodi tam \|*  
*vede vivicya vṛttaṃ ca tadvicāryaṃ manīṣibhiḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

*virodhiyaugapadyaikakartṛke ca tathā dvayam \|*  
*parabrahmaṇi śaṃbho tu karmarcchaṃti na kiṃcana \|\| 55 \|\|*

54-55. In the Vedas two sorts of actions are ordained—direct and renunciatory. Scholars differentiate between these two and hold that they cannot be simultaneous and they cannot occur in a single entity. But in Śiva the great Brahman, these actions do not have any effect.

## \|\| 3.29.56-57 \|\|

*mā vaḥ padavyassma pitaryā asmadāsthitāssadā \|*  
*yajñaśālāsu vo dhūmravartmabhuktojjhitāḥ param \|\| 56 \|\|*

*no'vyaktaliṃgassatatamavadhūtasusevitaḥ \|*  
*abhimānamato na tvaṃ kuru tāta kubuddhidhṛk \|\| 57 \|\|*

56-57. Let us not take to your path of egoism as displayed in your sacrificial chambers enjoyed and cast-off by the fire. Ours is the manifest path followed by Avadhūtas. O father, with a crooked mind you need not be haughty and conceited.

## \|\| 3.29.58 \|\|

*kiṃbahūktena vacasā duṣṭastvaṃ sarvathā kudhīḥ \|*  
*tvadudbhavena dehena na me kiṃcitprayojanam \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Why say more? You are wicked in every respect. You are evil-minded. I have nothing further to do with this body born of you.

## \|\| 3.29.59 \|\|

*tajjanma dhigyo mahatāṃ sarvathāvadyakṛtkhalaḥ \|*  
*parityājyo viśeṣeṇa tatsaṃbaṃdho vipaścitā \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Fie upon Him who is always wicked and who perpetrates actions of unspeakable demerit. Sensible man should shun even the contact with such a man.

## \|\| 3.29.60 \|\|

*gotraṃ tvadīyaṃ bhagavān yadāha vṛṣabhadhvajaḥ \|*  
*dākṣāyaṇīti sahasāhaṃ bhavāmi sudurmanāḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. I am the offspring of your race as the bull-bannered lord Śiva has often said. Hence naturally my name has come to be Dākṣāyaṇī. This is distressing to me.

## \|\| 3.29.61 \|\|

*tasmāttvadaṃgajaṃ dehaṃ kuṇapaṃ garhitaṃ sadā \|*  
*vyutsṛjya nūnamadhunā bhaviṣyāmi sukhāvahā \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. This body born of your limbs I shall cast off as a corpse. It is worthy of contempt. I shall abandon it and gain happiness.

## \|\| 3.29.62 \|\|

*he surā munayassarve yūyaṃ śṛṇuta madvacaḥ \|*  
*sarvathānucitaṃ karma yuṣmākaṃ duṣṭacetasām \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. O sages and devas, you listen to my words. Your action is improper in every respect. You have become evil-minded

## \|\| 3.29.63 \|\|

*sarve yūyaṃ vimūḍhā hi śivaniṃdāḥ kalipriyāḥ \|*  
*prāpsyaṃti daṇḍaṃ niyatamakhilaṃ ca harāddhruvam \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. You are deluded. You revel in reproaching Śiva and quarrelling with Him. Everyone of you will get due punishment from Śiva.

## \|\| 3.29.64 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*dakṣamuktvādhvare tāṃśca vyaramatsā satī tadā \|*  
*anūdya cetasā śambhumasmaratprāṇavallabham \|\| 64 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

64\. Having said thus to Dakṣa and others present in the sacrifice, Satī stopped. After thinking upon her dear lord she desisted from her speech.

## Chapter 30 - Satī’s casting off of her body and the subsequent disorder

## \|\| 3.30.1 \|\|

*\|\| nārada uvāca \|*  
*maunībhūtā yadā sāsītsatī śaṃkaravallabhā \|*  
*caritraṃ kimabhūttatra vidhe tadvada cādarāt \|\| 1 \|\|*

Nārada said:—

1\. When Satī, Śiva’s beloved became silent what happened there? O Brahmā please tell me.

Brahmā said

## \|\| 3.30.2 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*maunībhūtā satī devī smṛtvā svapatimādarāta \|*  
*kṣitāvudīcyāṃ sahasā niṣasāda praśāṃtadhīḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Observing silence and remembering her lord with great respect, Satī the Goddess calmed down and sat on the ground in the northern wing.

## \|\| 3.30.3 \|\|

*jalamācamya vidhivat saṃvṛtā vāsasā śuciḥ \|*  
*dṛṅnimīlya patiṃ smṛtvā yogamārgaṃ samāviśat \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Having sipped water duly, covering up her body entirely with her cloth she closed her eyes and remembered her lord. She then entered the yogic trance.

## \|\| 3.30.4-5 \|\|

*kṛtvāsamānāvanilau prāṇāpānau sitānanā \|*  
*utthāpyodānamatha ca yatnātsā nābhicakrataḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*hṛdi sthāpyorasi dhiyā sthitaṃ kaṃṭhādbhruvossatī \|*  
*aniṃditānayanmadhyaṃ śaṃkaraprāṇavallabhā \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. Keeping her face steady she balanced the winds Prāṇa and Apāna. She then lifted up the wind Udāna from the umbilical region, stabilised it in the cardiac region took it through the throat and finally fixed it in the middle of the eyebrows.

## \|\| 3.30.6-7 \|\|

*evaṃ svadehaṃ sahasā dakṣakopājjihāsatī \|*  
*dagdhe gātre vāyuśucirdhāraṇaṃ yogamārgataḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*tatassvabhartuścaraṇaṃ ciṃtayaṃtī na cāparam \|*  
*apaśyatsā satī tatra yogamārganiviṣṭadhīḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. She desired to cast-off her body due to her anger with Dakṣa. She desired to burn off the body and retain the pure wind by yogic means. In this posture she remembered the feet of her lord and nothing else.

## \|\| 3.30.8 \|\|

*hatakalmaṣataddehaḥ prāpatacca tadagninā \|*  
*bhasmasādabhavatsadyo muniśreṣṭha tadicchayā \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Her body divested of its sins fell in the yogic fire and was reduced to ashes, O excellent sage, in accordance with her own wish.

## \|\| 3.30.9 \|\|

*tatpaśyatāṃ ca khe bhūmau vādo'bhūtsumahāṃstadā \|*  
*hāheti sodbhutaścitrassurādīnāṃ bhayāvahaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The loud shouts and cries of “Hā. Hā” of those who witnessed it spread everywhere on the earth and rose up in the sky. Everything was surprisingly wonderful and terrifying to the devas and others.

## \|\| 3.30.10 \|\|

*haṃ priyā parā śaṃbhordevī daivatamasya hi \|*  
*ahādasūn satī kena suduṣṭena prakopitā \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. “Alas, Śiva’s beloved Goddess, nay his deity, Satī has cast-off her life. Who is that wicked person who angered her?

## \|\| 3.30.11 \|\|

*aho tvanātmyaṃ sumahadasya dakṣasya paśyata \|*  
*carācaraṃ prajā yasya yatputrasya prajāpateḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. See the unholy unspiritual misdeed of Dakṣa the patriarch, the son of Brahmā whose subjects are the mobile and immobile creatures of the world.

## \|\| 3.30.12 \|\|

*ahodya dvimanā'bhūtsā satī devī manasvinī \|*  
*vṛṣadhvajapriyā'bhīkṣṇaṃ mānayogyā satāṃ sadā \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Alas, Satī, the noble beloved of the bull-bannered deity has become dispirited. She ought to have been honoured duly.

## \|\| 3.30.13 \|\|

*soyaṃ durmarṣahṛdayo brahmadhṛk sa prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*mahatīmapakīrtiṃ hi prāpsyati tvakhile bhave \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. This patriarch of hardened heart, inimical to the Brahman, will definitely become infamous in the whole world.

## \|\| 3.30.14 \|\|

*yatsvāṃgajāṃ sutāṃ śaṃbhudviṭ nyaṣe dhatsamudyatām \|*  
*mahānarakabhogī sa mṛtaye no'parādhataḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Since he refused to comply with the request of his own daughter he will be falling into a terrible hell after death due to his own guilt.

## \|\| 3.30.15 \|\|

*vadatyevaṃ jane satyā dṛṣṭvā'sutyāgamadbhutam \|*  
*drutaṃ tatpārṣadāḥ krodhādudatiṣṭhannudāyudhāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. When people were saying thus on seeing the self-immolation of Satī, her attendants rose up in anger with their weapons.

## \|\| 3.30.16 \|\|

*dvāri sthitā gaṇāssarve rasāyutamitā ruṣā \|*  
*śaṃkarasya prabhoste vā'kudhyannatimahābalāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. They had been waiting near the door numbering sixty thousand. Those powerful attendants of lord Śiva became furious.

## \|\| 3.30.17 \|\|

*hāhākāramakurvaṃste dhikdhik na iti vādinaḥ \|*  
*uccaissarve'sakṛdvīraḥśśaṃkarasya gaṇādhipāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Those attendants of Śiva shouted exclamations—Hā Hā, fie, fie, no, no, loudly and frequently.

## \|\| 3.30.18 \|\|

*hāhākāreṇa mahatā vyāpta māsīddigantaram \|*  
*sarve prāpan bhayaṃ devā munayonyepi te sthitāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The quarters were pervaded with the shouts of Hā, Hā. The devas and sages who had assembled there were struck with fear.

## \|\| 3.30.19 \|\|

*gaṇāssaṃmaṃtrya te sarve'bhūvan kruddhā udāyudhāḥ \|*  
*kurvantaḥ pralayaṃ vādyaśastrairvyāptaṃ digaṃtaram \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Consulting one another, the attendants lifted their weapons furiously and the atmosphere was pervaded with the sound of their arms.

## \|\| 3.30.20 \|\|

*śastrairaghnannijāṃgāni kecittatra śucākulāḥ \|*  
*śiromukhāni devarṣe sutīkṣṇaiḥ prāṇanāśibhiḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. O celestial sage, some of them excessively stricken with grief cut off their limbs with their weapons, some their heads, some their faces, with the sharp lethal weapons they had.

## \|\| 3.30.21 \|\|

*itthaṃ te vilayaṃ prāptā dākṣāyaṇyā samaṃ tadā \|*  
*gaṇāyute dve ca tadā tadadbhutamivābhavat \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Thus about twenty-thousand of those attendants courted death along with Satī. It was very surprising.

## \|\| 3.30.22 \|\|

*gaṇā nāśā'vaśiṣṭā ye śaṃkarasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*dakṣaṃ taṃ krodhitaṃ hantuṃ mudā tiṣṭhannudāyudhāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Such of the attendants of the noble-souled Śiva who survived, jumped up with their weapons to kill the furious Dakṣa.

## \|\| 3.30.23 \|\|

*teṣāmāpatatāṃ vegaṃ niśamya bhagavān bhṛguḥ \|*  
*yajñaghnaghnena yajuṣā dakṣiṇāgnau juhonmune \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. On seeing the force of their onslaught, O sages, the holy sage Bhṛgu poured offering in the Dakṣiṇa fire with the Yajur mantra to quell the obstructors of sacrifice.

## \|\| 3.30.24 \|\|

*hūyamāne ca bhṛguṇā samutpeturmahāsurāḥ \|*  
*ṛbhavo nāma prabalavīrāstatra sahasraśaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. While the sage Bhṛgu\[2\] was pouring the offerings, thousands of powerful demons—Ṛbhus rose up.

## \|\| 3.30.25 \|\|

*tairalātāyudhaistatra pramathānāṃ munīśvara \|*  
*abhūdyuddhaṃ suvikaṭaṃ śṛṇvatāṃ romaharṣaṇam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. O excellent sage, a terrible fight ensued between Śiva’s attendants and the demons who had firebrands for their weapons. Their hair stood on end when people heard the uproar.

## \|\| 3.30.26 \|\|

*ṛbhubhistairmahāvīrairhanyamānāssamantataḥ \|*  
*ayatnayānāḥ pramathā uśadbhirbrahmatejasā \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The attendants were killed by the Ṛbhus of powerful valour and favoured with Brahminical splendour. They were forced to run without difficulty.

## \|\| 3.30.27 \|\|

*evaṃ śivagaṇāste vai hatā vidrāvitā drutam \|*  
*śivecchayā mahāśaktyā tadadbhutamivā'bhavat \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. It had been the desire of Śiva of the great Śakti that the attendants were killed and routed quickly. It was a wonderful scene.

## \|\| 3.30.28 \|\|

*taddṛṣṭvā ṛṣayo devāśśakrādyāssamarudgaṇāḥ \|*  
*viśveśvinau lokapālāstūṣṇīṃ bhūtāstadā'bhavan \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. On seeing this, the sages, Indra and other devas, the Maruts, the Viśvedevas, the Aśvins and the guardians of the quarters kept silent.

## \|\| 3.30.29 \|\|

*kecidviṣṇuṃ prabhuṃ tatra prārthayantassamantataḥ \|*  
*udvignā mantrayaṃtaśca viprābhāvaṃ muhurmuhuḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Some of them went to request and consult with Viṣṇu frequently for preventing obstacles. They were greatly agitated.

## \|\| 3.30.30 \|\|

*suvicāryodarkaphalaṃ mahodvignāssubuddhayaḥ \|*  
*suraviṣṇvādayobhūvan tannāśādrāvaṇānmuhuḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. The sensible devas, Viṣṇu and others, became agitated on pondering over the results of Pramathas’ destruction and routing.

## \|\| 3.30.31 \|\|

*evaṃbhūtastadā yajño vighno jāto durātmanaḥ \|*  
*brahmabaṃdhośca dakṣasya śaṃkaradrohiṇo mune \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Such was the obstacle to the sacrifice of Dakṣa who rivalled with Śiva, who was wicked and who professed to be a kinsman of Brahmā, O sage.

## Chapter 31 - The Celestial Voice

## \|\| 3.31.1 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*etasminnantare tatra nabhovāṇī munīśvara \|*  
*avocacchṛṇvatāṃ dakṣasurādīnāṃ yathārthataḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

1\. O excellent sage, in the meantime a celestial voice arose, even as Dakṣa, the devas and others were listening.

## \|\| 3.31.2 \|\|

*vyomavāṇyuvāca \|*  
*re re dakṣa durācāra daṃbhācāraparāyaṇa \|*  
*kiṃ kṛtaṃ te mahāmūḍha karma cānarthakārakam \|\| 2 \|\|*

The celestial Voice said:—

2\. O Dakṣa, of evil conduct, of haughty disposition, what is it that you have foolishly done now, this misdeed bringing in many an unhappy calamity in its wake?

## \|\| 3.31.3 \|\|

*na kṛtaṃ śaivarājasya dadhīcervacanasya hi \|*  
*pramāṇaṃ tatkṛte mūḍha sarvānaṃdakaraṃ śubham \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. You never gave any credence to the words of Dadhīci, the king of devotees of Śiva. O fool, if it had been carried out, everything would have been auspicious and pleasing.

## \|\| 3.31.4 \|\|

*nirgataste makhādvipraḥ śāpaṃ dattvā sudussaham \|*  
*tatopi buddhaṃ kiṃcinno tvayā mūḍhena cetasi \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. After cursing you terribly, the brahmin had walked out of the sacrificial hall in protest. Still you did not understand anything, fool that you were.

## \|\| 3.31.5 \|\|

*tataḥ kṛtaḥ kathaṃ no vai svaputryāstvādaraḥ paraḥ \|*  
*samāgatāyāssatyāśca maṃgalāyā gṛhaṃ svataḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. How is it that you did not honour Satī your daughter, the auspicious lady who herself came to your house?

## \|\| 3.31.6 \|\|

*satībhavau nārcitau hi kimidaṃ jñānadurbala \|*  
*brahmaputra iti vṛthā garvitosi vimohitaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. O you weak in knowledge, how is it that you did not worship Satī and Śiva? In vain do you feel proud of being Brahmā’s son. You are actually deluded.

## \|\| 3.31.7 \|\|

*sā satyeva sadārādhyā sarvā pāpaphalapradā \|*  
*trilokamātā kalyāṇī śaṃkarārddhāṃgabhāginī \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. That Satī alone, who quells all sins, who is the mother of three worlds, who has occupied half the body of Śiva and who confers all welfare should be propitiated always.

## \|\| 3.31.8 \|\|

*sā satyevārcitā nityaṃ sarvasaubhāgyadāyinī \|*  
*māheśvarī svabhaktānāṃ sarvamaṃgaladāyinī \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. That Satī alone when worshipped for ever confers good fortunes. She is the great goddess who bestows everything auspicious on her devotees.

## \|\| 3.31.9 \|\|

*sā satyevārcitā nityaṃ saṃsārabhayanāśinī \|*  
*manobhīṣṭapradā daivī sarvopadravahāriṇī \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. That Satī alone when propitiated for ever destroys the fear from worldly existence. She is the goddess who confers what we desire and who removes all disorders.

## \|\| 3.31.10 \|\|

*sā satyevārcitā nityaṃ kīrtisaṃpatpradāyinī \|*  
*paramā parameśānī bhuktimuktipradāyinī \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. That Satī alone when propitiated for ever bestows fame and wealth. She is the great Goddess who confers worldly pleasures and salvation.

## \|\| 3.31.11 \|\|

*sā satyeva jagaddhātrī jagadrakṣaṇakāriṇī \|*  
*anādiśaktiḥ kalpānte jagatsaṃhārakāriṇī \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. That Satī alone is the creator of the universe, the protectress of the universe, the cause of destruction of the universe at the end of the Kalpa. She is the primordial Śakti.

## \|\| 3.31.12 \|\|

*sā satyeva jaganmātā viṣṇu mātāvilāsinī \|*  
*brahmendracandravahnyarkadevādijananī smṛtā \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. That Satī alone is the Māyā of the universe, the mother of Viṣṇu, of diverse shining features, and the mother of Brahmā, Indra, the moon, the fire, the sun and the devas.

## \|\| 3.31.13 \|\|

*sā satyeva tapodharmadātādiphaladāyinī \|*  
*śaṃbhuśaktirmahādevī duṣṭahaṃtrī parātparā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. That Satī alone is the bestower of the fruits of penance, charitable gifts and virtuous actions. She is the Śakti of Śiva, the great Goddess, the destroyer of the wicked and the greatest of the great.

## \|\| 3.31.14 \|\|

*īdṛgvidhā satī devī yasya patnī sadā priyā \|*  
*tasyai bhāgo na dattaste mūḍhena kuvicāriṇā \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The due share has not been offered by you who are foolish and evil-minded to the lord whose ever beloved wife is the goddess Satī of such glorious features.

## \|\| 3.31.15 \|\|

*śaṃbhurhi parameśānassarvasvāmī parātparaḥ \|*  
*viṣṇubrahmādisaṃsevyaḥ sarvakalyāṇakārakaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Śiva indeed is the great lord, the lord of all, the greatest of the great, worthy of being served by Viṣṇu, Brahmā and others and the cause of all welfare.

## \|\| 3.31.16 \|\|

*tapyate hi tapaḥ siddhairetaddarśanakāṃkṣibhiḥ \|*  
*yujyate yogibhiryogairetaddarśanakāṃkṣibhiḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Penances are performed by the Siddhas who desire to have a vision of Him. Yogic meditations and exercises are performed by Yogins who desire to have a vision of Him.

## \|\| 3.31.17 \|\|

*anaṃtadhanadhānyānāṃ yāgādīnāṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*darśanaṃ śaṃkarasyaiva mahatphalamudāhṛtam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Vision of Śiva yields great fruits, endless wealth and foodgrains and the fructification of all sacrifices.

## \|\| 3.31.18 \|\|

*śiva eva jagaddhātā sarvavidyāpatiḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*ādividyāvarasvāmī sarvamaṃgalamaṃgalaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Śiva alone is the creator of the universe, the lord of all lores, the upholder of the primordial learning and the lord, the most auspicious of the auspicious.

## \|\| 3.31.19 \|\|

*tacchakterna kṛto yasmātsatkarodya tvayā khala \|*  
*ataevā'dhvarasyāsya vināśo hi bhaviṣyati \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Since you have not duly respected His Śakti, and since you are wicked, this sacrifice will definitely be destroyed.

## \|\| 3.31.20 \|\|

*amaṃgalaṃ bhavatyeva pūjārhāṇāmapūjayā \|*  
*pūjyamānā ca nāsau hi yataḥ pūjyatamā śivā \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Inauspicious results befall one when those worthy of worship are not worshipped and they are quelled when they are worshipped, since Śivā is the worthiest of all worship.

## \|\| 3.31.21 \|\|

*sahasreṇāpi śirasāṃ śeṣo yatpādajaṃ rajaḥ \|*  
*vahatyaharahaḥ prītyā tasya śaktiḥ śivā satī \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. That Śakti is Śivā, Satī, the dust from whose feet is worn everyday by Śeṣa with his thousand heads.

## \|\| 3.31.22 \|\|

*yatpādapadmamaniśaṃ dhyātvā saṃpūjya sādaram \|*
