*viṣṇuviṣṇutvamāpannastasya śaṃbhoḥ priyā satī \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Satī is the beloved of Śiva by meditating upon whose lotus-like feet for ever and by worshipping which Viṣṇu attained his Viṣṇu-hood.

## \|\| 3.31.23 \|\|

*yatpādapadmamaniśaṃ dhyātvā saṃpūjya sādaram \|*  
*brahmā brahmatvamāpannastasya śaṃbhoḥ priyā satī \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Satī is the beloved of Śiva, by meditating upon whose lotus-like feet for ever and by worshipping which, Brahmā attained his Brahmā-hood.

## \|\| 3.31.24 \|\|

*yatpādapadmamaniśaṃ dhyātvā saṃpūjya sādaram \|*  
*indrādayo lokapālāḥ prāpussvaṃ svaṃ paraṃ padam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Śiva is the lord, by meditating upon whose lotuslike feet for ever and by worshipping which the guardians of quarters—Indra and others attained their respective positions.

## \|\| 3.31.25 \|\|

*jagatpitā śivaśśaktirjaganmātā ca sā satī \|*  
*satkṛtau na tvayā mūḍha kathaṃ śreyo bhaviṣyati \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Śiva is the father of the universe. That Satī is the mother of the universe. O fool, they were not honoured duly by you. How can you attain welfare?

## \|\| 3.31.26 \|\|

*daurbhāgyaṃ tvayi saṃkrāṃtaṃ saṃkrāṃtāstvayi cāpadaḥ \|*  
*yau cānārādhitau bhaktyā bhavānīśaṃkarau ca tau \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Since Satī and Śiva are not propitiated by you, misfortune has befallen you. Miseries have attacked you.

## \|\| 3.31.27 \|\|

*anabhyarcya śivaṃ śaṃbhuṃ kalyāṇaṃ prāpnuyāmiti \|*  
*kimasti garvo durvārassa garvodya vinaśyati \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Do you feel proud enough to suppose that you can attain welfare without worshipping Śiva? That haughty pride will be quashed today.

## \|\| 3.31.28 \|\|

*sarveśavimukho bhūtvā deveṣveteṣu kastava \|*  
*kariṣyati sahāyaṃ taṃ na te paśyāmi sarvathā \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. I do not see anyone among these devas who will come to your assistance, since you are averse to the Lord.

## \|\| 3.31.29 \|\|

*yadi devāḥ kariṣyaṃti sāhāyyamadhunā tava \|*  
*tadā nāśaṃ samāpsyaṃti śalabhā iva vahninā \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. If the devas were to come to your assistance, they are sure to be destroyed like moths by fire.

## \|\| 3.31.30 \|\|

*jvalatvadya mukhaṃ te vai yajñadhvaṃso bhavatvati \|*  
*sahāyāstava yāvaṃtaste jvalaṃtvadya satvaram \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Let your face burn. Let your sacrifice be quashed. Whoever comes as your assistant—let him be burnt today immediately.

## \|\| 3.31.31 \|\|

*amarāṇāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ śapatho'maṃgalāya te \|*  
*kariṣyaṃtyadya sāhāyyaṃ yadetasya durātmanaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. An oath on all the devas for your inauspiciousness, if they are to assist your wickedness.

## \|\| 3.31.32 \|\|

*nirgacchaṃtvamarāssvokametadadhvaramaṃḍapāt \|*  
*anyathā bhavato nāśo bhaviṣyatyadya sarvathā \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Let all the devas depart quickly from this sacrificial altar. Otherwise you all will perish today without an escape.

## \|\| 3.31.33 \|\|

*nirgacchaṃtvapare sarve munināgādayo makhāt \|*  
*anyathā bhavatāṃ nāśo bhaviṣyatyadya sarvathā \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Let all the sages, Nāgas and others leave this sacrifice. Otherwise, you all will perish today, without an escape.

## \|\| 3.31.34 \|\|

*nirgaccha tvaṃ hare śīghrametadadhvaramaṃḍapāt \|*  
*anyathā bhavato nāśo bhaviṣyatyadya sarvathā \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. O Viṣṇu, come out of this sacrificial platform quickly. Otherwise you will perish today without an escape.

## \|\| 3.31.35 \|\|

*nirgaccha tvaṃ vidhe śīghrametadadhvaramaṃḍapāt \|*  
*anyathā bhavato nāśo bhaviṣyatyadya sarvathā \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. O Brahmā, come out of this sacrificial platform quickly. Otherwise you will perish today, by all means.

## \|\| 3.31.36-37 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityuktvādhvaraśālāyāmakhilāyāṃ susaṃsthitān \|*  
*vyaramatsā nabhovāṇī sarvakalyāṇakāriṇī \|\| 36 \|\|*

*tacchrutvā vyomavacanaṃ sarve haryādayassurāḥ \|*  
*akārṣurvismayaṃ tāta munayaśca tathā pare \|\| 37 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

36-37. After saying this to those who had gathered in the sacrificial hall, the celestial voice that conferred welfare stopped. O dear one, on hearing the astral voice Viṣṇu and other devas were surprised. The sages too were wonder-struck.

## Chapter 32 - Vīrabhadra is born and Śiva advises him

## \|\| 3.32.1-2 \|\|

*\|\| nārada uvāca \|*  
*śrutvā vyomagiraṃ dakṣaḥ kimakārṣīttadā'budhaḥ \|*  
*anye ca kṛtavaṃtaḥ kiṃ tataśca kimabhūdvada \|\| 1 \|\|*

*parājitāḥ śivagaṇā bhṛgumaṃtrabalena vai \|*  
*kimakārṣuḥ kutra gatāstattvaṃ vada mahāmate \|\| 2 \|\|*

Nārada said:—

1-2. On hearing the ethereal voice what did the unwise Dakṣa do? What did the others do? What happened thereafter? Please narrate. O intelligent one, please tell me what those attendants of Śiva who were defeated by the power of Bhṛgu’s mantras did and where they went.

## \|\| 3.32.3 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*śrutvā vyomagiraṃ sarve vismitāśca surādayaḥ \|*  
*nāvocatkiṃcidapi te tiṣṭhantastu vimohitāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

3\. On hearing the voice of the Sky, the devas and others were stunned with surprise. They did not say anything. They stood perplexed and dazed.

## \|\| 3.32.4 \|\|

*palāyamānā ye vīrā bhṛgumaṃtrabalena te \|*  
*avaśiṣṭā śśivagaṇāśśivaṃ śaraṇamāyayuḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The remaining attendants of Śiva who were defeated and routed by the power of Bhṛgu’s mantras fled and sought refuge in Śiva.

## \|\| 3.32.5 \|\|

*sarvaṃ nivedayāmāsū rudrāyāmitatejase \|*  
*caritraṃ ca tathābhūtaṃ supraṇamyādarācca te \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Bowing with great respect to Śiva of immeasurable splendour they narrated everything that transpired there.

## \|\| 3.32.6 \|\|

*gaṇā ūcuḥ \|*  
*devadeva mahādeva pāhi naśśaraṇāgatān \|*  
*saṃśṛṇvādarato nātha satī vārtāṃ ca vistarāt \|\| 6 \|\|*

Gaṇas said:—

6\. O lord of Devas, save us who have sought refuge in you. Please listen with condescension to the detailed description of the events connected with Satī.

## \|\| 3.32.7 \|\|

*garvitena maheśānadakṣena sudurātmanā \|*  
*avamānaḥ kṛtassatyā'nādaro nirjaraistathā \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. O Lord, great disrespect was shown to Satī by the haughty and wicked Dakṣa. The devas too did not show due respect to her.

## \|\| 3.32.8 \|\|

*tubhyaṃ bhāgamadātro sa devebhyaśca pradattavān \|*  
*durvacāṃsyavadatproccairduṣṭo dakṣassugarvitaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. He did not allot your share but gave it to all the devas. The extremely haughty Dakṣa wickedly and loudly spoke harsh words.

## \|\| 3.32.9 \|\|

*tato dṛṣṭvā na te bhāgaṃ yajñe'kupyatsatī prabho \|*  
*viniṃdya bahuśastātamadhākṣītsvatanuṃ tadā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. O lord, not seeing your share in the sacrifice Satī became angry. After censuring her father many times she burnt her body (in the yogic fire).

## \|\| 3.32.10 \|\|

*gaṇāstvayutasaṃkhyākā mṛtāstatra vilajjayā \|*  
*svāṃgānyāchidya śastraiśca krudhyāma hyapare vayam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Gaṇas exceeding ten-thousand put an end to their lives out of shame by cutting off their limbs with weapons. We, the rest, became infuriated.

## \|\| 3.32.11 \|\|

*tadyajñe dhvaṃsituṃ vegātsannaddhāstu bhayāvahāḥ \|*  
*tiraskṛtā hi bhṛguṇā svaprabhāvādvirodhinā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Assuming a terrifying attitude we suddenly got ready to destroy the sacrifice. But we were repelled by Bhṛgu by means of his (spiritual) power. He opposed us.

## \|\| 3.32.12 \|\|

*te vayaṃ śaraṇaṃ prāptāstava viśvaṃbhara prabho \|*  
*nirbhayān kuru nastasmāddayamānabhavādbhayāt \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. O lord, the sustainer of the world, we have now sought refuge in you. We are now grieved and fear-stricken. Please make us free from fear.

## \|\| 3.32.13 \|\|

*apamānaṃ viśeṣeṇa tasmin yajñe mahāprabho \|*  
*dakṣādyāste'khilā duṣṭā akurvan garvitā ati \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. O great lord, Dakṣa and the other wicked persons have shown great disrespect because they are very haughty.

## \|\| 3.32.14 \|\|

*ityuktaṃ nikhilaṃ vṛttaṃ sveṣāṃ satyāśca nārada \|*  
*teṣāṃ ca mūḍhabuddhīnāṃ yathecchasi tathā kuru \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. O bestower of honour we have told you all that happened to us and to Satī. Please deal with those deluded fools in the manner you deem fit.

## \|\| 3.32.15 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*ityākarṇyavacastasya svagaṇānāṃ vacaḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*sasmāra nāradaṃ sarvaṃ jñātuṃ taccaritaṃ laghu \|\| 15 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

15\. On hearing the words of his attendants, the lord remembered you, Nārada, in order to know their activities.

## \|\| 3.32.16 \|\|

*āgatastvaṃ drutaṃ tatra devarṣe divyadarśana \|*  
*praṇamya śaṃkaraṃ bhaktyā sāṃjalistatra tasthivān \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. O celestial sage, endowed with divine vision you reached the place and after bowing to Śiva with devotion you waited there with palms joined in reverence.

## \|\| 3.32.17 \|\|

*tvāṃ praśasyātha sa svāmī satyā vārttāṃ ca pṛṣṭavān \|*  
*dakṣayajñagatāyā vai paraṃ ca caritaṃ tathā \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. After praising you, the lord asked you about Sati’s news at the sacrifice of Dakṣa and the incidents there.

## \|\| 3.32.18 \|\|

*pṛṣṭena śaṃbhunā tāta tvayāśveva śivātmanā \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ kathitaṃ vṛtaṃ jātaṃ dakṣādhvare hi yat \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. O dear, when you were thus asked by Śiva, you identified with Śiva and narrated to him in detail about what had happened in Dakṣa’s sacrifice.

## \|\| 3.32.19 \|\|

*tadākarṇyeśvaro vākyaṃ mune tattvanmukhoditam \|*  
*cukopātidrutaṃ rudro mahāraudraparākramaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. O sage, on hearing the words spoken by you, Śiva became furious in a trice, Śiva of great fury and valour.

## \|\| 3.32.20 \|\|

*utpāṭyaikāṃ jaṭāṃ rudro lokasaṃhārakārakaḥ \|*  
*āsphālayāmāsa ruṣā parvatasya tadopari \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Then Rudra, the destroyer of the world, plucked out a cluster of his matted hair and struck the top of the mountain with it.

## \|\| 3.32.21 \|\|

*todanācca dvidhā bhūtā sā jaṭā ca mune prabhoḥ \|*  
*saṃbabhūva mahārāvo mahāpralayabhīṣaṇaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. O sage, the cluster of the matted hair of the lord split into two, on being struck on the mountain. A loud explosive sound was heard which was as terrific as the sound at the time of dissolution.

## \|\| 3.32.22 \|\|

*tajjaṭāyāssamudbhūto vīrabhadro mahābalaḥ \|*  
*pūrvabhāgena devarṣe mahābhīmo gaṇāgraṇīḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. O celestial sage, from the first half of that cluster of matted hair, rose up the powerful Vīrabhadra, the terrific leader of the Gaṇas.

## \|\| 3.32.23 \|\|

*sa bhūmiṃ viśvato vṛttvātyatiṣṭhaddaśāṃgulam \|*  
*pralayānalasaṃkāśaḥ pronnato dossahasravān \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. He. stood lofty with two thousand hands blazing like the consuming fire. He enveloped the world all round and towered over it ten inches more.

## \|\| 3.32.24 \|\|

*kopaniśvāsatastatra mahārudrasya ceśituḥ \|*  
*jātaṃ jvarāṇāṃ śatakaṃ saṃnipātāstrayodaśa \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. From the furious breath of Śiva, the great Rudra, hundred fevers and thirteen humours came out.

## \|\| 3.32.25 \|\|

*mahākālī samutpannā tajjaṭāparabhā gataḥ \|*  
*mahābhayaṃkarā tāta bhūtakoṭibhirāvṛtā \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. From the other half of the cluster of matted hair Mahākālī was born. O dear one, she was very terrible and was surrounded by crores of goblins.

## \|\| 3.32.26 \|\|

*sarve mūrttidharāḥ krūrāḥ svara lokabhayaṃkarāḥ \|*  
*svatejasā prajvalaṃto dahaṃta iva sarvataḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The ruthless fevers had embodied forms. They were capable of terrifying the world. They were blazing with their fiery splendour.

## \|\| 3.32.27 \|\|

*atha vīro vīrabhadraḥ praṇamya parameśvaram \|*  
*kṛtāṃjalipuṭaḥ prāha vākyaṃ vākyaviśāradaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Then the heroic Vīrabhadra, eloquent in speech, joined his palms in reverence and bowed to lord Śiva. Vīrabhadra said thus:—

## \|\| 3.32.28 \|\|

*vīrabhadra uvāca \|*  
*mahārudra mahāraudra somasūryāgnilocana \|*  
*kiṃ kartavyaṃ mayā kāryaṃ śīghramājñāpaya prabho \|\| 28 \|\|*

Vīrabhadra said:—

28\. O Rudra of terrific appearance, with the moon, the sun and the fire for your eyes what am I to do? O lord, command me quickly.

## \|\| 3.32.29 \|\|

*śoṣaṇīyāḥ kimīśāna kṣaṇārddhenaiva siṃdhavaḥ \|*  
*peṣaṇīyāḥ kimīśāna kṣaṇārddhenaiva parvatāḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. O Śiva, are the oceans to be dried up in half a moment? O Śiva, are the mountains to be ground into powder in half a moment.

## \|\| 3.32.30 \|\|

*kṣaṇena bhasmasātkuryāṃ brahmāṃḍamuta kiṃ hara \|*  
*kṣaṇena bhasmasātkuryāmsurānvā kiṃ munīśvarān \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. O Śiva, shall I reduce the whole universe to ashes in a moment? Shall I reduce the gods or the sages to ashes in a moment?

## \|\| 3.32.31 \|\|

*vyāśvāsaḥ sarvalokānāṃ kimu cāryo hi śaṃkara \|*  
*kartavya kimuteśāna sarvaprāṇivihiṃsanam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. O Śiva, shall the destruction of the universe be carried out? Or, O Śiva, shall the harassment of all living beings be carried out?

## \|\| 3.32.32 \|\|

*mamāśakyaṃ na kutrāpi tvatprasādānmaheśvara \|*  
*parākrameṇa mattulyo na bhūto na bhaviṣyati \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. O lord Śiva, thanks to your favour there is nothing impossible for me. A person equal to me in valour has not been born, nor will he be born.

## \|\| 3.32.33 \|\|

*yatra yatkāryamuddiśya preṣayiṣyasi māṃ prabho \|*  
*tatkāryaṃ sādhayāmyeva satvaraṃ tvatprasādataḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. O lord, wherever you send me and on whatever errand, I shall execute that job quickly and earn your favour.

## \|\| 3.32.34 \|\|

*kṣudrāstaraṃti lokābdhiṃ śāsanācchaṃkarasya te \|*  
*harātohaṃ na kiṃ tartuṃ mahāpatsāgaraṃ kṣamaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. At your bidding, O Śiva, even worthless persons swim across the ocean of the world. O Śiva, am I not therefore competent to cross the ocean of great adversity?

## \|\| 3.32.35 \|\|

*tvatpreṣitatṛṇenāpi mahatkāryaṃ mayatnataḥ \|*  
*kṣaṇena śakyate kartuṃ śaṃkarātra na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. O Śiva, there is no doubt in this that even the blade of grass despatched by you will achieve great tasks without difficulty in a moment.

## \|\| 3.32.36 \|\|

*līlāmātreṇa te śaṃbho kāryaṃ yadyapi siddhyati \|*  
*tathāpyahaṃ preṣaṇīyo tavaivānugraho hyayam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. O Śiva, verily any task can be fulfilled by your mere sport. But it is your blessing and favour, that I shall be sent to do the job.

## \|\| 3.32.37 \|\|

*śaktiretādṛśī śaṃbho mamāpi tvadanugrahāt \|*  
*vinā śaktirna kasyāpi śaṃkara tvadanugrahāt \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. It is by your blessing that I am qualified in this task. O Śiva, without your blessing and favour none will have that power and efficiency.

## \|\| 3.32.38 \|\|

*tvadājñayā vinā kopi tṛṇādīnapi vastutaḥ \|*  
*naiva cālayituṃ śaktassatyametanna saṃśayaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. This is true. There is no doubt in this that without your command and permission no one shall move even a blade of grass.

## \|\| 3.32.39 \|\|

*śaṃbho niyamyāssarvepi devādyāste maheśvara \|*  
*tathaivāhaṃ niyamyaste niyaṃtussarvadehinām \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. O Śiva, devas and others are subject to your control. I too am subject to the control exercised by you. I am the controller of all living beings.

## \|\| 3.32.40 \|\|

*praṇatosmi mahādeva bhūyopi praṇatosmyaham \|*  
*preṣaya sveṣṭa siddhyarthaṃ māmadya hara satvaram \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. O Śiva, I have knelt before you. Again and again I kneel before you. O Śiva send me immediately for the fulfilment of your desire.

## \|\| 3.32.41 \|\|

*spaṃdopi jāyate śaṃbho sakhyāṃgānāṃ muhurmuhuḥ \|*  
*bhaviṣyatyadya vijayo māmataḥ preṣaya prabho \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. O Śiva, my right limbs throb frequently. I am sure to be victorious today. O lord, so please send me.

## \|\| 3.32.42 \|\|

*harṣotsāhaviśeṣopi jāyate mama kaścana \|*  
*śaṃbho tvatpādakamale saṃsaktaśca mano mama \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. I feel a peculiar exhilaration and zeal. O Śiva, my mind sticks to your lotus-like feet.

## \|\| 3.32.43 \|\|

*bhaviṣyati pratipadaṃ śubhasaṃtānasaṃtatiḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. At every step a series of auspicious things and events have occurred.

## \|\| 3.32.44 \|\|

*tasyaiva vijayo nityaṃ tasyaiva śubhamanvaham \|*  
*yasya śaṃbhau dṛḍhā bhaktistvayi śobhanasaṃśraye \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Surely he alone is victorious for ever, his alone is the welfare every day who, O Śiva, is firmly devoted to you who are the resort of everything auspicious.

## \|\| 3.32.45 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityuktaṃ tadvacaḥ śrutvā saṃtuṣṭo maṃgalāpatiḥ \|*  
*vīrabhadra jayeti tvaṃ proktāśīḥ prāha taṃ punaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

45\. On hearing these words of Vīrabhadra, the consort of Satī became glad. He blessed him saying “O Vīrabhadra be victorious” and said these words thereafter:—

## \|\| 3.32.46 \|\|

*maheśvara uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu madvacanaṃ tāta vīrabhadra sucetasā \|*  
*karaṇīyaṃ prayatnena taddrutaṃ me pratoṣakam \|\| 46 \|\|*

Lord Śiva said:—

46\. O dear Vīrabhadra, listen to my words attentively. You must carry them out quickly. It will then delight me.

## \|\| 3.32.47 \|\|

*yāgaṃ kartuṃ samudyukto dakṣo vidhisutaḥ khalaḥ \|*  
*madvirodhī viśeṣeṇa mahāgarvo'budho'dhunā \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Dakṣa, the wicked son of Brahmā, has made arrangement to perform a sacrifice. He is particularly inimical to me. He is unwise and conceited now.

## \|\| 3.32.48 \|\|

*tanmakhaṃ bhasmasātkṛtvā sayāgaparivārakam \|*  
*punarāyāhi matsthānaṃ satvaraṃ gaṇasattama \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. O best of Gaṇas, destroy the sacrifice with all the ancillary adjuncts and then return to my abode quickly.

## \|\| 3.32.49 \|\|

*surā bhavaṃtu gaṃdharvā yakṣā vānye ca kecana \|*  
*tānapyadyaiva sahasā bhasmasātkuru satvaram \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Even if there be devas, Gandharvas, Yakṣas or others, reduce them also to ashes quickly.

## \|\| 3.32.50 \|\|

*tatrāstu viṣṇurbrahmā vā śacīśo vā yamopi vā \|*  
*api cādyaiva tānsarvānpātayasva prayatnataḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Let there be Viṣṇu, Brahmā, Indra or Yama. Fell them to the ground now itself with strenuous efforts.

## \|\| 3.32.51-52 \|\|

*surā bhavaṃtu gaṃdharvā yakṣā vānye ca kecana \|*  
*tānapyadyaiva sahasā bhasmasātkuru satvaram \|\| 51 \|\|*

*dadhīcikṛtamullaṃghya śapathaṃ mayi tatra ye \|*  
*tiṣṭhaṃti te prayatnena jvālanīyāstvayā dhruvam \|\| 52 \|\|*

51-52. Transgressing the imprecations of Dadhīci whoever stays in the sacrifice shall be burnt by you of course.

## \|\| 3.32.53 \|\|

*pramathāścāgamiṣyaṃti yadi viṣṇvādayo bhramāt \|*  
*nānākarṣaṇamaṃtreṇa jvālayānīya satvaram \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. If Viṣṇu and others, out of erroneous notions were to withstand, other gaṇas will come for your help. They shall be burnt by you after dragging them with mantras.

## \|\| 3.32.54 \|\|

*ye tatrollaṃghya śapathaṃ madīyaṃ garvitāḥ sthitāḥ \|*  
*te hi maddrohiṇo'tastān jvālayānalamālayā \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Transgressing my injunctions many haughty persons are lingering there. They are also my enemies. So burn them with a series of blazing fires.

## \|\| 3.32.55 \|\|

*sapatnīkānsasārāṃśca dakṣayāgasthalasthitān \|*  
*prajvālya bhasmasātkṛtvā punarāyāhi satvaram \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. After reducing them to ashes, along with their wives, and all the paraphernalia at the sacrifice of Dakṣa, you shall return quickly.

## \|\| 3.32.56 \|\|

*tatra tvayi gate devā viśvādya api sādaram \|*  
*stoṣyaṃti tvāṃ tadāpyāśu jvālayā jvālayaiva tān \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. It is possible that when you go there, devas and others may praise you. Still you shall burn them in the flames.

## \|\| 3.32.57 \|\|

*devānapi kṛtadrohān jvālāmālāsamākulaḥ \|*  
*jvālaya jvalanaiśśīghraṃ mādhyāyādhyāyapālakam \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Burn the devas too who have committed offence, in the blazing fire, after meditating on me, your protector.

## \|\| 3.32.58 \|\|

*dakṣādīnsakalāṃstatra sapatnīkānsabāṃdhavān \|*  
*prajvālya vīra dakṣaṃ nu salīlaṃ salilaṃ piba \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. After burning Dakṣa and all others along with their wives and kinsmen, without any effort, in a playful manner you shall drink waters.

## \|\| 3.32.59 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityukto roṣatāmrākṣo vedamaryādapālakaḥ \|*  
*virarāma mahāvīraṃ kālārissakaleśvaraḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

59\. After saying thus to Vīrabhadra the great hero, Śiva the lord of all, the slayer of Kāla, the protector of Vedic conventions, stopped, with his eyes still resembling copper (due to anger).

## Chapter 33 - The March of Vīrabhadra

## \|\| 3.33.1 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityuktaṃ śrīmaheśasya śrutvā vacanamādarāt \|*  
*vīrabhadrotisaṃtuṣṭaḥ praṇanāma maheśvarama \|\| 1 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

1\. On hearing these words of lord Śiva with great respect, Vīrabhadra was highly delighted. He bowed to Him.

## \|\| 3.33.2 \|\|

*śāsanaṃ śirasā dhṛtvā devadevasya śūlinaḥ \|*  
*pracacāla tataḥ śīghraṃ vīrabhadro makhaṃ prati \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Receiving his command, with his head bowed down in reverence, Vīrabhadra set off immediately to the place of sacrifice.

## \|\| 3.33.3 \|\|

*śivotha preṣayāmāsa śobhārthaṃ koṭiśo gaṇān \|*  
*tena sārddhaṃ mahāvīrānmalayānalasannibhān \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. To add lustre to the campaign, Śiva sent crores of Gaṇas, very valorous and equal to the fire of dissolution.

## \|\| 3.33.4 \|\|

*atha te vīrabhadrasya purataḥ prabalā gaṇāḥ \|*  
*paścādapi yayurvīrāḥ kutūhalakarā gaṇāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Those powerful Gaṇas enthusiastic and gay both preceded and followed Vīrabhadra.

## \|\| 3.33.5 \|\|

*vīrabhadrasametā yegaṇāśśatasahasraśaḥ \|*  
*pārṣadāḥ kālakālasya sarve rudrasvarūpiṇaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. All the personal attendants of Kālakāla assuming the form of Rudra accompanied Vīrabhadra in their hundreds and thousands.

## \|\| 3.33.6 \|\|

*gaṇaissametaḥ kilatairmahātmā sa vīrabhadro haraveṣabhūṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*sahasrabāhurbhujagādhipāḍhyo yayau rathasthaḥ prabalotibhīkaraḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Accompanied by these Gaṇas, the noble-souled Vīrabhadra who had the same dress, features and embellishments as Śiva went ahead in a chariot. He had a thousand arms each like hoods of the serpent king. He was powerful and terrifying.

## \|\| 3.33.7 \|\|

*nalvānaṃ ca sahasre dve pramāṇaṃ syaṃdanasya hi \|*  
*ayutenaiva siṃhānāṃ vāhanānāṃ prayatnataḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The chariots numbered as many as two thousand Nalvas of land could contain. Ten thousand lions pulled the chariots strenuously.

## \|\| 3.33.8 \|\|

*tathaiva prabalāḥ siṃhā bahavaḥ pārśvarakṣakāḥ \|*  
*śārdūlā makarā matsyā gajāstatra sahasraśaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Many strong lions, tigers, crocodiles, huge fishes and thousands of elephants constituted his body-guard.

## \|\| 3.33.9 \|\|

*vīrabhadre pracalite dakṣanāśāya satvaram \|*  
*kalpavṛkṣasamutsṛṣṭā puṣpavṛṣṭirabhūttadā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. When Vīrabhadra\[2\] set-off quickly for slaying Dakṣa, a shower of flowers fell there let loose by the divine Kalpa tree.

## \|\| 3.33.10 \|\|

*tuṣṭuvuśca gaṇā vīra śipiviṣṭe praceṣṭitam \|*  
*cakruḥ kutūhalaṃ sarve tasmiṃśca gamanotsavaiḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. During the festivities of their march, the Gaṇas eulogised the heroic Vīrabhadra who was carrying out the job of Śiva and they exhibited their enthusiasm.

## \|\| 3.33.11-12 \|\|

*kālī kātyāyinīśānī cāmuṃḍā muṃḍamardinī \|*  
*bhadrakālī tathā bhadrā tvaritā vaiṣṇavī tathā \|\| 11 \|\|*

*etābhirnavadurgābhirmahākālī samanvitā \|*  
*yayau dakṣavināśāya sarvabhūtagaṇaissaha \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. Mahākālī went ahead for the destruction of Dakṣa accompanied by nine Durgās Viz:—Kālī, Kātyāyanī, Īśānī, Cāmuṇḍā, Muṇḍamardinī, Bhadrakālī, Bhadrā, Tvaritā and Vaiṣṇavī and the goblins.

## \|\| 3.33.13-14 \|\|

*ḍākinī śākinī caiva bhūtapramathaguhyakāḥ \|*  
*kūṣmāṃḍāḥ parpaṭā ścaiva caṭakā brahmarākṣasāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*bhairavāḥ kṣetrapālāśca dakṣayajñavināśakāḥ \|*  
*niryayustvaritaṃ vīrāśśivājñāpratipālakāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. Eager in executing the command of Śiva, they accompanied the marching heroes—Ḍākinī, Śākinī, Bhūtas, Pramathas, Guhyakas, Kūṣmāṇḍas, Parpaṭas, Caṭakas, Brahma-Rākṣasas, Bhairavas and Kṣetrapālas and set out quickly for the destruction of Dakṣa’s sacrifice.

## \|\| 3.33.15 \|\|

*tathaiva yoginīcakraṃ catuḥṣaṣṭigaṇānvitam \|*  
*niryayau sahasā kruddhaṃ dakṣayajñaṃ vināśitum \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The host of Yoginīs with their sixty-four groups set out angrily and hurriedly to destroy Dakṣa’s sacrifice.

## \|\| 3.33.16 \|\|

*teṣāṃ gaṇānāṃ sarveṣāṃ saṃkhyānaṃ śṛṇu nārada \|*  
*mahābalavatāṃ saṃghomukhyānāṃ dhairyaśālinām \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. O Nārada, listen to the numerical strength of the most important and courageous of those groups.

## \|\| 3.33.17 \|\|

*abhyayācchaṃkukarṇaśca daśakoṭyā gaṇeśvaraḥ \|*  
*daśabhiḥ kekarākṣaśca vikṛto ṣṭābhireva \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The chief of Gaṇas-Śaṅkukarṇa went ahead with ten crores of his attendants; Kekarākṣa with ten crores and Vikṛta with eight crores.

## \|\| 3.33.18 \|\|

*catuḥṣaṣṭyā viśākhaśca navabhiḥ pāriyātrikaḥ \|*  
*ṣaḍbhissarvāṅgako vīrastathaiva vikṛtānanaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Viśākha with sixty-four crores, Pāriyātraka with nine crores; Sarvāṅkaka and the heroic Vikṛtānana each with six crores.

## \|\| 3.33.19 \|\|

*jvālakeśo dvādaśabhiḥ koṭibhirgaṇapuṃgavaḥ \|*  
*saptabhiḥ samadajjīmān dudrabhoṣṭābhireva ca \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The chief of Gaṇas, Jvālakeśa went with twelve crores; Dhīmān with seven crores and Dudrabha with eight crores.

## \|\| 3.33.20 \|\|

*paṃcabhiśca kapālīśaḥ ṣaḍbhissaṃdārako gaṇaḥ \|*  
*koṭikoṭibhireveha koṭikuṇḍastathaiva ca \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Kapālīśa with five crores and the Sandāraka group. with six crores; Koṭikuṇḍa with crores of crores.

## \|\| 3.33.21 \|\|

*viṣṭaṃbho'ṣṭābhirvīraiḥ koṭibhirgaṇasaptamaḥ \|*  
*sahasrakoṭibhistāta saṃnādaḥ pippalastathā \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Viṣṭambha, the most excellent of the Gaṇas, went with sixty-four crores of heroes. O dear, Sannāda and Pippala went with a thousand crores.

## \|\| 3.33.22 \|\|

*āveśanastathāṣṭābhiraṣṭābhiścaṃdratāpanaḥ \|*  
*mahāveśaḥ sahasreṇa koṭinā gaṇapo vṛtaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Āveśana went with eight crores and Candratāpana too with eight crores. Mahāveśa, the chief of Gaṇas, was accompanied by a thousand crores.

## \|\| 3.33.23 \|\|

*kuṇḍī dvādaśakoṭībhistathā parvatako mune \|*  
*vināśituṃ dakṣayajñaṃ niryayau gaṇasattama \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. O sage, Kuṇḍī the most excellent of the Gaṇas and Pavataka went each with twelve crores in order to destroy Dakṣa’s sacrifice.

## \|\| 3.33.24 \|\|

*kālaśca kālakaścaiva mahākālastathaiva ca \|*  
*koṭīnāṃ śatakenaiva dakṣayajñaṃ yayau prati \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Kāla, Kālaka and Mahākāla went to the sacrifice of Dakṣa with a hundred crores.

## \|\| 3.33.25 \|\|

*agnikṛcchatakoṭyā ca koṭyāgnimukha eva ca \|*  
*ādityamūrddhā koṭyā ca tathā caiva ghanāvahaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Agnikṛt with hundred crores; Agnimukha with a crore; Ādityamūrdhā and Ghanāvaha each with a crore.

## \|\| 3.33.26 \|\|

*sannāhaśśatakoṭyā ca koṭyā ca kumudo gaṇaḥ \|*  
*amoghaḥ kokilaścaiva koṭikoṭyā gaṇādhipaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Sannāha with hundred crores; Kumuda with a crore; Amogha and Kokila the chief of Gaṇas each with a crore of crores.

## \|\| 3.33.27 \|\|

*kāṣṭhāgūḍhaścatuḥṣaṣṭyā sukeśī vṛṣabhastathā \|*  
*sumantrako gaṇādhīśastathā tāta suniryayau \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Kāṣṭhāgūḍha, Sukeśī, Vṛṣabha, and Sumantraka the chief of Gaṇas, O dear, each went with sixty-four crores.

## \|\| 3.33.28 \|\|

*kākapādodaraḥ ṣaṣṭikoṭibhirgaṇasattamaḥ \|*  
*tathā santānakaḥ ṣaṣṭikoṭibhirgaṇapuṃgavaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Kākapādodara and Santānaka both excellent chiefs of Gaṇas went with sixty crores each.

## \|\| 3.33.29 \|\|

*mahābalaśca navabhiḥ koṭibhiḥ puṃgavastathā \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Mahābala as well as Puṅgava went with nine crores each.

## \|\| 3.33.30 \|\|

*madhupiṃgastathā tāta gaṇādhīśo hi niryayau \|*  
*nīlo navatyā koṭīnāṃ pūrṇabhadrastathaiva ca \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. O dear, the chief of Gaṇas, Madhupiṅga was the leader of ninety crores. Pūrṇabhadra also started with as many attendants.

## \|\| 3.33.31 \|\|

*niryayau śatakoṭībhiścaturvaktro gaṇādhipaḥ \|*  
*kāṣṭhāgūḍheścatuṣṣaṣṭyā sukeśo vṛṣabhastathā \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Caturvaktra, the chief of Gaṇas, started with hundred crores.

## \|\| 3.33.32 \|\|

*virūpākṣaśca koṭīnāṃ catuḥṣaṣṭyā gaṇeśvaraḥ \|*  
*tālaketuḥ ṣaḍāsyaśca paṃcāsyaśca gaṇādhipaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Virūpākṣa, the lord of Gaṇas, with sixty-four crores. So also the chiefs of Gaṇas Tālaketu, Ṣaḍāsya and Pañcāsya.

## \|\| 3.33.33-34 \|\|

*saṃvartakastathā caiva kulīśaśca svayaṃ prabhuḥ \|*  
*lokāṃtakaśca dīptātmā tathā daityāntako mune \|\| 33 \|\|*

*gaṇo bhṛṃgīriṭiḥ śrīmān devadevapriyastathā \|*  
*aśanirbhālakaścaiva catuḥṣaṣṭyā sahsrakaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

33-34. O sage, Saṃvartaka, Kulīśa, Svayamprabhu, Lokāntaka, Dīptātmā, Daityāntaka, Bhṛṅgīriṭi, Devadevapriya, Aśani and Bhālaka each went with sixty-four thousand Gaṇas.

## \|\| 3.33.35 \|\|

*koṭikoṭisahasrāṇāṃ śatairviṃśa tibhirvṛtaḥ \|*  
*vīreśo hyabhyayādvīraḥ vīrabhadra śivājñayā \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Thus at the bidding of Śiva, the heroic Vīrabhadra went ahead followed by crores and crores, thousands and thousands, hundreds and hundreds of Gaṇas.

## \|\| 3.33.36 \|\|

*bhūtakoṭisahasraistu prayayau koṭibhistribhiḥ \|*  
*romajaiḥ śvagaṇai ścaiva tathā vīro yayau drutam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. The hero was accompanied by thousands of crores of goblins, and three crores of canine species born of the hair of Śiva. He went ahead quickly.

## \|\| 3.33.37 \|\|

*tadā bherīmahānādaḥ śaṃkhāśca vividhasvanāḥ \|*  
*jaṭāharomukhāścaiva śṛṃgāṇi vividhāni ca \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Trumpets and drums sounded loudly. Conchs blew in diverse ways. Horns of all kinds were blown.

## \|\| 3.33.38 \|\|

*te tāni vitatānyeva baṃdhanāni sukhāni ca \|*  
*vāditrāṇi vineduśca vividhāni mahotsave \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. In that joyous festivity various musical instruments were played in a pleasing manner.

## \|\| 3.33.39 \|\|

*vīrabhadrasya yātrāyāṃ sabalasya mahāmune \|*  
*śakunānyabhavaṃstatra bhūrīṇi sukhadāni ca \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. While the march of Vīrabhadra was in progress, O great sage, many pleasing fortutious omens occurred.

## Chapter 34 - The devas witness bad omens at the place of sacrifice

## \|\| 3.34.1 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*evaṃ pracalite cāsmin vīrabhadre gaṇānvite \|*  
*duṣṭacihnāni dakṣeṇa dṛṣṭāni vibudhairapi \|\| 1 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

1\. When Vīrabhadra set off thus, bad omens were seen by Dakṣa and the devas.

## \|\| 3.34.2 \|\|

*utpātā vividhāścāsan vīrabhadre gaṇānvite \|*  
*trividhā api devarṣe yajñavidhvaṃsasūcakāḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. O celestial sage, when Vīrabhadra accompanied by the Gaṇas proceeded thus, many portentous phenomena occurred at the sacrifice of Dakṣa including the three evil omens, boding the imminent destruction of Dakṣa’s sacrifice.

## \|\| 3.34.3 \|\|

*dakṣavāmākṣibāhūruvispaṃdassamajāyata \|*  
*nānākaṣṭapradastāta sarvathā'śubhasūcakaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The left eye, arm and thigh of Dakṣa throbbed. In every respect, it indicated everything inauspicious It was harassing to him.

## \|\| 3.34.4 \|\|

*bhūkaṃpassamabhūttatra dakṣayāgasthale tadā \|*  
*dakṣopaśyacca madhyāhne nakṣatrāṇyadbhutāni ca \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. There was an earthquake at the site of sacrifice. Dakṣa observed the mysterious phenomena of stars at noon.

## \|\| 3.34.5 \|\|

*diśaścāsansumalināḥ karburobhūddivākaraḥ \|*  
*pariveṣasahasreṇa saṃkrāṃtaśca bhayaṃkaraḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The quarters became dirty and gloomy. The sun appeared spotted and terrifying with thousands of circlets all round.

## \|\| 3.34.6 \|\|

*nakṣatrāṇi pataṃti sma vidyudagniprabhāṇi ca \|*  
*nakṣatrāṇāmabhūdvakrā gatiścādhomukhī tadā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Stars, brilliant like lightning and blazing fire were seen falling. Some of them went zigzag and some fell with face downwards.

## \|\| 3.34.7 \|\|

*gṛdhrā dakṣa śiraḥ spṛṣṭvā samudbhūtāḥ sahasraśaḥ \|*  
*āsīdgṛdhrapakṣacchāyaissacchāyo yāgamaṃḍapaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Thousands of vultures hovered above touching Dakṣa’s head. Shadows of these darkened the sacrificial platform.

## \|\| 3.34.8 \|\|

*vavāśire yāgabhūmau kroṣṭāro netrakastadā \|*  
*ulkāvṛṣṭirabhūttatra śvetavṛścikasaṃbhavā \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Jackals howled in the surroundings of the sacrificial ground. The evil star Netraka and meteors seemed to fall like white scorpions.

## \|\| 3.34.9 \|\|

*kharā vātā vavustatra pāṃśuvṛṣṭisamanvitāḥ \|*  
*śalabhāśca samudbhūtā vivartānilakaṃpitāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Rough winds raising a lot of dust blew there. Locusts and moths were tossed about by whirlwinds.

## \|\| 3.34.10 \|\|

*rītaiśca pavanai rūrddhvaṃ sa dakṣādhvaramaṃḍapaḥ \|*  
*daivānvitena dakṣeṇa yaḥ kṛto nūtanodbhutaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The wonderfully new sacrificial platform erected by Dakṣa and the devas was thrown up by the winds.

## \|\| 3.34.11 \|\|

*vemurdakṣādayassarve tadā śoṇitamadbhutam \|*  
*vemuśca māṃsakhaṇḍāni saśalyāni muhurmuhuḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Surprisingly enough, Dakṣa and others vomitted blood, pieces of flesh and bones very frequently.

## \|\| 3.34.12 \|\|

*sakaṃpāśca babhūvuste dīpā vātahatā iva \|*  
*duḥkhitāścābhavansarve śastradhārāhatā iva \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. They became unsteady and tremulous like lamps blown by wind. They felt miserable as if struck with the sharp edges of weapons.

## \|\| 3.34.13-14 \|\|

*tadā ninādajātāni bāṣpavarṣāṇi tatkṣaṇe \|*  
*prātastuṣāravarṣīṇi padmānīva vanāṃtare \|\| 13 \|\|*

*dakṣādyakṣīṇi jātāni hyakasmādviśadānyapi \|*  
*niśāyāṃ kamalāścaiva kumudānīva saṃgave \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. The eyes of Dakṣa and others sometimes resembled the fading lotuses of the summer; sometimes they resembled the flowers in forests with dews trickling from them; sometimes they seemed like lotuses at night and sometimes like Kumuda flowers in the forenoon.

## \|\| 3.34.15 \|\|

*asṛgvavarṣa devaśca timireṇāvṛtā diśaḥ \|*  
*digdāhobhūdviśeṣeṇa trāsayan sakalāñjanān \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The deities seemed to shower blood; the quarters became enveloped in darkness; there was a peculiar blaze everywhere terrifying all.

## \|\| 3.34.16 \|\|

*evaṃ vidhānyariṣṭāni dadṛśurvibudhādayaḥ \|*  
*bhayamāpedire'tyaṃtaṃ mune viṣṇvādikāstadā \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. O sage, devas and others saw such evil portents as these. Viṣṇu and others were struck with great fear.

## \|\| 3.34.17 \|\|

*bhuvi te mūrchitāḥ peturhā hatāḥ sma itīrayan \|*  
*taravastīrasaṃjātā nadīvegahatā iva \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. “Ha, we are doomed” saying thus they fell unconscious on the ground like trees on the edges of rivers when felled by the force of the current.

## \|\| 3.34.18 \|\|

*patitvā te sthitā bhūmau krūrāḥ sarpā hatā iva \|*  
*kaṃdukā iva te bhūyaḥ patitāḥ punarutthitāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Fallen on the ground they remained motionless like cruel serpents struck dead. Sometimes those fallen bounced up like balls.

## \|\| 3.34.19 \|\|

*tataste tāpasaṃtaptā ruruduḥ kurarī iva \|*  
*rodanadhvanisaṃkrātoruktipratyuktikā iva \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Then due to extreme distress they cried like twittering sparrows. Their groans and their voices got confusingly mingled with each other.

## \|\| 3.34.20 \|\|

*savaikuṃṭhāstatassarve tadā kuṃṭhitaśaktayaḥ \|*  
*svasvopakaṃṭhamākaṃṭhaṃ luluṭhuḥ kamaṭhā iva \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Everyone including Viṣṇu had their power blunted and impeded. They rolled and dashed against one another like tortoises.

## \|\| 3.34.21 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare tatra saṃjātā cāśarīravāk \|*  
*śrāvayatyakhilān devāndakṣaṃ caiva viśeṣataḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. In the meantime a disembodied voice arose there within the hearing of the devas and that of Dakṣa particularly. The ethereal voice said.

## \|\| 3.34.22 \|\|

*ākāśavāṇyuvāca \|*  
*dhik janma tava dakṣādya mahāmūḍhosi pāpadhīḥ \|*  
*bhaviṣyati mahadduḥkhamanivāryaṃ harodbhavam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Fie upon your life now, O Dakṣa. You are evil-minded and excessively foolish. Great misery caused by Śiva will inevitably befall you.

## \|\| 3.34.23 \|\|

*hāhāpi notra ye mūḍhāstava devādayasthitāḥ \|*  
*teṣāmapi mahāduḥkhaṃ bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Certainly great misery will befall those foolish devas and others who are here crying out “Hā Hā”.

## \|\| 3.34.24 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|\| tacchrutvākāśavacanaṃ dṛṣṭvāriṣṭāni tāni ca \|*  
*dakṣaḥ prāpadbhayaṃ cāti pare devādayopi ha \|\| 24 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

24\. On hearing that voice of the sky, and seeing those ill omens, Dakṣa was terribly afraid. The others—devas etc.—too followed suit.

## \|\| 3.34.25 \|\|

*vepamānastadā dakṣo vikalaścāti cetasi \|*  
*agacchaccharaṇaṃ viṣṇoḥ svaprabhoriṃdirāpateḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Trembling miserably and utterly shaken, Dakṣa sought refuge in Viṣṇu, the consort of Lakṣmī and his own lord.

## \|\| 3.34.26 \|\|

*supraṇamya bhayāviṣṭaḥ saṃstūya ca vicetanaḥ \|*  
*avocaddevadevaṃ taṃ viṣṇuṃ svajanavatsalam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Making humble obeisance in his fright, and eulogising in his mental distress, he said thus to Viṣṇu endearing to his own men.

## Chapter 35 - Viṣṇu’s statement

## \|\| 3.35.1 \|\|

*dakṣa uvāca \|*  
*devadeva hare viṣṇo dīnabaṃdho kṛpānidhe \|*  
*mama rakṣā vidhātavyā bhavatā sādhvarasya ca \|\| 1 \|\|*

Dakṣa said:—

1\. O Hari, Viṣṇu, lord of devas, friend of the poor, storehouse of mercy, you must protect me and my sacrifice.

## \|\| 3.35.2 \|\|

*rakṣakastvaṃ makhasyaiva makhakarmā makhātmakaḥ \|*  
*kṛpā vidheyā yajñasya bhaṃgo bhavatu na prabho \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. You are the guardian of sacrifice. You are identical with the activity of sacrifice, the performer of sacrifice; O lord, be merciful, let not the sacrifice be destroyed.

## \|\| 3.35.3 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*itthaṃ bahuvidhāṃ dakṣaḥ kṛtvā vijñaptimādarāt \|*  
*papāta pādayostasya bhayavyākulamānasaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

3\. Thus submitting entreaties of diverse sorts with great respect, in his mental agitation due to fear, he fell at his feet.

## \|\| 3.35.4 \|\|

*utthāpya taṃ tato viṣṇurdakṣaṃ viklinnamānasam \|*  
*śrutvā ca tasya tadvākyaṃ kumaterasmaracchivam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Viṣṇu raised Dakṣa of agitated mind and on hearing the words of that evil-minded one, Viṣṇu remembered Śiva.

## \|\| 3.35.5 \|\|

*smṛtvā śivaṃ maheśānaṃ svaprabhuṃ parameśvaram \|*  
*avadacchivatattvajño dakṣaṃ sabodhayanhariḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. After remembering Śiva his own lord, Viṣṇu, the knower of Śiva’s principles, said thus, addressing Dakṣa:—

## \|\| 3.35.6 \|\|

*hariruvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu dakṣa pravakṣyāmi tattvataḥ śṛṇu me vacaḥ \|*  
*sarvathā te hitakaraṃ mahāmaṃtrasukhapradam \|\| 6 \|\|*

Viṣṇu said:—

6\. Listen, O Dakṣa, I shall explain everything true to fact; listen to my words which are as efficacious as mantras, beneficent and pleasing.

## \|\| 3.35.7 \|\|

*avajñā hi kṛtā dakṣa tvayā tattvamajānatā \|*  
*sakalādhīśvarasyaiva śaṃkarasya parātmanaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Not knowing the principle of Śiva, the great Self and lord of everything, you have insulted Him.

## \|\| 3.35.8 \|\|

*īśvarāvajñayā sarvaṃ kāryaṃ bhavati sarvathā \|*  
*viphalaṃ kevalaṃ naiva vipattiśca padepade \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. By insulting Him, not only does every activity become futile in every respect but also it engenders adversities at every step.

## \|\| 3.35.9 \|\|

*apūjyā yatra pūjyaṃte pūjanīyo na pūjyate \|*  
*trīṇi tatra bhaviṣyaṃti dāridryaṃ maraṇaṃ bhayam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Poverty, death and fear, these three take place when people worthy of worship are not worshipped and when undeserving people are honoured.

## \|\| 3.35.10 \|\|

*tasmātsarvaprayatnena mānanīyo vṛṣadhvajaḥ \|*  
*amānitānmaheśācca mahadbhayamupasthitam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Hence with all efforts, the bull-bannered deity shall be respected and revered. A great terror has befallen us because lord Śiva has been dishonoured here.

## \|\| 3.35.11 \|\|

*adyāpi na vayaṃ sarve prabhavaḥ prabhavāmahe \|*  
*bhavato durnayenaiva mayā satyamudīryyate \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Although we are all lords, we are unable to accomplish anything due to your misdeeds. It is a fact I am mentioning.

## \|\| 3.35.12 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*viṣṇostadvacanaṃ śrutvā dakṣaściṃtāparo'bhavat \|*  
*vivarṇavadano bhūtvā tūṣṇīmāsīdbhuvi sthitaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

12\. On hearing these words of Viṣṇu, Dakṣa began to ponder. He sat quietly on the ground with his face turned pale.

## \|\| 3.35.13 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare vīrabhadraḥ sainyasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*agacchadadhvaraṃ rudraprerito gaṇanāyakaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Meanwhile Vīrabhadra, the leader of the Gaṇas, sent by Rudra, came to the place of sacrifice accompanied by his army.

## \|\| 3.35.14-15 \|\|

*pṛṣṭhe kecitsamāyātā gagane kecidāgatāḥ \|*  
*diśaśca vidiśaḥ sarve samāvṛtya tathāpare \|\| 14 \|\|*

*śarvājñayā gaṇāḥ śūrā nirbhayā rudravikramāḥ \|*  
*asaṃkhyāḥ siṃhanādānvai kurvaṃto vīrasattamāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. Some of his attendants followed him closely; some came through the sky and others came from the different quarters and sub-quarters. At the bidding of Śiva, these innumerable heroic, fearless Gaṇas came there roaring like lions.

## \|\| 3.35.16 \|\|

*tena nādena mahatā nāditaṃ bhuvanatrayam \|*  
*rajasā cāvṛtaṃ vyoma tamasā cāvṛtā diśaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. By that great sound, the three worlds echoed and the quarters were plunged in darkness.

## \|\| 3.35.17 \|\|

*saptadvīpānvitā pṛthvī cacālāti bhayākulā \|*  
*saśailakānanā tatra cukṣubhussakalābdhayaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The whole earth containing the seven continents shook with fear. All the oceans, forests and mountains were excessively agitated.

## \|\| 3.35.18 \|\|

*evaṃbhūtaṃ ca tatsainyaṃ lokakṣayakaraṃ mahat \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā ca vismitāssarve babhūvuramarādayaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. On seeing that vast army of destructive potentiality, devas and others were quite surprised.

## \|\| 3.35.19 \|\|

*sainyodyogamathālokya dakṣaścāsṛṅmukhākulaḥ \|*  
*daṃḍavatpatito viṣṇuṃ sakalatro'bhyabhāṣata \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. On seeing the enterprising activity of the army, Dakṣa’s face turned red with agitation. He fell at the feet of Viṣṇu straight like a staff, prostrated at his feet, along with his wife and said thus.

## \|\| 3.35.20 \|\|

*\|\| dakṣa uvāca \|*  
*bhavadbalenaiva mayā yajñaḥ prāraṃbhito mahān \|*  
*satkarmasiddhaye viṣṇo pramāṇaṃ tvaṃ mahāprabho \|\| 20 \|\|*

Dakṣa said:—

20\. Depending upon you, this great sacrifice was started by me. O Viṣṇu, great lord, you are the final authority in the matter of realising good rites.

## \|\| 3.35.21 \|\|

*viṣṇo tvaṃ karmaṇāṃ sākṣī yajñānāṃ pratipālakaḥ \|*  
*dharmasya vedagarbhasya brahmaṇastvaṃ mahāprabho \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. O Viṣṇu you are the cosmic witness of sacred rites and the protector of sacrifices. You are the saviour of Vedic virtue, O great lord.

## \|\| 3.35.22 \|\|

*tasmādrakṣā vidhātavyā yajñasyāsya mama prabho \|*  
*tvadanyaḥ yassamarthosti yatastvaṃ sakalaprabhuḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Hence, O lord, you shall offer protection to my sacrifice here. Who else, other than you, is competent for it? You are the lord of all.

## \|\| 3.35.23 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*dakṣasya vacanaṃ śrutvā viṣṇurdīnataraṃ tadā \|*  
*avocadbodhayaṃstaṃ vai śivatattvaparāṅmukham \|\| 23 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

23\. On hearing these piteous words of Dakṣa, Viṣṇu spoke enlightening Dakṣa who was averse to Śiva’s principles.

## \|\| 3.35.24 \|\|

*viṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*mayā rakṣā vidhātavyā tava yajñasya dakṣa vai \|*  
*khyāto mama paṇaḥ satyo dharmasya paripālanam \|\| 24 \|\|*

Viṣṇu said:—

24\. O Dakṣa, protection shall be offered to your sacrifice. My promise of protecting Dharma is truly well known.

## \|\| 3.35.25 \|\|

*tatsatyaṃ tu tvayoktaṃ hi kiṃ tattasya vyatikramaḥ \|*  
*śṛṇu tvaṃ vacmyahaṃ dakṣa krūrabuddhiṃ tyajā'dhunā \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. You have stated the truth, but you have transgressed the same. O Dakṣa listen, I shall tell you. Cast off your cruelty.

## \|\| 3.35.26 \|\|

*naimiṣe nimiṣakṣetre yajjātaṃ vṛttamadbhutam \|*  
*tatkiṃ na smaryate dakṣa vismṛtaṃ kiṃ kubuddhinā \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. What transpired at Naimiṣa, the holy place in a surprisingly mysterious manner is evidently not remembered by you, O Dakṣa. Did you forget it in your evil way?

## \|\| 3.35.27 \|\|

*rudrakopācca ko hyatra samartho rakṣaṇe tava \|*  
*na yasyābhimataṃ dakṣa yastvāṃ rakṣati durmatiḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Who can save you from Rudra’s anger? O Dakṣa, a person who protects you, the wicked one, finds no approval anywhere.

## \|\| 3.35.28 \|\|

*kiṃ karma kimakarmeti tatra paśyasi durmate \|*  
*samarthaṃ kevalaṃ karma na bhaviṣyati sarvadā \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. An evil-minded man does not see what is good and what is not. A sacred action or rite cannot be efficacious always.

## \|\| 3.35.29 \|\|

*svakarmaviddhi tadyena samarthatvena jāyate \|*  
*na tvanyaḥ karmaṇo dātā śaṃ bhavedīśvaraṃ vinā \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. You must know that to be your duty which is naturally efficacious. Except Śiva none can be the bestower of action.

## \|\| 3.35.30 \|\|

*īśvarasya ca yo bhaktyā śāṃtastadgatamānasaḥ \|*  
*karmaṇo hi phalaṃ tasya prayacchati tadā śivaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Śiva bestows the fruit of the actions upon the person who is tranquil on account of devotion to the lord and whose mind is fixed in him alone.

## \|\| 3.35.31 \|\|

*kevalaṃ jñānamāśritya nirīśvaraparā narāḥ \|*  
*nirayaṃ te ca gacchaṃti kalpakoṭiśatāni ca \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Depending upon Knowledge alone if they eschew devotion to God they will fall into hell and remain there for hundreds of crores of Kalpas.

## \|\| 3.35.32 \|\|

*punaḥ karmamayaiḥ pāśairvaddhā janmani janmani \|*  
*nirayeṣu prapacyaṃte kevalaṃ karmarūpiṇaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Those who solely depend on actions are bound by its nooses, are born in lives after lives and are finally scorched and tortured in hells.

## \|\| 3.35.33 \|\|

*ayaṃ rudragaṇādhīśo vīrabhadro'ri mardanaḥ \|*  
*rudrakopāgnisaṃbhūtaḥ samāyātodhvarāṃgaṇe \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Here, Vīrabhadra, the chief of Rudra’s attendants, who suppresses all his enemies and who is born of the fire of Rudra’s anger has now come to the sacrificial yard.

## \|\| 3.35.34 \|\|

*ayamasmadvināśārthamāgatosti na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*aśakyamasya nāstyeva kimapyastu tu vastutaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. There is no doubt in this that he has come for destroying us. There is nothing impossible for him to do, whatever it may be really.

## \|\| 3.35.35 \|\|

*prajvālyāsmānayaṃ sarvān dhruvameva mahāprabhuḥ \|*  
*tataḥ praśāṃtahṛdayo bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. It is certain that this great lord will become tranquil only after burning us all.

## \|\| 3.35.36 \|\|

*śrīmahādevaśapathaṃ samullaṃghya bhramānmayā \|*  
*yataḥ sthitaṃ tataḥ prāpyaṃ mayā duḥkhaṃ tvayā saha \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Since by my mistake I have transgressed the affirmation of lord Śiva, I too shall bear the miseries along with you.

## \|\| 3.35.37 \|\|

*śaktirmama tu nāstyeva dakṣādyaitannivāraṇe \|*  
*śapathollaṃghanādeva śivadrohī yatosmyaham \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. O Dakṣa, I have no power to prevent this since I have become an enemy of Śiva by transgressing his affirmation.

## \|\| 3.35.38 \|\|

*kālatrayepi na yato maheśadrohiṇāṃ sukham \|*  
*tato'vaśyaṃ mayā prāptaṃ duḥkhamadya tvayā saha \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. There can be no happiness to the enemies of Śiva in the three periods of time; misery has of necessity been invited by me along with you.

## \|\| 3.35.39 \|\|

*sudarśanābhidhaṃ cakrametasminna lagiṣyati \|*  
*śaivacakramidaṃ yasmādaśaivalayakāraṇam \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. My discus Sudarśana will not hit him. My discus is Śaiva (belonging to Śiva) and it can cause the death of only non-Śaivas.

## \|\| 3.35.40 \|\|

*vināpi vīrabhadreṇa nāmaitaccakramaiśvaram \|*  
*hatvā gamiṣyatyadhunā satvaraṃ harasannidhau \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Even if Vīrabhadra had not been here, this discus would have killed us and returned to Siva.

## \|\| 3.35.41 \|\|

*śaivaṃ śapathamullaṃghya sthitaṃ māṃ cakramīdṛśam \|*  
*asaṃhatyaiva sahasā kṛpayaiva sthiraṃ param \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. This discus has remained without killing me, although I had transgressed the avowal of Śiva. It indicates that it is compassionate.

## \|\| 3.35.42 \|\|

*ataḥ paramidaṃ cakramapi na sthāsyati dhruvam \|*  
*gamiṣyatyadhunā śīghraṃ jvālāmālāsamākulam \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Hereafter this discus will not stay with me. With its fiery effusions it will depart quickly.

## \|\| 3.35.43 \|\|

*vīrabhadraḥ pūjitopi śīghramasmābhirādarāt \|*  
*mahākrodhasamākrāṃto nāsmānsaṃrakṣayiṣyati \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Even if he is worshipped and honoured by us with respect, Vīrabhadra will not protect us since he is extremely angry.

## \|\| 3.35.44 \|\|

*akāṃḍapralayo'smākamāgatodya hi hā hahā \|*  
*hā hā bata tavedānīṃ nāśosmākamupasthitaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. A sudden dissolution of every one of us is imminent. Alas, it has already set upon us.

## \|\| 3.35.45 \|\|

*śaraṇyo'smākamadhunā nāstyeva hi jagattraye \|*  
*śaṃkaradrohiṇo loke kaśśaraṇyo bhaviṣyati \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. There is none to offer us refuge in the three worlds. Who can be the refuge of an enemy of Śiva in this world?

## \|\| 3.35.46 \|\|

*tanunāśepi saṃprāpyāstaiścāpi yamayātanāḥ \|*  
*tānaiva śakyate soḍhuṃ bahuduḥkhapradāyinīḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Even if the body undergoes destruction, the torture at the hands of Yama is in store for us. It is impossible to bear as it generates much misery.

## \|\| 3.35.47 \|\|

*śivadrohiṇamālokya daṣṭadaṃto yamaḥ svayam \|*  
*taptatailakaṭāheṣu pātayatyeva nānyathā \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. On seeing an enemy of Śiva, Yama gnashes his teeth. He puts him in cauldrons of oil and not otherwise.

## \|\| 3.35.48 \|\|

*gantumevāhamudyuktaṃ sarvathā śapathottaram \|*  
*tathāpi na gataśśīghraṃ duṣṭasaṃsargapāpataḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Actually I was preparing to leave after an open declaration. Still I did not leave immediately by the contagious sin of this wicked person.

## \|\| 3.35.49 \|\|

*yadadya kriyatesmābhiḥ palāyanamitastadā \|*  
*śārvo nā karṣakaśśastrairasmānākarṣayiṣyati \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Even if we flee from this place, Vīrabhadra the devotee of Śiva, will drag and pull us by means of his weapons.

## \|\| 3.35.50 \|\|

*svarge vā bhuvi pātāle yatra kutrāpi vā yataḥ \|*  
*śrīvīrabhadraśastrāṇāṃ gamanaṃ na hi durla bham \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Whether it is heaven or earth, Pātāla or any where else, it is not difficult for the weapons of Vīrabhadra to gain access there.

## \|\| 3.35.51 \|\|

*yāvataśca gaṇāssaṃti śrīrudrasya triśūlinaḥ \|*  
*tāvatāmapi sarveṣāṃ śaktiretādṛśī dhuvam \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Such is the power of everyone of the attendants of the trident-bearing Rudra.

## \|\| 3.35.52 \|\|

*śrīkālabhairavaḥ kāśyāṃ nakhāgreṇaiva līlayā \|*  
*purā śiraśca ciccheda paṃcamaṃ brahmaṇo dhruvam \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Formerly at Kāśī, Kālabhairava had plucked off the fifth head of Brahmā playfully with the tip of his nail.

## \|\| 3.35.53 \|\|

*etaduktvā sthito viṣṇuratitrastamukhāmbujaḥ \|*  
*vīrabhadropi saṃprāpa tadaivā'dhvaramaṃḍapam \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. After saying this, Viṣṇu resumed his seat, his lotus-face showing signs of great fear. At the same time Vīrabhadra too reached the sacrificial platform.

## \|\| 3.35.54 \|\|

*evaṃ bruvati govinda āgataṃ sainyasāgaram \|*  
*vīrabhadreṇa sahitaṃ dadṛśuśca surādayā \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. While Viṣṇu was saying this, the gods and others saw the vast ocean of the army led by Vīrabhadra already come there.

## Chapter 36 - The dialogue between Viṣṇu and Vīrabhadra

## \|\| 3.36.1 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*indro'pi prahasan viṣṇumātmavādarataṃ tadā \|*  
*vajrapāṇissuraissārddhaṃ yoddhukāmo'bhavattadā \|\| 1 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

1\. Indra mocked at Viṣṇu who was engrossed in his own arguments. He, the bearer of the thunderbolt, was desirous of fighting Vīrabhadra along with the other devas.

## \|\| 3.36.2 \|\|

*tadendro gajamārūḍho bastārūḍho'nalastathā \|*  
*yamo mahiṣamārūḍho nirṛtiḥ pretameva ca \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Then Indra rode on his elephant, the fire-god rode on a goat, Yama rode on his buffalo and Nirṛti rode on a ghost.

## \|\| 3.36.3 \|\|

*pāśī ca makarārūḍho mṛgārūḍho ssadāgatiḥ \|*  
*kuberaḥ puṣpakārūḍhassaṃnaddhobhūdataṃdritaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Varuṇa rode on a crocodile; the wind-god rode on a deer; Kubera sat in his chariot Puṣpaka and he was ready and alert.

## \|\| 3.36.4 \|\|

*tathānye surasaṃghāśca yakṣacāraṇaguhyakāḥ \|*  
*āruhya vāhanānyeva svāni svāni pratāpinaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The others in the hosts of devas, Yakṣas, Cāraṇas and Guhyakas all very powerful, rode on their own respective vehicles.

## \|\| 3.36.5 \|\|

*teṣāmudyogamālokya dakṣaścāsṛṅmukhastathā \|*  
*tadaṃtikaṃ samāgatya sakalatro'bhyabhāṣata \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Seeing their enterprise, Dakṣa with blood rushing to his face in his excitement approached them along with his wife and spoke.

## \|\| 3.36.6 \|\|

*dakṣauvāca \|*  
*yuṣmadbalenaiva mayā yajñaḥ prāraṃbhito mahān \|*  
*satkarmasiddhaye yūyaṃ pramāṇāssyurmahāprabhāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

Dakṣa said:—

6\. Depending on your support and strength alone have I begun this great sacrifice. Such brilliant persons as you, are authorities in the achievement of all good actions.

## \|\| 3.36.7 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*tacchrutvā dakṣavacanaṃ sarve devāssavāsavāḥ \|*  
*niryayustvaritaṃ tatra yuddhaṃ kartuṃ samudyatāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

7\. On hearing these words of Dakṣa. the gods including Indra set off immediately in their readiness to fight.

## \|\| 3.36.8 \|\|

*atha devagaṇāḥ sarve yuyudhuste balānvitāḥ \|*  
*śakrādayo lokapālā mohitāḥ śivamāyayā \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Indra and other devas and the guardians of the quarters, deluded by Śiva’s Māyā fought with their full power.

## \|\| 3.36.9 \|\|

*devānāṃ ca gaṇānāṃ ca tadāsītsamaro mahān \|*  
*tīkṣṇatomaranārācairyuyudhuste parasparam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. A great fight ensued between the devas and the gaṇas. Those powerful warriors fought with each other with sharp spikes, iron clubs etc.

## \|\| 3.36.10 \|\|

*neduśśaṃkhāśca bheryyaśca tasmin raṇamahotsave \|*  
*mahāduṃdubhayo neduḥ paṭahā ḍiṃḍimādayaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Conchs were blown. Drums were beaten in that great war festival. Battle drums were sounded both big and small.

## \|\| 3.36.11 \|\|

*tena śabdena mahatā ślāghmānāstadā surāḥ \|*  
*lokapālaiśca sahitā jaghnustāñchivakiṃkarān \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Being encouraged by that sound, the devas in the company of the guardians of the quarters hit and thrashed the attendants of Śiva.

## \|\| 3.36.12 \|\|

*indrādyairlokapālaiśca gaṇāśśaṃbho parāṅmukhāḥ \|*  
*kṛttāśca muniśārdūla bhṛgormaṃtrabalena ca \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. O excellent sage, on account of the incantations of Bhṛgu,the attendants of Śiva were routed by Indra and other guardians of the quarters.

## \|\| 3.36.13 \|\|

*uccāṭanaṃ kṛtaṃ teṣāṃ bhṛguṇā yajvanā tadā \|*  
*yajanārthaṃ ca devānāṃ tuṣṭyarthaṃ dīkṣitasya ca \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Their defeat was effected by Bhṛgu the sacrificial priest, for the continuance of the worship of the deities and for the satisfaction of Dakṣa who had been initiated in the sacrifice.

## \|\| 3.36.14-15 \|\|

*parājitānsvakāndṛṣṭvā vīrabhadro ruṣānvitaḥ \|*  
*bhūtapretapiśācāṃśca kṛtvā tāneva pṛṣṭhataḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*vṛṣabhasthān puraskṛtya svayaṃ caiva mahābalaḥ \|*  
*mahātriśūlamādāya pātayāmāsa nirjarān \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. On seeing his people defeated, Vīrabhadra became infuriated. He asked the goblins, ghosts and spirits to keep back. The attendants riding on bulls were sent to the front ranks. Accompanied by his forces and wielding his great trident he felled the devas.

## \|\| 3.36.16 \|\|

*devānyakṣān sādhyagaṇān guhyakān cāraṇānapi \|*  
*śūlaghātaiśca sarve gaṇā vegāt prajaghnire \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The attendants of Śiva hit and thrashed the devas, the Yakṣas, Sādhyas, Guhyakas and Cāraṇas with their javelins, spears and tridents.

## \|\| 3.36.17 \|\|

*keciddvidhā kṛtāḥ khaḍgairmudgaraiśca vipothitāḥ \|*  
*anyaiśśastrairapi surā gaṇairbhinnāstadā'bhavan \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Some were split with swords and smashed with iron-clubs. The devas were hit and smothered with various weapons by the attendants of Śiva.

## \|\| 3.36.18 \|\|

*evaṃ parājitāssarve palāyanaparāyaṇāḥ \|*  
*parasparaṃ parityajya gatā devāstriviṣṭapam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Thus defeated, the devas left one another in lurch and fled to heaven.

## \|\| 3.36.19 \|\|

*kevalaṃ lokapālāste śakrādyāstasthurutsukāḥ \|*  
*saṃgrāme dāruṇe tasmin dhṛtvā dhairyaṃ mahābalāḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Only the guardians of the quarters, Indra and others, had the courage and strength to stay behind in that terrible battle with what little enthusiasm they had.

## \|\| 3.36.20 \|\|

*sarve militvā śakrādyā devāstatra raṇājire \|*  
*bṛhaspatiṃ ca papracchurvinayāvanatāstadā \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Indra and others collectively approached Bṛhaspati in that battlefield and asked him humbly.

## \|\| 3.36.21 \|\|

*lokapālā ūcuḥ \|*  
*guro bṛhaspate tāta mahāprājña dayānidhe \|*  
*śīghraṃ vada pṛcchato naḥ kuto' smākaṃ jayo bhavet \|\| 21 \|\|*

The guardians of the quarters said:—

21\. O dear preceptor Bṛhaspati, intelligent and merciful, please tell us quickly how we can be victorious.

## \|\| 3.36.22 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya vacasteṣāṃ smṛtvā śaṃbhuṃ prayatnavān \|*  
*bṛhaspatiruvācedaṃ mahendraṃ jñānadurbalam \|\| 22 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

22\. On hearing their words, Bṛhaspati remembered Śiva and spoke to Indra who was confused and confounded to slove the difficulty.

## \|\| 3.36.23 \|\|

*bṛhaspatiruvāca \|*  
*yaduktaṃ viṣṇunā pūrvaṃ tatsarvaṃ jātamadya vai \|*  
*tadeva vivṛṇomīndra sāvadhānatayā śṛṇu \|\| 23 \|\|*

Bṛhaspati said:—

23\. O Indra, what Viṣṇu had said before has taken place now. I shall explain it further. Listen attentively.

## \|\| 3.36.24 \|\|

*asti yakṣeśvaraḥ kaścit phaladaḥ sarvakarmaṇām \|*  
*kartāraṃ bhajate sopi na svakarttuḥ prabhurhi saḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. There is the presiding deity of sacrifices who dispenses the fruits of all sacrifices. He does it with reference to the performer. He is not independent of the performer.

## \|\| 3.36.25-26 \|\|

*amaṃtrauṣadhayassarve nābhicārā na laukikāḥ \|*  
*na karmāṇi na vedāśca na mīmāṃsādvayaṃ tathā \|\| 25 \|\|*

*anyānyapi ca śāstrāṇi nānāvedayutāni ca \|*  
*jñātuṃ neśaṃ saṃbhavaṃti vadaṃtyevaṃ purātanāḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. Neither Mantras nor medicinal herbs, nor black magic, nor worldly activities, nor the Vedas, nor the two systems of Mīmāṃsās, nor other sacred texts based on Vedic passages are able to know Śiva—so the ancient authorities say.

## \|\| 3.36.27 \|\|

*na svajñeyo maheśānassarvavedāyutena saḥ \|*  
*bhakterananyaśaraṇairnānyatheti mahāśrutiḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Lord Śiva is not unknowable entirely. He can be known by devotees who have no other refuge though he is unknowable through thousands of Vedic passages without devotion. So says the great Vedic passage.

## \|\| 3.36.28 \|\|

*śāṃtyā ca parayā dṛṣṭyā sarvathā nirvikārayā \|*  
*tadanugrahato nūnaṃ jñātavyo hi sadāśivaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Sadāśiva shall be known through his own blessings by mental tranquility and supreme vision without aberrations and distractions.

## \|\| 3.36.29 \|\|

*paraṃ tu saṃvadiṣyāmi kāryākārya vivakṣitau \|*  
*sidhyaṃśaṃ ca sureśāna taṃ śṛṇu tvaṃ hitāya vai \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. But, O Lord of devas, in the matter of discussion about what shall be done and what not, I shall explain the aspect of fulfilment of our desire. Hear that in your own interest.

## \|\| 3.36.30 \|\|

*tvamiṃdra bāliśo bhūtvā lokapālaiḥ sadādya vai \|*  
*āgato dakṣa yajñaṃ hi kiṃ kariṣyasi vikramam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. It is your childishness that prompted you to be present here in the sacrifice of Dakṣa along with the other guardians of quarters. What shall you do with the exhibition of your valour?

## \|\| 3.36.31 \|\|

*ete rudrasahāyāśca gaṇāḥ paramakopanāḥ \|*  
*āgatā yajñavighnārthaṃ taṃ kariṣyaṃtyasaṃśayama \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. These infuriated assistants of Rudra have come here to stop the sacrifice and they will do it undoubtedly.

## \|\| 3.36.32 \|\|

*sarvathā na hyupāyotra keṣāṃcidapi tattvataḥ \|*  
*yajñavighnavināśārtha satyaṃ satyaṃ bravīmyaham \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. There is no remedy to prevent the destruction of the sacrifice. True, I am telling you the truth.

## \|\| 3.36.33 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*evaṃ bṛhaspatervākyaṃ śrutvā te hi divaukasaḥ \|*  
*ciṃtāmāpedire sarve lokapālāssavāsavāḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

33\. On hearing these words of Bṛhaspati the guardians of the quarters, dwellers in heaven including Indra fell athinking.

## \|\| 3.36.34 \|\|

*tatobravīdvīrabhadro mahāvīragaṇairvṛtaḥ \|*  
*indrādīn lokapālāṃstān smṛtvā manasi śaṃkaram \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Then, remembering Śiva mentally Vīrabhadra surrounded by the heroic attendants of Śiva spoke to Indra and other guardians of the quarters.

## \|\| 3.36.35 \|\|

*vīrabhadra uvāca \|*  
*sarve yūyaṃ bāliśatvādavadānārthamāgatāḥ \|\| \|*  
*avadānaṃ prayacchāmi āgacchata mamāṃtikam \|\| 35 \|\|*

Vīrabhadra said:—

35\. “On account of your childishness you came here for this glorious act. I shall now offer you Avadāna (i.e. I shall cut you to pieces). Come near me.

## \|\| 3.36.36-37 \|\|

*he śakra he śuce bhāno he śaśin he dhanādhipa \|*  
*he pāśapāṇe he vāyo nirṛte yama śeṣa he \|\| 36 \|\|*

*he surāsurasaṃghāhīhaita yūyaṃ he vicakṣaṇāḥ \|*  
*avadānāni dāsyāmi ātṛptyādyāsatāṃ varāḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

36-37. O Indra, O Agni, O Sun, O Moon, O Kubera, O Varuṇa, O Wind, O Nirṛti, O Yama, O Śeṣa, O Devas and Asuras, O clever ones, come here. I shall give you Avadānas. The boon will be tasted by you till you are satiated.”

## \|\| 3.36.38-39 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*evamuktvā sitairbāṇairjaghānātha ruṣānvitaḥ \|*  
*nikhilāṃstān surān sadyo vīrabhadro gaṇāgraṇīḥ \|*  
*tairbāṇairnihatāssarve vāsavādyāḥ sureśvarāḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*palāyanaparā bhūtvā jagmuste ca diśo daśa \|*  
*gateṣu lokapāleṣu vidruteṣu sureṣu ca \|*  
*yajñavāṭopakaṃṭhaṃ hi vīrabhadrogamadgaṇaiḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

Brahmā said:

38-39. Saying so, Vīrabhadra, the leader of the attendants became furious and hit all the devas with sharp arrows. Severely wounded by the arrows, Indra and other leaders of devas fled in all the ten directions. When the guardians of the quarters and other devas had fled, Vīrabhadra came very near the entrance of the sacrificial chamber along with the Gaṇas.

## \|\| 3.36.40 \|\|

*tadā te ṛṣayassarve subhītā hi rameśvaram \|*  
*vijñaptukāmāssahasā śīghramūcurnatā bhṛśam \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Then all the sages who had assembled there were terribly afraid and bowing to Viṣṇu and desirous of informing him said thus:—

## \|\| 3.36.41-42 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*devadeva ramānātha sarveśvara mahāprabho \|*  
*rakṣa yajñaṃ hi dakṣasya yajñosi tvaṃ na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*yajñakarmā yajñarūpo yajñāṃgo yajñarakṣakaḥ \|*  
*rakṣa yajñamato rakṣa tvattonyo na hi rakṣakaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

The sages said:—

41-42. “O lord of Lakṣmī, lord of devas, O great lord, lord of everyone, save the sacrifice of Dakṣa. Undoubtedly you are the sacrifice, the performer of sacrifice, the sacrifice embodied, ancillary to sacrifice and the protector of sacrifice. Please save, save the sacrifice. There is none else than you to protect it.”

## \|\| 3.36.43 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya vacasteṣāmṛṣīṇāṃ vacanaṃ hariḥ \|*  
*yoddhukāmo bhayādviṣṇurvīrabhadreṇa tena vai \|\| 43 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

43\. On hearing these words of the sages Viṣṇu, desirous of fighting with Vīrabhadra went ahead.

## \|\| 3.36.44 \|\|

*caturbhujassusanaddho cakrāyudhadharaḥ karaiḥ \|*  
*mahābalomaragaṇairyajñavāṭātsa niryayau \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. The powerful Viṣṇu, the four-armed discus-bearing Viṣṇu, fully equipped, came out of the sacrificial chamber along with the devas.

## \|\| 3.36.45 \|\|

*vīrabhadraḥ śūlapāṇirnānāgaṇasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*dadarśa viṣṇuṃ saṃnaddhaṃ yoddhukāmaṃ mahāprabhum \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. The trident-wielding Vīrabhadra accompanied by the different Gaṇas saw Viṣṇu the great lord desirous of fighting and ready for it.

## \|\| 3.36.46 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā vīrabhadrobhūdbhrukuṭīkuṭilānanaḥ \|*  
*kṛtāṃta iva pāpiṣṭhaṃ mṛgendra iva vāraṇam \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. On seeing him Vīrabhadra knit his eyebrows and his face became awful. He met him as the god of death meeting a sinner or the lion meeting an elephant.

## \|\| 3.36.47 \|\|

*tathāvidhaṃ hariṃ dṛṣṭvā vīrabhadro rimardanaḥ \|*  
*avadattvaritaḥ kruddho gaṇairvīraissamāvṛtaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. On seeing Viṣṇu in such a manner Vīrabhadra the suppressor of enemies, surrounded by the Gaṇas became furious and said.

## \|\| 3.36.48 \|\|

*vīrabhadra uvāca \|*  
*rere hare mahādeva śapathollaṃghanaṃ tvayā \|*  
*kathamadya kṛtaṃ citte garvaḥ kimabhavattava \|\| 48 \|\|*

Vīrabhadra said:

48\. O Viṣṇu, how is it that you set at nought the affirmation of lord Śiva? Why were you haughty?

## \|\| 3.36.49 \|\|

*tava śrīrudraśapathollaṃghane śaktirasti kim \|*  
*ko vā tvamasiko vā te rakṣa kosti jagattraye \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Can you dare to transgress the affirmation of lord Śiva? Who are you? In the three worlds who is your saviour?

## \|\| 3.36.50 \|\|

*atra tvamāgataḥ kasmādvayaṃ tannaiva vidmahe \|*  
*dakṣasya yajñapātāttvaṃ kathaṃ jātosi tadvada \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Why did you come here? We do not know that. How did you become the guardian and saviour of Dakṣa’s sacrifice? Explain it.

## \|\| 3.36.51 \|\|

*dākṣāyaṇyākṛtaṃ yacca tanna dṛṣṭaṃ kimu tvayā \|*  
*proktaṃ yacca dadhīcena śrutaṃ tanna kimu tvayā \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Haven’t you seen what Satī did? Haven’t you heard what Dadhīci said?

## \|\| 3.36.52 \|\|

*tvañcāpi dakṣayajñesminnavadānārthamāgataḥ \|*  
*avadānaṃ prayacchāmi tava cāpi mahābhuja \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. You too came to Dakṣa’s sacrifice for the sake of sacrificial gifts. O long-armed one, I shall now offer you Avadāna (i.e. I shall cut you to pieces).

## \|\| 3.36.53 \|\|

*vakṣo vidārayiṣyāmi triśūlena hare tava \|*  
*kastavāsti samāyāto rakṣakodya mamāṃtikam \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. O Viṣṇu, I shall split your chest with my trident. Who is your protector who dare come near me?

## \|\| 3.36.54 \|\|

*pātayiṣyāmi bhūpṛṣṭhe jvālayiṣyāmi vahninā \|*  
*dagdhaṃ bhavaṃtamadhunā peṣayiṣyāmi satvaram \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. I shall dash you to the ground. I shall burn you with fire. I shall pound you after burning you.

## \|\| 3.36.55 \|\|

*rere hare durācāra maheśa vimukhādhama \|*  
*śrīmahārudramāhātmyaṃ kinna jānāsi pāvanam \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. O Viṣṇu, of evil conduct, O the worst of Śiva’s haters, don’t you know the greatness and sanctity of lord Śiva?

## \|\| 3.36.56 \|\|

*tathāpi tvaṃ mahābāho yoddhukāmogrataḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*neṣyāmi punarāvṛttiṃ yadi tiṣṭhestvamātmanā \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Still O long-armed one, if you stand face to face with me wishing for a fight I shall rout you, if at all you can steady yourself.

## \|\| 3.36.57 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā vīrabhadrasya buddhimān \|*  
*uvāca vihasan prītyā viṣṇustra sureśvaraḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

57\. On hearing the words of Vīrabhadra, Viṣṇu the intelligent lord of Devas, laughed gleefully and said:—

## \|\| 3.36.58 \|\|

*viṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu tvaṃ vīrabhadrādya pravakṣyāmi tvadagrataḥ \|*  
*na rudravimukhaṃ māṃ tvaṃ vada śaṃkarasevakam \|\| 58 \|\|*

Viṣṇu said:—

58\. O Vīrabhadra, listen. I shall tell you. I am a servant of Śiva. Do not call me inimical to Śiva.

## \|\| 3.36.59 \|\|

*anena prārthitaḥ pūrvaṃ yajñārthaṃ ca punaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*dakṣeṇāviditārthena karmaniṣṭhena mauḍhyataḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. At first I had been requested repeatedly by Dakṣa foolishly, since he is too much addicted to rituals and did not know the true state of facts. He wanted me to protect the sacrifice.

## \|\| 3.36.60 \|\|

*ahaṃ bhaktaparādhīnastathā sopi maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*dakṣo bhakto hi me tāta tasmādatrāgato makhe \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. I am subservient to my devotees, so also is lord Śiva. O dear one, Dakṣa is my devotee. Hence I came to this sacrifice.

## \|\| 3.36.61 \|\|

*śṛṇu pratijñāṃ me vīra rudrakopasamudbhava \|*  
*rudratejassvarūpo hi supratāpālayaṃprabho \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. O heroic one, you have the features and splendour of Śiva, you are born of Śiva’s fury. O lord, you are the receptacle of exploits; listen to the vow taken by me.

## \|\| 3.36.62 \|\|

*ahaṃ nivārayāmi tvāṃ tvaṃ ca māṃ vinivāraya \|*  
*tadbhaviṣyati yadbhāvi kariṣye'haṃ parākramam \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. I shall withstand you. You can try to stop me. Let whatever is destined to happen, befall. I shall definitely show my prowess.

## \|\| 3.36.63 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*ityuktavati govinde prahasya sa mahābhujaḥ \|*  
*avadatsuprasannosmi tvāṃ jñātvāsmatprabhoḥ priyam \|\| 63 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

63\. When Viṣṇu said thus, the long-armed (Vīrabhadra) laughed and said “I am glad to know that you are a favourite of our lord”.

## \|\| 3.36.64 \|\|

*tato vihasya suprīto vīrabhadro gaṇāgraṇīḥ \|*  
*praśrayāvanatovādīdviṣṇuṃ devaṃ hi tattvataḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Then the delighted Vīrabhadra, the leader of the Gaṇas, laughed and stooped humbly and spoke to lord Viṣṇu,

## \|\| 3.36.65 \|\|

*\|\| vīrabhadra uvāca \|*  
*tava bhāvaparīkṣārthamityuktaṃ me mahāprabho \|*  
*idānīṃ tattvato vacmi śṛṇu tvaṃ sāvadhānataḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

Vīrabhadra said:—

65\. O great lord, I had said thus in order to test your feelings. Now I shall speak in real earnest. You listen with attention.

## \|\| 3.36.66 \|\|

*yathā śivastathā tvaṃ hi yathā tvaṃ ca tathā śivaḥ \|*  
*iti vedā varṇayaṃti śivaśāsanato hare \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. As Śiva, so you. As you, so Śiva. O Viṣṇu, thus speak the Vedas at the bidding of Śiva.

## \|\| 3.36.67 \|\|

*śivājñayā vayaṃ sarve sevakāḥ śaṃkarasya vai \|*  
*tathāpi ca ramānātha pravādocitamādarāt \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. O lord of Lakṣmī, all of us are the servants of Śiva. We work at the bidding of Śiva. Still due to respect we speak and argue thus.

## \|\| 3.36.68 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*tacchrutvā vacanaṃ tasya vīrabhadrasya so'cyutaḥ \|*  
*prahasya cedaṃ provāca vīrabhadramidaṃ vacaḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

68\. On hearing these words of Vīrabhadra, Viṣṇu laughed and spoke these words beneficent to Vīrabhadra.

## \|\| 3.36.69 \|\|

*\|\| viṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*yuddhaṃ kuru mahāvīra mayā sārddhamaśaṃkitaḥ \|*  
*tavāstraiḥ pūryamāṇohaṃ gamiṣyāmi svamāśramam \|\| 69 \|\|*

Viṣṇu said:—

69\. O great hero, unhesitatingly fight with me. Hit all over my body by your arrows. I shall return to my hermitage.

## \|\| 3.36.70 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*ityuktvā hi viramyāsau sannaddhobhūdraṇāya ca \|*  
*svagaṇairvīrabhadropi sannaddhotha mahābalaḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

Brahmā said:

70\. Saying thus, he stopped and got ready for the fight. The powerful Vīrabhadra too got ready in the company of his attendants.

## Chapter 37 - Destruction of Dakṣa’s sacrifice

## \|\| 3.37.1-2 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*vīrabhadrotha yuddhe vai viṣṇunā sa mahābalaḥ \|*  
*saṃsmṛtya śaṃkaraṃ citte sarvāpadvinivāraṇam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*āruhya syaṃdanaṃ divyaṃ sarvavairivimardanaḥ \|*  
*gṛhītvā paramāstrāṇi siṃhanādaṃ jagarja ha \|\| 2 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

1-2. Mentally meditating on Śiva, the remover of all adversities and seated in his divine chariot, the powerful Vīrabhadra took up all the great miraculous weapons for his fight with Viṣṇu and roared like a lion.

## \|\| 3.37.3 \|\|

*viṣṇuścāpi mahāghoṣaṃ pāṃcajanyā bhidhannijam \|*  
*dadhmau balī mahāśaṃkhaṃ svakīyān harṣayanniva \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Viṣṇu, the powerful, loudly blew his conch “Pāñcajanya” delighting his own people.

## \|\| 3.37.4 \|\|

*tacchrutvā śaṃkhanirhrādaṃ devā ye ca palāyitāḥ \|*  
*raṇaṃ hitvā gatāḥ pūrvaṃ te drutaṃ punarāyayuḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. On hearing the sound of the conch, the devas who had fled before leaving off the battle-field returned quickly.

## \|\| 3.37.5 \|\|

*vīrabhadra gaṇaisteṣāṃ lokapālāssavāsavāḥ \|*  
*yuddhañcakrustathā siṃhanādaṃ kṛtvā balānvitāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The guardians of the quarters including Indra roared like lions and fought forcefully with the Gaṇas of Vīrabhadra.

## \|\| 3.37.6 \|\|

*gaṇānāṃ lokapālānāṃ dvandvayuddhaṃ bhayāvaham \|*  
*abhavattatra tumulaṃ garjatāṃ siṃhanādataḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. A noisy terrible fight ensued between the Gaṇas and the guardians of the quarters, both roaring like lions.

## \|\| 3.37.7 \|\|

*nandinā yuyudhe śakro'nalo vai vaiṣṇavāstathā \|*  
*kuberopi hi kūṣmāṇḍapatiśca yuyudhe balī \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Indra fought with Nandin; the fire-god with Aśman and the powerful Kubera fought with Kūṣmāṇḍapati.

## \|\| 3.37.8-9 \|\|

*tadendreṇa hato nandī vajreṇa śataparvaṇā \|\| 8 \|\|*

*nandinā ca hataśśakrastriśūlena stanāṃtare \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. Nandin was hit hard by Indra with the thunderbolt that had a hundred spikes. Indra was hurt in the middle of his chest by Nandin with the trident.

## \|\| 3.37.10 \|\|

*balinau dvāvapi prītyā yuyudhāte parasparam \|*  
*nānāghātāṃśca kurvaṃtau nandiśakrau jigīṣayā \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Nandin and Indra both equally powerful fought with each other gleefully, and hit each other in diverse ways with a desire to overpower each other.

## \|\| 3.37.11 \|\|

*śaktyā jaghāna cāśmānaṃ śuciḥ paramakopanaḥ \|*  
*sopi śūlena taṃ vegācchitadhāreṇa pāvakam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The infuriated fire-god hit Aśman with his (spear). He too hit back the fire god with his trident of very sharp point.

## \|\| 3.37.12 \|\|

*yamena saha saṃgrāmaṃ mahāloko gaṇāgraṇīḥ \|*  
*cakāra tumulaṃ vīro mahādevaṃ smaranmudā \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Mahāloka, the heroic chieftain of the Gaṇas, remembered Lord Śiva with joy and fought with Yama.

## \|\| 3.37.13 \|\|

*nairṛtena samāgamya caṃḍaśca balavattaraḥ \|*  
*yuyudhe paramāstraiśca nairṛtiṃ nibiḍaṃ vayan \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Caṇḍa, the brawny, grappled with Nairṛṭa and mortified him with many great miraculous weapons.

## \|\| 3.37.14 \|\|

*varuṇena samaṃ vīro muṃḍaścaiva mahābalaḥ \|*  
*yuyudhe parayā śaktyā trilokīṃ vismayanniva \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The powerful hero Muṇḍa fought with Varuṇa surprising the three worlds with his great spear.

## \|\| 3.37.15 \|\|

*vāyunā ca hato bhṛṃgī svāstreṇa paramojasā \|*  
*bhṛṃgiṇā ca hato vāyustriśūlena pratāpinā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Bhṛṅgī was struck by the wind god with his weapon of great force. Vāyu was struck (in return) by Bhṛṅgī with a powerful trident.

## \|\| 3.37.16 \|\|

*kubereṇaiva saṃgamya kūṣmāṃḍapatirādarāt \|*  
*yuyudhe balavān vīro dhyātvā hṛdi maheśvaram \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Meditating on Lord Śiva in his heart, the strong and heroic Kūṣmāṇḍapati clashed with Kubera and fought terribly.

## \|\| 3.37.17 \|\|

*yoginīcakrasaṃyukto bhairavīnāyako mahān \|*  
*vidīryya devānakhilānpapau śoṇitamadbhutam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Splitting up all the Devas, the great leader of Bhairavī in collaboration with the circle of Yoginīs, drank much of their blood.

## \|\| 3.37.18 \|\|

*kṣetrapālāstathā tatra bubhukṣuḥ surapuṃgavān \|*  
*kālī cāpi vidāryaiva tānpapau rudhiraṃ bahu \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Desirous of gobbling up the leading devas, Kālī split them and drank their blood. Kṣetrapāla too did the same.

## \|\| 3.37.19 \|\|

*atha viṣṇurmahātejā yuyudhe taiśca śatruhā \|*  
*cakraṃ cikṣepa vegena dahanniva diśo daśa \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Then Viṣṇu, the slayer of enemies and who was excessively brilliant, hurled his discus and fought with them. The discus seemed to burn the ten directions.

## \|\| 3.37.20 \|\|

*kṣetrapālassamāyāṃtaṃ cakramālokya vegataḥ \|*  
*tatrāgatyāgato vīraścāgrasatsahasā balī \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Kṣetrapāla saw the discus coming on. He ran to the place and bravely caught hold of it.

## \|\| 3.37.21 \|\|

*cakraṃ grasitamālokya viṣṇuḥ parapuraṃjayaḥ \|*  
*mukhaṃ tasya parāmṛjya tamudgālitavānarim \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. On seeing the discus held in his mouth, Viṣṇu the conqueror of enemies’ cities caught hold of his throat and made him spit out the discus.

## \|\| 3.37.22 \|\|

*svacakramādāya mahānubhāvaścukopa cātīva bhavaikabharttā \|*  
*mahābalī tairyuyudhe pravīraissakruddhanānāyudhadhārakostraiḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Regaining his discus, Viṣṇu the sole sustainer of the world, of great dignity became very angry. In that infuriated state he took up different weapons and fought with the brave warriors.

## \|\| 3.37.23 \|\|

*cakre mahāraṇaṃ viṣṇustaissārddhaṃ yuyudhe mudā \|*  
*nānāyudhāni saṃkṣipya tumulaṃ bhīmavikramam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Viṣṇu fought a great battle with them by hurling many weapons and evincing boisterous display of his terrific exploits.

## \|\| 3.37.24 \|\|

*atha te bhairavādyāśca yuyudhustena bhūriśaḥ \|*  
*nānāstrāṇi vimuṃcaṃtassaṃkuddhāḥ paramojasā \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Bhairava and others displayed their strength furiously by hurling several weapons and by fighting with him.

## \|\| 3.37.25 \|\|

*itthaṃ teṣāṃ raṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā hariṇātulatejasā \|*  
*vinivṛtya samāgamya tānsvayaṃ yuyudhe balī \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Vīrabhadra saw their battle with Viṣṇu of unequalled splendour, returned and clashed with him in a great battle.

## \|\| 3.37.26 \|\|

*atha viṣṇurmahātejāścakramudyamya mūrcchitaḥ \|*  
*yuyudhe bhagavāṃstena vīrabhadreṇa mādhavaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Then Viṣṇu of great brilliance lifted up his discus and fought with Vīrabhadra.

## \|\| 3.37.27 \|\|

*tayoḥ samabhavadyuddhaṃ sughoraṃ romaharṣaṇam \|*  
*mahāvīrādhipatyostu nānāstradharayormune \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. O sage, a terrible fight provoking harripilation (horripilation?) took place between Mahābali and Varuṇa with various weapons.

## \|\| 3.37.28 \|\|

*viṣṇoryogabalāttasya devadeva sudāruṇāḥ \|*  
*śaṅkhacakragadāhastā asaṃkhyātāśca jajñire \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Thanks to the Yogic power of Viṣṇu, innumerable soldiers terrible and wielding conch, discus and mace in their hands emerged from his own body.

## \|\| 3.37.29 \|\|

*te cāpi yuyudhustena vīrabhadreṇa bhāṣatā \|*  
*viṣṇuvat balavaṃto hi nānāyudhadharā gaṇāḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. They too fought against Vīrabhadra who continued to shout. These strong groups of warriors were as strong as Viṣṇu and had various weapons with them.

## \|\| 3.37.30 \|\|

*tānsarvānapi vīrosau nārāyaṇasamaprabhān \|*  
*bhasmīcakāra śūlena hatvā smṛtvā śivaṃ prabhum \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Remembering Śiva, his lord and hitting them, who were as lustrous as Nārāyaṇa with his trident, he reduced them to ashes.

## \|\| 3.37.31 \|\|

*tataścorasi taṃ viṣṇuṃ līlayaiva raṇājire \|*  
*jaghāna vīrabhadro hi triśūlena mahābalī \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. The most powerful Vīrabhadra struck Viṣṇu in the chest playfully with his trident in the course of the battle.

## \|\| 3.37.32 \|\|

*tena ghātena sahasā vihataḥ puruṣottamaḥ \|*  
*papāta ca tadā bhūmau visaṃjñobhūnmune hariḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. O sage, hit suddenly by that blow, Viṣṇu Puruṣottama, fell unconscious on the ground.

## \|\| 3.37.33 \|\|

*tato yajñodbhutaṃ tejaḥ pralayānalasannibham \|*  
*trailokyadāhakaṃ tīvraṃ vīrāṇāmapi bhīkaram \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Then arose a wonderful brilliance as terrible as the fire at the time of dissolution. It seemed to burn all the three worlds. It was severe and terrifying even to great heroes.

## \|\| 3.37.34 \|\|

*krodharaktekṣaṇaḥ śrīmān punarutthāya sa prabhuḥ \|*  
*prahartuṃ cakramudyamya hyatiṣṭhatpuruṣarṣabhaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. That glorious lord, with eyes red by anger, got up again. The best of beings lifted up his discus and stood ready to strike.

## \|\| 3.37.35 \|\|

*tasya cakraṃ mahāraudraṃ kālā dityasamaprabham \|*  
*vyaṣṭaṃbhayadadīnātmā vīrabhadraśśivaḥ prabhuḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Vīrabhadra of no weak soul, nay, identical with lord Śiva, held his terrific discus luminous like black sun suspended and motionless.

## \|\| 3.37.36 \|\|

*mune śaṃbhoḥ prabhāvāttu māyeśasya mahāprabhoḥ \|*  
*na cacāla hareścakraṃ karasthaṃ staṃbhitaṃ dhruvam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. O sage, thanks to the power of Śiva, the great lord controlling Māyā, the Cakra held in the hand of Viṣṇu became stunned and motionless.

## \|\| 3.37.37 \|\|

*atha viṣṇurgaṇeśena vīrabhadreṇa bhāṣatā \|*  
*atiṣṭhatstaṃbhitastena śṛṃgavāniva niścalaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*
