41\. O Śiva, the helper of the distressed, Thou art greater than the greatest. Thou art favourably disposed to thy devotees. Thou art satisfied by thine own action of great value.

## \|\| 3.42.42 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*iti stutvā maheśānaṃ śaṃkaraṃ lokaśaṃkaram \|*  
*prajāpatirvinītātmā virarāma mahāprabhum \|\| 42 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

42\. Having thus eulogised lord Śiva, the benefactor of the worlds and the great lord, the patriarch Dakṣa humbly stopped.

## \|\| 3.42.43 \|\|

*atha viṣṇuḥ prasannātmā tuṣṭāva vṛṣabhadhvajam \|*  
*bāṣpagadgadayā vāṇyā supraṇamya kṛtāṃjaliḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Then the delighted Viṣṇu, with palms joined in reverence, eulogised the bull-bannered Śiva in a speech choked with tears after bowing to him.

## \|\| 3.42.44 \|\|

*viṣṇuvāca \|*  
*mahādeva maheśāna lokānugrahakāraka \|*  
*parabrahma parātmā tvaṃ dīnabaṃdho dayānidhe \|\| 44 \|\|*

Viṣṇu said:—

44\. O great God, O supreme God, the bestower of blessings on the world, O storehouse of mercy, the helper of the distressed, Thou art the great Brahman, the great soul.

## \|\| 3.42.45-46 \|\|

*sarvavyāpī svairavartī vedavedyayaśāḥ prabhoḥ \|*  
*anugrahaḥ kṛtastena kṛtāścāsukṛtā vayam \|\| 45 \|\|*

*dakṣoyaṃ mama bhaktastvāṃ yanniniṃda khalaḥ purā \|*  
*tat kṣaṃtavyaṃ maheśādya nirvikāro yato bhavān \|\| 46 \|\|*

45-46. O Lord, Thou art all-pervasive and independent. Thy glory can be known only through the Vedas. This Dakṣa is my devotee. He has been wicked to censure you before. He has committed an offence making us meritless. O great lord, Thou must forgive him since thou art free from aberrations.

## \|\| 3.42.47 \|\|

*kṛto mayāparādhopi tava śaṃkara mūḍhataḥ \|*  
*tvadgaṇena kṛtaṃ yuddhaṃ vīrabhadreṇa pakṣataḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. O Śiva, out of delusion. I too have committed offence against you since I took sides with Dakṣa and fought with Vīrabhadra, Thy attendant.

## \|\| 3.42.48 \|\|

*tvaṃ me svāmī parabrahma dāsohaṃ te sadāśiva \|*  
*poṣyaścāpi sadā te hi sarveṣāṃ tvaṃ pitā yataḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. O Sadāśiva, Thou art my master, the supreme Brahman. I am Thy slave. I shall be sustained by Thee always since thou art the father unto us all.

## \|\| 3.42.49 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*devadeva mahādeva karuṇāsāgara prabho \|*  
*svataṃtraḥ paramātmā tvaṃ parameśo dvayovyayaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

49\. O great lord, lord of devas, O lord, O ocean of mercy, Thou art the independent great soul, the great Śiva, unchanging and without a second.

## \|\| 3.42.50 \|\|

*mama putropari kṛto devānugraha īśvara \|*  
*svāpamānamagaṇayan dakṣayajñaṃ samuddhara \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. O Śiva, blessing has been conferred on my son in granting him a body. Thou dost not mind the offence to Thee. Resuscitate the sacrifice of Dakṣa.

## \|\| 3.42.51 \|\|

*prasanno bhava deveśa sarvaśāpānnirākuru \|*  
*sabodhaḥ prerakastvaṃ me tvamevaṃ vinivārakaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. O Lord of gods, be pleased. Remove all curses. Thou art my conscious encourager. Thou alone art the restrainer.

## \|\| 3.42.52 \|\|

*iti stutvā maheśānaṃ paramaṃ ca mahāmune \|*  
*kṛtāṃjalipuṭo bhūtvā vinamrīkṛtamastakaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. O great sage, after thus eulogising lord Śiva, I joined my palms in reverence and bent my head in humility.

## \|\| 3.42.53 \|\|

*atha śakrādayo devā lokapālāssucetasaḥ \|*  
*tuṣṭuvuḥ śaṃkaraṃ devaṃ prasannamukhapaṃkajam \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Then Indra and other gods, the guardians of the quarters, of good mentality lauded lord Śiva whose lotuslike face beamed with brilliance.

## \|\| 3.42.54 \|\|

*tataḥ prasannamanasaḥ sarve devāstathā pare \|*  
*siddharṣayaḥ prajeśāśca tuṣṭuvuḥ śaṃkaraṃ mudā \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. The other gods too of delighted minds, the Siddhas, the sages and the Prajāpatis lauded Śiva joyously.

## \|\| 3.42.55 \|\|

*tathopadevanāgāśca sadasyā brāhmaṇāstathā \|*  
*praṇamya parayā bhaktyā tuṣṭuvuśca pṛthak pṛthak \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Then the gods of lower rank, Nāgas, and the brahmins, the members of the assembly, bowed with devotion and eulogised Śiva severally.

## Chapter 43 - The Arrangement in Dakṣa’s Sacrifice

## \|\| 3.43.1 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*iti stuto rameśena mayā caiva surarṣibhiḥ \|*  
*tathānyaiśca mahādevaḥ prasannassaṃbabhūva ha \|\| 1 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

1\. Thus eulogised by Viṣṇu, by me, by the gods, sages and others, the great lord became delighted.

## \|\| 3.43.2 \|\|

*atha śaṃbhuḥ kṛpā dṛṣṭyā sarvān ṛṣisurādikān \|*  
*brahmaviṣṇū samādhāya dakṣametaduvāca ha \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. After consoling Braḥmā, Viṣṇu, the sages and the gods by His benign glance, Śiva spoke to Dakṣa.

## \|\| 3.43.3 \|\|

*mahādeva uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu dakṣa pravakṣyāmi prasannosmi prajāpate \|*  
*bhaktādhīnaḥ sadāhaṃ vai svataṃtropyakhileśvaraḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

Lord Śiva said:—

3\. O Dakṣa, listen. I shall explain. O patriarch, I am delighted. Although I am independent lord of all, I am subservient to my devotees always.

## \|\| 3.43.4 \|\|

*caturvidhā bhajaṃte māṃ janāḥ sukṛtinassadā \|*  
*uttarottarataḥ śreṣṭhāsteṣāṃ dakṣaprajāpate \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Four kinds of meritorious persons worship me always. O patriarch Dakṣa, the latter are greater than the former.

## \|\| 3.43.5 \|\|

*ārto jijñāsurarthārthī jñānī caiva caturthakaḥ \|*  
*pūrve trayaśca sāmānyāścaturtho hi viśiṣyate \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. They are—the distressed, the inquisitive, the fortune-seeker and the wise. The first three are ordinary and the fourth one is extraordinary person.

## \|\| 3.43.6 \|\|

*tatra jñānī priyatara mamarūpañca sa smṛtaḥ \|*  
*tasmātpriyataro nānyaḥ satyaṃ satyaṃ vadāmyaham \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The wise among these four is a great favourite of mine. He is of my own form. None is dearer to me than the wise. It is the truth. I tell you the truth.

## \|\| 3.43.7 \|\|

*jñānagamyohamātmajño vedāṃtaśrutipāragaiḥ \|*  
*vinā jñānena māṃ prāptuṃ yatante cālpabuddhayaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. I am the knower of Self. I can be known through knowledge by those who have mastered Vedanta and the Vedas.

## \|\| 3.43.8 \|\|

*na vedaiśca na yajñaiśca na dānaistapasā kvacit \|*  
*na śaknuvaṃti māṃ prāptuṃ mūḍhāḥ karmavaśā narā \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Deluded men engrossed in rituals alone cannot attain me through the Vedas, sacrifices, gifts or austerities.

## \|\| 3.43.9 \|\|

*kevalaṃ karmmaṇā tvaṃ sma saṃsāraṃ tartumicchasi \|*  
*ata evābhavaṃ ruṣṭo yajñavidhvaṃsakārakaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. You wished to cross the ocean of worldly existence by observance of rituals alone. That was why I became angry and caused the destruction of the sacrifice.

## \|\| 3.43.10 \|\|

*itaḥ prabhṛti bho dakṣa matvā māṃ parameśvaram \|*  
*buddhyā jñānaparo bhūtvā kuru karma samāhitaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Hereafter, O Dakṣa, thinking upon me as the great Lord and giving more importance to knowledge you carry on rituals with care and attention.

## \|\| 3.43.11 \|\|

*anyacca śṛṇu sadbuddhyā vacanaṃ me prajāpate \|*  
*vacmi guhyaṃ dharmahetoḥ saguṇatvepyahaṃ tava \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. O patriarch, listen to another statement of mine with a clear conscience. Although it is based on the qualitative aspect it is esoteric. For the sake of virtue I shall tell you.

## \|\| 3.43.12 \|\|

*ahaṃ brahmā ca viṣṇuśca jagataḥ kāraṇaṃ param \|*  
*ātmeśvara upadraṣṭā svayaṃdṛgaviśeṣaṇaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Brahmā, Viṣṇu and I constitute the chief cause of the universe. But I am the soul, the witness, self-seer and without attributes.

## \|\| 3.43.13 \|\|

*ātmamāyāṃ samāviśya sohaṃ guṇamayīṃ mune \|*  
*sṛjanrakṣanharanviśvaṃ dadhe saṃjñāḥ kriyocitāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. O sage, entering into my own illusion consisting of three attributes, I create, sustain and annihilate the universe and acquire designations consistent with the activities.

## \|\| 3.43.14 \|\|

*advitīye pare tasmin brahmaṇyātmani kevale \|*  
*ajñaḥ paśyati bhedena bhūtāni brahmaceśvaram \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. In that supreme, sole, universal God which is the pure Self, the ignorant sees different living beings, Brahman, Īśvara etc.

## \|\| 3.43.15 \|\|

*śiraḥ karādisvāṃgeṣu kurute na yathā pumān \|*  
*pārakyaśemuṣīṃ kvāpi bhūteṣvevaṃ hi matparaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Even as an ordinary man does not consider his head, hands and other limbs as separate from his own self so also my follower does not feel separateness about the living beings.

## \|\| 3.43.16 \|\|

*sarvabhūtātmanāmekabhāvanāṃ yo na paśyati \|*  
*trisurāṇāṃ bhidāṃ dakṣa sa śāṃtimadhigacchati \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. He attains peace, who does not see any difference among the three deities who constitute the soul of all living beings and who have the same innate property, O Dakṣa.

## \|\| 3.43.17 \|\|

*yaḥ karoti trideveṣu bhedabuddhiṃ narādhamaḥ \|*  
*narake sa vasennūnaṃ yāvadācandratārakam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The base man who differentiates the deities of the Trinity certainly stays in hell as long as the moon and the stars shine.

## \|\| 3.43.18 \|\|

*matparaḥ pūjayeddevān sarvānapi vicakṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*sa jñānaṃ labhate yena muktirbhavati śāśvatī \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. My devotee may worship the gods. Being so absorbed he will attain knowledge leading to eternal salvation.

## \|\| 3.43.19 \|\|

*vidhibhaktiṃ vinā naiva bhaktirbhavati vaiṣṇavī \|*  
*viṣṇubhaktiṃ vinā me na bhaktiḥ kvāpi prajāyate \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Without devotion to Brahmā one cannot have the devotion to Viṣṇu; without devotion to Viṣṇu none will have devotion towards me.

## \|\| 3.43.20 \|\|

*ityuktvā śaṃkarassvāmī sarveṣāṃ parameśvaraḥ \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ tatrovāca vāṇīṃ kṛpākaraḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. After saying this, Śiva, the great lord, the merciful god spoke these words within the hearing of everyone.

## \|\| 3.43.21 \|\|

*haribhakto hi māṃ nindettathā śaivobhave dyadi \|*  
*tayoḥ śāpā bhaveyuste tattvaprāptirbhavenna hi \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. “If a devotee of Viṣṇu hates me or if a devotee of Śiva hates Viṣṇu, both will incur curses and never realise reality”.

## \|\| 3.43.22 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya maheśasya vacanaṃ sukhakārakam \|*  
*jahṛṣussakalāstatra suramunyādayo mune \|\| 22 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

22\. On hearing these pleasing words of lord Śiva, O sage, the devas, sages and others were greatly delighted.

## \|\| 3.43.23-24 \|\|

*dakṣobhavanmahāprītyā śivabhaktiratastadā \|*  
*sakuṭumbassurādyāste śivaṃ matvākhileśvaram \|\| 23 \|\|*

*yathā yena kṛtā śaṃbhoḥ saṃstutiḥ paramātmanaḥ \|*  
*tathā tasmai varo dattaśśaṃbhunā tuṣṭacetasā \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. With great joy, Dakṣa, his family and the gods realised Śiva as the lord of all and was engrossed in devotion to Śiva. Lord Śiva who was delighted in mind granted boons to all, as he received reverence to His great self.

## \|\| 3.43.25 \|\|

*jñaptaḥ śivenāśu dakṣaḥ śivabhaktaḥ prasannadhīḥ \|*  
*yajñaṃ cakāra saṃpūrṇaṃ śivānugrahato mune \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Permitted by Śiva and with his blessings, O sage, Dakṣa the devotee of Śiva, with a delighted heart completed his sacrifice.

## \|\| 3.43.26 \|\|

*dadau bhāgānsurebhyo hi pūrṇabhāgaṃ śivāya saḥ \|*  
*dānaṃ dadau dvijebhyaśca prāptaḥ śaṃbhoranugrahaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. He allotted the full share to Śiva and gave the gods their respective shares. He gave charitable gifts to the brahmins and secured the good blessings of Siva.

## \|\| 3.43.27 \|\|

*atho devasya sumahattatkarma vidhipūrvakam \|*  
*dakṣaḥ samāpya vidhivatsahartvigbhiḥ prajāpatiḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Thus the patriarch, Dakṣa, in collaboration with the Ṛtviks, completed that great rite of the gods in accordance with the sacred injunction.

## \|\| 3.43.28 \|\|

*evaṃ dakṣamakhaḥ pūrṇobhavattatra munīśvaraḥ \|*  
*śaṃkarasya prasādena parabrahmasvarūpiṇaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. O excellent sage, thus the sacrifice of Dakṣa was completed, thanks to the grace of Śiva who is identical with the supreme Brahman.

## \|\| 3.43.29 \|\|

*atha devarṣayassarve śaṃsaṃtaśśāṃkaraṃ yaśaḥ \|*  
*svadhāmāni yayustu ṣṭāḥ parepi sukhatastadā \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Then the celestial sages, sang the glory of Śiva and left for their abodes with delighted minds. Others too were pleased and left for their homes.

## \|\| 3.43.30 \|\|

*ahaṃ viṣṇuśca suprītāvapi svaṃsvaṃ paraṃ mudā \|*  
*gāyantau suyaśaśśaṃbhoḥ sarvamaṃgaladaṃ sadā \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Viṣṇu and I, went to our regions, joyfully singing the ever auspicious glory of Śiva.

## \|\| 3.43.31 \|\|

*dakṣa saṃmānitaḥ prītyā mahādevopi sadgatiḥ \|*  
*kailāsaṃ sa yayau śailaṃ suprītassagaṇo nijam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Lovingly honoured by Dakṣa, the great lord Śiva, the goal of the good, returned to Kailāsa along with his Gaṇas. He was greatly delighted.

## \|\| 3.43.32 \|\|

*āgatya svagiriṃ śaṃbhussasmāra svapriyāṃ satīm \|*  
*gaṇebhyaḥ kathayāmāsa pradhānebhyaśca tatkathām \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. After returning to his mountain, Śiva remembered His beloved Satī and mentioned her story to the most important of his Gaṇas.

## \|\| 3.43.33 \|\|

*kālaṃ nināya vijñānī bahu taccaritaṃ vadan \|*  
*laukikīṃ gatimāśritya darśayan kāmitāṃ prabhuḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Narrating her story, lord Śiva passed many days. He then evinced the lover’s humour according to the conventions of the world.

## \|\| 3.43.34 \|\|

*nānītikārakaḥ svāmī parabrahma satāṃ gatiḥ \|*  
*tasya mohaḥ kva vā śokaḥ kva vikāraḥ paro mune \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. O sage, the lord is never unjust. The supreme Brahman is the goal of the good. How can He be deluded? What sorrow has He? How can he have other aberrations?

## \|\| 3.43.35 \|\|

*ahaṃ viṣṇuśca jānīvastadbhedaṃ na kadācana \|*  
*kepare munayo devā manuṣādyāśca yoginaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Even Viṣṇu and I do not know His real secret. What then about others, the sages, gods, human beings and even Yogins.

## \|\| 3.43.36 \|\|

*mahimā śāṃkaronaṃto durvijñeyo manīṣibhiḥ \|*  
*bhaktajñātaśca sadbhaktyā tatprasādādvinā śramam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. The greatness of Śiva is endless and inscrutable even to the learned sages. It is known to the devotees without difficulty, thanks to good devotion and his favour.

## \|\| 3.43.37 \|\|

*ekopi na vikāro hi śivasya paramātmanaḥ \|*  
*saṃdarśayati lokebhyaḥ kṛtvā tāṃ tādṛśīṃ gatim \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. There is no emotion or aberration at all in Śiva the supreme Being. He points out to the people of the world by his different actions, their respective goals.

## \|\| 3.43.38 \|\|

*yatpaṭhitvā ca saṃśrutya sarvalokasudhīrmune \|*  
*labhate sadgatiṃ dibyāmihāpi sukhamuttamam \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. O sage, by reading or listening to this, intelligent persons in the world secure good goal hereafter and excellent happiness in this world.

## \|\| 3.43.39 \|\|

*itthaṃ dākṣāyaṇī hitvā nijadehaṃ satī punaḥ \|*  
*jajñe himavataḥ patnyāṃ menāyāmiti viśrutam \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. After forsaking her body thus, Satī, the daughter of Dakṣa, was born as the daughter of Menā, the wife of Himavat. This is well known.

## \|\| 3.43.40 \|\|

*punaḥ kṛtvā tapastatra śivaṃ vavre patiṃ ca sā \|*  
*gaurī bhūtvārddhavāmāṃgī līlāścakredbhutāśśivā \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. After performing penance again she wooed Śiva as her husband. Attaining white complexion she performed many wonderful, divine sports and gained half the body of Śiva.

## \|\| 3.43.41 \|\|

*itthaṃ satīcaritraṃ te varṇitaṃ paramādbhutam \|*  
*bhuktimuktipradaṃ divyaṃ sarvakāmapradāyakam \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Thus I have described the fascinating story of Satī to you which confers worldly pleasures and salvation, which is divine and bestows all wishes.

## \|\| 3.43.42 \|\|

*idamākhyānamanaghaṃ pavitraṃ parapāvanam \|*  
*svargyaṃ yaśasyamāyuṣyaṃ putrapautraphalapradam \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. This narrative is flawless, pure, sanctifying, conferring heavenly pleasures, glory, longevity and the pleasure of sons and grandsons.

## \|\| 3.43.43 \|\|

*ya idaṃ śṛṇuyādbhaktyā śrāvayedbhaktimānnarān \|*  
*sarvakarmā labhettāta paratra paramāṃ gatim \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Whoever listens to this or recites this with devotion, O dear, will attain the greatest goal in every rite.

## \|\| 3.43.44 \|\|

*yaḥ paṭhetpāṭhayedvāpi samākhyānamidaṃ śubham \|*  
*sopi bhuktvākhilān bhogānaṃte mokṣamavāpnuyāt \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. He who reads or teaches this auspicious narrative will attain salvation on death after enjoying all worldly pleasures.

## Section 4 - Rudra-saṃhitā (3): Pārvatī-khaṇḍa

## Chapter 1 - The marriage of Himācala

## \|\| 4.1.1 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*dākṣāyaṇī satī devī tyaktadehā piturmakhe \|*  
*kathaṃ girisutā brahmanbabhūva jagadambikā \|\| 1 \|\|*

Note: Himavat or Himācala is represented in two forms (1) the mobile and (2) immobile. The former is the subtle human form while the latter is the gross, stationary form identical with the mountain Himālayas. The present section recounts the marriage of Himavat with Menā in his mobile form. See RS III. 1. 15.

Nārada said:—

1\. O Brahmā, how did the goddess Satī, the daughter of Dakṣa who forsook her body in her father’s sacrifice, become the daughter of Himācala, and the mother of the universe?

## \|\| 4.1.2 \|\|

*kathaṃ kṛtvā tapo'tyugrampatimāpa śivaṃ ca sā \|*  
*etanme pṛcchate samyakkathaya tvaṃ viśeṣataḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. How could she secure Śiva as her husband after performing a severe penance? Please explain this clearly to me who ask you about it.

## \|\| 4.1.3 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*śṛṇu tvaṃ muniśārdūla śivācaritamuttamam \|*  
*pāvanaṃ paramaṃ divyaṃ sarvapāpaharaṃ śubham \|\| 3 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

3\. O foremost of sages, listen to the story of Śivā which is excellent, sanctifying, highly divine, auspicious and destructive of all sins.

## \|\| 4.1.4-5 \|\|

*yadā dākṣāyaṇī devī hareṇa sahitā mudā \|*  
*himācale sucikrīḍe līlayā parameśvarī \|\| 4 \|\|*

*matsuteyamiti jñātvā siṣeve mātṛvarcasā \|*  
*himācalapriyā menā sarvarddhibhiranirbharā \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. When the great goddess Satī, the daughter of Dakṣa, was sporting about on the Himālayas with Śiva, Menā, the beloved of Himācala thought that she was her own daughter and loved her like a mother with all kinds of nourishments.

## \|\| 4.1.6-7 \|\|

*yadā dākṣāyaṇī ruṣṭā nādṛtā svatanuṃ jahau \|*  
*pitrā dakṣeṇa tadyajñe saṃgatā parameśvarī \|\| 6 \|\|*

*tadaiva menakā tāṃ sā himācalapriyā mune \|*  
*śivalokasthitāṃ devīmārirādhayiṣustadā \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. When the great Goddess Satī, the daughter of Dakṣa who had been to her father’s sacrifice and who did not receive his due attention became angry and cast off her body, at the very same time, O sage, Himācala’s beloved Menā wanted to propitiate her in Śivaloka.

## \|\| 4.1.8 \|\|

*tasyāmahaṃ sutā syāmityavadhārya satī hṛdā \|*  
*tyaktadehā mano dadhre bhavituṃ himavatsutā \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Satī thought to herself:—“I shall be her daughter” and cast off her body in order to become the daughter of Himācala.

## \|\| 4.1.9 \|\|

*samayaṃ prāpya sā devī sarvadevastutā punaḥ \|*  
*satī tyaktatanuḥ prītyā menakātanayābhavat \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. At the proper time Satī who had cast off her body and who was worshipped and eulogised by the gods became the daughter of Menā out of sheer joy.

## \|\| 4.1.10 \|\|

*nāmnā sā pārvatī devī tapaḥ kṛtvā sudussaham \|*  
*nāradasyopadeśādvai patimprāpa śivaṃ punaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. On being advised by Nārada, the goddess who was named Pārvatī, performed a severe penance and thereby secured Śiva as her husband.

## \|\| 4.1.11 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*brahmanvidhe mahāprājña vada me vadatāṃ vara \|*  
*menakāyāssamutpatiṃ vivāhaṃ caritaṃ tathā \|\| 11 \|\|*

Nārada said:—

11\. O Brahmā, of great intellect and foremost of eloquent gods, please tell me the origin and details of the marriage of Menā.

## \|\| 4.1.12 \|\|

*dhanyā hi menakā devī yasyāṃ jātā sutā satī \|*  
*ato mānyā ca dhanyā ca sarveṣāṃ sā pativratā \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Blessed indeed is the gentle lady Menakā of whom Satī was born as a daughter. Hence that chaste lady is worthy of the honour and blessings of everyone.

## \|\| 4.1.13 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*śṛṇu tvaṃ nārada mune pārvatīmāturudbhavam \|*  
*vivāhaṃ caritaṃ caiva pāvanaṃ bhaktivarddhanam \|\| 13 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

13\. O sage Nārada, you listen to the story of the origin of Pārvatī’s mother and her marriage and other details both sanctifying and conducive to the growth of devotion.

## \|\| 4.1.14 \|\|

*astyuttarasyāṃ diśi vai girīśo himavānmahān \|*  
*parvato hi muniśreṣṭha mahātejāssamṛddhibhāk \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. O excellent sage, there in the northern region is a mountain called Himavat who is the lord of mountains and has great splendour and prosperity.

## \|\| 4.1.15 \|\|

*dvairūpyaṃ tasya vikhyātaṃ jaṃgamasthirabhedataḥ \|*  
*varṇayāmi samāsena tasya sūkṣmasvarūpakam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. His twofold aspects—that of a mobile nature and that of the immobile one—are well known. I succinctly describe his subtle form.

## \|\| 4.1.16 \|\|

*pūrvāparau toyanidhī suvigāhya sthito hi yaḥ \|*  
*nānāratnākaro ramyo mānadaṇḍa iva kṣiteḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. He is beautiful and is the storehouse of multifarious gems. Extending from the eastern to the western ocean he appears like a measuring rod of the Earth.

## \|\| 4.1.17 \|\|

*nānāvṛkṣasamākīrṇo nānāśṛṃgasucitritaḥ \|*  
*siṃhavyāghrādipaśubhissevitassukhibhissadā \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. He abounds in various trees. Being of variegated shape and features he is adorned by many peaks on him. Lions, tigers and other animals frequent it. Many happy persons live there for ever.

## \|\| 4.1.18 \|\|

*tuṣāranidhiratyugro nānāścaryavicitritaḥ \|*  
*devarṣisiddhamunibhissaṃśritaḥ śivasaṃpriyaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. He is the storehouse of snow (and yet) very fierce. He is the resort of wonderful things. He is resorted to by the gods, sages and seers. He is a great favourite of Śiva.

## \|\| 4.1.19 \|\|

*tapasthāno'tipūtātmā pāvanaśca mahātmanām \|*  
*tapassiddhipradotyaṃtaṃ nānādhātvākaraḥ śubhaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. He is of pure soul, an abode of austerities. He sanctifies even the great souls. He is the bestower of the benefit of austerities. He is the auspicious storehouse of multifarious minerals.

## \|\| 4.1.20 \|\|

*sa eva divyarūpo hi ramyaḥ sarvāṅgasundaraḥ \|*  
*viṣṇvaṃśo'vikṛtaḥ śailarājarājassatāmpriyaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. He is of a divine form. He is beautiful in every part. He is the unaffected part of Viṣṇu. He is the king of leading mountains and a great favourite of the good.

## \|\| 4.1.21 \|\|

*kulasthityai ca sa girirdharmmavarddhanahetave \|*  
*svavivāhaṃ karttumaicchatpitṛdevahitecchayā \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Due to the desire for the benefit of the manes and the gods and for the stabilisation of his race as well as for the increase of virtue, Himācala wanted to marry.

## \|\| 4.1.22 \|\|

*tasminnavasare devāḥ svārthamācintya kṛtsnaśaḥ \|*  
*ūcuḥ pitṝnsamāgatya divyānprītyā munīśvara \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. At that time, considering their own interest entirely, O excellent sage, the gods approached the celestial forefathers and said lovingly to them.

## \|\| 4.1.23 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*sarve śṛṇuta no vākyaṃ pitaraḥ prītamānasāḥ \|*  
*karttavyaṃ tattathaivāśu devakāryyepsavo yadi \|\| 23 \|\|*

The gods said:—

23\. “O ye forefathers, listen to our words with pleasure. If you desire that the affairs of the gods be fulfilled you must act accordingly soon.

## \|\| 4.1.24-25 \|\|

*menā nāma sutā yā vo jyeṣṭhā maṅgalarūpiṇī \|*  
*tāmvivāhya ca suprītyā himākhyena mahībhṛtā \|\| 24 \|\|*

*evaṃ sarvamahālābhaḥ sarveṣāṃ ca bhaviṣyati \|*  
*yuṣmākamamarāṇāṃ ca duḥkhahāniḥ pade pade \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. Uniting your eldest daughter Menā of auspicious features with Himācala, a great benefit will accrue to everyone. At every step, the miseries of the gods and those of yours as well can be reduced”.

## \|\| 4.1.26 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityākarṇyāparavacaḥ pitaraste vimṛśya ca \|*  
*smṛtvā śāpaṃ sutānāṃ ca procuromiti tadvacaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

26\. On hearing these words of the gods, pondering over them and remembering the curse incurred by their daughters, the forefathers said “Amen” to their proposals.

## \|\| 4.1.27 \|\|

*dadurmenāṃ suvidhinā himāgāya nijātmajām \|*  
*samutsavo mahānāsīttadvivāhe sumaṅgale \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. They gave their daughter Menā to Himavat. In that auspicious marriage there were great festivities.

## \|\| 4.1.28 \|\|

*haryyādayā'pi te devā munayaścāparokhilāḥ \|*  
*ājagmustatra saṃsmṛtya vāmadevaṃ bhavaṃ dhiyā \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Viṣṇu, the other gods and the sages reached there with their hearts set on Śiva.

## \|\| 4.1.29 \|\|

*utsavaṃ kārayāmāsurdattvā dānānyanekaśaḥ \|*  
*supraśasya pitṝndivyānpraśaśaṃsurhimācalam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Giving many charitable gifts they made the celebration a great success. They praised the celestial forefathers and the Himavat.

## \|\| 4.1.30 \|\|

*mahāmodānvitā devāste sarve samunīśvarāḥ \|*  
*saṃjagmuḥ svasvadhāmāni saṃsmarantaḥ śivāśivau \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. All the gods and the sages rejoiced and returned to their own abodes with their hearts set on Śiva.

## \|\| 4.1.31 \|\|

*kautukaṃ bahu samprāpya suvivāhya priyāṃ ca tām \|*  
*ājagāma svabhavanaṃ mudamāpa girīśvaraḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. After receiving many articles as gifts and marrying the beloved lady Menā, the lord of mountains returned to his abode and rejoiced.

## \|\| 4.1.32 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|\| menayā hi himāgasya suvivāho munīśvara \|*  
*prokto me sukhadaḥ prītyā kimbhūyaḥ śrotumicchasi \|\| 32 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

32\. O excellent sage, the pleasing details of the splendid marriage of Himavat with Menā have been recounted to you thus. What more do you wish to hear?

## Chapter 2 - Menā and others incur the imprecation of Sanaka etc.

## \|\| 4.2.1 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*vidhe prājña vadedānīṃ menotpattiṃ samādarāt \|*  
*api śāpaṃ samācakṣva kuru saṃdehabhaṃjanam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Nārada said:—

1\. O Brahmā, the intelligent one, please now tell me reverently about the origin of Menā as well as the imprecation. Please clear my doubts.

## \|\| 4.2.2 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*śṛṇu nārada suprītyā menotpattiṃ vivekataḥ \|*  
*munibhiḥ saha vakṣyehaṃ sutavaryya mahābudha \|\| 2 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

2\. O Nārada and the sages, listen to the narrative of the origin of Menā. O excellent son, O great scholar, I shall mention it now.

## \|\| 4.2.3 \|\|

*dakṣanāmā mama suto yaḥ purā kathito mune \|*  
*tasya jātāḥ sutāḥ ṣaṣṭipramitāssṛṣṭikāraṇāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. O sage, I have already told you about my son Dakṣa. He had sixty daughters all of whom were the instruments of creation.

## \|\| 4.2.4 \|\|

*tāsāṃ vivāhamakarotsa varaiḥ kaśyapādibhiḥ \|*  
*viditaṃ te samastaṃ tatprastutaṃ śṛṇu nārada \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. He celebrated their marriages with Kaśyapa and other bridegrooms. You know all that already. O Nārada, now, listen to the present story.

## \|\| 4.2.5 \|\|

*tāsāṃ madhye svadhānāmnīṃ pitṛbhyo dattavānsutām \|*  
*tisrobhavansutāstasyāssubhagā dharmamūrtayaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Among those, the daughter Svadhā was given to the forefathers. She had three daughters all of whom were of handsome features and virtuous forms.

## \|\| 4.2.6 \|\|

*tāsāṃ nāmāni śṛṇu me pāvanāni munīśvara \|*  
*sadā vighnaharāṇyeva mahāmaṃgaladāni ca \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. O excellent sage, listen to their holy names which remove obstacles and confer blessings.

## \|\| 4.2.7 \|\|

*menānāmnī sutā jyeṣṭhā madhyā dhanyā kalāvatī \|*  
*antyā etāssutāssarvāḥ pitṝṇāmmānasodbhavāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Menā was the eldest. Dhanyā was the middle. Kalāvatī was the youngest. All these were mentally conceived daughters of the forefathers.

## \|\| 4.2.8 \|\|

*ayonijāḥ svadhāyāśca lokatastatsutā matāḥ\|\| \|*  
*āsāmprocya sunāmāni sarvānkāmāñjano labhet \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. They were not born of the womb of Svadhā. They were conventionally considered her children. On reciting their names, men can achieve their desires.

## \|\| 4.2.9 \|\|

*jagadvaṃdyāḥ sadā lokamātaraḥ paramodadāḥ \|*  
*yoginyaḥ paramā jñānanidhānāstāstrilokagāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The mothers of the worlds are worthy of reverence of the entire universe always. They are the bestowers of great joy. They are great yoginīs, storehouses of knowledge. They pervade the three worlds.

## \|\| 4.2.10 \|\|

*ekasminsamaye tisro bhaginyastā munīśvara \|*  
*śvetadvīpaṃ viṣṇulokaṃ jagmurdarśanahetave \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. O excellent sage, once the three sisters went to Śvetadvīpa (white island) in the world of Viṣṇu for sightseeing purpose.

## \|\| 4.2.11 \|\|

*kṛtvā praṇāmaṃ viṣṇośca saṃstutiṃ bhaktisaṃyutāḥ \|*  
*tasthustadājñayā tatra susamājo mahānabhūt \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. After bowing to and eulogising Viṣṇu with great devotion they halted there at his bidding. A great concourse of people was held there.

## \|\| 4.2.12 \|\|

*tadaiva sanakādyāstu siddhā brahmasutā mune \|*  
*gatāstatra hariṃ natvā stutvā tasthustadājñayā \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. O sage, at the same time, Siddhas, sons of Brahmā—Sanaka and others came there. They bowed to and lauded Viṣṇu and stayed there at his bidding.

## \|\| 4.2.13 \|\|

*sanakādyānmunīndṛṣṭvottasthuste sakalā drutam \|*  
*tatrasthānsaṃsthitānnatvā devādyāṃllokavanditān \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. On seeing those sages Sanaka and others and the persons who had assembled there, stood up. When they, the elders of gods respected by the people, sat they all bowed to them.

## \|\| 4.2.14 \|\|

*tisro bhaginyastāṃstatra nottasthurmohitā mune \|*  
*māyayā daivavivaśāśśaṅkarasya parātmanaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Helpless by misfortune and deluded by lord Śiva’s illusion O sage, the three sisters did not stand up.

## \|\| 4.2.15 \|\|

*mohinī sarva lokānāṃ śivamāyā garīyasī \|*  
*tadadhīnaṃ jagatsarvaṃ śivecchā sā prakīrtyate \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Śiva’s illusion is weighty and capable of deluding the worlds. The entire universe is subservient to it. It is also called Śiva’s Will.

## \|\| 4.2.16 \|\|

*prārabdhaṃ procyate saiva tannāmāni hyanekaśaḥ \|*  
*śivecchayā bhavatyeva nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The same is also called an action that has begun to fructify. Its names are many. Everything takes place on Śiva’s wish. There is nothing to be pondered over in this respect.

## \|\| 4.2.17 \|\|

*bhūtvā tadvaśagāstā vai na cakrurapi tannatim \|*  
*vismitāssampradṛśyaiva saṃsthitāstatra kevalam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Becoming a victim thereof, the sisters did not make obeisance to them. They remained surprised and stunned thereafter seeing them.

## \|\| 4.2.18 \|\|

*tādṛśīṃ tadgatiṃ dṛṣṭvā sanakādyā munīśvarāḥ \|*  
*jñānino'pi paraṃ cakruḥ krodhaṃ durviṣahaṃ ca te \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. On seeing such a behaviour on their part the great sages, Sanaka and others, despite being wise, became unbearably furious.

## \|\| 4.2.19 \|\|

*śivecchāmohitastatra sakrodhastā uvāca ha \|*  
*sanatkumāro yogīśaśśāpandaṇḍakaraṃ dadan \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Himself deluded by Śiva’s illusion Sanaka, a perfect Yogin, furiously told them giving a curse as punishment.

## \|\| 4.2.20 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*yūyaṃ tisro bhaginyaśca mūḍhāḥ sadvayunojjhitāḥ \|*  
*ajñātaśrutitattvā hi pitṛkanyā api dhruvam \|\| 20 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

20\. Inspite of being the daughters of the forefathers, ye three sisters are foolish, bereft of wisdom and ignorant of the essence of the Vedas.

## \|\| 4.2.21 \|\|

*abhyutthānaṃ kṛtaṃ no yannamaskāropi garvataḥ \|*  
*mohitā narabhāvatvātsvargāddūrā bhavantu hi \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. You did not stand up nor did you pay any respects to us. You were haughty and deluded and so evinced a deluded disposition of human beings. Hence all of you shall leave heaven.

## \|\| 4.2.22 \|\|

*narastriyaḥ sambhavantu tisro'pi jñānamohitāḥ \|*  
*svakarmaṇaḥ prabhaṇāve labhadhvaṃ phalamīdṛśam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. May the three sisters deluded by ignorance be born as human womenfolk. May ye reap this fruit as a result of the power of your own action.

## \|\| 4.2.23 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya ca sādhvastāstisro'pi cakitā bhṛśam \|*  
*patitvā pādayostasya samūcūrnatamastakāḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

23\. On hearing this, the chaste maidens got perplexed. The three fell at his feet and spoke with their heads bent down.

## \|\| 4.2.24 \|\|

*pitṛtanayā ūcuḥ \|*  
*munivaryya dayāsindho prasanno bhava cādhunā \|*  
*tvatpraṇāmaṃ vayaṃ mūḍhāḥ kurmahe sma na bhāvataḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

The daughters of the forefathers said:—

24\. “O excellent sage, ocean of mercy, be pleased now. Because we were mentally confounded we did not bow to you.

## \|\| 4.2.25 \|\|

*prāptaṃ ca tatphalaṃ vipra na te doṣo mahāmune \|*  
*anugrahaṃ kuruṣvātra labhema svargatimpunaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. O Brahmin, the result thereof has been achieved by us. O great sage it is not your fault. Bless us now whereby we shall regain heavenly abode again.”

## \|\| 4.2.26 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*śrutvā tadvacanaṃ tāta provāca sa munistadā \|*  
*śāpoddhāraṃ prasannātmā preritaḥ śivamāyayā \|\| 26 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

26\. On hearing their words, O dear, the sage spoke to them. He had been induced by Śiva’s illusion to give them redemption from the curse. He was a bit consoled.

## \|\| 4.2.27 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*pitṝṇāṃ tanayāstisraḥ śṛṇuta prītamānasāḥ \|*  
*vacanaṃ mama śokaghnaṃ sukhadaṃ sarvadaiva vaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

27\. “O ye three daughters of forefathers, listen with pleasure to my words that will dispel your sorrow and bestow happiness on you.

## \|\| 4.2.28 \|\|

*viṣṇoraṃśasya śailasya himādhārasya kāminī \|*  
*jyeṣṭhā bhavatu tatkanyā bhaviṣyatyeva pārvatī \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. May the eldest among you become the wife of Himavat the mountain that is a part of Viṣṇu. Pārvatī shall be her daughter.

## \|\| 4.2.29 \|\|

*dhanyā priyā dvitīyā tu yoginī janakasya ca \|*  
*tasyāḥ kanyā mahālakṣmīrnāmnā sītā bhaviṣyati \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. The second daughter Dhanyā shall be the Yoginī, the wife of Janaka. Her daughter shall be Mahālakṣmī in the name of Sītā.

## \|\| 4.2.30 \|\|

*vṛṣabhānasya vaiśyasya kaniṣṭhā ca kalāvatī \|\| \|*  
*bhaviṣyati priyā rādhā tatsutā dvāparāntataḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. The youngest Kalāvatī shall be the wife of the Vaiśya—Vṛṣabhāna. At the end of Dvāpara, Rādhā shall be her daughter.

## \|\| 4.2.31 \|\|

*menakā yoginī patyā pārvatyāśca vareṇa ca \|*  
*tena dehena kailāsaṃ gamiṣyati parampadam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. The Yoginī Menā shall attain the great region Kailāsa along with her body and in the company of her husband due to the boon of Pārvatī.

## \|\| 4.2.32 \|\|

*dhanyā ca sītayā sīradhvajo janakavaṃśajaḥ \|*  
*jīvanmukto mahāyogī vaikuṇṭhaṃ ca gamiṣyati \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Janaka shall be blessed by Sītā born in Janaka’s race and he shall be a living liberated soul. A great Yogin, he will attain Vaikuṇṭha.

## \|\| 4.2.33 \|\|

*kalāvatī vṛṣabhānasya kautukātkanyayā saha \|*  
*jīvanmuktā ca golokaṃ gamiṣyati na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Kalāvatī by the virtue of Vṛṣabhāna shall become a living liberated soul and attain Goloka along with her daughter. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 4.2.34 \|\|

*vinā vipattiṃ mahimā keṣāṃ kutra bhaviṣyati \|*  
*sukarmiṇāṃ gate duḥkhe prabhaveddurlabhaṃ sukham \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Without adversity how can one attain greatness? To persons of good rites, if misery vanishes happiness is likely to be difficult of access.

## \|\| 4.2.35 \|\|

*yūyaṃ pitṝṇāṃ tanayāssarvāssvargavilāsikāḥ \|*  
*karmakṣayaśca yuṣmākamabhavadviṣṇudarśanāt \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Ye the daughters of forefathers shall shine in heaven. By the vision of Viṣṇu your evil actions have been quelled.”

## \|\| 4.2.36 \|\|

*ityuktvā punarapyāha gatakrodho munīśvaraḥ \|*  
*śivaṃ saṃsmṛtya manasā jñānadaṃ bhuktimuktidam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. After saying this, the sage was freed of his fury on thinking of Śiva, the bestower of wisdom, worldly pleasures and salvation.

## \|\| 4.2.37 \|\|

*aparaṃ śṛṇuta prītyā madvacassukhadaṃ sadā \|*  
*dhanyā yūyaṃ śivaprītā mānyāḥ pūjyā hyabhīkṣṇaśaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Listen further to my words always pleasing to you. You are all blessed by Śiva’s pleasure. Hence you will be worthy of honour and respect immediately.

## \|\| 4.2.38 \|\|

*menāyāstanayā devī pārvatī jagadambikā \|*  
*bhaviṣyati priyā śambhostapaḥ kṛtvā sudussaham \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Menā’s daughter, goddess Pārvatī, the mother of the universe shall become Śiva’s beloved after performing severe penance.

## \|\| 4.2.39 \|\|

*dhanyā sutā smṛtā sītā rāmapatnī bhaviṣyati \|*  
*laukikācāramāśritya rāmeṇa vihariṣyati \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Dhanyā’s daughter Sītā will become Rāma’s wife. Based on worldly conventions she will sport about with Rāma.

## \|\| 4.2.40 \|\|

*kalāvatīsutā rādhā sākṣādgolokavāsinī \|*  
*guptasnehanibaddhā sā kṛṣṇapatnī bhaviṣyati \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Kalāvatī’s daughter Rādhā, resident of Goloka shall become the wife of Kṛṣṇa united with him in secret love.

## \|\| 4.2.41 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|\| itthamābhāṣya sa munirbhrātṛbhissaha saṃstutaḥ \|*  
*sanatkumāro bhagavāṃstatraivāntarhito'bhavat \|\| 41 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

41\. After saying this, that holy sage Sanatkumāra vanished there itself along with his brothers after he was eulogised duly.

## \|\| 4.2.42 \|\|

*tisro bhaginyastāstāta pitṝṇāṃ mānasīḥ sutāḥ \|*  
*gatapāpāssukhaṃ prāpya svadhāma prayayurdrutam \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. The three sisters, the mentally conceived daughters of the forefathers were freed of their sins and attained happiness. They returned to their residence quickly.

## Chapter 3 - Hymn to Śiva by Viṣṇu and other gods

## \|\| 4.3.1 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*vidhe prājña mahādhīmanvada me vadatāṃ vara \|*  
*tataḥ paraṃ kimabhavaccaritaṃ viṣṇusadguro \|\| 1 \|\|*

Nārada said:—

1\. O Brahmā, the best of eloquent ones, of great wisdom, please tell me. What is the subsequent story of the good auspicious mountain?

## \|\| 4.3.2 \|\|

*adbhuteyaṃ kathā proktā menā pūrvagatiḥ śubhā \|*  
*vivāhaśca śrutassamyakparamaṃ caritaṃ vada \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. You have narrated the wonderful story of the auspicious antecedents of Menā. The details of the marital rites too are heard. Please continue the subsequent narrative.

## \|\| 4.3.3 \|\|

*menāṃ vivāhya sa giriḥ kṛtavānkiṃ tataḥ param \|*  
*pārvatī kathamutpannā tasyāṃ vai jagadambikā \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. After marrying Menā what did the mountain do afterwards? How was Pārvatī, the mother of the universe, born of her?

## \|\| 4.3.4 \|\|

*tapassudussahaṃ kṛtvā kathaṃ prāpa patiṃ haram \|*  
*etatsarvaṃ samācakṣva vistarācchāṃkaraṃ yaśaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. How did she secure Śiva as her husband after performing a severe penance? Narrate all these things in detail regarding the glory of Śiva.

## \|\| 4.3.5 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*mune tvaṃ śṛṇu suprītyā śāṃkaraṃ suyaśaḥ śubham \|*  
*yacchrutvā brahmahā śuddhyetsarvānkāmānavāpnuyāt \|\| 5 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

5\. O sage, lovingly listen to the auspicious glory of Śiva on hearing which even a slayer of a brahmin becomes pure and attains all desires.

## \|\| 4.3.6 \|\|

*yadā menāvivāhantu kṛtvāgacchadgirirgṛham \|*  
*tadā samutsavo jātastriṣu lokeṣu nārada \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. O Nārada, there was great pomp and ceremony in the three worlds when Himācala returned to his abode after marrying Menā.

## \|\| 4.3.7 \|\|

*himācalo'pi suprītaścakāra paramotsavam \|*  
*bhūsurānbaṃdhuvargāṃśca parānānarca saddhiyā \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The delighted Himācala too celebrated a great festival. With good intention he worshipped and revered brahmins, kinsmen and others.

## \|\| 4.3.8 \|\|

*sarve dvijāśca santuṣṭā dattvāśīrvacanaṃ varam \|*  
*yayustasmai svasvadhāma baṃdhuvargāstathāpare \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The contented brahmins returned to their respective abodes after blessing them. The kinsmen and the others also returned.

## \|\| 4.3.9 \|\|

*himācalo'pi suprīto menayā sukhade gṛhe \|*  
*reme'nyatra ca susthāne nandanādivaneṣvapi \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The delighted Himacāla sported with Menā in his cosy abode, Nandana and other parks as well as in several nice places.

## \|\| 4.3.10 \|\|

*tasminnavasare devā mune viṣṇvādayo'khilāḥ \|*  
*munayaśca mahātmānaḥ prajagmurbhūdharāntike \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. At that time, O sage, Viṣṇu, the gods and the noble-sould sages approached the mountain.

## \|\| 4.3.11 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā tānāgatāndevānpraṇanāma mudā giriḥ \|*  
*saṃmānaṃ kṛtavānbhaktyā praśaṃsansva vidhiṃ mahān \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. On seeing the gods after their arrival, the noble Himācala bowed to them gladly and honoured them with devotion. He praised his own good fortune.

## \|\| 4.3.12 \|\|

*sāñjalirnataśīrṣo hi sa tuṣṭāva subhaktitaḥ \|*  
*romodgamo mahānāsīdgireḥ premāśravo'patan \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. With the head bent down and palms joined in reverence, he eulogised them with great devotion. Himācala’s hair stood on end and tears of love fell from his eyes.

## \|\| 4.3.13 \|\|

*tataḥ praṇamya suprīto himaśailaḥ prasannadhīḥ \|*  
*uvāca praṇato bhūtvā mune viṣṇvādikānsurān \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. O sage, after bowing to them, the delighted Himācala spoke thus to Viṣṇu and other gods.

## \|\| 4.3.14 \|\|

*himācala uvāca \|*  
*adya me saphalaṃ janma saphalaṃ sumahattapaḥ \|*  
*adya me saphalaṃ jñānamadya me saphalāḥ kriyāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

Himācala said:—

14\. Today my life has become fruitful. My good penance has become fruitful. Today my knowledge has become fruitful. Today my sacred rites have become fruitful.

## \|\| 4.3.15 \|\|

*dhanyo'hamadya saṃjāto dhanyā me sakalā kṣitiḥ \|*  
*dhanyaṃ kulaṃ tathā dārāssarvaṃ dhanyaṃ na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. I have become blessed today. My entire kingdom, my wife and family have become blessed. Everything has become blessed. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 4.3.16 \|\|

*yataḥ samāgatā yūyaṃ militvā sarva ekadā \|*  
*māṃ nideśayata prītyocitaṃ mattvā svasevakam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Wherefore have all of you come in a body? Lovingly command me, considering me your own servant.

## \|\| 4.3.17 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*iti śrutvā mahīdhrasya vacanaṃ te surāstadā \|*  
*ūcurharyādayaḥ prītāḥ siddhiṃ matvā svakāryataḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

17\. On hearing these words of Himācala, Viṣṇu and other gods considered their affair fulfilled and were delighted. They spoke.

## \|\| 4.3.18 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*himācala mahāprājña śṛṇva smadvacanaṃ hitam \|*  
*yadarthamāgatāssarve tadbrūmaḥ prītito vayam \|\| 18 \|\|*

Gods said:—

18\. “O Himācala of great intellect, please listen to our beneficent words. We shall gladly tell you why we have come.

## \|\| 4.3.19 \|\|

*yā purā jagadambomā dakṣakanyā'bhavadgire \|*  
*rudrapatnī hi sā bhūtvā cikrīḍe suciraṃ bhuvi \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. O Himācala, the mother of the universe Umā, who was born as Dakṣa’s daughter, became Rudra’s wife and sported for a long time on the: earth.

## \|\| 4.3.20 \|\|

*pitṛto'nādaraṃ prāpya saṃsmṛtya svapaṇaṃ satī \|*  
*jagāma svapadaṃ tyaktvā taccharīraṃ tadāmbikā \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. On being disrespected by her father, Satī remembered her vow, abandoned her body and returned to her own region.

## \|\| 4.3.21-22 \|\|

*sā kathā viditā loke tavāpi himabhūdhara \|*  
*evaṃ sati mahālābho bhaveddevagaṇasya hi \|\| 21 \|\|*

*sarvasya bhavataścāpi syussarve te vaśāssurāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. O Himācala, this story is well known in the world. You too know it. If this takes place it will be an asset to all gods as well as to you. The gods too will be under your control.”

## \|\| 4.3.23 \|\|

*\|\|brahmovāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya vacasteṣāṃ haryādīnāṃ girīśvaraḥ \|*  
*tathāstviti prasannātmā provāca na ca sādaram \|\| 23 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

23\. On hearing these words of Viṣṇu and others the delighted lord Himācala said—“So be it” and worshipped them with respect.

## \|\| 4.3.24 \|\|

*atha te ca samādiśya tadvidhimparamādarāt \|*  
*svayaṃ jagmuśca śaraṇamumāyāśśaṃkara striyaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. After instructing him in the method to be followed with great devotion they approached Umā, the consort of Śiva.

## \|\| 4.3.25 \|\|

*susthale manasā sthitvā sasmarurjagadambikām \|*  
*praṇamya bahuśastatra tuṣṭuvuḥ śraddhayā surāḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. They stationed themselves in a good place and remembered the mother of the universe, and bowing to her repeatedly eulogised her with devotion.

## \|\| 4.3.26 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*devyume jagatāmamba śivalokanivāsinī \|*  
*sadāśivapriye durge tvāṃ namāmo maheśvari \|\| 26 \|\|*

The gods said:—

26\. O goddess Umā, mother of the universe, resident of Śivaloka, favourite of Śiva, O great goddess, O Durgā, we bow to you,

## \|\| 4.3.27 \|\|

*śrīśaktiṃ pāvanāṃ śāntāṃ puṣṭimparamapāvanīm \|*  
*vayannāmāmahe bhaktyā mahadavyaktarūpiṇīm \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. With great devotion we bow to the illustrious Energy, the holy, the tranquil, the holy nourishment and the one with the forms of Mahat and the Avyakta.

## \|\| 4.3.28 \|\|

*śivāṃ śivakarāṃ śuddhāṃ sthūlāṃ sūkṣmāṃ parāyaṇām \|*  
*antarvidyāsuvidyābhyāṃ suprītāṃ tvāṃ namāmahe \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. We worship you, Śiva the cause of welfare, the pure, the gross, the subtle, the great goal and the one delighted with the inner and good learning.

## \|\| 4.3.29 \|\|

*tvaṃ śraddhā tvaṃ dhṛtistvaṃ śrīstvameva sarvagocarā \|*  
*tvandīdhitissūryyagatā svaprapañcaprakāśinī \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. You are faith, fortitude and prosperity. You alone have control over everything; you are the splendour and energy of the sun illuminating your own universe.

## \|\| 4.3.30 \|\|

*yā ca brahmāṇḍasaṃsthāne jagajjīveṣu yā jagat \|*  
*āpyāyayati brahmāditṛṇāntaṃ tāṃ namāmahe \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. We bow to her who promotes robustness in all the beings of the universe from Brahmā to a blade of grass in the whole Cosmos.

## \|\| 4.3.31 \|\|

*gāyatrī tvaṃ vedamātā tvaṃ sāvitrī sarasvatī \|*  
*tvaṃ vārtā sarvajagatāṃ tvaṃ trayī dharmarūpiṇī \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. You are Gāyatrī, the mother of the Vedas, Sāvitrī, Sarasvatī, the sustenance of all the universe; you are the triad of the Vedas having Dharma for its form.

## \|\| 4.3.32 \|\|

*nidrā tvaṃ sarvabhūteṣu kṣudhā tṛptistvameva hi \|*  
*tṛṣṇā kāntiśchavistuṣṭissarvānandakarī sadā \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. You are sleep in all living beings; you are hunger, satiety, thirst, splendour, brilliance and contentment. You are the delighter of every one for ever.

## \|\| 4.3.33 \|\|

*tvaṃ lakṣmīḥ puṇyakartṝṇāṃ tvaṃ jyeṣṭhā pāpināṃ sadā \|*  
*tvaṃ śāntiḥ sarvajagatāṃ tvaṃ dhātrī prāṇapoṣiṇī \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. To those who perform meritorious actions you are the goddess of fortune. To the sinners you are the eldest sister, the deity of Ignominy; you are peace for the universe, and the mother sustaining lives.

## \|\| 4.3.34 \|\|

*tvantasvarūpā bhūtānāṃ pañcānāmapi sārakṛt \|*  
*tvaṃ hi nītibhṛtāṃ nītirvyavasāyasvarūpiṇī \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. You are the essential feature of five elements. You are Justice in those who uphold justice. You are endeavour personified.

## \|\| 4.3.35 \|\|

*gītistvaṃ sāmavedasya granthistvaṃ yajuṣāṃ hutiḥ \|*  
*ṛgvedasya tathā mātrātharvaṇasya parā gatiḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Of the Ṛgveda you are the invocation; of the Yajurveda you are the blending knot of the mantras; of Sāmaveda you are the song and of the Atharvaṇa Veda you are the measure of time, you are the final goal.

## \|\| 4.3.36 \|\|

*samastagīrvāṇagaṇasya śaktistamomayī dhātṛguṇaikadṛśyā \|*  
*rajaḥ prapaṃcāttu bhavaikarūpā yā na śrutā bhavyakarī stuteha \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. She who is the Tāmasika power of all the Gods, she who is visible in the Rājasika quality of the Creator, she who is heard by us as the benefactress and of the form of Śiva is eulogised here.

## \|\| 4.3.37 \|\|

*saṃsārasāgarakarālabhavāṅgaduḥkhanistārakāritaraṇiśca nivītahīnā \|*  
*aṣṭāṅgayogaparipālanakelidakṣāṃ vindhyāgavāsaniratāṃ praṇamāma tāṃ vai \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Let us bow to her who is interested in residing on the Vindhya mountains; who is clever in the playful activity of affording protection to Aṣṭāṅga Yoga; who is devoid of cessation and who acts like a raft that enables the crossing of the ocean of worldly existence with its terrible miseries.

## \|\| 4.3.38 \|\|

*nāsākṣi vaktrabhujavakṣasi mānase ca dhṛtyā sukhāni vitanoṣi sadaiva jantoḥ \|*  
*nidreti yāti subhagā jagatī bhavā naḥ sā naḥ prasīdaṃtu bhavasthitipālanāya \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. May she be pleased with us, for keeping up the sustenance of the world, she, who in the form of slumber that is extremely exhilarating to all born in the universe, extends pleasure in the nose, eyes, face, arms, chest and the mind.

## \|\| 4.3.39 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*iti stutvā maheśānīṃ jagadambāmumāṃ satīm \|*  
*supreyamanasaḥ sarve tasthuste darśanepsavaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

39\. Thus eulogising the great Goddess Satī, the mother of the universe, all of them stood waiting lovingly desirous of seeing her.

## Chapter 4 - The Goddess consoles the Gods

## \|\| 4.4.1 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*itthaṃ devaiḥ stutā devī durgā durgārtināśinī \|*  
*āvirbabhūva devānāṃ purato jagadaṃbikā \|\| 1 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

1\. Thus eulogised by the Gods, the Goddess Durgā, the mother of the universe, the destroyer of impassable distress, appeared in front of them.

## \|\| 4.4.2 \|\|

*rathe ratnamaye divye saṃsthitā paramādbhute \|*  
*kiṃkiṇījālasaṃyukte mṛdusaṃstaraṇe vare \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. She was seated in a wonderful divine gem-set chariot over which a soft cushion had been spread and which was decorated with tinkling ornaments.

## \|\| 4.4.3 \|\|

*koṭisūryādhikābhāsa ramyāvayavabhāsinī \|*  
*svatejorāśimadhyasthā vararūpā samacchavi \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. She was shining with the brilliance of her limbs that surpassed even the lustre of a crore of suns. She was surrounded by a halo created by her own lustre. She was of symmetrical splendour.

## \|\| 4.4.4 \|\|

*anūpamā mahāmāyā sadāśivavilāsinī \|*  
*triguṇā nirguṇā nityā śivalokanivāsinī \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. She was the unequalled supreme illusion, the beautiful wife of Sadāśiva. She had all the three qualities and was devoid of attributes also, she had been staying in the region of Śiva.

## \|\| 4.4.5 \|\|

*tridevajananī caṇḍī śivā sarvārtināśinī \|*  
*sarvamātā mahānidrā sarvasvajanatāriṇī \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. She was the mother of the three deities, Caṇḍī, Śivā, the destroyer of the distress of all, the mother of all supreme slumber and the redeemer of all her own people.

## \|\| 4.4.6 \|\|

*tejorāśeḥ prabhāvāttu sā tu dṛṣṭvā suraiśśivā \|*  
*tuṣṭuvustāṃ punaste vai surā darśanakāṃkṣiṇaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Śivā was seen by the gods through the power of huge column of brilliance. Again the gods eulogised her in order to have a sight of her.

## \|\| 4.4.7 \|\|

*atha devagaṇāssarve viṣṇvādyā darśanepsavaḥ \|*  
*dadṛśurjagadambāṃ tāṃ tatkṛpāṃ prāpya tatra hi \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Then Viṣṇu and other gods who were desirous of seeing her saw the mother of the universe there itself after receiving her favour.

## \|\| 4.4.8 \|\|

*babhūvānandasandohassarveṣāṃ tridivaukasām \|*  
*punaḥ punaḥ praṇemustāṃ tuṣṭuvuśca viśeṣataḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The dwellers of heaven were extremely pleased, they bowed to her again and again and particularly eulogised her.

## \|\| 4.4.9 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*śive śarvāṇi kalyāṇi jagadamba maheśvari \|*  
*tvāṃ natāssarvathā devā vayaṃ sarvārtināśinīm \|\| 9 \|\|*

The gods said:—

9\. O Śivā, O great Goddess, O mother of the universe we gods bow to you, the destroyer of all distress.

## \|\| 4.4.10 \|\|

*na hi jānanti deveśi vedaśśāstrāṇi kṛtsnaśaḥ \|*  
*atīto mahimā dhyānaṃ tava vāṅmanasośśive \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. O Goddess, neither the Vedas nor the sacred texts know you perfectly. Your greatness, O Śivā, is beyond the scope of speech and mind and cannot even be meditated upon.

## \|\| 4.4.11 \|\|

*atadvyāvṛttitastāṃ vai cakitaṃ cakitaṃ sadā \|*  
*abhidhatte śrutirapi pareṣāṃ kā kathā matā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Even the Vedas mention you, trembling with fright, by negating what you are not. What will be the matter in regard to others?

## \|\| 4.4.12 \|\|

*jānanti bahavo bhaktāstvatkṛpāṃ prāpya bhaktitaḥ \|*  
*śaraṇāgatabhaktānāṃ na kutrāpi bhayādikam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Many devotees know the same after getting your favour through devotion. There is no cause for fear to the devotees who seek refuge in you.

## \|\| 4.4.13 \|\|

*vijñaptiṃ śṛṇu suprītā yasyā dāsāssadāmbike \|*  
*tava devi mahādevi hīnato varṇayāmahe \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. O great Goddess listen to our submission which we, your slaves for ever, are going to explain.

## \|\| 4.4.14 \|\|

*purā dakṣasutā bhūtvā saṃjātā haravallabhā \|*  
*brahmaṇaśca pareṣāṃ vā nāśayatvamakaṃmahat \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Formerly you were born as the daughter of Dakṣa and were married to Śiva. You destroyed the great misery of Brahmā and others.

## \|\| 4.4.15 \|\|

*pitṛto'nādaraṃ prāpyātyajaḥ paṇavaśāttanum \|*  
*svalokamagamastvaṃ vālabhadduḥkhaṃ haro'pi hi \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Being disrespected by your father, you cast off your body in accordance with your vow. You then went to your own world and Śiva became miserable.

## \|\| 4.4.16 \|\|

*na hi jātamprapūrṇaṃ taddevakāryaṃ maheśvari \|*  
*vyākulā munayo devāśśaraṇantvāṃ gatā vayam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. O great Goddess, the purpose of the gods has not been completely carried out. The sages are agitated. Hence we, Gods, have sought refuge in you.

## \|\| 4.4.17 \|\|

*pūrṇaṃ kuru maheśāni nirjarāṇāṃ manoratham \|*  
*sanatkumāravacanaṃ saphalaṃ syādyathā śive \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. O great Goddess, please fulfil the desire of the God, O Śivā, so that the words of Sanatkumāra may be fruitful.

## \|\| 4.4.18 \|\|

*avatīrya kṣitau devi rudrapatnī punarbhava \|*  
*līlāṃ kuru yathāyogyaṃ prāpnuyurnirjarāssukham \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. O Goddess, incarnating again on the earth please be the wife of Rudra (Śiva) again. Carry on your sports in a fitting manner and let the Gods be happy.

## \|\| 4.4.19 \|\|

*sukhī syāddevi rudro'pi kailāsācalasaṃsthitaḥ \|*  
*sarve bhavantu sukhino duḥkhaṃ naśyatu kṛtsnaśaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. O Goddess, may Rudra too, the resident of Kailāsa be happy. Let all become happy. Let misery perish entirely.

## \|\| 4.4.20 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*iti procyāmarāssarve viṣṇvādyāḥ premasaṃkulāḥ \|*  
*maunamāsthāya saṃtasthurbhaktinamrā tmamūrtayaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

20\. Saying so, Viṣṇu and the other gods, full of loving devotion remained waiting silently and humbly.

## \|\| 4.4.21-22 \|\|

*śivāpi suprasannābhūdākarṇyāmarasaṃstutim \|*  
*ākalayyātha taddhetuṃ saṃsmṛtya svaprabhuṃ śivam \|\| 21 \|\|*

*uvācomā tadā devī sambodhya vibudhāṃśca tān \|*  
*vihasya māpatimukhānsadayā bhaktavatsalā \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. Śivā too was delighted on hearing the eulogy of the gods and ascertaining the course of the same after remembering her lord Śiva, the compassionate Umā addressed smilingly the gods, chief of whom was Viṣṇu. The Goddess, favourably disposed to her devotees, said:—

## \|\| 4.4.23 \|\|

*umovāca \|*  
*he hare he vidhe devā munayaśca gatavyathāḥ \|*  
*sarve śṛṇuta madvākyaṃ prasannāhaṃ na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

Umā said:—

23\. O Viṣṇu, O, Brahmā, O Gods and sages who are free from sorrow and pain ye listen to my words. I am delighted undoubtedly.

## \|\| 4.4.24 \|\|

*caritaṃ mama sarvatra trailokyasya sukhāvaham \|*  
*kṛtaṃ mayaivaṃ sakalaṃ dakṣamohādikaṃ ca tat \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. My activities are conducive to happiness everywhere in the three worlds. The delusion of Dakṣa and other things were carried out by me alone.

## \|\| 4.4.25 \|\|

*avatāraṃ kariṣyāmi kṣitau pūrṇaṃ na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*bahavo hetavo'pyatra tadvadāmi mahādarāt \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. I shall take a full incarnation on the earth. There is no doubt in this. There are many reasons for the same. I shall mention them with respect.

## \|\| 4.4.26 \|\|

*purā himācalo devā menā cātisubhaktitaḥ \|*  
*sevāṃ me cakratustāta jananīvatsatītanoḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Formerly, O gods, with great devotion Himācala and Menā rendered service to me in my life as Sati, like my parents.

## \|\| 4.4.27 \|\|

*idānīṃ kurutassevāṃ subhaktyā mama nityaśaḥ \|*  
*menā viśeṣatastatra sutātvenātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Even now they continuously render me service and Menā particularly (does so). There is no doubt about my becoming their daughter.

## \|\| 4.4.28 \|\|

*rudro gacchatu yūyaṃ cāvatāraṃ himavadgṛhe \|*  
*ataścāvatariṣyāmi duḥkhanāśo bhaviṣyati \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Just as you, Rudra too, desires my incarnation in the abode of Himavat. Hence I shall incarnate. That shall be the end of misery in the world.

## \|\| 4.4.29 \|\|

*sarve gacchata dhāma svaṃ svaṃ sukhaṃ labhatāṃ ciram \|*  
*avatīrya sutā bhūtvā menāyā dāsya utsukham \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. All of you return to your abodes. You shall be happy for a long time. After incarnating I shall give Menā full happiness.

## \|\| 4.4.30 \|\|

*harapatnī bhaviṣyāmi suguptaṃ matamātmanaḥ \|*  
*adbhutā śivalīlā hi jñānināmapi mohinī \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. I shall become Śiva’s wife. But this desire is a great secret with me. Śiva’s divine sport is wonderful. It deludes even the wise.

## \|\| 4.4.31-32 \|\|

*yāvatprabhṛti me tyaktā svatanurdakṣajā surāḥ \|*  
*pitṛto'nādaraṃ dṛṣṭvā svāminastatkratau gatā \|\| 31 \|\|*

*tadāprabhṛti sa svāmī rudraḥ kālāgnisaṃjñakaḥ \|*  
*digambaro babhūvāśu maccintanaparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

31-32. Ever since I cast off my body born of Dakṣa on seeing my lord’s disrespect at the hands of my father at the altar of sacrifice, my lord Rudra is tormented by thoughts about me.

## \|\| 4.4.33-34 \|\|

*mama roṣaṃ kratau dṛṣṭvā pitustatra gatā satī \|*  
*atyajatsvatanuṃ prītyā dharmajñeti vicārataḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*yogyabhūtsadanaṃ tyaktvā kṛtvā veṣamalaukikam \|*  
*na sehe virahaṃ satyā madrūpāyā maheśvaraḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

33-34. He saw my anger at the altar of my father’s sacrifice. Thinking that the virtuous lady had cast-off her body out of love for him he became a Yogin and abandoned home-life. He assumed an unearthly form and features. But he could not bear my separation.

## \|\| 4.4.35 \|\|

*mama hetormahāduḥkhī sa babhūva kuveṣabhṛt \|*  
*atyajatsa tadārabhya kāmajaṃ sukhamuttamam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. On account of me he was much distressed. He put on an abnormal dress. Ever since he forsook the excellent pleasure of love.

## \|\| 4.4.36 \|\|

*anyacchṛṇuta he viṣṇo he vidhe munayaḥ surāḥ \|*  
*mahāprabhormaheśasya līlāṃ bhuvanapālinīm \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Hear further, O Viṣṇu, O Brahmā, O sages and O gods, the divine sports of the supreme lord Śiva, that protect the universe.

## \|\| 4.4.37 \|\|

*vidhāya mālāṃ suprītyā mamāsthnāṃ virahākulaḥ \|*  
*na śāntiṃ prāpa kutrāpi prabuddho 'pyeka eva saḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Oppressed by the pangs of bereavement He wreathed a garland of my bones. Although He is the sole enlightened god He did not get peace anywhere.

## \|\| 4.4.38 \|\|

*itastato rurodoccairanīśa iva sa prabhuḥ \|*  
*yogyāyogyaṃ na bubudhe bhramansarvatra sarvadā \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Like a non-god, like a helpless creature he roamed about here and there and cried aloud. The lord Himself could not distinguish between the proper and the improper.

## \|\| 4.4.39 \|\|

*itthaṃ līlāṃ haro'kārṣīddarśayankāmināṃ prabhuḥ \|*  
*ūce kāmukavadvāṇīṃ virahavyākulāmiva \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. The lord Śiva did this just to show the behaviour of a love-lorn lover. He blabbered like a lover in despair due to separation.

## \|\| 4.4.40 \|\|

*vastuto'vikṛto'dīno'styajitaḥ parameśvaraḥ \|*  
*paripūrṇaḥ śivaḥ svāmī māyādhīśo'khileśvaraḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. But really the supreme lord has no aberrations, is not distressed and remains unconquered. My master Śiva is perfect, lord of all and the controller of illusion.

## \|\| 4.4.41 \|\|

*anyathā mohatastasya kiṃ kāmācca prayojanam \|*  
*vikāreṇāpi kenāśu māyālipto na sa prabhuḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. He is not tarnished by illusion. Of what avail are illusion, love and other emotions for Him?

## \|\| 4.4.42 \|\|

*rudro'tīvecchati vibhussa me kartuṃ karagraham \|*  
*avatāraṃ kṣitau menāhimācalagṛhe surāḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Rudra, the lord, is anxious to marry me and hence my incarnation on the Earth at the residence of Menā and Himācala, O gods.

## \|\| 4.4.43 \|\|

*ataścāvatariṣyāmi rudrasantoṣahetave \|*  
*himāgapatnyāṃ menāyā laukikīṃ gatimāśritā \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. In order to propitiate Rudra, I shall incarnate as the daughter of Menā, the wife of Himācala, in accordance with the way of the world.

## \|\| 4.4.44 \|\|

*bhaktā rudrapriyā bhūtvā tapaḥ kṛtvā sudussaham \|*  
*devakāryaṃ kariṣyāmi satyaṃ satyaṃ na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. After performing a severe penance as His devotee I shall become Rudra’s beloved and then perform the work of the gods. This is truth, real truth, there is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 4.4.45 \|\|

*gacchata svagṛhaṃ sarve bhava bhajata nityaśaḥ \|*  
*tatkṛpāto'khilaṃ duḥkhaṃ vinaśyati na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. All of you return to your abodes. Continuously worship Śiva. Undoubtedly your miseries will be quelled by His favour.

## \|\| 4.4.46 \|\|

*bhaviṣyati kṛpālostu kṛpayā maṃgalaṃ sadā \|*  
*vandyā pūjyā triloke'haṃ tajjāyeti ca hetutaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. By the grace of merciful lord Śiva, you will achieve auspicious results. As the wife of that lord I shall be honoured and worshipped in the world.

## \|\| 4.4.47 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*ityuktvā jagadambā sā devānāṃ paśyatāntadā \|*  
*antardadhe śivā tāta svaṃ lokamprāpa vai drutam \|\| 47 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

47\. O dear, even as the gods were watching, Śiva, the mother of the universe, vanished after saying this and returned immediately to her world.

## \|\| 4.4.48 \|\|

*viṣṇvādayassurāssarve munayaśca mudānvitāḥ \|*  
*kṛtvā taddiśi saṃnāmaṃ svasvadhāmāni saṃyayuḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. After making obeisance to the direction in which she went, the delighted Viṣṇu and others, sages and the gods, returned to their abodes.

## \|\| 4.4.49 \|\|

*itthaṃ durgāsucaritaṃ varṇitaṃ te munīśvara \|*  
*sarvadā sukhadaṃ nṝṇāṃ bhuktimuktipradāyakam \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. O excellent sages, thus I have narrated to you the auspicious narrative of the goddess Durgā. It is always pleasing to men and it bestows worldly pleasures and salvation.

## \|\| 4.4.50 \|\|

*ya idaṃ śṛṇuyānnityaṃ śrāvayedvā samāhitaḥ \|*  
*paṭhedvā pāṭhayedvāpi sarvānkāmāna vāpnuyāt \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Whoever hears or recites this with concentration, reads or teaches this, will obtain the fruits of all desires.

## Chapter 5 - Menā obtains the boon

## \|\| 4.5.1 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*antarhitāyāndevyāṃ tu durgāyāṃ svagṛheṣu ca \|*  
*gateṣvamaravṛndeṣu kimabhūttadanantaram \|\| 1 \|\|*

Nārada said:—

1\. When the Goddess Durgā vanished and the gods returned to their abodes, what happened next?

## \|\| 4.5.2 \|\|

*kathaṃ menāgirīśau ca tepāte paramantapaḥ \|*  
*kathaṃ sutā'bhavattasya menāyāntāta tadvada \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. O dear, how did Menā and the lord of the mountains perform the great penance? How did he beget a daughter of Menā. Please narrate.

## \|\| 4.5.3 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*vipravarya sutaśreṣṭha śṛṇu taccaritaṃ mahat \|*  
*praṇamya śaṃkaraṃ bhaktyā vacmi bhaktivivarddhanam \|\| 3 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

3\. O best of brahmins, O most excellent of my sons, listen to that great account. After bowing to Śiva with devotion I shall narrate that story which increases devotion.

## \|\| 4.5.4 \|\|

*upadiśya gate tāta suravṛnde girīśvaraḥ \|*  
*haryādau menakā cāpi tepāte paramantapaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. When Viṣṇu and other gods returned after instructing him, the lord of the mountains and Menā performed a great penance.

## \|\| 4.5.5 \|\|

*aharniśaṃ śivāṃ śambhuṃ cintayantau ca dampatī \|*  
*samyagāredhaturnityaṃ bhaktiyuktena cetasā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Meditating on Śivā and Śiva day and night with devout mind, the couple worshipped them continuously.

## \|\| 4.5.6 \|\|

*giripriyātīva mudānarca devīṃ śivena sā \|*  
*dānandadau dvijebhyaśca sadā tattoṣahetave \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The beloved of the mountain worshipped the goddess along with Śiva, joyously. She gave charitable gifts always to the brahmins for their satisfaction.

## \|\| 4.5.7 \|\|

*caitramāsaṃ samārabhya saptaviṃśativatsarān \|*  
*śivāṃ sampūjayāmāsāpattyārthinyanvahaṃ ratā \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Desirous of obtaining a child, she worshipped Śivā everyday for twenty-seven years beginning it in the month of March-April.

## \|\| 4.5.8 \|\|

*aṣṭamyāmupavāsantu kṛtvādānnavamītithau \|*  
*modakairbalipiṣṭaiśca pāyasairgandhapuṣpakaiḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Observing a fast on the eighth day of the lunar fortnight, she made charitable gifts of sweets, offerings of oblation rice cakes, puddings and fragrant flowers on the ninth day.

## \|\| 4.5.9 \|\|

*gaṅgāyāmauṣadhiprasthe kṛtvā mūrtiṃ mahīmayīm \|*  
*umāyāḥ pūjayāmāsa nānāvastusamarpaṇaiḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. She made clay idol of the Goddess and worshipped her by offering various things on the banks of the Gaṅgā in Auṣadhiprastha.

## \|\| 4.5.10 \|\|

*kadācitsā nirāhārā kadācitsā dhṛtavratā \|*  
*kadācitpavanāhārā kadācijjalabhughyabhūt \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. On some days she observed a complete fast. On some days she observed sacred rites. Some days wind alone constituted her food and some days she drank only water.

## \|\| 4.5.11 \|\|

*śivāvinyastacetaskā saptaviṃśativatsarān \|*  
*nināya menakā prītyā paraṃ sā mṛṣṭavarcasā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. With her mind fixed on Śivā, Menā passed twenty seven years with pleasure and brilliant lustre.

## \|\| 4.5.12 \|\|

*saptaviṃśativarṣānte jaganmātā jaganmayī \|*  
*suprītābhavadatyarthamumā śaṃkarakāminī \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. At the end of twenty-seven years, Umā the beloved of Śiva, the mother of the world and identical with the universe became highly delighted.

## \|\| 4.5.13 \|\|

*anugrahāya menāyāḥ purataḥ parameśvarī \|*  
*āvirbabhūva sā devī santuṣṭā tatsubhaktitaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The goddess Śivā, delighted by her good devotion appeared in front of Menā in order to bless her.

## \|\| 4.5.14 \|\|

*divyāvayavasaṃyuktā tejomaṇḍalamadhyagā \|*  
*uvāca vihasantī sā menāṃ pratyakṣatāṃ gatā \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Appearing to her in a form of divine limbs through a lustrous zone, she smilingly said to Menā.

## \|\| 4.5.15 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|\| varaṃ brūhi mahāsādhvi yatte manasi vartate \|*  
*suprasannā ca tapasā tavāhaṃ girikāmini \|\| 15 \|\|*

The Goddess said:—

15\. O beloved of the mountain, I am delighted by your penance. O chaste lady, tell me what you desire in your mind.

## \|\| 4.5.16 \|\|

*yatprārthitaṃ tvayā mene tapovratasamādhinā \|*  
*dāsye te'haṃ ca tatsarvaṃ vāñchitaṃ yadyadā bhavet \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. O Menā, whatever is desired by you by penance, sacred rites and ecstatic contemplation I shall grant you and that too whenever you wish for it.

## \|\| 4.5.17 \|\|

*tatassā menakā devīṃ pratyakṣāṃ kālikāntadā \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā ca praṇanāmātha vacanaṃ cedamabravīt \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Then seeing the goddess in her presence Menā bowed and spoke these words:—

## \|\| 4.5.18 \|\|

*menovāca \|*  
*devi pratyakṣato rūpandṛṣṭantava mayā'dhunā \|*  
*tvāmahaṃ stotumicchāmi prasannā bhava kālike \|\| 18 \|\|*

Menā said:—

18\. O Goddess, your form has been perceived by me directly, just now. I wish to eulogise you. Be pleased.

## \|\| 4.5.19 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*atha sā menayetyuktā kālikā sarvamohinī \|*  
*bāhubhyāṃ suprasannātmā menakāṃ pariṣasvaje \|\| 19 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

19\. On being thus requested by Menā, the goddess Umā, the enchantress of everyone, embraced Menā and was highly delighted.

## \|\| 4.5.20 \|\|

*tataḥ prāptamahājñānā menakā kālikāṃ śivam \|*  
*tuṣṭāva vāgbhi riṣṭābhirbhaktyā pratyakṣatāṃ gatām \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Acquiring very great wisdom, Menā eulogised Śivā, who had appeared in person, by means of pleasing words with great devotion.

## \|\| 4.5.21 \|\|

*menovāca \|*  
*mahāmāyāṃ jagaddhātrīṃ caṇḍikāṃ lokadhāriṇīm \|*  
*praṇamāmi mahādevīṃ sarvakāmārthadāyinīm \|\| 21 \|\|*

Menā said:—

21\. I bow to the great goddess, the bestower of all desires, I bow to her who wields great illusion, the creator and sustainer of the universe.

## \|\| 4.5.22 \|\|

*nityānandakarīṃ māyāṃ yoganidrāṃ jagatprasūm \|*  
*praṇamāmi sadāsiddhāṃ śubhasārasamālinīm \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. I bow to her of contemplative sleep, and to her the wielder of great illusion and the cause of permanent bliss. I bow to the mother of the universe. I bow to Siddhā having the garland of auspicious lotuses.

## \|\| 4.5.23 \|\|

*mātāmahīṃ sadānandāṃ bhaktaśokavināśinīm \|*  
*ākalpaṃ vanitānāṃ ca prāṇināṃ buddhirūpiṇīm \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. I bow to the grandmother, of perpetual bliss. I bow to the goddess who dispels the sorrow of the devotees, who is a model for all women and who constitutes the intellect of all living beings.

## \|\| 4.5.24 \|\|

*sā tvaṃ baṃdhacchedaheturyatīnāṃ kaste geyo mādṛśībhiḥ prabhāvaḥ \|*  
*hiṃsāyā vātharvavedasya sā tvaṃ nityaṃ kāmaṃ tvaṃ mameṣṭaṃ vidhehi \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. You are the cause of the snapping of all fetters of ascetics. Which one of your powers can be sung by women like me? You are violence mentioned in the Atharvaveda. You (of such powerful means) fulfil my desire.

## \|\| 4.5.25 \|\|

*nityānityairbhāvahīnaiḥ parāstaistattanmātrairyojyate bhūtavargaḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ śaktistvaṃ sadā nityarūpā kāle yoṣā yogayuktā samarthā \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The living beings are being united to the different principles of the nature of permanence and otherwise and those without substance are discarded. You are the inherent power of those permanent principles. In the proper time you become a woman of ability with Yogic powers.

## \|\| 4.5.26 \|\|

*yonirdharitrī jagatāṃ tvameva tvameva nityā prakṛtiḥ parastāt \|*  
*yathā vaśaṃ kriyate brahmarūpaṃ sā tvaṃ nityā me prasīdādya mātaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. You are the origin and the sustainer of the worlds. You are the eternal Prakṛti, the great, by whom even the Brahman is brought under control. O you, of noble nature, O mother, be pleased with me.

## \|\| 4.5.27 \|\|

*tvaṃ jātavedogataśaktirugrā tvaṃ dāhikā sūryakarasya śaktiḥ \|*  
*āhlādikā tvaṃ bahucandrikā yā tāntvāmahaṃ staumi namāmi caṇḍīm \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. You are the great power latent in fire; you are the burning power of the sun’s rays; you are the pleasing power of the extensive moonlight. O Goddess, I bow to you.

## \|\| 4.5.28 \|\|

*yoṣāṇāṃ satpriyā ca tvaṃ nityā tvaṃ cordhvaretasām \|*  
*vāṃchā tvaṃ sarvajagatāṃ dhāyā ca tvaṃ yathā hareḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. To good women you manifest yourself as their beloved; to persons of perfect self-control and sublimation you manifest yourself as eternal; to the entire universe you manifest as desire; as of Viṣṇu you are the Māyā so you are of Śiva.

## \|\| 4.5.29 \|\|

*yā ceṣṭarūpāṇi vidhāya devī sṛṣṭisthitānāśamayī ca kartrī \|*  
*brahmācyutasthāṇuśarīrahetussā tvaṃ prasīdādya punarnamaste \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. You assume different forms as you please for the purpose of creation, sustenance and annihilation and give birth to the bodies of Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva. You, of such potentiality, be pleased. Obeisance to you again.

## \|\| 4.5.30 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*tata itthaṃ stutā durgā kālikā punareva hi \|*  
*uvāca menakāṃ devīṃ vāṃchitaṃ varayetyuta \|\| 30 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

30\. Thus eulogised, the goddess spoke to Menā desiring her to choose a boon.

## \|\| 4.5.31 \|\|

*\|\| umovāca \|*  
*prāṇapriyā mama tvaṃ hi himācalavilāsinī \|*  
*yadicchasi dhruvandāsye nādeyaṃ vidyate mama \|\| 31 \|\|*

Umā said:—

31\. O Himācala’s beloved, you are as favourite to me as my vital air. Whatever you desire I shall give you. There is nothing that I can withhold from you.

## \|\| 4.5.32 \|\|

*iti śrutvā maheśānyāḥ pīyūṣasadṛśaṃ vacaḥ \|*  
*uvāca parituṣṭā sā menakā girikāminī \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. On hearing these nectar-like words of the Goddess, the delighted Menā, the wife of Himācala, said.

## \|\| 4.5.33 \|\|

*menovāca \|*  
*śive jayajaya prājñe maheśvari bhavāmbike \|*  
*varayogyāsmahaṃ cette vṛṇe bhūyo varaṃ varam \|\| 33 \|\|*

Menā said:—

33\. O Śivā, Hail, Hail! O great goddess, If you consider me worthy of a boon, I shall choose one.

## \|\| 4.5.34 \|\|

*prathamaṃ śataputrā me bhavantu jagadambike \|*  
*bahvāyuṣo vīryavanta ṛddhisiddhisamanvitāḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. O mother of the universe, at first let me have a hundred sons endowed with longevity, heroism, prosperity and accomplishments.

## \|\| 4.5.35 \|\|

*paścāttathaikā tanayā svarūpaguṇaśālinī \|*  
*kuladvayānaṃdakarī bhuvanatrayapūjitā \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. After that let me have a daughter of comely features and good qualities who will delight both the families and who will be revered by the three worlds.

## \|\| 4.5.36 \|\|

*sutā bhava mama śive devakāryārthameva hi \|*  
*rudrapatnī bhava tathā līlāṃ kuru bhavāmbike \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. O Śivā, be my daughter for fulfilling the needs of the gods. O Goddess, be Rudra’s wife and indulge in divine sports with the lord.

## \|\| 4.5.37 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*tacchrutvā menakoktaṃ hi prāha devī prasannadhīḥ \|*  
*smitapūrvaṃ vacastasyāḥ pūrayantī manoratham \|\| 37 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

37\. On hearing the words of Menā, the delighted goddess spoke smilingly, fulfilling her desire.

## \|\| 4.5.38 \|\|

*\|\| devyuvāca \|*  
*śataputrāssaṃ bhavantu bhavatyā vīryasaṃyutāḥ \|*  
*tatraiko balavānmukhyaḥ pradhamaṃ saṃbhaviṣyati \|\| 38 \|\|*

The Goddess said:—

3 8. May hundred heroic sons be born to you. One of them very strong will be born at first.

## \|\| 4.5.39 \|\|

*sutāhaṃ saṃbhaviṣyāmi santuṣṭā tava bhaktitaḥ \|*  
*deva kāryaṃ kariṣyāmi sevitā nikhilaissuraiḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. I shall be born as your daughter since I am delighted by your devotion. Since I have been served by the gods I shall fulfil their desire and carry out their activities.

## \|\| 4.5.40 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*evamuktvā jagaddhātrī kālikā parameśvarī \|*  
*paśyantyā menakāyāstu tatraivāntardadhe śivā \|\| 40 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

40\. Saying so, the Goddess Śivā vanished from there even as Menā was watching.

## \|\| 4.5.41 \|\|

*menakāpi varaṃ labdhvā maheśānyā abhī psitam \|*  
*mudaṃ prāpāmitāṃ tāta tapaḥkleśopyanaśyata \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. O dear one, on getting the desired boon from the Goddess, Menā attained immeasurable joy. Her misery occasioned by penance vanished.

## \|\| 4.5.42 \|\|

*diśi tasyāṃ namaskṛtya suprahṛṣṭamanāssatī \|*  
*jayaśabdaṃ proccaraṃtī svasthānampraviveśa ha \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Bowing down in that direction, the chaste lady of delighted mind returned to her abode repeating the benedictory word “Jaya” (be victorious).

## \|\| 4.5.43 \|\|

*atha tasmai svapataye śaśaṃsa suvaraṃ ca tam \|*  
*svacihnabuddhamiva vai suvācā punaruktayā \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. She told her husband about the boon, which had already been understood by him through good omens, by her words which were rendered useless.

## \|\| 4.5.44 \|\|

*śrutvā śailapatirhṛṣṭo'bhavanmenāvaco hi tat \|*  
*praśaśaṃsa priyāṃ prītyā śivābhaktiratāṃ ca tām \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. On hearing the words of Menā, the lord of mountains became delighted. He praised his wife who was devoted to Śiva lovingly.

## \|\| 4.5.45 \|\|

*kālakrameṇā'tha tayoḥ pravṛtte surate mune \|*  
*garbho babhūva menāyā vavṛdhe pratyahaṃ ca saḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. O sage, when their mutual sexual intercourse took place, Menā conceived and the child in the womb gradually grew up.

## \|\| 4.5.46-48 \|\|

*asūta sā nāgavadhūpabhogyaṃ sutamuttamam \|*  
*samudrabaddhasatsakhyaṃ mainākābhidhamadbhutam \|\| 46 \|\|*

*vṛtraśatrāvapi kruddhe vedanāśaṃ sapakṣakam \|*  
*pavikṣatānāṃ devarṣe pakṣacchidi varāṅgakam \|\| 47 \|\|*

*pravaraṃ śataputrāṇāṃ mahābalaparākramam \|*  
*svodbhavānāṃ mahīdhrāṇāṃ parvatendraikadhiṣṭhitam \|\| 48 \|\|*

46-48. She gave birth to a beautiful son Maināka who later on became the worthy recepient of the love of Nāga ladies and who later on entered into an alliance with the lord of ocean. O celestial sage, when Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra, became angry and began to chop off the wings of mountains, he retained his wings, nay, he did not even feel the pain of being wounded by the thunderbolt. He had good limbs. He had neat strength and prowess. He was the most important of all the mountains born of him. He too became the lord of mountains.

## \|\| 4.5.49 \|\|

*āsīnmahotsavastatra himācalapure'dbhutaḥ \|*  
*dampatyoḥ pramudādhikyaṃ babhūva kleśasaṃkṣayaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. In the city of Himācala there was a wonderful celebration of the event. The couple were highly delighted. Their pain was at an end.

## \|\| 4.5.50 \|\|

*dānandadau dvijātibhyo'nyebhyaśca pradadau dhanam \|*  
*śivāśivapadadvandve sneho'bhūdadhikastayoḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. He gave monetary gifts and charitable offerings to brahmins. Their devotion to Śivā and Śiva became increased.

## Chapter 6 - Pārvatī’s birth

## \|\| 4.6.1 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*atha saṃsmaraturbhaktyā dampatī tau bhavāmbikām \|*  
*prasūtihetave tatra devakāryārthamādarāt \|\| 1 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

1\. Then the couple, with great devotion remembered the goddess for her birth in order to carry out the work of the gods.

## \|\| 4.6.2 \|\|

*tatassā caṇḍikā yogāttyaktadehā purā pituḥ \|*  
*īhayā bhatituṃ bhūyassamaicchadriridārataḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Then the Goddess who formerly had cast off her body to spite her father, by means of her Yogic powers, desired to be born of the wife of the mountain.

## \|\| 4.6.3 \|\|

*satyaṃ vidhātuṃ svavacaḥ prasannākhilakāmadā \|*  
*pūrṇāṃśācchailacitte sā viveśātha maheśvarī \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. In order to make her own words true, the great goddess, who bestows everything desired, delightedly entered the mind of the mountain with all her constituent elements.

## \|\| 4.6.4 \|\|

*virarāja tatassotipramadopūrvasudyutiḥ \|*  
*hutāśana ivādhṛṣyastejorāśirmahāmanāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Hence he shone with an extraordinary splendour and great joy. With a resplendent brilliance, he, of lofty mind, became invincible like a blazing fire.

## \|\| 4.6.5 \|\|

*tato girissvapriyāyāṃ paripūrṇaṃ śivāṃśakam \|*  
*samādhimatvātsamaye samadhatta suśaṃkare \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Then, in a beneficent hour, the lord of the mountains deposited in his beloved the entire constituent element of Śiva by means of ecstatic contemplation.

## \|\| 4.6.6 \|\|

*samadhatta gireḥ patnī garbhaṃ devyāḥ prasādataḥ \|*  
*citte sthitāyāḥ karuṇākarāyāḥ sukhadaṃ gireḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The wife of the mountain, by the grace of the goddess who had sympathetically stationed herself in the mind of the mountain, conceived.

## \|\| 4.6.7 \|\|

*giripriyā sarvajagannivāsāsaṃśrayādhikam \|*  
*vireje sutarāṃ menā tejomaṇḍalagā sadā \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The beloved of the mountain, Menā, shone all the more by the presence of the goddess who bore the entire universe. She appeared as if she was in a brilliant sphere.

## \|\| 4.6.8 \|\|

*sukhodayaṃ svabhartuśca menā dauhṛdalakṣaṇam \|*  
*dadhau nidānandevānāmānandasyepsitaṃ śubham \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Menā bore the characteristic signs of pregnancy which almost indicated the imminent rise in pleasure of her lord and served as the auspicious cause for the future bliss of the gods.

## \|\| 4.6.9 \|\|

*deha sādādasaṃpūrṇabhūṣaṇā lodhrasaṃmukhā \|*  
*svalpabhendukṣaye kālaṃ viceṣyarkṣā vibhāvarī \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The weakness of her body did not allow her to wear ornaments. Her face became pale like the Lodhra flower. She resembled the night when there are very few stars and the moon is in a waning state.

## \|\| 4.6.10 \|\|

*tadānanaṃ mṛtsurabhināyaṃ tṛptiṃ girīśvaraḥ \|*  
*mune rahasyupāghrāya premādhikyaṃ babhūva tat \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Kissing her face, emitting the fragrance of the earth in the course of his secret dalliance, the lord of the mountains, was not satiated. His love increased.

## \|\| 4.6.11 \|\|

*menā spṛhāvatī keṣu na me śaṃsati vastuṣu \|*  
*kiṃcidiṣṭaṃ hriyāpṛcchadanuvelaṃ sakhī giriḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*
