11\. The lord of mountains asked Menā’s friends frequently—“What are the desires of Menā? She herself does not express them out of bashfulness.”

## \|\| 4.6.12 \|\|

*upetya dauhadaṃ śalyaṃ yadvavre'paśyadāśu tat \|*  
*ānītaṃ neṣṭamasyāddhā nāsādhyaṃ tridivai'pi hi \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Whatever product of the mountain she wished to have in the course of her pregnancy she found brought to her. There was nothing which he, the lord of the mountain, could not accomplish in the heaven too.

## \|\| 4.6.13 \|\|

*pracīyamānāvayavā nistīrya dohadavyathām \|*  
*reje menā bālalatā naddhapatrādhikā yathā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Surmounting the difficulties of the early days of pregnancy, she grew more plump in her limbs. Menā then shone like a tender creeper putting forth more leaves and flowers.

## \|\| 4.6.14 \|\|

*girissagarbhāṃ mahiṣīmamaṃsta dharaṇīmiva \|*  
*nidhānagarbhāmabhyantarlīnavahniṃ śamīmiva \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The lord of the mountains considered his pregnant queen like the earth with a treasure within and like the Śamī twig with latent fire in it.{GL\_NOTE::}

## \|\| 4.6.15 \|\|

*priyāprīteśca manasaḥ svārjitadraviṇasya ca \|*  
*samunnataiḥ śruteḥ prājñaḥ kriyāścakre yathocitāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The intelligent lord of mountains performed all the sacred rites befitting his love for his wife, the loftiness of his mind, the vastness of riches earned by him and the injunctions of the Vedas.

## \|\| 4.6.16-17 \|\|

*dadarśa kāle menāṃ sa pratītaḥ prasavonmukhīm \|*  
*abhritāṃ ca divaṃ garbhagṛhe bhiṣagadhiṣṭhite \|\| 16 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭvā priyāṃ śubhāṅgī vai mumodātigirīśvaraḥ \|*  
*garbhasthajagadambāṃ hi mahātejovatīntadā \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. At the proper time, he saw his wife Menā about to be delivered of the child, with delight, as one sees the sky enveloped with clouds. The lord of the mountains felt greatly rejoiced on seeing his wife of sound and auspicious in limbs the “labour-chamber” presided over by physicians. She felt very brilliant with the mother of the universe in her womb.

## \|\| 4.6.18 \|\|

*tasminnavasare devā mune viṣṇvādayastathā \|*  
*munayaśca samāgamya garbhasthāṃ tuṣṭuvuśśivām \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. In the mean time, O sage, Viṣṇu, and other gods as well as the sages came there and eulogised Śivā who was in the womb.

## \|\| 4.6.19 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*durge jaya jaya prājñe jagadamba maheśvari \|*  
*satyavrate satyapare trisatye satyarūpiṇī \|\| 19 \|\|*

The gods said:—

19\. O Goddess, be victorious, O intelligent one, O mother of the universe, O great Goddess, O you of true rites, prone to truth, true in three things, O truth-formed.

## \|\| 4.6.20 \|\|

*satyasthe satyasuprīte satyayone ca satyataḥ \|*  
*satyasatye satyanetre prapannāḥ śaraṇaṃ ca te \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. O you stationed in truth, we have sought refuge in you. O you delighted with truth, Origin of truth, Truth of Truth, of truthful sight.

## \|\| 4.6.21 \|\|

*śivapriye maheśāni devaduḥkhakṣayaṃkari \|*  
*trailokyamātā śarvāṇī vyāpinī bhaktavatsalā \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. O beloved of Śiva, great goddess, O destroyer of the miseries of gods, you are the mother of the three worlds, consort of Śiva, pervasive and favourably disposed to your devotees.

## \|\| 4.6.22 \|\|

*āvirbhūya trilokeśi devakāryaṃ kuruṣva ha \|*  
*sanāthāḥ kṛpayā te hi vayaṃ sarve maheśvari \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. O goddess of the three worlds, manifest yourself and perform the function of the gods. O goddess, all of us are well protected only due to your favour.

## \|\| 4.6.23 \|\|

*tvattaḥ sarve ca sukhino labhante sukhamuttamam \|*  
*tvāmvinā na hi kiṃcidvai śobhate tribhaveṣvapi \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Happy persons attain their happiness only from you. Nothing shines in the three worlds without you.

## \|\| 4.6.24 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*itthaṃ kṛtvā maheśānyā garbhasthāyā bahustutim \|*  
*prasannamanaso devāssvaṃ svaṃ dhāma yayustadā \|\| 24 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

24\. Thus eulogising, in many ways, the great goddess stationed in the womb, the gods returned to their abodes, highly delighted in their minds.

## \|\| 4.6.25 \|\|

*vyatīte navame māse daśame māsi pūrṇataḥ \|*  
*garbhasthāyā gatindradhre kālikā jagadambikā \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. When nine months were completed, in the tenth month, the goddess, the mother of the universe, bore all the states of a child in the womb in the complete form.

## \|\| 4.6.26 \|\|

*tadā susamayaścāsīcchāntabhagrahatārakaḥ \|*  
*nabhaḥ prasannatāṃ yātaṃ prakāśassarvadikṣu hi \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The time was good. The planets, stars and the luminary heavenly bodies were quiet; the sky was clear and there was brilliance in all the quarters.

## \|\| 4.6.27 \|\|

*mahī maṃgalabhūyiṣṭhā savanagrāmasāgarā \|*  
*sarassravantīvāpīṣu puphulluḥ paṃkajāni vai \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. The earth consisting of forests, villages and oceans was very auspicious. Lotuses blossomed in lakes, rivers and tanks.

## \|\| 4.6.28 \|\|

*vavuśca vividhā vātāssukhasparśā munīśvara \|*  
*mumudussādhavassarve'satānduḥkhamabhūddrutam \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. O excellent sage, diverse winds gentle to the touch blew; good men rejoiced and bad people became unhappy.

## \|\| 4.6.29 \|\|

*dundubhīnvādayāmāsurnabhasyāgatya nirjarāḥ \|*  
*puṣpavṛṣṭirabhūttatra jagurgandharvasattamāḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. The gods stood in the sky and sounded big drums. A shower of flowers fell. Excellent Gandharvas sang sweet songs.

## \|\| 4.6.30 \|\|

*vidyādharastriyo vyomni nanṛtuścāpsarāstathā \|*  
*tadotsavo mahānāsīddevādīnāṃ nabhaḥsthale \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Vidyādhara women and the celestial nymphs danced in the sky; in the heavenly region great festivities were celebrated by the gods and others.

## \|\| 4.6.31 \|\|

*tasminnavasare devī pūrvaśaktiśśivā satī \|*  
*āvirbabhūva purato menāyā nijarūpataḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. At that time Śivā, Satī of perfect power formerly appeared in front of Menā in her real form.

## \|\| 4.6.32 \|\|

*vasaṃtartau madhau māse navamyāṃ mṛgadhiṣṇyake \|*  
*arddharātre samutpannā gaṃgeva śaśimaṇḍalāt \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. She was born at midnight when the constellation Mṛgaśiras was in conjunction with the moon on the ninth day in the month of Madhu (March-April) in the spring season like the Gaṅgā from the moon’s sphere.

## \|\| 4.6.33 \|\|

*samaye tatsvarūpeṇa menakā jaṭharācchivā \|*  
*samudbhūya samutpannā sā lakṣmīriva sāgarāt \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Coming out of the belly of Menā at the proper time in her real form, she resembled Lakṣmī coming out of the ocean.

## \|\| 4.6.34 \|\|

*tatastasyāṃ tu jātāyāṃ prasanno'bhūttadā bhavaḥ \|*  
*anukūlo vavau vāyurgambhīro gaṃdhayukśubhaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. When she was born, Śiva was glad. A slow, fragrant and auspicious wind blew favourably.

## \|\| 4.6.35 \|\|

*babhūva puṣpavṛṣṭiśca toyavṛṣṭi purassaram \|*  
*jajvaluścāgnayaḥ śāntā jagarjuśca tadā ghanāḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Along with the rain there was a shower of flowers. Fires calmly glowed and the clouds rumbled.

## \|\| 4.6.36 \|\|

*tasyāṃ tu jāyamānāyāṃ sarvasvaṃ samapadyata \|*  
*himavannagare tatra sarva duḥkhaṃ kṣayaṃ gatam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. At the time of her birth, riches and prosperity flourished in the city of Himavat. All miseries perished.

## \|\| 4.6.37 \|\|

*tasminnavasare tatra viṣṇvādyāssakalāssurāḥ \|*  
*ājagmuḥ sukhinaḥ prītyā dadṛśurjagadambikām \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Viṣṇu and other gods reached there in time and saw the mother of the universe. They were delighted and happy.

## \|\| 4.6.38 \|\|

*tuṣṭuvustāṃ śivāmambāṃ kālikāṃ śivakāminīm \|*  
*divyārūpāṃ mahāmāyāṃ śivalokanivāsinīm \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. They eulogised Śivā the mother of the universe, the beloved of Śiva, of great illusory power, of divine features and resident of Śiva’s region.

## \|\| 4.6.39 \|\|

*\|\| devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*jagadamba mahādevi sarvasiddhividhāyini \|*  
*devakāryakarī tvaṃ hi sadātastvāṃ namāmahe \|\| 39 \|\|*

The Gods said:—

39\. O great goddess, O mother of the universe, O achiever of all accomplishments, you alone can carry out the work of the gods. Hence we bow to you always.

## \|\| 4.6.40 \|\|

*sarvathā kuru kalyāṇaṃ devānāṃ bhaktavatsale \|*  
*menāmanorathaḥ pūrṇaḥ kṛtaḥ kuru harasya ca \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. O you favourably disposed to the devotees, do everything conducive to the happiness of the Gods. You have fulfilled the desire of Menā. Now, you fulfil that of Śiva.

## \|\| 4.6.41 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*itthaṃ stutvā śivāṃ devīṃ viṣṇvādyā supraṇamya tām \|*  
*svaṃsvaṃ dhāma yayuḥ prītāśśaṃsantastadgatiṃ parām \|\| 41 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

41\. After eulogising Śivā thus, Viṣṇu and other gods bowed to her again delightedly and returned to their abodes praising her great divine ways.

## \|\| 4.6.42 \|\|

*tāntu dṛṣṭvā tathā jātāṃ nīlotpaladalaprabhāma \|*  
*śyāmā sā menakā devī mudamāpāti nārada \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. O Nārada, Menā rejoiced much on seeing goddess Umā of the splendour of the blue lotus as her daughter.

## \|\| 4.6.43 \|\|

*divyarūpaṃ vilokyānu jñānamāpa giripriyā \|*  
*vijñāya parameśānīṃ tuṣṭāvātipraharṣitā \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. On seeing her divine features, the beloved of the mountain attained perfect knowledge. After that realisation she eulogised the supreme Goddess with very great delight.

## \|\| 4.6.44 \|\|

*menovāca \|*  
*jagadamba maheśāni kṛtātikaruṇā tvayā \|*  
*āvirbhūtā mama puro vilasantī yadambike \|\| 44 \|\|*

Menā said:—

44\. “Great favour has been shown by you, O Goddess, O mother of the universe, inasmuch as you have manifested yourself in front of me brilliantly.

## \|\| 4.6.45 \|\|

*tvamādyā sarvaśaktīnāṃ trilokajananī śive \|*  
*śivapriyā sadā devī sarvadevastutā parā \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. You are the primordial one among all Energies. O Śivā, you are the mother of the three worlds. O Goddess you are the beloved of Śiva, you are great goddess eulogised by the gods.

## \|\| 4.6.46 \|\|

*kṛpāṃ kuru maheśāni mama dhyānasthitā bhava \|*  
*etadrūpeṇa pratyakṣaṃ rūpaṃ dhehi sutāsamam \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. O great Goddess, be pleased. Remain in my meditation in this form, but have the form of my daughter in public view.”

## \|\| 4.6.47 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya vacastasyā menāyā bhūdharastriyāḥ \|*  
*pratyuvāca śivā devī suprasavāmaaripriyām \|\| 47 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

47\. On hearing these words of Menā, the wife of the mountain, the delighted goddess Śiva replied to Menā, the beloved of the mountain thus.

## \|\| 4.6.48 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*he mene tvaṃ purā māṃ ca susevitavatī ratā \|*  
*tvadbhaktyā suprasannāhaṃ varandātuṃ gatāntikam \|\| 48 \|\|*

The Goddess said:—

48\. “O Menā, formerly you served me excellently. I am delighted by your devotion. I have come near you to grant you a boon.

## \|\| 4.6.49 \|\|

*varaṃ brūhīti madvāṇīṃ śrutvā te tadvaro vṛtaḥ \|*  
*sutā bhava mahādevī sā me devahitaṃ kuru \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. On hearing my words “Express your wish and choose a boon” you had chosen the boon “great Goddess, become my daughter. Do what is beneficent to the gods.”

## \|\| 4.6.50 \|\|

*tathā dattvā varaṃ te'haṃ gatā svampadamādarāt \|*  
*samayaṃ prāpya tanayā bhavante girikāmini \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Accordingly granting you the boon I returned to my abode. O beloved of the mountain, I have become your daughter at the proper time.

## \|\| 4.6.51 \|\|

*divyarūpaṃ dhṛtaṃ medya yatte matsmaraṇaṃ bhavet \|*  
*anyathā martyabhāvena tavājñānaṃ bhavenmayi \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. I have assumed the divine form now, so that you may be reminded of me. In a human form if I had appeared, it would have put you out of knowledge about me.

## \|\| 4.6.52 \|\|

*yuvāṃ māṃ putribhāvena divyabhāvena vā sakṛt \|*  
*cintayantau kṛtasnehau yātāsstho madgatimparām \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Constantly thinking of me in the form of your daughter, or in the divine form with love, both of you will surely attain my region, the great goal.

## \|\| 4.6.53 \|\|

*devakāryaṃ kariṣyāmi līlāṃ kṛtvā dbhutāṃ kṣitau \|*  
*śambhupatnī bhaviṣyāmi tārayiṣyāmi sajjanān \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. I shall do the work of the gods showing my wonderfully divine sports. I shall become the wife of Śiva and redeem good men.”

## \|\| 4.6.54 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityuktvāsīcchivā tūṣṇīmambikā svāttmamāyayā \|*  
*paśyantyāṃ mātari prītyā sadyo''bhūttanayā tanuḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

54\. After saying thus Śivā kept quiet. Even as the mother was watching with pleasure, she assumed the body of a daughter by her power of illusion.

## Chapter 7 - The childhood sports of Pārvatī

## \|\| 4.7.1 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*tato menā purassā vai sutā bhūtvā mahādyutiḥ \|*  
*cakāra rodanaṃ tatra laukikīṃ gatimāśritā \|\| 1 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

1\. The goddess of great brilliance assumed the form of her baby child in front of Menā and began to cry in accordance with the ways of the world.

## \|\| 4.7.2 \|\|

*ariṣṭaśayyāṃ paritassadvisārisutejasā \|*  
*niśīthadīpā vihatatviṣa āsannaraṃ mune \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. On account of her splendour that diffused all round the lying-in-couch, the midnight lamps that burnt in the lying-in-chamber were rendered dim in a trice, O sage.

## \|\| 4.7.3 \|\|

*śrutvā tadrodanaṃ ramyaṃ gṛhasthāssarvayoṣitaḥ \|*  
*jahṛṣussambhramāttatrāgatāḥ prītipurassarāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The women in the house were extremely glad on hearing the gentle cry of the child. In their excited flutter and great pleasure they rushed in.

## \|\| 4.7.4 \|\|

*tacchuddhāntacaraḥ śīghraṃ śaśaṃsa bhūbhṛte tadā \|*  
*pārvatījanma sukhadaṃ devakāryakaraṃ śubham \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The superintendent of the harem immediately informed the king about the birth of Pārvatī which was pleasant and conducive to the work of the gods.

## \|\| 4.7.5 \|\|

*tacchuddhāntacarāyāśu putrījanma suśaṃsate \|*  
*sitātapatraṃ nādeyamāsīttasya mahībhṛtaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. To the superintendent of the harem who brought the news, there was nothing which the king could not give even including his royal white umbrella.

## \|\| 4.7.6 \|\|

*gatastatra giriḥ prītyā sapurohitasadvijaḥ \|*  
*dadarśa tanayāṃ tāntu śobhamānāṃ subhāsasā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Accompanied by the chief priest and learned brahmins, the lord of mountains came there and saw the child who shone in her lovely clothes.

## \|\| 4.7.7 \|\|

*nīlotpaladala śyāmāṃ sudyutiṃ sumanoramām \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā ca tādṛśīṃ kanyāṃ mumodāti girīśvaraḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The lord of mountains rejoiced on seeing the child shining in dark splendour like that of the blue lotus.

## \|\| 4.7.8 \|\|

*sarve ca mumudustatra paurāśca puruṣāḥ striyaḥ \|*  
*tadotsavo mahānāsīnnedurvādyāni bhūriśaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. All the citizens there, both men and women, rejoiced much. There were great festivities. Different sorts of musical instruments were played.

## \|\| 4.7.9 \|\|

*babhūva maṃgalaṃ gānaṃ nanṛturvārayoṣitaḥ \|*  
*dānaṃ dadau dvijātibhyo jātakarmavidhāya ca \|\| 9 \|\|*

9 Auspicious songs were sung. The dancing girls exhibited their saltatorial skill. The lord of mountains performed post-natal sacred rites and made charitable gifts to the brahmins.

## \|\| 4.7.10 \|\|

*atha dvāraṃ samāgatya cakāra sumahotsavam \|*  
*himācalaḥ prasannātmā bhikṣubhyo draviṇandadau \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Himavat came to the outer gate of the palace and joined the festivities. With a delighted mind he distributed monetary gifts to the beggars.

## \|\| 4.7.11 \|\|

*atho muhūrtte sumate himavānmunibhiḥ saha \|*  
*nāmā'karotsutāyāstu kālītyādi sukhapradam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. In an auspicious hour, in the company of the sages, Himavat named his daughter Kālī and assigned other pleasing names to her.

## \|\| 4.7.12 \|\|

*dānaṃ dadau tadā prītyā dvijebhyo bahu sādaram \|*  
*utsavaṃ kārayāmāsa vividhaṃ gānapūrvvakam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. He gave charitable gifts to the brahmins out of love and respect. Varieties of festivities were gone through with suitable music.

## \|\| 4.7.13 \|\|

*itthaṃ kṛtvotsavaṃ bhūri kālīṃ paśyanmuhurmuhuḥ \|*  
*lebhe mudaṃ sapatnīko bahuputro'pi bhūdharaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Though he had many sons, the lord of mountain and his wife rejoiced more on seeing Kālī frequently, after these celebrations.

## \|\| 4.7.14 \|\|

*tatra sā vavṛdhe devī girirājagṛhe śivā \|*  
*gaṃgeva varṣāsamaye śaradīvātha candrikā \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. There in the palace of the lord of mountains the goddess Śivā grew up like Gaṅgā in the rainy season and like the moon-light in the autumn.

## \|\| 4.7.15 \|\|

*evaṃ sā kālikā devī cārvaṅgī cārudarśanā \|*  
*dadhre cānudinaṃ ramyāṃ candrabimbakalāmiva \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The goddess Kālī of exquisite body and comely appearance acquired more and more splendour like the disk of the moon acquiring more and more digits day by day.

## \|\| 4.7.16 \|\|

*kulocitena nāmnā tāṃ pārvatītyājuhāvahā \|*  
*bandhupriyāṃ bandhujanaḥ sauśīlyaguṇasaṃyutām \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The child was fondly attached to every member of the family, Hence the kinsmen called her Pārvatī, a name befitting her family. The girl had all the qualities of good conduct and behaviour.

## \|\| 4.7.17 \|\|

*umeti mātrā tapase niṣiddhā kālikā ca sā \|*  
*paścādumākhyāṃ sumukhī jagāma bhuvane mune \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Afterwards when Kālī wanted to perform a penance she was forbidden by her mother who said—“O, no (Umā). Hence O sage, the sweetfaced lady came to be called Umā in the world.

## \|\| 4.7.18-19 \|\|

*dṛṣṭiḥ putravato'pyadrestasmiṃstṛptiṃ jagāma na \|*  
*apatye pārvatītyākhye sarvasaubhāgya saṃyute \|\| 18 \|\|*

*madhoranantapuṣpasya cūte hi bhramarāvaliḥ \|*  
*viśeṣasaṃgā bhavati sahakāre munīśvara \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. Although he had many sons, the eyes of the mountain were never satiated on seeing the child Pārvatī endowed with good fortune. In the spring season there may be many flowers in full bloom but the swarms of bees, O excellent sage, are specially drawn to the mango blossom.

## \|\| 4.7.20 \|\|

*pūto vibhūṣitaścāpi sa babhūva tayā giriḥ \|*  
*saṃskāravatyeva girā manīṣīva himālayaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. The mountain Himālaya was both embellished and sanctified by his daughter like a learned man by his speech of grammatical purity.

## \|\| 4.7.21 \|\|

*prabhāmahatyā śikhayeva dīpo bhuvanasya ca \|*  
*trimārgayeva sanmārgastadvadgirijayā giriḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Just as a lamp in the house is praised by leaping flames of brilliance, just as the path of the good by the Gaṅgā, so also the lord of mountains was respected on account of Pārvatī.

## \|\| 4.7.22 \|\|

*kandukaiḥ kṛtrimaiḥ putraissakhīmadhyagatā ca sā \|*  
*gaṃgāsaikatavedībhirbālye reme muhurmuhuḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. During her childhood, the goddess played frequently on the sandy banks of the Gaṅgā in the middle of her playmates with balls and dolls.

## \|\| 4.7.23 \|\|

*atha devī śivā sā copadeśasamaye mune \|*  
*papāṭha vidyātsuprītyā yatacittā ca sadguroḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. O sage, the goddess Śivā when the suitable time for her education arrived learnt all the lores from a good preceptor, with concentrated mind and great pleasure.

## \|\| 4.7.24 \|\|

*prāktanā janmavidyāstāṃ śaradīva prapedire \|*  
*haṃsālissvarṇadī naktamātmabhāso mahauṣadhim \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Just as the flock of swans returns to the Gaṅgā in the autumnal season and just as the brilliant lustre manifests itself in the medicinal herbs during the night, so also all the learning of the previous birth returned to Kālī.

## \|\| 4.7.25 \|\|

*itthaṃ suvarṇitā līlā śivāyāḥ kācideva hi \|*  
*anyalīlāmpravakṣye'haṃ śṛṇu tvaṃ premato mune \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. O sage, thus I have described one of the divine sports of Śivā. I shall narrate another one of her divine sports. You listen to it lovingly.

## Chapter 8 - Nārada-Himālaya Conversation

## \|\| 4.8.1 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*ekadā tu śivajñānī śivalīlāvidāṃvaraḥ \|*  
*himācalagṛhaṃ prītyāgamastvaṃ śivapreritaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Brahmā said:

1\. Once, induced by Śiva, you went to the abode of Himācala lovingly, you who have the knowledge of Śiva and who are the foremost among those who know the divine sports of Śiva.

## \|\| 4.8.2 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā mune girīśastvāṃ natvānarca sa nārada \|*  
*āhūya ca svatanayāṃ tvadaṅghryostāmapātayat \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. O sage Nārada, on seeing you, the lord of the mountains bowed to you and worshipped you. He called his daughter and asked her to fall at your feet.

## \|\| 4.8.3 \|\|

*punarnatvā munīśa tvāmuvāca himabhūdharaḥ \|*  
*sāñjaliḥ svavidhiṃ matvā bahusannatamastakaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. O excellent sage, he bowed to you again. Himavat joined his palms in reverence and bent his head considering it his duty and spoke to you.

## \|\| 4.8.4 \|\|

*himālaya uvāca \|*  
*he mune nārada jñāninbrahmaputravara prabho \|*  
*sarvajñastvaṃ sakaruṇaḥ paropakaraṇe rataḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

Himavat said:—

4\. O sage Nārada, of good knowledge, O lord, foremost among the sons of Brahmā, you are omniscient. You are sympathetic. You are engaged in rendering help to others.

## \|\| 4.8.5 \|\|

*matsutājātakaṃ brūhi guṇadoṣasamudbhavam \|*  
*kasya priyā bhāgyavatī bhaviṣyati sutā mama \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Please read the horoscope of my daughter and tell me about her good and bad fortune. Whose beloved wife will my fortunate daughter be?

## \|\| 4.8.6-7 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*ityukto munivarya tvaṃ girīśena himādriṇā \|*  
*vilokya kālikāhastaṃ sarvāṃgaṃ ca viśeṣataḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*avocastvaṃ giriṃ tāta kautukī vāgviśāradḥ \|*  
*jñānī viditavṛttānto nāradaḥ prītamānasaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

Bramhā said:—

6-7. O excellent sage, being thus requested by Himavat the lord of mountains, you looked at Kālī’s palm and the limbs as well. O dear, you are wise. You know many facts. You are eloquent in speech. You then spoke.

## \|\| 4.8.8 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*eṣā te tanayā mene sudhāṃśoriva varddhitā \|*  
*ādyā kalā śailarāja sarvalakṣaṇaśālinī \|\| 8 \|\|*

Nārada said:

8\. “O Menā, O king of mountains, this daughter of yours has all auspicious signs. Like the first digit of the moon she will increase day by day.

## \|\| 4.8.9 \|\|

*svapatessukhadātyantaṃ pitroḥ kīrtivivarddhinī \|*  
*mahāsādhvī ca sarvāsu mahānandakarī sadā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. She will delight her husband, and heighten the glory of her parents. She will be a great chaste lady. She will grant bliss to everyone always.

## \|\| 4.8.10 \|\|

*sulakṣaṇāni sarvāṇi tvatsutāyāḥ kare gire \|*  
*ekā vilakṣaṇā rekhā tatphalaṃ śṛṇu tattvataḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. I see all good signs in the palm of your daughter, O lord of mountains. There is an abnormal line also. Listen to the indication thereof.

## \|\| 4.8.11 \|\|

*yogī nagno'guṇo'kāmī mātṛtātavivarjitaḥ \|*  
*amāno'śivaveṣaśca patirasyāḥ kiledṛśaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Her husband will be a naked Yogin, without any qualities. He will be free from lust. He will have neither mother nor father. He will be indifferent to honours. His dress and manners will be inauspicious.

## \|\| 4.8.12 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya vacaste hi satyaṃ mattvā ca dampatī \|*  
*menā himācalaścāpi duḥkhitau tau babhūvatuḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

12\. On hearing your words the couple thought them true. Both Menā and Himavat were much distressed.

## \|\| 4.8.13 \|\|

*śivākarṇyavacaste hi tādṛśaṃ jagadambikā \|\| \|*  
*lakṣaṇaistaṃ śivaṃ mattvā jaharṣāti mune hṛdi \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. O sage, on hearing your words, and inferring that indications referred to Śiva, Pārvatī’s joy knew no bounds.

## \|\| 4.8.14 \|\|

*na mṛṣā nāradavacastviti saṃcintya sā śivā \|*  
*snehaṃ śivapadadvandve cakārāti hṛdā tadā \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Convinced that Nārada’s words could not be false, Śivā turned her mind and love to Śiva’s feet.

## \|\| 4.8.15 \|\|

*uvāca duḥkhitaḥ śailastvāntadā hṛdi nārada \|*  
*kamupāyaṃ mune kuryāmatiduḥkhamabhūditi \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The lord of mountains who was very much grieved in mind spoke to you, “O Nārada, O sage, what is the way out? What shall I do? A great misery has befallen us”.

## \|\| 4.8.16 \|\|

*tacchutvā tvaṃ mune prāttha mahākautukakārakaḥ \|*  
*himācalaṃ śubhairvākyairharṣayanvāgviśāradaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. On hearing that, O sage, you who are eloquent in speech, delighted Himavat by your sweet words of auspicious import and spoke to console him.

## \|\| 4.8.17 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*snehācchṛṇu gire vākyaṃ mama satyaṃ mṛṣā na hi \|*  
*kararekhā brahmalipirna mṛṣā bhavati dhuvam \|\| 17 \|\|*

Nārada said:—

17\. “O lord of mountains, listen to my words with affability. They are true. They cannot be false. The lines in the palm are the lines of Brahmā. They cannot be untrue.

## \|\| 4.8.18 \|\|

*tādṛśo'syāḥ patiḥ śaila bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*tatropāyaṃ śṛṇu prītyā yaṃ kṛtvā lapsyase sukham \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. O lord of mountains, there is no doubt that her husband will be such a person. You now hear what you have to do whereby you will be happy.

## \|\| 4.8.19 \|\|

*tādṛśo'sti varaḥ śambhulīlārūpadharaḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*kulakṣaṇāni sarvāṇi tatra tulyāni sadguṇaiḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. There is a bridegroom like that. He is lord Śiva who has sportively assumed a physical form. In Him all bad characteristics are equal to good characteristics.

## \|\| 4.8.20 \|\|

*prabhau doṣo na duḥkhāya duḥkhado'tyaprabhau hi saḥ \|*  
*ravipāvakagaṃgānāṃ tatra jñeyā nidarśanā \|\| 20 \|\|*

20.In a majestic person a defect does not produce misery. It may well cause misery in a non-majestic person. Sun, fire and Gaṅgā may be cited as examples.

## \|\| 4.8.21 \|\|

*tasmācchivāya kanyā svāṃ śivāṃ dehi vivekataḥ \|*  
*śivassarveśvarassevyo'vikārī prabhuravyayaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Hence you give your daughter in marriage to Śiva. That will be a wise step. Lord Śiva who is the sole lord, unchanging and without any aberration is worthy of being resorted to.

## \|\| 4.8.22 \|\|

*śīghraprasādaḥ sa śivastāṃ grahīṣyatyasaṃśayam \|*  
*tapaḥsādhyo viśeṣeṇa yadi kuryācchivā tapaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. By performing penance, Śiva can be propitiated quickly and He will accept her undoubtedly.

## \|\| 4.8.23 \|\|

*sarvathā susamartho hi sa śivassakaleśvaraḥ \|*  
*kuliperapi vidhvaṃsī brahmādhīnastvakapradaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. In every respect, Śiva, the lord of all, is the most suitable person. He cannot be slain even by thunderbolts. He can render Brahmā and others distressed.”

## \|\| 4.8.24 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*ityuktvā tvaṃ punastāta kautukī brahmavinmune \|*  
*śailarājamavoco hi harṣayanvacanaiśśubhaiḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. O dear sage, after saying this you continued. You delighted him with auspicious words. You spoke to the king of the mountains.

## \|\| 4.8.25 \|\|

*bhāvinī dayitā śambhossānukūlā sadā hare \|*  
*mahāsādhvī suvratā ca pitrossukhavivarddhinī \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. “O lord of mountains, she will be the wife of Śiva and will remain his favourite always. She will be a chaste lady of good rites. She will increase the pleasure of her parents.

## \|\| 4.8.26 \|\|

*śambhościttaṃ vaśe caiṣā kariṣyati tapasvinī \|*  
*sa cāpyenāmṛte yoṣāṃ na hyanyāmudvahiṣyati \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Performing a penance she will fascinate Śiva’s mind towards herself. He too will marry none else except her.

## \|\| 4.8.27 \|\|

*etayossadṛśaṃ prema na kasyāpyeva tādṛśam \|*  
*bhūtaṃ vā bhavitā vāpi nādhunā ca pravartate \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. A love akin to this pair will not be found anywhere. Never in the past was it seen nor will it occur in future. Nor it is current now.

## \|\| 4.8.28 \|\|

*anayossurakāryyāṇi kartavyāni mṛtāni ca \|*  
*yāni yāni nagaśreṣṭha jīvitāni punaḥ punaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. O best of mountains, the two will fulfil the work of the gods. They will resuscitate those who have breathed their last.

## \|\| 4.8.29 \|\|

*anayā kanyayā te'dre ardhanārīśvaro haraḥ \|*  
*bhaviṣyati tathā harṣadinayormilitampunaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. O lord of mountains, Śiva will become Ardhanārīśvara (half male and half female), with your daughter forming half the part of your body. Their meeting once again will be delightful.

## \|\| 4.8.30 \|\|

*śarīrārdhaṃ harasyaiṣā hariṣyati sutā tava \|*  
*tapaḥ prabhāvātsaṃtoṣya maheśaṃ sakaleśvaram \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. After propitiating lord Śiva, the lord of all, by the power of her penance, your daughter will take away half the body of Siva.

## \|\| 4.8.31 \|\|

*svarṇagaurī suvarṇābhā tapasā toṣya taṃ haram \|*  
*vidyudgauratamā ceyaṃ tava putrī bhaviṣyati \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. By propitating Śiva with her penance she will acquire the lustre of gold and will be known as Svarṇagaurī. Your daughter will be as fair-complexioned as lightning.

## \|\| 4.8.32 \|\|

*gaurīti nāmnā kanyā tu khyātimeṣā gamiṣyati \|*  
*sarvadevagaṇaiḥ pūjyā haribrahmādibhistathā \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. This girl will be famous in the name of Gaurī, She will deserve the respect of Viṣṇu, Brahmā and the other Gods.

## \|\| 4.8.33 \|\|

*nānyasmai tvamimāṃ dātumihārhasi nagottama \|*  
*idaṃ copāṃśu devānāṃ na prakāśyaṃ kadācana \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. O excellent mountain, you shall not give her to anyone else. This is a secret of the gods. This shall not be revealed to any one else.

## \|\| 4.8.34 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*iti tasya vacaḥ śrutvā devarṣe tava nārada \|*  
*uvāca himavānvākyaṃ mune tvāmvāgviśāradaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. O celestial sage, Nārada, on hearing these words that you spoke O, sage, the eloquent Himavat spoke thus:

## \|\| 4.8.35 \|\|

*himālaya uvācā \|*  
*he mune nārada prājña vijñaptiṃ kāṃcideva hi \|*  
*karomi tāṃ śṛṇu prītyā tastvaṃ pramudamāvaha \|\| 35 \|\|*

Himavat said:—

35\. O sage Nārada, O intelligent one, I have one submission to make. Please listen to it lovingly and make us delightful.

## \|\| 4.8.36 \|\|

*śrūyate tyaktasaṃgassa mahādevo yatātmavān \|*  
*tapaścarati sannityaṃ devānāmapyagocaraḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. It is heard that the great God abhors all attachments. He has perfect self-control. He is ever busy in

penance and is out of reach of even the Gods.

## \|\| 4.8.37 \|\|

*sa kathaṃ dhyāna mārgasthaḥ parabrahmārpitaṃ manaḥ \|*  
*bhraṃśayiṣyati devarṣe tatra me saṃśayo mahān \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. O celestial sage, He is in the path of meditation. How can He withdraw His mind from the supreme Brahman? I have a great doubt in this respect.

## \|\| 4.8.38-39 \|\|

*akṣaraṃ paramaṃ brahma pradīpakalikopamam \|*  
*sadāśivākhyaṃ svaṃ rūpaṃ nirvikāramajāparam \|\| 38 \|\|*

*nirguṇaṃ saguṇaṃ tacca nirviśeṣaṃ nirīhakam \|*  
*ataḥ paśyati sarvatra na tu bāhyaṃ nirīkṣate \|\| 39 \|\|*

38-39. The supreme Brahman is great and imperishable. It is like the streak of a lamp. It is termed Sadāśiva. It is without aberration. It is beyond Brahmā. It is both full and devoid of qualities. It has no special traits, no desires. It sees within and not without.

## \|\| 4.8.40 \|\|

*iti sa śrūyate nityaṃ kiṃnarāṇāṃ mukhānmune \|*  
*ihāgatānāṃ suprītyā kintanmithyā vaco dhuvam \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. O sage, from the Kinnaras who come here, such are the things heard about Him. Can it be untrue?

## \|\| 4.8.41 \|\|

*viśeṣataḥ śrūyate sa sākṣānnāmnā tathā haraḥ \|*  
*samayaṃ kṛtavānpūrvvaṃ tanmayā gaditaṃ śṛṇu \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. This is also heard that Śiva had entered into a contract with the lady Satī. Listen to what I say?

## \|\| 4.8.42 \|\|

*na tvāmṛte'nyāṃ varaye dākṣāyaṇi priye satī \|*  
*bhāryārthaṃ na grahīṣyāmi satyametadbravīmi te \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. “O Satī, Dākṣāyaṇī, my beloved, I shall not take the hand of any woman except you as my wife. This is the truth that I say.”

## \|\| 4.8.43 \|\|

*iti satyāsamaṃ tena puraiva samayaḥ kṛtaḥ \|*  
*tasyāṃ mṛtāyāṃ sa kathaṃ svayamanyāṃ grahīṣyati \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. This was the agreement that He made with Satī formerly. She is dead. How then will He take another woman to be His wife.

## \|\| 4.8.44 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*ityuktvā sa giristūṣṇīmāsa tasya purastava \|*  
*tadākarṇyātha devarṣe tvaṃ prāvocassutattvataḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

44\. After saying these words, the lord of mountains kept quiet in your presence. O celestial sage, on hearing that,you spoke words that revealed the truth.

## \|\| 4.8.45 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*na vai kāryā tvayā ciṃtā girirāja mahāmate \|*  
*eṣā tava sutā kālī dakṣajā hyabhavatpurā \|\| 45 \|\|*

Nārada said:—

45\. “O lord of mountains, of great intellect, you need not worry. This daughter of yours, Pārvatī, was formerly the daughter of Dakṣa.

## \|\| 4.8.46 \|\|

*satīnāmābhavattasyāssarvamaṃgaladaṃ sadā \|*  
*satī sā vai dakṣakanyā bhūtvā rudrapriyābhavata \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Satī was her auspicious name. Satī who was Dakṣa’s daughter became Rudra’s wife.

## \|\| 4.8.47 \|\|

*pituryajñe tathā prāpyānādaraṃ śaṃkarasya ca \|*  
*taṃ dṛṣṭvā kopamādhāyātyākṣīddehaṃ ca sā satī \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Being dishonoured at the sacrifice of her father, and being the witness of Śiva’s dishonour she was furious and she cast off her body.

## \|\| 4.8.48 \|\|

*punassaiva samutpannā tava gehe'mbikā śivā \|*  
*pārvatī harapatnīyaṃ bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. She herself is born in your house as Pārvatī. There is no doubt that she will become Śiva’s wife.”

## \|\| 4.8.49-50 \|\|

*etatsarvaṃ vistarāttvaṃ proktavānbhūbhṛte mune \|*  
*pūrvarūpaṃ caritraṃ ca pārvatyāḥ prītivardhanam \|\| 49 \|\|*

*taṃ sarvaṃ pūrvavṛttānyaṃ kālyā munimukhādgiriḥ \|*  
*śrutvā saputradāraḥ sa tadā niḥsaṃśayo'bhavat \|\| 50 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

49-50. O sage, all these details you mentioned to the lord of mountains. You told the previous history of Pārvatī that increased her pleasure and on hearing which, the lord of mountains, his wife and children were freed from all suspicions.

## \|\| 4.8.51 \|\|

*tataḥ kālī kathāṃ śrutvā nāradasya mukhāttadā \|*  
*lajjayādhomukhī bhūtvā smitavistāritānanā \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. On hearing the story from Nārada, Pārvatī bent down her head in bashfulness but her smile heightened the beauty of her face.

## \|\| 4.8.52 \|\|

*kareṇa tāṃ tu saṃspṛśya śrutvā taccaritaṃ giriḥ \|*  
*mūrdhni śaśvattathāghrāya svāsa nānte nyaveśayat \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. On hearing the story, the lord of mountains stroked her fondly, kissed her on the head and placed her on his seat.

## \|\| 4.8.53 \|\|

*tatastvaṃ tāṃ punardṛṣṭvā'vocastatra sthitāṃ mune \|*  
*harṣayan girirājaṃ ca menakāntanayaiḥ saha \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. O sage, on seeing her seated there you spoke again delighting the lord of mountains, Menakā and her sons.

## \|\| 4.8.54-55 \|\|

*siṃhāsanantu kintvasyāśśailarāja bhavedataḥ \|*  
*śambhorūrau sadaitasyā āsanaṃ tu bhaviṣyati \|\| 54 \|\|*

*harorūrvāsanamprāpya tanayā tava santatam \|*  
*na yatra kasyācidṛṣṭirmānasaṃ vā gamiṣyati \|\| 55 \|\|*

54-55. “O king of mountains, she will have a better throne than this. Śiva’s thigh will be her permanent abode. On getting the seat on the thigh of Śiva your daughter will go to the world where no eye or mind can reach.”

## \|\| 4.8.56 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*iti vacanamudāraṃ nārada tvaṃ girīśaṃ tridivamagama uktvā tatkṣaṇādevaprītyā \|*  
*giripatirapi citte cārusaṃmodayuktassvagṛhamagamadevaṃ sarvasaṃpatsamṛddham \|\| 56 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

56\. O Nārada, after saying this to the lord of mountains, you went to heaven immediately. The lord of mountains too, whose mind was filled with joy, returned to his palace endowed with all riches.

## Chapter 9 - Śiva appears before Pārvatī in dream

## \|\| 4.9.1 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*vidhe tāta tvayā śaivavara prājñādbhutā kathā \|*  
*varṇitā karuṇāṃ kṛtvā prītirme varddhitādhikam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Nārada said:—

1\. O Brahmā, O dear one, O foremost among the devotees of Śiva, O intelligent one, taking pity on me you have narrated a wonderful story to me and have increased my pleasure thereby.

## \|\| 4.9.2 \|\|

*vidhe gate svakaṃ dhāma mayi vai divyadarśage \|*  
*tataḥ kimabhavattāta kṛpayā tadvadādhunā \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. O Brahmā, when I, of divine vision, had gone to my abode what happened thereafter? Please tell me now.

## \|\| 4.9.3 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*gate tvayi mune svarge kiyatkāle gate sati \|*  
*menā prāpyekadā śailanikaṭaṃ praṇanāma sā \|\| 3 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

3\. After you had gone to heaven, some time passed. Once Menā approached the lord of mountains and bowed to him.

## \|\| 4.9.4 \|\|

*sthitvā savinayamprāha svanāthaṃ girikāminī \|*  
*tatra śailādhināthaṃ sā prāṇapriyasutā satī \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. After waiting there for some time with humility, the beloved of the mountain addressed her lord; the chaste lady who loved her daughter as ardently as her own life spoke to the lord of mountains thus.

## \|\| 4.9.5 \|\|

*menovāca \|*  
*munivākyaṃ na buddhaṃ me samyaṅ nārīsvabhāvataḥ \|*  
*vivāhaṃ kuru kanyāyāssundareṇa vareṇa ha \|\| 5 \|\|*

Menā said:—

5\. As but is natural to women, the words of the sage have not been understood by me well. (I think it is better) that you perform the marriage of our daughter with a handsome bridegroom.

## \|\| 4.9.6 \|\|

*sarvathā hi bhavettatrodvāho'pūrvasukhāvahaḥ \|*  
*varaśca girijāyāstu sulakṣaṇakulodbhavaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Let the bridegroom of Pārvatī be born of a good family endowed with good characteristic signs. In every respect that marriage will yield an unprecedented happiness.

## \|\| 4.9.7 \|\|

*prāṇapriyā sutā me hi sukhitā syādyathā priya \|*  
*sadvaraṃ prāpya suprītā tathā kuru namo'stu te \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Obeisance to you. Do everything necessary to make our daughter, as beloved to us as our own lives, very happy and delighted after being united with a good bridegroom.

## \|\| 4.9.8 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityuktāśrumukhī menā patyaṃghryoḥ patitā tadā \|*  
*tāmutthāpya giriḥ prāha yathāvatprajñasattamaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

8\. After saying this, with tears in her eyes Menā fell at the feet of her husband. Raising her, the lord of mountains, the most excellent among intelligent people, made a true statement.

## \|\| 4.9.9 \|\|

*himālaya uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu tvaṃ menake devi yathārthaṃ vacmi tattvataḥ \|*  
*bhramaṃ tyaja munervākyaṃ vitathaṃ na kadācana \|\| 9 \|\|*

Himācala said:—

9\. O gentle lady Menakā, listen. I shall tell you the truth. Do not be under false impressions. The sage’s statement will never be false.

## \|\| 4.9.10 \|\|

*yadi snehaḥ sutāyāste sutāṃ śikṣaya sādaram \|*  
*tapaḥ kuryācchaṃkarasya sā bhaktyā sthiracetasā \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. If you feel affectionate towards your daughter, zealously instruct your daughter. Let her perform the penance with Śiva as the object, devotedly and steadily.

## \|\| 4.9.11 \|\|

*cetprasannaḥ śivaḥ kālyāḥ pāṇiṃ gṛhṇāti menake \|*  
*sarvaṃ bhūyācchubhaṃ naśyennāradoktamamaṃgalam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. If Śiva is delighted, O Menakā, He will marry her. Everything shall be auspicious. The inauspicious features indicated by Nārada will perish.

## \|\| 4.9.12 \|\|

*amaṃgalāni sarvāṇi maṃgalāni sadāśive \|*  
*tasmātsutāṃ śivaprāptyai tapase śikṣaya drutam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. All inauspicious things are auspicious in Sadāśiva. Hence immediately teach your daughter to hasten to perform the penance for attaining Śiva.

## \|\| 4.9.13 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya girervākyaṃ menā prītatarā'bhavat \|*  
*sutopakaṃṭhamagamadupadeṣṭuṃ tadorucim \|\| 13 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

13\. On hearing these words of the lord of mountains, Mena was greatly delighted. She approached her daughter to advise her to take interest in penance.

## \|\| 4.9.14 \|\|

*sutāṅgaṃ sukumāraṃ hi dṛṣṭvātīvātha menakā \|*  
*vivyathe netrayugme cāśrupūrṇe'bhavatāṃ drutam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. On seeing the tender limbs of her daughter, Menakā was greatly distressed. Her eyes welled up in tears immediately.

## \|\| 4.9.15 \|\|

*sutāṃ samupadeṣṭuṃ tanna śaśāka giripriyā \|*  
*bubudhe pārvatī tadvai jananīṅgitamāśu sā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The beloved of the lord of mountains was unable to advise her daughter to perform penance. Pārvatī understood the implied wish of her mother quickly.

## \|\| 4.9.16 \|\|

*atha sā kālikā devī sarvajñā parameśvarī \|*  
*uvāca jananīṃ sadyaḥ samāśvāsya punaḥ punaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Then the omniscient supreme goddess Pārvatī immediately spoke to her mother after consoling her again and again.

## \|\| 4.9.17 \|\|

*pārvatyuvāca \|*  
*mātaśśṛṇu mahāprājñe'dyatane 'jamuhūrtake \|*  
*rātrau dṛṣṭo mayā svapnastaṃ vadāmi kṛpāṃ kuru \|\| 17 \|\|*

Pārvatī said:—

17\. O mother, of great intelligence, listen in the early dawn to-day. At night I had a dream I shall tell you. Be pleased.

## \|\| 4.9.18 \|\|

*vipraścaiva tapasvī māṃ sadayaḥ prītipūrvakam \|*  
*upādideśa sutapaḥ kartuṃ mātaśśivasya vai \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. A brahmin sage advised me lovingly and compassionately to perform the penance of Śiva, O mother.

## \|\| 4.9.19 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*tacchrutvā menakā śīghraṃ patimāhūya tatra ca \|*  
*tatsvapnaṃ kathayāmāsa sutā dṛṣṭamaśeṣataḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

Brahhmā said:—

19\. On hearing that, Menakā called her husband there and told him the dream as seen by her daughter.

## \|\| 4.9.20 \|\|

*sutāsvapnamathākarṇya menakāto girīśvaraḥ \|*  
*uvāca paramaprītaḥ priyāṃ sambodhayangirā \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. After hearing the dream of his daughter from Menakā, the lord of the mountains was pleased and he spoke thus to his wife.

## \|\| 4.9.21 \|\|

*\|\| girīśvara uvāca \|*  
*he priye'pararātrānte svapno dṛṣṭo mayāpi hi \|*  
*taṃ śṛṇu tvaṃ mahāprītyā vacmyahaṃ taṃ samādarāt \|\| 21 \|\|*

The lord of the mountains said:—

21\. O dear, at the end of the latter half of the night, I too had a dream. Please listen to it lovingly. I shall zealously explain it.

## \|\| 4.9.22 \|\|

*ekastapasvī paramo nāradoktavarāṃ gadhṛk \|*  
*puropakaṃṭhaṃ suprītyā tapaḥ kartuṃ samāgataḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. A great saint of exquisite limbs, as mentioned by Nārada, arrived near my city with very great pleasure in order to perform penance there.

## \|\| 4.9.23 \|\|

*gṛhītvā svasutāṃ tatrāgamaṃ prītataropyaham \|*  
*mayā jñātassa vai śambhurnārado ktavaraḥ prabhuḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Delighted much I took my daughter there with me. He was recognised as Lord Śiva, the bridegroom as mentioned by Nārada

## \|\| 4.9.24 \|\|

*sevārthaṃ tasya tanayāmupadiśya tapasvinaḥ \|\| taṃ \|*  
*vai prārthitavāṃstasyāṃ na tadāṃgīcakāra saḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Advising our daughter to render service to that saint I requested him to approve of it but He didn’t.

## \|\| 4.9.25 \|\|

*abhūdvivādastumahānsāṃkhyavedāntasaṃmataḥ \|*  
*tatastadājñayā tatra saṃsthitāsītsutā mama \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. A great discussion took place (between her and Śiva based on Sāṅkhya and Vedānta). Thereafter at His bidding my daughter stayed there.

## \|\| 4.9.26 \|\|

*nidhāya hṛdi taṃ kāmaṃ siṣeve bhaktitaśca sā \|*  
*iti dṛṣṭaṃ mayā svapnaṃ proktavāṃste varānane \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Concealing her love in the heart she served Him with devotion. This is the dream I had, O bright-faced lady and I have told you all.

## \|\| 4.9.27 \|\|

*tato mene kiyatkālaṃ parīkṣyaṃ tatphalaṃ priye \|*  
*yogyamastīdameveha budhyasva tvaṃ mama dhruvam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Hence, dear Mena, for some time the result of this has to be watched. Certainly know this to be the proper step for me.

## \|\| 4.9.28 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*ityuktvā girirājaśca menakā vai munīśvara \|*  
*santasthatuḥ parīkṣantīṃ tatphalaṃ śuddhacetasau \|\| 28 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

28\. O excellent sage, the lord of the mountains having thus explained to Menakā, both of them remained watching its result, pure in mind.

## \|\| 4.9.29-30 \|\|

*itthamvyatīte'lpadine parameśaḥ satāṃ gatiḥ \|*  
*satīvirahasuvyagro bhramansarvatra sūtikṛt \|\| 29 \|\|*

*tatrājagāma suprītyā kiyadguṇayutaḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*tapaḥ kartuṃ satīpremavirahākulamānasaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. When a few days passed by, lord Śiva, the goal of saintly men, the cause of protection and enjoyment wandering here and there in his flutter and excitement due to the separation from Satī, came there with pleasure accompanied by a few of his Gaṇas, in order to perform penance. The lord was completely agitated due to Satī’s love and separation from her.

## \|\| 4.9.31 \|\|

*tapaścakāra svaṃ tatra pārvatī sevane ratā \|*  
*sakhībhyāṃ sahitā nityaṃ prasannārthamabhūttadā \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. He performed his penance there. Pārvatī engaged herself in His service continuously accompanied by two of her maids.

## \|\| 4.9.32 \|\|

*viddho''pi mārgaṇaiśśambhurvikṛtiṃ nāpa sa prabhuḥ \|*  
*preṣitena suraissvātmamohanārthaṃ smareṇa vai \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Although the lord Śiva was hit and wounded by the arrows of Kāma who was sent thither by the gods to enchant Him, He was not swayed at all.

## \|\| 4.9.33 \|\|

*dagdhvā smaraṃ ca tatraiva svavahninayanena saḥ \|*  
*smṛtvā mama vacaḥ kruddho mahyamantardadhe tataḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Burning Kāma there by His fiery eye, on remembering my words, the lord became angry with me and vanished from the scene.

## \|\| 4.9.34 \|\|

*tataḥ kālena kiyatā vināśya girijāmadam \|*  
*prasāditassutapasā prasanno'bhūnmaheśvaraḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. After sometime, Lord Śiva quelled the pride of Pārvatī but he was propitiated by her again performing great penance.

## \|\| 4.9.35 \|\|

*laukikācāramāśritya rudro viṣṇuprasāditaḥ \|*  
*kālīṃ vivāhayāmāsa tato'bhūdbahumaṃgalam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Following the conventions of the world, the lord married Pārvatī after being sponsored by Viṣṇu. Then everything auspicious ensued.

## \|\| 4.9.36 \|\|

*ityetatkathitaṃ tāta samāsāccaritaṃ vibhoḥ \|*  
*śaṃkarasya paraṃ divyaṃ kiṃ bhūyaḥ śrotumi cchasi \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. O dear, thus the story of the lord, the divine story of Śiva, has been narrated in brief. What is it that you wish to hear again?

## Chapter 10 - Mars is born and is raised to the status of a Planet by Śiva’s grace

## \|\| 4.10.1 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*viṣṇuśiṣya mahābhāga vidhe śaivavara prabho \|*  
*śivalīlāmimāṃ vyāsātprītyā me vaktumarhasi \|\| 1 \|\|*

Nārada said:—

1\. O Brahmā, the fortunate disciple of Viṣṇu, O lord, foremost among the devotees of Śiva, please narrate the divine sport of Śiva in detail to me.

## \|\| 4.10.2 \|\|

*satīvirahayukśaṃmbhuḥ kiṃ cakre caritantathā \|*  
*tapaḥ kartuṃ kadāyāto himavatprasthamuttamam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. What did Śiva, separated from Satī, do? When did He go to the excellent ridge of the Himavat to perform penance?

## \|\| 4.10.3 \|\|

*śivāśivaśivādo 'bhūtkathaṃ kāmakṣayaśca me \|*  
*tapaḥ kṛtvā kathamprāpa śivaṃ śambhuṃ ca pārvatī \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. How did the discussion between Śivā and Śiva take place? How did Pārvatī attain Śiva by performing penance?

## \|\| 4.10.4 \|\|

*tatsarvamaparaṃ cāpi śivasaccaritaṃ param \|*  
*vaktumarhasi me brahmanmahānandakaraṃ śubham \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. O Brahmā, these and other things, connected with the divine life of Śiva, pleasing and auspicious, you kindly narrate.

## \|\| 4.10.5 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*iti śrutvā nāradasya praśnaṃ lokādhipottamaḥ \|*  
*vidhiḥ provāca suprītyā smṛtvā śivapadāmbujam \|\| 5 \|\|*

Sūta said:—

5\. On hearing this inquiry of Nārada, Brahmā, the excellent lord of the worlds, remembered the lotus-like feet of Śiva and spoke.

## \|\| 4.10.6 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|\| devarṣe śaivavaryāya tadyaśaḥ śṛṇu cādarāt \|*  
*pāvanaṃ maṅgalakaraṃ bhaktivardhanamuttamam \|\| 6 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

6\. O celestial sage, most excellent among the devotees of Śiva, listen to His glory that sanctifies, renders everything auspicious and increases devotion.

## \|\| 4.10.7 \|\|

*āgatya svagiriṃ śambhuḥ priyāvirahakātaraḥ \|*  
*sasmāra svapriyāṃ devīṃ satīṃ prāṇādhikāṃ hṛdā \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Returning to His mountain, Śiva in his excitement caused by his separation from his beloved, remembered Satī, who was dearer to Him than his very life.

## \|\| 4.10.8 \|\|

*gaṇānābhāṣya śocaṃstāṃ tadguṇānpre mavardhanān \|*  
*varṇayāmāsa suprītyā darśayaṃllaukikīṃ gatim \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Addressing His Gaṇas, He bewailed her and narrated her good qualities heightening love. In this way He showed the way of the world to the people.

## \|\| 4.10.9 \|\|

*digambaro babhūvātha tyaktvā gārhasthyasadgatim \|*  
*punarbabhrāma lokanvai sarvāṃllīlāviśāradaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Abandoning the polished manners of a householder, He cast off his dress and roamed about all the worlds, clever in divine sports that He was.

## \|\| 4.10.10-11 \|\|

*darśanamprāpya kutrāpi satīvirahaduḥkhitaḥ \|*  
*punaśca girimāyātaśśaṃkaro bhaktaśaṃkaraḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*samādhāya mano yatnātsamādhinduḥkhanāśinama \|*  
*cakāra ca dadarśāsau svarūpaṃ nijamavyayam \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. Not seeing her anywhere, the pangs of his separation from Satī increasing, Śiva, the benefactor of His devotees, returned to His mountain and entered into trance for the destruction of misery. Thereupon He saw His imperishable real form.

## \|\| 4.10.12 \|\|

*itthaṃ cirataraṃ sthāṇustasthau dhvastaguṇatrayaḥ \|*  
*nirvikārī parambrahma māyādhīśassvayaṃprabhuḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Thus Śiva remained for a long time eliminating the three attributes, and unaffected by aberrations. The lord Himself, the controller of illusion remained in the state of the Supreme Brahman.

## \|\| 4.10.13 \|\|

*tatassamādhintattyāja vyatīya hyamitāssamāḥ \|*  
*yadā tadā babhūvāśu caritaṃ tadvadāmi vaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Then He gave up trance. Many years elapsed. What happened thereafter, I shall now recount to you.

## \|\| 4.10.14 \|\|

*prabhorlalāṭadeśāttu yatpṛṣacchramasaṃbhavam \|*  
*papāta dharaṇau tatra sa babhūva śiśurdrutam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The drops of sweat caused by exhaustion fell on the Earth from the lord’s forehead and took the shape of a child immediately.

## \|\| 4.10.15 \|\|

*caturbhujo'ruṇākāro ramaṇīyākṛtirmune \|*  
*alaukikadyutiḥ śrīmāṃstejasvī paradussahaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. O sage, the child was tawny-coloured and had four arms. He was comely in features. His brilliance was supermundane and unbearable to others.

## \|\| 4.10.16 \|\|

*ruroda sa śiśustasya puro hi parameśituḥ \|*  
*prākṛtātmajavattatra bhavācāraratasya hi \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Like a common child he cried in front of the Great lord who was engaged in worldly activities.

## \|\| 4.10.17 \|\|

*tadā vicārya sudhiyā dhṛtvā sustrītanuṃ kṣitiḥ \|*  
*āvirbabhūva tatraiva bhayamānīya śaṃkarāt \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Afraid of Śiva, the Earth pondered deeply over it and appeared before him in the guise of a good lady.

## \|\| 4.10.18 \|\|

*tambālaṃ drutamutthāya kroḍayāṃ nidadhe varam \|*  
*stanyaṃ sāpāyayatprītyā dugdhaṃ svoparisambhavam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. She lifted up the child immediately and held him to her chest. Lovingly she suckled the child with her excellent breast milk that flowed over her body.

## \|\| 4.10.19 \|\|

*cucumba tanmukhaṃ snehātsmitvā krīḍayadātmajam \|*  
*satyabhāvātsvayaṃ mātā parameśahitāvahā \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. She kissed the child’s face lovingly and petted him smilingly. In the absence of Satī she herself acted as his mother in the interest of lord Śiva.

## \|\| 4.10.20 \|\|

*taddṛṣṭvā caritaṃ śambhuḥ kautukī sūtikṛtkṛtī \|*  
*antaryāmī vihasyāthovāca jñātvā rasāṃ haraḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Śiva knew that she was the Earth. Śiva, the cause of protection and enjoyment, the immanent soul, on seeing her activities became contented and eagerly said to her laughingly.

## \|\| 4.10.21 \|\|

*dhanyā tvaṃ dharaṇi prītyā pālayaitaṃ sutaṃ mama \|*  
*tvayyudbhūtaṃśramajalānmahātejasvino varam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. “O Earth, you are blessed. Rear this child of mine lovingly, born of my glittering drops of sweat over you.

## \|\| 4.10.22 \|\|

*mama śramakabhūrbālo yadyapi priyakṛtkṣite \|*  
*tvannāmnā syādbhavetkhyātastritāparahitassadā \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Although the child is born of the sweat of my body, O Earth, he will be famous in the world after your name. He will be a bestower of pleasures and will be free from the three distresses always.

## \|\| 4.10.23 \|\|

*asau bālaḥ kudātā hi bhaviṣyati guṇī tava \|*  
*mamāpi sukhadātā hi gṛhāṇainaṃ yathāruci \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. This boy of yours will be a bestower of lands and will have good qualities. He will make me too happy. Accept him with pleasure”.

## \|\| 4.10.24 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityuktvā virarāmātha kiṃcidvirahamuktadhīḥ \|*  
*lokācārakaro rudro nirvikārī satāmpriyaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

24\. After saying this He stopped. He was a bit relieved of His pangs of separation. Śiva, free from aberrations, and a lover of good men, acted thus only for following the worldly conventions.

## \|\| 4.10.25 \|\|

*api kṣitirjagāmāśu śivājñāmadhigamya sā \|*  
*svasthānaṃ sasutā prāpa sukhamātyaṃtikaṃ ca vai \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The Earth too, as Śiva bade her, returned to her abode along with the child. She was extremely happy.

## \|\| 4.10.26 \|\|

*sa bālo bhauma ityākhyāṃ prāpya bhūtvā yuvā drutam \|*  
*tasyāṃ kāśyāṃ ciraṃ kālaṃ siṣeve śaṃkaramprabhum \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The child acquired the name Bhauma (son of the Earth). He attained youth immedately. For a long time he worshipped lord Śiva at Kāśī.

## \|\| 4.10.27 \|\|

*viśveśvaraprasādena grahatvaṃ prāpya bhūmijaḥ \|*  
*divyaṃ lokaṃ jagāmāśu śukralokātparaṃ varam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. By the grace of lord Śiva, the son of the Earth, acquired the status of a planet. He went to the heavenly sphere beyond the region of Venus.

## \|\| 4.10.28 \|\|

*ityuktaṃ śambhucaritaṃ satīvirahasaṃyutam \|*  
*tapasyācaraṇaṃ śambhośśṛṇu cādarato mune \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. O sage, thus I have told you the story of Śiva and His separation from Satī. Now listen to the story of His performance of penance.

## Chapter 11 - Śiva and Himavat meet together

## \|\| 4.11.1-2 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*varddhamānā gireḥ putrī sā śakti lokapūjitā \|*  
*aṣṭavarṣā yadā jātā himālayagṛhe satī \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tajjanma giriśo jñātvā satīvirahakātaraḥ \|*  
*kṛtvā tāmadbhutāmantarmumodātīva nārada \|\| 2 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

1-2. O Nārada, the daughter of the mountain, honoured in the three worlds, was brought up in the palace of Himācala. When she was eight years old, Śiva distressed by Śatī’s separation came to know of her birth. Keeping her wonderful memory within his heart He rejoiced much.

## \|\| 4.11.3 \|\|

*tasminnevāntare śambhurlaukikīṃ gatimāśritaḥ \|*  
*samādhātuṃ manassamyaktapaḥ karttuṃ samaicchata \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. In the meantime, following the conventions of the world, Śiva wished to perform penance in order to concentrate his mind properly.

## \|\| 4.11.4-5 \|\|

*kāṃścidgaṇavarāñchāntānnaṃdyādīnavagṛhya ca \|*  
*gaṅgāvatāramagamaddhimavatprasthamuttamam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*yatra gaṃgā nipatitā purā brahmapurātsrutā \|*  
*sarvāghaughavināśāya pāvanī paramā mune \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. Taking some important Gaṇas of quiet nature, Nandin and others, with Him, He went to the excellent Himālayan ridge—Gaṅgāvatāra, O sage, where the great holy river Gaṅgā flowed from Brahmapura formerly, in order to quell sins.

## \|\| 4.11.6-7 \|\|

*tapaḥprārambhamakarotsthitvā tatra vaśī haraḥ \|*  
*ekāgraṃ ciṃtayāmāsa svamātmānamatandritaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*ceto jñānabhavaṃ nityaṃ jyotīrūpaṃ nirāmayam \|*  
*jaganmayaṃ cidānandaṃ dvaitahīnaṃ nirāśrayam \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. Staying there, Śiva of full self-control, started His activities of penance. With full concentration and alertness He thought on His own Self, the cause of mental knowledge, the eternal, the luminous, free from affliction, identical with the universe, consciousness and Bliss, without a second and having no support.

## \|\| 4.11.8-9 \|\|

*hare dhyānapare tisminpramathā dhyānatatparāḥ \|*  
*abhavankecidapare nandibhṛṃgyādayo gaṇāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*sevāṃ cakrustadā kecidgaṇāḥ śambhoḥ parātmanaḥ \|*  
*naivākūjaṃstu maunā hi dvarapāḥ kecanābhavan \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. When Śiva began His meditation, the Pramathas also began their meditation as well as some Gaṇas, Nandin, Bhṛṅgi etc. Some of the Gaṇas rendered service to Śiva, the Supreme Self. Some of them became His gatekeepers. They observed silence and did not shout.

## \|\| 4.11.10 \|\|

*etasminnantare tatra jagāma himabhūdharaḥ \|*  
*śaṅkarasyauṣadhiprasthaṃ śrutvāgamanamādarāt \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. In the meantime on hearing that Śiva had come to Auṣadhiprastha, the mountain Himavat too went there.

## \|\| 4.11.11 \|\|

*praṇanāma prabhuṃ rudraṃ sagaṇo bhūdhareśvaraḥ \|*  
*samānarca ca suprītastuṣṭāva sa kṛtāñjaliḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Accompanied by his attendants, the lord of the mountains bowed to the lord Śiva, worshipped Him with pleasure and eulogised Him with palms joined in reverence.

## \|\| 4.11.12 \|\|

*himālaya uvāca \|*  
*devadeva mahādeva kapardicchaṃkara prabho \|*  
*tvayaiva lokanāthena pālitaṃ bhuvanatrayam \|\| 12 \|\|*

Lord Himavat said:—

12\. O great god, lord of the gods, O lord Śiva, the three worlds are sustained by you alone who are lord of the worlds.

## \|\| 4.11.13 \|\|

*namaste devadeveśa yogirūpadharāya ca \|*  
*nirguṇāya namastubhyaṃ saguṇāya vihāriṇe \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Obeisance to Thee, O lord of gods, obeisance to the one who has assumed the form of a Yogin, obeisance to Thee that art possessed and devoid of attributes and obeisance to Thee who art sportive.

## \|\| 4.11.14 \|\|

*kailāsavāsine śambho sarvalokāṭanāya ca \|*  
*namaste parameśāya līlākārāya śūline \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. O Śiva, obeisance to the resident of Kailāsa, obeisance to one who wanders all over the worlds, obeisance to thee the great lord, to the one indulging in divine sports, obeisance to the trident-holder.

## \|\| 4.11.15 \|\|

*paripūrṇaguṇādhānavikārarahitāyate \|*  
*namo'nīhāya vīhāya dhīrāya paramātmane \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. O lord, of complete and perfect qualities, obeisance to Thee, devoid of aberrations. Obeisance to Thee without aspirations. Obeisance to Thee without desires. Obeisance to the bold one, to the great soul.

## \|\| 4.11.16 \|\|

*abahirbhogakārāya janavatsalate namaḥ \|*  
*triguṇādhīśa māyeśa brahmaṇe paramātmane \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. O overlord of the three attributes, O lord of delusion, favourably disposed towards the people, obeisance unto you, who grant inner pleasures of the soul. Obeisance to Brahman, the great soul.

## \|\| 4.11.17 \|\|

*viṣṇubrahmādisevyāya viṣṇubrahmasvarūpiṇe \|*  
*viṣṇubrahmakadātre te bhaktapriya namo'stu te \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Obeisance to Thee, worthy of being served by Viṣṇu Brahmā and others; obeisance to Thee of the form of Viṣṇu and Brahmā; obeisance to Thee, the creator of Viṣṇu and Brahmā, obeisance to Thee O one favourably disposed to the devotees.

## \|\| 4.11.18 \|\|

*taporata tapasthānasutapaḥ phaladāyine \|*  
*tapaḥpriyāya śāntāya namaste brahmarūpiṇe \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. O one engaged in penance, O one the venue of penance; obeisance to Thee the bestower of fruits of penance; obeisance to Thee who lovest penance; obeisance to Thee of the form of Brahman and quiescent.

## \|\| 4.11.19 \|\|

*vyavahārakarāyaiva lokācārakarāya te \|*  
*saguṇāya pareśāya namostu paramātmane \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Obeisance to Thee who lay down the principles of dealings and worldly conventions; obeisance to the great Śiva full of attributes; obeisance to Thee the great soul.

## \|\| 4.11.20 \|\|

*līlā tava maheśānāvedyā sādhusukhapradā \|*  
*bhaktādhīnasvarūpo'si bhaktavaśyo hi karmakṛt \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. O great lord, your divine sports are incomprehensible. They bestow happiness on saintly men. Your nature is subservient to the devotees and you are under their control. You are the performer of all activities.

## \|\| 4.11.21 \|\|

*mama bhāgyodayādatra tvamāgata iha prabho \|*  
*sanātha kṛtavānmāṃ tvaṃ varṇito dānavatsalaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. O lord, you have come here because my fortune is in its ascendancy. You have been described as a bestower of favours to the distressed. You have put me under your patronage and protection.

## \|\| 4.11.22 \|\|

*adya me saphalaṃ janma saphalaṃ jīvanaṃ mama \|*  
*adya me saphalaṃ sarvaṃ yadatra tvaṃ samāgataḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Today my life has borne fruit, in fact everything connected with me has become fruitful since you have come here.

## \|\| 4.11.23 \|\|

*jñātvā māṃ dāsamavyagramājñāndehi maheśvara \|*  
*tvatsevāṃ ca mahāprītyā kuryāmahamananyadhīḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Knowing me to be your slave of great composure, O great lord, you can freely command me. With my mind not fascinated by other things I shall serve you with great pleasure.

## \|\| 4.11.24 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya vacastasya girīśasya maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*kiṃcidunmīlya netre ca dadarśa sagaṇaṃ girim \|\| 24 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

24\. On hearing these words of the lord of mountains, lord Śiva slightly opened his eyes and cast a glance on the lord of mountains who was accompanied by his attendants.

## \|\| 4.11.25 \|\|

*sagaṇaṃ tantathā dṛṣṭvā girirājaṃ vṛṣadhvajaḥ \|*  
*uvāca dhyānayogasthaḥ smayanniva jagatpatiḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. On seeing the lord of mountains with his followers, the bull-bannered god Śiva, the lord of the universe permanently engaged in meditation and Yogic practice said smilingly.

## \|\| 4.11.26 \|\|

*maheśvara uvāca \|*  
*tava pṛṣṭhe tapastaptuṃ rahasyamahamāgataḥ \|*  
*yathā na kopi nikaṭaṃ samāyātu tathā kuru \|\| 26 \|\|*

Lord Śiva said:—

26\. I have come to perform penance in secret on your top. Make arrangements so that none should be able to come near me.

## \|\| 4.11.27 \|\|

*tvaṃ mahātmā tapodhāmā munīnāṃ ca sadāśrayaḥ \|*  
*devānāṃ rākṣasānāṃ ca pareṣāṃ ca mahātmanām \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. You are a noble soul, the abode of penance and permanent residence of sages, gods, demons and other great men.

## \|\| 4.11.28 \|\|

*sadā vāso dvijādīnāṃ gaṃgāpūtaśca nityadā \|*  
*paropakārī sarveṣāṃ girīṇāmadhipaḥ prabhuḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. You are the permanent residence of brahmins and others; you are always sanctified by Gaṅgā; you render help to others and you are the lord and king of all mountains.

## \|\| 4.11.29 \|\|

*ahaṃ tapaścarāmyatra gaṃgāvataraṇe sthale \|*  
*āśritastava suprīto girirāja yatātmavān \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. O king of mountains, delighted in resorting to you and controlling my senses and mind I am going to perform penance here at Gaṅgāvataraṇa.

## \|\| 4.11.30 \|\|

*nirvighnaṃ me tapaścātra hetunā yena śailapa \|*  
*sarvathā hi giriśreṣṭha suyatnaṃ kuru sāmpratam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. O lord of mountains, O best of mountains, now put forth all endeavour whereby my penance can be conducted without obstacles.

## \|\| 4.11.31 \|\|

*mamedameva paramaṃ sevanaṃ parvatottama \|*  
*svagṛhaṃ gaccha satprītyā tatsaṃpādaya yatnataḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. O excellent Mountain, this alone is the greatest service that you can render. Please arrange for it with due effort. Please return to your abode with your mind full of pleasure.

## \|\| 4.11.32 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*ityuktvā jagatāṃ nāthastūṣṇīmāsa sa sūtikṛt \|*  
*girirājastadā śambhuṃ praṇayādidamabravīt \|\| 32 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

32\. After saying this, the lord of the worlds, the cause of protection and enjoyment kept silent. The lord of the mountains then spoke to Śiva with affection.

## \|\| 4.11.33 \|\|

*\|\| himālaya uvāca \|*  
*pūjito'si jagannātha mayā tvamparameśvara \|*  
*svāgatenādya viṣaye sthitaṃ tvāmprārthayāmi kim \|\| 33 \|\|*

Himicala said:—

33\. O great lord of the universe, I have come myself and worshipped you. What shall I ask you who stay in my own kingdom?

## \|\| 4.11.34 \|\|

*mahatā tapasā tvaṃ hi devairyatnaparāśritaiḥ \|*  
*na prāpyase maheśāna sa tvaṃ svayamupasthitaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. O great lord, you cannot be attained by great penance even by the gods who put forth great efforts. But you yourself have come here.

## \|\| 4.11.35 \|\|

*mattopyanyatamo nāsti na matto'nyo'sti puṇyavān \|*  
*bhavāniti ca matpṛṣṭhe tapase samupasthitaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. There is none more fortunate than me; there is none more meritorious than me, since you have come to perform penance on my summit.

## \|\| 4.11.36 \|\|

*devendrādadhikammanye svātmānamparameśvara \|*  
*sagaṇena tvayāgatya kṛto'nugrahabhāgaham \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. O great lord, I consider myself greater than the god of gods. You have come here with your Gaṇas and made me blessed.

## \|\| 4.11.37 \|\|

*nirvighnaṃ kuru deveśa svatantraḥ paramantapaḥ \|*  
*kariṣye'hantathā sevāṃ dāso'hante sadā prabho \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. O lord of gods, independently and without any obstacles perform your great penance. O lord, I am your slave always. I shall do all service to you.

## \|\| 4.11.38 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityuktvā girirājo'sau svaṃ veśma drutamāgataḥ \|*  
*vṛttāṃttaṃ taṃ samācakhyau priyāyai ca samādarāt \|\| 38 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

38\. After saying this, the lord of the mountains returned at once to his abode and enthusiastically narrated everything to his beloved wife.

## \|\| 4.11.39 \|\|

*nīyamānānparīvārānsvagaṇānapi nārada \|*  
*samāhūyākhilāñchailapatiḥ provāca tattvataḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. O Nārada, calling together all his attendants with the members of their families, the lord of the mountains said emphatically.

## \|\| 4.11.40 \|\|

*himālaya uvāca \|*  
*adya prabhṛti no yātu kopi gaṃgāvatāraṇam \|*  
*macchāsanena matprasthaṃ satyametadbravīmyaham \|\| 40 \|\|*

Himācala said:—

40\. From now onwards, none of you shall go to the ridge of mine, called Gaṅgāvataraṇa. This is my command. I am telling you the truth.

## \|\| 4.11.41 \|\|

*gamiṣyati janaḥ kaścittatra cettaṃ mahākhalam \|*  
*daṇḍayiṣye viśeṣeṇa satyametanmayoditam \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. If anyone of you goes there I shall punish that rogue particularly. This is the truth I am speaking.

## \|\| 4.11.42 \|\|

*iti tānsa niyamyāśu svagaṇānnikhilānmune \|*  
*suyatnaṃ kṛtavāñchailastaṃ śṛṇu tvaṃ vadāmi te \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. O sage, after thus checking all of his attendants, the mountain made other arrangements also. I now tell you all about the same.

## Chapter 12 - Śiva-Himavat dialogue

## \|\| 4.12.1 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*atha śailapatirhṛṣṭaḥ satpuṣpaphalasaṃcayam \|*  
*samādāya svatanayāsahito'gāddharāṃtikam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

1\. Then, the delighted lord of the mountains, took some fresh flowers and fruits with him and approached Śiva along with his daughter.

## \|\| 4.12.2 \|\|

*sa gatvā trijagannāthaṃ praṇamya dhyānatatparam \|*  
*arthayāmāsa tanayāṃ kālīṃ tasmai hṛdādbhutām \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Approaching the lord of the three worlds, engaged in meditation and bowing to Him he mentally dedicated to Him, his wonderful daughter.

## \|\| 4.12.3 \|\|

*phalapuṣpādikaṃ sarvaṃ tattadagre nidhāya saḥ \|*  
*agre kṛtvā sutāṃ śambhumidamāha ca śailarāṭ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Placing the fruits and flowers in front of Him and making his daughter stand before Him, the lord of the mountains spoke to Śiva.

## \|\| 4.12.4 \|\|

*himagiriruvāca \|*  
*bhagavaṃstanayā me tvāṃ sevituṃ candraśekharam \|*  
*samutsukā samānītā tvadārādhanakāṃkṣayā \|\| 4 \|\|*

Himācala said:—

4\. O lord, my daughter who is eager to serve you, the moon-crested lord, I have brought here with a desire to propitiate you.

## \|\| 4.12.5 \|\|

*sakhībhyāṃ saha nityaṃ tvāṃ sevatāmeva śaṃkaram \|*  
*anujānīhi tāṃ nātha mayi te yadyanugrahaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Let her serve you, the benefactor, for ever, along with two of her maids. O lord, if you wish to bless me, please permit her.

## \|\| 4.12.6-10 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*atha tāṃ śaṃkaro'paśyatprathamārūḍhayauvanām \|*  
*phullendīvarapatrābhā pūrṇacandranibhānanām \|\| 6 \|\|*

*samastalīlāsaṃsthānaśubhaveṣavijṛmbhikām \|*  
*kambugrīvāṃ viśālākṣīṃ cārukarṇayugojjvalām \|\| 7 \|\|*

*mṛṇālāyataparyyantabāhuyugmamanoharām \|*  
*rājīvakuḍmalaprakhyau ghanapīnaudṛḍhaustanau \|\| 8 \|\|*

*bibhratīṃ kṣīṇamadhyāṃ ca trivalīmadhyarājitām \|*  
*sthalapadmapratīkāśapādayugmavirājitām \|\| 9 \|\|*

*dhyānapaṃjaranirbaddhamunimānasamapyalam \|*  
*darśanādbhraṃśane śaktāṃ yoṣidgaṇaśiromaṇim \|\| 10 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

6-10. Then Śiva looked at her in the first flush of her youth. Her complexion resembled the full blown blue lotus petals. Her face appeared as the full moon. Her auspicious dress and features were the repositories of all graceful charms. Her neck had the shape of the conch-shell. Her eyes were wide and her ears shone exquisitely. On either side, her long-rounded arms resembling a lotus-stalk shone beautifully. Her two breasts resembling lotus-buds were stout, plump and firm. Her waist was slender and the curly locks of her hair shone well. Her feet resembled the land-lotus and were comely in appearance. She was competent to shake the minds of even the sages deeply engrossed in meditation, even at the very sight. She was a crest-jewel of all the maidens in the world.

## \|\| 4.12.11-12 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā tāṃ tādṛśīṃ tāta dhyānināṃ ca manoharām \|*  
*vigrahe tantramantrāṇāṃ varddhinīṃ kāmarūpiṇīm \|\| 11 \|\|*

*nyamīlayadṛśau śīghraṃ dadhyau svaṃ rūpamuttamam \|*  
*paratattvaṃ mahāyogī triguṇātparamavyayam \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. On seeing her in that exquisite form as increased the pleasure and love of even those who meditate, the great Yogin Śiva closed His eyes immediately and meditated upon His real form, the great principle that is beyond the three attributes and is imperishable.

## \|\| 4.12.13-14 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā tadānīṃ sakaleśvaraṃ vibhuṃ tapojuṣāṇaṃ vinimīlitekṣaṇam \|*  
*kapardinaṃ candrakalāvibhūṣaṇaṃ vedāntavedyaṃ paramāsane sthitam \|\| 13 \|\|*

*vavanda śīrṣṇā ca punarhimācalaḥ sa saṃśayaṃ prāpadadīnasattvaḥ \|*  
*uvāca vākyaṃ jagadekabandhuṃ girīśvaro vākyavidāṃ variṣṭhaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. On seeing Śiva the lord of all, the chief of those devoted to penance, the lord with the moon as his ornament, who can be known through spiritual insight and who was sitting in the meditative posture closing His eyes, Himācala saluted Him again. Though he was not disheartened, he entertained some doubts. Thus he, the lord of mountains, foremost of the eloqueut, spoke to Śiva, the sole kinsman of the universe.

## \|\| 4.12.15 \|\|

*himācala uvāca \|*  
*devadeva mahādeva karuṇākara śaṃkara \|*  
*paśya māṃ śaraṇamprāptamunmīlya nayane vibho \|\| 15 \|\|*

Himācala said:—

15\. O great lord of the gods, O Śiva, the merciful, O lord, open your eyes and look at me who have sought refuge in you.

## \|\| 4.12.16 \|\|

*śiva śarva maheśāna jagadānandakṛtprabho \|*  
*tvāṃ nato'haṃ mahādeva sarvāpadvinivartakam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. O Śiva, O great lord, the delighter ofthe universe, O great God, I bow to you who destroy all adversities.

## \|\| 4.12.17 \|\|

*na tvāṃ jānaṃti deveśa vedāśśāstrāṇi kṛtsnaśaḥ \|*  
*atīto mahimādhvānaṃ tava vāṅmanasoḥ sadā \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. O lord of gods, the Vedas and the sacred lore do

not know you entirely. Your greatness is beyond the sphere of words and minds, inexpressible by means of words and incomprehensible.

## \|\| 4.12.18 \|\|

*atadvyāvṛttitastvāṃ vai cakitaṃ cakitaṃ sadā \|*  
*abhidhatte śrutiḥ sarvā pareṣāṃ kā kathā matā \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Not to speak of others, even the Vedas describe you with awe and timidity not positively but negating what you are not.

## \|\| 4.12.19 \|\|

*jānaṃti bahavo bhaktāstvatkṛpāṃ prāpya bhaktitaḥ \|*  
*śaraṇāgata bhaktānāṃ na kutrāpi bhramādikam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Securing your grace through devotion, many devotees become acquainted with you. Seeking refuge in you they get correct knowledge about your real self.

## \|\| 4.12.20 \|\|

*vijñaptiṃ śṛṇu matprītyā svadāsasya mamādhunā \|*  
*tava devājñayā tāta dīnatvādvarṇayāmi hi \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Please listen to my entreaty with a long heart. I am your slave. O dear lord, in humility I shall explain the same to you.

## \|\| 4.12.21 \|\|

*sabhāgyohaṃ mahādeva prasādāttava śaṃkara \|*  
*matvā svadāsaṃ māṃ nātha kṛpāṃ kuru namo'stu te \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. O great god Śiva, by your favour I feel most fortunate. O lord, consider me your slave and be sympathetic towards me. Obeisance to you.

## \|\| 4.12.22 \|\|

*pratyahaṃ cāgamiṣyāmi darśanārthaṃ tava prabho \|*  
*anayā sutayā svāminnideśaṃ dātumarhasi \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. O lord, I shall be visiting you daily along with my daughter. O lord, be pleased to command me accordingly.

## \|\| 4.12.23 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya vacastasyonmīlya netre maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*tyaktadhyānaḥ parāmṛśya devadevo'bravīdvacaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

23\. On hearing his words, the great lord of the gods broke His meditation, opened His eyes, thought a little and spoke.

## \|\| 4.12.24 \|\|

*\|\| maheśvara uvāca \|*  
*āgaṃtavyaṃ tvayā nityaṃ darśanārthaṃ mamācala \|*  
*kumārīṃ sadane sthāpya nānyathā mama darśanam \|\| 24 \|\|*

Lord Śiva said:—

24\. “O mountain, you shall come every day to see me, leaving your daughter in your abode. Otherwise I cannot be seen”

## \|\| 4.12.25 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*maheśavacanaṃ śrutvā śivātātastathāvidham \|*  
*acalaḥ pratyuvācedaṃ giriśaṃ natakamadharaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

25\. On hearing the words of Śiva in that view, the father of Śivā the mountain, bowed his head and replied to Śiva.

## \|\| 4.12.26 \|\|

*himācala uvāca \|*  
*kasmānmayānayā sārddhaṃ nāgaṃtavyaṃ taducyatām \|*  
*sevane kimayogyeyaṃ nāhaṃ vedmyatra kāraṇam \|\| 26 \|\|*

Himācala said:—

26\. “Let this be kindly mentioned why this girl cannot accompany me here. Is she unworthy of your service? I do not know the reason thereof.”

## \|\| 4.12.27 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*tato'bravīdgiriṃ śaṃbhuḥ prahasanvṛṣabhadhvajaḥ \|*  
*lokācāraṃ viśeṣeṇa darśayanhi kuyoginām \|\| 27 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

27\. Particularly pointing out the worldly conduct of fake ascetics, the bull-bannered god Śiva laughingly spoke to the mountain.

## \|\| 4.12.28 \|\|

*śaṃbhuruvāca \|*  
*iyaṃ kumārī suśroṇī tanvī candrānanā śubhā \|*  
*nānetavyā matsamīpe vārayāmi punaḥ punaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

Śiva said:—

28\. This auspicious slender-bodied maiden of comely hips and moon-like face should not be brought near me. I forbid you again and again.

## \|\| 4.12.29 \|\|

*māyārūpā smṛtā nārī vidvadbhirvedapāragaiḥ \|*  
*yuvatī tu viśeṣeṇa vighnakartrī tapasvinām \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. A woman is a phase of illusion. As the scholars who have mastered the Vedas say particularly, a young damsel is a hindrance to ascetics.

## \|\| 4.12.30 \|\|

*ahaṃ tapasvī yogī ca nirlipto māyayā sadā \|*  
*prayojanaṃ na yuktyā vai striyā kiṃ mesti bhūdhara \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. O mountain, I am an ascetic, a yogin, never affected by illusion. Of what avail is a woman thrust on me?

## \|\| 4.12.31 \|\|

*evaṃ punarna vaktavyaṃ tapasvivarasaṃśrita \|*  
*vedadharmapravīṇastvaṃ yato jñānivaro budhaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. O friend resorted to by great ascetics, you shall not say so again, since you are an adept in Vedic religion, a scholar and one foremost among the wise.

## \|\| 4.12.32 \|\|

*bhavatyacala tatsaṃgādviṣayotpattirāśu vai \|*  
*vinaśyati ca vairāgyaṃ tato bhraśyati sattapaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. O mountain, by contact with a woman, worldliness springs up; non-attachment perishes and the virtuous penance is destroyed.

## \|\| 4.12.33 \|\|

*atastapasvinā śaila na kāryā strīṣu saṃgatiḥ \|*  
*mahāviṣayamūlaṃ sā jñānavairāgyanāśinī \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Hence, O mountain, no ascetic shall have any truck with women. A woman is the root of all worldly attachments. She destroys all wisdom and detachment together.

## \|\| 4.12.34 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*ityādyuktvā bahutaraṃ mahāyogī maheśvaraḥ \|\| \|*  
*virarāma girīśaṃ taṃ mahāyogivaraḥ prabhuḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

34\. Speaking these and many other similar things to the lord of mountains, lord Śiva the great Yogin, stopped.

## \|\| 4.12.35 \|\|

*etacchrutvā vacanaṃ tasya śaṃbhornirāmayaṃ niḥspṛhaṃ niṣṭhuraṃ ca \|*  
*kālītātaścakito'bhūtsurarṣe tadvatkiṃcidvyākulaścāsa tūṣṇīm \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. On hearing these ruthless words of Śiva free from sickness and desire, the father of Pārvatī became nervous, O celestial sage, and a little agitated. But he kept quiet.

## \|\| 4.12.36 \|\|

*tapasvinoktaṃ vacanaṃ niśamya tathā girīśaṃ cakitaṃ vicāryya \|*  
*ataḥ praṇamyaiva śivaṃ bhavānī jagāda vākyaṃ viśadantadānīm \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. On hearing the words of the ascetic and finding her father, the lord of the mountains, frightened, Pārvatī bowed to Śiva and spoke these words clearly.

## Chapter 13 - Śiva-Pārvatī dialogue

## \|\| 4.13.1 \|\|

*bhavānyuvāca \|*  
*kimuktaṃ girirājāya tvayā yogistapasvinā \|*  
*taduttaraṃ śṛṇu vibho matto jñāniviśārada \|\| 1 \|\|*

Pārvatī said:—

1\. O Yogin, O lord, wise and clever, please listen to the reply to what you, as an ascetic, said to the lord of mountains.

## \|\| 4.13.2 \|\|

*tapaśśaktyānvitaśśambho karoṣi vipulaṃ tapaḥ \|*  
*tava buddhiriyaṃ jātā tapastaptuṃ mahātmanaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. O Śiva, you perform this great penance because you possess the energy of penance. Your intellect is inclined to perform penance because you are a noble soul.

## \|\| 4.13.3 \|\|

*sā śaktiḥ prakṛtirjñeyā sarveṣāmapi karmaṇām \|*  
*tayā viracyate sarvaṃ pālyate ca vināśyate \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. That energy is the Prakṛti, the cause of all activities. Everything is created, sustained and destroyed by it.

## \|\| 4.13.4 \|\|

*kastvaṃ kā prakṛtissūkṣmā bhagavaṃstadvimṛśyatām \|*  
*vinā prakṛtyā ca kathaṃ liṃgarūpī maheśvaraḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. O lord, please ponder over who you are and who this subtle Prakṛti is. Without Prakṛti how can the great lord of the phallic form exist?

## \|\| 4.13.5 \|\|

*arcanīyo'si vaṃdyo'si dhyeyo'si prāṇināṃ sadā \|*  
*prakṛtyā ca vicāryeti hṛdā sarvaṃ taducyatām \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. You are worthy of the worship, respect and meditation of all living beings for ever, thanks to Prakṛti. Thinking of this in your heart, please reply.

## \|\| 4.13.6 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*pārvatyāstadvacaḥ śrutvā mahotikaraṇe rataḥ \|*  
*suvihasya prasannātmā maheśo vākyamabravīt \|\| 6 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

6\. On hearing these words of Pārvatī, the great lord engaged in the causation of great enjoyment and protection became delighted. He laughed and said.

## \|\| 4.13.7 \|\|

*\|\| maheśvara uvāca \|*  
*tapasā parameṇeva prakṛtiṃ nāśayāmyaham \|*  
*prakṛtyā rahitaśśambhurahaṃ tiṣṭhāmi tattvataḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

The great lord said:—

7\. I am destroying the Prakṛti with my great penance. I remain in reality without Prakṛti.

## \|\| 4.13.8 \|\|

*tasmācca prakṛtessadbhirna kāryassaṃgrahaḥ kvacit \|*  
*sthātavyaṃ nirvikāraiśca lokācāra vivarjitaiḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Indeed Prakṛti should not be taken in by good people. They should remain unaffected eschewing all worldly conduct.

## \|\| 4.13.9 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*ityuktā śambhunā tāta laukikavyavahārataḥ \|*  
*suvihasya hṛdā kālī jagāda madhuraṃ vacaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

9\. O dear one, this was said by Śiva in accordance with worldly conventions and dealings. Pārvatī thereupon laughed to herself and spoke these sweet words.

Pārvatī said.—

## \|\| 4.13.10 \|\|

*\|\| kālyuvāca \|*  
*yaduktaṃ bhavatā yoginvacanaṃ śaṃkara prabho \|*  
*sā ca kiṃ prakṛtirna syādatītastāṃ bhavānkatham \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. O Yogin, O lord Śiva, based on what you said how can that Prakṛti cease to exist and how can you be considered beyond that Prakṛti?

## \|\| 4.13.11 \|\|

*etadvicārya vaktavyaṃ tattvato hi yathātatham \|*  
*prakṛtyā sarvametacca baddhamasti niraṃtaram \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. You shall ponder over this and say with reference to the facts as they are. All these (the universe etc) are bound by Prakṛti continuously.

## \|\| 4.13.12 \|\|

*tasmāttvayā na vaktavyaṃ na kāryaṃ kiṃcideva hi \|*  
*vacanaṃ racanaṃ sarvaṃ prākṛtaṃ viddhi cetasā \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Hence you shall not say anything, not do anything. Know that speaking, doing etc. is a Prākṛta activity.

## \|\| 4.13.13 \|\|

*yacchṛṇoṣi yadaśnāsi yatpaśyasi karoṣi yat \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ prakṛteḥ kāryaṃ mithyāvādo nirarthakaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. What you hear, what you eat, what you see and what you do—all these are (essentially) the activities of Prakṛti. To say that it is unreal is meaningless.

## \|\| 4.13.14 \|\|

*prakṛteḥ paramaścettvaṃ kimarthaṃ tapyase tapaḥ \|*
