*tvayā śaṃbho'dhunā hyasmingirau himavati prabho \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. O lord, if you are greater than Prakṛti, wherefore do you perform penance, O Śiva, now, on this mountain Himavat,

## \|\| 4.13.15 \|\|

*prakṛtyā gilito'si tvaṃ na jānāsi nijaṃ hara \|*  
*nijaṃ jānāsi cedīśa kimarthaṃ tapyase tapaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. O Śiva, you have been swallowed by Prakṛti, you do not know your own situation. O lord, if you do not know your own situation why do you perform penance?

## \|\| 4.13.16 \|\|

*vāgvādena ca kiṃ kāryaṃ mama yogistvayā saha \|*  
*pratyakṣe hyanumānasya na pramāṇaṃ vidurbudhāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. O yogin, what have I to do with an argument with you? Scholars say that without perception inference has no authority at all.

## \|\| 4.13.17 \|\|

*iṃdriyāṇāṃ gocaratvaṃ yāvadbhavati dehinām \|*  
*tāvatsarvaṃ vimaṃtavyaṃ prākṛtaṃ jñānibhirdhiyā \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. As long as the embodied beings remain the objects of the sense-organs, everything is Prākṛta. Wise men consider it so.

## \|\| 4.13.18 \|\|

*kiṃ bahūktena yogīśa śṛṇu madvacanaṃ param \|*  
*sā cāhaṃ puruṣo'si tvaṃ satyaṃ satyaṃ na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. O lord of ascetics, a long-winded talk is of no avail. Listen to my emphatic statement. I am Prakṛti and you are Puruṣa. This is the truth. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 4.13.19 \|\|

*madanugrahatastvaṃ hi saguṇo rūpavānmataḥ \|*  
*māṃ vinā tvaṃ nirīho'si na kiṃcitkartumarhasi \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. With my blessings you become qualitative and embodied. Without me, you are attributeless and incompetent to perform any activity.

## \|\| 4.13.20 \|\|

*parādhīnassadā tvaṃ hi nānākarmmakaro vaśī \|*  
*nirvikārī kathaṃ tvaṃ hi na liptaśca mayā katham \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Being always subservient to Prakṛti you perform all activities. Self-controlled, free from aberrations and untainted by me how can you perform them?

## \|\| 4.13.21 \|\|

*prakṛteḥ paramo'si tvaṃ yadi satyaṃ vacastava \|*  
*tarhi tvayā na bhetavyaṃ samīpe mama śaṃkara \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. If you are really superior to Prakṛti, if what you say is true, you need not be afraid to be near me, O Śiva.

## \|\| 4.13.22 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya vacastasyāḥ sāṃkhyaśāstroditaṃ śivaḥ \|*  
*vedāṃtamatasaṃstho hi vākyamūce śivāṃ prati \|\| 22 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

22\. On hearing these words of Pārvatī based on the Sāṃkhya system, Śiva replied to her, upholding the Vedāntin’s point of view.

## \|\| 4.13.23 \|\|

*śrīśiva uvāca \|*  
*ityevaṃ tvaṃ yadi brūṣe girije sāṃkhyadhāriṇī \|*  
*pratyahaṃ kuru me sevāmaniṣiddhāṃ subhāṣiṇi \|\| 23 \|\|*

Lord Śiva said:—

23\. O Pārvatī, O upholder of the Sāṃkhya system, if you say so, O sweet-voiced lady, you render me unforbidden service every day.

## \|\| 4.13.24 \|\|

*yadyahaṃ brahma nirlipto māyayā parameśvaraḥ \|*  
*vedāṃtavedyo māyeśastvaṃ kariṣyasi kiṃ tadā \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. If I am the Brahman, the supreme lord, unsullied by illusion, comprehensible through spiritual knowledge and the master of illusion what will you do then?

## \|\| 4.13.25 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*ityevamuktvā girijāṃ vākyamūce giriṃ prabhuḥ \|*  
*bhaktānuraṃjanakaro bhaktānugrahakārakaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

25\. Having spoken to Pārvatī thus, the lord, the conciliator and the blesser of the devotees spoke to the mountain thus.

## \|\| 4.13.26 \|\|

*śiva uvāca \|*  
*atraiva so'haṃ tapasā pareṇa gire tava prasthavare'tiramye \|*  
*carāmi bhūmau paramārthabhāvasvarūpamānaṃdamayaṃ sulocayan \|\| 26 \|\|*

Śiva said:—

26\. O lord of mountains, here itself on your beautiful excellent ridge, I shall perform my penance showing to the world my real blissful form and nature.

## \|\| 4.13.27 \|\|

*tapastaptumanujñā me dātavyā parvatādhipa \|*  
*anujñayā vinā kiṃcittapaḥ kartuṃ na śakyate \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. O lord of mountains, permission shall be given to me to perform penance. Without your permission it is not possible for me (or any one else) to perform any penance here.

## \|\| 4.13.28 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*etacchrutvā vacastasya devadevasya śūlinaḥ \|*  
*praṇamya himavāñchaṃbhumidaṃ vacanamabravīt \|\| 28 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

28\. On hearing these words of Śiva, the lord of gods, Himavat bowed to Śiva and said.

## \|\| 4.13.29 \|\|

*himavānuvāca \|*  
*tvadīyaṃ hi jagatsarvaṃ sadevāsuramānuṣam \|*  
*kimapyahaṃ mahādeva tuccho bhūtvā vadāmi te \|\| 29 \|\|*

Himavat said:—

29\. The entire universe consisting of gods, Asuras and human beings, is yours. O great god, though insignificant, I blabber something to you.

## \|\| 4.13.30 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*evamukto himavatā śaṃkaro lokaśaṃkaraḥ \|*  
*vihasya girirājaṃ taṃ prāha yāhīti sādaram \|\| 30 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

30\. Thus addressed by Himavat, Śiva, the benefactor of the worlds, laughingly permitted him to go.

## \|\| 4.13.31 \|\|

*śaṃkareṇābhyanujñātassvagṛhaṃ himavānyayau \|*  
*sārddhaṃ girijayā vai sa pratyahaṃ darśane sthitaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Permitted by Śiva, Himavat returned to his abode along with Pārvatī. He wanted to visit Him daily.

## \|\| 4.13.32 \|\|

*pitrā vināpi sā kālī sakhībhyāṃ saha nityaśaḥ \|*  
*jagāma śaṃkarābhyāśaṃ sevāyai bhaktitatparā \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Even without her father but accompanied by her maids, Pārvatī approached Śiva everyday for serving Him with devotion.

## \|\| 4.13.33 \|\|

*niṣiṣedha na tāṃ ko'pi gaṇo naṃdīśvarādikaḥ \|*  
*maheśaśāsanāttāta tacchāsanakaraśśuciḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. O dear, at the bidding of lord Śiva, none of the Gaṇas, Nandīśvara and others, purely carrying out the orders of Śiva, prevented her.

## \|\| 4.13.34 \|\|

*sāṃkhyavedāṃtamatayośśivayośśi vadassadā \|*  
*saṃvādaḥ sukhakṛccokto'bhinnayossuvicārataḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. The discourse of Śivā and Śiva who represented the principles of Sāṃkhya and Vedanta and who, if thoughtfully considered, are not different from each other, was very happy and pleasing for ever.

## \|\| 4.13.35 \|\|

*girirājasya vacanāttanayāṃ tasya śaṃkaraḥ \|*  
*pārśve samīpe jagrāha gauravādapi goparaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. At the request of the lord of mountains, Śiva permitted Pārvatī to remain with Him being true to His words though with all gravity and seriousness.

## \|\| 4.13.36 \|\|

*uvācedaṃ vacaḥ kālīṃ sakhībhyāṃ saha gopatiḥ \|*  
*nityaṃ māṃ sevatāṃ yātu nirbhītā hyatra tiṣṭhatu \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. He, the lord of individual souls, said to Pārvatī in the company of her maids—“You can serve me everyday You can go (as you please). You can stay here fearlessly.”

## \|\| 4.13.37 \|\|

*evamuktvā tu tāṃ devīṃ sevāyai jagṛhe haraḥ \|*  
*nirvikāro mahāyogī nānālīlākaraḥ prabhuḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Saying this, He accepted the goddess in his service. Śiva is free from aberrations. He is a great Yogin, the lord who indulges in different kinds of divine sports.

## \|\| 4.13.38 \|\|

*idameva mahaddhairyyaṃ dhīrāṇāṃ sutapasvinām \|*  
*vighravantyapi saṃprāpya yadvighnairna vihanyate \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. This is the supreme courage of great ascetics possessed of fortitude that though surrounded by obstacles they are not overpowered by them.

## \|\| 4.13.39 \|\|

*tataḥ svapuramāyāto girirāṭ paricārakaiḥ \|*  
*mumodātīva manasi sapriyassa munīśvara \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Then, the lord of mountains, returned to his city and rejoiced in the company of his wife, the sages and attendants.

## \|\| 4.13.40 \|\|

*haraśca dhyānayogena paramātmānamādarāt \|*  
*nirvighnena svamanasā tvāsīcciṃtayituṃ sthitaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Śiva mentioned the Yoga of meditation on the great Ātman with His mind freed from obstacles.

## \|\| 4.13.41 \|\|

*kālī sakhībhyāṃ sahitā pratyahaṃ caṃdraśekharam \|*  
*sevamānā mahādevaṃ gamanāgamane sthitā \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Pārvatī, along with her maids, continued her daily service to the moon-crested lord, coming and going without any hindrance.

## \|\| 4.13.42 \|\|

*prakṣālya caraṇau śaṃbhoḥ papau taccaraṇodakam \|*  
*vahniśaucaina vastreṇa cakre tadgātramārjanam \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. She washed Śiva’s feet and drank that holy water. With a cloth heated in fire she wiped his body.

## \|\| 4.13.43 \|\|

*ṣoḍaśenopacāreṇa saṃpūjya vidhivaddharam \|*  
*punaḥpunaḥ supraṇamya yayau nityaṃ piturgṛham \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. After worshipping Him with sixteen types of offerings duly, and bowing to Him repeatedly she used to return to her father’s abode.

## \|\| 4.13.44 \|\|

*evaṃ saṃsevamānāyāṃ śaṃkaraṃ dhyānatatparam \|*  
*vyatīyāya mahānkālaśśivāyā munisattama \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. O excellent sage, a long time elapsed as she continued her service to Him who was engrossed in meditation.

## \|\| 4.13.45 \|\|

*kadācitsahitā kālī sakhībhyāṃ śaṃkarāśrame \|*  
*vitene suṃdaraṃ gānaṃ sutālaṃ smaravarddhanam \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Sometimes accompanied by her maids, she sang exquisite songs of good note that increased love in the hermitage of Siva.

## \|\| 4.13.46 \|\|

*kadācitkuśapuṣpāṇi samidhaṃ nayati svayam \|*  
*sakhībhyāṃ sthānasaṃskāraṃ kurvatī nyavasattadā \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Sometimes she brought Kuśa grass, flowers and sacrificial twigs. Sometimes, assisted by her maids, she scubbed (scrubbed?) and cleaned the place.

## \|\| 4.13.47 \|\|

*kadācinniyatā gehe sthitā candrabhṛto bhrṛśam \|*  
*vīkṣaṃtī vismayāmāsa sakāmā candraśekharam \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Sometimes she stayed in the house of the moon-crescent lord, pure and holy. Sometimes she used to gaze at the lord lovingly and with surprise.

## \|\| 4.13.48-49 \|\|

*tatastaptena bhūteśastāṃ nissaṃgāṃ paristhitām \|*  
*so'ciṃtayattadā vīkṣya bhūtadehe sthiteti ca \|\| 48 \|\|*

*nāgrahīdgiriśaḥ kālīṃ bhāryārthe nikaṭe sthitām \|*  
*mahālāvaṇyanicayāṃ munīnāmapi mohinīm \|\| 49 \|\|*

48-49 In the course of his penance sometimes the lord of the goblins thought about her as free from attachment. But as she was in her physical form He did not take her as His wife though she was near Him, though she was endowed with every feature of beauty, though she was capable of deluding even the sages.

## \|\| 4.13.50 \|\|

*mahādevaḥ punardṛṣṭvā tathā tāṃ saṃyatedriyām \|*  
*svasevane ratāṃ nityaṃ sadayassamaciṃtayat \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. On seeing her with perfect control over her sense-organs and engrossed in serving Him always, the lord mercifully thought.

## \|\| 4.13.51 \|\|

*yadaivaiṣā tapaścaryāvrataṃ kālī kariṣyati \|*  
*tadā ca tāṃ grahīṣyāmi garvabījavivarjitām \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. “I shall take her only when the last seed of ego goes away from her; when she herself performs a penance.”

## \|\| 4.13.52 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*iti saṃcintya bhūteśo drutaṃ dhyānasamāśritaḥ \|*  
*mahayogīśvaro'bhūdvai mahālīlākaraḥ prabhuḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Thinking thus, the lord of the Bhūtas reverted to meditation. The lord who could indulge in great sports became a great Yogin.

## \|\| 4.13.53 \|\|

*dhyānāsaktasya tasyātha śivasya paramātmanaḥ \|*  
*hṛdi nāsīnmune kācidanyā ciṃtā vyavasthitā \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. O sage, when Śiva, the great Ātman, sank into meditation, no other thought entered His mind.

## \|\| 4.13.54 \|\|

*kālī tvanudinaṃ śaṃbhuṃ sadbhaktyā samasevata \|*  
*viciṃtayaṃtī satataṃ tasya rūpaṃ mahātmanaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. As for Pārvatī, she served Him everyday with great devotion, always thinking on the form of that Great Soul.

## \|\| 4.13.55 \|\|

*haro dhyānaparaḥ kālīṃ nityaṃ praikṣata susthitam \|*  
*vismṛtya pūrvaciṃtāṃ tāṃ paśyannapi na paśyati \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Śiva who was engrossed in meditation saw her every day in full composure. Forgetting His previous thoughts about her, He did not see her although He saw her.

## \|\| 4.13.56 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare devāśśakrādyā munayaśca te \|*  
*brahmājñayā smaraṃ tatra preṣayāmāsurādarāt \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. In the mean time Indra, other gods and the sages eagerly sent Kāma there at the bidding of Brahmā.

## \|\| 4.13.57 \|\|

*tena kārayituṃ yogaṃ kālyā rudreṇa kāmataḥ \|*  
*mahāvīryeṇāsureṇa tārakeṇa prapīḍitāḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. They had been harassed by the demon Tāraka. the demon of great strength. Hence they wanted to unite Pārvatī and Śiva in love.

## \|\| 4.13.58 \|\|

*gatvā tatra smarassarvamupāyamakaronnijam \|*  
*cukṣubhe na haraḥ kiñcittaṃ ca bhasmīcakāra ha \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. After reaching there Kāma tried all his tricks but Śiva was not at all agitated. He reduced Kāma to ashes.

## \|\| 4.13.59 \|\|

*pārvatyapi vigarvābhūnmune tasya nideśataḥ \|*  
*tatastapo mahatkṛtvā śivaṃ prāpa patiṃ satī \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. O sage, Pārvatī too was divested of her ego. At his bidding she performed a penance and obtained Him as her husband.

## \|\| 4.13.60 \|\|

*babhūvatustau suprītau pārvatīparameśvarau \|*  
*cakraturdevakāryyaṃ hi paropakaraṇe ratau \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Pārvatī and Śiva were very happy. Engrossed in helping others they carried out the work of the gods.

## Chapter 14 - The Birth of Tāraka and Vajrāṅga and their Penance

## \|\| 4.14.1 \|\|

*\|\| nārada uvāca \|*  
*viṣṇuśiṣya mahāśaiva samyaguktaṃ tvayā vidhe \|*  
*caritaṃ paramaṃ hyetacchivāyāśca śivasya ca \|\| 1 \|\|*

Nārada said:—

1\. O Brahmā, great devotee of Śiva and disciple of Viṣṇu, this great story of Śivā and Śiva has been narrated very well by you.

## \|\| 4.14.2 \|\|

*kastārakāsuro brahmanyena devāḥ prapīḍitāḥ \|*  
*kasya putrasya vai brūhi tatkathāṃ ca śivāśrayām \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Who was this Tāraka demon, O Brahmā, by whom the gods were harassed. Whose son was he? Narrate his story with reference to Śiva.

## \|\| 4.14.3 \|\|

*bhasmī cakāra sa kathaṃ śaṃkaraśca smaraṃ vaśī \|*  
*tadapi brūhi suprītyādbhutaṃ taccaritaṃ vibhoḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. How did Śiva of full control reduce Kāma to ashes? Please narrate that too with pleasure. The story of the lord is indeed wonderful.

## \|\| 4.14.4 \|\|

*kathaṃ śivā tapo'tyugraṃ cakāra sukhahetave \|*  
*kathaṃ prāpa patiṃ śaṃbhumādiśaktirjagatparā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. How did Śivā perform the severe penance for the sake of happiness? How did the primordial energy who is greater than the universe secure Śiva as her husband?

## \|\| 4.14.5 \|\|

*etatsarvamaśeṣeṇa viśeṣeṇa mahābudha \|*  
*brūhi me śraddadhānāya svaputrāya śivātmane \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. O great scholar, narrate all these complete in every detail to me, your son, who has dedicated his soul to Śiva and who has developed full faith in Him.

## \|\| 4.14.6 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|\| putravarya mahāprājña surarṣe śaṃsitavrataḥ \|*  
*vacmyahaṃ śaṃkaraṃ smṛtvā sarvaṃ taccaritaṃ śṛṇu \|\| 6 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

6\. O celestial sage, of great intellect, O foremost of my sons, whose sacred rites are laudable, I explain the entire story after thinking on Śiva. Listen.

## \|\| 4.14.7 \|\|

*prathamaṃ tārakasyaiva bhavaṃ saṃśṛṇu nārada \|*  
*yadvadhārthaṃ mahā yatnaḥ kṛto daivaiśśivāśrayaiḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. O Nārada, first of all, you hear the birth of Tāraka himself, to secure whose death great effort was made by the gods depending on Śiva.

## \|\| 4.14.8 \|\|

*mama putro marīciryaḥ kaśyapastasya cātmajaḥ \|*  
*trayodaśamitāstasya striyo dakṣasutāśca yāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. My son Marīci begot Kaśyapa who married thirteen daughters of Dakṣa.

## \|\| 4.14.9 \|\|

*ditirjyeṣṭhā ca tatstrī hi suṣuve sā sutadvayam \|*  
*hiraṇyakaśipurjyeṣṭho hiraṇyākṣo'nujastataḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The eldest of them Diti bore two sons: Hiraṇyakaśipu the elder and Hiraṇyākṣa the younger.

## \|\| 4.14.10 \|\|

*tau hatau viṣṇunā daityau nṛsiṃhakroḍarūpataḥ \|*  
*suduḥkhadau tato devāḥ sukhamāpuśca nirbhayāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. When these two began to harass the gods, Viṣṇu assumed the forms of Man-lion and Boar and killed them. Then the gods became fearless and happy.

## \|\| 4.14.11 \|\|

*ditiśca duḥkhitāsītsā kaśyapaṃ śaraṇaṃ gatā \|*  
*punassaṃsevya taṃ bhaktyā garbhamādhatta suvratā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The distressed Diti sought refuge in Kaśyapa and and serving him with devotion and observing the sacred rites she conceived.

## \|\| 4.14.12 \|\|

*tadvijñāya maheṃdro'pi labdhacchidro mahodyamī \|*  
*tadgarbhaṃ vyacchinattatra praviśya pavinā muhuḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. On coming to know of it, Indra entered her womb forcibly and cut it off many a time with his thunderbolt.

## \|\| 4.14.13 \|\|

*tadvratasya prabhāveṇa na tadgarbho mamāra ha \|*  
*svapaṃtyā daivayogena sapta saptābhavansutāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. By the power of her sacred rites, the child in the womb did not die as she was sleeping at that time, by a stroke of good luck. They were cut into seven pieces and so she had seven sons.

## \|\| 4.14.14 \|\|

*devā āsansutāste ca nāmato maruto'khilāḥ \|*  
*svargaṃ yayustadendreṇa devarājātmasātkṛtāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. These sons became gods by the name of Maruts. They all went to heaven along with Indra and were taken as his own attendants by the king of gods.

## \|\| 4.14.15 \|\|

*punarditiḥ patiṃ bheje'nutaptā nijakarmataḥ \|*  
*cakāra suprasannaṃ taṃ muniṃ paramasevayā ' \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Diti resorted again to her husband repenting for her action. She made the sage pleased by means of great service.

## \|\| 4.14.16 \|\|

*\|\| kaśyapa uvāca \|*  
*tapaḥ kuru śucirbhūtvā brahmaṇaścāyutaṃ samāḥ \|*  
*cedbhaviṣyati tatpūrvaṃ bhavitā te sutastadā \|\| 16 \|\|*

Kaśyapa said:—

16\. Be pure and perform penance for ten thousand years of Brahmā. When it is completed you will have a son.

## \|\| 4.14.17 \|\|

*tathā dityā kṛtaṃ pūrṇaṃ tattapaśśraddhayā mune \|*  
*tataḥ patyuḥ prāpya garbhaṃ suṣuve tādṛśaṃ sutam \|\| 17 \|\|*

(? Brahmā said:—)

17\. O sage, the penance was completed by Diti who performed it with faith. Thereafter from him she conceived and delivered of a son.

## \|\| 4.14.18 \|\|

*vajāṃganāmā so'bhūdvai ditiputro'maropamaḥ \|*  
*nāmatulyatanurvīrassupratāpyudbhavādbalī \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. That son of Diti named Vajrāṅga (of adamantine limbs) was on a par with the gods. Befitting his name, his body was strong and powerful even from his very birth.

## \|\| 4.14.19 \|\|

*jananīśāsanātsadyassa suto nirjarādhipam \|*  
*balāddhṛtvā dadau daṃḍaṃ vividhaṃ nirjarānapi \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. At the bidding of his mother, he immediately abducted Indra, the lord of gods, the other gods and punished them in various ways.

## \|\| 4.14.20 \|\|

*ditissukhamatīvāpa dṛṣṭvā śakrādidurdaśām \|*  
*amarā api śakrādyā jagmurduḥkhaṃ svakarmataḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Seeing the distress of Indra and others, Diti became very happy. Indra and other gods became miserable due to their own actions.

## \|\| 4.14.21 \|\|

*tadāhaṃ kaśyapenāśu tatrāgatya susāmagīḥ \|*  
*devānatyājayaṃstasmātsadā devahite rataḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Always engaged in the welfare of the gods, I went there accompanied by Kaśyapa. Employing gentle and peaceful words I got the gods released.

## \|\| 4.14.22 \|\|

*devānmuktvā sa vajrāṃgastataḥ provāca sādaram \|*  
*śivabhakto'tiśuddhātmā nirvikāraḥ prasannadhīḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Releasing the gods with respect, Vajrāṅga, a great devotee of Śiva, was delighted in his heart, and he of pure soul, without any aberration, spoke.

## \|\| 4.14.23 \|\|

*\|\| vajrāṃga uvāca \|*  
*iṃdro duṣṭaḥ prajāghātī māturme svārthasādhakaḥ \|*  
*sa phalaṃ prāptavānadya svarājyaṃ hi karotu saḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

Vajrāṅga said:—

23\. In order to achieve his interest, Indra killed the foetus of my mother. He has now tasted the fruit thereof. Well may he rule over his kingdom.

## \|\| 4.14.24 \|\|

*māturājñāvaśādbrahmankṛtametanmayākhilam \|*  
*na me bhogābhilāṣo vai kasyaci dbhuvanasya hi \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. O Brahmā, I did this only at the bidding of my mother. I have no desire for the enjoyments of any one of the worlds.

## \|\| 4.14.25 \|\|

*tattvasāraṃ vidhe sūta mahyaṃ vedavidāmvara \|*  
*yena syāṃ susukhī nityaṃ nirvikāraḥ prasannadhīḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. O Brahmā, foremost of those who know the Vedas, tell me the essence of real philosophy whereby I can ever remain happy, pleased in heart and free from aberrations.

## \|\| 4.14.26 \|\|

*tacchrutvāhaṃ mune'vocaṃ sāttviko bhāva ucyata \|*  
*tattvasāra iti prītyā sṛjāmyekāṃ varāṃ striyam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. On hearing that, O sage, I said—“Sāttvika feelings constitute the essence of real philosophy. I shall lovingly create an exquisite lady.”

## \|\| 4.14.27 \|\|

*varāṃgīṃ nāma tāṃ dattvā tasmai ditisutāya vai \|*  
*ayāṃ svadhāma suprītaḥ kaśyapastatpitāpi ca \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. After offering her who was named Varāṅgī, to that son of Diti, I went to my abode in great delight. So also Kaśyapa, his father.

## \|\| 4.14.28 \|\|

*tato daityasya vajrāṃgassātvikaṃ bhāvamāśritaḥ \|*  
*āsuraṃ bhāvamutsṛjya nirvairassukhamāptavān \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Thereafter the demon eschewed his diabolical feelings and resorted to sublime thoughts. Since he was free from fiendish feelings he became happy.

## \|\| 4.14.29 \|\|

*na babhūva varāṃgyā hi hṛdi bhāvotha sātvikaḥ \|*  
*sakāmā svapatiṃ bheje śraddhayā vividhaṃ satī \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. But no sublime feeling entered in the heart of Varāṅgī. With chastity and faith she served her husband lovingly in diverse ways.

## \|\| 4.14.30 \|\|

*atha tatsevanādāśu saṃtuṣṭo'bhūnmahāprabhuḥ \|*  
*sa vajrāṃgaḥ patistasyā uvāca vacanaṃ tadā \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Her husband Vajrāṅga of great lordly status was glad very soon on account of her service. He then spoke thus:—

## \|\| 4.14.31 \|\|

*vajrāṃga uvāca \|*  
*kimicchasi priye brūhi kiṃ te manasi vartate \|*  
*tacchutvānamya taṃ prāha sā patiṃ svamanoratham \|\| 31 \|\|*

Vajrāṅga said:—

31\. O beloved, what do you wish? What is it that you cherish in your mind? On hearing that, she bowed to her husband and revealed her desire.

## \|\| 4.14.32 \|\|

*varāṃgyuvāca \|*  
*cet prasanno'bhavastvaṃ vai sutaṃ me dehi satpate \|*  
*mahābalaṃ trilokasya jetāraṃ hariduḥkhadam \|\| 32 \|\|*

Varāṅgī said:—

32\. “O my good husband, if you are so pleased grant me a powerful son who will conquer three worlds and cause misery to Viṣṇu.”

## \|\| 4.14.33 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*iti śrutvā priyāvākyaṃ vismito'bhūtsa ākulaḥ \|*  
*uvāca hṛdi sa jñānī sātviko vairavarjitaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

33\. On hearing the words of his beloved, he was disagreeably surprised and vexed. He was free from inimical thoughts. With perfect wisdom and Sāttvika feelings in his heart he said:—

## \|\| 4.14.34 \|\|

*priyecchati virodhaṃ vai surairme na hi rocate \|*  
*kiṃ kuryāṃ hi kva gaccheyaṃ kathaṃ naśye na me paṇaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. My beloved wishes enmity with the gods. It does not appeal to me. What shall I do? Where shall I go? How can my vow be preserved from destruction?

## \|\| 4.14.35 \|\|

*priyāmanorathaścaiva pūrṇassyāttrijagadbhavet \|*  
*kleśayuṅnitarā bhūyo devāśca munayastathā \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. If my wife’s wishes are fulfilled, the three worlds will be much distressed, so too the gods and the sages.

## \|\| 4.14.36 \|\|

*na pūrṇassyātpriyākāmastadā me narako bhavet \|*  
*dvidhāpi dharmahānirvai bhavatītyanuśuśruvān \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. If my beloved’s desires are not fulfilled, I am sure to be cast into hell. In either case righteousness will be lost. This is what we have heard.

## \|\| 4.14.37 \|\|

*vajrāṃga itthaṃ babhrāma sa mune dharmasaṃkaṭe \|*  
*balābalaṃ dvayostatra viciciṃta ca buddhitaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. O sage, thus Vajrāṅga whirled a lot in a dilemma. Intelligently he considered the corresponding strength and weakness of both the alternatives.

## \|\| 4.14.38 \|\|

*śivecchayā sa hi mune vākyaṃ mene striyo budhaḥ \|*  
*tathāstviti vacaḥ prāha priyāṃ prati sa daityarāṭ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. O sage, as willed by Śiva, though intelligent the king of demons agreed to the proposal. He told his wife “So be it.”

## \|\| 4.14.39 \|\|

*tadarthamakarottīvraṃ taponyadduṣkaraṃ sa tu \|*  
*māṃ samuddiśya suprītyā bahuvarṣaṃ jiteṃdriyaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. For that purpose he performed another very difficult penance with great zeal with me as the object of worship, for number of years.

## \|\| 4.14.40 \|\|

*varaṃ dātumagāṃ tasmai dṛṣṭvāhaṃ tattapo mahat \|*  
*varaṃ brūhi hyavocaṃ taṃ suprasannena cetasā \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. On seeing the great penance I went to him for granting the boon. With a delighted mind I told him “speak out the boon you wish to have.”

## \|\| 4.14.41 \|\|

*vajrāṃgastu tadā prītaṃ māṃ dṛṣṭvā sthitaṃ vibhum \|*  
*supraṇamya bahustutvā varaṃ vavre priyāhitam \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. On seeing me in the firmament in the pleasant mood he worshipped and eulogised me as well as craved for the boon as desired by his wife.

## \|\| 4.14.42 \|\|

*vajrāṃga uvāca \|*  
*sutaṃ dehi svamāturme mahāhitakaraṃ prabho \|*  
*mahābalaṃ supratāpaṃ susamarthaṃ taponidhim \|\| 42 \|\|*

Vajrāṅga said:—

42\. O lord, give me a son who will be carrying out what is beneficent to his mother, who will be strong, valorous and efficient, who will be a storehouse of penance.

## \|\| 4.14.43 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya ca tadvākyaṃ tathāstvityabravaṃ mune \|*  
*ayā svadhāma taddattvā vimanāssasmaracchivam \|\| 43 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

43\. On hearing his words, O sage, I said “So be it.” After granting the boon I returned to my abode thinking on Śiva, though a bit distressed.

## Chapter 15 - The penance and reign of Tārakāsura

## \|\| 4.15.1 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*atha sā garbhamādhatta varāṃgī tatpurādarāt \|*  
*sa vavarddhābhyaṃtare hi bahuvarṣaiḥ sutejasā \|\| 1 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

1\. Then that Varāṅgī. devoted to him, conceived. The child within her body developed in many years with its brilliance.

## \|\| 4.15.2 \|\|

*tataḥ sā samaye pūrṇe varāṃgī suṣuve sutam \|*  
*mahākāyaṃ mahāvīryaṃ prajvalaṃtaṃ diśo daśa \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. That Varāṅgī, when the time was complete, delivered of a son of huge body and great strength dazzling the ten quarters.

## \|\| 4.15.3 \|\|

*tadaiva ca mahotpātā babhūvurduḥkhahetavaḥ \|*  
*jāyamāne sute tasminvarāṃgyātsukhaduḥkhade \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. At the same time, several phenomena of evil portent forboding misery and distress happened, when the son of Varāṅgī was born making the gods miserable.

## \|\| 4.15.4 \|\|

*divi bhuvyaṃtarikṣe ca sarvalokabhayaṃkarāḥ \|*  
*anarthasūcakāstāta trividhāstānbravīmyaham \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. O dear, the phenomena of three varieties indicating great calamity and terrifying the worlds occurred in the sky, heaven and earth. I shall narrate them.

## \|\| 4.15.5 \|\|

*solkāścāśanayaḥ peturmahāśabdā bhayaṃkarāḥ \|*  
*udayaṃ cakrurutkṛṣṭāḥ ketavo duḥkhadāyakāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. With a terrifying noise, thunderbolts fell along with comets; shooting meteors rose up, making the world miserable.

## \|\| 4.15.6 \|\|

*cacāla vasudhā sādrirjajvalussakalā diśaḥ \|*  
*cukṣubhussaritassarvāḥ sāgarāśca viśeṣataḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The earth with all the mountains quaked; the quarters blazed; the rivers and oceans were particularly agitated.

## \|\| 4.15.7 \|\|

*hūtkarānīrayandhīrānkharasparśo marudvavau \|*  
*unmūlayanmahāvṛkṣānvātyānīkorajodhvajaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The rough wind blew with a hissing noise. Gusts of wind with troops of tempests and dust for banner uprooted several trees.

## \|\| 4.15.8 \|\|

*sarāhvossūryyavidhvostu muhuḥ paridhayo'bhavan \|*  
*mahābhayasya viprendra sūcakāssukhahārakaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. O great brahmin, the misty haloes around the sun and the moon in the grip of Rāhu became the harbingers of great fear and unhappiness.

## \|\| 4.15.9 \|\|

*mahīdhravivarebhyaśca nirghātā bhayasūcakāḥ \|*  
*rathanirhrādatulyāśca jajñire'vasare tataḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9 At that time terrifying sounds that resembled those of the chariot issued forth from cracks and crevices in the mountains.

## \|\| 4.15.10 \|\|

*sṛgālolūkaṭaṃkārairvamantyo mukhato'nalam \|*  
*aṃtargrāmeṣu vikaṭaṃ praṇeduraśivāśśivāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Within villages, inauspicious vixens howled hideously vomitting fires; as it were, through their mouths along with the hissing and twanging sounds of the hootings and howlings of owls and jackals.

## \|\| 4.15.11 \|\|

*yatastato grāmasiṃhā unnamayya śirodharām \|*  
*saṃgītavadrodanavadvyamucanvividhānravān \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Lifting up their necks, the dogs barked in diverse ways producing sounds of singing or lamenting here and there.

## \|\| 4.15.12 \|\|

*khārkārarabhasā mattāḥ surairghnaṃto rasāṃkharāḥ \|*  
*varūthaśastadā tāta paryadhāvannitastataḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. O dear, groups of mad asses ran here and there braying loudly and digging the ground with their hoofs.

## \|\| 4.15.13 \|\|

*khagā udapatannīḍādrāsabhatrastamānasaḥ \|*  
*krośaṃto vyagracittāśca sthitamāpurna kutracit \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Terrified by the asses, birds flew up from their nests. In their excitement and flutter they honked and cronked. They did not find a peaceful perch anywhere.

## \|\| 4.15.14 \|\|

*śakṛnmūtramakārṣuśca goṣṭhe'raṇye bhayākulaḥ \|*  
*babhramuḥ sthitimāpurno paśavastāḍitā iva \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Beasts in sheds and forests roamed here and there in great fright as though beaten and driven about, passing urine and shitting dungs as they pleased.

## \|\| 4.15.15 \|\|

*gāvo'trasannasṛgdohā vāṣpanetrā bhayākulāḥ \|*  
*toyadā abhavaṃstatra bhayadāḥ pūyavarṣiṇaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Frightened cows sprayed blood through their udders; their eyes brimmed with tears, clouds showering putrid matter became terrifying.

## \|\| 4.15.16 \|\|

*vyarudanpratimāstatra devānāmutpatiṣṇavaḥ \|*  
*vinā'nilaṃ drumāḥ peturgrahayuddhaṃ babhūva khe \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Idols and images of deities appeared to cry and fly up. Even when there was no gale, trees fell down. Planets in the sky clashed with one another.

## \|\| 4.15.17 \|\|

*ityādikā bahūtpātā jajñire munisattama \|*  
*ajñānino janāstatra menire viśvasaṃplavam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. O excellent sage, these and similar portending phenomena occurred: Ignorant persons thought the submersion of the whole universe was imminent.

## \|\| 4.15.18 \|\|

*atha prajāpatirnāmākarottasyāsurasya vai \|*  
*tāraketi vicāryaiva kaśyapo hi mahaujasaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Then Kaśyapa Prajāpati thought well and named the powerful demon Tāraka.

## \|\| 4.15.19 \|\|

*mahāvīrasya sahasā vyajyamānātmapauruṣaḥ \|*  
*vavṛdhetyaśmasāreṇa kāyenādripatiryathā \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. That heroic demon, with his manliness and valour manifesting quickly grew and developed with his steely frame like the lord of mountains.

## \|\| 4.15.20 \|\|

*atho sa tārako daityo mahābalaparākramaḥ \|*  
*tapaḥ kartuṃ jananyāścājñāṃ yayāce mahāmanāḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Then the demon Tāraka, of great strength and exploit, endowed with a lofty mind, requested permission of his mother for performing penance.

## \|\| 4.15.21 \|\|

*prāptājñaḥ sa mahāmāyī māyināmapi mohakaḥ \|*  
*sarvadevajayaṃ kartuṃ taporthaṃ mana ādadhe \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. The permission having been secured, that demon possessing great power of illusion and capable of deluding even experts in the magical art, thought of performing penance in order to conquer all the gods.

## \|\| 4.15.22 \|\|

*madhorvanamupāgamya gurvājñāpratipālakaḥ \|*  
*vidhimuddiśya vidhivattapastepe sudāruṇam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Strictly adhering to the directions of his elders and preceptors he went to the forest of Madhu and performed a severe penance duly, having Brahmā as his objective.

## \|\| 4.15.23 \|\|

*ūrddhvabāhuścaikapādo raviṃ paśyansa cakṣuṣā \|*  
*śatavarṣaṃ tapaścakre dṛḍhacitto dṛḍhavrataḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. For a hundred years he performed penance with his hands lifted up, standing on only one leg and gazing at the sun. With his mind steady and firm he observed all sacred rites.

## \|\| 4.15.24 \|\|

*aṃguṣṭhena bhuvaṃ spṛṣṭvā śata varṣaṃ ca tādṛśaḥ \|*  
*tepe tapo dṛḍhātmā sa tārako'surarāṭprabhuḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Then for a hundred years, the lord and king of Asuras, Tāraka performed the penance: stood steady touching the ground with the single big toe.

## \|\| 4.15.25 \|\|

*śatavarṣaṃ jalaṃ prāśnañcchatavarṣaṃ ca vāyubhuk \|*  
*śatavarṣa jale tiṣṭhañcchataṃ ca sthaṃḍile'tapat \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. For hundred years he performed penance by drinking only water; another hundred years by sustaining himself on air alone, another hundred years standing in water and another hundred years standing on dry land.

## \|\| 4.15.26 \|\|

*śatavarṣaṃ tathā cāgnau śatavarṣamadhomukhaḥ \|*  
*śatavarṣaṃ tu hastasya talena ca bhuvaṃ sthita \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. A hundred years he performed the penance amidst fires, a hundred years in a topsy-turvy position and a hundred years supported on the ground by the palms of his hands.

## \|\| 4.15.27 \|\|

*śatavarṣaṃ tu vṛkṣasya śākhāmālabya vai mune \|*  
*pādābhyāṃ śucidhūmaṃ hi pibaṃścādhomukhastathā \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. O sage, a hundred years he remained with his head down and feet up clinging fast to the branch of a tree and inhaling the pure smoke of the sacrificial fire.

## \|\| 4.15.28 \|\|

*evaṃ kaṣṭataraṃ tepe sutapassa tu daityarāṭ \|*  
*kāmamuddiśya vidhivacchṛṇvatāmapi dussaham \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Thus with ardour, the king of the demons performed the severe penance duly unbearable even to those who heard about it.

## \|\| 4.15.29 \|\|

*tatraivaṃ tapatastasya mahattejo vinissṛtam \|*  
*śirasassarvaṃsaṃsarpi mahopadravakṛnmune \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. O sage, in the process of such a penance, a huge mass of light shot up from his head and spread all round. It caused great havoc.

## \|\| 4.15.30 \|\|

*tenaiva devalokāste dagdhaprāyā babhūvire \|*  
*abhito duḥkhamāpannāssarve devarṣayo mune \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. All the worlds of the gods were well nigh consumed by it alone. O sage, all the celestial sages were hard hit and distressed.

## \|\| 4.15.31-32 \|\|

*iṃdraśca bhayamāpede 'dhikaṃ deveśvarastadā \|*  
*tapasyatyadya kaścidvai matpadaṃ dharṣayiṣyati \|\| 31 \|\|*

*akāṃḍe caiva brahmāṇḍaṃ saṃhariṣyatyayaṃ prabhu \|*  
*iti saṃśayamāpannā niścayaṃ nopalebhire \|\| 32 \|\|*

31-32. Indra, the lord of gods, was extremely terrified. He thought “Some one is performing a penance. Surely he will usurp my position. This master mind shall in a trice destroy the whole cosmos”. All those who entertained similar doubts could not decide what to do.

## \|\| 4.15.33 \|\|

*tatassarve susaṃmantrya mithaste nirjararṣayaḥ \|*  
*mallokamagamanbhītā dīnā māṃ samupasthitāḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Then all those gods and sages consulted one another and in their great fright they came to my world and approached me in a piteous plight.

## \|\| 4.15.34 \|\|

*māṃ praṇamya susaṃstūya sarve te kliṣṭacetasaḥ \|*  
*kṛtasvaṃjalayo mahyaṃ vṛttaṃ sarvaṃ nyavedayan \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Bowing to and eulogising me with palms joined in reverence, all of them explained everything to me distressed in mind that they were.

## \|\| 4.15.35 \|\|

*ahaṃ sarvaṃ suniścitya kāraṇaṃ tasya saddhiyā \|*  
*varaṃ dātuṃ gatastatra yatra tapyati so'suraḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Coming to a definite conclusion with adequate thought as to the reason for the same, I went where the demon was performing penance in order to grant him the boon.

## \|\| 4.15.36 \|\|

*avocaṃ vacanaṃ taṃ vai varaṃ brūhītyahaṃ mune \|*  
*tapastaptaṃ tvayā tīvraṃ nādeyaṃ vidyate tava \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. O sage, I told him thus—“Tell me what boon you want. A severe penance has been performed by you. There is nothing which cannot be granted to you”.

## \|\| 4.15.37 \|\|

*ityevaṃ madvacaḥ śrutvā tārakassa mahāsuraḥ \|*  
*māṃ praṇamya susaṃstūya varaṃ vavre'tidāruṇam \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. On hearing these words of mine, Tāraka, the great demon, bowed and eulogised me and requested for a terrible boon.

## \|\| 4.15.38 \|\|

*tāraka uvāca \|*  
*tvayi prasanne varade kimasādhyaṃ bhavenmama \|*  
*ato yāce varaṃ tvattaḥ śṛṇu tanme pitāmaha \|\| 38 \|\|*

Tāraka said:—

38\. “O Pitāmaha, if you are glad and ready to grant me the boon what is it that cannot be achieved by me? Hence I request you for this boon. Please listen.

## \|\| 4.15.39 \|\|

*yadi prasanno deveśa yadi deyo varo mama \|*  
*deyaṃ varadvayaṃ mahyaṃ kṛpāṃ kṛtvā mamopari \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. O lord of gods, if you are pleased and if a boon is to be given to me, be kind enough to grant me two boons.

## \|\| 4.15.40 \|\|

*tvayā ca nirmite loke sakale'sminmahāprabho \|*  
*mattulyo balavānnūnaṃ na bhavetko'pi vai pumān \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. O great lord, there should certainly be no man equal to me in strength in this entire universe created by you.

## \|\| 4.15.41 \|\|

*śivavīryasamutpannaḥ putrassenāpatiryadā \|*  
*bhūtvā śastraṃ kṣipenmahyaṃ tadā me maraṇaṃ bhavet \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. If a son born of Śiva becomes the commander-inchief of an army and discharges weapons against me, let my death occur then”.

## \|\| 4.15.42 \|\|

*ityukto'tha tadā tena daityenāhaṃ munīśvara \|*  
*varaṃ ca tādṛśaṃ dattvā svalokamagamaṃ drutam \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. O excellent sage, thus requested by that demon, I granted him two boons and hastened back to my abode.

## \|\| 4.15.43 \|\|

*daityo'pi sa varaṃ labdhvā manasepsitamuttamam \|*  
*suprasannotaro bhūtvā śoṇitākhyapuraṃ gataḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Securing the excellent boon in accordance with his cherished desire, the demon was very glad and went to the town Śoṇita.

## \|\| 4.15.44 \|\|

*abhiṣiktastadā rājye trailokyasyāsuraissaha \|*  
*śukreṇa daityaguruṇājñayā me sa mahāsuraḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. That great demon was crowned the king of the three worlds with the permission of Śukra, the preceptor of the demons.

## \|\| 4.15.45 \|\|

*tatastu sa mahādaityo'bhavastrailokyanāyakaḥ \|*  
*svājñāṃ pravartayāmāsa pīḍayansacarācaram \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Then the great demon became the leader of the three worlds. He inaugurated his commanding position by harassing the mobile and immobile beings.

## \|\| 4.15.46 \|\|

*rājyaṃ cakāra vidhivastrilokasya sa tārakaḥ \|*  
*prajāśca pālayāmāsa pīḍayannirjarādikān \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. He duly established his suzerainty over the three worlds. He protected his subjects but inflicted pain on the gods and others.

## \|\| 4.15.47 \|\|

*tatassa tārako daityasteṣāṃ ratnānyupādade \|*  
*iṃdrādilokapālānāṃ svato dattāni tadbhayāt \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Then the demon Tāraka seized gems and jewels of all the guardians of the quarters, Indra and others, offered under duress by them on being afraid of him.

## \|\| 4.15.48 \|\|

*iṃdreṇairāvatastasya bhayāttasmai samarpitaḥ \|*  
*kubereṇa tadā dattā nidhayo navasaṃkhyakā \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Afraid of him, Indra surrendered his Airāvata (white elephant) and Kubera all his nine treasures.

## \|\| 4.15.49 \|\|

*varuṇena hayāḥ śubhrā ṛṣibhiḥ kāmakṛttathā \|*  
*sūryeṇoccaiśśravā divyo bhayāttasmai samarpitaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. White horses were surrendered by Varuṇa, the wish-yielding cow Kāmadhenu by the sages, and the sun out of fear for him surrendered his divine horse Uccaiḥśravas.

## \|\| 4.15.50 \|\|

*yatra yatra śubhaṃ vastu dṛṣṭaṃ tenāsureṇa hi \|*  
*tattadgṛhītaṃ tarasā nissārastribhavo'bhavat \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Wherever a fine article was espied by the demon, he seized it immediately. The three worlds became void of all valuable things.

## \|\| 4.15.51 \|\|

*samudrāśca tathā ratnānyadustasmai bhayānmune \|*  
*akṛṣṭapacyāsītpṛthvī prajāḥ kāmadughāḥ khilāḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. O sage, the oceans the offered him their gems on account of fear. The entire earth became exuberant in productivity without being tilled and yielded what his subjects desired.

## \|\| 4.15.52 \|\|

*sūryaśca tapate tadvattadduḥkhaṃ na yathā bhavet \|*  
*caṃdrastu prabhayā dṛśyo vāyussarvānukūlavān \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. The sun glowed gently and mildly as not to make him distressed. The moon was always visible with his brilliant light and the wind blew always favouring him.

## \|\| 4.15.53 \|\|

*devānāṃ caiva yaddravyaṃ pitṝṇāṃ ca parasya ca \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ samupādattamasureṇa durātmanā \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Whatever riches the gods possessed or the manes or others had, were forfeited by the wicked demon.

## \|\| 4.15.54 \|\|

*vaśīkṛtya sa lokāṃstrīnsvayamiṃdro babhūva ha \|*  
*advitīyaḥ prabhuścāsīdrājyaṃ cakre'dbhutaṃ vaśī \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Bringing the three worlds under his control, he declared Indra himself. He became the undisputed lord and ruled over them with perfect self-control.

## \|\| 4.15.55 \|\|

*nissārya sakalāndevāndaityānasthāpayattataḥ \|*  
*svayaṃ niyojayāmāsa devayonissvakarmaṇi \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Dismissing the gods he installed demons in their places. Some gods he engaged in his personal service.

## \|\| 4.15.56 \|\|

*atha tadbādhitā devāssarve śakrapurogamāḥ \|*  
*mune māṃ śaraṇaṃ jagmuranāthā ativihvalāḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. O sage, the gods harassed by him, led by Indra, sought refuge in me. They were helpless and extremely agitated.

## Chapter 16 - Brahmā consoles the gods

## \|\| 4.16.1 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*atha te nirjarāssarve supraṇamya prajeśvaram \|*  
*tuṣṭuvuḥ parayā bhaktyā tārakeṇa prapīḍitāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Summary: Brahmā consoles the gods harassed and frightened by the demon Tāraka.

Brahmā said:—

1\. The gods terribly tormented by Tāraka, bowed to and eulogised me, the lord of subjects with great devotion.

## \|\| 4.16.2 \|\|

*ahaṃ śrutvāmaranutiṃ yathārthāṃ hṛdayaṃgamā \|*  
*suprasannataro bhūtvā pratyavocaṃ divaukasaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. On hearing the eulogy of the gods pleasing and true to facts I was highly pleased and replied to the heaven-dwellers thus.

## \|\| 4.16.3 \|\|

*svāgataṃ svādhikārā vai nirvighnāḥ saṃti vastutaḥ \|*  
*kimarthamāgatā yūyamatra sarve vadaṃtu me \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. O gods, welcome to you. I hope you are all fulfilling your duties without obstacles. Why have you all come here? Tell me.

## \|\| 4.16.4 \|\|

*iti śrutvā vaco me te natvā sarve divaukasaḥ \|*  
*māmūcurnatakā dīnāstārakeṇa prapīḍitāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. On hearing my words those gods bowed to me duly and spoke. Being tormented by Tāraka they were in a piteous plight.

## \|\| 4.16.5 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*lokeśa tārako daityo vareṇa tava darpita \|*  
*nirasyāsmānhaṭhātsthānānyagrahīnno balātsvayam \|\| 5 \|\|*

The gods said:—

5\. O lord of the worlds, thanks to the boon received from you. The demon Tāraka is very haughty. Driving us out with force he has taken possession of our positions.

## \|\| 4.16.6 \|\|

*bhavataḥ kimu na jñātaṃ duḥkhaṃ yannaḥ upasthitam \|*  
*tadduḥkhaṃ nāśaya kṣipraṃ vayaṃ te śaraṇaṃ gatāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Is it not known to you what misery has befallen us? Please dispel our misery quickly. We seek refuge in you.

## \|\| 4.16.7 \|\|

*aharniśaṃ bādhatesmānyatra tatrāsthitānsa vai \|*  
*palāyamānāḥ paśyāmo yatra tatrāpi tārakam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. He torments us wherever we happen to stay by day or at night. Wherever we flee we see Tāraka.

## \|\| 4.16.8 \|\|

*tārakānnaśca yadduḥkhaṃ saṃbhūtaṃ sakaleśvara \|*  
*tena sarve vayaṃ tāta pīḍitā vikalā ati \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. O dear, lord of all, we are extremely harassed and agitated due to Tāraka.

## \|\| 4.16.9 \|\|

*agniryamotha varuṇo nirṛtirvāyureva ca \|*  
*anye dikpatayaścāpi sarve yadvaśagāminaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Agni, Yama, Varuṇa, Nirṛti, Vāyu and other guardians of the deities are under his control.

## \|\| 4.16.10 \|\|

*sarve manuṣyadharmāṇassarveḥ parikarairyutāḥ \|*  
*sevaṃte taṃ mahādaityaṃ na svataṃtrāḥ kadācana \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. None of them is ever independent. All serve him in the manner of human beings accompanied by their followers.

## \|\| 4.16.11 \|\|

*evaṃ tenārditā devā vaśagāstasya sarvadā \|*  
*tadicchākāryyaniratāssarve tasyānujīvinaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Being harassed by him, the gods have become subservient of him. They are engaged in carrying out his wishes. All of us are his servants.

## \|\| 4.16.12 \|\|

*yāvatyo vanitāssarvā ye cāpyapsarasāṃ gaṇāḥ \|*  
*sarvāṃstānagrahīddaityastārako'sau mahābalī \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Our woman folk, the groups of heavenly nymphs have been captured by Tāraka, the powerful.

## \|\| 4.16.13 \|\|

*na yajñāssaṃpravartate na tapasyaṃti tāpasāḥ \|*  
*dānadharmādikaṃ kiṃcinna lokeṣu pravarttate \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. No sacrifice is in the making. No ascetic is in penances. The charitable and virtuous activities are being seldom pursued in the worlds.

## \|\| 4.16.14 \|\|

*tasya senāpatiḥ krauṃco mahāpāpyasti dānavaḥ \|*  
*sa pātālatalaṃ gatvā bādhate tvaniśaṃ prajāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. His commander-in-chief is a simple demon—Krauñca. He has now gone to the nether worlds and is harassing the people very much.

## \|\| 4.16.15 \|\|

*tena nastārakeṇedaṃ sakalaṃ bhuvanatrayam \|*  
*hṛtaṃ haṭhājjagaddhātaḥ pāpenākaruṇātmanā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The regions of our three worlds have been forcibly taken, O Brahamā (Brahmā?), by this Tāraka of sinful and ruthless temperament.

## \|\| 4.16.16 \|\|

*vayaṃ ca tatra yāsyāmo yatsthānaṃ tvaṃ vinirdiśeḥ \|*  
*svasthāstadvāritāstena lokanāthasurāriṇā \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. O lord of the worlds, we were in heaven but now that we have been turned out by that demon we shall go to any place which you may kindly suggest.

## \|\| 4.16.17 \|\|

*tvaṃ no gatiśca śāstā ca dhātā trātā tvameva hi \|*  
*vayaṃ sarve tārakākhyavahnau dagdhāssuvihvalāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. You are our final resort. You are our ruler, creator, and protector. But we are scorched in the fire of the name Tāraka. We are extremely agitated.

## \|\| 4.16.18 \|\|

*tena krūrā upāya naḥ sarve hatabalāḥ kṛtāḥ \|*  
*vikāre sāṃnipāte vā vīryavaṃtyauṣadhāni ca \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Our ruthless activities against him have turned out to be weak and ineffective, even as medicinal herbs of great potency are rendered ineffective in an ailment brought about by the combination of all deranged humours.

## \|\| 4.16.19 \|\|

*yatrāsmākaṃ jayāśā hi haricakre sudarśane \|*  
*utkuṃṭhitamabhūttasya kaṃṭhe puṣpamivārpitam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. We had some hope of victory in Sudarśana the discus of Viṣṇu. But even that discus has become ineffective in his neck where it has fallen as though it were a floral offering to a deity.

## \|\| 4.16.20 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityetadvacanaṃ śrutvā nirjarāṇāmahaṃ mune \|*  
*pratyavocaṃ surānsarvāṃstatkālasadṛśaṃ vacaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

20\. O sage, on hearing these words of the gods, I told them befitting the occasion.

## \|\| 4.16.21 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*mamaiva vacasā daityastārakākhyassamedhitaḥ \|*  
*na mattastasya hananaṃ yujyate hi divaukasaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. “O gods, the demon Tāraka has flourished, thanks to my words of blessings. His destruction through me does not seem proper.

## \|\| 4.16.22 \|\|

*tato naiva vadho yogyo yato vṛddhimupāgataḥ \|*  
*viṣa vṛkṣo'pi saṃvardhya svayaṃ chettumasāṃpratam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Improper is the destruction through that source wherefrom he has flourished. Even a poisonous tree tended and nurtured by one cannot be cut and felled down by oneself.24

## \|\| 4.16.23 \|\|

*yuṣmākaṃ cākhilaṃ kāryaṃ kartuṃ yogyo hi śaṃkaraḥ \|*  
*kintu svayaṃ na śakto hi pratikartuṃ praco ditaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Śiva is the most suitable agent to carry out your task. But I myself cannot do anything remedial in this case.

## \|\| 4.16.24 \|\|

*tārakākhyastu pāpena svayameṣyati saṃkṣayam \|*  
*yathā yūyaṃ saṃvidadhvamupadeśakarastvaham \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Tāraka will be destroyed by his own sin. How that shall be done you know from me. I shall advise you.

## \|\| 4.16.25 \|\|

*na mayā tārako vadhyo hariṇāpi hareṇa ca \|*  
*nānyenāpi surairvāpi madvarātsatyamucyate \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Thanks to the power of the boon granted by me. Tāraka cannot be killed by me or by Viṣṇu or by Śiva or by any one of the gods. It is true.

## \|\| 4.16.26 \|\|

*śivavīryyasamutpanno yadi syāttanayassurāḥ \|*  
*sa eva tārakākhyasya haṃtā daityasya nāparaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. O gods, if there is a son born of Śiva, he alone can kill the demon Tāraka.

## \|\| 4.16.27 \|\|

*yamupāyamahaṃ vacmi taṃ kurudhvaṃ surottamāḥ \|*  
*mahādevaprasādena siddhimeṣyati sa dhuvam \|\| 27 \|\|*

2 7. O best of gods, you carry out the remedy I am suggesting. By the grace of lord Śiva, it can be successfully accomplished.

## \|\| 4.16.28 \|\|

*satī dākṣā yiṇī pūrvaṃ tyaktadehā tu yābhavat \|*  
*sotpannā menakāgarbhātsā kathā viditā hi vaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Satī, the daughter of Dakṣa, formerly cast off her body. She is now born of Menakā’s womb. That event is already known to you all.

## \|\| 4.16.29 \|\|

*tasyā avaśyaṃ giriśaḥ kariṣyati kara graham \|*  
*tatkurudhvamupāyaṃ ca tathāpi tridivaukasaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. O gods, it is certain that lord Śiva will marry her. Still you shall pursue your endeavour.

## \|\| 4.16.30 \|\|

*tathā vidadhvaṃ sutarāṃ tasyāṃ tu pariyatnataḥ \|*  
*pārvatyāṃ menakājāyāṃ retaḥ pratinipātane \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Make such arrangements as to ensure the discharge of semen into Pārvatī, the daughter of Menakā.

## \|\| 4.16.31 \|\|

*tamūrddhvaretasaṃ śaṃbhuṃ saiva pracyutaretasam \|*  
*kartuṃ samarthā nānyāsti tathā kāpyabalā balāt \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Śiva is a great Yogin who can make semen flow upwards in the body. Only Pārvatī can make him discharge the semen downwards, out of the body. There is no other woman capable of it.

## \|\| 4.16.32 \|\|

*sā sutā girirājasya sāṃprataṃ prauḍhayauvanā \|*  
*tapasyate himagirau nityaṃ saṃsevate haram \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. That daughter of the lord of the mountains is now in her prime of youth. She is serving Śiva in his penance on the Himalayas.

## \|\| 4.16.33 \|\|

*vākyāddhimavataḥ kālīṃ svapiturhaṭhataśśivā \|*  
*sakhībhyāṃ sevate sārddhaṃ dhyānasthaṃ parameśvaram \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. As a result of the tenacious pleadings of her father, she is serving Him in meditation.

## \|\| 4.16.34 \|\|

*tāmagrato'rccamānāṃ vai trailokye varavarṇinīm \|*  
*dhyānasakto maheśo hi manasāpi na hīyate \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. She is the most beautiful lady in the three worlds. She stands in front of Him and worships Him. Still lord Śiva who is engrossed in His meditation is not distracted by her presence.

## \|\| 4.16.35 \|\|

*bhāryyāṃ samīheta yathā sa kālīṃ candraśekharaḥ \|*  
*tathā vidhadhvaṃ tridaśā na cirādeva yatnataḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. It is your duty to ascertain means to make Him desire Pārvatī for His wife. O gods, do something in that direction very quickly.

## \|\| 4.16.36 \|\|

*sthānaṃ gatvātha daityasya tamahaṃ tārakaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*nivārayiṣye kuhaṭhātsvasthānaṃ gacchatāmarāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. I shall go to the demon’s abode and try to dissuade him from his obstinacy. O gods, you can go to your abode

## \|\| 4.16.37 \|\|

*ityuktvāhaṃ surānśīghraṃ tārakākhyāsurasya vai \|*  
*upasaṃgamya suprītyā samābhāṣyedamabravam \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. After saying thus to the gods I hastened to the demon Tāraka. I addressed him thus.

## \|\| 4.16.38 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*tejosāramidaṃ svargaṃ rājyaṃ tvaṃ paripāsi naḥ \|*  
*yadarthaṃ sutapastaptaṃ vāñchasi tvaṃ tato'dhikam \|\| 38 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

38\. You are ruling over our heaven which contains the essence of all brilliance. You are desirous of getting more than what you bargained for at the time of your penance.

## \|\| 4.16.39 \|\|

*varaścāpyavaro datto na mayā svargarājyatā \|*  
*tasmātsvargaṃ parityajya kṣitau rājyaṃ samācara \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. I granted you a boon but not the kingdom of heaven. Hence leave off this region. You can rule over the earth.

## \|\| 4.16.40 \|\|

*devayogyāni tatraiva kāryyāṇi nikhilānyapi \|*  
*bhaviṣyatyarasuraśreṣṭha nātra kāryyā vicāraṇā \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. O best of Asuras, even there you can achieve the fruit of your activities as here in Devaloka. There is nothing to hesitate in this matter.

## \|\| 4.16.41 \|\|

*ityuktvāhaṃ ca saṃbodhyāsuraṃ taṃ sakaleśvaraḥ \|*  
*smṛtvā śivaṃ ca saśivaṃ tatrāṃtardhānamāgataḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. After thus exhorting the demon to leave off heaven I, the lord of all, remembered Śiva and Śivā and vanished from the scene.

## \|\| 4.16.42 \|\|

*tārako'pi parityajya svargaṃ kṣitimathābhyagāt \|*  
*śoṇitākhya pure sthitvā sarvarājyaṃ cakāra saḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Leaving the heaven, Tāraka descended to the earth. Stationed in the town Śoṇita, he ruled over the entire kingdom.

## \|\| 4.16.43 \|\|

*devāssarve'pi tacchutvā madvākyaṃ supraṇamya mām \|*  
*śakrasthānaṃ yayuḥ prītyā śakreṇa susa māhitāḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. On hearing my words, the gods bowed to me and went to Indra’s abode. They were duly received by Indra.

## \|\| 4.16.44 \|\|

*tatra gatvā militvā ca vicāryya ca parasparam \|*  
*te sarve marutaḥ prītyā maghavaṃtaṃ vaco'bruvan \|\| 44 \|\|*

44, After reaching there and consulting one another, the gods in a body lovingly told Indra.

## \|\| 4.16.45 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*śambhoryyathā śivāyāṃ vai rucijāyeta kāmataḥ \|*  
*maghavaṃste prakartavyaṃ brahmoktaṃ sarvameva tat \|\| 45 \|\|*

The gods said:—

45\. “O lord, you should carry out the suggestions of Brahmā and see that Śiva is lovingly inclined towards Śivā.

## \|\| 4.16.46 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityevaṃ sarvavṛttāṃtaṃ vinivedya sureśvaram \|*  
*jagmuste sarvato devāḥ svaṃ svaṃ sthānaṃ mudānvitāḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

46\. After explaining every thing to the lord, the gods went in all directions to their respective abodes with great pleasure.

## Chapter 17 - The dialogue between Indra and Kāmadeva

## \|\| 4.17.1 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*gateṣu teṣu deveṣu śakraḥ sasmāra vai smaram \|*  
*pīḍitastārakenātidetyena ca durātmanā \|\| 1 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

1\. When the gods had gone, Indra remembered Kama. He was so afflicted by Tāraka, the wicked demon.

## \|\| 4.17.2 \|\|

*āgatastatkṣaṇātkāmassavasaṃto ratipriyaḥ \|*  
*sāvalepo yuto ratyā trailokya vijayī prabhuḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. In an instant, Kāma, the lover of Rati, came there along with Vasanta. He was accompanied by Rati too. Being powerful enough to conquer the three worlds he was very haughty.

## \|\| 4.17.3 \|\|

*praṇāmaṃ ca tataḥ kṛtvā sthitvā tatpuratassmaraḥ \|*  
*mahonnatamanāstāta sāṃjaliśśakramabravīt \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Making due obeisance standing in front of Indra, the lofty-minded Kāma joined his palms in reverence and said:—

## \|\| 4.17.4 \|\|

*kāma uvāca \|*  
*kiṃ kāryyaṃ te samutpannaṃ smṛto'haṃ kena hetunā \|*  
*tattvaṃ kathaya deveśa tatkartuṃ samupāgataḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

Kāma said:—

4\. “What is the matter that has cropped up now? Wherefore was I remembered? Please tell me. I am here to carry it out”.

## \|\| 4.17.5 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*tacchrutvā vacanaṃ tasya kaṃdarpasya sureśvaraḥ \|*  
*uvāca vacanaṃ prītyā yuktaṃ yuktamiti stuvan \|\| 5 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

5\. On hearing the words of Kāma, Indra, the lord of the gods, said praising him lovingly saying “well done, very proper”.

## \|\| 4.17.6 \|\|

*\|\| śakra uvāca \|*  
*tava sādhu samārambho yanme kāryyamupasthitam \|*  
*tatkaturmudyato'si tvaṃ dhanyo'si makaradhvaja \|\| 6 \|\|*

Indra said:—

6\. O Kāma you are blessed indeed, since you are in readiness to carry out the affair I have on hand. You have begun well.

## \|\| 4.17.7 \|\|

*prastutaṃ śṛṇu madvākyaṃ kathayāmi tavāgrataḥ \|*  
*madīyaṃ caiva yatkāryaṃ tvadīyaṃ tanna cānyathā \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Listen to what is relevant to the context. I shall tell you everything. My job is equally your job and not otherwise.

## \|\| 4.17.8 \|\|

*mitrāṇi mama saṃtyeva bahūni sumahāṃti ca \|*  
*paraṃ tu smara sanmitraṃ tvattulyaṃ na hi kutracit \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. I have many friends and great friends at that. But, O Kāma, I have no other friend on a par with you anywhere.

## \|\| 4.17.9 \|\|

*jayārthaṃ me dvayaṃ tāta nirmitaṃ vajamuttamam \|*  
*vajraṃ ca niṣphalaṃ syādvai tvaṃ tu naiva kadācana \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. O dear, for my conquest, the unparallelled thunderbolt has been made. Even that weapon may sometimes be ineffective but you are never so.

## \|\| 4.17.10 \|\|

*yato hitaṃ prajāyeta tataḥ ko nu priyaḥ paraḥ \|*  
*tasmānmitravarastvaṃ hi matkāryyaṃ kartumarhasi \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Who can be dearer than the person from whom

one derives benefit? Hence you, my greatest friend, must carry out my task.

## \|\| 4.17.11 \|\|

*mama duḥkhaṃ samutpannamasādhya cāpi kālajam \|*  
*kenāpi naiva tacchakyaṃ dūrīkartuṃ tvayā vinā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Time being accursed, a great irremediable misery has befallen me. None other than you can dispel it.

## \|\| 4.17.12 \|\|

*dātuḥ parīkṣā durbhikṣe raṇe śūrasya jāyate \|*  
*āpatkāle tu mitrasyāśaktau strīṇāṃ kulasya hi \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The test of a donor is at the time of famine; the test of a warrior is at the time of battle; the test of a friend is at the time of adversity and the test of a woman is in the financial weakness of the family.

## \|\| 4.17.13 \|\|

*vinaye saṃkaṭe prāpte'vitathasya parokṣataḥ \|*  
*susnehasya tathā tāta nānyathā satyamīritam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. O dear, the test of a real friend is in the time of distress and is also based on what he does behind the back. It is not otherwise. This is truth.

## \|\| 4.17.14 \|\|

*prāptāyāṃ vai mamāpattāvavāryāyāṃ pareṇa hi \|*  
*parīkṣā ca tvadīyā'dya mitravarya bhaviṣyati \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Now that an adversity has befallen me, which cannot be thwarted by anyone else, O dear friend, it shall be a test for you today.

## \|\| 4.17.15 \|\|

*na kevalaṃ madīyaṃ ca kāryyamasti sukhāvaham \|*  
*kiṃ tu sarvasurādīnāṃ kāryyametanna saṃśayaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. This is not a matter that brings pleasure to me alone. This is a matter that concerns all the gods and others too.

## \|\| 4.17.16 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityetanmaghavadvākyaṃ śrutvā tu makaradhvajāḥ \|*  
*uvāca premagabhīraṃ vākyaṃ susmitapūrvakam \|\| 16 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

16\. On hearing these words of Indra the fish-bannered god Kāma spoke smilingly in words indicating love and gravity.

## \|\| 4.17.17 \|\|

*\|\| kāma uvāca \|*  
*kimarthamitthaṃ vadasi nottaraṃ vacmyahaṃ tava \|*  
*upakṛtkṛtrimaṃ loke dṛśyate kathyate na ca \|\| 17 \|\|*

Kāma said:—

17\. Why do you say like this? I make no answer to you. A helping unreal friend is neither seen nor spoken of in the world.

## \|\| 4.17.18 \|\|

*saṅkaṭe bahu yo brūte sa kiṃ kāryyaṃ kariṣyati \|*  
*tathāpi ca mahārāja kathayāmi śṛṇu prabho \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. He who speaks much at the time of adversity will not turn out much. Yet, O king, my lord, I shall say something. Please listen.

## \|\| 4.17.19 \|\|

*padaṃ te karṣituṃ yo vai tapastapati dāruṇam \|*  
*pātayiṣyāmyahaṃ taṃ ca śatruṃ te mitra sarvathā \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. O dear friend, I shall cause the downfall of that enemy of yours who is performing a severe penance to usurp your position.

## \|\| 4.17.20 \|\|

*kṣaṇena bhraṃśayiṣyāmi kaṭākṣeṇa varastriyāḥ \|*  
*devarṣidānavādīṃśca narāṇāṃ gaṇanā na me \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. I shall topple gods, sages, demons and others through the side-glances of a beautiful woman. I do not at all take human beings into consideration.

## \|\| 4.17.21 \|\|

*vajraṃ tiṣṭhatu dūre vai śastrāṇyanyānyanekaśaḥ \|*  
*kiṃ te kāryaṃ kariṣyaṃti mayi mitra upasthite \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Let your thunderbolt and other weapons of innumerable varieties be set aside. What will they do when I, your friend, am present?

## \|\| 4.17.22 \|\|

*brahmāṇaṃ vā hariṃ vāpi bhraṣṭaṃ kuryyāṃ na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*anyeṣāṃ gaṇanā nāsti pātayeyaṃ haraṃ tvapi \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. I can undoubtedly make Brahmā and Viṣṇu go astray. Others are of no consideration. I shall make even Śiva fall.

## \|\| 4.17.23 \|\|

*paṃcaiva mṛdavo bāṇāste ca puṣpamayā mama \|*  
*cāpastridhā puṣpamayaśśiṃjinī bhramarārjjitā \|*  
*balaṃ sudayitā me hi vasaṃtaḥ sacivassmṛtaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. I have only five arrows that are soft and flowery. My bow is of three types. That too is flowery. The bowstring consists of bees.

## \|\| 4.17.24 \|\|

*ahaṃ pañcabalodevā mitraṃ mama sudhānidhiḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. My support and strength is my beloved wife Ratī. Spring is my minister. O god, I am having five forces. The moon, the storehouse of nectar, is my friend.

## \|\| 4.17.25 \|\|

*senādhipaśca śṛṃgāro hāvabhāvāśca sainikāḥ \|*  
*sarve me mṛdavaḥ śakra ahaṃ cāpi tathāvidhaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The sentiment of love is my commander-in-chief. The coquettish gestures and emotions are my soldiers. All these are soft and gentle. O Indra, I too am of that sort.

## \|\| 4.17.26 \|\|

*yadyena pūryate kāryyaṃ dhīmāṃstattena yojayet \|*  
*mama yogyaṃ tu yatkāryyaṃ sarvaṃ tanme niyojaya \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. An intelligent man shall put together things that are mutually complementary. You shall therefore engage me in a task that accords with my capacity.

## \|\| 4.17.27 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*ityevaṃ tu vacastasya śrutvā śakrassuharṣitaḥ \|*  
*uvāca praṇamanvācā kāmaṃ kāṃtāsukhāvaham \|\| 27 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

27\. On hearing his words, Indra was much pleased. Pleasing Kāma, the bestower of cherished happiness, by means of his words, he spoke.

## \|\| 4.17.28 \|\|

*śakra uvāca \|*  
*yatkāryyaṃ manasoddiṣṭaṃ mayā tāta manobhava \|*  
*karttuṃ tattvaṃ samartho'si nānyasmāttasyasambhavaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

Indra said:—

28\. O dear Kāma, you are competent to carry out the task which I have conceived in my mind. It cannot be realised through anyone else.

## \|\| 4.17.29 \|\|

*śṛṇu kāma pravakṣyāmi yathārthaṃ mitrasattama \|*  
*yadarthe ca spṛhā jātā tava cādya manobhava \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. O Kāma, foremost among my friends, listen. I shall explain truly for what I remembered you and desired your presence, O Kāma.

## \|\| 4.17.30 \|\|

*tārakākhyo mahādaityo brahmaṇo varamadbhutam \|*  
*abhūdajeyassaṃprāpya sarveṣāmapi duḥkhadaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Securing a wonderful boon from Brahmā, the great demon Tāraka has become invincible and a pest for everyone.

## \|\| 4.17.31 \|\|

*tena saṃpīḍyate loko naṣṭā dharmā hyanekaśaḥ \|*  
*duḥkhitā nirjarāssarve ṛṣayaśca tathākhilāḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. The entire world is harassed by him. Many virtuous rites are destroyed. The gods have become miserable and so also the sages.

## \|\| 4.17.32 \|\|

*devaiśca sakalaistena kṛtaṃ yuddhaṃ yathābalam \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ cāyudhānyatra viphalānyabhavanpurā \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. He had been fought by the gods to the utmost of their ability formerly. But the weapons of all the gods became quite futile.

## \|\| 4.17.33 \|\|

*bhagnaḥ pāśo jaleśasya hariṃ cakraṃ sudarśanam \|*  
*tatkuṇṭhitamabhūttasya kaṇṭhe kṣiptaṃ ca viṣṇunā \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The noose of Varuṇa, the god of waters, snapped. When hurled at his neck by Viṣṇu, the discus Sudarśana was blunted.

## \|\| 4.17.34 \|\|

*etasya maraṇaṃ proktaṃ prajeśena durātmanaḥ \|*  
*śambhorvīryodbhavādbālānmahāyogīśvarasya hi \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. The death of this wicked demon has been foretold by Brahmā, the lord of the people, at the hands of the boy born of Śiva. the great Yogin.

## \|\| 4.17.35 \|\|

*etatkāryyaṃ tvayā sādhu kartavyaṃ suprayatnataḥ \|*  
*tatassyānmitravaryyāti devānāṃ naḥ paraṃ sukham \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. O dear friend, this task must be achieved by you diligently. Then we, the gods, can be very happy.

## \|\| 4.17.36 \|\|

*mamāpi vihitaṃ tasmātsarvalokasukhāvaham \|*  
*mitradharmaṃ hṛdi smṛtvā kartumarhasi sāṃpratam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. It will be beneficent to me. It will render the whole world happy. Realising the duties of a friend you are now to act.

## \|\| 4.17.37 \|\|

*śaṃbhussa girirāje hi tapaḥ paramamāsthitaḥ \|*  
*sa prabhurnāpi kāmena svataṃtraḥ parameśvaraḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Śiva is at present engaged in a great penance. The supreme lord is always independent. It is not to achieve any desire that He performs the penance.

## \|\| 4.17.38 \|\|

*tatsamīpe ca devātha pārvatī svasakhīyutā \|*  
*sevamānā tiṣṭhatīti pitrājñaptā mayā śrutam \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. For the sake of gods, at the bidding of her father, Pārvatī is attending on Him, I hear.

## \|\| 4.17.39 \|\|

*yathā tasyāṃ rucistasya śivasya niyatātmanaḥ \|*  
*jāyate nitarāṃ māra tathā kāryaṃ tvayā dhruvam \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. O Kāma, you shall certainly do everything necessary to bring about an interest in her in the mind of Śiva who has self-control.

## \|\| 4.17.40 \|\|

*iti kṛtvā kṛtī syāstvaṃ sarvaṃ duḥkhaṃ vinaṃkṣyati \|*  
*loke sthāyī pratāpaste bhaviṣyati na cānyathā \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. You will become contented after this. Your miseries will be destroyed. Your exploit will be permanently established in the world. Not otherwise.

## \|\| 4.17.41 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityuktasya tu kāmo hi praphullamukhapaṃkaja \|*  
*premṇovāceti deveśaṃ kariṣyāmi na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

41\. On being thus addressed, Kāma was glad, his face beaming like a full blown lotus. He lovingly said to the lord of gods, “I shall undoubtedly do it.”

## \|\| 4.17.42-43 \|\|

*ityuktvā vacanaṃ tasmai tathetyomiti tadvacaḥ \|*  
*agrahīttarasā kāmaḥ śivamāyāvimohitaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

*yatra yogīśvarassākṣāttapyate paramaṃ tapaḥ \|*  
*jagāma tatra suprītassadārassavasaṃtakaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

42-43. After saying this when he said “So be it” he said “yes.” Kāma accepted it because he was deluded by Śiva’s illusion. Accompanied by his wife and Spring he went to the place where Śiva, the Yogin, was performing penance.

## Chapter 18 - Description of the perturbation caused by Kāma

## \|\| 4.18.1 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*tatra gatvā smaro garvī śivamāyāvimohitaḥ \|*  
*mohakassamadhoścādau dharmaṃ vistārayansthitaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

1\. After going there, the haughty Kāma, deluded by Śiva’s magic power, stationed himself, after first spreading the enchanting power of Spring all around.

## \|\| 4.18.2 \|\|

*vasaṃtasya ca yo dharmmaḥ prasasāra sa sarvataḥ \|*  
*tapasthāne maheśasyauṣadhiprasthe munīśvara \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The enchanting influence of Spring spread everywhere around Oṣadhiprastha, the penance-grove of Śiva, the supreme lord, O excellent sage.

## \|\| 4.18.3 \|\|

*vanāni ca praphullāni pādapānāṃ mahāmune \|*  
*āsanviśeṣatastatra tatprabhāvānmunīśvara \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. O great sage, the groves bloomed with special exuberance, O excellent sage, due to his power.

## \|\| 4.18.4 \|\|

*puṣpāṇi sahakārāṇāmaśokavanikāsu vai \|*  
*virejussusmaroddīpakārāṇi surabhīṇyapi \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The fragrant flowers of Mango and Aśoka trees shone heightening feelings of love.

## \|\| 4.18.5 \|\|

*kairavāṇi ca puṣpāṇi bhramarākalitāni ca \|*  
*babhūburmadanāveśakarāṇi ca viśeṣataḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The water lilies with bees hovering on them proved to be the causes for the rise of love in the minds of everyone.

## \|\| 4.18.6 \|\|

*sakāmoddīpanakaraṃ kokilākalakūjitam \|*  
*āsīdati suramyaṃ hi manoharamatipriyam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The sweet cooings of the cuckoos heightened emotions of love. They were exquisite and pleasing to the mind.

## \|\| 4.18.7 \|\|

*bhramarāṇāṃ tathā śabdā vividhā abhavanmune \|*  
*manoharāśca sarveṣāṃ kāmoddīpakarā api \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. O sage, diverse sounds of the hummings of the bees rang sweet in the ears of everyone heightening temptations of love.

## \|\| 4.18.8 \|\|

*caṃdrasya viśadā kāṃtirvikīrṇā hi samaṃtata \|*  
*kāmināṃ kāminīnāṃ ca dūtikā iva sābhavat \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The bright light of the moon scattered all around appeared to be the emissary of lovers and their beloveds.

## \|\| 4.18.9 \|\|

*mānināṃ preraṇāyāsīttatkāle kāladīpikā \|*  
*mārutaśca sukhaḥ sādho vavau virahiṇo'priyaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. At that time the Kāladīpikā (brilliant lamp) induced reticent haughty persons to love. O good sir, the wind blew gently but distressed those who were separated from their beloveds.

## \|\| 4.18.10 \|\|

*evaṃ vasaṃtavistāro madanāveśakārakaḥ \|*  
*vanaukasāṃ tadā tatra munīnāṃ dussaho'tyabhūt \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Thus the vast diffusion of Spring caused the display of emotions of love. It was unbearable to the forestdwelling sages.

## \|\| 4.18.11 \|\|

*acetasāmapi tadā kāmāsaktirabhūnmune \|*  
*sucetāsāṃ hi jīvānāṃ seti kiṃ varṇyate kathā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. O sage, then, even the insentient beings had the emotions of love. What about the state of sentient ones?

## \|\| 4.18.12 \|\|

*evaṃ cakāra sa madhussvaprabhāvaṃ sudussaham \|*  
*sarveṣā caiva jīvānāṃ kāmoddīpanakārakaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Thus spring employed his unbearable power heightening the love of all living beings.

## \|\| 4.18.13 \|\|

*akālanimitaṃ tāta madhorvīkṣya harastadā \|*  
*āścaryyaṃ paramaṃ mene svalīlāttatanuḥ prabhuḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. On seeing the untimely display of spring, Śiva the lord, who had assumed a physical body indulging in divine sports, thought it surprising.

## \|\| 4.18.14 \|\|

*atha līlākarastatra tapaḥ paramaduṣkaram \|*  
*tatāpa sa vaśīśo hi haro duḥkhaharaḥ prabhuḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. But He, the chief of the self-controlled and the remover of man’s misery continued his severe penance.

## \|\| 4.18.15 \|\|

*vasaṃte prasṛte tatra kāmo ratisamanvitaḥ \|*  
*cūtaṃ bāṇaṃ samākṛṣya sthitastadvāmapārśvataḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. When spring spread everywhere, Kāma accompanied by Rati stood on his left side, with the arrow of mango blossom taken out and kept in readiness.

## \|\| 4.18.16 \|\|

*svaprabhāvaṃ vitastāra mohayansakalāñjanān \|*  
*ratyāyuktaṃ tadā kāmaṃ dṛṣṭvā ko vā na mohitaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Enchanting all people, he spread his influence. Who was not enchanted on seeing Kāma in the company of Rati?

## \|\| 4.18.17 \|\|

*evaṃ pravṛttasuratau śṛṃgāro'pi gaṇaissaha \|*  
*hāvabhāvayutastatra praviveśa harāṃtikam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Thus they initiated their dalliance. The sentiment of love too accompanied by coquettish gestures and emotions reached the vicinity of Śiva along with his attendants.

## \|\| 4.18.18 \|\|

*madanaḥ prakaṭastatra nyavasaccittago bahiḥ \|*  
*na dṛṣṭavāṃstadā śaṃbhośchidraṃ yena praviśyate \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Kāma, usually stationed within the mind manifested himself outside. But he could not find any vulnerable loop-hole in Śiva whereby he could enter Him.

## \|\| 4.18.19 \|\|

*yadā cāprāptavivarastasminyogivare smaraḥ \|*  
*mahādevastadā so'bhūnmahābhayavimohitaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. When Kāma did not secure any entry within the great Yogin, he became deluded and frightened much through the magical power of Śiva.

## \|\| 4.18.20 \|\|

*jvalajjvālāgnisaṃkāśaṃ bhālanetrasamanvitam \|*  
*dhyānasthaṃ śaṃkaraṃ ko vā samāsādayituṃ kṣamaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Who could gain access to Śiva in meditation, who could fix an eye in his forehead that resembled fire with shooting blazing flames?

## \|\| 4.18.21 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare tatra sakhībhyāṃ saṃyutā śivā \|*  
*jagāma śivapūjārthaṃ nītvā puṣpāṇyanekaśaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. In the mean time Pārvatī came there along with her two maids and brought various kinds of flowers for Śiva’s worship.

## \|\| 4.18.22 \|\|

*pṛthivyāṃ yādṛśaṃ lokaissauṃdaryaṃ varṇyate mahat \|*  
*tatsarvamadhikaṃ tasyāṃ pārvatyāmasti niścitam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Certainly Pārvatī had a greater beauty than the most exquisite lady described by people on the earth.

## \|\| 4.18.23 \|\|

*ārtavāṇi supuṣpāṇi dhṛtāni ca tayā yadā \|*  
*tatsauṃdaryaṃ kathaṃ varṇyamapi varṣaśatairapi \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. When she wore pretty flowers of the season how could her beauty be described even in a hundred years?

## \|\| 4.18.24 \|\|

*yadā śivasamīpe tu gatā sā parvatātmajā \|*  
*tadaiva śaṃkaro dhyānaṃ tyaktvā kṣaṇamavasthitaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. No sooner did she enter within the proximity of Śiva than He came out of his meditation for a short while.

## \|\| 4.18.25 \|\|

*tacchidraṃ prāpya madanaḥ prathamaṃ harṣaṇena tu \|*  
*bāṇena harṣayāmāsa pārśvasthaṃ candraśekharam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Profiting by that opportune moment, Kāma, by means of his arrow Harṣaṇa delighted the moon-crest god Śiva who was nearby.

## \|\| 4.18.26 \|\|

*śṛṃgāraiśca tadā bhāvaissahitā pārvatī haram \|*  
*jagāma kāmasāhāyye mune surabhiṇā saha \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. O sage, in assistance to Kāma, Pārvatī reached the place near Śiva with emotions of love and accompanied by Spring.

## \|\| 4.18.27 \|\|

*tadevākṛṣya taccāpaṃ rucyarthaṃ śūladhāriṇaḥ \|*  
*drutaṃ puṣpaśaraṃ tasmai smaro'muṃcatsusaṃyataḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. In order to make the trident-bearing lord take interest in her, Kāma drew his bow very carefully and discharged his flowery arrow on Him.

## \|\| 4.18.28 \|\|

*yathā niraṃtaraṃ nityamāgacchati tathā śivam \|*  
*tannamaskṛtya tatpūjāṃ kṛtvā tatpurataḥ sthitā \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. As was her usual practice she approached Śiva, bowed to Him, worshipped Him and stood in front of Him (awaiting further instructions).

## \|\| 4.18.29 \|\|

*sā dṛṣṭā pārvatī tatra prabhuṇā giriśena hi \|*  
*vivṛṇvatī tadāṃgāni strīsvabhāvātsulajjayā \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Pārvatī was stared at by lord Śiva, while she was laying bare some of the limbs bashfully, as is natural to women in such circumstances.

## \|\| 4.18.30 \|\|

*susaṃsmṛtya varaṃ tasyā vidhidattaṃ purā prabhuḥ \|*  
*śivopi varṇayāmāsa tadaṃgāni mudā mune \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Remembering the boon granted to her by Brahmā formerly, O sage, lord Śiva began to describe her limbs joyfully.

## \|\| 4.18.31 \|\|

*śiva uvāca \|*  
*ki mukhaṃ kiṃ śaśāṃkaśca kiṃ netre cotpale ca kim \|*  
*bhrukuṭyau dhanuṣī caite kaṃdarpasya mahātmanaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

Śiva said:—

31\. “Is this your face or the moon? Are these your eyes or lotus petals? These two eyebrows are the bows of Kāma of noble soul.

## \|\| 4.18.32 \|\|

*adharaḥ kiṃ ca biṃbaṃ kiṃ kiṃ nāsā śukacaṃcukā \|*  
*kiṃ svaraḥ kokilālāpaḥ kiṃ madhyaṃ cātha vedikā \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Is this your lower lip or Bimba fruit? Is this your nose or the beak of a parrot? Do I hear your voice or the cooing of the cuckoo? Is this your slender waist or the sacrificial altar?

## \|\| 4.18.33 \|\|

*kiṃ gatirvarṇyate hyasyāḥ kiṃ rūpaṃ varṇyate muhuḥ \|*  
*puṣpāṇi kiṃ ca varṇyaṃte vastrāṇi ca tathā punaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. How can her gait be described? How can her comely appearance be described? How can the flowers be described? How can the clothes be described?

## \|\| 4.18.34 \|\|

*lālityaṃ cāru yatsṛṣṭau tadekatra vinirmitam \|*  
*sarvathā ramaṇīyāni sarvāṃgāni na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Whatever is graceful and sweet in the creation has been incorporated here. Indeed, all her limbs are exquisite in every respect.

## \|\| 4.18.35 \|\|

*aho dhanyatarā ceyaṃ pārvatyadbhutarūpiṇī \|*  
*etatsamā na trailokye nārī kāpi surūpiṇī \|\| 35 \|\|*

35 How blessed is this Pārvatī of mysteriously wonderful features. There is no other woman equal to her in beauty in the three worlds.

## \|\| 4.18.36 \|\|

*sulāvaṇyānidhiśceyamadbhutāṃgāni bibhratī \|*  
*vimohinī munīnāṃ ca mahāsukhavivarddhinī \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. She is a storehouse of the finest beauty. She has wondrous beautiful limbs. She is an enchantress of even sages. She increases great happiness.”

## \|\| 4.18.37 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*ityevaṃ varṇayitvā tu tadaṃgāni muhurmuhuḥ \|*  
*vidhidattavarādhyāsāddharastu virarāma ha \|\| 37 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

37\. After describing her body again and again, recollecting the boon granted by Brahmā, Śiva stopped.

## \|\| 4.18.38 \|\|

*hastaṃ vastrāṃtare yāvadacālayata śaṃkaraḥ \|*  
*strīsvabhāvācca sā tatra lajjitā dūrato gatā \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. When Śiva put His hand within her garment and moved it, she, as is natural to women, bashfully withdrew and kept aloof.

## \|\| 4.18.39 \|\|

*vivṛṇvatī nijāṃgāni paśyaṃtī ca muhurmuhuḥ \|*  
*suvīkṣaṇairmahāmodātsusmitābhūcchivā mune \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. O sage, then Pārvatī smilingly laid bare some parts of her body and cast graceful glances at Him with great pleasure.

## \|\| 4.18.40 \|\|

*evaṃ ceṣṭāṃ tadā dṛṣṭvā śaṃbhurmohamupāgataḥ \|*  
*uvāca vacanaṃ caivaṃ mahālīlo maheśvaraḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. On seeing these movements and gestures Śiva became fascinated. Lord Śiva indulging in great divine sports spoke these words.

## \|\| 4.18.41 \|\|

*asyā darśanamātreṇa mahānaṃdo bhavatyalam \|*  
*yadāliṃganamenasyāḥ kuryyāṃ kintu tatassukham \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. “I feel great pleasure on merely seeing her. What pleasure shall I derive by embracing her?”

## \|\| 4.18.42 \|\|

*kṣaṇamātraṃ vicāryyetthaṃ saṃpūjya girijāṃ tataḥ \|*  
*prabuddhasya mahāyogī suvirakto jagāviti \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Thinking thus only for a moment, the enlightened Śiva became detached, honoured Pārvatī and spoke.

## \|\| 4.18.43 \|\|

*kiṃ jātaṃ caritaṃ citraṃ kimahaṃ mohamāgataḥ \|*  
*kāmena vikṛtaścādya bhūtvāpi prabhurīśvaraḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. “How wonderful and mysterious is the situation that has arisen! How is it that I have been deluded and fascinated? Though I am the lord and master, I have been perturbed by Kāma.

## \|\| 4.18.44 \|\|

*īśvarohaṃ yadīccheyaṃ parāṃgasparśanaṃ khalu \|*  
*tarhi ko'nyo'kṣamaḥ kṣudraḥ kiṃ kiṃ naiva kariṣyati \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. If I, the master, were to yearn for the touch of a woman’s limbs what will not be done by other incompetent and insignificant creatures”.

## \|\| 4.18.45 \|\|

*evaṃ vairāgyamāsādya paryyaṃkāsādanaṃ ca tat \|*  
*vārayāmāsa sarvātmā pareśaḥ kiṃ patediha \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Thus resuming detachment, lord Śiva forbade her sitting on the couch. How can there be a downfall for the great lord Śiva?

## Chapter 19 - Kāma’s destruction by Śiva

## \|\| 4.19.1 \|\|

*\|\| nārada uvāca \|*  
*brahmanvidhe mahābhāga kiṃ jātaṃ tadanaṃtaram \|*  
*kathaya tvaṃ prasādena tāṃ kathāṃ pāpanāśinīm \|\| 1 \|\|*

Nārada said:—

1\. O Brahmā, the most fortunate one, what happened then? Be pleased to tell me that story that destroys our sins altogether.

## \|\| 4.19.2 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*śrūyatāṃ sā kathā tāta yajjātaṃ tadanaṃtaram \|*  
*tava snehātpravakṣyāmi śivalīlāṃ mudāvahām \|\| 2 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

2\. O dear one, hear the story of what happened thereafter. Out of love for me I shall recount Śiva’s sports that bring about joy.

## \|\| 4.19.3 \|\|

*dhairyasya vyasanaṃ dṛṣṭvā mahāyogī maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*viciṃtitaṃ manasyevaṃ vismito'titataḥ param \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. On seeing the dissipation of His courage, lord Śiva, the great Yogin, thought within Himself wondering much.

## \|\| 4.19.4 \|\|

*\|\| śiva uvāca \|*  
*kimu vighnāḥ samutpannāḥ kurvatastapa uttamam \|*  
*kena me vikṛtaṃ cittaṃ kṛtamatra kukarmiṇā \|\| 4 \|\|*

Śiva said:—

4\. How is it that obstacles have cropped up while I am performing the great penance? Who can be that wicked person who has made my mind highly perturbed?

## \|\| 4.19.5 \|\|

*kuvarṇanaṃ mayā prītyā parastryupari vai kṛtam \|*  
*jāto dharmavirodho'tra śrutisīmā vilaṃghitā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. With love I have described in bad taste another man’s woman. I have contravened rules of virtue and transgressed the bounds of the Vedas.

## \|\| 4.19.6 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*viciṃtyetthaṃ mahāyogī parameśassatāṃ gatiḥ \|*  
*diśo vilokayāmāsa paritaśśaṃkitastadā \|\| 6 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

6\. After thinking like this, the great Yogin, the goal of the good, surveyed all round, his suspicion having been aroused.

## \|\| 4.19.7 \|\|

*vāmabhāge sthitaṃ kāmaṃ dadarśākṛṣṭabāṇakam \|*  
*svaśaraṃ kṣeptukāmaṃ hi garvitaṃ mūḍhacetasam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. He saw Kāma stationed on His left side with his bow fully drawn and ready to discharge the arrow. Kāma was haughty and so was very senseless.

## \|\| 4.19.8 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā tādṛśaṃ kāmaṃ girīśasya parātmanaḥ \|*  
*saṃjātaḥ krodhasaṃmardastatkṣaṇādapi nārada \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. O Nārada, on seeing Kāma in that attitude, instantaneously anger was aroused in lord Śiva, the supreme soul.

## \|\| 4.19.9 \|\|

*kāmaḥ sthito'ntarikṣe sa dhṛtvā tatsaśaraṃ dhanuḥ \|*  
*cikṣepāstraṃ durnivāramamoghaṃ śaṃkare mune \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. O sage, standing high up in the air, holding the arrow and the bow, Kāma discharged his arrow, usually unerring on Śiva.

## \|\| 4.19.10 \|\|

*babhūvāmoghamastraṃ tu moghaṃ tatparamātmani \|*  
*samaśāmyattatastasminsaṃkuddhe parameśvare \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The infallible weapon became futile on the great lord. The furious weapon calmed down in regard to the great soul, Śiva.

## \|\| 4.19.11 \|\|

*moghībhūte śive svestre bhayamāpāśu manmathaḥ \|*  
*cakaṃpe ca puraḥ sthitvā dṛṣṭvā mṛtyuṃjayaṃ prabhum \|\| 11 \|\|*
