11\. Kāma was frightened when his weapon failed, Standing there and seeing lord Śiva, the conqueror of death in front, he trembled.

## \|\| 4.19.12 \|\|

*sasmāra tridaśānsarvānśakrādīnbhayavihvalaḥ \|*  
*sa smaro muniśārdūla svaprayāse nirarthake \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. O great sage, when his endeavour became futile, Kāma who was frightened much remembered Indra and all other gods.

## \|\| 4.19.13 \|\|

*kāmena susmṛtā devāśśakrādyāste munīśvara \|*  
*āyayuḥ sakalāste hi śaṃbhuṃ natvā ca tuṣṭuvuḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. O great sage, remembered by Kāma, Indra and other gods came there, bowed to and eulogised Śiva.

## \|\| 4.19.14 \|\|

*stutiṃ kurvatsu deveṣu kuddhasyāti harasya hi \|*  
*tṛtīyāttasya netrādvai nissasāra tato mahān \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. When the gods eulogised thus, a great flame of fire sprang up from the third eye of the infuriated Śiva.

## \|\| 4.19.15 \|\|

*lalāṭa madhyagāttasmātsavahnirdrutasambhavaḥ \|*  
*jajvālorddhvaśikho dīptaḥ pralayāgnisamaprabhaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. That fire originating instantaneously from the eye in the middle of His forehead blazed with flames shooting up and resembling the fire of final dissolution in refulgence.

## \|\| 4.19.16 \|\|

*utpatya gagane tūrṇaṃ niṣpatya dharaṇī tale \|*  
*bhrāmaṃbhrāmaṃ svaparitaḥ papāta medanīṃ pari \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. After shooting up in the sky, it fell on the ground and rolled over the earth all round.

## \|\| 4.19.17 \|\|

*bhasmasātkṛtavānsādho madanaṃ tāvadeva hi \|*  
*yāvacca marutāṃ vācaḥ kṣamyatāṃ kṣamyatāmiti \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Even before the gods had the time to say “Let him be forgiven, let him be excused” it reduced Kāma to ashes.

## \|\| 4.19.18 \|\|

*hate tasminsmare vīre deva duḥkhamupāgatāḥ \|*  
*rurudurvihvalāścātikrośataḥ kimabhūditi \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. When the heroic Kāma was thus slain, the gods became miserable. In their agitation they lamented much and saying “O what has happened?” they cried aloud.

## \|\| 4.19.19 \|\|

*śvetāṃgā vikṛtātmā ca girirājasutā tadā \|*  
*jagāma maṃdiraṃ svaṃ ca samādāya sakhījanam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. With pallid face and limbs, the extremely agitated daughter of the king of mountains returned to her palace taking the maids along with her.

## \|\| 4.19.20 \|\|

*kṣaṇamātraṃ ratistatra visaṃjñā sābhavattadā \|*  
*bhartṛmṛtyujaduḥkhena patitā sā mṛtā iva \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Due to the misery on account of the death of her husband, Rati fell down unconscious, as if dead.

## \|\| 4.19.21 \|\|

*jātāyāṃ caiva saṃjñāyāṃ ratiratyaṃtavihvalā \|*  
*vilalāpa tadā tatroccaraṃtī vividhaṃ vacaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. When she regained consciousness after a while, Rati in her great agitation lamented loudly and said:—

## \|\| 4.19.22 \|\|

*\|\| ratiruvāca \|*  
*kiṃ karomi kva gacchāmi kiṃ kṛtaṃ daivatairiha \|*  
*matsvāminaṃ samāhūya nāśayāmāsuruddhatam \|\| 22 \|\|*

Rati said:—

22\. “What shall I do? Where can I go? What is it that the gods have done in making my husband a victim thus? They have called him here and destroyed him.

## \|\| 4.19.23 \|\|

*hā hā nātha smara svāminprāṇapriya sukhaprada \|*  
*idaṃ tu kimabhūdatra hā hā priya priyeti ca \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. O! O! O lord Kāma, dearer to me than my vital airs, O bestower of happiness, what has happened here? Ha, Ha, my dear, my dear!”

## \|\| 4.19.24 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|\| \|*  
*itthaṃ vilapatī sā tu vadaṃtī bahudhā vacaḥ \|*  
*hastau pādau tadāsphālya keśānatroṭayattadā \|\| 24 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

24\. Lamenting thus and crying out various piteous words she beat with her hands, kicked with her legs and plucked her hairs.

## \|\| 4.19.25 \|\|

*tadvilāpaṃ tadā śrutvā tatra sarve vanecarāḥ \|*  
*abhavanduḥkhitāssarve sthāvarā api nārada \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. O Nārada, on hearing her lamentation even the beasts and residents of the forest, nay all the immobile trees and bushes became miserable.

## \|\| 4.19.26 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare tatra devāśśakrādayo'khilāḥ \|*  
*ratimūcussamāśvāsya saṃsmaraṃto maheśvaram \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. In the meantime Indra and other gods remembered lord Śiva and consoled Rati saying as follows:—

## \|\| 4.19.27 \|\|

*\|\| devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*kiṃcidbhasma gṛhītvā tu rakṣa yatnādbhayaṃ tyaja \|*  
*jīvayiṣyati sa svāmī lapsyase tvaṃ punaḥ priyam \|\| 27 \|\|*

The gods said:—

27\. Take some ashes and preserve them. With effort check your fear. The lord will resuscitate your lover. You will regain your lover again.

## \|\| 4.19.28 \|\|

*sukhadātā na kopyasti duḥkhadātā na kaścana \|*  
*sarvo'pi svakṛtaṃ bhuṃkte devāñśocasi vai vṛthā \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. There is none who gives us happiness or misery. All enjoy and experience the fruit of what they do. In vain do you curse the gods.

## \|\| 4.19.29 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*ityāśvāsya ratiṃ devāssarve śivamupāgatāḥ \|*  
*suprasādya śivaṃ bhaktyā vacanaṃ cedamabruvan \|\| 29 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

29\. After consoling Rati thus, all the gods approached Śiva and propitiated Him. With great devotion they spoke these words to Him.

## \|\| 4.19.30 \|\|

*\|\| devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*bhagavañchrūyatometadvacanaṃ naśśubhaṃ prabho \|*  
*kṛpāṃ kṛtvā maheśāna śaraṇāgatavatsala \|\| 30 \|\|*

The gods said:—

30\. O lord, O great god, favourably disposed to those who seek refuge in you, be pleased to listen to these well intended words of ours.

## \|\| 4.19.31 \|\|

*suvicāraya suprītyā kṛti kāmasya śaṃkara \|*  
*kāmenaitatkṛtaṃ yatra na svārthaṃ tanmaheśvara \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. O Śiva, be pleased to ponder over the action of Kāma. O lord Śiva, there is no tinge of selfishness in what Kāma has done.

## \|\| 4.19.32 \|\|

*duṣṭena pīḍitairdevaistārakeṇā'khilairvibho \|*  
*karma tatkāritaṃ nātha nānyathā viddhi śaṃkara \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. O lord, he had been induced to do so by all the gods harassed by the wicked Tāraka. O Śiva, please know that it is not otherwise.

## \|\| 4.19.33 \|\|

*ratirekākinī deva vilāpaṃ duḥkhitā satī \|*  
*karoti giriśa tvaṃ ca tāmāśvāsaya sarvadā \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. O lord, the chaste Rati is lonely and miserable now. O lord Śiva, she is in great lamentation, O bestower of everything, please console her.

## \|\| 4.19.34 \|\|

*saṃhāraṃ kartukāmo'si krodhenānena śaṃkara \|*  
*daivataissaha sarveṣāṃ hatavāṃstaṃ yadi smaram \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. If you have finally disposed off Kāma, O Śiva, you are desirous of annihilating all the gods by means of your fury.

## \|\| 4.19.35 \|\|

*duḥkhaṃ tasyā raterdṛṣṭvā naṣṭaprāyāśca devatāḥ \|*  
*tasmāttvayā ca karttavyaṃ ratyāśokāpanodanam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. On seeing the distress of Rati, the gods are almost doomed. Hence you must remove the distress of Rati.

## \|\| 4.19.36 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya vacasteṣāṃ prasanno bhagavāñchivaḥ \|*  
*devānāṃ sakalānāṃ ca vacanaṃ cedamabravīt \|\| 36 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

36\. On hearing their words, lord Śiva was pleased. He said this to all the gods.

## \|\| 4.19.37 \|\|

*\|\| śiva uvāca \|*  
*devāśca ṛṣayassarve madvacaśśṛṇutādarāt \|*  
*matkopena ca yajjātaṃ tattathā nānyathā bhavat \|\| 37 \|\|*

Śiva said:—

37\. O gods, O sages, all of you listen attentively to my words. What has happened, thanks to my fury, cannot be altered.

## \|\| 4.19.38 \|\|

*anaṃgastāvadeva syātkāmo ratipatiḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*yāvaccāvataretkṛṣṇo dharaṇyāṃ rukmiṇīpatiḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. The lord Kāma, the husband of Rati, shall remain bodiless till Viṣṇu incarnates as Kṛṣṇa on the earth and marries Rukmiṇī.

## \|\| 4.19.39 \|\|

*dvārakāyāṃ yadā sthitvā putrānutpādayiṣyati \|*  
*tadā kṛṣṇastu rukmiṇyāṃ kāmamutpādayiṣyati \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Kṛṣṇa will beget Kāma in Rukmiṇī when he goes to Dvārakā25 and begins to procreate children.

## \|\| 4.19.40 \|\|

*pradyumnanāma tasyaiva bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*jātamātraṃ tu taṃ putraṃ śaṃbarassaṃhariṣyati \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. His name will certainly be Pradyumna. The demon Sambara will abduct the boy at the time of his very birth.

## \|\| 4.19.41 \|\|

*hṛtvā prāsya samudraṃ taṃ śaṃbaro dānavottamaḥ \|*  
*mṛtaṃ jñātvā vṛthā mūḍho nagaraṃ svaṃ gamiṣyati \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. After abducting the boy, the great demon, Śambara, will throw him in the sea. The foolish fellow will take him for dead and will return to his city.

## \|\| 4.19.42 \|\|

*tāvacca nagaraṃ tasya rate stheyaṃ yathāsukham \|*  
*tatraiva svapateḥ prāptiḥ pradyumnasya bhaviṣyati \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. O Rati, you shall stay in his city till then. There alone you will get back your husband Pradyumna.

## \|\| 4.19.43 \|\|

*tatra kāmo militvā taṃ hatvā śambaramāhave \|*  
*bhaviṣyati sukhī devāḥ pradyumnākhyassvakāminīm \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Kāma in the name of Pradyumna will regain his wife after killing Śambara in a battle. O gods, he will be happy thereafter.

## \|\| 4.19.44 \|\|

*tadīyaṃ caiva yaddravyaṃ nītvā sa nagaraṃ punaḥ \|*  
*gamiṣyati tayā sārddhaṃ devāssatyaṃ vaco mama \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. After taking all the valuable properties of Śambara, O gods, he will go to the city again along with her. These words of mine are true.

Brahmā said—

## \|\| 4.19.45 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*iti śrutvā vacaśśaṃbhordevā ūcuḥ praṇamya tam \|*  
*kiṃciducchvasitāścitte karau baddhvā natāṃgakāḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. On hearing these words of Śiva, the gods heaved a sigh of relief. Joining their palms in reverence and bowing to Him they said:—

## \|\| 4.19.46 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*devadeva mahādeva karuṇāsāgara prabho \|*  
*śīghraṃ jīvaya kāmaṃ tvaṃ rakṣa prāṇān raterhara \|\| 46 \|\|*

The gods said:—

46\. “O great god, lord of the gods, O lord, the ocean of mercy, please resuscitate Kāma quickly. O Śiva, save the life of Ratī.”

## \|\| 4.19.47 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityākarṇyāmaravacaḥ prasannaḥ parameśvaraḥ \|*  
*punarbabhāṣe karuṇāsāgarassakaleśvaraḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

47\. On hearing these words of the gods, great God became delighted. The lord of all, the ocean of mercy, spoke again.

## \|\| 4.19.48 \|\|

*śiva uvāca \|*  
*he devāssuprasanno'smi jīvayiṣyāmi cāṃtare \|*  
*kāmaḥ sa madgaṇo bhūtvā vihariṣyati nityaśaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

Śiva said:—

48\. O gods, I am delighted. I shall resuscitate Kāma within myself. He will be one of my Gaṇas and will sport about always.

## \|\| 4.19.49 \|\|

*nākhyeyamidamākhyānaṃ kasyacitpuratassurāḥ \|*  
*gacchata svasthalaṃ dukhaṃ nāśayiṣyāmi sarvataḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. O gods, this story should not be narrated in the presence of any one. All of you return to your abodes. I shall destroy all miseries.

## \|\| 4.19.50 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityuktvāṃtardadhe rudro devānāṃ stuvatāṃ tadā \|*  
*sarve devāssuprassannā babhūvurgatavismayāḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

50\. After saying this Rudra vanished even as the gods were eulogising Him. The gods became delighted and free from mental suspense.

## \|\| 4.19.51 \|\|

*tatastāṃ ca samāśvāsya rudrasya vacane sthitāḥ \|*  
*uktvā vacastadīyaṃ ca svaṃ svaṃ dhāma yayurmune \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. O sage, abiding by the directions of Śiva and consoling Rati by means of the conciliatory words of Śiva, the gods returned to their respective places.

## \|\| 4.19.52 \|\|

*kāmapatnī samādiṣṭaṃ nagaraṃ sā gatā tadā \|*  
*pratīkṣamāṇā taṃ kālaṃ rudrādiṣṭaṃ munīśvara \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. O excellent sage, then Rati, the wife of Kāma went to the city and waited for the time mentioned by Siva.

## Chapter 20 - The story of the submarine fire

## \|\| 4.20.1 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*vidhe netrasamudbhūtavahnijvālā harasya sā \|*  
*gatā kutra vada tvaṃ taccaritraṃ śaśimaulinaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Nārada said:—

1\. O Brahmā, please tell me “Where did the flame of fire emerging from the eye of Śiva go?” Please tell me also the further story of the moon-crested lord.

## \|\| 4.20.2 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*yadā bhasma cakārāśu tṛtīyanayanānalaḥ \|*  
*śambhoḥ kāmaṃ prajajvāla sarvato viphalastadā \|\| 2 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

2\. When the fire from the third eye of Śiva reduced Kāma to ashes it began to blaze all round without burning anything.

## \|\| 4.20.3 \|\|

*hāhākāro mahānāsīttrailokye sacarācare \|*  
*sarvadevarṣayastāta śaraṇaṃ māṃ yayurdrutam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. A huge hue and cry was raised in the three worlds consisting of the mobile and immobile creatures. Immediately the gods and sages sought refuge in me.

## \|\| 4.20.4 \|\|

*sarve nivedayāmāsustaddukhaṃ mahyamākulāḥ \|*  
*supraṇamya susaṃstutya karau baddhvā natānanā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. All of them in their agitation bowed to and eulogised me with their palms joined in reverence and the heads bent down. They intimated to me their grief.

## \|\| 4.20.5 \|\|

*tacchrutvāhaṃ śivaṃ smṛtvā taddhetuṃ suvimṛśya ca \|*  
*gatastatra vinītātmā trilokāvanahetave \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. On hearing that I pondered over the reason for the same, and remembering Śiva humbly I went there in order to protect the three worlds.

## \|\| 4.20.6 \|\|

*saṃdagdhukāmaḥ sa śucijvālāmālātidīpitaḥ \|*  
*staṃbhito'raṃ mayā śaṃbhuprasādāptasutejasā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. That fire, out to burn everything, very brilliant with its shooting flames, was thwarted by me as I had the capacity by Śiva’s grace.

## \|\| 4.20.7 \|\|

*atha krodhamayaṃ vahniṃ dagdhukāma jagattrayam \|*  
*vāḍavāṃtakamārṣaṃ ca saumyajvālāmukhaṃ mune \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. O sage, then I made that fire of fury, out to burn the three worlds, tender in its blaze and mare-like in shape.

## \|\| 4.20.8 \|\|

*taṃ vāḍavatanumahaṃ samādāya śivecchayā \|*  
*sāgaraṃ samagāṃ lokahitāya jagatāṃ patiḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Taking that fire mare-like in form, at the will of Śiva, I, the lord of the worlds, went to the sea shore, for the benefit of the worlds.

## \|\| 4.20.9 \|\|

*āgataṃ māṃ samālokya sāgarassāṃjalirmune \|*  
*dhṛtvā ca pauruṣaṃ rūpamāgatassaṃnidhiṃ mama \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. O sage, on seeing me arrived there, the sea took a human form and approached me with palms joined in reverence.

## \|\| 4.20.10 \|\|

*supraṇamyātha māṃ siṃdhussaṃstūya ca yathā vidhi \|*  
*sa māmuvāca suprītyā sarvalokapitāmaham \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Bowing to and duly eulogising me, the grandfather of all the worlds, the ocean said lovingly.

## \|\| 4.20.11-12 \|\|

*sāgara uvāca \|*  
*kimarthamāgato'si tvaṃ brahmannatrākhilādhipa \|*  
*tannideśaya suprītyā matvā māṃ ca svasevakam \|\| 11 \|\|*

*athāhaṃ sāgaravacaśśrutvā prītipurassaram \|*  
*prāvocaṃ śaṃkaraṃ smṛtvā laukikaṃ hitamāvahan \|\| 12 \|\|*

The ocean said:—

11-12. “O Brahmā, the lord of all, why have you come here? Please command me with pleasure knowing me to be your servant”. On hearing the words of the ocean I remembered Śiva. I spoke with love in order to benefit the world.

## \|\| 4.20.13 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*śṛṇu tāta mahādhīmansarvalokahitāvaha \|*  
*vacmyahaṃ prītitassiṃdho śivecchāprerito hṛdā \|\| 13 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

13\. O dear, intelligent one, causing the welfare of all the worlds, O ocean, induced by Śiva’s will, I shall explain to you.

## \|\| 4.20.14 \|\|

*ayaṃ krodho maheśasya vāḍavātmā mahāprabhuḥ \|*  
*dagdhvā kāmaṃ drutaṃ sarvaṃ dagdhukāmo'bhavattataḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. This is the fire of fury of lord Śiva, the great lord. It is in the form of a mare now. After burning Kāma it was about to burn everything.

## \|\| 4.20.15 \|\|

*prārthito'haṃ suraiśśīghraṃ pīḍitaiśśaṃkarecchayā \|*  
*tatrāgatya drutaṃ taṃ vai tāta staṃbhitavāñśucim \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. At the will of Śiva I was requested by the gods who were harassed by it, and so I went there and suppressed the fire.

## \|\| 4.20.16 \|\|

*vāḍavaṃ rūpamādhatta tamādāyāga totra ha \|*  
*nirdiśāmi jalādhāra tvāmahaṃ karuṇākaraḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. I gave it the form of a mare. I have brought it here. O ocean, I ask you to be merciful.

## \|\| 4.20.17 \|\|

*ayaṃ krodhī maheśasya vāḍavaṃ rūpamāśritaḥ \|*  
*jvālāmukhastvayā dhāryyo yāvadābhūtasaṃplavam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. This fury of lord Śiva, now in the form of a mare, you will bear till the final dissolution of all living beings.

## \|\| 4.20.18 \|\|

*yadātrāhaṃ samāgamya vatsyāmi saritāṃ pate \|*  
*tadā tvayā parityājyaḥ krodho'yaṃ śāṃkaro'dbhutaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. O lord of rivers, when I shall come and stay here, you shall release it. This is Śiva’s wonderful fire of fury.

## \|\| 4.20.19 \|\|

*bhojanaṃ toyametasya tava nityaṃ bhaviṣyati \|*  
*yatnādevāvadhāryyo'yaṃ yathā nopaiti cāṃtaram \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. His perpetual diet shall consist of your waters. This shall be preserved by you with effort lest it should go down.

## \|\| 4.20.20 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityukto hi mayā siṃdhuraṃgīcakre tadā dhuvam \|*  
*grahītuṃ vāḍavaṃ vahniṃ raudraṃ cāśakyamanyataḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Thus requested by me, the ocean agreed. None else could have grasped Śiva’s fire of fury thus.

## \|\| 4.20.21 \|\|

*tataḥ praviṣṭo jaladhau sa vāḍavatanuḥ śuciḥ \|*  
*vāryoghānsudahaṃstasya jvālāmālābhidīpitaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. That fire in the form of a mare entered the ocean and began to consume the currents of water. It blazed with all its shooting flames.

## \|\| 4.20.22 \|\|

*tatassaṃtuṣṭacetaskassvaṃ dhāmāhaṃ gato mune \|*  
*aṃtardhānamagātsiṃdhurdivyarūpaḥ praṇamya mām \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. O sage, then, delighted in mind I returned to my abode. The ocean of divine form bowed to me and vanished.

## \|\| 4.20.23 \|\|

*svāsthyaṃ prāpa jagatsarvaṃ nirmuktaṃ tadbhavādbhayāt \|*  
*devā babhūvuḥ sukhino munayaśca mahāmune \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. O great sage, the entire universe, freed from the fear of that fire became normal. The gods and the sages became happy.

## Chapter 21 - Nārada instructs Pārvatī

## \|\| 4.21.1 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*vidhe tāta mahāprājña viṣṇuśiṣya trilokakṛt \|*  
*adbhuteyaṃ kathā proktā śaṃkarasya mahātmanaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Nārada said:—

1\. O dear Brahmā, O disciple of Viṣṇu, of great intellect. O Creator of three worlds, this is a very wonderful story of the great soul Śiva that has been narrated.

## \|\| 4.21.2 \|\|

*bhasmībhūte smare śaṃbhutṛtīyanayanāgninā \|*  
*tasminpraviṣṭe jaladhau vada tvaṃ kimabhūttataḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. When Kāma had been reduced to ashes by the fire from the third eye of Śiva and when that fire had been deposited in the ocean what happened thereafter?

## \|\| 4.21.3 \|\|

*kiṃ cakāra tato devī pārvatī kudharātmajaḥ \|*  
*gatā kutra sakhībhyāṃ sā tadvadādya dayānidhe \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. What did Goddess Pārvatī, the daughter of the lord of mountains, do? O storehouse of mercy, please tell me now where she went along with her maids.

## \|\| 4.21.4 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*śṛṇu tāta mahāprājña caritaṃ śaśimaulinaḥ \|*  
*mahotikārakasyaiva svāmino mama cādarāt \|\| 4 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

4\. O dear, of great intellect, listen to the story of the moon crested lord, my master and the cause of great enjoyment and protection.

## \|\| 4.21.5 \|\|

*yadāhacchaṃbhunetrodbhavo hi madanaṃ śuciḥ \|*  
*mahāśabdo'dbhuto'bhūdvai yenākāśaḥ prapūritaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. A wonderfully loud sound arose covering the whole firmament when the fire issuing from Śiva’s eye burnt Kāma.

## \|\| 4.21.6 \|\|

*tena śabdena mahatā kāmaṃ dagdhaṃ samīkṣya ca \|*  
*sakhībhyāṃ saha bhītā sā yayau svagṛhamākulā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. On hearing that loud report and seeing Kāma burnt, Pārvatī was terribly frightened and she returned to her abode along with her maids.

## \|\| 4.21.7 \|\|

*tena śabdena himavānparivārasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*vismito'bhūdatikliṣṭassutāṃ smṛtvā gatāṃ tataḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Himavat along with his attendants and relatives was surprised on hearing that loud report. He was agitated on remembering that his daughter had gone there.

## \|\| 4.21.8 \|\|

*jagāma śokaṃ śaileśo sutāṃ dṛṣṭvātivihvalām \|*  
*rudatīṃ śaṃbhuvirahādāsasādācaleśvaraḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. On seeing his daughter excessively agitated, the lord of the mountains was sorry. The lord of the mountains approached her gently as she was crying due to her separation from Śiva.

## \|\| 4.21.9-10 \|\|

*āsādya pāṇinā tasyā mārjayannayanadvayam \|*  
*mā bibhīhi śive'rodīrityuktvā tāṃ tadāgrahīt \|\| 9 \|\|*

*kroḍe kṛtvā sutāṃ śīghraṃ hima vānacaleśvaraḥ \|*  
*svamālayamathāninye sāṃtvayannativihvalām \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. Approaching her and wiping off her eyes with his hand he said—“Dear daughter, do not be afraid, do not cry. He took her on his lap and consoled her. The lord of the mountains took her immediately to his palace.

## \|\| 4.21.11 \|\|

*aṃtarhite smaraṃ dagdhvā hare tadvirahācchivā \|*  
*vikalābhūd bhṛśaṃ sā vai lebhe śarma na kutracit \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. When Śiva had vanished after burning Kāma, Pārvatī became extremely agitated due to His separation. She did not attain pleasure anywhere.

## \|\| 4.21.12 \|\|

*piturgṛhaṃ tadā gatvā militvā mātaraṃ śivā \|*  
*punarjātaṃ tadā mene svātmānaṃ sā dharātmajā \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Returning to her father’s abode and meeting her mother, Śivā, the daughter of the mountain, considered herself born again.

## \|\| 4.21.13 \|\|

*niniṃda ca svarūpaṃ sā hā hatāsmītyathābravīt \|*  
*sakhībhirbodhitā cāpi na bubodha girīndrajā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. She cursed her own beauty. She said to herself. “O, I am doomed”. The daughter of the lord of mountains did not regain composure though consoled and assuaged by the maids.

## \|\| 4.21.14 \|\|

*svapatī ca pibaṃtī ca sā snātī gacchatī śivā \|*  
*tiṣṭhaṃtī ca sakhīmadhye na kiṃcitsukhamāpa ha \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. She did not achieve happiness and peace in sleeping, drinking, bathing, or sitting amidst her maids.

## \|\| 4.21.15 \|\|

*dhiksvarūpaṃ madīyaṃ ca tathā janma ca karma ca \|*  
*iti bruvaṃtī satataṃ smaraṃtī haraceṣṭitam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Remembering the various gestures and movements of Śiva, she muttered to herself ever and anon—“Fie upon my beauty. Fie on my birth and activity”.

## \|\| 4.21.16 \|\|

*evaṃ sā pārvatī śaṃbhuvirahotkliṣṭamānasā \|*  
*sukhaṃ na lebhe kiṃcidrā'bravīcchivaśiveti ca \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Thus Pārvatī was much distressed in mind due to separation from Śiva. She did not at all feel happy. She always muttered “Śiva, Śiva.”

## \|\| 4.21.17 \|\|

*nivasaṃtī piturggehe pinākigatacetanā \|*  
*śuśocātha śivā tāta mumoha ca muhurmuhuḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. O dear, with her consciousness centred round the Pināka-bearing lord, she continued to stay in the palace of her father. Śiva bewailed much and fainted frequently.

## \|\| 4.21.18 \|\|

*śailādhirājopyatha menakāpi mainākamukhyāstanayāśca sarve \|*  
*tāṃ sāṃtvayāmāsuradīnasattvā haraṃ visasmāra tathāpi no sā \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The lord of the mountains, Menakā, and their sons chief of whom was Maināka of undisturbed mind, tried to console her but still she did not forget Śiva.

## \|\| 4.21.19 \|\|

*atha devamune dhīmanhimava tprastare tadā \|*  
*niyojito balabhidāgamastvaṃ kāmacārataḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. O celestial sage, O intelligent one, employed by Indra, the slayer of Bala, you came to Himalaya mountain roaming here and there as you pleased.

## \|\| 4.21.20 \|\|

*tatastvaṃ pūjitastena bhūdhareṇa mahātmanā \|*  
*kuśalaṃ pṛṣṭavāṃstaṃ vai tadāviṣṭo varāsane \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. You were then worshipped by the noble-souled mountain. You enquired of his health and happiness and you were seated in a noble seat.

## \|\| 4.21.21 \|\|

*tataḥ provāca śaileśaḥ kanyācaritamāditaḥ \|*  
*harasevānvitaṃ kāmadahanaṃ ca hareṇa ha \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Then the lord of the mountains told you the story of his daughter from her service to Śiva to the burning of Kāma by Him.

## \|\| 4.21.22 \|\|

*śrutvāvoco mune tvaṃ tu taṃ śaileśaṃ śivaṃ bhaja \|*  
*tamāmaṃtryodatiṣṭhastvaṃ saṃsmṛtya manasā śivam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. O sage, on hearing that, you told the lord of the mountains—“Worship Śiva.” You stood up, remembered Śiva mentally and took leave of him.

## \|\| 4.21.23 \|\|

*taṃ samutsṛjya rahasi kālīṃ tāmagamaṃstvarā \|*  
*lokopakārako jñānī tvaṃ mune śivavallabhaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. O sage, leaving him you hastened to meet Pārvatī secretly, you a favourite of Śiva, perfectly wise and engaged in helping the world.

## \|\| 4.21.24 \|\|

*āsādya kālīṃ saṃbodhya taddhite sthita ādarāt \|*  
*avocastvaṃ vacastathyaṃ sarveṣāṃ jñānināṃ varaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Approaching Pārvatī and addressing her, you spoke to her respectfully. You are foremost among the wise and you were interested in her welfare. Your words were true.

## \|\| 4.21.25 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu kāli vaco me hi satyaṃ vacmi dayārataḥ \|*  
*sarvathā te hitakaraṃ nirvikāraṃ sukāmadam \|\| 25 \|\|*

Nārada said:—

25\. O Pārvatī, listen. I am sympathetic to you. I shall speak truly. My words will be beneficent to you in all respects. They will lead to the achievement of your desire. They are free from aberrations.

## \|\| 4.21.26 \|\|

*sevitaśca mahādevastvayeha tapasā vinā \|*  
*garvavatyā yadadhvaṃsīddīnānugrahakārakaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The great god has been served by you without austerities. You had some pride which He, the blesser of the distressed, eradicated.

## \|\| 4.21.27 \|\|

*viraktaśca sa te svāmī mahāyogī maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*visṛṣṭavānsmaraṃ dagdhvā tvāṃ śive bhaktavatsalaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. O Śivā, after burning Kāma, lord Śiva though favourably disposed to His devotees, left you, since the lord is a great Yogin and so unattached to you.

## \|\| 4.21.28 \|\|

*tasmāttvaṃ sutapoyuktā ciramārādhayeśvaram \|*  
*tapasā saṃskṛtāṃ rudrassa dvitīyāṃ kariṣyati \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Hence you shall propitiate Him by performing a great penance. Śiva will take you as His wife, after you have been sanctified by austerities.

## \|\| 4.21.29 \|\|

*tvaṃ cāpi śaṃkaraṃ śambhuṃ na tyakṣyasi kadācana \|*  
*nānyaṃ patiṃ haṭhāddevi grahīṣyasi śivādṛte \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. You will never forsake the auspicious Śiva. O goddess, you will not take any one other than Śiva as your husband.

## \|\| 4.21.30 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*ityākarṇyavacaste hi mune sā bhūdharātmajā \|*  
*kiṃciducchvasitā kālī prāha tvāṃ sāṃjalirmudā \|\| 30 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

30\. On hearing your words, O sage, Pārvatī, the daughter of the mountain, heaved a sigh of relief and gladly spoke to you with palms joined in reverence.

## \|\| 4.21.31 \|\|

*śivovāca \|*  
*tvaṃ tu sarvajña jagatāmupakārakara prabho \|*  
*rudrasyārādhanārthāya maṃtraṃ dehi mune hi me \|\| 31 \|\|*

Pārvatī said:—

31\. O sage, O omniscient one, you help all the worlds, please tell me a formula for the propitiation of lord Siva.

## \|\| 4.21.32 \|\|

*na sidyati kriyā kāpi sarveṣāṃ sadguruṃ vinā \|*  
*mayā śrutā purā satyaṃ śrutireṣā sanātanī \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. No sacred rite will ever fructify without a good preceptor. Truly this eternal statement of the Vedas was heard by me before.

## \|\| 4.21.33 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*iti śrutvā vacastasyāḥ pārvatyā munisattamaḥ \|*  
*paṃcākṣaraṃ śambhumantraṃ vidhipūrvamupādiśaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

33\. On hearing these words of Pārvatī, O excellent sage, you taught her the five-syllabled mantra of Śiva in accordance with the sacred law.

## \|\| 4.21.34 \|\|

*avocaśca vacastāṃ tvaṃ śraddhāmutpādayanmune \|*  
*prabhāvaṃ mantrarājasya tasya sarvādhikaṃ mune \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. O sage, generating her faith you told her the supreme efficacy of the great formula thus.

## \|\| 4.21.35 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu devi manorasya prabhāvaṃ paramādbhutam \|*  
*yasya śravaṇamātreṇa śaṃkarastu prasīdati \|\| 35 \|\|*

Nārada said:—

35\. O goddess, listen to the wonderful efficacy of this formula on hearing which Śiva becomes excessively pleased.

## \|\| 4.21.36 \|\|

*maṃtroyaṃ sarvamaṃtrāṇāmadhirājaśca kāmadaḥ \|*  
*bhuktimuktiprado'tyaṃtaṃ śaṃkarasya mahāpriyaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. This formula is a king of all formulas. It yields all cherished desires, bestows all worldly pleasures and salvation, and appeals much to Siva.

## \|\| 4.21.37 \|\|

*subhage yena japtena vidhinā so'cirād drutam \|*  
*ārādhitaste pratyakṣo bhaviṣyati śivo dhruvam \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Repeating this formula in accordance with the injunctions you shall propitiate Śiva. He will certainly appear before you.

## \|\| 4.21.38 \|\|

*ciṃtayatī ca tadrūpaṃ niyamasthā śarākṣaram \|*  
*japa mantraṃ śive tvaṃ hi saṃtuṣyati śivo drutam \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. O Śiva, meditate on His form, observing all restraints. Repeat the five-syllabled mantra. Śiva will be pleased quickly.

## \|\| 4.21.39 \|\|

*evaṃ kuru tapa sādhvi tapassādhyo maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*tapasyeva phalaṃ sarvaiḥ prāpyate nānyathā kvacit \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. O chaste lady, perform the penance thus. Lord Śiva can be attained through penance. Every one attains the desired fruits in penance and not otherwise.

## \|\| 4.21.40 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*evamuktvā tadā kālīṃ nārada tvaṃ śivapriyaḥ \|*  
*yādṛcchiko'gamastvaṃ tu svargaṃ devahite rataḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

40\. O Nārada, after saying thus to Pārvatī, you, the favourite of Śiva, went to heaven, a casual visitor engaged in the welfare of the gods.

## \|\| 4.21.41 \|\|

*pārvatī ca tadā śrutvā vacanaṃ tava nārada \|*  
*suprasannā tadā prāpa paṃcākṣaramanūttamam \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. O Nārada, on hearing your words and securing the excellent five-syllabled mantra, Pārvatī was extremely pleased.

## Chapter 22 - Description af Pārvatī’s penance

## \|\| 4.22.1 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*tvayi devamune yāte pārvatī hṛṣṭamānasā \|*  
*tapassādhyaṃ haraṃ mene taporthaṃ mana ādadhe \|\| 1 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

1\. After your departure, O celestial sage, convinced that Śiva could be achieved by means of penance, Pārvatī became glad and decided to perform penance.

## \|\| 4.22.2 \|\|

*tataḥ sakhyau samādāya jayāṃ ca vijayāṃ tathā \|*  
*mātaraṃ pitaraṃ caiva sakhībhyāṃ paryapṛcchata \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. She took her maids Jayā and Vijayā into confidence and through them made her parents acquainted.

## \|\| 4.22.3 \|\|

*prathamaṃ pitaraṃ gatvā himavantaṃ nageśvaram \|*  
*paryapṛcchatsupraṇamya vinayena samanvitā \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. First she wanted her father Himavat, the lord of mountains, to hear her humble words.

## \|\| 4.22.4-5 \|\|

*sakhyāvūcatuḥ \|*  
*himavañcchrūyatāṃ putrī vacanaṃ kathyate'dhunā \|*  
*sā svayaṃ caiva dehasya rūpasyāpi tathā punaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*bhavato hi kulasyāsya sāphalyaṃ kartumicchati \|*  
*tapasā sādhanīyo'sau nānyathā dṛśyatāṃ vrajet \|\| 5 \|\|*

The maids said:—

4-5. O Himavat, let the words of your daughter be heard through us. She wishes to make her body, beauty and family fruitful. This can be achieved through penance and not otherwise.

## \|\| 4.22.6 \|\|

*tasmācca parvataśreṣṭha dehyājñāṃ bhavatādhunā \|*  
*tapaḥ karotu girijā vanaṃ gatveti sādaram \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. O excellent mountain, the permission may kindly be given—“Let Pārvatī go to the forest and perform penance there”.

## \|\| 4.22.7 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityevaṃ ca tadā pṛṣṭassakhībhyāṃ munisattama \|*  
*pārvatyā suvicāryātha girirājo'bravīdidam \|\| 7 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

7\. O excellent sage, thus requested by Pārvatī through the maids, the lord of the mountains carefully considered the proposal and said:

## \|\| 4.22.8 \|\|

*himālaya uvāca \|*  
*mahyaṃ ca rocate'tyarthaṃ menāyai rucyatāṃ punaḥ \|*  
*yathedaṃ bhavitavyaṃ ca kimataḥ paramuttamam \|\| 8 \|\|*

Himācala said:—

8\. This appeals to me. I it appeals to Menā as it ought to be, what else can be a better course?

## \|\| 4.22.9 \|\|

*sāphalyaṃ tu madīyasya kulasya ca na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*mātre tu rucyate cedvai tataḥ śubhataraṃ nu kim \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. There is no doubt about it that my House will be fortunate. If her mother also likes this, what can be more auspicious than this?

## \|\| 4.22.10 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityevaṃ vacanaṃ pitrā proktaṃ śrutvā tu te tadā \|*  
*jagmaturmātaraṃ sakhyau tadājñapte tayā saha \|\| 10 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

10\. After hearing the words spoken by her father and (in a way) commanded by him, the two maids went to her mother along with her.

## \|\| 4.22.11 \|\|

*gatvā tu mātaraṃ tasyāḥ pārvatyāste ca nārada \|*  
*supraṇamya karo badhvocaturvacanamādarāt \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. O Nārada, approaching Pārvatī’s mother, they bowed down and with palms joined in reverence they respectfully spoke thus.

## \|\| 4.22.12 \|\|

*sakhyāvūcatuḥ \|*  
*mātastvaṃ vacanaṃ putryāḥ śṛṇu devi namo'stu te \|*  
*suprasannatayā tadvai śrutvā kartumihārhasi \|\| 12 \|\|*

The maids said:—

12\. O mother, O gentle lady, please listen to the words of your daughter. Obeisance be to you. You will listen with pleasure and act accordingly.

## \|\| 4.22.13 \|\|

*taptukāmā tu te putrī śivārthaṃ paramaṃ tapaḥ \|*  
*prāptānujñā pituścaiva tubhyaṃ ca paripṛcchati \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. For the sake of attaining Śiva, your daughter wishes to perform a severe penance. She has secured the permission of her father. She now wants to seek it from you.

## \|\| 4.22.14 \|\|

*iyaṃ svarūpasāphalyaṃ kartukāmā pativrate \|*  
*tvadājñayā yadi jāyeta tapyate ca tathā tapaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. O chaste lady, she is desirous of making her beauty fruitful. If your permission too is received, the penance can be performed.

## \|\| 4.22.15 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*ityuktvā ca tatassakhyau tūṣṇīmāstāṃ munīśvara \|*  
*nāṃgīcakāra menā sā tadvākyaṃ khinnamānasā \|\| 15 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

15\. O excellent sage, after saying this, the maids became silent. Distressed in mind, Mena did not accept the proposal.

## \|\| 4.22.16 \|\|

*tatassā pārvatī prāha svayamevātha mātaram \|*  
*karau baddhvā vinītātmā smṛtvā śivapadāṃbujam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Then Pārvatī herself spoke to her mother joining her palms in humility and remembering the lotus-like feet of Śiva.

## \|\| 4.22.17 \|\|

*pārvatyuvāca \|*  
*mātastaptuṃ gamiṣyāmi prātaḥ prāptuṃ maheśvaram \|*  
*anujānīhi māṃ gaṃtuṃ tapase'dya tapovanam \|\| 17 \|\|*

Pārvatī said:—

17\. O mother, I shall be going in the morning for performing penance to achieve Śiva. Please permit me to go to the penance-grove for the task.

## \|\| 4.22.18 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya vacaḥ putryā menā duḥkha mupāgatā \|*  
*sopāhūya tadā putrīmuvāca vikalā satī \|\| 18 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

18\. On hearing the words of her daughter, Menā was distressed. That chaste lady called her daughter near and spoke to her in dejection.

## \|\| 4.22.19 \|\|

*menovāca \|*  
*duḥkhitāsi śive putrī tapastaptuṃ purā yadi \|*  
*tapaścara gṛhe'dya tvaṃ na bahirgaccha pārvati \|\| 19 \|\|*

Menā said:—

19\. O daughter Śiva, if you are distressed, if you wish to perform penance, you can do it at home. O Pārvatī, do not go out.

## \|\| 4.22.20 \|\|

*kutra yāsi tapaḥ kartuṃ devāssaṃti gṛhe mama \|*  
*tīrthāni ca samastāni kṣetrāṇi vividhāni ca \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Where do you wish to go for performing penance? All the deities are in my house. All the holy centres and the different temples too are here.

## \|\| 4.22.21 \|\|

*kartavyo na haṭhaḥ putri gaṃtavyaṃ na bahiḥ kvacit \|*  
*sādhitaṃ kiṃ tvayā pūrvaṃ punaḥ kiṃ sādhayiṣyasi \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Do not be stubborn, dear daughter. You shall not go out of your home. What did you achieve when you went out previously? What are you going to achieve at present?

## \|\| 4.22.22 \|\|

*śarīraṃ komalaṃ vatse tapastu kaṭhinaṃ mahat \|*  
*evasmāttu tvayā kāryaṃ tapo'tra na bahirvraja \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Dear child, slender is your body and hard is the penance. Hence you shall perform penance here. You shall not go out.

## \|\| 4.22.23 \|\|

*strīṇāṃ tapovanagatirna śrutā kāmanārthinī \|*  
*tasmāttvaṃ putri mā kārṣīstaporthaṃ gamanaṃ prati \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. For a woman to go to a penance-grove for the realisation of her desire is what we have never heard of before. Hence, dear daughter, do not go out for penance.

## \|\| 4.22.24 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*ityevaṃ bahudhā putrī tanmātrā vinavāritā \|*  
*saṃvede na sukhaṃ kiṃcidvinārādhya maheśvaram \|\| 24 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

24\. Thus, in various ways, the daughter was dissuaded by her mother. But she did not find any pleasure except in propitiating Śiva.

## \|\| 4.22.25 \|\|

*taponiṣiddhā tapase vanaṃ gaṃtuṃ ca menayā \|*  
*hetunā tena someti nāma prāpa śivā tadā \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Pārvatī acquired the name Umā since she was prevented from going to forest by Menā and forbidden to perform penance.

## \|\| 4.22.26 \|\|

*atha tāṃ dukhitāṃ jñātvā menā śailapriyā śivām \|*  
*nideśaṃ sā dadau tasyāḥ pārvatyāstapase mune \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. O sage, on realising that Pārvatī was quite dejected, Menā, the beloved of the mountain, permitted her to perform penance.

## \|\| 4.22.27 \|\|

*māturājñāṃ ca saṃprāpya suvratā munisattama \|*  
*tataḥ svāṃte sukhaṃ lebhe pārvatī smṛtaśaṃkarā \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. O excellent sage, on getting permission from her mother, Pārvatī remembered Śiva and felt happy.

## \|\| 4.22.28 \|\|

*mātaraṃ pitaraṃ sātha praṇipatya mudā śivā \|*  
*sakhībhyāṃ ca śivaṃ smṛtvā tapastaptuṃ samudgatā \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Bowing to her parents with joy, Pārvatī remember

ed Śiva and set out for performing penance along with her maids.

## \|\| 4.22.29 \|\|

*hitvā matānyanekāni vastrāṇi vividhāni ca \|*  
*valkalāni dhṛtānyāśu mauṃjīṃ baddhvā tu śobhanām \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Discarding all the fine clothes of her taste, she wore tree-barks and the fine girdle of Muñja grass.

## \|\| 4.22.30 \|\|

*hitvā hāraṃ tathā carmma mṛgasya paramaṃ dhṛtam \|*  
*jagāma tapase tatra gaṃgāvataraṇaṃ prati \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. She eschewed necklace and wore the pure deer skin. She arrived at Gaṅgāvataraṇa for performing penance.

## \|\| 4.22.31 \|\|

*śaṃbhunā kurvatā dhyānaṃ yatra dagdho manobhavaḥ \|*  
*gaṃgāvataraṇo nāma prastho himavatassa ca \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. The Gaṅgāvataraṇa was in the Himālayan ridge where Kāma was burnt by Śiva who was performing meditation.

## \|\| 4.22.32 \|\|

*haraśūnyo'tha dadṛśe sa prastho himabhūbhṛtaḥ \|*  
*kālyā tatretya bhostāta pārvatyā jagadambayā \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Oh dear, that Himalayan ridge devoid of Śiva was painfully seen by Pārvatī, the mother of the universe, the daughter of the mountain.

## \|\| 4.22.33 \|\|

*yatra sthitvā purā śaṃbhustaptavāndustaraṃ tapaḥ \|*  
*tatra kṣaṇaṃ tu sā sthitvā babhūva virahārditā \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. She stood for a while in the place where formerly Śiva had performed penance and became dispirited by the pangs of separation.

## \|\| 4.22.34 \|\|

*hā hareti śivā tatra rudantī sā giressutā \|*  
*vilalāpātiduḥkhārtā cintāśokasamanvitā \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Crying aloud “Alas O Śiva” she, the daughter of the mountain, lamented sorrowfully and anxiously.

## \|\| 4.22.35 \|\|

*tataścireṇa sā mohaṃ dhairyyā tsaṃstabhya pārvatī \|*  
*niyamāyā'bhavattatra dīkṣitā himavatsutā \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Suppressing the delusion with fortitude after a long time Pārvatī, the daughter of Himavat, got herself initiated for the observance of ritualistic activities.

## \|\| 4.22.36 \|\|

*tapaścakāra sā tatra śṛṃgitīrthe mahottame \|*  
*gaurīśikhara nāmāsīttattapaḥkaraṇāddhi tat \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. She performed penance in the excellent holy centre Śṛṅgitīrtha which (later) acquired the title “Gaurī-Śikhara” due to her performance of penance thereon.

## \|\| 4.22.37 \|\|

*suṃdarāśca drumāstatra pavitrāśśivayā mune \|*  
*āropitāḥ parīkṣārthaṃ tapasaḥ phalabhāginaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. O sage, many beautiful holy plants were laid there by Pārvatī for testing the fruitfulness of her penance.

## \|\| 4.22.38 \|\|

*bhūbhiśuddhiṃ tataḥ kṛtvā vedīṃ nirmāya sundarī \|*  
*tathā tapassamārabdhaṃ munīnāmapi duṣkaram \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Neatly cleaning the ground, the beautiful lady built the altar. Then the penance, difficult to be performed even by the sages, was begun.

## \|\| 4.22.39 \|\|

*vigṛhya manasā sarvāṇīṃdriyāṇi sahāśu sā \|*  
*samupasthānike tatra cakāra paramaṃ tapaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Suppressing her sense-organs with her mind, she started the great penance in a place within the proximity.

## \|\| 4.22.40 \|\|

*grīṣme ca parito vahniṃ prajvalaṃtaṃ divāniśam \|*  
*kṛtvā tasthau ca tanmadhye satataṃ japatī manuma \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. In the summer she kept a perpetually blazing fire all round and remaining within continued muttering the mantra.

## \|\| 4.22.41 \|\|

*satataṃ caiva varṣāsu sthaṃḍile susthirāsanā \|*  
*śilāpṛṣṭhe ca saṃsiktā babhūva jaladhārayā \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. In the rainy season she continuously remained sitting on the bare ground on the rock and got herself drenched by the downpour of rain.

## \|\| 4.22.42 \|\|

*śīte jalāṃtare śaśvattasthau sā bhaktitatparā \|*  
*anāhārātapattatra nīhāre niśāsu ca \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. During the winter, with great devotion she remained in water throughout. During snowfall and in the nights too she performed her penance observing fast.

## \|\| 4.22.43 \|\|

*evaṃ tapaḥ prakurvāṇā paṃcākṣarajape ratā \|*  
*dadhyau śivaṃ śivā tatra sarvakāmaphalapradam \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Performing such austerities and engrossed in the muttering of the five-syllabled mantra, Pārvatī meditated on Śiva, the bestower of fruits of our cherished desires.

## \|\| 4.22.44 \|\|

*svāropitācchubhānvṛkṣānsakhībhissiṃcatī mudā \|*  
*pratyahaṃ sāvakāśe sā tatrātithyamakalpayat \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Everyday during leisure time she used to water the trees planted by her along with her maids and extended acts of hospitality.

## \|\| 4.22.45 \|\|

*vātaścaiva tathā śītavṛṣṭiśca vividhā tathā \|*  
*dussaho'pi tathā gharmmastayā sehe sucittayā \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Chill gusts of wind, cool showers, and unbearable heat she bore with equanimity.

## \|\| 4.22.46 \|\|

*duḥkhaṃ ca vividhaṃ tatra gaṇitaṃ na tayāgatam \|*  
*kevalaṃ mana ādhāya śive sāsītsthitā mune \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Different sorts of worries she did not mind at all. O sage, fixing her mind in Śiva alone she remained firm and steady.

## \|\| 4.22.47 \|\|

*prathamaṃ phalabhogena dvitīyaṃ parṇabhojanaiḥ \|*  
*tapaḥ prakurvatī devī kramānninye'mitāḥ samāḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. The first year she spent in taking fruits, the second in taking leaves, in the course of her penance. She spent many years thus.

## \|\| 4.22.48 \|\|

*tataḥ parṇānyapi śivā nirasya himavatsutā \|*  
*nirāhārābhavaddevī tapaścaraṇasaṃratā \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Then Śivā, the daughter of Himavat, eschewed even the leaves. She did not take any food. She was engrossed in the performance of penance.

## \|\| 4.22.49 \|\|

*āhāre tyaktaparṇābhūdyasmāddhimavataḥ sutaḥ \|*  
*tena devairaparṇeti kathitā nāmataḥ śivā \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Since she, the daughter of Himavat, eschewed leaves from her diet she was called Aparṇā by the gods.

## \|\| 4.22.50 \|\|

*ekā pādasthitā sāsīcchivaṃ saṃsmṛtya pārvatī \|*  
*paṃcākṣaraṃ japaṃtī ca manuṃ tepe tapo mahat \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Then Pārvatī performed great penance standing on one leg and remembering Śiva, she continued muttering the five-syllabled mantra.

## \|\| 4.22.51 \|\|

*cīravalkalasaṃvītā jaṭāsaṃghātadhāriṇī \|*  
*śivaciṃtanasaṃsaktā jigāya tapasā munīm \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Clad in barks of trees, wearing matted hair and eager in the meditation of Śiva, she surpassed even sages by her penance.

## \|\| 4.22.52 \|\|

*evaṃ tasyāstapasyantyā ciṃtayaṃtyā maheśvaram \|*  
*trīṇi varṣa sahasrāṇi jagmuḥ kālyāstapovane \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Pārvatī thus spent three thousand years in the penance-grove performing penance and meditating on lord Śiva.

## \|\| 4.22.53 \|\|

*ṣaṣṭivarṣasahasrāṇi yatra tepe tapo haraḥ \|*  
*tatra kṣaṇamathoṣitvā ciṃtayāmāsa sā śivā \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Remaining for a short while in the place where Śiva had performed penance for sixty thousand years, Pārvatī thought like this.

## \|\| 4.22.54 \|\|

*niyamasthāṃ mahādeva kiṃ māṃ jānāsi nādhunā \|*  
*yenāhaṃ suciraṃ tena nānuyātā tavoratā \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Does not the Supreme lord know me observing these ritualistic activities now? Wherefore am I not followed by him though engaged in penance?

## \|\| 4.22.55 \|\|

*loke vede ca giriśo munibhirgīyate sadā \|*  
*śaṃkarasya hi sarvajñassarvātmā sarvadarśanaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. In the Śāstras and the Vedas, lord Śiva is always sung in praise by the sages as the bestower of welfare, omniscient, all-pervading and all-seer.

## \|\| 4.22.56 \|\|

*sarvabhūtiprado devassarvabhāvānubhāvanaḥ \|*  
*bhaktābhīṣṭaprado nityaṃ sarvakleśanivāraṇaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. The lord is the bestower of all riches, the moulder of fine emotions, the bestower of the desires of devotees and the remover of their distress.

## \|\| 4.22.57 \|\|

*sarvakāmānparityajya yadi cāhaṃ vṛṣadhvaje \|*  
*anuraktā tadā sotra saṃprasīdatu śaṃkaraḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. If I am devoted to the bull-bannered lord, discarding all desires, may He be pleased with me.

## \|\| 4.22.58 \|\|

*yadi nārada tatroktamaṃtro japtaśśarākṣaraḥ \|*  
*subhaktyā vidhinā nityaṃ saṃprasīdatu śaṃkaraḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. If the mantra of the Nārada Tantra, consisting of five syllables has been continuously repeated by me with great devotion may He be pleased with me.

## \|\| 4.22.59 \|\|

*yadi bhaktyā śivasyāhaṃ nirvikārā yathoditam \|*  
*sarveśvarasya cātyaṃtaṃ saṃprasīdatu śaṃkaraḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. If I am a devotee without aberrations of Śiva, the lord of all, may He be extremely pleased with me.

## \|\| 4.22.60 \|\|

*evaṃ ciṃtayatī nityaṃ tepe sā suciraṃ tapaḥ \|*  
*adhomukhī nirvikārā jaṭāvalkaladhāriṇī \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Pondering frequently like this incessantly, she performed penance for a long time, with her face turned downwards, her apparel of bark and mind without any aberrations.

## \|\| 4.22.61 \|\|

*tathā tayā tapastaptaṃ munīnāmapi duṣkaram \|*  
*smṛtvā ca puruṣāstatra paramaṃ vismayaṃ gatāḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. She performed penance difficult to be performed even by the sages, so much so that people were struck with surprise.

## \|\| 4.22.62 \|\|

*tattapodarśanārthaṃ hi samājagmuśca te'khilāḥ \|*  
*dhanyānnijānmanyamānā jagaduśceti sammatāḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. All of them came there to witness her penance. Considering themselves blessed, they proclaimed thus approvingly.

## \|\| 4.22.63 \|\|

*mahatāṃ dharmmavṛddheṣu gamanaṃ śreya ucyate \|*  
*pramāṇaṃ tapaso nāsti mānyo dharmmassadā budhaiḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. “To follow the standard of the virtuous personages is declared to be conducive to greatness. There is no delimitation in penance. Virtue shall be honoured by the wise always.

## \|\| 4.22.64 \|\|

*śrutvā dṛṣṭvā tapo'syāstu kimanyaiḥ kriyate tapaḥ \|*  
*asmāttapo'dhikaṃ loke na bhūtaṃ na bhaviṣyati \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. After seeing or hearing about the penance of this lady what penance will be pursued by a man? A penance greater than this has never been before, nor will it ever be”.

## \|\| 4.22.65 \|\|

*jalpaṃta iti te sarve supraśasya śivātapaḥ \|*  
*jagmuḥ svaṃ dhāma muditāḥ kaṭhināṃgāśca ye hyapi \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Saying thus, they praised the penance of Pārvatī and joyously returned to their abodes. Even persons of sturdy countenance praised her penance.

## \|\| 4.22.66 \|\|

*anyacchṛṇu maharṣe tvaṃ prabhāvaṃ tapaso'dhunā \|*  
*pārvatyā jagadambāyāḥ parāścaryyakaraṃ mahat \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. O sage, listen to another surprising influence of the penance of Pārvatī, the mother of the universe.

## \|\| 4.22.67 \|\|

*tadāśramagatā ye ca svabhāvena virodhinaḥ \|*  
*tepyāsaṃstatprabhāveṇa virodharahi tāstadā \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Even the naturally inimical beings in and around her hermitage became free from animosity due to her power.

## \|\| 4.22.68 \|\|

*siṃhā gāvaśca satataṃ rāgādidoṣasaṃyutāḥ \|*  
*tanmahimnā ca te tatra nābādhaṃta parasparam \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Lions and cows prone to the passions of love, hatred etc. ceased to harass one another, thanks to her greatness.

## \|\| 4.22.69 \|\|

*athānye ca muniśreṣṭha mārjjārā mūṣakādayaḥ \|*  
*nisargādvairiṇo yatra vikriyaṃte sma na kvacit \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. O excellent sage, creatures like cats, mice etc. who are born enemies to one another did not exhibit any bad characteristics there.

## \|\| 4.22.70 \|\|

*vṛkṣāśca saphalāstatra tṛṇāni vividhāni ca \|*  
*puṣpāṇi ca vicitrāṇi tatrāsanmunisattama \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. O excellent sage, trees bore fruits, grasses grew in plenty and flowers of variegated nature and colour blossomed there.

## \|\| 4.22.71 \|\|

*tadvanaṃ ca tadā sarvaṃ kailāsenopamānvitam \|*  
*jātaṃ ca tapastasyāssiddhirūpamabhūttadā \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. The entire forest became comparable to Kailāsa as it were the achievement of her penance.

## Chapter 23 - Attempt of Himavat to dissuade Pārvatī; gods go to meet Śiva

## \|\| 4.23.1 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*evaṃ tapatyāṃ pārvatyāṃ śivaprāptau munīśvara \|*  
*cirakālo vyatīyāya prādurbhūto haro na hi \|\| 1 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

1\. O excellent sage, while Pārvatī was engaged in penance thus for attaining Śiva, a long time elapsed but Śiva did not appear.

## \|\| 4.23.2 \|\|

*himālayastadāgatya pārvatīṃ kṛtaniścayām \|*  
*sabhāryassasutāmātya uvāca parameśvarīm \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Then Himavat came there along with his wife, sons and ministers and spoke to Pārvatī, who had resolved to continue her penance.

## \|\| 4.23.3 \|\|

*himālaya uvāca \|*  
*mā khidyatāṃ mahābhāge tapasānena pārvatī \|*  
*rudro na dṛśyate bāle virakto nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

Himavat said:—

3\. O Pārvatī, O fortunate one, do not torture yourself by this penance. Dear girl, Śiva is not to be seen. Certainly he is detached.

## \|\| 4.23.4 \|\|

*tvaṃ tanvī sukumārāṃgī tapasā ca vimohitā \|*  
*bhaviṣyasi na saṃdehassatyaṃ satyaṃ vadāmi te \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. You are a young woman of tender limbs. You will be overpowered and exhausted by this penance. There is no doubt about it. I am speaking the truth.

## \|\| 4.23.5 \|\|

*tasmāduttiṣṭha caihi tvaṃ svagṛhaṃ varavarṇini \|*  
*kiṃ tena tava rudreṇa yena dagdhaḥ purā smaraḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Hence, O comely lady, get up. Come back to our house. Of what avail is Śiva by whom Kāma has been reduced to ashes?

## \|\| 4.23.6 \|\|

*ato hi nirvikāra tvāttvāmādātuṃ varāṃ harāḥ \|*  
*nāgamiṣyati deveśi taṃ kathaṃ prārthayiṣyasi \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. O goddess, hence not being emotional, Śiva will not come to claim you as the excellent lady. Why do you yearn for him?

## \|\| 4.23.7 \|\|

*gaganastho yathā caṃdro grahītuṃ na hi śakyate \|*  
*tathaiva durgamaṃ śaṃbhuṃ jānīhi tvamihānaghe \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Just as the moon in the sky cannot be caught, O sinless girl, so also Śiva is inaccessible. Know this.

## \|\| 4.23.8-9 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*tathaiva menayā coktā tathā sahyādriṇā satī \|*  
*meruṇā maṃdareṇaiva mainākena tathaiva sā \|\| 8 \|\|*

*evamanyaiḥ kṣitibhaiśca krauṃcādibhiranāturā \|*  
*tathaiva girijā proktā nānāvādavidhāyibhiḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

8-9. The same thing was said by Menā, Sahya\[1\] mountain, Meru,\[2\] Mandara\[3\], Maināka\[4\] and Krauñca and others, The unafflicted Pārvatī was thus sought to be dissuaded by various arguments.

## \|\| 4.23.10 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*evaṃ proktā yadā tanvī sā sarvaistapasi sthitā \|*  
*uvāca prahasaṃtyeva himavaṃtaṃ śucismitā \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. When she was thus addressed by all of them, she with a broad smile, spoke to Himavat.

## \|\| 4.23.11 \|\|

*pārvatyuvāca \|*  
*purā proktaṃ mayā tāta mātaḥ kiṃ vismṛtaṃ tvayā \|*  
*adhunāpi pratijñāṃ ca śṛṇudhvaṃ mama bāṃdhavāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

Pārvatī said:—

11\. O father, O mother, O kinsmen, have all of you forgotten what I had said formerly. Even now listen to my vow.

## \|\| 4.23.12 \|\|

*viraktosau mahādevo yena dagdhā ruṣā smaraḥ \|*  
*taṃ toṣayāmi tapasā śaṃkaraṃ bhaktavatsalam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. This great God by whom Kāma has been burnt in fury is detached (you say). I shall propitiate him, by means of penance. He is favourably disposed to His devotees.

## \|\| 4.23.13 \|\|

*sarve bhavaṃto gacchaṃtu svaṃ svaṃ dhāma praharṣitāḥ \|*  
*bhaviṣyatyeva tuṣṭo'sau nātra kāryyā vicāraṇā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. All of you please go to your respective abodes with delight. He will certainly be pleased. You need not be anxious over this.

## \|\| 4.23.14 \|\|

*dagdho hi madano yena yena dagdhaṃ girervanam \|*  
*tamānayiṣye cātraiva tapasā keva lena hi \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. With my penance alone here itself, I shall bring Him who burnt Kāma and the mountainous forest.

## \|\| 4.23.15 \|\|

*tapobalena mahatā susevyo hi sadāśivaḥ \|*  
*jānīdhvaṃ hi mahābhāgāssatyaṃ satyaṃ vadāmi vaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Sadāśiva can be easily served through penance. Ye fortunate Sirs, please know this truth. I am telling you the truth.

## \|\| 4.23.16 \|\|

*ābhāṣya caivaṃ girijā ca menakāṃ mainākabaṃdhuṃ pitaraṃ himālayam \|*  
*tūṣṇīṃ babhūvāśu subhāṣiṇī śivā samaṃdaraṃ parvatarājabālikā \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. After addressing thus, her father Himalaya, her mother Menakā, her brothers Maināka and Mandara, the eloquent Pārvatī, the daughter of the king of mountains, kept quiet.

## \|\| 4.23.17 \|\|

*jagmustathoktāḥ śivayā hi parvatā yathāgatenāpi vicakṣaṇāste \|*  
*praśaṃsamānā girijā muhurmuhussuvismitā hemanageśvarādyāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Thus addressed by Pārvatī, the lord of mountains and the other mountains went back the way they came, surprised within and praising her.

## \|\| 4.23.18 \|\|

*gateṣu teṣu sūryeṣu sakhībhiḥ parivāritā \|*  
*tapastepe tadadhikaṃ paramārthasuniścayā \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. After all of them had departed, she with firm resolve in the great Truth, accompanied by her maids performed a severe penance.

## \|\| 4.23.19 \|\|

*tapasā mahatā tena taptamāsīccarācaram \|*  
*trailokyaṃ hi muniśreṣṭha sadevāsuramānuṣam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. O excellent sage, by that great penance the three worlds including the gods, Asuras and men, nay all the mobile and immobile beings, became heated.

## \|\| 4.23.20-21 \|\|

*tadā surāsurāḥ sarve yakṣakinnaracāraṇāḥ \|*  
*siddhāssādhyāśca munayo vidyādharamahoragāḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*saprajāpatayaścaiva guhyakāśca tathāpare \|*  
*kaṣṭāt kaṣṭataraṃ prāptāḥ kāraṇaṃ na viduḥ sma tat \|\| 21 \|\|*

20-21. The Prajāpatis, the Guhyakas and others experienced great distress but could not understand the reason thereof. The gods, Asuras, Yakṣas, Kinnaras, Cāraṇas, Siddhas, Sādhyas, the sages, the serpents and the Vidyādharas too had the same experience.

## \|\| 4.23.22 \|\|

*sarve militvā śakrādyā gurumāmaṃtrya vihvalāḥ \|*  
*sumerau taptasarvāṃgā vidhiṃ māṃ śaraṇaṃ yayuḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. All of them, Indra and others, who were extremely agitated, took leave of their preceptor and sought refuge in me on the mountain Sumeru. All their limbs had been scorched.

## \|\| 4.23.23 \|\|

*tatra gatvā praṇamyāśu vihvalā naṣṭasutviṣaḥ \|*  
*ūcussarve ca saṃstūya hyaikapadyena māṃ hi te \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Devoid of splendour, and agitated excessively they bowed to and eulogised me. They spoke simultaneously thus.

## \|\| 4.23.24 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*tvayā sṛṣṭamidaṃ sarvaṃ jagadetaccarācaram \|*  
*saṃtaptamati kasmādvai na jñātaṃ kāraṇaṃ vibho \|\| 24 \|\|*

The gods said:—

24\. “O lord, the whole of this universe consisting of the mobile and immobile has been created by you. Why is it scorched so much? We do not understand.

## \|\| 4.23.25 \|\|

*tadbrūhi kāraṇaṃ brahman jñātumarhasi naḥ prabho \|*  
*dagdhabhūtatanūndevān tvatto nānyo'sti rakṣaka \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. O Brahmā, please tell us the reason. O lord, you shall protect us, the gods whose bodies have been scorched. There is none else to protect us”.

## \|\| 4.23.26-27 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya vacasteṣāmahaṃ smṛtvā śivaṃ hṛdā \|*  
*vicārya manasā sarvaṃ girijāyāstapaḥ phalam \|\| 26 \|\|*

*dagdhaṃ viśvamiti jñātvā taiḥ sarvairiha sādarāt \|*  
*haraye tatkathayituṃ kṣīrābdhimagamaṃ drutam \|\| 27 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

26-27. On hearing their words I remembered Śiva and pondered over everything. I realised that the universe was scorched as a result of Pārvatī’s penance. Accompanied by them I hastened respectfully to the milk ocean to inform Viṣṇu about it.

## \|\| 4.23.28 \|\|

*tatra gatvā hariṃ dṛṣṭvā vilasaṃtaṃ sukhāsane \|*  
*supraṇamya susaṃstūya prāvocaṃ sāṃjaliḥ suraiḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Reaching that place along with the gods, I saw Viṣṇu shining lustrously on a splendid seat. Bowing to and eulogising him with palms joined in reverence I spoke.

## \|\| 4.23.29 \|\|

*trāhi trāhi mahāviṣṇo taptānnaśśaraṇāgatān \|*  
*tapasogreṇa pārvatyāstapatyāḥ parameṇa hi \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. “Save, save, O Viṣṇu, save us who have sought refuge in you, being scorched by the great and severe penance of Pārvatī.

## \|\| 4.23.30 \|\|

*ityākarṇya vacasteṣāmasmadādi divaukasām \|*  
*śeṣāsane samāviṣṭo'smānuvāca rameśvaraḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. On hearing these words of mine on behalf of the heaven-dwellers, lord Viṣṇu seated on the Serpent couch spoke to us:—

## \|\| 4.23.31 \|\|

*\|\| viṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*jñātaṃ sarvaṃ nidānaṃ me pārvatī tapasodya vai \|*  
*yuṣmābhissahitastvadya vrajāmi parameśvaram \|\| 31 \|\|*

Viṣṇu said:—

31\. The entire reason has been known to me. It is caused by Pārvatī’s penance. I shall now go to lord śiva accompanied by all of you.

## \|\| 4.23.32 \|\|

*mahādevaṃ prārthayāmo girijāprāpaṇāya tam \|*  
*pāṇigrahārthamadhunā lokānāṃ svastaye'marāḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. O gods, we shall request lord Śiva to approach Pārvatī and marry her for the welfare of all the worlds.

## \|\| 4.23.33 \|\|

*varaṃ dātuṃ śivāyai hi devadeva pinākadhṛk \|*  
*yathā ceṣyati tatraiva kariṣyāmo'dhunā hi tat \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. We shall do everything necessary to make the Pināka-bearing lord of the gods go there to grant the boon to Śivā.

## \|\| 4.23.34 \|\|

*tasmādvayaṃ gamiṣyāmo yatra rudro mahāprabhuḥ \|*  
*tapasogreṇa saṃyukto'dyāste paramamaṃgalaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Therefore now we shall go to the place where the great lord Śiva of severe penance, the conferrer of all auspicious things, stays.

## \|\| 4.23.35 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*viṣṇostadvacanaṃ śrutvā sarva ūcussurādayaḥ \|*  
*mahābhītā haṭhāt kruddhāddagdhukāmāt layaṃkarāt \|\| 35 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

35\. On hearing those words of Viṣṇu, the gods and the rest became excessively afraid of Śiva, the furious, the annihilator and the one desirous of burning everything.

## \|\| 4.23.36 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*mahābhayaṃkaraṃ kruddhaṃ kālānalasamaprabham \|*  
*na yāsyāmo vayaṃ sarve virūpākṣaṃ mahāprabham \|\| 36 \|\|*

The gods said:—

36\. We dare not go near the great lord Śiva who is very terrifying, furious and who has the burning brilliance of the deadly fire of dissolution.

## \|\| 4.23.37 \|\|

*yathā dagdhaḥ purā tena madano duratikramaḥ \|*  
*tathaiva krodhayukto naḥ sa dhakṣyati na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Undoubtedly he will burn us all in His anger as Kāma, the indefatigable god, has been burnt by him.

## \|\| 4.23.38 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|\| tadākarṇya vacasteṣāṃ śakrādīnāṃ rameśvaraḥ \|*  
*sāṃtvayaṃstānsurānsarvānprovāca sa harirmune \|\| 38 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

38\. O sage, on hearing the words of Indra and others, Viṣṇu, the lord of Lakṣmī spoke these words, consoling all the gods.

## \|\| 4.23.39 \|\|

*\|\| hariruvāca \|*  
*he surā madvacaḥ prītyā śṛṇutādarato'khilāḥ \|*  
*na vo dhakṣyati sa svāmī devānāṃ bhayanāśanaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

Viṣṇu said:—

39\. O gods, listen with pleasure and attention to my words. The lord, the destroyer of the fear of gods, will not consume you in fire.

## \|\| 4.23.40 \|\|

*tasmādbhavadbhirgaṃtavyaṃ mayā sārddhaṃ vicakṣaṇaiḥ \|*  
*śaṃbhuṃ śubhakaraṃ matvā śaraṇaṃ tasya suprabho \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Considering Śiva to be benevolent you shall shrewdly seek refuge in Him.

## \|\| 4.23.41 \|\|

*śivaṃ purāṇaṃ puruṣamadhīśaṃ vareṇyarūpaṃ hi paraṃ purāṇam \|*  
*tapojuṣāṇāṃ paramātmarūpaṃ parātparaṃ taṃ śaraṇaṃ vrajāmaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. We shall all seek refuge in Śiva, the ancient Puruṣa, the lord, of excellent features, greater than the greatest, the supreme self, the great one resorting to penance.

## \|\| 4.23.42 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*evamuktāstadā devā viṣṇunā prabhavi ṣṇunā \|*  
*jagmussarve tena saha draṣṭukāmāḥ pinākinam \|\| 42 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

42\. Thus urged by the great lord Viṣṇu they set out desirous of seeing the Pināka-bearing lord Śiva.

## \|\| 4.23.43 \|\|

*prathamaṃ śailaputryāstattapo draṣṭuṃ tadāśramam \|*  
*jagmurmārgavaśātsarve viṣṇvādyassakutūhalāḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. At first Viṣṇu and others who were anxious to see the penance of Pārvatī went to her hermitage which was on the way.

## \|\| 4.23.44 \|\|

*pārvatyāstu tapo dṛṣṭvā tejasā vyāpṛtāstadā \|*  
*praṇemustāṃ jagaddhātrīṃ tejorūpāṃ tapaḥ sthitām \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. On seeing the excellent penance of Pārvatī and being enveloped by her refulgence they bowed to her who was engaged in penance and who had brilliant features.

## \|\| 4.23.45 \|\|

*praśaṃsaṃtastapastasyāssākṣātsiddhitanossurāḥ \|*  
*jagmustatra tadā te ca yatrāste vṛṣabhadhvajaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. After praising the penance of Pārvatī whose body was achievement personified, the gods went to the place where the bull-bannered lord was present.

## \|\| 4.23.46 \|\|

*tatra gatvā ca te devāstvāṃ mune praiṣayaṃstadā \|*  
*paśyato dūratastasthuḥ kāmabhasmakṛtoharāt \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. After reaching there the gods sent you in, O sage, and stood at a distance from Śiva who had reduced Kāma to ashes. They were watching.

## \|\| 4.23.47 \|\|

*nārada tvaṃ śivasthānaṃ tadā gatvā'bhayassadā \|*  
*śivabhakto viśeṣeṇa prasannaṃ dṛṣṭavān prabhum \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. O Nārada, you the fearless devotee of Śiva approached Śiva and saw the lord extremely pleased.

## \|\| 4.23.48 \|\|

*punarāgatya yatnena devānāhūya tāṃstataḥ \|*  
*nināya śaṃkarasthānaṃ tadā viṣṇvādikānmune \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. O sage, you came back again and beckoning to the gods, with effort you took them, Viṣṇu and others, to Him.

## \|\| 4.23.49 \|\|

*atha viṣṇvādayassarve tatra gatvā śivaṃ prabhum \|*  
*dadṛśussukhamāsīnaṃ prasannaṃ bhaktavatsalam \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Then Viṣṇu and other gods went there and saw lord Śiva, favourably disposed to His devotees, delighted and comfortably seated.

## \|\| 4.23.50-51 \|\|

*yogapaṭṭasthitaṃ śaṃbhuṃ gaṇaiśca parivāritam \|*  
*taporūpaṃ dadhānaṃ ca parameśvararūpiṇam \|\| 50 \|\|*

*tato viṣṇurmayānye ca surasiddhamunīśvarāḥ \|*  
*praṇamya tuṣṭuvussūktairvedopaniṣadanvitaiḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

50-51. Then Viṣṇu, the gods, the Siddhas, the sages and I bowed to and eulogised Śiva seated in the Yogic posture, surrounded by the Gaṇas. He was seated in the form. of penance. We eulogised Him with hymns from the Vedas and Upaniṣads.

## Chapter 24 - Śiva consents to marry Pārvatī

## \|\| 4.24.1 \|\|

*\|\| devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*namo rudrāya devāya madanāṃtakarāya ca \|*  
*stutyāya bhūribhāsāya trinetrāya namonamaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

The gods said:—

1\. Obeisance to lord Śiva, obeisance to the destroyer of Kāma; obeisance, obeisance to one worthy of eulogy; to one of profuse splendour, to the three-eyed lord.

## \|\| 4.24.2 \|\|

*śipiviṣṭāya bhīmāya bhīmākṣāya namonamaḥ \|*  
*mahādevāya prabhave triviṣṭapataye namaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Obeisance to Śiva clad in skin; obeisance to the terrible, to the terrible-eyed, to great lord and to the lord of the three worlds.

## \|\| 4.24.3 \|\|

*tvaṃ nāthaḥ sarvalokānāṃ pitā mātā tvamīśvaraḥ \|*  
*śaṃbhurīśaśśaṃkarosi dayālustvaṃ viśeṣataḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. You are the lord of worlds; you are the father, the mother and the lord; you are Śiva the benefactor. You are particularly compassionate.

## \|\| 4.24.4 \|\|

*tvaṃ dhātā sarvajagatāṃ trātumarhasi naḥ prabho \|*  
*tvāṃ vinā kassamarthosti duḥkhanāśe maheśvara \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. You are the creator of all the worlds; O lord, you shall save us. O great God, except you who else is competent to destroy misery?

## \|\| 4.24.5 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya vacasteṣāṃ surāṇāṃ nandikeśvaraḥ \|*  
*kṛpayā parayā yukto vijñaptuṃ śaṃbhumārabhat \|\| 5 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

5\. On hearing these words of the gods, Nandikeśvara who was endowed with great sympathy began to inform Śiva.

## \|\| 4.24.6 \|\|

*\|\| naṃdikeśvara uvāca \|*  
*viṣṇvādayassuragaṇā munisiddhasaṃghāstvāṃ draṣṭumeva suravaryya viśeṣayaṃti \|*  
*kāryārthino'suravaraiḥ paribhartsya mānāssamyak parābhavapadaṃ paramaṃ prapannāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

Nandikeśvara said:—

6\. O foremost among the gods, Viṣṇu, other gods, the sages and Siddhas eulogise you in order to see you. They are being threatened by Asuras. Hence they seek some remedy and resort to thy feet, the seat of great fearlessness.

## \|\| 4.24.7 \|\|

*tasmāttvayā hi sarveśa trātavyā munayassurāḥ \|*  
*dīnabaṃdhurviśeṣeṇa tvamukto bhaktavatsalaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Hence, O lord of all, the sages and the gods shall be protected by you. You have been particularly mentioned as the kinsman of the distressed and favourably disposed towards your devotees.

## \|\| 4.24.8 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*evaṃ dayāvatā śaṃbhurvijñapto naṃdinā bhṛśam \|*  
*śanaiśśanairuparamaddhyānādunmīlya cākṣiṇī \|\| 8 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

8\. Śiva, who was thus informed by Nandin and who was extremely sympathetic, slowly reverted from His meditation and opened His eyes.

## \|\| 4.24.9 \|\|

*īśo'thoparataśśaṃbhustadā paramakovidaḥ \|*  
*samādheḥ paramātmāsau surānsarvānuvāca ha \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Then lord Śiva, the highly efficient great Ātman, reverted from His trance and spoke to the gods.

Śiva said.—

## \|\| 4.24.10 \|\|

*śaṃbhuruvāca \|*  
*kasmādyūyaṃ samāyātā matsamīpaṃ sureśvaraḥ \|*  
*haribrahmādayassarve brūta kāraṇamāśu tat \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. “O great gods, Viṣṇu, Brahmā and others, why have you come near me? Mention the reason for the same.”

## \|\| 4.24.11 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*iti śrutvā vacaśśambhossarve devā mudā'nvitāḥ \|*  
*viṣṇorvilokayāmāsurmukhaṃ vijñaptihetave \|\| 11 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

11\. On hearing these words of Śiva, all the gods rejoiced. They looked at Viṣṇu as if to induce him to speak.

## \|\| 4.24.12 \|\|

*atha viṣṇurmahābhakto devānāṃ hitakārakaḥ \|*  
*madīritamuvācedaṃ surakāryaṃ mahattaram \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Then Viṣṇu, the great devotee and benefactor of

the gods mentioned the matter of great importance of the gods as mentioned by me (before).

## \|\| 4.24.13 \|\|

*tārakeṇa kṛtaṃ śaṃbho devānāṃ paramādbhutam \|*  
*kaṣṭātkaṣṭataraṃ devā vijñaptuṃ sarva āgatāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

Viṣṇu said:—

13\. “O Śiva, all the gods have come here to submit to you their misery perpetrated mysteriously by Tāraka.

## \|\| 4.24.14-15 \|\|

*he śaṃbho tava putreṇaurasena hi bhaviṣyati \|*  
*nihatastārako daityo nānyathā mama bhāṣitam \|\| 14 \|\|*

*vicāryyetthaṃ mahādeva kṛpāṃ kuru namo'stu te \|*  
*devānsamuddhara svāmin kaṣṭāttārakanirmitāt \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. O Śiva, the demon Tāraka will be killed only by your self-begotten son and not otherwise. Ponder over what I have said and take pity on me. Obeisance, O great lord, to you. O lord, redeem the gods from the misery brought about by Tāraka.

## \|\| 4.24.16 \|\|

*tasmāttvayā girijā deva śaṃbho grahītavyā pāṇinā dakṣiṇena \|*  
*pāṇigraheṇaiva mahānubhāvāṃ dattāṃ girīṃdreṇa ca tāṃ kuruṣva \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Hence, O lord Śiva, Pārvatī shall be accepted by you and grasped with your right hand. Accept her hand as offered in marriage by the lord of mountains. She is full of noble attributes.

## \|\| 4.24.17 \|\|

*viṣṇostadvacanaṃ śrutvā prasanno hyabravīcchivaḥ \|*  
*darśayan sadgatiṃ teṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ yogatatparaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. On hearing those words of Viṣṇu, Śiva was pleased and said indicating to them the goal of the good, eager in Yogic feats as He was.

## \|\| 4.24.18-19 \|\|

*śiva uvāca \|*  
*yadā me svīkṛtā devī girijā sarvasuṃdarī \|*  
*tadā sarve sureṃdrāśca munayo ṛṣayastadā \|\| 18 \|\|*

*sakāmāśca bhaviṣyanti na kṣamāśca pare pathi \|*  
*jīvayiṣyati durgā sā pāṇigrahaṇatassmaram \|\| 19 \|\|*

Śiva said:—

18-19. “If goddess Pārvatī, the most beautiful lady were to be accepted by me, she will be able to resuscitate Kāma on account of the marriage. Then all the gods, sages and ascetics will become lusty and incompetent in the great path of Yoga.

## \|\| 4.24.20 \|\|

*madano hi mayā dagdhassarveṣāṃ kāryyasiddhaye \|\| \|*  
*brahmaṇo vacanādviṣṇo nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Kāma was burnt by me for the achievement of universal goal. It was at the suggestion of Brahmā, O Viṣṇu. No anxiety need be felt in this connection.

## \|\| 4.24.21 \|\|

*evaṃ vimṛśya manasā kāryākāryavyavasthitau \|*  
*sudhīḥ sarvaiśca deveṃdra haṭhaṃ no kartumarhasi \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. O lord of gods, O intelligent one, it is your duty not to be obdurate after considering the situation of what shall be done and what not.

## \|\| 4.24.22 \|\|

*dagdhe kāme mayā viṣṇo surakāryaṃ mahat kṛtam \|*  
*sarve tiṣṭhaṃtu niṣkāmā mayā saha suniścitam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. O Viṣṇu, a great favour to the gods has been done by me when Kāma was burnt. May ye all stay free from lust certainly along with me.

## \|\| 4.24.23 \|\|

*yathā'haṃ ca surāssarve tathā yūyamayatnataḥ \|*  
*tapaḥ paramasaṃyuktāḥ kariṣyadhvaṃ suduṣkaram \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Just as I, so also you, O gods, can without effort perform difficult tasks being endowed with the energy of great penance.

## \|\| 4.24.24 \|\|

*yūyaṃ samādhinā tena madanena vinā surāḥ \|*  
*paramānaṃdasaṃyuktā nirvikārā bhavaṃtu vai \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Kāma not being with you, you can be endowed with the supreme bliss and be free from aberrations by means of spiritual contemplation, O Gods.

## \|\| 4.24.25 \|\|

*purāvṛttaṃ smarakṛtaṃ vismṛtaṃ yadvidhe hare \|*  
*mahendra munayo devā yattatsarvaṃ vimṛśyatām \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. O Brahmā, O Viṣṇu, O Indra, O sages and O gods, what had been done by Kāma formerly and forgotten by you may be recollected and pondered over.

## \|\| 4.24.26 \|\|

*mahādhanurdhareṇaiva madanena haṭhātsurāḥ \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ dhyānavidhvaṃsaḥ kṛtastena purāpurā \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. O gods, meditation of everyone had been spoiled by the stubborn Kāma, the great archer formerly.

## \|\| 4.24.27 \|\|

*kāmo hi narakāyaiva tasmāt krodhobhijāyate \|*  
*krodhādbhavati saṃmoho mohācca bhraṃśate tapaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Kāma leads to hell; lust to anger, anger to delusion and delusion destroys penance.

## \|\| 4.24.28 \|\|

*kāmakrodhau parityājyau bhavadbhissurasattamaiḥ \|*  
*sarvaireva ca maṃtavyaṃ madvākyaṃ nānyathā kvacit \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Anger and lust shall be eschewed by you, the best of gods. My words shall be headed by you all and not otherwise.

## \|\| 4.24.29 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*evaṃ viśrāvya bhagavān mahādevo vṛṣadhvajaḥ \|*  
*surān pravācayāmāsa vidhiviṣṇū tathā munīm \|\| 29 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

29\. After saying thus, the bull-bannered lord Śiva expressed the wish that Brahmā, Viṣṇu, the gods and the sages, should speak.

## \|\| 4.24.30 \|\|

*tūṣṇīṃbhūto'bhavacchaṃbhurdhyānamāśritya vai punaḥ \|*  
*āste purā yathā sthāṇurgaṇaiśca parivāritaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Śiva became quiet after resorting to meditation again. Śiva, as before, was surrounded by His Gaṇas.

## \|\| 4.24.31-33 \|\|

*svātmānamātmanā śaṃbhurātmanyeva vyaciṃtayat \|*  
*niraṃjanaṃ nirābhāsaṃ nirvikāraṃ nirāmayam \|\| 31 \|\|*

*parātparataraṃ nityaṃ nirmamaṃ niravagraham \|*  
*śabdātītaṃ nirguṇaṃ ca jñānagamyaṃ parātparam \|\| 32 \|\|*

*evaṃ svarūpaṃ paramaṃ ciṃtayan dhyānamāsthitaḥ \|*  
*paramānaṃdasaṃmagno babhūva bahusūtikṛt \|\| 33 \|\|*

31-33. Śiva thought within Himself His own Soul, the form that is unsullied, free from distortions, aberrations and ailments, the form which is greater than the greatest, eternal, free from sense of possession, free from obsessions, beyond the ken of sounds and words, devoid of attributes and knowable through perfect wisdom. Thinking upon His own features thus in His meditation, the lord, the cause of great enjoyment and protection became engrossed in supreme bliss.

## \|\| 4.24.34 \|\|

*dhyānasthitaṃ ca sarveśaṃ dṛṣṭvā sarve divaukasaḥ \|*  
*hari śakrādayassarve naṃdinaṃ procurānatāḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. On seeing Śiva again engaged in meditation all the dwellers of heaven, Viṣṇu, Indra and others, humbly told Nandin.

## \|\| 4.24.35 \|\|

*\|\| devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*kiṃ vayaṃ karavāmādya virakto dhyānamāsthitaḥ \|*  
*śaṃbhustvaṃ śaṃkara sakhassarvajñaḥ śucisevakaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

The gods said:—

35\. What shall we do now? Śiva has become detached and has gone on meditation. You are a companion of Śiva and pure assistant. You are omniscient.

## \|\| 4.24.36 \|\|

*kenopāyena giriśaḥ prasannaḥ syādgaṇādhipa \|*  
*tadupāyaṃ samācakṣva vayaṃ tvaccharaṇaṃ gatāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. O chief of the Gaṇas, we seek refuge in you. Please guide us. What is the remedy by which Śiva can be propitiated?

## \|\| 4.24.37 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*iti vijñāpito devairmune harṣādibhistadā \|*  
*pratyuvāca surāṃstānsa naṃdī śaṃbhupriyo gaṇaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

37\. O sage, thus urged by the gods, Viṣṇu and others, Nandin, the favourite Gaṇa of Śiva replied to the gods.

## \|\| 4.24.38 \|\|

*naṃdīśvara uvāca \|*  
*he hare he vidhe śakranirjarā munayastathā \|*  
*śṛṇudhvaṃ vacanaṃ me hi śivasaṃtoṣakārakam \|\| 38 \|\|*

Nandīśvara said:—

38\. O Viṣṇu, O Brahmā, O Indra, O gods and O sages, pay heed to my words gratifying to Śiva.

## \|\| 4.24.39 \|\|

*yadi vo haṭha evādya śiva dāraparigrahe \|*  
*atidīnatayā sarve sunutiṃ kurutādarāt \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. If you persist still in your wish that Śiva shall marry, you shall eulogise with respect and piteous request.

## \|\| 4.24.40 \|\|

*bhaktervaśyo mahādevo na sādhāraṇatasturāḥ \|*  
*akāryamapi sadbhaktyā karoti parameśvaraḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. O gods, great lord cannot be made subservient by ordinary devotion. The supreme lord does even what shall not be done when moved by extraordinary devotion.

## \|\| 4.24.41 \|\|

*evaṃ kuruta sarve hi vidhiviṣṇumukhāḥ surāḥ \|*  
*yathāgatena mārgeṇānyathā gacchata mā ciram \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. O Brahmā, Viṣṇu and other gods, then act accordingly, otherwise go the way you have come. Tarry not.

## \|\| 4.24.42 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya vacastasya mune viṣṇvādayassurāḥ \|*  
*tatheti mattvā suprītyā śaṃkaraṃ tuṣṭuvurhi te \|\| 42 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

42\. O sage, on hearing his words, Viṣṇu and other gods, considering that it must be so, eulogised Śiva with pleasure.

## \|\| 4.24.43 \|\|

*devadeva mahādeva karuṇāsāgara prabho \|*  
*samuddhara mahākleśāttrāhi naśśaraṇāgatān \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. O great lord, lord of the gods, O ocean of mercy, lift us up from the great distress. Save us who have sought refuge in you.

## \|\| 4.24.44 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityevaṃ bahudīnoktyā tuṣṭuvuśśaṃkaraṃ surāḥ \|*  
*rurudussusvaraṃ sarve premavyākulamānasaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

44\. Thus the gods eulogised Śiva with many piteous entreaties. They cried loudly being agitated by their devotion.

## \|\| 4.24.45 \|\|

*harirmayā sudīnoktyā suvijñaptaṃ cakāra ha \|*  
*saṃsmaranmanasā śaṃbhuṃ bhaktyā paramayānvitaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Viṣṇu accompanied by me spoke out many piteous words, remembering Śiva with great devotion.

## \|\| 4.24.46 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*surairevaṃ stutaśśaṃbhurhariṇā ca mayā bhṛśam \|*  
*bhaktavātsalyato dhyānādviratobhūnmaheśvaraḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Śiva was thus eulogised by the gods, Viṣṇu and me. He, the great lord, ceased His meditation due to His attachment for His devotees.

## \|\| 4.24.47 \|\|

*uvāca suprasannātmā haryādīnharṣayanharaḥ \|*  
*vilokya karuṇādṛṣṭyā śaṃkaro bhaktavatsalaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. The delighted Śiva said heightening the pleasure of Viṣṇu and other gods, after glancing at them with merciful looks. Śiva is favourably disposed to His devotees.

## \|\| 4.24.48 \|\|

*śaṃkara uvāca \|*  
*he hare he vidhe devāśśakrādyā yugapatsame \|*  
*kimarthamāgatā yūyaṃ satyaṃ brūta mamāgrataḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

Śiva said:—

48\. O, Viṣṇu, O Brahmā, O Indra and other gods, why have you all collectively come here in my presence? Tell me the truth.

## \|\| 4.24.49 \|\|

*hariruvāca \|*  
*sarvajñastvaṃ maheśāna tvaṃtaryāmyakhileśvaraḥ \|*  
*kiṃ na jānāsi cittasthaṃ tathā vacmyapi śāsanāt \|\| 49 \|\|*

Viṣṇu said:—

49\. O great lord, you are omniscient. You are the immanent being and the lord of all. Don’t you know what is in our mind? Still I speak at you bidding.

## \|\| 4.24.50 \|\|

*tārakāsurato duḥkhaṃ saṃbhūtaṃ vividhaṃ mṛḍa \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ nastadarthaṃ hi prasanno'kāri vai suraiḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. O Śiva, many kinds of miseries have befallen us due to the demon Tāraka. It is for that that you have been propitiated by the gods.

## \|\| 4.24.51 \|\|

*śivā sā janitā śailāttvadarthaṃ hi himālayāt \|*  
*tasyāṃ tvadudbhavātputrāttasya mṛtyurna cānyathā \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. For attaining you Śivā is born of mountain Himācala. The demon’s death can be at the hands of your son alone begotten of her.

## \|\| 4.24.52 \|\|

*iti datto brahmaṇā hi tasmai daityāya yadvaraḥ \|*  
*tadanyasmādamṛtyussa bādhate nikhilaṃ jagat \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. This is the boon granted to him by Brahmā. Incapable of being killed by others, the demon harasses the entire universe.

## \|\| 4.24.53 \|\|

*nāradasya nirdeśātsā karoti kaṭhinaṃ tapaḥ \|*  
*tattejasākhilaṃ vyāptaṃ trailokyaṃ sacarācaram \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. At the instance of Nārada, she is performing a great penance. All the three worlds consisting of the mobile and immobile beings have been enveloped by her refulgence.

## \|\| 4.24.54 \|\|

*varaṃ dātuṃ śivāyai hi gaccha tvaṃ parameśvara \|*  
*devaduḥkhaṃ jahi svāminnasmākaṃ sukhamāvaha \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. O lord Śiva, please go and grant Śivā the boon. O lord, destroy our misery and bestow happiness on us.

## \|\| 4.24.55 \|\|

*devānāṃ me mahotsāho hṛdaye cāsti śaṃkara \|*  
*vivāhaṃ tava saṃdraṣṭuṃ tattvaṃ kuru yathocitam \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. O Śiva, there is a great enthusiasm in my heart as well as in those of the gods to witness your marriage. Please get it performed in a fitting manner.

## \|\| 4.24.56 \|\|

*ratyai yadbhavatā datto varastasya parātpara \|*  
*prāpto'vasara evāśu saphalaṃ svapaṇaṃ kuru \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. The opportune moment for the fulfilment of the boon granted by you to Ratī has arrived. Make your promise fruitful.

## \|\| 4.24.57 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityuktvā taṃ praṇamyaiva viṣṇurdevā maharṣayaḥ \|*  
*saṃstūya vividhaistotraissaṃtasthustatpuro'khilāḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

57\. After saying this and bowing to and eulogising Him with different hymns, Viṣṇu, the gods and the sages, all of us waited in front of Him.

## \|\| 4.24.58 \|\|

*bhaktādhīnaḥ śaṃkaro'pi śrutvā devavacastadā \|*  
*vihasya pratyuvācāśu vedamaryādarakṣakaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. On hearing the words of the gods Śiva, subservient to His devotees, laughed and replied. Śiva is a strict preserver of Vedic conventions.

## \|\| 4.24.59 \|\|

*\|\| śaṃkara uvāca \|*  
*he hare he vidhe devāśśṛṇutādarato'khilāḥ \|*  
*yathocitamahaṃ vacmi saviśeṣaṃ vivekataḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

Śiva said:—

59\. O Viṣṇu, O Brahmā, O gods, all of you please hear with attention. I am going to say a specific thing in a suitable manner.

## \|\| 4.24.60 \|\|

*nocitaṃ hi vidhānaṃ vai vivāhakaraṇaṃ nṛṇām \|*  
*mahānigaḍasaṃjño hi vivāho dṛḍhabandhanaḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Marrying is not a proper thing for men. Marriage is a great fetter that binds firmly.

## \|\| 4.24.61 \|\|

*kusaṃgā bahavo loke strīsaṃgastatra cādhikaḥ \|*  
*uddharetsakalabaṃdhairna strīsaṃgātpramucyate \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. There are many base bondages in the world. Association with women is the toughest of all. One can free oneself from all bondages except that of women.

## \|\| 4.24.62 \|\|

*lohadārumayaiḥ pāśairdṛḍhaṃ baddho'pi mucyate \|*  
*stryādipāśasusaṃbaddho mucyate na kadācana \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Anyone bound with nooses of iron and timber can secure release but one bound with nooses of women never frees oneself.

## \|\| 4.24.63 \|\|

*varddhaṃte viṣayāśśaśvanmahābaṃdhanakāriṇaḥ \|*  
*viṣayākrāṃtamanasassvapne mokṣo'pi durlabhaḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Worldly enjoyment tightens the bondage. Salvation is inaccessible to a man drawn to worldly enjoyment even in his dream.

## \|\| 4.24.64 \|\|
