*sukhamicchatu cetprājño vidhivadviṣayāṃstyajet \|*  
*viṣavadviṣayānāhurviṣayairyairnihanyate \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. If he wishes for happiness, an intelligent man shall duly forsake all worldly pleasures. Worldly enjoyment that dooms persons is on a par with poison.

## \|\| 4.24.65 \|\|

*jano viṣayiṇā sākaṃ vārtātaḥ patati kṣaṇāt \|*  
*viṣayaṃ prāhurācāryāssitāliteṃdravāruṇīm \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. O Indra, a man attains downfall even by conversing with a sensuous person. Great preceptors say that worldly enjoyment is a bitter beer mixed with sugar.

## \|\| 4.24.66 \|\|

*yadyapyevaṃ hi jānāmi sarvaṃ jñānaṃ viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*tathāpyahaṃ kariṣyāmi prārthanāṃ saphalāṃ ca vaḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Although I know and realise all these, although I have specific wisdom yet I shall accede to your request and make it fruitful.

## \|\| 4.24.67 \|\|

*bhaktādhīno'hamevāsmi tadvaśātsarvakārya kṛt \|*  
*ayathocitakartā hi prasiddho bhuvanatraye \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. I am definitely subservient to my devotees. Hence I may do everything. I am known all over the three worlds as one who performs ill fitting things.

## \|\| 4.24.68 \|\|

*kāmarūpādhipasyaiva paṇaśca saphalaḥ kṛtaḥ \|*  
*sudakṣiṇasya bhūpasya bhaimabaṃdhagatasya hi \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. The vow of the king of Assam (Kāmarūpa) was made fruitful. I saved king Sudakṣiṇā who had become a hireling and a prisoner.

## \|\| 4.24.69 \|\|

*gautamakleśakartāhaṃ tryaṃbakātmā sukhāvahaḥ \|*  
*tatkaṣṭapradaduṣṭānāṃ śāpadāyī viśeṣataḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. I am the three-eyed God who bestows happiness but brought about the misery of Gautama. I especially curse those wicked persons who harass my devotees.

## \|\| 4.24.70 \|\|

*viṣaṃ pītaṃ surārthaṃ hi bhaktavatsalabhāvadhṛk \|*  
*devakaṣṭaṃ hṛtaṃ yatnātsarvadaiva mayā surāḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. I have the feelings of endearment towards devotees. I drank up poison for the welfare of the gods. O gods, the miseries of the gods have always been removed by me.

## \|\| 4.24.71 \|\|

*bhaktārthamasahaṃ kaṣṭaṃ bahuśo bahuyatnataḥ \|*  
*viśvānara munerduḥkhaṃ hṛtaṃ gṛhapatirbhavan \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. For my devotees, I experienced many sufferings. I removed the misery of the sage Viśvānara by becoming a householder.

## \|\| 4.24.72 \|\|

*kiṃ bahūktena ca hare vidhe satyaṃ bravīmyaham \|*  
*matpaṇo'stīti yūyaṃ vai sarve jānītha tattvataḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. What is the use of talking much? O Viṣṇu, O Brahmā, I speak the truth. All of you know truly that I have vowed as follows.

## \|\| 4.24.73 \|\|

*yadā yadā vipattirhi bhaktānāṃ bhavati kvacit \|*  
*tadā tadā haramyāśu tatkṣaṇātsarvaśassadā \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. Whenever any devotee of mine is involved in any adversity I remove it instantaneously and completely.

## \|\| 4.24.74 \|\|

*jāne'haṃ tārakādduḥkhaṃ sarveṣāṃ vassamutthitam \|*  
*asurā ttaddhariṣyāmi satyaṃsatyaṃ vadāmyaham \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. I know the sufferings you undergo from the demon Tāraka. I shall remove them. Truth, I tell you the truth.

## \|\| 4.24.75 \|\|

*nāsti yadyapi me kācidvihārakaraṇe ruciḥ \|*  
*vivāhayiṣye girijā putrotpādanahetave \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. Although I am not interested at all in dalliance I shall marry Pārvatī for begetting a son.

## \|\| 4.24.76 \|\|

*gacchata svagṛhāṇyeva nirbhayāssakalāḥ surāḥ \|*  
*kāryaṃ vassādhayiṣyāmi nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. O gods, all of you go back to your respective abodes fearlessly. I shall achieve your task. In this respect you need not be anxious at all.

## \|\| 4.24.77 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*ityuktvā maunamāsthāya samādhistho'bhavaddharaḥ \|*  
*sarve viṣṇvādayo devāssvadhāmāni yayurmune \|\| 77 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

77\. O sage, after saying this, Śiva became silent and entered into spiritual contemplation. Viṣṇu and other gods went back to their respective abodes.

## Chapter 25 - The seven celestial sages test Pārvatī

## \|\| 4.25.1 \|\|

*\|\| nārada uvāca \|*  
*gateṣu teṣu deveṣu vidhi viṣṇvādikeṣu ca \|*  
*sarveṣu muniṣu prītyā kiṃ babhūva tataḥ param \|\| 1 \|\|*

Nārada said:—

1\. When Brahmā, Viṣṇu and other gods had gone along with the sages what happened thereafter?

## \|\| 4.25.2 \|\|

*kiṃ kṛtaṃ śaṃbhunā tāta varaṃ dātuṃsamāgataḥ \|*  
*kiyatkālena ca kathaṃ tadvada prītimāvahan \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. O dear one, what did Śiva do? Within what time did He go to grant the boon? How? Please tell me for my pleasure.

## \|\| 4.25.3 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*gateṣu teṣu deveṣu brahmādiṣu nijāśramam \|*  
*tattapassu parīkṣārthaṃ samādhistho'bhavadbhavaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

3\. When Brahmā and other gods had gone back to their respective abodes, Śiva entered into spiritual contemplation in order to test her penance.

## \|\| 4.25.4 \|\|

*svātmānamātmanā kṛtvā svātmanyeva vyaciṃtayat \|*  
*parātparataraṃ svasthaṃ nirmāya niravagraham \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. He meditated upon His own soul within Himself, the Ātman that is greater than the greatest, free from illusion and obsessions and stationed within itself.

## \|\| 4.25.5 \|\|

*tadvastubhūto bhagavānīśvaro vṛṣabhadhvajaḥ \|*  
*avijñātagatissūtissa haraḥ parameśvaraḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The bull-bannered lord Śiva, the object of the expression That, whose movements are unknown, is the cause of enjoyment and protection. Śiva is the lord Supreme.

## \|\| 4.25.6 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*girijā hi tadā tāta tatāpa paramaṃ tapaḥ \|*  
*tapasā tena rudro'pi paraṃ vismayamāgataḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

6\. O dear then, Pārvatī was engaged in great penance. Even Śiva wondered at that.

## \|\| 4.25.7 \|\|

*samādheścalitasso'bhūdbhaktādhīno'pi nānyathā \|*  
*vasiṣṭhādīnmunīnsapta sasmāra sūtikṛddharaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. He became distracted from spiritual contemplation. A deity subservient to His devotees cannot be otherwise. Śiva, the cause of great enjoyment and protection remembered the seven celestial sages, Vasiṣṭha and others.

## \|\| 4.25.8 \|\|

*saptāpi munayaśśīghramāyayussmṛti mātrataḥ \|*  
*prasannavadanāḥ sarve varṇayaṃto vidhiṃ bahu \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Immediately on being remembered, the seven sages came there with faces beaming with delight and praising their good fate.

## \|\| 4.25.9 \|\|

*praṇamya taṃ maheśānaṃ tuṣṭuvurharṣanirbharāḥ \|*  
*vāṇyā gadgadayā baddhakarā vinatakaṃdharāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Bowing to Him with folded arms and bent shoulders they eulogised lord Śiva with extreme pleasure by means of words choked with devotional feelings.

## \|\| 4.25.10 \|\|

*saptarṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*devadeva mahādeva karuṇāsāgara prabho \|*  
*jātā vayaṃ sudhanyā hi tvayā yadadhunā smṛtāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

The seven sages said:—

10\. “O great God, lord of gods, O lord, O ocean of mercy, we have become very well blessed since we have been remembered by you now.

## \|\| 4.25.11 \|\|

*kimarthaṃ saṃsmṛtā vātha śāsanaṃ dehi taddhi naḥ \|*  
*svadāsasadṛśīṃ svāminkṛpāṃ kuru namo'stu te \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Why have we been remembered? We may kindly be commanded. O lord, have pity on us as on your own slaves. Obeisance be to you.

## \|\| 4.25.12 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya nīnāṃ tu vijñaptiṃ karuṇānidhiḥ \|*  
*provāca vihasanprītyā protphullanayanāmbujaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

12\. On hearing the words of the sages, lord Śiva, the storehouse of sympathy spoke lovingly and laughingly with eyes beaming like full-blown lotus.

## \|\| 4.25.13 \|\|

*\|\| maheśvara uvāca \|*  
*he saptamunayastātāśśṛṇutāraṃ vaco mama \|*  
*asmaddhitakarā yūyaṃ sarvajñānavicakṣaṇāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

Lord Śiva said:—

13\. O dear seven celestial sages, listen to my words. You are all my benefactors. You are clever and perfectly wise.

## \|\| 4.25.14 \|\|

*tapaścarati deveśī pārvatī girijā'dhunā \|*  
*gaurīśikharasaṃjñe hi pārvate dṛḍhamānasā \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The great Goddess Pārvatī, the daughter of the mountain is performing a penance now in the mountain called Gaurīśikhara, with a steady mind.

## \|\| 4.25.15 \|\|

*māṃ patiṃ prāptukāmā hi sā sakhīsevitā dvijāḥ \|*  
*sarvānkāmānvihāyānyānparaṃ niścayamāgatā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. O brahmins, she is desirous of attaining me as her husband. She is being served by her maids. She has discarded all other desires. She is determined in her resolve.

## \|\| 4.25.16 \|\|

*tatra gacchata yūyaṃ macchāsanānmunisattamāḥ \|*  
*parīkṣāṃ dṛḍhatāyāstatkuruta premacetasaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. O excellent sages, you go there at my bidding. With love in mind, conduct the test of her resolve.

## \|\| 4.25.17 \|\|

*sarvathā chalasaṃyuktaṃ vacanīyaṃ vacaśca vaḥ \|*  
*na saṃśayaḥ prakartavyaśśāsanānmama suvratāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. O virtuous ones of good rites, at my bidding, you need not hesitate to employ even deceitful and critical remarks.

## \|\| 4.25.18 \|\|

*\|\|brahmovāca \|*  
*ityājñaptāśca munayo jagmustatra drutaṃ hi te \|*  
*yatra rājati sā dīptā jaganmātā nagātmajā \|\| 18 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

18\. Thus commanded those sages quickly went there where the mother of universe, the brilliant daughter of the mountain, shone with refulgence.

## \|\| 4.25.19 \|\|

*tatra dṛṣṭvā śivā sākṣāttapaḥsiddhirivāparā \|*  
*mūrtā paramatejaskā vilasaṃtī sutejasā \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. There she was seen as the personified achievement of penance itself. She was shining brilliantly with great splendour.

## \|\| 4.25.20 \|\|

*hṛdā praṇamya tāṃ te tu ṛṣayassapta suvratāḥ \|*  
*sannatā vacanaṃ procuḥ pūjitāśca viśeṣataḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Mentally bowing to her, the seven sages, of good rites, humbly spoke to her after being warmly welcomed and worshipped by her.

## \|\| 4.25.21 \|\|

*\|\| ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*śṛṇu śailasute devī kimarthaṃ tapyate tapaḥ \|*  
*icchasi tvaṃ suraṃ kaṃ ca kiṃ phalaṃ tadvadādhunā \|\| 21 \|\|*

The sages said:—

21\. O daughter of the mountain, listen. Why do you perform this penance? Which god do you wish to propitiate? For what purpose? Please tell us now.

## \|\| 4.25.22 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityuktā sā śivā devī girīṃdratanayā dvijaiḥ \|*  
*pratyuvāca vacassatyaṃ sugūḍhamapi tatpuraḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

22\. Thus addressed by the brahmins, the goddess Śivā, daughter of the lord of mountains, replied truly before them though it was a great secret.

## \|\| 4.25.23 \|\|

*\|\| pārvatyuvāca \|*  
*munīśvarāssaṃśṛṇuta madvākyaṃ prītito hṛdā \|*  
*bravīmi svavicāraṃ vai ciṃtito yo dhiyā svayā \|\| 23 \|\|*

Pārvatī said:—

23\. O great sages, listen to my words with hearty affection. I am saying only what I thought in my own way.

## \|\| 4.25.24 \|\|

*kariṣyatha prahāsaṃ me śrutvā vāco hyasaṃbhavāḥ \|*  
*saṃkoco varṇanādviprā bhavatyeva karomi kim \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. On hearing my words you will laugh at me considering my proposal impossible. O brahmins, I hesitate in revealing it but what can I do?

## \|\| 4.25.25 \|\|

*idaṃ mano hi sudṛḍhamavaśaṃ parakarmakṛt \|*  
*jalopari mahābhittiṃ cikīrṣati mahonnatām \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. This mind of mine is resolute helplessly attempting at a great task. Verily it is trying to erect a high wall on the surface of water.

## \|\| 4.25.26 \|\|

*surarṣeśśāsanaṃ prāpya karomi sudṛḍhaṃ tapaḥ \|*  
*rudraḥ patirbhavenme hi vidhāyeti manoratham \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. At the bidding of the celestial sage I am performing this steady penance with the desire that Rudra be my husband.

## \|\| 4.25.27 \|\|

*apakṣo manmanaḥ pakṣī vyomni uḍḍīyate haṭhāt \|*  
*tadāśāṃ śaṃkarasvāmī piparttu karuṇānidhiḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. The unfledged birdling of my mind flies up tenaciously. May lord Śiva, the storehouse of mercy fulfil its desire.

## \|\| 4.25.28 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya vacastasyā vihasya munayaśca te \|*  
*saṃmānya girijāṃ prītyā procuśchalavaco mṛṣā \|\| 28 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

28\. On hearing her words, the sages honoured Pārvatī mentally with pleasure but spoke these deceptive false words laughingly.

## \|\| 4.25.29 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*na jñātaṃ tasya caritaṃ vṛthāpaṇḍitamāninaḥ \|*  
*devarṣeḥ kūramanasaḥ sujñā bhūtvāpyagātmaje \|\| 29 \|\|*

The sages said:—

29\. O daughter of the mountain, although you are wise and intelligent, you are not able to see through the conduct of that celestial sage who professes to be a great scholar but who is cruel-minded.

## \|\| 4.25.30 \|\|

*nāradaḥ kūṭavādī ca paracittapramaṃthakaḥ \|*  
*tasya vārttāśravaṇato hānirbhavati sarvathā \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Nārada is a quibbler. He misleads others. If his words are paid heed to, you stand to lose in every respect.

## \|\| 4.25.31 \|\|

*tatra tvaṃ śṛṇu sadbudhyā cetihāsaṃ suśobhitam \|*  
*kramāttvāṃ bodhayaṃto hi prītyā tamupadhāraya \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Now listen to a true anecdote that sheds light thereon, with keen intellect. We are enlightening you out of love and affection, take it to heart.

## \|\| 4.25.32 \|\|

*brahmaputro hi yo dakṣassuṣuve piturājñayā \|*  
*svapatnyāmayutaṃ putrānayuṃkta tapasi priyān \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Dakṣa, the son of Brahmā, at the bidding of his father, begot ten thousand sons of his wife. He dearly loved them and employed them in performing a great penance.

## \|\| 4.25.33 \|\|

*te sutāḥ paścimāṃ diśi nārāyaṇasaro gatāḥ \|*  
*taporthe te pratijñāya nāradastatra vai yayau \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The sons went to the holy lake Nārāyaṇasaras in the western zone for performing penance. Nosing it out, Nārada too went there.

## \|\| 4.25.34 \|\|

*kūṭopadeśamāśrāvya tatra tānnārado muniḥ \|*  
*tadājñayā ca te sarve piturna gṛhamāyayuḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Sage Nārada misled them with his deceptive instructions. At his instance, they never went back home to their father.

## \|\| 4.25.35 \|\|

*tacchrutvā kupito dakṣaḥ pitrāśvāsitamānasaḥ \|*  
*utpādya putrānprāyuṃkta sahasrapramitāṃstataḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. On hearing this, Dakṣa was infuriated but his father consoled him. Thereafter he begot a thousand other sons and engaged them in penance.

## \|\| 4.25.36 \|\|

*te'pi tatra gatāḥ putrāstaporthaṃ piturājñayā \|*  
*nārado'pi yayau tatra punastatsvopadeśakṛt \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. The sons too went to the same place for penance at the bidding of their father. Nārada too went there, a self-appointed instructor for them.

## \|\| 4.25.37 \|\|

*dadau tadupadeśaṃ te tebhyo bhrātṛpathaṃ yayuḥ \|*  
*āyayurna piturgehaṃ bhikṣuvṛttiratāśca te \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. He gave them the same instruction and they went the way of their brothers. They never returned to the parental abode. They were engrossed in the avocation of mendicants.

## \|\| 4.25.38 \|\|

*itthaṃ nāradasadvṛttirviśruttā śailakanyake \|*  
*anyāṃ śṛṇu hi tadvṛttiṃ vairāgyakaraṇīṃ nṛṇām \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. O daughter of mountain, the good conduct of Nārada is thus well-known. Now hear about another activity of his in making men detached.

## \|\| 4.25.39 \|\|

*vidyādharaścitraketuryo babhūva purākarot \|*  
*svopadeśamayaṃ dattvā tasmai śūnyaṃ ca tadgṛham \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. There was a Vidyādhara named Citraketu. The sage instructed him and made him detached from his house.

## \|\| 4.25.40 \|\|

*prahlādāya svopadeśānhiraṇyakaśipoḥ param \|*  
*dattvā dukhaṃ dadau cāyaṃ parabuddhiprabhedakaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. He bestowed his instructions on Prahlāda and made him suffer much at the hands of Hiraṇyakaśipu. He is definitely a person who splits others’ intellect.

## \|\| 4.25.41 \|\|

*muninā nijavidyā yacchrāvitā karṇarocanā \|*  
*sa svagehaṃ vihāyāśu bhikṣāṃ carati prāyaśaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Whomsoever this sage advocates his philosophy, very pleasing to the ears, generally the same person discards his hearth and home and begins to beg for alms.

## \|\| 4.25.42 \|\|

*nārado malinātmā hi sarvado jjvaladehavān \|*  
*jānīmastaṃ viśeṣeṇa vayaṃ tatsahavāsinaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Nārada has a dirty soul though he is endowed with a white brilliant complexion for ever. We know him particularly because we are his associates.

## \|\| 4.25.43 \|\|

*bakaṃ sādhuṃ varṇayaṃti na matsyānatti sarvathā \|*  
*sahavāsī vijānīyāccaritraṃ sahavāsinām \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. People from a distance may describe a stork as a gentle bird that does not prey on fish. But in fact an associate knows the conduct of his associates.

## \|\| 4.25.44 \|\|

*labdhvā tadupadeśaṃ hi tvamapi prājñasaṃmatā \|*  
*vṛthaiva mūrkhībhūtā tu tapaścarasi duṣkaram \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. You too who are honoured by the wise have followed his advice and thus become a fool. That is why you are performing this severe penance.

## \|\| 4.25.45 \|\|

*yadarthamīdṛśaṃ bāle karoṣi vipulaṃ tapaḥ \|*  
*sadodāsī nirvikāro madanārirnasaṃśayaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. O young lady, He, for whose sake you are performing this elaborate penance is a perpetually indifferent person of no emotional disturbance. Undoubtedly He is an enemy of Kāma.

## \|\| 4.25.46 \|\|

*amaṃgalavapurdhārī nirlajjo'sadano'kulī \|*  
*kuveṣī pretabhūtādisaṃgī nagnau hi śūlabhṛt \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. The trident-bearing Śiva has an inauspicious body, is free from shame and has no home or pedigree. He is naked and ill-featured. He associates with ghosts and goblins and the like.

## \|\| 4.25.47 \|\|

*sa dhūrtastava vijñānaṃ vināśya nijamāyayā \|*  
*mohayāmāsa sadyuktyā kārayāmāsa vai tapaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. That rogue of a sage has destroyed your discretion with his deception. He has deluded you with apparently good arguments and made you perform this penance.

## \|\| 4.25.48 \|\|

*īdṛśaṃ hi varaṃ labdhvā kiṃ sukhaṃ saṃbhaviṣyati \|*  
*vicāraṃ kuru deveśi tvameva girijātmaje \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. O great Goddess, daughter of the mountain, you alone think within yourself how much pleasure could be derived by getting such a bridegroom.

## \|\| 4.25.49 \|\|

*prathamaṃ dakṣajāṃ sādhvī vivāhya sudhiyā satīm \|*  
*nirvāhaṃ kṛtavānnaiva mūḍhaḥ kiṃciddināni hi \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. At first he married Satī, the chaste daughter of Dakṣa, eagerly but the fool that he was he could not maintain the household even for a few days.

## \|\| 4.25.50 \|\|

*tāṃ tathaiva sa vai doṣaṃ dattvātyākṣītsvayaṃ prabhuḥ \|*  
*dhyāyansvarūpa makalamaśokamaramatsukhī \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. He accused her and forsook her Himself. The lord went on meditating on His own form, free from stains and sorrows and sported happily.

## \|\| 4.25.51 \|\|

*ekalaḥ paranirvāṇo hyasaṃgo'dvaya eva ca \|*  
*tena nāryāḥ kathaṃ devi nirvāhaḥ saṃbhaviṣyati \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. He is single without a second and without attachment. He is after salvation, O gentle lady, how can a woman put up with him.

## \|\| 4.25.52 \|\|

*adyāpi śāsanaṃ prāpya gṛhamāyāhi durmatim \|*  
*tyajāsmākaṃ mahābhāge bhaviṣyati ca śaṃ tava \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. O blessed one, even now, at our bidding, return to your house. Cast off this foolish intention. You will benefit thereby.

## \|\| 4.25.53 \|\|

*tvadyogyo hi varo viṣṇussarvasadguṇavānprabhuḥ \|*  
*vaikuṇṭhavāsī lakṣmīśo nānākrīḍāviśāradaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. A befitting bridegroom for you is lord Viṣṇu endowed with all good qualities. He is a resident of Vaikuṇṭha, lord of wealth and is skilled in sports.

## \|\| 4.25.54 \|\|

*tena te kārayiṣyāmo vivāhaṃ sarvasaukhyadam \|*  
*itīdṛśaṃ tyaja haṭhaṃ sukhitā bhava pārvati \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. O Pārvatī, with him we shall fix your marriage that will confer all happiness on you. Leave off this obduracy. Be happy.

## \|\| 4.25.55 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityedaṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā pārvatī jagadambikā \|*  
*vihasya ca punaḥ prāha munīnjñāna viśāradān \|\| 55 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

55\. On hearing these words, Pārvatī, the mother of the universe, laughed and spoke to the wise sages.

## \|\| 4.25.56 \|\|

*pārvatyuvāca \|*  
*satyaṃ bhavadbhiḥ kathitaṃ svajñānena munīśvarāḥ \|*  
*paraṃtu me haṭho naiva mukto bhavati vai dvijāḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

Pārvatī said:—

56\. O excellent sages, what you have said may be true according to your light and wisdom; but O brahmins, my tenacity cannot be affected.

## \|\| 4.25.57 \|\|

*svatanoḥ śailajātatvātkāṭhinyaṃ sahajaṃ sthitam \|*  
*itthaṃ vicārya sudhiyā māṃ niṣeddhuṃ na cārhatha \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Being born of a mountain, toughness is congenital to my body. Pondering over this with a short intellect you will please desist from preventing me.

## \|\| 4.25.58 \|\|

*surarṣervacanaṃ pathyaṃ tyakṣye naiva kadācana \|*  
*gurūṇāṃ vacanaṃ pathyamiti vedavido viduḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. I shall never discard the wholesome advice of the celestial sage. Vedic scholars know and affirm that the advice of a preceptor is wholesome.

## \|\| 4.25.59 \|\|

*gurūṇāṃ vacanaṃ satyamiti yeṣāṃ dṛḍhā matiḥ \|*  
*teṣāmihāmutra sukhaṃ paramaṃ nāsukhaṃ kvacit \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Those who firmly believe that the advice of the preceptor is true will experience great happiness here and hereafter. They will have no unhappiness anywhere.

## \|\| 4.25.60 \|\|

*gurūṇāṃ vacanaṃ satyamiti yaddhṛdaye na dhīḥ \|*  
*ihāmutrāpi teṣāṃ hi dukhaṃ na ca sukhaṃ kvacit \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Those who distrust the maxim in their heart of hearts that the advice of preceptors is true will experience nothing but misery here and hereafter, no happiness anywhere.

## \|\| 4.25.61 \|\|

*sarvathā na parityājyaṃ gurūṇāṃ vacanaṃ dvijāḥ \|*  
*gṛhaṃ vasedvā śūnyaṃ syānme haṭhassukhadassadā \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. O brahmins, the advice of the preceptors is not to be eschewed at all. Whether it leads to the attachment of a household or otherwise, my tenacity will remain pleasing to me for ever.

## \|\| 4.25.62 \|\|

*yadbhavadbhissubhaṇitaṃ vacanaṃ munisattamāḥ \|*  
*tadanyathā tadvivekaṃ varṇayāmi samāsataḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. O excellent sages, what you have just spoken shall be interpreted in another way. I shall explain it in brief.

## \|\| 4.25.63 \|\|

*guṇālayo vihārī ca viṣṇussatyaṃ prakīrtitaḥ \|*  
*sadāśivo'guṇaḥ proktastatra kāraṇa mucyate \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. When you glorify Viṣṇu as the abode of noble qualities or as a sportive deity I do not contradict. As to your statement that Sadāśiva is devoid of attributes I shall tell you the reason.

## \|\| 4.25.64 \|\|

*śivo brahmāvikāraḥ sa bhaktahetordhṛtākṛtiḥ \|*  
*prabhutāṃ laukikīṃ naiva saṃdarśayitumicchati \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Śiva is Brahman, unchanging and without aberration. He assumes shapes and forms for the welfare of his devotees. He does not make a show of worldly lordship.

## \|\| 4.25.65 \|\|

*ataḥ paramahaṃsānāṃ dhāryaye supriyā gatiḥ \|*  
*avadhūtasvarūpeṇa parānaṃdena śaṃbhunā \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Therefore he assumes the attitude and behaviour of great Yogins. Śiva is a supreme bliss personified and an Avadhūta in form.

## \|\| 4.25.66 \|\|

*bhūṣūṇādirucirmāyārliptānāṃ brahmaṇo na ca \|*  
*sa prabhurnirguṇo'jo nirmāyo'lakṣyagatirvirāṭ \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Interest in embellishment and ornaments shall be found in those who are deluded by illusion and who are not in unison with the Brahman. The lord is devoid of attributes, unborn, free from illusion, of invisible movement and a cosmic Being.

## \|\| 4.25.67 \|\|

*dharmajātyādibhiśśambhurnānugṛhṇāti va dvijāḥ \|*  
*guroranugraheṇaiva śivaṃ jānāmi tattvataḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. O brahmins, Śiva does not shower His blessings on the ground of faith, caste etc. I know Śiva truly only through the blessings of the preceptor.

## \|\| 4.25.68 \|\|

*cecchivassa hi me viprā vivāhaṃ na kariṣyati \|*  
*avivāhā sadāhaṃ syāṃ satyaṃ satyaṃ vadāmyaham \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. O brahmins, if Śiva does not marry me I shall remain for ever a virgin. Truth, I tell you the truth.

## \|\| 4.25.69 \|\|

*udayati yadi bhānuḥ paścime digvibhāge pracalati yadi meruśśītatāṃ yāti vahniḥ \|*  
*vikasati yadi padmaṃ parvatāgre śilāyāṃ na hi calati haṭho me satyametadbravīmi \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. Even if the sun were to rise in the west, even if the mountain Meru were to move; even if the fire were to be cool and even if the lotus were to bloom on a rock at the top of a mountain, my stubbornness cannot be nullified. I am telling you the truth.

## \|\| 4.25.70 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*ityuktvā tānpraṇamyāśu munīnsā parvatātmajā \|*  
*virarāma śivaṃ smṛtvā nirvikāreṇa cetasā \|\| 70 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

70\. After saying thus and bowing to those sages, the daughter of the mountain stopped and remembered Śiva with an unruffled mind.

## \|\| 4.25.71 \|\|

*ṛṣayo'pītthamājñāya girijāyāssuniścayam \|*  
*procurjayagiraṃ tatra daduścāśiṣamuttamām \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. On realising the resoluteness of Pārvatī, the sages hailed her and bestowed excellent blessings upon her.

## \|\| 4.25.72 \|\|

*atha prāṇamya tāṃ devīṃ munayo hṛṣṭamānasāḥ \|*  
*śivasthānaṃ drutaṃ jagmustatparīkṣākarā mune \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. O sage, after bowing to the goddess, the sages who wanted to test her, were delighted. They immediately returned to Śiva’s abode.

## \|\| 4.25.73 \|\|

*tatra gatvā śivaṃ natvā vṛttāṃtaṃ vinivedya tam \|*  
*tadājñāṃ samanuprāpya svarlokaṃ jagmurādarāt \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. Having reached the place they informed Śiva of all the details. Taking leave of Him with respect, they went to the heaven.

## Chapter 26 - Pārvatī-Jaṭila dialogue

## \|\| 4.26.1 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*gateṣu teṣu muniṣu svaṃ lokaṃ śaṃkaraḥ svayam \|*  
*parīkṣituṃ tapo devyā aicchatsūtikaraḥ prabhuḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

1\. When those sages returned to their abodes, lord Śiva, the cause of great enjoyment and protection wanted to test the penance of the goddess.

## \|\| 4.26.2 \|\|

*parīkṣā chadmanā śaṃbhurdraṣṭuṃ tāṃ tuṣṭamānasaḥ \|*  
*jāṭilaṃ rūpamāsthāya sa yayau pārvatīvanam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Under the pretext of testing, Śiva wanted to see her. With a delighted mind He assumed the form of a Jaṭila (an ascetic with matted hair) and went to the forest of penance of Pārvatī.

## \|\| 4.26.3 \|\|

*atīva sthaviro vipradehadhārī svatejasā \|*  
*prajvalanmanasā hṛṣṭo daṃḍī chatrī babhūva saḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. He took the form of a very old man with the body of a brahmin. His brilliance shone. He was delighted in mind. He had an umbrella and a staff (to support Him).

## \|\| 4.26.4 \|\|

*tatrāpaśyatsthitāṃ devīṃ sakhībhiḥ parivāritām \|*  
*vedikopari śuddhāṃ tāṃ śivāmiva vidhoḥ kalām \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. There He saw the goddess surrounded by her maids on the platform, as pure as the digit of the moon.

## \|\| 4.26.5 \|\|

*śaṃbhu nirīkṣya tāṃ devīṃ brahmacārisvarūpavān \|*  
*upakaṃṭhaṃ yayau prītyā tadā'sau bhaktavatsalaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Śiva, who is favourably disposed towards His devotees, approached her with pleasure in the guise of a celibate.

## \|\| 4.26.6 \|\|

*āgataṃ taṃ tadā dṛṣṭvā brāhmaṇaṃ tejasādbhutam \|*  
*apūjayacchivā devī sarvapūjopahārakaiḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. On seeing that brahmin of wonderful refulgence come, goddess Pārvatī worshipped Him with all the articles of worship.

## \|\| 4.26.7 \|\|

*susatkṛtaṃ saṃvidhābhiḥ pūjitaṃ parayā mudā \|*  
*pārvatī kuśalaṃ prītyā papraccha dvijamādarāta \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. She worshipped him with great joy by means of well prepared and arranged articles of worship. Thereafter Pārvatī enquired after the health of the brahmin with respect.

## \|\| 4.26.8 \|\|

*\|\| pārvatyuvāca \|*  
*brahmacārisvarūpeṇa kastvaṃ hi kuta āgataḥ \|*  
*idaṃ vanaṃ bhāsayase vada vedavidāṃ vara \|\| 8 \|\|*

Pārvatī said:—

8\. Who are you and whence have you come in the guise of a Brahmacārin? You are making this forest refulgent by your splendour. Please speak, O foremost among Vedic scholars.

## \|\| 4.26.9 \|\|

*\|\| vipra uvāca \|*  
*ahamicchābhigāmī ca vṛddho vipratanussudhīḥ \|*  
*tapasvī sukhado'nyeṣāmupakārī na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

The brahmin said:—

9\. I am an aged brahmin roaming about as I please. I am an intelligent ascetic bestowing happiness and helping others.

## \|\| 4.26.10 \|\|

*kā tvaṃ kasyāsi tanayā kimartha vijane vane \|*  
*tapaścarasi durdharṣaṃ munibhiḥ prapadairapi \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Who are you? What is your parentage? Why do you perform penance in this isolated forest? Your penance cannot be surpassed even by the sages of eminent status.

## \|\| 4.26.11 \|\|

*na bālā na ca vṛddhāsi taruṇī bhāsi śobhanā \|*  
*kathaṃ patiṃ vinā tīkṣṇaṃ tapaścarasi vai vane \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. You are neither a small girl nor an old woman. You appear to be an auspicious young woman. How is it that you are performing this penance even when you are unmarried.

## \|\| 4.26.12 \|\|

*ki tvaṃ tapasvinī bhadre kasyacitsahacāriṇī \|*  
*tapasvī sa na puṣṇāti devi tvāṃ ca gato'nyataḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. O gentle lady, are you the wife of an ascetic who does not provide you with food and shelter and so leaving you has gone to another place?

## \|\| 4.26.13 \|\|

*vada kasya kule jātā kaḥ pitā tava kā vidhā \|*  
*mahāsaubhāgyarūpā tvaṃ vṛthā tava taporatiḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Tell me, in which family are you born? Who is your father? What are your undertakings? You are very fortunate. Futile is your interest in penance.

## \|\| 4.26.14 \|\|

*kiṃ tvaṃ vedaprasūrlakṣmīḥ kiṃ surūpā sarasvatī \|*  
*etāsu madhye kā vā tvaṃ nāhaṃ tarkitumutsahe \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Are you the mother of the Vedas? Are you Lakṣmī or Sarasvatī? I dare not guess who you are?

## \|\| 4.26.15 \|\|

*\|\| pārvatyuvāca \|*  
*nāhaṃ vedaprasūrvipra na lakṣmīśca sarasvatī \|*  
*ahaṃ himācalasutā sāṃprataṃ nāma pārvatī \|\| 15 \|\|*

Pārvatī said:—

15\. O brahmin, I am not the mother of the Vedas, nor Lakṣmī nor Sarasvatī. I am the daughter of Himācala and my name is Pārvatī.

## \|\| 4.26.16 \|\|

*purā dakṣasutā jātā satī nāmānyajanmani \|*  
*yogena tyaktadehā'haṃ yatpitrā ninditaḥ patiḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Previously I had been born as Satī, the daughter of Dakṣa. By Yogic means I cast off my body since my husband was insulted by my father.

## \|\| 4.26.17 \|\|

*atra janmani saṃprāptaśśivo'pi vidhivaibhavāt \|*  
*māṃ tyaktvā bhasmasātkṛtya manmathaṃ sa jagāma ha \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Even in this life, Śiva came to me but due to ill luck, He reduced Kāma to ashes, left me and went away.

## \|\| 4.26.18 \|\|

*prayāte śaṃkare tāpodvijitāhaṃ piturgṛhāt \|*  
*āgatā tapase vipra sudṛḍhā svarṇadītaṭe \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. O brahmin, when Śiva went away, I came out of my father’s house, being greatly dejected, to perform this steady penance on the banks of the celestial river.

## \|\| 4.26.19 \|\|

*kṛtvā tapaḥ kaṭhoraṃ ca suciraṃ prāṇavallabham \|*  
*na prāpyāgnau vivikṣantī tvaṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃsthitā kṣaṇam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Even after performing this severe penance for a long time, I could not attain Him. I was just to consign myself to fire but on seeing you, I have stopped for a while.

## \|\| 4.26.20 \|\|

*gaccha tvaṃ praviśāmyagnau śivenāṃgīkṛtā na hi \|*  
*yatra yatra janurlapsye variṣyāmi śivaṃ varam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Now you can go. I shall enter fire since I have not been accepted by Śiva. Wherever I take birth I shall woo only Śiva.

## \|\| 4.26.21 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityuktvā pārvatī vahnau tatpuraḥ praviveśa sā \|*  
*niṣidhyamānā purato brāhmaṇena punaḥ punaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

21\. After saying so, Pārvatī jumped into the fire in the presence of the brahmin although she was forbidden by Him again and again.

## \|\| 4.26.22 \|\|

*vahnipraveśaṃ kurvatyāḥ pārvatyāstatprabhāvataḥ \|*  
*babhūva tatkṣaṇaṃ sadyo vahni ścaṃdanapaṃkavat \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Even as she jumped into the fire, it became as cool as sandal paste due to her ascetic power.

## \|\| 4.26.23 \|\|

*kṣaṇaṃ tadaṃtare sthitvā hyutpataṃtī divaṃ dvijaḥ \|*  
*punaḥ papraccha sahasā vihasansutanuṃ śivaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. The brahmin stopped her standing on her way as she was trying to go away and asked her laughingly.

## \|\| 4.26.24 \|\|

*dvija uvāca \|*  
*aho tapaste kiṃ bhadre na buddhaṃ kiṃcideva hi \|*  
*na dagdho vahninā deho na ca prāptaṃ manīṣitam \|\| 24 \|\|*

The Brahmin said:—

24\. O gentle lady, I cannot understand anything. Your penance is wonderful. Your body is not charred by the fire. Still your desire remains unsatiated so far.

## \|\| 4.26.25 \|\|

*atassatyaṃ nikāmaṃ vai vada devi manoratham \|*  
*mamāgre vipravaryasya sarvānaṃdapradasya hi \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. O gentle lady, let me know about your desire; I am a brahmin who can bestow pleasure upon everyone.

## \|\| 4.26.26 \|\|

*yathāvidhi tvayā devi kīrtyatāṃ sarvathātmanā \|*  
*tasmānmaitrī ca saṃjātā kāryyaṃ gopyaṃ tvayā na hi \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Please tell me everything truly and methodically. Since we have become friends nothing should be kept a secret from me.

## \|\| 4.26.27 \|\|

*kimicchasi varaṃ devi praṣṭumicchāmyataḥ param \|*  
*tvayyeva tadasau devi phalaṃ sarvaṃ pradṛśyate \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. I wish to ask you now. O gentle lady, whom do you wish to have as your husband? It is in you that the fruit of penance is seen.

## \|\| 4.26.28 \|\|

*parārthe ca tapaścedvai tiṣṭhettu tapa eva tat \|*  
*ratnaṃ haste samādāya hitvā kācastu saṃcitaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. If your penance is for others or for the supreme object, wherefore should you perform it at all? You had a jewel in your hand, you cast it off and have taken up a base metal instead.

## \|\| 4.26.29 \|\|

*īdṛśaṃ tava sauṃdaryaṃ kathaṃ vyarthīkṛtaṃ tvayā \|*  
*hitvā vastrāṇyanekāni carmādi ca dhṛtaṃ tvayā \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Why have you rendered your beauty in vain by taking recourse to this penance that eschewing different sorts of fine clothes hide is worn by you.

## \|\| 4.26.30 \|\|

*tatsarvaṃ kāraṇaṃ brūhi tapasastvasya satyataḥ \|*  
*tacchrutvā vipravaryo'haṃ yathā harṣamāvāpnuyām \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Hence tell me the reason, truthfully, for this penance. Let me, a great brahmin, be pleased on hearing the same.

## \|\| 4.26.31 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*iti pṛṣṭā tadā tena sakhīṃ prairayatāmbikā \|*  
*tanmukhenaiva tatsarvaṃ kathayāmāsa suvratā \|\| 31 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

31\. Thus asked by him, Pārvatī urged her maid. She of good rites made everything narrated to him through her maid.

## \|\| 4.26.32 \|\|

*tayā ca preritā tatra pārvatyā vijayābhidhā \|*  
*prāṇapriyā suvratajñā sakhī jaṭilamabravīt \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Induced by Pārvatī, her bosom friend Vijayā who knew all about her good rites spoke to the ascetic.

## \|\| 4.26.33 \|\|

*sakhyuvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu sādho pravakṣyāmi pārvatīcaritaṃ param \|*  
*hetuṃ ca tapasassarvaṃ yadi tvaṃ śrotumicchasi \|\| 33 \|\|*

The maid said:—

33\. O saintly sir, listen. I shall recount the story of Pārvatī as well as the reason for penance, if you wish to hear.

## \|\| 4.26.34 \|\|

*sakhā me girirājasya suteyaṃ himabhūbhṛtaḥ \|*  
*khyātā vai pārvatī nāmnā sā kālīti ca menakā \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. This my friend is the daughter of Himācala, lord of mountains. She is the daughter of Menakā named Kālī but famous as Pārvatī.

## \|\| 4.26.35 \|\|

*ūḍheyaṃ na ca kenāpi na vāñchati śivātparam \|*  
*trīṇi varṣasahasrāṇi tapaścaraṇasādhinī \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. She is not married to anyone nor does she desire any other than Śiva for her husband. She has performed this penance for three thousand years.

## \|\| 4.26.36 \|\|

*tadarthaṃ me'nayā sakhyā prārabdhaṃ tapa īdṛśam \|*  
*tadatra kāraṇaṃ vakṣye śṛṇu sādho dvijottama \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. It was for that purpose that my friend started penance like this. I shall tell you the reason. Listen, O excellent brahmin, O saintly one.

## \|\| 4.26.37 \|\|

*hitvendrapramukhāndevān hariṃ brahmāṇameva ca \|*  
*patiṃ pinākapāṇiṃ vai prāpnumicchati pārvatī \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Leaving off Indra and other gods, Viṣṇu and Brahmā, Pārvatī wishes to attain the Pināka-bearing Śiva as her husband.

## \|\| 4.26.38 \|\|

*iyaṃ sakhī madīyā vai vṛkṣānāropa yatpurā \|*  
*teṣu sarveṣu saṃjātaṃ phalapuṣpādikaṃ dvija \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. She my friend planted many trees before. O brahmin, all of them have put forth flowers and fruits.

## \|\| 4.26.39-40 \|\|

*rūpasārthāya janakakulālaṃkaraṇāya ca \|*  
*samuddiśya maheśānaṃ kāmasyānugrahāya ca \|\| 39 \|\|*

*matsakhī nāradopadeśāttapastapati dāruṇam \|*  
*manorathaḥ kutastasyā na phaliṣyati tāpasa \|\| 40 \|\|*

39-40. My friend has been performing severe penance at the bidding of Nārada to make her beauty fruitful, to embellish her father’s race and to bless Kama. She has directed this penance to lord Śiva. O holy ascetic, how is it that her desire is not fulfilled.

## \|\| 4.26.41 \|\|

*yatte pṛṣṭaṃ dvijaśreṣṭha matsakhyā manasīpsitam \|*  
*mayā khyātaṃ ca tatprītyā kimanyacchrotumicchasi \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. O excellent brahmin, you enquired of her desire. I have just told you out of my love for her. What else do you wish to hear.

## \|\| 4.26.42 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityevaṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā vijayāyā yathārthataḥ \|*  
*mune sa jaṭilo rudro vihasanvākyamabravīt \|\| 42 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

42\. On hearing these truthful words of Vijayā, O sage, Śiva who came disguised as an ascetic said laughingly.

## \|\| 4.26.43 \|\|

*jaṭila uvāca \|*  
*sakhyedaṃ kathitaṃ tatra parihāsonumīyate \|*  
*yathārthaṃ cettadā devī svamukhenābhibhāṣatām \|\| 43 \|\|*

The ascetic said:—

43\. The maid has said something, but I deduce only a huge joke therefrom. If it be true, let the gentle lady herself speak out.

## \|\| 4.26.44 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*ityukte ca tadā tena jaṭilena dvijanmanā \|*  
*uvāca pārvatī devī svamukhenaiva taṃ dvijam \|\| 44 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

44\. When these words were uttered by that brahmin ascetic, goddess Pārvatī spoke to the brahmin thus.

## Chapter 27 - Description of the fraudulent words of the Brahmacārin

## \|\| 4.27.1 \|\|

*pārvatyuvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu dvijendra jaṭila madvṛttaṃ nikhilaṃ khalu \|*  
*sakhyuktaṃ me'dya yatsatyaṃ tattathaiva na cānyathā \|\| 1 \|\|*

Pārvatī said:—

1\. O great brahmin, listen to my story entirely. What my friend has said just now is the whole truth, not otherwise.

## \|\| 4.27.2 \|\|

*manasā vacasā sākṣātkarmmaṇā patibhāvataḥ \|*  
*satyaṃ bravīmi no'satyaṃ vṛto vai śaṃkaro yā \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. I am telling you the truth and not a lie. Śiva has been wooed by me, by mind, speech and action as well as by means of ascetic feelings.

## \|\| 4.27.3 \|\|

*jānāmi durllabhaṃ vastu kathamprāpyaṃ mayā bhavet \|*  
*tathāpi mana autsukyāttapyate'dya tapo mayā \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. I know that it is an inaccessible object. How can I attain it? Still out of my eagerness I am performing this penance.

## \|\| 4.27.4 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*ityuktvā vacanantasmai sthitā sā girijā tadā \|*  
*uvāca brāhmaṇastatra tacchrutvā pārvatīvacaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

4\. After saying these words to him, the daughter of the mountain kept quiet. On hearing the words of Pārvatī the brahmin said.

## \|\| 4.27.5 \|\|

*brāhmaṇa uvāca \|*  
*etāvatkālaparyyantammamecchā mahatī hyabhūt \|*  
*kiṃ vastu kāṃkṣatī devī kurute sumahattapaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

The brahmin said:—

5\. So long I had been desirous of knowing what our gentle lady craves for that she performs this great penance.

## \|\| 4.27.6 \|\|

*tajjñātvā nikhilaṃ devi śrutvā tvanmukhapaṃkajāt \|*  
*ito gacchāmyahaṃ sthānādyathecchasi tathā kuru \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. O dear lady, I have now known it through your own words. I am now going away from this place. You can do as you please.

## \|\| 4.27.7 \|\|

*na kathyate tvayā mahyaṃ mitratvaṃ niṣphalambhavet \|*  
*yathā kāryyaṃ tathā bhāvi kathanīyaṃ sukhena ca \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. What should be done by you is not mentioned by me. To me your further friendship is useless. -But this should be mentioned that your future should be happy.

## \|\| 4.27.8 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*ityuktvā vacanaṃ tasya yāvadgantumiyeṣa saḥ \|*  
*tāvacca pārvatī devī praṇamyovāca taṃ dvijam \|\| 8 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

8\. After saying these words to her when he proposed to go, goddess Pārvatī bowed to and spoke to the brahmin.

## \|\| 4.27.9 \|\|

*\|\| pārvatyuvāca \|*  
*kiṃ gamiṣyasi viprendra sthito bhava hitaṃ vada \|*  
*ityukte ca tayā tatra sthitvovāca sa daṇḍadhṛk \|\| 9 \|\|*

Pārvatī said:—

9\. “O excellent brahmin, why do you go? Stay

and tender me wholesome advice”. When she said thus, the staff-bearing brahmin stopped and spoke.

## \|\| 4.27.10 \|\|

*dvija uvāca \|*  
*yadi śrotumanā devi māṃ sthāpayasi bhaktitaḥ \|*  
*vadāmi tattvaṃ tatsarvaṃ yena te vayunambhavet \|\| 10 \|\|*

The brahmin said:—

10\. If you are stopping me with devotion, truly desirous of hearing then I shall explain everything whereby you may gain some wisdom.

## \|\| 4.27.11 \|\|

*jānāmyahaṃ mahādevaṃ sarvathā gurudharmmataḥ \|*  
*pravadāmi yathārthaṃ hi sāvadhānatayā śṛṇu \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. I know Śiva through and through with all His weighty attributes. I shall tell you the truth. Listen with attention.

## \|\| 4.27.12 \|\|

*vṛṣadhvajo mahādevo bhasmadigdho jaṭādharaḥ \|*  
*vyāghracarmmāṃbaradharaḥ saṃvīto gajakṛttinā \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The great lord is bull-bannered. His body is smeared with ashes. His hair is matted. He is clad in the hide of a tiger. He has covered His body with the hide of an elephant.

## \|\| 4.27.13 \|\|

*kapāladhārī sarpaughaissarvagātreṣu veṣṭitaḥ \|*  
*viṣadigdho'bhakṣyabhakṣo virūpākṣo vibhīṣaṇaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. He holds the skull. Serpents twine round His limbs. Poison has left a mark on his neck. He eats even forbidden stuffs. He has odd eyes and is definitely awful.

## \|\| 4.27.14 \|\|

*avyaktajanmā satataṃ gṛhabhogavivarjitaḥ \|*  
*digaṃbaro daśabhujo bhūta pretānvitassadā \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. His birth and pedigree cannot be traced. He is devoid of the enjoyment of a householder. He has ten arms. He is mostly naked and is ever accompanied by ghosts and goblins.

## \|\| 4.27.15 \|\|

*kena kāraṇena tvaṃ taṃ bhartāraṃ samīhase \|*  
*kva jñānaṃ te gataṃ devi tadvadādya vicārataḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. What is the reason whereby you wish Him to be your husband? O gentle lady, where has your wisdom gone? Think well and tell me.

## \|\| 4.27.16 \|\|

*pūrvaṃ śrutaṃ mayā caiva vratantasya bhayaṃkaram \|*  
*śṛṇu te nigadāmyadya yadi te śravaṇe ruciḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. A previous terrible activity of His has been heard by me. If you are interested in hearing I shall tell you.

## \|\| 4.27.17 \|\|

*dakṣasya duhitā sādhvī satī vṛṣabhavāhanam \|*  
*vavre patiṃ purā daivāttatsaṃbhogaḥ pariśrutaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Dakṣa’s daughter, the chaste lady Satī wooed Vṛṣabhavāhana. (Śiva) as her husband. Fortunately their union was well known.

## \|\| 4.27.18 \|\|

*kapālijāyeti satī dakṣeṇa parivarjitā \|*  
*yajñe bhāgapradānāya śaṃbhuścāpi vivarjitaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Satī was discarded by Dakṣa because she was the wife of the skull-bearing Śiva. Śiva too was eschewed in the allocation of shares in the sacrifice.

## \|\| 4.27.19 \|\|

*sā tathaivāpamānena bhṛśaṃ kopākulā satī \|*  
*tatyājāsūnpriyāṃstatra tayā tyaktaśca śaṃkaraḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. On account of the insult Satī was infuriated and she discarded her dear life. Śiva too was abandoned by her.

## \|\| 4.27.20 \|\|

*tvaṃ strīratnaṃ tava pitā rājā nikhila bhūbhṛtām \|*  
*tathāvidhaṃ patiṃ kasmādugreṇa tapasehase \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. You are a jewel among women. Your father is the king of all mountains. Why do you crave for a husband like this and that too by means of a severe penance?

## \|\| 4.27.21 \|\|

*dattvā suvarṇamudrāṃ ca grahītuṃ kācamicchasi \|*  
*hitvā ca caṃdanaṃ śubhraṃ kardamaṃ leptumicchasi \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Handing over a gold coin you wish to buy a piece of glass. Setting aside the pure sandal paste you wish to smear mud over your body.

## \|\| 4.27.22 \|\|

*sūryyatejaḥ parityajya khadyotadyutimicchasi \|*  
*cīnāṃśukaṃ vihāyaiva carmmāṃbaramihecchasi \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Unmindful of the sunlight you wish to have the light of the glow worm. Throwing away the fine China silk you wish to wear the hide.

## \|\| 4.27.23 \|\|

*gṛhavāsamparityajya vanavāsaṃ samīhase \|*  
*lohamicchasi deveśa tyaktvā śevadhimuttamam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Discarding the life at home you yearn for a life in the forest, O madam, throwing away excellent treasure you wish a piece of iron in return.

## \|\| 4.27.24 \|\|

*indrādilokapālāṃśca hitvā śivamanu vratā \|*  
*naitatsūktaṃ hi lokeṣu viruddhaṃ dṛśyate'dhunā \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Leaving off the guardians of the quarters you run after Śiva. This is not well said. It is against the conventions of the world.

## \|\| 4.27.25 \|\|

*kva tvaṃ kamalapatrākṣī kvāsau vai trivilocanaḥ \|*  
*śaśāṃkavadanā tvaṃ ca paṃcavaktraḥ śivassmṛtaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Where you with eyes like the petals of a lotus? Where this three-eyed creature—Śiva? You are moon-faced while Śiva is five-faced.

## \|\| 4.27.26 \|\|

*veṇī śirasi te divyā sarpiṇīva vibhāsitā \|*  
*jaṭājūṭaṃ śivasyeva prasiddhamparicakṣate \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. On your head the divine plaited hair shines with glossy splendour like a serpent. But Śiva has only the matted hair to boast of.

## \|\| 4.27.27 \|\|

*caṃdanaṃ ca tvadīyāṃge citābhasma śivasya ca \|*  
*kva dukūlaṃ tvadīyaṃ vai śāṃkaraṃ kva gajājinam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Sandal paste is applied on your body, while the ashes of the funeral pyre on that of Śiva. Where your silken garment and where the elephant-hide of Śiva.

## \|\| 4.27.28 \|\|

*bhūṣaṇāni divyāni kva sarpāśśaṃkarasya ca \|*  
*kva carā devatāssarvāḥ kva ca bhūtabalipriyaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Where the divine ornaments and where the serpents of Śiva? Where the deities that move about and where Śiva, fond of goblins and their oblations?

## \|\| 4.27.29 \|\|

*kva vā mṛdaṃgavādaśca kva ca taḍḍamarustathā \|*  
*kva ca bherīkalāpaśca kva ca śṛṃgaravo'śubhaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Where the pleasing sound of his tabor? Where His peculiar drum called Damaru? Where the set of fine drums and the inauspicious sound of his horn?

## \|\| 4.27.30 \|\|

*kva ca ḍhakkāmayaḥ śabdo galanādaḥ kva cāśubhaḥ \|*  
*bhavatyāśca śivasyaiva na yuktaṃ rūpamuttamam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Where the inauspicious sound of double drum and where the sound of his throat? There is no matching beauty between you both.

## \|\| 4.27.31 \|\|

*yadi dravyaṃ bhavettasya kathaṃ syātsa digambaraḥ \|*  
*vāhanaṃ ca balīvardassāmagrī kāpi tasya na \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. If He had money to spare how could He have been a naked being? His vehicle is a bull. He has no other appendages.

## \|\| 4.27.32 \|\|

*vareṣu ye guṇāḥ proktā nārīṇāṃ sukhadāyakāḥ \|*  
*tanmadhye hi virūpākṣe ekopi na guṇaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. There is not even a single quality in the odd-eyed Śiva out of the innumberable qualities pleasing to women and expected in bride-grooms.

## \|\| 4.27.33 \|\|

*tavāpi kāmo dayito dagdhastena hareṇa ca \|*  
*anādarastadā dṛṣṭo hitvā tvāmanyato gataḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Your friend Kāma was burnt by Śiva. He insulted you also by leaving you off and going elsewhere.

## \|\| 4.27.34 \|\|

*jātirna dṛśyate tasya vidyājñānaṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*sahāyāśca piśācā hi viṣaṃ kaṇṭhe hi dṛśyate \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. His caste is not recognised. He has no learning or wisdom. His assistants are the ghosts. Poison is seen even in His throat.

## \|\| 4.27.35 \|\|

*ekākī ca sadā nityaṃ virāgī ca viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*tasmāttvaṃ hi hare naiva mano yoktuṃ tu cārhasi \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. He also moves about in isolation. He is detached from everything particularly. Hence you cannot fix your mind in Him.

## \|\| 4.27.36 \|\|

*kva ca hārastvadīyo vai kva ca tanmuṇḍamālikā \|*  
*aṃgarāgaḥ kva te divyaḥ citābhasma kva tattanau \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Where your necklace and where the garland of skulls that he wears? Where your rich divine unguent and where the ash from the funeral pyre that He has on His body?

## \|\| 4.27.37 \|\|

*sarvaṃ viruddhaṃ rūpādi tava devi harasya ca \|*  
*mahyaṃ na rocate hyetadyadicchasi tathā kuru \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. O divine lady, everything concerning you and Śiva, such as form, features etc. is mutually discordant. I do not like your resolution. You can do whatever you please.

## \|\| 4.27.38 \|\|

*asadvastu ca yatkiṃcit tatsarvaṃ svayamīhase \|*  
*nirvartaya manastasmānnocedicchasi tatkuru \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. You yourself have evolved taste for all bad objects. Turn your mind from Him. If not, do whatever you please.

## \|\| 4.27.39 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityevaṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā tasya viprasya pārvatī \|*  
*uvāca kruddhamanasā śivanindāparaṃ dvijam \|\| 39 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

39\. On hearing these words of that brahmin, Pārvatī said angrily to the brahmin who discredited Śiva.

## Chapter 28 - Pārvatī sees Śiva’s real form

## \|\| 4.28.1 \|\|

*pārvatyuvāca \|*  
*etāvaddhi mayā jñātaṃ kaścidanyoyamāgataḥ \|*  
*idānīṃ sakalaṃ jñātamavadhyastvamviśeṣataḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Pārvatī said:—

1\. So long I have been thinking that some one else has come. Now everything has become clear. You are a person who cannot be killed.

## \|\| 4.28.2 \|\|

*tvayoktaṃ viditaṃ deva tadalīkaṃ na cānyathā \|*  
*yadi tvayoditaṃ syādvai viruddhaṃ nocyate tvayā \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. O lord, what has been said by you is known. It is not otherwise. If what has been said by you is real, it cannot be called unreal.

## \|\| 4.28.3 \|\|

*kadāciddṛśyate tādṛk veṣadhārī maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*svalīlayā parabrahma svarāgopāttavigrahaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Sometimes lord Śiva is seen in that guise. But He is the supreme Brahman who, out of his own accord, takes up bodies in his own sports.

## \|\| 4.28.4 \|\|

*brahmacārisvarūpeṇa pratārayitumudyataḥ \|*  
*āgataśchalasaṃyuktaṃ vacovādīḥ kuyuktitaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. You have now come in the form of a student ascetic for the sake of deceiving me. Using false arguments, you have spoken fraudulent words.

## \|\| 4.28.5 \|\|

*śaṃkarasya svarūpaṃ tu jānāmi suviśeṣataḥ \|*  
*śivatattvamato vacmi suvicāryya yathārhataḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. I know the real form of Śiva very particularly. I shall therefore explain Śiva’s reality in the proper perspective after careful consideration.

## \|\| 4.28.6 \|\|

*vastuto nirguṇo brahma saguṇaḥ kāraṇena saḥ \|*  
*kuto jātirbhavettasya nirguṇasya guṇātmanaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. He is in fact devoid of attributes- But for some re-sons He takes up attributes. How can He have a birth, he who is really attributeless but takes up attributes?

## \|\| 4.28.7 \|\|

*sa sarvāsāṃ hi vidyānāmadhiṣṭhānaṃ sadāśivaḥ \|*  
*kiṃ tasya vidyayā kāryyaṃ pūrṇasya paramātmanaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Sadāśiva is the support and receptacle of all lores. Of what avail is learning to Him who is perfect and the supreme soul?

## \|\| 4.28.8 \|\|

*vedā ucchvāsarūpeṇa purā dattāśca viṣṇave \|*  
*śaṃbhunā tena kalpādau tatsamaḥ ko'sti suprabhuḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. At the beginning of the Kalpa, all the Vedas were given by Śiva to Viṣṇu in the form of breath. Who can be a good lord equal to Him?

## \|\| 4.28.9 \|\|

*sarveṣāmādibhūtasya vayomānaṃ kutastataḥ \|*  
*prakṛtistu tato jātā kiṃ śaktestasya kāraṇam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. How can He be measured in age, He who is primordial to everything and everyone. Even primordial nature (Prakṛti) is born of Him. Of what avail is then Energy to Him?

## \|\| 4.28.10 \|\|

*ye bhajaṃti ca taṃ prītyā śaktīśaṃ śaṃkaraṃ sadā \|*  
*tasmai śaktitrayaṃ śaṃbhuḥ sa dadāti sadāvyayam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. With the threefold Energies, Śiva blesses those who worship Him always as the lord of Energies.

## \|\| 4.28.11 \|\|

*tasyaiva bhajanājjīvo mṛtyuṃ jayati nirbhayaḥ \|*  
*tasmānmṛtyuṃjayannāma prasiddhambhuvanatraye \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Every individual soul becomes fearless and conquers death by worshipping Him. Hence His designation ‘the conqueror of death’ is famous in all the three worlds.

## \|\| 4.28.12 \|\|

*tasyaiva pakṣapātena viṣṇurviṣṇutvamāpnuyāt \|*  
*brahmatvaṃ ca yathā brahmā devā devatvameva ca \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Viṣṇu attains and retains his Viṣṇuhood by His favour. Similarly Brahmā his Brahmahood and the gods their godhood.

## \|\| 4.28.13-14 \|\|

*darśanārthaṃ śivasyādau yathā gacchati devarāṭ \|*  
*bhūtādayastatparasya dvārapālāśśivasya tu \|\| 13 \|\|*

*daṇḍaiśca mukuṭaṃ viddhaṃ mṛṣṭaṃ bhavati sarvataḥ \|*  
*kiṃ tasya bahupakṣeṇa svayameva mahāprabhuḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14 Whenever the lord of the gods wants to see Śiva he has to propitiate His gate-keepers, the ghosts etc., otherwise his crown becomes shattered by batons. Really Śiva is a great lord. He has no need for many attendants.

## \|\| 4.28.15 \|\|

*kalyāṇarūpiṇastasya sevayeha na kiṃ bhavet \|*  
*kiṃ nyūnaṃ tasya devasya māmicchati sadāśivaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. What is it that cannot befall one who serves the auspicious-featured Śiva. What is deficient in that lord? Does Sadāśiva like me?

## \|\| 4.28.16 \|\|

*saptajanmadaridraḥ syātsevenno yadi śaṃkaram \|*  
*tasyaitatsevanālloko lakṣmīḥ syādanapāyinī \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Even if a person is perpetually poor for seven lives, after serving Śiva, his prosperity becomes unhampered.

## \|\| 4.28.17 \|\|

*yadagre siddhayoṣṭau ca nityaṃ nṛtyaṃti toṣitum \|*  
*avāṅmukhāssadā tatra taddhitaṃ durllabhaṃ kutaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. How can he find benefit inaccessible—he in whose presence the eight Siddhis (achievements) dance always for the sake of propitiation with speechless mouths or with lowered faces.

## \|\| 4.28.18 \|\|

*yadyasya maṃgālānīha sevate śaṃkarasya na \|*  
*yathāpi maṃgalantasya smaraṇādeva jāyate \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Although Śiva resorts to inauspicious things yet by thinking on Him everything becomes auspicious.

## \|\| 4.28.19 \|\|

*yasya pūjāprabhāveṇa kāmāssiddhyanti sarvaśaḥ \|*  
*kuto vikārastasyāsti nirvikārasya sarvadā \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. His worship fulfils all desires. How can there be aberration in Him who always remains in an unmodified state.

## \|\| 4.28.20 \|\|

*śiveti maṃgalannāma mukhe yasya nirantaram \|*  
*tasyaiva darśanādanye pavitrāssaṃti sarvadā \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. People are sanctified by merely seeing the person in whose mouth the auspicious name “Śiva” is ever present.

## \|\| 4.28.21 \|\|

*yadyapūtambhavedbhasma citāyāśca tvayoditam \|*  
*nityamasyāṃgagaṃ devaiśśirobhirddhāryate katham \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. If, as you say, the ash from the funeral pyre is unholy, how is it that the same transferred to Śiva’s body is taken thence and worn on the head by the gods?

## \|\| 4.28.22 \|\|

*yo devo jagatāṃ kartā bhartā hartā guṇānvitaḥ \|*  
*nirguṇaśśivasaṃjñaśca sa vijñeyaḥ kathambhavet \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. How can He be easily realised, He who is the deity that creates, sustains and annihilates the worlds, all the same who is devoid of attributes and is termed Śiva?

## \|\| 4.28.23 \|\|

*aguṇaṃ brahmaṇo rūpaṃ śivasya paramātmanaḥ \|*  
*tatkathaṃ hi vijānanti tvādṛśāstadbahirmukhāḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. The form of Śiva, the supreme soul, is that of Brahman, devoid of attributes. How can people like you know it, people with extrovert faces?

## \|\| 4.28.24 \|\|

*durācārāśca pāpāśca devebhyaste vinirgatāḥ \|*  
*tattvaṃ te naiva jānanti śivasyāguṇarūpiṇaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Persons of evil conduct, sinners and those who have gone astray from the path of the gods do not at all know the reality of Śiva of attributeless form.

## \|\| 4.28.25 \|\|

*śivanindāṃ karotīha tattvamajñāya yaḥ pumān \|*  
*ājanmasaṃcitaṃ puṇyaṃ bhasmībhavati tasya tat \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. If, out of ignorance of His reality, any one were to discredit Śiva, his merit hoarded ever since birth becomes reduced to ashes.

## \|\| 4.28.26 \|\|

*tvayā niṃdā kṛtā yātra harasyāmita tejasaḥ \|*  
*tvatpūjā ca kṛtā yanme tasmātpāpambhajāmyaham \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. You have censured Śiva of immeasurable splendour and I have worshiped you, hence I have become sinful.

## \|\| 4.28.27 \|\|

*śivavidveṣiṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā sacelaṃ snānamācaret \|*  
*śivavidveṣiṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā prāyaścitaṃ samācaret \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. On seeing a person who hates Śiva one should take bath along with one’s clothes. On seeing a person who hates Śiva one should perform expiatory rites.

## \|\| 4.28.28 \|\|

*re re duṣṭa tvayā coktamahaṃ jānāmi śaṃkaram \|*  
*niścayena na vijñātaśśiva eva sanātanaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. O wicked one, you profess knowledge of Śiva. But you should know that the eternal Śiva is not known at all.

## \|\| 4.28.29 \|\|

*yathā tathā bhavedrudro yathā vā bahurūpavān \|*  
*mamābhīṣṭatamo nityaṃ nirvikārī satāṃ priyaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Whatever may be the form or feature of Śiva, He is multiformed. Still He is my favourite. He is without aberration and beloved of the good.

## \|\| 4.28.30 \|\|

*viṣṇurbrahmāpi na samastasya kvāpi mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*kuto'nye nirjarādyāśca kālādhīnāssadaivatam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Neither Viṣṇu nor Brahmā can equal that noble soul. How can then the gods and others be? They are always dependent on Time and are not eternal.

## \|\| 4.28.31 \|\|

*iti budhyā samālokya svayā satyā sutattvataḥ \|*  
*śivārthaṃ vanamāgatya karomi vipulaṃ tapaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. After realising this with my sharp intellect factually, I have come to this forest and am performing the elaborate penance for attaining Śiva.

## \|\| 4.28.32 \|\|

*sa eva parameśānassarveśo bhaktavatsalaḥ \|*  
*saṃprāptumme'bhilāṣo hi dīnānugrahakārakam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. My ambition is to attain the supreme lord who is favourably disposed to His devotees and who blesses the distressed.

## \|\| 4.28.33 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityuktvā girijā sā hi girīśvarasutā mune \|*  
*virarāma śivaṃ dadhyo nirvikāreṇa cetasā \|\| 33 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

33\. After saying this, O sage, Pārvatī, the daughter of the mountain, stopped and meditated on Śiva with unaffected mind.

## \|\| 4.28.34-35 \|\|

*tadākarṇya vaco devyā brahmacārī sa vai dvijaḥ \|*  
*punarvacanamākhyātuṃ yāvadeva pracakrame \|\| 34 \|\|*

*uvāca girijā tāvatsvasakhīṃ vijayāṃ drutam \|*  
*śiva saktamanovṛttiśśivaniṃdāparāṅmukhī \|\| 35 \|\|*

34-35. On hearing the words of the goddess when the brahmin ascetic began to say something, Pārvatī whose mind was fixed on Śiva and who was averse to hear any disparaging remarks about Śiva spoke immediately to Vijayā, her maid.

## \|\| 4.28.36 \|\|

*girijovāca \|*  
*vāraṇīyaḥ prayatnena sakhyayaṃ hi dvijādhamaḥ \|*  
*punarvaktumanāścaiva śivaniṃdāṃ kariṣyati \|\| 36 \|\|*

Pārvatī said:—

36\. This base brahmin must be prevented strenuously. He is inclined to say something again. He will surely censure Śiva.

## \|\| 4.28.37 \|\|

*na kevalambhavetpāpaṃ nindāṃ kartuśśivasya hi \|*  
*yo vai śṛṇoti tannindāṃ pāpabhāk sa bhavediha \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Not only does he who disparages Śiva incur sin but also he who hears the same.

## \|\| 4.28.38 \|\|

*śivanindākaro vadhyassarvathā śivakiṃkaraiḥ \|*  
*brāhmaṇaścetsa vai tyājyo gantavyaṃ tatsthalāddrutam \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. A person who disparages Śiva is definitely worthy of being killed by Śiva’s attendants. If it is a brahmin he must be dismissed or the hearer shall go away from that place immediately.

## \|\| 4.28.39 \|\|

*ayaṃ duṣṭaḥ punarnindāṃ kariṣyati śivasya hi \|*  
*brāhmaṇatvādavadhyaścaittyājyo'dṛśyaśca sarvathā \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. This wicked man will again disparage Śiva. Since he is a brahmin, he is not to be killed. He shall be abandoned. He shall not be seen at all.

## \|\| 4.28.40 \|\|

*hitvaitatsthalamadyeva yāsyāmo'nyatra mā ciram \|*  
*yathā saṃbhāṣaṇaṃ na syādanenā'viduṣā punaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Let us leave this place at once and go elsewhere. Do not tarry. Let there be no more talk with this ignorant man.

## \|\| 4.28.41 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityuktvā comayā yāvatpādamutkṣipyate mune \|*  
*asau tāvacchivassākṣādālaṃbe priyayā svayam \|\| 41 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

41\. Saying this, O sage, even as Pārvatī was about to step ahead, the brahmin manifesting as Śiva clasped his beloved.

## \|\| 4.28.42 \|\|

*kṛtvā svarūpaṃ subhagaṃ śivādhyānaṃ yathā tathā \|*  
*darśayitvā śivāyai tāmuvācāvāṅmukhīṃ śivaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. After assuming the handsome form in the manner Pārvatī had meditated upon and manifesting it to Pārvatī, Śiva addressed her while she stood with her lowered head.

## \|\| 4.28.43 \|\|

*śiva uvāca \|*  
*kutra yāsyasi māṃ hitvā na tvaṃ tyājyā mayā punaḥ \|*  
*prasanno'smi varaṃ brūhi nādeyamvidyate tava \|\| 43 \|\|*

Śiva said:—

43\. “Where will you go, leaving me? You are not to be discarded again by me. I am delighted. Tell me what boon shall I grant you. There is nothing that cannot be given to you.

## \|\| 4.28.44 \|\|

*adyaprabhṛti te dāsastapobhiḥ krīta eva te \|*  
*krīto'smi tavasaundaryātkṣaṇamekaṃ yugāya te \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. From today I am your slave bought by you by performing penance. I have been bought by your beauty. Even a moment appears like a Yuga.

## \|\| 4.28.45 \|\|

*tyajyatāṃ ca tvayā lajjā mama patnī sanātanī \|*  
*girije tvaṃ hi sadbudhyā vicāraya maheśvari \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. O Pārvatī, O great Goddess, you are my eternal wife. Let this shyness be eschewed. You please ponder with your keen intellect.

## \|\| 4.28.46 \|\|

*mayā parīkṣitāsi tvaṃ bahudhā dṛḍhamānase \|*  
*tatkṣamasvāparādhamme lokalīlānusāriṇaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. O steady-minded one, you have been tested by me in various ways. Let my guilt be excused in following this worldly game.

## \|\| 4.28.47 \|\|

*na tvādṛśīmpraṇayinīṃ paśyāmi ca trilokake \|*  
*sarvathāhaṃ tavādhīnassvakāmaḥ pūryyatāṃ śive \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Even in the three worlds I do not see a beloved like you. O Pārvatī, in every respect I am subservient to you. You can fulfil all your desires.

## \|\| 4.28.48 \|\|

*ehi priye matsakāśaṃ patnī tvaṃ me varastava \|*  
*tvayā sākaṃ drutaṃ yāsye svagṛhamparvattottamam \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. O beloved, come on near me. You are my wife. I am your bridegroom. I shall immediately go to my abode—the excellent mountain, along with you.

## \|\| 4.28.49 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityukte devadevena pārvatī mudamāpa sā \|*  
*tapojātaṃ tu yatkaṣṭaṃ tajjahau ca purātanam \|\| 49 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

49\. When the lord of the gods spoke in this way, Pārvatī rejoiced. Whatever distress she had felt during penance she cast off as something old.

## \|\| 4.28.50 \|\|

*sarvaḥ śramo vinaṣṭobhūtsa tyāstu munisattama \|*  
*phale jāte śramaḥ pūrvo jantornāśamavāpnuyāt \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. O excellent sage, her weariness subsided. In fact, when the fruit is realised, the exertion felt during the process of undertaking perishes.

## Chapter 29 - Śivā-Śiva dialogue

## \|\| 4.29.1 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*brahman vidhe mahābhāga kiṃ jātaṃ tadanantaram \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ śrotumicchāmi kathaya tvaṃ śivāyaśaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Nārada said:—

1\. O Brahmā, O fortunate one, what happened thereafter? I wish to hear everything. Please narrate the glory of Pārvatī to me.

## \|\| 4.29.2 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*devarṣe śrūyatāṃ samyakkathayāmi kathāṃ mudā \|*  
*tāṃ mahāpāpasaṃhartrīṃ śivabhaktivivarddhinīm \|\| 2 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

2\. O celestial sage, let this be listened to. I shall resume the story joyfully, the story that quells all sins and increases devotion to Śiva.

## \|\| 4.29.3 \|\|

*pārvatī vacanaṃ śrutvā harassa paramātmanaḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭvānandakaraṃ rūpaṃ jaharṣātīva ca dvija \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. O brahmin, on hearing the words of Śiva, the great Soul and on seeing His pleasant form and features Pārvatī was delighted much.

## \|\| 4.29.4 \|\|

*pratyuvāca mahā sādhvī svopakaṇṭhasthitaṃ vibhum \|*  
*atīva sukhitā devī prītyutphullānanā śivā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The highly chaste lady, goddess Pārvatī replied to the lord standing near with great pleasure and face beaming with love.

## \|\| 4.29.5 \|\|

*pārvatyuvāca \|*  
*tvaṃ nātho mama deveśa tvayā kiṃ vismṛtampurā \|*  
*dakṣayajñavināśaṃ hi yadarthaṃ kṛtavānhaṭhāt \|\| 5 \|\|*

Pārvatī said:—

5\. O lord, O lord of gods, you are my husband. Has it been forgotten by you why you destroyed the sacrifice of Dakṣa formerly with great tenacity?

## \|\| 4.29.6 \|\|

*sa tvaṃ sāhaṃ samutpannā menayāṃ kāryyasiddhaye \|*  
*devānāṃ deva dedeśa tārakāptā'sukhātmanām \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Listen, O lord of gods, I am born of Menā for the achievement of the task of the gods terrified to the quick by Tāraka.

## \|\| 4.29.7 \|\|

*yadi prasanno deveśa karoṣi ca kṛpāṃ yadi \|*  
*patirbhava mameśāna mama vākyaṃ kuru prabho \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. O lord of gods, if you are delighted, if you are sympathetic, O lord, become my husband. O lord do as I say.

## \|\| 4.29.8 \|\|

*piturgehe mayā samyaggamyate tvadanujayā \|*  
*prasiddhaṃ kriyatāṃ tadvai viśuddhaṃ paramaṃ yaśaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. With your permission I am going to my father’s abode. Let your pure great glory be made well known.

## \|\| 4.29.9 \|\|

*gantavyaṃ bhavatā nātha himavatpārśvataṃ prabho \|*  
*yācasva māṃ tato bhikṣu bhūtvā līlāviśāradaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. O lord, you will please go to Himavat. Clever in divine sports, be the mendicant and beg of him, me as your alms.

## \|\| 4.29.10 \|\|

*tathā tvayā prakartavyaṃ loke khyāpayatā yaśaḥ \|*  
*piturme saphalaṃ sarvaṃ kuruṣvaivaṃ gṛhā mam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Spreading your glory in the worlds you shall make everything about my father fruitful. Thus you start your householder’s life.”

## \|\| 4.29.11 \|\|

*ṛṣibhirbodhitaḥ prītyā svabandhuparivāritaḥ \|*  
*kariṣyati na saṃdehastava vākyaṃ pitā mama \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. There is no doubt that my father with his kinsmen will accede to your request as he has already been urged by the sages lovingly.

## \|\| 4.29.12 \|\|

*dakṣakanyā purāhaṃ vai pitrā dattā yadā tava \|*  
*yathoktavidhinā tatra vivāho na kṛtastvayā \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Formerly as Dakṣa’s daughter I was offered to you by my father. But the marriage rites were not duly performed then.

## \|\| 4.29.13 \|\|

*na grahāḥ pūjitāstena dakṣeṇa janakena me \|*  
*grahāṇāṃ viṣayastena sacchidroyaṃ mahānabhūt \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The planets were not worshipped by my father. Therefore a great defect occurred in our marriage in regard to the planets.

## \|\| 4.29.14 \|\|

*tasmādyathoktavidhinā kartumarhasi me prabho \|*  
*vivāhaṃ tvaṃ mahādeva devānāṃ kāryyasiddhaye \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Hence, O lord, you will celebrate marriage in accordance with the rules for the fulfilment of the task of the gods.

## \|\| 4.29.15 \|\|

*vivāhasya yathā rītiḥ kartavyā sā tathā dhuvam \|*  
*jānātu himavān samyak kṛtaṃ putryā śubhaṃ tapaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The customary procedures of the marriage shall certainly be followed. Let Himavat know that an auspicious penance has been performed well by his daughter.

## \|\| 4.29.16 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|\| ityevaṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā suprasannassadāśivaḥ \|*  
*provāca vacanaṃ prītyā girijāṃ prahasanniva \|\| 16 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

16\. On hearing these words, Sadāśiva was highly delighted. Laughingly and lovingly He spoke to Pārvatī.

Śiva said—

## \|\| 4.29.17 \|\|

*śiva uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu devi maheśāni paramaṃ vacanaṃ mama \|*  
*yathocitaṃ sumāṅgalyamavikāri tathā kuru \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. O great Goddess, listen to my important statement. See that our marriage rites are performed in the proper manner without deficiency.

## \|\| 4.29.18 \|\|

*brahmādikāni bhūtāni tvanityāni varānane \|*  
*dṛṣṭaṃ yatsarvametacca naśvaraṃ viddhi bhāmini \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. O sweet-faced one, all the living beings Brahmā and others are non-eternal. O beautiful lady, know all these visible things to be perishable.

## \|\| 4.29.19 \|\|

*ekonekatvamāpanno nirguṇo hi guṇānvitaḥ\|\| \|*  
*jyotsnayā yo vibhāti parajyotsnānvito'bhavat \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Know that the single beings assumed manifold forms. The attributeless took over the attributes. That which is self-luminous had other lights imposed on it.

## \|\| 4.29.20 \|\|

*svatantraḥ paratantraśca tvayā devi kṛto hyaham \|*  
*sarvakartrī ca prakṛtirmahāmāyā tvameva hi \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. O gentle lady, I, the independent, have been made subservient by you. You alone are the great illusory power, the Primordial nature that creates.

## \|\| 4.29.21 \|\|

*māyāmayaṃ kṛtamidaṃ ca jagatsamagraṃ sarvātmanā hi vidhṛtaṃ parayā svabuddhyā \|*  
*savārtmabhissukṛtibhiḥ paramātmabhāvaissaṃsiktamātmani gaṇaḥ pariveṣṭitaśca \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. This entire universe has been made of illusion; it is held by the supreme soul with His great intellect. It is united and enveloped by the Gaṇas of the nature of pervading souls of meritorious deeds, akin to the nature of supreme soul.

## \|\| 4.29.22 \|\|

*ke grahāḥ ke ṛtugaṇāḥ ke vānyepi tvayā grahāḥ \|*  
*kimuktaṃ cādhunā devi śivārthaṃ varavarṇini \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. What are these planets? What are these sets of seasons? What are those other planets? o gentle lady, what is said by you, O fair-complexioned one.

## \|\| 4.29.23 \|\|

*guṇakāryyaprabhedenāvābhyāṃ prādurbhavaḥ kṛtaḥ \|*  
*bhaktahetorjagatyasminbhaktavatsalabhāvataḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. We two have created the universe different in attributes and actions for the sake of the devotees and with a disposition favourable to them.

## \|\| 4.29.24 \|\|

*tvaṃ hi vai prakṛtissūkṣmā rajassattvatamomayī \|*  
*vyāpāradakṣā satataṃ saguṇā nirguṇāpi ca \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. You are indeed the subtle primordial nature consisting of Rajas, Sattva and Tamas. You are capable of perpetual activity. You are both possessed and devoid of attributes.

## \|\| 4.29.25 \|\|

*sarveṣāmiha bhūtānāmahamātmā sumadhyame \|*  
*nirvikārī nirīhaśca bhaktecchopāttavigrahaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. O slender-waisted lady, of all living beings I am the soul without abberation without yearnings. I take up bodies at the requests and wishes of my devotees.

## \|\| 4.29.26 \|\|

*himālayaṃ na gaccheyaṃ janakaṃ tava śailaje \|*  
*tatastvāṃ bhikṣuko bhūtvā na yāceyaṃ kathaṃcana \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. O daughter of the mountain, I will not go up to Himavat your father. I will not become a mendicant and beg of him for you.

## \|\| 4.29.27 \|\|

*mahāguṇairgariṣṭhopi mahātmāpi girīndraje \|*  
*dehītivacanātsadyaḥ puruṣo yāti lāghavam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. O daughter of the lord of mountains, even a weighty person endowed with great qualities, even a noble soul, is considered base immediately after uttering the words—“Please give me”.

## \|\| 4.29.28 \|\|

*itthaṃ jñātvā tu kalyāṇi kimasmākaṃ vadasyatha \|*  
*kāryyaṃ tvadājñayā bhadre yathecchasi tathā kuru \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. O benevolent lady, after knowing this what is it that you say is our duty? Gentle lady, do as you wish.

## \|\| 4.29.29 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*tenoktāpi mahādevī sā sādhvī kamalekṣaṇā \|*  
*jagāda śaṃkaraṃ bhaktyā supraṇamya punaḥ punaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

29\. Thus addressed, the great goddess, the chaste lady of lotus-like eyes told Śiva with devotion after bowing to Him again and again.

## \|\| 4.29.30 \|\|

*pārvatyuvāca \|*  
*tvamātmā prakṛtiścāhaṃ nātra kāryyā vicāraṇā \|*  
*svatantrau bhaktavaśagau nirguṇau saguṇāvapi \|\| 30 \|\|*

Pārvatī said:—

30\. “You are the cosmic soul and I am the cosmic nature. There is nothing to deliberate on this. We two are independent and subservient to the devotees. We two are both possessed and devoid of attributes.

## \|\| 4.29.31 \|\|

*prayatnena tvayā śambho kāryaṃ vākyaṃ mama prabho \|*  
*yācasva māṃ himagiressaubhāgyaṃ dehi śaṅkara \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. O lord Śiva, with effort, you will please do according to my request. O Śiva, beg of Himavat for me, You will bestow a fortune on him.

## \|\| 4.29.32 \|\|

*kṛpāṃ kuru maheśāna tava bhaktāsmi nityaśaḥ \|*  
*tava patnī sadā nātha hyahaṃ janmani janmani \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. O great lord, be sympathetic. I am your devotee for ever. I am your wife for ever in ever birth.

## \|\| 4.29.33 \|\|

*tvaṃ brahma paramātmā hi nirguṇaḥ prakṛteḥ paraḥ \|*  
*nirvikārī nirīhaśca svatantraḥ parameśvaraḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. You are Brahman, the great soul, devoid of attributes greater than primordial nature, without abberration, free from yearnings, independent, great lord.

## \|\| 4.29.34 \|\|

*tathāpi saguṇopīha bhaktoddhāraparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*vihārī svātmanirato nānālīlāviśāradaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Still you are possessed of attributes too and enthusiastic in the uplift of the devotees. You sport about in your own soul engrossed in it and you are clever in your different sports.

## \|\| 4.29.35 \|\|

*sarvathā tvāmahaṃ jāne mahādeva maheśvara \|*  
*kimuktena ca sarvajña bahunā hi dayāṃ kuru \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. O great lord, I know you in every respect. O omniscient, of what avail is a detailed talk. Take pity on me.

## \|\| 4.29.36 \|\|

*vistāraya yaśo loke kṛtvā līlāṃ mahādbhutām \|*  
*yatsugīya janā nāthāṃjasottīrṇā bhavāmbudheḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Spread your glory in the world indulging in your wonderful divine sports. Singing them, O lord, people can cross the ocean of worldly existence.

## \|\| 4.29.37 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityevamuktvā girijā supraṇamya punaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*virarāma maheśānaṃ nataskandhā kṛtāṃjaliḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

37\. After saying these words to the great lord, Pārvatī stopped and bowed to Him frequently with shoulders stooping and palms joined in reverence.

## \|\| 4.29.38 \|\|

*ityevamuktassa tayā mahātmā maheśvaro lokaviḍambanāya \|*  
*tatheti mattvā prahasanbabhūva mudānvitaḥ kartumanāstadeva \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Thus addressed by her, Śiva of the noble soul, just to follow and imitate the worldly conventions thought that it should be so. Being desirous of doing so he rejoiced.

## \|\| 4.29.39 \|\|

*tato hyantarhitaśśambhurbabhūva supraharṣitaḥ \|*  
*kailāsaṃ prayayau kālyā virahākṛṣṭamānasaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Then Śiva vanished. With a great delight He went to Kailāsa but at His separation from Pārvatī his mind was distressed.

## \|\| 4.29.40 \|\|

*tatra gatvā maheśāno nandyādibhyassa ūcivān \|*  
*vṛttāntaṃ sakalaṃ tamvai paramānandanirbharaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. After reaching there He mentioned the news to Nandin and others. He was very much delighted.

## \|\| 4.29.41 \|\|

*te'pi śrutvā gaṇāssarve bhairavādyāśca sarvaśaḥ \|*  
*babhūvussukhinotyantaṃ vidadhuḥ paramotsavam \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Those Gaṇas, Bhairava and others were greatly pleased. They celebrated the occasion with great festivities.

## \|\| 4.29.42 \|\|

*sumaṃgalaṃ tatra dvija babhūvātīva nārada \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ duḥkhanāśobhūdrudraḥ prāpāpi saṃmudam \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. O Nārada, all went on auspiciously. All misery was at an end. Śiva too was in a pleasant mood.

## Chapter 30 - The Celebration of Pārvatī’s Return

## \|\| 4.30.1 \|\|

*\|\| nārada uvāca \|*  
*vidhe tāta mahābhāga dhanyastvaṃ paramārthadṛk \|*  
*adbhuteyaṃ kathāśrāvi tvadanugrahato mayā \|\| 1 \|\|*

Nārada said:—

1\. O Brahmā, O dear, of great fortune, you have the real vision and are blessed. This wonderful story was heard by me, thanks to your blessings.

## \|\| 4.30.2 \|\|

*gate hare svaśaile hi pārvatī sarvamaṃgalā \|*  
*kiṃ cakāra gatā kutra tanme vada mahāmate \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. When Śiva returned to His mountain, O intelligent one, what did Pārvatī allauspicious do and where did she go? Please tell me.

## \|\| 4.30.3 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*śṛṇu suprītitastāta yajjātaṃ tadanantaram \|*  
*hare gate nijasthāne tadvadāmi śivaṃ smaran \|\| 3 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

3\. O dear, listen with pleasure to what happened thereafter when Śiva returned to His place. I shall mention it, remembering Śiva,

## \|\| 4.30.4 \|\|

*pārvatyapi sakhīyuktā rūpaṃ kṛtvā tu sārthakam \|*  
*jagāma svapiturgehaṃ mahādeveti vādinī \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Accompanied by her maids and assuming meaningful dress and features she returned to her father’s house repeating the name of lord Śiva.

## \|\| 4.30.5 \|\|

*pārvatyāgamanaṃ śrutvā menā ca sa himācalaḥ \|*  
*divyaṃ yānaṃ samāruhya prayayau harṣavihvalaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. On hearing that Pārvatī was returning, Menā and Himavat excessively delighted went ahead seated in a divine vehicle.

## \|\| 4.30.6-7 \|\|

*purohitaśca paurāśca sakhyaścaivāpyanekaśaḥ \|*  
*samvandhinastathānye ca sarve te ca samāyayuḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*bhrātaraḥ sakalā jagmurmainākapramukhāstadā \|*  
*jayaśabdaṃ prabruvanto mahāharṣasamanvitāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7 The chief priest, the citizens, the maids, the kinsmen and also others accompanied them. All the brothers with Maināka, the eldest, accompanied them highly delighted and crying shouts of victory.

## \|\| 4.30.8-12 \|\|

*saṃsthāpya maṃgalaghaṭaṃ rājavartmani rājite \|*  
*candanāgarukastūrīphalaśākhāsamanvite \|\| 8 \|\|*

*sapurodhobrāhmaṇaiśca munibhirbrahmavādibhiḥ \|*  
*nārībhirnartakībhiśca gajendrādrisuśobhitaiḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*paritaḥ parito raṃbhāstambhavṛndasamanvite \|*  
*patiputravatīyoṣitsamūhairdīpahastakaiḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*dvijavṛndaiśca saṃyukte kurvadbhirmaṅgaladhvanim \|*  
*nānāprakāravādyaiśca śaṃkhadhvanibhiranvite \|\| 11 \|\|*

*etasminnantare durgā jagāma svapurāntikam \|*  
*viśaṃtī nagaraṃ devī dadarśa pitarau punaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

8-12. The auspicious waterpot was placed in the main highway decorated with sandal paste, aguru, musk and branches of trees with fruits. The priests, brahmins and sages reciting the Vedas, dancing girls, all went ahead seated on lofty elephants to receive her. All round stumps of plantain trees were fixed. Women along with their sons and husbands held lamps in their hands. Brahmins were shouting mantras etc. in an auspicious voice. Various instruments were played. Conch shells were sounded. In the meantime Pārvatī reached the outskirts of the city. Entering the city she saw her parents again.

## \|\| 4.30.13 \|\|

*suprasannau pradhāvantau harṣavihvalamānasau \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā kālī suprahṛṣṭā svālibhiḥ praṇanāma tau \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. On seeing the parents rushing at her in their great delight, she gladly bowed to them along with her maids.

## \|\| 4.30.14 \|\|

*tau sampūrṇāśiṣaṃ dattvā cakratustau svavakṣasi \|*  
*he vatse tvevamuccārya rudantau premavihvalau \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. They gave her their blessings and embraced her. Saying “O darling,” they shed tears in their excitement of love.

## \|\| 4.30.15 \|\|

*tatassvakīyā apyasyā anyā nāryāpi saṃmudā \|*  
*bhrātṛstriyopi suprītyā dṛḍhāliṃganamādadhuḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Women near and dear as also the wives of her brothers embraced her closely with great pleasure.

## \|\| 4.30.16 \|\|

*sādhitaṃ hi tvayā samyaksukāryaṃ kulatāraṇam \|*  
*tvatsadācaraṇenāpi pāvitāḥ smākhilā vayam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. “A great task has been well accomplished by you. It has saved the whole family. All of us are sanctified by your noble conduct”.

## \|\| 4.30.17 \|\|

*iti sarve supraśaṃsya praṇemustāṃ praharṣitāḥ \|*  
*candanaiḥ suprasūnaiśca samānarcuśśivāṃ mudā \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Praising her with these and similar words they bowed to her with great delight. They worshipped her with sandal paste and sweet scented flowers in great joy.

## \|\| 4.30.18 \|\|

*tasminnavasare devā vimānasthā mudāmbare \|*  
*puṣpavṛṣṭiṃ śubhāṃ cakrurnatvā tāṃ tuṣṭuvuḥ stavaiḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. At that time the gods, seated in their aerial chariots in the sky, showered auspicious flowers, bowed to and eulogised her with hymns.

## \|\| 4.30.19 \|\|

*tadā tāṃ ca rathe sthāpya sarve śobhānvite vare \|*  
*puraṃ praveśayāmāsussarve viprādayo mudā \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Then the Brahmins and others joyfully took you within the city in a resplendent chariot.

## \|\| 4.30.20 \|\|

*atha viprāḥ purodhāśca sakhyonyāśca striyaḥ śivām \|*  
*gṛhaṃ praveśayāmāsurbahumānapurassaram \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Then the brahmins, the maids and other women took her within the house with due honour.

## \|\| 4.30.21 \|\|

*striyo nirmacchanaṃ cakrurviprā yuyujurāśiṣaḥ \|*  
*himavānmenakā mātā mumodāti munīśvara \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. O great sage, ladies performed her ceremonial ablution; the brahmins offered benedictions. Himvat and Menakā rejoiced much.

## \|\| 4.30.22 \|\|

*svāśramaṃ saphalaṃ mene kuputrātputrikā varā \|*  
*himavānnāradaṃ tvāñca saṃstuvan sādhusādhviti \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Himavat considered his household life fruitful. A daughter is far better than an ignoble son. He praised you too, Nārada, saying “Well done, Well done”.

## \|\| 4.30.23 \|\|

*brāhmaṇebhyaśca baṃdibhyaḥ parvatendro dhanaṃ dadau \|*  
*maṅgalaṃ pāṭhayāmāsa sa dvijebhyo mahotsavam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. The lord of the mountains gave monetary gifts to brahmins and lords. He made the brahmins recite auspicious hymns, as part of the festivities.

## \|\| 4.30.24 \|\|

*evaṃ svakanyayā hṛṣṭau pitarau bhrātarastathā \|*
