*jāmayaśca mahāprītyā samūṣuḥ prāṃgaṇe mune \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. The parents delighted with their daughter; the brothers and the sisters gathered joyfully in the courtyard, O sage.

## \|\| 4.30.25 \|\|

*tatassa himavān tāta suprahṛṣṭāḥ prasannadhīḥ \|*  
*sammānya sakalānprītyā snātuṃ gaṃgāṃ jagāma ha \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The happy and delighted Himavat, honoured everyone. Then he went to the Gaṅgā for his bath.

## \|\| 4.30.26 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare śaṃbhussulīlo bhaktavatsalaḥ \|*  
*sunartakanaṭo bhūtvā menakāsaṃnidhiṃ yayau \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. In the meantime, Śiva, favourably disposed to His disciples and prone to divine sports, assumed the guise of a dancer and approached Menakā.

## \|\| 4.30.27-28 \|\|

*śṛṃgaṃ vāme kare dhṛtvā dakṣiṇe ḍamaru tathā \|*  
*pṛṣṭhe kaṃthāṃ raktavāsā nṛtyagānaviśāradaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*tatassunaṭarūposau menakāyā gaṇe mudā \|*  
*cakre sunṛtyaṃ vividhaṃ gānaṃ cātimanoharam \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. He held the blowing horn in his left and the drum in his right hand. He wore a red cloth and had the wallet suspended behind his back. In the guise of a dancer with the skill of dancing and singing, he danced well and sang many songs in sweet voice.

## \|\| 4.30.29 \|\|

*śṛṃgaṃ ca ḍamaruṃ tatra vādayāmāsa sudhvanim \|*  
*mahatīṃ vividhāṃ tatra sa cakāra manoharām \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. He blew the horn and played on the drum in very sweet tunes. Everything was very pleasant.

## \|\| 4.30.30 \|\|

*tāṃ draṣṭuṃ nāgarāssarve puruṣāśca striyastathā \|*  
*ājagmussahasā tatra bālā vṛddhā api dhruvam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30 All the citizens men, women, children and old folks assembled there to witness the performance.

## \|\| 4.30.31 \|\|

*śrutvā sugītaṃ taddṛṣṭvā sunṛtyaṃ ca manoharam \|*  
*sahasā mumuhussarve menāpi ca tadā mune \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. O sage, on hearing the sweet songs, and seeing the delightful dance, the people entered into raptures of ecstacy.

## \|\| 4.30.32-35 \|\|

*mūrcchāṃ saṃprāpya sā durgā sudṛṣṭvā hṛdi śaṃkaram \|*  
*triśūlādikacihnāni bibhrataṃ cātisundaram \|\| 32 \|\|*

*vibhūtivibhūṣitaṃ ramyamasthimālāsamanvitam \|*  
*trilocanojjvaladvaktraṃ nāgāyajñopavītakam \|\| 33 \|\|*

*varaṃ vṛṇvityuktavantaṃ gauravarṇaṃ maheśvaram \|*  
*dīnabandhu dayāsindhuṃ sarvathā sumanoharam \|\| 34 \|\|*

*hṛdayasthaṃ haraṃ dṛṣṭvedṛśaṃ sā praṇanāma tam \|*  
*varaṃ vavre mānasaṃ hi patirme tvaṃ bhaveti ca \|\| 35 \|\|*

32-35 Pārvatī became unconscious. She saw Śiva’s handsome form, bearing trident and other symbols before her vision. He had smeared the ashes all over His body. He was wearing a garland of bones. His face was beaming with his shining three eyes. He had the sacred thread of a serpent. Exquisitely white in complexion, the handsome lord Śiva, the friend of the distressed, the ocean of mercy was repeating the words “Choose the boon (or the bridegroom).” On seeing Him thus in her mind she bowed to Him. Mentally she had chosen the boon when she had said, “Be my husband”.

## \|\| 4.30.36 \|\|

*varaṃ dattvā śivaṃ cātha tādṛśaṃ prītito hṛdā \|*  
*antardhāya punastatra sunanartta sa bhikṣukaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. And He had granted her the auspicious boon with pleasure and vanished. The mendicant now continued the dance.

## \|\| 4.30.37 \|\|

*tato menā suratnāni svarṇapātrasthitāni ca \|*  
*tasmai dātuṃ yayau prītyā tadbhūti prītamānasaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Menā who was greatly delighted took gems and jewels in gold vessels in order to give them to Him.

## \|\| 4.30.38 \|\|

*tāni na svīcakārāsau bhikṣāṃ yāce śivāṃ ca tām \|*  
*punassunṛtyaṃ gānaśca kautukātkartumudyataḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. But the dancer did not accept the gifts. He requested for the hand of Pārvatī and began to dance and sing again.

## \|\| 4.30.39 \|\|

*menā tadvacanaṃ śrutvā cukopāti suvismitā \|*  
*bhikṣukaṃ bhartsayāmāsa bahiṣkartumiyeṣa sā \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Menā was surprised on hearing his words and she was furious. She rebuked the mendicant and wished to drive him out.

## \|\| 4.30.40 \|\|

*etasminnantare tatra gaṃgāto girirāyayau \|*  
*dadarśa purato bhikṣuṃ prāṃgaṇasthaṃ narākṛtim \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. In the meantime the lord of mountains returned from the Gaṅgā. He saw the mendicant in the human form in his court-yard.

## \|\| 4.30.41 \|\|

*śrutvā menāmukhādvṛttaṃ tatsarvaṃ sucukopa saḥ \|*  
*ājñāṃ cakārānucarānbahiṣkartuñca taṃ naṭam \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. On hearing the details from Menā he became very angry. He ordered his attendants to drive out the dancer.

## \|\| 4.30.42 \|\|

*mahāgnimiva duḥsparśaṃ prajvalantaṃ sutejasam \|*  
*na śaśāka bahiṣkartuṃ kopi taṃ munisattama \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. But, O excellent sage, none of them could push him out as he was hot to the touch like a blazing fire and very brilliant.

## \|\| 4.30.43 \|\|

*tatassa bhikṣukastāta nānālīlāviśāradaḥ \|*  
*darśayāmāsa śailāya svaprabhāvamanantakam \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. O dear, then the mendicant who was clever at diverse sports showed his endless great power to the mountain.

## \|\| 4.30.44 \|\|

*śailo dadarśa taṃ tatra viṣṇurūpadharaṃ drutam \|*  
*kirīṭinaṃ kuṇḍalinaṃ pītavastraṃ caturbhujam \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. The mountain saw him immediately transmuted in to the form of Viṣṇu the four-armed, with crown earrings and yellow garment.

## \|\| 4.30.45 \|\|

*yadyatpuṣpādikaṃ dattaṃ pūjākāle gadābhṛte \|*  
*gātre śirasi tatsarvaṃ bhikṣukasya dadarśa ha \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Flowers etc. which had been offered to the macebearing lord, Viṣṇu, at the time of worship, he saw on the body and over the head of the mendicant.

## \|\| 4.30.46 \|\|

*tato dadarśa jagatāṃ sraṣṭāraṃ sa caturmukham \|*  
*raktavarṇaṃ paṭhantañca śrutisūktaṃ girīśvaraḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Then the lord of mountains saw the four-faced deity, the creator of worlds, red in colour and reciting the Vedic hymns.

## \|\| 4.30.47 \|\|

*tatassūryyasvarūpañca jagaccakṣussvarūpakam \|*  
*dadarśa girirājassa kṣaṇaṃ kautukakāriṇām \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Then the lord of mountains saw the form of the sun, the eye of the universe, much to his enthusiastic amazement.

## \|\| 4.30.48 \|\|

*tato dadarśa taṃ tāta rudrarūpaṃ mahādbhutam \|*  
*pārvatī sahitaṃ ramyaṃ vihasantaṃ sutejasam \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Then, O dear one, he saw him in the wonderful form of Śiva accompanied by Pārvatī. He was smiling and shining beautifully.

## \|\| 4.30.49 \|\|

*tatastejassvarūpañca nirākāraṃ niraṃjanam \|*  
*nirupādhiṃ nirīhañca mahādbhutamarūpakam \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Then he saw him in the form of a mass of splendour of no specific shape. It was unsullied, free from peculiar attributes and desires. It was wonderfully formless.

## \|\| 4.30.50 \|\|

*evaṃ bahūni rūpāṇi tasya tatra dadarśa saḥ \|*  
*suvismito babhūvāśu paramānandasaṃyutaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Thus he saw many forms and features there. He was surprised and delighted much.

## \|\| 4.30.51 \|\|

*athāsau bhikṣuvaryyo hi tasmāttasyāśca sūtikṛt \|*  
*bhikṣāṃ yayāce durgāntāṃ nānyajjagrāha kiñcana \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Then the chief of mendicants begged of Himavat and Menā the hand of Pārvatī as alms. He, the source of great enjoyment did not accept anything else.

## \|\| 4.30.52-54 \|\|

*na svīcakāra śailaindro mohitaśśivamāyayā \|*  
*bhikṣuḥ kiṃcinna jagrāha tatraivāntardadhe tataḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

*tadā babhūva sujñānaṃ menāśaileśayoriti \|*  
*āvāṃ śivo vañcayitvā svasthānaṃ gatavānprabhuḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

*tayorvicintya tatraiva śive bhaktirabhūtparā \|*  
*mahāmokṣakarī divyā sarvānandapradāyinī \|\| 54 \|\|*

52-54. The lord of mountains deluded by Śiva’s magic did not accede to this request. The mendicant too did not take anything. He vanished from the scene. Then Himavat and Menā realised that Śiva had deceived them and gone to His abode. After some pondering, they developed a feeling of devotion to Śiva who is the cause of salvation, the bestower of divine bliss.

## Chapter 31 - Description of Śiva’s magic

## \|\| 4.31.1 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*tayorbhaktiṃ śive jñātvā parāmavyabhicāriṇīm \|*  
*sarve śakrādayo devāścicinturiti nārada \|\| 1 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

1\. On knowing their undistracted great devotion to Śiva, O Nārada, Indra and other gods, thought like this.

## \|\| 4.31.2 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*ekāntabhaktyā śailaścetkanyāṃ tasmai pradāsyati \|*  
*dhruvaṃ nirvāṇatā sadyassa prāpsyati ca bhārate \|\| 2 \|\|*

The gods said:—

2\. If the mountain were to give his daughter to Śiva with single-minded devotion he will attain salvation immediately and will disappear from Bhārata.

## \|\| 4.31.3 \|\|

*anantaratnādhāraścetpṛthvī tyaktvā prayāsyati \|*  
*ratnagarbhābhidhā bhūmirmithyaiva bhavitā dhruvam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The mountain is the storehouse of endless gems. If he were to leave off the Earth and go, the name of the Earth—Ratnagarbhā (having gems in the womb)—shall be a misnomer.

## \|\| 4.31.4 \|\|

*sthāvaratvaṃ parityajya divyarūpaṃ vidhāya saḥ \|*  
*kanyāṃ śūlabhṛte dattvā śivalokaṃ gamiṣyati \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. He will cast off his immobile aspect and assume a divine form. He will give his daughter to the Trident bearing deity and will go to Śiva’s region.

## \|\| 4.31.5 \|\|

*mahādevasya sārūpyaṃ lapsyate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*tatra bhuktvā varānbhogāṃstato mokṣamavāpsyati \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. He will undoubtedly attain mergence into lord Śiva. having enjoyed pleasures there, he will attain salvation.

## \|\| 4.31.6 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityālocya surāssarve kṛtvā cāmantraṇaṃ mithaḥ \|*  
*prasthāpayitumaicchaṃste guruṃ tatra suvismitāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

6\. Thinking like this and consulting one another they, in their bewilderment, decided to send god Bṛhaspati there.

## \|\| 4.31.7 \|\|

*tataḥ śakrādayo devāssarve guruniketanam \|*  
*jagmuḥ prītyā savinayā nārada svārthasādhakāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. O Nārada, then Indra and other gods, went to Bṛhaspati’s abode lovingly with humility, in their eagerness to achieve their self-interest.

## \|\| 4.31.8 \|\|

*gatvā tatra guruṃ natvā sarve devāssavāsavāḥ \|*  
*cakrurnivedanaṃ tasmai gurave vṛttamādarāt \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Reaching there, all the gods including Indra bowed to Bṛhaspati and submitted every detail to him.

## \|\| 4.31.9 \|\|

*\|\| devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*guro himālayagṛhaṃ gacchāsmatkāryyasiddhaye \|*  
*tatra gatvā prayatnena kuru nindāñca śūlinaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

The gods said:—

9\. O revered preceptor, please go to the abode of Himavat for the fulfilment of our task. After going there, you shall make disparaging remarks about the trident-bearing deity.

## \|\| 4.31.10-11 \|\|

*pinākinā vinā durgā varaṃ nānyaṃ variṣyati \|*  
*anicchayā sutāṃ dattvā phalaṃ tūrṇaṃ labhiṣyati \|\| 10 \|\|*

*kālenaivādhunā śaila idānīṃ bhuvi tiṣṭhatu \|*  
*anekaratnādhāraṃ taṃ sthāpaya tvaṃ kṣitau gurau \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. Pārvatī will not marry any other person except Śiva. The mountain will derive the benefit only after sometime if he gives the daughter in marriage without his full concurrence. Let the mountain stay on earth for the present. O preceptor, you shall make him stay on the earth as he is the support of many gems.

## \|\| 4.31.12 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*iti devavacaḥ śrutvā pradadau karṇayoḥ karam \|*  
*na svīcakāra sa gurussmarannāma śiveti ca \|\| 12 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

12\. On hearing these words of the gods, the preceptor of the gods, plugged his ears with his hands. He did not accept the proposal of the gods. He remembered the name “Śiva”.

## \|\| 4.31.13 \|\|

*atha smṛtvā mahādevaṃ bṛhaspatirudāradhīḥ \|*  
*uvāca devavaryāṃśca dhikkṛtvā ca punaḥ punaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Then remembering lord Śiva, Bṛhaspati of liberal mind rebuked the gods again and again and said.

## \|\| 4.31.14 \|\|

*bṛhaspatiruvāca \|*  
*sarve devāssvārthaparāḥ parārthadhvaṃsakārakāḥ \|*  
*kṛtvā śaṃkaraniṃdā hi yāsyāmi narakaṃ dhruvam \|\| 14 \|\|*

Bṛhaspati said:—

14\. All of you gods seem to be selfish in nature. You want to destroy other’s interests. Indeed I will go to hell by disparaging Śiva.

## \|\| 4.31.15 \|\|

*kaścinmadhye ca yuṣmākaṃ gacchecchailāntikaṃ surāḥ \|*  
*saṃpādayetsvābhimataṃ śailendraṃ pratibodhya ca \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. O gods, one of you shall go to the mountain. Let him urge the lord of the mountains and achieve the desired object.

## \|\| 4.31.16 \|\|

*anicchayā sutāṃ dattvā sukhaṃ tiṣṭhatu bhārate \|*  
*tasmai bhaktyā sutāṃ dattvā mokṣaṃ prāpsyati niścitam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Let him stay in Bhārata after giving his daughter without willingness. It is certain he will attain salvation if he gives his daughter with devotion.

## \|\| 4.31.17 \|\|

*paścātsaptarṣayassarve bodhayiṣyanti parvatam \|*  
*pinākinā vinā durgā varaṃ nānyaṃ variṣyati \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Afterwards the seven celestial sages will properly persuade the mountain. Except Pināka-bearing deity, Pārvatī will not marry any other person.

## \|\| 4.31.18 \|\|

*athavā gacchata surā brahmalokaṃ savāsavāḥ \|*  
*vṛttaṃ kathayata svaṃ tatsa vaḥ kāryaṃ kariṣyati \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Or, O gods, all of you go to Brahmā’s region taking Indra with you. Tell Brahmā all your details. He will get your work done immediately.

## \|\| 4.31.19 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*tacchrutvā te samālocyājagmurmama sabhāṃ surāḥ \|*  
*sarve nivedayāṃcakrurnatvā tadgatamādarāt \|\| 19 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

19\. On hearing it and consulting among themselves the gods came to my Assembly. After duly bowing to me they informed me about the details.

## \|\| 4.31.20 \|\|

*devānāṃ tadvacaḥ śrutvā śivanindākaraṃ tadā \|*  
*vedavaktā vilapyāhaṃ tānavocaṃ surānmune \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. On hearing the words of the gods about censuring Śiva, O sage, I the reciter of the Vedas spoke to them in an aggrieved tone.

## \|\| 4.31.21 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*nāhaṃ kartuṃ kṣamo vatsāḥ śivanindāṃ sudussahām \|*  
*saṃpadvināśa rūpāñca vipadāṃ bījarūpiṇīm \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. “Dear children, I am incompetent to decry Śiva. It is unbearable. It destroys all riches. It is the seed of all adversities.

## \|\| 4.31.22 \|\|

*surā gacchata kailāsaṃ santoṣayata śaṃkaram \|*  
*prasthāpayata taṃ śīghraṃ himālayagṛhaṃ prati \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. O gods, all of you go to Kailāsa and propitiate Śiva. Make Him go to Himavat’s abode quickly.

## \|\| 4.31.23 \|\|

*sa gacchedupaśaileśamātmanindāṃ karotu vai \|*  
*paranindāvināśāya svanindā yaśase matā \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Let him approach the lord of mountains and make disparaging remarks about Himself. Rebuking others is conducive to destruction. Rebuking oneself is conducive to fame”.

## \|\| 4.31.24 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*śrutveti madvaco devā māṃ praṇamya mudā ca te \|*  
*kailāsaṃ prayayuḥ śīghraṃ śailānāmadhipaṃ girim \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. On hearing my words, all the gods, joyously bowed to me and went to Kailāsa, the chief of mountains.

## \|\| 4.31.25 \|\|

*tatra gatvā śivaṃ dṛṣṭvā praṇamya natamastakāḥ \|*  
*sukṛtāṃjalayassarve tuṣṭuvustaṃ surā haram \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Going there and seeing Śiva they bowed to Him with bent heads and palms joined in reverence. The gods eulogised Śiva.

## \|\| 4.31.26 \|\|

*\|\| devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*devadeva mahādeva karuṇākara śaṃkara \|*  
*vayaṃ tvāṃ śaraṇāpannāḥ kṛpāṃ kuru namo'stu te \|\| 26 \|\|*

The gods said:—

26\. O great lord, lord of gods, O Śiva, the merciful, we seek refuge in you. Be sympathetic. Obeisance be to you.

## \|\| 4.31.27 \|\|

*tvaṃ bhaktavatsalaḥ svāminbhaktakāryakarassadā \|*  
*dīnoddharaḥ kṛpāsindhurbhaktāpadvinimocakaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. O lord, you are favourably disposed to your devotees, always carrying out their tasks. You are the uplifter of the distressed, and an ocean of mercy. You save us from all our miseries and distresses.

## \|\| 4.31.28 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*iti stutvā maheśānaṃ sarve devāssavāsavāḥ \|*  
*sarvaṃ nivedayāṃcakrustadvṛttaṃ tata ādarāt \|\| 28 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

28\. Eulogising lord Śiva thus, Indra and other gods respectfully submitted all the details.

## \|\| 4.31.29 \|\|

*tacchrutvā devavacanaṃ svīcakāra maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*devān suyāpayāmāsa tānāśvāsya vihasya saḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. On hearing the words of the gods, lord Śiva agreed to the proposal. He made the gods return after assuring them smilingly.

## \|\| 4.31.30 \|\|

*devā mumudire sarve śīghraṃ gatvā svamaṃdiram \|*  
*siddhaṃ matvā svakāryyaṃ hi praśaṃsantassadāśivam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Hastening to their abodes, the gods rejoiced much considering their work fully fulfilled and praising Sadāśiva.

## \|\| 4.31.31 \|\|

*tataḥ sa bhagavāñchambhurmaheśo bhaktavatsalaḥ \|*  
*prayayau śailabhūpañca māyeśo nirvikāravān \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Then the lord Śiva who is favourably disposed to his devotees, the lord of magic and free from aberrations went to the lord of mountains.

## \|\| 4.31.32-33 \|\|

*yadā śailassabhāmadhye samuvāsa mudānvitaḥ \|*  
*bandhuvargaiḥ parivṛtaḥ pārvatīsahitassvayam \|\| 32 \|\|*

*etasminnantare tatra hyājagāma sadāśivaḥ \|*  
*daṇḍī chatrī divyavāsā bibhrattilakamujjvalam \|\| 33 \|\|*

32-33. When the lord of the mountains was seated in his royal assembly along with Pārvatī and kinsmen, Sadāśiva came there, in the meantime bearing a staff and an umbrella. He was dressed in divine clothes and had a shining mark on the forehead.

## \|\| 4.31.34 \|\|

*kare sphaṭikamālāñca śālagrāmaṃ gale dadhat \|*  
*japannāma harerbhaktyā sādhuveṣadharau dvijaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. He was in the guise of a saintly brahmin. He was repeating the name of Viṣṇu with devotion. He had the garland of crystal beads in his hand and the Śālagrama stone round his neck.

## \|\| 4.31.35 \|\|

*taṃ ca dṛṣṭvā samuttasthau sagaṇo'pi himālayaḥ \|*  
*nanāma daṇḍavadbhūmau bhaktyātithimapūrvakam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. On seeing that extraordinary guest, Himavat with his attendants stood up in reverence and prostrated before him with devotion.

## \|\| 4.31.36 \|\|

*nanāma pārvatī bhaktyā prāṇeśaṃ viprarūpiṇam \|*  
*jñātvā taṃ manasā devī tuṣṭāva parayā mudā \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Pārvatī bowed with devotion to her dear lover in the guise of a brahmin. On realising him mentally the goddess eulogised him with great joy.

## \|\| 4.31.37 \|\|

*āśiṣaṃ yuyuje viprassarveṣāṃ prītitaśśivaḥ \|*  
*śivāyā adhikaṃ tāta manobhilaṣitaṃ hṛdā \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. With great pleasure Śiva bestowed his blessings on all. O dear, He bestowed on Pārvatī her cherished desire in addition.

## \|\| 4.31.38 \|\|

*madhuparkādikaṃ sarvaṃ jagrāha brāhmaṇo mudā \|*  
*dattaṃ śailādhirājena himāṃgena mahādarāt \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. The brahmin received with pleasure the articles of homage etc. offered by Himavat, the lord of mountains.

## \|\| 4.31.39 \|\|

*papraccha kuśalaṃ cāsya himādriḥ parvatottamaḥ \|*  
*taṃ dvijendraṃ mahāprītyā sampūjya vidhivanmune \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. O sage, after duly worshipping the excellent brahmin with pleasure, the mountain Himavat enquired of his welfare.

## \|\| 4.31.40 \|\|

*punaḥ papraccha śaileśastaṃ tataḥ ko bhavāniti \|*  
*uvāca śīghraṃ viprendro girīdraṃ sādaraṃ vacaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Again, the lord of mountains asked him “Who are you, please?” Immediately the chief of brahmins, spoke to the lord of mountains thus.

## \|\| 4.31.41 \|\|

*viprendra uvāca \|*  
*brāhmaṇo'haṃ giriśreṣṭha vaiṣṇavo budhasattamaḥ \|*  
*ghaṭikīṃ vṛtimāśritya bhramāmi dharaṇītale \|\| 41 \|\|*

The chief of brahmins said:—

41\. O foremost among mountains, I am a brahmin devotee of Viṣṇu, and a great scholar. My occupation is that of a match-maker. I roam about on the earth.

## \|\| 4.31.42 \|\|

*manoyāyī sarva gāmī sarvajñohaṃ gurorbalāt \|*  
*paropakārī śuddhātmā dayāsindhurvikārahā \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. I go where I wish. I go everywhere. By the power of my preceptor I am omniscient. I am simple-minded and by nature I help others and I am sympathetic and quell aberrations.

## \|\| 4.31.43 \|\|

*mayā jñātaṃ harāya tvaṃ svasutāṃ dātumicchasi \|*  
*imāṃ padmasamāṃ divyāṃ vararūpāṃ sulakṣaṇām \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. I have come to know that you desire to give your daughter to Śiva, this daughter so tender like a lotus flower, of divinely excellent form and endowed with all accomplishments.

## \|\| 4.31.44-47 \|\|

*nirāśrayāyāsaṃgāya kurūpāyāguṇāya ca \|*  
*śmaśānavāsine vyālagrāhirūpāya yogine \|\| 44 \|\|*

*digvāsase kugātrāya vyālabhūṣaṇadhāriṇe \|*  
*ajñātakulanāmne ca kuśīlāyāvihāriṇe \|\| 45 \|\|*

*vibhūtidigdhadehāya saṃkruddhāyāvivekine \|*  
*ajñātavayase'tīva kujaṭādhāriṇe sadā \|\| 46 \|\|*

*sarvāśrayāya bhramiṇe nāgahārāya bhikṣave \|*  
*kumārganiratāyātha vedā'dhvatyāgine haṭhāt \|\| 47 \|\|*

44-47. To Śiva—who has no support, who is devoid of associations, who is deformed, who is without attributes, who resides in the cremation-ground, who has the form of a snake-catcher, who is a Yogin, who is naked, who has deficient limbs, who wears snakes as his ornaments, whose name and pedigree are unknown, whose conduct is bad, who has no sport, whose body is smeared with ashes, who is furious, who lacks in discrimination, whose age is not known, whose matted hair is ill worn, who supports all who roam about, who has garland of snakes who is a mendicant, who is engaged in following wrong-paths and who tenaciously discards the Vedic path.

## \|\| 4.31.48 \|\|

*iyaṃ te buddhiracala na hi maṃgaladā khalu \|*  
*vibodha jñānināṃ śreṣṭha nārāyaṇakulodbhava \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. O mountain, this inclination of yours is not at all conducive to auspiciousness. O foremost among the wise, born of Nārāyaṇa’s family, learn sense.

## \|\| 4.31.49 \|\|

*na te pātrānurūpaśca pārvatīdānakarmaṇi \|*  
*mahājanaḥ smeramukhaḥ śrutamātrādbhaviṣyati \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. For the marriage of Pārvatī, He is not at all a deserving person. On hearing of this, the general public will smile in derision.

## \|\| 4.31.50 \|\|

*paśya śailādhipa tvaṃ ca na tasyaikosti bāndhavaḥ \|*  
*mahāratnākarastvañca tasya kiñciddhanaṃ na hi \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. O lord of mountains, see for yourself. He has not a single kinsman. You are the storehouse of great gems and jewels. He has no assets at all.

## \|\| 4.31.51 \|\|

*bāndhavānmenakāṃ kudhrapate śīghraṃ sutāṃstathā \|*  
*sarvānpṛccha prayatnena paṇḍitānpārvatī vinā \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. O lord of mountains, you shall consult your kinsmen, sons, wife and wise counsellors, except Pārvatī.

## \|\| 4.31.52 \|\|

*rogiṇo nauṣadhaṃ śaśvadrocate girisattama \|*  
*kupathyaṃ rocate'bhīkṣṇaṃ mahādoṣakaraṃ sadā \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. O lord of mountains, the medicine does not appeal at all to the patient. Wrong diet that brings about great defects always appeals to him.

## \|\| 4.31.53 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityuktvā brāhmaṇaḥ śīghraṃ sa vai bhuktvā mudānvitaḥ \|*  
*jagāma svālayaṃ śānto nānālīlākara śśivaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

53\. Saying this, the brahmin stopped. He took food and left the place with pleasure for his abode. Śiva is one who quietly indulges in His divine sports.

## Chapter 32 - The seven celestial sages arrive

## \|\| 4.32.1 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*brāhmaṇasya vacaḥ śrutvā menovāca himālayam \|*  
*śokenāsādhunayanā hṛdayena vidūyatā \|\| 1 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

1\. On hearing the words of the brahmin, Menā spoke to Himavat with tears welling up in her eyes, due to grief and with. the heart extremely dejected.

## \|\| 4.32.2 \|\|

*menovāca \|*  
*śṛṇu śailendra madvākyaṃ pariṇāme sukhāvaham \|*  
*pṛccha śaivavarānsarvānkimuktaṃ brāhmaṇena ha \|\| 2 \|\|*

Menā said:—

2\. O lord of mountains, please listen to my words conducive to happiness. Please consult important devotees of Śiva regarding what has been mentioned by the brahmin.

## \|\| 4.32.3 \|\|

*nindānena kṛtā śambhorvaiṣṇavena dvijanmanā \|*  
*śrutvā tāṃ me mano'tīva nirviṇṇaṃ hi nageśvara \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Many disparaging remarks about Śiva have been made by this brahminical devotee of Viṣṇu. O lord of mountains, on hearing these words, my mind is very much dejected.

## \|\| 4.32.4 \|\|

*tasmai rudrāya śaileśa na dāsyāmi sutāmaham \|*  
*kurūpaśīlanamme hi sulakṣaṇayutāṃ nijām \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. O lord of mountains, I shall not give my daughter endowed with all good accomplishments to Śiva with ugly features, ignoble conduct and defiled name.

## \|\| 4.32.5 \|\|

*na manyase vaco cenme mariṣyāmi na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*tyakṣyāmi ca gṛhaṃ sadyo bhakṣayiṣyāmi vā viṣam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. If you do not accede to my request, I shall undoubtedly die. I will immediately leave this house or swallow poison.

## \|\| 4.32.6 \|\|

*gale baddhvāṃbikāṃ rajjvā yāsyāmi gahanaṃ vanam \|*  
*mahāmbudhau majjayiṣye tasmai dāsyāmi no sutām \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. With a rope I shall tie Pārvatī round my neck and go to a thick forest. I would rather drown myself in the great ocean. I shall never give my daughter to him.

## \|\| 4.32.7 \|\|

*ityuktvāśu tathā gatvā menā kopālayaṃ śucā \|*  
*tyaktvā hāraṃ rudantī sā cakāra śayanaṃ bhuvi \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Saying thus with great grief, Menā entered the chamber of anger. Casting off her necklaces she lay down on the ground sighing and sobbing.

## \|\| 4.32.8 \|\|

*etasminnantare tāta śambhunā sapta eva te \|*  
*saṃsmṛtā ṛṣayassadyo virahavyākulātmanā \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. O dear, in the meantime all those seven celestial sages were remembered by Śiva whose mind was agitated by the pangs of separation from Pārvatī.

## \|\| 4.32.9 \|\|

*ṛṣayaścaiva te sarve śambhunā saṃsmṛtā yadā \|*  
*tadā''jagmuḥ svayaṃ sadyaḥ kalpavṛkṣā ivāpare \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. All those seven sages, as soon as they were remembered by Śiva, came there in person as though they were another set of wish-yielding Kalpa trees.

## \|\| 4.32.10 \|\|

*arundhatī tathā''yātā sākṣātsiddhirivāparā \|*  
*tāndraṣṭvā sūryasaṃkāśānvijahau svajapaṃ haraḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Arundhatī too came there as though she was an achievement personified. On seeing them resplendent like the sun, Śiva stopped his recitation of mantras.

## \|\| 4.32.11 \|\|

*sthitvāgre ṛṣayaḥ śreṣṭhaṃ natvā stutvā śivaṃ mune \|*  
*menire ca tadātmānaṃ kṛtārthaṃ te tapasvinaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. O sage, standing in front of Śiva and bowing to and eulogising Him, the seven sages of great austerity considered themselves blessed.

## \|\| 4.32.12 \|\|

*tato vismayamāpannā nama skṛtya sthitāḥ punaḥ \|*  
*procuḥ prāñjalayaste vai śivaṃ lokanamaskṛtam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Then, as they were struck with surprise, they joined their palms in reverence, bowed to and addressed Śiva adored by all the worlds:—

## \|\| 4.32.13 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*sarvotkṛṣṭaṃ mahārāja sārvabhauma divaukasām \|*  
*svabhāgyaṃ varṇyate'smābhiḥ kiṃ punassakalottamam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The sages said:—“O most excellent of all, O great ruler, O Emperor of the heaven-dwellers, how can our fortune which is very excellent be described by us?

## \|\| 4.32.14-15 \|\|

*tapastaptaṃ tridhā pūrvaṃ vedādhyayanamuttamam \|*  
*agnayaśca hutāḥ pūrvaṃ tīrthāni vividhāni ca \|\| 14 \|\|*

*vāṅmanaḥkāyajaṃ kiṃcitpuṇyaṃ smaraṇasambhavam \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ saṃgataṃ cādya smaraṇānugrahāttava \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. Formerly we had performed three kinds of penance; we had studied the excellent Vedas; we had made offerings in the fire, we had visited many holy centres; thus whatever merit we have acquired verbally, mentally and physically that entire merit has now accrued to us by your blessing in remembering us.

## \|\| 4.32.16 \|\|

*yo vai bhajati nityaṃ tvāṃ kṛtakṛtyo bhavennaraḥ \|*  
*kiṃ puṇyaṃ varṇyate teṣāṃ yeṣāṃ ca smaraṇaṃ tava \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. A man who worships you always shall be blessed. How can that merit be properly described, the merit of those whom you yourself remember?

## \|\| 4.32.17 \|\|

*sarvotkṛṣṭā vayaṃ jātāḥ smaraṇātte sadāśiva \|*  
*manorathapathaṃ naiva gacchasi tvaṃ kathaṃcana \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. O Sadāśiva, we have become the most excellent of all people by your remembering us. Usually you never even come across the path of ambitions and aspirations of ordinary people.

## \|\| 4.32.18-19 \|\|

*vāmanasya phalaṃ yadvajjanmāndhasya dṛśau yathā \|*  
*vācālatvañca mūkasya raṃkasya nidhidarśanam \|\| 18 \|\|*

*paṅgorgirivarākrāntirvandhyāyaḥ prasavastathā \|*  
*darśanaṃ bhavatastadvajjātaṃ no durlabhaṃ prabho \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. O lord, your vision, very difficult to be acquired, is like the fruit stooping down within the reach of the dwarf, like sight to a man born blind, like eloquency acquired by a dumb man, like the indigent meeting with a treasure-trove, like the lame man reaching the top of a high mountain and like the barren woman bearing a child.

## \|\| 4.32.20 \|\|

*adya prabhṛti lokeṣu mānyāḥ pūjyā munīśvarāḥ \|*  
*jātāste darśanādeva svamuccaiḥ padamāśritāḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. By seeing you today we have become the most respectable sages worthy of the worship of all the worlds. We have reached the highest position.

## \|\| 4.32.21 \|\|

*atra kiṃ bahunoktena sarva thā mānyatāṃ gatāḥ \|*  
*darśanāttava deveśa sarvadeveśvarasya hi \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. O lord of gods, by seeing you who are the lord of all gods we have become worthy of great respect. There is no necessity of talking more.

## \|\| 4.32.22 \|\|

*pūrṇānāṃ kiñca kartavyamasti cetparamā kṛpā \|*  
*sadṛśaṃ sevakānāṃ tu deyaṃ kāryaṃ tvayā śubham \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. If any duty is assigned to us it will be a favour to us. An auspicious task befitting us, your utter slaves, shall be given to us.

## \|\| 4.32.23 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*ityevaṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā teṣāṃ śambhurmaheśvaraḥ \|*  
*laukikācāramāśritya ramyaṃ vākyamupādade \|\| 23 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

23\. On hearing their words, Śiva the great lord, in conformity with the conventions of the world, spoke these pleasant words:—

## \|\| 4.32.24 \|\|

*śiva uvāca \|*  
*ṛṣayaśca sadā pūjyā bhavantaśca viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*yuṣmākaṃ kāraṇādviprāḥ smaraṇaṃ ca mayā kṛtam \|\| 24 \|\|*

Śiva said:—

24\. Sages are always to be adored and particularly you all. O brahmins, it was for a specific reason that you have been summoned here.

## \|\| 4.32.25 \|\|

*mamāvasthā bhavadbhiśca jñāyate hyupakārikā \|*  
*sādhanīyā viśeṣeṇa lokānāṃ siddhihetave \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. My attitude of being helpful is known to you. That must be achieved, especially in the interest of the fulfilment of the desires of the world.

## \|\| 4.32.26 \|\|

*devānāṃ duḥkhamutpannaṃ tā rakātsudurātmanaḥ \|*  
*brahmaṇā ca varau dattaḥ kiṃ karomi durāsadaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Cause for great misery has arisen for the gods at the hands of Tāraka the wicked. Boon has already been granted. He is invincible. What shall I do?

## \|\| 4.32.27 \|\|

*mūrtayo'ṣṭau ca yāḥ proktā madīyāḥ paramarṣayaḥ \|*  
*tāssarvā upakārāya na tu svārthāya tatsphuṭam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. O great sages, all the eight cosmic bodies that I possess are not for furthering my self-interest, they are for helping the wide world.

## \|\| 4.32.28-29 \|\|

*tathā ca kartukāmohaṃ vivāhaṃ śivayā saha \|*  
*tayā vai sutapastaptaṃ duṣkaraṃ paramarṣibhiḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*tasyai paraṃ phalaṃ deyamabhīṣṭaṃ taddhitāvaham \|*  
*etādṛśaḥ paṇo me hi bhaktānandapradaḥ sphuṭam \|\| 29 \|\|*

28-29. A great penance has been performed by Pārvatī. That cannot be performed even by great sages. I have to give her the great fruit thereof. Indeed my vow is to render delight to my devotees. The fruit I bestow on her shall be conducive to her welfare. Hence I wish to marry her.

## \|\| 4.32.30 \|\|

*pārvatīvacanādbhikṣurūpo yāto girergṛham \|*  
*ahaṃ pāvitavānkālīṃ yato līlāviśāradaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. At the request of Pārvatī I went to the abode of the mountain in the guise of a mendicant. Clever in divine sports I thereby sanctified her.

## \|\| 4.32.31 \|\|

*māṃ jñātvā tau paraṃ brahma dampatī parabhaktitaḥ \|*  
*dātukāmāvabhūtāṃ ca svasutāṃ vedarītitaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. On hearing to know that I am the supreme Brahman, the couple were desirous of giving me their daughter with great devotion in accordance with the Vedic manner.

## \|\| 4.32.32 \|\|

*devapreraṇayāhaṃ vai kṛtavānasmi nindanam \|*  
*tadā svasya ca tadbhaktiṃ vihantuṃ vaiṣṇṇavātmanā \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. On the inducement of the gods, in order to reduce the quality of devotion (of Himavat and Menā) I took the guise of a devotee of Viṣṇu and rebuked myself.

## \|\| 4.32.33 \|\|

*tacchrutvā tau sunirviṇṇo taddhīnau saṃbabhūvatuḥ \|*  
*svakanyāṃ necchato dātuṃ mahyaṃ hi munayo'dhunā \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. O sages, on hearing it they were dejected and have now lost interest in me and do not wish to give their daughter to me.

## \|\| 4.32.34 \|\|

*tasmādbhavanto gacchantu himācalagṛhaṃ dhruvam \|*  
*tatra gatvā girivaraṃ tatpatnīñca prabodhaya \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Hence you all go to the abode of Himavat and urge the excellent mountain and his wife.

## \|\| 4.32.35 \|\|

*kathanīyaṃ prayatnena vacanaṃ vedasammitam \|*  
*sarvathā karaṇīyantadyathā syātkāryyamuttamam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Speak out the words as venerable as the Vedas. Do everything necessary to get the matter straightened out and settled.

## \|\| 4.32.36 \|\|

*udvāhaṃ kartumicchāmi tatputryā saha sattamāḥ \|*  
*svīkṛtasta dvivāho me varo dattaśca tādṛśaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. O excellent ones, I wish to marry their daughter. I have agreed to marry her and have already granted her that boon.

## \|\| 4.32.37 \|\|

*atra kiṃ bahunoktena bodhanīyo himālayaḥ \|*  
*tathā menā ca boddhavyā devānāṃ syāddhitaṃ yathā \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. What is the use of talking too much? Himavat must be convinced. Menā too must be convinced similarly, so that the purpose of the gods shall be served well.

## \|\| 4.32.38 \|\|

*bhavadbhiḥ kalpito yo vai vidhissyādadhikastataḥ \|*  
*bhavatāñcaiva kāryyaṃ tu bhavantaḥ kāryyabhāginaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Whatever mode is selected by you shall be more than necessary. The task is yours. You alone are the sharers of the credit.

## \|\| 4.32.39 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*ityevaṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā munayaste'malāśayāḥ \|*  
*ānandaṃ lebhire sarve prabhuṇānugrahīkṛtāḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

39\. On hearing these words, the seven sages of pure mind became delighted and thought themselves blessed by the lord.

## \|\| 4.32.40 \|\|

*vayaṃ dhanyā abhūvaṃśca kṛtakṛtyāśca sarvathā \|*  
*vaṃdyā yātāśca sarveṣāṃ pūjanīyā viśeṣataḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. “We have become blessed and contented in every respect. We have become venerable to every one, especially adorable.

## \|\| 4.32.41 \|\|

*brahmaṇā viṣṇunā yo vai vandyassarvārthasādhakaḥ \|*  
*sosmānpreṣayate preṣyānkārye lokasukhāvahe \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. He who is worthy of being respected by Brahmā and Viṣṇu, he who secures everything accomplished is sending us, his emissaries on an errand that is conducive to the happiness of all the worlds.

## \|\| 4.32.42 \|\|

*ayaṃ vai jagatāṃ svāmī pitā sā jananī matā \|*  
*ayaṃ yuktaśca sambandho varddhatāṃ candravatsadā \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. He is the master of the worlds and their father. She is considered the mother. Let this proper alliance increase for ever like the moon”.

## \|\| 4.32.43 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityuktvā hyṛṣayo divyā namaskṛtya śivaṃ tadā \|*  
*gatā ākāśamārgeṇa yatrāsti himavatpuram \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Saying thus the celestial sages bowed to Śiva and went by aerial path in the direction of the city of Himavat.

## \|\| 4.32.44 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā tāṃ ca puraṃ divyā mṛṣayaste'tivismitāḥ \|*  
*varṇayantaśca svaṃ puṇyamabruvanvai parasparam \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. On seeing that city of heavenly splendour, the sages were surprised. Expatiating on their good fortune they spoke to one another.

## \|\| 4.32.45 \|\|

*\|\| ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*puṇyavanto vayaṃ dhanyā dṛṣṭvaitaddhimava tpuram \|*  
*yasmādevaṃvidhe kāryye śivenaiva niyojitāḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

The sages said:—

45\. We are really blessed and meritorious in being able to see this city because we have been engaged in a task like this.

## \|\| 4.32.46 \|\|

*alakāyāśca svargācca bhogavatyāstathā punaḥ \|*  
*viśeṣeṇāmarāvatyā dṛśya te puramuttamam \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. This city seems to be better than Alakā,\[4\] heaven,\[5\] Bhogavatī\[6\] and even Amarāvatī.

## \|\| 4.32.47 \|\|

*sugṛhāṇi suramyāṇi sphaṭikairvividhairvaraiḥ \|*  
*maṇibhirvā vicitrāṇi racitānyaṅgaṇāni ca \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. The houses are beautiful and well-built. The courtyards are well laid out and paved with different kinds of crystals and jewels of variegated colours.

## \|\| 4.32.48 \|\|

*sūryakāntāśca maṇayaścandrakāntāstathaiva ca \|*  
*gṛhe gṛhe vicitrāśca vṛkṣātsvargasamudbhavāḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Slabs of solar and lunar stones are found in every house. Different kinds of celestial trees are also growing here.

## \|\| 4.32.49 \|\|

*toraṇānāṃ tathā lakṣmīrdṛśyate ca gṛhegṛhe \|*  
*vividhāni vicitrāṇi śukahaṃsairvimānakaiḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. The splendour of festoons is also seen in every house. They are of different colours and sorts with shapes of parrots and swans carved on the walls of the palaces.

## \|\| 4.32.50 \|\|

*vitānāni vicitrāṇi cailavattoraṇaissaha \|*  
*jalāśayānyanekāni dīrghikā vividhāḥ sthitāḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. The canopies with hanging festoons are of diverse character. There are many lakes and ponds.

## \|\| 4.32.51 \|\|

*udyānāni vicitrāṇi prasannaiḥ pūjitānyatha \|*  
*narāśca devatāssarve striyaścāpsarasastathā \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. The gardens and parks are of various kinds frequented by delighted people. Here men are like gods and the women are like the celestial damsels.

## \|\| 4.32.52 \|\|

*karmabhūmau yājñikāśca paurāṇāssvargakāmyayā \|*  
*kurvanti te vṛthā sarve vihāya himavatpuram \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. In the land of activities (i.e. Bhārata), the sacrificial priests and the followers of Purāṇas perform holy rites with a desire to attain heaven. That is in vain because they have left off the city of Himavat.

## \|\| 4.32.53 \|\|

*yāvanna dṛṣṭametacca tāvatsvargaparā narāḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭrametadyadā viprāḥ kiṃ svargeṇa prayojanam \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Men are eager to go to heaven only as long as this city is not seen. O brahmins, when this city is seen what is the use of heaven?

## \|\| 4.32.54 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*ityevamṛṣivaryyāste varṇayantaḥ puraśca tat \|*  
*gatā haimālayaṃ sarve gṛhaṃ sarvasamṛddhimat \|\| 54 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

54\. Describing the city thus all those excellent sages went to the rich and well-furnished abode of Himavat.

## \|\| 4.32.55 \|\|

*tāndraṣṭvā sūryasaṃkāśān himavānvismito'bravīt \|*  
*dūrādākāśamārgasthānmunīnsapta sutejasaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. On seeing those seven sages, resplendent like the sun, coming along the aerial path from a distance, Himavat was surprised and said:—

## \|\| 4.32.56 \|\|

*\|\| himavānuvāca \|*  
*saptaite sūryyasaṃkāśāḥ samāyāṃti madantike \|*  
*pūjā kāryyā prayatnena munīnāṃ ca mayādhunā \|\| 56 \|\|*

Himavat said:—

56\. The seven venerable persons, resplendant like the sun, are approaching me. These sages shall be worshipped by me now.

## \|\| 4.32.57 \|\|

*vayaṃ dhanyā gṛhasthāśca sarveṣāṃ sukhadāyinaḥ \|*  
*yeṣāṃ gṛhe samāyānti mahātmāno yadīdṛśāḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. We householders are really blessed, to whom great men like these, bestowing happiness on all, pay their visit.

## \|\| 4.32.58 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*etasminnantare caivākāśādetya bhuvi sthitān \|*  
*sanmukhe himavāndṛṣṭvā yayau mānapurassaram \|\| 58 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

58\. In the meantime they descended on the ground from the sky. On seeing them Himavat advanced to welcome them.

## \|\| 4.32.59 \|\|

*kṛtāṃjalirnataskandhaḥ saptarṣīnsupraṇamya saḥ \|*  
*pūjāṃ cakāra teṣāṃ vai bahumānapurassaram \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. With palms joined in reverence he bowed to them with stooping shoulders and worshipped them with due respect and honour.

## \|\| 4.32.60 \|\|

*hitāssaptarṣayaste ca himavantannageśvaram \|*  
*gṛhītvocuḥ prasannāsyā vacanaṃ maṅgalālayam \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Desiring welfare of others, the seven sages embraced Himavat, the lord of mountains and spoke words of auspicious blessings with pleasant faces.

## \|\| 4.32.61 \|\|

*yathāgrataśca tānkṛtvā dhanyā mama gṛhāśramaḥ \|*  
*ityuktvāsanamānīya dadau bhaktipurassaram \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Keeping them ahead he said—“My household life is blessed”. With great devotion he got and offered them seats.

## \|\| 4.32.62 \|\|

*āsaneṣūpaviṣṭeṣu tadājñaptassvayaṃ sthitaḥ \|*  
*uvāca himavāṃstatra munīñjyotirmayāstadā \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. When they were duly seated, he too sat with their permission. Then Himavat spoke to the refulgent sages:—

## \|\| 4.32.63-64 \|\|

*himālaya uvāca \|*  
*dhanyo hi kṛtakṛtyohaṃ saphalaṃ jīvita mama \|*  
*lokeṣu darśanīyohaṃ bahutīrthasamo mataḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

*yasmādbhavanto madgehamāgatā viṣṇurūpiṇaḥ \|*  
*pūrṇānāṃ bhavatāṃ kāryyaṃ kṛpaṇānāṃ gṛheṣu kim \|\| 64 \|\|*

Himavat said:—

63-64. I am blessed. I am contented. My life is fruitful. I am the best person worthy of being seen in the three worlds. I am as pure as any of the holy centres. All this is because you, verily in lord Viṣṇu’s forms, have come to my abode. Perfect ones such as you, what special purpose can there be in visiting poor persons like me?

## \|\| 4.32.65 \|\|

*tathāpi kiñcitkāryaṃ ca sadṛśaṃ sevakasya me \|*  
*kathanīyaṃ sudayayā saphalaṃ syājjanurmama \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Still I am your servant. Some task there may be to be entrusted to me. Mercifully may it be spoken out. May my life be fruitful.

## Chapter 33 - The appeasement of Himavat

## \|\| 4.33.1 \|\|

*\|\| ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*jagatpitā śivaḥ prokto jaganmātā śivā matā \|*  
*tasmāddeyā tvayā kanyā śaṃkarāya mahātmane \|\| 1 \|\|*

The sages said:—

1\. Śiva is the father of the universe. Pārvatī is the mother of the universe. Hence your daughter shall be given to Śiva, the supreme soul.

## \|\| 4.33.2 \|\|

*evaṃ kṛtvā himagire sārthakaṃ te bhavejjanuḥ \|*  
*jagadgurorgurustvaṃ hi bhaviṣyasi na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. O Himālaya, by this activity your life will be fruitful. You will become the venerable person of the most venerable in the universe. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 4.33.3 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*evaṃ vacanamākarṇya saptarṣīṇāṃ munīśvara \|*  
*praṇamya tānkarau baddhvā girirājo'bravīdidam \|\| 3 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

3\. O great sage, on hearing these words of the seven usages, the lord of the mountains bowed to them with joined palms and spoke thus.

## \|\| 4.33.4 \|\|

*himālaya uvāca \|*  
*saptarṣayo mahābhāgā bhavadbhiryadudīritam \|*  
*tatpramāṇīkṛtaṃ me hi puraiva giriśecchayā \|\| 4 \|\|*

Himavat said:—

4\. O ye seven sages of great enlightenment, what you have just now said has been already cherished by me by the will of Śiva.

## \|\| 4.33.5 \|\|

*idānīmeka āgatya vipro vaiṣṇavadharmavān \|*  
*śivamuddiśya suprītyā viparītaṃ vaco'bravīt \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Now, a certain brahmin professing Vaiṣṇava cult came here and spoke very critically about Śiva.

## \|\| 4.33.6 \|\|

*tadārabhya śivāmātā jñānabhraṣṭā babhūva ha \|*  
*sutāvivāhaṃ rudreṇa yoginā tena necchati \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Ever since, the mother Pārvatī has gone out of sense. Hences she does not wish her daughter’s marriage with Śiva.

## \|\| 4.33.7 \|\|

*kopāgāramagātsā hi sutaptā malināmbarā \|*  
*kṛtvā mahāhaṭhaṃ viprā bodhyamānāpi'nābudhat \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. She has entered the chamber of anger. She is aggrieved and her clothes have become dirty. O brahmins, her obduracy is so great that she does not pay heed to any ad vice.

## \|\| 4.33.8 \|\|

*ahaṃ ca jñānavibhraṣṭo jātohaṃ satyamīryyate \|*  
*dātuṃ sutāṃ maheśāya necchāmi bhikṣurūpiṇe \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. I too am, you can say, out of sense. I am telling you the truth. I do not wish to give my daughter to Śiva who is apparently a mendicant.

## \|\| 4.33.9 \|\|

*brahmovāca\|\|ityuktvā śailarājastu śivamāyāvimohitaḥ \|*  
*tūṣṇīṃ babhūva tatrastho munīnāṃ madhyato mune \|\| 9 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

9\. O sage, after saying these words, the king of mountains deluded by Śiva’s magic became silent and sat amidst the sages.

## \|\| 4.33.10 \|\|

*sarve saptarṣayaste hi śivamāyāṃ praśasya vai \|*  
*preṣayāmāsuratha tāṃ menakāṃ pratyarundhatīm \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The seven celestial sages praised the magic of Śiva and sent Arundhatī to Menakā.

## \|\| 4.33.11 \|\|

*atha patyussamādāya nideśaṃ jñānadā hi sā \|*  
*jagāmārundhatī tūrṇaṃ yatra menā ca pārvatī \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Then at the bidding of her husband Arundhatī, the bestower of knowledge, went quickly to the place where Menā and Pārvatī were sitting.

## \|\| 4.33.12 \|\|

*gatvā dadarśa menāṃ tāṃ śayānāṃ śokamūrcchitām \|*  
*uvāca madhuraṃ sādhvī sāvadhānā hitaṃ vacaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. After going in she saw Menā lying in her grief. The chaste lady spoke to her these carefully selected sweet and wholesome words:—

## \|\| 4.33.13 \|\|

*arundhatyuvāca \|*  
*uttiṣṭha menake sādhvi tvadgṛhe'hamarundhatī \|*  
*āgatā munayaścāpi saptāyātāḥ kṛpālavaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

Arundhatī said:—

13\. O Menakā, get up. O chaste lady, I, Arundhatī, have come to your house. The seven sages of sympathetic nature have also come.

## \|\| 4.33.14 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*arundhatīsvaraṃ śrutvā śīghramutthāya menakā \|*  
*uvāca śirasā natvā tāṃ padmāmiva tejasā \|\| 14 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

14\. On hearing Arundhatī’s voice, Menā got up quickly and bowed to her who was on a par with Lakṣmī in her brilliance.

## \|\| 4.33.15 \|\|

*menovāca \|*  
*ahodya kimidaṃ puṇyamasmākaṃ puṇyajanmanām \|*  
*vadhūrjagadvidheḥ patnī vasiṣṭhasyāgateha vai \|\| 15 \|\|*

Menā said:—

15\. Ha, what a meritorious thing is this! We are blessed. Arundhatī, the daughter-in-law of the Creator of the universe, the wife of Vasiṣṭha, has come here.

## \|\| 4.33.16 \|\|

*kimarthamāgatā devi tanme brūhi viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*ahaṃ dāsīsamā te hi sasutā karuṇāṃ kuru \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. O gentle lady, what for is your visit now? Please tell me specifically. My daughter and I are your slaves. Be merciful to us.

## \|\| 4.33.17 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityuktvā menakāṃ sādhvī bodhayitvā ca tāṃ bahu \|*  
*tathāgatā ca suprītyā sāste yatrarṣayo'pi te \|\| 17 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

17\. Arundhatī, the chaste lady thus addressed, advised her in various ways and returned to the place where the sages were seated.

## \|\| 4.33.18 \|\|

*atha śaileśvaraṃ te ca bodhayāmāsurādarāt \|*  
*smṛtvā śivapadadvandvaṃ sarve vākyaviśāradāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Then they began to advise the lord of the mountains, after thinking on the feet of Śiva. They were clever in speech and they spoke respectfully.

## \|\| 4.33.19 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*śailendra śrūyatāṃ vākyamasmākaṃ śubhakāraṇam \|*  
*śivāya pārvatīṃ dehi saṃharttuḥ śvaśuro bhava \|\| 19 \|\|*

The sages said:—

19\. O lord of the mountains, may our words, the cause of everything auspicious, be heard. Give Pārvatī to Śiva. Become the father-in-law of the world-destroyer.

## \|\| 4.33.20 \|\|

*ayācitāraṃ sarveśaṃ prārthayāmāsa yatnataḥ \|*  
*tārakasya vināśāya brahmāsambaṃdhakarmmaṇi \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. For the destruction of Tāraka, formerly Brahmā requested Śiva who is the lord of all and who does not beg of any one, to strive for this alliance.

## \|\| 4.33.21 \|\|

*notsuko dārasaṃyoge śaṃkaro yogināṃ varaḥ \|*  
*vidheḥ prārthanayā devastava kanyāṃ grahīṣyati \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Śiva, the foremost of Yogins was not eager to marry. But since requested by Brahmā, the lord agreed to take your daughter.

## \|\| 4.33.22 \|\|

*duhituste tapastaptaṃ pratijñānaṃ cakāra sā \|*  
*hetudvayena yogīndro vivāhaṃ ca kariṣyati \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Pārvatī performed a penance and the lord promised her. Thus for these two reasons the lord of Yogins wishes to marry her.

## \|\| 4.33.23 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ṛṣīṇāṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā prahasya sa himālayaḥ \|*  
*uvāca kiñcidbhītastu paraṃ vinayapūrvakam \|\| 23 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

23\. On hearing the words of the sages, Himavat laughed but he was a little frightened. He spoke with humility.

## \|\| 4.33.24 \|\|

*himālaya uvāca \|*  
*śivasya rājasāmagrīṃ na hi paśyāmi kāñcana \|*  
*kañcidāśrayamaiśvaryaṃ kaṃ vā svajanabāndhavam \|\| 24 \|\|*

Himavat said:—

24\. I do not see any royal paraphernalia with Śiva, He has none to support him. He has no assets. He has no kinsman.

## \|\| 4.33.25 \|\|

*necchāmyati vinirliptayogine svāṃ sutāmaham \|*  
*yūyaṃ vedavidhātuśca putrā vadata niścitam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. I do not wish to give my daughter to a Yogin who is extremely detached. O ye sons of the Creator of the Vedas tell me decisively.

## \|\| 4.33.26 \|\|

*varāyānanurūpāya pitā kanyāṃ dadāti cet \|*  
*kāmānmohādbhayāllobhātsa naṣṭo narakaṃ yajet \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. If a father were to give his daughter in marriage to an unsuitable person, out of love, delusion, fear or covetousness, he is doomed. He will go to hell.

## \|\| 4.33.27 \|\|

*na hi dāsyāmyahaṃ kanyāmicchayā śūlapāṇaye \|*  
*yadvidhānaṃ bhavedyogyamṛṣayasta dvidhīyatām \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Out of my own free will, I will not give her to the trident-bearing Śiva. O sages, whatever arrangement is befitting here, may kindly be carried out.

## \|\| 4.33.28 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya vacastasya himāgasya munīśvara \|*  
*pratyuvāca vasiṣṭhastaṃ teṣāṃ vākyaviśārada \|\| 28 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

28\. O excellent sages, on hearing these words of the mountain Himavat, Vasiṣṭha, the most eloquent among them replied:—

## \|\| 4.33.29 \|\|

*vasiṣṭha uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu śaileśa madvākyaṃ sarvathā te hitāvaham \|*  
*dharmāviruddhaṃ satyaśca paratreha mudāvaham \|\| 29 \|\|*

Vasiṣtha said:—

29\. O lord of mountains, listen to my words in every respect conducive to your welfare; they are not against virtue. They are true and shall bring about your joy here and hereafter.

## \|\| 4.33.30 \|\|

*vacanaṃ trividhaṃ śaila laukike vaidike'pi ca \|*  
*sarvaṃ jānāti śāstrajño nirmalajñānacakṣuṣā \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Statements, in ordinary language and in the Vedas, are of three forms. A scholar knowing all lores understands them by means of his pure vision of knowledge.

## \|\| 4.33.31 \|\|

*asatyamahitaṃ paścātsāṃprataṃ śrutisundaram \|*  
*subuddhirvakti śatrurhi hitaṃ naiva kadācana \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. It is only an enemy, though keen in intellect, who says what is pleasing to the ears now but what transpires to be untrue and unwholesome afterwards. He never speaks wholesome things.

## \|\| 4.33.32 \|\|

*ādāvaprītijanakaṃ pariṇāme sukhāvaham \|*  
*dayālurdhamaśīlo hi bodhayatyeva bāṃdhavaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Only a virtuous and sympathetic friend will speak such words as are unpleasant in the beginning but conducive to happiness in the end.

## \|\| 4.33.33 \|\|

*śrutimātrātsudhātulyaṃ sarvakālasukhāvaham \|*  
*satyasāraṃ hitakaraṃ vacanaṃ śreṣṭhamīpsitam \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. But the third variety of behaviour nectarlike to the ears, conducive to happiness on all occasions, essential and truthful is considered to be the most excellent.

## \|\| 4.33.34 \|\|

*evañca trividhaṃ śaila nītiśāstroditaṃ vacaḥ \|*  
*kathyatāṃ triṣu madhye kiṃ bruve vākyaṃ tvadīpsitam \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. O mountain, these are the three types of behaviour as mentioned in the treatises on polity. Tell me which type of behaviour shall I adopt to please you.

## \|\| 4.33.35 \|\|

*brāhmasampadvihīnaśca śaṃkarastridaśeśvaraḥ \|*  
*tattvajñānasamudreṣu sannimagnaikamānasaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Śiva, the lord of gods, is devoid of riches created by Brahmā. But His mind is engrossed in the ocean of true knowledge.

## \|\| 4.33.36 \|\|

*jñānānandasyeśvarasya brāhmavastuṣu kā spṛhā \|*  
*gṛhī dadāti svasutāṃ rājyasampattiśāline \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. How can lord Śiva who is knowledge-Bliss Himself have any desire for articles created by Brahmā? An ordinary householder gives his daughter to one who has a kingdom and riches in his possession?

## \|\| 4.33.37 \|\|

*kanyakāṃ duḥkhine dattvā kanyāghātī bhavetpitā \|*  
*ko veda śaṃkaro duḥkhī kubero yasya kiṃkaraḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. By offering his daughter to a miserable person, a father may be guilty of slaughtering his daughter. Who can think Śiva miserable whose servant is Kubera?

## \|\| 4.33.38 \|\|

*bhrūbhaṅgalīlayā sṛṣṭiṃ sraṣṭuṃ harttuṃ kṣamo hi saḥ \|*  
*nirguṇaḥ paramātmā ca pareśaḥ prakṛteḥ paraḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. He is attributeless, supreme soul, great lord and greater than Prakṛti. He can create and annihilate things by a mere sportive touch of His eyebrows.

## \|\| 4.33.39 \|\|

*yasya ca trividhā mūrttirvidhā tussṛṣṭikarmaṇi \|*  
*sṛṣṭisthityantajananī brahmaviṣṇuharābhidhā \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. His manifestations are threefold, He is the cause of creation sustenance and annihilation in the names of Brahmā Viṣṇu and Śiva.

## \|\| 4.33.40 \|\|

*brahmā ca brahmalokastho viṣṇuḥ kṣīrodavāsakṛt \|*  
*haraḥ kailāsanilayaḥ sarvāḥ śivavibhūtayaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Brahmā stays in Brahmaloka, Viṣṇu in the milk ocean, Śiva in Kailāsa, all these are the attributes of Śiva.

## \|\| 4.33.41 \|\|

*dhatte ca trividhā mūrtī prakṛtiḥ śivasambhavā \|*  
*aṃśena līlayā sṛṣṭau kalayā bahudhā api \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. The primordial nature, born of Śiva, maintains threefold forms in the creative activity, partially out of sport with diverse digits.

## \|\| 4.33.42 \|\|

*mukhodbhavā svayaṃ vāṇī vāgadhiṣṭhātṛdevatā \|*  
*vakṣaḥsthalodbhavā lakṣmīssarvasampatsvarūpiṇī \|\| 42 \|\|*

42 Vāṇī, the deity presiding over the activity of speech, is born of his mouth; Lakṣmī, in the form of riches, is born out of his chest.

## \|\| 4.33.43 \|\|

*śivā tejassu devānāmāvirbhāvaṃ cakāra sā \|*  
*nihatya dānavānsarvāndevebhyaśca śriyaṃ dadau \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Pārvatī manifested herself in the splendours of the gods. After killing all the demons she granted riches and glory to the gods.

## \|\| 4.33.44 \|\|

*prāpa kalpāntare janma jaṭhare dakṣa yoṣitaḥ \|*  
*nāmnā satī haraṃ prāpa dakṣastasmai dadau ca tām \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. In another Kalpa she was born of the womb of Dakṣa’s wife. Her name was Satī. She attained Śiva. Dakṣa gave her to Him.

## \|\| 4.33.45 \|\|

*dehaṃ tatyāja yogena śrutvā sā bhartṛnindanam \|*  
*sādya tvattastu menāyāṃ jajñe jaṭharataśśivā \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. By her Yogic power she cast off her body on hearing about the insult to her husband. She is now born of you in the womb of Menā.

## \|\| 4.33.46 \|\|

*śivā śivasya patnīyaṃ śaila janmanijanmani \|*  
*kalpekalpe buddhirūpā jñānināṃ jananī parā \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. This Pārvatī is the wife of Śiva in every birth. In every Kalpa she is the great cosmic intellect, mother of wise men.

## \|\| 4.33.47 \|\|

*jāyate sma sadā siddhā siddhidā siddhirūpiṇī \|*  
*satyā asthi citābhasma bhaktyā dhatte harassvayam \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. She is victorious always in the form of Siddhā, the bestower of Siddhi (achievement) and is Siddhi personified. Śiva carefully preserves the bones and ashes from the funeral pyre of Satī.

## \|\| 4.33.48 \|\|

*atastvaṃ svecchayā kanyāṃ dehi bhadrāṃ harāya ca \|*  
*athavā sā svayaṃ kāntasthāne yāsyatyadāsyasi \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Hence, you give your daughter, this gentle lady to Śiva out of your own free will. Otherwise she will herself go and surrender herself as his beloved wife.

## \|\| 4.33.49 \|\|

*kṛtvā pratijñāṃ deveśo dṛṣṭvā kleśamasaṃkhyakam \|*  
*duhituste tapaḥsthānamājagāma dvijātmakaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Taking the firm decision on seeing her innumerable sufferings He came to the place of your daughter’s penance in the guise of a brahmin.

## \|\| 4.33.50 \|\|

*tāmāśvāsya varaṃ dattvā jagāma nijamandiram \|*  
*tatprārthanāvaśācchambhuryayāce tvāṃ śivāṃ gire \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. After consoling her and granting her the boon He returned to His abode. It was for complying with her request that Śiva requested you for the hand of Śivā, O mountain.

## \|\| 4.33.51 \|\|

*aṃgīkṛtaṃ yuvābhyāṃ tacchivabhaktiratātmanā \|*  
*viparītamatirjātā vada kasmādgirīśvara \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Both of you had accepted the proposal as you were drawn by devotion to Śiva. O lord of mountains, how is it that your mind has taken a somersault now? Please tell me.

## \|\| 4.33.52 \|\|

*tadgatvā prabhuṇā deva prārthitena tvadantikam \|*  
*prasthāpitā vayaṃ śīghraṃ hyṛṣayassāpyarundhatī \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. On being requested by the gods, the lord has sent us, the sages and Arundhatī to you.

## \|\| 4.33.53 \|\|

*śikṣayāmo vayaṃ tvā hi dattvā rudrāya pārvatīm \|*  
*evaṃkṛte mahānando bhaviṣyati gire tava \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. O mountain, we instruct you plainly. By giving Pārvatī to Śiva you will meet with great bliss.

## \|\| 4.33.54 \|\|

*śivāṃ śivāya śailendra svecchayā cenna dāsyasi \|*  
*bhavitā tadvivāho'tra bhavitavyabalena hi \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. O lord of mountains, even if you do not give Pārvatī to Śiva out of your own free will, their marriage will take place as a result of the inexorable workings of fate.

## \|\| 4.33.55 \|\|

*varaṃ dadau śivāyai sa tapantyai tāta śaṃkaraḥ \|*  
*nahīśvarapratijñātaṃ viparītāya kalpate \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. O dear one, Śiva has already granted Pārvatī the boon at the time of her penance. A promise of Śiva cannot be turned topsyturvy.

## \|\| 4.33.56 \|\|

*aho pratijñā durlaṃghyā sādhūnāmīśavartinām \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ jagatāṃ madhye kimīśasya punargire \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Oh! even the promise of ordinary good men acting under the guidance of Śiva cannot be transgressed in all the worlds. O mountain, what then about that of Śiva Himslf.

## \|\| 4.33.57 \|\|

*eko mahendraśśailānāṃ pakṣāṃściccheda līlayā \|*  
*pārvatī līlayā merośśṛṅgabhaṅgaṃ cakāra ca \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Working singlehanded, Lord Indra chopped off the wings of mountains as though at play. Pārvatī too sportively broke the peak of Meru.

## \|\| 4.33.58 \|\|

*ekārthe nahi śaileśa nāśyāssarvā hi sampadaḥ \|*  
*ekaṃ tyajetkulasyārthe śrutireṣā sanātanī \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. All riches can be sacrificed, O lord of mountains, for the sake of a single entity, but the eternal Śruti has it that one should forsake a single entity for the sake of a unit.

## \|\| 4.33.59 \|\|

*dattvā viprāya svasutāmanaraṇyo nṛpeśvara \|*  
*brāhmaṇādbhayamāpanno rarakṣa nijasampadam \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. When danger was imminent at the hands of a brahmin, the chief of kings, Anaraṇya, saved his entire asset by giving his daughter to him.

## \|\| 4.33.60 \|\|

*tamāśu bodhayāmāsurnītiśāstravido janāḥ \|*  
*brahmaśāpādvibhītāśca guravo jñātisattamāḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. When he was threatened by the curse of brahmin his preceptors, wise kinsmen and people well-versed in the science of polity advised him hastily.

## \|\| 4.33.61 \|\|

*śailarāja tvamapyeva sutāṃ dattvā śivāya ca \|*  
*rakṣa sarvānbaṃdhuvargānvaśaṃ kuru surānapi \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. O king of mountains, you too save your kinsmen by giving your daughter to Śiva. You can claim thus the gods too to your side.

## \|\| 4.33.62 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya vasiṣṭhasya vacanaṃ sa praha sya ca \|*  
*papraccha nṛpavārttāśca hṛdayena vidūyatā \|\| 62 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

62\. On hearing the words of Vasiṣṭha, Himavat, with a dejected heart but laughing outwardly asked him about the details of the story of the king.

## \|\| 4.33.63 \|\|

*himālaya uvāca \|*  
*kasya vaṃśodbhavo brahmannanaraṇyo nṛpaścasaḥ \|*  
*sutāṃ dattvā sa ca kathaṃ rarakṣākhilasampadaḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

Himavat said:—

63\. O brahmin, what is the race to which the king Anaraṇya belonged? How did he save his assets by giving his daughter?

## \|\| 4.33.64 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*iti śrutvā vasiṣṭhastu śailavākyaṃ prasannadhīḥ \|*  
*provāca giraye tasmai nṛpavārttā sukhāvahām \|\| 64 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

64\. On hearing these words of the mountain, Vasiṣṭha became glad and told him the details of the interesting story of the king.

## Chapter 34 - The Story of Anaraṇya

## \|\| 4.34.1 \|\|

*\|\| vasiṣṭha uvāca \|*  
*manorvaṃśodbhavo rājā so'naraṇyo nṛpeśvara \|*  
*indrasāvarṇisaṃjñasya caturdaśamitasya hi \|\| 1 \|\|*

Vasiṣtha said:—

1\. The king Anaraṇya hailed from the race of the fourteenth Manu Indrasāvarṇi,

## \|\| 4.34.2 \|\|

*anaraṇyo nṛpaśreṣṭhassa ptadvīpamahīpatiḥ \|*  
*śambhubhakto viśeṣeṇa maṅgalāraṇyajo balī \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The great king Anaraṇya, born of Maṅgalāraṇya\[1\] was very strong. He was a special devotee of Śiva and ruled over the seven continents.

## \|\| 4.34.3 \|\|

*bhṛguṃ purodhasaṃ kṛtvā śataṃ yajñāṃścakāra saḥ \|*  
*na svīcakāra śakratvaṃ dīyamānaṃ surairapi \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Having Bhṛgu as his priest he performed a hundred sacrifices. He did not accept the position of Indra even when offered by the gods.

## \|\| 4.34.4 \|\|

*babhūvaśśataputrāśca rājñastasya himālaya \|*  
*kanyaikā sundarī nāmnā padmā padmālayā samā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. O Himavat, hundred sons were born to him and a beautiful daughter Padmā who was equal to Lakṣmī.

## \|\| 4.34.5 \|\|

*yassnehaḥ putraśatake kanyāyāñca tato'dhikaḥ \|*  
*nṛpasya tasya tasyāṃ hi babhūva nagasattama \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. O excellent mountain, he was more fond of his daughter than of his hundred sons.

## \|\| 4.34.6 \|\|

*prāṇādhikāḥ priyatamā mahiṣyassarvayoṣitaḥ \|*  
*nṛpasya patnyaḥ pañcāsansarvāssaubhāgyasaṃyutā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. He had five queens who were endowed with great qualities and fortunes and were loved by him over and above his life.

## \|\| 4.34.7 \|\|

*sā kanyā yauvanasthā ca babhūva svapiturgṛhe \|*  
*patraṃ prasthāpayāmāsa suvarāna yanāyasaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The girl entered the prime of her youth in her father’s palace. The king issued letters of invitation for the requisition of good bridegrooms.

## \|\| 4.34.8 \|\|

*ekadā pippalādarṣirgarntuṃ svāśramamutsukaḥ \|*  
*tapaḥsthāne nirjane ca gandharvaṃ sa dadarśa ha \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. In the meantime the sage Pippalāda eagerly hastening back to his hermitage saw a certain Gandharva in an isolated place in the penance-grove.

## \|\| 4.34.9 \|\|

*strīyutaṃ magnacittaṃ ca śṛṅgāre rasasāgare \|*  
*viharantaṃ mahāpremṇā kāmaśāstraviśāradam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The Gandharva was an expert in the science of erotics. He was in the company of a woman. He was therefore completely submerged in the ocean of pleasure, sexual dalliance and was lusty.

## \|\| 4.34.10 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā taṃ muniśārdūlaḥ sakāmaḥ saṃbabhūva saḥ \|*  
*tapatsvadattacittaścāciṃtayaddārasaṃgraham \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. On seeing him the great sage became very lustful. He lost interest in penance and began to think of acquiring a wife.

## \|\| 4.34.11 \|\|

*evaṃvṛttasya tasyaiva pippalādasya sanmuneḥ \|*  
*kiyatkālo gatastatra kāmonmathitacetasaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Thus the good sage spent a long time with his mind utterly agitated by pangs of love.

## \|\| 4.34.12 \|\|

*ekadā puṣpabhadrāyāṃ snātuṃ gacchanmunīśvaraḥ \|*  
*dadarśa padmāṃ yuvatīṃ padmāmiva manoramām \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Once while the good sage was on his way to the river Puṣpabhadrā for taking his bath he happened to see the young maiden Padmā who was as charming as goddess Lakṣmī.

## \|\| 4.34.13 \|\|

*keyaṃ kanyeti papraccha samīpasthāñjanānmuniḥ \|*  
*janā nivedayāṃcakrurnatvā śāpaniyantritāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The sage asked the persons standing by—“Who is this girl?” The people, afraid of the curse bowed to the sage and replied.

## \|\| 4.34.14 \|\|

*janā ūcuḥ \|*  
*anaraṇyasuteyaṃ vai padmā nāma ramāparā \|*  
*varārohā prārthyamānā nṛpaśreṣṭhairguṇālayā \|\| 14 \|\|*

The people said:—

14\. This excellent lady, the repository of all good qualities, is the daughter of Anaraṇya and is called Padmā. She is another Lakṣmī (goddess of fortune). She is being wooed by great kings.

## \|\| 4.34.15 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*tacchrutvā sa munirvākyaṃ janānāṃ tathyavādinām \|*  
*cukṣobhātīva manasi tallipsura bhavacca saḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

15\. On hearing the words of the people who spoke the truth, the sage became much agitated in the mind and was eager to possess her.

## \|\| 4.34.16 \|\|

*muniḥ snātvābhīṣṭadevaṃ sampūjya vidhivacchivam \|*  
*jagāma kāmī bhikṣārthamanaraṇyasabhāṃ gire \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. O mountain, the sage took bath and worshipped his favourite deity Śiva duly. The lustful sage went to the council-chamber of Anaraṇya for the sake of alms.

## \|\| 4.34.17 \|\|

*rājā śīghraṃ muniṃ dṛṣṭvā praṇanāma bhayākulaḥ \|*  
*madhuparkādikaṃ dattvā pūjayāmāsa bhaktitaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Immediately after seeing the sage, the king was struck with awe and bowed to him. He offered him homage (Madhuparka) and devoutly worshipped him.

## \|\| 4.34.18 \|\|

*kāmātsarvaṃ gṛhītvā ca yayāce kanyakāṃ muniḥ \|*  
*maunī babhūva nṛpatiḥ kiñcinirvaktumakṣamaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Out of love, the sage accepted everything and ultimately requested for the hand of his daughter. The king kept quiet, being unable to give any decisive reply.

## \|\| 4.34.19 \|\|

*muniryayāce kanyāṃ sa tāṃ dehīti nṛpeśvara \|*  
*anyathā bhasmasātsarvaṃ kariṣyāmi kṣaṇena ca \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The sage repeated his request saying—“O great king, give me your daughter. Otherwise in a trice I will reduce everything to ashes”.

## \|\| 4.34.20 \|\|

*sarve babhūvavurācchannā gaṇāstattejasā mune \|*  
*ruroda rājā sagaṇo dṛṣṭvā vipraṃ jarāturam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. The king and his attendants were overwhelmed by the splendour of the sage. Staring at the old emaciated brahmin, they began to cry.

## \|\| 4.34.21 \|\|

*mahiṣyo rurudussarvā itikarttavyatākṣamāḥ \|*  
*mūrcchāmāpa mahārājñī kanyāmātā śucākulā \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. The queens, knowing not what shall be done, lamented. The chief queen, the mother of the girl, fell unconscious in the excess of her grief.

## \|\| 4.34.22 \|\|

*babhūvustanayāssarve śokākuli tamānasāḥ \|*  
*sarvaṃ śokākulaṃ jātaṃ nṛpasambandhi śailapa \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The brothers of the girl were agitated with sorrow. O lord of mountains, everything and every one connected with the king was overwhelmed with grief.

## \|\| 4.34.23 \|\|

*etasminnantare prājño dvijo gururanuttamaḥ \|*  
*purohitaśca matimānāgato nṛpasannidhim \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. In the meantime the wise brahmin, the excellent preceptor of the king, as well as his intelligent priest came there.

## \|\| 4.34.24 \|\|

*rājā praṇamya sampūjya ruroda ca tayoḥ puraḥ \|*  
*sarvaṃ nivedayāṃcakre papracchocitamāśu tat \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. The king bowed to them and paid homage. He cried before them. He explained to them everything and asked them what was the proper step to be taken immediately.

## \|\| 4.34.25-26 \|\|

*atha rājño gururvipraḥ paṇḍitaśca purohitaḥ \|*  
*api dvau śāstranītijñau bodhayāmāsaturnṛpam \|\| 25 \|\|*

*śokākulāśca mahiṣīrnṛpabālāṃśca kanyakām \|*  
*uttamā nītimādṛtya sarveṣāṃ hitakāriṇīm \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. The brahmin, the preceptor of the king and the scholarly priest were experts in sacred lore and polity. They advised the king in that matter.

## \|\| 4.34.27 \|\|

*gurupurodhasāvūcatuḥ \|*  
*śṛṇu rājanmahāprājña vaco nau saddhitāvaham \|*  
*mā śucaḥ saparīvāraśśāstre kuru matiṃ satīm \|\| 27 \|\|*

The preceptor and the priest said:—

27\. O wise king, listen to our beneficial words. Do not be anxious. In the company of your kinsmen turn your good attention to the sacred texts.

## \|\| 4.34.28 \|\|

*adya vābdadinānte vā dātavyā kanyakā nṛpa \|*  
*pātrāya viprāyānyasmai kasmai cidvā viśeṣataḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. O king, whether today or after a year, the princess is to be given to a deserving person, a brahmin or anyone else.

## \|\| 4.34.29 \|\|

*satpātraṃ brāhmaṇādanyanna paśyāvo jagattraye \|*  
*sutāṃ dattvā ca munaye rakṣa svāṃ sarvasampadam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. In the three worlds we do not see more deserving person than this brahmin. Give your daughter to this sage and save your riches.

## \|\| 4.34.30 \|\|

*rājannekanimittena sarvasaṃpadvinaśyati \|*  
*sarvaṃ rakṣati taṃ tyaktvā vinā taṃ śaraṇāgatam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. O king, if all riches face the danger of destruction due to one object or person, the wise man saves everything by abandoning that object or person unless it be that who has sought refuge.

## \|\| 4.34.31 \|\|

*vasiṣṭha uvāca \|*  
*rājā prājñavacaḥ śrutvā vilapya ca muhurmuhuḥ \|*  
*kanyāṃ sālaṃkṛtāṃ kṛtvā munīndrāya dadau kila \|\| 31 \|\|*

Vasiṣṭha said:—

31\. On hearing the words of the wise, the king lamented again and again but ultimately offered his daughter fully bedecked in ornaments to the excellent sage.

## \|\| 4.34.32 \|\|

*kāntāṃ gṛhītvā sa munirvivāhya vidhivadgire \|*  
*padmāṃ padmopamāṃ tāṃ vai muditassvālayaṃ yayau \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. O mountain, accepting and marrying the beautiful maiden Padmā, on a par with goddess Lakṣmī, in accordance with holy laws, the delighted sage returned to his abode.

## \|\| 4.34.33 \|\|

*rājā sarvānparityajya dattvā vṛddhāya cātmajām \|*  
*glāniṃ citte samādhāya jagāma tapase vanam \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. After giving his daughter to an old man, the king was much dejected in mind. Abandoning everything he went to the forest for performing penance.

## \|\| 4.34.34 \|\|

*tadbhāryyāpi vanaṃ yāte prāṇanāthe tadā gire \|*  
*bhartuśca duhituśśokātprāṇāṃstatyāja sundarī \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. O mountain, when the king went to the forest, the queen, passed away, due to the pangs of separation from her husband and daughter.

## \|\| 4.34.35 \|\|

*pūjyāḥ putrāśca bhṛtyāśca mūrcchāmāpurnṛpaṃ vinā \|*  
*śuśucuḥ śvāsasaṃyuktaṃ jñātvā sarvepare janāḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Without the king, the respectable sons and officers of the king became unconscious. The other people thinking that the king was dead lamented much.

## \|\| 4.34.36 \|\|

*anaraṇyo vanaṃ gatvā tapastaptvāti śaṃkaram \|*  
*samārādhya yayau bhaktyā śivalokamanāmayam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Anaraṇya went to the forest, performed great penance, and worshipped Śiva with devotion. In the end, he attained Śivaloka free from all ailments.

## \|\| 4.34.37 \|\|

*nṛpasya kīrtimānnāmnā jyeṣṭhaputrotha dhārmikaḥ \|*  
*putravatpālayāmāsa prajā rājyaṃ cakāra ha \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. The eldest son of the king, Kīrtimān, virtuously ruled over the kingdom and tended the subjects like his own children.

## \|\| 4.34.38 \|\|

*iti te kathitaṃ śailānaraṇyacaritaṃ śubham \|*  
*kanyāṃ dattvā yathārakṣadvaṃśaṃ cāpyakhilaṃ dhanam \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Thus, O mountain, I have narrated to you the auspicious story of Anaraṇya, how he saved his race and his wealth by offering his daughter to the sage.

## \|\| 4.34.39 \|\|

*śailarāja tvamapyevaṃ sutāṃ dattvā śivāya ca \|*  
*rakṣa sarvakulaṃ sarvānvaśānkuru surānapi \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. O king of mountains, you too, give your daughter to Śiva, save the entire family and keep even the gods under your control.

## Chapter 35 - The story of Padmā and Pippalāda

## \|\| 4.35.1 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*anaraṇyasya caritaṃ sutādānasamanvitam \|*  
*śrutvā girivarastāta kiṃ cakāra ca tadvada \|\| 1 \|\|*

Nārada said:—

1\. O dear, what did the excellent mountain do after hearing the anecdote of Anaraṇya and the marriage of his daughter? Please tell me.

## \|\| 4.35.2 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*anaraṇyasya caritaṃ kanyādānasamanvitam \|*  
*śrutvā papraccha śaileśo vasiṣṭhaṃ sāñjaliḥ punaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

2\. After hearing the story of Anaraṇya including the anecdote of the offer of his daughter, the lord of mountains again asked Vasiṣṭha with palms joined in reverence.

## \|\| 4.35.3 \|\|

*śaileśa uvāca \|*  
*vasiṣṭha muniśārdūla brahmaputra kṛpānidhe \|*  
*anaraṇyacaritrante kathitaṃ paramādbhutam \|\| 3 \|\|*

The lord of mountains said:—

3\. O leading sage Vasiṣṭha, O son of Brahmā, O merciful one, you have narrated the wonderful story of Anaraṇya.

## \|\| 4.35.4 \|\|

*anaraṇyasutā yasmāt pippalādaṃ muniṃ patim \|*  
*samprāpya kimakārṣītsā taccaritraṃ mudāvaham \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. What did Padmā, the daughter of Anaraṇya, do after marrying sage Pippalāda. Please mention her story fully.

## \|\| 4.35.5-6 \|\|

*vasi \|*  
*pippalādo munivaro vayasā jarjarodhikaḥ \|*  
*gatvā nijāśramaṃ nāryā'naraṇyasutayā tayā \|\| 5 \|\|*

*uvāsa tatra suprītyā tapasvī nātilampaṭaḥ \|*  
*tatrāraṇye girivara sa nityaṃ nijadharmakṛt \|\| 6 \|\|*

Vasiṣṭha said:—

5-6 The very old and venerable sage Pippalāda returned to his hermitage along with his wife Padmā and passed time in pleasure. He was not too much sensuous. He continued to perform his penance and holy rites in the forest and on the mountain.

## \|\| 4.35.7 \|\|

*athānaraṇyakanyā sā siṣeve bhaktito munim \|*  
*karmaṇā manasā vācā lakṣmīnārāyaṇaṃ yathā \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The daughter of Anaraṇya served the sage devoutly physically, mentally and verbally like Lakṣmī serving Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 4.35.8 \|\|

*ekadā svarṇadīṃ snātuṃ gacchantīṃ susmitāṃ ca tām \|*  
*dadarśa pathi dharmaśca māyayā vṛṣarūpadhṛk \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Once Dharma (Virtue) assumed the guise of a king by his magical power and happened to see on the way that lady of gentle smiles going to the celestial river for her holy dip.

## \|\| 4.35.9-10 \|\|

*cāruratnarathasthaśca nānālaṃ kārabhūṣitaḥ \|*  
*navīnayauvanaśśrīmānkāmadevasabhaprabhaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭvā tāṃ sundarīṃ padmāmuvāca sa vṛṣo vibhuḥ \|*  
*vijñātuṃ bhāvamantaḥsthaṃ tasyāśca muniyoṣitaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. The lord Dharma was seated in a beautiful chariot studded with gems. He was bedecked in many kinds of ornaments. He was in the prime of fresh youth, glorious and lustrous like the cupid. On seeing Padmā he spoke thus, in order to know the innermost feelings of the sage’s wife.

## \|\| 4.35.11 \|\|

*\|\| dharma uvāca \|*  
*ayi sundari lakṣmīrvai rājayogye manohare \|*  
*atīva yauvanasthe ca kāmini sthirayauvane \|\| 11 \|\|*

Dharma said:—

11\. O beautiful woman, you are Lakṣmī herself; you are charming, you are worthy of a king; you are in the very prime of youth; you will be ever young; you are a lovely sweet lady.

## \|\| 4.35.12 \|\|

*jarāturasya vṛddhasya pippalādasya vai muneḥ \|*  
*satyaṃ vadāmi tanvaṃgi samīpe naiva rājase \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. I am telling you the truth, O slender-limbed lady. You lack lustre and colour in the presence of the sage Pippalāda who is old and weak.

## \|\| 4.35.13 \|\|

*vipraṃ tapassu nirataṃ nirghṛṇaṃ maraṇonmukham \|*  
*tvaktvā māṃ paśya rājendraṃ ratiśūraṃ smarāturam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Cast off that ruthless old brahmin always engaged in penances. Look up to me a great king, heroic in sexual dalliance and agitated by Kāma.

## \|\| 4.35.14 \|\|

*prāpnoti sundarī puṇyātsaundaryyaṃ pūrvajanmanaḥ \|*  
*saphalaṃ tadbhavetsarvaṃ rasikāliṃganena ca \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. A beautiful woman acquires beauty as a result of the merit of a previous birth. The beauty becomes completely fruitful only after embracing a man of aesthetic taste.

## \|\| 4.35.15 \|\|

*sahasrasundarīkāntaṃ kāmaśāstraviśāradam \|*  
*kiṃkaraṃ kuru māṃ kānte samparityajya taṃ patim \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. I am the lover of a thousand beautiful women. I am an expert in the erotic science and literature. Abandon that husband and make me your slave.

## \|\| 4.35.16 \|\|

*nirjane kānane ramye śaile śaile nadītaṭe \|*  
*viharasva mayā sārddhaṃ janmedaṃ saphalaṃ kuru \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. You can indulge in sexual dalliance in the beautiful secluded forests, mountains and banks of rivers in my company. Make your life fruitful.

## \|\| 4.35.17 \|\|

*\|\| vasiṣṭha uvāca \|*  
*ityevamuktavantaṃ sā svarathādavaruhya ca \|*  
*grahītumutsukaṃ haste tamuvāca pativratā \|\| 17 \|\|*

Vasiṣtha said:—

17\. Saying this, he got down and was eager to catch her hands. The chaste lady then addressed him thus.

## \|\| 4.35.18 \|\|

*padmo vāca \|*  
*gaccha dūraṃ gaccha dūraṃ pāpiṣṭhastvaṃ narādhipa \|*  
*māṃ cetpaśyasi kāmena sadyo naṣṭo bhaviṣyasi \|\| 18 \|\|*

Padmā said:—

18\. Away, away, go away you sinful king. If you cast your lustful ogles at me you will be doomed in a trice.

## \|\| 4.35.19 \|\|

*pippalādaṃ muni śreṣṭhaṃ tapasā pūtavigraham \|*  
*tyaktvā kathaṃ bhajeyaṃ tvāṃ strījitaṃ ratilampaṭam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. How can I resort to you, lecherous and mad after women, after forsaking the excellent sage Pippalāda whose body is sanctified by austerities?

## \|\| 4.35.20 \|\|

*strījitasparśamātreṇa sarvaṃ puṇyaṃ praṇaśyati \|*  
*strījitaḥ parapāpī ca taddarśanamaghāvaham \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. By the very touch of a person under the influence of women all merits are destroyed. He is a great sinner. His very sight promotes sins.

## \|\| 4.35.21 \|\|

*satkriyo hyaśucirnityaṃ sa pumān yaḥ striyā jitaḥ \|*  
*nindanti pitaro devā māna vāssakalāśca tam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Even if he performs holy rites, a person succumbing to the viles of women is always impure. The manes, the gods and all men despise him.

## \|\| 4.35.22 \|\|

*tasya kiṃ jñāna sutapo japahomaprapūjanaiḥ \|*  
*vidyayā dānataḥ kimvā strībhiryasya mano hṛtam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Of what avail is knowledge, penance, repetition of sacred mantras, sacrifice, adoration, learning and charitable gift to him who is henpecked?

## \|\| 4.35.23 \|\|

*mātaraṃ māṃ striyo bhāvaṃ kṛtvā yena bravīṣi ha \|*  
*bhaviṣyati kṣayastena kālena mama śāpataḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Since you spoke to me viewing me with the feelings that I am your wife although I ought to have been viewed as your mother, you will have a gradual decline as a result of my curse.

Vasiṣtha Said:—

## \|\| 4.35.24 \|\|

*vasiṣṭha uvāca \|*  
*śrutvā dharmassatīśāpaṃ nṛpa mūrtiṃ vihāya ca \|*  
*dhṛtvā svamūrtiṃ deveśaḥ kampamāna uvāca saḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. On hearing the curse of the chaste woman, O lord of mountains, Dharma cast off the guise of a king and assumed his real form. Tremblingly he spoke thus—

## \|\| 4.35.25 \|\|

*dharma uvāca \|*  
*mātarjānīhi māṃ dharmaṃ jñānināñca guro rgurum \|*  
*parastrīmātṛbuddhiśca kuvvarntaṃ satataṃ sati \|\| 25 \|\|*

Dharma said:—

25\. O mother, know me as Dharma elderly and venerable to men of wisdom and preceptors. O chaste lady, I always consider other’s wives as mothers.

## \|\| 4.35.26 \|\|

*ahaṃ tavāntaraṃ jñātumāgatastava sannidhim \|*  
*tavāhañca mano jāne tathāpi vidhinoditaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. It was to know your innermost feelings that I approached you. I knew your mind, still I was urged by fate.

## \|\| 4.35.27 \|\|

*kṛtaṃ me damanaṃ sādhvi na viruddhaṃ yathocitam \|*  
*śāstiḥ samutpathasthānāmīśvareṇa vinirmitā \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Only proper suppression, not the contrary, is carried out by you. Chastisement of those who go astray from the right path is carried out by Śiva Himself.

## \|\| 4.35.28 \|\|

*svayaṃ pradātā sarvebhyaḥ sukhaduḥkhavarānkṣamaḥ \|*  
*sampadaṃ vipadaṃ yo hi namastasmai śivāya hi \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Obeisance to Śiva who distributes happiness, misery, boons, prosperity or adversity on all.

## \|\| 4.35.29 \|\|

*śatruṃ mitraṃ samvidhātuṃ prītiñca kalahaṃ kṣamaḥ \|*  
*sraṣṭuṃ naṣṭuṃ ca yassṛṣṭiṃ namastasmai śivāya hi \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Obeisance to Śiva who can make people enemies or friends, create affection or quarrel, to generate or destroy things.

## \|\| 4.35.30 \|\|

*yena śuklīkṛtaṃ kṣīraṃ jale śaityaṃ kṛtampurā \|*  
*dāhīkṛto hutā śaśca namastasmai śivāya hi \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Obeisance to Śiva who has made milk white, who has bestowed chillness on water and heat on fire.

## \|\| 4.35.31 \|\|

*prakṛtirnirmitā yena taptvāti mahadāditaḥ \|*  
*brahmaviṣṇumaheśādyā namastasmai śivāya hi \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Obeisance to Śiva, by whom the primordial nature, the principles Mahat etc, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva and others are created.

## \|\| 4.35.32 \|\|

*brahmovācaḥ \|*  
*ityuktvā puratastasyāstasthau dharmo jagadguruḥ \|*  
*kiñcinnovāca cakitastatpātivratya toṣitaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

32\. After saying thus Dharma, the most venerable god in the universe stood in front of her, stunned but delighted at her chastity. But he did not say anything.

## \|\| 4.35.33 \|\|

*padmāpi nṛpakanyā sā pippalādaprisā tadā \|*  
*sādhvī taṃ dharmamājñāya vismitovāca parvata \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Princess Padmā, the chaste beloved of Pippalāda, O mountain, was surprised on realising that it was Dharma and said.

## \|\| 4.35.34 \|\|

*padmovāca \|*  
*tvameva dharma sarveṣāṃ sākṣī nikhilakarmaṇām \|*  
*kathaṃ mano me vijñātuṃ viḍambayasi māṃ vibho \|\| 34 \|\|*

Padmā said:—
