30\. On hearing your words lord Indra who was frightened from head to foot, immediately spoke to Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 4.41.31 \|\|

*\|\| devendra uvāca \|*  
*devadeva ramānātha tvaṣṭā māṃ nihaniṣyati \|*  
*putraśokena tapto'sau vyājenānena nānyathā \|\| 31 \|\|*

Lord Indra said:—

31\. O lord of Lakṣmī, O lord of gods, Tvaṣṭṛ who is agitated due to the grief over his son will surely kill me under this pretext and not otherwise.

## \|\| 4.41.32 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā devadevo janārdanaḥ \|*  
*uvāca prahasan vākyaṃ śakramāśvāsayaṃstadā \|\| 32 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

32\. On hearing his words Viṣṇu, the lord of gods laughingly consoled Indra by speaking thus.

## \|\| 4.41.33 \|\|

*viṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*nivātakavacaiḥ pūrvaṃ mohito'si śacīpate \|*  
*mahāvidyāvalenaiva dānavaiḥ pūrvavairibhiḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

Viṣṇu said:—

33\. O lord of Śacī, formerly you had been enchanted by the demons Nivātakavacas, your previous enemies, by the power of their great spell.

## \|\| 4.41.34 \|\|

*parvato himavāneṣa tathānya'khilaparvatāḥ \|*  
*vipakṣā hi kṛtāssarve mama vākyācca vāsava \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. O Indra, at my instance, this mountain Himavat and others too were rendered wingless.

## \|\| 4.41.35 \|\|

*tenusmṛtyā tu vai dṛṣṭvā māyayā girayo hyamī \|*  
*jetumicchantu ye mūḍhā na bhetavyamarāvapi \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Let the mountains now create magic on remembering that and wish to surpass us foolishly. We are not to be afraid of our enemies.

## \|\| 4.41.36 \|\|

*īśvaro no hi sarveṣāṃ śaṃkaro bhaktavatsalaḥ \|*  
*sarvathā kuśalaṃ śakra kariṣyati na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. O Indra, Śiva favourably disposed to His devotees, will undoubtedly look to our welfare.

## \|\| 4.41.37 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*evaṃ saṃvadamānantaṃ śakraṃ vikṛtamānasam \|*  
*hariṇoktaśca giriśo laukikīṃ gatimāśritaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. While he was speaking this to Indra of agitated mind, Śiva spoke to Viṣṇu following the worldly custom.

## \|\| 4.41.38 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*he hare he sureśāna kimbrūtho'dya parasparam \|*  
*ityuktvā tau maheśāno mune tvāmpratyuvāca saḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

Śiva said:—

38\. “O Viṣṇu, O lord of gods, what are you speaking to each other?” O sage, after speaking thus to them Śiva addressed you.

## \|\| 4.41.39 \|\|

*kiṃnu vakti mahāśailo yathārthaṃ vada nārada \|*  
*vṛttāntaṃ sakalambrūhi na gopyaṃ kartumarhasi \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. “O Nārada, what does the great mountain say? Tell me the truth with details. You must not keep any secret.

## \|\| 4.41.40 \|\|

*dadāti vā naiva dadāti śailassutāṃ svakīyāṃ vada tacca śīghram \|*  
*kinte dṛṣṭaṃ kiṃ kṛtantatra gatvā prītyā sarvaṃ tadvadāśvadya tāta \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Does the mountain want to give the daughter or not? Tell me that quickly. O dear one, on going there, what did you see? What did you do? Tell me that quickly.

## \|\| 4.41.41 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*hatyuktaśśambhunā tatra mune tvandevadarśanaḥ \|*  
*sarvaṃ rahasyavoco vai yaddṛṣṭantatra maṇḍape \|\| 41 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

41\. Addressed thus by Śiva, O sage, you endowed with divine vision told him secretly what you saw in the altar.

## \|\| 4.41.42 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*devadeva mahādeva śṛṇu madvacanaṃ śubham \|*  
*nāsti vighnabhayaṃ nātha vivāhe kiṃcideva hi \|\| 42 \|\|*

Nārada said:—

42\. O great lord, lord of gods, listen to my auspicious words. O lord, there is no fear of any hindrance in the celebration of marriage.

## \|\| 4.41.43 \|\|

*avaśyameva śaileśastubhyaṃ dāsyati kanyakām \|*  
*tvāmānayitumāyātā ime śailā na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. The lord of mountains will surely give his daughter to you. It is certainly to take you there that these mountains have come here.

## \|\| 4.41.44 \|\|

*kintu hyamaramohārthaṃ māyā viracitādbhutā \|*  
*kutūhalārthaṃ sarvajña na kaścidvighnasambhavaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. But to delude the gods a wonderful spell has been created. O omniscient, it is only to inspire curiosity. There is no possibility of any obstacle.

## \|\| 4.41.45 \|\|

*vicitrammaṇḍapaṃ gehe'kārṣīttasya tadājñayā \|*  
*viśvakarmā mahāmāyī nānāścaryamayaṃ vibho \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. O lord, Viśvakarman, a great expert in creating illusion has constructed a peculiar altar in his house at his instance. It is full of surprising things.

## \|\| 4.41.46 \|\|

*sarvadevasamājaśca kṛtastatra vimohanaḥ \|*  
*tandṛṣṭvā vismayaṃ prāptohaṃ tanmāyāvimohitaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. A fascinating assembly of gods has been built there. On seeing it I was deluded by his skill and was struck with surprise.

## \|\| 4.41.47 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*tacchrutvā tadvacastāta lokācārakaraḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*harṣādīnprahasañchambhuruvāca sakalānsurān \|\| 47 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

47\. O dear, on hearing your words, the lord Śiva following the worldly convention, laughingly spoke to Viṣṇu and other gods.

## \|\| 4.41.48 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*kanyāṃ dāsyati cenmahyaṃ parvato hi himācalaḥ \|*  
*māyayā mama kiṃ kāryaṃ vada viṣṇo yathātatham \|\| 48 \|\|*

Śiva said:—

48\. O Viṣṇu, if the mountain Himavat gives his daughter to me, what have I to do with this spell? Speak to me what is true.

## \|\| 4.41.49 \|\|

*he brahmañchakra munayasturā brūta yathārthataḥ \|*  
*māyayā mama kiṃ kāryaṃ kanyāṃ dāsyati cedgiriḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. O Brahmā, O Indra, O sages, O gods, speak truly. What have I to do with the spell if the mountain gives his daughter?

## \|\| 4.41.50 \|\|

*kenāpyupāyena phalaṃ hi sādhyamityucyate paṇḍitairnyāyavidbhiḥ \|*  
*tasmātsarvairgamyatāṃ śīghrameva kāryārthibhirviṣṇupurogamaiśca \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. It is held by scholars, knowing cogent reasons, that somehow or other the fruit should be achieved. Hence you, with Viṣṇu at the head, will hasten seeking only the task on hand.

## \|\| 4.41.51 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*evaṃ saṃvadamāno'sau devaiśśambhurabhūttadā \|*  
*kṛtaḥ smareṇaiva vaśī vaśaṃ vā prākṛto naraḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

51\. Discussing thus with gods, Śiva appeared to be completely overpowered by Kāma like an ordinary man.

## \|\| 4.41.52-54 \|\|

*atha śambhvājñayā sarve viṣṇvādyā nirjarāstadā \|*  
*ṛṣayaśca mahātmāno yayurmohabhramāpaham \|\| 52 \|\|*

*puraskṛtya mune tvāṃ ca parvatāṃstānsavismayāḥ \|*  
*himādreśca tadā jagmurmandiramparamādbhutam \|\| 53 \|\|*

*atha viṣṇvādisaṃyukto muditaissvabalairyutaḥ \|*  
*ājagāmopahaimāgapuraṃ pramudito haraḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

52-54. At the bidding of Śiva, Viṣṇu and other gods, the noble sages and others, O sage, kept you and mountains at the head and started for the abode of Himavat. They were surprised to see the wonderful abode. The delighted Śiva reached the outskirts of the city accompanied by Viṣṇu and others as well as his delighted Gaṇas.

## Chapter 42 - Description of the meeting of the lord and the mountain

## \|\| 4.42.1 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*athākarṇya girīśaśca nijapuryyupakaṇṭhataḥ \|*  
*prāptamīśaṃ sarvagaṃ vai mumudeti himālayaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

1\. On hearing that the all-pervading Śiva had come very near his city, the lord of mountains Himavat rejoiced much.

## \|\| 4.42.2 \|\|

*atha sambhṛtasambhāra ssambhāṣāṃ kartumīśvaram \|*  
*śailānprasthāpayāmāsa brāhmaṇānapi sarvaśaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Then, gathering all the requisite things he sent mountains and the brahmins to welcome Siva.

## \|\| 4.42.3 \|\|

*svayaṃ jagāma sadbhaktyā prāṇepsundraṣṭu'mīśvaram \|*  
*bhaktyudrutamanāśśailaḥ praśaṃsan svavidhimmudā \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. With his mind melting with devotion and joyously praising his luck, the mountain personally went to see Śiva as dear as the very vital air.

## \|\| 4.42.4 \|\|

*devasenāṃ tadā dṛṣṭvā himavānvi smayaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*jagāma sammukhastatra dhanyo'hamiti cintayan \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. On seeing the army of the gods Himavat was struck with wonder. Considering himself blessed he appeared in front of them.

## \|\| 4.42.5 \|\|

*devā hi tadbalaṃ dṛṣṭvā vismayamparamaṃ gatāḥ \|*  
*ānandamparamamprāpurdevāśca girayastathā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The gods too were struck with wonder on seeing his army. The gods and the mountains became delighted.

## \|\| 4.42.6 \|\|

*parvatānāṃ mahāsenā devānāṃ ca tathā mune \|*  
*militvā virarājeva pūrvapaścimasāgarau \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The vast army of the mountains and the gods, O sage, on coming together shone like the eastern and western oceans in juxtaposition.

## \|\| 4.42.7 \|\|

*parasparaṃ militvā te devāśca parvatāstathā \|*  
*kṛtakṛtyantathātmānammenire parayā mudā \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Meeting each other, the gods and the mountains considered themselves blessed. They were greatly delighted.

## \|\| 4.42.8 \|\|

*atheśvarampuro dṛṣṭvā praṇanāma himālayaḥ \|*  
*sarve praṇemurgirayo brāhmaṇāśca sadāśivam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Seeing Śiva in front, Himavat bowed to Him. The mountains and the brahmins bowed to Sadāśiva.

## \|\| 4.42.9-14 \|\|

*vṛṣabhasthamprasannāsyannānābharaṇabhūṣitam \|*  
*divyāvayavalāvaṇyaprakāśitadigantaram \|\| 9 \|\|*

*susūkṣmāhatasatpaṭṭavastraśobhitavigraham \|*  
*sadratnavilasanmauliṃ vihasantaṃ śuciprabham \|\| 10 \|\|*

*bhūṣābhūtāhiyuktāṃgamadbhutāvayavaprabham \|*  
*divyadyutiṃ sureśaiśca sevitaṃ karacāmaraiḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*vāmasthitācyutandakṣabhāgasthitavibhumprabhum \|*  
*pṛṣṭhasthitahariṃ pṛṣṭhapārśvasthitasurādikam \|\| 12 \|\|*

*nānāvidhisurādyaiśca saṃstutaṃ lokaśaṃkaram \|*  
*svahetvāttatanumbrahmasarveśaṃ varadāyakam \|\| 13 \|\|*

*saguṇaṃ nirguṇaṃ cāpi bhaktādhīnaṃ kṛpākaram \|*  
*prakṛteḥ puruṣasyāpi paraṃ saccitsukhātmakam \|\| 14 \|\|*

9-14. He was seated on his bull, fully bedecked in ornaments and beaming in the face. The beauty of his divine person illuminated the quarters. His body shone in the delicate silken garments. His crown was lustrous with the gems set in it. He was smiling shedding pure brilliance everywhere. Serpents had transformed themselves into ornaments on his body. He had a wonderful lustre and a divine refulgence. Gods served him with chowries in their hands. Viṣṇu was standing to the left, Brahmā to the right, Indra at his back. Behind on either side, the gods were standing. He was being eulogised by the gods and others. He looked benevolent to the people. Being one He had assumed different physical bodies for his own reasons. He was Brahman itself, the lord of all and the bestower of boons. He was both with or without attributes, subservient to the devotees, merciful, greater than primordial Being and primordial nature, Existence, Knowledge and Bliss itself.

## \|\| 4.42.15 \|\|

*prabhordakṣiṇabhāge tu dadarśa harimacyutam \|*  
*vinatātanayārūḍhaṃ nānābhūṣaṇabhūṣitam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The mountain saw Viṣṇu, bedecked in ornaments and seated on Garuḍa to the right of lord Śiva.

## \|\| 4.42.16 \|\|

*prabhośca vāmabhāge tu mune māṃ sandadarśa ha \|*  
*caturmukhaṃ mahāśobhaṃ svaparīvārasaṃyutam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. O sage, to the left of the lord stood I, the fourfaced deity, shining brilliantly and accompanied by my attendants.

## \|\| 4.42.17 \|\|

*etau sureśvarau dṛṣṭvā śivasyāti priyau sadā \|*  
*praṇanāma girīśaśca saparīvāra ādarāt \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. On seeing us both, great favourites of Śiva for ever, the lord of mountains with all his retinue respectfully bowed to us.

## \|\| 4.42.18 \|\|

*tathā śivasya pṛṣṭhe ca pārśvayostu virājitān \|*  
*devādīnpraṇanāmāsau dṛṣṭvā girivareśvaraḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Similarly, on seeing the gods and others brilliantly shining behind lord Śiva and at his sides, the lord of mountains bowed to them.

## \|\| 4.42.19 \|\|

*śivājñayā puro bhūtvā jagāma svapuraṃ giriḥ \|*  
*śeṣaharyātmabhūśśīghraṃ munibhiḥ nirjarādibhiḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. At the bidding of Śiva the mountain went ahead to his city. Behind him went Viṣṇu, Brahmā, the sages and the gods.

## \|\| 4.42.20 \|\|

*sarve munisurādyāśca gacchantaḥ prabhuṇā saha \|*  
*gireḥ puraṃ samuditāḥ śaśaṃsurbahu nārada \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. O Nārada, the sages, the gods and others accompanying the lord, praised the city of Himavat with great delight.

## \|\| 4.42.21 \|\|

*racite śikhare ramye saṃsthāpya devatādikam \|*  
*jagāma himavāṃstatra yatrāsti vidhivedikā \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Stationing the gods and others on his beautiful summit specially arranged for them, Himavat went to the place where the altar for the rites had been erected.

## \|\| 4.42.22 \|\|

*kārayitvā viśeṣeṇa catuṣkanto raṇairyutam \|*  
*snānadānādikaṃ kṛtvā parīkṣāmakarottadā \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. After causing squares and quadrangles to be made with festoons, he performed the ceremonial ablutions, gave charitable gifts and supervised everything.

## \|\| 4.42.23 \|\|

*svaputrānpreṣayāmāsa śivasya nikaṭe tathā \|*  
*himo viṣṇvādisampūrṇavargayuktasya śailarāṭ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Then he sent his sons to Śiva accompanied by all his attendants and followers, Viṣṇu and others.

## \|\| 4.42.24 \|\|

*kartumecchadvarācāraṃ mahotsavapurassaram \|*  
*mahāharṣayutassarvabandhuyugghimaśailarāṭ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. The extremely delighted lord of mountains in the company of his kinsmen desired to perform the reception to the bridegroom with great pomp and ceremony.

## \|\| 4.42.25 \|\|

*atha te giripu trāśca tatra gatvā praṇamya tam \|*  
*sasvavargaṃ prārthanāntāmūcuśśaileśvarasya vai \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The sons of the mountain accompanied by their relatives went to Śiva and acquainted him with the request of the mountain.

## \|\| 4.42.26 \|\|

*tataste svālayaṃ jagmuśśailaputrāstadājñayā \|*  
*śailarājāya saṃcakhyuste cāyāntīti harṣitāḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The sons of the mountain came back to their abode with his permission and informed the king of mountains gladly that the bridegroom and the party were on their way there.

## \|\| 4.42.27 \|\|

*atha devāḥ prārthanāntāṃ gireḥ śrutvātiharṣitāḥ \|*  
*mune viṣṇvādayassarve seśvarā mumudurbhṛśam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. O sage, on hearing the request thus made, Viṣṇu and other gods with the lord rejoiced much.

## \|\| 4.42.28 \|\|

*kṛtvā suveṣaṃ sarvepi nirjarā munayo gaṇāḥ \|*  
*gamanaṃ cakruranyepi prabhuṇā girirāḍgṛham \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Dressed richly and exquisitely the gods, the gaṇas, the sages and others started towards the abode of lord Himavat.

## \|\| 4.42.29 \|\|

*tasminnavasare menā draṣṭukāmābhavacchivam \|*  
*prabhorāhvāyayāmāsa mune tvāṃ munisattamam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. In the meantime, Menā desired to see Śiva. O sage, through her lord, you, the excellent sage, were requisitioned there.

## \|\| 4.42.30 \|\|

*agamastvaṃ mune tatra prabhuṇā preritastadā \|*  
*manasā śivahṛddhetuṃ pūrṇaṃ kartuṃ tamicchatā \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. O sage, urged by the lord who desired to fulfil the task of Śiva you went there.

## \|\| 4.42.31 \|\|

*tvāmpraṇamya mune menā prāha vismitamānasā \|*  
*draṣṭukāmā prabho rūpaṃ śaṃkarasya madāpaham \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. O sage, after bowing to you, Menā with her heart full of surprise told you that she wanted to see the real form of lord Śiva that dispels haughtiness.

## Chapter 43 - Description of Śiva’s wonderful sport

## \|\| 4.43.1 \|\|

*menovāca \|*  
*nirīkṣiṣyāmi prathamaṃ mune taṃ girijāpatim \|*  
*kīdṛśaṃ śivarūpaṃ hi yadarthe tapa uttamam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Menā said:—

1\. O sage, I shall first see the bridegroom of Pārvatī. Let me have an idea of the form and features of Śiva for which she performed the great penance.

## \|\| 4.43.2 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityajñānaparā sā ca darśanārthaṃ śivasya ca \|*  
*tvayā mune samaṃ sadyaścandraśālāṃ samāgatā \|\| 2 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

2\. Thus, urged by ignorance, O sage, she went to the terrace along with you to see Śiva.

## \|\| 4.43.3 \|\|

*śivo'pi ca tadā tasyāṃ jñātvāhaṃkāramātmanaḥ \|*  
*prāha viṣṇuṃ ca māntāta līlākṛtvādbhutāmprabhuḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Then Śiva, realising her false pride in herself, spoke to Viṣṇu and me as a part of His wonderful sport.

## \|\| 4.43.4 \|\|

*śiva uvāca \|*  
*madājñayā yuvāntātau sadevau ca pṛthakpṛthak \|*  
*gacchataṃ hi giridvāraṃ vayaṃ paścādvrajemahi \|\| 4 \|\|*

Śiva said:—

4\. “At my bidding, O dear ones, both of you go one by one accompanied by the gods to the threshold of the mountain. I shall follow afterwards.”

## \|\| 4.43.5 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya harissarvānāhūyovāca tanmayāḥ \|*  
*surāssarve tathaivāśu gamanaṃ cakrurutsukāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

5\. On hearing it Viṣṇu called all and told them of his suggestion. The gods then walked in accordance with that suggestion enthusiastically.

## \|\| 4.43.6 \|\|

*sthitāṃ śirogṛhe menāṃ mune viśveśvara tvayā \|*  
*tathaiva darśayāmāsa hṛdvibhraṃśo yathā bhavet \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. O sage, the lord of the universe, let Menā stand on the terrace and see the procession along with you in order to make her mind confused.

## \|\| 4.43.7 \|\|

*etasminsamaye menā senāṃ ca paramāṃ śubhām \|*  
*nirīkṣantī mune dṛṣṭvā sāmānyaṃ harṣitā'bhavat \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. In the meantime, seeing the splendid vast army, O sage, Menā became delighted as usual.

## \|\| 4.43.8 \|\|

*prathamaṃ caiva gandharvāssundarāssubhagāstadā \|*  
*āyātāśśubhavastrāḍhyā nānālaṃkārabhūṣitāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. At the head of procession came the beautiful fastidious Gandharvas, dressed in rich clothes and bedecked in fine ornaments.

## \|\| 4.43.9 \|\|

*nānāvāhanasaṃyuktā nānāvādyaparā yaṇā \|*  
*patākābhirvicitrābhirapsarogaṇasaṃyutāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. They rode on different vehicles. They played on musical instruments. Flags and banners of various colours and sizes fluttered on their chariots. The heavenly nymphs accompanied them.

## \|\| 4.43.10 \|\|

*atha dṛṣṭvā vasuṃ tatra tatpatiṃ paramaprabhum \|*  
*menā praharṣitā hyāsīcchivoyamiti cābravīt \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. On seeing Vasu, the lord of Vasus, along with Vasus, Menā became delighted and exclaimed—“O this is Śiva”.

## \|\| 4.43.11 \|\|

*śivasya gaṇakā ete na śivoyaṃ śivāpatiḥ \|*  
*ityevaṃ tvaṃ tatastāṃ vai avoca ṛṣisattama \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. O excellent sage, you told her “These are only the attendants of Śiva. This is not Śiva, the bridegroom.”

## \|\| 4.43.12 \|\|

*evaṃ śrutvā tadā menā vicāre tatparā'bhavat \|*  
*itaścābhyadhiko yo vai sa ca kīdṛgbhaviṣyati \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. On hearing this, Menā fell athinking “A person greater than this! Hā, how will he be!”

## \|\| 4.43.13 \|\|

*etasminnantare yakṣā maṇigrīvādayaśca ye \|*  
*teṣāṃ senā tayā dṛṣṭā śobhādidviguṇīkṛtā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. In the meantime she saw Maṇigrīva, the other Yakṣas and their vast army with twice the splendour of Vasus.

## \|\| 4.43.14 \|\|

*tatpatiṃ ca maṇigrīvaṃ dṛṣṭvā śobhānvitaṃ hi sā \|*  
*ayaṃ rudraśśivāsvāmī menā prāheti harṣitā \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. On seeing the lustrous Maṇigrīva the lord of Yakṣas, Menā was delighted and said—“This is Śiva, the bridegroom of Pārvatī.”

## \|\| 4.43.15 \|\|

*nāyaṃ rudraśśivāsvāmī sevakoyaṃ śivasya vai \|*  
*ityavocogapatnyai tvaṃ tāvadvahnissa āgataḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. “This is not Śiva, the bridegroom of Pārvatī. He is only an attendant of Śiva” said you to Menā, the wife of the mountain. By that time the god of fire passed by.

## \|\| 4.43.16 \|\|

*tato'pi dviguṇāṃ śobhāṃ dṛṣṭvā tasya ca sābravīt \|*  
*rudro'yaṃ girijāsvāmī tadā neti tvamabravīḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. On seeing his splendour twice that of Yakṣas, she said “This is Śiva, the bridegroom of Pārvatī” but you said “No”.

## \|\| 4.43.17 \|\|

*tāvadyamassamāyātastato'pi dviguṇaprabhaḥ \|*  
*taṃ dṛṣṭvā prāha sā menā rudro'yamiti harṣitā \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. By that time Yama passed by with twice the splendour of the previous one. On seeing him delighted Menā exclaimed “This is Śiva”.

## \|\| 4.43.18 \|\|

*neti tvamabravīstāṃ vai tāvannirṛtirāgataḥ \|*  
*bibhrāṇo dviguṇāṃ śobhāṃ śubhaḥ puṇyajanaprabhuḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. “No” said you. By that time Nirṛti, the lord of Puṇyajanas, passed by having twice the splendour of Yama.

## \|\| 4.43.19 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā prāha sā menā rudro'yamiti harṣitā \|*  
*neti tvamabravīstāṃ vai tāvadvaruṇa āgataḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. On seeing him the delighted Menā said “This is Śiva”. “No” said you to her. By that time Varuṇa passed that way.

## \|\| 4.43.20 \|\|

*tato'pi dviguṇāṃ śobhāṃ dṛṣṭvā tasya ca sābravīt \|*  
*rudro'yaṃ girijāsvāmī tadvā neti tvamabravīḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. On seeing his splendour twice that of Nirṛti, she said “This is Śiva, the bridegroom of Pārvatī”. But you said “No”.

## \|\| 4.43.21 \|\|

*tāvadvāyussamāyātastato'pi dviguṇaprabhaḥ \|*  
*taṃ dṛṣṭvā prāha sā menā rudroyamiti harṣitā \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. By that time Vayu passed by with twice the splendour of Varuṇa. On seeing him the delighted Menā said “This is Śiva”.

## \|\| 4.43.22 \|\|

*neti tvamabravīstāṃ vai tāvaddhanada āgataḥ \|*  
*tato'pi dviguṇāṃ śobhāṃ bibhrāṇo guhyakādhipaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. “No” said you. By that time Kubera, the lord of Guhyakas, passed by with twice the splendour of Vāyu.

## \|\| 4.43.23 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā prāha sā menā rudro'yamiti harṣitā \|*  
*neti tvamabravīstāṃ vai tāvadīśāna āgataḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. On seeing him the delighted Menā said “This is Śiva”. “No”, said you to her. By that time Īśāna passed by.

## \|\| 4.43.24 \|\|

*tato'pi dviguṇāṃ śobhāṃ dṛṣṭvā tasya ca sābravīt \|*  
*rudro'yaṃ girijāsvāmī tadā neti tvamabravīḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. On seeing his splendour twice that of Kubera, she said “This is Rudra, the bridegroom of Pārvatī”. But you said “No”.

## \|\| 4.43.25 \|\|

*tāvadindrassamāyātastato'pi dviguṇaprabhaḥ \|*  
*sarvāmaravaro nānādivyabhastridiveśvaraḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Then came Indra, the most important of all the gods, the lord of the three worlds, endowed with divine refulgence and who had twice the splendour of Isāna.

## \|\| 4.43.26 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā śaṃkarasso'yamiti sā prāha menakā \|*  
*śakrassurapatiścāyaṃ neti tvaṃ tadābravīḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. On seeing him Menakā said—“This is Śiva”. “Not he”, said you then “This is Indra, the lord of gods”.

## \|\| 4.43.27 \|\|

*tāvaccandrassamāyātaśśobhā taddviguṇā dadhata \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā taṃ prāha rudro'yaṃ tāṃ tu neti tvamabravīḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. By that time the moon passed by with twice the splendour of Indra. On seeing him she said “This is Siva” and you denied it.

## \|\| 4.43.28 \|\|

*tāvatsūryassamāyātaśśobhā taddviguṇā dadhat \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā taṃ prāha sā soyantāṃtu neti tvamabravīḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. By that time the Sun passed by with twice the splendour of the moon. On seeing him she said “It is he”. You said to her “No”.

## \|\| 4.43.29 \|\|

*tāvatsamāgatāstatra bhṛgvādyāśca munīśvarāḥ \|*  
*tejaso rāśayassarve svaśiṣyagaṇasaṃyutāḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. By that time Bhṛgu and other sages, all highly lustrous and accompanied by their disciples, passed by.

## \|\| 4.43.30 \|\|

*tanmadhye caiva vāgīśaṃ dṛṣṭvā sā prāha menakā \|*  
*rudro'yaṃ girijāsvāmī tadā neti tvamabravīḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. On seeing Bṛhaspati in their midst Menakā said:—“This is Śiva the master of Pārvatī”. Then you said “No”.

## \|\| 4.43.31 \|\|

*tāvadbrahmā samāyātastejasāṃ gaśiruttamaḥ \|*  
*sarṣivaryyasutassākṣāddharmapuṃja iva stutaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. By that time Brahmā passed by. He was in an excellent from of lustre, praised by excellent sages and looking like an embodied Dharma itself.

## \|\| 4.43.32 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā sā taṃ tadā menā mahāharṣavatī mune \|*  
*so'yaṃ śivāpatiḥ prāha tāṃ tu neti tvamabravīḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. O sage, seeing me the highly delighted Menā said—“This is Pārvatī’s husband”. You said to her “No”.

## \|\| 4.43.33-35 \|\|

*etasminnantare tatra viṣṇurdevassamāgataḥ \|*  
*sarvaśobhānvitaḥ śrīmānmeghaśyāmaścaturbhujaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*koṭikandarpyalāvaṇyaḥ pītāmbaradharassvarāṭ \|*  
*rājīvalocanaśśāntaḥ pakṣīndravaravāhanaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*śaṃkhādilakṣaṇairyukto mukuṭādivibhūṣitaḥ \|*  
*śrīvatsavakṣā lakṣmīśo hyaprameya prabhānvitaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

33-35. In the meantime lord Viṣṇu came that way. He looked glorious and splendid, dark-blue like the fresh cloud and having four arms. He had the handsome features of numberless cupids. He wore yellow garments. He was the king of heaven with eyes resembling the petals of a lotus, and looked very calm. He had Garuḍa as his vehicle. He possessed all the characteristic signs conch etc. He was bedecked in crown and other ornaments. He wore Śrīvatsa on his chest. He had an uncommon splendour that was incomprehensible

## \|\| 4.43.36 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā cakitākṣyāsīnmahāharṣeṇa sābravīt \|*  
*so'yaṃ śivāpatiḥ sākṣācchivo vai nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. On seeing him Menā’s eyes became dazed. With great delight she said—“This is Śiva himself the bridegroom of Pārvatī. There is no doubt about it”.

## \|\| 4.43.37-39 \|\|

*atha tvaṃ menakāvākyamākarṇyovāca ūtikṛt \|*  
*nāyaṃ śivāpatirayaṃ kintvayaṃ keśavo hariḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*śaṃkarokhilakāryyasya hyadhikārī ca tatpriyaḥ \|*  
*ato'dhiko varo jñeyassa śivaḥ pārvatīpatiḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*tacchobhāṃ varṇituṃ mene mayā naiva hi śakyate \|*  
*sa evākhilabrahmāṇḍapatissarveśvaraḥ svarāṭ \|\| 39 \|\|*

37-39. On hearing Menakā’s words you said—“No, this is not the lord, the cause of protection and enjoyment. This is not the bridegroom of Pārvatī. This is Viṣṇu, the officer-in-charge of the marriage-party of Śiva and a great favourite of Śiva. The bridegroom Śiva is better than him. O Menā, it is impossible for me to describe his beauty. He is the lord of the entire universe, the lord of all, the Self-Emperor”.

## \|\| 4.43.40 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya vacastasya menā mene ca tāṃ śubhām \|*  
*mahādhanāṃ bhāgyavatī kulatrayasukhāvahām \|\| 40 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

40\. On hearing your words, Menā thought her daughter auspicious, rich, fortunate and harbinger of happiness for the three families.

## \|\| 4.43.41 \|\|

*uvāca ca prasannāsyā prītiyuktena cetasā \|*  
*svabhāgyamadhikaṃ cāpi varṇayantī muhurmuhuḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Her face was beaming with pleasure and her heart was delighted. Frequently congratulating herself on her good luck she said:—

## \|\| 4.43.42 \|\|

*menovāca \|*  
*dhanyāhaṃ sarvathā jātā pārvatyā janmanādhunā \|*  
*dhanyo girīśvaropyadya sarvaṃ dhanyatamaṃ mama \|\| 42 \|\|*

Menā said:—

42\. By the birth of Pārvatī, I have become blessed in every respect. The lord of mountains too is blessed. Every thing connected with me is blessed.

## \|\| 4.43.43 \|\|

*yeye dṛṣṭvā mayā devā nāyakāssuprabhānvitāḥ \|*  
*eteṣāṃ yaḥ patisso'tra patirasyā bhaviṣyati \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Her would-be-husband is the lord of these leaders of great lustre whom I have seen now.

## \|\| 4.43.44 \|\|

*asyāḥ kiṃ varṇyate bhāgyamapi varṣaśatairapi \|*  
*varṇituṃ śakyate naiva tatprabhuprāptidarśanāta \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. How can I describe her good luck even in hundred years? It is impossible to describe it when I see the lustre of these leaders.

## \|\| 4.43.45 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityavādīcca sā menā premanirbharamānasā \|*  
*tāvatsamāgato rudro'dbhutotikārakaḥ prabhuḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

45\. Thus spoke Menā with her mind full of love and hope. By that time Śiva, the wonderful source of enjoyment and protection, came that way.

## \|\| 4.43.46 \|\|

*adbhutātmāgaṇāstāta menāgarvāpahārakāḥ \|*  
*ātmānaṃ darśayan māyānirliptaṃ nirvikārakam \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. He showed himself in his real form free from change of illusion. O dear, the Gaṇas of wonderful forms proved to be the dispeller of Menā’s pride.

## \|\| 4.43.47 \|\|

*tamāgatamabhipretya nārada tvaṃ mune tadā \|*  
*menāmavocaḥ suprītyā darśayaṃstaṃ śivāpatim \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. O sage Nārada, on seeing Him come, you lovingly pointed him out to her as the bridegroom of Śiva and spoke to her.

## \|\| 4.43.48 \|\|

*\|\| nārada uvāca \|*  
*ayaṃ sa śaṃkarassākṣāddṛśyatāṃ sundari tvayā \|*  
*yadarthe śivayā taptaṃ tapo'ti vipine mahat \|\| 48 \|\|*

Nārada said:—

48\. This is Śiva Himself, O comely maiden, see. It was for him that Pārvatī performed a great penance in the forest.

## \|\| 4.43.49 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*ityuktvā harṣitā menā taṃ dadarśa mudā prabhum \|*  
*adbhutākṛtimīśānamadbhutānugamadbhutam \|\| 49 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

49\. Thus addressed by you the delighted Menā stared at the lord with joy; the lord Īśāna of wonderful features and of wonderful attendants.

## \|\| 4.43.50 \|\|

*tāvadeva samāyātā rudrasenā mahādbhutā \|*  
*bhūtapretādisaṃyuktā nānāgaṇasamanvitā \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Immediately the army of Śiva came there consisting of wonderful arrays of Bhūtas, Pretas and Gaṇas.

## \|\| 4.43.51 \|\|

*vātyārūpadharāḥ kecitpatākāmarmarasvanā \|*  
*vakratuṃḍāstatra kecidvirūpāścāpare tathā \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Some were in the form of violent gusts of wind, producing hissing sounds with waving flags. Some had crooked faces. Others were deformed.

## \|\| 4.43.52 \|\|

*karālāḥ śmaśrulāḥ kecitkecitkhañjā hyalocanāḥ \|*  
*daṇḍapāśadharāḥ kecitkecinmudgarapāṇayaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Some were awful with overgrown moustaches and beards. Some were lame. Some were blind. Some held staffs and nooses and some great iron clubs in their hands.

## \|\| 4.43.53 \|\|

*viruddhavāhanāḥ kecicchṛṃganādavivādinaḥ \|*  
*ḍamarorvādinaḥ kecitkecidgomukhavādinaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Some rode on peculiar vehicles. Some played on horns. Some played on Ḍamarus. Some played on Gomukhas.

## \|\| 4.43.54 \|\|

*amukhā vimukhāḥ kecitkecidbahumukhā gaṇāḥ \|*  
*akarā vikarāḥ kecitkecidbahukarā gaṇāḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Some had no faces. Some had distorted and deformed faces. Some had many faces. Some had no hands. Others had deformed hands. Some of them had many hands.

## \|\| 4.43.55 \|\|

*anetrā bahunetrāśca viśirāḥ kuśirāstathā \|*  
*akarṇā bahukarṇāśca nānāveṣadharā gaṇāḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Some had no eyes. Some had many eyes. Some had no head. Some had deformed heads. Some had no ears. Some had many ears. The Gaṇas had all types of dresses and features.

## \|\| 4.43.56 \|\|

*ityādivikṛtākārā aneke prabalā gaṇāḥ \|*  
*asaṃkhyātāstathā tāta mahāvīrā bhayaṃkarāḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Such and other innumerable deformed Gaṇas, heroic and terrible, strong and strenuous passed by, O dear.

## \|\| 4.43.57 \|\|

*aṃgulyā darśayaṃstvaṃ tāṃ mune rudragaṇāṃstataḥ \|*  
*harasya sevakānpaśya haraṃ cāpi varānane \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. O sage, you pointed out the Gaṇas of Śiva to her with your finger and said—“O lovely lady, see the attendants of Śiva and Śiva Himself.”

## \|\| 4.43.58 \|\|

*asaṃkhyātān gaṇān dṛṣṭvā bhūtapretādikān mune \|*  
*tatkṣaṇādabhavatsā vai menakā trāsasaṃkulā \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. O sage, on seeing the innumerable Gaṇas, Bhūtas and Pretas, Menakā was terribly frightened instantaneously.

## \|\| 4.43.59-61 \|\|

*tanmadhye śaṃkaraṃ caiva nirguṇaṃ guṇavattaram \|*  
*vṛṣabhasthaṃ pañcavaktraṃ trinetraṃ bhūtibhūṣitam \|\| 59 \|\|*

*kapardinaṃ candramauliṃ daśahastaṃ kapāli nam \|*  
*vyāghracarmottarīyañca pinākavarapāṇinam \|\| 60 \|\|*

*śūlayuktaṃ virūpākṣaṃ vikṛtākāramākulam \|*  
*gajacarma vasānaṃ hi vīkṣya trese śivāprasūḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

59-61. On seeing Śiva in their midst, the mother of Pārvatī trembled. She saw Śiva who though devoid of attributes was better than those who had all the attributes, He was seated on the Bull. He had five faces and three eyes. He had ashes smeared over the body. He had matted hair with the crescent moon on His head. He had ten hands with the skull in one of them. His upper cloth was tiger’s hide. He held the bow Pināka in one of his hands and the Trident in another. He had odd eyes, ugly features utterly dishevelled and untidy. He wore the hide of an elephant.

## \|\| 4.43.62 \|\|

*cakitāṃ kampasaṃyuktāṃ vihvalāṃ vibhramaddhiyam \|*  
*śivo'yamiti cāṃgulyā darśayaṃstāṃ tvamabravīḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. She was stunned, tremulous agitated and confused. You said to her “This is Śiva” and pointed Him out to her.

## \|\| 4.43.63 \|\|

*tvadīyaṃ tadvacaḥ śrutvā vātāhatalatā iva \|*  
*sā papāta drutambhūmau menā duḥkhabharā satī \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. On hearing your words she fell on the ground like a tender creeper blown by the wind. Menā the chaste lady was grief-stricken.

## \|\| 4.43.64 \|\|

*kimidaṃ vikṛtaṃ dṛṣṭvā vañcitāhaṃ durāgrahe \|*  
*ityuktvā mūrcchitā tatra menakā sā'bhavatkṣaṇāt \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. “What is this? I have been deceived for being too ambitious. Of what use is it to see this deformity?” Saying this, Menakā fell unconscious there in a trice.

## \|\| 4.43.65 \|\|

*atha prayatnairvividhaissakhībhirupasevitā \|*  
*lebhe saṃjñāṃ śanai menā girīśvarapriyā tadā \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Her maids exerted themselves in various ways and attended on her. Then gradually she, the beloved of the lord of mountains, regained consciousness.

## Chapter 44 - Menā regains consciousness

## \|\| 4.44.1-2 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*saṃjñāṃ labdhā tatassā ca menā śailapriyā satī \|*  
*vilalāpātisaṃkṣubdhā tiraskāramathākarot \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tatra tāvatsvaputrāṃśca nininda khalitā muhuḥ \|*  
*prathamaṃ sā tataḥ putrī kathayāmāsa durvacaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

1-2. On regaining consciousness, the chaste beloved of the mountain lamented with great agitation and began to rebuke everyone. In faltering words she frequently censured her sons at first and then scolded her daughter.

## \|\| 4.44.3 \|\|

*\|\| menovāca \|*  
*mune purā tvayā proktaṃ variṣyati śivā śivam \|*  
*paścāddhimavataḥ kṛtyaṃ pūjārthaṃ viniveśitam \|\| 3 \|\|*

Menā said:—

3\. O sage, formerly it was mentioned be you that Pārvatī would marry Śiva. Afterwards you assigned some activity of worship to Himavat.

## \|\| 4.44.4 \|\|

*tato dṛṣṭaṃ phalaṃ satyaṃ viparītamanarthakam \|*  
*mune'dhamāhaṃ durbuddhe sarvathā vañcitā tvayā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Its fruit is visible now, to be sure. But it is adverse and meaningless. O sage, O wicked minded one, I the innocent woman have been cheated by you by all means.

## \|\| 4.44.5 \|\|

*punastayā tapastaptaṃ duṣkaraṃ munibhiśca yat \|*  
*tasya labdhaṃ phalaṃ hyetatpaśyatāṃ duḥkhadāyakam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The fruit of penance which she performed and which is very difficult even for the sages to perform, has been this, painful to every onlooker.

## \|\| 4.44.6 \|\|

*kiṃ karomi kva gacchāmi ko me duḥkhaṃ vyapohatām \|*  
*kulādikaṃ vinaṣṭaṃ me vihitaṃ jīvitaṃ mama \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. What shall I do? Where shall I go? Who will dispel my sorrow? My family is wrecked. My life is doomed.

## \|\| 4.44.7 \|\|

*kva gatā ṛṣayo divyāḥ śmaśrūṇi troṭayāmyaham \|*  
*tapasvinī ca yā patnī sā dhūrtā svayamāgatā \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Where are those so called celestial sages? I shall pluck out their beards. Where is that mischievous woman who came here by herself in the guise of the wire of one of them?

## \|\| 4.44.8 \|\|

*keṣāñcaivāparādhena sarvaṃ naṣṭaṃ mamādhunā \|*  
*ityuktvā vīkṣya ca sutāmuvāca vacanaṃ kaṭu \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. By whose guilt have I been ruined now?” Saying this she turned to her daughter and began to say harsh words.

## \|\| 4.44.9 \|\|

*kiṃ kṛtaṃ te sute duṣṭe karma duḥkhakaraṃ mama \|*  
*hema dattvā tvayānītaḥ kāco vai duṣṭayā svayam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. O wretched daughter, what is it that you have done? This is extremely painful to me. You have given gold and brought a glass piece, O wicked girl.

## \|\| 4.44.10 \|\|

*hitvā tu candanaṃ bhūyo lepitaḥ kardamastvayā \|*  
*haṃsamuḍḍīya kāko vai gṛhīto hastapañjare \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. You have cast away sandal paste and smeared yourself with mud. You have driven away the swan and have held a crow in your hands.

## \|\| 4.44.11 \|\|

*hitvā brahmajalaṃ dūre pītaṃ kūpodakaṃ tvayā \|*  
*sūryaṃ hitvā tu khadyoto gṛhīto yatnatastvayā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Setting aside the sacred river water you have drunk the well-water. Losing the sun you have clung to the glowworm in all earnestness.

## \|\| 4.44.12 \|\|

*taṇḍulāṃśca tathā hitvā kṛtaṃ vai tuṣabhakṣaṇam \|*  
*prakṣipyājyaṃ tathā tailaṃ kāraṇḍaṃ bhuktamādarāt \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Throwing away cooked rice you have eaten the husk. Spilling away the clarified butter you have eagerly swallowed castor oil.

## \|\| 4.44.13 \|\|

*siṃhasevāṃ tathā muktvā śṛgālassevitastvayā \|*  
*brahmavidyāṃ tathā muktvā kugāthā ca śrutā tvayā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Setting the lion aside a jackal has been served by you. Without listening to the lore of Supreme Brahman you have heard base ballads.

## \|\| 4.44.14 \|\|

*gṛhe yajñavibhūtiṃ hi dūrīkṛtya sumaṃgalām \|*  
*gṛhītaśca citābhasma tvayā putri hyamaṃgalam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. O daughter, casting off the holy sacrificial ashes at home you have taken the inauspicious ashes from the funeral pyre.

## \|\| 4.44.15 \|\|

*sarvān devavarāṃstyaktvā viṣṇvādīnparameśvarān \|*  
*kṛtaṃ tvayā kubuddhyā vai śivārthaṃ tapa īdṛśam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Abandoning the great lords, Viṣṇu and others you have performed penance for Śiva. Your intellect has really gone astray.

## \|\| 4.44.16 \|\|

*dhiktvā ca tava buddhiśca dhigrūpaṃ caritaṃ tava \|*  
*dhik copadeśakarttāraṃ dhiksakhyāvapi te tathā \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Fie on you. Fie on your intellect. Fie on your beauty and conduct. Fie on your adviser. Fie on your maids too.

## \|\| 4.44.17 \|\|

*āvāṃ ca dhiktathā putrī yau te janmapravartakau \|*  
*dhikte nārada buddhiñca saptarṣīṃśca subuddhidān \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Fie on us who brought you thus to the world, O daughter. O Nārada, fie on your intelligence and fie on those seven sages who gave us wrong advice.

## \|\| 4.44.18 \|\|

*dhikkulaṃ dhikkriyādākṣyaṃ sarvaṃ dhigyatkṛtaṃ tvayā \|*  
*gṛhantu dhukṣitaṃ tvetanmaraṇaṃ tu mamaiva hi \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Fie on the whole family. Fie on the efficiency in performing the rites. Fie on everything done by you. You have inflamed this household. Almost it has been a death blow to me.

## \|\| 4.44.19 \|\|

*pārvatānāmayaṃ rājā nāyātu nikaṭe mama \|*  
*saptarṣayassvayaṃ naiva darśayantu mukhammama \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Let not the king of the mountains come near me. Let not the seven sages show their faces to me.

## \|\| 4.44.20 \|\|

*sādhitaṃ kiñca sarvaistu militvā ghātitaṃ kulam \|*  
*vandhyāhaṃ na kathaṃ jātā garbho na galitaḥ katham \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Has anything been achieved? Our whole race is wrecked by all conspiring together. How is it that I have not remained a barren woman? How is it that a miscarriage did not take place when I conceived?

## \|\| 4.44.21 \|\|

*atho na vā mṛtā cāhaṃ putrikā na mṛtā katham \|*  
*rakṣasādya kathaṃ no vā bhakṣitā gagane punaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. How is it that I did not die? How is it that this girl did not die? Why is she not devoured by the demons and others from the sky?

## \|\| 4.44.22 \|\|

*chedayāmi śiraste'dya kiṃ karomi kalevaraiḥ \|*  
*tyaktvā tvāṃ ca kuto yāyāṃ hāhā me jīvitaṃ hatam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. I shall cut off your head. What shall I do with the bodies? Abandoning you where shall I go? Alas, my whole life is doomed,

## \|\| 4.44.23 \|\|

*\|\|brahmovāca \|*  
*ityuktvā patitā sā ca menā bhūmau vimūrchitā \|*  
*vyākulā śokaroṣādyairna gatā bhartṛsannidhau \|\| 23 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

23\. After saying this Menā fell unconscious on the ground. Agitated by grief and anger she did not go near her husband.

## \|\| 4.44.24 \|\|

*hāhākāro mahānāsītta sminkāle munīśvara \|*  
*sarve samāgatāstatra kramāttatsannidhau surāḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. There was a great hue and cry at that time, O great sage. The gods came near her.

## \|\| 4.44.25 \|\|

*purā devamune cāhamāgatastu svayaṃ tadā \|*  
*māṃ dṛṣṭvā tvaṃ vacastā vai prāvoca ṛṣisattama \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. O celestial sage, I too came myself. On seeing me, O excellent sage, you spoke to her.

## \|\| 4.44.26 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*yathārthaṃ suṃdaraṃ rūpaṃ nā jñātaṃ te śivasya vai \|*  
*līlayedaṃ dhṛtaṃ rūpaṃ na yathārthaṃ śivena ca \|\| 26 \|\|*

Nārada said:—

26\. The real handsome form of Śiva is not known by you. This form is assumed by Śiva in a sportive mood. It is not the real form.

## \|\| 4.44.27 \|\|

*tasmātkrodhaṃ parityajya svasthā bhava pativrate \|*  
*kāryyaṃ kuru haṭhaṃ tyaktvā śivāṃ dehi śivāya ca \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Hence, O chaste lady, cast off anger. Be calm. Leave off your obduracy. Do what is proper to be done. Give Pārvatī to Śiva.

## \|\| 4.44.28 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*tadākarṇya vacaste sā menā tvāṃ vākyamabravīt \|*  
*uttiṣṭheto gaccha dūraṃ duṣṭādhamavaro bhavān \|\| 28 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

28\. On hearing your words, Menā spoke to you—“O wicked one, get up and go away. You are base”.

## \|\| 4.44.29 \|\|

*ityukte tu tayā deva indrādyāḥ sakalāḥ kramāt \|*  
*samāgatya ca dikpālā vacanaṃ cedamabruvan \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. When she said thus, Indra and all other gods and the guardians of the quarters came and spoke.

## \|\| 4.44.30 \|\|

*\|\| devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*he mene pitṛkanye hi śṛṇvasmadvacanammudā \|*  
*ayaṃ vai paramaḥ sākṣācchivaḥ parasukhāvahaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

The gods said:—

30\. O Menā, O daughter of the Pitṛs, listen to our words joyously. This Śiva is the Supreme lord Himself, the bestower of the greatest happiness.

## \|\| 4.44.31 \|\|

*kṛpayā ca bhavatputryāstapo dṛṣṭvātidussaham \|*  
*darśanaṃ dattavāñchambhurvaraṃ sadbhaktavatsalaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. He is favourably disposed to good devotees. On seeing your daughter’s severe penance He had appeared before her and granted her the boon.

## \|\| 4.44.32 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*athovāca surānmenā vilapyāti muhurmuhuḥ \|*  
*na deyā tu mayā kanyā giriśāyograrūpiṇe \|\| 32 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

32\. Menā cried aloud frequently and spoke to the gods—“My daughter will not be given to Śiva of fierce features.

## \|\| 4.44.33 \|\|

*kimarthantu bhavantaśca sarve devāḥ prapañcitāḥ \|*  
*rūpamasyāḥ parannāma vyarthīkartuṃ samudyataḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Why have you all conspired together to render her beauty futile?”

## \|\| 4.44.34 \|\|

*ityukte ca tayā tatra ṛṣayassapta eva hi \|*  
*ūcuste vaca āgatya vasiṣṭhādyā munīśvara \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. O excellent sages, when she uttered thus, the seven sages, Vasiṣṭha and others, came there and spoke:—

## \|\| 4.44.35 \|\|

*saptarṣayaḥ ūcuḥ \|*  
*kāryyaṃ sādhayitumprāptāḥ pitṛkanye giripriye \|*  
*viruddhaṃ cātra uktārthe kathammanyāmahe vayam \|\| 35 \|\|*

The seven sages said:—

35\. “O daughter of the Pitṛs, O beloved of the mountain, we have come here to achieve a purpose. In this important affair how can we entertain opposite views?

## \|\| 4.44.36 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ayaṃ vai paramo lābho darśanaṃ śaṃkarasya yat \|*  
*dānapātraṃ sa te bhūtvāgatastava ca maṃdiram \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. The very vision of Śiva is the greatest gain. He has come to your palace as the suppliant for your gift”.

## \|\| 4.44.37 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*ityuktvā taistato menā munivākyaṃ mṛṣākarot \|*  
*pratyuvāca ca ruṣṭā sā tānṛṣīñjñānadurbalā \|\| 37 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

37\. Though advised by them, Mena did not accept their proposal. Weak in knowledge she spoke to the sages in anger.

## \|\| 4.44.38 \|\|

*menovāca \|*  
*śastrādyairghātayiṣyehaṃ na hāsye śaṃkarāyatām \|*  
*dūraṃ gacchata sarve hi nāgantavyaṃ madantike \|\| 38 \|\|*

Menā said:—

38\. I would rather slay her with weapons than give her to Śiva. All of you go away. You shall never come near me.

## \|\| 4.44.39 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityuktvā virarāmāśu sā vilapyātivihvalā \|*  
*hāhākāro mahānāsīttatra tadvṛttato mune \|\| 39 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

39\. O sage, on saying thus she stopped. She cried aloud in great excitement. A great hue and cry ensued due to her intercession.

## \|\| 4.44.40 \|\|

*tato himālayastatrājagāmātisamākulaḥ \|*  
*tāñca bodhayituṃ prītyā prāha tattvañca darśayan \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Then Himācala himself came there extremely agitated. In order to convince her he spoke lovingly pointing to her the reality of the situation.

## \|\| 4.44.41 \|\|

*himālaya uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu mene vaco me'dya vikalā'si kathampriye \|*  
*ke ke samāgatā gehaṃ kathaṃ caitānvinindasi \|\| 41 \|\|*

Himācala said:—

41\. O beloved Menā, listen to my words. How is it that you have become dispirited? How many important persons have come to our abode! And you are insulting them!

## \|\| 4.44.42 \|\|

*śaṃkaraṃ tvaṃ ca jānāsi rūpaṃ dṛṣṭvāsi vihvalā \|*  
*vikaṭaṃ tasya śaṃbhostu nānārūpābhidhasya hi \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. You do not know Śiva. Śiva has many names and many forms. Seeing a peculiar distorted form you have become excited.

## \|\| 4.44.43 \|\|

*sa śaṃkaro mayā jñātassarveṣāṃ pratipālakaḥ \|*  
*pūjyānāṃ pūjya evāsau kartānugrahanigrahān \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. He has been realised by me. He is the protector of everyone. He is worthy of worship of the most adorable. He can bless and countermand.

## \|\| 4.44.44 \|\|

*haṭhaṃ na kuru muñca tvaṃ duḥkhaṃ prāṇapriye'naghe \|*  
*uttiṣṭhāraṃ tathā kāryaṃ kartumarhasi suvrate \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Do not be obstinate. O faultless beloved, do not be grief-stricken. Get up. Hasten. O virtuous one, carry on your duties.

## \|\| 4.44.45 \|\|

*yadvai dvāragataśśaṃbhuḥ purā vikaṭarūpadhṛk \|*  
*nānālīlāñca kṛtavāñcetayāmi ca tāmimām \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Let me remind you of a former incident when Śiva came to our place in a hideous form and exhibited his sports.

## \|\| 4.44.46 \|\|

*tanmāhātmyaṃ paraṃ dṛṣṭvā kanyāṃ dātuṃ tvayā mayā \|*  
*aṃgīkṛtaṃ tadā devi tatpramāṇaṃ kuru priye \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. But on seeing his greatness we both consented to give our daughter in marriage to him. O beloved, keep that promise.

## \|\| 4.44.47 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityuktvā so'drinātho hi virarāma tato mune \|*  
*tadākarṇya śivāmātā menovāca himālayam \|\| 47 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

47\. After saying thus, the lord of the mountains stopped, O sage. On hearing it Menā, the mother of Śivā, spoke to Himavat.

## \|\| 4.44.48-50 \|\|

*menovāca \|*  
*madvacaḥ śrūyatāṃ nātha tathā kartuṃ tvamarhasi \|*  
*gṛhītvā tanujāṃ caināṃ baddhvā kaṇṭhe tu pārvatīm \|\| 48 \|\|*

*adhaḥ pātaya niḥśaṃkaṃ dāsye tāṃ na harāya hi \|*  
*tathaināmathavā nātha gatvā vai sāgare sutām \|\| 49 \|\|*

*nimajjaya dayāṃ tyaktvā tato'drīśa sukhī bhava \|*  
*yadi dāsyasi putrī tvaṃ rudrāya vikaṭātmane \|*  
*tarhi tyakṣyāmyahaṃ svāminniścayena kalevaram \|\| 50 \|\|*

Menā said:—

48-50. “O lord, let my words be heard. You can carry out what I say. Take your daughter Pārvatī, tie her up and cast her down into a deep abysmal chasm. Or drown her in the deep sea and be happy. I am not going to give her to Śiva. If you give your daughter to him who is of hideous features, O lord, I shall certainly leave off this mortal frame.

## \|\| 4.44.51 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*ityukte ca tadā tatra vacane menayā haṭhān \|*  
*uvāca vacanaṃ ramyaṃ pārvatī svayamāgatā \|\| 51 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

51\. When these words were spoken by Menā in her obduracy, Pārvatī voluntarily spoke in a sweet voice.

## \|\| 4.44.52 \|\|

*pārvatyuvāca \|*  
*mātaste viparītā hi buddhirjātā'śubhāvahā \|*  
*dharmāvalambanāttvaṃ hi kathandharmaṃ jahāsi vai \|\| 52 \|\|*

Pārvatī said:—

52\. “O mother, your noble intellect has become perverted. Why do you foresake virtue, you who ought to depend on virtue alone?

## \|\| 4.44.53 \|\|

*ayaṃ rudro'parassākṣātsarvaprabhava īśvaraḥ \|*  
*śambhussurūpassukhadassarvaśrutiṣu varṇitaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. This Śiva has no one else greater than him. He is Śiva. the source of everything. He is beautiful, pleasing and eulogised in all the Vedas.

## \|\| 4.44.54 \|\|

*maheśaśśaṃkaraścāyaṃ sarvadevaprabhussvarāṭ \|*  
*nānārūpābhidho mātarharibrahmādisevitaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Śiva is the benefactor. He is the lord of gods. He is self-ruler. O mother, He is of many forms and names. He is served by Viṣṇu, Brahmā and others.

## \|\| 4.44.55 \|\|

*adhiṣṭhānaṃ ca sarveṣāṃ kartā hartā ca sa prabhuḥ \|*  
*nirvikārī trideveśo hyavināśī sanātanaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. He is the support of everything. He is the creator and annihilator. He is free from aberrations. He is the lord of the three deities. He is indestructible and eternal.

## \|\| 4.44.56 \|\|

*yadarthe devatāssarvā āyātā kiṃkarīkṛtāḥ \|*  
*dvāri te sotsavāścādya kimato'nyatparaṃ sukham \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. It is for him that all the gods, as attendants, have come here. They stand in a festive mood at your threshold. What more pleasure do you need?

## \|\| 4.44.57 \|\|

*uttiṣṭhātaḥ prayatnena jīvitaṃ saphalaṃ kuru \|*  
*dehi māṃ tvaṃ śivāyāsmai svāśramaṃ kuru sārthakam \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Hence get up. Endeavour to make your life fruitful. Give me to Śiva. Make my effort meaningful.

## \|\| 4.44.58 \|\|

*dehi māṃ parameśāya śaṃkarāya jananyaho \|*  
*svīkuru tvamimaṃ mātarvinayamme bravīmi te \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. O mother, give me to lord Śiva. O mother, agree to my humble entreaty. I request you.

## \|\| 4.44.59 \|\|

*cenna dāsyasi tasmai māṃ na vṛṇe'nyamahaṃ varam \|*  
*bhāgaṃ labhetkathaṃ saiṃhaṃ śṛgālaḥ paravaṃcakaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. If you do not give me to Śiva, I am not going to woo anyone else. How can a jackal, the cunning cheat, seize the share of the lion?

## \|\| 4.44.60 \|\|

*manasā vacasā mātaḥ karmaṇā ca harastvayam \|*  
*mayā vṛto vṛtaścaiva yadicchasi tathā kuru \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. O mother, Śiva has been wooed, yes, wooed by me mentally, verbally, and physically. You can do what you please.

## \|\| 4.44.61-62 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya śivāvākyaṃ menā śaileśvarapriyā \|*  
*suvilapya mahākruddhā gṛhītvā tatkalevaram \|\| 61 \|\|*

*muṣṭibhiḥ kūrparaiścaiva dantāndharṣayatī ca sā \|*  
*tāḍayāmāsa tāṃ putrīṃ vihvalātiruṣānvitā \|\| 62 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

61-62. On hearing these words of Pārvatī, Menā, the beloved of the lord of mountains lamented much. She became angry. She caught hold of Pārvatī and thrashed her with fists, elbows gnashing her teeth. She was greatly agitated and furious.

## \|\| 4.44.63 \|\|

*ye tatra ṛṣayastāta tvadādyāścāpare mune \|*  
*taddhastāttāmparicchidya nityurdūrataraṃ tataḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. O dear one, O sage, you and other sages who were there, separated her from the mother and took her far off.

## \|\| 4.44.64 \|\|

*tānvai tathā vidhāndṛṣṭvā bhartsayitvā punaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*uvāca śrāvayantī sā durvaco nikhilānpunaḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Menā then rebuked them again and again. She hurled harsh repulsive words at all of them.

## \|\| 4.44.65 \|\|

*menovāca \|*  
*kiṃ menā hi kariṣye'haṃ duṣṭāṃ grahavatīṃ śivām \|*  
*dāsyāmyasyai garantīvraṃ kūpe kṣepsyāmi vā dhruvam \|\| 65 \|\|*

Menā said:—

65\. See what I will do to Pārvatī of evil inclination. I will give her deadly poison or I will push her down in a deep well.

## \|\| 4.44.66 \|\|

*chetsyāmi kālīmathavā śastrāstrairbhūrikhaṇḍaśaḥ \|*  
*nimajjayiṣye vā sindhau svasutāmpārvatīṃ khalu \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Or I will cut her into many pieces with weapons and arrows. Or I will drown my daughter Pārvatī in the deep sea.

## \|\| 4.44.67 \|\|

*athavā svaśarīraṃ hi tyakṣyāmyāśvanyathā dhruvam \|*  
*na dāsye śambhave kanyāṃ durgāṃ vikaṭarūpiṇe \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Or I will certainly cast off my body. But I will never give my daughter to Śiva of hideous form.

## \|\| 4.44.68 \|\|

*varo'yaṃ kīdṛśo bhīmo'nayā labdhaśca duṣṭayā \|*  
*kāritaścopahāso me gireścāpi kulasya hi \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. What an awful bridegroom has been secured by this wicked girl? The mountain and I, nay the whole family, has been made a laughing stock.

## \|\| 4.44.69 \|\|

*na mātā na pitā bhrātā na bandhurgotrajo'pi hi \|*  
*no surūpaṃ na cāturyyaṃ na guhaṃ vāsya kiṃcana \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. He has neither a mother nor a father. He has no brother no kinsman. He has not even a fellow clansman. He has no beauty, no skill, not even a house of His own!

## \|\| 4.44.70 \|\|

*na vastraṃ nāpyalaṅkārāssahāyāḥ ke'pi tasya na \|*  
*vāhanaṃ na śubhaṃ hyasya na vayo na dhanantathā \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. He has no good dress, no ornaments, no assistant? His vehicle is not good. He is neither rich nor even in the prime of youth.

## \|\| 4.44.71 \|\|

*na pāvitryaṃ na vidyā ca kīdṛśaḥ kāya ārtidaḥ \|*  
*kiṃ vilokya mayā putrī deyāsmai syātsumaṃgalā \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. He has no tidiness about him. He is not learned. What a repulsive body he has! What has he, on seeing which I may be tempted to give my good daughter to him?”

## \|\| 4.44.72 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityādi suvilapyātha bahuśo menakā tadā \|*  
*rurodoccairmune sā hi duḥkhaśokapariplutā \|\| 72 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

72\. O sage she lamented thus and in many a similar manner she cried in the excess of her grief.

## \|\| 4.44.73 \|\|

*athāhandrutamāgatyākathayammenakāṃ ca tām \|*  
*śivatattvaṃ ca paramaṃ kujñānaharamuttamam \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. Then I came there quickly and narrated to her the principles of Śiva which ought to have dispelled her perverted knowledge.

## \|\| 4.44.74 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*śrotavyamprītito mene madīyaṃ vacanaṃ śubham \|*  
*yasya śravaṇataḥ prītyā kubuddhiste vinaśyati \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. “O Menā, you shall listen lovingly to my auspicious words whereby your evil inclination shall cease.

## \|\| 4.44.75 \|\|

*śaṅkaro jagataḥ kartā bhartā hartā tathaiva ca \|*  
*na tvaṃ jānāsi tadrūpaṃ kathanduḥkhaṃ samīhase \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. Śiva is the creator, sustainer and annihilator of the universe. You do not know His real form. Wherefore do you then seek sorrow?

## \|\| 4.44.76 \|\|

*anekarūpanāmā ca nānā līlākaraḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*sarvasvāmī svatantraśca māyādhīśo'vikalpakaḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. The lord has several forms and names. He indulges in many kinds of divine sports. He is the lord of all and independent. He is the master of delusion and free from doubtful alternatives.

## \|\| 4.44.77 \|\|

*iti vijñāya mene tvaṃ śivāndehi śivāya vai \|*  
*kuhaṭhantyaja kujñānaṃ sarvakāryavināśanam \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. Realising this, O Menā, give your daughter to Śiva. Abandon your misplaced stubbornness. Your evil inclination is destructive of all affairs”.

## \|\| 4.44.78 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityuktā sā mayā menā vilapantī muhurmuhuḥ \|*  
*lajjāṃ kiṃcicchanaistyaktvā mune māṃ vākyamabravīt \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. Thus addressed by me Menā continued to cry again and again. Slowly, O sage, she eschewed all shame and spoke to me.

## \|\| 4.44.79 \|\|

*menovāca \|*  
*kimarthantu bhavānbrahmanrūpamasya mahāvaram \|*  
*vyarthīkaroti kimiyaṃ hanyatāṃ na svayaṃ śivā \|\| 79 \|\|*

Menā said:—

79\. O Brahmā, why do you render her excellent beauty futile? Why don’t you kill her yourself?

## \|\| 4.44.80 \|\|

*na vaktavyaṃ ca bhavatā śivāya pratidīyatām \|*  
*na dāsye'haṃ śivāyaināṃ svasutāmprāṇavallabhām \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. You shall not tell me again that she should be given to Śiva. I will not give my daughter, dearer than my own life, to Śiva.

## \|\| 4.44.81 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityukte tu tadā siddhāḥ sanakādyā mahāmune \|*  
*samāgatya mahāprītyā vacanaṃ hīdamabruvan \|\| 81 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

81\. O great sage, when she expressed thus, Sanaka and other Siddhas came there and spoke lovingly.

## \|\| 4.44.82 \|\|

*siddhā ūcuḥ \|*  
*ayamvai paramassākṣācchivaḥ parasukhāvahaḥ \|*  
*kṛpayā ca bhavatputryai darśanandattavānprabhuḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

Siddhas said:—

82\. This Śiva is the supreme being, the bestower of

supreme happiness. Out of His sympathy He has granted His vision to your daughter.

## \|\| 4.44.83 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*athovāca tu tānmenā vilapya ca muhurmuhuḥ \|*  
*na deyā tu mayā samyaggiriśāyograrūpiṇe \|\| 83 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

83\. Then Menā said to them after sobbing frequently—“My riches are not to be given to Śiva of hideous form.

## \|\| 4.44.84 \|\|

*kimarthantu bhavantaśca sarve siddhāḥ prapañcinaḥ \|*  
*rūpamasyāḥ paraṃ nāma vyarthīkarttuṃ samudyatāḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

84 Why are you Siddhas collectively attempting to make her exquisite beauty futile?”

## \|\| 4.44.85 \|\|

*ityukte ca tayā tatra mune'haṃ cakito'bhavam \|*  
*sarve vismayamāpannā devasiddharṣimānavāḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. When this was mentioned by her I became stunned. All the gods, Siddhas, sages and human beings were bewildered.

## \|\| 4.44.86 \|\|

*etasminsamaye tasyā haṭhaṃ śrutvā dṛḍhaṃ mahat \|*  
*drutaṃ śivapriyo viṣṇussamāgatyā'bravīdidam \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. In the meantime, on hearing of her persistent obduracy, Viṣṇu a favourite of Śiva came there and spoke as follows.

## \|\| 4.44.87-88 \|\|

*viṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*pitṝṇāṃ ca priyā putrī mānasī guṇasaṃyutā \|*  
*patnī himavatassākṣādbrahmaṇaḥ kulamuttamam \|\| 87 \|\|*

*sahāyāstādṛśā loke dhanyā hyasi vadāmi kim \|*  
*dharmasyādhārabhūtāsi kathaṃ dharmaṃ jahāsi hi \|\| 88 \|\|*

Viṣṇu said:—

87-88. You are the beloved mental daughter of the Pitṛs. You are endowed with all good qualities. You are wife of Himavat himself. Yours is the excellent race of Brahmā. Your well-wishers in the world are also like him (Brahmā). You are really blessed. What more can I say? You are reputed to be a patron of virtue. Why do you then eschew virtue?

## \|\| 4.44.89 \|\|

*devaiśca ṛṣibhiścaiva brahmaṇā vā mayā tathā \|*  
*viruddhaṃ kathyate kiṃ nu tvayaiva suvicāryatām \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. May this be pondered over by you yourself. Can anything against you be mentioned by the gods, sages, or Brahmā or by myself?

## \|\| 4.44.90 \|\|

*śivatvaṃ na ca jānāsi nirguṇasya guṇassa hi \|*  
*virūpassa surūpo hi sarvasevyassatāṃ gatiḥ \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. You do not know Śiva. He is both possessed and devoid of attributes. He is hideous as well as comely. He is worthy of worship by all. He is the ultimate goal of the good.

## \|\| 4.44.91 \|\|

*tenaiva nirmitā devī mūlaprakṛtirīśvarī \|*  
*tatpārśve ca tadā tena nirmitaḥ puruṣottamaḥ \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. The primordial nature is created by Him alone. Near her, the excellent primordial Being has also been created by Him.

## \|\| 4.44.92 \|\|

*tābhyāṃ cāhaṃ tathā brahmā tataśca guṇarūpataḥ \|*  
*avatīrya svayaṃ rudro lokānāṃ hitakārakaḥ \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. Brahmā and I are created thereafter. Then, with the three attributes, Śiva Himself, incarnated in order to be beneficial to the worlds.

## \|\| 4.44.93 \|\|

*tato vedāstathā devā yatkiṃciddṛśyate jagat \|*  
*sthāvaraṃ jaṃgamaṃ caiva tatsarvaṃ śakarādabhūt \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. The Vedas originated from Him. The gods sprang up from Him. Whatever mobile and immobile there is in the universe, sprang up from him.

## \|\| 4.44.94 \|\|

*tadrūpamvarṇitaṃ kena jñāyate kena vā punaḥ \|*  
*mayā ca brahmaṇā yasya hyato labdhaśca naiva hi \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. Who has described His form? By whom can it be

known? Even Brahmā and I were not able to gauge him.

## \|\| 4.44.95 \|\|

*ābrahmastambaparyaṃtaṃ yatkiñciddṛśyate jagat \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ ca śivaṃ viddhi nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. Whatever is seen in the universe from Brahmā down to a blade of grass is identical with Śiva. Know it. There need not be any hesitation in this matter.

## \|\| 4.44.96 \|\|

*sa evedṛksurūpeṇāvatīrṇo nijalīlayā \|*  
*śivātapaḥ prabhāvāddhi tava dvāri samāgataḥ \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. He alone, in the course of his divine sport, has incarnated himself in divine form. It was by the fascination of Pārvatī’s penance that He has come to your threshold.

## \|\| 4.44.97 \|\|

*tasmāttvaṃ himavatpatni duḥkhaṃ muñca śivambhaja \|*  
*bhaviṣyati mahānandaḥ kleśo yāsyati saṃkṣayam \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. Hence, O wife of Himavat, eschew your sorrow. Worship Śiva. You will have great pleasure. All pain will be quelled.

## \|\| 4.44.98 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|\| evamprabodhitāyāstu menakāyā abhūnmune \|*  
*tasyāstu komalaṃ kiṃcinmano viṣṇuprabodhitam \|\| 98 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

98\. O sage, when instructed by Viṣṇu, Menakā’s mind was somewhat softened.

## \|\| 4.44.99 \|\|

*paraṃ haṭhaṃ na tatyāja kanyāndātuṃ harāya na \|*  
*svīcakāra tadā menā śivamāyāvimohi tā \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. But she did not give up her obduracy. She did not consent to the proposal of giving her daughter to Śiva. Menā was deluded by Śiva’s magic.

## \|\| 4.44.100 \|\|

*uvāca ca hariṃ menā kiñcidbuddhvā giripriyā \|*  
*śrutvā viṣṇuvaco ramyaṃ girijājananī hi sā \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. On hearing the pleasing words of Viṣṇu, the beloved of the mountain, the mother of Pārvatī became slightly enlightened and spoke to Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 4.44.101 \|\|

*yadi ramyatanussa syāttadā deyā mayā sutā \|*  
*nānyathā koṭiśo yatnairvacmi satyandṛḍhaṃ vacaḥ \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. If He assumes a lovely form and body my daughter may be given to Him and not otherwise even if you attempt it a thousand times. This is my firm decision.

## \|\| 4.44.102 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityuktvā vacanaṃ menā tūṣṇīmāsa dṛḍhavratā \|*  
*śivecchāpreritā dhanyā tathā yākhilamohinī \|\| 102 \|\|*

102\. After saying thus Menā of steady resolve kept quiet. She was induced by Śiva’s will whose magical power deludes all.

## Chapter 45 - Śiva’s comely form and the Jubilation of the Citizens

## \|\| 4.45.1 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*etasminnantare tvaṃ hi viṣṇunā prerito drutam \|*  
*anukūlayituṃ śaṃbhumayāstannikaṭe mune \|\| 1 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

1\. In the meantime, O sage, urged by Viṣṇu you went immediately to Śiva to conciliate Him.

## \|\| 4.45.2 \|\|

*tatra gatvā sa vai rudro bhavatā suprabodhitaḥ \|*  
*stotrairnānāvidhaisstutvā devakāryacikīrṣayā \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. After reaching there, with a desire to get the task of the gods fulfilled, you pleaded with Śiva after eulogising Him with different kinds of hymns.

## \|\| 4.45.3 \|\|

*śrutvā tvadvacanaṃ prītyā śaṃbhunā dhṛtamadbhutam \|*  
*svarūpamuttamandivyaṃ kṛpālutvaṃ ca darśitam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. On hearing your words Śiva joyously assumed a wonderfully excellent and divine form and showed His mercifulness.

## \|\| 4.45.4 \|\|

*taddṛṣṭvā sundaraṃ śambhuṃ svarūpammanmathā dhikam \|*  
*atyahṛṣyo mune tvaṃ hi lāvaṇyaparamāyanam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. O sage, on seeing the comely form of Śiva, the receptacle of exquisite beauty, far better than that of the cupid, you were greatly delighted.

## \|\| 4.45.5 \|\|

*stotrairnānāvidhaisstutvā paramānandasaṃyutaḥ \|*  
*āgacchastvaṃ mune tatra yatra menā sthitākhilaiḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Highly delighted you eulogised Him again and again with different kinds of hymns and returned to the place where Mena was seated along with other gods.

## \|\| 4.45.6 \|\|

*tatrāgatya suprasanno mune'tipremasaṃkulaḥ \|*  
*harṣayaṃstāṃ śailapatnī menāntvaṃ vākyamabravīḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Reaching there, O sage, with great affection and delight, you spoke to the great pleasure of Mena, the wife of Himavat.

## \|\| 4.45.7 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*mene paśya viśālākṣi śivarūpamanuttamam \|*  
*kṛtā śivena tenaiva sukṛpā karuṇātmanā \|\| 7 \|\|*

Nārada said:—

7\. O Mena of wide eyes, see the excellent features of Śiva. The merciful Śiva has taken great pity on us.

## \|\| 4.45.8 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*śrutvā sā tadvaco menā vismitā śailakāminī \|*  
*dadarśa śivarūpantatparamānandadāyakam \|\| 8 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

8\. Extremely surprised on hearing your words, Menā the beloved wife of the mountain, saw Śiva’s form that afforded great bliss.

## \|\| 4.45.9-12 \|\|

*koṭisūryapratīkāśaṃ sarvāvayavasundaram \|*  
*vicitravasanaṃ cātra nānābhūṣaṇabhūṣitam \|\| 9 \|\|*

*suprasannaṃ suhāsaṃ ca sulāvaṇyaṃ manoharam \|*  
*gaurābhaṃ dyutisaṃyuktaṃ candrarekhāvibhūṣitam \|\| 10 \|\|*

*sarvairdevagaṇaiḥ prītyā viṣṇvādyassevitaṃ tathā \|*  
*sūryeṇa cchatritaṃ mūrdhni candreṇa ca viśobhitam \|\| 11 \|\|*

*sarvathā ramaṇīyaṃ ca bhūṣitasya vibhūṣaṇaiḥ \|*  
*vāhanasya mahāśobhā varṇituṃ naiva śakyate \|\| 12 \|\|*

9-12. It was as refulgent as that of a thousand suns. Every part of the body was exquisite. The garments were of variegated colours. He was embellished with different ornaments. He was smiling with great delight. His comeliness was highly pleasing. He was fair-complexioned and lustrous. The crescent moon added to his beauty. Viṣṇu and other gods lovingly served Him. The sun acted as His royal umbrella. The moon embellished Him. In every way He was extremely handsome bedecked in ornaments. It was impossible to describe adequately the great beauty of His vehicle.

## \|\| 4.45.13 \|\|

*gaṃgā ca yamunā caiva vidhattaḥ sma sucāmare \|*  
*siddhayo'ṣṭau purastasya kurvanti sma sunarttanam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The Gaṅgā and the Yamunā were waving the Chowries. The eight Siddhis danced in front of Him.

## \|\| 4.45.14 \|\|

*mayā caiva tadā viṣṇurindrādyā hyamarāstathā \|*  
*svaṃ svaṃ veṣaṃ susambhūṣya giriśenācaranyutāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Viṣṇu, I, Indra and the other gods bedecked their bodies and dress and accompanied Śiva.

## \|\| 4.45.15 \|\|

*tathā jayeti bhāṣanto nānārūpā gaṇāstadā \|*  
*svalaṅkṛtamahāmodā girīśapurato'caran \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The Gaṇas of various forms and features shouted cries of “Victory” “Victory” and walked in front of Śiva.

## \|\| 4.45.16 \|\|

*siddhāścopasurāssarve munayaśca mahāsukhāḥ \|*  
*yayuśśivena suprītāssakalāścāpare tathā \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The Siddhas, the secondary gods, the extremely delighted sages went in company of Śiva. The others too were equally delighted.

## \|\| 4.45.17 \|\|

*evandevādayassarve kutūhalasamanvitāḥ \|*  
*paraṃbrahma gṛṇantaste svapatnībhiralaṃkṛtāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Thus the fully decorated gods, were very jubilant and in the company of their wives they eulogised Śiva, the Supreme Brahman.

## \|\| 4.45.18 \|\|

*viśvāvasumukhāstatra hyapsarogaṇasaṃyutāḥ \|*  
*gāyantopyagratastasya paramaṃ śāṅkaraṃ yaśaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Viśvāvasu and others along with the celestial damsels sang songs of Śiva’s glory.

## \|\| 4.45.19 \|\|

*itthaṃ mahotsavastatra babhūva munisa ttama \|*  
*nānāvidho maheśe hi śailadvāri ca gacchati \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. O excellent sage, when Śiva was nearing the threshold of the palace of Himavat, there was much jubilation there.

## \|\| 4.45.20 \|\|

*tasmiṃśca samaye tatra suṣamā yā parātmanaḥ \|*  
*varṇituṃ tāṃ viśeṣeṇa kaśśaknoti munīśvara \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. O excellent sage, who can describe the exquisite splendour of the supreme lord at that time.

## \|\| 4.45.21 \|\|

*tathāvidhaṃ ca tandṛṣṭvā menā citragatā iva \|*  
*kṣaṇamāsīttataḥ prītyā provāca vacanaṃ mune \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. On seeing Him in that form Menā stood stunned as though drawn in a picture for a moment, O sage, and spoke these words.

## \|\| 4.45.22 \|\|

*menovāca \|*  
*dhanyā putrī madīyā ca yayā taptaṃ mahattapaḥ \|*  
*yatprabhāvānmaheśāna tvaṃ prāpta iha madgṛhe \|\| 22 \|\|*

Menā said:—

22\. O great lord, my daughter is indeed blessed, she by whom the great penance was performed. It is by virtue of that penance that you have come to my threshold.

## \|\| 4.45.23 \|\|

*mayā kṛtā purā yā vai śivanindā duratyayā \|*  
*tāṃ kṣamasva śivāsvāminsuprasanno bhavādhunā \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. O lord of Pārvatī, be pleased now. Pardon me for the heap of repulsive words I showered on Śiva.

## \|\| 4.45.24 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*itthaṃ sambhāṣya sā menā saṃstūyendulalāṭakam \|*  
*sāñjaliḥ praṇatā śailapriyā lajjāparā'bhavat \|\| 24 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

24\. After saying thus and eulogising the moon-crested lord, Menā, the beloved of the mountain, bowed to Him with palms joined in reverence and stood shy.

## \|\| 4.45.25 \|\|

*tāvatstriyassamājagmurhitvā kāmānanekaśaḥ \|*  
*bahvyastāḥ puravāsinyaśśivadarśanalālasāḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. By that time the ladies of the town left the work they were engaged in, in their eagerness to see Śiva.

## \|\| 4.45.26 \|\|

*majjanaṃ kurvatī kācittaccūrṇasahitā yayau \|*  
*draṣṭuṃ kutūhalāḍhyā ca śaṅkaraṃ girijāvaram \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. A certain lady in the midst of her bath and toilet was overwhelmed with the desire to see Śiva, the bridegroom of Pārvatī. She came out with the shampoo powder still held in her hands.

## \|\| 4.45.27 \|\|

*kācittu svāminassevāṃ sakhīyuktā vihāya ca \|*  
*sucāmarakarā prītyāgācchambhordarśanāya vai \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. A certain lady engaged in fanning her husband in the company of her maid left that job and came out to see Śiva with the fan still in her hands.

## \|\| 4.45.28 \|\|

*kācittu bālakaṃ hitvā pibantaṃ stanyamādarāt \|*  
*atṛptaṃ śaṅkarandraṣṭuṃ yayau darśanalālasā \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Another lady engaged in suckling her babe at her breast left him dissatisfied and came out eagerly to see the lord.

## \|\| 4.45.29 \|\|

*raśanāṃ badhnatī kācittayaiva sahitā yayau \|*  
*vasanaṃ viparītaṃ vai dhṛtvā kācidyayau tataḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Another lady engaged in trying her waist girdle came out with it. Another lady came out with garments worn inside out

## \|\| 4.45.30 \|\|

*bhojanārthaṃ sthitaṃ kāntaṃ hitvā kācidyayau priyā \|*  
*draṣṭuṃ śivāvaraṃ prītyā satṛṣṇā sakutūhalā \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Another lady left her husband who had sat down to dine and came out athirsting and enthusiastic to see the bridegroom.

## \|\| 4.45.31 \|\|

*kāciddhaste śalākāṃ ca dhṛtvāṃjanakarā priyā \|*  
*añjitvaikākṣi sandraṣṭuṃ yayau śailasutāvaram \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. A certain lady holding the collyrium in her hand after applying it to one of her eyes came out to see the bridegroom of the daughter of the mountain with the salve stick still in her hand.

## \|\| 4.45.32 \|\|

*kācittu kāminī pādau rañjayantī hyalaktakaiḥ \|*  
*śrutvā ghoṣaṃ ca taddhitvā darśanārthamupāgatā \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Another damsel engaged in applying the red lac juice to her feet heard the tumult outside and so left it in the middle and came out to see the procession.

## \|\| 4.45.33 \|\|

*ityādi vividhaṃ kāryaṃ hitvā vāsaṃ striyo yayuḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā tu śāṃkaraṃ rūpaṃ mohaṃ prāptāstadā'bhavan \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Thus the ladies forsook their activities, left their houses and came out. On seeing the exquisite form of Śiva they were greatly fascinated.

## \|\| 4.45.34 \|\|

*tatastāḥ premasaṃvignāśśivadarśanaharṣitāḥ \|*  
*nidhāya hṛdi tanmūrtiṃ vacanaṃ cedamabruvan \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Delighted on seeing Śiva and overwhelmed by affection they cherished the comely form in their hearts and spoke as follows:—

## \|\| 4.45.35 \|\|

*puravāsinya ūcuḥ \|*  
*netrāṇi saphalānyāsanhimavatpuravāsinām \|*  
*yo yo'paśyadado rūpaṃ tasya vai sārthakaṃ januḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

The ladies said:—

35\. The eyes of the residents of this town have become fruitful. The life of the persons who have seen this comely form has become meaningful.

## \|\| 4.45.36 \|\|

*tasyaiva saphalaṃ janma tasyaiva saphalāḥ kriyāḥ \|*  
*yena dṛṣṭaśśivassākṣātsarvapāpapraṇāśakaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. The life is fruitful and the rites are fruitful only of the person who has seen Śiva, the destroyer of all sins.

## \|\| 4.45.37 \|\|

*pārvatyā sādhitaṃ sarvaṃ śivārthaṃ yattapaḥ kṛtam \|*  
*dhanyeyaṃ kṛtakṛtyeyaṃ śivā prāpya śivampatim \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Pārvatī has accomplished everything inasmuch as she performed penance for Śiva. She is blessed, she is contented in securing Śiva as her husband.

## \|\| 4.45.38 \|\|

*yadīdaṃ yugalaṃ brahmā na yuṃjyācchivayormudā \|*  
*tadā ca sakalo'pyasya śramo niṣphalatāmiyāt \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. If Brahmā had not joined this pair, Śiva and Śivā, his endeavour of creation would have entirely become fruitless.

## \|\| 4.45.39 \|\|

*samyak kṛtaṃ tathā cātra yojitaṃ yugmamuttamam \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ sārthatā jātā sarvakāryasamudbhavā \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. This is well done. The excellent pair has been united. Everything has become meaningful in every activity.

## \|\| 4.45.40 \|\|

*vinā tu tapasā śambhordarśanaṃ durlabhannṛṇām \|*  
*darśanācchaṃkarasyaiva sarve yātāḥ kṛtārthatām \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. A vision of Śiva is inaccessible to men without penance. All of us have now become contented by seeing Śiva.

## \|\| 4.45.41 \|\|

*lakṣmīrnārāyaṇaṃ lebhe yathā vai svāminampurā \|*  
*tathāsau pārvatī devī haramprāpya subhūṣitā \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Just as Lakṣmī was blessed by securing Viṣṇu as her lord, formerly, so also the gentle lady Pārvatī has become embellished on securing Śiva.

## \|\| 4.45.42 \|\|

*brahmāṇaṃ ca yathā lebhe svāminaṃ vai sarasvatī \|*  
*tathāsau pārvatī devī haramprāpya subhūṣitā \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Just as Sarasvatī was blessed by securing Brahmā as her husband, so also the gentle lady Pārvatī has become embellished on getting Śiva as her husband.

## \|\| 4.45.43 \|\|

*vayandhanyāḥ striyassarvāḥ puruṣāssakalā varāḥ \|*  
*ye ye paśyanti sarveśaṃ śaṃkaraṃ girijāpatim \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. All of us, men and women, are blessed—we who see Śiva, the lord of all, the husband of Pārvatī.

## \|\| 4.45.44 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|\| itthamuktvā tu vacanaṃ candanaiścākṣatairapi \|*  
*śivaṃ samarcayāmāsurlājānvavṛṣurādarāt \|\| 44 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

44\. Saying thus they worshipped Śiva with sandal paste and raw rice grains. They showered Him with fried grains respectfully.

## \|\| 4.45.45 \|\|

*tasthustatra striyaḥ sarvā menayā saha sotsukāḥ \|*  
*varṇayantyo'dhikambhāgyammenāyāśca girerapi \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. The ladies standing near Menā were enthusiastically praising the good luck of Menā and the mountain.

## \|\| 4.45.46 \|\|

*kathāstathāvidhāśśṛṇvaṃstadvāmā varṇitāśśubhāḥ \|*  
*prahṛṣṭo'bhūtprabhuḥ sarvairmune viṣṇvādibhistadā \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Hearing the auspicious stores and anecdotes of the ladies, the lord became delighted, O sage, along with Viṣṇu and others.

## Chapter 46 - The arrival of the bridegroom

## \|\| 4.46.1 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*atha śaṃbhuḥ prasannātmā sadūtaṃ svagaṇaissuraiḥ \|*  
*sarvairanyairgirerddhāma jagāma sakutūhalam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

1\. The delighted Śiva accompanied by His Bhūtas, Gaṇas, gods and others went to the abode of the mountain zealously.

## \|\| 4.46.2 \|\|

*menāpi strīgaṇaistaiśca himācalavarapriyā \|*  
*tata utthāya svagṛhā bhyaṃtaraṃ sā jagāma ha \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Menā, the exquisite beloved of Himācala, got up from her seat and went into the harem along with the women-folk.

## \|\| 4.46.3 \|\|

*nīrājanārthaṃ śambhośca dīpapātrakarā satī \|*  
*sarvarṣistrīgaṇaissākamagacchaddvāramādarāt \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. For the customary Nīrājana (waving of lights) rites of Śiva, the chaste lady came near the entrance with lights and vessels in her hands along with womenfolk of the sages.

## \|\| 4.46.4 \|\|

*tatrāgataṃ maheśānaṃ śaṃkaraṃ girijāvaram \|*  
*dadarśa prītito menā sevitaṃ sakalaissuraiḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Menā saw with pleasure lord Śiva, the bridegroom of Pārvatī, served by all the gods and who by that time had come there.

## \|\| 4.46.5-11 \|\|

*cārucaṃpakavarṇābhaṃ hyekavaktraṃ trilocanam \|*  
*īṣaddhāsyaprasannāsyaṃ ratnasvarṇādibhūṣitam \|\| 5 \|\|*

*mālatīmālayā yuktaṃ sadratnamukuṭojjvalam \|*  
*satkaṃṭhābharaṇaṃ cāruvalayāṃgadabhūṣitam \|\| 6 \|\|*

*vahniśaucenātulena tvatisūkṣmeṇa cāruṇā \|*  
*amūlyavastrayugmena vicitreṇātirājitam \|\| 7 \|\|*

*candanāgarukastūrīcārukuṃkuma bhūṣitam \|*  
*ratnadarpaṇahastaṃ ca kajjalojjvalalocanam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*sarvasvaprabhayācchannamatīvasumanoharam \|*  
*atīva taruṇaṃ ramyaṃ bhūṣitāṃgaiśca bhūṣitam \|\| 9 \|\|*

*kāminīkāṃtamavyagraṃ koṭicandrānanāṃbujam \|*  
*koṭismarādhikatanucchaviṃ sarvāṃgasuṃdaram \|\| 10 \|\|*

*īdṛgvidhaṃ sudevaṃ taṃ sthitaṃ svapurataḥ prabhum \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā jāmātaraṃ menā jahau śokammudā'nvitā \|\| 11 \|\|*

5-11. Śiva had the complexion of the colour of the Campaka flower. He had only one face but retained the three eyes. The face was beaming with a simple smile. He was bedecked in gems and gold and wore a garland of Mālatī flowers. The gemset crown was lustrous. He wore brilliant necklaces. He was bedecked in bangles and bracelets of fine workmanship. He was shining well with the two clothes of great value, fine texture and unrivalled beauty and purified in fire. Highly embellished in sandal paste, aguru, musk and fine saffron, he had a gemset mirror in his hand and his eyes were lustrous with the collyrium. He was shedding a halo around him enveloping everything. He was extremely beautiful. He appeared to be very young. His limbs had the full complement of their ornaments. He was very attractive to the ladies. He was not nervous or self-conscious. His lotuslike face had the brilliance of a thousand moons. His body shone with a refulgence more than that of a thousand cupids. He was beautiful in every limb. Seeing the lord thus as her son-in-law, Menā forgot all her grief. She was glad.

## \|\| 4.46.12 \|\|

*praśaśaṃsa svabhāgyaṃ sā girijāṃ bhūdharaṃ kulam \|*  
*mene kṛtārthamātmānaṃ jaharṣa ca punaḥ punaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. She praised her good luck. She congratulated Pārvatī, the mountain and his entire family. She congratulated herself. She rejoiced again and again.

## \|\| 4.46.13 \|\|

*nīrājanaṃ cakārāsau praphullavadanā satī \|*  
*avalokaparā tatra menā jāmātaraṃ mudā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Gazing at her son-in-law joyously with beaming face, the chaste lady performed the Nīrājana rite.

## \|\| 4.46.14 \|\|

*girijoktamanusmṛtya menā vismayamāgatā \|*  
*manasaiva hyuvācedaṃ harṣaphullānanāmbujā \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Remembering what Pārvatī had told her, Menā was agreeably surprised and with a beaming lotus-like face full of delight she muttered to herself.

## \|\| 4.46.15 \|\|

*yadvai puroktaṃ ca tayā pārvatyā mama tatra ca \|*  
*tatodhikaṃ prapaśyāmi saundaryyaṃ parameśituḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. “I see the beauty of the great lord far in excess of what Pārvatī had told me before.

## \|\| 4.46.16 \|\|

*maheśasya sulāvaṇyamanirvācyaṃ ca saṃprati \|*  
*evaṃ vismayamāpannā menā svagṛhamāyayau \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Śiva’s loveliness cannot be expressed adequately now.” In the same state of pleasant surprise she went in.

## \|\| 4.46.17 \|\|

*praśaśaṃsuryuvatayo dhanyā dhanyā gireḥ sutā \|*  
*durgā bhagavatītyevamūcuḥ kāścana kanyakāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The young ladies proclaimed that the daughter of the mountain was fortunate. Some girls said that she had become a goddess.

## \|\| 4.46.18 \|\|

*na dṛṣṭo vara ityevamasmābhirddānagocaraḥ \|*  
*dhanyā hi girijā devīmūcuḥ kāścana kanyakāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Some said—“Such a bridegroom has never been seen, not to our knowledge.” Some girls said to Menā—“Pārvatī is really blessed.”

## \|\| 4.46.19 \|\|

*jagurgandharvvapravarā nanṛtuścāpsarogaṇāḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā śaṃkararūpaṃ ca prahṛṣṭāssarvadevatāḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The chief of Gandharvas sang songs. The celestial damsels danced. On seeing Śiva’s lovely form, the gods were delighted.

## \|\| 4.46.20 \|\|

*nānāprakāravādyāni vādakā madhurākṣaram \|*  
*nānāprakāraśilpena vādayāmāsurādarāt \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. The instrument players played on musical instruments in sweet tones showing their diverse skill.

## \|\| 4.46.21 \|\|

*himācalo'pi mudito dvārācāramathākarot \|*  
*menāpi sarvanārībhirmahotsavapurassaram \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. The delighted Himācala too carried out the customary rites of reception at the entrance. Menā also jubilantly took part in the same along with all the womenfolk.

## \|\| 4.46.22 \|\|

*parapucchāṃ cakārāsau muditā svagṛhaṃ yayau \|*  
*śivo niveditaṃ sthānaṃ jagāma gaṇanirjaraiḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. She made formal inquiries about the health of the bridegroom and gladly went into the house. Śiva went to the apartments assigned to Him along with the Gaṇas and the gods.

## \|\| 4.46.23 \|\|

*etasminnantare durgāṃ śailāntaḥpuracārikā \|*  
*bahirjagmussamādāya pūjituṃ kuladevatām \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. In the meantime the servant-maids in the harem of the mountain took Pārvatī out in order to worship the tutelar family deity.

## \|\| 4.46.24-30 \|\|

*tatra tāṃ dadṛśurdevā nimeṣarahitā mudā \|*  
*sunīlāṃjanavarṇābhāṃ svāṃgaiśca pratibhūṣitām \|\| 24 \|\|*

*trinetrādṛtanetrāṃtāmanyavāritalocanām \|*  
*īṣaddhāsyaprasannāsyāṃ sakaṭākṣāṃ manoharām \|\| 25 \|\|*

*sucārukabarībhārāṃ cārupatraka śobhitām \|*  
*kastūrībindubhissārddhaṃ sindūrabinduśobhitām \|\| 26 \|\|*

*ratnendrasārahāreṇa vakṣasā suvirājitām \|*  
*ratnakeyūravalayāṃ ratnakaṅkaṇamaṃḍitām \|\| 27 \|\|*

*sadratnakuṇḍalābhyāṃ ca cārugaṇḍasthalojjvalām \|*  
*maṇiratnaprabhāmuṣṭidantarājivirājitām \|\| 28 \|\|*

*madhubimbādharoṣṭhāṃ ca ratnayāvakasaṃyutām \|*  
*ratnadarppaṇahastāṃ ca krīḍāpadmavibhūṣitām \|\| 29 \|\|*

*candanāgurukastūrīkuṃkumenāti ca rcitām \|*  
*kvaṇanmaṃjīrapādāṃ ca raktāṃghritalarājitām \|\| 30 \|\|*
