*asahañśivaretastaddhimādriḥ kaṃpamudvahan \|*  
*gaṃgāyāṃ prākṣipattūrṇamasahyaṃ dāhapīḍitaḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Unable to bear that semen of Śiva and trembling much, Himavat became scorched by it and hurled it in the Gaṅgā.

## \|\| 5.2.66 \|\|

*gaṃgayā'pi ca tadvīryaṃ dussahaṃ paramātmanaḥ \|*  
*niḥkṣiptaṃ hi śarastaṃbe taraṃgaiḥ svairmunīśvara \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. O great sage, the intolerable semen of lord Śiva was deposited by Gaṅgā in the forest of Śara grass by means of its waves.

## \|\| 5.2.67 \|\|

*patitaṃ tatra tadreto drutaṃ bālo babhūva ha \|*  
*sundarassubhagaḥ śrīmāṃstejasvī prītivarddhanaḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. The semen that fell was turned in a handsome good-featured boy, full of glory and splendour. He increased everyone’s pleasure.

## \|\| 5.2.68 \|\|

*mārgamāse site pakṣe tithau ṣaṣṭhyāṃ munīśvara \|*  
*prādurbhāvo'bhavattasya śivaputrasya bhūtale \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. O great sage, on the sixth day of the bright half of the lunar month of Mārgaśīrṣa, the son of Śiva was born in the world.

## \|\| 5.2.69 \|\|

*tasminnavasare brahmanna kasmāddhima śailajā \|*  
*abhūtaḥ sukhinau tatra svagirau giriśo'pi ca \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. At that time, O Brahmin, on their mountain, Pārvatī the daughter of Himavat and Śiva became very happy.

## \|\| 5.2.70 \|\|

*śivākucābhyāṃ susrāva paya ānandasaṃbhavam \|*  
*tatra gatvā ca sarveṣāṃ sukhamāsīnmune'dhikam \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Out of joy, milk exuded from the breasts of Pārvatī. On reaching the spot everyone felt very happy.

## \|\| 5.2.71 \|\|

*maṃgalaṃ cā'bhavattāta trilokyāṃ sukhadaṃ satām \|*  
*khalānāmabhavadvighno daityānāṃ ca viśeṣataḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. O dear, there was auspiciousness in the three worlds, pleasing to the good. There occurred obstacles to the wicked and particularly to the demons.

## \|\| 5.2.72 \|\|

*akasmādabhavadvyomni paramo duṃdubhidhvaniḥ \|*  
*puṣpavṛṣṭiḥ papātā'śu bālakopari nārada \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. O Nārada, there was a mysterious sound of Dundubhi drum in the sky. Showers of flowers fell on the boy.

## \|\| 5.2.73 \|\|

*viṣṇvādīnāṃ samastānāṃ devānāṃ munisattama \|*  
*abhūdakasmātparama ānandaḥ paramotsavaḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. O excellent sage, there was great delight to Viṣṇu and the gods. There was great jubilation everywhere.

## Chapter 3 - The boyhood sports of Kārttikeya

## \|\| 5.3.1 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*devadeva prajānātha brahman sṛṣṭikara prabho \|*  
*tataḥ kimabhavattatra tadvadā'dya kṛpāṃ kuru \|\| 1 \|\|*

Nārada said:—

1\. O lord of subjects, O Brahmin, O creator, what happened thereafter? Please tell me the same.

## \|\| 5.3.2 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*tasminnavasare tāta viśvāmitraḥ pratāpavān \|*  
*prerito vidhinā tatrāgacchatprīto yadṛcchayā \|\| 2 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

2\. O dear, then the powerful sage Viśvāmitra, urged by Brahmā, came there casually and was delighted.

## \|\| 5.3.3 \|\|

*sa dṛṣṭvā'laukikaṃ dhāma tatsutasya sutejasaḥ \|*  
*abhavatpūrṇakāmastu suprasanno nanāma ca \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. On seeing the unearthly splendour of that brilliant boy, he became very delighted. He bowed to the boy.

## \|\| 5.3.4 \|\|

*akarotsunutiṃ tasya suprasannena cetasā \|*  
*vidhipreritavāgbhiśca viśvāmitraḥ prabhāvavit \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. With a delighted mind he eulogised him with the words prompted by Brahmā. Viśvāmitra realised his power.

## \|\| 5.3.5 \|\|

*tatasso'bhūtsutastatra suprasanno mahoti kṛt \|*  
*suprahasyādbhutamaho viśvāmitramuvāca ca \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The boy too was delighted and became the source of great enjoyment. Laughingly he spoke to Viśvāmitra. It was very surprising.

## \|\| 5.3.6 \|\|

*śivasuta uvāca \|*  
*śivecchayā mahājñāninnakasmāttvamihāgataḥ \|*  
*saṃskāraṃ kuru me tāta yathāvadvedasaṃmitam \|\| 6 \|\|*

Śiva’s son said:—

6\. “O great one of perfect wisdom, it is due to the will of Śiva that you have come here by chance. O dear, perform my purificatory rites in accordance with Vedic injunctions.

## \|\| 5.3.7 \|\|

*adyārabhya purodhāstvaṃ bhava me prītimāvahan \|*  
*bhaviṣyasi sadā pūjyassarveṣāṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. From now onwards you remain my priest conferring your love on me. It is certain that you will become the object of worship of all.”

## \|\| 5.3.8 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya vacastasya suprasanno hi gādhijaḥ \|*  
*tamuvācānudāttena svareṇa ca suvismitaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

8\. On hearing his words, Gādhi’s son (Viśvāmitra) was highly delighted and surprised. He spoke to him in a tone, by no means highly accented.

## \|\| 5.3.9 \|\|

*viśvāmitra uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu tāta na vipro'haṃ gādhikṣatriyabālakaḥ \|*  
*viśvāmitreti vikhyātaḥ kṣatriyo viprasevakaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

Viśvāmitra said:—

9\. Listen, O dear, I am not a brahmin. I am a Kṣatriya, son of Gādhi, famous as Viśvāmitra and a servant of brahmins.

## \|\| 5.3.10 \|\|

*iti svacaritaṃ khyātaṃ mayā te varabālaka \|*  
*kastvaṃ svacaritaṃ brūhi vismitāyākhilaṃ hi me \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. O excellent boy, I have thus narrated my life to you. Who are you? Now mention everything about your life to me who am surprised.

## \|\| 5.3.11 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya vaca stasya tatsvavṛttaṃ jagāda ha \|*  
*tataścovāca suprītyā gādhijaṃ taṃ mahotikṛt \|\| 11 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

11\. On hearing his words the boy told him about his life. The divine boy, the cause of great enjoyment and protection, said to Gādhi’s son with great pleasure.

## \|\| 5.3.12 \|\|

*\|\| śivasuta uvāca \|*  
*viśvāmitra varānme tvaṃ brahmarṣirnā'tra saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*vaśiṣṭhādyāśca nityaṃ tvāṃ praśaṃsiṣyaṃti cādarāt \|\| 12 \|\|*

Śiva’s son said:—

12\. O Viśvāmitra, thanks to my favour, you now become a brahminical sage. Vasiṣṭha and others will for ever regard you with respect.

## \|\| 5.3.13 \|\|

*atastvamājñayā me hi saṃskāraṃ kartumarhasi \|*  
*idaṃ sarvaṃ sugopyaṃ te kathanīyaṃ na kutracit \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Hence, at my behest you shall perform my purificatory rites. Keep this as a great secret. You shall not mention it anywhere.

## \|\| 5.3.14 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*tatokārṣītsa saṃskāraṃ tasya prītyā'khilaṃ yathā \|*  
*śivabālasya devarṣe vedoktavidhinā param \|\| 14 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

14\. O celestial sage, in the manner laid down in the Vedas he performed the purificatory rites for the son of Śiva.

## \|\| 5.3.15 \|\|

*śivabālopi suprīto divyajñānamadātparam \|*  
*viśvāmitrāya munaye mahotikārakaḥ prabhuḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Śiva’s son, the cause of great enjoyment and protection, was glad and conferred divine wisdom on the sage.

## \|\| 5.3.16 \|\|

*purohitaṃ cakārāsau viśvāmitraṃ śucessuta \|*  
*tadārabhya dvijavaro nānālīlāviśāradaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The son of Agni made Viśvāmitra his priest. Form that time onwards he became a great brahmin and an expert in divine sports of various sorts.

## \|\| 5.3.17 \|\|

*itthaṃ līlā kṛtā tena kathitā sā mayā mune \|*  
*tallīlāmaparāṃ tāta śṛṇu prītyā vadāmyaham \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. O sage, the very first sport that he performed thus has been narrated to you by me. O dear, listen to another sport of his with wonder. I shall narrate it to you.

## \|\| 5.3.18-19 \|\|

*tasminnavasare tāta śvetanāmā ca saṃprati \|*  
*tatrā'paśyatsutaṃ divyaṃ nijaṃ parama pāvanam \|\| 18 \|\|*

*tatastaṃ pāvako gatvā dṛṣṭvāliṃgya cucumba ca \|*  
*putreti coktvā tasmai sa śastraṃ śaktindadau ca saḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. At that time he was known as white in colour. Agni went there and seeing his son who was divine and very holy called him “O dear son.” Agni embraced and kissed him too. He gave him a miraculous weapon, spear.

## \|\| 5.3.20 \|\|

*guhastāṃ śaktimādāya tacchṛṃgaṃ cāruroha ha \|*  
*taṃ jaghāna tayā śaktyā śṛṃgo bhuvi papāta saḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20 Guha took the spear and ascended the peak. He hit the peak with his spear and the peak fell down.

## \|\| 5.3.21 \|\|

*daśapadmamitā vīrā rākṣasāḥ pūrvamāgatāḥ \|*  
*tadvadhārthaṃ drutaṃ naṣṭā babhūvustatprahārataḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Ten thousand billions of heroic demons came there to attack him but were killed on being hit with the spear.

## \|\| 5.3.22 \|\|

*hāhākāro mahānāsīccakaṃpe sācalā mahī \|*  
*trailokyaṃ ca sureśānassadevastatra cāgamat \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. There was great hue and cry. The Earth, the mountains and the three worlds quaked. Indra the lord of gods came there.

## \|\| 5.3.23 \|\|

*dakṣiṇe tasya pārśve ca vajreṇa sa jaghāna ca \|*  
*śākhanāmā tato jātaḥ pumāṃścaiko mahābalaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. With his thunderbolt he hit on his right side. A person named “Śākha” of great strength came out of that side.

## \|\| 5.3.24 \|\|

*punaśśakro jaghānā''śu vāmapārśve hi taṃ tadā \|*  
*vajreṇā'nyaḥ pumāñjāto viśākhākhyo'paro balī \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Śakra struck him again with his thunderbolt on his left side. Another strong person named Viśākha came out of that side.

## \|\| 5.3.25 \|\|

*tatastaddhṛdayaṃ śakro jaghāna pavinā tadā \|*  
*paro'bhūnnaigamopākhyaḥ pumāṃstadvanmahābalaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Then Indra struck his heart with his thunderbolt. Another person very powerful like him named Naigama came out.

## \|\| 5.3.26 \|\|

*tadā skaṃdādicatvāro mahāvīrā mahābalāḥ \|*  
*indraṃ haṃtuṃ drutaṃ jagmussoyaṃ taccharaṇaṃ yayau \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Then the four of great heroic strength including Skanda rushed to attack Indra. I offered my protection to Indra.

## \|\| 5.3.27 \|\|

*śakrassa sāmaragaṇo bhayaṃ prāpya guhāttataḥ \|*  
*yayau svalokaṃ cakito na bhedaṃ jñātavānmune \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Afraid of Guha, Indra with all the gods went away to his region agitatedly. O sage, he did not know his secret.

## \|\| 5.3.28 \|\|

*sa bālakastu tatraiva tasthā''vānaṃdasaṃyutaḥ \|*  
*pūrvavannirbhayastāta nānālīlākaraḥ prabhuḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. That boy remained there itself as fearless as before. O dear, he was highly pleased and continued his divine sports of various sorts.

## \|\| 5.3.29 \|\|

*tasminnavasare tatra kṛttikākhyāśca ṣaṭ striyaḥ \|*  
*snātuṃ samāgatā bālaṃ dadṛśustaṃ mahāprabhum \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Meanwhile the six ladies named Kṛttikās came there for bath and they saw the lordly boy.

## \|\| 5.3.30 \|\|

*grahītuṃ taṃ manaścakrussarvāstā kṛttikāḥ striyaḥ \|*  
*vādo babhūva tāsāṃ tadgrahaṇecchāparo mune \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. All of them desired to take and fondle him O sage, as a result of their simultaneous desire for taking and fondling the boy, a dispute arose.

## \|\| 5.3.31 \|\|

*tadvādaśamanārthaṃ sa ṣaṇmukhāni cakāra ha \|*  
*papau dugdhaṃ ca sarvāsāṃ tuṣṭāstā abhavanmune \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. In order to quell their mutual dispute, the boy assumed six faces and drank milk off their breasts. O sage, they were all satisfied.

## \|\| 5.3.32-33 \|\|

*tanmanogatimājñāya sarvāstāḥ kṛttikāstadā \|*  
*tamādāya yayurlokaṃ svakīyaṃ muditā mune \|\| 32 \|\|*

*taṃ bālakaṃ kumārākhyaṃ stanaṃ dattvā stanārthine \|*  
*varddhayāmāsurīśasya sutaṃ sūryādhikaprabham \|\| 33 \|\|*

32-33. Realising his desire, the Kṛttikās, O sage, took him to their region joyously. Feeding him with their breast milk they nursed and nurtured Śiva’s son who was more refulgent than the sun.

## \|\| 5.3.34 \|\|

*na cakrurbālakaṃ yāśca locanānāmagocaram \|*  
*prāṇebhyopi premapātraṃ yaḥ poṣṭā tasya putraka \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. They never let him go out of their sight. He became the object of their love, dearer to them than their own lives. Verily he who nurses and nurtures the child has the right of possession over the son.

## \|\| 5.3.35 \|\|

*yāni yāni ca vastrāṇi trailokye durlabhāni ca \|*  
*dadustasmai ca tāḥ premṇā bhūṣaṇāni varāṇi vai \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. With great love they gave him the rarest garments and excellent ornaments in the three worlds.

## \|\| 5.3.36 \|\|

*dinedine tāḥ pupuṣurbālakaṃ taṃ mahāprabhum \|*  
*prasaṃsitāni svādūni bhojayitvā viśeṣataḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Feeding him specially on the choicest delicacies day by day they brought up the boy prodigy.

## \|\| 5.3.37 \|\|

*athaikasmin dine tāta sa bālaḥ kṛttikātmajaḥ \|*  
*gatvā devasabhāṃ divyāṃ sucaritraṃ cakāra ha \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. O dear, once that son of the Krttikās went to the celestial assembly and showed wonderful feats.

## \|\| 5.3.38 \|\|

*svamaho darśayāmāsa devebhyo hi mahādbhutam \|*  
*saviṣṇubhyo'khilebhyaśca mahotikarabālakaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. The boy of wonderful miracles showed his rare splendour to the gods including Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 5.3.39-40 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā sakalāste vai sācyutāssarṣayassurāḥ \|*  
*vismayaṃ prāpuratyantaṃ papracchustaṃ ca bālakam \|\| 39 \|\|*

*ko bhavāniti tacchrutvā na kiṃcitsa jagāda ha \|*  
*svālayaṃ sa jagāmā'śu guptastasthau hi pūrvavat \|\| 40 \|\|*

39-40. On seeing him, the gods and sages including Viṣṇu became surprised and asked the boy “Pray, who are you?” On hearing it he did not say anything in reply. He returned to his abode and remained concealed as before.

## Chapter 4 - Search for Kārttikeya and his conversation with Nandin

## \|\| 5.4.1 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*devadeva prajānātha tataḥ kimabhavadvidhe \|*  
*vadedānīṃ kṛpātastu śivalīlāsamanvitam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Nārada said:—

1\. O lord of people, O Brahmā, O lord of gods, what happened after that? Narrate it to me kindly besides the description of Śiva’s sports.

## \|\| 5.4.2 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*kṛttikābhirgṛhīte vai tasmiñśaṃbhusute mune \|*  
*kaścitkālo vyatīyāya bubudhe na himādrijā \|\| 2 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

2\. O sage, after the son of Śiva had been taken over by the Krttikās some time elapsed but the daughter of Himavat had no knowledge of the same.

## \|\| 5.4.3 \|\|

*tasminnavasare durgā smerānanasaroruhā \|*  
*uvāca svāminaṃ śaṃbhuṃ devadeveśvaraṃ prabhum \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Meanwhile Pārvatī beaming with her lotus like face told her husband Śiva, the lord of the gods.

## \|\| 5.4.4 \|\|

*pārvatyuvāca \|*  
*devadeva mahādeva śṛṇu me vacanaṃ śubham \|*  
*pūrvapuṇyātibhāreṇa tvaṃ mayā prāpta īśvara \|\| 4 \|\|*

Pārvatī said:—

4\. O lord of the gods, listen to my auspicious words. O lord, you have been attained by me, thanks to my previous merits.

## \|\| 5.4.5 \|\|

*kṛpayā yogiṣu śreṣṭho vihāraistatparo'bhavaḥ \|*  
*ratibhaṃgaḥ kṛto devaistatra me bhavatā bhava \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Although you are the most excellent among the Yogins, O lord, you became desirous of dalliance. But my dalliance with you was interrupted in the middle by the gods.

## \|\| 5.4.6 \|\|

*bhūmau nipatitaṃ vīryaṃ nodare mama te vibho \|*  
*kutra yātaṃ ca taddeva kena daivena nihṇutam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. O lord, your semen fell on the ground and not in my womb. Where did it go? Among the gods by whom could it have been concealed?

## \|\| 5.4.7 \|\|

*kathaṃ matsvāmino vīryamamoghaṃ te maheśvara \|*  
*moghaṃ yātaṃ ca kiṃ kiṃvā śiśurjātaśca kutracit \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. O lord, infallible is your semen, how can it be fruitless? Or has it developed into a child somewhere?

## \|\| 5.4.8 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*pārvatīvacanaṃ śrutvā prahasya jagadīśvaraḥ \|*  
*uvāca devānāhūya munīṃścāpi munīśvara \|\| 8 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

8\. O great sage, on hearing the words of Pārvatī, the lord of the universe called the gods and the sages and laughingly said to them.

## \|\| 5.4.9 \|\|

*\|\| maheśvara uvāca \|*  
*devāḥ śṛṇuta madvākyaṃ pārvatīvacanaṃ śrutam \|*  
*amoghaṃ kutra me vīryaṃ yātaṃ kena ca nihnutam \|\| 9 \|\|*

Lord Śiva said:—

9\. O gods, listen to my words. Has Pārvatī’s statement been heard by you? Where has my unfailing semen gone? By whom has it been concealed?

## \|\| 5.4.10 \|\|

*sabhayaṃ nāpatatkṣipraṃ sa ceddaṃḍaṃ na cārhati \|*  
*śaktau rājā na śāstā yaḥ prajābādhyaśca bhakṣakaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. If he, out of fear, falls at my feet quickly he may not be punished. If a king, competent enough, does not rule firmly he will be harrassed by the subjects. He cannot be a protector.

## \|\| 5.4.11 \|\|

*śaṃbhostadvacanaṃ śrutvā samālocya parasparam \|*  
*ūcussarve krameṇaiva trastāstu purataḥ prabhoḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

11\. On hearing the words of Śiva and after consulting one another they replied one by one. They were so afraid of the great lord.

## \|\| 5.4.12 \|\|

*viṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*te mithyāvādinassaṃtu bhārate gurudārikāḥ \|*  
*gurunindāratāśśaśvattvadvīryaṃ yaiśca nihnutam \|\| 12 \|\|*

Viṣṇu said:—

12\. Let those who have concealed your semen incur the sins of those who utter lies, of those who outrage the modesty of preceptor’s wife, and of those who are engaged in insulting the preceptor always.

## \|\| 5.4.13 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*tvadvīryaṃ nihnutaṃ yena puṇyakṣetre ca bhārate \|*  
*sa nā'nvito bhavettatra sevane pūjane tava \|\| 13 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

13\. Let him who has concealed your semen anywhere in the holy centres of Bhārata be debarred from the privilege of serving or worshipping you.

## \|\| 5.4.14 \|\|

*lokapālā ūcuḥ \|*  
*tvadavīryaṃ nihnutaṃ yena pāpinā patitabhramāt \|*  
*bhājanaṃ tasya sotyantaṃ tattapaṃ karma saṃtatim \|\| 14 \|\|*

The guardians of the quarters said:—

14\. Let him who has concealed your semen suffer continuously from the pang as a result of that sinful action.

## \|\| 5.4.15 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*kṛtvā pratijñāṃ yo mūḍho nā''pādayati pūrṇatām \|*  
*bhājanaṃ tasya pāpasya tvadvīryaṃ yena nihnutam \|\| 15 \|\|*

The gods said:—

15\. Let him who has concealed your semen incur the sin of that stupid person who does not fulfil the promise he himself has made.

## \|\| 5.4.16 \|\|

*devapatnya ūcuḥ \|*  
*yā nidati svabhartāraṃ paraṃ gacchati pūruṣam \|*  
*mātṛbandhuvihīnā ca tvadvīryaṃ nihnutaṃ yayā \|\| 16 \|\|*

The wives of the gods said:—

16\. Let her who has concealed your semen be deprived of mother and kinsmen and incur the sin of those base women who hate their husband and carry on an affair with another man.

## \|\| 5.4.17 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*devānāṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā devadeveśvaro haraḥ \|*  
*karmmaṇāṃ sākṣiṇaścāha dharmādīnsabhayaṃ vacaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

17\. On hearing the words of the gods, Śiva the lord of the gods threatened Dharma and others the cosmic witnesses of all activities.

## \|\| 5.4.18 \|\|

*śrīśiva uvāca \|*  
*devairna nihnutaṃ kena tadvīryaṃ nihnutaṃ dhruvam \|*  
*tadamoghaṃ bhagavato maheśasya mama prabhoḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

Lord Śiva said:—

18\. The infallible semen of mine, has not been concealed by the gods. By whom could it then have been concealed?

## \|\| 5.4.19 \|\|

*yūyaṃ ca sākṣiṇo viśve satataṃ sarvakarmaṇām \|*  
*yuṣmākaṃ nihnutaṃ kimvā kiṃ jñātuṃ vaktumarhatha \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. All of you are the witnesses of all actions always. Has it been concealed by you? Have you come to know of it? Please narrate.

## \|\| 5.4.20 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*īśvarasya vacaḥ śrutvā sabhāyāṃ kaṃpitāśca te \|*  
*parasparaṃ samālokya krameṇocuḥ purāḥ prabhoḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. On hearing the words of Śiva they nervously looked at one another and spoke before the lord one by one.

## \|\| 5.4.21 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*rate tu tiṣṭhato vīryaṃ papāta vasudhātale \|*  
*mayā jñātamamoghaṃ tacchaṃkarasya prakopataḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

21\. The infallible semen of Śiva, infuriated at the intervention in the course of his sexual dalliance, fell on the ground. This was observed by me.

## \|\| 5.4.22 \|\|

*\|\| kṣitiruvāca \|*  
*vīryaṃ soḍhumaśaktāhaṃ tadvahno nyakṣipaṃ purā \|*  
*ato'tra durvahaṃ brahmannabalāṃ kṣaṃtumarhasi \|\| 22 \|\|*

The Earth said:—

22\. I was unable to bear the terrible semen. Hence I dropped it into the fire. O lord, please forgive me.

## \|\| 5.4.23 \|\|

*vahniruvāca \|*  
*vīryaṃ soḍhumaśaktohaṃ tava śaṃkara parvate \|*  
*kailāse nyakṣipaṃ sadyaḥ kapotātmā sudussaham \|\| 23 \|\|*

The fire said:—

23\. O Śiva, assuming the form of a dove I gulped the semen but could not bear the terrible thing. Hence I immediately dropped it on the mountain Kailasa.

## \|\| 5.4.24 \|\|

*\|\| giriruvāca \|*  
*vīryaṃ soḍhumaśakto'haṃ tava śaṃkara lokapa \|*  
*gaṃgāyāṃ prākṣipaṃ sadyo dussahaṃ parameśvara \|\| 24 \|\|*

The mountain said:—

24\. O lord of the worlds, I too was unable to bear the terrible thing. O lord, I dropped it in the Gaṅgā.

## \|\| 5.4.25 \|\|

*\|\| gaṃgovāca \|*  
*vīryaṃ soḍhumaśaktāhaṃ tava śaṃkara lokapa \|*  
*vyākulā'ti prabho nātha nyakṣipaṃ śarakānane \|\| 25 \|\|*

Gaṅgā said:—

25\. O lord of the worlds, I too was unable to bear your terrible semen. O lord, completely exhausted, I dropped it in the grove of Sara plants.

## \|\| 5.4.26 \|\|

*\|\| vāyuruvāca \|*  
*śareṣu patitaṃ vīryaṃ sadyo bālo babhūva ha \|*  
*atīva sundaraśśambho svarnadyāḥ pāvane taṭe \|\| 26 \|\|*

Vāyu said:—

26\. O Śiva, the semen that fell among the Śara plants immediately became a very beautiful boy on the holy banks of the celestial river.

## \|\| 5.4.27 \|\|

*sūrya uvāca \|*  
*rudaṃtaṃ bālakaṃ dṛṣṭvā gamamastācalaṃ prabho \|*  
*preritaḥ kālacakreṇa niśāyāṃ sthātumakṣamaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

The sun said:—

27\. On seeing the crying boy, O lord, I went to the western mountain, urged by the revolving wheel of time, being unable to stay there at night.

## \|\| 5.4.28 \|\|

*candra uvāca \|\| rudaṃtaṃ bālakaṃ prāpya gṛhītvā kṛttikāgaṇaḥ \|*  
*jagāma svālayaṃ śaṃbho gacchanbadarikāśramam \|\| 28 \|\|*

The moon said:—

28\. Taking the crying boy, the Kṛttikās returned to their abode. O Śiva, they went to Badarikā hermitage.

## \|\| 5.4.29 \|\|

*jalamuvāca \|*  
*amuṃ rudaṃtamānīya stanyapānena tāḥ prabho \|*  
*varddhayāmāsurīśasya sutaṃ tava raviprabham \|\| 29 \|\|*

The waters said:—

29\. O lord, taking the crying child with them and feeding him with their own breast milk they nurtured your son, as refulgent as the sun.

## \|\| 5.4.30 \|\|

*\|\| saṃdhyovāca \|*  
*adhunā kṛttikānāṃ ca vanaṃ tampoṣya putrakam \|*  
*tannāma cakrustāḥ premṇā kārttikaśceti kautukāt \|\| 30 \|\|*

The dusk said:—

30\. Now, he is the nursling son of the Kṛttikās in the forest. In their eagerness they named him Kārttikeya lovingly.

## \|\| 5.4.31 \|\|

*rātriruvāca \|*  
*na cakrurbālakaṃ tāśca locanānāmagocaram \|*  
*prāṇebhyopi prītipātraṃ yaḥ poṣṭā tasya putrakaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

The night said:—

31\. They never let the boy go out of their sight. He is the object of their love, dearer to them than their own lives. Verily he who nurtures, possesses the son.

## \|\| 5.4.32 \|\|

*dinamuvāca \|*  
*yāni yāni ca vastrāṇi bhūṣaṇāni varāṇi ca \|*  
*praśaṃsitāni svādūni bhojayāmāsureva tam \|\| 32 \|\|*

The day said:—

32\. They fed him on the choicest delicacies. They gave him the rarest garments and excellent ornaments.

## \|\| 5.4.33 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*teṣāṃ tadvacanaṃ śrutvā saṃtuṣṭaḥ purasūdanaḥ \|*  
*mudaṃ prāpya dadau prītyā viprebhyo bahudakṣiṇām \|\| 33 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

33\. On hearing their words, the destroyer of Pura became glad. In his joy he gave monetary gifts to the brahmins.

## \|\| 5.4.34 \|\|

*putrasya vārttāṃ saṃprāpya pārvatī hṛṣṭamānasā \|*  
*koṭiratnāni viprebhyo dadau bahudhanāni ca \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. On receiving the news of her son, Pārvatī was delighted. She distributed a crore of gems and much wealth among the brahmins.

## \|\| 5.4.35 \|\|

*lakṣmī sarasvatī menā sāvitrī sarvayoṣitaḥ \|*  
*viṣṇussarve ca devāśca brāhmaṇebhyo dadurdhanam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Lakṣmī, Sarasvatī, Menā, Sāvitrī and all other women, Viṣṇu and all other gods gave much wealth to the brahmins.

## \|\| 5.4.36 \|\|

*preritassa prabhurdevairmunibhiḥ parvatairatha \|*  
*dūtān prasthāpayāmāsa svaputro yatra tān gaṇān \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Urged by the gods, sages and mountains, the lord sent his Gaṇas as his emissaries to the place where his son was staying.

## \|\| 5.4.37-39 \|\|

*vīrabhadraṃ viśālākṣaṃ śaṃkukarṇaṃ karākramam \|*  
*nandīśvaraṃ mahākālaṃ vajradaṃṣṭraṃ mahonmadam \|\| 37 \|\|*

*gokarṇāsyaṃ dadhimukhaṃ jvaladagniśikhopamam \|*  
*lakṣaṃ ca kṣetrapālānāṃ bhūtānāṃ ca trilakṣakam \|\| 38 \|\|*

*rudrāṃśca bhairavāṃścaiva śivatulyaparākramān \|*  
*anyāṃśca vikṛtākārānasaṃkhyānapi nārada \|\| 39 \|\|*

37-39. O Nārada, he sent Vīrabhadra, Viśālākṣa, Śaṅkukarṇa, Parākrama, Nandīśvara, Mahākāla, Vajradaṃṣṭra, Mahonmada, Gokarṇāsya, Dadhimukha who was comparable to the blazing flame of fire, a hundred thousand Kṣetrapālas, three hundred thousand Bhūtas, Rudras, Bhairavas, and innumerable others of the same exploit as that of Śiva and of hideous features.

## \|\| 5.4.40 \|\|

*te sarve śivadūtāśca nānāśastrāstrapāṇayaḥ \|*  
*kṛttikānāṃ ca bhavanaṃ veṣṭayāmāsuruddhatāḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. All the emissaries of Śiva went and haughtily encircled the abode of the Kṛttikās with various miraculous weapons in their hands.

## \|\| 5.4.41 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā tān kṛttikāssarvā bhayavihnalamānasāḥ \|*  
*kārttikaṃ kathayāmāsurjvalaṃtaṃ brahmatejasā \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. On seeing them the Kṛttikās were extremely terrified. They spoke to Kārttikeya blazing with divine splendour.

## \|\| 5.4.42 \|\|

*\|\| kṛttikā ūcuḥ \|*  
*vatsa sainyānyasaṃkhyāni veṣṭayāmāsurālayam \|*  
*kiṃ kartavyaṃ kva gaṃtavyaṃ mahābhayamupasthitam \|\| 42 \|\|*

Kṛttikās said:—

42\. Dear boy, innumerable soldiers have encircled the house. What shall be done? Where are we to gc. A great danger has beset us.

## \|\| 5.4.43 \|\|

*kārtikeya uvāca \|*  
*bhayaṃ tyajata kalyāṇyo bhayaṃ kiṃ vā mayi sthite \|*  
*durnivāryo'smi bālaśca mātaraḥ kena vāryate \|\| 43 \|\|*

Kārttikeya said:—

43\. O good women, O mothers, cast off your fear. When I am here what fear need you have? Although I am a boy I am invincible. Who can thwart me?

## \|\| 5.4.44 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*etasminnaṃtare tatra sainyendro nandikeśvaraḥ \|*  
*purataḥ kārtikeyasyopaviṣṭassamuvāca ha \|\| 44 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

44\. In the meantime, Nandīśvara the commander-inchief sat in front of Kārttikeya and said.

## \|\| 5.4.45 \|\|

*nandīśvara uvāca \|*  
*bhrātaḥ pravṛttiṃ śṛṇu me mātaraśca śubhāvahām \|*  
*prerito'haṃ maheśena saṃhartrā śaṃkareṇa ca \|\| 45 \|\|*

Nandīśvara said:—

45\. O brother, O mothers, listen to my auspicious mission. I have been commissioned by lord Śiva, the annihilator.

## \|\| 5.4.46 \|\|

*kailāse sarvadevāśca brahmaviṣṇuśivādayaḥ \|*  
*sabhāyāṃ saṃsthitāstāta mahatyutsavamaṃgale \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. O dear, all the gods, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva and others are holding a jubilant conference at Kailāsa.

## \|\| 5.4.47 \|\|

*tadā śivā sabhāyāṃ vai śaṃkaraṃ sarva śaṃkaram \|*  
*sambodhya kathayāmāsa tavānveṣaṇahetukam \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. At that time Pārvatī addressed Śiva the benefactor of all, in that assembly urging a search for you.

## \|\| 5.4.48 \|\|

*papraccha tāñśivo devān kramāttvatprāptihetave \|*  
*pratyuttaraṃ daduste tu pratyekaṃ ca yathocitam \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Śiva asked the assembly severally about you in order to get you back. They too replied in a suitable manner.

## \|\| 5.4.49 \|\|

*tvāmatra kṛttikāsthāne kathayāmāsurīśvaram \|*  
*sarve dharmādayo dharmādharmasya karmasākṣiṇaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. They said to Śiva that you were here in the abode of Kṛttikās. Dharma and others who are the cosmic witnesses of all righteous and unrighteous activities revealed your whereabouts.

## \|\| 5.4.50 \|\|

*prababhūva rahaḥ krīḍā pārvatīśivayoḥ purā \|*  
*dṛṣṭasya ca suraiśśaṃbhorvīryaṃ bhūmau papāta ha \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Formerly Pārvatī and Śiva indulged in their secret sexual dalliance. The semen of Śiva seen by the gods fell on the ground.

## \|\| 5.4.51 \|\|

*bhūmistadakṣipadvahnau vahniścādrau sa bhūdharaḥ \|*  
*gaṃgāyāṃ so'kṣipadvegāt taraṃgaiśśarakānane \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. The earth dropped it into the fire, the fire on the mountain, the mountain in the Gaṅgā and the Gaṅgā transmitted it to the grove of Sara plants by her following currents and waves.

## \|\| 5.4.52 \|\|

*tatra bālo'bhavastvaṃ hi devakāryakṛti prabhuḥ \|*  
*tatra labdhaḥ kṛttikābhistvaṃ bhūmiṃ gaccha sāṃpratam \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. There you developed into a boy, the lord with the mission of fulfilling the task of the gods. There you were picked up by the Kṛttikas. Now you shall come down to the Earth.

## \|\| 5.4.53 \|\|

*tavābhiṣekaṃ śaṃbhustu kariṣyati suraissaha \|*  
*lapsyase sarvaśastrāṇi tārakākhyaṃ haniṣyasi \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Śiva will be crowning you in the company of the gods. You will get miraculous weapons and will slay the demon Tāraka.

## \|\| 5.4.54 \|\|

*putrastvaṃ viśvasaṃharttustvāṃ prāptuñcā'kṣamā imāḥ \|*  
*nāgniṃ goptuṃ yathā śaktaśśuṣkavṛkṣassva koṭare \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. You are the son of the annihilator of the universe and these (Kṛttikas) are impatient to gain possession of you as the dry tree tries to conceal fire within its hollow though it is incapable of holding it.

## \|\| 5.4.55 \|\|

*dīptavāṃstvaṃ ca viśveṣu nāsāṃ geheṣu śobhase \|*  
*yathā patanmahākūpe dvijarājo na rājata \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. You are brilliant enough to illuminate the universe. You do not fit in well in this abode just as a majestic elephant fallen in a deep well does not retain splendour.

## \|\| 5.4.56 \|\|

*karoṣi ca yathā'lokaṃ nā''cchanno'smāsu tejasā \|*  
*yathā sūryaḥ kalāchanno na bhavenmānavasya ca \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. You can shed splendour if your brilliance is not hidden just as the sun illuminates the world only when it is not hidden by the cloud.

## \|\| 5.4.57 \|\|

*viṣṇustvaṃ jagatāṃ vyāpī nānyo jātosi śāṃbhava \|*  
*yathā na keṣāṃ vyāpyaṃ ca tatsarvaṃ vyāpakaṃ nabhaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. In the matter of omnipresence in the universe you alone are Viṣṇu, O Śiva’s son. The all-pervading sky is not pervaded by anything else.

## \|\| 5.4.58 \|\|

*yogīndro nā'nuliptaśca bhāgī cetparipoṣaṇe \|*  
*naiva lipto yathātmā ca karmayogeṣu jīvinām \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. A Yogin is not entangled in the activities of nurturing himself. The soul is not involved in the physical activities.

## \|\| 5.4.59 \|\|

*viśvāraṃbhastvamīśaśca nāsu te saṃbhavet sthitiḥ \|*  
*guṇānāṃ tejasāṃ rāśiryathātmānaṃ ca yoginaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. You are the creator of the universe, you are the lord. Your place is not among these. You are a mass of attributes and splendour as the soul of a Yogin.

## \|\| 5.4.60 \|\|

*bhrātarye tvāṃ na jānaṃti te narā hatabuddhayaḥ \|*  
*nādriyante yathā bhekāstvekavāsāśca paṃkajān \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. O brother, those who do not know you are of damned intellect. Although the toads and lotuses are in the same pond toads are not honoured.

## \|\| 5.4.61 \|\|

*kārttikeya uvāca \|*  
*bhrātassarvaṃ vijānāsi jñānaṃ traikālikaṃ ca yat \|*  
*jñānī tvaṃ kā praśaṃsā te yato mṛtyuñjayāśritaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

Kārttikeya said:—

61\. O brother, you know everything. You are perfectly wise possessing the knowledge of the past, present and future, since you are an attendant of Śiva. Hence no praise of yours is specially called for.

## \|\| 5.4.62 \|\|

*karmaṇāṃ janma yeṣāṃ vā yāsu yāsu yoniṣu \|*  
*tāsu te nirvṛtiṃ bhrātaḥ prāpnuvaṃtīha sāṃpratam \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. O brother, people get reconciled to whatever form of species of life they are born. Their own actions are responsible for their birth and they are satisfied.

## \|\| 5.4.63 \|\|

*kṛttikā jñānavatyaśca yoginyaḥ prakṛteḥ kalāḥ \|*  
*stanyenāsāṃ varddhito'hamupakāreṇa saṃtatam \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. The Kṛttikās are wise women of Yogic practice. They are the digits of Prakṛti. They have helped in nurturing me with their own breast milk.

## \|\| 5.4.64 \|\|

*āsāmahaṃ poṣyaputro madaṃśā yoṣitastvimāḥ \|*  
*tasyāśca prakṛteraṃśāstatastatsvāmivīryajaḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. I am their fostered son. They are my own part and parcel. I am born of Prakṛti and the semen of the lord of Prakṛti.

## \|\| 5.4.65 \|\|

*na madbhaṃgo he śailendrakanyayā nandikeśvara \|*  
*sā ca me dharmato mātā yathemāssarvasaṃmatāḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. O Nandikeśvara, I am not severed from the daughter of the lord of mountains who is virtually my mother just as these ladies on the basis of virtuous rites.

## \|\| 5.4.66 \|\|

*śambhunā preṣitastvaṃ ca śaṃbhoḥ putrasamo mahān \|*  
*āgacchāmi tvayā sārddhaṃ drakṣyāmi devatākulam \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. You have been sent by Śiva. You are like a son unto Śiva. I am coming with you. I shall see the gods.

## \|\| 5.4.67 \|\|

*ityevamuktvā taṃ śīghraṃ saṃbodhya kṛttikāgaṇam \|*  
*kārttikeyaḥ pratasthe hi sārddhaṃ śaṃkarapārṣadaiḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. After saying so and hurriedly taking leave of the Kṛttikās, Kārttikeya started along with the attendants of Śiva.

## Chapter 5 - Kārttikeya is crowned

## \|\| 5.5.1-2 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*etasminnaṃtare tatra dadarśa rathamuttamam \|*  
*adbhutaṃ śobhitaṃ śaśvadviśvakarmavinirmitam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*śatacakraṃ suvistīrṇaṃ manoyāyi manoharam \|*  
*prasthāpitaṃ ca pārvatyā veṣṭitaṃ pārṣadairvaraiḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

1-2. In the meantime he saw an excellent, lustrous and wonderful chariot, made by Viśvakarman. It was a commodious with a hundred wheels. It was beautiful and had the quickness of the mind. It had been sent by Pārvatī and was surrounded by the excellent attendants of Śiva.

## \|\| 5.5.3 \|\|

*samārohattato'naṃto hṛdayena vidūyatā \|*  
*kārttikaḥ parama jñānī parameśānavīryajaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. With an aching heart, Kārttikeya, born of the semen of lord Śiva, the perfectly wise and endless Being, got into it.

## \|\| 5.5.4 \|\|

*tadaiva kṛttikāḥ prāpya muktakeśyaśśucā''turāḥ \|*  
*unmattā iva tatraiva vaktumārebhire vacaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. At the same time, the distressed grief-stricken Kṛttikās approached him with dishevelled hair and began to speak like mad women.

Kṛttikās said'.—

## \|\| 5.5.5 \|\|

*kṛttikā ūcuḥ \|*  
*vihāyā'smān kṛpāsindho gacchasi tvaṃ hi nirdayaḥ \|*  
*nāyaṃ dharmo mātṛvargān pālito yat sutastyajet \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. O ocean of mercy, how is it that you ruthlessly leave us and go? This is not a virtuous thing for a fostered son to forsake his mothers.

## \|\| 5.5.6 \|\|

*snehena varddhito'smābhiḥ putro'smākaṃ ca dharmataḥ \|*  
*kiṃ kurmaḥ kva ca yāsyāmo vayaṃ kiṃ karavāma ha \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. You have been brought up by us affectionately. Hence you are our son in virtue of that. What shall we do? Where shall we go? What can we do?

## \|\| 5.5.7 \|\|

*ityuktvā kṛttikāssarvāḥ kṛtvā vakṣasi kārttikam \|*  
*drutaṃ mūrcchāmavāpustāssutavicchedakāraṇāt \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. After saying this and closely embracing Kārttikeya, the Kṛttikās fell into a swoon due to the imminent separation from their son.

## \|\| 5.5.8 \|\|

*tāḥ kumāro bodhayitvā adhyātmavacanena vai \|*  
*tābhiśca pārṣadaissārddhamāruroha rathaṃ mune \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Restoring them to consciousness and instructing them with spiritual utterances, O sage, he got into the chariot along with them and the Pārṣadas too.

## \|\| 5.5.9 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā śrutvā maṃgalāni bahūni sukhadāni vai \|*  
*kumāraḥ pārṣadaissārddhaṃ jagāma pitṛmandiram \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Seeing and hearing various auspicious and pleasing things Kumāra went to the palace of his father along with the Pārṣadas.

## \|\| 5.5.10 \|\|

*dakṣeṇa naṃdiyuktaśca manoyāyirathena ca \|*  
*kumāraḥ prāpa kailāsaṃ nyagrodhā'kṣayamūlake \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Kumāra reached the foot of a Nyagrodha tree at Kailāsa in the fast chariot along with Nandin seated to his right.

## \|\| 5.5.11 \|\|

*tatra tasthau kṛttikābhiḥ pārṣadapravaraiḥ saha \|*  
*kumāraśśāṃkariḥ prīto nānālīlāviśāradaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. There Kumāra, the son of Śiva, an expert in various divine sports, waited along with the Kṛttikās and the chief of Pārṣadas, in great delight.

## \|\| 5.5.12 \|\|

*tadā sarve suragaṇā ṛṣayaḥ siddhacāraṇāḥ \|*  
*viṣṇunā brahmaṇā sārddhaṃ samācakhyustadāgamam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Then all the gods, sages, Siddhas, Cāraṇas, Viṣṇu and Brahmā announced his arrival.

## \|\| 5.5.13 \|\|

*tadā dṛṣṭvā ca gāṃgeyaṃ yayau pramuditaśśivaḥ \|*  
*anyaissameto hariṇā brahmaṇā ca surarṣibhiḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Then in order to see him Śiva, along with Viṣṇu, Brahmā, the gods, sages and others went there.

## \|\| 5.5.14 \|\|

*śaṃkhāśca bahavo nedurbherī tūryāṇyanekaśaḥ \|*  
*utsavastu mahānāsīddevānāṃ tuṣṭacetasām \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Many conches, Bherīs and Tūryas were sounded. There was great jubilation among the delighted gods.

## \|\| 5.5.15 \|\|

*tadānīmeva taṃ sarve vīrabhadrādayo gaṇāḥ \|*  
*kurvantaḥ svanvayuḥ keliṃ nānātāladharasvarāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Vīrabhadra and other Gaṇas followed them with different chiming cymbols beating the time and sporting about.

## \|\| 5.5.16 \|\|

*stāvakāḥ stūyamānāśca cakruste guṇakīrttanam \|*  
*jayaśabdaṃ namaśśabdaṃ kurvāṇāḥ prītamānasāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Eulogising and being eulogised they sang songs of praise.

## \|\| 5.5.17 \|\|

*draṣṭuṃ yayustaṃ śarajaṃ śivātmajamanuttamam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Shouting cries of “Victory” and “Obeisance” the delighted people went to see the excellent son of Śiva born in the grove of Śara plants.

## \|\| 5.5.18 \|\|

*pārvatī maṃgalaṃ cakre rājamārgaṃ manoharam \|*  
*padmarāgādimaṇibhissaṃskṛtaṃ paritaḥ puram \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Pārvatī caused the entire outskirts of the city fully decorated with Padmarāga and other gems. The main highway was rendered beautiful and auspicious.

## \|\| 5.5.19 \|\|

*patiputravatībhiśca sādhvībhiḥ strībhiranvitā \|*  
*lakṣmyāditriṃśaddevīśca puraḥ kṛtvā samāyayau \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The thirty goddesses Lakṣmī and others stood in front, along with chaste ladies whose husbands and sons were alive and Pārvatī stood ahead of them.

## \|\| 5.5.20 \|\|

*rambhādyapsaraso divyāssa smitā veṣasaṃyutāḥ \|*  
*saṃgītanartanaparā babhūvuśca śivājñayā \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. At the bidding of Pārvatī, the smiling celestial damsels, Rambhā and others, dressed gorgeously, were engaged in singing and dancing.

## \|\| 5.5.21 \|\|

*ye taṃ samīkṣayāmāsurgāgeyaṃ śaṃkaropamam \|*  
*dadṛśuste mahattejo vyāptamāsījjagattraye \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Those who looked at Kumāra resembling Śiva saw a great halo pervading the three worlds.

## \|\| 5.5.22 \|\|

*tattejasā vṛtaṃ bālaṃ taptacāmīkaraprabham \|*  
*vavaṃdire drutaṃ sarve kumāraṃ sūryavarcasam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Immediately they saluted Kumāra who was enveloped by the brilliant halo, the lustre of molten gold and the refulgence of the sun.

## \|\| 5.5.23 \|\|

*jahurṣurvinataskaṃdhā namaśśabdaratāstadā \|*  
*parivāryopatasthuste vāmadakṣiṇamāgatāḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. With shoulders stooping down and eagerly engaged in shouting the cry of “Obeisance” they flanked him to the right and left and stood by.

## \|\| 5.5.24 \|\|

*ahaṃ viṣṇuśca śakraśca tathā devādayo'khilāḥ \|*  
*daṇḍavatpatitā bhūmau parivāryya kumārakam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Viṣṇu, Indra and I as well as the gods prostrated on the ground and went round Kumāra.

## \|\| 5.5.25 \|\|

*etasminnantare śaṃbhurgirijā ca mudānvitā \|*  
*mahotsavaṃ samāgamya dadarśa tanayaṃ mudā \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. In the meantime Śiva, and Pārvatī highly delighted and jubilant came there and saw their son.

## \|\| 5.5.26 \|\|

*putraṃ nirīkṣya ca tadā jagadekabaṃdhuḥ prītyānvitaḥ paramayā parayā bhavānyā \|*  
*snehānvito bhujagabhogayuto hi sākṣātsarveśvaraḥ parivṛtaḥ pramathaiḥ pareśaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. On seeing his son, the great lord Śiva, the sole kinsman of the universe along with the great goddess Pārvatī was filled with pleasure and love—the lord who wore snakes on his body and was surrounded by the Pramathas.

## \|\| 5.5.27 \|\|

*atha śaktidharaḥ skandau dṛṣṭvā tau pārvatīśivau \|*  
*avaruhya rathāttūrṇaṃ śirasā praṇanāma ha \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. On seeing Pārvatī and Śiva, Kārttikeya got down from the chariot immediately and saluted them.

## \|\| 5.5.28 \|\|

*upaguhya śivaḥ prītyā kumāraṃ mūrdhni śaṃkaraḥ \|*  
*jaghrau premṇā parameśānaḥ prasannaḥ snehakartṛkaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Embracing him with love, Śiva kissed Kumāra on the head. He, the cause of great affection, was highly delighted.

## \|\| 5.5.29 \|\|

*upaguhya guhaṃ tatra pārvatī jātasaṃbhramā \|*  
*prasnutaṃ pāyayāmāsa stanaṃ snehapariplutā \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Embracing him in great excitement and melting with love, Pārvatī suckled him at her breasts.

## \|\| 5.5.30 \|\|

*tadā nīrājito devaissakalatrairmudānvitaiḥ \|*  
*jayaśabdena mahatā vyāptamāsīnnabhastalam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. The Nīrājana rite was performed by the delighted gods in the company of their wives.

## \|\| 5.5.31 \|\|

*ṛṣayo brahmaghoṣeṇa gītenaiva ca gāyakāḥ \|*  
*vādyaiśca bahavastatropatasthuśca kumārakam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. The sages adored Kumāra with the Vedic chants, the musicians by singing songs, and others by playing upon musical instruments.

## \|\| 5.5.32 \|\|

*svamaṃkamāropya tadā maheśaḥ kumārakaṃ taṃ prabhayā samujjvalam \|*  
*babhau bhavānīpatireva sākṣācchriyā'nvitaḥ putravatāṃ variṣṭhaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Placing Kumāra shining with brilliant lustre on his lap Pārvatī shone with glory as the greatest among women who carried sons.

## \|\| 5.5.33 \|\|

*kumāraḥ svagaṇaiḥ sārddhamājagāma śivālayam \|*  
*śivājñayā mahotsāhaissaha devairmahāsukhī \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. At the bidding of Śiva, Kumāra in the company of his Gaṇas came to Śiva’s abode. He felt very happy in the company of jubilant gods.

## \|\| 5.5.34 \|\|

*daṃpatī tau tadā tatraikapadyena virejatuḥ \|*  
*vivaṃdyamānāvṛṣibhirāvṛtau surasattamaiḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. The couple shone simultaneously being saluted by the sages and surrounded by the important gods.

## \|\| 5.5.35 \|\|

*kumāraḥ krīḍayāmāsa śivotsaṃge mudānvitaḥ \|*  
*vāsukiṃ śivakaṃṭhasthaṃ pāṇibhyāṃ samapīḍayat \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Kumāra delightedly played about in the lap of Śiva. He teased Vāsuki round Śiva’s neck with his hands.

## \|\| 5.5.36 \|\|

*prahasya bhagavāñ śaṃbhuśśaśaṃsa girijāṃ tadā \|*  
*nirīkṣya kṛpayā dṛṣṭyā kṛpālurlīlayākṛtim \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Seeing that sportive act with his merciful vision, lord Śiva spoke about it to Pārvatī laughingly.

## \|\| 5.5.37 \|\|

*madasmitena ca tadā bhagavānmaheśaḥ prāpto mudaṃ ca paramāṃ girijāsametaḥ \|*  
*premṇā sa gadgadagiro jagadekabaṃdhurnovāca kiṃcana vibhurbhuvanaikabharttā \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Seeing the gentle smile of Kumāra, lord Śiva and Pārvatī attained great joy. The lord, the sole ruler of the worlds and kinsman of the universe uttered nothing with his throat choked through affection.

## \|\| 5.5.38 \|\|

*atha śaṃbhurjagannātho hṛṣṭo laukikavṛttavān \|*  
*ratnasiṃhāsane ramye vāsayāmāsa kārttikam \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Then Śiva, the lord of the universe, following the worldly convention delightedly placed Kārttikeya on a beautiful gemset throne.

## \|\| 5.5.39 \|\|

*vedamaṃtrābhipūtaiśca sarvatīrthodapūrṇakaiḥ \|*  
*sadratnakuṃbhaśatakaiḥ snāpayā māsa taṃ mudā \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. With hundreds of gemset pots filled with the waters of holy centres sanctified by Vedic mantras he performed his ceremonial ablution joyously.

## \|\| 5.5.40 \|\|

*sadratnasāraracitakirīṭamukuṭāṃgadam \|*  
*vaijayantī svamālāṃ ca tasmai cakraṃ dadau hariḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Viṣṇu gave him a crown, a coronet and bracelets moulded and set in gems, his own necklace Vaijayanti and the discus.

## \|\| 5.5.41 \|\|

*śūlaṃ pinākaṃ paraśuṃ śakti pāśupataṃ śaram \|*  
*saṃhārāstraṃ ca paramāṃ vidyāṃ tasmai dadau śivaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Śiva gave him the trident, the bow Pināka, the axe, the arrow Paśupata, the weapon of destruction and the greatest lore.

## \|\| 5.5.42 \|\|

*adāmahaṃ yajñasūtraṃ vedāṃśca vedamātaram \|*  
*kamaṇḍaluṃ ca brahmāstraṃ vidyāṃ caivā'rimardinīm \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. I gave him the holy thread, the Vedas, the mantra Gāyatrī, the vessel Kamaṇḍalu, the arrow Brahmāstra and the lore that destroys the enemy.

## \|\| 5.5.43 \|\|

*gajendraṃ caiva vajraṃ ca dadau tasmai sureśvaraḥ \|*  
*śvetacchatraṃ ratnamālāṃ dadau vastuṃ jaleśvaraḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Then Indra gave him a lordly elephant and a thunderbolt. The lord of the waters, Varuṇa, gave him a white umbrella and a necklace of gems to wear.

## \|\| 5.5.44 \|\|

*manoyāyirathaṃ sūryassannāhaṃ ca mahācayam \|*  
*yamadaṃḍaṃ yamaścaiva sudhākuṃbhaṃ sudhānidhiḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. The sun gave him a chariot as fast as the mind and a coat of mail with great equipments; Yama his own staff: the moon a vessel full of nectar.

## \|\| 5.5.45 \|\|

*hutāśano dadau prītyā mahāśaktiṃ svasūnave \|*  
*dadau svaśastraṃ nirṛtirvāyavyāstraṃ samīraṇaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Agni lovingly gave him a spear; Nirṛti his own weapon and the wind his own weapon.

## \|\| 5.5.46 \|\|

*gadāṃ dadau kuberaśca śūlamīśo dadau mudā \|*  
*nānāśastrāṇyupāyāṃśca sarve devā dadurmudā \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Kubera gave him a mace; Śiva a spear; the gods different kinds of weapons and implements.

## \|\| 5.5.47 \|\|

*kāmāstraṃ kāmadevo'tha dadau tasmai mudānvitaḥ \|*  
*gadāṃ dadau svavidyāśca tasmai ca parayā mudā \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. The delighted lord of Kāma gave him the weapon of love, a club and his own lore with great pleasure.

## \|\| 5.5.48 \|\|

*kṣīrodo'mūlyaratnāni viśiṣṭaṃ ratnanūpuram \|*  
*himālayo hi divyāni bhūṣaṇānyaṃśukāni ca \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. The ocean of milk gave him valuable gems and a splendid anklet set with gems. Himavat gave him divine ornaments and garments.

## \|\| 5.5.49 \|\|

*citrabarhaṇanāmānaṃ svaputraṃ garuḍo dadau \|*  
*aruṇastāmracūḍākhyaṃ balinaṃ caraṇāyudham \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Garuḍa gave him his own son Citrabarhaṇa; Aruṇa a powerful cock Tāmracūḍa.

## \|\| 5.5.50 \|\|

*pārvatī sasmitā hṛṣṭā paramaiśvaryamuttamam \|*  
*dadau tasmai mahāprītyā ciraṃjīvitvameva ca \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Pārvatī gave him power and prosperity smilingly and joyously. She gave him longevity too with great pleasure.

## \|\| 5.5.51 \|\|

*lakṣmīśca saṃpadaṃ divyāṃ mahāhāraṃ manoharam \|*  
*sāvitrī siddhavidyāṃ ca samastāṃ pradadau mudā \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Lakṣmī gave him divine wealth and a great and beautiful necklace. Sāvitrī gave him the entire Siddhavidyā with joy.

## \|\| 5.5.52 \|\|

*anyāścāpi mune devyo yāyāstatra samāgatāḥ \|*  
*svātmavatsu dadustasmai tathaiva śiśupālikāḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. O sage, the other goddesses too who had come there gave him their respective presents. The Kṛttikās too did the same.

## \|\| 5.5.53 \|\|

*mahāmahotsavastatra babhūva munisattama \|*  
*sarve prasannatāṃ yātā viśeṣācca śivāśivau \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. O excellent sage, there was great jubilation there. Everyone was delighted, especially Pārvatī and Śiva.

## \|\| 5.5.54 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare kāle provāca prahasan mudā \|*  
*mune brahmādikān devān rudro bhargaḥ pratāpavān \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. In the meantime, O sage, the powerful Śiva, spoke to Brahmā and to other gods laughingly and joyously.

## \|\| 5.5.55 \|\|

*śiva uvāca \|*  
*he hare he vidhe devāssarve śṛṇuta madvacaḥ \|*  
*sarvathāhaṃ prasannosmi varānvṛṇuta aicchikān \|\| 55 \|\|*

Śiva said:—

55\. “O Viṣṇu, O Brahmā, O gods, you listen to my words. I am delighted in all respects. Please choose the boons you wish.”

## \|\| 5.5.56 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*tacchrutvā vacanaṃ śaṃbhormuneviṣṇvādayassurāḥ \|*  
*sarve procuḥ prasannāsyā devaṃ paśupatiṃ prabhum \|\| 56 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

56\. O sage, on hearing those words of Śiva, Viṣṇu and other gods spoke to Śiva with faces beaming with pleasure.

## \|\| 5.5.57 \|\|

*kumāreṇa hato hyeṣa tārako bhavitā prabho \|*  
*tadarthameva saṃjātamidaṃ caritamuttamam \|\| 57 \|\|*

The gods said:—

57\. “O lord, Tāraka will certainly be killed by Kumāra. It is for that purpose that he is born.

## \|\| 5.5.58 \|\|

*tasmādadyaiva yāsyāmastārakaṃ hantumudyatā \|*  
*ājñāṃ dehi kumārāya sa taṃ haṃtuṃ sukhāya naḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Hence in our effort to kill him we shall start this very day. Please give your directions to Kumāra. Let him slay Tāraka for our happiness.

## \|\| 5.5.59 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*tatheti matvā sa vibhurdattavāṃstanayaṃ tadā \|*  
*devebhyastārakaṃ haṃtuṃ kṛpayā paribhāvitaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Thinking that it shall be so, lord Śiva entrusted his son to the gods in order to kill Tāraka, urged by his mercy that he was.

## \|\| 5.5.60 \|\|

*śivājñayā surāssarve brahmaviṣṇumukhāstadā \|*  
*puraskṛtya guhaṃ sadyo nirjagmurmilitā gireḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. At the bidding of Śiva, Brahmā, Viṣṇu and other gods jointly started from the mountain keeping Kumāra in front.

## \|\| 5.5.61 \|\|

*bahirnissṛtya kailāsāttvaṣṭā śāsanato hareḥ \|*  
*virece nagaraṃ ramyamadbhutaṃ nikaṭe gireḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. After coming out of Kailasa, at the behest of Viṣṇu, Tvaṣṭṛ built a wonderfully fine city very near the mountain.

## \|\| 5.5.62 \|\|

*tatra ramyaṃ gṛhaṃ divyamadbhutaṃ paramo jjvalam \|*  
*guhārthaṃ nirmame tvaṣṭā tatra siṃhāsanaṃ varam \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. There he built a divine, exquisite and wonderfully brilliant house for Kumāra. Tvaṣṭṛ set up an excellent throne there.

## \|\| 5.5.63 \|\|

*tadā harissudhīrbhaktyā kārayāmāsa maṃgalam \|*  
*kārttikasyābhiṣekaṃ hi sarvatīrthajalaissuraiḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. The intelligent Viṣṇu performed the auspicious ceremony of crowning Kārttikeya in the company of the gods by means of waters from all holy centres.

## \|\| 5.5.64 \|\|

*sarvathā samalaṃkṛtya vāsayāmāsa saṃgraham \|*  
*kārttikasya vidhiṃ prītyā kārayāmāsa cotsavam \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. He bedecked Kārttikeya in every manner and dressed him gorgeously. He went through the ceremony in brief and made everyone celebrate the event with pleasure.

## \|\| 5.5.65 \|\|

*brāhmāṃḍādhipatitvaṃ hi dadau tasmai mudā hariḥ \|*  
*cakāra tilakaṃ tasya samānarca suraissaha \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Viṣṇu joyously gave him the suzerainty of the universe. He applied the Tilaka mark and worshipped him along with the gods.

## \|\| 5.5.66 \|\|

*praṇamya kārttikaṃ prītyā sarvadevarṣibhissaha \|*  
*tuṣṭāva vividhasstotraiḥ śivarūpaṃ sanātanam \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Bowing to Kārttikeya with pleasure along with the gods and sages he eulogised the eternal form of Śiva with various hymns.

## \|\| 5.5.67 \|\|

*varasiṃhāsanastho hi śuśubhe'tīva kārtikaḥ \|*  
*svāmibhāvaṃ samāpanno brahmāṃḍasyāsi pālakaḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Karttikeya seated in the excellent throne and assuming the lordship and protectorate of the universe shone extremely well.

## Chapter 6 - The miraculous feat of Kārttikeya

## \|\| 5.6.1 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*atha tatra sa gāṃgeyo darśayāmāsa sūtikām \|*  
*tāmeva śṛṇu suprītyā nārada tvaṃ svabhaktidām \|\| 1 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

1\. There Kumāra showed a miraculous feat. O Nārada, listen to it that bestows devotion.

## \|\| 5.6.2 \|\|

*dvija eko nāradākhya ājagāma tadaiva hi \|*  
*tatrādhvarakaraḥ śrīmāñśaraṇārthaṃ guhasya vai \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Then a certain brahmin Nārada came there, seeking refuge in Kumāra. He was glorious and had been performing a sacrifice.

## \|\| 5.6.3 \|\|

*sa vipraḥ prāpya nikaṭaṃ kārttikasya prasannadhīḥ \|*  
*svābhiprāyaṃ samācakhyau supraṇamya śubhaiḥ stavaiḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Approaching Kumāra, bowing to and eulogising him with auspicious hymns the delighted brahmin related his tale.

## \|\| 5.6.4 \|\|

*\|\| vipra uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu svāminvaco medya kaṣṭaṃ me vinivāraya \|*  
*sarvabrahmāṃḍanāthastvamataste śaraṇaṃ gataḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

The brahmin said:—

4\. O lord, listen to my words. Relieve my distress. You are the lord of the universe. I seek refuge in you.

## \|\| 5.6.5 \|\|

*ajamedhādhvaraṃ kartumāraṃbhaṃ kṛtavānaham \|*  
*so'jo gato gṛhānme hi troṭayitvā svabaṃdhanam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. I began a goat sacrifice. The goat got loosened and strayed away from my house.

## \|\| 5.6.6 \|\|

*na jāne sa gataḥ kutrā'nveṣaṇaṃ tatkṛtaṃ bahu \|*  
*na prāpto'tassa balavān bhaṃgo bhavati me kratoḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. I do not know where it has gone. I have searched for it here and there but have not found it. Hence this will cause a serious default in my sacrifice.

## \|\| 5.6.7 \|\|

*tvayi nāthe sati vibho yajñabhaṃgaḥ kathaṃ bhavet \|*  
*vicāryyaivā'khileśāna kāma pūrṇaṃ kuruṣva me \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. While you are the lord, how can there be an obstacle to my sacrifice? O lord, after pondering over this matter please fulfil my task.

## \|\| 5.6.8 \|\|

*tvāṃ vihāya śaraṇyaṃ kaṃ yāyāṃ śivasuta prabho \|*  
*sarvabrahmāṃḍanāthaṃ hi sarvāmarasusevitam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. O lord, O son of Śiva, who else can I approach except you, who are worthy of being resorted to, who are the lord of the entire universe and are served by all the gods.

## \|\| 5.6.9-10 \|\|

*dīnabaṃdhurdayāsindhussusevyā bhaktavatsalaḥ \|*  
*haribrahmādidevaiśca sustutaḥ parameśvaraḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*pārvatīnandanasskandaḥ paramekaḥ paraṃtapaḥ \|*  
*paramātmā'tmadassvāmī satāṃ ca śaraṇārthinām \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. You are the kinsman of the distressed. You are worthy of being served well. You are favourably disposed to your devotees. You are the great lord eulogised by Viṣṇu, Brahmā and other gods. You are Skanda the delighter of Pārvatī, the sole destroyer of enemies, the great soul, the lord who bestows his own self upon the good seeking refuge in him.

## \|\| 5.6.11 \|\|

*dīnānātha maheśa śaṃkarasuta trailokyanātha prabho māyādhīśa samāgato'smi śaraṇaṃ māṃ pāhi viprapriya \|*  
*tvaṃ sarvaprabhupriyaḥ khilavidabrahmādidevaistutastvaṃ māyākṛtirātmabhaktasukhado rakṣāparo māyikaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. O lord of the distressed, O great lord, O son of Śiva, O lord of the three worlds, O master of magical art, I have to seek refuge in you. O favourite of the brahmins, save me. You are the lord of all. You are eulogised by Brahmā and other gods who bow to you. You have assumed forms through magical art. You are the bestower of happiness to your devotees. You are eager to protect. You wield power of deluding others.

## \|\| 5.6.12 \|\|

*bhaktaprāṇaguṇākarastriguṇato bhinnosi śaṃbhupriyaḥ śaṃbhuḥ śaṃbhusutaḥ prasannasukhadassaccitsvarūpo mahān \|*  
*sarvajñastripuraghnaśaṃkarasutaḥ satpremavaśyassadā ṣaḍvaktraḥ priyasādhurānatapriyassarveśvara śśaṃkaraḥ \|*  
*sādhudrohakaraghna śaṃkaraguro brahmāṃḍanātho prabhuḥ sarveṣāmamarādisevitapado māṃ pāhi sevāpriya \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. You love devotees as your own vital air. You are the receptacle of all attributes. You are beyond three attributes. You are the beloved of Śiva. You are Śiva Himself. You confer welfare. You are the bestower of happiness with delight. You are the great Existent and cosmic consciousness. You are the son of Śiva, the omniscient who ḍestroyed the three cities of Asuras. You are always subservient to great and pious love. You have six faces. You love the saintly persons who kneel to you. You are the lord of all people and their benefactor. You destroy those, who harass the good. You are the preceptor of even Śiva. You are the lord of the entire universe. Your feet are served by all the gods. O lover of service, save me.

## \|\| 5.6.13 \|\|

*vairibhayaṃkara śaṃkara janaśaraṇasya vande tava padapadmaṃ sukhakaraṇasya \|*  
*vijñaptiṃ mama karṇe skanda nidhehi nijabhaktiṃ janacetasi sadā vidhehi \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. O Skanda, terrible to the enemies, the benefactor of the devotees, I bow to your lotus-like feet. You are the refuge of people and source of their happiness. Please hear my submission through your ears. Please instil into the heart of everyone the feelings of devotion to you.

## \|\| 5.6.14 \|\|

*karoti kiṃ tasya balī vipakṣo dakṣo'pi pakṣobhayāpārśvaguptaḥ \|*  
*kintakṣakopyāmiṣabhakṣako vā tvaṃ rakṣako yasya sadakṣamānaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. If you are the protector with efficient honour what harm can an opponent do even if he be strong and efficient and protected on either side? What harm can even Takṣaka or even a carnivorous animal do unto him.

## \|\| 5.6.15 \|\|

*vibudhagururapi tvāṃ stotumīśo na hi syātkathaya kathamahaṃ syāṃ maṃdabuddhirvarārcyaḥ \|*  
*śuciraśuciranāryo yādṛśastādṛśo vā padakamala parāgaṃ skanda te prārthayāmi \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Even the preceptor of the gods cannot eulogise you adequately. Then tell me, how can I a foolish and wretched creature? O Skanda, pure or impure, noble or ignoble, of whatever nature I be, I pray unto the dust of your lotus-like feet.

## \|\| 5.6.16 \|\|

*he sarveśvara bhaktavatsala kṛpāsindho tvadīyo'smyahaṃ bhṛtyassvasya na sevakasya gaṇapasyā'' gaśśataṃ satprabho \|*  
*bhaktiṃ kvāpi kṛtāṃ manāgapi vibho jānāsi bhṛtyārtihā \|*  
*tvatto nāstyaparo'vitā na bhagavan matto naraḥ pāmaraḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. O lord of all, ocean of mercy, favourably disposed to devotees, I am your own servant. May even a hundred sins of your own servant or a leader of the Gaṇas be forgiven. O lord, you know even the slightest act of devotion done anywhere. You are the destroyer of the distress of your servants. O lord, there is no other protector save you and no other wretched vulgar person than I.

## \|\| 5.6.17 \|\|

*kalyāṇakarttā kalikalmaṣaghnaḥ kuberabandhuḥ karuṇārdracittaḥ \|*  
*triṣaṭkanetro rasavaktraśobhī yajñaṃ prapūrṇaṃ kuru me guha tvam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. O lord, you are the cause of welfare, the destroyer of the sins of Kali age and a friend of Kubera. Your heart melts with pity. You have twelve eyes and you shine with six faces. Please make my sacrifice complete and perfect.

## \|\| 5.6.18 \|\|

*rakṣakastvaṃ trilokasya śaraṇāgatavatsalaḥ \|*  
*yajñakarttā yajñabharttā harase vighnakāriṇām \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. You are the protector of the three worlds, favourite of those who seek refuge in you. You are the performer and sustainer of sacrifices. You remove those who bring in obstacles.

## \|\| 5.6.19 \|\|

*vighnavāraṇa sādhūnāṃ sarga kāraṇa sarvataḥ \|*  
*pūrṇaṃ kuru mameśāna sutayajña namostu te \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. O warder of obstacles, the cause of the creation of the good in every respect, O son of Īśāna, please make my sacrifices complete. Obeisance be to you,

## \|\| 5.6.20 \|\|

*sarvatrātā skanda hi tvaṃ sarvajñātā tvameva hi \|*  
*sarveśvarastvamīśāno niveśasakalā'vanaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. O Skanda, you are the protector of all, the knower of all and the lord of all and Īśāna. By your penetration you protect all.

## \|\| 5.6.21 \|\|

*saṃgītajñastvamevāsi vedavijñaḥ paraḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*sarvasthātā vidhātā tvaṃ devadevassatāṃ gatiḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. You alone are the knower of music, the great lord and knower of the Vedas. You are all-in-all, the creator, the lord of the gods and the goal of the good.

## \|\| 5.6.22 \|\|

*bhavānīnandanaśśaṃbhutanayo vayunaḥ svarāṭ \|*  
*dhyātā dhyeyaḥ pitṝṇāṃ hi pitā yoniḥ sadātmanām \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. You are the joy of Pārvatī, the son of Śiva. You are the perfect wisdom, the self-ruler, the meditator and the object of meditation. You are the father of the fathers and the source of origin of good souls.

## \|\| 5.6.23 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya vacastasya devasamrāṭ śivātmajaḥ \|*  
*svagaṇaṃ vīrabāhvākhyaṃ preṣayāmāsa tatkṛte \|\| 23 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

23\. On hearing his words, Śiva’s son, the emperor of the gods, sent his attendant Vīrabāhu on that mission.

## \|\| 5.6.24 \|\|

*tadājñayā vīrabāhustadanveṣaṇahetave \|*  
*praṇamya svāminaṃ bhaktyā mahāvīro drutaṃ yayau \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. At his bidding, the great hero Vīrabāhu who bowed to his master with devotion started in search of it.

## \|\| 5.6.25 \|\|

*anveṣaṇaṃ cakārāsau sarvabrahmāṇḍagolake \|*  
*na prāpa tamajaṃ kutra śuśrāva tadupadravam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. He searched throughout the universe but nowhere did he find the goat (although) he heard about the havoc done by it.

## \|\| 5.6.26 \|\|

*jagāmā'tha sa vaikuṃṭhaṃ tatrā'jaṃ pradadarśa tam \|*  
*upadravaṃ prakurvantaṃ galayūpaṃ mahābalam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Then he went to Vaikuṇṭha where he saw the powerful goat working havoc with the sacrificial stake tied to its neck.

## \|\| 5.6.27 \|\|

*dhṛtvā taṃ śṛṃgayo vīro dharṣayitvā tivegataḥ \|*  
*ānināya svāmipuro vikurvaṃtaṃ ravaṃ bahu \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. The hero dragged it catching hold of its horns and brought it quickly before his lord even as it was bleating loudly.

## \|\| 5.6.28 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā taṃ kārtikasso'ramāruroha sa taṃ prabhuḥ \|*  
*dhṛtabrahmāṇḍagarimā mahāsūtikaro guhaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. On seeing it, lord Kārttikeya who could carry the weighty universe, and the worker of great miracles, quickly rode on it.

## \|\| 5.6.29 \|\|

*muhūrtamātratasso'jo brahmāṃḍaṃ sakalaṃ mune \|*  
*babhrāma śrama evāśu punastatsthānamāgataḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Within a Muhūrta, O sage, the goat walked round the universe and without exhaustion returned to the same place.

## \|\| 5.6.30 \|\|

*tata uttīrya sa svāmī samuvāsa svamāsanam \|*  
*so'jaḥ sthitastu tatraiva sa nārada uvāca tam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Then the lord got down and resumed his seat. The goat stood there itself. Then the brahmin Nārada told the lord.

## \|\| 5.6.31 \|\|

*\|\| nārada uvāca \|*  
*namaste deva deveśa dehi me'jaṃ kṛpānidhe \|*  
*kuryāmadhvaramānandātsakhāyaṃ kuru māmaho \|\| 31 \|\|*

Nārada said:—

31\. Obeisance to you, O lord of gods, O storehouse of mercy, give the goat to me. Let me perform the sacrifice with pleasure. Please assist me as my friend.

## \|\| 5.6.32 \|\|

*\|\| kārttika uvāca \|*  
*vadhayogyo na viprā'jaḥ svagṛhaṃ gaccha nārada \|*  
*pūrṇo'stu te'dhvarassarvaḥ prasādādeva me kṛtaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

Kārttikeya said:—

32\. O brahmin Nārada, this goat does not deserve to be killed. Return home. May your sacrifice be complete. It has been so ordained by my favour.

## \|\| 5.6.33 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya dvijassvāmī vacanaṃ prītamānasaḥ \|*  
*jagāma svālayaṃ dattvā tasmā āśiṣamuttamām \|\| 33 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

33\. On hearing the words of the lord, the brahmin was delighted. He returned home after bestowing his excellent blessings.

## Chapter 7 - Commencement of the War

## \|\| 5.7.1 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*haryyādayassurāste ca dṛṣṭvā taccaritaṃ vibhoḥ \|*  
*suprasannā babhūvurhi viśvāsāsaktamānasāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

1\. On seeing that miraculous feat of Kumāra, Viṣṇu and other gods became delighted. They were convinced of his prowess.

## \|\| 5.7.2 \|\|

*valgaṃtaḥ kurvato nādaṃ bhāvitāśśivatejasā \|*  
*kumārante puraskṛtya tārakaṃ haṃtumāyayuḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Keeping Kumāra at the head, shouting and roaring, purified by Śiva’s splendour they started to attack Tāraka.

## \|\| 5.7.3 \|\|

*devānāmudyamaṃ śrutvā tārako'pi mahābalaḥ \|*  
*sainyena mahatā sadyo yayau yoddhuṃ surān prati \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. When he heard about the preparation of the gods, the powerful Tāraka rushed to fight back the gods with a great army.

## \|\| 5.7.4 \|\|

*devā dṛṣṭvā samāyāṃtaṃ tārakasya mahābalam \|*  
*balena bahukurvantaḥ siṃhanādaṃ visismiyuḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. On seeing the great army of Tāraka approaching, the gods were surprised but roared like lions.

## \|\| 5.7.5 \|\|

*tadā nabho''ṅganā vāṇīṃ jagādopari satvaram \|*  
*śaṅkarapreritā sadyo haryādīnakhilān surān \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Then a celestial voice, prompted by Śiva addressed Viṣṇu and all other gods.

The celestial Voice said;—

## \|\| 5.7.6 \|\|

*\|\| vyomavāṇyuvāca \|*  
*kumāraṃ ca puraskṛtya surā yūyaṃ samudyatāḥ \|*  
*daityānvijitya saṃgrāme jayino'tha bhaviṣyatha \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. O gods, keeping Kumāra at the head you have entered the lists. Defeating the Asuras in the battle, you will be victorious.

## \|\| 5.7.7 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*vācaṃ tu khecarīṃ śrutvā devāssarve samutsukāḥ \|*  
*vīraśabdān prakurvaṃto nirbhayā hyabhavaṃstadā \|\| 7 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

7\. On hearing the celestial voice, the gods became enthusiastic. Fearlessly they roared like heroes.

## \|\| 5.7.8 \|\|

*kumāraṃ ca puraskṛtya sarve te jātasādhvasāḥ \|*  
*yoddhukāmāssurā jagmurmahīsāgarasaṃgamam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. With their fear subsided, and keeping Kumāra ahead, the gods went to the confluence of the river Mahī and the ocean desirous of fighting.

## \|\| 5.7.9 \|\|

*ājagāma drutaṃ tatra yatra devāssa tārakaḥ \|*  
*sainyena mahatā sārddhaṃ surai rbahubhirāvṛt \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Immediately Tāraka, along with a great army, came to the place where the gods stood and was surrounded by them in a body.

## \|\| 5.7.10 \|\|

*raṇaduṃdubhayo neduḥ pralayāṃbudnissvanāḥ \|*  
*karkaśāni ca vādyāni parāṇi ca tadāgame \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Battle drums were sounded as loud as the rumbling sound of the clouds at the dissolution of the world. The harsh musical instruments were also played when he came.

## \|\| 5.7.11 \|\|

*garjamānāstadā daityāstārakeṇasureṇa ha \|*  
*kaṃpayanto bhuvaṃ pādakramairvalgunakārakāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The Asuras in the company of Tāraka roared and shook the ground with their thudding footsteps, leapings and bouncings.

## \|\| 5.7.12 \|\|

*tacchrutvā ravamatyugraṃ sarve devā vinirbhayāḥ \|*  
*aikapadyena cottasthuryoddhukāmāśca tārakam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Undaunted by that terrible noise, the gods simultaneously rose up to fight Tāraka.

## \|\| 5.7.13 \|\|

*gajamāropya devendraḥ kumāraṃ tyagrato'bhavat \|*  
*surasainyena mahatā lokapālaissamāvṛtaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Accompanied by the great army of the gods and the guardians of the quarters, lord Indra seated Kumāra on an elephant and rushed forward.

## \|\| 5.7.14 \|\|

*tadā duṃdubhayo nedurbherītūryāṇyanekaśaḥ \|*  
*vīṇāveṇumṛdaṃgāni tathā gaṃdharvanissvanāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Great war-drums, Dundubhis, Bherīs and Tūryas, lutes, flutes and Mṛdaṅgas were sounded and the Gandharvas sang war songs.

## \|\| 5.7.15 \|\|

*gajaṃ dattvā mahendrāya kumāro yānamāruhat \|*  
*anekāścaryasaṃbhūtaṃ nānāratnasamanvitam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Leaving the elephant to lord Indra, Kumāra got in an aerial chariot of wonderful build and studded with different sets of gems.

## \|\| 5.7.16 \|\|

*vimānamāruhya tadā mahāyaśāssa śāṃkarissarvaguṇairupetaḥ \|*  
*śriyā sametaḥ parayā babhau mahān saṃvījyamānaścamarairmahāgrabhaiḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Seated in the aerial chariot, the son of Śiva endowed with good qualities and of great renown shone with great splendour. He was being fanned with lustrous chowries.

## \|\| 5.7.17 \|\|

*prācetasaṃ chatramatīvasuprabhaṃ ratnairupetaṃ vividhairvirājitam \|*  
*dhṛtaṃ tadā tacca kumāramūrdhni vai hyanantacāndraiḥ kiraṇairmahāprabhaiḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The lustrous umbrella presented by Varuṇa, shining with various gems was held aloft over his head. Beams of light as though of infinite moons shed great lustre around.

## \|\| 5.7.18 \|\|

*militāste tadā sarve devāśśakrapurogamā \|*  
*svaiḥsvairbalaiḥ parivṛtā yuddhakāmā mahābalāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Indra and other gods of great strength, desirous of fighting, joined him with their own divisions of the army.

## \|\| 5.7.19 \|\|

*evaṃ devāśca daityāśca yoddhukāmāḥ sthitā bhuvi \|*  
*sainyena mahatā tena vyūhaṃ kṛtvā pṛthak pṛthak \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The gods and the demons stood in their arrays on the ground with a vast army ready to start the battle.

## \|\| 5.7.20 \|\|

*te sene suradaityānāṃ śuśubhāte parasparam \|*  
*haṃtukāme tadānyonyaṃ stūyamāne ca bandibhiḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. With the bards singing their songs of praise, the armies of the gods and the Asuras shone in their eagerness to pounce on and crush each other.

## \|\| 5.7.21 \|\|

*ubhe senaṃ tadā teṣāmagarjetāṃ vanopame \|*  
*bhayaṃkare'tyavīrāṇāmitareṣāṃ sukhāvahe \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. The two armies as vast as a wild jungle roared. They were terrific to the coward and pleasing to the brave.

## \|\| 5.7.22 \|\|

*etasminnantare tatra balonmattāḥ parasparam \|*  
*daityā devā mahāvīrā yuyudhuḥ krodhavihvalāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. In the meantime the rank and file of the Asuras and the gods, haughty of their strength and blazing with fury came together in a mutual clash.

## \|\| 5.7.23 \|\|

*āsītsutumulaṃ yuddhaṃ devadaityasamākulam \|*  
*ruṇḍamuṃḍāṃkitaṃ sarvaṃ kṣaṇena samapadyata \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. A terrific tumultuous fight between the gods and the Asuras ensued. Within a moment the place was littered with severed heads and headless trunks.

## \|\| 5.7.24 \|\|

*bhūmau nipatitāstatra śataśo'tha sahasraśaḥ \|*  
*nikṛttāṃgā mahāśastrairnihatā vīrasaṃmatāḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Wounded and killed by great weapons, hundreds and thousands of heroic soldiers fell on the ground.

## \|\| 5.7.25 \|\|

*keṣāṃcidbāhavaśchinnā khaḍpātaissudāruṇaiḥ \|*  
*keṣāṃcidūravaśchinnā vīrāṇāṃ mānināṃ mṛdhe \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The arms of some were cut off by terrible blows from swords. Others lost their thighs in the battle of those honourable, heroic people.

## \|\| 5.7.26 \|\|

*kecinmathitasarvāṃgā gadābhirmudgaraistathā \|*  
*kecinnirbhinnahṛdayāḥ pāśairbhallaiśca pātitāḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The entire body of some was smashed by the maces; the chests and hearts of some were pounded by iron clubs; some were felled to the ground by spears and dragged with nooses.

## \|\| 5.7.27 \|\|

*kecidvidāritāḥ pṛṣṭhe kuṃtairṛṣṭibhiraṃkuśaiḥ \|*  
*chinnānyapi śirāṃsyeva patitāni ca bhūtale \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. The backs of some were torn with javelins and goads. Several heads chopped off by double-edged swords fell on the ground.

## \|\| 5.7.28 \|\|

*bahūni ca kabaṃdhāni nṛtyamānāni tatra vai \|*  
*valgamānāni śataśo udyatāstrakarāṇi ca \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Hundreds of headless, limbless trunks were seen dancing and bouncing with arrows sticking to their hands.

## \|\| 5.7.29 \|\|

*nadyaḥ pravartitāstatra śataśo'sṛṅvahāstadā \|*  
*bhūtapretādayastatra śataśaśca samāgatāḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Blood flowed like streams in hundreds of places. Hundreds of ghosts and goblins flocked there.

## \|\| 5.7.30 \|\|

*gomāyavaśśivā tatra bhakṣayantaḥ palaṃ bahu \|*  
*tathā gṛdhravaṭāśyenā vāyasā māṃsabhakṣakāḥ \|*  
*bubhujuḥ patitānāṃ ca palāni subahūni vai \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Jackals and vixens began eating the flesh. Numbers of vultures, kites, crows and carnivorous birds devoured the flesh of those falling down.

## \|\| 5.7.31 \|\|

*etasminnantare tatra tārakākhyo mahābalaḥ \|*  
*sainyena mahatā sadyo yayau yoddhuṃ surān prati \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. In the meantime Tāraka, the demon of great strength, came there with a huge army to fight with the gods.

## \|\| 5.7.32 \|\|

*devā dṛṣṭvā samāyāntaṃ tārakaṃ yuddhadurmadam \|*  
*yoddhukāmaṃ tadā sadyo yayuśśakrādayastadā \|*  
*babhūvātha mahonnādassenayorubhayorapi \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. On seeing the haughty warrior rushing on them, Indra and others, turned against him. Then a tumultuous sound arose from both the armies.

## \|\| 5.7.33 \|\|

*athābhūddvaṃdvayuddhaṃ hi surāsuravimardanam \|*  
*yaṃ dṛṣṭvā harṣitā vīrāḥ klībāśca bhayamāgatā \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Duels were fought by the gods and the Asuras crushing each other, on seeing which heroes were delighted and cowards were terrified.

## \|\| 5.7.34 \|\|

*tārako yuyudhe yuddhe śakreṇa ditijo balī \|*  
*agninā saha saṃhrādo jaṃbhenaiva yamaḥ svayam \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. The Asura Tāraka of great strength fought with Indra, Saṃhrāda with Agni and Yama with Jambha.

## \|\| 5.7.35 \|\|

*mahāprabhurnairṛtena pāśī saha balena ca \|*  
*suvīro vāyunā sārdhaṃ pavamānena guhyarāṭ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Lord Varuṇa fought with Nairṛta and Bala. Suvīra, the king of Guhyas, fought with Vāyu.

## \|\| 5.7.36 \|\|

*īśānena samaṃ śaṃbhuryuyudhe raṇavittamaḥ \|*  
*śuṃbhaśśeṣeṇa yuyudhe kuṃbhaścandreṇa dānavaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Śambhu fought with Īśāna. Śumbha an expert in battle fought with Śeṣa. Kumbha the Asura fought with the Moon.

## \|\| 5.7.37 \|\|

*kuṃbaro mihireṇājau mahābala parākramaḥ \|*  
*yuyudhe paramāstraiśca nānāyuddhaviśāradaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Kuñjara of great strength and exploit, an expert in different kinds of battles, fought with Mihira, using great weapons.

## \|\| 5.7.38 \|\|

*evaṃ dvandvena yuddhena mahatā ca surāsurāḥ \|*  
*saṃgare yuyudhussarve balena kṛtaniśca yāḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Thus the gods and the Asuras, fought duels using their full strength with resolution.

## \|\| 5.7.39 \|\|

*anyonyaṃ sparddhamānāste'marā daityā mahābalāḥ \|*  
*tasmindevāsure yuddhe durjayā abhavanmune \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. O sage, desiring to gain the upper hand and vying with each other, the powerful gods and the Asuras were equally invincible in the battle.

## \|\| 5.7.40 \|\|

*tadā ca teṣāṃ suradānavānāṃ babhūva yuddhaṃ tumulaṃ jayaiṣiṇām \|*  
*sukhāvahaṃ vīramanasvināṃ vai bhayāvahaṃ caiva tathetareṣām \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. The fight between the gods and the Asuras desirous of victory over each other was very tumultuous. It was pleasing to the brave and terrible to the others.

## \|\| 5.7.41 \|\|

*mahī mahāraudratarā vinaṣṭakaissurāsurairvai patitairanekaśaḥ \|*  
*tasminnagamyātibhayānakā tadā jātā mahāsaukhyavahā manasvinām \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. The battle ground became impassable and awful with the corpses of the gods and Asuras lying there in thousands but it was very pleasing to the brave.

## Chapter 8 - The battle between the gods and Asuras

## \|\| 5.8.1 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*iti te varṇitastāta devadānava senayoḥ \|*  
*saṃgrāmastumulo'tīva tatprabhvo śṛṇu nārada \|\| 1 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

1\. O Nārada, O dear, thus I have described to you the fight between the rank and file of both the armies of the gods and Asuras. The fight was very tumultuous. Now listen to the fight between the two leaders on either side.

## \|\| 5.8.2-3 \|\|

*evaṃ yuddhe'titumule devadānavasaṃkṣaye \|*  
*tārakeṇaiva devendraśśaktyā ramayā saha \|\| 2 \|\|*

*sadyaḥ papāta nāgāśca dharaṇyāṃ mūrcchito'bhavat \|*  
*paraṃ kaśmalamāpede vajradhārī sureśvaraḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. In the tumultuous fight that ensued reducing the numbers of the gods and the demons, lord Indra struck by the great spear fell from his elephant and became unconscious. The thunderbolt-bearing lord of gods attained great depression of spirits and swooned.

## \|\| 5.8.4 \|\|

*tathaiva lokapāssarve'suraiśca balavattaraiḥ \|*  
*parājitā raṇe tāta mahāraṇaviśāradaiḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. In the same manner, O dear, the guardians of the quarters, though powerful, were defeated in battle by the Asuras, great experts in warfare.

## \|\| 5.8.5 \|\|

*anye'pi nirjarā daityairyuddhyamānāḥ parājitāḥ \|*  
*asahaṃto hi tattejaḥ palāyanaparāyaṇāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The other gods too were fought and defeated by the Asuras. Unable to bear their ferocity they took to flight.

## \|\| 5.8.6 \|\|

*jagarjurasurāstatra jayinassukṛtodyamāḥ \|*  
*siṃhanādaṃ prakurvantaḥ kolāhalaparāyaṇāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The victorious Asuras, their effort having been successful, roared like lions and raised shouts of jubilation.

## \|\| 5.8.7 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare tatra vīrabhadro ruṣānvitaḥ \|*  
*āsasāda gaṇairvīraistārakaṃ vīramāninam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. In the meantime Vīrabhadra reached the place furiously along with his heroic Gaṇas and approached Tāraka who professed to be a great hero.

## \|\| 5.8.8 \|\|

*nirjarān pṛṣṭhataḥ kṛtvā śivakopodbhavo balī \|*  
*tatsammukho babhūvātha yoddhukāmo gaṇāgraṇīḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The leader of the Gaṇas, the strong one born of the anger of Śiva, kept the gods in the rear and faced Tāraka desirous of fighting him.

## \|\| 5.8.9 \|\|

*tadā te pramathāssarve daityāśca paramotsavāḥ \|*  
*yuyudhussaṃyuge'nyonyaṃ prasaktāśca mahāraṇe \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Then the Pramathas and the jubilant Asuras, fond of great battle, fought one another.

## \|\| 5.8.10 \|\|

*triśūlairṛṣṭibhiḥ pāśaiḥ khaḍgaiḥ paraśupaṭṭiśaiḥ \|*  
*nijaghnussamare'nyonyaṃ raṇe raṇaviśāradāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Skilled adepts in warfare they hit and smashed one another with tridents, double-edged swords, nooses, axes and sharp-edged spikes.

## \|\| 5.8.11 \|\|

*tārako vīrabhadreṇa sa triśūlāhato bhṛśam \|*  
*papāta sahasā bhūmau kṣaṇaṃ mūrchāpariplutaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Immediately after being hit hard with a trident by Vīrabhadra, Tāraka fell unconscious on the ground.

## \|\| 5.8.12 \|\|

*utthāya sa drutaṃ vīrastārako daityasattamaḥ \|*  
*labdhasaṃjño balācchaktyā vīrabhadraṃ jaghāna ha \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Regaining consciousness quickly Tāraka the excellent Asura got up and forcefully hit Vīrabhadra with his spear.

## \|\| 5.8.13 \|\|

*vīrabhadrastathā vīro mahātejā hi tārakam \|*  
*jaghāna triśikhenāśu ghoreṇa niśitena tam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. In the same manner, the heroic Vīrabhadra of great brilliance hit Tāraka with his sharp terrible trident.

## \|\| 5.8.14 \|\|

*sopi śaktyā vīrabhadraṃ jaghāna samare tataḥ \|*  
*tārako ditijādhīśaḥ prabalo vīrasaṃmataḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The powerful king of the Asuras, the heroic Tāraka, hit Vīrabhadra again with spear.

## \|\| 5.8.15 \|\|

*evaṃ saṃyuddhyamānau tau jaghnatuścetaretaram \|*  
*nānāstraśastraissamare raṇavidyāviśāradau \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Fighting each other thus they hit each other with various weapons and missiles both being equally skilful in the art of warfare.

## \|\| 5.8.16 \|\|

*tayormahātmanostatra dvandvayuddhamabhūttadā \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ paśyatāmeva tumulaṃ romaharṣaṇam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Even as others stood gazing, the two of great energy continued their duel causing hair to stand on ends, with tumultuous noise.

## \|\| 5.8.17 \|\|

*tato bherīmṛdaṃgāśca paṭahānakagomukhāḥ \|*  
*vinedurvihatā vīraiśśṛṇvatāṃ subhayānakāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Then various military bands and drums like Bherīs, Mṛdaṅgas, Paṭahas, Āṇakas and Gomukhas were sounded by the soldiers terrifying those who happened to hear.

## \|\| 5.8.18 \|\|

*yuyudhātetisannaddhau prahārairjarjarīkṛtau \|*  
*anyonyamatisaṃrabdhau tau budhāṃgārakāviva \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Both of them were severely wounded by the mutual hits and thrusts but still they continued their fight with added vigour like Mercury and Mars.

## \|\| 5.8.19 \|\|

*evaṃ dṛṣṭvā tadā yuddhaṃ vīrabhadrasya tena ca \|*  
*tatra gatvā vīrabhadramavocastvaṃ śivapriyaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. On seeing the fight between him and Vīrabhadra, you, the favourite of Śiva went there and said to Vīrabhadra,

## \|\| 5.8.20 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*vīrabhadra mahāvīra gaṇānāmagraṇīrbhavān \|*  
*nivartasva raṇādasmādrocate na vadhastvayā \|\| 20 \|\|*

Nārada said:—

20\. “O Vīrabhadra, of great heroism, you are the leader of the Gaṇas. Please desist from this fight. Your killing him does not fit in properly”.

## \|\| 5.8.21 \|\|

*evaṃ niśamya tvadvākyaṃ vīrabhadro gaṇāgraṇīḥ \|*  
*avadatsa ruṣāviṣṭastvāṃ tadā tu kṛtāṃjaliḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. On hearing your words, the leader of the Gaṇas Vīrabhadra became furious but spoke to you with palms joined in reverence.

## \|\| 5.8.22 \|\|

*vīrabhadra uvāca \|*  
*munivarya mahāprājña śṛṇu me paramaṃ vacaḥ \|*  
*tārakaṃ ca vadhiṣyāmi paśya me'dya parākramam \|\| 22 \|\|*

Vīrabhadra said:—

22\. O excellent sage, of great wisdom, listen to my weighty words. I will kill Tāraka. See my exploit today.

## \|\| 5.8.23 \|\|

*ānayaṃti ca ye vīrāssvāminaṃ raṇasaṃsadi \|*  
*te pāpino mahāklībā vinaśyanti raṇaṃ gatāḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. The soldiers who bring their masters to the battlefield are sinners. They are no better than eunuchs. They are doomed in the battle.

## \|\| 5.8.24 \|\|

*asadgatiṃ prāpnuvanti teṣāṃ ca nirayo dhuvam \|*  
*vīrabhadro hi vijñeyo na vācyaste kadācana \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. They will go the way of the wicked. Hell is definitely in store for them. Vīrabhadra should never be considered by you as such a despicable person.

## \|\| 5.8.25 \|\|

*śastrāstrairbhinnagātrā ye raṇaṃ kurvaṃti nirbhayāḥ \|*  
*ihāmutra praśaṃsyāste labhyante sukhamadbhutam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Those whose bodies are rent and split with weapons and missiles, but who still fight fearlessly shall be praised here and hereafter. They derive wonderful happiness.

## \|\| 5.8.26 \|\|

*śṛṇvantu mama vākyāni devā haripurogamāḥ \|*  
*atārakāṃ mahīmadya kariṣye svāmivarjitām \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Let Viṣṇu and other gods listen to my words—I shall make the earth freed of Tāraka today even without bringing my master here.

## \|\| 5.8.27 \|\|

*ityuktvā pramarthaissārddhaṃ vīrabhadro hi śūladhṛk \|*  
*viciṃtya manasā śaṃbhuṃ yuyudhe tārakeṇa hi \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Saying thus and taking up his trident, Vīrabhadra mentally meditated on Śiva and fought with Tāraka, accompanied by Pramathas.

## \|\| 5.8.28 \|\|

*vṛṣārūḍhairanekaiśca triśūlavaradhāribhiḥ \|*  
*mahāvīrastrinetraiśca sa reje raṇasaṃgataḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*
