28\. With many heroic soldiers riding on bulls, wielding the tridents and possessing three eyes he shone well in the midst of that battle.

## \|\| 5.8.29 \|\|

*kolāhalaṃ prakurvaṃto nirbhayāśśataśo gaṇāḥ \|*  
*vīrabhadraṃ puraskṛtya yuyudhurdānavaissaha \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Keeping Vīrabhadra at their head, and shouting fearlessly jubilantly, hundreds of the Gaṇas fought with the Asuras.

## \|\| 5.8.30 \|\|

*asurāste'pi yuyudhustārakāsurajīvinaḥ \|*  
*balotkaṭā mahāvīrā mardayanto gaṇān ruṣā \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. The Asuras too, the dependants of the demon Tāraka, all equally strong and heroic, began to smash the Gaṇas furiously.

## \|\| 5.8.31 \|\|

*punaḥ punaścaiva babhūva saṃgaro mahotkaṭo daityavarairgaṇānām \|*  
*praharṣamāṇāḥ paramāstrakovidāstadā gaṇāste jayino babhūvuḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. The terrific mutual fights between the demons and the Gaṇas happened again and again. Ultimately the Gaṇas, experts in the use of great missiles, came out victorious and were jubilant.

## \|\| 5.8.32 \|\|

*gaṇairjitāste prabalairasurā vimukhā raṇe \|*  
*palāyanaparā jātā vyathitā vyagramānasāḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Defeated by the Gaṇas of great strength, the Asuras turned their faces and began to flee. They were distressed and agitated.

## \|\| 5.8.33 \|\|

*evaṃ bhraṣṭaṃ svasainyaṃ taddṛṣṭvā tatpālako'suraḥ \|*  
*tārako hi ruṣāviṣṭo haṃtuṃ devagaṇān yayau \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. On seeing his army vanishing thus in flight, their protector, the Asura Tāraka, furiously rushed at the gods and the Gaṇas.

## \|\| 5.8.34 \|\|

*bhujānāmayutaṃ kṛtvā siṃhamāruhya vegataḥ \|*  
*pātayāmāsa tāndevāngaṇāṃśca raṇamūrddhani \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. He assumed ten thousand hands and rode on a lion. In the battle that followed he felled the gods and the Gaṇas quickly.

## \|\| 5.8.35-36 \|\|

*sa dṛṣṭvā tasya tatkarma vīrabhadro gaṇāgraṇīḥ \|*  
*cakāra sumahatkopaṃ tadvadhāya mahābalī \|\| 35 \|\|*

*smṛtvā śivapadāṃbhojaṃ jagrāha triśikhaṃ param \|*  
*jajvalustejasā tasya diśaḥ sarvā nabhastathā \|\| 36 \|\|*

35-36. On seeing such a perpetration of Tāraka, Vīrabhadra, the leader of the Gaṇas, became very furious. In order to kill him he took up his trident after remembering the lotuslike feet of Śiva. His brilliance then brightly illuminated all the quarters and the sky.

## \|\| 5.8.37 \|\|

*etasminnantare svāmī vārayāmāsa taṃ raṇam \|*  
*vīrabāhumukhānsadyo mahākautukadarśakaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. In the meantime, the master stopped the war. He prevented Vīrabāhu and others immediately in order to show his own might.

## \|\| 5.8.38 \|\|

*tadājñayā vīrabhadro nivṛtto'bhūdraṇāttadā \|*  
*kopaṃ cakre mahāvīrastārako'suranāyakaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. At his bidding Vīrabhadra returned from the battle. The heroic leader of the Asuras, Tāraka, was still in his unabated fury.

## \|\| 5.8.39 \|\|

*cakāra bāṇavṛṣṭiṃ ca suropari tadā'suraḥ \|*  
*tapto'hvāsītsurānsadyo nānāstraraṇakovidaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Then the Asura showered arrows on the gods and put them to distress. He was skilful in the use of various missiles in the war.

## \|\| 5.8.40 \|\|

*evaṃ kṛtvā mahatkarma tārako'surapālakaḥ \|*  
*sarveṣāmapi devānāmaśakyo balināṃ varaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. After causing a great havoc, Tāraka, the protector of Asuras, the most excellent among the brave, seemed invincible to the gods.

## \|\| 5.8.41 \|\|

*evaṃ nihanyamānāṃstān dṛṣṭvā devān bhayākulān \|*  
*kopaṃ kṛtvā raṇāyāśu saṃnaddho'bhavadacyutaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. On seeing the gods terrified and slaughtered, Viṣṇu became furious and got ready to fight.

## \|\| 5.8.42 \|\|

*cakraṃ sudarśanaṃ śārṅgaṃ dhanurādāya sāyudhaḥ \|*  
*abhyudyayau mahādaityaṃ raṇāya bhagavān hariḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Taking discus Sudarśana, the bow Śārṅga and other weapons with him, lord Viṣṇu rushed to meet the great Asura in the battle.

## \|\| 5.8.43 \|\|

*tatassamabhavadyuddhaṃ haritārakayormahat \|*  
*lomaharṣaṇamatyugraṃ sarveṣāṃ paśyatāṃ mune \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. O sage, a great fight ensued between Viṣṇu and Tāraka. It was very fierce. It caused horripilation to the onlookers.

## \|\| 5.8.44 \|\|

*gadāmudyamya sa harirjaghānāsuramojasā \|*  
*dvidhā cakāra tāṃ daityastriśikhena mahābalī \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Lifting up his club, Viṣṇu hit the Asura with great force but the powerful Asura split it with his trident.

## \|\| 5.8.45 \|\|

*tatassa kruddho bhagavāndevānāmabhayaṃkaraḥ \|*  
*śārṅgacyutaiśśaravyūhairjaghānāsuranāyakam \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. The infuriated lord offering shelter to the gods hit the leader of the Asuras by arrows discharged from his bow.

## \|\| 5.8.46 \|\|

*so'pi daityo mahāvīrastārakaḥ paravīrahā \|*  
*ciccheda sakalānbāṇānsvaśarairniśitairdrutam \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. The heroic Asura Tāraka, the slayer of enemies, immediately split the arrows of the gods by his own sharp arrows.

## \|\| 5.8.47 \|\|

*atha śaktyā jaghānāśu murāriṃ tārakāsuraḥ \|*  
*bhūmau papāta sa haristatprahāreṇa mūrcchitaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. The Asura Tāraka then quickly hit Viṣṇu with his spear. On being hit thus, Viṣṇu fell unconscious on the ground.

## \|\| 5.8.48 \|\|

*jagrāha sa ruṣā cakramutthitaḥ kṣaṇato'cyutaḥ \|*  
*siṃhanādaṃ mahatkṛtvā jvalajjvālāsamākulam \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. In a trice, Viṣṇu got up and in rage seized his discus that was blazing with flames and he roared like a lion.

## \|\| 5.8.49 \|\|

*tena tañca jaghānāsau daityānāmadhipaṃ hariḥ \|*  
*tatprahāreṇa mahatā vyathito nyapatadbhuvi \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Viṣṇu hit the king of Asuras with it. Overwhelmed by the forceful hit he fell on the ground.

## \|\| 5.8.50 \|\|

*punaścotthāya daityendrastārako'suranāyakaḥ \|*  
*ciccheda tvaritaṃ cakraṃ svaśaktyātibalānvitaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Getting up again, the foremost among Asuras and their leader, Tāraka using all his strength immediately split the discus with his spear.

## \|\| 5.8.51 \|\|

*punastayā mahāśaktyā jaghānāmaravallabham \|*  
*acyuto'pi mahāvīrā nandakena jaghāna tam \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Again he struck Viṣṇu the favourite of the gods with that great spear. The heroic Viṣṇu hit him back with Nandaka.

## \|\| 5.8.52 \|\|

*evamanyonyamasuro viṣṇuśca balavānubhau \|*  
*yuyudhāte raṇe bhūri tatrākṣatabalau mune \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. O sage, both Viṣṇu and the Asura, equally powerful, hit each other in the battle with unabated strength.

## Chapter 9 - Boasting of Tāraka and fight between him and Indra, Viṣṇu, Vīrabhadra

## \|\| 5.9.1 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*devadeva guha svāmiñśāṃkare pārvatīsuta \|*  
*na śobhate raṇo viṣṇu tārakāsurayorvṛthā \|\| 1 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

1\. O Guha, O lord of gods, O son of Śiva and Pārvatī, the fight between Viṣṇu and Tāraka is not proper. It is futile.

## \|\| 5.9.2 \|\|

*viṣṇunā na hi vadhyo'sau tārako balavānati \|*  
*mayā dattavarastasmātsatyaṃ satyaṃ vadāmyaham \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Tāraka the powerful cannot be killed by Viṣṇu. He has been granted such a boon by me. It is truth. I am telling you the truth.

## \|\| 5.9.3 \|\|

*nānyo haṃtāsya pāpasya tvāṃ vinā pārvatīsuta \|*  
*tasmāttvayā hi kartavyaṃ vacanaṃ me mahāprabho \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. O son of Pārvatī, none except you can be the slayer of this sinner. O great lord, my words shall be carried out by you.

## \|\| 5.9.4 \|\|

*sannaddho bhava daityasya vadhāyāśu paraṃtapa \|*  
*tadvadhārthaṃ samutpannaḥ śaṃkarāttvaṃ śivāsuta \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. O scorcher of enemies, please get ready to slay him. O son of Pārvatī you are born of Śiva for killing that demon.

## \|\| 5.9.5 \|\|

*rakṣa rakṣa mahāvīra tridaśānvyathitānraṇe \|*  
*na bālastvaṃ yuvā naiva kiṃ tu sarveśvaraḥ prabhuḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. O great hero, save the gods distressed in the battle. You are neither a boy nor a youth but the lord of all.

## \|\| 5.9.6 \|\|

*śakraṃ paśya tathā viṣṇuṃ vyākulaṃ ca surān gaṇān \|*  
*evaṃ jahi mahādaityaṃ trailokyaṃ sukhinaṃ kuru \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. See Indra and Viṣṇu. They are agitated and distressed, So also the gods and the Gaṇas. Slay this great demon. Make the three worlds happy.

## \|\| 5.9.7 \|\|

*anena vijitaścendro lokapālaiḥ purā saha \|*  
*viṣṇuścāpi mahāvīro tarjitastapaso balāt \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Formerly Indra and the guardians of the quarters had been conquered by him. Due to the power of his penance, the heroic Viṣṇu too has been threatened by him.

## \|\| 5.9.8 \|\|

*trailokyaṃ nirjitaṃ sarvamasureṇa durātmanā \|*  
*idānīṃ tava sānnidhyātpunaryuddhaṃ kṛtaṃ ca taiḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The entire universe of the three worlds has been defeated by this wicked Asura. Now, because of your presence, they have fought again.

## \|\| 5.9.9 \|\|

*tasmāttvayā nihaṃtavyastārakaḥ pāpapūruṣaḥ \|*  
*anyavadhyo na caivāyaṃ madvarācchaṃkarātmaja \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Hence, O son of Śiva, this sinful being Tāraka shall be killed by you. Due to the boon granted by me he cannot be slain by any one else.”

## \|\| 5.9.10 \|\|

*\|\|brahmovāca \|*  
*iti śrutvā mama vacaḥ kumāraḥ śaṃkarātmajaḥ \|*  
*vijahāsa prasannātmā tathāstviti vaco'bravīt \|\| 10 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

10\. On hearing these words of mine, Kumāra, son of Śiva, was delighted and he laughed. “So be it”, said he.

## \|\| 5.9.11 \|\|

*viniścityāsuravadhaṃ śāṃkarissa mahā prabhuḥ \|*  
*vimānādavatīryātha padātirabhavattadā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Resolving to kill the Asura, the great lord, son of Śiva got down from the aerial chariot and stood on the ground.

## \|\| 5.9.12 \|\|

*padbhyāṃ tadāsau paridhāvamāno reje'tivīraḥ śivajaḥ kumāraḥ \|*  
*kare samādāya mahāprabhāṃ tāṃ śaktiṃ maholkāmiva dīptidīptām \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Running on foot, seizing his lustrous spear blazing like a meteor, the powerful warrior Kumāra born of Śiva shone well.

## \|\| 5.9.13 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā tamāyātamatipracaṃḍamavyākulaṃ ṣaṇmukhamaprameyam \|*  
*daityo babhāṣe surasattamānsa kumāra eṣa dviṣatāṃ prahaṃtā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. On seeing the incomprehensible six-headed deity coming forward, fierce and unagitated, the Asura spoke to the gods derisively—“O this child indeed will slay the enemies!”

## \|\| 5.9.14 \|\|

*anena sākaṃ hyahamekavīro yotsye ca sarvānahameva vīrān \|*  
*gaṇāṃśca sarvānapi ghātayāmi salokapālānharināyakāṃśca \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. I will fight with him single-handed. I will kill the soldiers, the Gaṇas and the guardians of the quarters led by Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 5.9.15 \|\|

*ityevamuktvā sa tadā mahābalaḥ kumāramuddiśya yayau ca yoddhum \|*  
*jagrāha śaktiṃ paramādbhutāṃ ca sa tārako devavarānbabhāṣe \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Saying thus, the powerful Asura rushed at Kumāra to fight with him. Tāraka seized his wonderful spear and spoke to the gods.

## \|\| 5.9.16 \|\|

*\|\| tāraka uvāca \|*  
*kumāro me'grataścādya bhavadbhiśca kathaṃ kṛtaḥ \|*  
*yūyaṃ gatatrapā devā viśeṣācchakrameśvarau \|\| 16 \|\|*

Tāraka said:—

16\. “How is it that you all kept Kumāra face to face with me? You gods are shameless especially Indra and Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 5.9.17 \|\|

*puraitābhyāṃ kṛtaṃ karma viruddhaṃ vedamārgataḥ \|*  
*tacchṛṇudhvaṃ mayā proktaṃ varṇayāmi viśeṣataḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Formerly, both of them had acted in violation of the Vedic path. Listen. I shall describe the same.

## \|\| 5.9.18 \|\|

*tatra viṣṇuśchalī doṣī hyavivekī viśe ṣataḥ \|*  
*baliryena purā baddhaśchalamāśritya pāpataḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Viṣṇu is deceptive, defective and indiscreet. It was by him that Bali was formerly bound by taking recourse to deception with sinful intention.

## \|\| 5.9.19 \|\|

*tenaiva yatnataḥ pūrvamasurau madhukaiṭabhau \|*  
*śirauhīnau kṛtau dhaurtyādvedamārgo vivarjitaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The Asuras Madhu and Kaiṭabha were beheaded by his roguishness. He forsook the Vedic path.

## \|\| 5.9.20 \|\|

*mohinīrūpato'nena paṃktibhedaḥ kṛto hi vai \|*  
*devāsurasudhāpāne vedamārgo vigarhitaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. When the gods and Asuras sat for drinking the nectar it was he who violated the sanctity of the vows when he assumed the form of an enchantress. Thus he slighted the Vedic path.

## \|\| 5.9.21 \|\|

*rāmo bhūtvā hatā nārī vālī vidhvaṃsito hi saḥ \|*  
*punarvaiśravaṇo viprau hato nītirhatā śruteḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Taking birth as Rama he killed a woman (Tāḍakā). Bālī’s death was brought about by him with a vile trick. A brahmin descendant of Viśravas was killed by him. Thus he violated the injunction of the Śruti.

## \|\| 5.9.22 \|\|

*pāpaṃ vinā svakīyā strī tyaktā pāparatena yat \|*  
*tatrāpi śrutimārgaśca dhvaṃsitassvārthahetave \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Sinful that he was, he forsook his own innocent wife. There too, he violated the path of Śruti for achieving his selfish end.

## \|\| 5.9.23 \|\|

*svajananyāśśiraśchinnamavatāre rasākhyake \|*  
*guruputrāpamānaśca kṛto'nena durātmanā \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. In his sixth incarnation (as Paraśurāma) \[5\] he cut off the head of his own mother. This wicked man insulted his own preceptor’s son.

## \|\| 5.9.24 \|\|

*kṛṣṇo bhūtvānyanāryaśca dūṣitāḥ kuladharmataḥ \|*  
*śrutimārgaṃ parityajya svavivāhāḥ kṛtāstathā \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Incarnating as Kṛṣṇa he defiled the wives of others and forced them to violate the traditional virtues of the family. He contracted his marriages without any reference to the Vedic path.

## \|\| 5.9.25 \|\|

*punaśca vedamārgo hi niṃdito navame bhave \|*  
*sthāpitaṃ nāstikamataṃ vedamārgavirodhakṛt \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Again in his ninth incarnation he slighted the Vedic path and contrary to its principles, preached and established the atheistic philosophy called Buddhism.

## \|\| 5.9.26 \|\|

*evaṃ yena kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ vedamārgaṃ visṛjya vai \|*  
*sa kathaṃ vijayedyuddhe bhaveddharmavatāṃvaraḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. How can he be considered an excellent, virtuous man, how can he be victorious in battle who has committed sin without caring for Vedic cult?

## \|\| 5.9.27 \|\|

*bhrātā jyeṣṭhaśca yastasya śakraḥ pāpī mahānmataḥ \|*  
*tena pāpānyanekāni kṛtāni nijahetutaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Indra, his elder brother, is a greater sinner. He has committed many sins for his self-interest.

## \|\| 5.9.28 \|\|

*nikṛtto hi ditergarbhassvārtha hetorviśeṣataḥ \|*  
*dharṣitā gautamastrī vai hato vṛtraśca viprajaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. To gain his selfish end, by him Diti’s foetus was destroyed;\[8\] the modesty of Gautama’s wife was outraged,\[9\] Vṛtra, the son of a brahmin, was killed.

## \|\| 5.9.29 \|\|

*viśvarūpadvijātervai bhāgineyasya yadguroḥ \|*  
*nikṛttāni ca śīrṣāṇi tadadhvādhvaṃsitaśśruteḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. He beheaded the brahmin Viśvarūpa, the nephew of Bṛhaspati. Thus he transgressed the Vedic path.

## \|\| 5.9.30 \|\|

*kṛtvā bahūni pāpāni hariśśakraḥ punaḥpunaḥ \|*  
*tejobhirvihatāveva naṣṭavīryau viśeṣataḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Doing such sinful acts frequently Viṣṇu and Śiva are already deficient in splendour and their prowess is spent out.

## \|\| 5.9.31 \|\|

*tayorbalena no yūyaṃ saṃgrāme jayamāpsyatha \|*  
*kimarthaṃ mūḍhatāṃ prāpya prāṇāṃstyaktumihāgatāḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. You will never gain victory in the battle by relying on them. Why then did you foolishly come here to lose your lives?

## \|\| 5.9.32 \|\|

*jānantau dharmametau na svārthalaṃpaṭamānasau \|*  
*dharmaṃ vinā'marāḥ kṛtyaṃ niṣphalaṃ sakalaṃ bhavet \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. These two, always seeking selfish ends, do not know what is virtue. O gods, without virtue every rite becomes futile.

## \|\| 5.9.33 \|\|

*mahādhṛṣṭāvimau medya kṛtavaṃtau puraśśiśum \|*  
*ahaṃ bālaṃ vadhiṣyāmi tayosso'pi bhaviṣyati \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. These two impudent fellows are presumptuous enough to place a child in front of me. Why? I will kill the child too. They too will have it.

## \|\| 5.9.34 \|\|

*kiṃ bāla ito yāyāddūraṃ prāṇaparīpsayā \|*  
*ityuktoddiśya ca harī vīrabhadramuvāca saḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. But let the child leave from here and save his life.” After saying this, hinting at Indra and Viṣṇu he turned to Vīrabhadra and said.

## \|\| 5.9.35 \|\|

*purā hatāstvayā viprā dakṣayajñe hyanekaśaḥ \|*  
*tatkarmaṇaḥ phalaṃ cādya darśayiṣyāmi te'nagha \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. “Formerly in the sacrifice of Dakṣa, many brahmins had been killed by you, O sinless one, I shall show you the fruit thereof.”

## \|\| 5.9.36 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityevamuktvā tu vidhūya puṇyaṃ nijaṃ sa tanniṃdanakarmaṇā vai \|*  
*jagrāha śaktiṃ paramādbhutāṃ ca sa tārako yuddhavatāṃ variṣṭhaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

36\. Saying this and dispossessing himself of his own merit by that act of censure, Tāraka the foremost among war-mongers seized his wonderful spear.

## \|\| 5.9.37 \|\|

*taṃ bālāntikamāyātaṃ tārakāsuramojasā \|*  
*ājaghāna ca vajreṇa śakro guhapurassaraḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Indra who was going ahead of Kumāra hit the demon Tāraka forcibly with his thunderbolt as he was approaching the boy.

## \|\| 5.9.38 \|\|

*tena vajraprahāreṇa tārako jarjarīkṛtaḥ \|*  
*bhūmau papāta sahasā niṃdāhatabalaḥ kṣaṇam \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Tāraka was shattered and split by that blow of the thunderbolt, his power being sapped up already by the act of censure. He fell on the ground.

## \|\| 5.9.39 \|\|

*patito'pi samutthāya śaktyā taṃ prāharadruṣā \|*  
*puraṃdaraṃ gajasthaṃ hi pātayāmāsa bhūtale \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Though he fell down, he got up immediately and furiously hit Indra who was seated on an elephant, with his spear and felled him to the ground.

## \|\| 5.9.40 \|\|

*hāhākāro mahānāsītpatite ca puraṃdare \|*  
*senāyāṃ nirjarāṇāṃ hi taddṛṣṭvā kleśa āviśat \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. When Indra fell down there was a great hue and cry. On seeing it a great pain entered the army of the gods.

## \|\| 5.9.41 \|\|

*tārakeṇā'pi tatraiva yatkṛtaṃ karma duḥkhadam \|*  
*svanāśakāraṇaṃ dharmavirudaṃ tannibodha me \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Know from me the vile action that Tāraka has committed against virtue which is sure to bring about his own ruin.

## \|\| 5.9.42 \|\|

*patitaṃ ca padākramya hastādvajraṃ pragṛhya vai \|*  
*punarudvajraghātena śakramātāḍayadbhṛśam \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. He stamped on Indra with his foot after he fell down and seized his thunderbolt with which he hit him with great force.

## \|\| 5.9.43 \|\|

*evaṃ tiraskṛtaṃ dṛṣṭvā śakraviṣṇupratāpavān \|*  
*cakramudyasya bhagavāṃstārakaṃ sa jaghāna ha \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Seeing Indra thus insulted, the powerful lord Viṣṇu lifted his discus and hit Tāraka.

## \|\| 5.9.44 \|\|

*cakraprahārābhito nipapāta kṣitau hi saḥ \|*  
*punarutthāya daityendraśaktyā viṣṇuṃ jaghāna tam \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Hit by the discus he fell on the ground. Getting up again, the lord of the Asuras hit Viṣṇu with his spear.

## \|\| 5.9.45 \|\|

*tena śaktiprahāreṇa patito bhuvi cācyutaḥ \|*  
*karo mahānāsīccukruśuścā'tinirjarāḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. On being hit by the spear Viṣṇu fell on the ground. There was a great uproar. The gods lamented much.

## \|\| 5.9.46-47 \|\|

*nimeṣeṇa punarviṣṇuryāvaduttiṣṭhate svayam \|*  
*tāvatsa vīrabhadro hi tatkṣaṇādāgato'suram \|\| 46 \|\|*

*triśūlaṃ ca samudyamya vīrabhadraḥ pratāpavān \|*  
*tārakaṃ ditijādhīśaṃ jaghāna prasabhaṃ balī \|\| 47 \|\|*

46-47. Within a moment Viṣṇu got up but by that time Vīrabhadra came near the demon and dexterously raised his trident. The powerful Vīrabhadra hit him with all his force.

## \|\| 5.9.48 \|\|

*tattriśūlaprahāreṇa sa papāta kṣitau tadā \|*  
*patito'pi mahātejāstārakaḥ punarutthitaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Hit by the trident he fell on the ground. Though he fell down, Tāraka of mighty splendour got up again.

## \|\| 5.9.49 \|\|

*kṛtvā krodhaṃ mahāvīrassakalāsuranāyakaḥ \|*  
*jaghāna parayā śaktyā vīrabhadraṃ tadorasi \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. The great hero, the leader of the entire host of Asuras hit Vīrabhadra in his chest with his great spear.

## \|\| 5.9.50 \|\|

*vīrabhadro'pi patito bhūtale mūrchitaḥ kṣaṇam \|*  
*tacchaktyā parayā krodhānnihato vakṣasi dhuvam \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Vīrabhadra, hit by the spear furiously in his chest, fell unconscious on the ground.

## \|\| 5.9.51 \|\|

*sagaṇaścaiva devāste gaṃdharvoragarākṣasāḥ \|*  
*hāhākāreṇa mahatā cukruśuśca muhurmuhuḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. The gods, the Gaṇas, Gandharvas, Serpents and Rākṣasas lamented frequently with cries of “Alas” “Alas.”

## \|\| 5.9.52 \|\|

*nimeṣamātrātsahasā mahaujāssa vīrabhadro dviṣatāṃ nihaṃtā \|*  
*triśūlamudyamya taḍitprakāśaṃ jājvalyamānaṃ prabhayā vireje \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Within a moment, the powerful Vīrabhadra, the slayer of enemies, got up lifting his trident aloft, that had the lustre of lightning and was blazing forth.

## \|\| 5.9.53 \|\|

*svarociṣā bhāsitadigvitānaṃ sūryendubimbāgnisamānamaṃḍalam \|*  
*mahāprabhaṃ vīrabhayāvahaṃ paraṃ kālākhyamatyaṃtakaraṃ mahojjvalam \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. The trident had a halo around, like that of the sun, the moon and the fire. It illuminated the quarters by means of its brilliance; caused terror even in the hearts of the brave. It had a deadly splendour and blazed well.

## \|\| 5.9.54 \|\|

*yāvattriśūlena tadā haṃtukāmo mahābalaḥ \|*  
*vīrabhadro'suraṃ yāvatkumāreṇa nivāritaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. When the powerful Vīrabhadra was about to hit the Asura with his trident, he was prevented by Kumāra.

## Chapter 10 - Jubilation of the gods at the death of Tāraka

## \|\| 5.10.1 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*nivārya vīrabhadraṃ taṃ kumāraḥ paravīrahā \|*  
*samaicchattārakavadhaṃ smṛtvā śivapadāmbujau \|\| 1 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

1\. After preventing Vīrabhadra, Kumāra, the slayer of enemies, desired the destruction of Tāraka after remembering the lotuslike feet of Śiva.

## \|\| 5.10.2 \|\|

*jagarjātha mahātejāḥ kārtikeyo mahābalaḥ \|*  
*sannaddhaḥ so'bhavatkruddha sainyena mahatā vṛtaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Then the powerful Kārttikeya of great splendour roared. Angrily he got ready for the fight. He was surrounded by a vast army.

## \|\| 5.10.3 \|\|

*tadā jayajayetyuktaṃ sarvairdervergaṇai stathā \|*  
*saṃstuto vāgbhiriṣṭābhistadaiva ca surarṣibhiḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Shouts of victory were raised by the gods and the Gaṇas. He was eulogised by the celestial sages with pleasing words.

## \|\| 5.10.4 \|\|

*tārakasya kumārasya saṃgrāmo'tīva dussahaḥ \|*  
*jātastadā mahāghorassarvabhūta bhayaṃkaraḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The fight between Tāraka and Kumāra was terrific and unbearable. All the living beings were afraid.

## \|\| 5.10.5 \|\|

*śaktihastau ca tau vīrau yuyudhāte parasparam \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ paśyatāṃ tatra mahāścaryavatāṃ mune \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. O sage, even as all the persons stood gazing wonderingly, both of them fought each other with spears in their hands.

## \|\| 5.10.6 \|\|

*śaktinirbhinnadehau tau mahāsādhanasaṃyutau \|*  
*parasparaṃ vaṃcayaṃtau siṃhāviva mahābalau \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Each was wounded in the heart by the other with the spear. Each tried to escape from the other’s. thrust. Both were equally strong like two lions. Both were fully equipped for the fight.

## \|\| 5.10.7 \|\|

*vaitālikaṃ samāśritya tathā khecarakaṃ matam \|*  
*pāpaṃ taṃ ca samāśritya śaktyā śaktiṃ vijaghnatuḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. They fought and hit each other’s spear taking recourse to the mantras Vaitālika, Khecaraka, Prāptika etc.

## \|\| 5.10.8 \|\|

*ebhirmaṃtrairmahāvīrau cakraturyuddhamadbhutam \|*  
*anyonyaṃ sādhakau bhūtvā mahābalaparākramau \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. With these mantras they were possessed of magical properties. They wonderfully fought each other using their full strength and exploits.

## \|\| 5.10.9 \|\|

*mahābalaṃ prakurvatau parasparavadhaiṣiṇau \|*  
*jaghnatuśśaktidhārābhī raṇe raṇaviśāradau \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. They were equally good adepts in fighting. Each wanted to kill the other. They utilised all their power. With the edges of spears they hit each other.

## \|\| 5.10.10 \|\|

*mūrdhni kaṃṭhe tathā corvorjānvoścaiva kaṭītaṭe \|*  
*vakṣasyurasi pṛṣṭhe ca cicchiduśca parasparam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. They hit or cut each other’s head, neck, thighs, knees, hips, heart, chest and the back.

## \|\| 5.10.11 \|\|

*tadā tau yudhyamānau ca hantukāmau mahābalau \|*  
*valgantau vīraśabdaiśca nānāyuddhaviśāradau \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. They continued the fight swaggering and vaunting with heroic words. They were experts in different tactics of warfare. They were equally strong. They desired to kill each other.

## \|\| 5.10.12 \|\|

*abhavanprekṣakāssarve devā gaṃdharvakinnarāḥ \|*  
*ūcuḥ parasparaṃ tatra kosminyuddhe vijeṣyate \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. All the gods Gandharvas and Kinnaras stood as mere onlookers. “Who will win this battle?” they asked each other.

## \|\| 5.10.13 \|\|

*tadā nabhogatā vāṇī jagau devāṃśca sāṃtvayan \|*  
*asuraṃ tārakaṃ cātra kumāro'yaṃ haniṣyati \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Then a celestial voice rose appeasing the gods—“In this battle Kumāra will kill the Asura Tāraka.

## \|\| 5.10.14 \|\|

*mā śocyatāṃ suraiḥ sarvai sukhena sthīyatāmiti \|*  
*yuṣmadarthaṃ śaṃkaro hi putrarūpeṇa saṃsthitaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. None of the gods need be anxious. All shall rest assured. For your welfare Śiva Himself is standing here in the form of His son.”

## \|\| 5.10.15 \|\|

*śrutvā tadā tāṃ gagane samīritāṃ vācaṃ śubhāṃ sapramathessamāvṛtaḥ \|*  
*nihaṃtukāmaḥ sukhitaḥ kumārako daityādhipaṃ tārakamāśvabhūttadā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. On hearing the auspicious words uttered by the celestial voice, Kumāra became happy. He was surrounded by the Pramathas. He resolved to kill Tāraka, the king of Asuras.

## \|\| 5.10.16 \|\|

*śaktyā tayā mahābāhurājaghānastanāṃtare \|*  
*kumāraḥ sma ruṣāviṣṭastārakāsuramojasā \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The infuriated Kumāra of powerful arms used his full strength and hit Asura Tāraka in between his nipples.

## \|\| 5.10.17 \|\|

*taṃ prahāramanādṛtya tārako daityapuṃgavaḥ \|*  
*kumāraṃ cāpi saṃkruddhassvaśaktyā saṃjaghāna saḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Slighting that blow, the leading demon Tāraka, hit Kumāra angrily with his spear.

## \|\| 5.10.18 \|\|

*tena śaktiprahāreṇa śāṃkarirmūcchi to'bhavat \|*  
*muhūrtāccetanāṃ prāpa stūyamāno maharṣibhiḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. At the blow of the spear, the son of Śiva became unconscious. He regained his consciousness in a few minutes. He was eulogised by the great sages.

## \|\| 5.10.19 \|\|

*yathā siṃho madonmatto haṃtukāmastathāsuram \|*  
*kumārastārakaṃ śaktyā sa jaghāna pratāpavān \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Kumāra became furious like a maddened lion and was desirous of killing the Asura. The powerful Kumāra hit Tāraka with his spear.

## \|\| 5.10.20 \|\|

*evaṃ parasparaṃ tau hi kumāraścāpi tārakaḥ \|*  
*yuyudhāte'tisaṃrabdhau śaktiyuddhaviśāradau \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Thus both Kumāra and Tāraka equally inflamed and equally well versed in the battle of spears fought each other.

## \|\| 5.10.21 \|\|

*abhyāsaparamāvāstāmanyonyaṃ vijigīṣayā \|*  
*padātinau yudhyamānnau citrarūpau tarasvinau \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Both appeared to possess plenty of practice. Both had the desire to gain the upper hand. Both fought on foot, had wonderful forms and features and were equally courageous.

## \|\| 5.10.22 \|\|

*vividhairghātapuṃjaistāvanyonyaṃ vini jaghnatuḥ \|*  
*nānāmārgānprakurvantau garjaṃtau suparākramau \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. With massive heaps of fatal missiles they hit each other. They had various ways of attack. They roared. They exhibited their all exploits.

## \|\| 5.10.23 \|\|

*avalokaparāssarve devagaṃdharvakinnarāḥ \|*  
*vismayaṃ paramaṃ jagmurnocuḥ kiṃcana tatra te \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. The onlookers, the gods, the Gandharvas and the Kinnaras were much surprised. They did not speak anything there.

## \|\| 5.10.24 \|\|

*na vavau pavamānaśca niṣprabho'bhūddivākaraḥ \|*  
*cacāla vasudhā sarvā saśailavanakānanā \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. The wind did not blow. The sun became dim. The earth quaked along with mountains and forests.

## \|\| 5.10.25 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare tatra himālayamukhā dharāḥ \|*  
*snehārditāstadā jagmuḥ kumāraṃ ca parīpsavaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. In the meantime Himālaya and other mountains anxious to see Kumāra out of affection came there.

## \|\| 5.10.26 \|\|

*tatassa dṛṣṭvā tānsarvānbhayabhītāṃśca śāṃkariḥ \|*  
*parvatāngirijāputro babhāṣe paribodhayan \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. On seeing the mountains extremely terrified, Kumāra the son of Śiva and Pārvatī spoke enlightening them thereby.

## \|\| 5.10.27 \|\|

*kumāra uvāca \|*  
*mā khidyatāṃ mahābhāgā mā ciṃtāṃ kurvatāṃ nagāḥ \|*  
*ghātayāmyadya pāpiṣṭhaṃ sarveṣāṃ vaḥ prapaśya tām \|\| 27 \|\|*

Kumāra said:—

27\. O mountains, O fortunate sirs, do not be vexed, or worried. Even as you stand looking on I will kill this sinner.

## \|\| 5.10.28 \|\|

*evaṃ samāśvāsya tadā parvatānnirjarāngaṇān \|*  
*praṇamya girijāṃ śaṃbhumādade śaktimutprabhām \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Consoling the mountains, the gods and the Gaṇas thus, and bowing to Śiva and Pārvatī he took up his brilliant spear.

## \|\| 5.10.29 \|\|

*taṃ tārakaṃ haṃtumanāḥ karaśaktirmahāprabhuḥ \|*  
*virarāja mahāvīraḥ kumāraśśaṃbhubālakaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. The heroic Kumāra, son of Śiva the great lord, with the spear in his hand shone in his resolve to kill Tāraka.

## \|\| 5.10.30 \|\|

*śaktyā tayā jaghānātha kumārastārakāsuram \|*  
*tejasāḍhyaśśaṃkarasya lokakleśakaraṃ ca tam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Possessing the brilliance of Śiva, Kumāra with his spear struck Tāraka who had harrassed the worlds.

## \|\| 5.10.31 \|\|

*papāta sadyassahasā viśīrṇāṃgo'suraḥ kṣitau \|*  
*tārakākhyo mahāvīrassarvāsuragaṇādhipaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Immediately the Asura Tāraka the ruler of the hosts of Asuras, although very heroic, fell on the ground with all his limbs shattered.

## \|\| 5.10.32 \|\|

*kumāreṇa hatassotivīrassa khalu tārakaḥ \|*  
*layaṃ yayau ca tatraiva sarveṣāṃ paśyatāṃ mune \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. The great warrior Tāraka was slain by Kumāra. O sage, even as all were looking on, he passed away.

## \|\| 5.10.33 \|\|

*tathā taṃ patitaṃ dṛṣṭvā tārakaṃ balavattaram \|*  
*na jaghāna punarvīrassa gatvā vyasumāhave \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. On seeing the powerful Asura fallen dead in the battle, the hero did not go and attack him again.

## \|\| 5.10.34 \|\|

*hate tasminmahādaitye tārakākhye mahābale \|*  
*kṣayaṃ praṇītā bahavo'surā devagaṇaistadā \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. When the powerful Asura was slain, other Asuras were killed by gods and Gaṇas.

## \|\| 5.10.35 \|\|

*kecidbhītāḥ prāṃjalayo babhūvustatra cāhave \|*  
*chinnabhinnāṃgakāḥ kecinmṛtā daityāssahasraśaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Some of the Asuras who were afraid joined their palms in reverence. In the battle the limbs of many Asuras were chopped off and severed. Thousands were killed too.

## \|\| 5.10.36 \|\|

*kecijjātāḥ kumārasya śaraṇaṃ śaraṇārthinaḥ \|*  
*vadantaḥ pāhi pāhīti daityāḥ sāṃjalayastadā \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Some of the Asuras shrieking “O save O save” with palms joined in reverence sought refuge in Kumāra.

## \|\| 5.10.37 \|\|

*kiyaṃtaśca hatāstatra kiyaṃtaśca palāyitāḥ \|*  
*palāyamānā vyathitā stāḍitā nirjjarairgaṇaiḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Numberless Asuras were killed. Many fled. The fleeing Asuras were beaten and harassed by the gods and the Gaṇas.

## \|\| 5.10.38 \|\|

*sahasraśaḥ praviṣṭāste pātāle ca jijīṣavaḥ \|*  
*palāyamānāste sarve bhagnāśā dainyamāgatāḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Thousands of them fled to Pātāla for their life. Those who tried to flee were disappointed and put to distress.

## \|\| 5.10.39 \|\|

*evaṃ sarvaṃ daityasainyaṃ bhraṣṭaṃ jātaṃ munīśvara \|*  
*na kecittatra saṃtasthurgaṇadevabhayāttadā \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. O great sage, thus the entire army of the Asuras disappeared. None dared to remain there for fear of the gods and the Gaṇas.

## \|\| 5.10.40 \|\|

*āsīnniṣkaṃṭakaṃ sarvaṃ hate tasmindurātmani \|*  
*te devāḥ sukhamāpannāssarve śakrādayastadā \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. When the wicked Asura was killed, the whole universe became freed of thorns, freed from the danger and nuisance of the Asuras. Indra and other gods became happy.

## \|\| 5.10.41 \|\|

*evaṃ vijayamāpannaṃ kumāraṃ nikhilāssurāḥ \|*  
*babhūvuryugapaddhṛṣṭāstrilokāśca mahāsukhā \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Thus when Kumāra came out victorious the gods were happy. The three worlds attained great pleasure.

## \|\| 5.10.42 \|\|

*tadā śivo'pi taṃ jñātvā vijayaṃ kārtikasya ca \|*  
*tatrājagāma sa mudā sagaṇaḥ priyayā saha \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. On knowing about the victory of Kārttikeya, Śiva came there joyously with his beloved and the Gaṇas.

## \|\| 5.10.43 \|\|

*svātmajaṃ svāṃkamāropya kumāraṃ sūryavarcasam \|*  
*lālayāmāsa suprītyā śivā ca snehasaṃkulā \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. He took his son on his lap and fondled him with pleasure. Pārvatī in her flutter of affection took Kumāra, resplendent as the sun, on her lap and fondled him with pleasure.

## \|\| 5.10.44 \|\|

*himālayastadāgatya svaputraiḥ parivāritaḥ \|*  
*sabaṃdhussānugaśśaṃbhuṃ tuṣṭāva ca śivāṃ guham \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Then Himavat came there along with his sons, kinsmen and servants. He eulogised Śiva and Guha.

## \|\| 5.10.45 \|\|

*tato devagaṇāssarve munayassiddhacāraṇāḥ \|*  
*tuṣṭuvuśśāṃkariṃ śaṃbhuṃ girijāṃ tuṣitāṃ bhṛśam \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. The delighted gods, Gaṇas and sages, Siddhas and Cāraṇas eulogised Pārvatī, Śiva and the son of Śiva.

## \|\| 5.10.46 \|\|

*puṣpavṛṣṭiṃ sumahatīṃ cakruścopasurāstadā \|*  
*jagurgaṃdharvapatayo nanṛtuścāpsarogaṇāḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. The secondary gods poured a great shower of flowers. The chiefs of Gandharvas sang. The celestial damsels danced.

## \|\| 5.10.47 \|\|

*vāditrāṇi tathā nedustadānīṃ ca viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*jayaśabdo namaḥ śabdo babhūvoccairmuhurmuhuḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. The musical instruments were played sweetly then. Frequent loud shouts of “Victory” and “Obeisance” were raised.

## \|\| 5.10.48 \|\|

*tato mayācyutaścāpi saṃtuṣṭobhūdviśeṣataḥ \|*  
*śivaṃ śivāṃ kumāraṃ ca saṃtuṣṭāva samādarāt \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Viṣṇu too in my company was very glad. He respectfully eulogised Śiva, Pārvatī and Kumāra.

## \|\| 5.10.49 \|\|

*kumāramagrataḥ kṛtvā harikendramukhāssurāḥ \|*  
*cakrurnīrājanaṃ prītyā munayaścāpare tathā \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Keeping Kumāra in front, Brahmā, Indra and other gods performed the rite of Nirājana lovingly. Other sages too did likewise.

## \|\| 5.10.50 \|\|

*gītavāditraghoṣeṇa brahmaghoṣeṇa bhūyasā \|*  
*tadotsavo mahānāsītkīrtanaṃ ca viśeṣataḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Then there was great jubilation with vocal and instrumental music and chantings of the Vedas. Hymns too were sung.

## \|\| 5.10.51 \|\|

*gītavādyaissuprasannaistathā sāñjalibhirmune \|*  
*stūyamāno jagannāthassarvairdaivairgaṇairabhūta \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. The lord of the universe was eulogised, O sage, by the delighted gods and Gaṇas by means of vocal and instrumental music.

## \|\| 5.10.52 \|\|

*tatassa bhagavānrudro bhavānyā jagadaṃbayā \|*  
*sarvaiḥ stuto jagāmātha svagiriṃ svagaṇairvṛtaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Then eulogised by all, lord Śiva along with Pārvatī the mother of the universe, went to his mountain surrounded by the Gaṇas.

## Chapter 11 - The Victory of Kumāra and the death of Bāṇa and Pralamba

## \|\| 5.11.1 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*etasminnaṃtare tatra krauñcanāmācalo mune \|*  
*ājagāma kumārasya śaraṇaṃ bāṇapīḍita \|\| 1 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

1\. O sage, in the meantime the mountain Krauñca, harassed by Bāṇa came there and sought refuge in Kumāra.

## \|\| 5.11.2 \|\|

*palāyamāno yo yuddhādasoḍhā teja aiśvaram \|*  
*tutodātīva sa krauñcaṃ koṭyāyutabalānvitaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. This Bāṇa had been fleeing from the previous battle, unable to bear the brilliance of the lord. He with the army of ten thousand persons, inflicted pain on Krauñca with the tip of his missiles.

## \|\| 5.11.3 \|\|

*praṇipatya kumārasya sa bhaktyā caraṇāmbujam \|*  
*premanirbharayā vācā tuṣṭāva guhamādarāt \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The mountain Krauñca devoutly bowed at the lotuslike feet of Kumāra and eulogised him with reverence with words full of love.

## \|\| 5.11.4 \|\|

*krauṃca uvāca \|*  
*kumāra skaṃda deveśa tārakāsuranāśaka \|*  
*pāhi māṃ śaraṇāpannaṃ bāṇāsuranipīḍitam \|\| 4 \|\|*

Krauñca said:—

4\. O Kumāra, O Skanda, O lord of gods, O slayer of the Asura Tāraka protect me who have sought refuge in you. I am harassed by the Asura Bāṇa.

## \|\| 5.11.5 \|\|

*saṃgarātte mahāsena samucchinnaḥ palāyitaḥ \|*  
*nyapīḍayacca māgatya hā nātha karuṇākara \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. O Mahāsena, O lord, O merciful one, routed and uprooted from the battle with you he came and harassed me.

## \|\| 5.11.6 \|\|

*tatpīḍitaste śaraṇamāgato'haṃ suduḥkhitaḥ \|*  
*palāyamāno deveśa śarajanmandayāṃ kuru \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Afflicted by him I have run from him and sought refuge in you. O lord of gods, born amongst the reeds, be merciful.

## \|\| 5.11.7 \|\|

*daityaṃ taṃ nāśaya vibho bāṇāhvaṃ māṃ sukhīkuru \|*  
*daityaghnastvaṃ viśeṣeṇa devāvanakarassvarāṭ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. O lord, please slay the Asura Bāṇa. Make me happy. You are the slayer of Asuras and a special saviour of the gods. You are a self-ruler.

## \|\| 5.11.8 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*iti krauṃcastutasskandaḥ prasanno bhaktapālakaḥ \|*  
*gṛhītvā śaktimatulāṃ svāṃ sasmāra śivo dhiyā \|\| 8 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

8\. Skanda who was thus eulogised by Krauñca became delighted. He, the saviour of the devotees, took up his matchless spear and remembered Śiva.

## \|\| 5.11.9 \|\|

*cikṣepa tāṃ samuddiśya sa bāṇaṃ śaṃkarātmajaḥ \|*  
*mahāśabdo babhūvātha jajvaluśca diśo nabhaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The son of Śiva hurled the spear aiming at Bāṇa. It gave loud report, blazing forth the quarters and the sky.

## \|\| 5.11.10 \|\|

*sabalaṃ bhasmasātkṛtvāsuraṃ taṃ kṣaṇamātrataḥ \|*  
*guhopakaṃṭhaṃ śaktissā jagāma paramā mune \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. O sage, reducing the Asuras to ashes along with his army in a trice, the great spear returned to Kumāra.

## \|\| 5.11.11 \|\|

*tataḥ kumāra provāca krauṃcaṃ girivaraṃ prabhuḥ \|*  
*nirbhayassvagṛhaṃ gaccha naṣṭassa sabalo'suraḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The lord Kumāra told Krauñca, the chief of the mountains, “Go home fearlessly. That Asura has been slain along with his army.”

## \|\| 5.11.12 \|\|

*tacchutvā svāmivacanaṃ mudito girirāṭ tadā \|*  
*stutvā guhaṃ tadārātiṃ svadhāma pratyapadyata \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. On hearing the words of the lord, the delighted lord of the mountains eulogised Kumāra the slayer of his enemy and went back to his abode.

## \|\| 5.11.13 \|\|

*tataḥ skando maheśasya mudā sthāpitavānmune \|*  
*trīṇi liṃgāni tatraiva pāpaghnāni vidhānataḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. O sage, with great pleasure and observing the rules Skanda installed three phallic emblems of Śiva that quell all sins.

## \|\| 5.11.14 \|\|

*pratijñeśvaranāmādau kapāleśvaramādarāt \|*  
*kumāreśvaramevātha sarvasiddhipradaṃ trayam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The first is called Pratijñeśvara, the second Kapāleśvara and the last Kumāreśvara. The three are capable of conferring all the achievements.

## \|\| 5.11.15 \|\|

*punassarveśvarastatra jayastaṃbhasamīpataḥ \|*  
*staṃbheśvarābhidhaṃ liṃgaṃ guhaḥ sthāpitavānmudā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Thereafter Kumāra, the lord of all, joyously installed the phallic image Stambheśvara, near the column of victory.

## \|\| 5.11.16 \|\|

*tatassarve surāstatra viṣṇuprabhṛtayo mudā \|*  
*liṃgaṃ sthāpitavaṃtaste devadevasya śūlinaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Then Viṣṇu and other gods joyously installed the phallic emblem of Śiva, the lord of the gods.

## \|\| 5.11.17 \|\|

*sarveṣāṃ śivaliṃgānāṃ mahimābhūttadādbhutaḥ \|*  
*sarvakāmapradaścāpi muktido bhaktikāriṇām \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The glory of the phallic emblems of Śiva was marvellous, conferring all cherished desires and salvation to the devotees.

## \|\| 5.11.18 \|\|

*tatassarve surā viṣṇupramukhāḥ prītamānasāḥ \|*  
*aicchangirivaraṃ gaṃtuṃ puraskṛtya guhaṃ mudā \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Then the delighted Viṣṇu and the gods desired to go to the chief of mountains joyously putting Bṛhaspati ahead.

## \|\| 5.11.19 \|\|

*tasminnavasare śeṣaputraḥ kumuda nāmakaḥ \|*  
*ājagāma kumārasya śaraṇaṃ daityapīḍitaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Then Kumuda the son of Śeṣa who was harassed by the Asuras came and sought refuge in Kumāra.

## \|\| 5.11.20 \|\|

*pralaṃbākhyo'suro yo hi raṇādasmātpalāyitaḥ \|*  
*sa tatropadravaṃ cakre prabalastārakānugaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Another follower of Tāraka—Pralamba who had fled from the previous battle wrought great havoc with full force.

## \|\| 5.11.21 \|\|

*so'tha śeṣasya tanayaḥ kumudo'hipatermahān \|*  
*kumāraśaraṇaṃ prāptastuṣṭāva girijātmajam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Kumuda, the great son of Śeṣa the lord of serpents, sought refuge in Kumāra the son of Pārvatī and eulogised him.

## \|\| 5.11.22 \|\|

*kumuda uvāca \|*  
*devadeva mahādeva varatāta mahāprabho \|*  
*pīḍito'haṃ pralaṃbena tvāhaṃ śaraṇamāgataḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

Kumuda said:—

22\. O excellent son of great lord, lord of the gods, O great chief, I am afflicted by Pralamba and am seeking refuge in you.

## \|\| 5.11.23 \|\|

*pāhi māṃ śaraṇāpannaṃ pralaṃbā surapīḍitam \|*  
*kumāra skanda deveśa tārakāre mahāprabho \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. O Kumāra, O Skanda, O lord of the gods, O great lord, O slayer of Tāraka, save me harassed by the Asura Pralamba and seeking refuge in you.

## \|\| 5.11.24 \|\|

*tvaṃ dīnabaṃdhuḥ karuṇāsindhurānatavatsalaḥ \|*  
*khalanigrahakartā hi śaraṇyaśca satāṃ gatiḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. You are the kinsman of the distressed, the ocean of mercy, favourably disposed to the devotees, the slayer of the wicked, worthy of refuge and the goal of the good.

## \|\| 5.11.25 \|\|

*kumudenastutaścetthaṃ vijñaptastadvadhāya hi \|*  
*svāśca śaktiṃ sa jagrāha smṛtvā śivapadāṃbujau \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Eulogised thus by Kumuda and requested to slay the demon Pralamba, the lord took up his spear after remembering the lotus-like feet of Śiva.

## \|\| 5.11.26 \|\|

*cikṣepa tāṃ samuddiśya pralaṃbaṃ girijāsutaḥ \|*  
*mahāśabdo babhūvātha jajvaluśca diśo nabhaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The son of Pārvatī hurled the spear at Pralamba. It made a loud report. The quarters and the sky blazed.

## \|\| 5.11.27 \|\|

*taṃ sāyutabalaṃ śaktirdrutaṃ kṛtvā ca bhasmasāt \|*  
*guhopakaṃṭhaṃ sahasājagāmākliṣṭavāriṇī \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Reducing that powerful Asura to ashes in a trice the spear carried out the job without strain and returned to Kumāra.

## \|\| 5.11.28 \|\|

*tataḥ kumāraḥ provāca kumudaṃ nāgabālakam \|*  
*nirbhayaḥ svagṛhaṃ gaccha naṣṭassa sabalo'suraḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Then Kumāra told the Nāga child Kumuda—“Go home fearlessly. That Asura has been slain along with his army.”

## \|\| 5.11.29 \|\|

*tacchutvā guhavākyaṃ sa kumudohipatessutaḥ \|*  
*stutvā kumāraṃ natvā ca pātālaṃ mudito yayau \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. On hearing the words of Guha, Kumuda, the son of the Nāga chief eulogised and bowed to Kumāra and went to Pātāla in great delight.

## \|\| 5.11.30 \|\|

*evaṃ kumāravijayaṃ varṇitaṃ te munīśvara \|*  
*caritaṃ tārakavadhaṃ paramāścaryakārakam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Thus the story of the victory of Kumāra, including the wonderful way in which Tāraka was slain, has been narrated by me, O noble sage.

## \|\| 5.11.31 \|\|

*sarvapāpaharaṃ divyaṃ sarvakāmapradaṃ nṛṇām \|*  
*dhanyaṃ yaśasyamāyuṣyaṃ bhuktimuktipradaṃ satām \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. It is the divine story that removes all sins. It bestows all desires on men. It is conducive to the increase of wealth, glory and longevity. It confers worldly pleasures and salvation on the good.

## \|\| 5.11.32 \|\|

*ye kīrtayaṃti suyaśo'mitabhāgyayutā narāḥ \|*  
*kumāracaritaṃ divyaṃ śiva lokaṃ prayāṃti te \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Those who recite this divine story of Kumāra and glorify him are infinitely fortunate and attain Śivaloka.

## \|\| 5.11.33 \|\|

*śroṣyaṃti ye ca tatkīrtiṃ bhaktyā śraddhānvitā janāḥ \|*  
*muktiṃ prāpsyanti te divyāmiha bhuktvā paraṃ sukham \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Those who listen to his glory with devotion and faith will attain divine salvation hereafter after enjoying great happiness here.

## Chapter 12 - The story of Śiva and Pārvatī including that of Kārttikeya

## \|\| 5.12.1 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*nihataṃ tārakaṃ dṛṣṭvā devā viṣṇupurogamāḥ \|*  
*tuṣṭuvuśśāṃkariṃ bhaktyā sarve'nye muditānanāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

1\. On seeing Tāraka killed, Viṣṇu and other gods, with faces refulgent with pleasure, eulogised Kārttikeya with devotion.

## \|\| 5.12.2 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*namaḥ kalyāṇarūpāya namaste viśvamaṃgala \|*  
*viśvabaṃdho namaste'stu namaste viśvabhāvana \|\| 2 \|\|*

The gods said:—

2\. Obeisance to you of good features, obeisance to you who confer auspiciousness on the universe, O kinsman of the universe, obeisance be to you. Obeisance to you, O purifier of the universe.

## \|\| 5.12.3 \|\|

*namostu te dānavavaryahaṃtre bāṇāsuraprāṇaharāya deva \|*  
*pralaṃbanāśāya pavitrarūpiṇe namonamaśśaṃkaratāta tubhyam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Obeisance to you, the slayer of the chief of the Asuras. O lord, obeisance to the slayer of the Asura Bāṇa. Obeisance to the destroyer of Pralamba. Obeisance to you of holy features. Obeisance to you, O son of Śiva.

## \|\| 5.12.4 \|\|

*tvameva karttā jagatāṃ ca bharttā tvameva harttā śucija prasīda \|*  
*prapañcabhūtastava lokabiṃbaḥ prasīda śambhvātmaja dīnabaṃdho \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. You alone are the creator, sustainer and annihilator of the universe. You, born of firegod, be pleased. Your cosmic image is identical with the universe. O son of Śiva, kinsman of the distressed, be pleased.

## \|\| 5.12.5 \|\|

*devarakṣākara svāminrakṣa nassarvadā prabho \|*  
*devaprāṇāvana kara prasīda karuṇākara \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. O lord, protector of the gods, O lord, save us always. O merciful one, protector of gods, be pleased.

## \|\| 5.12.6 \|\|

*hatvā te tārakaṃ daityaṃ parivārayutaṃ vibho \|*  
*mocitāssakalā devā vipadbhyaḥ parameśvara \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. After killing the Asura Tāraka along with his followers, O great lord, the gods have been freed from adversities by you.

## \|\| 5.12.7 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*evaṃ stutaḥ kumāro'sau devairviṣṇumukhaiḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*varāndadāvabhinavānsarvebhyaḥ kramaśo mune \|\| 7 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

7\. O sage, thus eulogised by Viṣṇu and the other gods, lord Kumāra granted them fresh boons in order.

## \|\| 5.12.8 \|\|

*śailānnirīkṣya stuvatastatassa giriśātmajaḥ \|*  
*suprasannataro bhūtvā provāca pradadadvarān \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. On seeing the mountains eulogising, the son of Śiva became very glad and spoke to them after granting boons.

## \|\| 5.12.9 \|\|

*skanda uvāca \|*  
*yūyaṃ sarve parvatā hi pūjanīyāstapasvibhiḥ \|*  
*karmibhirjñānibhiścaiva sevyamānā bhaviṣyatha \|\| 9 \|\|*

Skanda said:—

9\. All of you mountains will become worthy of being worshipped by the sages and resorted to by persons following the paths of action and knowledge.

## \|\| 5.12.10 \|\|

*śaṃbhorviśiṣṭarūpāṇi liṃgarūpāṇi caiva hi \|*  
*bhaviṣyatha na saṃdehaḥ parvatā vacanānmama \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. O mountains, at my word you will be assuming the forms of phallic emblems, the special forms of Śiva. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 5.12.11 \|\|

*yo'yaṃ mātāmaho me'dya himavānparvatottamaḥ \|*  
*tapasvināṃ mahābhāgaḥ phalado hi bhaviṣyati \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. My maternal grandfather, the excellent mountain Himavat, will become the fortunate bestower of fruits to ascetics.

## \|\| 5.12.12 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*evaṃ dattvā varānhatvā tārakaṃ cāsurādhipam \|*  
*tvayā kṛtāśca sukhino vayaṃ sarve carācarāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

The gods said:—

12\. By killing Tāraka the lord of Asuras, and by granting boons thus, all of us including the mobile and immobile beings have been made happy by you.

## \|\| 5.12.13 \|\|

*idānīṃ khalu suprītyā kailāsaṃ giriśālayam \|*  
*jananī janakau draṣṭuṃ śivāśaṃbhū tvamarhasi \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Now, it behoves you to go to Kailāsa with great pleasure, to the abode of Śiva in order to see your mother and father Śiva and Pārvatī.

## \|\| 5.12.14 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityuktvā nikhilā devā viṣṇvādyā prāptaśāsanāḥ \|*  
*kṛtvā mahotsavaṃ bhūri sakumārā yayurgirim \|\| 14 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

14\. After saying thus and obtaining his permission, Viṣṇu and other gods went jubilantly to that mountain along with Kumāra.

## \|\| 5.12.15 \|\|

*kumāre gacchati vibhau kailāsaṃ śaṃkarālayam \|*  
*mahāmaṃgalamuttasthau jayaśabdo babhūva ha \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. When the lord Kumāra started to Kailāsa, the abode of Śiva, sounds of “Victory” arose indicating great auspiciousness.

## \|\| 5.12.16 \|\|

*āruroha kumāro'sau vimānaṃ paramarddhimat \|*  
*sarvatolaṃkṛtaṃ ramyaṃ sarvopari virājitam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Kumāra got in the richly decorated aerial chariot that shone above all the things.

## \|\| 5.12.17 \|\|

*ahaṃ viṣṇuśca samudau tadā cāmaradhāriṇau \|*  
*guha mūrdhni mahāprītyā mune'bhūva hyataṃdritau \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. O sage, with great pleasure, Viṣṇu and I held the chowries aloft above the head of the lord with alertness.

## \|\| 5.12.18 \|\|

*indrādyā amarāssarve kurvaṃto guhasevanam \|*  
*yathocitaṃ caturdikṣu jagmuśca pramudāstadā \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Indra and other gods, rendering suitable service to Kumāra went ahead joyously flanking him on all sides.

## \|\| 5.12.19 \|\|

*śaṃbhorjayaṃ prabhāṣaṃtaḥ prāpuste śaṃbhuparvatam \|*  
*sānaṃdā viviśustatroccarito maṃgaladhvaniḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. They reached Śiva’s mountain crying shouts of victory to Śiva. They entered the precincts with delight. Auspicious sounds arose.

## \|\| 5.12.20 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā śivaṃ śivāṃ caiva sarve viṣṇvādayo drutam \|*  
*praṇamya śaṃkaraṃ bhaktyā karau baddhvā vinamrakāḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. On seeing Śiva and Pārvatī, Viṣṇu and other gods bowed to Śiva with devotion and stood there humbly with palms joined in reverence.

## \|\| 5.12.21 \|\|

*kumāro'pi vinītātmā vimānādavatīrya ca \|*  
*praṇanāma mudā śaṃbhuṃ śivāṃ siṃhāsanasthitām \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Kumāra descended from the aerial chariot in all humility and bowed joyously to Śiva and Pārvatī seated on a throne.

## \|\| 5.12.22 \|\|

*atha dṛṣṭvā kumāraṃ taṃ tanayaṃ prāṇavallabham \|*  
*tau daṃpatī śivau devau mumudāte'ti nārada \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. O Nārada, on seeing their beloved son Kumāra, the lordly couple Śiva and Pārvatī rejoiced much.

## \|\| 5.12.23 \|\|

*mahāprabhussamutthāpya tamutsaṃge nyaveśayat \|*  
*mūrdhni jaghrau mudā snehāttaṃ pasparśa kareṇa ha \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. The great lord got up, kissed him on the head with joy, stroked him with the hand and placed him on his lap.

## \|\| 5.12.24 \|\|

*mahānaṃdabharaḥ śaṃbhuścakāra mukhacuṃbanam \|*  
*kumārasya mahāsnehāt tārakārermahāprabhoḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. With great affection, the highly delighted Śiva kissed the face of Kumāra, the great lord and the slayer of Tāraka.

## \|\| 5.12.25 \|\|

*śivāpi taṃ samutthāpya svotsaṃge saṃnyaveśayat \|*  
*kṛtvā mūrdhni mahāsnehāt tanmukhābjaṃ cucumba hi \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Pārvatī, too got up and placed him on her lap. Keeping him close to her head with great affection she kissed his lotus-like face.

## \|\| 5.12.26 \|\|

*tayostadā mahāmodo vavṛdhe'tīva nārada \|*  
*daṃpatyoḥ śivayostāta bhavācāraṃ prakurvatoḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. O dear Nārada, the joy of the couple—Śiva and Pārvatī who followed the worldly conventions, increased very much.

## \|\| 5.12.27 \|\|

*tadotsavo mahānāsīnnānāvidhiḥ śivālaye \|*  
*jayaśabdo namaśśabdo babhūvātīva sarvataḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. There was great jubilation in the abode of Śiva. Everywhere the sound of shouts “Victory” and “Obeisance” rose up.

## \|\| 5.12.28 \|\|

*tatassuragaṇāssarve viṣṇvādyā munayastathā \|*  
*supraṇamya mudā śaṃbhuṃ tuṣṭuvussaśivaṃ mune \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. O sage, then Viṣṇu, other gods and the sages bowed joyously to Śiva. They eulogised Him.

## \|\| 5.12.29 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*devadeva mahādeva bhaktānāmabhayaprada \|*  
*namo namaste bahuśaḥ kṛpākara maheśvara \|\| 29 \|\|*

The gods said:—

29\. O lord of the gods, O bestower of protection to your devotees, Obeisance, Obeisance to you many times, O merciful lord Śiva.

## \|\| 5.12.30 \|\|

*adbhutā te mahādeva mahālīlā sukhapradā \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ śaṃkara satāṃ dīnabaṃdho mahāprabho \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Wonderful indeed, O great lord, is your divine sport, conferring happiness to all good men, O Śiva, kinsman to the distressed, O lord.

## \|\| 5.12.31 \|\|

*evaṃ mūḍhadhiyaścājñāḥ pūjāyāṃ te sanātanam \|*  
*āvāhanaṃ na jānīmo gatiṃ naiva prabhodbhutām \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. We are deluded in our intellects. We are ignorant of the procedure of your worship, O eternal one. We do not know your invocation nor your wonderful course, O lord.

## \|\| 5.12.32 \|\|

*gaṃgāsaliladhārāya hyādhārāya guṇātmane \|*  
*namaste tridaśeśāya śaṃkarāya namonamaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Obeisance to you, the support of the waters of the Gaṅgā, to the deity possessed of the attributes, obeisance to the lord of the gods, obeisance to Śiva.

## \|\| 5.12.33 \|\|

*vṛṣāṃkāya maheśāya gaṇānāṃ pataye namaḥ \|*  
*sarveśvarāya devāya trilokapataye namaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Obeisance to the bull-bannered lord Śiva, obeisance to the lord of Gaṇas; Obeisance to the lord of all. Obeisance to the lord of the three worlds.

## \|\| 5.12.34 \|\|

*saṃhartre jagatāṃ nātha sarveṣāṃ te namo namaḥ \|*  
*bhartre kartre ca deveśa triguṇeśāya śāśvate \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. O lord, obeisance to you, the annihilator, the sustainer and creator of the worlds. O lord of gods, obeisance to you, the lord of three attributes and the eternal.

## \|\| 5.12.35 \|\|

*visaṃgāya pareśāya śivāya paramātmane \|*  
*niṣprapaṃcāya śuddhāya paramāyāvyayāya ca \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Obeisance to the lord free from attachment; obeisance to Śiva the great soul. Obeisance to the pure beyond the world of matter, obeisance to the great, the unwasting.

## \|\| 5.12.36 \|\|

*daṇḍahastāya kālāya pāśahastāya te namaḥ \|*  
*vedamaṃtrapradhānāya śatajihvāya te namaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Obeisance to you the god of death holding the staff of punishment and noose in the hand. Obeisance to the chief of the deities invoked by Vedic mantras. Obeisance to you the hundred-tongued deity.

## \|\| 5.12.37 \|\|

*bhūtaṃ bhavyaṃ bhaviṣyacca sthāvaraṃ jaṃgamaṃ ca yat \|*  
*tava dehātsamutpannaṃ sarvathā parameśvara \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. O lord, everything has come out of your body whether past, present or future, whether mobile or immobile.

## \|\| 5.12.38 \|\|

*pāhi nassarvadā svāminprasīda bhagavanprabho \|*  
*vayaṃ te śaraṇāpannāḥ sarvathā parameśvara \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. O lord, protect us always. O supreme lord, we have sought refuge in you in every respect.

## \|\| 5.12.39 \|\|

*śitikaṇṭhāya rudrāya svāhākārāya te namaḥ \|*  
*arūpāya sarūpāya viśvarūpāya te namaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Obeisance to you, the blue-necked Rudra, of the form of offering. Obeisance to you both possessed and devoid of forms, the multiformed one.

## \|\| 5.12.40 \|\|

*śivāya nīlakaṃṭhāya citābhasmāṃgadhāriṇe \|*  
*nityaṃ nīlaśikhaṃḍāya śrīkaṇṭhāya namonamaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Obeisance to Śiva, the blue-necked, the wearer of ashes on the limbs from the funeral pyre. Obeisance to you Śrīkaṇṭha and Nīlaśikhaṇḍa.

## \|\| 5.12.41 \|\|

*sarvapraṇatadehāya saṃyamapraṇatāya ca \|*  
*mahādevāya śarvāya sarvārcitapadāya ca \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Obeisance to you saluted by all, saluted by the Yogins. Obeisance to you, the great lord, whose feet are worshipped by all.

## \|\| 5.12.42 \|\|

*tvaṃ brahmā sarvadevānāṃ rudrāṇāṃ nīlalohitaḥ \|*  
*ātmā ca sarvabhūtānāṃ sāṃkhyaiḥ puruṣa ucyase \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. You are Brahmā among all the gods, you are Nīlalohita among Rudras; you are the soul in all living beings; you are the Puruṣa of Sāṅkhya system.

## \|\| 5.12.43 \|\|

*parvatānāṃ sumerustvaṃ nakṣatrāṇāṃ ca candramā \|*  
*ṛṣīṇāṃ ca vaśiṣṭhastvaṃ devānāṃ vāsavastathā \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. You are Sumeru among mountains, you are the moon among the stars. You are Vasiṣṭha among the sages and you are Indra among the gods.

## \|\| 5.12.44 \|\|

*akārassarvavedānāṃ trātā bhava maheśvara \|*  
*tvaṃ ca lokahitārthāya bhūtāni pariṣiṃcasi \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. You are Oṃkāra among all Vedic passages; O great lord, be our protector. For the benefit of the worlds you nourish the Beings.

## \|\| 5.12.45 \|\|

*maheśvara mahābhāga śubhāśubhanirīkṣaka \|*  
*āpyāyāsmānhi deveśa kartṝnvai vacanaṃ tava \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. O great lord, O fortunate one, O scrutinizer of the good and evil, O lord of gods, make us flourish as those who carry out your instructions.

## \|\| 5.12.46 \|\|

*rūpakoṭisahasreṣu rūpakoṭiśateṣu te \|*  
*aṃtaṃ gaṃtuṃ na śaktāḥ sma devadeva namostu te \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. In your millions and millions of forms we are unable to realize your true self. O lord of gods, obeisance be to you.

## \|\| 5.12.47 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*iti stutvākhilā devā viṣṇvādyā pramukhasthitāḥ \|*  
*muhurmuhussupraṇamya skaṃdaṃ kṛtvā purassaram \|\| 47 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

47\. After eulogising thus and bowing to him frequently, Viṣṇu and other gods stood before him after placing Skanda ahead.

## \|\| 5.12.48 \|\|

*devastutiṃ samākarṇya śivassarveśvarassvarāṭ \|*  
*suprasanno babhūvātha vijahāsa dayāparaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. On hearing the eulogy of the gods, Śiva, the lord of all, the self-ruler was delighted. The compassionate lord then laughed.

## \|\| 5.12.49 \|\|

*uvāca suprasannātmā viṣṇvādīnsurasattamān \|*  
*śaṃkaraḥ parameśāno dīnabaṃdhussatāṃ gatiḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Śiva the great Īśāna, the kinsman of the distressed, the goal of the good, became delighted and spoke to Viṣṇu and other important gods.

## \|\| 5.12.50 \|\|

*śiva uvāca \|*  
*he hare he vidhe devā vākyaṃ me śṛṇutādarāt \|*  
*sarvathāhaṃ satāṃ trātā devānāṃ vaḥ kṛpānidhiḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

Śiva said:—

50\. O Viṣṇu, O Brahmā, O gods, listen to my words with attention. I am merciful. I shall by all means protect you, the gods.

## \|\| 5.12.51 \|\|

*duṣṭahaṃtā trilokeśaśśaṃkaro bhaktavatsalaḥ \|*  
*kartā bhartā ca hartā ca sarveṣāṃ nirvikāravān \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. The lord of the three worlds is a slayer of the wicked. He is favourably disposed to his devotees. He is the creator, sustainer and annihilator of all yet free from aberrations.

## \|\| 5.12.52 \|\|

*yadā yadā bhavedduḥkhaṃ yuṣmākaṃ devasattamāḥ \|*  
*tadā tadā māṃ yūyaṃ vai bhajaṃtu sukhahetave \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. O excellent gods, whenever you are faced with misery you shall worship me for your happiness.

## \|\| 5.12.53-54 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityājñaptastadā devā viṣṇvādyāssamunīśvarāḥ \|*  
*śivaṃ praṇamya saśivaṃ kumāraṃ ca mudānvitāḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

*kathayaṃto yaśo ramyaṃ śivayośśāṃkareśca tat \|*  
*ānandaṃ paramaṃ prāpya svadhāmāni yayu rmune \|\| 54 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

53-54. O sage, thus ordered, Viṣṇu, the other gods and the sages bowed to Śiva, Pārvatī, and Kumāra joyously, and returned to their abodes in great delight singing the pleasant glory of Śiva, Pārvatī and their son.

## \|\| 5.12.55 \|\|

*śivopi śivayā sārddhaṃ sagaṇaḥ parameśvaraḥ \|*  
*kumāreṇayutaḥ prītyovāsa tasmingirau mudā \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Śiva stayed on the mountain joyously along with Pārvatī, the Gaṇas and Kumāra. Lord Śiva was much pleased.

## \|\| 5.12.56 \|\|

*ityevaṃ kathitaṃ sarvaṃ kaumāraṃ caritaṃ mune \|*  
*śaivaṃ ca sukhadaṃ divyaṃ kimanyacchrotumicchasi \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Thus O sage, the divine and pleasant story of Kumāra and Śiva has been narrated to you. What else do you wish to hear?

## Chapter 13 - The birth of Gaṇeśa

## \|\| 5.13.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tārakāreriti śrutvā vṛttamadbhutamuttamam \|*  
*nāradassuprasannotha papraccha prītito vidhim \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sūta said:—

1\. On hearing the marvellously excellent story of the slayer of Tāraka thus, Nārada was highly delighted and he lovingly asked Brahmā.

## \|\| 5.13.2 \|\|

*\|\| nārada uvāca \|*  
*devadeva prajānātha śivajñānanidhe mayā \|*  
*śrutaṃ kārtikasadvṛttamamṛtādapi cottamam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. O lord of gods and people, O storehouse of Śiva’s cult, the excellent story of Kārttikeya, far better than nectar, has been heard by me.

## \|\| 5.13.3 \|\|

*adhunā śrotumicchāmi gāṇeśaṃ vṛttamuttamam \|*  
*tajjanmacaritaṃ divyaṃ sarvamaṃgalamaṃgalam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Now I wish to hear the excellent story of Gaṇeśa, the details of his divine nativity, auspicious of the auspicious.

## \|\| 5.13.4 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya vacastasya nāradasya mahāmune \|*  
*prasannamānaso brahmā pratyuvāca śivaṃ smaran \|\| 4 \|\|*

Sūta said:—

4\. On hearing the words of Nārada the great sage, Brahmā became delighted and replied to him remembering Śiva.

## \|\| 5.13.5 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*kalpabhedādgaṇeśasya janiḥ proktā vidheḥ parāt \|*  
*śanidṛṣṭaṃ śiraśchinnaṃ saṃcitaṃ gajamānanam \|\| 5 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

5\. Due to the difference of Kalpas, the story of the birth of Gaṇeśa is told in different ways. According to one account he is born of the great lord. His head looked at by Śani was cut off and an elephant’s head was put on him.

## \|\| 5.13.6 \|\|

*idānīṃ śvetakalpoktā gaṇeśotpattirucyate \|*  
*yatra cchinnaṃ śirastasya śivena ca kṛpālunā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Now we narrate the story of the birth of Gaṇeśa in Śvetakalpa when his head was cut off by the merciful Śiva.

## \|\| 5.13.7 \|\|

*saṃdeho nātra kartavyaḥ śaṃkarassūtikṛnmune \|*  
*sa hi sarvādhipaḥ śaṃbhurnirguṇassaguṇo 'pi hi \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. No suspicion need be entertained, O sage. Śiva is certainly the cause of enjoyment and protection. He is the lord of all. Śiva is possessed as well as devoid of attributes.

## \|\| 5.13.8 \|\|

*tallīlayākhilaṃ viśvaṃ sṛjyate pālyate tathā \|*  
*vināśyate muniśreṣṭha prastutaṃ śṛṇu cādarāt \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. It is by His divine sport that the entire universe is created, sustained and annihilated. O excellent sage, listen to what is relevant to the context, with attention.

## \|\| 5.13.9 \|\|

*udvāhite śive cātra kailāsaṃ ca gate sati \|*  
*kiyatā caiva kālena jāto gaṇapaterbhavaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. A long time had lapsed after the marriage of Śiva and His return to Kailāsa that Gaṇeśa was born.

## \|\| 5.13.10 \|\|

*ekasminneva kāle ca jayā ca vijayā sakhī \|*  
*pārvatyā ca militvā vai vicāre tatparābhavat \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Once the friends Jayā and Vijayā conferred with Pārvatī and discussed.

## \|\| 5.13.11 \|\|

*rudrasya ca gaṇāssarve śivasyājñāparāyaṇāḥ \|*  
*te sarvepyasmadīyāśca nandibhṛṃgipurassarāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. All the Gaṇas of Rudra carry out the orders of Śiva. They all, Nandin, Bhṛṅgin and others are in a way our own.

## \|\| 5.13.12 \|\|

*pramathāste hyasaṃkhyātā asmadīyo na kaścana \|*  
*dvāri tiṣṭhanti te sarve śaṃkarājñāparāyaṇāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Pramathas are numerous. But none of them can be called our own. They all stand at the portals, subservient to Śiva’s behests.

## \|\| 5.13.13 \|\|

*te sarvepyasmadīyāṃśca tathāpi na milenmanaḥ \|*  
*ekaścaivāsmadīyo hi racanīyastvayānaghe \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. They also may be called our own but our mind is not in unison with them. Hence, O sinless lady, one, our own must be created.

## \|\| 5.13.14 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityuktvā pārvatī devī sakhībhyāṃ sundaraṃ vacaḥ \|*  
*hitaṃ mene tadā tacca kartuṃ smāpyadhyavasyati \|\| 14 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

14\. Goddess Pārvatī to whom this charming suggestion was made by the two friends considered it wholesome and resolved to carry it out.

## \|\| 5.13.15 \|\|

*tataḥ kadācinmajjatyāṃ pārvatyāṃ vai sadāśivaḥ \|*  
*naṃdinaṃ paribhartsyātha hyājagāma gṛhāṃtaram \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Once when Pārvatī was taking her bath, Sadāśiva rebuked Nandin and came into the inner apartment.

## \|\| 5.13.16 \|\|

*āyāṃtaṃ śaṃkaraṃ dṛṣṭvā'samaye jagadaṃbikā \|*  
*uttasthau majjatī sā vai lajjitā sundarī tadā \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The mother of the universe, seeing the untimely arrival of Śiva in the midst of her bath and toilet stood up. The beautiful lady was very shy then.

## \|\| 5.13.17 \|\|

*tasminnavasare devī kautukenātisaṃyutā \|*  
*tadīyaṃ tadvacaścaiva hitaṃ mene sukhāvaham \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The goddess decided that her friend’s suggestion would be conducive to her good and was so enthusiastic.

## \|\| 5.13.18 \|\|

*evaṃ jāte sadā kāle kadācitpārvatī śivā \|*  
*viciṃtya manasā ceti paramāyā pareśvarī \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. At the time when the incident occurred, Pārvatī, the great Māyā, the great goddess, thought as follows.

## \|\| 5.13.19 \|\|

*madīyassevakaḥ kaścidbhavecchubhataraḥ kṛtī \|*  
*madājñayā paraṃ nānyadrekhāmātraṃ calediha \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. “There must be a servant of my own who will be expert in his duties. He must not stray from my behest even a speck.”

## \|\| 5.13.20 \|\|

*vicāryeti ca sā devī vapuṣo malasaṃbhavam \|*  
*puruṣaṃ nirmamau sā tu sarvalakṣaṇasaṃyutam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Thinking thus the goddess created a person with all the characteristics, out of the dirt from her body.

## \|\| 5.13.21 \|\|

*sarvāvayavanirddoṣaṃ sarvāvayava sundaram \|*  
*viśālaṃ sarvaśobhāḍhyaṃ mahābalaparākramam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. He was spotless and handsome in every part of his body. He was huge in size and had all brilliance, strength and valour.

## \|\| 5.13.22-23 \|\|

*vastrāṇi ca tadā tasmai dattvā sā vividhāni hi \|*  
*nānālaṃkaraṇaṃ caiva bahvāśiṣamanuttamām \|\| 22 \|\|*

*matputrastvaṃ madīyosi nānyaḥ kaścidihāsti me \|*  
*evamuktasya puruṣo namaskṛtya śivāṃ jagau \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. She gave him various clothes and ornaments. She blessed him with benediction and said—“You are my son. You are my own. I have none else to call my own”. Thus addressed the person bowed to her and said:—

## \|\| 5.13.24 \|\|

*\|\| gaṇeśa uvāca \|*  
*kiṃ kāryaṃ vidyate tedya karavāṇi tavoditam \|*  
*ityuktā sā tadā tena pratyuvāca sutaṃ śivā \|\| 24 \|\|*

Gaṇeśa said:—

24\. “What is your order? I shall accomplish what you command.” Thus addressed, Pārvatī replied to her son.

## \|\| 5.13.25 \|\|

*śivovāca \|*  
*he tāta śṛṇu madvākyaṃ dvārapālo bhavādya me \|*  
*matputrastvaṃ madīyo'si nānyathā kaścidasti me \|\| 25 \|\|*

Pārvatī said:—

25\. “O dear, listen to my words. Work as my gatekeeper from today. You are my son. You are my own. It is not otherwise. There is none-else who belongs to me.

## \|\| 5.13.26 \|\|

*vinā madājñāṃ matputra naivāyānma dgṛhāntaram \|*  
*ko'pi kvāpi haṭhāttāta satyametanmayoditam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. O good son, without my permission, no one, by any means, shall intrude my apartment. I tell you the fact.”

## \|\| 5.13.27 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityuktvā ca dadau tasmai yaṣṭiṃ cātidṛḍhāṃ mune \|*  
*tadīyaṃ rūpamālokya sundaraṃ harṣamāgatā \|\| 27 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

27\. O sage, saying this, she gave him a hard stick. On seeing his handsome features she was delighted.

## \|\| 5.13.28 \|\|

*mukhamācuṃbya suprītyāliṃgya taṃ kṛpayā sutam \|*  
*svadvāri sthāpayāmāsa yaṣṭipāṇiṃ gaṇādhipam \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Out of love and mercy she embraced and kissed him. She placed him armed with a staff at her entrance as the gatekeeper.

## \|\| 5.13.29 \|\|

*atha devīsutastāta gṛhadvāri sthito gaṇaḥ \|*  
*yaṣṭipāṇirmahāvīraḥ pārvatīhitakāmyayā \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Then the son of the goddess, of great heroic power, stayed at the doorway armed with a staff with a desire to do what was good to her.

## \|\| 5.13.30 \|\|

*svadvāri sthāpayitvā taṃ gaṇeśaṃ svasutaṃ śivā \|*  
*svayaṃ ca majjatī sā vai saṃsthitāsītsakhīyutā \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Thus placing her son at the doorway, Pārvatī began to take bath with her friends, unworried.

## \|\| 5.13.31 \|\|

*etasminneva kāle tu śivo dvāri samāgataḥ \|*  
*kautukī munirśādūla nānālīlāviśāradaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. O excellent sage, at this very moment Śiva who is eagerly indulgent and an expert in various divine sports came near the door.

## \|\| 5.13.32 \|\|

*uvāca ca śiveśaṃ tamavijñāya gaṇādhipaḥ \|*  
*māturājñāṃ vinā deva gamyatāṃ na tvayā dhunā \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Not knowing that he was lord Śiva, the consort of Pārvatī, Gaṇeśa said—“O sir, without my mother’s permission you shall not go in now.

## \|\| 5.13.33 \|\|

*majjanārthaṃ sthitā mātā kva yāsīto vrajādhunā \|*  
*ityuktvā yaṣṭikāṃ tasya rodhanāya tadāgrahīt \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. My mother has entered the bath. Where are you going now? Go away” saying thus, he took up his staff to ward him off.

## \|\| 5.13.34 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā tu śivaḥ prāha kaṃ niṣedhasi mūḍhadhīḥ \|*  
*māṃ na jānāsyasadbuddhe śivohamiti nānyathā \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. On seeing him Śiva said “O foolish fellow, whom are you forbidding? O wicked knave, don’t you know me? I Śiva, none else”.

## \|\| 5.13.35 \|\|

*tāḍitastena yaṣṭyā hi gaṇeśena maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*pratyuvāca sa taṃ putraṃ bahulīlaśca kopitaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Thereupon Gaṇeśa beat Śiva with the staff. Śiva expert in various sports became infuriated and spoke to his son thus.

## \|\| 5.13.36 \|\|

*śiva uvāca \|*  
*murkhosi tvaṃ na jānāsi śivohaṃ girijāpatiḥ \|*  
*svagṛhaṃ yāmi re bāla niṣedhasi kathaṃ hi mām \|\| 36 \|\|*

Śiva said:—

36\. “You are a fool, You do not know that I am Śiva, the husband of Pārvatī. O boy, I go in my own house. Why do you forbid me?”

## \|\| 5.13.37 \|\|

*ityuktvā praviśaṃtaṃ taṃ maheśaṃ gaṇanāyakaḥ \|*  
*krodhaṃ kṛtvā tato vipra daṃḍenātāḍayatpunaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

37\. When lord Śiva tried to enter the house, Gaṇeśa became infuriated, O brahmin, and struck him with his staff once again.

## \|\| 5.13.38 \|\|

*tataśśivaśca saṃkruddho gaṇānājñāpayannijān \|*  
*ko vāyaṃ vartate kiṃca kriyate paśyatāṃ gaṇāḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Then Śiva too became furious. He commanded his own Gaṇas—“Who is this fellow here? What is he doing? O Gaṇas, enquire.”

## \|\| 5.13.39 \|\|

*ityuktvā tu śivastatra sthitaḥ kruddho gṛhādbahiḥ \|*  
*bhavācāraratassvāmī bahvadbhutasulīlakaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. After saying this, the furious Śiva stood outside the house. The lord, following the worldly conventions, is capable of various wonderful sports.

## Chapter 14 - The Gaṇas argue and wrangle

## \|\| 5.14.1 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*gaṇāste krodhasaṃpannāstatra gatvā śivājñayā \|*  
*papracchurgirijāputraṃ taṃ tadā dvārapālakam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

1\. The infuriated Gaṇas of Śiva at his bidding went there and questioned the son of Pārvatī who stood at the gate.

## \|\| 5.14.2 \|\|

*\|\| śivagaṇā ūcuḥ \|*  
*ko'si tvaṃ kuta āyātaḥ kiṃ vā tvaṃ ca cikīrṣasi \|*  
*ito'dya gaccha dūraṃ vai yadi jīvitumicchasi \|\| 2 \|\|*

Śiva’s Gaṇas said:—

2\. “Who are you? Whence do you come? What do you propose to do? If you have a desire to remain alive go away from here.”

## \|\| 5.14.3 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*tadīyaṃ tadvacaḥ śrutvā girijātanayassa vai \|*  
*nirbhayo daṇḍapāṇiśca dvārapānabravīdidam \|\| 3 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

3\. On hearing their words, the son of Pārvatī who was armed with the staff spoke to the Gaṇas as follows:—

## \|\| 5.14.4 \|\|

*gaṇeśa uvāca \|*  
*yūyaṃ ke kuta āyātā bhavaṃtassundarā ime \|*  
*yāta dūraṃ kimarthaṃ vai sthitā atra virodhinaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

Gaṇeśa said:—

4\. O “handsome fellows, who are you? Whence have you come? Go away. Why have you come here and why do you stand in opposition to me?”

## \|\| 5.14.5 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*evaṃ śrutvā vacastasya hāsyaṃ kṛtvā parasparam \|*  
*ūcussarve śivagaṇā mahāvīrā gatasmayāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

5\. On hearing his words, Śiva’s Gaṇas of great heroism and arrogance laughingly spoke to one another.

## \|\| 5.14.6 \|\|

*parasparamiti procya sarve te śivapārṣadāḥ \|*  
*dvārapālaṃ gaṇeśaṃ taṃ pratyūcuḥ kuddhamānasāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. After conferring with one another, the infuriated Pārṣadas of Śiva replied to Gaṇeśa, the doorkeeper.

## \|\| 5.14.7 \|\|

*śivagaṇā ūcuḥ \|*  
*śrūyatāṃ dvārapālā hi vayaṃ śivagaṇā varāḥ \|*  
*tvāṃ nivārayituṃ prāptāśśaṃkarasyājñayā vibhoḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

Śiva’s Gaṇas said:—

7\. “Listen. We are the excellent Gaṇas of Śiva. We are his doorkeepers. We have come here to throw you out at the bidding of lord Śiva.

## \|\| 5.14.8 \|\|

*tvāmapīha gaṇaṃ matvā na hanyāmīnyathā hataḥ \|*  
*tiṣṭha dūre svatastvaṃ ca kimarthaṃ mṛtyumīhase \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Considering you too, as one of the Gaṇas, we are not going to kill you. Otherwise you would have been killed. Better stay away yourself. Why do you court death?”

## \|\| 5.14.9 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|\| ityukto'pi gaṇeśaśca girijātanayo'bhayaḥ \|*  
*nirbhartsya śaṃkaragaṇānna dvāraṃ muktavāṃstadā \|\| 9 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

9\. Though warned thus, Gaṇeśa, the son of Pārvatī, stood fearless. He did not leave his post at the door. He rebuked Śiva’s Gaṇas.

## \|\| 5.14.10 \|\|

*te sarvepi gaṇāśśaivāstatratyā vacanaṃ tadā \|*  
*śrutvā tatra śivaṃ gatvā tadvṛttāṃtamathābruvan \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. After hearing his words, the Gaṇas of Śiva went back and informed Śiva about his stand.

## \|\| 5.14.11 \|\|

*tataśca tadvacaḥ śrutvādbhutalīlo maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*vinirbhartsya gaṇānūce nijāṃllokagatirmune \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. O sage, on hearing their words, lord Śiva of wonderful divine sports, following the worldly conventions rebuked his Gaṇas.

## \|\| 5.14.12 \|\|

*maheśvara uvāca \|*  
*kaścāyaṃ vartate kiṃ ca bravītyarivaducchritaḥ \|*  
*kiṃ kariṣyatyasadbuddhiḥ svamṛtyuṃ vāṃchati dhruvam \|\| 12 \|\|*

Lord Śiva said:—

12\. “Who is this fellow? What does he say? He is standing there haughtily as though he is our enemy. What will that wicked knave do? Certainly he wants to die.

## \|\| 5.14.13 \|\|

*dūrataḥ kriyatāṃ hyeṣa drārapālo navīnakaḥ \|*  
*klībā iva sthitāstasya vṛttaṃ vadatha me katham \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Why? Are you dastardly eunuchs to stand here helplessly and complain to me about him. Let this new doorkeeper be thrown out.”

## \|\| 5.14.14 \|\|

*svāminoktā gaṇāste cādbhutalīlena śaṃbhunā \|*  
*punarāgatya tatraiva tamūcurdvārapālakam \|\| 14 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

14\. Thus commanded by lord Śiva of wonderful sports the Gaṇas returned to the place and spoke to the doorkeeper.

## \|\| 5.14.15 \|\|

*\|\| śivagaṇā ūcuḥ \|*  
*re re dvārapa kastvaṃ hi sthitaśca sthāpitaḥ kutaḥ \|*  
*naivāsmāngāṇayasyevaṃ kathaṃ jīvitumicchasi \|\| 15 \|\|*

Śiva’s Gaṇas said:—

15\. O gatekeeper, who are you standing here? Why have you been stationed here? Why don’t you care for us. How can you thus remain alive?

## \|\| 5.14.16 \|\|

*dvārapālā vayaṃ sarve sthitaḥ kiṃ paribhāṣase \|*  
*siṃhāsanagṛhītaśca śṛgālaḥ śivamīhate \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. We are here the duly appointed doorkeepers. What are you saying? A jackal sitting on a lion’s seat wishes for happiness.

## \|\| 5.14.17 \|\|

*tāvadgarjasi mūrkha tvaṃ yāvadgaṇa parākramaḥ \|*  
*nānubhūtastvayātraiva hyanubhūtaḥ patiṣyasi \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. O fool, you will roar only as long as you do not feel the brunt of our attack. Erelong you will fall by feeling the same.”

## \|\| 5.14.18 \|\|

*ityuktastaissusaṃkuddho hastābhyāṃ yaṣṭikāṃ tadā \|*  
*gṛhītvā tāḍayāmāsa gaṇāṃstānparibhāṣiṇaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Thus taunted by them, Gaṇeśa became furious and took the staff with his hands and struck the Gaṇas even as they continued to speak harsh words.

## \|\| 5.14.19 \|\|

*uvācātha śivāputraḥ paribhartsya gaṇeśvarān \|*  
*śaṃkarasya mahāvīrānnirbhayastāngaṇeśvaraḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Then the fearless Gaṇeśa, son of Pārvatī rebuked the heroic Gaṇas of Śiva and spoke as follows:—

## \|\| 5.14.20 \|\|

*śivāputra uvāca \|*  
*yāta yāta tato dūre no cedvo darśayāmi ha \|*  
*svaparākramamatyugraṃ yāsyathātyupahāsyatām \|\| 20 \|\|*

The son of Pārvatī said:—

20\. “Get away. Get away. Or I shall give you a foretaste of my fierce valour. You will be the laughing-stock of all.”

## \|\| 5.14.21 \|\|

*ityākarṇya vacastasya girijātanayasya hi \|*  
*parasparamathocuste śaṃkarasya gaṇāstadā \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. On hearing these words of Geṇeśa, the Gaṇas of Śiva spoke to one another.

## \|\| 5.14.22 \|\|

*śivagaṇā ūcuḥ \|*  
*kiṃ kartavyaṃ kva gaṃtavyaṃ mākriyate sa na kiṃ punaḥ \|*  
*maryādā rakṣyate'smābhiranyathā kiṃ bravīti ca \|\| 22 \|\|*

Śiva’s Gaṇas said:—

22\. What shall be done? Where shall we go? Why shall we not act? Bounds of decency are observed by us. He would not have acted thus, otherwise.

## \|\| 5.14.23 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*tataśśaṃbhugaṇāssarve śivaṃ dūre vyavasthitam \|*  
*krośamātraṃ tu kailāsādgatvā te ca tathābruvan \|\| 23 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

23\. Then the Gaṇas of Śiva went to Śiva who was standing at the distance of a Krośa from Kailāsa and spoke to him.

## \|\| 5.14.24 \|\|

*śivo vihasya tānsarvāṃstriśūlakara ugradhīḥ \|*  
*uvāca parameśo hi svagaṇān vīrasaṃmatān \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Śiva ridiculed them all. The trident-armed great lord of fierce temperament spoke to his Gaṇas who professed to be heroes.

## \|\| 5.14.25 \|\|

*śiva uvāca \|*  
*rere gaṇāḥ klībamatā na vīrā vīramāninaḥ \|*  
*madagre nodituṃ yogyā bhartsitaḥ kiṃ punarvadet \|\| 25 \|\|*

Śiva said:—

25\. “Hello, Gaṇas, impotent wretches, you profess to be heroic but are never so. You are unfit to stand before me and speak. If he is only taunted he will speak in similar tone again.

## \|\| 5.14.26 \|\|

*gamyatāṃ tāḍyatāṃ caiṣa yaḥ kaścitprabhavediha \|*  
*bahunoktena kiṃ cātra dūrīkartavya eva saḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Go and beat him. Some one among you may be competent to do so. Why should I speak more? He must be driven away.”

## \|\| 5.14.27 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*iti sarve maheśena jagmustatra munīśvara \|*  
*bhartsitāstena devena procuśca gaṇasattamāḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

27\. O great sage, when rebuked thus by lord Śiva, the excellent Gaṇas went back and spoke to him.

## \|\| 5.14.28 \|\|

*śivagaṇā ūcuḥ \|*  
*rere tvaṃ śṛṇu vai bāla balātkiṃ paribhāṣase \|*  
*itastvaṃ dūrato yāhi no cenmṛtyurbhaviṣyati \|\| 28 \|\|*

Śiva’s Gaṇas said:—

28\. Hello you boy there, listen. Why do you speak so arrogantly? You go away from here. If not, your death is certain.

## \|\| 5.14.29 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*iti śrutvā vacasteṣāṃ śivājñākāriṇāṃ dhruvam \|*  
*śivāsutastadābhūtsa kiṃ karomīti duḥkhitaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

29\. On hearing the words of Śiva’s servants the son of Pārvatī became unhappy and thought “What shall I do?”

## \|\| 5.14.30 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare devī teṣāṃ tasya ca vai punaḥ \|*  
*śrutvā tu kalahaṃ dvāri sakhīṃ paśyeti sābravīt \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. In the meantime, the goddess heard the noise of this wrangle between the Gaṇas and the doorkeeper, then looked at her friend and spoke. “Go and see.”

## \|\| 5.14.31 \|\|

*samāgatya sakhī tatra vṛttāṃtaṃ samabudhyata \|*  
*kṣaṇamātraṃ tadā dṛṣṭvā gatā hṛṣṭā śivāṃtikam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. The friend came to the door and saw them for a moment. She understood the whole matter. She was delighted and returned to Pārvatī.

## \|\| 5.14.32 \|\|

*tatra gatvā tu tatsarvaṃ vṛttaṃ tadyadabhūnmune \|*  
*aśeṣeṇa tayā sakhyā kathitaṃ girijāgrataḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. O sage, coming back she reported the matter to Pārvatī as it had occurred.

## \|\| 5.14.33 \|\|

*sakhyuvāca \|*  
*asmadīyo gaṇo yo hi sthito dvāri maheśvari \|*  
*nirbhartsayati taṃ vīrāśśaṃkarasya gaṇā dhruvam \|\| 33 \|\|*

The friend said:—

33\. O great Goddess, the heroic Gaṇas of Śiva arc taunting and rebuking our own Gaṇa who is standing at the door.

## \|\| 5.14.34 \|\|

*śivaścaiva gaṇāssarve vinā te'vasaraṃ katham \|*  
*praviśaṃti haṭhādgehe naitacchubhataraṃ tava \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. How do these Gaṇas and Śiva enter your apartment suddenly without looking to your convenience? This is not good for you.

## \|\| 5.14.35 \|\|

*samyak kṛtaṃ hyanenaiva na hi kopi praveśitaḥ \|*  
*duḥkhaṃ caivānubhūyātra tiraskārādikaṃ tathā \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Even after undergoing the misery of rebuke etc. he, our Gaṇa, has done well in not allowing anyone in.

## \|\| 5.14.36 \|\|

*ataḥ parantu vāgvādaḥ kriyate ca parasparam \|*  
*vāgvāde ca kṛte naiva tarhyāyāntu sukhena vai \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. What is more? They are arguing too. When the argument has started, they cannot come in happily.

## \|\| 5.14.37 \|\|

*kṛtaścaivātra vāgvādastaṃ jitvā vijayena ca \|*  
*praviśaṃtu tathā sarve nānyathā karhicitpriye \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Now that they have started the argument let them conquer him and enter victoriously. Not otherwise, my dear friend.

## \|\| 5.14.38 \|\|

*asminnevāsmadīye vai sarve saṃbhartsitā vayam \|*  
*tasmāddevi tvayā bhadre na tyājyo māna uttamaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*
