33\. The earth has been circumambulated by me frequently, for seven times. Why then, my parents should say thus?

## \|\| 5.19.34 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*tadvacastu tadā śrutvā laukikīṃ gatimāśritau \|*  
*mahālīlākarau tatra pitarāvūcatuśca tam \|\| 34 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

34\. On hearing his words, the sportively inclined parents, following the worldly conventions spoke to him thus—

## \|\| 5.19.35 \|\|

*pitarāvūcatuḥ \|*  
*kadā krāṃtā tvayā putra pṛthivī sumahattarā \|*  
*saptadvīpā samudrāṃtā mahadbhirgahanaiyutā \|\| 35 \|\|*

The parents said:—

35\. “O son, when was the great earth circumambulated by you, the earth consisting of seven continents extending to the oceans and consisting of vast jungles?

## \|\| 5.19.36 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*tayorevaṃ vacaḥ śrutvā śivāśaṃkarayormune \|*  
*mahābuddhinidhiḥ putro gaṇeśo vākyamabravīt \|\| 36 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

36\. O sage, on hearing the words of Pārvatī and Śiva, Gaṇeśa, the storehouse of great intellect spoke thus.

## \|\| 5.19.37 \|\|

*gaṇeśa uvāca \|*  
*bhavatoḥ pūjanaṃ kṛtvā śivāśaṃkarayoraham \|*  
*svabuddhyā hi samudrāntapṛdhvīkṛtaparikramaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

Gaṇeśa said:—

37\. By worshipping you, Pārvatī and Śiva, I have intelligently circumambulated the earth extending to the oceans.

## \|\| 5.19.38 \|\|

*ityevaṃ vacanaṃ deve śāstre vā dharmasañcaye \|*  
*varttate kiṃ ca tattathyaṃ nahi kiṃ tathyameva vā \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Is it not the verdict of the Vedas or the Śāstras or any other sacred code? Is it true or otherwise?

## \|\| 5.19.39 \|\|

*pitrośca pūjanaṃ kṛtvā prakrāṃtiṃ ca karoti yaḥ \|*  
*tasya vai pṛthivījanyaphalaṃ bhavati niścitam \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. “He who worships his parents and circumambulates them, will certainly derive the fruit and merit of circumambulating the earth.

## \|\| 5.19.40 \|\|

*apahāya gṛhe yo vai pitarau tīrthamāvrajet \|*  
*tasya pāpaṃ tathā proktaṃ hanane ca tayoryathā \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. He who leaves his parents at home and goes on a pilgrimage incurs the sin of their murder.

## \|\| 5.19.41 \|\|

*putrasya ca mahattīrthaṃ pitroścaraṇapaṃkajam \|*  
*anyatīrthaṃ tu dūre vai gatvā samprāpyate punaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. The holy centre of a son consists of the lotus-like feet of his parents. The other holy centres can be reached only after going a long distance.

## \|\| 5.19.42 \|\|

*idaṃ saṃnihitaṃ tīrthaṃ sulabhaṃ dharmasādhanam \|*  
*putrasya ca striyāścaiva tīrthaṃ gehe suśobhanam \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. This holy centre is near at hand, easily accessible and a means of virtue. For a son and wife, the auspicious holy centre is in the house itself.”

## \|\| 5.19.43 \|\|

*iti śāstrāṇi vedāśca bhāṣante yanniraṃtaram \|*  
*bhavadbhyāṃ tatprakarttavyamasatyaṃ punareva ca \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. These things are mentioned frequently in the Śāstras and the Vedas. Now, are they going to be falsified by you?

## \|\| 5.19.44 \|\|

*bhavadīyaṃ tvidaṃ rūpamasatyaṃ ca bhavediha \|*  
*tadā vedopyasatyo vai bhavediti na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. If so, your very forms will come false. Even the Vedas will become false. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 5.19.45 \|\|

*śīghraṃ ca bhavitavyo me vivāhaḥ kriyatāṃ śubhaḥ \|*  
*atha vā vedaśāstrañca nyalīkaṃ kathyatāmiti \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Let my auspicious marriage be celebrated and that too very quickly. Otherwise let the Vedas and Śāstras be declared false.

## \|\| 5.19.46 \|\|

*dvayoḥ śreṣṭhatamaṃ madhye yatsyātsamyagvicārya tat \|*  
*kartavyaṃ ca prayatnena pitarau dharmarūpiṇau \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Of the two alternatives whatever is excellent shall be followed, O parents, embodied virtues!

## \|\| 5.19.47 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*ityuktvā pārvatīputrassa gaṇeśaḥ prakṛṣṭadhīḥ \|*  
*virarāma mahājñānī tadā buddhimatāṃ varaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

47\. Saying thus, Gāṇeśa of excellent intellect, of great wisdom and foremost among intelligent persons assumed silence.

## \|\| 5.19.48 \|\|

*tau daṃpatī ca viśveśau pārvatīśaṃkarau tadā \|*  
*iti śrutvā vacastasya vismayaṃ paramaṃ gatā \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. On hearing his words, Pārvatī and Śiva, the rulers of the universe, were very much surprised.

## \|\| 5.19.49 \|\|

*tataḥ śivā śivaścaiva putraṃ buddhivicakṣaṇam \|*  
*supraśasyocatuḥ prītyā tau yathārthaprabhāṣiṇam \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Then, Śiva and Pārvatī praised their son who was clever and intelligent and spoke to him who had spoken the truth.

## \|\| 5.19.50 \|\|

*śivāśivāvūcatuḥ \|*  
*putra te vimalā buddhissamutpannā mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*tvayoktaṃ yadvacaścaiva tataścaiva ca nānyathā \|\| 50 \|\|*

Śiva and Pārvatī said:—

50\. O son, you are a supreme soul and your thoughts are pure. What you have said is true and not otherwise.

## \|\| 5.19.51 \|\|

*samutpanne ca duḥkhe ca yasya buddhirviśiṣyate \|*  
*tasya dukhaṃ vinaśyeta sūrye dṛṣṭe yathā tamaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. When misfortune comes, if a person is keenly intelligent, his misfortunes perish even as darkness perishes when the sun rises.

## \|\| 5.19.52 \|\|

*buddhiryasya balaṃ tasya nirbuddhestu kuto balam \|*  
*kūpe siṃho madonmattaśśaśakena nipātitaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. He who has intelligence possesses strength as well. How can he who is devoid of intellect have strength? The proud lion was drowned in a well with a trick by a little hare.

## \|\| 5.19.53 \|\|

*vedaśāstrapurāṇeṣu bālakasya yathoditam \|*  
*tvayā kṛtaṃ tu tatsarvaṃ dharmasya paripālanam \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Whatever has been mentioned in the Vedas, Śāstras and Purāṇas for a boy, all that has been performed by you, namely, the observance of virtue.

## \|\| 5.19.54 \|\|

*samyakkṛtaṃ tvayā yacca tatkenāpi bhavediha \|*  
*āvābhyāṃ mānitaṃ tacca nānyathā kriyate'dhunā \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. What has been executed by you shall be done by anyone. We have honoured it. It will not be altered now.

## \|\| 5.19.55 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityuktvā tau samāśvāsya gaṇeśaṃ buddhisāgaram \|*  
*vivāhakaraṇe cāsya matiṃ cakraturuttamām \|\| 55 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

55\. After saying this and appeasing Gaṇeśa, the ocean of intelligence, they resolved to perform his marriage.

## Chapter 20 - The celebration of Gaṇeśa’s marriage

## \|\| 5.20.1 \|\|

*\|\|brahmovāca \|*  
*etasminnaṃtare tatra viśvarūpaḥ prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*tadudyogaṃ saṃvicārya sukhamāpa prasannadhīḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

1\. In the meantime Prajāpati Viśvarūpa became delighted and happy on knowing their intention.

## \|\| 5.20.2 \|\|

*viśvarūpaprajeśasya divyarūpe sute ubhe \|*  
*siddhibuddhiriti khyāte śubhe sarvāṃgaśobhane \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Prajāpati Viśvarūpa had two daughters of divine features. They were famous as Siddhi and Buddhi. They were exquisite in every part of their body.

## \|\| 5.20.3 \|\|

*tābhyāṃ caiva gaṇeśasya girijā śaṃkaraḥ prabhū \|*  
*mahotsavaṃ vivāhaṃ ca kārayāmāsaturmudā \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The lord Śiva and Pārvatī, jubilantly celebrated the marriage of Gaṇeśa with them.

## \|\| 5.20.4 \|\|

*saṃtuṣṭā devatāssarvāstadvivāhe samāgaman \|*  
*yathā caiva śivasyaiva girijāyā manorathaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The delighted gods attended their marriage as desired by Śiva and Pārvatī.

## \|\| 5.20.5 \|\|

*tathā ca viśvakarmā'sau vivāhaṃ kṛtavāṃstathā \|*  
*tathā ca ṛṣayo devā lebhire paramāṃ mudam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Viśvakarman made all arrangements for the marriage. The sages and the gods were full of great joy.

## \|\| 5.20.6 \|\|

*gaṇeśopi tadā tābhyāṃ sukhaṃ caivāpticiṃtakam \|*  
*prāptavāṃśca mune tattu varṇituṃ naiva śakyate \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The happiness that Gaṇeśa derived by virtue of this marriage, O sage, cannot be adequately described.

## \|\| 5.20.7 \|\|

*kiyatā caiva kālena gaṇeśasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*dvayoḥ patnyośca dvau divyau tasya putrau babhūvatuḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. After some time, the noble Gaṇeśa begot two sons, one each of his wives. They were endowed with divine features.

## \|\| 5.20.8 \|\|

*siddhergaṇeśapatnyāstu kṣemanāmā suto'bhavat \|*  
*buddherlābhābhidhaḥ putro hyāsītparabhaśobhanaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The son Kṣema was born to Siddhi. The highly brilliant son Lābha was born to Buddhi.

## \|\| 5.20.9 \|\|

*evaṃ sukhamaciṃtyaṃ va bhuṃjāne hi gaṇeśvare \|*  
*ājagāma dvitīyaśca krāṃtvā pṛthvīṃ sutastadā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. While Gāṇeśa was enjoying the inconceivable happiness, the second son returned after circumambulating the earth.

## \|\| 5.20.10 \|\|

*tāvaśca nāradenaiva prāpto gehe mahātmanā \|*  
*yathārthaṃ vacmi no'satyaṃ na chalena na matsarāt \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Thereupon he was addressed by Nārada, the great soul. “I speaking the truth, no lies. I am not actuated by deception or rivalry.

## \|\| 5.20.11 \|\|

*pitṛbhyāṃ tu kṛtaṃ yacca śivayā śaṃkareṇa te \|*  
*tanna kuryyātparo loke satyaṃ satyaṃ bravīmyaham \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. What has been done by Śiva and Pārvatī your parents, no other person in the world will ever do. Truth. It is the truth I am speaking.

## \|\| 5.20.12 \|\|

*niṣkāsya tvāṃ kukramaṇaṃ miṣamutpādya yatnataḥ \|*  
*gaṇeśasya varokāri vivāhaḥ paraśobhanaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. After driving you out under the pretext of circumambulating the earth, they have celebrated the excellent and auspicious marriage of Gaṇeśa.

## \|\| 5.20.13 \|\|

*gaṇeśasya kṛtodvāho labdhavāṃsstrīdvayaṃ mudā \|*  
*viśvarūpaprajeśasya kanyāratnaṃ mahottamam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. By this marriage that was celebrated, Gaṇeśa has obtained two wives joyously. They are the excellent daughters of Prajāpati Viśvarūpa.

## \|\| 5.20.14 \|\|

*putradvayaṃ lalābhāsau dvayoḥ patnyośśubhāṃgayoḥ \|*  
*siddhe kṣemaṃ tathā buddherlābhaṃ sarvaṃ sukhapradam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. He has begot of his two wives of auspicious body two sons, Kṣema of Siddhi and Lābha of Buddhi. They bestow happiness on every one.

## \|\| 5.20.15 \|\|

*patnyordvayorgaṇeśo'sau labdhvā putradvayaṃ śubham \|*  
*mātāpitrormatenaiva sukhaṃ bhuṃkte niraṃtaram \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Begetting two sons of auspicious features of his wives Gaṇeśa is continuously enjoying happiness as conceived by your parents.

## \|\| 5.20.16 \|\|

*bhavatā pṛthivī krāṃtā sasamudrā sakānanā \|*  
*tacchalājñāvaśāttāta tasya jātaṃ phalaṃ tvidam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The entire earth consisting of oceans and jungles has been traversed by you due to their deceptive behest. O dear, this is the result of that.

## \|\| 5.20.17 \|\|

*pitṛbhyāṃ kriyatāsmaivacchalaṃ tāta vicāryatām \|*  
*svasvāmibhyāṃ viśeṣeṇa hyanyaḥ kinna karoti vai \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. O dear, consider. If parents begin to deceive or particularly if our masters begin to deceive, won’t others also begin to deceive.

## \|\| 5.20.18 \|\|

*asamyakca kṛtaṃ tābhyāṃ tvatpitṛbhyāṃ hi karma ha \|*  
*vicāryatāṃ tvayā'pīha maccitte na śubhaṃ matam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Your parents have not done well. Just ponder over it. I don’t think their action has been good.

## \|\| 5.20.19 \|\|

*dadyādyadi garaṃ mātā vikrīṇīyātpitā yadi \|*  
*rājā harati sarvasvaṃ kasmai kiṃ ca bravītu vai \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. If mother were to poison her son, if father were to sell his son, if the king were to confiscate the assets of his subjects what can be said and to whom?

## \|\| 5.20.20 \|\|

*yenaivedaṃ kṛtaṃ syādvai karmānarthakaraṃ param \|*  
*śāṃtikāmassudhīstāta tanmukhaṃ na vilokayet \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. O dear, an intelligent peace-loving person shall never look at the face of the person who has committed this harmful deed.

## \|\| 5.20.21 \|\|

*iti nītiḥ śrutau proktā smṛtau śāstreṣu sarvataḥ \|*  
*niveditā ca sā te'dya yathecchasi tathā kuru \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. This policy has been mentioned in the Vedas, Smṛtis and sacred texts. It has been intimated to you now. Do as you wish.”

## \|\| 5.20.22 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityuktvā nārada tvaṃ tu maheśvaramanogatiḥ \|*  
*tasmai tathā kumārāya vākyaṃ maunamupāgataḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

22\. O Nārada, following the mental process of lord Śiva, you spoke these words to Kumāra and then kept quiet.

## \|\| 5.20.23 \|\|

*skando'pi pitaraṃ natvā kopāgnijvalitastadā \|*  
*jagāma parvataṃ krauṃcaṃ pitṛbhyāṃ vārito'pi san \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. After bowing to his father, the infuriated Skanda went to the Krauñca mountain though forbidden by his parents.

## \|\| 5.20.24 \|\|

*vāraṇe ca kṛte tvadya gamyate ca kathaṃ tvayā \|*  
*ityevaṃ ca niṣiddhopi procya neti jagāma saḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. “Even when forbidden by us why do you go?” Although he was prevented by saying this, he went away saying “No”.

## \|\| 5.20.25 \|\|

*na sthātavyaṃ mayā tātau kṣaṇamapyatra kiṃcana \|*  
*yadyevaṃ kapaṭaṃ prītimapahāya kṛtaṃ mayi \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. “O parents, I shall not stay here even a moment when deception has been practised on me eschewing affection towards me.”

## \|\| 5.20.26 \|\|

*evamuktvā gatastatra mune so'dyāpi vartate \|*  
*darśanenaiva sarveṣāṃ lokānāṃ pāpahārakaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. O sage, he went away saying so. Even today he is staying there removing the sin of all by his very vision.

## \|\| 5.20.27 \|\|

*taddinaṃ hi samārabhya kārtikeyasya tasya vai \|*  
*śivaputrasya devarṣe kumāratvaṃ pratiṣṭhitam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Ever since that day, O celestial sage, the son of Śiva, Kārttikeya remains a bachelor.

## \|\| 5.20.28 \|\|

*tannāma śubhadaṃ loke prasiddhaṃ bhuvanatraye \|*  
*sarvapāpaharaṃ puṇyaṃ brahmacaryapradaṃ param \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. His name bestows auspiciousness in the world. It is famous in the three worlds. It dispels all sins, is meritorious and confers the sanctity of celibacy.

## \|\| 5.20.29 \|\|

*kārtikyāṃ ca sadā devā ṛṣayaśca satīrthakāḥ \|*  
*darśanārthaṃ kumārasya gacchaṃti ca munīśvarāḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. In the month of Kārttika, the gods, the holy sages and great ascetics go there to see Kumāra.

## \|\| 5.20.30 \|\|

*kārtikyāṃ kṛttikāsaṃge kuryādyaḥ svāmidarśanam \|*  
*tasya pāpaṃ dahetsarvaṃ cittepsita phalaṃ labhet \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. He who has the vision of the lord in the Kṛttikā Nakṣatra in the month of Kārttika is divested of all sins. He derives all desired fruits.

## \|\| 5.20.31 \|\|

*umāpi duḥkhamāpannā skandasya virahe sati \|*  
*uvāca svāminaṃ dīnā tatra gaccha mayā prabho \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Pārvatī became grief-stricken by separation from Skanda. She piteously told her lord. “O lord, let us go there.”

## \|\| 5.20.32 \|\|

*tatsukhārthaṃ svayaṃ śaṃbhurgatassvāṃśena parvate \|*  
*mallikārjunanāmāsījjyotirliṅgaṃ sukhāvaham \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Śiva went to that mountain partially for her happiness. He assumed the pleasing form of Jyotirliṅga named Mallikārjuna.

## \|\| 5.20.33 \|\|

*adyāpi dṛśyate tatra śivayā sahitaśśivaḥ \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ nijabhaktānāṃ kāmapūrassatāṃ gatiḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Even now Śiva is seen there with Pārvatī satisfying the desires of his devotees. He is the goal of the good.

## \|\| 5.20.34 \|\|

*tamāgataṃ sa vijñāya kumārassaśivaṃ śivam \|*  
*sa virajya tato'nyatra gaṃtumāsītsamutsukaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. On coming to know that Śiva had come there with Pārvatī, Kumāra became unattached and was eager to go elsewhere.

## \|\| 5.20.35 \|\|

*devaiśca munibhiścaiva prārthitassopi dūrataḥ \|*  
*yojanatrayamutsṛjya sthitaḥ sthāne ca kārtikaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. On being requested by the gods and sages he stayed in a place three Yojanas away.

## \|\| 5.20.36 \|\|

*putrasnehāturau tau vai śivau parvaṇi parvaṇi \|*  
*darśanārthaṃ kumārasya tasya nārada gacchataḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. O Nārada, on the full and new moon days, Pārvatī and Śiva are excited by love towards their son and they go there to see him.

## \|\| 5.20.37 \|\|

*amāvāsyādine śaṃbhuḥ svayaṃ gacchati tatra ha \|*  
*pūrṇamāsī dine tatra pārvatī gacchati dhruvam \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. On new moon days, Śiva himself goes there. On full moon days, Pārvatī goes there certainly.

## \|\| 5.20.38 \|\|

*yadyattasya ca vṛttāṃtaṃ bhavatpṛṣṭaṃ munīśvara \|*  
*kārtikasya gaṇeśasya paramaṃ kathitaṃ mayā \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. O great sage, whatever you had asked in regard to Kārttikeya and Gaṇeśa has been narrated by me.

## \|\| 5.20.39 \|\|

*etacchrutvā naro dhīmān sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate \|*  
*śobhanāṃ labhate kāmānīpsitānsakalānsadā \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. On hearing this, an intelligent man becomes free from all sins. He achieves all desired fruits of auspicious nature.

## \|\| 5.20.40 \|\|

*yaḥ paṭhetpāṭhayedvāpi śṛṇuyācchrāvayettathā \|*  
*sarvānkāmānavāpnoti nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Whoever reads, teaches, listens or narrates this story derives all desires. No doubt need be entertained in this respect.

## \|\| 5.20.41 \|\|

*brāhmaṇo brahmavarcasvī kṣatriyo vijayī bhavet \|*  
*vaiśyo dhana samṛddhassyācchūdrassatsamatāmiyāt \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. A brahmin derives brahminical splendour, a Kṣatriya becomes victorious, a Vaiśya prosperous and a Śūdra attains equality with the good.

## \|\| 5.20.42 \|\|

*rogī rogātpramucyeta bhayānmucyeta bhītiyuk \|*  
*bhūtapretādibādhābhyaḥ pīḍito na bhavennaraḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. A sick man becomes free from sickness; a frightened man becomes free from fear; no man is harassed by the visitation of goblins, ghosts etc.

## \|\| 5.20.43 \|\|

*etadākhyānamanaghaṃ yaśasyaṃ sukhavarddhanam \|*  
*āyuṣyaṃ svargyamatulaṃ putrapautrādikārakam \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. This narrative is sinless, conducive to glory and enhancer of happiness. It is conducive to longevity and attainment of heaven. It is unequalled and bestows sons and grandsons.

## \|\| 5.20.44 \|\|

*apavargapradaṃ cāpi śivajñānapradaṃ param \|*  
*śivāśivaprītikaraṃ śivabhaktivivarddhanam \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. It confers salvation and reveals Śiva’s principles. It is pleasing to Pārvatī and Śiva and increases devotion to Śiva.

## \|\| 5.20.45 \|\|

*śravaṇīyaṃ sadā bhaktairniḥkāmaiśca mumukṣubhiḥ \|*  
*śivādvaitapradaṃ caitatsadāśivamayaṃ śivam \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. This shall always be heard by devotees and by those who seek liberation and are free from worldly desires. It confers identity with Śiva. It is conducive to welfare and is identical with Śiva himself.

## Section 6 - Rudra-saṃhitā (5): Yuddha-khaṇḍa

## Chapter 1 - Description of Tripura (the three cities)

## \|\| 6.1.1 \|\|

*\|\| śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ \|*  
*\|\| śrīgaurīśaṃkarābhyāṃ namaḥ \|*  
*\|\| nārada uvāca \|*  
*śrutamasmābhirānaṃdapradaṃ caritamuttamam \|*  
*gṛhasthasyaiva śaṃbhośca gaṇaskaṃdādisatkatham \|\| 1 \|\|*

Nārada said:—

1\. The excellent story of the householder Śiva, including that of Gaṇeśa, Skanda and others which confers bliss has been heard by us.

## \|\| 6.1.2 \|\|

*idānīṃ brūhi suprītyā caritaṃ varamuttamam \|*  
*śaṃkaro hi yathā rudro jaghāna viharankhalān \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Now please narrate lovingly the story of how Śiva killed wicked persons playfully.

## \|\| 6.1.3 \|\|

*kathaṃ dadāha bhagavānnagarāṇi suradviṣām \|*  
*trīṇyekena ca bāṇena yugapatkena vīryavān \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. How did the lord burn off three cities (tripura) of the Asuras with a single arrow simultaneously? What sort of an arrow was it?

## \|\| 6.1.4 \|\|

*etatsarvaṃ samācakṣva caritaṃ śaśimaulinaḥ \|*  
*devarṣisukhadaṃ śaśvanmāyāviharataḥ prabhoḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Please narrate the story of the moon-crested lord conducive to the happiness of the gods and sages and a play of the magic of Śiva.

## \|\| 6.1.5 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*evametatpurā pṛṣṭo vyāsena ṛṣisattamaḥ \|*  
*sanatkumāraṃ provāca tadeva kathayāmyaham \|\| 5 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

5\. When he was asked by Vyāsa formerly, the excellent sage Sanatkumāra narrated the story. I will repeat the same.

## \|\| 6.1.6 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu vyāsa mahāprājña caritaṃ śaśimaulinaḥ \|*  
*yathā dadāha tripuraṃ bāṇenaikena viśva hṛt \|\| 6 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

6\. O Vyāsa of great intellect, listen to the story of the moon-crested lord, how the annihilator of the universe burnt the three cities (tripura) with a single arrow.

## \|\| 6.1.7 \|\|

*śivātmajena skandena nihate tārakāsure \|*  
*tatputrāstu trayo daityāḥ paryatapyanmunīśvara \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. O great sage, when the Asura Tāraka was killed by Skanda, the son of Śiva, his three sons performed austerities.

## \|\| 6.1.8 \|\|

*tārakākhyastu tajjeṣṭho vidyunmālī ca madhyamaḥ \|*  
*kamalākṣaḥ kanīyāṃśca sarve tulyabalāssadā \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The eldest of them was Tārakākṣa, the middle one Vidyunmālī and the youngest Kamalākṣa. All of them were of equal strength.

## \|\| 6.1.9 \|\|

*jitendriyāssasannaddhāssaṃyatāssatyavādinaḥ \|*  
*dṛḍhacittā mahāvīrā devadrohiṇa eva ca \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. They were self-controlled, well prepared, disciplined, truthful, of steady mind, heroic and inimical to the gods.

## \|\| 6.1.10 \|\|

*te tu meruguhāṃ gatvā tapaścakrurmahādbhutam \|*  
*trayassarvānsubhogāṃśca vihāya sumanoharān \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Eschewing all enjoyments captivating the mind, they went to the cavern of the mountain Meru and performed a wonderful penance.

## \|\| 6.1.11 \|\|

*vasaṃte sarvakāmāṃśca gītavāditranissvanam \|*  
*vihāya sotsavaṃ tepustrayaste tārakātmajāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The three sons of Tāraka eschewed all desires in the season of spring. They disdained music, the sound of instruments as well as jubilation and performed penances.

## \|\| 6.1.12 \|\|

*grīṣme sūryaprabhāṃ jitvā dikṣu prajvālya pāvakam \|*  
*tanmadhyasaṃsthāḥ siddhyarthaṃ juhuvurhavyamādarāt \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. In the summer season they mastered sunshine. They lighted fires in all directions. Standing in their midst they performed sacrifice with great devotion for the attainment of success.

## \|\| 6.1.13 \|\|

*mahāpratāpapatitāssarvepyāsan sumūrchitāḥ \|*  
*varṣāsu gatasaṃtrāsā vṛṣṭiṃ mūrddhanyadhārayan \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. They lay unconscious in the blazing sunshine. During the rainy season, they fearlessly bore all the showers on their heads.

## \|\| 6.1.14-15 \|\|

*śaratkāle prasūtaṃ tu bhojanaṃ tu bubhukṣitāḥ \|*  
*ramyaṃ snigdhaṃ sthiraṃ hṛdyaṃ phalaṃ mūlamanuttamam \|\| 14 \|\|*

*saṃyamātkṣuttṛṣo jitvā pānānyuccāvacānyapi \|*  
*bubhukṣitebhyo dattvā tu bubhūvurupalā iva \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. In the autumn they controlled their hunger and thirst. All good foodstuffs, steady, wholesome, and viscid, fruits, roots and beverages they distributed among the hungry. They themselves remained like stones.

## \|\| 6.1.16 \|\|

*saṃsthitāste mahātmāno nirādhārāścaturdiśam \|*  
*hemaṃte girimāśritya dhairyeṇa parameṇa tu \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. In the early winter they remained on top of the mountain with fortitude, unsupported in any of the four quarters.

## \|\| 6.1.17 \|\|

*tuṣāradehasaṃchannā jalaklinnena vāsasā \|*  
*āsādya dehaṃ kṣaumeṇa śiśire toyamadhyagāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. In the late winter they stayed under water or wore wet dripping silken cloth or allowed themselves to be covered with dew drops.

## \|\| 6.1.18 \|\|

*anirviṇṇāstatassarve kramaśo'varddhayaṃstapaḥ \|*  
*tepustrayaste tatputrā vidhimuddiśya sattamāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. They were not at all vexed or distressed thereby. They gradually increased the severity of their austerities. Thus the three excellent sons of Tāraka performed penance with Brahmā as the object of their worship.

## \|\| 6.1.19 \|\|

*tapa ugraṃ samāsthāya niyame parame sthitā \|*  
*tapasā karṣayāmāsurdehān svān dānavottamāḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Maintaining strict severity in their austerities, the excellent Asuras made their bodies emaciated by their penance.

## \|\| 6.1.20 \|\|

*varṣāṇāṃ śatakaṃ caiva padamekaṃ nidhāya ca \|*  
*bhūmau sthitvā paraṃ tatra tepuste balavattarāḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Standing on the bare ground on a single foot, the strong Asuras performed the penance for a hundred years.

## \|\| 6.1.21 \|\|

*te sahasraṃ tu varṣāṇāṃ vātabhakṣāssudāruṇāḥ \|*  
*tapastepurdurātmānaḥ paraṃ tāpamupāgatāḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Taking in only air and enduring excessive heat and distress, the terrible and wicked souls continued the penance for a thousand years.

## \|\| 6.1.22 \|\|

*varṣāṇāṃ tu sahasraṃ vai mastakenāsthitāstathā \|*  
*varṣāṇāṃ tu śatenaiva ūrddhvabāhava āsitāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. They remained standing on their heads for a thousand years. They remained standing with their arms lifted for hundred years.

## \|\| 6.1.23 \|\|

*evaṃ duḥkhaṃ paraṃ prāptā durāgrahaparā ime \|*  
*īdṛkte saṃsthitā daityā divārātramataṃdritā \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Thus they bore extreme distress in their tenacious evil intent. They remained alert day and night.

## \|\| 6.1.24 \|\|

*evaṃ teṣāṃ gataḥ kālo mahān sutapatāṃ mune \|*  
*brahmātmanāṃ tārakāṇāṃ dharmeṇeti matirmama \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. O sage, thus many years elapsed even as they performed the penance. I think they had a virtuous dedication of their souls in Brahmā, these sons of Tāraka.

## \|\| 6.1.25 \|\|

*prādurāsīttato brahmā surāsuragururmahān \|*  
*saṃtuṣṭastapasā teṣāṃ varaṃ dātuṃ mahāyaśāḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Satisfied by their penance, Brahmā the supreme lord of the gods and Asuras, of great glory, appeared in front of them in order to grant them boons.

## \|\| 6.1.26 \|\|

*munidevāsuraissārddhaṃ sāṃtvapūrvamidaṃ vacaḥ \|*  
*tatastānabravītsarvān sarvabhūtapitāmahaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. He was accompanied by sages, gods and Asuras. The grandfather of all living beings spoke to them thus, appeasing them.

## \|\| 6.1.27 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*prasanno'smi mahādaityā yuṣmākaṃ tapasā mune \|*  
*sarvaṃ dāsyāmi yuṣmabhyaṃ varaṃ brūta yadīpsitam \|\| 27 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

27\. O great Asuras, I am now pleased with your penance. I shall grant you everything. Speak out the boons you wish to have.

## \|\| 6.1.28 \|\|

*kimarthaṃ sutapastaptaṃ kathayadhvaṃ suradviṣāṃ \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ tapaso dātā sarvakartāsmi sarvadā \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. O enemies of the gods, tell me why you have been performing this penance. I am the bestower of the fruits of all sorts of penance. I am the creator of everything for ever.

## \|\| 6.1.29 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā śanaiste svātmano gatam \|*  
*ūcuḥ prāṃjalayassarve praṇipatya pitāmaham \|\| 29 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

29\. On hearing his words they bowed to the grandfather, with their palms joined in reverence and spoke to him revealing their mind’s desire slowly.

## \|\| 6.1.30 \|\|

*daityā ūcuḥ \|*  
*yadi prasanno deveśa yadi deyo varastvayā \|*  
*avadhyatvaṃ ca sarveṣāṃ sarvabhūteṣu dehinaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

The Asuras said:—

30\. O lord of gods, if you are pleased, if boons are to be given to us, please grant us indestructibility at the hands of everyone, every living being.

## \|\| 6.1.31 \|\|

*sthirān kuru jagannātha pāṃtu naḥ paripaṃthinaḥ \|*  
*jarārogādayassarve nāsmānmṛtyuragāt kvacit \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. O lord of the universe, make us steady. Protect us from enemies. Let not old age, sickness and death befall us at any time.

## \|\| 6.1.32 \|\|

*ajarāścāmarāssarve bhavāma iti no matam \|*  
*samṛtyavaḥ kariṣyāmassarvānanyāṃstrilokake \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. We wish to become free from old age and death. In the three worlds we shall subject all others to death.

## \|\| 6.1.33 \|\|

*lakṣmyā kiṃ tadvipulayā kiṃ kāryaṃ hi purottamaiḥ \|*  
*anyaiśca vipulairbhogaissthānaiśvaryeṇa vā punaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Of what avail are riches, vast earth, excellent cities, other sorts of vast enjoyments or big positions and power?

## \|\| 6.1.34 \|\|

*yatraiva mṛtyunā grasto niyataṃ paṃcabhirdinaiḥ \|*  
*vyarthaṃ tasyākhilaṃ brahman niścitaṃ na itīva hi \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. If one is to be swallowed by death in five days, O Brahmā, everything else belonging to him is futile. This is our decisive thought.

## \|\| 6.1.35 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*iti śrutvā vacasteṣāṃ daityānāṃ ca tapasvinām \|*  
*pratyuvāca śivaṃ smṛtvā svaprabhuṃ giriśaṃ vidhiḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

35\. On hearing the words of those ascetic Asuras, Brahmā replied to them after remembering Śiva, his lord.

## \|\| 6.1.36 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*nāsti sarvāmaratvaṃ ca nivartadhvamato'surāḥ \|*  
*anyaṃ varaṃ vṛṇīdhvaṃ vai yādṛśo vo hi rocate \|\| 36 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

36\. O Asuras, there cannot be invariable indestructibility. Please desist from asking for it. Seek some other boon whatever you wish.

## \|\| 6.1.37 \|\|

*jāto janiṣyate nūnaṃ jaṃtuḥ kopyasurāḥ kvacit \|*  
*ajaraścāmaro loke na bhaviṣyati bhūtale \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. O Asuras, a creature is born, dies and will be born surely. But no one will be free from old age or death in this world.

## \|\| 6.1.38 \|\|

*ṛte tu khaṃḍaparaśoḥ kālakālāddharestathā \|*  
*tau dharmādharmaparamāvavyaktau vyaktarūpiṇau \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Except Śiva the destroyer of Death, and Viṣṇu all else are mortals. These two are the supervisers of virtue and evil and have manifest and unmanifest forms.

## \|\| 6.1.39 \|\|

*saṃpīḍanāya jagato yadi sa kriyate tapaḥ \|*  
*saphalaṃ tadgataṃ vedyaṃ tasmātsuvihitaṃ tapaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. If penance is performed for the harassment of the world, it shall be understood as gone. It is only a well-performed penance that can be fruitful.

## \|\| 6.1.40 \|\|

*tadvicārya svayaṃ buddhyā na śakyaṃ yatsurāsuraiḥ \|*  
*durlabhaṃ vā sudussādhyaṃ mṛtyuṃ vaṃcayatānaghāḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Ponder over this keenly, O faultless ones, desist from seeking immortality. Immortality is impossible for the gods and the Asuras. It is inaccessible. It cannot be warded off.

## \|\| 6.1.41 \|\|

*tatkiṃcinmaraṇe hetuṃ vṛṇīdhvaṃ sattvamāśritāḥ \|*  
*yena mṛtyurnaiva vṛto rakṣatastatpṛthak pṛthak \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Hence choose a boon whereby you shall do something equal to your own strength.

## \|\| 6.1.42 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*etadvidhivacaḥ śrutvā muhūrttaṃ dhyānamāsthitāḥ \|*  
*procuste ciṃtayitvātha sarvalokapitāmaham \|\| 42 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

42\. On hearing the words of Brahmā, they thought for a while and then replied to the grandfather of all the worlds.

## \|\| 6.1.43 \|\|

*daityā ūcuḥ \|*  
*bhagavannāsti no veśma parākramavatāmapi \|*  
*adhṛṣyāḥ śātravānāṃ tu yanna vatsyāmahe sukham \|\| 43 \|\|*

The Asuras said:—

43\. O lord, we have no mansion where we can stay happily although we are valorous and invincible to our enemies.

## \|\| 6.1.44 \|\|

*purāṇi trīṇi no dehi nirmāyātyadbhutāni hi \|*  
*sarvasaṃpatsamṛddhānya pradhṛṣyāṇi divaukasām \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Build and give us three wonderful cities richly endowed with wealth and unassailable even to the gods.

## \|\| 6.1.45 \|\|

*vayaṃ purāṇi trīṇyeva samāsthāya mahīmimām \|*  
*cariṣyāmo hi lokeśa tvatprasādājjagadguro \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. O Preceptor of the universe, Lord of the worlds, by your grace we shall move about on the earth occupying these cities.

## \|\| 6.1.46 \|\|

*tārakākṣastataḥ prāha yadabhedyaṃ surairapi \|*  
*karoti viśvakarmā tanmama hemamayaṃ puram \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Tārakākṣa then said—“Let Viśvakarmā make a city which cannot be broken even by the gods. Let that golden city be mine”.

## \|\| 6.1.47 \|\|

*yayāce kamalākṣastu rājataṃ sumahatpuram \|*  
*vidyunmālī ca saṃhṛṣṭo vajrāyasamayaṃ mahat \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Kamalākṣa requested for a great silver city. The delighted Vidyunmālī requested for a steel-set magnetic city.

## \|\| 6.1.48-50 \|\|

*pureṣveteṣu bho brahmannekasthānasthiteṣu ca \|*  
*madhyāhnābhijite kāle śītāṃśau puṣpa saṃsthite \|\| 48 \|\|*

*uparyuparyadṛṣṭeṣu vyomni līlābhrasaṃsthite \|*  
*varṣatsu kālamegheṣu puṣkarāvartanāmasu \|\| 49 \|\|*

*tathā varṣasahasrāte sameṣyāmaḥ parasparam \|*  
*ekībhāvaṃ gamiṣyaṃti purāṇyetāni nānyathā \|\| 50 \|\|*

48-50. We will join together during midday at the time of Abhijit when the moon shall be in the constellation Puṣya, when the dark clouds Puṣkara and Āvarta shower in plenty without being visible in the firmament with sporting clouds, at the end of a thousand years. These cities shall never join otherwise.

## \|\| 6.1.51-53 \|\|

*sarvadevamayo devassarveṣāṃ me kuhelayā \|*  
*asaṃbhave rathe tiṣṭhan sarvopaskaraṇānvite \|\| 51 \|\|*

*asaṃbhāvyaikakāṃḍena bhinattu nagarāṇi naḥ \|*  
*nirvairaḥ kṛttivāsāstu yosmākamiti nityaśaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

*vaṃdyaḥ pūjyobhivādyaśca sosmākaṃ nirdahetkatham \|*  
*iti cetasi saṃdhāya tādṛśo bhuvi durlabhaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

51-53. O Brahmā, when these cities are joined together, the lord who embodies all the gods sitting in a wonderful chariot containing all necessary adjuncts, may, in his distorted sport, discharge a wonderful single arrow and pierce our cities. Lord Śiva is free from enmity with us. He is worthy of our worship and respect. How can he burn us? This is what we think in our minds. A person like him is difficult to get in the world.

## \|\| 6.1.54 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*etacchrutvā vacasteṣāṃ brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ \|*  
*evamastīti tān prāha sṛṣṭikartā smarañśivam \|\| 54 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

54\. On hearing their words, Brahmā, the grandfather and creator of the worlds remembered Śiva and told them “Let it be so.”

## \|\| 6.1.55 \|\|

*ājñāṃ dadau mayasyāpi kutra tvaṃ nagaratrayam \|*  
*kāṃcanaṃ rājataṃ caiva āyasaṃ ceti bho maya \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. He ordered Maya—“O Maya, build three cities, one of gold, another of silver and a third one of steel.”

## \|\| 6.1.56 \|\|

*ityādiśya mayaṃ brahmā pratyakṣaṃ prāviśaddivam \|*  
*teṣāṃ tārakaputrāṇāṃ paśyatāṃ nijadhāma hi \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. After ordering directly like this, Brahmā returned to his abode in heaven even as the sons of Tāraka were watching.

## \|\| 6.1.57-58 \|\|

*tato mayaśca tapasā cakre dhīraḥ purāṇyatha \|*  
*kāṃcanaṃ tārakākṣasya kamalākṣasya rājatam \|\| 57 \|\|*

*vidyunmālyāyasaṃ caiva trividhaṃ durgamuttamam \|*  
*svarge vyomni ca bhūmau ca kramājjñeyāni tāni vai \|\| 58 \|\|*

57-58. Then the intelligent Maya built the cities by means of his penance: the golden one for Tārakākṣa, the silver one for Kamalākṣa and the steel one for Vidyunmālī. The three fortlike excellent cities were in order in heaven, sky and on the earth.

## \|\| 6.1.59 \|\|

*datvā tebhyo surebhyaśca purāṇi trīṇi vai mayaḥ \|*  
*praviveśa svayaṃ tatra hitakāmaparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. After building the three cities (tripura) for the Asuras, Maya established them there desiring their welfare.

## \|\| 6.1.60 \|\|

*evaṃ putratrayaṃ prāpya praviṣṭāstārakātmajāḥ \|*  
*bubhujussakalānbhogānmahābalaparākramāḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Entering the three cities (tripura) thus, the sons of Tāraka, of great strength and valour experienced all enjoyments.

## \|\| 6.1.61 \|\|

*kalpadrumaiśca saṃkīrṇaṃ gajavājisamākulam \|*  
*nānāprāsādasaṃkīrṇaṃ maṇijālasamā vṛtam \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. They had many Kalpa trees there. Elephants and horses were in plenty. There were many palaces set with gems.

## \|\| 6.1.62 \|\|

*sūryamaṇḍalasaṃkāśairvimānaissarvatomukhaiḥ \|*  
*padmarāgamayaiścaiva śobhitaṃ candrasannibhaiḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Aerial chariots shining like the solar sphere, set with Padmarāga stones, moving in all directions looking like moonshine illuminated the cities.

## \|\| 6.1.63-64 \|\|

*prāsādairgopurairdivyaiḥ kailāsaśikharopamaiḥ \|*  
*divyastrījanasaṃkīrṇairgaṃdharvaissiddhacāraṇaiḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

*rudrālayaiḥ pratigṛhamagnihotraiḥ pratiṣṭhitaiḥ \|*  
*dvijottamaiśśāstra jñaiśśivabhaktirataissadā \|\| 64 \|\|*

63-64. There were many palaces, divine minarets resembling the summits of the mount Kailāsa. Celestial damsels, Gandharvas, Siddhas, and Cāraṇas were also there. There were temples of Rudra. In every house, people performed the rites of Agnihotra. There were excellent brahmins well-versed in sacred texts and devoted to Śiva always.

## \|\| 6.1.65-66 \|\|

*vāpīkūpataḍāgaiśca dīrghikābhissuśobhitam \|*  
*udyānavanavṛkṣaiśca svargacyuta guṇottamaiḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

*nadīnadasarinmukhyapuṣkaraiḥ śobhitaṃ sadā \|*  
*sarvakāmaphalādyaiścānekairvṛkṣairmanoharam \|\| 66 \|\|*

65-66. The cities were embellished with many trees in the well-laid out gardens and parks as if they had dropped from heaven. There were beautiful tanks, lakes, wells, rivers and huge ponds. They were very beautiful with plenty of fruit-bearing trees.

## \|\| 6.1.67 \|\|

*mattamātaṃgayūthaiśca turaṃgaiśca suśobhanaiḥ \|*  
*rathaiśca vividhākāraiśśibikābhiralaṃkṛtam \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. The cities were decorated with camps and tents of various sizes and chariots with beautiful horses. There were herds of elephants in rut too.

## \|\| 6.1.68 \|\|

*samayādiśikaiścaiva krīḍāsthānaiḥ pṛthakpṛthak \|*  
*vedādhyayanaśālābhirvividhābhiḥ pṛthakpṛthak \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. There were time-indicators, playgrounds and different halls for Vedic studies.

## \|\| 6.1.69 \|\|

*adṛṣṭaṃ manasā vācā pāpānvitanaraissadā \|*  
*mahātmabhiśśubhācāraiḥ puṇyavadbhiḥ pravīkṣyate \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. There were persons of various types—sinners, virtuous, pious, noble and those of good conduct too.

## \|\| 6.1.70 \|\|

*pativratābhiḥ sarvatra pāvitaṃ sthalamuttamam \|*  
*patisevanaśīlābhirvimukhābhiḥ kudharmataḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. The place was sanctified everywhere by chaste ladies engaged in serving their husbands and averse to evil practices.

## \|\| 6.1.71 \|\|

*daityaśūrairmahābhāgaissadāraissasutairdvijaiḥ \|*  
*śrautasmārtārthatattvajñaissvadharmaniratairyutam \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. The cities contained heroic Asuras of great fortune accompanied by their wives, sons and brahmins well versed in the principles and practices of the Vedic and Smārta rites. They were strict adherents to their duties.

## \|\| 6.1.72 \|\|

*vyūḍhoraskairvṛṣaskaṃdhaissāmayuddhadharaissadā \|*  
*praśāṃtaiḥ kupitaiścaiva kubjairvāmanakaistathā \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. People had broad chests and bull-like shoulders. Some were of peaceful nature and some of warlike temperament. Some were calm and some furious. Some were hunchbacked, Some were dwarfish.

## \|\| 6.1.73 \|\|

*nīlotpaladalaprakhyairnīlakuṃcitamūrddhajaiḥ \|*  
*mayena rakṣitaissarvaiśśikṣitairyuddhalālasaiḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. They were protected by Maya. Some had the blue-lily petals. Their hair was curly and dark in hue. Maya had instructed them in the arts of warfare.

## \|\| 6.1.74 \|\|

*varasamararatairyutaṃ samaṃtādajaśivapūjanayā viśuddhavīryaiḥ \|*  
*ravimarutamahendrasaṃnikāśaissuramathanaissudṛḍhaissusevitaṃ yat \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. The cities abounded in people engaged in terrific battles. There were many Asuras whose heroism was sanctified by the worship of Brahmā and Śiva. The Asuras resembled the sun, the Maruts and Mahendra. They were sturdy.

## \|\| 6.1.75 \|\|

*śāstravedapurāṇeṣu yeye dharmāḥ prakīrtitāḥ \|*  
*śivapriyāssadā devāste dharmāstatra sarvataḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. Whatever sacred rites are mentioned in Śāstras, Vedas and Purāṇas, as favourites of Śiva, as also the deities, favourites of Śiva, were found there.

## \|\| 6.1.76 \|\|

*evaṃ labdhavarāste tu daiteyāstārakātmajāḥ \|*  
*śaivaṃ mayamupāśritya nivasaṃti sma tatra ha \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. Thus the Asuras, sons of Tāraka, after acquiring the boons, lived there subservient to Maya, a great devotee of Śiva.

## \|\| 6.1.77 \|\|

*sarvaṃ trailokyamutsārya praviśya nagarāṇi te \|*  
*kurvaṃti sma mahadrājyaṃ śivamārgaratāssadā \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. Abandoning the other parts in the three worlds they entered the cities and ruled the kingdom following the principles of Śiva.

## \|\| 6.1.78 \|\|

*tato mahān gataḥ kālo vasatāṃ puṇyakarmaṇām \|*  
*yathāsukhaṃ yathājoṣaṃ sadrājyaṃ kurvatāṃ mune \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. O sage, a long time elapsed even as they were engaged in meritorious activities and living happily ruling over the good kingdom.

Notes on the ‘three cities’ (tripura):

According to the present version, three Asuras Tāraka, Vidyunmāli and Kamalākṣa performed penances and obtained a boon from Brahmā to build three castles, the one of copper on earth, another of silver in the sky and the third of gold. Brahmā asked the Asura Maya to build these castles for the Asuras which were destroyed by Śiva later on. According to another Version, the Asura Bāṇa received in gift three cities from Śiva, Brahmā and Viṣṇu.

The Chedis adopted the name Tripurī for their capital on the banks of the Narmadā. It is now traceable in the insignificant village Tewar, thirteen miles from Jabalpur.

The legend of the three cities is as old as the Brāhmaṇa literature. It is said that the Asuras built the city of copper on the earth, of silver in the sky and of gold in the heavenly region:

“devāśca vā asurāśca \| ubhaye prājāpatyāḥ paspṛdhire \| tato'surā eṣu lokeṣu puraścakrire ayasmayīmevāsmin loke rajatāmantarikṣe hariṇīṃ divi” ŚB. 3.4.4.3

## Chapter 2 - The Prayer of the gods

## \|\| 6.2.1 \|\|

*\|\| vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*brahmaputra mahāprājña vada me vadatāṃ vara \|*  
*tataḥ kimabhavaddevāḥ kathaṃ ca sukhino'bhavan \|\| 1 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:—

1\. O son of Brahmā, of great intellect, and most eloquent, please narrate. What happened after that? How did the gods become happy?

## \|\| 6.2.2 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya vacastasya vyāsasyāmitadhīmataḥ \|*  
*sanatkumāraḥ provāca smṛtvā śivapadāmbujam \|\| 2 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

2\. On hearing the words of Vyāsa of immeasurable intellect, Sanatkumāra spoke after remembering the lotus-like feet of Śiva.

## \|\| 6.2.3 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*atha tatprabhayā dagdhā devā hīndrādayastathā \|*  
*saṃmaṃtrya duḥkhitāssarve brahmāṇaṃ śaraṇaṃ yayuḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

3\. Indra and other gods scorched by their brilliance and distressed consulted one another and sought refuge in Brahmā.

## \|\| 6.2.4 \|\|

*natvā pitāmahaṃ prītyā parikṣiptākhilāssurāḥ \|*  
*duḥkhaṃ vijñāpayāmāsurvilokyāvasaraṃ tataḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. After bowing to and circumambulating Brahmā, they narrated their grievances to him after awaiting the proper opportunity.

## \|\| 6.2.5 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*dhātastripuranāthena satārakasutena hi \|*  
*sarve pratāpitā nūnaṃ mayena tridivaukasaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

The gods said:—

5\. O Brahmā, the heaven-dwellers have been subjected to great distress by Maya the virtual ruler of the three cities, accompanied by the sons of Tāraka.

## \|\| 6.2.6 \|\|

*ataste śaraṇaṃ yātā duḥkhitā hi vidhe vayam \|*  
*kuru tvaṃ tadvadhopāyaṃ sukhinassyāma tadyathā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Hence, O Brahmā, we are distressed and we seek refuge in you. Please plan out the way of their annihilation whereby we can be happy.

## \|\| 6.2.7 \|\|

*\|\| sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*iti vijñāpito devairvihasya bhavakṛdvidhiḥ \|*  
*pratyuvācātha tānsarvānmayato bhītamānasān \|\| 7 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

7\. Requested thus by the gods, Brahmā, the creator of the worlds laughed and replied to them all who were utterly frightened of Maya.

## \|\| 6.2.8 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*na bhetavyaṃ surāstebhyo dānavebhyo viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*ācakṣe tadvadhopāyaṃ śivaṃ śarvaḥ kariṣyati \|\| 8 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

8\. O gods, I tell you, do not be afraid at all of those Asuras. Śiva will hit upon a good way of killing them.

## \|\| 6.2.9 \|\|

*matto vivardhito daityo vadhaṃ matto na cārhati \|*  
*tathāpi puṇyaṃ varddhaita nagare tripure punaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The Asuras have flourished due to my favour. They do not deserve destruction at my hands. Their merit is bound to increase in the three cities again.

## \|\| 6.2.10 \|\|

*śivaṃ ca prārthayadhvaṃ vai sarve devāssavāsavāḥ \|*  
*sarvādhīśaḥ prasannaścetsa vaḥ kāryaṃ kariṣyati \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. All of you gods including Indra pray to Śiva. If the lord of all is pleased, he will carry out your task.

## \|\| 6.2.11 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya vidhervāṇīṃ sarve devāssavāsavāḥ \|*  
*dukhitāste yayustatra yatrāste vṛṣabhadhvajaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

11\. On hearing the words of Brahmā, the distressed gods including Indra went to the place where the bull-bannered god Śiva was staying.

## \|\| 6.2.12 \|\|

*praṇamya bhaktyā deveśaṃ sarve prāṃjalayastadā \|*  
*tuṣṭuvurvinataskaṃdhāśśaṃkaraṃ lokaśaṃkaram \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Devoutly bowing to Śiva, the lord of the gods, with palms joined in reverence, all of them bent their shoulders and eulogised Śiva, the benefactor of the worlds.

## \|\| 6.2.13 \|\|

*\|\| devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*namo hiraṇyagarbhāya sarvasṛṣṭi vidhāyine \|*  
*namaḥ sthitikṛte tubhyaṃ viṣṇave prabhaviṣṇave \|\| 13 \|\|*

The gods said:—

13\. Obeisance to the gold-wombed lord, the creator of everything. Obeisance to Thee, the sustainer, the omnipresent and the omnipotent.

## \|\| 6.2.14 \|\|

*namo harasvarūpāya bhūtasaṃhārakāriṇe \|*  
*nirguṇāya namastubhyaṃ śivāyāmita tejase \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Obeisance to Thee of destroyer’s form, the annihilator of living beings. Obeisance to Thee devoid of attributes, and of immeasurable splendour.

## \|\| 6.2.15 \|\|

*avasthārahitāyātha nirvikārāya varcase \|*  
*mahābhūtātmabhūtāya nirliptāya mahātmane \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Obeisance to Thee devoid of states, possessed of splendour and free from aberrations; obeisance to Thee of the soul of Great Elements; obeisance to the unsullied, the great Ātman.

## \|\| 6.2.16 \|\|

*namaste bhūtapataye mahābhārasahiṣṇave \|*  
*tṛṣṇāharāya nirvairākṛtaye bhūritejase \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Obeisance to Thee, the lord of all beings, the sustainer of great burden, the remover of thirst, to Thee whose form is devoid of enmity, to Thee of excessive splendour.

## \|\| 6.2.17 \|\|

*mahādaityamahāraṇyanāśine dāvavahnaye \|*  
*daityadrumakuṭhārāya namaste śūlapāṇaye \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Obeisance to Thee, the destroyer of the great forest in the form of great Asuras, like conflagration. Obeisance to the Trident-bearing lord who acts as the axe for the trees of Asuras.

## \|\| 6.2.18 \|\|

*mahādanujanāśāya namaste parameśvara \|*  
*ambikāpataye tubhyaṃ namassarvāstradhāraka \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. O great lord, obeisance to Thee, the destroyer of great Asuras; obeisance to Thee the lord of Pārvatī, O wielder of all weapons.

## \|\| 6.2.19 \|\|

*namaste pārvatīnātha paramātmanmaheśvara \|*  
*nīlakaṃṭhāya rudrāya namaste rudrarūpiṇe \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. O lord of Pārvatī, Obeisance to Thee, O great soul, O great lord. Obeisance to Thee, the blue-necked Rudra and of the form of Rudra.

## \|\| 6.2.20 \|\|

*namo vedāntavedyāya mārgātītāya te namaḥ \|*  
*namoguṇasvarūpāya guṇine guṇavarjite \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Obeisance to Thee, knowable through Vedānta; Obeisance to Thee who art beyond the paths. Obeisance to Thee of the form of attributes, possessing attributes and also devoid of them.

## \|\| 6.2.21 \|\|

*mahādeva namastubhyaṃ trilokīnandanāya ca \|*  
*pradyumnāyāniruddhāya vāsudevāya te namaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. O great god, obeisance to Thee the delighter of the three worlds. Obeisance to Pradyumna, Aniruddha and Vāsudeva (these being your manifestations). Obeisance to Thee.

## \|\| 6.2.22 \|\|

*saṃkarṣaṇāya devāya namaste kaṃsanāśine \|*  
*cāṇūramardine tubhyaṃ dāmodara viṣādine \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Obeisance to Thee, the lord Saṃkarṣaṇa. Obeisance to Thee the destroyer of Kaṃsa. Obeisance to Thee O Dāmodara, the pounder of Cāṇūra,180 the partaker of poison.

## \|\| 6.2.23 \|\|

*hṛṣīkeśācyuta vibho mṛḍa śaṃkara te namaḥ \|*  
*adhokṣaja gajārāte kāmāre viṣabhakṣaṇaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Obeisance to Thee, O lord, Hṛṣīkeśa, Acyuta, Mṛḍa, Śaṅkara, Adhokṣaja, enemy of the Asuras, Gaja and Kāma. Obeisance to you, O partaker of poison.

## \|\| 6.2.24 \|\|

*nārāyaṇāya devāya nārāyaṇaparāya ca \|*  
*nārāyaṇasvarūpāya nārāṇayatanūdbhava \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Obeisance to Thee, O lord Nārāyaṇa, devoted to Nārāyaṇa, of the form of Nārāyaṇa, oh! one born of Nārāyaṇa’s body.

## \|\| 6.2.25 \|\|

*namaste sarvarūpāya mahānarakahāriṇe \|*  
*pāpāpahāriṇe tubhyaṃ namo vṛṣabhavāhana \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Obeisance to Thee of all forms, the destroyer of great hells, destroyer of sins. Obeisance to you, O bull-vehicled god.

## \|\| 6.2.26 \|\|

*kṣaṇādikālarūpāya svabhaktabaladāyine \|*  
*nānārūpāya rūpāya daityacakravimardine \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Obeisance to Thee of the form of time, moment etc. Obeisance to Thee who bestows strength on his devotees; obeisance to the multiformed; obeisance to the annihilator of the hosts of Asuras.

## \|\| 6.2.27 \|\|

*namo brahmaṇyadevāya gobrāhmaṇahitāya ca \|*  
*sahasramūrttaye tubhyaṃ sahasrāvayavāya ca \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Obeisance to the lord, conducive to the welfare of brahmins and cows. Obeisance to the thousand-formed, obeisance to Thee of thousand organs.

## \|\| 6.2.28 \|\|

*dharmarūpāya sattvāya namassattvātmane hara \|*  
*vedavedyasvarūpāya namo vedapriyāya ca \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. O Śiva, obeisance to Thee of the form of virtue, to the Sattva, to the Ātman of Sattva. Obeisance to thee whose form is knowable through the Vedas. Obeisance to thee, the beloved of the Vedas.

## \|\| 6.2.29 \|\|

*namo vedasvarūpāya vedavaktre namo namaḥ \|*  
*sadācārādhvagamyāya sadācārādhvagāmine \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Obeisance to Thee whose form is the Veda, obeisance to the reciter of the Vedas. Obeisance to Thee who traversest the path of good conduct and who art approachable through the path of good conduct.

## \|\| 6.2.30 \|\|

*viṣṭaraśravase tubhyaṃ namassatyamayāya ca \|*  
*satyapriyāya satyāya satyagamyāya te namaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Obeisance to Thee the glory-seated; to the Truthful, beloved of truth, to the truth. Obeisance to Thee know-able through the truth.

## \|\| 6.2.31 \|\|

*namaste māyine tubhyaṃ māyādhīśāya vai namaḥ \|*  
*brahmagāya namastubhyaṃ brahmaṇe brahmajāya ca \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Obeisance to Thee possessed of magic-power, obeisance to the lord of magic; Obeisance to Thee (knowable through the Vedas), to Brahman, to the one born of Brahmā.

## \|\| 6.2.32 \|\|

*tapase te namastvīśa tapasā phaladāyine \|*  
*stutyāya stutaye nityaṃ stutisaṃprītacetase \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Obeisance to Thee, O lord, the penance, the bestower of the fruits of penance, obeisance to thee, worthy of eulogy, the eulogy, and to Thee whose mind is pleased with eulogy always.

## \|\| 6.2.33 \|\|

*śrutyācāraprasannāya stutyācārapriyāya ca \|*  
*caturvidhasvarūpāya jalasthalajarūpiṇe \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Obeisance to Thee delighted with vedic conduct, to the one fond of praiseworthy conduct; to the one who has fourfold forms and the forms of aquatic and terrestrial beings.

## \|\| 6.2.34 \|\|

*sarve devādayo nātha śreṣṭhatvena vibhūtayaḥ \|*  
*devānāmindrarūpo'si grahāṇāṃ tvaṃ ravirmataḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. O lord, the gods and all others, being excellent, are your excellences. Among the gods you are Indra; among the planets you are the sun.

## \|\| 6.2.35 \|\|

*satyaloko'si lokānāṃ saritāṃ dyusaridbhavān \|*  
*śvetavarṇo'si varṇānāṃ sarasāṃ mānasaṃ saraḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Among the worlds you are Satyaloka. Among the rivers you are the celestial river Gaṅgā. Among the colours you are the white colour. Among the lakes you are the Mānasa lake.

## \|\| 6.2.36 \|\|

*śailānāṃ girijātātaḥ kāmadhuktvaṃ ca goṣu ha \|*  
*kṣīrodadhistu sindhūnāṃ dhātūnāṃ hāṭako bhavān \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Among the mountains you are the Himālaya mountain. Among the cows you are the Kāmadhenu, Among the oceans you are the milk ocean. Among the metals you are gold.

## \|\| 6.2.37 \|\|

*varṇānāṃ brāhmaṇo'si tvaṃ nṛṇāṃ rājāsi śaṃkara \|*  
*muktikṣetreṣu kāśī tvaṃ tīrthānāṃ tīrtharāḍ bhavān \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Among the four castes you are the brahmin. O Śiva, among men you are the king. Among holy centres of salvation you are Kāśī. Among the sacred rivers you are the supreme sacred river.

## \|\| 6.2.38 \|\|

*upaleṣu samasteṣu sphaṭikastvaṃ maheśvara \|*  
*kamalastvaṃ prasūneṣu śaileṣu himavāṃstathā \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Among all stones, you are the crystal, O great god, among the flowers you are the lotus; among mountains you are Himavat.

## \|\| 6.2.39 \|\|

*bhavānvāgvyavahāreṣu bhārgavastvaṃ kaviṣvapi \|*  
*pakṣiṣvevāsi śarabhaḥ siṃho hiṃsreṣu saṃmataḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Among all activities you are the speech; among poets you are Bhārgava. Among birds you are the eight-legged Śarabha. Among beasts of prey you are the lion.

## \|\| 6.2.40 \|\|

*śālagrāmaśilā ca tvaṃ śilāsu vṛṣabhadhvaja \|*  
*pūjya rūpeṣu sarveṣu narmadāliṃgameva hi \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. O bull-bannered deity, among rocks you are Śālagrāma; among the forms of worship you are Narmadā Liṅga.

## \|\| 6.2.41 \|\|

*nandīśvaro'si paśuṣu vṛṣabhaḥ parameśvara \|*  
*vedeṣūpaniṣadrūpī yajvanāṃ śītabhānumān \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Among animals, you are the bull Nandīśvara, O

lord Śiva. Among Vedic texts you are in the form of Upaniṣads; Among the sacrificers you are the cool-rayed moon.

## \|\| 6.2.42 \|\|

*pratāpināṃ pāvakastvaṃ śaivānāmacyuto bhavān \|*  
*bhārataṃ tvaṃ purāṇānāṃ makāro'syakṣareṣu ca \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Among the burning ones, you are the fire, among the devotees of Śiva, you are Viṣṇu, among Purāṇas you are Bharata; among the letters of the alphabet you are the letter Ma2.

## \|\| 6.2.43 \|\|

*praṇavo bījamaṃtrāṇāṃ dāruṇānāṃ viṣaṃ bhavān \|*  
*vyomavyaptimatāṃ tvaṃ vai paramātmāsi cātmanām \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Among the Bījamantras you are the Praṇava; among the terrible ones you are poison; among the pervading ones you are the firmament; among the Ātmans you are the supreme Ātman.

## \|\| 6.2.44 \|\|

*indriyāṇāṃ manaśca tvaṃ dānānāmabhayaṃ bhavān \|*  
*pāvanānāṃ jalaṃ cāsi jīvanānāṃ tathāmṛtam \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Among the sense-organs you are the mind; among the charitable gifts you are the gift of freedom from fear; among the sanctifying and life-giving agents you are considered the waters.

## \|\| 6.2.45 \|\|

*lābhānāṃ putralābho'si vāyurvegavatāmasi \|*  
*nityakarmasu sarveṣu saṃdhyopāstirbhavānmatā \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Among all acquisitions you are the acquisition of sons; among those with velocity you are the wind; among the routine sacred rites you are the Sandhyā worship.

## \|\| 6.2.46 \|\|

*kratūnāmaśvamedho'si yugānāṃ prathamo yugaḥ \|*  
*puṣyastvaṃ sarvadhiṇyānāmamāvāsyā tithiṣvasi \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Among sacrifices you are the horse-sacrifice. Among the Yugas you are the Kṛta yuga; among the asterisms you are Puṣya; among the Tithis you are Amāvāsyā.

## \|\| 6.2.47 \|\|

*sarvartuṣu vasaṃtastvaṃ sarvaparvasu saṃkramaḥ \|*  
*kuśo'si tṛṇajātīnāṃ sthūlavṛkṣeṣu vai vaṭaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Among the seasons you are the spring; among holy occasions you are the Saṃkrama; among grasses you are the Kuśa grass; among gross trees you are the Banyan tree.

## \|\| 6.2.48 \|\|

*yogeṣu ca vyatīpātassomavallī latāsu ca \|*  
*buddhīnāṃ dharmabuddhistvaṃ kalatraṃ suhṛdāṃ bhavān \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Among the Yogas you are the Vyatīpāta; among creepers you are the Soma creeper; among intellectual activities you are the virtuous inclination, among intimate ones you are the wife.

## \|\| 6.2.49 \|\|

*sādhakānāṃ śucīnāṃ tvaṃ prāṇāyāmo maheśvara \|*  
*jyotirliṃgeṣu sarveṣu bhavān viśve śvaro mataḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Among the pure activities of the aspirant, O great lord, you are Prāṇāyāma; among all Jyotirliṅgas you are Viśveśvara.

## \|\| 6.2.50 \|\|

*dharmastvaṃ sarvabaṃdhūnāmāśramāṇāṃ paro bhavān \|*  
*mokṣastvaṃ sarvavarṇeṣu rudrāṇāṃ nīlalohitaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Among all kindred beings you are Dharma. In all stages of life you are Sannyāsa. You are the supreme Liberation in all Vargas. Among Rudras you are Nīlalohita.

## \|\| 6.2.51 \|\|

*ādityānāṃ vāsudevo hanūmānvānareṣu ca \|*  
*yajñānāṃ japayajño'si rāmaḥ śastrabhṛtāṃ bhavān \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Among all Ādityas you are Vāsudeva; among the monkeys you are Hanumat; among the sacrifices you are Japayajña; among the weapon-bearers you are Rāma:

## \|\| 6.2.52 \|\|

*gaṃdharvāṇāṃ citraratho vasūnāṃ pāvako dhruvam \|*  
*māsānāmadhimāsastvaṃ vratānāṃ tvaṃ caturdaśī \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Among the Gandharvas you are Citraratha; among the Vasus you are certainly the fire; among the months you are the intercalary month; among the holy rites you are the Caturdaśī rite.

## \|\| 6.2.53 \|\|

*airāvato gajendrāṇāṃ siddhānāṃ kapilo mataḥ \|*  
*anaṃtastvaṃ hi nāgānāṃ pitṝṇāmaryamā bhavān \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Among all lordly elephants you are Airāvata3; among all Siddhas you are Kapila; among all serpents you are Ananta, among all Pitṛs you are Aryaman.

## \|\| 6.2.54-55 \|\|

*kālaḥ kalayatāṃ ca tvaṃ daityānāṃ balireva ca \|*  
*kiṃ bahūktena deveśa sarvaṃ viṣṭabhya vai jagat \|\| 54 \|\|*

*ekāṃśena sthitastvaṃ hi bahiḥstho'nvita eva ca \|\| 55 \|\|*

54-55. You are Kāla (Time) among those who calculate; among Asuras you are Bali. O lord of gods, of what avail is a detailed narration? You preside over the entire universe and remain partially stationed within and partially without.

## \|\| 6.2.56-57 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*iti stutvā surāssarve mahādevaṃ vṛṣadhvajam \|*  
*stotrairnānāvidhaidiṃvyaiḥ śūlinaṃ parameśvaram \|\| 56 \|\|*

*pratyūcuḥ prastutaṃ dīnāssvārthaṃ svārthavicakṣaṇāḥ \|*  
*vāsavādyā nataskadhāḥ kṛtāñjali puṭā mune \|\| 57 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

56-57. Eulogising thus the bull-bannered, the tridentbearing lord Śiva with various kinds of divine hymns, the gods replied thus relevant to the context. O sage, all of them including Indra and others were very much distressed. They were very shrewd in managing their selfish interests and so mentioned them to Śiva with stooping shoulders and palms joined in reverence.

## \|\| 6.2.58 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*parājitā mahādeva bhrātṛbhyāṃ sahitena tu \|*  
*bhagavaṃstārakotpannaiḥ sarve devāssavāsavāḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

The gods said:—

58\. O lord Śiva, the gods including Indra have been defeated by the Asura accompanied by his brothers. O lord, all the gods have been defeated by the sons of Tāraka.

## \|\| 6.2.59 \|\|

*trailokyaṃ svavaśaṃ nītaṃ tathā ca munisattamāḥ \|*  
*vidhvastāssarvasaṃsiddhāssarvamutsāditaṃ jagat \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. The three worlds have been brought under their sway. The excellent sages and the Siddhas have been destroyed. The entire universe has been exterminated by them.

## \|\| 6.2.60 \|\|

*yajñabhāgānsamagrāṃstu svayaṃ gṛhṇāti dāruṇaḥ \|*  
*pravartito hyadharmastairṛṣīṇāṃ ca nivāritaḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. The terrible Asuras take the entire share of the sacrificial benefits to themselves. They have initiated evil activities. They have prevented the sages from performing their virtuous rites.

## \|\| 6.2.61 \|\|

*avadhyāssarvabhūtānāṃ niyataṃ tārakātmajāḥ \|*  
*tadicchayā prakurvanti sarve karmāṇi śaṃkara \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Definitely the sons of Tāraka cannot be killed by any living being. Hence, O Śiva, they perform everything as they please.

## \|\| 6.2.62 \|\|

*yāvanna kṣīyate daityairghoraistripuravāsibhiḥ \|*  
*tāvadvidhīyatāṃ nītiryayā saṃrakṣyate jagat \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Let some policy be laid down for the protection of the universe lest the terrible Asuras, the denizens of the three cities, should destroy the world.

## \|\| 6.2.63 \|\|

*\|\| sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya vacasteṣāmindrādīnāṃ divaukasām \|*  
*śivaḥ saṃbhāṣamāṇānāṃ prativākyamuvāca saḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

63\. On hearing these words of Indra and other heaven-dwellers who were expatiating on their distress, Śiva spoke in return.

## Chapter 3 - The virtues of the Tripuras

## \|\| 6.3.1 \|\|

*śiva uvāca \|*  
*ayaṃ vai tripurādhyakṣa puṇyavānvartate'dhunā \|*  
*yatra puṇyaṃ pravarteta na haṃtavyo budhaiḥ kvacit \|\| 1 \|\|*

Śiva said:—

1\. A meritorious person is the presiding ruler of the Tripuras now. He who practises meritorious deeds should not be killed by sensible persons.

## \|\| 6.3.2 \|\|

*jānāmi devakaṣṭaṃ ca vibudhāssakalaṃ mahat \|*  
*daityāste prabalā haṃtumaśakyāstu surāsuraiḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. O gods, I know the misery of the gods completely. It is great. Those Asuras are very strong. They cannot be killed by the gods or demons.

## \|\| 6.3.3 \|\|

*puṇyavaṃtastu te sarve samayāstārakātmajāḥ \|*  
*dussādhyastu vadhasteṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ puravāsinām \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The sons of Tāraka and Maya are equally meritorious. O sensible ones, they are invincible to all the citizens.

## \|\| 6.3.4 \|\|

*mitradrohaṃ kathaṃ jānankaromi raṇakarkaśaḥ \|*  
*suhṛddrohe mahatpāpaṃ pūrvamuktaṃ svayaṃbhuvā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. How can I knowingly commit malicious deeds to my friends though I am hardy and powerful in battles? Even Brahmā has said that there is a great sin attending on even casual malicious actions.

## \|\| 6.3.5 \|\|

*brahmaghnaṃ ca surāpe ca steye bhagnavrate tathā \|*  
*niṣkṛtirvihitā sadbhiḥ kṛtaghne nāsti niṣkṛtiḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. There are ways of atonement and amends for a brahmin slayer, a wine addict, a thief or a person who violates sacred rites. But there is no expiation for ungrateful men.

## \|\| 6.3.6 \|\|

*mama bhaktāstu te daityā mayā vadhyā kathaṃ surāḥ \|*  
*vicāryatāṃ bhavadbhiśca dharmajñaireva dharmataḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Those Asuras are my devotees. O Gods, how can they be slain by us? Let this aspect be thought over by you who know what is virtue. You must consider this virtuously.

## \|\| 6.3.7 \|\|

*tāvatte naiva haṃtavyā yāvadbhaktikṛtaśca me \|*  
*tathāpi viṣṇave devā nivedyaṃ kāraṇaṃ tvidam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. They should not be slain as long as they continue their devotion to me. Yet, this reason may very well be intimated to Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 6.3.8 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityevaṃ tadvacaḥ śrutvā devāśśakrapurogamāḥ \|*  
*nyavedayan drutaṃ sarve brahmaṇe prathamaṃ mune \|\| 8 \|\|*

Samtkumāra said:—

8\. O sage, thus when they heard these words Indra and other gods immediately intimated this to Brahmā in the first instance.

## \|\| 6.3.9 \|\|

*tato vidhiṃ puraskṛtya sarve devāssavāsavāḥ \|*  
*vaikuṃṭhaṃ prayayuśśīghraṃ sarve śobhāsamanvitam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Then, with Brahmā at their head, the gods including Indra quickly went to Vaikuṇṭha in all glory.

## \|\| 6.3.10 \|\|

*tatra gatvā hariṃ dṛṣṭvā praṇemurjātasaṃbhramāḥ \|*  
*tuṣṭuvuśca mahābhaktyā kṛtāṃjalipuṭāssurāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. On going there and seeing Viṣṇu, the gods bowed to him in agitation, and with their palms joined in reverence they eulogised him with great devotion.

## \|\| 6.3.11 \|\|

*svaduḥkhakāraṇaṃ sarvaṃ pūrvavattadanaṃtaram \|*  
*nyavedayandrutaṃ tasmai viṣṇave prabhaviṣṇave \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. They intimated to Viṣṇu the powerful, the reasons for their misery, the earlier ones as well as the later.

## \|\| 6.3.12 \|\|

*devaduḥkhaṃ tataḥ śrutvā dattaṃ ca tripurālaye \|*  
*jñātvā vrataṃ ca teṣāṃ tadviṣṇurvacanamabravīt \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. On hearing the distress of the gods as well as the vows observed by the Tripuras, Viṣṇu spoke as follows.

## \|\| 6.3.13 \|\|

*viṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*idaṃ satyaṃ vacaścaiva yatra dharmassanātanaḥ \|*  
*tatra duḥkhaṃ na jāyeta sūrye dṛṣṭe yathā tamaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

Viṣṇu said:—

13\. This is true that where the eternal virtue reigns supreme, no misery raises its head like darkness when the sun is seen.

## \|\| 6.3.14 \|\|

*\|\| sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityetadvacanaṃ śrutvā devā duḥkhamupāgatāḥ \|*  
*punarūcustathā viṣṇuṃ parimlānamukhāmbujāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

14\. On hearing these words the gods became miserable and dejected. They spoke to Viṣṇu with their lotus-like faces depressed.

## \|\| 6.3.15 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*kathaṃ caiva prakarttavyaṃ kathaṃ duḥkhaṃ nirasyate \|*  
*kathaṃ bhavema sukhinaḥ kathaṃ sthāsyāmahe vayam \|\| 15 \|\|*

The gods said:—

15\. How are we to go about our activities. How can our misery be dispelled? How can we be happy? How are we to remain firm?

## \|\| 6.3.16 \|\|

*kathaṃ dharmā bhaviṣyaṃti tripure jīvite sati \|*  
*devaduḥkhapradā nūnaṃ sarve tripuravāsinaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. As long as the Tripuras are alive, how can we observe virtuous activities? All the residents of the three cities give troubles to us.

## \|\| 6.3.17 \|\|

*kiṃ vā te tripurasyeha vadhaścaiva vidhīyatām \|*  
*nocedakālikī devasaṃhatiḥ kriyatāṃ dhruvam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. What else can we say to you? Either the annihilation of the Tripuras shall be made or the untimely destruction of the gods shall be proceeded with.

## \|\| 6.3.18 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityuktvā te tadā devā duḥkhaṃ kṛtvā punaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*sthitiṃ naiva gatiṃ te vai cakrurdevavarādiha \|\| 18 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

18\. After saying this and lamenting frequently, the gods were in a fix and could neither stay nor leave the proximity of Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 6.3.19-21 \|\|

*tānvai tathāvidhāndṛṣṭvā hīnānvinayasaṃyutān \|*  
*sopi nārāyaṇaḥ śrīmāṃściṃtayeccetasā tathā \|\| 19 \|\|*

*kiṃ kāryaṃ devakāryeṣu mayā devasahā yinā \|*  
*śivabhaktāstu te daityāstārakasya sutā iti \|\| 20 \|\|*

*iti saṃcintya tatkāle viṣṇunā prabhaviṣṇunā \|*  
*tato yajñāssmṛtāstena devakāryārthamakṣayāḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

19-21. On seeing them in that plight, distressed and humiliated, Viṣṇu thought within himself, “I am the benefactor of the gods. But what can I do in this affair? The sons of Tāraka are the devotees of Śiva.” After thinking like this, he thought upon the Supreme Viṣṇu, the lord of sacrifices, the primordial Puruṣa.

## \|\| 6.3.22 \|\|

*tadviṣṇusmṛtimātreṇa yajñāste tatkṣaṇaṃ drutam \|*  
*āgatāstatra yatrāste śrīpatiḥ puruṣottamaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Immediately on being thought upon by Viṣṇu all the sacrifices came where Viṣṇu was stationed.

## \|\| 6.3.23 \|\|

*tato viṣṇuṃ yajñapatiṃ purāṇaṃ puruṣaṃ harim \|*  
*praṇamya tuṣṭuvuste vai kṛtāṃjalipuṭāstadā \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. With palms joined in reverence they bowed to and eulogised Viṣṇu, the lord of sacrifices and the primordial Puruṣa.

## \|\| 6.3.24 \|\|

*bhagavānapi tāndṛṣṭvā yajñānprāha sanātanam \|*  
*sanātanastadā seṃdrāndevānālokya cācyutaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. The eternal lord Viṣṇu saw the eternal sacrifices and told them looking at the gods too including Indra.

## \|\| 6.3.25 \|\|

*viṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*anenaiva sadā devā yajadhvaṃ parameśvaram \|*  
*puratrayavināśāya jagattrayavibhūtaye \|\| 25 \|\|*

Viṣṇu said:—

25\. In order to destroy the three cities and to bring about prosperity in the three worlds, O gods perform the worship of lord Śiva along with the lord of sacrifices.

## \|\| 6.3.26 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*acyutasya vacaḥ śrutvā devadevasya dhīmataḥ \|*  
*premṇā te praṇatiṃ kṛtvā yajñeśaṃ te'stuvansurāḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

26\. On hearing the words of Viṣṇu, the intelligent lord of the gods and bowing to him lovingly, the gods eulogised the lord of sacrifices.

## \|\| 6.3.27 \|\|

*evaṃ stutvā tato devā ajayanyajñapūruṣam \|*  
*yajñoktena vidhānena saṃpūrṇavidhayo mune \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. O sage, eulogising thus, the gods worshipped the Sacrificial Being in accordance with the rules governing the same with the complete rites.

## \|\| 6.3.28 \|\|

*tatastasmādyajñakuṃḍātsamutpetussahasraśaḥ \|*  
*bhūtasaṃghā mahākāyāḥ śūlaśaktigadāyudhāḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Then from the sacrificial pit rose up thousands of Bhūtas of huge size and armed with tridents, spears, iron clubs and other weapons.

## \|\| 6.3.29-31 \|\|

*dadṛśuste surāstān vai bhūtasaṃghānsahasraśaḥ \|*  
*śūla śaktigadāhastāndaṇḍacāpaśilāyudhān \|\| 29 \|\|*

*nānāpraharaṇopetān nānāveṣadharāṃstathā \|*  
*kālāgnirudrasadṛśānkālasūryopamāṃstadā \|\| 30 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭvā tānabravīdviṣṇuḥ praṇipatya puraḥsthitān \|*  
*bhūtānyajñapatiḥ śrīmānudrājñāpratipālakaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

29-31. The gods saw thousands of Bhūtasaṅghas armed with tridents and spears and possessing various weapons such as staffs, bows, stones, etc. They had various missiles to strike with. They were in different guises. They resembled the destructive fire and Rudra. They were on a par with the destructive Sun. When they bowed to him and stood waiting in front, Viṣṇu saw them. The glorious lord of sacrifices who carried out the behests of Rudra, spoke to them.

## \|\| 6.3.32 \|\|

*viṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*bhūtāḥ śṛṇuta madvākyaṃ devakāryārthamudyatāḥ \|*  
*gacchantu tripuraṃ sadyassarve hi balavattarāḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Viṣṇu said—“O Bhūtas, listen to my statement. You are all very powerful and have risen up for fulfilling the task of the gods. All of you go immediately to the three cities.

## \|\| 6.3.33 \|\|

*gatvā dagdhvā ca bhittvā ca bhaṅktvā daityapuratrayam \|*  
*punaryathāgatā bhūtāgaṃtumarhatha bhūtaye \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Go there, strike at, break and burn the three cities of the Asuras. O Bhūtas, thereafter you can go away as you please for prosperity.

## \|\| 6.3.34 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*tacchrutvā bhagavadvākyaṃ tato bhūtagaṇāśca te \|*  
*praṇamya devadevaṃ taṃ yayurdaityapuratrayam \|\| 34 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

34\. On hearing the words of the lord, the hosts of Bhūtas bowed to the lord of the gods and went to the three cities of the Asuras.

## \|\| 6.3.35 \|\|

*gatvā tatpraviśaṃtaśca tripurādhipatejasi \|*  
*bhasmasādabhavansadyaśśalabhā iva pāvake \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Immediately after their entry into the cities they were reduced to ashes like moths in the fire.

## \|\| 6.3.36 \|\|

*avaśiṣṭāśca ye kecitpalāyanaparāyaṇāḥ \|*  
*nissṛtyāraṃ samāyātā harernikaṭamākulāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Those who escaped fled out of the cities and came grief-stricken to Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 6.3.37 \|\|

*tāndṛṣṭvā sa hariḥ śrutvā tacca vṛttamaśeṣataḥ \|*  
*ciṃtayāmāsa bhagavānmanasā puruṣottamaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. On seeing them and hearing the incidents in detail, lord Viṣṇu pondered over this.

## \|\| 6.3.38 \|\|

*kiṃ kṛtyamadhunā kāryamiti saṃtaptamānasaḥ \|*  
*saṃtaptānamarānsarvānājñāya ca savāsavān \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. On realising that all the gods were distressed and dejected in the mind, he too was extremely grieved.

## \|\| 6.3.39 \|\|

*kathaṃ teṣāṃ ca daityānāṃ balāddhatvā puratrayam \|*  
*devakāryaṃ kariṣyāmītyāsīcciṃtāsamākulaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. He became much worried at the thought “How can I destroy the three cities of the Asuras, with force and carry out the task of the gods?”

## \|\| 6.3.40 \|\|

*nāśo'bhicārato nāsti dharmiṣṭhānāṃ na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*iti prāha svayaṃ ceśaḥ śrutyācārapramāṇakṛt \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. The lord who had authoritatively laid down the rules of conduct according to the Vedas, said “There is no doubt in this that the virtuous ones cannot be destroyed by black magic.

## \|\| 6.3.41 \|\|

*daityāśca te hi dharmiṣṭhāssarve tripuravāsinaḥ \|*  
*tasmādavadhyatāṃ prāptā nānyathā surapuṃgavāḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. O good gods, these Asuras and the other residents of the three cities are virtuous. Hence they have become invincible. Not in any other manner.

## \|\| 6.3.42 \|\|

*kṛtvā tu sumahatpāpaṃ rudramabhyarcayaṃti te \|*  
*mucyaṃte pātakaiḥ sarvaiḥ padmapatramivāṃbhasā \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. After perpetrating great sins they worship Śiva and so they are freed of all sins even as the leaves of the lotus from water.

## \|\| 6.3.43 \|\|

*rudrābhyarcanato devāḥ sarve kāmā bhavaṃti hi \|*  
*nānopabhogasaṃpattirvaśyatāṃ yāti vai bhuvi \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. O gods, thanks to the worship of Śiva, their cherished desires are realised. Different means of enjoyment in the world are brought under their control.

## \|\| 6.3.44 \|\|

*tasmāttadbhogino daityā liṃgārcanaparāyaṇāḥ \|*  
*anekavidhasaṃpattermokṣasyāpi paratra ca \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Hence these Asuras who are devoted to the phallic worship enjoy different kinds of pleasures and prosperity and salvation hereafter.

## \|\| 6.3.45 \|\|

*tataḥ kṛtvā dharmavighnaṃ teṣāmevātmamāyayā \|*  
*daityānāṃ devakāryārthaṃ hariṣye tripuraṃ kṣaṇāt \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Then putting obstacles in their activities of virtuous rites, by means of magic art I shall destroy the three cities of the Asuras quickly for accomplishing the task of the Asuras.”

## \|\| 6.3.46 \|\|

*vicāryetthaṃ tatasteṣāṃ bhagavānpuruṣottamaḥ \|*  
*kartuṃ vyavasthitaḥ paścāddharmavighnaṃ surāriṇām \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. After thinking thus, lord Viṣṇu set himself to the task of interfering with the sacred rites of the Asuras.

## \|\| 6.3.47 \|\|

*yāvacca veda dharmāstu yāvadvai śaṃkarārcanam \|*  
*yāvacca śucikṛtyādi tāvannāśo bhavenna hi \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. As long as the worship of Śiva is continued and as long as the pure activities are strictly adhered to, there is no question of their ruin at all.

## \|\| 6.3.48 \|\|

*tasmādevaṃ prakartavyaṃ vedadharmastato vrajet \|*  
*tyaktaliṃgārcanā daityā bhaviṣyaṃti na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Hence such means shall be followed as will make Vedic Dharma disappear thence. Undoubtedly the Asuras will foresake their worship of the phallic emblem of Siva.

## \|\| 6.3.49 \|\|

*iti niścitya vai viṣṇurvighnārthamakarottadā \|*  
*teṣāṃ dharmasya daityānāmupāyaṃ śruti khaṇḍanam \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Deciding thus, Viṣṇu started ridiculing the Vedas for putting up obstacles in the virtuous activities of the Asuras.

## \|\| 6.3.50 \|\|

*tadaivovāca devānsa viṣṇurdevasahāyakṛt \|*  
*śivājñayā śivenaivājñaptastrailokyarakṣaṇe \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. At the bidding of Śiva, Viṣṇu who was commanded to protect the three worlds, and who renders help to the gods spoke to them.

## \|\| 6.3.51 \|\|

*\|\| viṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*he devāssakalā yūyaṃ gacchata svagṛhāndhruvam \|*  
*devakāryaṃ kariṣyāmi yathāmati na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

Viṣṇu said:—

51\. O gods, you go to your own abodes. Undoubtedly I shall carry on the task of the gods to the extent of my intellect.

## \|\| 6.3.52 \|\|

*tānrudrādvimukhānnūnaṃ kariṣyāmi suyatnataḥ \|*  
*svabhaktirahitāñjñātvā tānkariṣyati bhasmasāt \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Strenuously I shall make them averse to Śiva. Coming to know that they are devoid of devotion to him he will reduce them to ashes.

## \|\| 6.3.53 \|\|

*\|\| sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*tadājñāṃ śirasādhāyaśvāsitāste'marā mune \|*  
*svasvadhāmāni viśvastā yayurbrahmāpi moditāḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

53\. O sage, accepting his behest with bent head, the gods and Brahmā felt satisfied and with faith in their hearts returned to their abodes.

## \|\| 6.3.54 \|\|

*tataścaivākarodviṣṇurdevārthaṃ hitamuttamam \|*  
*tadeva śrūyatāṃ samyaksarvapāpapraṇāśanam \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Thereafter Viṣṇu performed deeds conducive to the welfare of the gods. Listen to those excellent deeds destructive of all sins.

## Chapter 4 - The Tripuras are initiated

## \|\| 6.4.1 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*asṛjacca mahātejāḥ puruṣaṃ svātmasaṃbhavam \|*  
*ekaṃ māyāmayaṃ teṣāṃ dharmavighnārthamacyutaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

1\. For causing obstacles in their virtuous activities, Viṣṇu of great brilliance, created a Puruṣa born of himself.

## \|\| 6.4.2 \|\|

*muṃḍinaṃ mlānavastraṃ ca guṃphipātrasamanvitam \|*  
*dadhānaṃ puṃjikāṃ haste cālayaṃtaṃ padepade \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. He had a shaven head, wore dirty clothes, held a woven wicker vessel in his hand and a roll of cotton in his hand which he shook at every step.

## \|\| 6.4.3 \|\|

*vastrayuktaṃ tathā hastaṃ kṣīyamāṇaṃ mukhe sadā \|*  
*dharmeti vyāharaṃtaṃ hi vācā viklavayā munim \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. His hands tucking at the cloth were weak. His face was pale and weak. In a faltering voice he was muttering “Dharma, Dharma.”

## \|\| 6.4.4 \|\|

*sa namaskṛtya viṣṇuṃ taṃ tatpurassa sthito'tha vai \|*  
*uvāca vacanaṃ tatra hariṃ sa prāṃjalistadā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. He bowed to Viṣṇu and stood in front of him. He spoke to Viṣṇu with hands joined in reverence.

## \|\| 6.4.5 \|\|

*arihannacyutaṃ pūjyaṃ kiṃ karomi tadādiśa \|*  
*kāni nāmāni me deva sthānaṃ vāpi vada prabho \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. “O laudable, revered one, please tell me what my names are and what my place shall be.”

## \|\| 6.4.6 \|\|

*ityevaṃ bhagavānviṣṇuḥ śrutvā tasya śubhaṃ vacaḥ \|*  
*prasannamānaso bhūtvā vacanaṃ cedamabravīt \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. On hearing these auspicious words, Lord Viṣṇu became delighted and spoke these words.

## \|\| 6.4.7 \|\|

*\|\| viṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*yadarthaṃ nirmito'si tvaṃ nibodha kathayāmi te \|*  
*madaṃgaja mahāprājña madrūpastvaṃ na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

Viṣṇu said:—

7\. O intelligent one, born of me, you are certainly identical with me in form. Know why you have been created. I shall tell you.

## \|\| 6.4.8 \|\|

*mamāṃgācca samutpanno matkāryaṃ kartumarhasi \|*  
*madīyastvaṃ sadā pūjyo bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. You are born of me. You can perform my task. You are my own. Certainly you will be worthy of worship always.

## \|\| 6.4.9 \|\|

*arihannāma te syāttu hyanyāni na śubhāni ca \|*  
*sthānaṃ vakṣyāmi te paścācchṛṇu prastutamādarāt \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Let your name be Arihat. You will have other auspicious names too. I shall assign to you a place afterwards. Now hear with reverence what is relevant to the context.

## \|\| 6.4.10-11 \|\|

*māyinmāyāmayaṃ śāstraṃ tatṣoḍaśasahasrakam \|*  
*śrautasmārtaviruddhaṃ ca varṇāśrama vivarjitam \|\| 10 \|\|*

*apabhraṃśamayaṃ śāstraṃ karmavādamayaṃ tathā \|*  
*racayeti prayatnena tadvistāro bhaviṣyati \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. O you who wield Māyā, ceate a deceptive sacred text of sixteen hundred thousand verses, contrary to Śrutis and Smṛtis wherein Varṇas and Āśramas shall be eschewed. Let that holy text be in Apabhraṃśa lauguage. Let there be emphasis on actions. You shall strain yourself to extend it further.

## \|\| 6.4.12 \|\|

*dadāmi tava nirmāṇe sāmarthyaṃ tadbhaviṣyati \|*  
*māyā ca vividhā śīghraṃ tvadadhīnā bhaviṣyati \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. I shall bestow on you the ability to create it. Different kinds of magic arts shall be subservient to you.”

## \|\| 6.4.13 \|\|

*tacchrutvā vacanaṃ tasya hareśca paramātmanaḥ \|*  
*namaskṛtya pratyuvāca sa māyī taṃ janārdanam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. On hearing the words of Viṣṇu, the great soul, the Māyā Puruṣa bowed to and replied to Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 6.4.14 \|\|

*muṇḍyuvāca \|*  
*yatkartavyaṃ mayā deva drutamādiśa tatprabho \|*  
*tvadājñayākhilaṃ karma saphalaśca bhaviṣyati \|\| 14 \|\|*

The shaven-head said:—

14\. O lord, command me quickly what I shall do. At your bidding, all activities shall be fruitful.

## \|\| 6.4.15 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityuktvā pāṭhayāmāsa śāstraṃ māyāmayaṃ tathā \|*  
*ihaiva svarganarakapratyayo nānyathā punaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

15\. Saying this he recited the main tenet in the deceptive philosophy. “Heaven and hell are functioning here itself.”

## \|\| 6.4.16 \|\|

*tamuvāca punarviṣṇuḥ smṛtvā śivapadāṃbujam \|*  
*mohanīyā ime daityāḥ sarve tripuravāsinaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Remembering the lotus-like feet of Śiva, Viṣṇu told him again. “These Asuras, the residents of the three cities, shall be deluded.

## \|\| 6.4.17 \|\|

*kāryāste dīkṣitā nūnaṃ pāṭhanīyāḥ prayatnataḥ \|*  
*madājñayā na doṣaste bhaviṣyati mahāmate \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. O intellegent one, they shall be initiated by you. They shall be taught strenuously. At my bidding you will incur no sin on that account.

## \|\| 6.4.18 \|\|

*dharmāstatra prakāśante śrautasmārttā na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*anayā vidyayā sarve sphoṭanīyā dhruvaṃ yate \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. O ascetic, no doubt, Vedic and Smārta rites flourish and shine there. But these shall certainly be exploded through this Vidyā.

## \|\| 6.4.19 \|\|

*gaṃtumarhasi nāśārthaṃ muṇḍiṃstripuravāsinām \|*  
*tamodharmaṃ saṃprakāśya nāśayasva puratrayam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. O you with shaven head, you shall go there for destroying the residents of the three cities. Revealing the Tamasika rites, destroy the three cities.

## \|\| 6.4.20 \|\|

*tataścaiva punargatvā marusthalyāṃ tvayā vibho \|*  
*sthātavyaṃ ca svadharmeṇa kaliryāvatsamā vrajet \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. After that, O great one, you shall go to the desert region and stay there carrying on your own duties and activities till the advent of the Kali age.

## \|\| 6.4.21 \|\|

*pravṛtte tu yuge tasminsvīyo dharmaḥ prakāśyatām \|*  
*śiṣyaiśca pratiśiṣyaiśca vartanīyastvayā punaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. When the Kali age begins let your Dharma be revealed. You shall then continue to do so by means of disciples and disciples’ disciples.

## \|\| 6.4.22 \|\|

*madājñayā bhavaddharmo vistāraṃ yāsyati dhruvam \|*  
*madanujñāparo nityaṃ gatiṃ prāpsyasi māmakīm \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. At my bidding your cult shall certainly expand. Depending upon my permission and direction you will attain me as your goal.”

## \|\| 6.4.23 \|\|

*evamājñā tadā dattā viṣṇunā prabhaviṣṇunā \|*  
*śāsanāddevadevasya hṛdā tvaṃtardadhe hariḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*
