23\. At the bidding of the lord Śiva transmitted through the thought process, Viṣṇu, the powerful, commanded him thus and vanished.

## \|\| 6.4.24 \|\|

*tatassa muṃḍī paripālayanharerājñāṃ tathā nirmitavāṃśca śiṣyān \|*  
*yathāsvarūpaṃ caturastadānīṃ māyāmayaṃ śāstramapāṭhayatsvayam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Then the ascetic of shaven head acting in accordance with Viṣṇu’s behest created four disciples of the like form as himself and taught them the deceptive cult.

## \|\| 6.4.25 \|\|

*yathā svayaṃ tathā te ca catvāro muṃḍinaḥ śubhāḥ \|*  
*namaskṛtya sthitāstatra haraye paramātmane \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The four disciples had shaven heads and were of auspicious features. They bowed to Viṣṇu, the great soul and stood waiting.

## \|\| 6.4.26 \|\|

*hariścāpi munestatra caturastāṃstadā svayam \|*  
*uvāca paramaprītaśśivājñāparipālakaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. O sage, the delighted Viṣṇu too, who carries out the behests of Śiva spoke to those four disciples.

## \|\| 6.4.27 \|\|

*yathā gurustathā yūyaṃ bhaviṣyatha madājñayā \|*  
*dhanyāḥ stha sadgatimiha saṃprāpsyatha na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. “Just as your preceptor you too will become blessed at my bidding. There is no doubt in this that you will attain good goal.

## \|\| 6.4.28 \|\|

*catvāro muṃḍinaste'tha dharmaṃ pāṣaṃḍamāśritāḥ \|*  
*haste pātraṃ dadhānāśca tuṃḍavastrasya dhārakāḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. The four disciples with shaven heads followed the heretic cult. They had the wicker vessel in their hands. They covered their mouths with a piece of cloth.

## \|\| 6.4.29 \|\|

*malinānyeva vāsāṃsi dhārayaṃto hyabhāṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*dharmo lābhaḥ paraṃ tattvaṃ vadaṃtastvatiharṣataḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. They habitually wore dirty clothes. They did not talk much. Delightedly they used to speak “Dharma is the great gain, the true essence” and some similar words.

## \|\| 6.4.30 \|\|

*mārjanīṃ dhriyamāṇāśca vastrakhaṃḍavinirmitām \|*  
*śanaiḥ śanaiścalanto hi jīvahiṃsābhayāddhruvam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. They held a besom broom made of pieces of cloths. They used to walk step by step very slowly because they were afraid of injuring living beings.

## \|\| 6.4.31 \|\|

*te sarve ca tadā devaṃ bhagavaṃtaṃ mudānvitāḥ \|*  
*namaskṛtya punastatra mune tasthustadagrataḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. O sage, with great joy they bowed to the lord and stood in front of him.

## \|\| 6.4.32 \|\|

*hariṇā ca tadā haste dhṛtvā ca guraverpitāḥ \|*  
*abhyadhāyi ca suprītyā tannāmāpi viśeṣataḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. They were grasped by the hand by Viṣṇu and formally entrusted to the preceptor. Their names too were announced by him particularly and lovingly.

## \|\| 6.4.33 \|\|

*yathā tvaṃ ca tathaivaite madīyā vai na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*ādirūpaṃ ca tannāma pūjyatvātpūjya ucyate \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. “Just as you, these too also belong to me. The initial prefix to their names shall be the word “Pūjya” because they are worthy of respect.

## \|\| 6.4.34 \|\|

*ṛṣiryatistathā kīryaupādhyāya iti svayam \|*  
*imānyapi tu nāmāni prasiddhāni bhavaṃtu vaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Let the names Ṛṣi, Yati, Ācārya, and Upādhyāya also be well known appendages to you all.

## \|\| 6.4.35 \|\|

*mamāpi ca bhavadbhiśca nāma grāhyaṃ śubhaṃ punaḥ \|*  
*arihanniti tannāmadhyeyaṃ pāpapraṇāśanam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. My names shall also be assumed by you. The auspicious name “Arihat” shall be considered destructive of sins.

## \|\| 6.4.36 \|\|

*bhavadbhiścaiva kartavyaṃ kāryaṃ lokasukhāvaham \|*  
*lokānukūlaṃ caratāṃ bhaviṣyatyuttamā gatiḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. All activities conducive to the happiness of the worlds shall be performed by you. The goal of those who carry on activities favourable to the worlds shall become excellent.”

## \|\| 6.4.37 \|\|

*\|\| sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*tataḥ praṇamya taṃ māyī śiṣyayuktassvayaṃ tadā \|*  
*jagāma tripuraṃ sadyaḥ śivecchākāriṇaṃ mumā \|\| 37 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

37\. Then, bowing to Viṣṇu who carried out the wishes of Śiva, the deceptive sage went joyously to the three cities accompanied by his disciples.

## \|\| 6.4.38 \|\|

*praviśya tatpuraṃ tūrṇaṃ viṣṇunā nodito vaśī \|*  
*mahāmāyāvinā tena ṛṣirmāyāṃ tadākarot \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Urged by Viṣṇu of great magic, that sage of great self-control entered the three cities and created illusion.

## \|\| 6.4.39 \|\|

*nagaropavane kṛtvā śiṣyairyuktaḥ sthititadā \|*  
*māyāṃ pravartayāmāsa māyināmapi mohinīm \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Stationing himself in a garden at the outskirts of the city, accompanied by his disciples he set his magic in motion. That was powerful enough to fascinate even the expert magicians.

## \|\| 6.4.40 \|\|

*śivārcanaprabhāveṇa tanmāyā sahasā mune \|*  
*tripure na cacālāśu nirviṇṇobhūttadā yatiḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. O sage, his magic was ineffective in the three cities by virtue of Śiva’s worship. Then the heretic sage became distressed.

## \|\| 6.4.41 \|\|

*atha viṣṇuṃ sa sasmāra tuṣṭāva ca hṛdā bahu \|*  
*naṣṭotsāho vicetasko hṛdayena vidūyatā \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. He mentally remembered and eulogised Viṣṇu many times, with an aching heart. He had been so dispirited and listless.

## \|\| 6.4.42 \|\|

*tatsmṛtastvaritaṃ viṣṇussasmāra śaṃkaraṃ hṛdi \|*  
*prāpyājñāṃ manasā tasya smṛtavānnāradaṃ drutam \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. On being remembered by him Viṣṇu mentally thought of Śiva. Receiving his behest by the process of thought forms he remembered Nārada.

## \|\| 6.4.43 \|\|

*smṛtamātreṇa viṣṇośca nāradassamupasthitaḥ \|*  
*natvā stutvā purastasya sthitobhūtsāṃjalistadā \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Immediately after, Nārada approached Viṣṇu. After bowing to him and eulogising him, he stood before Viṣṇu with palms joined in reverence.

## \|\| 6.4.44 \|\|

*atha taṃ nāradaṃ prāha viṣṇurmunimatāṃ varaḥ \|*  
*lokopakāranirato devakāryakarassadā \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Viṣṇu, the foremost among the intelligent and who always carried out the tasks of the gods and who was engaged in rendering help to the worlds spoke to Nārada then.

## \|\| 6.4.45 \|\|

*śivājñayocyate tāta gaccha tvaṃ tripuraṃ drutam \|*  
*ṛṣistatra gataḥ śiṣyairmohārthaṃ tatsuvāsinām \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. “O dear, this is being mentioned to you at the bidding of Śiva. Go to the three cities immediately. The sage has gone there already for deluding the residents of the cities.”

## \|\| 6.4.46 \|\|

*\|\| sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya vacastasya nārado munisattamaḥ \|*  
*gatastatra drutaṃ yatra sa ṛṣirmāyināṃ varaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

46\. On hearing his words, Nārada, the excellent sage went there quickly where the ascetic expert in magic was stationed.

## \|\| 6.4.47 \|\|

*nārado'pi tathā māyī niyogānmāyinaḥ prabhoḥ \|*  
*praviśya tatpuraṃ tena māyinā saha dīkṣitaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Nārada, an expert in magic, at the bidding of the lord, an expert in the art of illusion, entered the three cities along with the deceptive sage, and got himself initiated.

## \|\| 6.4.48 \|\|

*tataśca nārado gatvā tripurādhīśasannidhau \|*  
*kṣemapraśnādikaṃ kṛtvā rājñe sarvaṃ nyavedayat \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Then Nārada approached the lord of the three cities. After the preliminary enquiries about his health and welfare he spoke to the king.

## \|\| 6.4.49 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|\| kaścitsamāgataścātra yatirdharmaparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*sarvavidyāprakṛṣṭo hi vedavidyāparānvitaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

Nārada said:—

49\. A certain sage, very virtuous and excellent master of lores has arrived here. He possesses complete knowledge of the Vedic lore.

## \|\| 6.4.50 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā ca bahavo dharmā naitena sadṛśāḥ punaḥ \|*  
*vayaṃ sudīkṣitāścātra dṛṣṭvā dharmaṃ sanātanam \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Many cults have been observed by me but none of them is like his. Seeing the eternal virtue in this cult we have got ourselves initiated into it.

## \|\| 6.4.51 \|\|

*tavecchā yadi varteta taddharme daityasattama \|*  
*taddharmasya mahārāja grāhyā dīkṣā tvayā punaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. O great king, O excellent Asuras, if you have any interest in that cult, you shall get yourself initiated into it.

## \|\| 6.4.52 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*tadīyaṃ sa vacaḥ śrutvā mahadarthasugarbhitam \|*  
*vismito hṛdi daityeśo jagau tatra vimohitaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

52\. On hearing his words full of significance, the lord of the Asuras was deluded and exclaimed with surprise in his heart.

## \|\| 6.4.53 \|\|

*nārado dīkṣito yasmādvayaṃ dīkṣāmavāpnumaḥ \|*  
*ityevaṃ ca viditvā vai jagāma svayameva ha \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. “Since Nārada has been initiated we too shall be initiated.” Resolving thus, the Asura approached the sage.

## \|\| 6.4.54 \|\|

*tadrūpaṃ ca tadā dṛṣṭvā mohito māyayā tathā \|*  
*uvāca vacanaṃ tasmai namaskṛtya mahātmane \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. On seeing his features, the Asura was deluded by his magic. After bowing to him be spoke thus.

## \|\| 6.4.55 \|\|

*tripurādhipa uvāca \|*  
*dīkṣā deyā tvayā mahyaṃ nirmalāśaya bho ṛṣe \|*  
*ahaṃ śiṣyo bhaviṣyāmi satyaṃ satyaṃ na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

The Tripura ruler said:—

55\. O sage of pure mind, you shall perform my initiation. I shall become your disciple. True. It is undoubtedly true.

## \|\| 6.4.56 \|\|

*ityevaṃ tu vacaḥ śrutvā daityarājasya nirmalam \|*  
*pratyuvāca suyatnena ṛṣissa ca sanātanaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. On hearing the frank words of the ruler of the Asuras the heretic sage, professing to be eternal, spoke emphatically.

## \|\| 6.4.57 \|\|

*madīyā karaṇīyā syādyadyājñā daityasattama \|*  
*tadā deyā mayā dīkṣā nānyathā koṭiyatnataḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. O excellent Asura, if you are prepared to act according to my behests, I shall initiate you, otherwise not, even if you strive for a number of times.

## \|\| 6.4.58 \|\|

*ityevaṃ tu vacaḥ śrutvā rājā māyāmayo'bhavat \|*  
*uvāca vacanaṃ śīghraṃ yatiṃ taṃ hi kṛtāṃjaliḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. On hearing these words the king was deluded by magic. With palms joined in reverence he immediately replied to the sage.

## \|\| 6.4.59 \|\|

*daitya uvāca \|*  
*yathājñāṃ dāsyasi tvaṃ ca tattathaiva na cānyathā \|*  
*tvadājñāṃ nollaṃghayiṣye satyaṃ satyaṃ na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

The Asura said:—

59\. I shall carry out whatever command you are pleased to give. I will not transgress your orders. True. It is certainly true.

## \|\| 6.4.60 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya vacastasya tripurādhīśitustadā \|*  
*dūrīkṛtya mukhādvastramuvāca ṛṣisattamaḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

60\. On hearing the words of the Tripura-ruler, the excellent sage removed the cloth from his mouth and said.

## \|\| 6.4.61 \|\|

*dīkṣāṃ gṛhṇīṣva daityendra sarvadharmottamottamām \|*  
*dadau dīkṣāvidhānena prāpsyasi tvaṃ kṛtārthatām \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. “O lord of Asuras, take initiation in this most excellent of all cults. By this initiation you will become contented.”

## \|\| 6.4.62 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityuktvā sa tu māyāvī daityarājāya satvaram \|*  
*dadau dīkṣāṃ svadharmoktāṃ tasmai vidhividhānataḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

62\. Saying thus, the deceptive sage immediately performed the initiation of the ruler of the Asuras, in accordance with his cult observing all rules.

## \|\| 6.4.63 \|\|

*daityarāje dīkṣite ca tasminsasahaje mune \|*  
*sarve ca dīkṣitā jātāstatra tripuravāsinaḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. O sage, when the ruler of the Asuras was initiated along with his brothers, the residents of the three cities too got themselves initiated.

## \|\| 6.4.64 \|\|

*muneḥ śiṣyaiḥ praśiṣyaiśca vyāptamāsīddrutaṃ tadā \|*  
*mahāmāyāvinastattu tripuraṃ sakalaṃ mune \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. O sage, the entire Tripuras were filled with the line of disciples of the sage, an expert in great art of illusion.

## Chapter 5 - The Tripuras are fascinated

## \|\| 6.5.1 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*daityarāje dīkṣite ca māyinā tena mohite \|*  
*kimuvāca tadā māyī kiṃ cakāra sa daityapaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:—

1\. When the ruler of the Asuras was initiated after being deluded by the deceptive sage expert in the magic art what did the sage say? What did the ruler of the Asuras do?

## \|\| 6.5.2 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*dīkṣāṃ dattvā yatistasmā arihannāradādibhiḥ \|*  
*śiṣyaissevitapādābjo daityarājānamabravīt \|\| 2 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

2\. After offering him initiation, the ascetic Arihan served by his disciples, Nārada and others, spoke to the ruler of the Asuras.

## \|\| 6.5.3 \|\|

*arihannuvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu daityapate vākyaṃ mama sañjñānagarbhitam \|*  
*vedāntasārasarvasvaṃ rahasyaṃ paramottamam \|\| 3 \|\|*

Arihan said:—

3\. O ruler of the Asuras, listen to my statement, pregnant with wisdom. It is the essence of the Vedānta and bears high esoteric importance.

## \|\| 6.5.4 \|\|

*anādisiddhassaṃsāraḥ kartṛkarmavivarjitaḥ \|*  
*svayaṃ prādurbhavatyeva svayameva vilīyate \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The entire universe is eternal. It has no creator nor it is an object of creation. It evolves itself and gets annihilated by itself.

## \|\| 6.5.5 \|\|

*brahmādistaṃbaparyantaṃ yāvaddehanibaṃdhanam \|*  
*ātmaivaikeśvarastatra na dvitīyastadīśitā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. There are many bodies from Brahmā down to a blade of grass. They themselves are the gods for them. There is no other God.

## \|\| 6.5.6 \|\|

*yadbrahmaviṣṇurudrākhyāstadākhyā dehināmimāḥ \|*  
*ākhyāyathāsmadādīnāmarihannādirucyate \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. What we mean by Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Rudra are only the names of embodied beings just like my name Arihan etc.

## \|\| 6.5.7 \|\|

*deho yathāsmadādīnāṃ svakālena vilīyate \|*  
*brahmādi maśakāṃtānāṃ svakālāllīyate tathā \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Just as our bodies perish when their time arrives, so also the bodies of all beings from Brahmā to a mosquito perish when their time arrives.

## \|\| 6.5.8 \|\|

*vicāryamāṇe dehe'sminna kiṃcidadhikaṃ kvacit \|*  
*āhāro maithunaṃ nidrā bhayaṃ sarvatra yatsamam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. When we consider, none of these bodies is superior to any other since in respect of taking food, copulation, sleep and fear these are invariably the same everywhere.

## \|\| 6.5.9 \|\|

*nirāhāraparīmāṇaṃ prāpya sarvo hi dehabhṛt \|*  
*sadṛśīmeva saṃtṛptiṃ prāpnuyānnādhiketarām \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Taking in water and foodstuffs to the required quantity, all living beings derive a kindred satisfaction, neither more nor less.

## \|\| 6.5.10 \|\|

*yathā vitṛṣitāḥ syāma pītvā peyaṃ mudā vayam \|*  
*tṛṣitāstu tathānyepi na viśeṣo'lpakodhikaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. After drinking water we are gladly relieved of thirst. Others too are equally relieved. There is no deviation this way or that.

## \|\| 6.5.11 \|\|

*saṃtu nāryaḥ sahasrāṇi rūpalāvaṇyabhūmayaḥ \|*  
*paraṃ nidhuvane kāle hyaikevehopayujyate \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. There may be a thousand damsels of exquisite beauty and comely features. But only one of them can be used at a time for the sexual intercourse.

## \|\| 6.5.12 \|\|

*aśvāḥ paraśśatāssaṃtu saṃtvenekaipyanekadhā \|*  
*adhirohe tathāpyeko na dvitīyastathātmanaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Let there be hundreds of horses, of different varieties. But for the purpose of riding only one can be used on one occasion.

## \|\| 6.5.13 \|\|

*paryaṃkaśāyināṃ svāpe sukhaṃ yadupajāyate \|*  
*tadeva saukhyaṃ nidrābhirbhūtabhūśāyināmapi \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The pleasure that one derives in that sleep on a cushioned couch is the same that one derives by sleeping on the bare ground.

## \|\| 6.5.14 \|\|

*yathaiva maraṇādbhītirasmadādivapuṣmatām \|*  
*brahmādikīṭakāṃtānāṃ tathā maraṇato bhayam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Just as we, the embodied beings, are afraid of death so also the bodies from Brahmā to the worm are afraid of death.

## \|\| 6.5.15 \|\|

*sarve tanubhṛtastulyā yadi buddhyā vicāryyate \|*  
*idaṃ niścitya kenāpi no hiṃsyaḥ ko'pi kutracit \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. If we analyse with a keen intellect, all the embodied being are equal. After coming to this conclusion it does not behove anyone to injure anyone else.

## \|\| 6.5.16 \|\|

*dharmo jīvadayātulyo na kvāpi jagatītale \|*  
*tasmātsarvaprayatnena kāryā jīvadayā nṛbhiḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. There is no other virtue equal to the mercy shown to living beings. Hence all men shall strenuously practise acts of mercy to living beings.

## \|\| 6.5.17 \|\|

*ekasminrakṣite jīve trailokyaṃ rakṣitaṃ bhavet \|*  
*ghātite ghātitaṃ tadvattasmādrakṣenna ghātayet \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. If a single living being is protected it amounts to the protection of the three worlds. If that is killed it amounts to the killing of all others. Hence it is our duty to protect and abstain from killing others.

## \|\| 6.5.18 \|\|

*ahiṃsā paramo dharmaḥ pāpamātmaprapīḍanam \|*  
*aparādhīnatā muktissvargo'bhilaṣitāśanam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Non-violence is the greatest virtue. Affliction of others is a great sin. Salvation is defined as non-dependence on others. Eating the food of our choice is heavenly bliss.

## \|\| 6.5.19 \|\|

*pūrvasūribhirityuktaṃ satpramāṇatayā dhruvam \|*  
*tasmānna hiṃsā karttavyo narairnarakabhīrubhiḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. This has been mentioned by the earlier sages with good justification to be sure. Hence no violence should be indulged in by men who are afraid of hell.

## \|\| 6.5.20 \|\|

*na hiṃsāsadṛśaṃ pāpaṃ trailokye sacarācare \|*  
*hiṃsako narakaṃ gacchetsvargaṃ gacchedahiṃsakaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. There is no sin equal to violence in the three worlds, consisting of the mobile and immobile. A person who afflicts others violently goes to hell. A non-violent man goes to heaven.

## \|\| 6.5.21 \|\|

*saṃti dānānyanekāni kiṃ taistucchaphalapradaiḥ \|*  
*abhītisadṛśaṃ dānaṃ paramekamapīha na \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. There are many kinds of charitable gifts. Of what avail are these which give very insignificant results. There is no other gift equal to that of protection.

## \|\| 6.5.22 \|\|

*iha catvāri dānāni proktāni paramarṣibhiḥ \|*  
*vicārya nānāśāstrāṇi śarmaṇe'tra paratra ca \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Four types of gifts have been mentioned by the great sages for the welfare of the people here and hereafter as a result of discussions and deliberations of various sacred texts.

## \|\| 6.5.23 \|\|

*bhītebhyaścābhayaṃ deyaṃ vyādhitebhyastathoṣadham \|*  
*deyā vidyārthināṃ vidyā deyamannaṃ kṣudhāture \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Protection shall be granted to the frightened, medicine to the sick, learning to the student and food to the hungry.

## \|\| 6.5.24 \|\|

*yāni yānīha dānāni bahumunyuditāni ca \|*  
*jīvābhayapradānasya kalāṃ nārhaṃti ṣoḍaśīm \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. All sorts of charitable gifts recommended by the sages do not merit even a sixteenth part of the gift of protection to a living being.

## \|\| 6.5.25 \|\|

*aviciṃtya prabhāvaṃ hi maṇimaṃtrauṣadhaṃ balam \|*  
*tadabhyasyaṃ prayatnena nāmārthopārjanāya vai \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The strength that one derives by the use of gems mantras, and herbs is of inconceivable influence. But it is practised strenuously only for earning money.

## \|\| 6.5.26 \|\|

*arthānupārjya bahuśo dvādaśāyatanāni vai \|*  
*paritaḥ paripūjyāni kimanyairiha pūjitaiḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The hoarding and amassing of vast wealth is useful only for the propitiation of twelve organs of senses. Of what avail is the propitiation of other things?

## \|\| 6.5.27 \|\|

*paṃcakarmendriyagrāmāḥ paṃca buddhīṃdriyāṇi ca \|*  
*mano buddhiriha proktaṃ dvādaśāyatanaṃ śubham \|\| 27 \|\|*

2 7. The twelve organs of senses are the five organs of activity and the five organs of knowledge together with the mind and intellect.

## \|\| 6.5.28 \|\|

*ihaiva svarganarakau prāṇināṃ nānyataḥ kvacit \|*  
*sukhaṃ svargaḥ samākhyātā duḥkhaṃ narakameva hi \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Living beings have heaven and hell here itself and not anywhere else. Happiness is heaven and misery is hell.

## \|\| 6.5.29 \|\|

*sukheṣu bhujyamāneṣu yatsyāddehavisarjanam \|*  
*ayameva paro mokṣo vijñeyastattvaciṃtakaiḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. If the body is cast off in the midst of enjoyment that is the greatest liberation conceived by the philosophers.

## \|\| 6.5.30 \|\|

*vāsanāsahite kleśasamucchede sati dhruvam \|*  
*ajñāno paramo mokṣo vijñeyastattvaciṃtakaiḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. When pain comes to an end along with its impressions, If ignorance too dies away, it is conceived as the greatest salvation by the philosophers.

## \|\| 6.5.31 \|\|

*prāmāṇikī śrutiriyaṃ procyate vedavādibhiḥ \|*  
*na hiṃsyātsarvabhūtāni nānyā hiṃsā pravartikā \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Supporters and exponents of the Vedas accept this as an authoritative Vedic text that no living being shall be injured. Violence is not justifiable.

## \|\| 6.5.32 \|\|

*agniṣṭomīyamiti yā bhrāmikā sā'satāmiha \|*  
*na sā pramāṇaṃ jñātṝṇāṃ paśvālaṃbhanakārikā \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. The Vedic text encouraging slaughter of animals cannot be held authoritative by the learned. To say that violence is allowed in Agniṣṭoma is an erroneous view of the wicked.

## \|\| 6.5.33 \|\|

*vṛkṣāṃśchitvā paśūnhatvā kṛtvā rudhirakardamam \|*  
*dagdhvā vahnau tilājyādi citraṃ svargo'bhilaṣyate \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. It is surprising that heaven is sought by cutting off trees, slaughtering animals, making a muddy mess with blood and by burning gingelly seeds and ghee.

## \|\| 6.5.34 \|\|

*ityevaṃ svamataṃ procya yatistripuranāyakam \|*  
*śrāvayitvākhilān paurānuvāca punarādarāt \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Narrating his opinions to the leader of the Tripuras, the ascetic addressed the citizens with great zeal.

## \|\| 6.5.35 \|\|

*dṛṣṭārthapratyayakarāndehasaukhyaikasādhakān \|*  
*bauddhāgama vinirdiṣṭāndharmānvedaparāṃstataḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. He referred to things which gave credence, being visible, which brought happiness to the body, which are indicated in Buddhistic theology and which are consistent with the Vedic passages.

## \|\| 6.5.36 \|\|

*ānaṃdaṃ brahmaṇo rūpaṃ śrutyaivaṃ yannigadyate \|*  
*tattathaiva ha maṃtavyaṃ mithyā nānātvakalpanā \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. It is said in the Vedas that Bliss is an aspect of the Brahman. That shall be taken as it is. It is false to bring in various alternatives.

## \|\| 6.5.37 \|\|

*yāvatsvasthamidaṃ varṣma yāvannendriyaviklavaḥ \|*  
*yāvajjarā ca dūre'sti tāvatsaukhyaṃ prasādhayet \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. One shall seek and enjoy happiness as long as the body is hale and hearty, as long as the sense-organs are not impaired and as long as the old age is far off.

## \|\| 6.5.38 \|\|

*asvāsthyendriyavaikalye vārddhake tu kutassukham \|*  
*śarīramapi dātavyamarthibhyo'tassukhepsubhiḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. When there is sickness, impairment of the sense-organs and old age how can one derive happiness? Hence those who seek happiness shall be prepared to give away even the body.

## \|\| 6.5.39 \|\|

*yācamānamanovṛttiprīṇane yasya no janiḥ \|*  
*tena bhūrbhāravatyeṣā samudrāgadrumairna hi \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. The Earth is burdened by those who are not ready to please and satisfy the suppliant. It is not burdened by oceans, mountains and trees.

## \|\| 6.5.40 \|\|

*satvaraṃ gatvaro dehaḥ saṃcayāssaparikṣayāḥ \|*  
*iti vijñāya vijñātā dehasaukhyaṃ prasādhayet \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. The body is ready to go in a trice, and hoarded things are attended with the risk of dwindling down. Realising this a sensible man shall see to the pleasure of his body.

## \|\| 6.5.41 \|\|

*śvavāya sakṛmīṇāṃ ca prātarbhojyamidaṃ vapuḥ \|*  
*bhasmāṃtaṃ taccharīraṃ ca vede satyaṃ prapaṭhyate \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. It is mentioned in the Vedas that this body is going to constitute the breakfast for dogs, crows and worms. The body has its ultimate end in being reduced to ashes.

## \|\| 6.5.42 \|\|

*mudhā jātivikaṣoyaṃ lokeṣu parikalpyate \|*  
*mānuṣye sati sāmānye ko'dharmaḥ ko'tha cottamaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. It is unnecessary to divide the people into different castes. When all are men who is superior and who is inferior?

## \|\| 6.5.43 \|\|

*brahmādisṛṣṭireṣeti procyate vṛddhapūruṣaiḥ \|*  
*tasya jātau sutau dakṣamarīcī ceti viśrutau \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Old men say that creation began with Brahmā. He begot two sons the famous Dakṣa and Marīci.

## \|\| 6.5.44 \|\|

*mārīcena kaśyapena dakṣakanyāssulocanāḥ \|*  
*dharmeṇa kila mārgeṇa pariṇītāstrayodaśa \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Kaśyapa, the son of Marīci married thirteen of the sweet-eyed daughters of Dakṣa, they say, in accordance with righteous path.

## \|\| 6.5.45 \|\|

*apīdānīṃtanairmartyairalpabuddhiparākramaiḥ \|*  
*api gamyastvagamyo'yaṃ vicāraḥ kriyate mudhā \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. But people of modern times whose intelligence and valour are but a modicum unnecessarily wrangle over the fact whether this is proper or improper.

## \|\| 6.5.46 \|\|

*mukhabāhūrusañjātaṃ cāturvarṇya sahoditam \|*  
*kalpaneyaṃ kṛtā pūrvairna ghaṭeta vicārataḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Some of the ancestors thought that the four castes are born of mouth, arms, thighs etc. of Brahmā. But when we consider, this does not fit in properly.

## \|\| 6.5.47 \|\|

*ekasyāṃ ca tanau jātā ekasmādyadi vā kvacit \|*  
*catvārastanayāstatkiṃ bhinnavarṇatvamāpnuyuḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. How can sons born of the same body or from the same body be of four different castes?

## \|\| 6.5.48 \|\|

*varṇāvarṇavibhāgo'yaṃ tasmānna pratibhāsate \|*  
*ato bhedo na maṃtavyo mānuṣye kenacitkvacit \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Hence the divisions of castes and outcastes do not appear to be sound. Hence no difference between man and man should be entertained.

## \|\| 6.5.49 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*itthamābhāṣya daityeśaṃ paurāṃśca sa yatirmune \|*  
*saśiṣyo vedadharmāśca nāśayāmāsa cādarāt \|\| 49 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

49\. O sage, addressing the lord of the Asuras and the citizens thus, the sage with his disciples spoiled the Vedic rites in a determined manner.

## \|\| 6.5.50 \|\|

*strīdharmaṃ khaṃḍayāmāsa pātivratyaparaṃ mahat \|*  
*jitendriyatvaṃ sarveṣāṃ puruṣāṇāṃ tathaiva saḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. He then criticised the womanly virtues of chastity and manly virtues of continence etc.

## \|\| 6.5.51 \|\|

*devadharmānviśeṣeṇa śrāddhadharmāṃstathaiva ca \|*  
*makhadharmānvratādīṃśca tīrthaśrāddhaṃ viśeṣataḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Similarly he attacked and repudiated the divine rites, Śrāddhika rites, sacrificial rites and holy observances and festivals, pilgrimages and anniversaries.

## \|\| 6.5.52 \|\|

*śivapūjāṃ viśeṣeṇa liṃgārādhanapūrvikām \|*  
*viṣṇusūryagaṇeśādipūjanaṃ vidhipūrvakam \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Worship of Śiva, propitiation of his phallic form, adoration of Viṣṇu, Sun, Gaṇeśa and other deities in accordance with the sacred texts were repudiated by him.

## \|\| 6.5.53 \|\|

*snānadānādikaṃ sarvaṃ parvakālaṃ viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*khaṃḍayāmāsa sa yatirmāyī māyāvināṃ varaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. The heretic sage, an expert in wielding magic art, foremost among the deceptive, criticised the ceremonial ablutions and charitable gifts that are made on auspicious occasions.

## \|\| 6.5.54 \|\|

*kiṃ bahūktena viprendra tripure tena māyinā \|*  
*vedadharmāśca ye kecitte sarve dūrataḥ kṛtāḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. O foremost among brahmins, why shall I dilate upon this topic? Suffice it to say that in the three cities every type of Vedic rites was completely stopped by that deceptive heretic sage.

## \|\| 6.5.55 \|\|

*patidharmāśrayāḥ sarvā mohitāstripurāṃganāḥ \|*  
*bhartṛśuśrūṣaṇavatīṃ vijahurmatimuttamām \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. The women of the three cities who were hitherto devotedly attached to their husbands were deluded and misguided and they abandoned their noble inclinations to serve their husbands.

## \|\| 6.5.56 \|\|

*abhyasyākarṣaṇīṃ vidyāṃ vaśīkṛtyamayīmapi \|*  
*puruṣāssaphalīcakruḥ paradāreṣu mohitāḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. The fascinated men practised rites of seduction and winning over and made their artifices fruitful in gaining other men’s wives.

## \|\| 6.5.57 \|\|

*aṃtaḥpuracarā nāryastathā rājakumārakāḥ \|*  
*paurāḥ purāṃganāścāpi sarve taiśca vimohitāḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. The attendant maids in the haremss, the princes, the citizens and the ladies were perfectly enchanted by him.

## \|\| 6.5.58 \|\|

*evaṃ paureṣu sarveṣu nijadharmeṣu sarvathā \|*  
*parāṅmukheṣu jāteṣu prollalāsa vṛṣetaraḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Thus when the citizens became averse to virtuous rites and actions, evil reigned supreme.

## \|\| 6.5.59 \|\|

*māyā ca devadevasya viṣṇostasyājñayā prabho \|*  
*alakṣmīśca svayaṃ tasya niyogāttripuraṃ gatā \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. At the bidding of lord Viṣṇu, his magic art and evil fortune visited the three cities.

## \|\| 6.5.60 \|\|

*yā lakṣmīstapasā teṣāṃ labdhā deveśvarādarāt \|*  
*bahirgatā parityajya niyogādbrahmaṇaḥ prabhoḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. The glory that they had acquired by the boon of Brahmā, the lord of the gods, went out forsaking them, at the behest of Brahmā.

## \|\| 6.5.61 \|\|

*buddhimohaṃ tathābhūtaṃ viṣṇo rmāyāvinirmitam \|*  
*teṣāṃ dattvā kṣaṇādeva kṛtārtho'bhūtsa nāradaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Blessing them with the utter delusion of their intellect, perpetrated by the illusion of Viṣṇu, Nārada became contented.

## \|\| 6.5.62 \|\|

*nāradopi tathārūpo yathā māyī tathaiva saḥ \|*  
*tathāpi vikṛto nābhūtparameśādanugrahāt \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Though Nārada and the heretic sage had been in that guise for long, they were not defiled, thanks to the benediction of lord Śiva.

## \|\| 6.5.63 \|\|

*āsītkuṃṭhitasāmarthyo daityarājo'pi bho mune \|*  
*bhrātṛbhyāṃ sahitastatra mayena ca śivecchayā \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. As Śiva willed, O sage, the capacity of the ruler of the Asuras became stunted and thwarted as also of his brothers and Maya.

## Chapter 6 - Prayer to Śiva

## \|\| 6.6.1 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*tasmin daityādhipe paure sabhrātari vimohite \|*  
*sanatkumāra kiṃ vāsīttadācakṣvākhilaṃ vibho \|\| 1 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:—

1\. When the ruler of the Asuras, his brothers and the citizens were thus deluded, O lord Sanatkumāra, what happened? Please mention everything.

## \|\| 6.6.2-3 \|\|

*\|\| sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*tripure ca tathābhūte daitye tyaktaśivārcane \|*  
*strīdharme nikhile naṣṭe durācāre vyavasthite \|\| 2 \|\|*

*kṛtārtha iva lakṣmīśo devaissārddhamumāpatim \|*  
*nivedituṃ taccaritraṃ kailāsamagamaddhariḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

2-3. When the Asuras had become so, when they had abandoned the worship of Śiva, when the virtuous rites of chaste women came to an end and evil conduct came to stay, Viṣṇu was apparently contented. Accompanied by the gods, Viṣṇu went to Kailāsa in order to intimate their activities to Śiva.

## \|\| 6.6.4-5 \|\|

*tasyopakaṃṭhaṃ sthitvā'sau devaissaha ramāpatiḥ \|*  
*tato bhūri sa ca brahmā parameṇa samādhinā \|\| 4 \|\|*

*manasā prāpya sarvajñaṃ brahmaṇā sa haristadā \|*  
*tuṣṭāva vāgbhiriṣṭvābhiśśaṃkaraṃ puruṣottamaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. Viṣṇu, the gods, Brahmā and others stood near him and with great concentration they meditated on him. Viṣṇu and Brahmā eulogised the omniscient Śiva with pleasing words.

## \|\| 6.6.6 \|\|

*\|\| viṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*maheśvarāya devāya namaste paramātmane \|*  
*nārāyaṇāya rudrāya brahmaṇe brahmarūpiṇe \|\| 6 \|\|*

Viṣṇu said:—

6\. “Obeisance to you, great lord, the great soul, Nārāyaṇa, Rudra and Brahmā, obeisance to you in the form of Brahman.”

## \|\| 6.6.7 \|\|

*evaṃ kṛtvā mahādevaṃ daṃḍavatpraṇipatya ha \|*  
*jajāpa rudramaṃtraṃ ca dakṣiṇāmūrtisaṃbhavam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. After eulogising lord Śiva thus and prostrating at length, he repeated the mantra of Dakṣināmūrti Rudra.

## \|\| 6.6.8-9 \|\|

*jale sthitvā sārddhakoṭipramitaṃ tanmanāḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*saṃsmaran manasā śaṃbhuṃ svaprabhuṃ parameśvaram \|\| 8 \|\|*

*tāvaddevāstadā sarve tanmanaskā maheśvaram \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. He repeated the mantra fifteen million times standing in water and concentrating his mind on him. Lord Viṣṇu meditated on the great lord Śiva. In the meantime, the gods too eulogised him with devotion.

## \|\| 6.6.10 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*namassarvātmane tubhyaṃ śaṃkarāyārtihāriṇe \|*  
*rudrāya nīlakaṃṭhāya cidrūpāya pracetase \|\| 10 \|\|*

The gods said:—

10\. Obeisance to you, the soul of all, obeisance to Śiva the remover of distress, obeisance to the blue-necked Rudra, obeisance to the knowledge-formed Śiva of great mind.

## \|\| 6.6.11 \|\|

*gatirnassarvadā tvaṃ hi sarvāpadvinivārakaḥ \|*  
*tvameva sarvadātmābhirvaṃdyo devārisūdana \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. You are our ultimate goal for ever. You are the remover of all adversities. O destroyer of the enemies of the gods, you alone are to be respected by us always.

## \|\| 6.6.12 \|\|

*tvamādistvamanādiśca svānaṃdaścākṣayaḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*prakṛteḥ puruṣasyāpi sākṣātsraṣṭā jagatprabhuḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. You are the beginning. You are the primordial being. You are self-bliss. You are the everlasting lord. You are the lord of the universe, the direct creator of Prakṛti and Puruṣa.

## \|\| 6.6.13 \|\|

*tvameva jagatāṃ kartā bhartā hartā tvameva hi \|*  
*brahmā viṣṇurharo bhūtvā rajassattvatamoguṇaiḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. You alone are the creator, sustainer and the annihilator of the worlds. Assuming the Guṇas of Rajas, Sattva, and Tamas you are Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva.

## \|\| 6.6.14 \|\|

*tārakosi jagatyasminsarveṣāmadhipo'vyayaḥ \|*  
*varado vāṅmayo vācyo vācyavācakavarjitaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. In this universe, you enable people to cross the ocean of Existence. You are the undecaying lord of all. You are the granter of boons. You are the subject and not the object of speech and contents.

## \|\| 6.6.15 \|\|

*yācyo muktyarthamīśāno yogibhiryogavittamaiḥ \|*  
*hṛtpuṃḍarīkavivare yogināṃ tvaṃ hi saṃsthitaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. You shall be requested for salvation by the Yogins, the formost among those who know the theory of Yoga. You are stationed inside the lotus like heart of the Yogins.

## \|\| 6.6.16 \|\|

*vadaṃti vedāstvāṃ saṃtaḥ parabrahmasvarūpiṇam \|*  
*bhavaṃtaṃ tattvamityadya tejorāśiṃ parātparam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The Vedas and the saintly men speak of you as the supreme Brahman. You are a heaped mass of splendour and greater than the greatest. They call you the great principle.

## \|\| 6.6.17 \|\|

*paramātmānamityāhurarasmin jagati yadvibho \|*  
*tvameva śarva sarvātman trilokādhipate bhava \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. What they call the great soul in the universe, O lord, are you yourself, O Śiva soul of all, ruler of the three worlds.

## \|\| 6.6.18 \|\|

*dṛṣṭaṃ śrutaṃ stutaṃ sarvaṃ jñāyamānaṃ jagadguro \|*  
*aṇoralpataraṃ prāhurmahatopi mahattaram \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Whatever is seen, heard or eulogised, whatever is being realised, O preceptor of the universe, are you alone. They call you minuter than the atom and greater than the greatest.

## \|\| 6.6.19 \|\|

*sarvataḥ pāṇipādāṃtaṃ sarvatokṣiśiromukham \|*  
*sarvataśśravaṇaghrāṇaṃ tvāṃ namāmi ca sarvataḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. I bow to you everywhere, you who have hands, legs, eyes, heads, mouths, ears and noses everywhere.

## \|\| 6.6.20 \|\|

*sarvajñaṃ sarvato vyāpin sarveśvaramanāvṛtam \|*  
*viśvarūpaṃ virūpākṣaṃ tvāṃ namāmi ca sarvataḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. I bow to you everywhere, you who are omniscient who pervade everything, you who are unveiled as the lord of al, you who are omniformed and odd-eyed.

## \|\| 6.6.21 \|\|

*sarveśvaraṃ bhavādhyakṣaṃ satyaṃ śivamanuttamam \|*  
*koṭi bhāskarasaṃkāśaṃ tvāṃ namāmi ca sarvataḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. I bow to you everywhere who are the lord of all, who preside over the worlds, who are the excellent Satya and Śiva and who have the refulgence of innumerable suns.

## \|\| 6.6.22 \|\|

*viśvadevamanādyaṃtaṃ ṣaṭtriṃśatkamanīśvaram \|*  
*pravartakaṃ ca sarveṣāṃ tvāṃ namāmi ca sarvataḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. I bow to you everywhere, you the lord of the universe devoid of beginning and end, the lord of the twenty six Tattvas and the activiser of everything.

## \|\| 6.6.23 \|\|

*pravartakaṃ ca prakṛtessarvasya prapitāmaham \|*  
*sarvavigrahamīśaṃ hi tvāṃ namāmi ca sarvataḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. I bow to you everywhere you the activiser of the Prakṛti, the great grandfather of everyone, the lord, the body of everyone.

## \|\| 6.6.24 \|\|

*evaṃ vadaṃti varadaṃ sarvāvāsaṃ svayambhuvam \|*  
*śrutayaḥ śrutisārajñaṃ śrutisāravidaśca ye \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. The Śrutis and those who know the essence of Śrutis speak of you thus. You are the abode of all, the selfborn and the knower of the essence of Śrutis.

## \|\| 6.6.25 \|\|

*adṛśyamasmābhiranekabhūtaṃ tvayā kṛtaṃ yadbhavatātha loke \|*  
*tvāmeva devāsurabhūsurāśca anye ca vai sthāvarajaṃgamāśca \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The various living beings created by you and to be created in future are invisible to us. The gods, the Asuras, the brahmins, nay, the mobile and immobile beings eulogise you alone.

## \|\| 6.6.26 \|\|

*pāhyananyagatīñśaṃbho surānno devavallabha \|*  
*naṣṭaprāyāṃstripurato vinihatyāsurānkṣaṇāt \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. O Śiva, dear to the gods, save us, the gods who have no other go, by killing all the Asuras instantaneously. We are practically destroyed by the Tripuras.

## \|\| 6.6.27 \|\|

*māyayā mohitāste'dya bhavataḥ parameśvara \|*  
*viṣṇunā proktayuktyā ta ujjhitā dharmataḥ prabho \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. O lord Śiva, they are now deluded by your magic. O lord, they have gone astray from the virtuous path through the expedient taught by Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 6.6.28 \|\|

*saṃtyaktasarvadharmāṃśca boddhāgamasamāśritāḥ \|*  
*asmadbhāgyavaśājjātā daityāste bhaktavatsala \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. O lord, favourably disposed towards your devotees, those Asuras have resorted to Buddha’s religion and philosophy, thanks to our good fortune and hence they have eschewed all Vedic sacred rites.

## \|\| 6.6.29 \|\|

*sadā tvaṃ kāryakarttāhi devānāṃ śaraṇaprada \|*  
*vayaṃ te śaraṇāpannā yathecchasi tathā kuru \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. You have always been the only one carrying out the task of the gods and the bestower of refuge. We have sought refuge in you. Please do as you desire.

## \|\| 6.6.30 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*iti stutvā maheśānaṃ devāstu purataḥ sthitāḥ \|*  
*kṛtāṃjalipuṭā dīnā āsan saṃnatamūrtayaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

30\. After eulogising lord Śiva thus, the distressed gods stood in front of him with palms joined in reverence and kneeling low.

## \|\| 6.6.31 \|\|

*stutaścaivaṃ surendrādyairviṣṇorjāpyena ceśvaraḥ \|*  
*agacchattatra sarveśo vṛṣamāruhya harṣitaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Eulogised thus by Indra and others and by the repetition of Japas by Viṣṇu, the delighted lord came there seated on his bull.

## \|\| 6.6.32 \|\|

*viṣṇumāliṃgya naṃdiśādavaruhya prasannadhīḥ \|*  
*dadarśa sudṛśā tatra nandīdattakaro'khilān \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Getting down from Nandīśa and embracing Viṣṇu, lord Śiva delighted in his mind cast his benign look on all with his hand resting on Nandin.

## \|\| 6.6.33 \|\|

*atha devān samālokya kṛpādṛṣṭyā hariṃ haraḥ \|*  
*prāha gaṃbhīrayā vācā prasannaḥ pārvatīpatiḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Casting a sympathetic glance on the gods, the delighted Śiva, lord of Pārvatī, spoke to Viṣṇu in a majestic tone.

## \|\| 6.6.34 \|\|

*śiva uvāca \|*  
*jñātaṃ mayedamadhunā devakāryaṃ sureśvara \|*  
*viṣṇormāyābalaṃ caiva nāradasya ca dhīmataḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

Śiva said:—

34\. “O lord of gods, all the intentions of the gods have been understood by me now. The power of Viṣṇu’s magic and that of the intelligent Nārada has been known.

## \|\| 6.6.35 \|\|

*teṣāmadharmaniṣṭhānāṃ daityānāṃ devasattama \|*  
*puratrayavināśaṃ ca kariṣye'haṃ na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. O most excellent of the gods, there is no doubt in this that I will destroy the three cities of the Asuras if they persist in indulging in evil activities.

## \|\| 6.6.36 \|\|

*parantu te mahādaityā madbhaktā dṛḍhamānasāḥ \|*  
*atha vadhyā mayaiva syurvyājatyaktavṛṣottamāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. But the great Asuras are my firm devotees. They shall be killed only by me, for they have been forced to abandon their excellent virtue under false persuasion.

## \|\| 6.6.37 \|\|

*viṣṇurhanyātparo vātha yattyājitavṛṣāḥ kṛtāḥ \|*  
*daityā madbhaktirahitāssarve tripuravāsinaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Let Viṣṇu or any one else slay them now that they have been made to abandon their Dharma. The Asuras of the three cities have become devoid of devotion to me.”

## \|\| 6.6.38 \|\|

*iti śaṃbhostu vacanaṃ śrutvā sarve divaukasaḥ \|*  
*vimanaskā babhūvuste hariścāpi munīśvara \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. O great sage, on hearing these words of Śiva, all the heaven-dwellers and Viṣṇu became dispirited.

## \|\| 6.6.39 \|\|

*devān viṣṇumudāsīnān dṛṣṭvā ca bhavakṛdvidhiḥ \|*  
*kṛtāṃjalipuraśśaṃbhuṃ brahmā vacanamabravīt \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. On seeing the gods and Viṣṇu sitting cheerless, Brahmā, the creator of the worlds spoke to Śiva with palms joined in reverence.

## \|\| 6.6.40 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*na kiṃcidvidyate pāpaṃ yasmāttvaṃ yogavittamaḥ \|*  
*parameśaḥ parabrahma sadā devarṣirakṣakaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

40\. There is no sin in this, since you are the foremost among those who know the Yogic theory; you are the great lord, the great Brahman and the saviour of gods and sages always.

## \|\| 6.6.41 \|\|

*tavaiva śāsanātte vai mohitāḥ prerako bhavān \|*  
*tyaktasvadharmatvatpūjāḥ paravadhyāstathāpi na \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. It is at your own bidding that they have been deluded. You induced them to be deluded. Although the Asuras have forsaken their duties and your worship, they cannot be killed by others.

## \|\| 6.6.42 \|\|

*atastvayā mahādeva surarṣiprāṇarakṣaka \|*  
*sādhūnāṃ rakṣaṇārthāya haṃtavyā mlecchajātayaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Hence, O great lord, the saviour of the lives of the gods and the sages, the Mlecchas shall be killed by you for the protection of the good.

## \|\| 6.6.43 \|\|

*rājñastasya na tatpāpaṃ vidyate dharmatastava \|*  
*tasmādrakṣeddvijān sādhūnkaṃṭakādvai viśodhayet \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. As it is the duty of a king, you will not be sinning by their destruction. Hence, the good people, brahmins etc shall be saved and the thorns uprooted.

## \|\| 6.6.44 \|\|

*evamicchedihānyatra rājā cedrājyamātmanaḥ \|*  
*prabhutvaṃ sarvalokānāṃ tasmādrakṣasva mā ciram \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Even an ordinary king would do so if he cares to maintain his sway. You have the suzerainty of all the worlds. Hence, tarry not to protect us.

## \|\| 6.6.45 \|\|

*munīndreśāstathā yajñā vedāśśāstrādayokhilāḥ \|*  
*prajāste devadeveśa hyayaṃ viṣṇurapi dhruvam \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Great sages, Indra, sacrifices, Vedas, all the Śāstras, Viṣṇu and even I—all these depend on you, O lord of gods.

## \|\| 6.6.46 \|\|

*devatā sārvabhaumastvaṃ samrāṭsarveśvaraḥ prabho \|*  
*parivārastavaivaiṣa haryādi sakalaṃ jagat \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. O lord, you are the emperor of all deities, the lord of all. Viṣṇu and the entire universe constitute your retinue.

## \|\| 6.6.47 \|\|

*yuvarājo haristeja brahmāhaṃ te purohitaḥ \|*  
*rājakāryakaraḥ śakrastvadājñāpari pālakaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Viṣṇu is your heir-apparent, O unborn one, I, Brahmā, am your priest and Śukra who carries out your behests is the Royal officer.

## \|\| 6.6.48 \|\|

*devā anyepi sarveśa tava śāsanayantritāḥ \|*  
*svasvakāryakarā nityaṃ satyaṃ satyaṃ na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. The other gods too, O lord, are subjects to your control. They continue to perform their own duties. True. It is undoubtedly true.

## \|\| 6.6.49 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*etacchrutvā vacastasya brahmaṇaḥ parameśvaraḥ \|*  
*pratyuvāca prasannātmā śaṃkarassurapo vidhim \|\| 49 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

49\. On hearing the words of Brahmā, Śiva, the delighted lord of the gods replied to Brahma.

## \|\| 6.6.50 \|\|

*śiva uvāca \|*  
*he brahman yadyahaṃ devarājassamrāṭ prakīrttitaḥ \|*  
*tatprakāro na me kaścidgṛhṇīyāṃ yamiha prabhuḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

Śiva said:—

50\. O Brahmā, if I am to be proclaimed the emperor of the gods, I do not have the paraphernalia characteristic of my lordship.

## \|\| 6.6.51 \|\|

*ratho nāsti mahādivyastādṛk sārathinā saha \|*  
*dhanurbāṇādikaṃ cāpi saṃgrāme jayakārakam \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. I do not have a divine chariot and a divine charioteer. I do not possess bows and arrows which accord victory in a battle.

## \|\| 6.6.52 \|\|

*yamāsthāya dhanurbāṇān gṛhītvā yojya va manaḥ \|*  
*nihaniṣyāmyahaṃ daityān prabalānapi saṃgare \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. If there had been a chariot I could have sat in it and with bow and arrows I could have killed even powerful Asuras, with a resolute determination.

## \|\| 6.6.53 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*adya sabrahmakā devāssendropendrāḥ praharṣitāḥ \|*  
*śrutvā prabhostadā vākyaṃ natvā procurmaheśvaram \|\| 53 \|\|*

Sanatakumāra said:—

53\. On hearing these words of the lord, the gods including Brahmā, Indra and Viṣṇu were delighted. After bowing to him they spoke to lord Śiva.

## \|\| 6.6.54 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|\| vayaṃ bhavāma deveśa tatprakārā maheśvara \|*  
*rathādikā tava svā minsaṃnaddhāssaṃgarāya hi \|\| 54 \|\|*

The gods said:—

54\. O lord of the gods, O great god, we shall constitute those paraphernalia—chariot etc. O lord, we are ready for the battle.

## \|\| 6.6.55 \|\|

*ityuktvā saṃhatāssarve śivecchāmadhigamya ha \|*  
*pṛthagūcuḥ prasannāste kṛtāñjalipuṭāssurāḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. After saying so jointly after realising Śiva’s wish they, the delighted gods, severally told him so, with palms joined in reverence.

## Chapter 7 - The gods pray

## \|\| 6.7.1 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*etacchutvā tu sarveṣāṃ devādīnāṃ vaco haraḥ \|*  
*aṃgīcakāra suprītyā śaraṇyo bhaktavatsalaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Samtkumāra said:—

1\. On hearing the words of the gods and others, Śiva accepted the proposal. The lord is worthy of being sought refuge and is also favourably disposed to his devotees.

## \|\| 6.7.2 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare devī putrābhyāṃ saṃyutā śivā \|*  
*ājagāma mune tatra yatra devānvito haraḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. O sage, in the meantime the goddess Pārvatī arrived there with the two sons where Śiva was in conversation with the gods.

## \|\| 6.7.3 \|\|

*athāgatāṃ śivāṃ dṛṣṭvā sarve viṣṇvādayo drutam \|*  
*praṇemuratinamrāste vismitā gatasaṃbhramāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. On seeing Pārvatī come there, Viṣṇu and others were surprised but without agitation they bowed to her in great humility.

## \|\| 6.7.4 \|\|

*procurjayeti sadvākyaṃ mune sarve sulakṣaṇam \|*  
*tūṣṇīmāsannajānaṃtastadāgamanakāraṇam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. O sage, they shouted cries of “Victory”. But unable to know the cause of her arrival, they remained silent.

## \|\| 6.7.5 \|\|

*atha sarvaiḥ stutā devairdevyadbhutakutūhalā \|*  
*uvāca svāminaṃ prītyā nānālīlāviśāradam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. On being eulogised by the gods, the goddess Pārvatī full of wonderful enthusiasm spoke lovingly to her lord, an expert in different kinds of sports.

## \|\| 6.7.6 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*krīḍamānaṃ vibho paśya ṣaṇmukhaṃ ravisaṃnibham \|*  
*putraṃ putravatāṃ śreṣṭha bhūṣitaṃ bhūṣaṇairvaraiḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

The goddess said:—

6\. “O lord, see the sportive six-faced Kārttikeya, refulgent like the sun our excellent son embellished by excellent ornaments.”

## \|\| 6.7.7 \|\|

*ityevaṃ lokamātrā ca vāgbhissaṃbodhitaśśivaḥ \|*  
*na yayau tṛptimīśānaḥ piban skaṃdānanāmṛtam \|\| 7 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

7\. Thus addressed by the mother of the worlds with pleasing words, Lord Śiva was never satiated in drinking nectar of the beauty of Skanda’s face.

## \|\| 6.7.8 \|\|

*na sasmārāgatāndaityānnijatejonipīḍitān \|*  
*skaṃdamāliṃgya cāghrāya mugodāti maheśvaraḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. He recollected the Asuras who had come (to fight and) pounded by his splendrous valour. Embracing and kissing Skanda on the head lord Śiva rejoiced much.

## \|\| 6.7.9 \|\|

*jagadambātha tatraiva saṃmaṃtrya prabhuṇā ca sā \|*  
*sthitvā kiñcitsamuttasthau nānālīlāviśāradā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Then the mother of the universe stayed there for a while and held conversation with the lord. Afterwards the goddess, an expert in different kinds of sports stood up.

## \|\| 6.7.10 \|\|

*tatassanaṃdī saha ṣaṇmukhena tayā ca sārddhaṃ girirājaputryā \|*  
*viveśa śambhurbhavanaṃ sulīlaḥ suraissamastairabhivaṃdyamānaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Then Śiva of good sports entered his apartment accompanied by Nandin and Pārvatī. He was then saluted by all the gods.

## \|\| 6.7.11 \|\|

*dvārasya pārśvataḥ tasthurdevadevasya dhīmataḥ \|*  
*te'tha devā mahāvyagrā vimanaskā mune'khilaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. O sage, all the gods dispirited and worried stood on either side of the doorway of mansion of Śiva, the intelligent lord of the gods.

## \|\| 6.7.12 \|\|

*kiṃ kartavyaṃ kva gaṃtavyaṃ kaḥ syādasmatsukhapradaḥ \|*  
*kiṃ tu kiṃtviti saṃjātaṃ hā hatāḥ smeti vādinam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. They began to mutter “What shall we do? Where shall we go? Who will make us happy? Everything has happened with a “but.” We are doomed.”

## \|\| 6.7.13 \|\|

*anyonyaṃ prekṣya śakrādyā babhūvuścātivihvalāḥ \|*  
*procurvikalavākyaṃ te dhikkurvanto nijaṃ vidhim \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Indra and others looked at one another’s face. They were much agitated. They spoke in faltering words. They cursed their fate.

## \|\| 6.7.14 \|\|

*pāpā vayamihetyanye hyabhāgyāśceti cāpare \|*  
*te bhāgyavaṃto daityendrā iti cānye'bruvan surāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Some gods said “We are sinners.” Others said “We are unfortunate.” Still others said “The great Asuras are very fortunate.”

## \|\| 6.7.15 \|\|

*tasminnevāṃtare teṣāṃ śrutvā śabdānanekaśaḥ \|*  
*kuṃbhodaro mahātejā daṃḍenātāḍayatsurān \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. In the meantime on hearing their multifarious voices, Kumbhodara of excessive refulgence beat the gods with a baton.

## \|\| 6.7.16 \|\|

*dudruvuste bhayāviṣṭā devā hāheti vādinaḥ \|*  
*apatanmunayaścānye vihvalatvaṃ babhūva ha \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The terrified gods shouting “Hā Hā” fled from there. The sages faltered and fell on the ground. There was excitement and great confusion.

## \|\| 6.7.17 \|\|

*indrastu vikalotīva jānubhyāmavanīṃ gataḥ \|*  
*anye devarṣayotīva vikalāḥ patitā bhuvi \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Unnerved and languid, Indra crawled on his knees. The celestial sages dropped to the ground.

## \|\| 6.7.18 \|\|

*sarve militvā munayassurāśca samamākulāḥ \|*  
*saṃgatā vidhiharyostu samīpaṃ mitracetasoḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The excessively agitated sages and gods gathered together and approached Brahmā and Viṣṇu of friendly tamperament.

## \|\| 6.7.19 \|\|

*aho vidhibalaṃ caitanmunayaḥ kaśyapādayaḥ \|*  
*vadaṃti sma tadā sarve hari lokabhayāpadam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The sages Kaśyapa and others said to Viṣṇu who removes the fear of all the worlds “O this is due to our ill luck.”

## \|\| 6.7.20 \|\|

*abhāgyānna samāptaṃ tu kāryamityapare dvijāḥ \|*  
*kasmādvighnamidaṃ jātamityanye hyati vismitāḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. The other brahmins said—“Our task is not completed due to our ill luck.” Still others who were greatly surprised said—“How did this obstacle happen?”

## \|\| 6.7.21 \|\|

*ityevaṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā kaśyapādyuditaṃ mune \|*  
*āśvāsayanmunīndevān harirvākyamupādade \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. O sage, on hearing these words of Kaśyapa and others, Viṣṇu consoled the sages and the gods and spoke thus.

## \|\| 6.7.22 \|\|

*viṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*he devā munayassarve madvacaḥ śṛṇutādarāt \|*  
*kimarthaṃ duḥkhamāpannā dukhaṃ tu tyajatākhilam \|\| 22 \|\|*

Viṣṇu said:—

22\. O gods, O sages, you listen to my words with attention. Why are you distressed? Eschew your sorrows.

## \|\| 6.7.23 \|\|

*mahadārādhanaṃ devā na susādhyaṃ vicāryyatām \|*  
*mahadārādhane pūrvaṃ bhavedduḥkhamiti śrutam \|*  
*vijñāya dṛḍhatāṃ devāḥ prasanno bhavati dhruvam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. O gods ponder over this. This propitiation of the great is not an easy task. It is heard that there is great difficulty at first in propitiating the great. The lord will certainly be pleased after coming to know of your resolute nature.

## \|\| 6.7.24 \|\|

*śivassarvagaṇāyakṣassahasā parameśvaraḥ \|*  
*vicāryatāṃ hṛdā sarvaiḥ kathaṃ vaśyo bhavediti \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Let this be pondered over well by all of you, how can lord Śiva, the presiding deity of the Gaṇas be made favourable immediately.

## \|\| 6.7.25-26 \|\|

*praṇavaṃ pūrvamuccāryya namaḥ paścādudāharet \|*  
*śivāyeti tataḥ paścācchubhadvayamataḥ param \|\| 25 \|\|*

*kurudvayaṃ tataḥ proktaṃ śivāya ca tataḥ punaḥ \|*  
*namaśca praṇavaścaiva maṃtramevaṃ sadā budhāḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. O scholars, the following mantra shall be repeated—Utter the syllable Oṃkāra first, then repeat the word Namaḥ (obeisance). Then say Śivāya (to Śiva). Then repeat “Śubham” twice and “Kuru” twice. Afterwards say “Śivāya Namaḥ Om.”

## \|\| 6.7.27 \|\|

*avartadhvaṃ punaryūyaṃ yadi śaṃbhukṛte tadā \|*  
*koṭimekaṃ tathā japtvā śivaḥ kāryaṃ kariṣyati \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. If you repeat this mantra a crore times thinking of Śiva, Śiva will carry out the task.

## \|\| 6.7.28 \|\|

*ityukte ca tadā tena hariṇā prabhaviṣṇunā \|*  
*tathā devāḥ punaścakrurharasyārādhanaṃ mune \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. O sage, when this was mentioned by Viṣṇu the powerful, the gods began to propitiate Śiva.

## \|\| 6.7.29 \|\|

*saṃjajāpa hariścāpi savidhiśśivamānasaḥ \|*  
*devānāṃ kāryasiddhyarthaṃ munīnāṃ ca viśeṣataḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. For the fulfilment of the task of the gods and the sages, Viṣṇu and Brahmā, with minds fixed in Śiva performed the Japa.

## \|\| 6.7.30 \|\|

*muhuḥ śiveti bhāṣaṃto devā dhairyasamanvitāḥ \|*  
*koṭisaṃkhyaṃ tadā kṛtvā sthitāste munisattama \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. O excellent sage, they stood there steady and repeated the mantra a crore times uttering the name “Śiva” several times.

## \|\| 6.7.31 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare sākṣācchivaḥ prādurabhūtsvayam \|*  
*yathoktena svarūpeṇa vacanaṃ cedamabravīt \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. In the meantime Śiva came into direct view assuming his real form and spoke.

## \|\| 6.7.32 \|\|

*śrīśiva uvāca \|*  
*he hare he vidhe devā munayaśca śubhavratāḥ \|*  
*prasanno'smi varaṃ brūta jayenānena cepsitam \|\| 32 \|\|*

Lord Śiva said:—

32\. O Viṣṇu, O Brahmā, O gods and O sages of auspicious rites, I am delighted by your Japa. Speak out the desired boon.

## \|\| 6.7.33 \|\|

*\|\| devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*yadi prasanno deveśa jagadīśvara śaṃkara \|*  
*surān vijñāya vikalān hanyaṃtāṃ tripurāṇi ca \|\| 33 \|\|*

The gods said:—

33\. O Śiva, lord of the gods, lord of the universe, if you are pleased, realising that the gods are unnerved, let the Tripuras be destroyed.

## \|\| 6.7.34 \|\|

*rakṣāsmānparameśāna dīnabaṃdho kṛpākara \|*  
*tvayaiva rakṣitā devāssadāpadbhyo muhurmuhuḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. O lord Śiva, O merciful one, O kinsman of the distressed, save us. We, gods, have always been saved from adversities by you alone.

## \|\| 6.7.35 \|\|

*\|\| sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityuktaṃ vacanaṃ teṣāṃ śrutvā saharivedhasām \|*  
*vihasyāṃtastadā brahmanmaheśaḥ punarabravīt \|\| 35 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

35\. O brahmin, on hearing these words uttered by them including Viṣṇu and Brahmā, lord Śiva laughed to himself and spoke again.

## \|\| 6.7.36 \|\|

*\|\| maheśa uvāca \|*  
*he hare he vidhe devā munayaścākhilā vacaḥ \|*  
*madīyaṃ śṛṇutādṛtya naṣṭaṃ matvā puratrayam \|\| 36 \|\|*

Lord Śiva said:—

36\. Viṣṇu, O Brahmā, O gods, O sages all of you listen to my words with attention considering that the three cities have been already destroyed.

## \|\| 6.7.37 \|\|

*rathaṃ ca sārathiṃ divyaṃ kārmukaṃ śaramuttamam \|*  
*pūrvamaṃgīkṛtaṃ sarvamupapādayatāciram \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Hence make arrangements for the chariot, charioteer, divine bow and excellent arrows as agreed to by you all. Do not delay.

## \|\| 6.7.38 \|\|

*he viṣṇo he vidhe tvaṃ hi trilokādhipatirdhruvam \|*  
*sarvasamrāṭprakāraṃ me kartumarhasi yatnataḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. O Brahmā, O Viṣṇu, you are the lord of the three worlds, to be sure. Hence provide me with the paraphernalia of an emperor.

## \|\| 6.7.39 \|\|

*naṣṭaṃ puratrayaṃ matvā devasāhāyyamityuta \|*  
*kariṣyathaḥ prayatnenādhikṛtau sargapālane \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. You too had been entrusted with the tasks of creation and sustenance. You shall make all efforts, considering the destruction of the three cities an act of help to the gods.

## \|\| 6.7.40 \|\|

*ayaṃ maṃtro mahāpuṇyo matprītijanakaśśubhaḥ \|*  
*bhuktimuktipradassarvakāmadaśśaivakāvaha \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. This mantra is highly meritorious and auspicious. It generates the pleasure of the gods. It yields both worlds by enjoyment and salvation, confers cherished desires and brings about the happiness of the devotees of Śiva.

## \|\| 6.7.41 \|\|

*dhanyo yaśasya āyuṣyaḥ svargakāmārthināṃ nṛṇām \|*  
*apavargo hyakāmānāṃ muktānāṃ bhuktimuktidaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. It is conducive to blessedness, fame, longevity to those who seek heaven. Those who are free from desires derive the benefit of salvation.

## \|\| 6.7.42 \|\|

*ya imaṃ kīrtayenmaṃtraṃ śucirbhūtvā sadā naraḥ \|*  
*śṛṇuyācchrāvayedvāpi sarvānkāmānavāpnuyāt \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. The man who repeats this mantra in purity, hears or narrates this to anyone, shall attain all desires.

## \|\| 6.7.43 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*iti śrutvā vacastasya śivasya paramātmanaḥ \|*  
*sarve devā mudaṃ prāpurharirbrahmādhikaṃ tathā \|\| 43 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

43\. On hearing these words of Śiva, the great Ātman, the gods derived more pleasure than Viṣṇu and Brahmā.

## \|\| 6.7.44 \|\|

*sarvadevamayaṃ divyaṃ rathaṃ paramaśobhanam \|*  
*racayāmāsa viśvārthe viśvakarmā tadājñayā \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. At his bidding, Viśvakarman made a splendid chariot of good features, consisting of all the gods, for the welfare of the people.

## Chapter 8 - The detailed description of the chariot etc.

## \|\| 6.8.1 \|\|

*\|\| vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*sanatkumāra sarvajña śaivapravara sanmate \|*  
*adbhuteyaṃ kathā tāta śrāvitā parimeśituḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:—

1\. O Sanatkumāra, of good intellect, O omniscient one, O foremost among the devotees of Śiva, this wonderful story of lord Śiva has been narrated to us.

## \|\| 6.8.2 \|\|

*idānīṃ rathanirmāṇaṃ brūhi devamayaṃ param \|*  
*śivārthaṃ yatkṛtaṃ divyaṃ dhīmatā viśvakarmaṇā \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Now please mention the structure of the chariot which consisted of all the gods and which had been made by the intelligent Viśvakarman.

## \|\| 6.8.3 \|\|

*\|\| sūta uvāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya vacastasya vyāsasya sa munīśvaraḥ \|*  
*sanatkumāraḥ provāca smṛtvā śivapadāṃbujam \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sūta said:—

3\. On hearing these words of Vyāsa, Sanatkumāra the great sage remembered the lotus-like feet of Śiva and spoke thus.

## \|\| 6.8.4 \|\|

*\|\| sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu vyāsa mahāprājña rathādernirmitiṃ mune \|*  
*yathāmati pravakṣye'haṃ smṛtvā śivapadāmbujam \|\| 4 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

4\. O sage Vyāsa, of great intellect, listen to the description of the structure of the chariot etc which I shall give to the extent of my intellect after remembering the lotus-like feet of Śiva.

## \|\| 6.8.5 \|\|

*atha devasya rudrasya nirmito viśvakarmaṇā \|*  
*sarvalokamayo divyo ratho yatnena sādaram \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The divine chariot of lord Śiva consisting of all the worlds was built by Viśvakarman with devoted effort.

## \|\| 6.8.6 \|\|

*sarvabhūtamayaścaiva sauvarṇassarvasaṃmataḥ \|*  
*rathāṃgaṃ dakṣiṇaṃ sūryastadvāmaṃ soma eva ca \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. It was appreciated by all. It was golden in colour and all the elements had gone into its making. The right wheel was the sun and the left wheel was the moon.

## \|\| 6.8.7-8 \|\|

*dakṣiṇaṃ dvādaśāraṃ hi ṣoḍaśāraṃ tathottaram \|*  
*areṣu teṣu viprendra ādityā dvādaśaiva tu \|\| 7 \|\|*

*śaśinaḥ ṣoḍaśārāstu kalā vāmasya suvrata \|*  
*ṛkṣāṇi tu tathā tasya vāmasyaiva vibhūṣaṇam \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. The right wheel had twelve spokes. O great brahmin, the twelve Ādityas presided over them. The left wheel had sixteen spokes. O you of excellent rites, the sixteen spokes of the left side wheel consisted of the sixteen digits of the moon. All the asterism? embellished the left side.

## \|\| 6.8.9 \|\|

*ṛtavo nemayaḥ ṣaṭ ca tayorvai viprapuṃgava \|*  
*puṣkaraṃ cāṃtarikṣaṃ vai rathanīḍaśca maṃdaraḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The six seasons constituted the rims of the wheels of the chariot, O great Brahmin. The Puṣkara of the chariot was the sky. The inner side of the chariot was Mandara.

## \|\| 6.8.10 \|\|

*astādrirudayādristu tāvubhau kūbarau smṛtau \|*  
*adhiṣṭhānaṃ mahāmerurāśrayāḥ keśarācalāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The rising and the setting mountains constituted the poleshafts. Mahāmeru was the support and the Keśara mountains the sharp sides.

## \|\| 6.8.11 \|\|

*vegassaṃvatsarāstasya ayane cakrasaṃgamau \|*  
*muhūrtā vaṃdhurāstasya śamyāścaiva kalāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The year constituted its velocity. The two Ayanas northern and southern constituted the junctions of the wheels and axles. The Muhūrtas constituted the joints and the Kalās the pins of the yoke.

## \|\| 6.8.12 \|\|

*tasya kāṣṭhāḥ smṛtā ghoṇāścākṣadaṃḍāḥ kṣaṇāśca vai \|*  
*nimeṣāścānukarṣaśca īṣāścānulavāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The division of time Kāṣṭhā constituted the nose of the chariot and the Kṣaṇas the axle-shaft. The Nimeṣas constituted the bottom of the carriage and the minutest divisions of time constituted the poles.

## \|\| 6.8.13 \|\|

*dyaurvarūthaṃ rathasyāsya svargamokṣāvubhau dhvajau \|*  
*yugāntakoṭitau tasya bhramakāmadughau smṛtau \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The firmament constituted the fender of the chariot; Heaven and salvation the flag staffs; Abhṛamu (Abhramu?) and Kāmadhenu constituted its harrows at the end of the shafts.

## \|\| 6.8.14 \|\|

*īṣādaṃḍastathā vyaktaṃ vṛddhistasyaiva naḍvalaḥ \|*  
*koṇāstasyāpyahaṃkāro bhūtāni ca balaṃ smṛtam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The unmanifest principle formed their shaft and cosmic intellect the chariot’s reeds. The cosmic Ego cosmic corners and elements its strength.

## \|\| 6.8.15 \|\|

*indriyāṇi ca tasyaiva bhūṣaṇāni samaṃtataḥ \|*  
*śraddhā ca gatirasyaiva rathasya munisattama \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. O excellent sage, the cosmic sense-organs constituted the embellishments of this chariot on all sides. Faith was its movements.

## \|\| 6.8.16 \|\|

*tadānīṃ bhūṣaṇānyeva ṣaḍaṃgānyupabhūṣaṇam \|*  
*purāṇanyāyamīmāṃsā dharmaśāstrāṇi suvratāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The six Vedāṅgas were its ornaments. O great ones of good rites, the Purāṇas, Nyāya, Mīmāṃsā and Dharma Śāstras constituted the side trinkets.

## \|\| 6.8.17 \|\|

*balāśayā varāścaiva sarvalakṣaṇasaṃyutāḥ \|*  
*maṃtrā ghaṃṭāḥ smṛtāsteṣāṃ varṇapādāstadāśramāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The forceful and excellent mantras with their syllables and feet, of all characteristic features and the stages in life constituted the tinkling bells.

## \|\| 6.8.18 \|\|

*atho bandho hyanantastu sahasraphaṇabhūṣitaḥ \|*  
*diśaḥ pādā rathasyāsya tathā copadiśaścaha \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Ananta embellished with thousand hoods constituted its fittings. and the main and subsidiary quarters, the pedestals of the chariot.

## \|\| 6.8.19 \|\|

*puṣkarādyāḥ patākāśca sauvarṇā ratnabhūṣitāḥ \|*  
*samudrāstasya catvāro rathakaṃbalinassmṛtāḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The clouds Puṣkara and others constituted the gem-studded banners of glowing colours. The four oceans are remembered as the bullocks of the chariot.

## \|\| 6.8.20 \|\|

*gaṃgādyāssarita śreṣṭhāḥ sarvābharaṇabhūṣitāḥ \|*  
*cāmarāsaktahastāgrāssarvāstrīrūpaśobhitāḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Gaṅgā and other rivers shining in excellent female forms and decorated in all ornaments held the Cāmaras in their hands.

## \|\| 6.8.21 \|\|

*tatra tatra kṛtasthānāḥ śobhayāṃcakrire ratham \|*  
*āvahādyāstathā sapta sopānaṃ haimamuttamam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Taking up their places in the different parts of the chariot, they brightened it up. The seven courses of the wind Āvaha etc. constituted the excellent steps of gold leading the chariot.

## \|\| 6.8.22 \|\|

*lokālokācalastasyopasopānassamaṃtataḥ \|*  
*viṣayaśca tathā bāhyo mānasādistu śobhanaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The Lokāloka mountain formed its side steps. The lake mānasa etc. constituted its brilliant outer and oblique steps.

## \|\| 6.8.23 \|\|

*pāśāssamaṃtatastasya sarve varṣācalāssmṛtāḥ \|*  
*talāstasya rathasyā'tha sarve talanivāsinaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. The Varṣa mountains constituted the cords and chains all round the chariot. All the residents of the region Tala constituted the bottem surface of the chariot.

## \|\| 6.8.24 \|\|

*sārathirbhagavānbrahmā devā raśmidharāḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*pratodo brahmaṇastasya praṇavo brahmadaivatam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Lord Brahmā was the charioteer, the gods were holders of the bridle. Praṇava the Vedic divinity constituted the long whip of Brahma.

## \|\| 6.8.25 \|\|

*akāraśca mahacchatraṃ maṃdaraḥ pārśvadaṃḍabhāk \|*  
*śailendraḥ kārmukaṃ tasya jyā bhujaṃgādhipassvayam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The syllable A constituted the great umbrella, Mandara the side staff. The lord of mountains became his bow and the lord of serpents the bowstring.

## \|\| 6.8.26 \|\|

*ghaṃṭā sarasvatī devī dhanuṣaḥ śrutirūpiṇī \|*  
*iṣurviṣṇurmahātejāstvagniśśalyaṃ prakīrtitam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Goddess Sarasvatī in the form of the Vedas constituted the bells of the bow. The brilliant Viṣṇu became the arrow and Agni the spear-head.

## \|\| 6.8.27 \|\|

*hayāstasya tathā proktāścatvāro nigamā mune \|*  
*jyotīṃṣi bhūṣaṇaṃ teṣāmavaśiṣṭānyataḥ param \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. O sage, the four Vedas are said to be his horses. The remaining planets became their embellishments.

## \|\| 6.8.28 \|\|

*anīkaṃ viṣasaṃbhūtaṃ vāyavo vājakā smṛtāḥ \|*  
*ṛṣayo vyāsamukhyāśca vāhavāhāstathābhavan \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. His army came up from water. The winds were his feathers, wings etc. Vyāsa and other sages were the drivers of the vehicle.

## \|\| 6.8.29 \|\|

*svalpākṣaraissaṃbravīmi kiṃ bahūktyā munīśvara \|*  
*brahmāṃḍe caiva yatkiṃcidvastutadvai rathe smṛtam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. O great sage, why should I dilate. I shall succinctly say. Everything in the world found a place in the chariot.

## \|\| 6.8.30 \|\|

*evaṃ samyakkṛtastena dhīmatā viśvakarmaṇā \|*  
*sarathādiprakāro hi brahmaviṣṇvājñayā śubhaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. At the bidding of Brahmā and Viṣṇu the chariot and its adjuncts were created bythe intelligent Viśvakarman.

## Chapter 9 - Śiva’s campaign

## \|\| 6.9.1 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*īdṛgvidhaṃ mahādivyaṃ nānāścaryamayaṃ ratham \|*  
*saṃnahya nigamānaśvāṃstaṃ brahmā prārpayacchivam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

1\. Brahmā handed over that divine chariot of various wonderful features to Śiva after yoking the Vedas as the horses.

## \|\| 6.9.2 \|\|

*śaṃbhave'sau nivedyādhiropayāmāsa śūlinam \|*  
*bahuśaḥ prārthya deveśaṃ viṣṇvādisurasamatam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. After dedicating the same to Śiva, he requested Śiva the lord of the gods, approved by Viṣṇu and other gods to mount the chariot.

## \|\| 6.9.3 \|\|

*tatastasminrathe divye rathaprākārasaṃyute \|*  
*sarvadevamayaḥ śaṃbhurāruroha mahāprabhuḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The great lord Śiva identifying himself with all the gods got into that chariot that had various scaffoldings attached to it.

## \|\| 6.9.4 \|\|

*ṛṣibhiḥ stūyamānaśca devagaṃdharvapannagaiḥ \|*  
*viṣṇunā brahmaṇā cāpi lokapālairbabhūva ha \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. He was then eulogised by the gods, Gandharvas, serpents, sages, Viṣṇu, Brahmā and the guardians of the quarters.

## \|\| 6.9.5-6 \|\|

*upāvṛtaścāpsarasāṃ gaṇairgītaviśāradaḥ \|*  
*śuśubhe varadaśśambhussa taṃ prekṣya ca sārathim \|\| 5 \|\|*

*tasminnāro'hatirathaṃ kalpitaṃ lokasaṃbhṛtam \|*  
*śirobhiḥ patitā bhūmau turagā vedasaṃbhavāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. Śiva, the granter of boons, surrounded by the groups of damsels, experts in music, shone well. Glancing at the charioteer when he mounted the chariot concocted with everything in the world, the horses constituted by the Vedas fell headlong to the ground.

## \|\| 6.9.7 \|\|

*cacāla vasudhā celussakalāśca mahīdharāḥ \|*  
*cakaṃpe sahasā śeṣo'soḍhā tadbhāramāturaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The earth quaked. The mountains became tremulous. Śeṣa, unable to bear his weight, became distressed and soon began to tremble.

## \|\| 6.9.8 \|\|

*athādhaḥ sa rathasyāsya bhagavāndharaṇīdharaḥ \|*  
*vṛṣendrarūpī cotthāya sthāpayāmāsa vai kṣaṇam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Lord Viṣṇu assumed the form of a lordly bull and went under the chariot. He lifted it up and steadied it for a short while.

## \|\| 6.9.9 \|\|

*kṣaṇāṃtare vṛṣendro'pi jānubhyāmagamaddharām \|*  
*rathārūḍhamaheśasya sutejassoḍhumakṣamaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. But in another instant, unable to bear the weighty splendour of lord Śiva seated in the chariot, the lordly bull had to kneel down and crawl on the ground.

## \|\| 6.9.10-12 \|\|

*abhīṣuhasto bhagavānudyamya ca hayāṃstadā \|*  
*sthāpayāmāsa devasya pacanādvairathaṃ varam \|\| 10 \|\|*

*tato'sau nodayāmāsa manomārutaraṃhasaḥ \|*  
*brahmā hayānvedamayānnaddhānrathavare sthitaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*purāṇyuddiśya vai trīṇi teṣāṃ khasthāni tāni hi \|*  
*adhiṣṭhite maheśe tu dānavānāṃ tarasvinām \|\| 12 \|\|*

10-12. But the lord touched the bridle and steadied the horses. Then Brahmā seated in the excellent chariot drove the excellent chariot with the velocity of mind and wind, at the bidding of the lord towards the three cities of the valiant Asuras. The cities were then in the sky. Lord Śiva was seated inside.

## \|\| 6.9.13 \|\|

*athāha bhagavānrudro devānālokya śaṃkaraḥ \|*  
*paśūnāmādhipatyaṃ me dhaddhvaṃ hanmi tato'surān \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Then lord Śiva looked at the gods and said—“Give me the lordship of the animals. Then I shall kill the Asuras.

## \|\| 6.9.14 \|\|

*pṛthakpaśutvaṃ devānāṃ tathānyeṣāṃ surottamāḥ \|*  
*kalpayitvaiva vadhyāste nānyathā daityasattamāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. O excellent gods, the excellent Asuras can be killed only after assigning separate animalhood to the gods and others. Not otherwise.”

## \|\| 6.9.15 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*iti śrutvā vacastasya devadevasya dhīmataḥ \|*  
*viṣādamagamansarve paśutvaṃ pratiśaṃkitāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

15\. On hearing these words of the intelligent lord of the gods, they became dispirited growing suspicious of animalhood.

## \|\| 6.9.16 \|\|

*teṣāṃ bhāvamatha jñātvā devadevo'mbikāpatiḥ \|*  
*vihasya kṛpayā devāñchaṃbhustānidamabravīt \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. On knowing what was passing through their minds, Śiva, the lord of the gods, the consort of Pārvatī sympathised with the gods and laughingly said.

## \|\| 6.9.17 \|\|

*śaṃbhuruvāca \|*  
*mā vo'stu paśubhāve'pi pāto vibudhasattamāḥ \|*  
*śrūyatāṃ paśubhāvasya vimokṣaḥ kriyatāṃ ca saḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

Śiva said:—

17\. “O excellent gods, you will not fall even in your animalhood. Let it be heard, and let the process of release from animalhood be practised.

## \|\| 6.9.18 \|\|

*yau vai pāśupataṃ divyaṃ cariṣyati sa mokṣyati \|*  
*paśutvāditi satyaṃ vaḥ pratijñātaṃ samāhitāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. He who performs the divine rite of Pāśupata will be released from animalhood. I promise this to you. Be attentive.

## \|\| 6.9.19 \|\|

*ye cāpyanye kariṣyaṃti vrataṃ pāśupataṃ mama \|*  
*mokṣyaṃti te na saṃdehaḥ paśutvātsurasattamāḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. O excellent gods, there is no doubt about it that those who perform my Pāśupata rite will become liberated.

## \|\| 6.9.20 \|\|

*naiṣṭhikaṃ dvādaśābdaṃ vā tadarthaṃ varṣakatrayam \|*  
*śuśrūṣāṃ kārayedyastu sa paśutvādvimucyate \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. He who renders service perpetually or for twelve years, becomes relieved of animalhood.

## \|\| 6.9.21 \|\|

*tasmātparamidaṃ divyaṃ cariṣyatha surottamāḥ \|*  
*paśutvānmokṣyatha tadā yūyamatra na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Hence O excellent gods, perform this divine rite. You will be released from animalhood. There is no doubt about this.”

## \|\| 6.9.22 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya vacastasya maheśasya parātmanaḥ \|*  
*tatheti cābruvandevā haribrahmādayastathā \|\| 22 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

22\. On hearing these words of lord Śiva, the great soul, Viṣṇu, Brahmā and other gods said. “So be it.”

## \|\| 6.9.23 \|\|

*tasmādvai paśavassarve devāsuravarāḥ prabhoḥ \|*  
*rudraḥ paśupatiścaiva paśupāśavimocakaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Hence all the gods and Asuras became the animals of the lord. Śiva became the lord of animals. He is the person who unties the nooses of the animals.

## \|\| 6.9.24 \|\|

*tadā paśupatītyetattasya nāma maheśituḥ \|*  
*prasiddhamabhavadvadhvā sarvalokeṣu śarmadam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Then the name Paśupati, that bestows welfare, spread in all the worlds and became renowned.

## \|\| 6.9.25 \|\|

*mudā jayeti bhāṣaṃtassarve devarṣayastadā \|*  
*amudaṃścāti deveśo brahmā viṣṇuḥ pare'pi ca \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Then the celestial sage, Indra, Brahmā, Viṣṇu and others rejoiced shouting “Victory.”

## \|\| 6.9.26 \|\|

*tasmiṃśca samaye yacca rūpaṃ tasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*jātaṃ tadvarṇituṃ śakyaṃ na hi varṣaśatairapi \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Even in hundreds of years it is impossible to describe adequately the form of the great soul which he assumed then.

## \|\| 6.9.27 \|\|

*evaṃ vidho maheśāno maheśānyakhileśvaraḥ \|*  
*jagāma tripuraṃ haṃtuṃ sarveṣāṃ sukhadāyakaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Śiva the lord of Pārvatī and everyone, the bestower of happiness to all, went ahead to destroy the three cities.

## \|\| 6.9.28 \|\|

*taṃ devadevaṃ tripuraṃ nihaṃtuṃ tadānu sarve tu raviprakāśāḥ \|*  
*gajairhayaissiṃhavarai rathaiśca vṛṣairyayuste'mararājamukhyāḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Then all the gods, resplendent like the sun, under the lord of the gods and others went on elephants, horses, lions, bulls and chariots to kill Tripuras, leaders of the Asuras.

## \|\| 6.9.29 \|\|

*halaiśca śālairmuśalairbhuśuṇḍairgirīndrakalpairgirisaṃnibhāśca \|*  
*nānāyudhaissaṃyutabāhavaste tato nu hṛṣṭāḥ prayayussureśāḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. The leading gods as huge as mountains went ahead delighted and well-armed with all sorts of missiles, plough-shares, mortars, iron clubs and uprooted trees as huge as mountains.

## \|\| 6.9.30 \|\|

*nānāyudhāḍhyāḥ paramaprakāśā mahotsavaśśaṃbhujayaṃ vadaṃtaḥ \|*  
*yayuḥ purastasya maheśvarasya tadendrapadmodbhavaviṣṇumukhyāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Then Indra, Brahmā, Viṣṇu and others went ahead of lord Śiva jubilantly shouting cries of victory to Śiva, well-armed with various weapons and shining brilliantly.

## \|\| 6.9.31 \|\|

*jahṛṣurmunayassarve daṃḍahastā jaṭādharāḥ \|*  
*vavṛṣuḥ puṣpavarṣāṇi khecarā siddhacāraṇāḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Sages with matted hair and staffs in the hands rejoiced. Siddhas and Cāraṇas moving about in the sky showered flowers.

## \|\| 6.9.32 \|\|

*putratrayaṃ ca viprendrā vrajansarve gaṇeśvarāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ saṃkhyā ca kaḥ kartuṃ samartho vacmi kāṃścana \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. O great brahmins, all the Gaṇeśvaras went to the three cities. Who can enumerate them fully? I shall mention a few.

## \|\| 6.9.33 \|\|

*gaṇeśvarairdevagaṇaiśca bhṛṅgī samāvṛtassarvagaṇendravaryaḥ \|*  
*jagāma yogāṃstripuraṃ nihaṃtuṃ vimānamāruhya yathā mahendraḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Bhṛṅgin, the chief of all Gaṇeśas, surrounded by lord of Gaṇas and gods went speedily to destroy the three cities like Mahendra seated in an aerial chariot.

## \|\| 6.9.34-39 \|\|

*keśo vigatavāsaśca mahākeśo mahājvaraḥ \|*  
*somavallīsavarṇaśca somadassanakastathā \|\| 34 \|\|*

*somadhṛk sūryavarcāśca sūryapreṣaṇakastathā \|*  
*sūryākṣassūrināmā ca surassundara eva ca \|\| 35 \|\|*

*praskaṃdaḥ kundaraścaṃḍaḥ kaṃpanaścātikaṃpanaḥ \|*  
*indraścendrajavaścaiva yaṃtā himakarastathā \|\| 36 \|\|*

*śatākṣaścaiva paṃcākṣaḥ sahasrākṣo mahodaraḥ \|*  
*satījahuśśatāsyaśca raṃkaḥ karpūrapūtanaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*dviśikhastriśikhaścaiva tathāhaṃkārakārakaḥ \|*  
*ajavaktro'ṣṭavaktraśca hayavaktro'rddhavaktrakaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*ityādyā gaṇapā vīrā bahavo'parimeyakāḥ \|*  
*prayayuḥ parivāryeśaṃ lakṣyalakṣaṇavarjitāḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

34-39. These were the important ones who were there—Keśa, Vigatavāsa, Mahākeśa, Mahājvara, Somavallīsavarṇa, Somapa, Sanaka, Somadhṛk, Sūryavarcas, Sūryapreṣaṇaka, Sūryākṣa, Sūrināman, Sura, Sundara, Praskanda, Kundara, Caṇḍa, Kampana, Atikampana, Indra, Indrajava, Yantṛ, Himakara, Śatākṣa, Pañcākṣa, Sahasrākṣa, Mahodara, Satijahru, Śatāsya, Raṅka, Karpūrapūtana, Dviśikha, Triśikha, Ahaṃkārakāraka, Ajavaktra, Aṣṭavaktra, Hayakāraka and Ardhavaktraka. These and other innumerable lords of Gaṇas who cannot be characterised and classified surrounded Śiva and went ahead.

## \|\| 6.9.40 \|\|

*samāvṛtya mahādevaṃ tadāpuste pinākinam \|*  
*dagdhuṃ samarthā manasā kṣaṇena sacarācaram \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. They were capable of burning the entire world including the mobile and immobile beings, within a trice by their very thought. Surrounding Śiva, the great lord, they went ahead.

## \|\| 6.9.41 \|\|

*dagdhuṃ jagatsarvamidaṃ samarthāḥ kiṃtvatra dagdhuṃ tripuraṃ pinākī \|*  
*rathena kiṃ cātra śareṇa tasya gaṇaiśca kiṃ devagaṇaiśca śambhoḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Śiva is capable of burning the entire world. Of what avail are the Gaṇas, gods, chariot, and arrows to Śiva in order to burn the three cities?

## \|\| 6.9.42 \|\|

*sa eva dagdhuṃ tripurāṇi tāni devadviṣāṃ vyāsa pinākapāṇiḥ \|*  
*svayaṃ gatastatra gaṇaiśca sārddhaṃ nijaissurāṇāmapi so'dbhutotiḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. O Vyāsa, that trident-bearing lord, of wonderful power of causing enjoyment and protection, himself went there with his own Gaṇas and the gods to burn the three cities of the enemies of gods.

## \|\| 6.9.43 \|\|

*kiṃ tatra kāraṇaṃ cānyadvacmi te ṛṣisattama \|*  
*lokeṣu khyāpanārthaṃ vai yaśaḥ paramalāpaham \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. What the reason was, I shall tell you, O excellent sage. It was to make his glory known to all the worlds, the glory that dispels all sins and dirt.

## \|\| 6.9.44 \|\|

*anyacca kāraṇaṃ hyetadduṣṭānāṃ pratyayāya vai \|*  
*sarveṣvapi ca deveṣu yasmānnānyo viśiṣyate \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Another reason was to convince the wicked, since there is none to excel him among the gods.

## Chapter 10 - The burning of the Tripuras

## \|\| 6.10.1 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*atha śambhurmahādevo rathasthassarvasaṃyutaḥ \|*  
*tripuraṃ sakalaṃ dagdhumudyato'bhūtsuradviṣām \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

1\. Then Śiva, the great lord, seated in the chariot and equipped with everything, got ready to burn the three cities completely, the cities of the enemies of the gods.

## \|\| 6.10.2-3 \|\|

*śīrṣaṃ sthānakamāsthāya saṃdhāya ca śarottamam \|*  
*sajjaṃ tatkārmukaṃ kṛtvā pratyālīḍhaṃ mahādbhutam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*niveśya dṛḍhamuṣṭau ca dṛṣṭiṃ dṛṣṭau niveśya ca \|*  
*atiṣṭhanniścalastatra śataṃ varṣasahasrakam \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. The lord stood in the wonderful posture of Pratyālīḍha for a hundred thousand years. The bow was well strung and kept near the head. The arrow was fixed. The fingers clenched at the bow firmly. The eyes were fixed.

## \|\| 6.10.4 \|\|

*tatoṅguṣṭhe gaṇādhyakṣassa tu daityaniśaṃsthitaḥ \|*  
*na lakṣyaṃ viviśustāni purāṇyasya triśūlinaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Gaṇeśa was stationed on the thumb. During this time the three cities did not come within the target path of the trident-bearing lord.

## \|\| 6.10.5 \|\|

*tatoṃtarikṣādaśṛṇoddhanurbāṇadharo haraḥ \|*  
*muṃjakeśo virūpākṣo vācaṃ paramaśobhanām \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Then from the firmament, the odd-eyed Śiva who was standing there holding the bow and the arrow heard an auspicious voice.

## \|\| 6.10.6 \|\|

*bho bho na yāvadbhagavannarcito'sau vināyakaḥ \|*  
*purāṇi jagadīśeśa sāṃprataṃ na haniṣyati \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. “O lord of the master of the universe, you will not kill the Tripuras as long as the lord Gaṇeśa is not adored”.

## \|\| 6.10.7 \|\|

*etacchrutvā tu vacanaṃ gajavaktramapūjayat \|*  
*bhadrakālīṃ samāhūya tatoṃdhakaniṣūdanaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. On hearing these words, Śiva the destroyer of Andhaka called Bhadrakālī and worshipped the elephant-faced god Gaṇeśa.

## \|\| 6.10.8-9 \|\|

*tasmin saṃpūjite harṣātparituṣṭe purassare \|*  
*vināyake tato vyomni dadarśa bhagavānharaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*purāṇi trīṇi daityānāṃ tārakāṇāṃ mahātmanām \|*  
*yathātathaṃ hi yuktāni keciditthaṃ vadaṃti ha \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. When Gaṇeśa was worshipped, when he standing ahead was pleased, lord Śiva saw the three cities of the powerful Asuras, sons of Tāraka, joined together.

## \|\| 6.10.10 \|\|

*parabrahmaṇi deveśa sarvopāsye maheśvare \|*  
*anyaprasādataḥ kāryaṃ siddhirghaṭati neti hi \|\| 10 \|\|*
