10\. It is said that when the great lord Śiva, the lord of the Gods, the supreme Brahman, worshipped by all is there, it is not proper -to say that he achieved success by another God’s grace.

## \|\| 6.10.11 \|\|

*sa svataṃtraḥ paraṃ brahma saguṇo nirguṇo'pi ha \|*  
*alakṣyaḥ sakalaissvāmī paramātmā niraṃjanaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. He is independent, the great Brahman, both possessed and devoid of attributes. He is invisible, the supreme soul and unsullied.

## \|\| 6.10.12 \|\|

*paṃcadevātmakaḥ paṃcadevopāsyaḥ paraḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*tasyopāsyo na kopyasti sa evopāsya ālayam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. He is the soul of five divinities. He is worshipped by the five deities. He is the great lord. There is none else worthy of worship. He is the ultimate abode of all.

## \|\| 6.10.13 \|\|

*atha vā līlayā tasya sarvaṃ saṃghaṭate mune \|*  
*caritaṃ devadevasya varadāturmaheśituḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Or, O sage, the activities of Śiva, the lord of the Gods, the granter of boons are but proper inasmuch as they constitute his divine sports.

## \|\| 6.10.14 \|\|

*tasmisthite mahādeve pūjayitvā gaṇādhipam \|*  
*purāṇi tatra kālena jagmurekatvamāśu vai \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. When the great God stood up after woeshipping Śiva, the three cities joined together into one unit.

## \|\| 6.10.15 \|\|

*ekībhāvaṃ mune tatra tripure samupāgate \|*  
*babhūva tumulo harṣo devādīnāṃ mahātmanām \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. O sage, when the three cities came to a unified whole, a tumultuous shout of joy rose up among the noble Gods and others.

## \|\| 6.10.16 \|\|

*tato devagaṇāssarve siddhāśca paramarṣayaḥ \|*  
*jayeti vāco mumucuḥ stuvaṃtaścāṣṭamūrtinam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Then all the Gods, Siddhas and the sages shouted out “Victory” and eulogised Śiva who has eight cosmic bodies.

## \|\| 6.10.17-18 \|\|

*athāheti tadā brahmā viṣṇuśca jagatāṃ patiḥ \|*  
*samayo'pi samāyāto daityānāṃ vadhakarmaṇaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*teṣāṃ tārakaputrāṇāṃ tripurāṇāṃ maheśvara \|*  
*devakāryaṃ kuru vibho ekatvamapi cāgatam \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. Then Brahmā and Viṣṇu, the lord of the worlds said—“The time for killing the Asuras has arrived, O great God. The three cities of the sons of Tāraka have come into one unified whole. O lord, please perform the task of the Gods.

## \|\| 6.10.19 \|\|

*yāvanna yānti deveśa viprayogaṃ purāṇi vai \|*  
*tāvadbāṇaṃ vimuṃcaśca tripuraṃ bhasmasātkuru \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. O lord of the gods please discharge the arrow and reduce the three cities to ashes lest they should be separated again.”

## \|\| 6.10.20 \|\|

*atha sajyaṃ dhanuḥ kṛtvā śarvassaṃdhāya taṃ śaram \|*  
*pūjya pāśupatāstraṃ sa tripuraṃ samaciṃtayat \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Then stringing the bow tight and fixing the arrow Pāśupata worthy of worship, he thought of the Tripuras.

## \|\| 6.10.21 \|\|

*atha devo mahādevo varalīlāviśāradaḥ \|*  
*kenāpi kāraṇenātra sāvajñaṃ tadavaikṣata \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Then lord Śiva, an expert in excellent divine sports for some reason looked at it with contempt.

## \|\| 6.10.22 \|\|

*puratrayaṃ virūpākṣaḥ kartuṃ tadbhasmasātkṣaṇāt \|*  
*samarthaḥ parameśāno mīnātu ca satāṃ gatiḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Śiva is capable of reducing the three cities to ashes in a trice, Still lord Śiva, the goal of the good bides his time.

## \|\| 6.10.23 \|\|

*dagdhuṃ samartho deveśo vīkṣaṇena jagattrayam \|*  
*asmadyaśo vivṛddhyarthaṃ śaraṃ moktumihārhasi \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. The lord of gods is capable of burning the three worlds by a single glance. O lord, for the flourish of our fame you shall discharge the arrow.

## \|\| 6.10.24 \|\|

*iti stuto'maraissarvaiviṣṇvādividhibhistadā \|*  
*dagdhuṃ puratrayaṃ tadvai bāṇenaicchanmaheśvaraḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. On being eulogised by Viṣṇu, Brahmā and other gods, lord Śiva desired to reduce the three cities to ashes with his arrow.

## \|\| 6.10.25-26 \|\|

*abhilākhyamuhūrte tu vikṛṣya dhanuradbhutam \|*  
*kṛtvā jyātalanirghoṣaṃ nādamatyaṃtadussaham \|\| 25 \|\|*

*ātmano nāma viśrāvya samābhāṣya mahāsurān \|*  
*mārtaṃḍakoṭivapuṣaṃ kāṃḍamugro mumoca ha \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. In the auspicious moment called Abhilāṣa he drew the bow and made a wonderful and unbearable twanging sound. He addressed the great Asuras and proclaimed his own name. Śiva discharged an arrow that had the refulgence of countless suns.

## \|\| 6.10.27 \|\|

*dadāha tripurasthāstāndaityāṃstrīnvimalāpahaḥ \|*  
*sa āśugo viṣṇumayo vahniśalyo mahājvalan \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. The arrow which was constituted by Viṣṇu and whose steel head was fire god blazed forth and burnt the three Asuras who lived in the three cities. It thereby removed their sins.

## \|\| 6.10.28 \|\|

*tataḥ purāṇi dagdhāni caturjaladhimekhalām \|*  
*gatāni yugapadbhūmiṃ trīṇi dagdhāni bhasmaśaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. The three cities reduced to ashes fell on the earth girt by the four oceans.

## \|\| 6.10.29 \|\|

*daityāstu śataśo dagdhāstasya bāṇasthavahninā \|*  
*hāhākāraṃ prakurvaṃtaśśivapūjāvyatikramāt \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Since they had refrained from the worship of Śiva, hundreds of Asuras were burnt by the fire generated by the arrow. They cried “Hā Hā” in distress.

## \|\| 6.10.30 \|\|

*tārakākṣastu nirdagdho bhrātṛbhyāṃ sahito'bhavat \|*  
*sasmāra svaprabhuṃ devaṃ śaṃkaraṃ bhaktavatsalam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Tārakākṣa was burnt along with his two brothers. He remembered his lord Śiva who is favourably disposed to his devotees.

## \|\| 6.10.31 \|\|

*bhaktyā paramayā yuktaḥ pralapan vividhā giraḥ \|*  
*mahādevaṃ samudvīkṣya manasā tamuvāca saḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Lamenting in diverse ways and looking up to lord Śiva, he mentally appealed to him.

## \|\| 6.10.32 \|\|

*tārakākṣa uvāca \|*  
*bhava jñātosi tuṣṭo'si yadyasmān saha baṃdhubhiḥ \|*  
*tena satyena bhūyo'pi kadā tvaṃ pradahiṣyasi \|\| 32 \|\|*

Tārakākṣa said:—

32\. “O Śiva, you are known to be pleased with us, if at any future hour you burn us, you will do so along with our kinsfolk. Let it be in accordance with this truth.

## \|\| 6.10.33 \|\|

*durlabhaṃ labdhamasmābhiryadaprāpyaṃ surāsuraiḥ \|*  
*tvadbhāvabhāvitā buddhirjātejāte bhavatviti \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. What is difficult and inaccessible to the gods and Asuras has been secured by us. Let our intellect be purified by our thoughts on you in every birth.”

## \|\| 6.10.34 \|\|

*ityevaṃ vibruvaṃtaste dānavāstena vahninā \|*  
*śivājñayādbhutaṃ dagdhā bhasmasādabhavanmune \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. O sage, at the bidding of Śiva, those Asuras were burnt and reduced to ashes by the fire even as they were muttering thus.

## \|\| 6.10.35 \|\|

*anye'pi bālā vṛddhāśca dānavāstena vahninā \|*  
*śivājñayā drutaṃ vyāsa nirdagdhā bhasmasātkṛtāḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Other Asuras too, children and old men were completely burnt out, O Vyāsa, at the bidding of Śiva and speedily reduced to ashes.

## \|\| 6.10.36 \|\|

*striyo vā puruṣā vāpi vāhanāni ca tatra ye \|*  
*sarve tenāgninā dagdhāḥ kalpānte tu jagadyathā \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Just as the universe is burnt at the end of a Kalpa so also every thing and every one there, whether woman or man or vehicles, was reduced to ashes by that fire.

## \|\| 6.10.37 \|\|

*bhartṝnkaṃṭhagatānhitvā kāściddagdhā varastriyaḥ \|*  
*kāścitsuptāḥ pramattāśca ratiśrāṃtāśca yoṣitaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Some women were forced to leave their husbands necking them and were burnt by the fire. Some were sleeping, some were intoxicated and some were exhausted after their sexual dalliance. All were burnt.

## \|\| 6.10.38-39 \|\|

*arddhadagdhā vibuddhāśca babhramurmohamūrcchitāḥ \|*  
*tena nāsītsusūkṣmo'pi ghoratripuravahninā \|\| 38 \|\|*

*avidagdho vinirmuktaḥ sthāvaro jaṃgamopi vā \|*  
*varjayitvā mayaṃ daityaṃ viśvakarmāṇamavyayam \|\| 39 \|\|*

38-39. Some who were partially burnt woke up and rushed here and there. They fell unconscious and fainted. There was not even a minute particle whether mobile or immobile which escaped unscathed by that terrible Tripura fire excepting Maya, the imperishable Viśvakarman of the Asuras.

## \|\| 6.10.40 \|\|

*aviruddhaṃ tu devānāṃ rakṣitaṃ śaṃbhutejasā \|*  
*vipatkālepi sadbhaktaṃ maheśaśaraṇāgatam \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Those who were not opposed to the Gods were saved by Śiva’s brilliance, those who devoutly sought refuge in lord Śiva at the time of adversity.

## \|\| 6.10.41 \|\|

*sannipāto hi yeṣāṃ no vidyate nāśakārakaḥ \|*  
*daityānāmanyasattvānāṃ bhāvābhāve kṛtākṛte \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Whether Asuras or other beings those whose collective activities were not destructive were saved; others of contrary activities were burnt in fire.

## \|\| 6.10.42 \|\|

*tasmādyatnassusaṃbhāvyaḥ sadbhiḥ kartavya eva hi \|*  
*garhaṇātkṣīyate loko na tatkarma samācaret \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Hence, all possible efforts shall be made by good men to avoid despicable activities whereby people waste away themselves.

## \|\| 6.10.43 \|\|

*na saṃyogo yathā teṣāṃ bhūyāttripuravāsinām \|*  
*matametaddhi sarveṣāṃ daivādyadi yato bhavet \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Let there be no predicament to any as it happened in regard to the residents of the three cities. This is the opinion of all. By chance if it happens, let it.

## \|\| 6.10.44 \|\|

*ye pūjayaṃtastatrāpi daityā rudraṃ sabāṃdhavāḥ \|*  
*gāṇapatyaṃ yayussarve śivapūjāvi dherbalāt \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Those who worshipped Śiva along with their family attained Gaṇapati’s region, thanks to the worship of Siva.

Notes on the Burning of Tripura:

The Purāṇas accord different versions of the burning of Tripurī. The present version is a regular legend based on an ancient tradition. There is however another version which describes graphically the devastation, oppression and barbarities practiced by the Gaṇas which remind us of those perpetrated by the Hūṇa-chief Mihirakula in his invasions There is a veiled allusion to this event, for Agni is addressed as a Mleccha (Matsya p. I88. 51). There is no such anachronism in the ŚP account of Tripuradāha.

## Chapter 11 - The Gods’ prayer

## \|\| 6.11.1 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*brahmaputra mahāprājña dhanyastvaṃ śaivasattama \|*  
*kimakārṣustato devā dagdhe ca tripure'khilāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:—

1\. O son of Brahmā, of great intellect, O most excellent among the devotees of Śiva, you are blessed. When the three cities were burnt what did the gods do?

## \|\| 6.11.2 \|\|

*mayaḥ kutra gato dagdho patayaḥ kutra te gatāḥ \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ me samācakṣva yadi śaṃbhukathāśrayam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Where did Maya who was spared go? Where did the ascetics go? Please narrate all, if it relates to Śiva’s story.

## \|\| 6.11.3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya vyāsavākyaṃ bhagavānbhavakṛtsutaḥ \|*  
*sanatkumāraḥ provāca śivapādayugaṃ smaran \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sūta said:—

3\. On hearing the words of Vyāsa, Sanatkumāra the holy son of the creator remembered the feet of Śiva and spoke.

## \|\| 6.11.4 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu vyāsa mahābuddhe pārāśaryaṃ maheśituḥ \|*  
*caritaṃ sarvapāpaghnaṃ lokalīlānusārariṇaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

4\. Listen O Vyāsa, son of Parāśara, and of great intellect, to the sin-destroying story of the great lord, who follows worldly conventions.

## \|\| 6.11.5 \|\|

*maheśvareṇa sarvasmiṃstripure daityasaṃkule \|*  
*dagdhe viśeṣatastatra vismitāste'bhavansurāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. When the three cities of Asuras were utterly burnt, the Gods became surprised.

## \|\| 6.11.6 \|\|

*na kiṃcidabruvandevāḥ sendropeṃdrādayastadā \|*  
*mahātejasvinaṃ rudraṃ sarve vīkṣya sasaṃbhramāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The gods including Indra, Viṣṇu and others became silent and bewildered on seeing the excessively brilliant Siva.

## \|\| 6.11.7-8 \|\|

*mahābhayaṃkaraṃ raudraṃ prajvalaṃtaṃ diśo daśa \|*  
*koṭisūryapratīkāśaṃ pralayānalasannibham \|\| 7 \|\|*

*bhayāddevaṃ nirīkṣyaiva devīṃ ca himavatsutām \|*  
*bibhyire nikhilā devapramukhā stasthurānatāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. On merely seeing the terrible form of Śiva, dazzling the ten quarters, resembling countless suns in refulgence and on a par with the fire at the hour of dissolution, and also the goddess Pārvatī, the daughter of Himavat, the illustrious gods stood humbly in their fright.

## \|\| 6.11.9 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvānīkaṃ tadā bhītaṃ devānāmṛṣipuṃgavāḥ \|*  
*na kiṃcidūcussaṃtasthuḥ praṇemuste samaṃtataḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. On seeing the army of the gods terrified, the excellent sages did not say anything. They stood all round and bowed.

## \|\| 6.11.10-11 \|\|

*atha brahmāpi saṃbhīto dṛṣṭvā rūpaṃ ca śāṃkaram \|*  
*tuṣṭāva tuṣṭahṛdayo devaissaha samāhitaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*viṣṇunā ca sabhītena devadevaṃ bhavaṃ haram \|*  
*tripurāriṃ sagirijaṃ bhaktādhīnaṃ maheśvaram \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. Then Brahmā too who was excessively afraid on seeing Śiva’s terrible form, was delighted at heart and fervently prayed along with the gods. Viṣṇu who was also afraid prayed to Śiva the lord of the Gods, the slayer of the Tripuras, who was accompanied by his consort Pārvatī, the lord who is subservient to his devotees.

## \|\| 6.11.12 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*devadeva mahādeva bhaktānugrahakāraka \|*  
*prasīda parameśāna sarva devahitaprada \|\| 12 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

12\. “O lord of the gods, O supreme lord, bestower of blessings to the devotees, be pleased, O bestower of wholesome blessings to all the gods.

## \|\| 6.11.13 \|\|

*prasīda jagatāṃ nātha prasīdānaṃdadāyaka \|*  
*prasīda śaṃkara svāmin prasīda parameśvara \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Be pleased, O lord of the worlds, be pleased. O bestower of bliss. Be pleased, O lord Śiva. Be pleased, O supreme lord.

## \|\| 6.11.14 \|\|

*oṃkārāya namastubhyamākāraparatāraka \|*  
*prasīda sarvadeveśa tripuraghna maheśvara \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Obeisance to you, of the form of Oṃkāra, O great lord who enable the devotees to cross the ocean of existence by your very form. Be pleased, O lord of gods, O destroyer of the Tripuras, O supreme lord.

## \|\| 6.11.15 \|\|

*nānāvācyāya devāya varaṇapriya śaṃkara \|*  
*aguṇāya namastubhyaṃ prakṛteḥ puruṣātpara \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. O Śiva, O favourite of your devotees. Obeisance to you, the lord of many names. Obeisance to you, free from attributes, O you who are greater than Prakṛti and Puruṣa.

## \|\| 6.11.16 \|\|

*nirvikārāya nityāya nityatṛptāya bhāsvate \|*  
*niraṃjanāya divyāya trigu ṇāya namo'stu te \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Obeisance to you, free from aberrations, the eternal, the ever satiated, the resplendent, the unsullied, the divine one of three attributes.

## \|\| 6.11.17 \|\|

*saguṇāya namastubhyaṃ svargeśāya namostu te \|*  
*sadāśivāya śāṃtāya maheśāya pinākine \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Obeisance to you, possessed of attributes. Obeisance to you, the lord of heaven. Obeisance to the calm, tridentbearing Śiva.

## \|\| 6.11.18 \|\|

*sarvajñāya śaraṇyāya sadyojātāya te namaḥ \|*  
*vāmadevāya rudrāya tadāpyapuruṣāya ca \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Obeisance to the omniscient, to one who is the refuge of all. Obeisance to you born in a trice. Obeisance to Vāmadeva, Rudra, the Puruṣa, accessible to the good.

## \|\| 6.11.19 \|\|

*aghorāya susevyāya bhaktādhīnāya te namaḥ \|*  
*īśānāya vareṇyāya bhaktānaṃdapradāyine \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Obeisance to Aghora, to one easily served. Obeisance to you, subservient to the devotees. Obeisance to īśāna, the most excellent, the bestower of bliss to his devotees.

## \|\| 6.11.20 \|\|

*rakṣarakṣa mahādeva bhītānnassakalāmarān \|*  
*dagdhvā ca tripuraṃ sarve kṛtārthā amarāḥ kṛ tāḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. O great lord, save, save us all the frightened gods. By burning the three cities, the gods have been satisfied and contented.”

## \|\| 6.11.21 \|\|

*stutvaivaṃ devatāssarvā namaskāraṃ pṛthakpṛthak \|*  
*cakruste paramaprītā brahmādyāstu sadāśivam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. After eulogising thus, the gods severally bowed to him. The delighted gods, Brahmā and others, bowed to lord Śiva.

## \|\| 6.11.22 \|\|

*atha brahmā svayaṃ devaṃ tripurāriṃ maheśvaram \|*  
*tuṣṭāva praṇato bhūtvā nataskaṃdhaḥ kṛtāṃjaliḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Then Brahmā himself eulogised lord Śiva the destroyer of the Tripuras after bowing to him with stooping shoulders and palms joined in reverence.

## \|\| 6.11.23 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|\| bhagavandevadeveśa tripurāntaka śaṃkara \|*  
*tvayi bhaktiḥ parā me'stu mahādevānapāyinī \|\| 23 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

23\. “O holy lord, lord of the gods, O slayer of the Tripuras, O Śiva, O great lord, let my devotion to you remain eternal.

## \|\| 6.11.24 \|\|

*sarvadā me'stu sārathyaṃ tava deveśa śaṃkara \|*  
*anukūlo bhava vibho sadā tvaṃ parameśvara \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. O Śiva, let me always remain your charioteer. O lord of the gods, O supreme lord, be favourable to me always.”

## \|\| 6.11.25 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*iti stutvā vidhiśśaṃbhuṃ bhaktavatsalamānataḥ \|*  
*virarāma nataskaṃdhaḥ kṛtāṃjalirudāradhīḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

25\. After thus eulogising Śiva who is favourably disposed to his devotees, with humility, the liberal hearted Brahmā stopped and stood there with stooping shoulders and palms joined in reverence.

## \|\| 6.11.26 \|\|

*janārdano'pi bhagavān namaskṛtya maheśvaram \|*  
*kṛtāṃjalipuṭo bhūtvā tuṣṭāva ca maheśvaram \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Lord Viṣṇu too bowed to lord Śiva. With palms joined in reverence, he eulogised lord Śiva.

## \|\| 6.11.27 \|\|

*viṣṇuruvāca \|\| devādhīśa maheśāna dīnabaṃdho kṛpākara \|*  
*prasīda parameśāna kṛpāṃ kuru natapriya \|\| 27 \|\|*

Viṣṇu said:—

27\. O overlord of the Gods, O great lord, O merciful one, O kinsman of the distressed. Be pleased, O supreme lord. Be merciful, O favourite of those who bow to you.

## \|\| 6.11.28 \|\|

*nirguṇāya namastubhyaṃ punaśca saguṇāya ca \|*  
*punaḥ prakṛtirūpāya punaśca puruṣāya ca \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Obeisance to you devoid of the attributes. Again obeisance to you possessed of attributes. Again obeisance to you of the form of Prakṛti and Puruṣa.

## \|\| 6.11.29 \|\|

*paścādguṇasvarūpāya nato viśvātmane namaḥ \|*  
*bhaktipriyāya śāṃtāya śivāya paramātmane \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Obeisance to you of the form of attributes. Obeisance to the soul of the universe. Obeisance to you who love devotion. Obeisance to Śiva the calm one, the great soul.

## \|\| 6.11.30 \|\|

*sadāśivāya rudrāya jagatāṃ pataye namaḥ \|*  
*tvayi bhaktirdṛḍhā me'dya varddhamānā bhavatviti \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Obeisance to Sadāśiva. Obeisance to Śiva, the lord of the worlds. Let my devotion to you steadily increase.

## \|\| 6.11.31 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityuktvā virarāmāsau śaivapravarasattamaḥ \|*  
*sarve devāḥ praṇamyocustatastaṃ parameśvaram \|\| 31 \|\|*

Samtkumāra said:—

31\. After saying this, lord Viṣṇu the most excellent of the great devotees of Śiva stopped. Then all the Gods bowed to him and spoke to lord Śiva.

## \|\| 6.11.32 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*devanātha mahādeva karuṇākara śaṃkara \|*  
*prasīda jagatāṃ nātha prasīda parameśvara \|\| 32 \|\|*

The gods said:—

32\. O lord of gods, O great god, O Śiva, the merciful. Be pleased O lord of the worlds. Be pleased O supreme lord.

## \|\| 6.11.33 \|\|

*prasīda sarvakartā tvaṃ namāmastvāṃ vayaṃ mudā \|*  
*bhaktirdṛḍhāsmākaṃ nityaṃ syādanapāyinī \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Be pleased. You are the creator of every thing. We bow to you joyously. Let our devotion to you be steady and endless.

## \|\| 6.11.34 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*iti stutaśca deveśo brahmaṇā hariṇāmaraiḥ \|*  
*pratyuvāca prasannātmā śaṃkaro lokaśaṃkaraḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

34\. Thus eulogised by Brahmā, Viṣṇu and the Gods, Śiva the benefactor of the worlds, the delighted lord of the gods, replied.

## \|\| 6.11.35 \|\|

*śaṃkara uvāca \|*  
*he vidhe he hare devāḥ prasanno'smi viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*mano'bhilaṣitaṃ brūta varaṃ sarve vicā rataḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

Śiva said:—

35\. O Brahmā, O Viṣṇu, O gods, I am very much pleased with you all. All of you consider carefully and then let me know the boon you desire.

## \|\| 6.11.36 \|\|

*sanatkumāraḥ uvāca \|*  
*ityuktaṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā hareṇa munisattama \|*  
*pratyūcussarvadevāśca prasannenāntarātmanā \|\| 36 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

36\. On hearing these words mentioned by Śiva, O excellent sage, all the Gods replied delightedly.

## \|\| 6.11.31-38 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityuktvā virarāmāsau śaivapravarasattamaḥ \|*  
*sarve devāḥ praṇamyocustatastaṃ parameśvaram \|\| 31 \|\|*

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*devanātha mahādeva karuṇākara śaṃkara \|*  
*prasīda jagatāṃ nātha prasīda parameśvara \|\| 32 \|\|*

*prasīda sarvakartā tvaṃ namāmastvāṃ vayaṃ mudā \|*  
*bhaktirdṛḍhāsmākaṃ nityaṃ syādanapāyinī \|\| 33 \|\|*

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*iti stutaśca deveśo brahmaṇā hariṇāmaraiḥ \|*  
*pratyuvāca prasannātmā śaṃkaro lokaśaṃkaraḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*śaṃkara uvāca \|*  
*he vidhe he hare devāḥ prasanno'smi viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*mano'bhilaṣitaṃ brūta varaṃ sarve vicā rataḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*sanatkumāraḥ uvāca \|*  
*ityuktaṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā hareṇa munisattama \|*  
*pratyūcussarvadevāśca prasannenāntarātmanā \|\| 36 \|\|*

*sarve devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*yadi prasanno bhagavanyadi deyo varastvayā \|*  
*devadeveśa cāsmabhyaṃ jñātvā dāsānhi nassurān \|\| 37 \|\|*

*yadā duḥkhaṃ tu devānāṃ saṃbhaveddevasattama \|*  
*tadā tvaṃ prakaṭo bhūtvā duḥkhaṃ nāśaya sarvadā \|\| 38 \|\|*

The gods said:—

31-38. O lord, if you are pleased, if the boon is to be granted by you to us, O lord of the master of gods, after knowing that we the gods are your slaves, then O most excellent deity, be pleased to appear always whenever misery befalls us and destroy the misery.

## \|\| 6.11.39 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityukto bhagavānudro brahmaṇā hariṇāmaraiḥ \|*  
*yugapatprāha tuṣṭātmā tathetyastu niraṃtaram \|\| 39 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

39\. Thus requested simultaneously by Brahmā, Viṣṇu and the gods, Rudra was pleased in his mind and he said “Let it be ever so.

## \|\| 6.11.40 \|\|

*stavairetaiśca tuṣṭo'smi dāsyāmi sarvadā dhruvam \|*  
*yadabhīṣṭatamaṃ loke paṭhatāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ surāḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. I am delighted by these hymns. O gods, I shall confer on those who read, recite and hear these hymns whatever they crave for”.

## \|\| 6.11.41 \|\|

*ityuktvā śaṃkaraḥ prīto devaduḥkhaharassadā \|*  
*sarvadevapriyaṃ yadvai tatsarvaṃ ca pradattavān \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Saying this, the delighted Śiva the remover of the distress of gods, gave them every thing that was highly delightful to all the gods.

## Chapter 12 - The Gods go back to their abodes

## \|\| 6.12.1 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*etasminnaṃtare śaṃbhuṃ prasannaṃ vīkṣya dānavaḥ \|*  
*tatrājagāma suprīto mayo'dagdhaḥ kṛpābalāt \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

1\. In the meantime the Asura Maya who was not burnt due to the strength of grace, came there on seeing Śiva delighted.

## \|\| 6.12.2 \|\|

*praṇanāma haraṃ prītyā surānanyānapi dhruvam \|*  
*kṛtāṃjalirnataskaṃdhaḥ praṇanāma puna śśivam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. With great delight he bowed to Śiva and other gods. With palms joined in reverence and with stooping shoulders he bowed to Śiva again.

## \|\| 6.12.3 \|\|

*athotthāya śivaṃ dṛṣṭvā premṇā gadgadasusvaraḥ \|*  
*tuṣṭāva bhaktipūrṇātmā sa dānavavaro mayaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Then he got up. Maya the foremost among the Asuras, with his mind full of devotion and voice choked with emotions of love he eulogised facing Śiva.

## \|\| 6.12.4 \|\|

*maya uvāca \|\| devadeva mahādeva bhaktavatsala śaṃkaraḥ \|*  
*kalpavṛkṣasvarūposi sarvapakṣavivarjitaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

Maya said:—

4\. O great lord, lord of the Gods and favourably disposed to your devotees, O Śiva, you are in the form of the wish-yielding Kalpa tree and devoid of special leaning to any side.

## \|\| 6.12.5 \|\|

*jyotīrūpo namastestu viśvarūpa namo'stu te \|*  
*namaḥ pūtātmane tubhyaṃ pāvanāya namonamaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Obeisance to you O splendour-formed, obeisance to you omniformed; obeisance to you, O sanctified soul; obeisance to you, O holy one.

## \|\| 6.12.6 \|\|

*citrarūpāya nityāya rūpātītāya te namaḥ \|*  
*divyarūpāya divyāya sudivyākṛtaye namaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Obeisance to you of variegated forms; to you, the eternal one; obeisance to you who extend beyond all forms. Obeisance to you of divine forms, shapes, and features.

## \|\| 6.12.7 \|\|

*namaḥ praṇatasarvārtināśakāya śivātmane \|*  
*kartre bhartre ca saṃhartre trilokānāṃ namonamaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Obeisance to the destroyer of the distress of those who bow to you; obeisance to the welfare-hearted; to the creator, sustainer and annihilator of the three worlds.

## \|\| 6.12.8 \|\|

*bhaktigamyāya bhaktānāṃ namastubhyaṃ kṛpā lave \|*  
*tapassatphaladātre te śivākāṃta śiveśvara \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. O Śiva, O consort of Pārvatī, obeisance to you who are accessible through devotion of the devotees; obeisance to the compassionate and the bestower of the good fruits of penance.

## \|\| 6.12.9 \|\|

*na jānāmi stutiṃ kartuṃ stutipriya pareśvara \|*  
*prasanno bhava sarveśa pāhi māṃ śaraṇāga tam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. O great lord, fond of eulogy, I know not how to eulogise you. O lord of all, be pleased. Save me who have sought refuge in you.”

## \|\| 6.12.10 \|\|

*\|\| sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya mayoktā hi saṃstutiṃ parameśvaraḥ \|*  
*prasanno'bhūddvijaśreṣṭha mayaṃ provāca cādarāt \|\| 10 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

10\. On hearing this eulogy of Maya, O excellent brahmin, lord Śiva, was delighted and he spoke to Maya eagerly.

## \|\| 6.12.11 \|\|

*\|\| śiva uvāca \|*  
*varaṃ brūhi prasanno'haṃ maya dānavasattama \|*  
*mano'bhilaṣitaṃ yatte taddāsyāmi na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

Śiva said:—

11\. O Maya, I am delighted. O excellent Asura speak out the boon you wish to have. There is no doubt. I shall grant you what you desire.

## \|\| 6.12.12 \|\|

*\|\| sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*śrutvā śivaṃ vacaśśaṃbhossa mayo dānavarṣabhaḥ \|*  
*pratyuvāca prabhuṃ natvā nataskaṃdhaḥ kṛtāṃjaliḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

12\. On hearing the auspicious words of Śiva, Maya the foremost among the Asuras spoke after bowing to the lord with stooping shoulders and palms joined in reverence.

## \|\| 6.12.13 \|\|

*maya uvāca \|*  
*devadeva mahādeva prasanno yadi me bhavān \|*  
*varayogyo'smyahaṃ ceddhi svabhaktiṃ dehi śāśvatīm \|\| 13 \|\|*

Maya said:—

13\. “O great lord, lord of the Gods, if you are delighted and if I deserve the grant of a boon please grant me parmanent devotion to you.

## \|\| 6.12.14 \|\|

*svabhakteṣu sadā sakhyaṃ dīneṣu ca dayāṃ sadā \|*  
*upekṣāmanyajīveṣu khaleṣu parameśvara \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. O supreme lord, grant me comradeship with your devotees for ever, compassion towards the distressed and indifference towards the wicked living beings.

## \|\| 6.12.15 \|\|

*kadāpi nāsuro bhāvo bhavenmama maheśvara \|*  
*nirbhayaḥ syāṃ sadā nātha magnastvadbhajane śubhe \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. O lord Śiva, let there be no demonaic instinct in me at any time. O lord, let me be fearless for ever engrossed in your auspicious worship.”

## \|\| 6.12.16 \|\|

*\|\| sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*iti saṃprārthyamānastu śaṃkaraḥ parameśvaraḥ \|*  
*pratyuvāca maye nātha prasanno bhaktavatsalaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

16\. On being thus requested, Śiva the great lord, who is favourably disposed to his devotees and was in a delightful mood replied to Maya.

## \|\| 6.12.17 \|\|

*maheśvara uvāca \|*  
*dānavarṣabha dhanyastvaṃ madbhakto nirvikāravān \|*  
*pradattāste varāssarve'bhīpsitā ye tavādhunā \|\| 17 \|\|*

Lord Śiva said:—

17\. O excellent Asuras you are my devotees and are blessed. You are free from aberrations. All the boons desired by you are granted now.

## \|\| 6.12.18 \|\|

*gaccha tvaṃ vitalaṃ lokaṃ ramaṇīyaṃ divo'pi hi \|*  
*sametaḥ parivāreṇa nijena mama śāsanāt \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. At my bidding, you go to the region Vitala, more beautiful than heaven. Go in the company of your family and kinsmen.

## \|\| 6.12.19 \|\|

*nirbhayastatra saṃtiṣṭha saṃhṛṣṭo bhaktimānsadā \|*  
*kadāpi nāsuro bhāvo bhaviṣyati madājñayā \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. You stay there without fear. Be devout always. At my bidding you will never have demonaic instinct.

## \|\| 6.12.20 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityājñāṃ śirasādhāya śaṃkarasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*taṃ praṇamya surāṃścāpi vitalaṃ prajagāma saḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

20\. Receiving this behest of Śiva, the great soul with bowing head and paying homage to him and to the gods he went to Vitala.

## \|\| 6.12.21 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare te vai muṇḍinaśca samāgatāḥ \|*  
*praṇamyocuśca tānsarvānviṣṇubrahmādikān surān \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. In the meantime those heretics of tonsured heads came there, knelt before Viṣṇu, Brahmā and others and spoke.

## \|\| 6.12.22 \|\|

*kutra yāma vayaṃ devāḥ karma kiṃ karavāmahe \|*  
*ājñāpayata naśśīghraṃ bhava dādeśakārakān \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. O gods, where shall we go? What shall we do now? We are ready to carry out your behests. Please command us quickly.

## \|\| 6.12.23 \|\|

*kṛtaṃ duṣkarma cāsmābhirhe hare he vidhe surāḥ \|*  
*daityānāṃ śivabhaktānāṃ śivabhaktirvināśitā \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. O Viṣṇu, O Brahmā, O gods, wicked deeds have been performed by us. We have destroyed the devotion to Śiva of all the Asuras who were great devotees of Śiva.

## \|\| 6.12.24 \|\|

*koṭikalpāni narake no vāsastu bhaviṣyati \|*  
*noddhāro bhavitā nūnaṃ śivabhaktavirodhinām \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. We will have to stay in hell for a countless Kalpas. Certainly there is no redemption for us that have offended devotees of Śiva.

## \|\| 6.12.25 \|\|

*parantu bhavadicchāta idaṃ duṣkarma naḥ kṛtam \|*  
*tacchāṃtiṃ kṛpayā brūta vayaṃ vaśśaraṇāgatāḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. But it was in accordance with your desire that this wicked deed was perpetrated. Please tell us the mode of atoning for the same. We have sought refuge in you.

## \|\| 6.12.26 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*teṣāṃ tadvacanaṃ śrutvā viṣṇubrahmādayassurāḥ \|*  
*abru vanmuṃḍinastāṃste sthitānagre kṛtāṃjalīn \|\| 26 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

26\. On hearing their words Viṣṇu, Brahmā and other gods spoke to the tonsured-heads who stood in front with joined palms.

## \|\| 6.12.27 \|\|

*viṣṇvādaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*na bhetavyaṃ bhavadbhistu muṃḍino vai kadācana \|*  
*śivājñayedaṃ sakalaṃ jātaṃ caritamuttamam \|\| 27 \|\|*

Viṣṇu and others said:—

27\. “O tonsured ones, you need not be afraid at all. These excellent activities have taken place at the bidding of Śiva.

## \|\| 6.12.28 \|\|

*yuṣmākaṃ bhavitā naiva kugatirduḥkhadāyinī \|*  
*śivavāsā yato yūyaṃ devarṣihitakārakāḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Since you are the servants of Śiva and have carried out the activities conducive to the welfare of the gods and the sages, no mishap shall ever befall you bringing you to distress.

## \|\| 6.12.29 \|\|

*surarṣihitakṛcchaṃbhussurarṣihitakṛtpriyaḥ \|*  
*surarṣihitakṛnnṝṇāṃ kadāpi kugatirnahi \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Śiva performs deeds conducive to the welfare of the gods and the sages. He is pleased with those who work for the welfare of the gods and sages. No mishap befalls those who work for the welfare of the gods and sages.

## \|\| 6.12.30 \|\|

*adyato matametaṃ hi praviṣṭānāṃ nṛṇāṃ kalau \|*  
*kugatirbhavitā brūmaḥ satyaṃ naivātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. From now onwards in the Kali age those who follow this cult will be faced with disastrous results. We tell you the truth. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 6.12.31 \|\|

*bhavadbhirmuṃḍino dhīrā guptabhāvānmamājñayā \|*  
*tāvanmarusthalī sevyā kaliryāvātsamāvrajet \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. O brave tonsured heads, till the advent of the Kali age, you shall stay incognito in the desert region. That is my behest.

## \|\| 6.12.32 \|\|

*āgate ca kalau yūyaṃ svamataṃ sthāpayiṣyatha \|*  
*kalau tu mohitā mūḍhāssaṃgrahīṣyaṃti vo matam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. When the Kali age begins, you can propagate your cult. In the Kali age deluded fools will follow your cult.

## \|\| 6.12.33 \|\|

*ityājñaptāḥ sureśaiśca muṃḍinaste munīśvara \|*  
*namaskṛtya gatāstatra yathoddiṣṭaṃ svamāśramam \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Thus bidden by the great gods, O great sage, the tonsured heads bowed to them and went to their allotted abode.

## \|\| 6.12.34-35 \|\|

*tatassa bhagavānrudro dagdhvā tripuravāsinaḥ \|*  
*kṛtakṛtyo mahāyogī brahmādyairabhipūjitaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*svagaṇairnikhilairdevyā śivayā sahitaḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*kṛtvāmaramahatkāryaṃ sasutoṃtaradhādatha \|\| 35 \|\|*

34-35. Then lord Śiva, the great Yogin after burning the residents of the three cities felt contented. He was duly worshipped by Brahmā and others. Then the lord, after completing the task of the gods, vanished from the scene accompanied by his Gaṇas, goddess Pārvatī and the sons.

## \|\| 6.12.36 \|\|

*tataścāṃtarhite deve parivārānvite śive \|*  
*dhanuśśarasthādyaśca prākāroṃtarddhimāgamat \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. When lord Śiva had vanished with his followers, the fortress too vanished along with the bow, arrows, chariot and other things.

## \|\| 6.12.37-38 \|\|

*tato brahmā harirdevā munigaṃdharvakinnarāḥ \|*  
*nāgāssarpāścāpsarasassaṃhṛṣṭāścātha mānuṣāḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*svaṃsvaṃ sthānaṃ mudā jagmuśśaṃsaṃtaḥ śāṃkaraṃ yaśaḥ \|*  
*svaṃsvaṃ sthānamanuprāpya nivṛtiṃ paramāṃ yayuḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

37-38. Then Brahmā, Viṣṇu, the gods, sages, Gandharvas, Kinnaras, Nāgas, serpents, celestial damsels and the delighted men went to their abodes praising the glory of Śiva. After reaching their abodes they were highly delighted.

## \|\| 6.12.39 \|\|

*etatte kathitaṃ sarvaṃ caritaṃ śaśimaulinaḥ \|*  
*tripurakṣayasaṃsūci paralīlānvitaṃ mahat \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Thus the exalted narrative of the moon-crested lord indicative of the annihilation of Tripuras coupled with the great divine sports has been narrated to you.

## \|\| 6.12.40 \|\|

*dhanyaṃ yaśasyamāyuṣyaṃ dhanadhānyapravarddhakam \|*  
*svargadaṃ mokṣadaṃ cāpi kiṃ bhūyaḥ śrotumicchasi \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. It is conducive to wealth, fame, and longevity. It increases prosperity and possession of food-grains. It yields heavenly pleasure and salvation. What else do you wish to hear?

## \|\| 6.12.41 \|\|

*idaṃ hi paramākhyānaṃ yaḥ paṭhecchraṇuyātsadā \|*  
*iha bhuktvākhilānkāmānaṃte muktimavāpnuyāt \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. He who reads and hears the exalted narrative will enjoy all pleasures here and attain salvation hereafter.

## Chapter 13 - Resuscitation of Indra in the context of the destruction of Jalandhara

## \|\| 6.13.1 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*bho brahmanbhagavanpūrvaṃ śrutaṃ me brahmaputraka \|*  
*jalaṃdharaṃ mahādaityamavadhīcchaṃkaraḥ prabhuḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:—

1\. O holy lord, son of Brahmā, it has been heard by me before that the lord Śiva killed the great Asura Jalandhara.

## \|\| 6.13.2 \|\|

*tattvaṃ vada mahāprājña caritaṃ śaśimaulinaḥ \|*  
*vistārapūrvakaṃ śṛṇvankastṛpyettadyaśo'malam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. O intelligent one, please narrate the story of the moon-crested lord in detail. Who can be satiated with listening to the spotless glory of the lord?

## \|\| 6.13.3 \|\|

*\|\| sūta uvāca \|*  
*ityevaṃ vyāsasaṃpṛṣṭo brahmaputro mahāmuniḥ \|*  
*uvācārthavadavyagraṃ vākyaṃ vākyaviśāradaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sūta said:—

3\. On being requested thus by Vyāsa, the great sage and son of Brahmā of eloquent speech spoke the following significant words without excitement.

## \|\| 6.13.4 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ekadā jīvaśakrau ca bhaktyā paramayā mune \|*  
*darśanaṃ kartumīśasya kailāsaṃ jagmaturbhṛśam \|\| 4 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

4\. O sage, once Bṛhaspati and Indra went to Kailāsa with great devotion, to see lord Śiva.

## \|\| 6.13.5-6 \|\|

*atha gurvindrayorjñātvāgamanaṃ śaṃkaraḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*parīkṣituṃ tayorjñānaṃ svadarśanaratātmanoḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*digambaro'tha tanmārgamāruddhya sadgatissatām \|*  
*jaṭābaddhena śiraśātiṣṭhatsaṃśobhitānanaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. Coming to know of the arrival of Bṛhaspati and Indra eager to see him, lord Śiva wished to test their knowledge. Accordingly, the lord, the excellent goal of the good, stood blocking their path in the naked form with matted hair and beaming face.

## \|\| 6.13.7-9 \|\|

*atha tau guruśakrau ca kurvaṃtau gamanaṃ mudā \|*  
*ālokya puruṣaṃ bhīmaṃ mārgamadhye'dbhutākṛtim \|\| 7 \|\|*

*mahātejasvinaṃ śāṃtaṃ jaṭāsaṃbaddhamastakam \|*  
*mahābāhuṃ mahoraskaṃ gauraṃ nayanabhīṣaṇam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*atho puraṃdaro'pṛcchatsvādhikāreṇa durmadaḥ \|*  
*puruṣaṃ taṃ svamārgāṃtasthitamajñāya śaṃkaram \|\| 9 \|\|*

7-9. Bṛhaspati and Indra were walking on gleefully. On their way they saw this wonderful person of huge size. He was quiet and composed and very refulgent with matted hair on his head. He was fair-complexioned with long arms and wide chest. He was terrible to look at. Without realising that the person who stood there blocking their path was Śiva himself, Indra who was proud of his authority said to him.

## \|\| 6.13.10 \|\|

*purandara uvāca \|*  
*kastvaṃ bhoḥ kuta āyātaḥ kiṃ nāma vada tattvataḥ \|*  
*svasthānesaṃsthitaśśaṃbhu kiṃ vānyatra gataḥ prabhuḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

Indra said:—

10\. O, who are you? Where have you come from? What is your name? Tell me truly. Is the lord Śiva in his apartment or has he gone anywhere?

## \|\| 6.13.11 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*śakreṇetthaṃ sa pṛṣṭastu kiṃcinnovāca tāpasaḥ \|*  
*śakraḥ punarapṛcchadvai novāca sa digaṃbaraḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

11\. O sage, on being asked by Indra thus, he did not say anything. Indra asked him again. But the naked person did not say anything.

## \|\| 6.13.12 \|\|

*punaḥ puraṃdaro'pṛcchllokānāmadhipeśvaraḥ \|*  
*tūṣṇīmāsa mahāyogī līlārūpadharaḥ prabhuḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Indra, the supreme lord of the worlds, asked again. The lord the great Yogin who assumes forms variously kept quiet.

## \|\| 6.13.13 \|\|

*itthaṃ punaḥ punaḥ pṛṣṭaśśakreṇa sa digambaraḥ \|*  
*novāca kiṃcidbhagavāñchakrajñānaparīkṣayā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The naked lord, though asked repeatedly by Indra, did not say anything, for he wanted to test the knowledge of Indra.

## \|\| 6.13.14 \|\|

*atha cukrodha deveśastrailokyaiśvaryagarvitaḥ \|*  
*uvāca vacanaṃ caiva taṃ nirbhartsya jaṭādharam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Then the lord of Gods, proud of the wealth of the three worlds, became enraged. Rebuking the lord with matted hair he spoke these words.

## \|\| 6.13.15 \|\|

*\|\| indra uvāca \|*  
*re mayā pṛcchyamāno'pi nottaraṃ dattavānasi \|*  
*atastvāṃ hanmi vajreṇa kaste trātāsti durmate \|\| 15 \|\|*

Indra said:—

15\. “O evil-minded one, though asked you did not reply to me. Hence I am going to kill you with my thunderbolt. Who can save you?”

## \|\| 6.13.16 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityudīrya tato vajrī saṃnirīkṣya krudhā hi tam \|*  
*haṃtuṃ digaṃbaraṃ vajramudyataṃ sa cakāra ha \|\| 16 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

16\. After saying this and looking at him ferociously Indra raised his thunderbolt in order to kill him.

## \|\| 6.13.17 \|\|

*puraṃdaraṃ vajrahastaṃ dṛṣṭvā devassadāśivaḥ \|*  
*cakāra staṃbhanaṃ tasya vajrapātasya śaṃkaraḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. On seeing Indra lifting up his thunderbolt, Śiva prevented the fall of the thunderbolt by making his hand benumbed.

## \|\| 6.13.18 \|\|

*tato rudraḥ krudhāviṣṭaḥ karālākṣo bhayaṃkaraḥ \|*  
*drutameva prajajvāla tejasā pradahanniva \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Then Śiva became furious. His eyes became terrible. He blazed with his burning splendour.

## \|\| 6.13.19 \|\|

*bāhupratiṣṭaṃbhabhuvāmanyunāṃtaśśacīpatiḥ \|*  
*samadahyata bhogīva maṃtraruddhaparākramaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Then Indra burnt within himself by the benumbing of his arm like a serpent whose exploits had been curbed by pronouncing magical formulas.

## \|\| 6.13.20 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā bṛhaspatistūrṇaṃ prajvalaṃtaṃ svatejasā \|*  
*puruṣaṃ taṃ dhiyā jñātvā praṇanāma haraṃ prabhum \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. On seeing him resplendent, Bṛhaspati realised immediately that he was lord Śiva himself and bowed to him.

## \|\| 6.13.21 \|\|

*kṛtāṃjalipuṭo bhūtvā tato gururudāradhīḥ \|*  
*natvā ca daṃḍavadbhūmau prabhuṃ stotuṃ pracakrame \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Then the noble-minded Bṛhaspati joined his palms in reverence. He prostrated before him on the ground and began to eulogise the lord.

## \|\| 6.13.22 \|\|

*gururuvāca \|*  
*namo devādhidevāya mahādevāya cātmane \|*  
*maheśvarāya prabhave tryambakāya kapardine \|\| 22 \|\|*

Bṛhaspati said:—

22\. Obeisance to Śiva, the chief lord of the gods, the supreme soul, the three-eyed, possessed of matted hair.

## \|\| 6.13.23 \|\|

*dīnanāthāya vibhave namoṃ'dhakaniṣūdine \|*  
*tripuraghnāya śarvāya brahmaṇe parameṣṭhine \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Obeisance to the succouring lord of the distressed, the destroyer of Andhaka and the Tripuras, and identical with Brahmā, the Parameṣṭhin.

## \|\| 6.13.24 \|\|

*virūpākṣāya rudrāya bahurūpāya śaṃbhave \|*  
*virūpāyātirūpāya rūpātītāya te namaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Obeisance to Śiva of odd eyes, of diverse, deformed and surpassing features, going beyond all forms.

## \|\| 6.13.25 \|\|

*yajñavidhvaṃsakartre ca yajñānāṃ phaladāyine \|*  
*namaste makharūpāya parakarmapravartine \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Obeisance to the destroyer of sacrifice of Dakṣa, to the bestower of fruits of sacrifice, identical with sacrifice and the initiator of the greatest rites.

## \|\| 6.13.26 \|\|

*kālāṃtakāya kālāya kālabhogidharāya ca \|*  
*namaste parameśāya sarvatra vyāpine namaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Obeisance to Śiva the annihilator of Time, of the form of Time, the wearer of black serpents, the great lord and the omnipresent.

## \|\| 6.13.27 \|\|

*namo brahmaśirohaṃtre brahmacaṃdra stutāya ca \|*  
*brahmaṇyāya namaste'stu namaste paramātmane \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Obeisance to the destroyer of Brahmā’s head, the one eulogised by Brahmā and the moon. Obeisance to you favourably disposed to Brahmins. Obeisance to you the great soul.

## \|\| 6.13.28 \|\|

*tvamagniranilo vyoma tvamevāpo vasuṃdharā \|*  
*tvaṃ sūryaścandramā bhāni jyotiścakraṃ tvameva hi \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. You are the fire, the wind, the ether, the waters, the earth, the sun, the moon, the stars, and the solar system.

## \|\| 6.13.29 \|\|

*tvameva viṣṇustvaṃ brahmā tatstutastvaṃ pareśvaraḥ \|*  
*munayaḥ sanakādyāstvaṃ nāradastvaṃ tapodhanaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. You alone are Viṣṇu, Brahmā, and eulogised by them; you are the great lord, the sages Sanaka etc. You are Nārada the great saint.

## \|\| 6.13.30 \|\|

*tvameva sarva lokeśastvameva jagadātmakaḥ \|*  
*sarvānvayassarvabhinnastvameva prakṛteḥ paraḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. You alone are the lord of all the worlds, the soul of the universe. You are converging in everything and different from everything; you alone are greater than Prakṛti.

## \|\| 6.13.31 \|\|

*tvaṃ vai sṛjasi lokāṃśca rajasā vidhināmabhāk \|*  
*sattvena harirūpastvaṃ sakalaṃ yāsi vai jagat \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. With the Rajas attribute you alone create the worlds assuming the name Brahma. You are identical with Viṣṇu in Sattva attribute and you protect the entire universe.

## \|\| 6.13.32 \|\|

*tvamevāsi mahādeva tamasā hararūpadhṛk \|*  
*līlayā bhuvanaṃ sarvaṃ nikhilaṃ pāṃcabhautikam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. With the Tamas attribute you assume the form of Śiva, O great God and you alone devour the universe composed of five elements.

## \|\| 6.13.33 \|\|

*tvaddhyānabalatassūryastapate viśvabhāvana \|*  
*amṛtaṃ cyavate loke śaśī vāti samariṇaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. With the strength of meditating on you, O creator of the universe, the sun blazes, the moon exudes nectar and the wind blows.

## \|\| 6.13.34 \|\|

*tvaddhyānabalato meghāścāṃbu varṣaṃti śaṃkara \|*  
*tvaddhyānabalataśśakrastrilokīṃ pāti putravat \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. O Śiva, with the strength of meditating on you, the clouds shower water. Indra protects the worlds like his sons.

## \|\| 6.13.35 \|\|

*tvaddhyānabalato meghāḥ sarve devā munīśvarāḥ \|*  
*svādhikāraṃ ca kurvaṃti cakitā bhavato bhayāt \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. With the strength of meditating on you, the clouds, the gods and the great sages carry on their tasks. They are afraid of you.

## \|\| 6.13.36 \|\|

*tvatpādakamalasyaiva sevanādbhuvi mānavāḥ \|*  
*nādriyante surānruda lokaiśvaryaṃ ca bhuṃjate \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. O Śiva, by serving your lotus like feet, the people in the world do not honour the gods and they enjoy the prosperity of the world.

## \|\| 6.13.37 \|\|

*tvatpādakamalasyaiva sevanādagamanparām \|*  
*gatiṃ yogadhanā nāmapyagamyāṃ sarvadurlabhām \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. By serving your lotus like feet the people attain the supreme goal inaccessible to every one and unattainable even to Yogins.

## \|\| 6.13.38 \|\|

*\|\| sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*bṛhaspatiriti stutvā śaṃkaraṃ lokaśaṃkaram \|*  
*pādayo pātayāmāsa tasyeśasya puraṃdaram \|\| 38 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

38\. After eulogising Śiva, the benefactor of the worlds thus Bṛhaspati made Indra fall at the feet of Śiva.

## \|\| 6.13.39 \|\|

*pātayitvā ca deveśamiṃdraṃ nata śirodharam \|*  
*bṛhaspatiruvācedaṃ praśrayāvanataśśivam \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. After making Indra, lord of the gods, fall at his feet with bowed head, Bṛhaspati humbly spoke these words to Śiva with bowed head.

## \|\| 6.13.40 \|\|

*\|\| bṛhaspatiruvāca \|*  
*dīnanātha mahādeva praṇataṃ tava pādayoḥ \|*  
*samuddhara ca śāṃtaṃ svaṃ krodhaṃ nayanajaṃ kuru \|\| 40 \|\|*

Bṛhaspati said:—

40\. O great lord, favourable to the distressed, please raise up Indra fallen at your feet. Please quieten the anger rising from your eyes.

## \|\| 6.13.41 \|\|

*tuṣṭo bhava mahādeva pāhīdra śaraṇāgatam \|*  
*agnireva śamaṃ yātu bhālanetrasamudbhavaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. O great lord, be pleased. Protect Indra who has sought refuge in you. Let this fire rising from the eye in the forehead be rendered calm.

## \|\| 6.13.42 \|\|

*\|\| sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya gurorvākyaṃ devadevo maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*uvāca karuṇāsindhurmeghanirhrādayā girā \|\| 42 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

42\. On hearing these words of Bṛhaspati, Śiva, the lord of Gods, the ocean of mercy, spoke in a thundering stentorian voice.

## \|\| 6.13.43 \|\|

*maheśvara uvāca \|*  
*krodhaṃ ca nissṛte netrāddhārayāmi bṛhaspateḥ \|*  
*kathaṃ hi kañcukīṃ sarpassaṃdhatte nojjhitāṃ punaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

Lord Śiva said:—

43\. O Bṛhaspati, how can I take up the fury that has already come out of my eye? A serpent does not wear again the slough that has been cast off.

## \|\| 6.13.44 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvācu \|*  
*iti śrutvā vacastasya śaṃkarasya bṛhaspatiḥ \|*  
*uvāca kliṣṭarūpaśca bhayavyākulamānasaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

44\. On hearing these words of Śiva, Bṛhaspati’s mind was agitated with fear and he spoke dejectedly.

## \|\| 6.13.45 \|\|

*bṛhaspatiruvāca \|*  
*he deva bhagavanbhaktā anukaṃpyāḥ sadaiva hi \|*  
*bhaktavatsalanāmeti tvaṃ satyaṃ kuru śaṃkara \|\| 45 \|\|*

Bṛhaspati said:—

45\. O holy lord, indeed the devotees should be pitied always. O Śiva, thus please make your name Bhaktavatsala (favourably disposed towards the devotees) true.

## \|\| 6.13.46 \|\|

*kṣeptumanyatra deveśa svatejo'tyugramarhasi \|*  
*uddhartassarvabhaktānāṃ samuddhara puraṃdaram \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. O lord of gods, you deserve to cast elsewhere the fierce brilliance. O uplifter of all devotees, raise up Indra.

## \|\| 6.13.47 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityukto guruṇā rudro bhaktavatsalanāmabhāk \|*  
*pratyuvāca prasannātmā surejyaṃ praṇatārttihā \|\| 47 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

47\. On being addressed thus by Bṛhaspati the delighted Śiva, the destroyer of the distress of those who bow to him and the one named Bhaktavatsala replied thus to Bṛhaspati.

## \|\| 6.13.48 \|\|

*śiva uvāca \|*  
*prītaḥ stutyānayā tāta dadāmi varamuttamam \|*  
*indrasya jīvadānena jīveti tvaṃ prathāṃ vraja \|\| 48 \|\|*

Śiva said:—

48\. O dear one, I am delighted by your eulogy. I shall grant you the excellent boon. Henceforth you shall be famous as Enlivener because you have conferred life on Indra.

## \|\| 6.13.49 \|\|

*samudbhūto'nalo yo'yaṃ bhālanetrātsureśahā \|*  
*enaṃ tyakṣyāmyahaṃ dūraṃ yathendraṃ naiva pīḍayet \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. I shall cast off this fire born of my eye in the forehead intended to kill Indra lest it should afflict him.

## \|\| 6.13.50 \|\|

*\|\| sanatkumāra uvāc \|*  
*ityuktvā taṃ kare dhṛtvā svatejo'nalamadbhutam \|*  
*bhālanetrātsamudbhūtaṃ prākṣipallavaṇāṃbhasi \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. On saying this he held that wonderful brilliance born of the eye in the forehead and cast it off in the briny ocean.

## \|\| 6.13.51 \|\|

*tataścāṃtardadhe rudro mahālīlākaraḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*guruśakrau bhayānmuktau jagmatuḥ sukhamuttamam \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Then the lord Rudra of great divine sports vanished from the scene. Bṛhaspati and Indra were relieved of their fright and they became happy.

## \|\| 6.13.52 \|\|

*yadarthaṃ gamanodyuktau darśanaṃ prāpya tasya vai \|*  
*kṛtārthau guruśakrau hi svasthānaṃ jagmaturmudā \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. After having the immediate perception of Śiva for which they had come here, Bṛhaspati and Indra became contented and went away to their abodes joyously.

## Chapter 14 - The birth of Jalandhara and his marriage

## \|\| 6.14.1 \|\|

*\|\| vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*sanatkumāra sarvajña brahmaputra namostu te \|*  
*śruteyamadbhutā me'dya kathā śaṃbhormahātmanaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:—

1\. O omniscient Sanatkumāra, son of Brahmā, obeisance be to you. This wonderful story of Śiva, the great soul, has been heard.

## \|\| 6.14.2 \|\|

*kṣipte svatejasi brahmanbhālanetrasamudbhave \|*  
*lavaṇāṃbhasi kiṃ tātābhavattatra vadāśu tat \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. O sage, when the brilliance born of the eye in the forehead had been cast off into the briny ocean, O dear sir, what happened? Please narrate it quickly.

## \|\| 6.14.3 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu tāta mahāprājña śivalīlāṃ mahādbhutām \|*  
*yacchrutvā śraddhayā bhakto yogināṃ gatimāpnuyāt \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

3\. O dear one of great intellect, listen to the extremely wonderful sport of Śiva, on hearing which with faith a devotee attains the goal of Yogins.

## \|\| 6.14.4 \|\|

*atho śivasya tattejo bhālanetrasamudbhavam \|*  
*kṣiptaṃ ca lavaṇāmbhodhau sadyo bālatvamāpa ha \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The brilliance of Śiva born of the eye in the forehead and cast off into the briny sea immediately assumed the form of a boy.

## \|\| 6.14.5 \|\|

*tatra vai siṃdhugaṃgāyāḥ sāgarasya ca saṃgame \|*  
*rurodoccaissa vai bāla sarvaloka bhayaṃkaraḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. At the confluence of the river Gaṅgā and the ocean, the boy of terrific features cried loudly.

## \|\| 6.14.6 \|\|

*rudatastasya śabdena prākaṃpaddharaṇī muhuḥ \|*  
*svargaśca satyalokaśca tatsvanādbadhirīkṛtaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. At the sound of the crying boy, the earth quaked frequently. The heaven and the Satyaloka became deafened at the noise.

## \|\| 6.14.7 \|\|

*bālasya rodanenaiva sarve lokāśca tatrasuḥ \|*  
*sarvato lokapālāśca vihvalīkṛtamānasāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. All the worlds were frightened. The guardians of the quarters became agitated in the mind.

## \|\| 6.14.8 \|\|

*kiṃ bahūktena viprendra cacāla sacarācaram \|*  
*bhuvanaṃ nikhilaṃ tāta rodanāttacchiśorvibho \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. O dear holy one, O great brahmin, the entire world including the mobile and immobile quaked at the cries of the boy.

## \|\| 6.14.9 \|\|

*atha te vyākulāssarve devāssamunayo drutam \|*  
*pitāmahaṃ lokaguruṃ brahmāṇaṃ śaraṇaṃ yayuḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Then the distressed gods and the sages immediately sought refuge in Brahmā the grandfather and preceptor of the worlds.

## \|\| 6.14.10 \|\|

*tatra gatvā ca te devā sunayaśca savāsavāḥ \|*  
*praṇamya ca susaṃstutya procustaṃ parameṣṭhinam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. After going there, those sages and the gods including Indra bowed to and eulogised Brahmā and spoke these words.

## \|\| 6.14.11 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*lokādhīśa surādhīśa bhayannassamupasthitam \|*  
*tannāśaya mahāyogiñjātoyaṃ hyadbhuto ravaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

The gods said:—

11\. “This mysterious sound has arisen. O lord of worlds, O lord of gods, we are frightened. O great Yogin please quell it.”

## \|\| 6.14.12 \|\|

*\|\| sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya vacasteṣāṃ brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ \|*  
*gaṃtumaicchattatastatra kimetaditi vismitaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

12\. On hearing their words, Brahmā the grandfather of the worlds wished to go there. He was perplexed as to what it was.

## \|\| 6.14.13 \|\|

*tato brahmā suraistātāvataratsatyalokataḥ \|*  
*rasāṃ tajjñātumicchansa samudramagamattadā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Then Brahmā descended from Satyaloka to the Earth along with the gods. Then he went to the ocean desirous of knowing what it was.

## \|\| 6.14.14 \|\|

*yāvattatrāgato brahmā sarvalokapitāmahaḥ \|*  
*tāvatsamudrasyotsaṃge taṃ bālaṃ sa dadarśa ha \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. When Brahmā the grandfather of the worlds came there, he saw the boy in the lap of the ocean.

## \|\| 6.14.15 \|\|

*āgataṃ vidhimālokya devarūpyatha sāgaraḥ \|*  
*praṇamya śirasā bālaṃ tasyotsaṃge nyaveśayat \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. On seeing Brahmā coming, the ocean assuming the form of a god bowed to him and placed the boy in his lap.

## \|\| 6.14.16 \|\|

*tato brahmābravīdvākyaṃ sāgaraṃ vismayānvitaḥ \|*  
*jalarāśe drutaṃ brūhi kasyāyaṃ śiśuradbhutaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Then the surprised Brahmā spoke these words to the ocean—“O ocean, tell me quickly about the parentage of this boy.”

## \|\| 6.14.17 \|\|

*\|\| sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*brahmaṇo vākyamākarṇya muditassāgarastadā \|*  
*pratyuvāca prajeśaṃ sa natvā stutvā kṛtāṃjaliḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

17\. On hearing the words of Brahmā, the ocean was delighted. After bowing to and eulogising him with palms joined in reverence he replied to Prajāpati Brahmā.

## \|\| 6.14.18 \|\|

*samudra uvāca \|*  
*bho bho brahmanmayā prāpto bālako'yamajānatā \|*  
*prabhavaṃ siṃdhugaṃgāyāmakasmātsarvalokapa \|\| 18 \|\|*

The ocean said:—

18\. “O Brahmā, O lord of the worlds, this boy was suddenly seen in the confluence of the river Gaṅgā. I do not know about the origin of this boy.

## \|\| 6.14.19 \|\|

*jātakarmādisaṃskārānkuruṣvāsya jagadguro \|*  
*jātakoktaphalaṃ sarvaṃ vidhātarvaktumarhasi \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. O preceptor of the universe, you perform the postnatal rites for this boy. O creator, let me know your predictions about his future according to his horoscope”

## \|\| 6.14.20 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ vadati pāthodhau sa bālassāgarātmajaḥ \|*  
*brahmāṇamagrahītkaṇṭhe vidhunvaṃtaṃ muhurmuhuḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

20\. Even as the ocean said these words, the son of the ocean caught hold of the neck of Brahmā and shook it several times.

## \|\| 6.14.21 \|\|

*vidhūnanaṃ ca tasyaivaṃ sarvalokakṛto vidheḥ \|*  
*pīḍitasya ca kāleya netrābhyāmagamajjalam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. In due course tears came out of the eyes of Brahmā, the creator of all the worlds, afflicted by the joggling and jolting.

## \|\| 6.14.22 \|\|

*karābhyāmabdhijātasya tatsutasya mahaujasaḥ \|*  
*kathaṃcinmuktakaṇṭhastu brahmā provāca sādaram \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Brahmā somehow extricated himself from the grip of the son of the ocean by means of his hands and spoke to the ocean.

## \|\| 6.14.23 \|\|

*\|\| brahmovāca \|*  
*śṛṇu sāgara vakṣyāmi tavāsya tanayasya hi \|*  
*jātakoktaphalaṃ sarvaṃ samādhānarataḥ khalu \|\| 23 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

23\. “O ocean, listen, I shall narrate the future as predicted from the horoscope, entirely. Be attentive please.

## \|\| 6.14.24 \|\|

*netrābhyāṃ vidhṛtaṃ yasmādanenaiva jalaṃ mama \|*  
*tasmājjalaṃdharetīha khyāto nāmnā bhavatvasau \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Since he was able to make my eyes water let him be famous in the name of Jalandhara.

## \|\| 6.14.25-26 \|\|

*adhunaivaiṣa taruṇassarvaśāstrārthapāragaḥ \|*  
*mahāparākramo dhīro yoddhā ca raṇadurmadaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*bhaviṣyati ca gaṃbhīrastvaṃ yathā samare guhaḥ \|*  
*sarvajetā ca saṃgrāme sarvasaṃpadvirājitaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. He will become a youth now itself. He will become a master of all sacred lores, very valorous, courageous, heroic, invincible and majestic like you. Like Kārttikeya he will be the conqueror of all in battles. He will shine with all sorts of prosperity.

## \|\| 6.14.27 \|\|

*daityānāmadhipo bālaḥ sarveṣāṃ ca bhaviṣyati \|*  
*viṣṇorapi bhavejjetā na kuta ścitparābhavaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. This boy will become the emperor of Asuras. He will conquer even Viṣṇu. He will face defeat from no quarter.

## \|\| 6.14.28 \|\|

*avadhyassarvabhūtānāṃ vinā rudraṃ bhaviṣyati \|*  
*yata eṣa samudbhūtastatredānīṃ gamiṣyati \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. He cannot be slain by any one except Śiva. He will return to the place from where he sprang up.

## \|\| 6.14.29 \|\|

*pativratāsya bhavitā patnī saubhāgyavarddhinī \|*  
*sarvāṅgasundarī ramyā priyavākchīlasāgarā \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. His wife will be a chaste lady who will increase good fortune. She will be exquisitely beautiful in every limb. She will be an ocean of good conduct and will speak pleasing words.

## \|\| 6.14.30 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityuktvā śukramāhūya rājye taṃ cābhyaṣecayat \|*  
*āmaṃtrya saritānnāthaṃ brahmāṃtarddhānamanvagāt \|\| 30 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

30\. After saying so he called Śukra and performed his coronation. Brahmā then took leave of the ocean and disappeared.

## \|\| 6.14.31 \|\|

*atha taddarśanotphullanayanassāgarastadā \|*  
*tamātmajaṃ samādāya svagehamagamanmudā \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Thereafter the ocean with blooming eyes saw the son, took him to his abode joyously.

## \|\| 6.14.32 \|\|

*apoṣayanmahopāyaissvabālaṃ muditātmakaḥ \|*  
*sarvāṃgasundaraṃ ramyaṃ mahādbhutasutejasam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. With a joyous heart he nurtured the boy with diverse great means. The boy grew into a beautiful youth of exquisite limbs and wonderful splendour.

## \|\| 6.14.33 \|\|

*athāmbudhissamāhūya kālanemiṃ mahāsuram \|*  
*vṛndābhidhāṃ sutāṃ tasya tadbhāryārthamayācata \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Then the ocean invited the great Asura Kālanemi and requested him to give his daughter named Vṛndā in marriage to his son.

## \|\| 6.14.34 \|\|

*kālanemyasuro vīro'surāṇāṃ pravarassudhīḥ \|*  
*sādhu yenembudheryāñcāṃ svakarmanipuṇo mune \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. O sage, the heroic Asura Kālanemi, foremost among the Asuras, intelligent and efficient in his activities, welcomed the request of the ocean.

## \|\| 6.14.35 \|\|

*jalaṃdharāya vīrāya sāgaraprabhavāya ca \|*  
*dadau brahmavidhānena svasutāṃ prāṇavallabhām \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. He gave his beloved daughter to Jalandhara, the brave son of the ocean, in marriage performing the nuptial rites according to the Brāhma style.

## \|\| 6.14.36 \|\|

*tadotsavo mahānāsīdvivāhe ca tayostadā \|*  
*sukhaṃ prāpurnadā nadyo'surāścaivākhilā mune \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. O sage, great festivities were held in the marriage. The rivers and Asuras were happy.

## \|\| 6.14.37 \|\|

*samudro'ti sukhaṃ prāpa sutaṃ dṛṣṭvā hi sastriyam \|*  
*dānaṃ dadau dvijātibhyo'pyanyebhyaśca yathāvidhi \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. The ocean too became extremely happy seeing his son united to a bride. In accordance with the rules he made charitable gifts to the brahmins and others.

## \|\| 6.14.38 \|\|

*ye devairnirjitāḥ pūrvaṃ daityāḥ pātāla saṃsthitāḥ \|*  
*te hi bhūmaṃḍalaṃ yātā nirbhayāstamupāśritāḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Those Asuras who had been formerly defeated by the gods and had sought shelter in Pātāla came fearlessly to the Earth and resorted to him.

## \|\| 6.14.39 \|\|

*te kālanemipramukhāstato'surāstasmai sutāṃ siṃdhusutāya dattvā \|*  
*babhūvuratyantamudānvitā hi tamāśritā deva vinirjayāya \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Kālanemi and other Asuras were pleased after giving the daughter in marriage to the son of the ocean. In order to defeat the gods they resorted to him.

## \|\| 6.14.40 \|\|

*sa cāpi vīrombudhibālako'sau jalaṃdharākhyo'suravīravīraḥ \|*  
*saṃprāpya bhāryāmatisundarī vaśī cakāra rājyaṃ hi kaviprabhāvāt \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. The heroic son of the ocean, Jalandhara, foremost among the Asura warriors, received a very beautiful lady as his wife and he ruled over the kingdom with the support of Śukra.

## Chapter 15 - The fight between the gods and Jalandhara

## \|\| 6.15.1 \|\|

*\|\| sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ekadā vāridhisuto vṛndāpati rudāradhīḥ \|*  
*sabhāryyassaṃsthito vīro'suraissarvaiḥ samanvitaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

1\. Once the son of the ocean, the noble-hearted husband of Vṛndā, was seated along with his wife and the Asuras.

## \|\| 6.15.2 \|\|

*tatrājagāma suprītassuvarcāstvatha bhārgavaḥ \|*  
*tejaḥ puṃjo mūrta iva bhāsayansakalā diśaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The brilliant Bhārgava came there joyously illuminating the ten quarters as the embodied brilliance.

## \|\| 6.15.3 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā gurumāyāntamasurāste'khilā drutam \|*  
*praṇemuḥ prītamanasassiṃdhuputro'pi sādaram \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. On seeing the preceptor coming, the Asuras were delighted in their minds and bowed to him. The son of the ocean too respectfully bowed to him.

## \|\| 6.15.4 \|\|

*dattvāśīrvacanaṃ tebhyo bhārgavastejasāṃ nidhiḥ \|*  
*niṣasādāsane ramye saṃtasthuste'pi pūrvavat \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. After bestowing his benediction on them, Bhārgava, the storehouse of splendour, sat on a beautiful seat. They too resumed their seats as before.

## \|\| 6.15.5 \|\|

*atha siṃdhvātmajo vīro dṛṣṭvā prītyā nijāṃ sabhām \|*  
*jalaṃdharaḥ prasanno'bhūdanaṣṭavaraśāsanaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Then the heroic son of the ocean, Jalandhara, saw his Assembly and was delighted to observe that his sway was unmitigated.

## \|\| 6.15.6 \|\|

*tatsthitaṃ chinnaśirasaṃ dṛṣṭvā rāhuṃ sa daityarāṭ \|*  
*papraccha bhārgavaṃ śīghramidaṃ sāgaranandanaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Seeing the headless Rāhu seated there, the son of the ocean, the emperor of the Asuras, immediately asked Bhārgava.

## \|\| 6.15.7 \|\|

*jalaṃdhara uvāca \|*  
*kenedaṃ vihitaṃ rāhośśiracchedanakaṃ prabho \|*  
*tadbrūhi nikhilaṃ vṛttaṃ yathāvattattvato guro \|\| 7 \|\|*

Jalandhara said:—

7\. O lord, by whom was this done to Rāhu? By whom was his head cut? Please tell me, O preceptor, everything in detail as it had happened.

## \|\| 6.15.8 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya vacastasya sindhuputrasya bhārgavaḥ \|*  
*smṛtvā śivapadāṃbhojaṃ pratyuvāca yathārthavat \|\| 8 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

8\. On hearing the words of the ocean’s son, Bhārgava remembered the lotus-like feet of Śiva and replied exactly as it had happened.

## \|\| 6.15.9 \|\|

*śukra uvāca \|*  
*jalaṃdhara mahāvīra sarvāsurasahāyaka \|*  
*śṛṇu vṛttāṃtamakhilaṃ yathāvatkathayāmi te \|\| 9 \|\|*

Bhārgava said:—

9\. O Jalandhara, O great hero, O benefactor of the Asuras, listen to the account. I shall relate everything exactly as it had happened.

## \|\| 6.15.10 \|\|

*purābhavadbalirvīro virocanasuto balī \|*  
*hiraṇyakaśipoścaiva prapautro dharmavittamaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Once there was a strong hero Bali, the son of Virocana and great-grandson of Hiraṇyakaśipu. He was foremost among the virtuous.

## \|\| 6.15.11 \|\|

*parājitāssurāstena rameśaṃ śaraṇaṃ yayuḥ \|*  
*savāsavāssvavṛttāṃtamācakhyuḥ svārthasādhakāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The gods including Indra being defeated by him sought refuge in Viṣṇu. Eager to gain their ends they told him all details.

## \|\| 6.15.12 \|\|

*tadājñayā suraiḥ sārddhaṃ cakrussaṃdhimatho surāḥ \|*  
*svakāryasiddhaye tātacchalakarmavicakṣaṇāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. O dear, at his bidding, the gods, very clever in deception, made an alliance with the Asuras, to further their own interest.

## \|\| 6.15.13 \|\|

*athāmṛtārthe siṃdhośca maṃthanaṃ cakrurādarāt \|*  
*viṣṇossahāyinaste hi surāssarve'suraissaha \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. All those gods, the assistants of Viṣṇu churned the ocean eagerly for the gain of nectar, along with the Asuras.

## \|\| 6.15.14 \|\|

*tato ratnopaharaṇamakārṣurdaityaśatravaḥ \|*  
*jagṛhuryatnato devāḥ papurapyamṛtaṃ chalāt \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The enemies of the Asuras extracted jewels from the ocean. The gods seized the nectar and drank it deceitfully.

## \|\| 6.15.15 \|\|

*tataḥ parābhavaṃ cakrurasurāṇāṃ sahāyataḥ \|*  
*viṣṇossurāssacakrāste'mṛtāpānādbalānvitāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Then the gods including Indra increased in strength and prowess by the drinking of the nectar and harassed the Asuras with the assistance of Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 6.15.16 \|\|

*śiraśchedaṃ cakārāsau pibataścāmṛtaṃ hariḥ \|*  
*rāhordevasabhāṃ hi pakṣapātī haressadā \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. This Viṣṇu who is always a partisan of Indra, cut off the head of Rahu as he was drinking the nectar along with the gods.

## \|\| 6.15.17-18 \|\|

*sanatkumrāra uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ kavistasya śiraśchedaṃ rāhośśaśaṃsa ca \|*  
*amṛtārthe samudrasya maṃthanaṃ devakāritam \|\| 17 \|\|*

*ratnopaharaṇaṃ caiva daityānāṃ ca parābhavam \|*  
*devairamṛtapānaṃ ca kṛtaṃ sarvaṃ ca vistarāt \|\| 18 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

17-18. Thus Bhargava narrated in detail the story of the headless Rahu, of the churning of the ocean pursued by the gods for the gain of nectar, of the removal of the jewels, of the drinking of the Amṛta by the gods and of the harassment to the Asuras.

## \|\| 6.15.19 \|\|

*tadākarṇya mahāvīrombudhibālaḥ pratāpavān \|*  
*cukrodha krodharaktākṣassvapiturmaṃthanaṃ tadā \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Then on hearing about the churning of his father, the heroic son of the ocean, the valorous Jalandhara became furious and his eyes turned red with anger.

## \|\| 6.15.20 \|\|

*atha dūtaṃ samāhūya ghasmarābhidhamuttamam \|*  
*sarvaṃ śaśaṃsa caritaṃ yadāha gururātmavān \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Then he called his excellent emissary Ghasmara and told him everything what the wise preceptor had said to him.

## \|\| 6.15.21 \|\|

*atha taṃ preṣayāmāsa svadūtaṃ śakrasannidhau \|*  
*saṃmānya bahuśaḥ prītyā'bhayaṃ dattvā viśāradam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. He then lovingly honoured the clever emissary in various ways, assured him of protection and sent him to Indra as his messenger.

## \|\| 6.15.22 \|\|

*dūtastriviṣṭapaṃ tasya jagāmāramalaṃ sudhīḥ \|*  
*ghasmaroṃ'budhibālasya sarvadevasamanvitam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Ghasmara, the intelligent emissary of Jalandhara, hastened to heaven where all the gods were present.

## \|\| 6.15.23 \|\|

*tatra gatvā sa dūtastu sudharmāṃ prāpya satvaram \|*  
*garvādakharvamaulirhi devendraṃ vākyamabravīt \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. After going there, the emissary entered the assembly of the gods. With his head kept straight as a token of haughtiness he spoke to lord Indra.

## \|\| 6.15.24 \|\|

*ghasmara uvāca \|*  
*jalaṃdharo'bdhi tanayassarvadaityajaneśvaraḥ \|*  
*supratāpī mahāvīrassvayaṃ kavisahāyavān \|\| 24 \|\|*

Ghasmara said:—

24\. Jalandhara, the son of the ocean, is the lord and emperor of all the Asuras. He is excessively heroic and valorous. He has the support and assistance of Bhargava.

## \|\| 6.15.25 \|\|

*dūto'haṃ tasya vīrasya ghasmarākhyo na ghasmaraḥ \|*  
*preṣitastena vīreṇa tvatsakāśamihāgataḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. I am his emissary. I have been sent by him. I have come to you here. My name is Ghasmara but I am not a devourer.

## \|\| 6.15.26 \|\|

*avyāhatājñasvarvatra jalaṃdhara udagradhīḥ \|*  
*nirjitākhiladaityārissa yadāha śṛṇuṣva tat \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. He is of exalted intellect. His behest has never been defied. He has defeated all the enemies of Asuras. Please listen to what he says.

## \|\| 6.15.27 \|\|

*jalaṃdhara uvāca \|*  
*kasmāttvayā mama pitā mathitassāgaro'driṇā \|*  
*nītāni sarvaratnāni piturme devatādhama \|\| 27 \|\|*

Jalandhara said:—

27\. “O base god, why was my father, the ocean, churned by you with the mountain? Why were all the jewels of my father taken away?

## \|\| 6.15.28 \|\|

*ucitaṃ na kṛtaṃ te'dya tāni śīghraṃ prayaccha me \|*  
*mamāyāhi vicāryetthaṃ śaraṇaṃ daivataissaha \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. What you have done is not proper. Return all of them to me immediately. Pondering over this, come along with the gods and seek refuge in me.

## \|\| 6.15.29 \|\|

*anyathā te bhayaṃ bhūri bhaviṣyati surādhama \|*  
*rājyavidhvaṃsanaṃ caiva satyametadbravīmyaham \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Otherwise, O base god, you will have a great cause to fear. You will run the risk of the annihilation of your kingdom.”

## \|\| 6.15.30 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*iti dūtavacaḥ śrutvā vismitastridaśādhipaḥ \|*  
*uvāca taṃ smarannindro bhayaroṣasamanvitaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

30\. On hearing the words of the messenger, Indra, the the lord of the gods, was bewildered. Remembering the previous incidents he was frightened as well as angry. He spoke to him thus.

## \|\| 6.15.31 \|\|

*adrayo madbhayāttrastāssvakukṣisthā yataḥ kṛtāḥ \|*  
*anye'pi maddviṣastena rakṣitā ditijāḥ purā \|\| 31 \|\|*

Indra said:—

31\. He gave shelter to the mountains who were terribly afraid of me. Others too, some of my enemies, the Asuras, were formerly saved by him.

## \|\| 6.15.32 \|\|

*tasmāttadratnajātaṃ tu mayā sarvaṃ hṛtaṃ kila \|*  
*na tiṣṭhati mama drohī sukhaṃ satyaṃ bravīmyaham \|\| 32 \|\|*

32 It was due to this that I took away his jewels. Those who oppose me can never remain happy. I am telling you the truth.

## \|\| 6.15.33 \|\|

*śaṃkhopyeva purā daityo māṃ dviṣansāgarātmajaḥ \|*  
*abhavanmūḍhacittastu sādhusaṃgātsamujjhita \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Formerly the Asura Śaṅkha the son of the ocean was stupid enough to be inimical to me. He was spared by me because he was associated with saintly men.

## \|\| 6.15.34 \|\|

*mamānujena hariṇā nihatasya hi pāpadhīḥ \|*  
*hiṃsakassādhusaṃdhasya pāpiṣṭhassāgarodare \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. But when his predilection became sinful and he became violent towards saintly men, he was killed in the interior of the ocean by Viṣṇu, my younger brother.

## \|\| 6.15.35 \|\|

*tadgaccha dūta śīghraṃ tvaṃ kathayasvāsya tattvataḥ \|*  
*abdhiputrasya sarvaṃ hi siṃdhormaṃthanakāraṇam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Hence O messenger, go immediately and explain to the Asura, son of the ocean, our purpose for churning the ocean.”

## \|\| 6.15.36 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*itthaṃ visarjito dūto ghasmarākhyassubuddhimān \|*  
*tadendreṇāgamattūrṇṇaṃ yatra vīro jalaṃdharaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

36\. Dismissed thus by Indra, the intelligent emissary Ghasmara hastened to the place where the heroic Jalandhara was present.

## \|\| 6.15.37 \|\|

*tadidaṃ vacanaṃ daityarājo hi tena dhīmatā \|*  
*kathito nikhilaṃ śakraproktaṃ dūtena vai tadā \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. All the words thus spoken by Indra were narrated to the king of Asuras by the intelligent emissary.

## \|\| 6.15.38 \|\|

*tanniśamya tato daityo roṣātprasphuritādharaḥ \|*  
*udyogamakarottūrṇaṃ sarvadevajigīṣayā \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. On hearing it, the lips of the Asura throbbed with anger. Desirous of conquering the gods he exerted himself immediately.

## \|\| 6.15.39 \|\|

*tadodyoge'surendrasya digbhyaḥ pātālatastathā \|*  
*ditijāḥ pratyapadyaṃta koṭiśaḥkoṭiśastathā \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. In that enterprise of the lord of the Asuras, countless Asuras from all the quarters and the nether region took part and helped him.

## \|\| 6.15.40 \|\|

*atha śuṃbhaniśuṃbhādyai balādhipatikoṭibhiḥ \|*  
*nirjagāma mahāvīraḥ sindhuputraḥ pratāpavān \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Then the extremely heroic and valorous son of the ocean set forth with countless generals, Śumbha, Niśumbha and others.

## \|\| 6.15.41 \|\|

*prāpa triviṣṭapaṃ sadyaḥ sarvasainyasamāvṛtaḥ \|*  
*dadhmau śaṃkhaṃ jaladhijo nedurvīrāśca sarvataḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Very soon, he reached the heaven along with his force. He blew his conch. All the heroic soldiers roared.

## \|\| 6.15.42 \|\|

*gatvā triviṣṭapaṃ daityo nandanādhiṣṭhito'bhavat \|*  
*sarva sainyaṃ samāvṛtya kurvāṇaḥ siṃhavadravam \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. After going to heaven he stationed himself in Nandana. In the midst of all his forces he roared like a lion.

## \|\| 6.15.43 \|\|

*puramāvṛtya tiṣṭhattaddṛṣṭvā sainyabalaṃ mahat \|*  
*niryayustvamarāvatyā devā yuddhāya daṃśitāḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. On seeing a vast army surrounding the city, the gods came out of Amarāvatī fully equipped with armour for the battle.

## \|\| 6.15.44-45 \|\|

*tatassamabhavadyuddhaṃ devadānavasenayoḥ \|*  
*musalaiḥ parighairbāṇairgadāparaśuśaktibhiḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

*te'nyonyaṃ samadhāvetāṃ jaghnatuśca parasparam \|*  
*kṣaṇenābhavatāṃ sene rudhiraughapariplute \|\| 45 \|\|*

44-45. Then a battle between the armies of the gods and Asuras ensued. They rushed against one another with iron clubs, arrows, maces, axes and spears. They hit one another. Within a short time both the armies began to wade through streams of blood.

## \|\| 6.15.46 \|\|

*patitaiḥ pātyamānaiśca gajāśvarathapattibhiḥ \|*  
*vyarājata raṇe bhūmissaṃdhyābhrapaṭalairiva \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. In that battle, the ground shone like the dusk with clouds scattered all round, for it was strewn with elephants, horses, chariots and foot-soldiers. Some were killed and others were being killed.

## \|\| 6.15.47 \|\|

*tatra yuddhe mṛtāndaityānbhārgavastānajīvayat \|*  
*vidyayāmṛtajīvinyā maṃtritaistoyabindubhiḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Bhārgava resuscitated the Asuras killed in the battle with the Vidyā of Amṛtajīvinī and drops of water infused with mantras.

## \|\| 6.15.48 \|\|

*devānapi tathā yuddhe tatrājīvayadaṃgirāḥ \|*  
*divyauṣadhaissamānīya droṇādressa punaḥpunaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. The sage Aṅgiras\[5\] too resuscitated the gods in the battle with the divine herbs frequently brought from the mountain Droṇa.

## \|\| 6.15.49 \|\|

*dṛṣṭavānsa tathā yuddhe punareva samutthitān \|*  
*jalaṃdharaḥ krodhavaśo bhārgavaṃ vākyamabravīt \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Jalandhara saw the gods restored to life again in the battle. He then spoke angrily to Bhārgava.

## \|\| 6.15.50 \|\|

*jalaṃdhara uvāca \|*  
*mayā devā hatā yuddhe uttiṣṭhaṃti kathaṃ punaḥ \|*  
*tataḥ saṃjīvinī vidyā naivānyatreti vai śrutā \|\| 50 \|\|*

Jalandhara said:—

50\. “The gods have been killed by me. How do they rise up again? The Vidyā of Sañjīvinī has not been heard by me to exist elsewhere.”

## \|\| 6.15.51 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya vacastasya sindhuputrasya bhārgavaḥ \|*  
*pratyuvāca prasannātmā guruśśukro jalaṃdharam \|\| 51 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

51\. On hearing these words of the son of the ocean, the delighted Bhārgava, the preceptor, replied to Jalandhara.

## \|\| 6.15.52 \|\|

*śukra uvāca \|*  
*divyauṣadhīssamānīya droṇādreraṃgirāssurān \|*  
*jīvayatyeṣa vai tāta satyaṃ jānīhi me vacaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

Bhārgava said:—

52\. “Aṅgiras is bringing divine herbs from the mountain Droṇa and enlivening the gods. O dear, know my words to be true.

## \|\| 6.15.53 \|\|

*jayamicchasi cettāta śṛṇu me vacanaṃ śubham \|*  
*tataḥ so'raṃ bhujābhyāṃ tvaṃ droṇamabdhāvupāhara \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. O dear, if you wish for victory listen to my auspicious suggestion. Immediately you shall uproot the mountain Droṇa with your arms and hurl it into the ocean.”

## \|\| 6.15.54 \|\|

*\|\|sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityuktassa tu daityendro guruṇā bhārgaveṇa ha \|*  
*drutaṃ jagāma yatrāsāvāste caivādrirāṭ ca saḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

54\. Thus addressed by his preceptor Bhārgava, the lord of the Asuras, hastened to the lofty mountain.

## \|\| 6.15.55 \|\|

*bhujābhyāṃ tarasā daityo nītvā droṇaṃ ca taṃ tadā \|*  
*prākṣipatsāgare tūrṇaṃ citraṃ na haratejasi \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. With his powerful arms, the Asura brought the mountain Droṇa and hurled it immediately into the ocean. There is nothing wonderful and mysterious in regard to the splendour of Śiva.

## \|\| 6.15.56 \|\|

*punarāyānmahāvīrassindhuputro mahāhavam \|*  
*jaghānāstraiśca vividhaissurānkṛtvā balaṃ mahat \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. The great hero, the son of the ocean, took a vast army with him, came to the battle ground and began to kill the gods with various weapons.

## \|\| 6.15.57 \|\|

*atha devānhatāndṛṣṭvā droṇādrimagamadguruḥ \|*  
*tāvattatra girīdraṃ taṃ na dadarśa surārcitaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. On seeing the gods being killed Bṛhaspati went to the mountain Droṇa. Then he, the object of praise and worship by the gods, did not see the mountain there.

## \|\| 6.15.58 \|\|

*jñātvā daityahṛtaṃ droṇaṃ dhiṣaṇo bhayavihvalaḥ \|*  
*āgatya devānprovāca jīvo vyākulamānasaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. On realising that the mountain Droṇa had been removed by the Asuras, Bṛhaspati was terrified. He returned and said dejectedly.

## \|\| 6.15.59 \|\|

*gururuvāca \|*  
*palāyadhvaṃ surāssarve droṇo nāsti girirmahān \|*  
*dhruvaṃ dhvastaśca daityena pāthodhitanayena hi \|\| 59 \|\|*

Bṛhaspati said:—

59\. “O gods, run away, all of you. There is no trace of the great mountain Droṇa. Certainly it has been destroyed by the Asura, the son of the ocean.

## \|\| 6.15.60 \|\|

*jalaṃdharo mahādaityo nāyaṃ jetuṃ kṣamo yataḥ \|*  
*rudrāṃśasaṃbhavo hyeṣa sarvāmaravimardanaḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Jalandhara is a great Asura. He cannot be conquered since he is born of a part of Śiva. He will pound all the gods.

## \|\| 6.15.61 \|\|

*mayā jñātaḥ prabhāvo'sya yathotpannaḥ svayaṃ surāḥ \|*  
*śivāpamānakṛcchakraceṣṭitaṃ smaratākhilam \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. His power has been understood by me as he is self-born. O gods, all of you remember the act of offence to Śiva perpetrated by Indra.

## \|\| 6.15.62 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*śrutvā tadvacanaṃ devāssurācāryaprakīrtitam \|*  
*jayāśāṃ tyaktavaṃtaste bhayavihvalitāstathā \|\| 62 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

62\. On hearing these words uttered by the preceptor of the gods, they abandoned all hopes of victory. They became excessively terrified.

## \|\| 6.15.63 \|\|

*daityarājena tenātihanyamānāssamaṃtataḥ \|*  
*dhairyaṃ tyaktvā palāyaṃta diśo daśa savāsavāḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. All the gods including Indra, struck by the king of the Asuras all round, lost courage and fled in all directions.

## \|\| 6.15.64 \|\|

*devānvidrāvitāndṛṣṭvā daityassāgaranaṃdanaḥ \|*  
*śaṃkhabherī jayaravaiḥ praviveśāmarāvatīm \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. On seeing the gods routed, the Asura, Jalandhara, the son of the ocean, entered Amarāvatī with sounds of victory from the conches and drums.

## \|\| 6.15.65 \|\|

*praviṣṭe nagarīṃ daitye devāḥ śakrapurogamāḥ \|*  
*suvarṇādriguhāṃ prāptā nyavasandaityatāpitāḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. When the Asura entered the city, Indra and other gods entered the cavern of the golden mountain Meru and remained there. They had been extremely harrassed by the Asuras.

## \|\| 6.15.66 \|\|

*tadaiva sarveṣvasuro'dhikāreṣvindrādikānāṃ viniveśya samyak \|*  
*śuṃbhādikāndaityavarān pṛthakpṛthaksvayaṃ suvarṇādiguhāṃ vyagānmune \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. O sage, at the same time the Asura appointed Śumbha and other Asuras severally in the places of authority of Indra and others. He then went into the cavern of the golden mountain.

## Chapter 16 - The battle of the gods

## \|\| 6.16.1 \|\|

*\|\| sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*punardaityaṃ samāyāṃtaṃ dṛṣṭvā devāssavāsavāḥ \|*  
*bhayātprakaṃpitāssarve sahaivādudruvurdrutam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

1\. On seeing the Asura coming again, the gods including Indra trembled with fear. They fled together.

## \|\| 6.16.2 \|\|

*vaikuṃṭhaṃ prayayussarve puraskṛtya prajāpatim \|*  
*tuṣṭuvuste surā natvā saprajāpatayo'khilāḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. With Brahmā at the head they went to Vaikuṇṭha. All of them including Prajāpati eulogised Viṣṇu after bowing down to him.

## \|\| 6.16.3 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*hṛṣīkeśa mahābāho bhagavan madhusūdana \|*  
*namaste devadeveśa sarvadaityavināśaka \|\| 3 \|\|*

The gods said:—

3\. O Hṛṣīkeśa of long arms, O lord, O slayer of Madhu, O lord of gods, Obeisance to you, O destroyer of all Asuras.

## \|\| 6.16.4 \|\|

*matsyarūpāya te viṣṇo vedānnītavate namaḥ \|*  
*satyavratena sadrājñā pralayābdhivihāriṇe \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. O Viṣṇu, of the form of fish who redeemed the Vedas through king Satyavrata, obeisance to you who sport about in the ocean of Dissolution.

## \|\| 6.16.5 \|\|

*kurvāṇānāṃ surāṇāṃ ca mathanāyodyamaṃ bhṛśam \|*  
*bibhrate maṃdaragiriṃ kūrmarūpāya te namaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Obeisance to you of the form of Tortoise who bore the mountain Mandara of the gods who were attempting to churn the ocean.

## \|\| 6.16.6 \|\|

*namaste bhagavannātha kratave sūkarātmane \|*  
*vasuṃdharāṃ janādhārāṃ mūddhato bibhrate namaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*
