6\. Obeisance to you O holy lord, of the form of Boar. Obeisance to you who hold the earth, the support of people. Obeisance to Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 6.16.7 \|\|

*vāmanāya namastubhyamupendrākhyāya viṣṇave \|*  
*viprarūpeṇa daityendraṃ baliṃ chalayate vibho \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Obeisance to you, the Dwarf. Obeisance to Viṣṇu the younger brother of Indra, the lord who deceived the king of Asuras in the guise of a Brahmin.

## \|\| 6.16.8 \|\|

*namaḥ paraśurāmāya kṣatraniḥkṣatrakāriṇe \|*  
*māturhitakṛte tubhyaṃ kupitāyāsatāṃ druhe \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Obeisance to Paraśurāma who exterminated the Kṣattriyas, who rendered help to your mother. Obeisance to you who are angry and inimical to the evil beings.

## \|\| 6.16.9 \|\|

*rāmāya lokarāmāya maryādāpuruṣāya te \|*  
*rāvaṇāṃtakarāyāśu sītāyāḥ pataye namaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Obeisance to Rama who delighted the worlds and who set the limits of decent behaviour. Obeisance to you the destroyer of Rāvaṇa and the lord of Sītā.

## \|\| 6.16.10 \|\|

*namaste jñānagūḍhāya kṛṣṇāya paramātmana \|*  
*rādhāvihāraśīlāya nānālīlākarāya ca \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Obeisance to you of hidden knowledge; to Kṛṣṇa the great Ātman; the sportive paramour of Rādhā; Obeisance to him of diverse divine sports.

## \|\| 6.16.11 \|\|

*namaste gūḍhadehāya vedaniṃdākarāya ca \|*  
*yogācāryāya jaināya vauddharūpāya māpate \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Obeisance to the preceptor of Yoga; Obeisance to you, O lord of Lakṣmī, of the form of Jaina and Bauddha; to you of hidden body and features and the censurer of the Vedas.

## \|\| 6.16.12 \|\|

*namaste kalkirūpāya mlecchānāmaṃtakāriṇe \|*  
*anantaśaktirūpāya saddharmasthāpanāya ca \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Obeisance to you of the form of Kalki; the destroyer of outcastes, Obeisance to him of infinite power and who establishes good virtue.

## \|\| 6.16.13 \|\|

*namaste kapilarūpāya devahūtyai mahātmane \|*  
*vadate sāṃkhyayogaṃ ca sāṃkhyācāryāya vai prabho \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Obeisance to you of the form of Kapila of great soul and who expounded the doctrines of Sāṃkhya and Yoga to Devahūtī; O lord, obeisance to you the preceptor of Sāṃkhya.

## \|\| 6.16.14 \|\|

*namaḥ paramahaṃsāya jñānaṃ saṃvadate param \|*  
*vidhātre jñānarūpāya yenātmā saṃprasīdati \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Obeisance to great yogin and saint who expounds the great wisdom. Obeisance to the creator of the form of knowledge whereby the soul is delighted.

## \|\| 6.16.15 \|\|

*vedavyāsāya vedānāṃ vibhāgaṃ kurvate namaḥ \|*  
*hitāya sarvalokānāṃ purāṇaracanāya ca \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Obeisance to you of the form of Vedavyāsa who classified the Vedas and who wrote the Purāṇas for the welfare of the worlds.

## \|\| 6.16.16 \|\|

*evaṃ matsyāditanubhirbhaktakāryodyatāya te \|*  
*sargasthitidhvaṃsakartre namaste brahmaṇe prabho \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Obeisance to you who are ready to perform the task of the devotees through incarnations of Fish etc. O lord, obeisance to you of the form of Brahman, the cause of creation, sustenance and annihilation.

## \|\| 6.16.17 \|\|

*ārtihaṃtre svadāsānāṃ sukhadāya śubhāya ca \|*  
*pītāmbarāya haraye tārkṣyayānāya te namaḥ \|*  
*sarvakriyāyaikakartre śaraṇyāya namonamaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Obeisance to the destroyer of the distress of your servants; the bestower of auspicious happiness. Obeisance to you wearing yellow robes, having Garuḍa for your vehicle. Obeisance to the performer of all rites. Obeisance to the sole doer. Obeisance to the one worthy of being resorted to.

## \|\| 6.16.18 \|\|

*daityasaṃtāpitāmartya duḥkhādidhvaṃsavajraka \|*  
*śeṣatalpaśayāyārkacandranetrāya te namaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. O thunderbolt for the destruction of misery etc. of the gods harassed by the Asuras. Obeisance to you lying on the Serpent-bed. Obeisance to the one who has sun and the moon for his eyes.

## \|\| 6.16.19 \|\|

*kṛpāsindho ramānātha pāhi naśśaraṇāgatān \|*  
*jalaṃdhareṇa devāśca svargātsarve nirākṛtāḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. O lord of Lakṣmī, O ocean of mercy, save us who have sought refuge in you. All the gods have been driven out of heaven by Jalandhara.

## \|\| 6.16.20 \|\|

*sūryo nissāritaḥ sthānāccandro vahnistathaiva ca \|*  
*pātālānnāgarājaśca dharmarājo nirākṛtaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. The sun has been dislodged from his post. Similarly the moon and the fire too have been removed. The Serpent-king has been removed from Pātāla and Dharmarāja has been dispossessed.

## \|\| 6.16.21 \|\|

*vicaraṃti yathā martyāśśobhaṃte naiva te surāḥ \|*  
*śaraṇaṃ te vayaṃ prāptā vadhastasya viciṃtyatām \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. While men freely move about, the gods do not shine. We have sought refuge in you. Let measures for his annihilation be thought of.

## \|\| 6.16.22 \|\|

*\|\| sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*iti dīnavacaśśrutvā devānāṃ madhusūdanaḥ \|*  
*jagāda karuṇāsindhurme ghanirhrādayā girā \|\| 22 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

22\. On hearing these piteous entreaties of the gods, Viṣṇu the slayer of Madhu, the ocean of mercy, spoke in a thundering voice.

## \|\| 6.16.23 \|\|

*\|\| viṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*bhayaṃ tyajata he devā gamiṣyāmyahamāhavam \|*  
*jalaṃdhareṇa daityena kariṣyāmi parākramam \|\| 23 \|\|*

Viṣṇu said:—

23\. “O gods, cast off your fear. I shall come to the battle-ground. I shall show my valour to Jalandhara.”

## \|\| 6.16.24 \|\|

*ityuktvā sahasotthāya daityāriḥ khinnamānasaḥ \|*  
*ārohadgaruḍaṃ vegātkṛpayā bhaktavatsalaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Having said this with distressed mind, Viṣṇu the enemy of the Asuras got up quickly. The god Viṣṇu who is favourably disposed to his devotees immediately mounted his vehicle Garuḍa.

## \|\| 6.16.25 \|\|

*gacchantaṃ vallabhaṃ dṛṣṭvā devaissārddhaṃ samudrajā \|*  
*sāṃjalirbāṣpanayanā lakṣmīrvacanamabravīt \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. On seeing her lord departing along with the gods, Lakṣmī, the daughter of the ocean, spoke with palms joined in reverence and tears welling up in the eyes.

## \|\| 6.16.26 \|\|

*lakṣmyuvāca \|*  
*ahaṃ te vallabhā nātha bhaktā yadi ca sarvadā \|*  
*tatkathaṃ te mama bhrātā yuddhe vadhyaḥ kṛpānidhe \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. “O lord, I am your beloved. If I am always devoted to you, O storehouse of mercy, how does my brother’s death be at your hands.

## \|\| 6.16.27-28 \|\|

*viṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*jalaṃdhareṇa daityena kariṣyāmi parākramam \|*  
*taissaṃstuto gamiṣyāmi yuddhāya tvaritānvitaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*rudrāṃśasaṃbhavatvācca brahmaṇo vacanādapi \|*  
*prītyā ca tava naivāyaṃ mama vadhyo jalaṃdharaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

Viṣṇu said:—

27-28. Since I have been eulogised by the gods I shall go to the battle ground immediately. I can only show my valour to the Asura Jalandhara. He cannot be slain by me because he is a part of Śiva. Moreover Brahmā has said so. Further, you love him too.”

## \|\| 6.16.29 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityuktvā garuḍārūḍhaśśaṃkhacakragadāsibhṛt \|*  
*viṣṇurvegādyayau yoddhuṃ devaiśśakrādibhissaha \|\| 29 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

29\. Having said this and seating himself on Garuḍa with the conch, discus, mace and the sword held in his hands, Viṣṇu hastened to the fight along with Indra and other gods.

## \|\| 6.16.30 \|\|

*drutaṃ sa prāpa tatraiva yatra daityo jalaṃdharaḥ \|*  
*kurvan siṃharavaṃ devairjvaladbhirviṣṇutejasā \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Roaring like a lion and accompanied by the gods who blazed with Viṣṇu’s splendour, he reached the place where Jalandhara was waiting.

## \|\| 6.16.31 \|\|

*athāruṇānujajavapakṣavātaprapīḍitāḥ \|*  
*vātyāvivartitā daityā babhramuḥ khe yathā ghanāḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Then the Daityas afflicted by the gusts of wind set in motion by the wings in the speedy flight of the younger brother of Aruṇa (i.e Garuḍa)\[5\] were blown here and there like the clouds in the sky tossed about in a stormy whirlwind.

## \|\| 6.16.32 \|\|

*tato jalaṃdharo dṛṣṭvā daityān vātyāprapīḍitān \|*  
*uddhṛtya vacanaṃ krodhāddrutaṃ viṣṇuṃ samabhyagāt \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Then on seeing the Asuras afflicted by the gusts of wind, Jalandhara rushed against Viṣṇu shouting out cries of bravery angrily.

## \|\| 6.16.33 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare devāścakruryuddhaṃ praharṣitāḥ \|*  
*tejasā ca hareḥ puṣṭā mahābalasamanvitāḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. In the meantime the delighted gods equipped with a vast army began to fight with their strength increased by the brilliance of Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 6.16.34 \|\|

*yuddhodyataṃ samālokya devasainyamupasthitam \|*  
*daityānājñāpayāmāsa samare cātidurmadān \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Seeing the army of the gods present there ready to fight Jalandhara commanded the invincible Asuras thus.

## \|\| 6.16.35 \|\|

*jalaṃdhara uvāca \|*  
*bhobho daityavarā yūyaṃ yuddhaṃ kuruta dustaram \|*  
*śakrādyairamarairadya prabalaiḥ kātaraissadā \|\| 35 \|\|*

Jalandhara said:—

35\. O Excellent Asuras, put up a stiff fight with Indra and other gods who are always cowardly though they have a huge army.

## \|\| 6.16.36-37 \|\|

*mauryāstu lakṣasaṃkhyātā dhaumrā hi śatasaṃkhyakāḥ \|*  
*asurāḥ koṭisaṃkhyātāḥ kālakeyāstathaiva ca \|\| 36 \|\|*

*kālakānāṃ daurhṛdānāṃ kaṃkānāṃ lakṣasaṃkhyayā \|*  
*anye'pi svabalairyuktā viniryāṃtu mamājñayā \|\| 37 \|\|*

36-37. At my bidding let all these come out with their entire army—the Mauryas numbering a hundred thousand, the Dhūmras in hundreds, the Asuras and the Kālakeyas in crores and the Kālakas, the Daurhṛdas and the Kaṅkas in lakhs.

## \|\| 6.16.38 \|\|

*sarve sajjā viniryāta bahusenābhisaṃyutāḥ \|*  
*nānāśastrāstrasaṃyuktā nirbhayāḥ gatasaṃśayāḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. All of you come out readily equipped with many divisions of the army and different kinds of weapons. Be fearless and free from hesitations.

## \|\| 6.16.39 \|\|

*bhobho śuṃbhaniśuṃbhau ca devānsamarakātarān \|*  
*kṣaṇena sumahāvīryau tucchānnāśayataṃ yuvām \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. O Śumbha, O Niśumbha, destroy in a trice the insignificant gods who feel nervous in the battle field. You are extremely valorous.

## \|\| 6.16.40-41 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*daityā jalaṃdharājñaptā itthaṃ yuddhaviśāradāḥ \|*  
*yuyudhuste surāssarve caturaṃgabalānvitāḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*gadābhistīkṣṇabāṇaiśca śūlapaṭṭiśatomaraiḥ \|*  
*kecitparaśuśūlaiśca nijaghnuste parasparam \|\| 41 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

40-41. Thus the Asuras clever and efficient in battle, commanded by Jalandhara on the one hand and gods equipped with the four sorts of fighting groups on the other fought one another with maces, arrows, javelins, spears etc. They hit one another with axes and spears.

## \|\| 6.16.42 \|\|

*nānāyudhaiśca paraistatra nijaghnuste balānvitā \|*  
*devāstathā mahāvīrā hṛṣīkeśabalānvitāḥ \|*  
*yuyudhustīkṣṇabāṇāśca kṣipaṃtassiṃhavadravāḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. The strong ones hit and struck with different weapons. The heroic gods supported and invigorated by Hṛṣīkeśa roared like lions and discharged sharp arrows.

## \|\| 6.16.43 \|\|

*kecidbāṇaistu tīkṣṇaiśca kecinmusalatomaraiḥ \|*  
*kecitparaśuśūlaiśca nijaghnuste parasparam \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Some fought with arrows of very sharp points; some with pestles and iron clubs and some with axes and spears.

## \|\| 6.16.44 \|\|

*itthaṃ surāṇāṃ daityānāṃ saṃgrāmassamabhūnmahān \|*  
*atyulbaṇo munīnāṃ hi siddhānāṃ bhaya kārakaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Thus the fight between the gods and the Asuras was terrific. It was very fierce frightening the sages and the Siddhas.

## Chapter 17 - The fight between Viṣṇu and Jalandhara

## \|\| 6.17.1 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*atha daityā mahāvīryāśśūlaiḥ paraśupaṭṭiśaiḥ \|*  
*nijaghnussarvadevāṃśca bhayavyākulamānasān \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

1\. Then the heroic Asuras hit and struck the gods distressed and terrified, with the spears, axes and clubs.

## \|\| 6.17.2 \|\|

*daityāyudhaiḥ samāviddhadehā devāssavāsavāḥ \|*  
*raṇādvidudruvussarve bhayavyākulamānasāḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. With their bodies cut and pierced by the weapons of the Asuras, the gods including Indra became distressed in mind by fear and they fled from the battle.

## \|\| 6.17.3 \|\|

*palāyanaparāndṛṣṭvā hṛṣīkeśassurānatha \|*  
*viṣṇurvai garuḍārūḍho yoddhumabhyāyayau drutam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. On seeing the gods fleeing, Viṣṇu hastened to the battle ground seated on his vehicle Garuḍa.

## \|\| 6.17.4 \|\|

*sudarśanena cakreṇa sarvataḥ prasphuranrucā \|*  
*suśobhitakarābjaśca reje bhaktābhayaṃkaraḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. By means of his discus Sudarśana he diffused his splendour all round. He shone with the brilliant lotus in his hand and offered fearlessness to his devotees.

## \|\| 6.17.5 \|\|

*śaṃkhakhaḍgagadāśārṅgadhārī krodhasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*kaṭhorāstro mahāvīrassarvayuddhaviśāradaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Holding the conch, sword, mace and the bow, the heroic deity was very furious. He was efficient in the battle using fierce weapons.

## \|\| 6.17.6 \|\|

*dhanuṣaṃ śārṅganāmānaṃ visphūryya vinanāda ha \|*  
*tasya nādena trailokyaṃ pūritaṃ mahatā mune \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. He produced the twanging sound from his bow and roared aloud. O sage, all the three worlds were filled with its loud sound.

## \|\| 6.17.7 \|\|

*śārṅganissṛtabāṇaiśca ditijānāṃ śirāṃsi vai \|*  
*cakartta bhagavān viṣṇuḥ koṭiśo ruṭ samākulaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The lord Viṣṇu who was highly infuriated cut off the heads of countless Asuras by means of the arrows discharged from his bow.

## \|\| 6.17.8 \|\|

*athāruṇānujajavapakṣavātaprapīḍitāḥ \|*  
*vātyādhivarttitā daityā babhramuḥ khe yathā ghanāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Then the Asuras afflicted by the gusts of wind set in motion by the wings of Garuḍa in his speedy flight were blown to and fro like the clouds in the sky tossed about in a stormy whirlwind.

## \|\| 6.17.9 \|\|

*tato jalaṃdharo dṛṣṭvā daityānvātyāprapīḍitān \|*  
*cukrodhāti mahādaityo devavṛndabhayaṃkaraḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. On seeing the Asuras afflicted by the gusts of wind Jalandhara the great Asura became furious and terrified all the gods.

## \|\| 6.17.10 \|\|

*marddayaṃtaṃ ca taṃ dṛṣṭvā daityān prasphuritādharaḥ \|*  
*yoddhumabhyāyayau vīro vegena hariṇā saha \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Seeing Viṣṇu suppressing and pounding the Asuras, the lips of the heroic Asura throbbed and he rushed at Viṣṇu to fight with him.

## \|\| 6.17.11 \|\|

*sa cakāra mahānādaṃ devāsurabhayaṃkaram \|*  
*daityānāmadhipaḥ karṇā vidīrṇāḥ śravaṇāttataḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The king of Asuras shouted and roared terrifying both the gods and the Asuras. On hearing it, the ears became pierced.

## \|\| 6.17.12 \|\|

*bhayaṃṅkareṇa daityasya nādena pūritaṃ tadā \|*  
*jalaṃdharasya mahatā cakampe sakalaṃ jagat \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The entire universe, filled with the terrible shouts of the Asura Jalandhara, quaked.

## \|\| 6.17.13 \|\|

*tatassamabhavadyuddhaṃ viṣṇudaityendrayormahat \|*  
*ākāśaṃ kurvatorbāṇaistadā niravakāśavat \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Then a great battle ensued between Viṣṇu and Jalandhara, the ruler of Asuras, both filling up the sky with their arrows.

## \|\| 6.17.14 \|\|

*tayośca tena yuddhena parasparamabhūnmune \|*  
*devāsurarṣisiddhānāṃ bhīkareṇātivismayaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. O sage, gods, Asuras, sages and the Siddhas were

very much surprised at the terrible mutual clash between the two.

## \|\| 6.17.15 \|\|

*viṣṇurdaityasya bāṇaughairdhvajaṃ chatraṃ dhanuśśarān \|*  
*ciccheda taṃ ca hṛdaye bāṇenaikena tāḍayan \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Striking with a single arrow, Viṣṇu smote the heart of the Asura. With innumerable arrows he cut off the umbrella, banner, bow and arrows of the demon.

## \|\| 6.17.16 \|\|

*tato daityassamutpatya gadāpāṇistvarānvitaḥ \|*  
*āhatya garuḍaṃ mūrdhni pātayāmāsa bhūtale \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Seizing the mace with his hand, the Asura jumped up quickly, hit Garuḍa on his head and felled him to the ground.

## \|\| 6.17.17 \|\|

*viṣṇuṃ jaghāna śūlena tīkṣṇena prasphuradrucā \|*  
*hṛdaye krodhasaṃyukto daityaḥ prasphuritādharaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The infuriated Asura with throbbing lips hit Viṣṇu in his heart with his sharp spear diffusing its splendour.

## \|\| 6.17.18 \|\|

*viṣṇurgadāṃ ca khaḍgena ciccheda prahasanniva \|*  
*taṃ vivyādha śaraistīkṣṇaiśśārṅgaṃ visphūrya daityahā \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Viṣṇu laughingly split the mace with his sword. The destroyer of Asuras twanged his bow and split him with sharp arrows.

## \|\| 6.17.19 \|\|

*viṣṇurjalaṃdharaṃ daityaṃ bhayadena śareṇa ha \|*  
*krodhāviṣṭo'titīkṣṇena jaghānāśu surārihā \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Viṣṇu the infuriated destroyer of the Asuras smote the Asura Jalandhara with a very sharp terrifying arrow.

## \|\| 6.17.20 \|\|

*āgataṃ tasya taṃ bāṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā daityo mahābalaḥ \|*  
*chittvā bāṇena viṣṇuṃ ca jaghāna hṛdaye drutam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. On seeing his arrow coming, the powerful Asura cut it off with another arrow and hit Viṣṇu in the chest.

## \|\| 6.17.21 \|\|

*keśavo'pi mahābāhuṃ vikṣiptamasureṇa tam \|*  
*śaraṃ tilapramāṇena cchittvā vīro nanāda ha \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. The heroic Viṣṇu of long arms split the arrow discharged by the Asura to the size of gingelly seeds and roared.

## \|\| 6.17.22 \|\|

*punarbāṇa samādhatta dhanuṣi krodhavepitaḥ \|*  
*mahābalo'tha bāṇena ciccheda sa śilīmukham \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The infuriated great Asura fixed an arrow again to his bow and split the arrow of Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 6.17.23 \|\|

*vāsudevaḥ punarbāṇaṃ nāśāya vibudhadviṣaḥ \|*  
*krodhenādhatta dhanuṣi siṃhavadvinanāda ha \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Vāsudeva fixed another arrow to his bow for the destruction of the enemy of the gods angrily and roared like a lion.

## \|\| 6.17.24 \|\|

*jalaṃdharo'tha daityendraḥ kopacchinnādharo balī \|*  
*śareṇa śvena śārṅgākhyaṃ dhanuściccheda vaiṣṇavam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Biting his lips with anger, Jalandhara the powerful king of Asuras split the bow of Viṣṇu with his arrow.

## \|\| 6.17.25 \|\|

*punarbāṇaissutīkṣṇaiśca jaghāna madhusūdanam \|*  
*ugravīryo mahāvīro devānāṃ bhayakārakaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The heroic Asura of fierce valour, terrible to the gods, hit Viṣṇu again with very sharp arrows.

## \|\| 6.17.26 \|\|

*sa cchinnadhanvā bhagavānkeśavo lokarakṣa kaḥ \|*  
*jalaṃdharasya nāśāya cikṣepa svagadāṃ parām \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. With his bow split, the lord Viṣṇu, protector of the worlds, hurled his great mace for the destruction of Jalandhara.

## \|\| 6.17.27 \|\|

*sā gadā hariṇā kṣiptā jvalajjvalanasannibhā \|*  
*amoghagatikā śīghraṃ tasya dehe lalāga ha \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. That mace resembling a blazing flame when hurled by Viṣṇu moved with unerring aim and dashed against his body.

## \|\| 6.17.28 \|\|

*tayā hato mahādaityo na cacālāpi kiṃcana \|*  
*jalaṃdharo madonmattaḥ puṣpamālāhato yathā \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Though hit by it, the great haughty Jalandhara did not move even slightly as though he was hit by a flower-garland.

## \|\| 6.17.29 \|\|

*tato jalaṃdharaḥ krodhī devatrāsakaro'kṣipat \|*  
*triśūlamanalākāraṃ haraye raṇadurmmadaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Then the infuriated Jalandhara, invincible in war, terrifying to the Asuras hurled a trident, resembling fire, at Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 6.17.30 \|\|

*atha viṣṇustattriśūlaṃ ciccheda tarasā drutam \|*  
*naṃdakākhyena khaḍgena smṛtvā śivapadāmbujam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Immediately Viṣṇu remembered the lotus-like feet of Śiva and cut the trident with his sword Nandaka.

## \|\| 6.17.31 \|\|

*chinne triśūle daityendra utplutya sahasā drutam \|*  
*āgatya hṛdaye viṣṇuṃ jaghāna dṛḍhamuṣṭinā \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. When the trident was split, the lord of the Asuras leapt and rushed against Viṣṇu and hit him in the chest with his fist.

## \|\| 6.17.32 \|\|

*sopi viṣṇurmahāvīro'vigaṇayya ca tadvyathāma \|*  
*jalaṃdharaṃ ca hṛdaye jaghāna dṛḍhamuṣṭinā \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Without minding the pain in the least, the heroic Viṣṇu hit Jalandhara in the chest with his firm fist.

## \|\| 6.17.33 \|\|

*tatastau bāhuyuddhena yuyudhāte mahābalau \|*  
*bāhubhirmuṣṭibhiścaiva jānubhirnādayanmahīm \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Then both of them equally powerful had a hand to hand fight hitting each other with arms, fists and knees. They filled the earth with reverberating sounds.

## \|\| 6.17.34 \|\|

*evaṃ hi suciraṃ yuddhaṃ kṛtvā tenāsureṇa vai \|*  
*vismito'bhūnmuniśreṣṭha hṛdi glānimavāpa ha \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Fighting with the Asura thus, for a long time, O excellent sage, Viṣṇu was surprised. He felt dejected in the heart.

## \|\| 6.17.35 \|\|

*atha prasanno bhagavānmāyī māyāvidāṃ varaḥ \|*  
*uvāca daityarājānaṃ meghagaṃbhīrayā girā \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Then he the foremost among the magic-wielders assumed a delightful aspect. He addressed the king of Asuras in a thundering voice.

## \|\| 6.17.36 \|\|

*viṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*bhobho daityavaraśreṣṭha dhanyastvaṃ raṇadurmadaḥ \|*  
*mahāyudhavarairyattvaṃ na bhīto hi mahāprabhuḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

Viṣṇu said:—

36\. “O excellent Asura, you are blessed. You are invincible in war. Since you are a great lord you are not at all afraid of even great weapons.

## \|\| 6.17.37 \|\|

*ebhirevāyudhairugrairdaityā hi bahavo hatāḥ \|*  
*mahājau durmadā vīrāśchinnadehā mṛtiṃ gatāḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Many Asuras have been killed by these very same weapons in great battles. The wicked and haughty people have been pierced through their bodies and killed.

## \|\| 6.17.38 \|\|

*yuddhena te mahādaitya prasanno'smi mahānbhavān \|*  
*na dṛṣṭastvatsamo vīrastrailokye sacarācare \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. O great Asura, I am delighted by this fight with you. You are really great. A hero like you has not been seen in the three worlds including the mobile and immobile beings.

## \|\| 6.17.39 \|\|

*varaṃ varaya daityendra prīto'smi tava vikramāt \|*  
*adeyamapi te dadmi yatte manasi vartate \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. O lord of Asuras, choose a boon. I am pleased at your valour. I shall give you anything even that which cannot be given, whatever is in your mind.

## \|\| 6.17.40 \|\|

*\|\| sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya vacastasya viṣṇormāyāvino hareḥ \|*  
*pratyuvāca mahābuddhirdaityarājo jalaṃdharaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

40\. On hearing these words of Viṣṇu, skilled in magic, the intelligent king of the Asuras replied thus.

## \|\| 6.17.41 \|\|

*jalaṃdhara uvāca \|*  
*yadi bhāvuka tuṣṭo'si varame tandadasva me \|*  
*madbhaginyā mayā sārdhaṃ madgehe sagaṇo vasa \|\| 41 \|\|*

Jalandhara said:—

41\. O Brother-in-law, if you are pleased give me this boon. You stay in my house with all your followers, my sister and myself.

## \|\| 6.17.42 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*tadākarṇya vacastasya mahādaityasya khinnadhīḥ \|*  
*tathāstviti ca deveśo jagāda bhagavān hariḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

42\. On hearing these words of the great Asura, lord Viṣṇu, the lord of gods, said distressingly—“So be it.”

## \|\| 6.17.43 \|\|

*uvāsa sa tato viṣṇussarvadevagaṇaissaha \|*  
*jalaṃdharaṃ nāma puramāgatya ramayā saha \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Then Viṣṇu came to the city called Jalandhara along with his followers, the gods and Lakṣmī.

## \|\| 6.17.44 \|\|

*atho jalaṃdharo daityassvabhaginyā ca viṣṇunā \|*  
*uvāsa svālayaṃ prāpto harṣākulitamānasaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Then the Asura Jalandhara returned to his abode and stayed very delightedly in the company of his sister and Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 6.17.45 \|\|

*jalaṃdharo'tha devānāmadhikāreṣu dānavān \|*  
*sthāpayitvā saharṣassanpunarāgānmahītalam \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Thereafter Jalandhara appointed Asuras in the authoritative posts of the gods. Joyously he returned to the Earth.

## \|\| 6.17.46 \|\|

*devagaṃdharvasiddheṣu yatkiṃcidratnasaṃci tam \|*  
*tadātmavaśagaṃ kṛtvā'tiṣṭhatsāgaranaṃdanaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. The son of the ocean confiscated whatever gem or jewel the gods, Gandharvas or Siddhas had hoarded.

## \|\| 6.17.47 \|\|

*pātālabhavane daityaṃ niśuṃbhaṃ sumahābalam \|*  
*sthāpayitvā sa śeṣādīnānaya dbhūtalaṃ balī \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. After appointing the powerful Asura, Niśumbha, in the nether-worlds, the powerful ruler of the Asuras brought Śeṣa and others to the Earth.

## \|\| 6.17.48 \|\|

*devagaṃdharvasiddhaughān sarparākṣasamānuṣān \|*  
*svapure nāgarānkṛtvā śaśāsa bhuvanatrayam \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Making gods, Gandharvas, Siddhas, Serpents, Rākṣasas and human beings, the denizens of his capital, he ruled over the three worlds.

## \|\| 6.17.49 \|\|

*evaṃ jalaṃdharaḥ kṛtvā devānsvavaśavartinaḥ \|*  
*dharmeṇa pālayāmāsa prajāḥ putrānivaurasān \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. After making the gods thus subservient to himself, Jalandhara protected them all virtuously, like his own sons.

## \|\| 6.17.50 \|\|

*na kaścidvyādhito naiva duḥkhito na kṛśastathā \|*  
*na dīno dṛśyate tasmindharmādrājyaṃ praśāsati \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. When he was ruling the kingdom virtuously, none in his realm was sick or miserable or lean and emaciated or indigent.

## Chapter 18 - The conversation between Nārada and Jalandhara

## \|\| 6.18.1 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ śāsati dharmeṇa mahīṃ tasminmahāsure \|*  
*babhūvurduḥkhino devā bhrātṛbhāvānmunīśvara \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

1\. When the great Asura was ruling over the Earth virtuously, the gods were reduced to be mere slaves, O great sage.

## \|\| 6.18.2 \|\|

*duḥkhitāste surāssarve śivaṃ śaraṇamāyayuḥ \|*  
*manasā śaṃkaraṃ devadevaṃ sarvaprabhuṃprabhum \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The distressed gods mentally sought refuge in Śiva the benefactor, lord of gods and of everyone.

## \|\| 6.18.3 \|\|

*tuṣṭuvurvāgbhiriṣṭābhirbhagavaṃtaṃ maheśvaram \|*  
*nivṛttaye svaduḥkhasya sarvadaṃ bhaktavatsalam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. They eulogised the great lord, the bestower of everything and favourably disposed to his devotees, by means of pleasant words.

## \|\| 6.18.4 \|\|

*āhūya sa mahādevo bhaktānāṃ sarvakāmadaḥ \|*  
*nāradaṃ prerayāmāsa devakāryacikīrṣayā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The great lord, the bestower of all desires to his devotees called Nārada and commissioned him with a desire to carry out the task of the gods.

## \|\| 6.18.5 \|\|

*atha devamunirjñānī śaṃbhubhaktassatāṃ gatiḥ \|*  
*śivājñayā yayau daityapure devānsa nāradaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Then the celestial sage, the wise devotee of Śiva, the goal of the good, went to the gods in the city of the Asuras at the bidding of Śiva.

## \|\| 6.18.6 \|\|

*vyākulāste surāssarve vāsavādyā drutaṃ munim \|*  
*āgacchaṃtaṃ samālokya samuttasthurhi nāradam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. On seeing the sage Nārada coming, the distressed gods, Indra and others, stood up.

## \|\| 6.18.7 \|\|

*dadusta āsanaṃ nattvā munaye prītipūrvakam \|*  
*nāradāya surāśśakramukhā utkaṃṭhitānanāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. After bowing to the sage, Indra and other gods, their anxiety apparently manifest in their faces, offered a seat to Nārada.

## \|\| 6.18.8 \|\|

*sukhāsīnaṃ munivaramāsane supraṇamya tam \|*  
*punaḥ procussurā dīnā vāsavādyā munīśvaram \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. After bowing to Nārada the great sage who sat comfortably, the distressed gods, Indra and others spoke to him again.

## \|\| 6.18.9 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*bhobho munivaraśreṣṭha duḥkhaṃ śṛṇu kṛpākara \|*  
*śrutvā tannāśaya kṣipraṃ prabhustvaṃ śaṃkarapriyaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

The gods said:—

9\. O excellent sage, listen to our misery. O merciful one, after listening to it, destroy it quickly. You are powerful and the favourite of Śiva.

## \|\| 6.18.10 \|\|

*jalaṃdhareṇa daityena surā vidrāvitā bhṛśam \|*  
*svasthānādbhartṛbhāvācca duḥkhitā vayamākulāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The gods have been routed by the Asura Jalandhara from their abodes and positions of controlling authority. Hence we are miserable and distressed.

## \|\| 6.18.11 \|\|

*svasthānāduṣṇaraśmiśca candro nissāritastathā \|*  
*vahniśca dharmarājaśca lokapālāstathetare \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The hot-rayed sun and the moon have been ousted from their positions. The fire-god and the god of death and guardians of the quarters have been expelled.

## \|\| 6.18.12 \|\|

*subaliṣṭhena vai tena sarve devāḥ prapīḍitāḥ \|*  
*duḥkhaṃ prāptā vayaṃ cātiśaraṇaṃ tvāṃ samāgatāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The gods have been harassed by that powerful Asura. We who have been subjected to great grief now seek refuge in you.

## \|\| 6.18.13 \|\|

*saṃgrāme sa hṛṣīkeśaṃ svavaśaṃ kṛtavān balī \|*  
*jalaṃdharo mahādaityaḥ sarvāmaravimardakaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The great Asura Jalandhara who has suppressed the gods and who is very powerful has made Viṣṇu subservient to him in the battle.

## \|\| 6.18.14 \|\|

*tasya vaśyo varādhīno'vātsīttatsadane hariḥ \|*  
*salakṣmyā sahito viṣṇuryo nassarvārthasādhakaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Becoming subservient because of helplessness occa. sioned by the boon granted to him, Viṣṇu who carried out our tasks has now begun to stay in his palace along with Lakṣmī.

## \|\| 6.18.15 \|\|

*jalaṃdharavināśāya yatnaṃ kuru mahāmate \|*  
*tvaṃ no daivavaśātprāptassadā sarvārthasādhakaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. O intelligent one, please exert yourself for the destruction of Jalandhara. You have fortunately come to us and you have always been the person who can achieve everything for us.

## \|\| 6.18.16 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya vacasteṣāmamarāṇāṃ sa nāradaḥ \|*  
*āśvāsya muniśārdūlastānuvāca kṛpākaraḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

16\. On hearing these words of the gods, the great sage Nārada, the merciful, consoled them and said.

## \|\| 6.18.17 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*jāne'haṃ vai surā yūyaṃ daityarājaparājitāḥ \|*  
*duḥkha prāptāḥ pīḍitāśca sthānānnissāritāḥ khaluḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

Nārada said:—

17\. O gods, I know that you have been defeated by the king of Asuras, that you are miserable and harassed and have been deposed.

## \|\| 6.18.18 \|\|

*svaśaktyā bhavatāṃ svārthaṃ kariṣye nātra saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*anukūlo'hamiva vo duḥkhaṃ prāptā yato 'marāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. There is no doubt in this that I shall carry out your task according to my ability. O gods, since you are in misery I shall be favourable to you.”

## \|\| 6.18.19 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*evamuktvā muniśreṣṭha draṣṭuṃ dānavavallabham \|*  
*āśvāsya sakalāndevāñjalaṃdharasabhāṃ yayau \|\| 19 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

19\. After saying so and consoling the gods, the excellent sage went to the assembly chamber of Jalandhara to see the favourite Asura.

## \|\| 6.18.20 \|\|

*athāgataṃ muniśreṣṭhaṃ dṛṣṭvā devo jalaṃdharaḥ \|*  
*utthāya parayā bhaktyā dadau śreṣṭhāsanaṃ varam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. On seeing the excellent sage, the king Jalandhara stood up and offered him a splendid seat with great devotion.

## \|\| 6.18.21 \|\|

*sa taṃ saṃpūjya vidhivaddānavendro'ti vismitaḥ \|*  
*suprahasya tadā vākyaṃ jagāda munisattamam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. After worshipping him duly the surprised king of the Asuras laughed loudly and spoke to the excellent sage.

## \|\| 6.18.22 \|\|

*jalaṃdhara uvāca \|*  
*kuta āgamyate brahmankiṃ ca dṛṣṭaṃ tvayā kvacit \|*  
*yadarthamiha āyātastadājñāpaya māṃ mune \|\| 22 \|\|*

Jalandhara said:—

22\. O brahmin, whence do you come from? What did you see here? O sage, what is the aim of your present visit here?

## \|\| 6.18.23 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya vacastasya daityendrasya mahāmuniḥ \|*  
*pratyuvāca prasannātmā nārado hi jalaṃdharam \|\| 23 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

23\. On hearing these words of king Jalandhara the delighted great sage Nārada replied to him.

## \|\| 6.18.24 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*sarvadānavadaityendra jalaṃdhara mahāmate \|*  
*dhanyastvaṃ sarvalokeśa ratnabhoktā tvameva hi \|\| 24 \|\|*

Nārada said:—

24\. O Jalandhara of great intellect, O lord of Dānavas and Daityas, O lord of all the worlds, you are blessed. You alone are the enjoyer of all jewels.

## \|\| 6.18.25 \|\|

*madāgamanahetuṃ vai śṛṇu daityendrasattama \|*  
*yadarthamiha cāyātastvahaṃ vakṣyekhilaṃ hi tat \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. O excellent king of Daityas, listen to the purpose for which I have come here. I shall explain it to you.

## \|\| 6.18.26 \|\|

*gataḥ kailāsaśikharaṃ daityendrāhaṃ yadṛcchayā \|*  
*yojanāyutavistīrṇaṃ kalpadrumamahāvanam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. O lord of Daityas, I had been to the summit of Kailāsa casually. It is ten thousand Yojanas wide. It has a grove of Kalpa trees.

## \|\| 6.18.27 \|\|

*kāmadhenuśatākīrṇaṃ ciṃtāmaṇisudīpitam \|*  
*sarvarukmamayaṃ divyaṃ sarvatrādbhutaśobhitam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Hundreds of Kāmadhenus are found there. It is illuminated by Cintāmaṇi gems. It abounds in gold. It is divine and wonderfully brilliant.

## \|\| 6.18.28 \|\|

*tatromayā sahāsīnaṃ dṛṣṭavānasmi śaṃkaram \|*  
*sarvāṅgasundaraṃ gauraṃ trinetraṃ candraśekharam \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. There I saw Śiva seated along with Pārvatī. He is fair-complexioned and exquisitely handsome. He has three eyes and the moon for his crest.

## \|\| 6.18.29 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā mahadāścaryaṃ vitarko me'bhavattadā \|*  
*kvāpīdṛśī bhavedvṛddhistrailokye vā na veti ca \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. On seeing this wonderfully great thing, a doubt arose in my mind. Can there be anywhere in the three worlds such a splendour as this?”

## \|\| 6.18.30 \|\|

*tāvattavāpi daityendra samṛddhissaṃsmṛtā mayā \|*  
*tadvilokanakāmo'haṃ tvatsāṃnidhyamihā gataḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. O lord of Daityas then the idea of your prosperity struck into my mind. Now I have come to you to see it personally.

## \|\| 6.18.31 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*iti nāradataḥ śrutvā sa daityendro jalaṃdharaḥ \|*  
*svasamṛddhiṃ samagrāṃ vai darśayāmāsa sādaram \|\| 31 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

31\. On hearing these words of Nārada the lord of Daityas Jalandhara showed all his glory to Nārada.

## \|\| 6.18.32 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā sa nārado jñānī devakāryasusādhakaḥ \|*  
*prabhupreraṇayā prāha daityendraṃ taṃ jalaṃdharam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. On seeing it, the wise Nārada, eager to realise the interests of the gods, spoke to the king of Daityas, Jalandhara, induced by the lord.

## \|\| 6.18.33 \|\|

*nārad uvāca \|*  
*tavāsti susamṛddhirhi varavīra khilādhunā \|*  
*trailokyasya patistvaṃ hi citraṃ kiṃ cātra saṃbhavam \|\| 33 \|\|*

Nārada said:—

33\. O foremost among heroes, you have everything conducive to prosperity. You are the lord of the three worlds. What wonder that you possess this wealth.

## \|\| 6.18.34 \|\|

*maṇayo ratnapuṃjāśca gajādyāśca samṛddhayaḥ \|*  
*te gṛhe'dya vibhāṃtīha yāni ratnāni tānyapi \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Big jewels, heaps of gems, elephants and other adjuncts to prosperity flourish in your mansion. Whatever valuable thing there is in the worlds finds a place here.

## \|\| 6.18.35 \|\|

*gajaratnaṃ tvayānītaṃ śakrasyairāvatastathā \|*  
*aśvaratnaṃ mahāvīra sūryasyoccaiḥśravā hayaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. O great hero, the most excellent of all elephants, Airāvata of lndra has been brought by you. The most excellent of all horses, Uccaiḥśravas of the sun has been brought by you.

## \|\| 6.18.36 \|\|

*kalpavṛkṣastvayānīto nidhayo dhanadasya ca \|*  
*haṃsayuktavimānaṃ ca tvayānītaṃ hi vedhasaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. The celestial Kalpa tree has been brought by you; the treasures of Kubera and the aerial chariot of Brahmā yoked to swan have been brought by you.

## \|\| 6.18.37 \|\|

*ityevaṃ vararatnāni divi pṛthvyāṃ rasātale \|*  
*yāni daityendra te bhāṃti gṛhe tāni samastataḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Thus all excellent things available in heaven, earth and nether worlds, O great Daitya, flourish in your mansion in their entirety.

## \|\| 6.18.38 \|\|

*tvatsamṛddhimimāṃ paśyansampūrṇāṃ vividhāmaham \|*  
*prasanno'smi mahāvīra gajāśvādisuśobhitām \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. O great hero, I am highly delighted on seeing your great affluence consisting of diverse objects—elephant horse etc.

## \|\| 6.18.39 \|\|

*jāyāratnaṃ mahāśreṣṭhaṃ jalaṃdhara na te gṛhe \|*  
*tadānetuṃ viśeṣeṇa strīratnaṃ vai tvamarhasi \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. But O Jalandhara, your mansion is deficient in the most excellent of all ladies. You deserve to bring that.

## \|\| 6.18.40 \|\|

*yasya gehe suratnāni sarvāṇi hi jalaṃdhara \|*  
*jāyāratnaṃ na cettāni na śobhaṃte vṛthā dhruvam \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. O Jalandhara, one who possesses all excellent things but does not possess the most excellent of women does not shine. His life is rendered waste.

## \|\| 6.18.41 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityevaṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā nāradasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*uvāca daityarājo hi madanākulamānasaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

41\. On hearing these words of Nārada the noble soul, the king of Daityas, with his mind excited by passion, spoke as follows—

## \|\| 6.18.42 \|\|

*jalaṃdhara uvāca \|*  
*bho bho nārada devarṣe namastestu mahāprabho \|*  
*jāyāratnavaraṃ kutra vartate tadvadādhunā \|\| 42 \|\|*

Jalandhara said:—

42\. “O celestial sage, O Nārada, obeisance be to you, O holy lord. Where is this most excellent of all ladies? Please tell me now.

## \|\| 6.18.43 \|\|

*brahmāṃḍe yatra kutrāpi tadratnaṃ yadi varttate \|*  
*tadāneṣye tato brahmansatyaṃ satyaṃ na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Wherever it may be in the whole of this universe, if such a lady exists anywhere, I will bring her here. Truth, it is certainly the truth.”

## \|\| 6.18.44 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*kailāse hyatiramye ca sarvaddhisusamākule \|*  
*yogirūpadharaśśaṃbhurasti tatra digambaraḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

Nārada said:—

44\. Kailāsa is very beautiful and it possesses all sorts of things conducive to prosperity. Śiva lives there assuming the form of a naked Yogin.

## \|\| 6.18.45 \|\|

*tasya bhāryā suramyā hi sarvalakṣaṇalakṣitā \|*  
*sarvāṃgasundarī nāmnā pārvatīti manoharā \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. His wife Pārvatī is exquisitely beautiful in every limb. She is charming and has all the characteristics of a beautiful lady.

## \|\| 6.18.46 \|\|

*tadīdṛśaṃ rūpamananyasaṃgataṃ dṛṣṭaṃ na kutrāpi kutūhalāḍhyam \|*  
*atyadbhutaṃ mohanakṛtsuyogināṃ sudarśanīyaṃ paramarddhikāri \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Such an exquisite beauteous form has never been seen anywhere. It incites the enthusiasm of everybody. It is highly wonderful. It fascinates even the Yogins. It is worthy of being seen. It is conducive to great prosperity.

## \|\| 6.18.47 \|\|

*svacitte kalpayāmyadya śivādanyassamṛddhivān \|*  
*jāyāratnānvitādvīra trilokyā na jalaṃdhara \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. This occurs to my mind, O valiant Jalandhara that there is none more prosperous in the three worlds than Śiva who possesses the most excellent of all ladies.

## \|\| 6.18.48 \|\|

*yasyā lāvaṇyajaladhau nimagnaścaturānanaḥ \|*  
*svadhairyyaṃ mumuce pūrvaṃ tayā kānyopamīyate \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Even the four-faced\[2\] lord Brahmā, immersed in her ocean of beauty, lost his mental steadiness formerly. Who can be compared to such a beautiful lady?

## \|\| 6.18.49 \|\|

*gatarāgo'pi hi yayā madanārissvalīlayā \|*  
*nijataṃtro'pi yatassa svātma vaśagaḥ kṛtaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Even Śiva reputed to be free from infatuation has been won over by her womanly sports. Śiva who is independent has been subjugated by her.

## \|\| 6.18.50 \|\|

*yathā strīratnasaṃbhoktussamṛddhistasya sābhavat \|*  
*tathā na tava daityendra sarvaratnādhipasya ca \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. The prosperity that he enjoys inasmuch as he indulges in dalliance with the most excellent of all ladies has not come to you O lord of Daityas though you are the master of excellent gems and jewels.

## \|\| 6.18.51 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityuktvā sa tu devarṣirnārado lokaviśrutaḥ \|*  
*yayau vihāyasā devopakārakaraṇodyataḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

51\. After saying this, the world-renowned celestial sage, Nārada, pursuing his attempt to help the gods departed from there by the aerial path.

## Chapter 19 - Jalandhara’s emissary to Śiva

## \|\| 6.19.1 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*sanatkumāra sarvajña nārade hi gate divi \|*  
*daityarāṭ kimakārṣītsa tanme vada suvistarāt \|\| 1 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:—

1\. O omniscient Sanatkumāra, what did the king of Daityas do after the departure of Nārada to heaven? Please narrate to me in detail.

## \|\| 6.19.2 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*tamāmaṃtrya gate daityaṃ nārade divi daityarāṭ \|*  
*tadrūpaśravaṇādāsīdanaṃgajvarapīḍitaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

2\. When Nārada departed to heaven after taking leave of the Daitya, the king of Daityas who had heard of the exquisite beauty of Pārvatī became harassed with pangs of love.

## \|\| 6.19.3 \|\|

*atho jalaṃdharo daityaḥ kālādhīnaḥ pranaṣṭadhīḥ \|*  
*dūtamāhvāya yāmāsa saiṃhikeyaṃ vimohitaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The deluded Daitya, Jalandhara, who had lost clear thinking, being swayed by Time (the annihilator) called his messenger Rāhu.

## \|\| 6.19.4 \|\|

*āgataṃ taṃ samālokya kāmākrāṃtamanāssa hi \|*  
*susaṃbodhya samācaṣṭa siṃdhuputro jalaṃdharaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The infatuated son of the ocean, Jalandhara, addressed him politely with these words.

## \|\| 6.19.5 \|\|

*jalaṃdhara uvāca \|*  
*bhobho dūtavaraśreṣṭha sarvakāryaprasādhaka \|*  
*saiṃhikeya mahāprājña kailāsaṃ gaccha parvatam \|\| 5 \|\|*

Jalandhara said:—

5\. O Rāhu of great intellect, most excellent of my emissaries, go to the mountain Kailāsa, O accomplisher of all activities.

## \|\| 6.19.6 \|\|

*tatrāsti yogī śaṃbhvākhya stapasvī ca jaṭādharaḥ \|*  
*bhasmabhūṣitasarvāṅgo virakto vijitendriyaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. A sage and a Yogin named Śiva lives there. He has matted locks of hair. He is detached. He has controlled his senses. His body is smeared with ashes.

## \|\| 6.19.7 \|\|

*tatra gatveti vaktavyaṃ yoginaṃ dūta śaṃkaram \|*  
*jaṭādharaṃ viraktaṃ taṃ nirbhayena hṛdā tvayā \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. O messenger, you shall go there and tell the detached Yogin Śiva with matted locks of hair, fearlessly.

## \|\| 6.19.8 \|\|

*he yogiṃste dayāsindho jāyāratnena kiṃ bhavet \|*  
*bhūtapretapiśācādisevitena vanaukasā \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. ‘O Yogin, ocean of mercy, of what avail is an exquisitely beautiful wife to you who stay in the jungle attended by ghosts, goblins, spirits and other beings?

## \|\| 6.19.9 \|\|

*mannāthe bhuvane yoginnocitā gatirīdṛśī \|*  
*jāyāratnamatastvaṃ me dehi ratnabhuje nijam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. O Yogin, this state of affairs is no good in a world with me as the Ruler. Hence you give up your wife, the most excellent lady, to me, the enjoyer of all excellent things.

## \|\| 6.19.10 \|\|

*yāniyāni suratnāni trailokye tāni saṃti me \|*  
*madadhīnaṃ jagatsarvaṃ viddhi tvaṃ sacarācaram \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Know that the whole universe including the mobile and immobile beings is under my suzerainty. All the excellent things of the three worlds have come into my possession.

## \|\| 6.19.11 \|\|

*indrasya gajaratnaṃ coccaiḥśravoratnamuttamam \|*  
*balādgṛhītaṃ sahasā pārijā tatarustathā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. I have forcibly seized the most excellent elephant of Indra, the most excellent horse, Uccaiḥśravas and the celestial tree pārijāta.

## \|\| 6.19.12 \|\|

*vimānaṃ haṃsasaṃyuktamaṃgaṇe mama tiṣṭhati \|*  
*ratnabhūtaṃ mahādivyamuttamaṃ vedhasodbhutam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The wonderfully excellent and the most divine aerial chariot fitted with the swan, belonging to Brahmā is now standing in my court-yard.

## \|\| 6.19.13 \|\|

*mahāpadmādikaṃ divyaṃ nidhiratnaṃ svadasya ca \|*  
*chatraṃ me vāruṇaṃ gehe kāṃcanasrāvi tiṣṭhati \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The divine and excellent treasure Mahāpadma etc. of Kubera is in my custody. The umbrella of Varuṇa stands in my house shedding its golden brilliance.

## \|\| 6.19.14 \|\|

*kiñjalkinī mahāmālā sarvadā'mlānapaṃkajā \|*  
*matpitussā mamaivāsti pāśaśca kaṃpatestathā \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The great garland of never-fading lotuses of fine filaments belonging to my father is as good as mine. The noose of Varuṇa lord of waters is also mine.

## \|\| 6.19.15 \|\|

*mṛtyorutkrāṃtidā śaktirmayā nītā balādvarā \|*  
*dadau mahyaṃ śucirdivye śuciśauce ca vāsasī \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The excellent Javelin of Mṛtyu has been seized by me with force. The god of fire has surrendered to me two clothes purified in fire.

## \|\| 6.19.16 \|\|

*evaṃ yogīndra ratnāni sarvāṇi vilasaṃti me \|*  
*atastvamapi me dehi svastrīratnaṃ jaṭādhara \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Thus, O great Yogin, all excellent things shine in my possession. Hence O ascetic (wearing matted hair) you too surrender your wife the most excellent of all ladies to me.

## \|\| 6.19.17 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*iti śrutvā vacastasya nandinā sa praveśitaḥ \|*  
*jagāmograsabhāṃ rāhurvismayodbhutalocanaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

17\. On hearing his words Rāhu went to Kailāsa and was allowed to enter by Nandin. With surprise and mystery manifest in his eyes, he went to the assembly chamber of Śiva.

## \|\| 6.19.18-20 \|\|

*tatra gatvā śivaṃ sākṣāddevadevaṃ mahāprabhum \|*  
*svatejodhvastatamasaṃ bhasmalepavirājitam \|\| 18 \|\|*

*mahārājopacāre vilasaṃtaṃ mahādbhutam \|*  
*sarvāṅgasundaraṃ divyabhūṣaṇairbhūṣitaṃ haram \|\| 19 \|\|*

*praṇanāma ca taṃ garvāttattejaḥ krāṃtavigrahaḥ \|*  
*nikaṭaṃ gatavāñchaṃbhossa dūto rāhusaṃjñakaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

18-20. On entering it, he saw Śiva, the lord of the gods, the great lord, quelling darkness with his refulgence, shining with ashes smeared (over his body), adorned with all Royal paraphernalia, of wonderful features, exquisite in every limb and embellished with divine ornaments. The emissary named Rāhu bowed to Śiva. His haughtiness subsided by the brilliance of his body. He went near Śiva.

## \|\| 6.19.21 \|\|

*atho tadagra āsīno vaktukāmo hi saiṃhikaḥ \|*  
*tryaṃbakaṃ sa tadā saṃjñāprerito vākyamabravīt \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Rāhu was desirous of speaking to him. He sat in front of Śiva. Urged by his gesture Rāhu spoke to the three-eyed god Śiva.

## \|\| 6.19.22 \|\|

*daityapannagasevyasya trailokyādhipatessadā \|*  
*dūto'haṃ preṣitastena tvatsakāśamihāgataḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

Rāhu said:—

22\. I am the messenger of the lord of the three worlds, worthy of being served for ever by Daityas and serpents. I have come here to you on being sent by him.

## \|\| 6.19.23 \|\|

*\|\| rāhuruvāca \|*  
*jalaṃdharobdhitanayassarvadaityajaneśvaraḥ \|*  
*trailokyasyeśvarassothābhavatsarvādhināyakaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

2 3. The son of the ocean Jalandhara became the lord of all Daityas and now he is the lord of the three worlds. He is the emperor of all.

## \|\| 6.19.24 \|\|

*sa daityarājo balavāndevānāmaṃtakopamaḥ \|*  
*yoginaṃ tvāṃ samuddiśya sa yadāha śṛṇuṣva tat \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. That powerful king of Daityas is like the god of death to the gods. Listen to what he says addressing you the Yogin.

## \|\| 6.19.25 \|\|

*mahādivyaprabhāvasya tasya daityapateḥ prabhoḥ \|*  
*sarvaratneśvarasya tvamājñāṃ śṛṇu vṛṣadhvaja \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. O bull-bannered god, listen to the behest of the lord of Daityas who has divine power and who is the master of all excellent things.

## \|\| 6.19.26 \|\|

*śmaśānavāsino nityamasthimālādharasya ca \|*  
*digaṃbarasya te bhāryā kathaṃ haimavatī śubham \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. How can the auspicious daughter of Himavat be a wife unto you who habitually stay in the cremation ground wearing garlands of bones and assuming the form of a naked ascetic.

## \|\| 6.19.27 \|\|

*ahaṃ ratnādhināthosmi sā ca strīratnasaṃjñitā \|*  
*tasmānmamaiva sā yogyā naiva bhikṣāśinastava \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. I am the possessor of all excellent things. She is the most excellent of all ladies. She deserves me better than you who live on alms.

## \|\| 6.19.28 \|\|

*mama vaśyāstrayo lokā bhuṃje'haṃ makhabhāgakān \|*  
*yāni saṃti trilokesminratnāni mama sadmani \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. The three worlds are under my control. I partake of shares in sacrifices. The excellent things of the three worlds are found in my palace.

## \|\| 6.19.29 \|\|

*vayaṃ ratnabhujastvaṃ tu yogī khalu digambaraḥ \|*  
*svastrīratnaṃ dehi mahyaṃ rājñassukhakarāḥ prajāḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. We are the enjoyers of excellent things. You are a mere naked ascetic and a Yogin. Surrender your wife unto me. Subjects shall always keep their king happy.

## \|\| 6.19.30 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*vadatyevaṃ tathā rāhau bhrūmadhyācchūlapāṇinaḥ \|*  
*abhavatpuruṣo raudrastīvrāśanisamasvanaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

30\. When Rāhu spoke thus, a terrific being resonant like the thunder came out from the space between the eyebrows of the trident-bearing deity.

## \|\| 6.19.31 \|\|

*siṃhāsyapracalajihvassajjvālanayano mahān \|*  
*ūrddhvakeśaśśuṣkatanurnṛsiṃha iva cāparaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. He had a leonine mouth with a moving tongue; his eyes shed fiery flames; his hair stood at its end; his body was dry and rough. He appeared to be the man-lion incarnation of Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 6.19.32 \|\|

*mahātanurmahābāhustālajaṃgho bhayaṃkaraḥ \|*  
*abhidudrāva vegena rāhuṃ sa puruṣo drutam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. He was huge in size. He had long arms. His calves were as stout and huge as the palmyra tree. He was very terrible. He immediately rushed at Rāhu.

## \|\| 6.19.33 \|\|

*sa taṃ khāditu māyāntaṃ dṛṣṭvā rāhurbhayāturaḥ \|*  
*adhāvadāta vegena bahistasya ca dadhāra tam \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. On seeing him rushing to devour, Rāhu was terrified. He ran out when he was caught by the terrible being.

## \|\| 6.19.34 \|\|

*rāhuruvāca \|*  
*devadeva maheśāna pāhi māṃ śaraṇā gatam \|*  
*surā'suraissadā vandyaḥ paramaiśvaryavān prabhuḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

Rāhu said:—

34\. “O great lord, O lord of the gods, save me who have sought refuge in you. You are always worthy of being worshipped by the gods and Asuras. You are the lord endowed with all riches and accomplishments.

## \|\| 6.19.35 \|\|

*brāhmaṇaṃ māṃ mahādeva khādituṃ samupāgataḥ \|*  
*puruṣoyaṃ taveśāna sevakotibhayaṃkaraḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. O great lord, your terrible servant has come here to swallow me, a brahmin.

## \|\| 6.19.36 \|\|

*etasmādrakṣa deveśa śaraṇāgatavatsalaḥ \|*  
*na khādeta yathāyaṃ māṃ namaste'stu muhurmuhuḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. O lord of gods, favourably disposed to your devotees, save me lest he should devour me. Obeisance be to you again and again.”

## \|\| 6.19.37 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*mahādevo vacaḥ śrutvā brāhmaṇasya tadā mune \|*  
*abravītsvagaṇaṃ taṃ vai dīnānāthapriyaḥ prabhuḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

37\. O sage, on hearing the words of the brahmin, the great lord, favourite of the distressed and helpless, spoke to his Gaṇa.

## \|\| 6.19.38 \|\|

*mahādeva uvāca \|*  
*prabhuṃ ca brāhmaṇaṃ dūtaṃ rāhvākhyaṃ śaraṇāgatam \|*  
*śaraṇyā rakṣaṇīyā hi na daṇḍyā gaṇasattama \|\| 38 \|\|*

The great lord said:—

38\. “Leave off this brahmin Rāhu, the emissary who has sought refuge. O excellent Gaṇa, those who seek shelter shall be protected, not punished.”

## \|\| 6.19.39 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityuktau girijeśena sagaṇaḥ karuṇātmanā \|*  
*rāhuṃ tatyāja sahasā brāhmaṇeti śrutākṣaraḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

39\. Commanded thus by the lord of Pārvatī, of sympathetic temperament, the Gaṇa set Rāhu free, immediately on hearing the word brahmin.

## \|\| 6.19.40 \|\|

*rāhuṃ tyaktvāmbare sotha puruṣo dīnayā girā \|*  
*śivopakaṃṭhamāgatya mahādevaṃ vyajijñapat \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. After leaving off Rāhu, the gaṇa came near Śiva and pleaded to the great lord in piteous words.

## \|\| 6.19.41 \|\|

*puruṣa uvāca \|*  
*devadeva mahādeva karuṇākara śaṃkara \|*  
*tyājitaṃ mama bhakṣyaṃ te śaraṇāgatavatsalaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

The gaṇa said:—

41\. O great lord, O lord of the gods, O Śiva the merciful, O deity favourable to the devotees, my prey has been taken away.

## \|\| 6.19.42 \|\|

*kṣudhā māṃ bādhate svāminkṣutkṣāmaścāsmi sarvathā \|*  
*kiṃ bhakṣyaṃ mama deveśa tadājñāpaya māṃ prabho \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. O lord, I am tormented by hunger. So I am utterly emaciated. O lord of the gods, what shall be eaten by me? Please command me, O lord.

## \|\| 6.19.43 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya vacastasya puruṣasya mahāprabhuḥ \|*  
*pratyuvācādbhutotiḥ sa kautukī svahitaṃkaraḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

43\. On hearing these words of the being, the great lord of wonderful sports, eager to help his own persons, replied.

## \|\| 6.19.44 \|\|

*maheśvara uvāca \|*  
*bubhukṣā yadi te'tīva kṣudhā tvāṃ bādhate yadi \|*  
*saṃbhakṣayātmanaśśīghraṃ māṃsaṃ tvaṃ hastapādayoḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

The great lord said:—

44\. “If you are badly in need of food, if hunger torments you, eat up immediately the flesh of your own hands and feet.”

## \|\| 6.19.45 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*śivenaivamājñaptaścakhāda puruṣassvakam \|*  
*hastapādodbhavaṃ māṃsaṃ śiraśśeṣo' bhavadyathā \|\| 45 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

45\. On being commanded thus by Śiva, the being ate up the flesh from his limbs. He was then left only with his head.

## \|\| 6.19.46 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā śirovaśeṣaṃ tu suprasannassadāśivaḥ \|*  
*puruṣaṃ bhīmakarmāṇaṃ tamuvāca savismayaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. On seeing that being of terrible activities, left only with his head, the delighted Sadāśiva spoke smilingly.

## \|\| 6.19.47 \|\|

*śiva uvāca \|*  
*he mahāgaṇa dhanyastvaṃ madājñāpratipālakaḥ \|*  
*saṃtuṣṭaścāsmi te'tīva karmaṇānena sattama \|\| 47 \|\|*

Śiva said:—

47\. “O great Gaṇa, you are blessed since you carried out my behest to the very letter. O excellent one, I am pleased with this action of yours.

## \|\| 6.19.48 \|\|

*tvaṃ kīrtimukhasaṃjño hi bhava maddvārakassadā \|*  
*mahāgaṇo mahāvīrassarvaduṣṭabhayaṃkaraḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. You shall hereafter be known by the title Kīrtimukha. You shall be my door-keeper. You shall be one of my great Gaṇas, very heroic and terrible to all wicked persons.

## \|\| 6.19.49 \|\|

*matpriyastvaṃ madarcāyāṃ sadā pūjyo'hi majjanaiḥ \|*  
*tvadarcāṃ ye na kurvaṃti naiva te matpriyaṃkarāḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. You are my favourite. In the course of my worship, you too shall be worshipped always by my devotees. Those who do not worship you cannot be pleasing to me.”

## \|\| 6.19.50 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*iti śaṃbhorvaraṃ prāpya puruṣaḥ prajaharṣa saḥ \|*  
*tadāprabhṛti deveśa dvāre kīrtimukhaḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

50\. With this excellent blessing from Śiva, he became delighted. From that time onwards Kīrtimukha was stationed at the entrance of the lord of the gods.

## \|\| 6.19.51 \|\|

*pūjanīyo viśeṣeṇa sa gaṇaśśivapūjane \|*  
*nārcayaṃtīha ye pūrvaṃ teṣāmarcā vṛthā bhavet \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. This Gaṇa shall be specially worshipped in the course of the adoration of Śiva. Those who do not worship him at the outset will find their worship in vain.

## Chapter 20 - The fight between the rank and file of the Gaṇas and the Asuras

## \|\| 6.20.1 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*sanatkumāra sarvajña kathā te śrāvitādbhutā \|*  
*mahāprabhośśaṃkarasya yatra līlā ca pāvanī \|\| 1 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:—

1\. O omniscient Sanatkumāra, a wonderful story has been narrated by you, wherein the sanctifying sports of Śiva the great lord are included.

## \|\| 6.20.2 \|\|

*idānīṃ brūhi suprītyā kṛpāṃ kṛtvā mamo pari \|*  
*rāhurmuktaḥ kutra gataḥ puruṣeṇa mahāmune \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Now take pity on me and tell me with pleasure. O great sage, when released by that being where did Rāhu go?

## \|\| 6.20.3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya vacastasya vyāsasyāmitamedhasaḥ \|*  
*pratyuvāca prasannātmā brahmaputro mahāmuniḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sūta said:—

3\. On hearing the words of Vyāsa of immeasurable intelligence, the great sage, the delighted son of Brahmā, replied.

## \|\| 6.20.4 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*rāhurvimukto yastena sopi tadvarvarasthale \|*  
*atassa varvaro bhūta iti bhūmau prathāṃ gataḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

4\. Rāhu had been let off in the land of the outcastes. He too became an outcaste and came to be known in the world as such.

## \|\| 6.20.5 \|\|

*tataḥ sa manyamānassvaṃ punarjanimathānataḥ \|*  
*gatagarvo jagāmātha jalaṃdharapuraṃ śanaiḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Considering that as his second birth he became humble. He became free from haughtiness. He slowly wended his way to the city of Jalandhara.

## \|\| 6.20.6 \|\|

*jalaṃdharāya so'bhyetya sarvamīśaviceṣṭitam \|*  
*kathayāmāsa tadvyāsādvyāsa daityeśvarāya vai \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. After approaching Jalandhara the lord of Daityas, he explained everything concerning Śiva in detail, O Vyāsa.

## \|\| 6.20.7 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*jalaṃdharastu tacchrutvā kopākulitavigrahaḥ \|*  
*babhūva balavānsindhuputro daityendrasattamaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. On hearing it, the powerful son of the ocean, the excellent lord of Daityas, Jalandhara became furious from head to foot.

## \|\| 6.20.8 \|\|

*tataḥ kopaparādhīnamānaso daityasattamaḥ \|*  
*udyogaṃ sarvasainyānāṃ daityānāmādideśa ha \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Then the infuriated excellent Daitya commanded the entire army of the Daityas to enter into the fray.

## \|\| 6.20.9-10 \|\|

*\|\| jalaṃdhara uvāca \|*  
*nirgacchaṃtvakhilā daityāḥ kālanemimukhāḥ khalu \|*  
*tathā śuṃbhaniśumbhādyā vīrāssvabalasaṃyutāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*koṭirvīrakulotpannāḥ kaṃbuvaṃśyāśca daurhṛdāḥ \|*  
*kālakāḥ kālakeyāśca mauryā dhaumrāstathaiva ca \|\| 10 \|\|*

Jalandhara said:—

9-10. Let all the Asuras such as Kālanemi and others set out with their entire divisions; Śumbha, Niśumbha and other heroes; the descendants of Koṭivīra, the scions of the family of Kambu. Daurhṛdas, Kalakas, Kālakeyas, Mauryas and Dhaumras—let all these start for the fight.

## \|\| 6.20.11 \|\|

*ityājñāpyāsurapatissiṃdhuputro pratāpavān \|*  
*nirjagāmāśu daityānāṃ koṭibhiḥ parivāritaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. After ordering thus, the lord of the Asuras the valorous son of the ocean set out quickly accompanied by crores of Daityas.

## \|\| 6.20.12 \|\|

*tatastasyāgrataśśukro rāhuśchinnaśiro'bhavat \|*  
*mukuṭaścāpatadbhūmau vegātpraskhalitastadā \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Then Śukra and Rāhu with his head severed went ahead of him. In his quick jerky movement, his crown became dislodged and fell on the ground.

## \|\| 6.20.13 \|\|

*vyarājata nabhaḥ pūrṇaṃ prāvṛṣīva yathā ghanaiḥ \|*  
*jātā aśakunā bhūri mahānidrāvi sūcakāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The sky was entirely enveloped by clouds as in the rainy season. Many ill omens occurred portending great slumber.

## \|\| 6.20.14 \|\|

*tasyodyogaṃ tathā dṛṣṭvā gīrvāṇāste savāsavāḥ \|*  
*alakṣitāstadā jagmuḥ kailāsaṃ śaṃkarālayam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. On seeing his enterprise, the gods including Indra went to Kailāsa, the abode of Śiva without being observed.

## \|\| 6.20.15 \|\|

*tatra gatvā śivaṃ dṛṣṭvā supraṇamya savāsavāḥ \|*  
*devāssarve nataskaṃdhāḥ karau baddhvā ca tuṣṭuvuḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. After going there and seeing Śiva, the gods including Indra, bowed to him with stooping shoulders. They joined their palms in reverence and eulogised.

## \|\| 6.20.16 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*devadeva mahādeva karuṇākara śaṃkara \|*  
*namastestu maheśāna pāhi naśśaraṇāgatān \|\| 16 \|\|*

The gods said:—

16\. O great lord, lord of the gods, O Śiva the merciful, obeisance be to you. Save us who have sought refuge in you.

## \|\| 6.20.17 \|\|

*vihvalā vayamatyugraṃ jalaṃdharakṛtātprabho \|*  
*upadravātsadevendrāḥ sthānabhraṣṭāḥ kṣitisthitāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. O lord, we are very much distressed by this harassment. All including Indra are deposed and compelled to stay on the earth.

## \|\| 6.20.18 \|\|

*na jānāsi kathaṃ svāmindevāpattimimāṃ prabho \|*  
*tasmānno rakṣaṇārthāya jahi sāgaranandanam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. O lord, how is it possible that you do not know this adversity of the gods? Hence in order to protect us please kill him.

## \|\| 6.20.19 \|\|

*asmākaṃ rakṣaṇārthāya yatpūrvaṃ garuḍadhvajaḥ \|*  
*niyojitastvayā nātha na kṣamasso'dya rakṣitum \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. O lord, Viṣṇu who was assigned by you the task of protection is now unable to protect us.

## \|\| 6.20.20 \|\|

*tadadhīno gṛhe tasya tiṣṭhatyadya mayā saha \|*  
*vayaṃ ca tatra tiṣṭhāmastadājñāvaśagāssurāḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. He is also subservient to him and stays in his mansion along with Lakṣmī. All of us gods stay there obeying his behests.

## \|\| 6.20.21 \|\|

*alakṣitā vayaṃ cātrāgatāśśaṃbho tvadaṃtikam \|*  
*sa āyāti tvayā karttuṃ raṇaṃ siṃdhusuto balī \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. O Śiva, we have approached you unobserved by him. That powerful son of the ocean is coming hither to fight with you.

## \|\| 6.20.22 \|\|

*atassvāminraṇe tvaṃ tamavilaṃbaṃ jalaṃdharam \|*  
*haṃtumarhasi sarvajña pāhi naśśaraṇāgatān \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. O omniscient lord, you shall kill Jalandhara in the battle without delay. Save us who have sought refuge in you.

## \|\| 6.20.23 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityuktvā te surāssarve prabhuṃ natvā savāsavāḥ \|*  
*pādau nirīkṣya saṃtasthurmaheśasya vinamrakāḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

23\. After saying this, the gods including Indra bowed to him and stood humbly glancing at the feet of lord Śiva.

## \|\| 6.20.24 \|\|

*\|\| sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*iti devavacaḥ śrutvā prahasya vṛṣabhadhvajaḥ \|*  
*drutaṃ viṣṇuṃ samāhūya vacanaṃ cedamabravīt \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. On hearing the words of the gods the bull-bannered deity laughed. He called Viṣṇu immediately and spoke these words.

## \|\| 6.20.25 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*hṛṣīkeśa mahāviṣṇo devāścātra samāgatāḥ \|*  
*jalaṃdharakṛtāpīḍāśśaraṇaṃ me'tivihvalāḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

The lord Śiva said:—

25\. O great Viṣṇu, the distressed gods harassed by Jalandhara have sought refuge in me.

## \|\| 6.20.26 \|\|

*jalaṃdharaḥ kathaṃ viṣṇo saṃgare na hata stvayā \|*  
*tadgṛhaṃ cāpi yāto'si tyaktvā vaikuṇṭhamātmanaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. O Viṣṇu, how is it that Jalandhara was not killed in battle by you? Leaving off your own Vaikuṇṭha you have gone to his mansion?

## \|\| 6.20.27 \|\|

*mayā niyojitastvaṃ hi sādhusaṃrakṣaṇāya ca \|*  
*nigrahāya khalānāṃ ca svataṃtreṇa vihāriṇā \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. As I wanted to be free and sportful, I had appointed you for the protection of the good and the curbing of the wicked.

## \|\| 6.20.28 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya maheśasya vacanaṃ garuḍadhvajaḥ \|*  
*pratyuvāca vinītātmā natakassāñjalirhariḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

28\. On hearing the words of lord Śiva, Viṣṇu replied humbly bowing down with palms joined in reverence.

## \|\| 6.20.29 \|\|

*viṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*tavāṃśasaṃbhavatvācca bhrātṛtvācca tathā śriyaḥ \|*  
*mayā na nihataḥ saṃkhye tvamenaṃ jahi dānavam \|\| 29 \|\|*

Viṣṇu said:—

29\. He was not killed in war by me because he was born of a part of yours. Moreover he is Lakṣmī’s brother. Please kill him.

## \|\| 6.20.30 \|\|

*mahābalo mahāvīro jeyassarvadivaukasām \|*  
*anyeṣāṃ cāpi deveśa satyametadbravīmyaham \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. O lord of the gods, he is very powerful, heroic and indefatigable by all the heaven-dwellers and others too. I am telling you the truth.

## \|\| 6.20.31 \|\|

*mayā kṛto raṇastena ciraṃ devānvitena vai \|*  
*madupāyo na pravṛttastasmindānavapuṃgave \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. In fact a war was fought with him by me in the company of the gods. But my strategy was ineffective in regard to this great Dānava.

## \|\| 6.20.32 \|\|

*tatparākramatastuṣṭo varaṃ brūhītyahaṃ khalu \|*  
*iti madvacanaṃ śrutvā sa vavre varamuttamam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. I told him “I am delighted with your valour. Tell me the boon you wish to have”. On hearing these words of mine he chose an excellent boon.

## \|\| 6.20.33 \|\|

*madbhaginyā mayā sārddhaṃ madgehe sasuro vasa \|*  
*madadhīno mahāviṣṇo ityahaṃ tadgṛhaṃ gataḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. “O great Viṣṇu please stay in my mansion subservient to me along with my sister, the gods and myself.” So I went to his mansion.

## \|\| 6.20.34 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*iti viṣṇorvacaśśrutvā śakarassa maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*vihasyovāca suprītassadayo bhaktavatsalaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

34\. On hearing the words of Viṣṇu, lord Śiva who is favourably disposed to his devotees laughed and said delightedly and sympathetically.

## \|\| 6.20.35 \|\|

*maheśvara uvāca \|*  
*he viṣṇo suravarya tvaṃ śṛṇu madvākyamādarāt \|*  
*jalaṃdharaṃ mahādaityaṃ haniṣyāmi na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

The great lord Śiva said:—

35\. O Viṣṇu, foremost among the gods, please listen to my words attentively. I will kill the great Daitya Jalandhara. There is no doubt about this.

## \|\| 6.20.36 \|\|

*svasthānaṃ gaccha nirbhīto devā gacchaṃtvapi dhruvam \|*  
*nirbhayā vītasaṃdehā hataṃ matvā'surādhipam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Go back to your abode fearlessly. Let the gods too go back without fear and hesitation, considering the ruler of the Asuras already killed.

## \|\| 6.20.37 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*iti śrutvā maheśasya vacanaṃ sa ramāpatiḥ \|*  
*sanirjaro jagāmāśu svasthānaṃ gatasaṃśayaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

37\. On hearing the words of lord Śiva, the lord of Lakṣmī immediately went to his abode without doubts along with the gods.

## \|\| 6.20.38 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare vyāsa sa daityendro'tivikramaḥ \|*  
*sannaddhairasuraissārddhaṃ śailaprāṃtaṃ yayau balī \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. In the meantime, O Vyāsa, that valorous king of the Daityas went along with the well-equipped Asuras to the outskirts of the mountain.

## \|\| 6.20.39 \|\|

*kailāsamavarudhyātha mahatyā senayā yutaḥ \|*  
*saṃtasthau kālasaṃkāśaḥ kurvansiṃharavaṃ mahān \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Accompanied by a vast army he laid siege to Kailāsa. He stood there like the god of death roaring like a lion.

## \|\| 6.20.40 \|\|

*atha kolāhalaṃ śrutvā daityanādasamudbhavam \|*  
*cukrodhātimaheśāno mahālīlaḥ khalāṃtakaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. On hearing the tumultuous roar of the Daityas, lord Śiva of great sports, the destroyer of the wicked, became very furious.

## \|\| 6.20.41 \|\|

*samādideśa saṃkhyāya svagaṇānsa mahābalān \|*  
*naṃdyādikānmahādevo mahotiḥ kautukī haraḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. The great lord of various sports, the enthusiastic Śiva commanded his powerful Gaṇas, Nandin and others, severally.

## \|\| 6.20.42 \|\|

*nandībhamukhasenānīmukhāssarve śivājñayā \|*  
*gaṇāśca samanahyaṃta yuddhāyā titvarānvitāḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Nandin, Vighneśvara, Kumāra and all other Gaṇas, at the bidding of Śiva hurriedly got ready for the battle.

## \|\| 6.20.43 \|\|

*avaterurgaṇāssarve kailāsātkrodhadurmadāḥ \|*  
*valgato raṇaśabdāṃśca mahāvīrā raṇāya hi \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. The infuriated and invincible Gaṇas descended from Kailāsa heroically shouting war cries and leaping to fight.

## \|\| 6.20.44 \|\|

*tatassamabhavadyuddhaṃ kailāsopatyakāsu vai \|*  
*pramathādhipadaityānāṃ ghoraṃ śastrāstrasaṃkulam \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Then at the ridges, valleys and sides of Kailāsa, a terrible battle was fought between the leaders of the Pramathas and the Daityas. Weapons clashed with weapons.

## \|\| 6.20.45 \|\|

*bherīmṛdaṃgaśaṃkhaughairnisvānairvīraharṣaṇaiḥ \|*  
*gajāśvarathaśabdaiśca nāditā bhūrvyakaṃpata \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. The whole earth shook resonant with the sounds of great war drums, Mṛdaṅgas and conches that inspired the heroes as well as the sounds of elephants, horses and chariots.

## \|\| 6.20.46 \|\|

*śaktitomarabāṇaughairmusalaiḥ pāśapaṭṭiśaiḥ \|*  
*vyarājata nabhaḥ pūrṇaṃ muktābhiriva saṃvṛtam \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. The whole atmosphere was filled with javeline, iron clubs, arrows, great pestles, iron rods, pikes etc. as if strewn with pearls.

## \|\| 6.20.47 \|\|

*nihatairiva nāgāśvaiḥ pattibhirbhūrvyarājata \|*  
*vajrāhataiḥ parvatendraiḥ pūrvamāsītsusaṃvṛtā \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. With the dead elephants, horses and foot soldiers, the earth shone in the same way as before when great mountains were scattered, smitten by the thunderbolt of Indra.

## \|\| 6.20.48 \|\|

*pramathāhatadaityaughairdaityāhatagaṇaistathā \|*  
*vasāsṛṅmāṃsapaṃkāḍhyā bhūragamyābhavattadā \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. With the groups of Daityas killed by the Pramathas, and with the Gaṇas killed by the Daityas, the whole ground was filled with suets, flesh and streams of blood. It became so marshy as it became impassable.

## \|\| 6.20.49 \|\|

*pramathāhatadaityaughānbhārgavassamajīvayat \|*  
*yuddhe punaḥ punaścaiva mṛtasaṃjīvanī balāt \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. With the power of Sañjīvanī, Bhārgava resuscitated the forces of the Daityas killed by the Pramathas in the battle again and again.

## \|\| 6.20.50 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā vyākulitāṃstāṃstu gaṇāssarve bhayārditāḥ \|*  
*śaśaṃsurdevadevāya sarve śukraviceṣṭitam \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. On seeing them, all the Gaṇas were agitated and terrified. They intimated to the lord of the gods what Śukra did.

## \|\| 6.20.51 \|\|

*tacchrutvā bhagavānrudraścakāra krodhamulbaṇam \|*  
*bhayaṃkaro'tiraudraśca babhūva prajvalandiśaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. On hearing it, lord Śiva became terribly furious. He became terrific blazing the quarters as it were.

## \|\| 6.20.52 \|\|

*atha rudramukhātkṛtyā babhūvātīvabhīṣaṇā \|*  
*tālajaṃghodarī vaktrā stanāpīḍitabhūruhā \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. A terrible Kṛtyā came out of Rudra’s mouth. Her calves were as stout as Palmyra trees. Her mouth was huge and deep like mountain caverns. With her breasts she crushed huge trees.

## \|\| 6.20.53 \|\|

*sā yuddhabhūmiṃ tarasā sasāda munisattama \|*  
*vicacāra mahābhīmā bhakṣayaṃtī mahāsurān \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. O excellent sage, she rushed immediately to the battle ground. The terrible Kṛtyā roamed the battleground devouring the great Asuras.

## \|\| 6.20.54 \|\|

*atha sā raṇamadhye hi jagāma gatabhīrdrutam \|*  
*yatrāste saṃvṛto daityavarendraissa hi bhārgavaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Fearlessly she rushed amid the battle-field where Bhargava was stationed surrounded by the leading Daityas.

## \|\| 6.20.55 \|\|

*svatejasā nabho vyāpya bhūmiṃ kṛtvā ca sā mune \|*  
*bhārgavaṃ svabhage dhṛtvā jagāmāṃtarhitā nabhaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. O sage, she enveloped the whole sky with her terrible brilliance. She split the ground she trod; she stuffed Bhārgava into her vaginal passage and vanished in the sky.

## \|\| 6.20.56 \|\|

*vidrutaṃ bhārgavaṃ dṛṣṭvā daityasainyagaṇāstathā \|*  
*pramlānavadanā yuddhānnirjagmuryuddhadurmadāḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. On seeing Bhārgava seized, the invincible armies of the Daityas became dejected and faded in their faces. They fled from the battle ground.

## \|\| 6.20.57 \|\|

*atho'bhajyata daityānāṃ senā gaṇabhayārditā \|*  
*vāyuvegahatā yadvatprakīrṇā tṛṇasaṃhatiḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. The army of the Daityas became scattered and split in their terrific fear of the Gaṇas like bundles of grass split and scattered when blown by the wind.

## \|\| 6.20.58 \|\|

*bhagnāṃ gaṇabhayāddaityasenāṃ dṛṣṭvātimarṣitāḥ \|*  
*niśuṃbhaśuṃbhau senānyau kālanemiśca cukrudhuḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. On seeing the army of the Daityas thus dispersed and frightened of the Gaṇas, the leaders Śumbha and Niśumbha and Kālanemi became infuriated.

## \|\| 6.20.59 \|\|

*trayaste varayāmāsurgaṇasenāṃ mahābalāḥ \|*  
*muṃcaṃtaśśaravarṣāṇi prāvṛṣīva balāhakāḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. All the three powerful Daityas obstructed the army of the Gaṇas showering arrows like the destructive clouds in the rainy season.

## \|\| 6.20.60 \|\|

*tato daityaśaraughāste śalabhānāmiva vrajāḥ \|*  
*rurudhuḥ khaṃ diśassarvā gaṇasenāmakaṃpayan \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. The volleys of arrows discharged by the Daityas enveloped all the quarters and the atmosphere like huge swarms of locusts. They shook the hosts of Gaṇas.

## \|\| 6.20.61 \|\|

*gaṇāśśaraśatairbhinnā rudhirāsāravarṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*vasaṃtakiṃśukābhāsā na prājānanhi kiṃcana \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Split by hundreds of arrows, the Gaṇas shed streams of blood. They resembled the red Kiṃśuka flowers of the spring season. They did not know what to do.

## \|\| 6.20.62 \|\|

*tataḥ prabhagnaṃ svabalaṃ vilokya nandyādilaṃbodarakārttikeyāḥ \|*  
*tvarānvitā daityavarānprasahya nivārayāmāsuramarṣaṇāste \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. On seeing their army thus shattered, the infuriated leaders Nandin, Gaṇeśa and Kārttikeya hurriedly checked the rushing Daityas.

## Chapter 21 - Description of the Special War

## \|\| 6.21.1 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*te gaṇādhipatīndṛṣṭvā nandībhamukhaṣaṇmukhān \|*  
*amarṣādabhyadhāvaṃta dvaṃdvayuddhāya dānavāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

1\. On seeing the leaders of the Gaṇas, Nandin, Gaṇeśa and Kārttikeya, the Dānavas rushed at them for a duel combat.

## \|\| 6.21.2 \|\|

*nandinaṃ kālanemiśca śuṃbho laṃbodaraṃ tathā \|*  
*niśuṃbhaḥ ṣaṇmukhaṃ devamabhyadhāvata śaṃkitaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Kālanemi clashed with Nandin; Śumbha fought Gaṇeśa and Niśumbha hesitatingly rushed at Kārttikeya.

## \|\| 6.21.3 \|\|

*niśuṃbhaḥ kārtikeyasya mayūraṃ paṃcabhiśśaraiḥ \|*  
*hṛdi vivyādha vegena mūrchitassa papāta ha \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. With five arrows Niśumbha hit the peacock of Kārttikeya in the chest and it fell unconscious.

## \|\| 6.21.4 \|\|

*tataḥ śaktidharaḥ kruddho bāṇaiḥ paṃcabhireva ca \|*  
*vivyādha syaṃdane tasya hayānyantārameva ca \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Then the infuriated Kārttikeya discharged five arrows at his chariot and pierced the horses and the charioteer.

## \|\| 6.21.5 \|\|

*śareṇānyena tīkṣṇena niśuṃbhaṃ devavairiṇam \|*  
*jaghāna tarasā vīro jagarja raṇadurmadaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The invincible hero hit Niśumbha with another sharp arrow quickly and roared.

## \|\| 6.21.6 \|\|

*asuro'pi niśuṃbhākhyo mahāvīro'tivīryavān \|*  
*jaghāna kārtikeyaṃ taṃ garjaṃtaṃ sveṣuṇā raṇe \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The Asura Niśumbha of great prowess and heroism hit Kārttikeya in the battle with his arrow as he roared.

## \|\| 6.21.7 \|\|

*tataśśaktiṃ kārtikeyo yāvajagrāha roṣataḥ \|*  
*tāvanniśuṃbho vegena svaśaktyā tamapātayat \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. By the time the furious Kārttikeya seized his spear, Niśumbha struck him with it.

## \|\| 6.21.8 \|\|

*evaṃ babhūva tatraiva kārtikeyaniśuṃbhayoḥ \|*  
*āhavo hi mahānvyāsa vīraśabdaṃ pragarjatoḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Thus, O Vyāsa, a great fight between Kārttikeya and Niśumbha ensued as they shouted heroically.

## \|\| 6.21.9 \|\|

*tato nandīśvaro bāṇaiḥ kālanemimavidhyata \|*  
*saptabhiśca hayānketuṃ rathaṃ sārathimācchinat \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Then Nandin hit Kālanemi with seven arrows and pierced his horses, banner, chariot and charioteer.

## \|\| 6.21.10 \|\|

*kālanemiśca saṃkuddho dhanuściccheda naṃdinaḥ \|*  
*svaśarāsananirmuktairmahātīkṣṇaiśśilīmukhaiḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. With very sharp shafts discharged from his bow, the infuriated Kālanemi cut the bow of Nandin.

## \|\| 6.21.11 \|\|

*atha nandīśvaro vīraḥ kālanemiṃ mahāsuram \|*  
*tamapāsya ca śūlena vakṣasyabhyahanaddṛḍham \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Defying the great demon Kālanemi the heroic Nandīśvara hit him in the chest with his spear.

## \|\| 6.21.12 \|\|

*sa śūlabhinnahṛdayo hatāśvo hatasārathiḥ \|*  
*adreḥ śikharamutpāṭya nandinaṃ samatāḍayat \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. With his horses and charioteer killed and himself wounded in the chest, he broke the top of a mountain and hit Nandin.

## \|\| 6.21.13 \|\|

*atha śuṃbho gaṇeśaśca rathamūṣaka vāhanau \|*  
*yudhyamānau śaravrātaiḥ parasparamavidhyatām \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Then Śumbha and Gaṇeśa seated respectively in a chariot and on a mouse fought each other with volleys of arrows.

## \|\| 6.21.14 \|\|

*gaṇeśastu tadā śuṃbhaṃ hṛdi vivyādha patriṇā \|*  
*sārathiṃ ca tribhirbāṇaiḥ pātayāmāsa bhūtale \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Gaṇeśa hit Śumbha in his chest with an arrow and felled his charioteer with three arrows on the ground.

## \|\| 6.21.15 \|\|

*tato'tikruddhaśśuṃbho'pi bāṇadṛṣṭyā gaṇādhipam \|*  
*mūṣakaṃ ca tribhirviddhvā nanāda jaladasvanaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Then the infuriated Śumbha covered Gaṇeśa with a shower of arrows. Hitting the mouse with three arrows he roared like thunder.

## \|\| 6.21.16 \|\|

*mūṣakaśśarabhinnāṅgaścacāla dṛḍhavedanaḥ \|*  
*lambodaraśca patitaḥ padātirabhavatsa hi \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The mouse pierced by the arrows, shook with acute pain. Gaṇeśa was thrown off (his vehicle) and he became a foot soldier (as it were).

## \|\| 6.21.17 \|\|

*tato lambodaraśśuṃbhaṃ hatvā paraśunā hṛdi \|*  
*apātayattadā bhūmau mūṣakaṃ cāruroha saḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Then Gaṇeśa hit Śumbha in his chest with his axe and felled him to the ground. Thereafter he mounted his mouse again.

## \|\| 6.21.18 \|\|

*samarāyodyataścābhūtpunargajamukho vibhuḥ \|*  
*prahasya jaghnatuḥ krodhāttotreṇaiva mahādvipam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Lord Gaṇeśa of elephantine face got ready for the fight. He hit him mockingly and angrily as if hitting a great elephant with a goad.

## \|\| 6.21.19 \|\|

*kālanemirniśuṃbhaśca hyubhau laṃbodaraṃ śaraiḥ \|*  
*yugapaccakhnatuḥ krodhādāśīviṣasamairdrutam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Kālanemi and Śumbha simultaneously attacked Gaṇeśa furiously with arrows as ruthless as serpents.

## \|\| 6.21.20 \|\|

*taṃ pīḍyamānamālokya vīrabhadro mahābalaḥ \|*  
*abhyadhāvata vegena koṭibhūtayutastathā \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. On seeing him afflicted, the powerful Vīrabhadra accompanied by a crore goblins rushed in.

## \|\| 6.21.21 \|\|

*kūṣmāṃḍā bhairavāścāpi vetālā yoginīgaṇāḥ \|*  
*piśācā ḍākinīsaṃghā gaṇāścāpi samaṃ yayuḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. The Kūṣmāṇḍas, Bhairavas, Vetālas, Yoginīs, Piśācas, Ḍākinīs and Gaṇas came there with him.

## \|\| 6.21.22 \|\|

*tataḥ kilakilā śabdaissiṃhanādaiśsaghargharaiḥ \|*  
*vināditā ḍamarukaiḥ pṛthivī samakaṃpata \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The Earth, resonant with various kinds of noise, shouts of joy, leonine roars and the sounds of Ḍamarukas, quaked.

## \|\| 6.21.23 \|\|

*tato bhūtāḥ pradhāvaṃto bhakṣayaṃti sma dānavān \|*  
*utpatya pātayaṃti sma nanṛtuśca raṇāṃgaṇe \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Then the Bhūtas ran here and there devouring the Dānavas. They jumped up and danced in the battle field and threw the Asura on the ground.

## \|\| 6.21.24 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare vyāsābhūtāṃ nandīguhaśca tau \|*  
*utthitāvāptasaṃjñau hi jagarjaturalaṃ raṇe \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. In the meantime, O Vyāsa, Nandin and Guha regained their consciousness and got up. They roared in the battlefield again.

## \|\| 6.21.25 \|\|

*sa nandī kārtikeyaśca samāyātau tvarānvitau \|*  
*jaghnatuśca raṇe daityānniraṃtaraśaravrajaiḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Nandin and Kārttikeya came hurriedly and struck the Daityas in the battle ground with incessant volleys of arrows.

## \|\| 6.21.26 \|\|

*chinnairbhinnairhatairdaityaiḥ patitairbhakṣitaistathā \|*  
*vyākulā sābhavatsenā viṣaṇṇavadanā tadā \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Then the army of the Daityas became agitated and dejected with many Daityas wounded, split, killed, felled to the ground and devoured.

## \|\| 6.21.27 \|\|

*evaṃ nandī kārtikeyo vikaṭaśca pratāpavān \|*  
*vīrabhadro gaṇāścānye jagarjussamare'dhikam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Thus Nandin, Kārttikeya the formidable and valorous, Vīrabhadra and the other Gaṇas roared much in the battle.

## \|\| 6.21.28 \|\|

*niśuṃbhaśuṃbhau senānyau sindhuputrasya tau tathā \|*  
*kālanemirmahādaityo'surāścānye parājitāḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Then those two generals of the son of the ocean, Niśumbha and Śumbha, the great Daitya Kālanemi and the other Asuras were defeated.

## \|\| 6.21.29 \|\|

*pravidhvastāṃ tatassenāṃ dṛṣṭvā sāgaranandanaḥ \|*  
*rathenātipatākena gaṇānabhiyayau balī \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. On seeing the army destroyed, the powerful son of the ocean rushed at the Gaṇas in his chariot of waving and wafting colours.

## \|\| 6.21.30 \|\|

*tataḥ parājitā daityā apyabhūvanmahotsavāḥ \|*  
*jagarjuradhikaṃ vyāsa samarāyodyatāstadā \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Thereat even the defeated Daityas became jubilant. O Vyāsa, they roared much and got ready for the fray.

## \|\| 6.21.31 \|\|

*sarve rudragaṇāścāpi jagarjurjayaśālinaḥ \|*  
*nandikārtikadaṃtyāsyavīrabhadrādikā mune \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. The victorious Gaṇas of Śiva too roared, led by Nandin, Kārttikeya, Gaṇeśa and Vīrabhadara, O sage.

## \|\| 6.21.32 \|\|

*hastyaśvarathasaṃhrādaśśaṃkhabherīravastathā \|*  
*abhavatsiṃhanādaśca senayorubhayostathā \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. The trumpets of the elephants, the neighing of the horses, the rumbling of the chariots, the sounds of the conches and war-drums and the leonine roars of the armies rose up.

## \|\| 6.21.33 \|\|

*jalaṃdharaśaravrātairnīhārapaṭalairiva \|*  
*dyāvāpṛthivyorācchannamaṃtaraṃ samapadyata \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The space between heaven and the earth became enveloped by the many arrows discharged by Jalandhara as if by floating masses of mist.

## \|\| 6.21.34 \|\|

*śailādiṃ paṃcabhirviddhvā gaṇeśaṃ paṃcabhiśśaraiḥ \|*  
*vīrabhadraṃ ca viṃśatyā nanāda jaladasvanaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Hitting Nandin and Gaṇeśa with five arrows each and Vīrabhadra with twenty he roared like thunder.

## \|\| 6.21.35 \|\|

*kārtikeyastato daityaṃ śaktyā vivyādha satvaram \|*  
*jalaṃdharaṃ mahāvīro rudraputro nanāda ca \|\| 35 \|\|*
