35\. Kārttikeya the heroic son of Śiva then swiftly hit the Daitya Jalandhara with his spear and roared.

## \|\| 6.21.36 \|\|

*sa pūrṇanayano daityaḥ śaktinirbhinnadehakaḥ \|*  
*papāta bhūmau tvaritamudatiṣṭhanmahābalaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. With the body pierced through by the spear, the Daitya fell on the ground with eyes rolling. But the powerful Asura swiftly stood up.

## \|\| 6.21.37 \|\|

*tataḥ krodhaparītātmā kārtikeyaṃ jalaṃdharaḥ \|*  
*gadayā tāḍayāmāsa hṛdaye daityapuṃgavaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Then Jalandhara the infuriated leader of the Daityas hit Kārttikeya in his chest with his mace.

## \|\| 6.21.38 \|\|

*gadāprabhāvaṃ saphalaṃ darśayanśaṃkarātmajaḥ \|*  
*vidhidattavarādvyāsa sa tūrṇaṃ bhūtale'patat \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. O Vyāsa, plainly exhibiting the successful efficiency of the Mace secured as a favour from Brahmā Kārttikeya fell on the ground suddenly.

## \|\| 6.21.39 \|\|

*tathaiva naṃdī hyapatadbhūtale gadayā hataḥ \|*  
*mahāvīro'pi ripuhā kiṃcidvyākulamānasaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Similarly, struck by the mace Nandin too fell on the ground, He was distressed a little although he was a great hero and a destroyer of enemies.

## \|\| 6.21.40 \|\|

*tato gaṇeśvaraḥ kruddhassmṛtvā śivapadāmbujam \|*  
*saṃprāpyātibalo daitya gadāṃ paraśunācchinat \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Then the infuriated hero Gaṇeśa came there after remembering the lotus like feet of Śiva and split the mace of the Daitya with his axe.

## \|\| 6.21.41 \|\|

*vīrabhadrastribhirbāṇairhṛdi vivyādha dānavam \|*  
*saptabhiśca hayānketuṃ dhanuśchatraṃ ca cicchide \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Vīrabhadra then hit the Dānava in his chest with three arrows. He cut off the banner, umbrella, bow and the horses of the Daitya with seven arrows.

## \|\| 6.21.42 \|\|

*tato'tikruddho daityendraśśaktimudyamya dāruṇām \|*  
*gaṇeśaṃ pātayāmāsa rathamanyaṃ samāruhat \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Then the infuriated leader of the Daityas lifted up his terrible Śakti and felled Gaṇeśa. He mounted another chariot then.

## \|\| 6.21.43 \|\|

*abhyagādatha vegena sa daityendro mahābalaḥ \|*  
*vigaṇayya hṛdā taṃ vai vīrabhadraṃ ruṣānvitaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. The powerful leader of the Daityas did not mind Vīrabhadra at all. Angrily he rushed at him.

## \|\| 6.21.44 \|\|

*vīrabhadraṃ jaghānāśu tīkṣṇenāśīviṣeṇa tam \|*  
*nanāda ca mahāvīro daityarājo jalaṃdharaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Jalandhara, the heroic king of Daityas, hit Vīrabhadra with a fierce arrow and roared.

## \|\| 6.21.45 \|\|

*vīrabhadro'pi saṃkuddhassitadhāreṇa ceṣuṇā \|*  
*ciccheda taccharaṃ caiva vivyādha maheṣuṇā \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. The infuriated Vīrabhadra split that arrow with a sharp-edged arrow. With another great arrow he hit him too.

## \|\| 6.21.46 \|\|

*tatastau sūryasaṃkāśau yuyudhāte parasparam \|*  
*nānāśastraistathāstraiśca ciraṃ vīravarottamau \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Then both of them, the most excellent of heroes refulgent like the sun, fought each other with different kinds of weapons and missiles.

## \|\| 6.21.47 \|\|

*vīrabhadrastatastasya hayānbāṇairapātayat \|*  
*dhanuściccheda rathinaḥ patākāṃ cāpi vegataḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Vīrabhadra then felled his horses with his arrows. He forcefully cut off him bow and flags too.

## \|\| 6.21.48 \|\|

*atho sa daityarājo hi pupluve parighāyudhaḥ \|*  
*vīrabhadropakaṭhaṃ sa drutamāpa mahābalaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Then the king of the Daityas leapt up to him with a great iron club. That powerful warrior reached very near Vīrabhadra very quickly.

## \|\| 6.21.49 \|\|

*parighenātimahatā vīrabhadraṃ jaghāna ha \|*  
*sabalo'bdhitanayo mūrdhni vīro jagarja ca \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. The heroic and powerful son of the ocean hit Vīrabhadra on his head with his great iron club. He then roared.

## \|\| 6.21.50 \|\|

*parighenātimahatā bhinnamūrddhā gaṇādhipaḥ \|*  
*vīrabhadraḥ papātorvyāṃ mumoca rudhiraṃ bahu \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Vīrabhadra, the leader of the Gaṇas, fell on the ground with his head shattered by the iron club and shed much blood.

## \|\| 6.21.51 \|\|

*patitaṃ vīrabhadraṃ tu dṛṣṭvā rudragaṇā bhayāt \|*  
*apāgacchanraṇaṃ hitvā krośamānā maheśvaram \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. On seeing Vīrabhadra fallen, the terrified Gaṇas abandoned the battle ground shrieking and fled to lord Śiva.

## \|\| 6.21.52 \|\|

*atha kolāhalaṃ śrutvā gaṇānāṃ candraśekharaḥ \|*  
*nijapārśvasthitān vīrānapṛcchadgaṇasattamān \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. On hearing the tumultuous uproar of the Gaṇas, the moon-crested lord asked the excellent Gaṇas, the heroes standing near him.

## \|\| 6.21.53 \|\|

*śaṃkara uvāca \|*  
*kimarthaṃ madgaṇānāṃ hi mahākolāhalo'bhavat \|*  
*vicāryatāṃ mahāvīrāśśāṃtiḥ kāryā mayā dhruvam \|\| 53 \|\|*

Śiva said:—

53\. How is this tumultuous uproar among my Gaṇas? O heroes, let this be enquired into. Peace shall be established by me, of course.

## \|\| 6.21.54 \|\|

*yāvatsa deveśo gaṇānpapraccha sādaram \|*  
*tāvadgaṇavarāste hi samāyātāḥ prabhuṃ prati \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Even as the lord of the gods was conducting the enquiry, the leaders of the Gaṇas approached the lord.

## \|\| 6.21.55 \|\|

*tāndṛṣṭvā vikalānrudraḥ papraccha iti kuśalaṃ prabhuḥ \|*  
*yathāvatte gaṇā vṛttaṃ samācakhyuśca vistarāt \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. On seeing them dejected, the lord enquired after their health. The Gaṇas then intimated to him everything in detail.

## \|\| 6.21.56 \|\|

*tacchrutvā bhagavānudro mahālīlākaraḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*abhayaṃ dattavāṃstebhyo mahotsāhaṃ pravarddhayan \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. On hearing it, lord Śiva, the expert in divine sports assured them of freedom from fear increasing their enthusiasm.

## Chapter 22 - Description of Jalandhara’s Battle

## \|\| 6.22.1 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*atha vīragaṇai rudro raudrarūpo mahāprabhuḥ \|*  
*abhyagādvṛṣabhārūḍhassaṃgrāmaṃ prahasanniva \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

1\. Then the great lord Śiva assuming a terrible form went laughingly to the battle-field and sat on his bull, accompanied by his heroic Gaṇas.

## \|\| 6.22.2 \|\|

*rudramāyāṃtamālokya siṃhanādairgaṇāḥ punaḥ \|*  
*nivṛttāḥ saṃgare raudrā ye hi pūrvaṃ parājitāḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. On seeing Śiva coming, the Gaṇas who were formerly defeated returned to fight roaring like lions.

## \|\| 6.22.3 \|\|

*vīra śabdaṃ ca kurvantaste'pyanye śāṃkarā gaṇāḥ \|*  
*sotsavāssāyudhā daityānnijaghnuśśaravṛṣṭibhiḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Other Gaṇas too shouted heroically and jubilantly. Well-equipped with their weapons they killed the Daityas with showers of arrows.

## \|\| 6.22.4 \|\|

*daityā hi bhīṣaṇaṃ rudraṃ sarve dṛṣṭvā vidudruvuḥ \|*  
*śāṃkaraṃ puruṣaṃ dṛṣṭvā pātakānīva tadbhayāt \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. On seeing Śiva the terrible, all the Daityas fled for fear from the battle field as the sins on seeing a devotee of Śiva.

## \|\| 6.22.5 \|\|

*atho jalaṃdharo daityānnivṛttānprekṣya saṃgare \|*  
*abhyadhāvatsa caṃḍīśaṃ muṃcanbāṇānsahasraśaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. On seeing the Daityas returning from the battle field, Jalandhara rushed at Śiva discharging thousands of arrows.

## \|\| 6.22.6 \|\|

*niśuṃbhaśuṃbhapramukhā daityendrāśca sahasraśaḥ \|*  
*abhijagmuśśivaṃ vegādroṣātsaṃdaṣṭadacchadāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Thousands of leading Daityas, Niśumbha, Śumbha and others rushed at Śiva, biting their lips.

## \|\| 6.22.7 \|\|

*kālanemistathā vīraḥ khaḍgaromā balāhakaḥ \|*  
*ghasmaraśca pracaṃḍaścāpare cāpi śivaṃ yayuḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Similarly Kālanemi the hero, Khaḍgaromā, Balāhaka, Ghasmara, Pracaṇḍa and others rushed at Śiva.

## \|\| 6.22.8 \|\|

*bāṇaissaṃchādayāmāsurdrutaṃ rudragaṇāṃśca te \|*  
*aṃgāni cicchidurvīrāḥ śuṃbhādyā nikhilā mune \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. O sage, the heroes Śumbha and others, covered the Gaṇas of Rudra with arrows and cut their limbs.

## \|\| 6.22.9 \|\|

*bāṇāṃdhakārasaṃchannaṃ dṛṣṭvā gaṇabalaṃ haraḥ \|*  
*tadbāṇajālamācchidya bāṇairāvavṛte nabhaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. On seeing his army of Gaṇas enveloped in darkness by the volleys of arrows, Śiva split the net of their arrows and encompassed the sky with his own.

## \|\| 6.22.10 \|\|

*daityāṃśca bāṇavātyābhiḥ pīḍitānakarottadā \|*  
*pracaṃḍabāṇajāloghairapātayata bhūtale \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. He afflicted the Daityas with the gusts of wind raised by the arrows. He felled them to the ground with fierce volleys of arrows.

## \|\| 6.22.11 \|\|

*khaḍgaromaśiraḥ kāyāttathā paraśunācchinat \|*  
*balāhakasya ca śiraḥ khaṭvāṃgenākaroddvidhā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. He severed the head of Khaḍgaromā from his body with his axe. He shattered the head of Balāhaka with his club into two pieces.

## \|\| 6.22.12 \|\|

*sa baddhvā ghasmaraṃ daityaṃ pāśenābhyahanadbhuvi \|*  
*mahāvīra pracaṃḍaṃ ca cakartta viśikhena ha \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. He tied the Daitya Ghasmara with his noose and dashed him on the ground. With his trident, he chopped off the great hero Pracaṇḍa.

## \|\| 6.22.13 \|\|

*vṛṣabheṇa hatāḥ kecitkecidbāṇairnipātitā \|*  
*na śekurasurāḥ sthātuṃ gajā siṃhārditā iva \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Some of the Asuras were killed by the bull. Some were struck by the arrows. Like elephants harassed by lions, the Asuras were unable to stay there.

## \|\| 6.22.14 \|\|

*tataḥ krodhaparītātmā daityāndhikkṛtavānraṇe \|*  
*śuṃbhādikānmahādaityaḥ prahasanprāha dhairyavān \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Then the great Asura Jalandhara became infuriated and rebuked the Daityas in the battle. The courageous Daitya mocked at Śumbha and others and spoke thus.

## \|\| 6.22.15 \|\|

*jalaṃdhara uvāca \|*  
*kiṃ va uccaritairmāturdhāvadbhiḥ pṛṣṭhato hataiḥ \|*  
*na hi bhītavadhaḥ ślāghyaḥ svargadaḥ śūramāninām \|\| 15 \|\|*

Jalandhara said:—

15\. Of what avail is your boasting about the pedigree of your mother if you flee back on being attacked? To die cowardly while you profess to be heroes is not commendable, nor does it yield heaven.

## \|\| 6.22.16 \|\|

*yadi vaḥ pradhane śradā sāro vā kṣullakā hṛdi \|*  
*agre tiṣṭhata mātraṃ me na cedgrāmyasukhe spṛhā \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. O trivial fellows, if you have faith in war or the essential strength in the heart or if you have no lurking pleasures for sexual indulgence then you come forward and stand before me.

## \|\| 6.22.17 \|\|

*raṇe mṛtyurvaraścāsti sarvakāmaphalapradaḥ \|*  
*yaśaḥprado viśeṣeṇa mokṣado'pi prakīrttitaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Death in battle is preferrable. It yields all cherished desires. It is especially conducive to fame. It has been proclaimed as the bestower of salvation too.

## \|\| 6.22.18 \|\|

*sūryasya maṃḍalaṃ bhittvā yāyādvai paramaṃ padam \|*  
*parivrāṭ paramajñānī raṇe yatsaṃmukhe hataḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The wandering recluse of supreme knowledge and wisdom as well as he who dies fighting face to face, attain the greatest region after breaking through the solar sphere.

## \|\| 6.22.19 \|\|

*mṛtyorbhayaṃ na kartavyaṃ kadācitkutracidbudhaiḥ \|*  
*anirvāryo yato hyeṣa upāyairnikhilairapi \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. No sensible man should ever be afraid of death. Death is inevitable notwithstanding all the remedies employed to ward it off.

## \|\| 6.22.20 \|\|

*mṛtyurjanmavatāṃ vīrā dehena saha jāyate \|*  
*adya vābdaśatāt vā mṛtyurvai prāṇināṃ dhruvaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. O heroes, death is congenital to any being born. Either today or at the end of a hundred years all living beings are sure to die.

## \|\| 6.22.21 \|\|

*tanmṛtyubhayamutsārya yudhyadhvaṃ samare mudā \|*  
*sarvathā paramānanda ihāmutrāpyasaṃśayaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Hence, cast off all fear for death. Come and fight in war joyously. In every respect there is certainly a great bliss here and hereafter.

## \|\| 6.22.22 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityuktvā bodhayāmāsa svavīrānbahuśassa hi \|*  
*dhairyaṃ dadhurna te bhītā palāyaṃta raṇāddrutam \|\| 22 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

22\. Saying this, he tried to encourage his heroes in several ways. But the frightened demons did not regain courage. They fled from the battle in a trice.

## \|\| 6.22.23 \|\|

*atha dṛṣṭvā svasainyaṃ tatpalāyanaparāyaṇam \|*  
*cukrodhāti mahāvīrassiṃdhuputro jalaṃdharaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. On seeing his army on the rout, the heroic son of the ocean Jalandhara became very furious.

## \|\| 6.22.24 \|\|

*tataḥ krodhaparītātmā krodhādrudraṃ jalaṃdharaḥ \|*  
*āhvāpayāmāsa raṇe tīvrāśanisamasvanaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Then the infuriated Jalandhara challenged for a battle in a stentorian voice like the sound of fierce thunderbolt.

## \|\| 6.22.25 \|\|

*\|\| jalaṃdhara uvāca \|*  
*yuddhyasvādya mayā sārddhaṃ kimebhirnihataistava \|*  
*yacca kiñcidbalaṃ te'sti taddarśaya jaṭādhara \|\| 25 \|\|*

Jalandhara said:—

25\. O ascetic, fight with me now. What is the use of slaying these? Show me what little strength you have.

## \|\| 6.22.26 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityuktvā bāṇa saptatyā jaghāna vṛṣabhadhvajam \|*  
*jalaṃdharo mahādaityaśśaṃbhumakliṣṭakāriṇam \|\| 26 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

26\. After saying this, Jalandhara the great Daitya hit the bull-bannered Śiva of indefatigable endeavour, with an incessant volley of arrows.

## \|\| 6.22.27 \|\|

*tānaprāptānmahādevo jalaṃdharaśarāndrutam \|*  
*nijairhi niśitairbāṇaiściccheda prahasanniva \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Laughingly, lord Śiva split all the arrows of Jalandhara by discharging his own sharp arrows even before his arrows reached him.

## \|\| 6.22.28 \|\|

*tato hayāndhvajaṃ chatraṃ dhanuściccheda saptabhiḥ \|*  
*jalaṃdharasya daityasya na taccitraṃ hare mune \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Then with seven arrows he split the horses, banner, umbrella and the bow of Daitya Jalandhara. O sage, it is not surprising in the case of Śiva.

## \|\| 6.22.29 \|\|

*sa cchinnadhanvā virathaḥ pāthodhitanayo'suraḥ \|*  
*abhyadhāvacchivaṃ kruddho gadāmudyamya vegavān \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. The infuriated Asura the son of the ocean, devoid of a chariot and with bow split up rushed at Śiva lifting his mace vigorously.

## \|\| 6.22.30 \|\|

*prabhurgadāṃ ca tatkṣiptāṃ sahasaiva maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*pārāśaryaṃ mahālīlo drutaṃ bāṇairdvidhākarot \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. O Vyāsa, lord Śiva of great sports immediately split asunder the mace hurled by him, by means of his arrows.

## \|\| 6.22.31 \|\|

*tathāpi muṣṭimudyamya mahākruddho mahāsuraḥ \|*  
*abhyudyayau mahāvegāddrutaṃ taṃ tajjighāṃsayā \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Yet the highly infuriated great Asura rushed at Śiva with the mailed fist lifted up, with a desire to kill him.

## \|\| 6.22.32 \|\|

*tāvadeveśvareṇāśu bāṇoghaissa jalaṃdharaḥ \|*  
*akliṣṭakarmakāreṇa krośamātramapākṛtaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. By a volley of arrows Jalandhara was hurled back a Krośa by Śiva of indefatigable enterprise.

## \|\| 6.22.33 \|\|

*tato jalaṃdharo daityo rudraṃ matvā balādhikam \|*  
*sasarja māyāṃ gāṃdharvīmadbhutāṃ rudramohinīm \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Then, considering Śiva more powerful, Jalandhara the Daitya, created the illusion of Gandharvas that mysteriously fascinated even Śiva.

## \|\| 6.22.34 \|\|

*tasya māyāprabhāvāttu gaṃdharvāpsarasāṃ gaṇāḥ \|*  
*āvirbhūtā aneke ca rudramohanahetave \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. By the power of his Māyā, hosts of Gandharvas and celestial damsels came into view for fascinating Śiva.

## \|\| 6.22.35 \|\|

*tato jaguśca nanṛturgaṃdharvāpsarasāṃ gaṇāḥ \|*  
*tālaveṇumṛdaṃgāṃśca vādayantisma cāpare \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. The Gandharvas and celestial damsels sang and danced. Others played on flutes, mṛdaṅgas and cymbals.

## \|\| 6.22.36 \|\|

*taddṛṣṭvā mahadāścaryaṃ gaṇai rudro vimohitaḥ \|*  
*patitānyapi śastrāṇi karebhyo na viveda saḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. On seeing that wonderful feat, Śiva was fascinated by the Gaṇas. He was not conscious of even the garments let down from the hands.

## \|\| 6.22.37 \|\|

*ekāgrībhūtamālokya rudraṃ daityo jalaṃdharaḥ \|*  
*kāmatassa jagāmāśu yatra gaurī sthitā'bhavat \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. On seeing Śiva concentrated in the dance Jalandhara urged by lust immediately went to the place where Gaurī stood.

## \|\| 6.22.38-39 \|\|

*yuddhe śuṃbhaniśuṃbhākhyau sthāpayitvā mahābalau \|*  
*daśadordaṇḍapaṃcāsyastrinetraśca jaṭādharaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*mahāvṛṣabhamārūḍhassarvathā rudrasaṃnibhaḥ \|*  
*āsuryyā māyayā vyāsa sa babhūva jalaṃdharaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

38-39. He entrusted the powerful Śumbha and Niśumbha with the conduct of war. With his demonaic Māyā he assumed the form of Śiva—with ten brawny arms, five faces, three eyes, and matted hair. He was seated on the great bull. In every respect, O Vyāsa, Jalandhara appeared like Śiva.

## \|\| 6.22.40 \|\|

*atha rudraṃ samāyātamālokya bhavavallabhā \|*  
*abhyāyayau sakhīmadhyāttaddarśanapathe'bhavat \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. On seeing Śiva coming, the beloved of Śiva came out from the midst of her female friends within the range of his vision.

## \|\| 6.22.41 \|\|

*yāvaddadarśa cārvaṃgī pārvatīṃ danujeśvaraḥ \|*  
*tāvatsa vīryaṃ mumuce jaḍāṃgaścābhavattadā \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. When the lord of Asuras saw the bauntiful Pārvatī, he let drops of semen fall and his limbs became benumbed.

## \|\| 6.22.42 \|\|

*atha jñātvā tadā gaurī dānavaṃ bhayavihvalā \|*  
*jagāmāṃtarhitā vegātsā tadottaramānasam \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. On realising that he was the demon, the terrified Gaurī vanished immediately to the northern shore of the Mānasa lake.

## \|\| 6.22.43 \|\|

*tāmadṛśya tato daityaḥ kṣaṇādvidyullatāmiva \|*  
*javenāgātpunaryoddhuṃ yatra devo maheśvaraḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Unable to see her who disappeared in a moment like lightning, the Daitya immediately went to the place where lord Śiva stood in order to fight him.

## \|\| 6.22.44 \|\|

*pārvatyapi mahāviṣṇuṃ sasmāra manasā tadā \|*  
*tāvaddadarśa taṃ devaṃ sopaviṣṭaṃ samīpagam \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Pārvatī remembered lord Viṣṇu mentally. Immediately she saw the lord seated near her.

## \|\| 6.22.45 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā pārvatī viṣṇuṃ jaganmātā śivapriyā \|*  
*prasannamanasovāca praṇamaṃtaṃ kṛtāṃjalim \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. On seeing Viṣṇu bowing to her with palms joined in reverence, Pārvatī the beloved of Śiva, the mother of the universe, spoke delightedly.

## \|\| 6.22.46 \|\|

*pārvatyuvāca \|*  
*viṣṇo jalaṃdharo daityaḥ kṛtavānparamādbhutam \|*  
*tatkiṃ na viditaṃ te'sti ceṣṭitaṃ tasya durmateḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

Pārvatī said:—

46\. O Viṣṇu, is it not known to you that the wicked Daitya Jalandhara perpetrated a wonderfully base deed?”

## \|\| 6.22.47 \|\|

*tacchrutvā jagadambāyā vacanaṃ garuḍadhvajaḥ \|*  
*pratyuvāca śivāṃ natvā sāṃjalirnamrakaṃdharaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. On hearing the words of the mother of the universe, the Garuḍa-bannered lord bowed to Pārvatī bending his neck and joining his palms in reverence and spoke.

## \|\| 6.22.48 \|\|

*\|\| śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*bhavatyāḥ kṛpayā devi tadvṛttaṃ viditaṃ mayā \|*  
*yadājñāpaya māṃ mātastatkuryyāṃ tvadanujñayā \|\| 48 \|\|*

Viṣṇu said:—

48\. O mother, by your favour that incident is known to me. What you shall be pleased to commend I shall perform with your permission.

## \|\| 6.22.49 \|\|

*sanatkumāra ucāca \|*  
*tacchrutvā viṣṇuvacanṃ punarapyāha pārvatī \|*  
*hṛṣīkeśaṃ jaganmātā dharmanītiṃ suśikṣayan \|\| 49 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

49\. On hearing the words of Viṣṇu, Pārvatī said again. The mother of the universe desired to teach Viṣṇu the policy based on Dharma.

## \|\| 6.22.50 \|\|

*pārvatyuvāca \|*  
*tenaiva darśitaḥ panthā budhyasva tvaṃ tathaiva hi \|*  
*tatstrīpātivrataṃ dharmaṃ bhraṣṭaṃ kuru madājñayā \|\| 50 \|\|*

Pārvatī said:—

50\. He himself has shown the path. Know that to be the way in the same manner. At my bidding, make the chastity of his wife violated.

## \|\| 6.22.51 \|\|

*nānyathā sa mahādaityo bhavedvadhyo rameśvara \|*  
*pātivratasamo nānyo dharmo'sti pṛthivītale \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. O Viṣṇu, that great Daitya cannot be killed otherwise. In the earth there is no other virtue equal to chastity.

## \|\| 6.22.52 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityanujñāṃ samākarṇya śirasādhāya tāṃ hariḥ \|*  
*chala karttuṃ jagāmāśu punarjālaṃdharaṃ puram \|\| 52 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

52\. On hearing this command and accepting it with lowered head, Viṣṇu immediately went to the city of Jalandhara for practising deception.

## Chapter 23 - Outraging the modesty of Vṛndā

## \|\| 6.23.1 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*sanatkumāra sarvajña vada tvaṃ vadatāṃ vara \|*  
*kimakārṣīddharistatra dharmaṃ tatyāja sā katham \|\| 1 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:—

1\. O omniscient Sanatkumāra, please narrate, O eloquent one, what did Viṣṇu do there? How did she err from her virtue?

## \|\| 6.23.2 \|\|

*sanatkumāra upāca \|*  
*viṣṇurjālaṃdharaṃ gatvā daityasya puṭabhedanam \|*  
*pātivratyasya bhaṃgāya vṛndāyāścā karonmatim \|\| 2 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

2\. After going to the city of Jalandhara, Viṣṇu thought of violating the chastity of Vṛndā.

## \|\| 6.23.3 \|\|

*vṛndāṃ sa darśayāmāsa svapnaṃ māyāvināṃ varaḥ \|*  
*svayaṃ tannagarodyānamāsthito'dbhutavigrahaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The foremost among those who wield illusion, he assumed a wonderful body and stationed himself in a park of the city. He made Vṛndā see a dream.

## \|\| 6.23.4 \|\|

*atha vṛndā tadā devī tatpatnī niśi suvratā \|*  
*harermāyāprabhāvāttu dussvapnaṃ sā dadarśa ha \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The gentle lady Vṛndā, the wife of Jalandhara, though of pure rites, had a very bad dream at night on account of Viṣṇu’s power of illusion.

## \|\| 6.23.5 \|\|

*svapnamadhye hi sā viṣṇumāyayā pradadarśa ha \|*  
*bharttāraṃ mahiṣārūḍhaṃ tailābhyaktaṃ digaṃbaram \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. In the dream as a result of Viṣṇu’s power of illusion she saw the naked form of her husband anointed with oil and seated on a buffalo.

## \|\| 6.23.6 \|\|

*kṛṣṇaprasūnabhūṣāḍhyaṃ kravyādagaṇasevitam \|*  
*dakṣiṇāśāṃ gataṃ muṃḍaṃ tamasā ca vṛtaṃ tadā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. He was proceeding in the southern direction. His head had been completely shaved. He was wearing black flowers to decorate himself. He was being served by a number of Asuras. He was completely encompassed by darkness.

## \|\| 6.23.7 \|\|

*svapuraṃ sāgare magnaṃ sahasaivātmanā saha \|*  
*ityādi bahudussvapnānniśāṃte sā dadarśa ha \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Later, towards the end of the night she had various bad dreams, such as the whole city was submerged in the sea, all of a sudden, along with herself.

## \|\| 6.23.8 \|\|

*tataḥ prabudhya sā bālā taṃ svapnaṃ svaṃ vicinvatī \|*  
*dadarśoditamādityaṃ sacchidraṃ niḥprabhaṃ muhuḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Then the lady woke up still thinking of the dream she had had. She saw the rising sun with a hole in the middle and fading repeatedly.

## \|\| 6.23.9 \|\|

*tadaniṣṭamidaṃ jñātvā rudaṃtī bhayavihvalā \|*  
*kutracinnāpa sā śarma gopurāṭṭālabhūmiṣu \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. On realising that it was a bad portent, the terrified lady began to cry. She did not feel happy at all in the spacious terraces and towers of the palace.

## \|\| 6.23.10 \|\|

*tatassakhīdvayayutā nagarodyānamāgamat \|*  
*tatrāpi sā gatā bālā na prāpa kutracitsukham \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. With two of her friends she then went to the park in the city. Even there she did not find herself at ease.

## \|\| 6.23.11 \|\|

*tato jalaṃdharastrī sā nirviṇṇodvignamānasā \|*  
*vanādvanāṃtaraṃ yātā naiva vedātmanā tadā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Then she, the dejected gloomy wife of Jalandhara, wandered from forest to forest. She was not conscious of even herself.

## \|\| 6.23.12 \|\|

*bhramatī sā tato bālā dadarśātīva bhīṣaṇau \|*  
*rākṣasau siṃhavadanau dṛṣṭvā daśanabhāsurau \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The wandering lady saw two demons of terrible leonine faces with shining curved fanglike teeth.

## \|\| 6.23.13 \|\|

*tau dṛṣṭvā vihvalātīva palāyanaparā tadā \|*  
*dadarśa tāpasaṃ śāṃtaṃ saśiṣyaṃ maunamāsthitam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Terrified much on seeing them, the lady fled from there and saw an ascetic of calm countenance observing silence and accompanied by his disciple.

## \|\| 6.23.14 \|\|

*tatastatkaṃṭhamāsādya nijāṃ bāhulatāṃ bhayāt \|*  
*mune māṃ rakṣa śaraṇamāgatāsmītyabhāṣata \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Putting her tender creeperlike hands round his neck due to fright she gasped out—“O sage, save me. I have sought refuge in you.”

## \|\| 6.23.15 \|\|

*munistāṃ vihvalāṃ dṛṣṭvā rākṣasānugatāṃ tadā \|*  
*huṃkāreṇaiva tau ghorau cakāra vimukhau drutam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Seeing the agitated lady followed by the demons the sage drove them back with a loud bellowing sound of “Hum”.

## \|\| 6.23.16 \|\|

*taddhuṃkārabhayatrastau dṛṣṭvā tau vimukhau gatau \|*  
*vismitātīva daityendrapatnī sābhūnmune hṛdi \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. O sage, seeing them routed and terrified by the mere Huṃkāra, the wife of the king of Daityas was struck with a great wonder in her heart.

## \|\| 6.23.17 \|\|

*tatassā munināthaṃ taṃ bhayānmuktā kṛtāṃjaliḥ \|*  
*praṇamya daṃḍavadbhūmau vṛndā vacanamabravīt \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Freed from the fear she bowed down to the great sage with palms joined in reverence and prostrated herself in front of him. Vṛndā then spoke.

## \|\| 6.23.18 \|\|

*vṛndovāca \|*  
*muninātha dayāsindho parapīḍānivāraka \|*  
*rakṣitāhaṃ tvayā ghorādbhayādasmātkha lodbhavāt \|\| 18 \|\|*

Vṛndā said:—

18\. “O leader of sages, O ocean of mercy, O remover of harassment from others, I have been saved by you from this terrible danger from the wicked demons.

## \|\| 6.23.19 \|\|

*samarthassarvathā tvaṃ hi sarvajño'pi kṛpānidhe \|*  
*kiṃcidvijñaptumicchāmi kṛpayā tanniśāmaya \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. You are competent in every respect. You are omniscient. Yet I wish to submit something. Be pleased to hear it.

## \|\| 6.23.20 \|\|

*jalaṃdharo hi madbhartā rudraṃ yoddhuṃ gataḥ prabho \|*  
*sa tatrāste kathaṃ yuddhe tanme kathaya suvrata \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. O lord, Jalandhara my husband has gone to fight Śiva. O holy one of good rites, how does he fare in the war? Please tell me.”

## \|\| 6.23.21 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*munistadvākyamākarṇya maunakapaṭamāsthitaḥ \|*  
*karttuṃ svārthaṃ vidhānajñaḥ kṛpayorddhvamavaikṣata \|\| 21 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

21\. On hearing her words, the sage feigned a deceptive silence. Fully aware of the means of achieving his selfish ends he looked up sympathetically.

## \|\| 6.23.22 \|\|

*tāvatkapīśāvāyātau taṃ praṇamyāgrataḥ sthitau \|*  
*tatastadbhrūlatāsaṃjñāniyuktau gaganaṃ gatau \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. In the meantime two lordly monkeys came there and stood bowing down in front of him. At a significant gesture from his eyebrows, the monkeys rose into the sky again.

## \|\| 6.23.23 \|\|

*nītvā kṣaṇārddhamāgatya punastasyāgrataḥ sthitau \|*  
*tasyaiva kaṃ kabaṃdhaṃ ca hastāvāstāṃ munīśvara \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. O great sage, within a trice, they came back taking with them his head, body and limbs and stood in front of the sage.

## \|\| 6.23.24 \|\|

*śiraḥ kabaṃdhaṃ hastau tau dṛṣṭvābdhitanayasya sā \|*  
*papāta mūrchitā bhūmau bhartṛvyasanaduḥkhitā \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. On seeing the head, body and limbs of her husband, Vṛndā fell unconscious, extremely pained at the misery of her lord.

## \|\| 6.23.25 \|\|

*\|\| vṛndovāca \|*  
*yaḥ purā sukhasaṃvādairvinodayasi māṃ prabho \|*  
*sa kathaṃ na vadasyadya vallabhāṃ māmanāgasam \|\| 25 \|\|*

Vṛndā said:—

25\. “O lord, formerly you used to humour me with pleasant chats. How is it that you do not speak to me now, to your pious beloved?

## \|\| 6.23.26 \|\|

*yena devāssagaṃdharvā nirjitā viṣṇunā saha \|*  
*kathaṃ sa tāpasenādya trailokyavijayī hata \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. How is it that you, by whom all the gods including the Gandharvas and Viṣṇu had been defeated, you who had conquered the three worlds, have now been killed by a poor sage?

## \|\| 6.23.27 \|\|

*nāṃgīkṛtaṃ hi me vākyaṃ rudratattvamajānatā \|*  
*paraṃ brahma śivaśceti vadaṃtyā daityasattama \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. O excellent Daitya, you did not know the reality of Śiva nor did you pay heed to my words ‘Śiva is Supreme Brahman.’

## \|\| 6.23.28 \|\|

*tatastvaṃ hi mayā jñātastava sevāprabhāvataḥ \|*  
*garvitena tvayā naiva kusaṃgavaśagena hi \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Having served you I found that it was not due to haughtiness but due to your association with bad men that you did all this.”

## \|\| 6.23.29 \|\|

*itthaṃprabhāṣya bahudhā svadharmasthā ca tatpriyā \|*  
*vilalāpa vicitraṃ sā hṛdayena vidūyatā \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Saying these and other words of lamentation, his beloved wife strictly adhering to virtue, cried in diverse ways with a pained heart.

## \|\| 6.23.30 \|\|

*tatassā dhairyamālaṃbya duḥkhocchravā sānvimuṃcatī \|*  
*uvāca munivaryaṃ taṃ supraṇamya kṛtāṃjaliḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Then steadying herself a little, and heaving deep sighs of grief she bowed to the excellent sage with palms joined in reverence.

## \|\| 6.23.31 \|\|

*vṛndovāca \|*  
*kṛpānidhe muniśreṣṭha paropakaraṇādara \|*  
*mayi kṛtvā kṛpāṃ sādho jīvayainaṃ mama prabhum \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. “O excellent sage, storehouse of mercy, eager to help others, O gentle sir, take pity on me and resuscitate my lord.

## \|\| 6.23.32 \|\|

*yattvamasya punaśśakto jīvanāya mato mama \|*  
*atassaṃjīvayainaṃ me prāṇanāthaṃ munīśvara \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. O great sage, I know that you are competent to enliven him again. Hence please resuscitate my beloved husband.”

## \|\| 6.23.33 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityuktvā daityapatnī sā pativratyaparāyaṇāḥ \|*  
*pādayoḥ patitā tasya duḥkhaśvāsān vimuñcatī \|\| 33 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

33\. After saying this, the chaste wife of the Daitya fell at his feet heaving sighs of grief.

## \|\| 6.23.34 \|\|

*muniruvāca \|*  
*nāyaṃ jīvayituṃ śakto rudreṇa nihato yudhi \|*  
*rudreṇa nihatā yuddhe na jīvanti kadācana \|\| 34 \|\|*

The sage said:—

34\. This Daitya cannot be enlivened because he has been killed by Śiva in the battle. Those killed in battle by Śiva never return to life.

## \|\| 6.23.35 \|\|

*tathāpi kṛpayāviṣṭa enaṃ saṃjīvayāmyaham \|*  
*rakṣyāśśaraṇagāśceti jānandharmaṃ sanātanam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Still, knowing the eternal Dharma that those who seek refuge should be protected, I shall resuscitate him urged by pity.

## \|\| 6.23.36 \|\|

*\|\| sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityuktvā sa munistasyā jīvayitvā patiṃ mune \|*  
*aṃtardadhe tato viṣṇussarvamāyāvināṃ varaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

36\. After saying this and restoring him to life, O sage, that sage who was Viṣṇu the foremost among those who wield illusion vanished from the scene.

## \|\| 6.23.37 \|\|

*drutaṃ sa jīvitastenotthitaḥ sāgaranandanaḥ \|*  
*vṛndāmāliṃgya tadvaktraṃ cucuṃba prītamānasaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Jalandhara thus revived to life by him stood up. Delighted in mind he embraced Vṛndā and kissed her face.

## \|\| 6.23.38 \|\|

*atha vṛndāpi bhartāraṃ dṛṣṭvā harṣitamānasā \|*  
*jahau śokaṃ ca nikhilaṃ svapnavaddhṛdyamanyata \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. On seeing her husband, Vṛndā too was delighted. She forgot her sorrow. She considered everything a dream.

## \|\| 6.23.39 \|\|

*atha prasannahṛdayā sā hi saṃjātahṛcchayā \|*  
*reme tadvanamadhyasthā tadyuktā bahuvāsarān \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Delighted in the heart and with all the dormant passions kindled up, she sported with him for many days in the middle of that forest.

## \|\| 6.23.40 \|\|

*kadācitsuratasyāṃte dṛṣṭvā viṣṇuṃ tameva hi \|*  
*nirbhartsya krodhasaṃyuktā vṛndā vacanamabravīt \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Once at the end of the sexual intercourse she realised that it was Viṣṇu. Vṛndā rebuked him angrily and spoke thus.

## \|\| 6.23.41 \|\|

*vṛndovāca \|*  
*dhik tadevaṃ hare śīlaṃ paradārābhigāminaḥ \|*  
*jñāto'si tvaṃ mayā samyaṅmāyī pratyakṣatāpasaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

Vṛndā said:—

41\. Fie on this misdeed of Viṣṇu in outraging the modesty of another man’s wife. I have now realised you as the wielder of illusion, appearing in the guise of an ascetic.

## \|\| 6.23.42 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityuktvā krodhamāpannā darśayaṃtī svatejasam \|*  
*śaśāpa keśavaṃ vyāsa pātivratyaratā ca sā \|\| 42 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

42\. O Vyāsa, saying thus in great anger she showed her brilliant powers as a staunch chaste lady by cursing Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 6.23.43 \|\|

*re mahādhama daityāre paradharmavidūṣaka \|*  
*gṛhṇīṣva śaṭha maddattaṃ śāpaṃ sarvaviṣolbaṇam \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. “O base foe of the Daityas, defiler of other people’s virtue, O wicked one, take this curse from me, greater in force than all persons.

## \|\| 6.23.44 \|\|

*yau tvayā māyayā khyātau svakīyau darśitau mama \|*  
*tāveva rākṣasau bhūtvā bhāryāṃ tava hariṣyataḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. The two persons whom you made to appear in front of me shall become Rākṣasas and abduct your wife.

## \|\| 6.23.45 \|\|

*tvaṃ cāpi bhāryāduḥkhārto vane kapisahāyavān \|*  
*bhrama sarpeśvareṇāyaṃ yaste śiṣyatvamāgataḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. You will be distressed on account of separation from your wife roaming about with Śeṣa ‘lord of snakes’\[2\] who posed as your disciple here. You will seek the help of monkeys in the forest.

## \|\| 6.23.46 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityuktvā sā tadā vṛndā praviśaddhavyavāhanam \|*  
*viṣṇunā vāryamāṇāpi tasmitāsaktacetasā \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. After saying this, Vṛndā entered fire though prevented by Viṣṇu who was fascinated by her charms.

## \|\| 6.23.47 \|\|

*tasminnavasare devā brahmādyā nikhilā mune \|*  
*āgatā khe samaṃ dāraiḥ sadgatiṃ vai didṛkṣavaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. O sage, then Brahmā and other gods, gathered in the sky accompanied by their wives in order to see the salvation of Vṛndā.

## \|\| 6.23.48 \|\|

*atha daityendrapatnyāstu tajjyotiḥ paramaṃ mahat \|*  
*paśyatāṃ sarvadevānāmalokamagamaddrutam \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Then the great brilliance of the wife of Jalandhara immediately went to Śivaloka even as the gods stood watching.

## \|\| 6.23.49 \|\|

*śivātanau vilīnaṃ tadvṛndātejo babhūva ha \|*  
*āsījjayajayārāvaḥ khasthitāmara paṃktiṣu \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. The refulgence of Vṛndā became merged in Pārvatī. There was a great shout of “Victory” in the rows of the gods standing in the sky.

## \|\| 6.23.50 \|\|

*evaṃ vṛndā mahārājñī kālanemisutottamā \|*  
*pātivratyaprabhāvācca muktiṃ prāpa parāṃ mune \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. O sage, thus the great queen Vṛndā the excellent daughter of Kālanemi attained great salvation, thanks to the power of her chastity.

## \|\| 6.23.51 \|\|

*tato haristāmanusaṃsmanmuhurvṛndācitābhasmarajovaguṃṭhitaḥ \|*  
*tatraiva tasthau surasiddhasaṃghakaiḥ prabodhyamānopi yayau na śāṃtim \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Viṣṇu thought of Vṛndā remorsefully. The smoke and dust from her funeral pyre covered his face. He stood there itself without any peace of mind though urged and consoled by hosts of gods and Siddhas.

## Chapter 24 - Jalandhara is slain

## \|\| 6.24.1 \|\|

*\|\| vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*vidheḥ śreṣṭhasuta prājñaḥ katheyaṃ śrāvitādbhutā \|*  
*tataśca kimabhūdājau kathaṃ daityo hato vada \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. O excellent son of Brahmā, O intelligent one, you have narrated a wonderful story. What happened thereafter in the battle? How was the Asura killed? Please narrate.

## \|\| 6.24.2 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*adṛśya girijāṃ tatra daityendre raṇamāgate \|*  
*gāṃdharve ca vilīne hi caitanyo'bhūdvṛṣadhvajaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

2\. Unable to see Pārvatī, the king of Daityas returned to the battle ground. The groups of deceptive Gandharvas vanished. It was only then that the bull-bannered deity regained awareness of the surroundings.

## \|\| 6.24.3 \|\|

*aṃtardhānagatāṃ māyāṃ dṛṣṭvā buddho hi śaṃkaraḥ \|*  
*cukrodhātīva saṃhārī laukikīṃ gatimāśritaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. On seeing the illusion vanished, Śiva woke up. Following the way of the world, the annihilator became very furious.

## \|\| 6.24.4 \|\|

*tataśśivo vismitamānasaḥ punarjagāma yuddhāya jalaṃdharaṃ ruṣā \|*  
*sa cāpi daityaḥ punarāgataṃ śivaṃ dṛṣṭvā śaroghaissamavākiradraṇe \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Then Śiva was a bit surprised in the mind. He approached Jalandhara angrily in order to fight with him. On seeing Śiva approaching again, the Asura showered him with arrows.

## \|\| 6.24.5 \|\|

*kṣiptaṃ prabhustaṃ śarajālamugraṃ jalaṃdhareṇātibalīyasā haraḥ \|*  
*praciccheda śarairvarairnijairnacitramatra tribhavaprahaṃtuḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Lord Śiva immediately split the cluster of arrows discharged by the powerful Jalandhara by means of his own excellent arrows. This was not surprising for the annihilator of the three worlds.

## \|\| 6.24.6 \|\|

*tato jalaṃdharo dṛṣṭvā rudrmadbhutavikramam \|*  
*cakāra māyayā gaurīṃ tryambakaṃ mohayanniva \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Seeing Śiva exhibiting wonderful feats of valour, Jalandhara created Pārvatī by means of his illusion in order to delude Śiva.

## \|\| 6.24.7 \|\|

*rathopari gatāṃ baddhāṃ rudaṃtīṃ pārvatīṃ śivaḥ \|*  
*niśuṃbha śuṃbhadaityaiśca badhyamānāṃ dadarśa saḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Śiva saw Pārvatī tied to the chariot and crying. She was being harrassed by Niśumbha, Śumbha and other Daityas.

## \|\| 6.24.8 \|\|

*gaurīṃ tathāvidhāṃ dṛṣṭvā laukikīṃ darśayangatim \|*  
*babhūva prākṛta iva śivopyudvignamānasaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. On seeing that in her plight, Śiva became dispirited and dejected in the mind like an ordinary man pursuing the way of the world.

## \|\| 6.24.9 \|\|

*avāṅmukhasthitastūṣṇīṃ nānālīlāviśāradaḥ \|*  
*śithilāṃgo viṣaṇṇātmā vismṛtya svaparākramam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. He, an expert in various kinds of sports, remained silent with face drooping down, utterly dejected, exhausted and forgetful of his own prowess.

## \|\| 6.24.10 \|\|

*tato jalaṃdharo vegāttribhirvivyādha sāyakaiḥ \|*  
*āpuṃkhamagnaistaṃ rudraṃ śirasyurasi codare \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Then Jalandhara hurriedly hit Śiva in his chest, belly and the head with three arrows that went deep down as far as their feathered tail.

## \|\| 6.24.11 \|\|

*tato rudro mahālīlo jñānatattvaḥ kṣaṇātprabhuḥ \|*  
*raudrarūpadharo jāto jvālāmālātibhīṣaṇaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Then within a trice, lord Śiva, the principle of perfect wisdom, expert in great sports, assumed a terrific form, dreadfully blazing.

## \|\| 6.24.12 \|\|

*tasyātīva mahāraudrarūpaṃ dṛṣṭvā mahāsurāḥ \|*  
*na śekuḥ pramukhe sthātuṃ bhejire te diśo daśa \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. On seeing his excessively terrible form, the Daityas fled to the ten different quarters. They were unable to stay facing him.

## \|\| 6.24.13 \|\|

*niśuṃbhaśuṃbhāvapi yau vikhyātau vīrasattamau \|*  
*āpe tau śekaturnaiva raṇe sthātuṃ munīśvara \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. O great sage, even Śumbha and Niśumbha who were renowned for their prowess could not stand in the battle ground.

## \|\| 6.24.14 \|\|

*jalaṃdharakṛtā māyāṃtarhitābhūcca tatkṣaṇam \|*  
*hāhākāro mahānāsītsaṃgrāme sarvatomukhe \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The illusion created by Jalandhara had vanished in an instant. In that all out battle there was great hue and cry.

## \|\| 6.24.15 \|\|

*tataśśāpaṃ dadau rudrastayośśuṃbhaniśuṃbhayoḥ \|*  
*palāyamānau tau dṛṣṭvā dhikkṛtya krodhasaṃyutaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. On seeing Śumbha and Niśumbha fleeing, the infuriated Śiva rebuked them and cursed as follows.

## \|\| 6.24.16 \|\|

*rudra uvāca \|*  
*yuvāṃ duṣṭāvatikhalāvaparādhakarau mama \|*  
*pārvatīdaṃḍadātārau raṇādasmātparāṅmukhau \|\| 16 \|\|*

Śiva said:—

16\. “You are wicked and excessively roguish. You have offended me by harassing Pārvatī. Now "both of you have deserted the battle ground.

## \|\| 6.24.17 \|\|

*parāṅmukho na haṃtavya iti vadhyau na me yuvām \|*  
*mama yuddhādatikrāṃtau gauryyā vadhyau bhaviṣyataḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. A person fleeing the battle ground shall not be killed. So I do not kill you. Since you have escaped from a fight with me you would be killed by Pārvatī.”

## \|\| 6.24.18 \|\|

*evaṃ vadati gaurīśe sindhuputro jalaṃdharaḥ \|*  
*cukrodhātīva rudrāya jvalajjvalanasannibhaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Even as Śiva was saying, Jalandhara, son of the ocean, became very furious with Śiva like the blazing fire.

## \|\| 6.24.19 \|\|

*rudre raṇe mahāvegādvavarṣa niśitāñcharān \|*  
*bāṇāṃdhakārasaṃchannaṃ tathā bhūmitalaṃ hyabhūt \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. One after the other, he showered many sharp arrows on Śiva in the battle. The whole of the Earth became enveloped in darkness by his arrows.

## \|\| 6.24.20 \|\|

*yāvadrudraḥ praciccheda tasya bāṇagaṇāndrutam \|*  
*tāvatsaparigheṇāśu jaghāna vṛṣabhaṃ balī \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Śiva split the arrows swiftly, the powerful Daitya hit the bull with an iron club.

## \|\| 6.24.21 \|\|

*vṛṣastena prahāreṇa paravṛtto raṇāṃgaṇāt \|*  
*rudreṇa kṛśyamāṇo'pi na tasthau raṇabhūmiṣu \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Due to that blow the bull turned away from the battle field. Even when dragged by Śiva it did not stand there.

## \|\| 6.24.22 \|\|

*atha loke mahārudrassvīyaṃ tejo'tidussaham \|*  
*darśayāmāsa sarvasmai satyametanmunīśvara \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Then the great Śiva put forth an unbearable splendour visible to all in the battle field. O great sage, this is true.

## \|\| 6.24.23 \|\|

*tataḥ paramasaṃkruddho rudro raudravapurdharaḥ \|*  
*pralayānalavaddhoro babhūva sahasā prabhuḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Then the infuriated Śiva assuming a terrible form, became as dreadful as the fire of dissolution, all of a sudden.

## \|\| 6.24.24 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā puraḥ sthitaṃ daityaṃ meghakūṭamiva sthitam \|*  
*avadhyatvamapi śrutvāpyanyairabhyudyato'bhavat \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. On seeing the Daitya standing in front like the lofty peak of Meru and hearing from others that he could not be killed, he stood ready for it.

## \|\| 6.24.25 \|\|

*brahmaṇo vacanaṃ rakṣanrakṣako jagatāṃ prabhuḥ \|*  
*hṛdānugrahamātanvaṃstadvadhāya mano dadhat \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. As desired by Brahmā, the lord protector of the worlds decided to kill Jalandhara, blessing him in the heart of his heart.

## \|\| 6.24.26 \|\|

*kopaṃ kṛtvā paraṃ śūlī pādāṃguṣṭhena līlayā \|*  
*mahāṃbhasi cakārāśu rathāṃgaṃ raudramadbhutam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Becoming excessively angry, the trident bearing deity made a mysteriously terrible wheel in the great waters by means of his big toe indulging in a divine sport.

## \|\| 6.24.27 \|\|

*kṛtvārṇavāṃbhasi śitaṃ bhagavānrathāṃgaṃ smṛtvā jagattrayamanena hataṃ purāriḥ \|*  
*dakṣāndhakāṃtakapuratrayayajñahaṃtā lokatrayāṃtakakaraḥ prahasannuvāca \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Creating a sharp wheel in the waters of the ocean and remembering that the three worlds had been harassed by Jalandhara, the lord Śiva who had slain Dakṣa, Andhaka Antaka and destroyed the three cities and the sacrifice of Dakṣa and annihilated the three worlds said laughingly.

## \|\| 6.24.28 \|\|

*mahārudra uvāca \|*  
*pādena nirmitaṃ cakraṃ jalaṃdhara mahāmbhasi \|*  
*balavānyadi coddharttuṃ tiṣṭha yoddhuṃ na cānyathā \|\| 28 \|\|*

Śiva said:—

28\. O Jalandhara, if you are powerful enough to lift the wheel created by me with the leg in the great waters, you will be competent to stand and fight with me, not otherwise.

## \|\| 6.24.29 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā krodhenādīptalocanaḥ \|*  
*pradahanniva cakṣurbhyāṃ prāhālokya sa śaṃkaram \|\| 29 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

29\. On hearing his words the Daitya’s eyes gleamed fiercely with anger. He looked at Śiva as if burning him with his eyes and said:—

## \|\| 6.24.30-31 \|\|

*jalaṃdhara uvāca \|*  
*rekhāmuddhṛtya hatvā ca sagaṇaṃ tvāṃ hi śaṃkara \|*  
*hatvā lokānsuraissārddhaṃ svabhāgaṃ garuḍo yathā \|\| 30 \|\|*

*haṃtuṃ carācaraṃ sarvaṃ samartho'haṃ savāsavam \|*  
*ko maheśvara madbāṇairabhedyo bhuvanatraye \|\| 31 \|\|*

Jalandhara said:—

30-31. After uplifting the wheel, I shall be killing you with your Gaṇas. Like Garuḍa killing the serpents I shall kill all the people in the world along with the gods. I can destroy the mobile and immobile along with Indra. O lord Śiva, who is there in the three worlds that can escape being pierced by my arrows?

## \|\| 6.24.32 \|\|

*bālabhāvena bhagavāṃtapasaiva vinirjitaḥ \|*  
*brahmā baliṣṭhaḥ sthāne me munibhissurapuṃgavaiḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Even in my childhood, lord Brahmā had been defeated by my vigour. That powerful Brahmā is in my abode now along with the sages and leading gods.

## \|\| 6.24.33 \|\|

*dagdhaṃ kṣaṇena sakalaṃ trailokyaṃ sacarācaram \|*  
*tapasā kiṃ tvayā rudra nirjito bhagavānapi \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Within a trice, the entire universe of the mobile and immobile has been burnt by me. O Śiva, what can be done by you or by your penance? Even lord Brahmā has been defeated.

## \|\| 6.24.34 \|\|

*indrāgniyamavitteśavāyuvārīśvarādayaḥ \|*  
*na sehire yathā nāgā gaṃdhaṃ pakṣipateriva \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Indra, Agni, Yama, Kubera, Vāyu, and Varuṇa and others were unable to endure my valour like the serpents unable to bear even the odour of the lord of birds.

## \|\| 6.24.35 \|\|

*na labdhaṃ divi bhūmau ca vāhanaṃ mama śaṃkara \|*  
*samastānparvatānprāpya dharṣitāśca gaṇeśvarāḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. O Śiva, I have never been obstructed either in the heaven or on the earth. I have gone over all the mountains and crushed all the leading Gaṇas.

## \|\| 6.24.36 \|\|

*girīndro mandaraḥ śrīmānnīlo merussuśobhanaḥ \|*  
*dharṣito bāhudaṇḍena kaṇḍā utsarpaṇāya me \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. To remove the itching sensation in my arms I have hit the lofty mountain Mandara, the glorious mountain Nīla and the lustrous mountain Meru.

## \|\| 6.24.37 \|\|

*gaṃgā niruddhā bāhubhyāṃ līlārthaṃ himavadgirau \|*  
*aroṇāṃ mama bhṛtyaiśca jayo labdho divaukasāt \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Just for the sport the river Gaṅgā was checked by me on the Himalaya mountain. Even my servants were victorious over the gods, my enemies.

## \|\| 6.24.38 \|\|

*vaḍavāyā mukhaṃ baddhaṃ gṛhītvā tāṃ kareṇa tu \|*  
*tatkṣaṇādeva sakalamekārṇavamabhūttadā \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. I seized the submarine fire and closed its mouth when the entire ocean became one single unit instantaneously.

## \|\| 6.24.39 \|\|

*airāvatādayo nāgāḥ kṣiptāḥ sindhujalopari \|*  
*saratho bhagavānindraḥ kṣiptaśca śatayojanam \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Airāvata and other elephants have been hurled into the ocean. Lord Indra along with his chariot has been thrown by me a hundred Yojanas away.

## \|\| 6.24.40 \|\|

*garuḍo'pi mayā baddho nāgapāśena viṣṇunā \|*  
*urvaśyādyā mayānītā nāryaḥ kārāgṛhāṃtaram \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Even Guruḍa (Garuḍa?) has been bound by me along with Viṣṇu by means of the serpent noose. Urvaśī and other women have been imprisoned by me.

## \|\| 6.24.41 \|\|

*māṃ na jānāsi rudra tvaṃ trailokyajayakāriṇām \|*  
*jalaṃdharaṃ mahādaityaṃ siṃdhuputraṃ mahābalam \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. O Śiva, you do not know me the conqueror of the three worlds, Jalandhara, the great Daitya and the powerful son of the ocean.

## \|\| 6.24.42 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityuktvātha mahādevaṃ tadā vāridhinandanaḥ \|*  
*na cacāla na sasmāra nihatāndānavānyudhi \|\| 42 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

42\. After saying this to lord Śiva, the son of the ocean did not move nor did he remember the Dānavas killed in the battle.

## \|\| 6.24.43 \|\|

*durmadenāvinītena dorbhyāmāsphoṭya dorbalāt \|*  
*tiraskṛto mahādevo vacanaiḥ kaṭukākṣaraiḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Lord Śiva was slighted and insulted by means of harsh words by the haughty impudent Daitya after slapping each arm by the other forcibly.

## \|\| 6.24.44 \|\|

*tacchrutvā daityavacanamamaṃgalamatīritam \|*  
*vijahāsa mahādevāḥ paramaṃ krodhamādadhe \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. On hearing the inauspicious words of the Daitya, lord Śiva laughed mockingly and became furious.

## \|\| 6.24.45 \|\|

*sudarśanākhyaṃ yaccakraṃ padāṃguṣṭhavinirmitam \|*  
*jagrāha tatkare rudrastena haṃtuṃ samudyataḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Śiva held in his hand the wheel Sudarśana which he had made with his toe and got ready to kill him.

## \|\| 6.24.46 \|\|

*sudarśanākhyaṃ taccakraṃ cikṣepa bhagavānharaḥ \|*  
*koṭisūryapratīkāśaṃ pralayānalasannibham \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Lord Śiva hurled the discus Sudarśana which resembled a crore suns and the fire of dissolution.

## \|\| 6.24.47 \|\|

*pradahadrodasī vegāttadāsādya jalaṃdharam \|*  
*jahāra tacchiro vegānmahadāyatalocanam \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Blazing the heaven and the earth, the discus hit Jalandhara and severed his head with wide gaping eyes.

## \|\| 6.24.48 \|\|

*rathātkāyaḥ papātorvyāṃ nādayanvasudhātalam \|*  
*śiraścāpyabdhiputrasya hāhākāro mahānabhūt \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. The body of the son of the ocean fell on the ground from the chariot making the earth resonant. The head too fell. There was a great hue and cry.

## \|\| 6.24.49 \|\|

*dvidhā papāta taddeho hyaṃjanādririvācalaḥ \|*  
*kuliśena yathā vārāṃnidhau girivaro dvidhā \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. His body fell in two halves like the mountain of collyrium split by the thunderbolt and hurled in the ocean.

## \|\| 6.24.50 \|\|

*tasya raudreṇa raktena sampūrṇamabhavajjagat \|*  
*tatassamastā pṛthivī vikṛtābhūnmunīśvara \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. The whole universe was filled with his terrible blood O great sage, the entire earth became deformed.

## \|\| 6.24.51 \|\|

*tadraktamakhilaṃ rudraniyogānmāṃsameva ca \|*  
*mahārauravamāsādya raktakuṃḍamabhūdiha \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. His entire blood and flesh, at the bidding of Śiva was taken to the hell Mahāraurava and became a big pit of blood there.

## \|\| 6.24.52 \|\|

*tattejo nirgataṃ dehādrudre ca layamāgamat \|*  
*vṛndādehodbhavaṃ yadvadgauryyāṃ hi vilayaṃ gatam \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. His splendour that came out of his body merged into Śiva just like the splendour that came out of the body of Vṛndā and merged into Pārvatī.

## \|\| 6.24.53 \|\|

*jalaṃdharaṃ hataṃ dṛṣṭvā devagandharvapannagāḥ \|*  
*abhavansuprasannāśca sādhu deveti cābruvan \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. On seeing Jalandhara killed, the gods, the Gandharvas and the serpents became highly delighted and said “Well done, O lord”.

## \|\| 6.24.54 \|\|

*sarve prasannatāṃ yātā devasiddhamunīśvarāḥ \|*  
*puṣpavṛṣṭiṃ prakurvāṇāstadyaśo jaguruccakaiḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. The gods, Siddhas and great sages were delighted. Making showers of flowers they sang his glory loudly.

## \|\| 6.24.55 \|\|

*devāṃganā mahāmodānnanṛtuḥ premavihvalāḥ \|*  
*kalasvarāḥ kalapadaṃ kinnaraissaha saṃjaguḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. The celestial damsels excited by love and joy danced. In the company of Kinnaras they sang in harmonious sweet voice.

## \|\| 6.24.56 \|\|

*diśaḥ prasedussarvāśca hate vṛndāpatau mune \|*  
*vavuḥ puṇyāssukhasparśā vāyavastrividhā api \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. O sage, the quarters became clear when Vṛndā’s husband was killed. The three winds, gentle to the touch and sanctifying, blew.

## \|\| 6.24.57 \|\|

*candramāḥ śītatāṃ yāto ravistepe sutejasā \|*  
*agnayo jajvaluśśāṃtā babhūva vikṛtaṃ nabhaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. The moon became cool. The sun blazed brilliantly. The fires blazed quietly. The sky became clear.

## \|\| 6.24.58 \|\|

*evaṃ trailokyamakhilaṃ svāsthyamāpādhikaṃ mune \|*  
*hate'bdhitanaye tasminhareṇānatamūrtinā \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. O sage, thus the entire universe of the three worlds regained their earlier health and normalcy much when the son of the ocean was killed by Śiva of infinite forms.

## Chapter 25 - Prayer by the gods

## \|\| 6.25.1 \|\|

*\|\| sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*atha brahmādayo devā munayaścākhilāstathā \|*  
*tuṣṭuvurdevadeveśaṃ vāgbhiriṣṭābhirānatāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

1\. Then Brahmā, other gods and the sages eulogised lord Śiva humbly by means of pleasing words.

## \|\| 6.25.2 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*devadeva mahādeva śaraṇāgatavatsala \|*  
*sādhusaukhyapradastvaṃ hi sarvadā bhaktaduḥkhahā \|\| 2 \|\|*

The gods said:—

2\. O great lord, lord of the gods favourably disposed to those who seek refuge, you always bestow happiness upon the saintly men and quell the misery of your devotees.

## \|\| 6.25.3 \|\|

*tvaṃ mahādbhutasallīlo bhaktigamyo durāsadaḥ \|*  
*durārādhyo'satāṃ nātha prasannassarvadā bhava \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. O lord, you exhibit wonderfully good divine sports and are available by devotion. You are incapable of being attained or propitiated by the evil-minded. Be favourable to us always.

## \|\| 6.25.4 \|\|

*vedo'pi mahimānaṃ te na jānāti hi tattvataḥ \|*  
*yathāmati mahātmānassarve gāyaṃti sadyaśaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Even the Veda does not know your greatness in reality. Noble men sing your great glory to the extent of their intellect.

## \|\| 6.25.5 \|\|

*māhātmyamatigūḍhaṃ te sahasravadanādayaḥ \|*  
*sadā gāyaṃti suprītyā punaṃti svagiraṃ hi te \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Indra and others sing your secret greatness always with pleasure and sanctify their own tongue.

## \|\| 6.25.6 \|\|

*kṛpayā tava deveśa brahmajñānī bhavejjaḍaḥ \|*  
*bhaktigamyassadā tvaṃ vā iti vedā bruvaṃti hi \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. O lord of gods, by your favour even a sluggish person realizes Brahman. The Vedas say that you are always attainable by devotion.

## \|\| 6.25.7 \|\|

*tvaṃ vai dīnadayāluśca sarvatra vyāpakassadā \|*  
*āvirbhavasi sadbhaktyā nirvikārassatāṃ gatiḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. You are merciful to the distressed. You are all pervasive. You manifest yourself by good devotion. You are free from aberrations. You are the goal of the good.

## \|\| 6.25.8 \|\|

*bhaktyaiva te maheśāna bahavassiddhimāgatāḥ \|*  
*iha sarvasukhaṃ bhuktvā duḥkhitā nirvikārataḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. O Lord Śiva, by devotion alone people have attained the power of miracles. They became indifferent to the pleasures they enjoy or the miseries they have to face.

## \|\| 6.25.9 \|\|

*purā yadupatirbhakto dāśārhassiddhimāgataḥ \|*  
*kalāvatī ca tatpatnī bhaktyaiva paramāṃ prabho \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. O lord, it was by his devotion alone that the founder of the Yadu family, the devotee Dāśārha and his wife Kalāvatī attained great success.

## \|\| 6.25.10 \|\|

*tathā mitrasaho rājā madayaṃtī ca tatpriyā \|*  
*bhaktyaiva tava deveśa kaivalyaṃ paramaṃ yayau \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. O lord of gods, the king Mitrasaha and his beloved queen Madayantī attained great salvation through devotion to you.

## \|\| 6.25.11 \|\|

*sauminī nāma tanayā kaikeyāgrabhuvastathā \|*  
*tava bhaktyā sukhaṃ prāpa paraṃ sadyogidurlabham \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The daughter of the elder brother of the king of Kekayas named Sauminī attained happiness inaccessible to even great Yogins, by his devotion to you.

## \|\| 6.25.12 \|\|

*vimarṣaṇo nṛpavarassaptajanmāvadhi prabho \|*  
*bhuktvā bhogāṃśca vividhāṃstvadbhaktyā prāpa sadgatim \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. O lord, by devotion to you the excellent king Vimarṣaṇa enjoyed worldly pleasures for seven births in various ways and ultimately attained the goal of the good.

## \|\| 6.25.13 \|\|

*candraseno nṛpavarastvadbhaktyā sarvabhogabhuk \|*  
*duḥkhamuktaḥ sukhaṃ prāpa paramatra paratra ca \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The excellent king Candrasena enjoyed all pleasures, became free from misery and experienced great happiness here and hereafter by devotion to you.

## \|\| 6.25.14 \|\|

*gopīputraḥ śrīkaraste bhaktyā bhuktveha sadgatim \|*  
*paraṃ sukhaṃ mahāvīraśiṣyaḥ prāpa paratra vai \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Śrīkara, the son of a cowherdess and the disciple of Mahāvīra enjoyed the goal of the good here and great happiness hereafter by his devotion to you.

## \|\| 6.25.15 \|\|

*tvaṃ satyarathabhūjānerduḥkhahartā gatipradaḥ \|*  
*dharmaguptaṃ rājaputramatārṣīssukhinaṃ tviha \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. You removed the misery of the king Satyaratha and you conferred good goal on him. You enabled the prince Dharmagupta to cross the ocean of worldly existence and made him happy here.

## \|\| 6.25.16 \|\|

*tathā śucivrataṃ vipramadaridraṃ mahāprabho \|*  
*tvadbhaktivartinaṃ mātrā jñāninaṃ kṛpayā'karoḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. O great lord, mercifully you made the brahmin Śucivrata strictly adhering to devotion to you gain knowledge along with his mother and made him rich too.

## \|\| 6.25.17 \|\|

*citravarmā nṛpavarastvadbhaktyā prāpa sadgatim \|*  
*iha loke sadā bhuktvā bhogānamaradurlabhān \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. By his devotion to you the excellent king Citravarman perpetually enjoyed in this world the pleasures inaccessible even to the gods and attained salvation, the goal of the good.

## \|\| 6.25.18 \|\|

*candrāṃgado rājaputrassīmaṃtinyā striyā saha \|*  
*vihāya sakalaṃ duḥkhaṃ sukhī prāpa mahāgatim \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The prince Candrāṅgada along with his wife Sīmantinī got rid of all miseries, enjoyed happiness and attained great goal.

## \|\| 6.25.19 \|\|

*dvijo maṃdaranāmāpi veśyāgāmī khalo'dhamaḥ \|*  
*tvadbhaktaḥ śiva saṃpūjya tayā saha gatiṃ gataḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The brahmin named Mandara who became a base knave indulging in lecherous association with prostitutes, O Śiva, worshipped one of your women devotees and attained salvation along with her.

## \|\| 6.25.20 \|\|

*bhadrāyuste nṛpasutassukhamāpa gatavyathaḥ \|*  
*tvadbhaktakṛpayā mātrā gatiṃ ca paramāṃ prabho \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. O lord, thanks to the favour of a devotee of yours, the prince Bhadrāyu attained happiness free from pain and achieved great goal along with his mother.

## \|\| 6.25.21 \|\|

*sarvastrībhoganirato durjanastava sevayā \|*  
*vimukto'bhūdapi sadā bhakṣyabhojī maheśvara \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. O lord Śiva, even wicked sinners eating forbidden foodstuffs and indulging in sexual dalliance with all sorts of women, have been liberated by their service to you.

## \|\| 6.25.22 \|\|

*śaṃbaraśśaṃkare bhaktaścitābhasmadharassadā \|*  
*niyamādbhasmanaśśaṃbho svastriyā te puraṃ gataḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. O Śiva, Śambara a devotee of yours, smearing himself with the ashes of the funeral pyre, attained your region along with his wife, thanks to his regular adherence to Bhasma.

## \|\| 6.25.23-25 \|\|

*bhadrasenasya tanayastathā maṃtrisutaḥ prabho \|*  
*sudharmaśubhakarmāṇau sadā rudrākṣadhāriṇau \|\| 23 \|\|*

*tvatkṛpātaśca tau muktāvāstāṃ bhukteha satsukham \|*  
*pūrvajanmani yau kīśakukkuṭau rudrabhūṣaṇau \|\| 24 \|\|*

*piṃgalā ca mahānandā veśye dve tava bhaktitaḥ \|*  
*sadgatiṃ prāpaturnātha bhaktoddhāraparāyaṇa \|\| 25 \|\|*

23-25. O lord, the son of Bhadrasena and the son of his minister both of virtuous and auspicious rites and regular wearers of Rudrākṣa beads, enjoyed good pleasures here and became liberated, thanks to your grace. The two devotees who had been monkey and a cock in a previous birth became the ornaments of Rudra. O lord, always engaged in uplifting the devotees, the two courtesans Piṅgalā and Mahānandā attained the goal of the good, thanks to their devotion to you.

## \|\| 6.25.26 \|\|

*śāradā vipratanayā bālavaidhavyamāgatā \|*  
*tava bhakteḥ prabhāvāttu putrasaubhā gyavatyabhūt \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The brahmin girl Śāradā who had become a widow in childhood, was fortunate to regain her lost husband and was blessed with sons, thanks to the power of devotion to you.

## \|\| 6.25.27 \|\|

*bindugo dvijamātro hi veśyābhogī ca tatpriyā \|*  
*vaṃcukā tvadyaśaḥ śrutvā paramāṃ gatimāyayau \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Binduga, a brahmin only in name, a harlot monger and his wife Cañculā attained great salvation on hearing your glory.

## \|\| 6.25.28 \|\|

*ityādi bahavassiddhiṃ gatā jīvāstava prabho \|*  
*bhaktibhāvānmaheśāna dīnabandho kṛpālaya \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. O lord Śiva, friend of the distressed, storehouse of mercy, many living beings have attained the goal in this way.

## \|\| 6.25.29 \|\|

*tvaṃ paraḥ prakṛterbrahma puruṣātparameśvara \|*  
*nirguṇastriguṇādhāro brahmaviṣṇuharātmakaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. O lord Śiva, you are greater than Prakṛti and Puruṣa. You are the Brahman. You are devoid of attributes as well as the support of attributes in the forms of Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Rudra.

## \|\| 6.25.30 \|\|

*nānākarmakaro nityaṃ nirvikāro'khileśvaraḥ \|*  
*vayaṃ brahmādayassarve tava dāsā maheśvara \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. You are free from aberrations, O lord of all, you perform different activities incessantly. O lord Śiva, we all, Brahmā and others are your slaves.

## \|\| 6.25.31 \|\|

*prasanno bhava deveśa rakṣāsmānsarvadā śiva \|*  
*tvatprajāśca vayaṃ nātha sadā tvaccharaṇaṃ gatāḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. O lord of gods, be pleased. O Śiva, protect us ever. O lord, we are your subjects and we ever seek refuge in you.”

## \|\| 6.25.32 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*iti stutvā ca te devā brahmādyāssamunīśvarāḥ \|*  
*tūṣṇīṃ babhūvurhi tadā śivāṃghridvandvacetasaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

32\. After eulogising Brahmā, other gods and the great sages, the gods remained silent with their minds fixed on Śiva’s feet.

## \|\| 6.25.33 \|\|

*atha śaṃbhurmaheśānaḥ śrutvā devastutiṃ śubhām \|*  
*dattvā varānvarānsadyastatraivāṃtardadhe prabhuḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The great lord Śiva heard the auspicious prayer of the gods, conferred boons on them and then vanished immediately from the scene.

## \|\| 6.25.34 \|\|

*devāssarve'pi muditā brahmādyā hataśatravaḥ \|*  
*svaṃ svaṃ dhāma yayuḥ prītā gāyaṃtaḥ śivasadyaśaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Brahmā and other gods were jubilant as the enemies had been killed. Delightfully singing the great glory of Śiva, they left for their own abodes.

## \|\| 6.25.35 \|\|

*idaṃ paramamākhyānaṃ jalaṃdharavimardanam \|*  
*maheśacaritaṃ puṇyaṃ mahāghaughavināśanam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. This great narrative describing the suppression of Jalandhara is a sanctifying story of lord Śiva that destroys all sins.

## \|\| 6.25.36 \|\|

*devastutiriyaṃ puṇyā sarvapāpapraṇāśinī \|*  
*sarvasaukhyapradā nityaṃ maheśānaṃdadāyinī \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. This prayer of the gods is holy and destructive of sins. It bestows happiness on the devotees and is delightful to Śiva.

## \|\| 6.25.37 \|\|

*yaḥ paṭhetpāṭhayedvāpi samākhyānamidaṃ dvayam \|*  
*bhuktveha paraṃ saukhyaṃ gāṇapatyamavāpnuyāt \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. He who reads or teaches the two narratives, enjoys great happiness here and becomes the lord of Gaṇas hereafter.

## Chapter 26 - The Vanishing of Viṣṇu’s delusion

## \|\| 6.26.1 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*brahmaputra namaste'stu dhanyastvaṃ śaivasattama \|*  
*yacchrāvitā mahādivyā katheyaṃ śāṃkarī śubhā \|\| 1 \|\|*

Viṣṇu said:—

1\. O son of Brahmā, obeisance be to you. O excellent devotee of Śiva, you are blessed, since you have narrated this highly divine and auspicious story of Siva.

## \|\| 6.26.2 \|\|

*idānīṃ brūhi suprītyā caritaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ mune \|*  
*sa vṛndāṃ mohayitvā tu kimakārṣītkuto gataḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. O sage, now narrate lovingly the story of Viṣṇu. After enchanting Vṛndā what did he do? Where did he go?

## \|\| 6.26.3 \|\|

*\|\| sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu vyāsa mahāprājña śaivapravara sattama \|*  
*vaiṣṇavaṃ caritaṃ śaṃbhucaritāḍhyaṃ sunirmalam \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

3\. O Vyāsa, listen. O intelligent excellent devotee of Śiva, listen to the good story of Viṣṇu mingled with the story of Śiva.

## \|\| 6.26.4 \|\|

*maunībhūteṣu deveṣu brahmādiṣu maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*suprasanno'vadacchaṃbhuśśaraṇāgata vatsalaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. When Brahmā and other gods became silent, lord Śiva, favourably disposed to those who seek refuge in him, was delighted and said.

## \|\| 6.26.5 \|\|

*śaṃbhuruvāca \|*  
*brahmandevavarāssarve bhavadarthe mayā hataḥ \|*  
*jalaṃdharo madaṃśopi satyaṃ satyaṃ vadāmyaham \|\| 5 \|\|*

Śiva said:—

5\. O Brahmā, O ye excellent gods, it is for you that Jalandhara has been killed by me although he was a part of myself. Truth. It is the truth that I say.

## \|\| 6.26.6 \|\|

*sukhamāpurna vā tātāssatyaṃ brūtāmarāḥ khalu \|*  
*bhavatkṛte hi me līlā nirvikārasya sarvadā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. O dear gods, tell me the truth. Have or have not you attained happiness? It is for you that I indulge in sports though I am always free from all aberrations.

## \|\| 6.26.7 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*atha brahmādayo devā harṣādutphullalocanāḥ \|*  
*praṇamya śirasā rudraṃ śaśaṃsurviṣṇuceṣṭitam \|\| 7 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

7\. Then Brahmā and other gods, with eyes blooming with delight, bowed to Śiva with bent heads and mentioned to him the activities of Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 6.26.8 \|\|

*\|\| devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*mahādeva tvayā devā rakṣitā śśatrujādbhayāt \|*  
*kiṃcidanyatsamudbhūtaṃ tatra kiṃ karavāmahai \|\| 8 \|\|*

The gods said:—

8\. “O great lord, all the gods have been saved by you from the danger of the enemy but another event has happened. What shall we do in that respect?

## \|\| 6.26.9 \|\|

*vṛndāṃ vimohitā nātha viṣṇunā hi prayatnataḥ \|*  
*bhasmībhūtā drutaṃ vahnau paramāṃ gatimāgatā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. O lord, Vṛndā was fascinated by Viṣṇu. She burnt herself on the pyre and attained the great goal.

## \|\| 6.26.10 \|\|

*vṛndālāvaṇyasaṃbhrāṃto viṣṇustiṣṭhati mohitaḥ \|*  
*taccitābhasma saṃdhārī tava māyāvimohitaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. But Viṣṇu deluded by your illusion is excessively agitated by the beauty of Vṛndā. He has smeared himself with the ashes from her pyre.

## \|\| 6.26.11 \|\|

*sa siddhamunisaṃghaiśca bodhito'smābhirādarāt \|*  
*na budhyate harissotha tava māyāvimohitaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Although advised and consoled by the Siddhas and sages, and pacified by us with respect, Viṣṇu deluded by your illusion does not come to his former self.

## \|\| 6.26.12 \|\|

*kṛpāṃ kuru maheśāna viṣṇuṃ bodhaya bodhaya \|*  
*tvadadhīnamidaṃ sarvaṃ prākṛtaṃ sacarācaram \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. O lord Śiva, be pleased. Restore Viṣṇu to his former self. This entire creation born of Prakṛti and consisting of the mobile and immobile beings, is subservient to you”.

## \|\| 6.26.13 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya maheśo hi vacanaṃ tridivaukasām \|*  
*pratyuvāca mahālīlassvacchandastānkṛtāṃjalīn \|\| 13 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

13\. On hearing these words of the gods, lord Śiva of great sports and free to act as he pleases replied to them as they stood with palms joined in reverence.

## \|\| 6.26.14 \|\|

*maheśa uvāca \|*  
*he brahmanhe surāssarve madvākyaṃ śṛṇutādarāt \|*  
*mohinī sarvalokānāṃ mama māyā duratyayā \|\| 14 \|\|*

Lord Śiva said:—

14\. O Brahmā, O gods, you listen to my words attentively. My illusion deludes all the worlds. It cannot be transgressed.

## \|\| 6.26.15 \|\|

*tadadhīnaṃ jagatsarvaṃ yaddevāsuramānuṣam \|*  
*tayaiva mohito viṣṇuḥ kāmādhīno'bhavaddhariḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The entire universe including gods and human beings is subservient to it. Viṣṇu too was deluded by that illusion and became a prey to the lustful love.

## \|\| 6.26.16 \|\|

*umākhyā sā mahādevī tridevajananī parā \|*  
*mūlaprakṛtirākhyātā surāmā girijātmikā \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. That illusion is given various names: Umā, Mahādevī, the mother of the three deities, the greatest, primordial Mūlaprakṛti and the lovely woman Pārvatī.

## \|\| 6.26.17 \|\|

*gacchadhvaṃ śaraṇā devā viṣṇumohāpanuttaye \|*  
*śaraṇyāṃ mohinīmāyāṃ śivākhyāṃ sarvakāmadām \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. O gods, seek refuge in that fascinating goddess named illusion, for the removal of Viṣṇu’s delusion. She is the bestower of cherished desires and worthy of being sought refuge in.

## \|\| 6.26.18 \|\|

*stutiṃ kuruta tasyāśca macchaktestoṣakāriṇīm \|*  
*suprasannā yadi ca sā sarvakāryaṃ kariṣyati \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Sing the eulogy that satisfies my Śakti. If she is delighted, she will carry out your tasks.

## \|\| 6.26.19 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityuktvā tānsurāñśaṃbhuḥ pañcāsyo bhagavānharaḥ \|*  
*aṃtardadhe drutaṃ vyāsa sarvaiśca svagaṇaissaha \|\| 19 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

19\. O Vyāsa, after saying this to the gods, the five-faced lord Śiva vanished suddenly along with his Gaṇas.

## \|\| 6.26.20 \|\|

*devāśca śāsanācchaṃbhorbrahmādyā hi savāsavā \|*  
*manasā tuṣṭuvurmūlaprakṛtiṃ bhaktavatsalām \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. At the bidding of Śiva, Brahmā and other gods including Indra mentally eulogised to the primordial Prakṛti favourably disposed to her devotees.

## \|\| 6.26.21 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*yadudbhavāssattvarajastamoguṇāḥ sargasthitidhvaṃsavidhāna kārakā \|*  
*yadicchayā viśvamidaṃ bhavābhavau tanoti mūlaprakṛtiṃ natāḥ sma tām \|\| 21 \|\|*

The gods said:—

21\. We bow to the primordial Prakṛti from which emanate the three attributes Sattva, Rajas and Tamas that cause creation, sustenance and annihilation, and by whose desire the universe is evolved and dissolved.

## \|\| 6.26.22 \|\|

*pāhi trayoviṃśaguṇānsuśabditāñjagatyaśeṣe samadhiṣṭhitā parā \|*  
*yadrūpakarmāṇijagattrayo'pi te vidurna mūlaprakṛtiṃ natāḥ sma tām \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. May the great illusion save us, the great Prakṛti that presides over the twentythree principles, well enunciated in the universe. We bow to the primordial Prakṛti whose forms and activities are not known to the three worlds.

## \|\| 6.26.23 \|\|

*yadbhaktiyuktāḥ puruṣāstu nityaṃ dāridryamohātyayasaṃbhavādīn \|*  
*na prāpnuvaṃtyeva hi bhaktavatsalāṃ sadaiva mūlaprakṛtiṃ natāḥ sma tām \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. We bow to the primordial Prakṛti favourably disposed to the devotees. Persons endowed with devotion to her are not bedevilled by poverty, delusion and destruction.

## \|\| 6.26.24 \|\|

*kuru kāryaṃ mahādevi devānāṃ naḥ pareśvari \|*  
*viṣṇumohaṃ ha śive durge devi namo'stu te \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. O great goddess, please carry out our tasks. O Pārvatī, please remove the delusion of Viṣṇu. O goddess Durgā, obeisance be to you.

## \|\| 6.26.25-26 \|\|

*jalaṃdharasya śaṃbhośca raṇe kailāsavāsinaḥ \|*  
*pravṛtte tadvadhārthāya gaurīśāsanataśśive \|\| 25 \|\|*

*vṛndā vimohitā devi viṣṇunā hi prayatnataḥ \|*  
*svavṛṣāttyājitā vahnau bhasmībhūtā gatiṃ gatā \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. O Śivā, when the fight between Jalandhara and Śiva started, for killing Jalandhara, Vṛndā was deluded by Viṣṇu at the bidding of Gaurī. She was made to forsake her virtue and reduced to ashes in the fire. She attained salvation.

## \|\| 6.26.27 \|\|

*jalaṃdharo hato yuddhe tadbhayānmo citā vayam \|*  
*giriśena kṛpāṃ kṛtvā bhaktānugrahakāriṇā \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Jalandhara was slain in the battle by Śiva who took pity on us and who always blesses his devotees. We have been relieved from his fear.

## \|\| 6.26.28 \|\|

*tadājñayā vayaṃ sarve śaraṇaṃ te samāgatāḥ \|*  
*tvaṃ hi śaṃbhuryuvāṃ devi bhaktoddhāraparāyaṇau \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. It is at his bidding that we all have sought refuge in you. You and Śiva, O goddess, are always engaged in uplifting your devotees.

## \|\| 6.26.29 \|\|

*vṛndālāvaṇyasaṃbhrāto viṣṇustiṣṭhati tatra vai \|*  
*taccitābhasmasaṃdhārī jñānabhraṣṭo vimohitaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Infatuated by the beauty of Vṛndā, Viṣṇu is staying there itself. He has lost his balance. He is deluded. He has smeared himself with the ashes from her pyre.

## \|\| 6.26.30 \|\|

*saṃsiddhasurasaṃghaiśca bodhito'pi maheśvari \|*  
*na budhyate harissotha tava māyāvimohitaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. O great goddess deluded by your illusion, Viṣṇu does not come to his own though advised and consoled by the gods and Siddhas.

## \|\| 6.26.31 \|\|

*kṛpāṃ kuru mahādevi hariṃ bodhaya bodhaya \|*  
*yathā svalokaṃ pāyātsa sucittassurakāryakṛt \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. O great goddess, be merciful. Enlighten Viṣṇu so that he shall return to his region and carry out the task of the gods with a settled mind.

## \|\| 6.26.32 \|\|

*iti stuvaṃtaste devāstejomaṃḍalamāsthitam \|*  
*dadṛśurgagane tatra jvālāvyāptā digaṃtaram \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Eulogising thus, the gods saw a sphere of refulgence in the sky pervading all the quarters with its flames.

## \|\| 6.26.33 \|\|

*tanmadhyādbhāratīṃ sarve brahmādyāśca savāsavāḥ \|*  
*amarāśśuśruvurvyāsa kāmadāṃ vyomacāriṇīm \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. O Vyāsa, Brahmā and other gods including Indra heard a celestial voice from the sky bestowing their desire.

## \|\| 6.26.34 \|\|

*ākāśavāṇyuvāca \|*  
*ahameva tridhā bhinnā tiṣṭhāmi trividhairguṇaiḥ \|*  
*gaurī lakṣmīḥ surā jyotī rajassattvatamoguṇaiḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

The celestial voice said:—

34\. O gods, it is I who stand in three forms by the variety of the three attributes, Rajas, Sattva and Tamas. The three forms are Gaurī, Lakṣmī, and Sarasvatī.

## \|\| 6.26.35 \|\|

*tatra gacchata yūyaṃ vai tāsāmaṃtika ādarāt \|*  
*madājñayā prasannāstā vidhāsyaṃte tadīpsitam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Hence you go to them respectfully at my bidding. If they are pleased they will fulfil your desire.

## \|\| 6.26.36 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇvatāmiti tāṃ vācamaṃtarddhānamagānmahaḥ \|*  
*devānāṃ vismayotphullanetrāṇāṃ tattadā mune \|\| 36 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

36\. Even as the gods were listening to this speech with eyes gaping with wonder, the refulgence vanished.

## \|\| 6.26.37 \|\|

*tatassaveṃ'pi te devāḥ śrutvā tadvākyamādarāt \|*  
*gaurīṃ lakṣmīṃ surāṃ caiva nemustadvākyacoditāḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. On hearing the speech, the gods, urged by it bowed respectfully to Gaurī, Lakṣmī and Sarasvatī.

## \|\| 6.26.38 \|\|

*tuṣṭuvuśca mahābhaktyā devīstāssakalāssurāḥ \|*  
*nānāvidhābhirvāgbhiste brahmādyā natamastakāḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Brahmā and other gods eulogised the goddesses with various speeches and bowed their heads.

## \|\| 6.26.39 \|\|

*tato'raṃ vyāsa devyastā āvirbhūtāśca tatpuraḥ \|*  
*mahādbhutaissvatejobhirbhāsayaṃtyo digaṃtaram \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Then the goddesses appeared in front of them, suddenly, O Vyasa, illuminating the quarters with their wonderful brilliance.

## \|\| 6.26.40 \|\|

*atha tā amarā dṛṣṭvā suprasannena cetasā \|*  
*praṇamya tuṣṭuvurbhaktyā svakāryaṃ ca nyavedayan \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. On seeing them, the gods eulogised them with great devotion and delighted minds. They submitted what they wanted to be carried out.

## \|\| 6.26.41 \|\|

*tataścaitāssurāndṛṣṭvā praṇatānbhaktavatsalaḥ \|*  
*bījāni pradadustebhyo vākyamūcuśca sādaram \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Thus bowed and eulogised, the goddesses who are favourably disposed to the devotees, faced the gods and addressed them eagerly after giving them seeds.

## \|\| 6.26.42 \|\|

*devya ūcuḥ \|*  
*imāni tatra bījāni viṣṇuryatrāvatiṣṭhati \|*  
*nirvapadhvaṃ tataḥ kāryaṃ bhavatāṃ siddhimeṣyati \|\| 42 \|\|*

The goddesses said:—

42\. “Sow these seeds in the place where Viṣṇu is standing. Then your task will be fulfilled.”

## \|\| 6.26.43 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityuktvā tāstato devyoṃtarhitā abhavanmune \|*  
*rudraviṣṇuvidhīnāṃ hi śaktayastriguṇātmikāḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

43\. O sage, after saying this, the goddesses, the Śaktis of Śiva, Viṣṇu and Brahmā, possessed of the three attributes, vanished.

## \|\| 6.26.44 \|\|

*tatastuṣṭāḥ surāssarve brahmādyāśca savāsavāḥ \|*  
*tāni bījāni saṃgṛhya yayuryatra hariḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Then Brahmā and other gods including Indra took the seeds and went to the place where Viṣṇu was standing.

## \|\| 6.26.45 \|\|

*vṛndācitābhūmitale cikṣipustāni te surāḥ \|*  
*smṛtvā tāssaṃsthitāstatra śivaśaktyaṃśakā mune \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. The gods sowed those seeds in the ground where the pyre of Vṛndā had been lit. O sage, they stayed there thinking these as parts of Śiva’s Śakti.

## \|\| 6.26.46 \|\|

*nikṣiptebhyaśca bījebhyo vanaspatyastrayo'bhavan \|*  
*dhātrī ca mālatī caiva tulasī ca munīśvara \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Out of the seeds sown, O great sage, three plants shot up—the Myrobalan, the Jasmine and the holy basil.

## \|\| 6.26.47 \|\|

*dhātryudbhavā smṛtā dhātrī mābhavā mālatī smṛtā \|*  
*gaurībhavā ca tulasī tamassattvarajoguṇāḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. The Myrobalan is born of the creator’s Śakti, the jasmine of Lakṣmī and holy basil of Gaurī, born of the attributes Tamas, Sattva and Rajas.

## \|\| 6.26.48 \|\|

*viṣṇurvanaspatīrdṛṣṭvā tadā strīrūpiṇīrmune \|*  
*udatiṣṭhattadā tāsu rāgātiśayavibhramāt \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. O sage, on seeing the plants in the forms of ladies Viṣṇu stood up with excitement of infatuation over them.

## \|\| 6.26.49 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā sa yācate mohātkāmāsaktena cetasā \|*  
*taṃ cāpi tulasī dhātrī rāgeṇaivāvalokatām \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. On seeing them he was deluded and his mind became overwhelmed by lust. The two plants—the holy basil and Myrobalan looked at him lovingly.

## \|\| 6.26.50 \|\|

*yacca bījaṃ purā lakṣmyā māyayaiva samarpitam \|*  
*tasmāttadudbhavā nārī tasminnīrṣyāparābhavat \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. The womanlike plant born out of the seed by the Śakti of Lakṣmī became jealous of him.

## \|\| 6.26.51 \|\|

*atassā barbarītyākhyāmavāpātīva garhitām \|*  
*dhātrītulasyau tadrāgāttasya prītiprade sadā \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Hence the plant came to be called Varvarī (a kind of wild basil) and was despised by all. The Dhātrī and the Tulasī are always pleasing to him due to their love and affection.

## \|\| 6.26.52 \|\|

*tato vismṛtaduḥkho'sau viṣṇustābhyāṃ sahaiva tu \|*  
*vaikuṃṭhamagamattuṣṭassarvadevairnamaskṛtaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Then Viṣṇu forgot his sorrow. Accompanied by them he went to Vaikuṇṭha fully satisfied. He was bowed to by all the gods.

## \|\| 6.26.53 \|\|

*kārtike māsi viprendra dhātrī ca tulasī sadā \|*  
*sarvadevapriyājñeyā viṣṇoścaiva viśeṣataḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. O great brahmin, myrobolan and the holy basil shall be understood as the favourites of gods in the month of Kārttika, especially of Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 6.26.54 \|\|

*tatrāpi tulasī dhanyātīva śreṣṭhā mahāmune \|*  
*tyaktvā gaṇeśaṃ sarveṣāṃ prītidā sarvakāmadā \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. There too, O great sage, the holy basil is the most blessed and the most excellent. Except Gaṇeśa it delights every deity and bestows all desires.

## \|\| 6.26.55 \|\|

*vaikuṇṭhasthaṃ hariṃ dṛṣṭvā brahmendrādyāśca te'marāḥ \|*  
*natvā stutvā mahāviṣṇuṃ svasvadhāmāni vai yayuḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. On seeing Viṣṇu settled again in Vaikuṇṭha, Brahmā, Indra and other gods bowed to and eulogised him and then left for their respective abodes.

## \|\| 6.26.56 \|\|

*vaikuṇṭho'pi svalokastho bhraṣṭamohassubodhavān \|*  
*sukhī cābhūnmuniśreṣṭha pūrvavatsaṃsmarañchivam \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. O excellent sage, Viṣṇu too, settled in his own world, freed from delusion and enlightened, became happy remembering Śiva as before.

## \|\| 6.26.57 \|\|

*ityākhyānamaghoghaghnaṃ sarvakāmapradaṃ nṛṇām \|*  
*sarva kāmavikāraghnaṃ sarvavijñānavarddhanam \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. This is the narrative that destroys sins, bestows desires to all men. It increases perfect knowledge and quells all aberrations of base lust.

## \|\| 6.26.58 \|\|

*ya idaṃ hi paṭhennityaṃ pāṭhayedvāpi bhaktiman \|*  
*śṛṇuyācchrāvayedvāpi sa yāti paramāṃ gatim \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. He who reads or teaches this every day, he who hears or narrates this with devotion attains the greatest goal.

## \|\| 6.26.59 \|\|

*paṭhitvā ya idaṃ dhīmānākhyānaṃ paramottamam \|*  
*saṃgrāmaṃ praviśedvīro vijayī syānna saṃśayaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. The intelligent man who reads this most excellent narrative and goes to war will certainly be victorious. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 6.26.60 \|\|

*viprāṇāṃ brahmavidyādaṃ satriyāṇāṃ jayapradam \|*  
*vaiśyānāṃ sarvadhanadaṃ śūdrāṇāṃ sukhadaṃ tvidam \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. This yields the knowledge of Vedas to the brahmins, victory to the Kṣatriyas, wealth to the Vaiśyas and happiness to the Śūdras.

## \|\| 6.26.61 \|\|

*śaṃbhubhaktipradaṃ vyāsa sarveṣāṃ pāpanāśanam \|*  
*ihaloke paratrāpi sadā sadgatidāyakam \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. O Vyāsa, it confers devotion to Śiva, it destroys the sins of all persons, it bestows the good goal here and hereafter.

## Chapter 27 - The birth of Śaṅkhacūḍa

## \|\| 6.27.1 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*athānyacchaṃbhucaritaṃ premataḥ śṛṇu vai mune \|*  
*yasya śravaṇamātreṇa śivabhaktirdṛḍhā bhavet \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

1\. O sage, now listen to another story of Śiva lovingly, by listening to which the devotion to Śiva is stabilised.

## \|\| 6.27.2 \|\|

*śaṃkhacūḍābhidho vīro dānavo devakaṃṭakaḥ \|*  
*yathā śivena nihato raṇamūrdhni triśūlataḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The story narrates how the heroic Dānava Śaṅkhacūḍa who harassed the gods was killed by Śiva in the battle by means of his trident.

## \|\| 6.27.3 \|\|

*tacchaṃbhucaritaṃ divyaṃ pavitraṃ pāpanāśanam \|*  
*śṛṇu vyāsa susaṃprītyā vacmi susnehatastava \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. O Vyāsa, listen lovingly to the story of Śiva, divine, holy and destructive of sins. I shall narrate the same because of my affection to you.

## \|\| 6.27.4 \|\|

*marīcestanayo dhātuḥ putro yaḥ kaśyapo muniḥ \|*  
*sa dharmiṣṭhassṛṣṭikarttā vidhyājñaptaḥ prajāpatiḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The sage Kaśyapa son of Marīci and grandson of Brahmā was a virtuous Prajāpati engaged in creation. He possessed great learning.

## \|\| 6.27.5 \|\|

*dakṣaḥ prītyā dadau tasmai nijakanyāstrayodaśa \|*  
*tāsāṃ prasūtiḥ prasabhaṃ na kathyā bahuvistṛtāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*
