5\. Dakṣa gave him his thirteen daughters in marriage. The descendants of these women are many and they cannot be enumerated easily.

## \|\| 6.27.6 \|\|

*yatra devādinikhilaṃ carācaramabhūjjagat \|*  
*vistarāttatpravaktuṃ ca kaḥ kṣamo'sti trilokake \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The whole universe consisting of gods and others the mobile and immobile is born of them. Who in the three worlds can mention this in detail?

## \|\| 6.27.7 \|\|

*prastutaṃ śṛṇu vṛttāṃtaṃ śaṃbhulīlānvitaṃ ca yat \|*  
*tadeva kathayāmyadya śṛṇu bhaktipra varddhanam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Listen to what is relevant to the context wherein the divine sports of Śiva too can be seen. It is conducive to the increase of devotion. I am narrating the same.

## \|\| 6.27.8 \|\|

*tāsu kaśyapatnīṣu danustvekā varāṃganā \|*  
*mahārūpavatī sādhvī patisaubhāgyavarddhitā \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Among the wives of Kaśyapa the excellent lady Danu was one. She was very beautiful, chaste and tenderly nurtured by her husband with all devotion and love.

## \|\| 6.27.9 \|\|

*āsaṃstasyā danoḥ putrā bahavo balavattarāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ nāmāni nocyaṃte vistārabhayato mune \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Many powerful sons were born to that lady Danu. Their names are not mentioned O sage, by the fear of dilation.

## \|\| 6.27.10 \|\|

*teṣveko vipracittistu mahābalaparākramaḥ \|*  
*tatputro dhārmiko daṃbho viṣṇubhakto jitendriyaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. One of them is Vipracitti who was very powerful and valorous. His virtuous son Dambha of self-control was a great devotee of Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 6.27.11-12 \|\|

*nāsīttattanayo vīrastataściṃtāparo'bhavat \|*  
*śukrācāryaṃ guruṃ kṛtvā kṛṣṇamaṃtramavāpya ca \|\| 11 \|\|*

*tapaścakāra paramaṃ puṣkare lakṣavarṣakam \|*  
*kṛṣṇamaṃtraṃ jajāpaiva dṛḍhaṃ baddhāsanaṃ ciram \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. No son was born to him. Hence the hero became worried. He made the preceptor Śukra his initiator and learnt the mantra of Kṛṣṇa. He performed a great penance in the holy centre Puṣkara for a hundred thousand years. Seating himself in a stable pose he performed the Japa of Kṛṣṇa mantra for a long time.

## \|\| 6.27.13 \|\|

*tapaḥ prakurvatastasya mūrdhno nissṛtya prajva lat \|*  
*visasāra ca sarvatra tattejo hi sudussaham \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. While be was performing the penance, an unbearable refulgence sprang up blazing from his head and spread everywhere.

## \|\| 6.27.14 \|\|

*tena taptāssurāssarve munayo manavastathā \|*  
*sunāsīraṃ puraskṛtya brahmāṇaṃ śaraṇaṃ yayuḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. All the gods, sages and Manus were scorched by that. With Indra ahead they sought refuge in Brahmā.

## \|\| 6.27.15 \|\|

*praṇamya ca vidhātāraṃ dātāraṃ sarvasaṃpadām \|*  
*tuṣṭuvurvikalāḥ procuḥ svavṛttāṃtaṃ viśeṣataḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Bowing to Brahmā, the bestower of riches, they eulogised him and narrated to him this event.

## \|\| 6.27.16 \|\|

*tadākarṇya vidhātāpi vaikuṃṭhaṃ tairyayau saha \|*  
*tadeva vijñāpayituṃ nikhilena hi viṣṇave \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. On hearing that, Brahmā accompanied them to Vaikuṇṭha in order to tell the same to Viṣṇu in its entirety.

## \|\| 6.27.17 \|\|

*tatra gatvā trilokeśaṃ viṣṇuṃ rakṣākaraṃ param \|*  
*praṇamya tuṣṭuvussarve karau baddhvā vinamrakāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. After going there they stood humbly joining their palms in reverence. After bowing to him they eulogised Viṣṇu the lord of the three worlds, the great saviour.

The gods said'.—

## \|\| 6.27.18 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*devadeva na jānīmo jātaṃ kiṃ kāraṇaṃ tviha \|*  
*saṃtaptāssa kalā jātāstejasā kena tadvada \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. “O lord of gods we do not know how this happened to cause this. Please tell us. By what refulgence have all of us been scorched?

## \|\| 6.27.19 \|\|

*taptātmanāṃ tvamavitā dīnabaṃdho'nujīvinām \|*  
*rakṣarakṣa ramānātha śaraṇyaśśaraṇāgatān \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. O friend of the distressed, you are the protector of the distressed and dispirited servants. Save, O lord of Lakṣrnī who are worthy of being sought refuge by us.

## \|\| 6.27.20 \|\|

*\|\| sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*iti śrutvā vaco viṣṇurbrahmādīnāṃ divaukasām \|*  
*uvāca vihasanpremṇā śaraṇāgatavatsalaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

20\. On hearing these words of Brahmā and other gods, Viṣṇu who is favourably disposed to those who seek refuge, said laughingly and lovingly.

## \|\| 6.27.21 \|\|

*\|\| viṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*susvasthā bhavatāvyagrā na bhayaṃ kurutāmarāḥ \|*  
*nopaplavā bhaviṣyante layakālo na vidyate \|\| 21 \|\|*

Viṣṇu said:—

21\. “O gods, be calm and unperturbed, do not be afraid. No deluge will take place, this is not the time of dissolution.

## \|\| 6.27.22 \|\|

*dānavo daṃbhanāmā hi madbhaktaḥ kurute tapaḥ \|*  
*putrārthī śamayiṣyāmi tamahaṃ varadānataḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The Asura Dambha a devotee of mine is performing a penance seeking for a son. I shall bestow a boon and quieten him.”

## \|\| 6.27.23 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityuktāste surāssarve dhairyamālaṃbya vai mune \|*  
*yayurbrahmādayassusthāssvasvadhāmāni sarvaśaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

23\. O sage, on being consoled thus, Brahmā and other gods became encouraged and they returned to their respective abodes.

## \|\| 6.27.24 \|\|

*acyuto'pi varaṃ dātuṃ puṣkaraṃ saṃjagāma ha \|*  
*tapaścarati yatrāsau daṃbhanāmā hi dānavaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. In order to grant the boon, Viṣṇu went to Puṣkara where Dambha was performing penance.

## \|\| 6.27.25 \|\|

*tatra gatvā varaṃ brūhītyuvāca parisāṃtvayan \|*  
*girā sūnṛtayā bhaktaṃ japaṃtaṃ svamanuṃ hariḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. On reaching there Viṣṇu consoled Dambha who was repeating his name and told him the pleasing words—“Mention the boon you wish to be granted.”

## \|\| 6.27.26 \|\|

*tacchrutvā vacanaṃ viṣṇordṛṣṭvā taṃ ca puraḥ sthitam \|*  
*praṇanāma mahābhaktyā tuṣṭvāva ca punaḥ punaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. On hearing his words and seeing Viṣṇu standing in front, the Danava bowed with great devotion and eulogised him again and again.

## \|\| 6.27.27 \|\|

*daṃbha uvāca \|*  
*devadeva namaste'stu puṃḍarīkavilocana \|*  
*ramānātha trilokeśa kṛpā kuru mamopari \|\| 27 \|\|*

Dambha said:—

27\. “O lord of gods, Obeisance be to you, O Lotuseyed one, O lord of Lakṣmī, O lord of the three worlds, please take pity on me.

## \|\| 6.27.28 \|\|

*svabhaktaṃ tanayaṃ dehi mahābala parākramam \|*  
*trilokajayinaṃ vīramajeyaṃ ca divaukasām \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Please give me a powerful and valorous son who will be your devotee, who will be invincible to the gods and who will conquer the three worlds.”

## \|\| 6.27.29 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityukto dānavendreṇa taṃ varaṃ pradadau hariḥ \|*  
*nivartya cogratapasastatassoṃtaradhānmune \|\| 29 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

29\. On being thus requested by the lord of Dānavas, Viṣṇu granted him the boon. O sage, making him desist from the penance he vanished from the place.

## \|\| 6.27.30 \|\|

*gate harau dānavendraḥ kṛtvā tasyai diśe namaḥ \|*  
*jagāma svagṛhaṃ siddhatadāḥ pūrṇa manorathaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. When Viṣṇu went away, the lord of Danavas performed obeisance to that direction and returned home, his penance having been fulfilled and his desires realised.

## \|\| 6.27.31 \|\|

*kālenālpena tatpatnī sagarbhā bhāgyavatyabhūt \|*  
*rarāja tejāsātyaṃtaṃ rocayaṃtī gṛhāṃtaram \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Within a short time, his fortunate wife became pregnant. Illuminating the inner apartments of her abode by her brilliance she shone much.

## \|\| 6.27.32 \|\|

*sudāmānāma gopo yo kṛṣṇasya pārṣadāgraṇīḥ \|*  
*tasyā garbhe viveśāsau rādhāśaptaśca yanmune \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. O sage, it was Sudāmā a cowherd, one of the leading comrades of Kṛṣṇa who had been cursed by Rādhā, that entered her womb.

## \|\| 6.27.33 \|\|

*asūta samaye sādhvī suprabhaṃ tanayaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*jātakaṃ sucakārāsau pitāhūya munīnbahūn \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. At the proper time the chaste lady gave birth to a brilliant son. The father invited sages and performed the post-natal rites.

## \|\| 6.27.34 \|\|

*utsavassumahānāsīttasmiñjāte dvijottama \|*  
*nāma cakre pitā tasya śaṃkha cūḍeti saddine \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. O excellent brahmin, when the boy was born there was great jubilation. On an auspicious day the father named him “Śaṅkhacūḍa.”

## \|\| 6.27.35 \|\|

*piturgehe sa vavṛdhe śuklapakṣe yathā śaśī \|*  
*śaiśavebhyastavidyastu sa babhūva sudīptimān \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. In the abode of his father he grew up like the moon in the bright half. Learning all lores in childhood he became resplendent.

## \|\| 6.27.36 \|\|

*sa bālakrīḍayā nityaṃ pitrorharṣaṃ tatāna ha \|*  
*priyo babhūva sarveṣāṃ kulajānāṃ viśeṣataḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. With his childish sports he increased the parents’ delight. He became a special favourite of all the members of the family.

## Chapter 28 - The penance and marriage of Śaṅkhacūḍa

## \|\| 6.28.1 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*tataśca śaṃkhacūḍo'sau jaigīṣavyopadeśataḥ \|*  
*tataścakāra suprītyā brahmaṇaḥ puṣkare ciram \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

1\. As instructed by Jaigīṣavya, Śaṅkhacūḍa performed a penance in Puṣkara for a long time in order to propitiate Brahmā with devotion.

## \|\| 6.28.2 \|\|

*gurudattāṃ brahmavidyāṃ jajāpa niyatendriyaḥ \|*  
*sa ekāgramanā bhūtvā karaṇāni nigṛhya ca \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. He concentrated his mind, controlled the senses and organs of activities, and muttered the mantra of Brahmā imparted by his preceptor.

## \|\| 6.28.3 \|\|

*tapaṃtaṃ puṣkare taṃ vai śaṃkhacūḍaṃ ca dānavam \|*  
*varaṃ dātuṃ jagāmāśu brahmālokagururvibhuḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Lord Brahmā, the preceptor of the worlds, went to Śaṅkhacūḍa who was practising penance at Puṣkara in order to grant him the boon soon.

## \|\| 6.28.4 \|\|

*varaṃ brūhīti provāca dānavendraṃ vidhistadā \|*  
*sa dṛṣṭvā taṃ nanāmāti namrastuṣṭāva sadgirā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Brahmā said to him: “Tell me the boon you wish to choose.” On seeing Brahmā, the king of Dānavas bowed to him humbly and eulogised him with words of devotion.

## \|\| 6.28.5 \|\|

*varaṃ yayāce brahmāṇamajeyatvaṃ divaukasām \|*  
*tathetyāha vidhistaṃ vai suprasannena cetasā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. He requested Brahmā to grant him the power of being invincible to the gods. With a delighted mind, Brahmā said “Be it so.”

## \|\| 6.28.6 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇakavacaṃ divyaṃ jaganmaṃgalamaṃgalam \|*  
*dattavāñśaṃkhacūḍāya sarvatra vijayapradam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. He gave Śaṅkhacūḍa the divine amulet of Śrīkṛṣṇa the most auspicious of all auspicious things in the universe, that yielded victory everywhere.

## \|\| 6.28.7 \|\|

*badarīṃ saṃprayāhi tvaṃ tulasyā saha tatra vai \|*  
*vivāhaṃ kuru tatraiva sā tapasyati kāmataḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. “You now go to Badari. There you marry Tulasī who is performing penance just at her own will.

## \|\| 6.28.8 \|\|

*dharmadhvajasutā seti saṃdideśa ca taṃ vidhiḥ \|*  
*antardhānaṃ jagāmāśu paśyatastasya tatkṣaṇāt \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. She is the daughter of Dharmadhvaja.” Brahmā instructed him thus and vanished even as he was watching him.

## \|\| 6.28.9 \|\|

*tatassa śaṃkhacūḍo hi tapaḥsiddho'tipuṣkare \|*  
*gale babaṃdha kavacaṃ jaganmaṃgalamaṃgalam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Then Śaṅkhacūḍa whose penance had been fruitful in the holy centre of Puṣkara tied the most auspicious amulet round his neck.

## \|\| 6.28.10 \|\|

*ājñayā brāhmaṇasso'pi tapaḥsiddhamanorathaḥ \|*  
*samāyayau prahṛṣṭāsyastūrṇaṃ badarikāśramam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. At the behest of Brahmā, the Dānava whose desire had been achieved through penance went to Badarikāśrama with delight beaming in his face.

## \|\| 6.28.11 \|\|

*yadṛcchayā''gatastatra śaṃkhacūḍaśca dānavaḥ \|*  
*tapaścarantī tulasī yatra dharmadhvajātmajā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The Dānava Śaṅkhacūḍa casually visited the place where the daughter of Dharmadhvaja, Tulasī was performing the penance.

## \|\| 6.28.12 \|\|

*surūpā susmitā tanvī śubhabhūṣaṇabhūṣitā \|*  
*sakaṭākṣaṃ dadarśāsau tameva puruṣaṃ param \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The smiling beautiful gentle woman fully bedecked in ornaments cast loving glances at the great man.

## \|\| 6.28.13 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā tāṃ lalitā ramyāṃ suśīlāṃ sundarīṃ satīm \|*  
*uvāsa tatsamīpe tu madhuraṃ tāmuvāca saḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. On seeing that charming, tender, beautiful and chaste lady, he stopped near her and spoke to her sweetly.

## \|\| 6.28.14 \|\|

*śaṃkhacūḍa uvāca \|*  
*kā tvaṃ kasya sutā tvaṃ hi kiṃ karoṣi sthitātra kim \|*  
*maunībhūtā kiṃkaraṃ māṃ saṃbhāvitumihārhasi \|\| 14 \|\|*

Śaṅkhacūḍa said:—

14\. “Who are you, please? Whose daughter? What are you doing? Why do you stay here and observe silence. Consider me as your devoted slave.”

## \|\| 6.28.15 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityevaṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā sakāmaṃ tamuvāca sā \|\| 15 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

15\. On hearing these words she spoke to him lovingly.

## \|\| 6.28.16 \|\|

*tulasyuvāca \|*  
*dharmadhvajasutāhaṃ ca tapasyāmi tapasvinī \|*  
*tapovane ca tiṣṭhāmi kastvaṃ gaccha yathāsukham \|\| 16 \|\|*

Tulasī said:—

16\. I am the daughter of Dharmadhvaja. I am performing penance. I stay in this hermitage. Who are you? You can go as you please.

## \|\| 6.28.17 \|\|

*nārījātirmohinī ca brahmādīnāṃ viṣopamā \|*  
*nindyā doṣakarī māyā śṛṃkhalā hyanuśāyinām \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The entire class of women is fascinating. It enchants even Brahmā, not to speak of others. It is censurable, poisonous and deceptive. It is illusion and a fetter to the devout and the faithful.

## \|\| 6.28.18 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityuktvā tulasī taṃ ca sarasaṃ virarāma ha \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā tāṃ sasmitāṃ sopi pravaktumupacakrame \|\| 18 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

18\. Tulasī thus spoke to the passionate Dambha and stopped. On seeing her smiling he began to say.

## \|\| 6.28.19 \|\|

*śaṃkhacūḍa uvāca \|*  
*tvayā yatkathitaṃ devi na ca sarvamalīkakam \|*  
*kiñcitsatyamalīkaṃ ca kiṃcinmatto niśāmaya \|\| 19 \|\|*

Śaṅkhacūḍa said:—

19\. O gentle lady, what you said now is not entirely false. It is partially true also. Now listen to me.

## \|\| 6.28.20 \|\|

*pativratāḥ striyo yāśca tāsāṃ madhye tvamagraṇīḥ \|*  
*na cāhaṃ pāpadṛkkāmī tathā tvaṃ neti dhīrmama \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. You are the foremost among chaste ladies. I am not a lusty person of sinful nature. I think you too are not like that.

## \|\| 6.28.21 \|\|

*āgacchāmi tvatsamīpamājñayā brahmaṇo'dhunā \|*  
*gāṃdharveṇa vivāhena tvāṃ grahīṣyāmi śobhane \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. I come to you now at the behest of Brahmā. O gently lady, I shall take your hand by the Gāndharva rites of marriage.

## \|\| 6.28.22 \|\|

*śaṃkhacūḍo'hamevāsmi devavidrāvakārakaḥ \|*  
*māṃ na jānāsi kiṃ bhadre na śruto'haṃ kadācana \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. I am Śaṅkhacūḍa, the router of the gods. O gentle lady, don’t you know me? Have I never been heard by you?

## \|\| 6.28.23 \|\|

*danuvaṃśyo viśeṣeṇa manda putraśca dānavaḥ \|*  
*sudāmā nāma gopohaṃ pārṣadaśca hareḥ purā \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. I am a scion of the family of Danu. I am a Dānava, the son of Dambha. In the previous birth I was the cowherd Sudāmā, a comrade of Kṛṣṇa.

## \|\| 6.28.24 \|\|

*adhunā dānavendro'haṃ rādhikāyāśca śāpataḥ \|*  
*jātismaro'haṃ jānāmi sarvaṃ kṛṣṇaprabhāvataḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Due to the curse of Rādhā I have become a Dānava now. By the favour of Kṛṣṇa I remember events of previous birth. I know everything.

## \|\| 6.28.25 \|\|

*\|\| sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*evamuktvā śaṃkhacūḍo virarāma ca tatpuraḥ \|*  
*dānaveṃdreṇa setyuktā vacanaṃ satyamādarāt \|*  
*sasmitaṃ tulasī tuṣṭā pravaktumupacakrame \|\| 25 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

25\. After saying thus to her, Śaṅkhacūḍa stopped. Tulasī who was thus addressed truthfully and respectfully by the king of Dānavas, was delighted and she spoke smilingly.

## \|\| 6.28.26 \|\|

*tulasyuvāca \|*  
*tvayāhamadhunā \|\| sattvavicāreṇa parājitā \|*  
*sa dhanyaḥ puruṣo loke na striyā yaḥ parājitaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

Tulasī said:—

26\. I have now been overpowered by you who have Sāttvika thoughts. That man is blessed in the world who is not overwhelmed by a woman.

## \|\| 6.28.27 \|\|

*satkriyopyaśucirnityaṃ sa pumānyaḥ striyā jitaḥ \|*  
*nindaṃti pitaro devā mānavāssakalāśca tam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Even though he may be the observer of sacred rites, if he is overpowered by a woman he becomes impure and unclean, so he remains for ever. The manes, gods and human beings censure him.

## \|\| 6.28.28-29 \|\|

*śudhyedvipro daśāhena jātake mṛtasūtake \|*  
*kṣatriyo dvādaśāhena vaiśyaḥ pañcadaśāhataḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*śūdro māsena śudhyettu hīti vedānuśāsanam \|*  
*na śuciḥ strījitaḥ kvāpi citādāhaṃ vinā pumān \|\| 29 \|\|*

28-29. A brahmin is purified from impurity arising from births or deaths in the family, after the tenth day. A Kṣatriya in twelve days, a Vaiśya in fifteen days and a Śūdra in a month. This is what the Vedas enjoin. But a henpecked man can never be purified till death.

## \|\| 6.28.30 \|\|

*na gṛhṇatīcchayā tasmātpitaraḥ piṇḍatarpaṇam \|*  
*na gṛhṇanti surāstena dattaṃ puṣpaphalādikam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. The manes do not receive willingly the balls of rice or holy waters offered by him. Nor do the gods accept his offering of fruits and flowers.

## \|\| 6.28.31 \|\|

*tasya kiṃ jñānasutapo japahoma prapūjanaiḥ \|*  
*vidyayā dānataḥ kiṃ vā strībhiryasya mano hṛtam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Of what avail are words of wisdom, penance, Japas, Homas, worships, learning or charitable gifts to that wretch whose mind is deadened by his thoughts of women?

## \|\| 6.28.32 \|\|

*vidyāprabhāvajñānārthaṃ mayā tvaṃ ca parīkṣitaḥ \|*  
*kṛtvā kāṃtaparīkṣāṃ vai vṛṇuyātkāminī varam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. You have been tested by me in order to know your knowledge and power. A woman must test her bridegroom before wooing him.

## \|\| 6.28.33 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityevaṃ pravadaṃtyāṃ tu tulasyāṃ tatkṣaṇe vidhiḥ \|*  
*tatrājagāma saṃsṛṣṭā provāca vacanaṃ tataḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

33\. Even as Tulasī was saying so, Brahmā the creator came there and spoke these words.

## \|\| 6.28.34 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*kiṃ karoṣi śaṃkhacūḍa saṃvādamanayā saha \|*  
*gāṃdharveṇa vivāhena tvamasyā grahaṇaṃ kuru \|\| 34 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

34\. “O Śaṅkhacūḍa, why do you hold discussion with her? Marry her according to the Gāndharva form of marriage.

## \|\| 6.28.35 \|\|

*tvaṃ vai puruṣaratnaṃ ca strīratnaṃ ca tviyaṃ satī \|*  
*vidagdhāyā vidagdhena saṃgamo guṇavān bhavet \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. You are jewel among men. And she, the chaste lady, is a jewel among women. The union of an intelligent lady with an intelligent man must necessarily be virtuous.

## \|\| 6.28.36 \|\|

*nirvirodhaṃ sukhaṃ rājan ko vā tyajati durlabham \|*  
*yo'virodhasukhatyāgī sa paśurnātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. O king, unless forced who will abandon a chance of happiness? He who does so unforced is a brute. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 6.28.37 \|\|

*kiṃ tvaṃ parīkṣase kāṃtamīdṛśaṃ guṇinaṃ sati \|*  
*devānāmasurāṇāṃ ca dānavānāṃ vimardakam \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. O chaste lady, why shall you test such a good and noble husband? He can suppress the gods, Asuras and Dānavas too.

## \|\| 6.28.38 \|\|

*anena sārddhaṃ suciraṃ vihāraṃ kuru sarvadā \|*  
*sthānesthāne yathecchaṃ ca sarvalokeṣu sundari \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. O beautiful woman, you may sport with him for long, as you please, in different centres all over the world.

## \|\| 6.28.39 \|\|

*aṃte prāpsyati goloke śrīkṛṣṇaṃ punareva saḥ \|*  
*caturbhujaṃ ca vaikuṇṭhe mṛte tasmiṃstvamāpsyasi \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. In the end, he will attain Śrīkṛṣṇa again in the Goloka. After he is dead, you will attain the four-armed lord in Vaikuṇṭha.”

## \|\| 6.28.40 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityevamāśiṣaṃ dattvā svālayaṃ tu yayau vidhiḥ \|*  
*gāṃdharveṇa vivāhena jagṛhe tāṃ ca dānavaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

40\. After conferring blessings, Brahmā returned to his abode. The Dānava accepted her by means of the Gāndharva rite.

## \|\| 6.28.41 \|\|

*evaṃ vivāhya tulasīṃ pituḥ sthānaṃ jagāma ha \|*  
*sa reme ramayā sārddhaṃ vāsagehe manorame \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. After marrying her he went to his father’s place. In the beautiful apartment he sported with her.

## Chapter 29 - The previous birth of Śaṅkhacūḍa

## \|\| 6.29.1 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*svagehamāgate tasmiñśaṃkhacūḍe vivāhite \|*  
*tapaḥ kṛtvā varaṃ prāpya mumudurdānavādayaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

1\. When Śaṅkhacūḍa returned home duly married, after performing the penance and receiving the boons, Dānavas and others rejoiced.

## \|\| 6.29.2 \|\|

*svalokādāśu nirgatya guruṇā svena saṃyutāḥ \|*  
*sarve surāssaṃmilitāssamājagmustadaṃtikam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Leaving their world and accompanied by their preceptor, the Asuras assembled and approached the Dānava.

## \|\| 6.29.3 \|\|

*praṇamya taṃ savinayaṃ saṃstutya vividhādarāt \|*  
*sthitāstatraiva suprītyā matvā tejasvinaṃ vibhum \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. They bowed to that resplendent Dānava their lord, humbly and eulogised him with love and respect. They stayed with him alone.

## \|\| 6.29.4 \|\|

*sopi dambhātmajo dṛṣṭvā gataṃ kula guruṃ ca tam \|*  
*praṇanāma mahābhaktyā sāṣṭāṃgaṃ paramādarāt \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. On seeing the family preceptor, Śaṅkhacūḍa, son of Dambha bowed to him with devotion and prostrated before him with respect.

## \|\| 6.29.5 \|\|

*atha śukraḥ kulācāryo dṛṣṭvāśiṣamanuttamam \|*  
*vṛttāṃtaṃ kathayāmāsa devadānavayostadā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. After conferring his excellent benediction, Śukra, the family preceptor, narrated the tales of the gods and Dānavas.

## \|\| 6.29.6 \|\|

*svābhāvikaṃ ca tadvairamasurāṇāṃ parābhavam \|*  
*vijayaṃ nirjarāṇāṃ ca jīvasāhāyyameva ca \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. He expatiated on the natural enmity of the two, the invariable defeat of the Asuras, the victory of the gods and the help rendered by Bṛhaspati.

## \|\| 6.29.7 \|\|

*tatassa sammataṃ kṛtvā suraissarvaissamutsavam \|*  
*dānavādyasurāṇāṃ tamadhipaṃ vidadhe guruḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. With the consent of the Asuras, the preceptor Śukra made him the emperor of Dānavas, Asuras and

others with jubilant festivities.

## \|\| 6.29.8 \|\|

*tadā samutsavo jāto'surāṇāṃ muditātmanām \|*  
*upāyanāni suprītyā dadustasmai ca te'khilāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The delighted Asuras were highly joyous. They offered him presents lovingly.

## \|\| 6.29.9 \|\|

*atha dambhātmajo vīraśśaṃkhacūḍaḥ pratāpavān \|*  
*rājyābhiṣekamāsādya sa reje surarāṭ tadā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The son of Dambha, the heroic and valorous Śaṅkhacūḍa shone as the Emperor of Asuras.

## \|\| 6.29.10 \|\|

*sa senāṃ mahatīṃ karṣandaityadānavarakṣasām \|*  
*rathamāsthāya tarasā jetuṃ śakrapurīṃ yayau \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Taking a vast army of Daityas, Dānavas and Rākṣasas and seated in his chariot, he marched quickly to the city of Indra with the intention to conquer it.

## \|\| 6.29.11 \|\|

*gacchansa dānavendrastu teṣāṃ sevanakurvatām \|*  
*vireje śaśivadbhānāṃ grahāṇāṃ graharāḍiva \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The leader of the Dānavas going in the midst of his attendants shone as the moon in the midst of stars or as the sun in the midst of planets.

## \|\| 6.29.12 \|\|

*āgacchaṃtaṃ śaṅkhacūḍamākarṇyākhaṇḍalassvarāṭ \|*  
*nikhilairamaraissārddhaṃ tena yoddhuṃ samudyataḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. On hearing that Śaṅkhacūḍa was coming, Indra the king of heaven, accompanied by the gods made preparations for a fight.

## \|\| 6.29.13 \|\|

*tadā'suraissurāṇāṃ ca saṃgrāmastumulo hyabhūt \|*  
*vīrā''nandakaraḥ klībabhayado romaharṣaṇaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Then a tremendous fight ensued between the Asuras and the gods delighting the heroic and terrifying the cowardly. It caused hairs to stand on end.

## \|\| 6.29.14 \|\|

*mahānkolāhalo jāto vīrāṇāṃ garjatāṃ raṇe \|*  
*vādyadhvanistathā cā''sīttatra vīratvavarddhinī \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. When the warriors roared in the battle, there was a tumultuous noise. The sound of drums and other instruments encouraged the warriors.

## \|\| 6.29.15 \|\|

*devāḥ prakupya yuyudhurasurairbalavattarāḥ \|*  
*parājayaṃ ca saṃprāpurasurā dudruvurbhayāt \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The powerful gods fought with the Asuras ferociously and defeated them. They were afraid and fled.

## \|\| 6.29.16 \|\|

*palāyamānāstāndṛṣṭvā śaṃkhacūḍassvayaṃ prabhuḥ \|*  
*yuyudhe nirjaraissākaṃ siṃhanādaṃ pragarjya ca \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. On seeing them fleeing, their leader Śaṅkhacūḍa roared like a lion and fought with the gods.

## \|\| 6.29.17 \|\|

*tarasā sahasā cakre kadanaṃ tridivaukasām \|*  
*pradudruvussurāssarve tatsutejo na sehire \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. With his power and force he distressed the gods. The gods could not endure his dazzling brilliance. They fled.

## \|\| 6.29.18 \|\|

*yatra tatra sthitā dīnā girīṇāṃ kaṃdarāsu ca \|*  
*tadadhīnā na svataṃtrā niṣprabhāḥ sāgarā yathā \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The gods thus vanquished took shelter in the caves of the mountains. They lost their independence. They were subjugated. They lost their lustre like the frozen sea.

## \|\| 6.29.19 \|\|

*sopi daṃbhātmajaśśūro dānavendraḥ pratāpavān \|*  
*surādhikārānsaṃjahre sarvāṃllokānvijitya ca \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Thus the son of Dambha, the valorous leader of the Dānavas, conquered all the worlds and took up the powers of the gods.

## \|\| 6.29.20 \|\|

*trailokyaṃ svavaśaṃcakre yajñabhāgāṃśca kṛtsnaśaḥ \|*  
*svayamindro babhūvāpi śāsitaṃ nikhilaṃ jagat \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. He kept the three worlds under his control. He partook of all the shares in sacrifices. He became Indra and ruled the universe.

## \|\| 6.29.21 \|\|

*kauberamaindavaṃ sauryamāgneyaṃ yāmyameva ca \|*  
*kārayāmāsa vāyavyamadhikāraṃ svaśaktitaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. He carried the tasks of Kubera, Moon, Sun, Fire, Yama and Vāyu, according to his ability.

## \|\| 6.29.22-23 \|\|

*devānāmasurāṇāṃ ca dānavānāṃ ca rakṣasām \|*  
*gaṃdharvāṇāṃ ca nāgānāṃ kinnarāṇāṃ rasaukasām \|\| 22 \|\|*

*trilokasya pareṣāṃ ca sakalānāmadhīśvaraḥ \|*  
*sa babhūva mahāvīraśśaṃkhacūḍo mahābalī \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. The great hero, the powerful Śaṅkhacūḍa became overlord of the gods, Asuras, Dānavas, Rākṣasas, Gandharvas, serpents, Kinnaras, Nāgas and in fact of all the people of the three worlds.

## \|\| 6.29.24 \|\|

*evaṃ sa bubhuje rājyaṃ rājarājeśvaro mahān \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ bhuvanānāṃ ca śaṃkhacūḍaściraṃ samāḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Thus Śaṅkhacūḍa enjoyed the kingdom of the worlds for many years. He became a great Emperor.

## \|\| 6.29.25 \|\|

*tasya rājye na durbhikṣaṃ na mārī nā'śubhagrahāḥ \|*  
*ādhayo vyādhayo naiva sukhinyaśca prajāḥ sadā \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. There was no famine, plague or pestilence in his realm. The planets were not inauspicious. There was no worry or sickness among the people. The subjects were happy for ever.

## \|\| 6.29.26 \|\|

*akṛṣṭapacyā pṛthivī dadau sasyānyanekaśaḥ \|*  
*oṣadhyo vividhāścāsansaphalāssarasāḥ sadā \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Even without being tilled, the earth yielded plenty of plants and vegetation. Many medicinal herbs grew up. Plants remained always fruitful and juicy.

## \|\| 6.29.27 \|\|

*maṇyākarāśca nitarāṃ ratnakhanyaśca sāgarāḥ \|*  
*sadā puṣpaphalā vṛkṣā nadyastu salilāvahāḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. The oceans yielded plenty of gems and jewels. Abundant flowers and fruits grew up on the Earth. Rivers

flowed with pure crystal clear water.

## \|\| 6.29.28 \|\|

*devān vinākhilā jīvāssukhino nirvikārakāḥ \|*  
*svasvadharmā sthitāssarve caturvarṇāśramāḥ pare \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Excepting the gods all living beings were happy and free from distress. The people of four castes and stages of life maintained their respective duties and activities.

## \|\| 6.29.29 \|\|

*tasmicchāsati trailokye na kaścid duḥkhito'bhavat \|*  
*bhrātṛvairatvamāśritya kevalaṃ duḥkhino'marāḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. When he ruled, none was miserable in the three worlds. Only the gods were reduced to misery and that too by their fratricidal jealousy and enmity.

## \|\| 6.29.30 \|\|

*sa śaṃkhacūḍaḥ prabalaḥ kṛṣṇasya paramassakhā \|*  
*kṛṣṇabhaktiratassādhussadā golokavāsinaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Śaṅkhacūḍa was a close friend of Kṛṣṇa, the resident of Goloka. He was powerful, and always engaged in devotion to Kṛṣṇa.

## \|\| 6.29.31 \|\|

*pūrvaśāpaprabhāveṇa dānavīṃ yonimāśritaḥ \|*  
*na dānavamatissobhūddānavatve'pi vai mune \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. O sage, although he was a Danava, his nature was different. He was born as a Danava due to a previous curse.

## \|\| 6.29.32 \|\|

*tatassuragaṇāssarve hṛtarājyā parājitāḥ \|*  
*saṃmaṃtrya sarṣayastāta prayayurbrahmaṇassabhām \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. O dear, thereafter, the defeated gods, deprived of their kingdom, consulted among themselves and went to Brahma’s assembly chamber along with the sages.

## \|\| 6.29.33 \|\|

*tatra dṛṣṭvā vidhātāraṃ natvā stutvā viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*brahmaṇe kathayāmāsussarvaṃ vṛttāṃtamākulāḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. They saw the creator and bowed to and eulogised him. With distress they explained to him everything in detail.

## \|\| 6.29.34 \|\|

*brahmā tadā samāśvāsya surān sarvānmunīnapi \|*  
*taiśca sārddhaṃ yayau loke vaikuṇṭhaṃ sukhadaṃ satām \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. After consoling the gods and the sages, Brahmā accompanied by them went to Vaikuṇṭḥa that yields happiness to the good.

## \|\| 6.29.35 \|\|

*dadarśa tatra lakṣmīśaṃ brahmā devagaṇaissaha \|*  
*kirīṭinaṃ kuṃḍalinaṃ vanamālāvibhūṣitam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Accompanied by the gods, Brahmā saw the lord of Lakṣmī decorated with a crown, earrings and a garland of wild flowers.

## \|\| 6.29.36-37 \|\|

*śaṃkhacakragadāpadmadharaṃ devaṃ caturbhujam \|*  
*sanaṃdanādyaiḥ siddhaiśca sevitaṃ pītavāsasam \|\| 36 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭvā viṣṇuṃ surāssarve brahmādyāssamunīśvarāḥ \|*  
*praṇamya tuṣṭuvurbhaktyā baddhāñjalikarā vibhum \|\| 37 \|\|*

36-37. On seeing Viṣṇu bearing Śaṅkha, Cakra, mace and the lotus, the lord with four arms, yellow garments, accompanied by Nandana, Siddhas, Brahmā and other gods bowed to the lord along with the great sages. They eulogised him with palms joined in reverence.

## \|\| 6.29.38 \|\|

*devā ūcu \|*  
*devadeva jagannātha vaikuṃṭhādhipate prabho \|*  
*rakṣāsmāñśaraṇāpannāñchrīhare trijagadguro \|\| 38 \|\|*

The gods said:—

38\. “O lord of the universe, lord of the gods, O lord of Vaikuṇṭha, save us who have sought refuge in you, O illustrious Viṣṇu, O elderly one in the three worlds.

## \|\| 6.29.39 \|\|

*tvameva jagatāṃ pātā trilokeśācyuta prabho \|*  
*lakṣmīnivāsa govinda bhaktaprāṇa namo'stu te \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. O lord Viṣṇu, O lord of the three worlds, you alone are the protector of the worlds. O supporter of Lakṣmī, O Govinda, O the vital air of the devotees, Obeisance be to you.”

## \|\| 6.29.40 \|\|

*iti stutvā surāssarve ruruduḥ purato hareḥ \|*  
*tacchrutvā bhagavānviṣṇurbrahmāṇamidamabravīt \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. After eulogising thus, all the gods cried in front of Viṣṇu. On hearing it lord Viṣṇu spoke to Brahmā thus.

## \|\| 6.29.41 \|\|

*viṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*kimarthamāgatosi tvaṃ vaikuṃṭhaṃ yogidurlabham \|*  
*kiṃ kaṣṭaṃ te samudbhūtaṃ tattvaṃ vada mamāgrataḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

Viṣṇu said:—

41\. Why have you come to Vaikuṇṭha inaccessible even to Yogins. What distress has befallen you. Tell me just here.

## \|\| 6.29.42-43 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*iti śrutvā harervākyaṃ praṇamya ca muhurmuhuḥ \|*  
*baddhāñjalipuṭo bhūtvā vina yānatakandharaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

*vṛttāṃtaṃ kathayāmāsa śaṃkhacūḍakṛtaṃ tadā \|*  
*devakaṣṭasamākhyānaṃ puro viṣṇoḥ parātmanaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

Samtkumāra said:—

42-43. On hearing the words of Viṣṇu and bowing to him with palms joined in reverence he narrated to him the activities of Śaṅkhacūḍa and the distress suffered by the gods.

## \|\| 6.29.44 \|\|

*haristadvacanaṃ śrutvā sarvatasarvabhāvavit \|*  
*prahasyovāca bhagavāṃstadrahasyaṃ vidhiṃ prati \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. On hearing that Viṣṇu who knew everything laughed. The lord then told Brahmā the secret of Śaṅkhacūḍa.

## \|\| 6.29.45 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*śaṃkhacūḍasya vṛttāṃtaṃ sarvaṃ jānāmi padmaja \|*  
*madbhaktasya ca gopasya mahātejasvinaḥ purā \|\| 45 \|\|*

Lord Viṣṇu said:—

45\. O lotus-born Brahmā, I know everything about Śaṅkhacūḍa, a great devotee of mine, of great splendour and who had been formerly a cowherd.

## \|\| 6.29.46 \|\|

*śṛṇutassarvavṛttāntamitihāsaṃ purātanam \|*  
*saṃdeho naiva kartavyaśśaṃ kariṣyati śaṅkaraḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Hear all the details about him, the old narrative. There is nothing to be suspected. Śiva will necessarily perform what is good.

## \|\| 6.29.47-50 \|\|

*sarvopari ca yasyāsti śivalokaḥ parātparaḥ \|*  
*yatra saṃrājate śaṃbhuḥ parabrahma parameśvaraḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

*prakṛteḥ puruṣasyāpi yodhiṣṭhātā triśaktidhṛk \|*  
*nirguṇassaguṇassopi paraṃ jyotiḥ svarūpavān \|\| 48 \|\|*

*yasyāṃgajāstu vai brahmaṃstrayassṛṣṭyādikārakāḥ \|*  
*sattvādiguṇasaṃpannā viṣṇubrahmaharābhidhāḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

*sa eva paramātmā hi viharatyumayā saha \|*  
*yatra māyāvinirmukto nityānitya prakalpakaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

47-50. His region called Śivaloka is greater than the greatest. It is above everything. Śiva, the supreme Brahman, the great god shines there. He is the presiding deity of Prakṛtī and Puruṣa. He wears three Śaktis. He is both devoid and possessed of attributes.\[2\] He has the great splendour for his form. O Brahmā, the three deities bringing about creation etc. are born of him. They are Viṣṇu, Brahmā and Śiva endowed with Śāttvika and other attributes. He alone is the supreme soul. He sports there with Pārvatī. He is free from illusion. He is the formulator of the eternal and the non-eternal.

## \|\| 6.29.51 \|\|

*tatsamīpe ca goloko gośālā śaṃkarasya vai \|*  
*tasyecchayā ca madrūpaḥ kṛṣṇo vasati tatra ha \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. The Goloka is near it. Śiva’s cowshed is situated there. Kṛṣṇa having my form stays there at Śiva’s behest.

## \|\| 6.29.52 \|\|

*tadgavāṃ rakṣaṇārthāya tenājñaptassadā sukhī \|*  
*tatsaṃprāptasukhassopi saṃkrīḍati vihāravit \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. It is to tend his cows and bulls that he has been ordered by him. Deriving happiness from him he too sports there.

## \|\| 6.29.53 \|\|

*tasya nārī samākhyātā rādheti jagadambikā \|*  
*prakṛteḥ paramā mūrtiḥ paṃcamī suvihāriṇī \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. His wife Rādhā\[4\] is the mother of the universe. Her form is greater than Prakṛti. It is the fifth sportive form.

## \|\| 6.29.54 \|\|

*bahugopāśca gopyaśca tatra saṃti tadaṃgajāḥ \|*  
*suvihāraparā nityaṃ rādhākṛṣṇānuvartinaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Many cowherds and cowherdesses born of her live there. They are sportively inclined and follow Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa.

## \|\| 6.29.55 \|\|

*sa eva līlayā śaṃbhoridānīṃ mohito'nayā \|*  
*saṃprāpto dānavīṃ yoniṃ mudhā śāpātsvaduḥkhadām \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. That very same (Sudāmā, now born as Śaṅkhacūḍa) has been fascinated by her by Śiva’s illusion. Cursed by Rādhā he is born as a Dānava to his distress.

## \|\| 6.29.56 \|\|

*rudraśūlena tanmṛtyu kṛṣṇena vihitaḥ purā \|*  
*tatassvadehamutsṛjya pārṣadassa bhaviṣyati \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Kṛṣṇa has already ordained that the death of Śaṅkhacūḍa will be by Rudra’s trident. Casting off his body he will become his comrade again.

## \|\| 6.29.57 \|\|

*iti vijñāya deveśa na bhayaṃ kartumarhasi \|*  
*śaṃkara śaraṇaṃ yāvassa sadyaśśaṃvidhāsyati \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. O lord of gods, knowing this you need not have any fear. Let us seek refuge in Śiva. He will do everything conducive to our good.

## \|\| 6.29.58 \|\|

*ahaṃ tvaṃ cāmarāssarve tiṣṭhaṃtīha visādhvasāḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. You, I and the gods stand here fearless (due to that only).

## \|\| 6.29.59 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityuktvā savidhirviṣṇuḥ śivalokaṃ jagāma ha \|*  
*saṃsmaranmanasā śaṃbhuṃ sarveśaṃ bhaktavatsalam \|\| 59 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

59\. After saying this and mentally thinking upon Śiva who, the lord of all, is favourably disposed to his devotees Viṣṇu went to Śivaloka accompanied by Brahmā.

## Chapter 30 - Prayer to the lord of gods

## \|\| 6.30.1-2 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*gatvā tadaiva sa vidhistadā vyāsa rameśvaraḥ \|*  
*śivalokaṃ mahādivyaṃ nirādhāramabhautikam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*sāhlādobhyantaraṃ viṣṇurjagāma muditānanaḥ \|*  
*nānāratnaparikṣiptaṃ vilasaṃtaṃ mahojjvalam \|\| 2 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

1-2. O Vyāsa, starting then itself along with Brahmā, Viṣṇu, the lord of Lakṣmī, went to Śivaloka, highly divine, propless and unearthly. He was glad and his face beamed with pleasure. The region was strewn over with many gems. It was highly brilliant.

## \|\| 6.30.3-4 \|\|

*saṃprāpya prathamadvāraṃ vicitraṃ gaṇasevitam \|*  
*śobhitaṃ parayā lakṣmyā mahoccamatisundaram \|\| 3 \|\|*

*dadarśa dvārapālāṃśca ratnasiṃhāsanasthitān \|*  
*śobhitāñśvetavastraiśca ratnabhūṣaṇabhūṣitān \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. The first entrance was of variegated nature with many Gaṇas standing there. It was resplendent, lofty and and beautiful. After reaching it he saw the gatekeepers seated on gem-set thrones. They had gem-set ornaments and white garments.

## \|\| 6.30.5 \|\|

*pañcavaktratrinayanāngaurasundaravigrahān \|*  
*triśūlādidharānvīrānbhasmarudrākṣaśobhitān \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. They had five faces, three eyes and fair handsome bodies. They were trident-bearing heroes shining with Bhasma and Rudrākṣa.

## \|\| 6.30.6 \|\|

*sabrahmāpi rameśaśca tān praṇamya vinamrakaḥ \|*  
*kathayāmāsa vṛttāntaṃ prabhusaṃdarśanārthakam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Both Brahmā and Viṣṇu bowed to them humbly and told them that they wanted to see the lord.

## \|\| 6.30.7 \|\|

*tadājñāṃ ca dadustasmai praviveśa tadājñayā \|*  
*paraṃ dvāraṃ mahāramyaṃ vicitraṃ parama prabham \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. They permitted them to enter. They saw another door very beautiful, variegated and very brilliant.

## \|\| 6.30.8 \|\|

*prabhūpakaṃṭhagatyarthaṃ vṛttāṃtaṃ saṃnyavedayat \|*  
*taddvārapāya cājñaptastenānyaṃ praviveśa ha \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. They informed the gatekeeper of their desire to approach the lord. Permitted by them they entered and saw another door.

## \|\| 6.30.9 \|\|

*evaṃ paṃcadaśadvārānpraviśya kamalodbhavaḥ \|*  
*mahādvāraṃ gatastatra nandinaṃ pradadarśa ha \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Thus Brahmā entered through fifteen doors and reached the main threshold. He saw Nandin.

## \|\| 6.30.10 \|\|

*samyaṅnatvā ca taṃ stutvā pūrvavattena nandinā \|*  
*ājñaptaśca śanairviṣṇurviveśābhyaṃtaraṃ mudā \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. After bowing to and eulogising Nandin as Brahmā did before, Viṣṇu was permitted by Nandin and he entered joyously.

## \|\| 6.30.11 \|\|

*dadarśa gatvā tatroccaissabhāṃ śaṃbhossamutprabhām \|*  
*tāṃ pārṣadaiḥ parivṛtāṃ lasaddehaissubhūṣitām \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Going in, they saw the grand assembly chamber of Śiva, highly decorated and thronged by his attendants with lustrous bodies.

## \|\| 6.30.12 \|\|

*maheśvarasya rūpaiśca digbhujaiśśubhakāṃtibhiḥ \|*  
*pañcavaktraistrinayanaiśśitikaṃṭhamahojjvalaiḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The attendants had similar forms with lord Śiva. They had ten arms, five faces, three eyes and blue necks. They had auspicious lustre and were brilliant.

## \|\| 6.30.13 \|\|

*sadratnayuktarudrākṣabhasmābharaṇabhūṣitaiḥ \|*  
*navendumaṃḍalākārāṃ caturasrāṃ manoharām \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. They were bedecked in ornaments set with gems, They wore Rudrākṣas. They had smeared themselves with the ashes. The chamber was square in shape and beautiful like the lunar sphere.

## \|\| 6.30.14 \|\|

*maṇīndrahāranirmāṇahīrasārasuśobhitām \|*  
*amūlyaratnaracitāṃ padmapatraiśca śobhitām \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Gems, necklaces, diamonds, etc. increased its brilliance. Valuable precious stones were used to stud them. It was brightened by lotus petals.

## \|\| 6.30.15 \|\|

*māṇikyajālamālābhirnānācitravicitritām \|*  
*padmarāgendraracitāmadbhutāṃ śaṃkarecchayā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Māṇikya, Padmarāga and other valuable gems were used in the same. It was very wonderful. It was laid according to the desire of Śiva.

## \|\| 6.30.16 \|\|

*sopānaśatakairyuktāṃ syamaṃtakavinirmitaiḥ \|*  
*svarṇasūtragranthiyuktaiścārucandanapallavaiḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. It had hundreds of steps leading to it, each made of Syamantaka stone; knotted golden threads joined them. Beautiful sprouts of sandal beautified it.

## \|\| 6.30.17 \|\|

*indranīlamaṇistaṃbhairveṣṭitāṃ sumanoharām \|*  
*susaṃskṛtāṃ ca sarvatra vāsitāṃ gaṃdhavāyunā \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Columns of sapphire supported it. It was richly decorated. The wind wafted fragrance everywhere.

## \|\| 6.30.18 \|\|

*sahasrayojanāyāmāṃ supūrṇāṃ bahukiṃkaraiḥ \|*  
*dadarśa śaṃkaraṃ sāṃbaṃ tatra viṣṇussureśvaraḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The chamber was a thousand Yojanas wide. Many servants were in attendance. Viṣṇu the lord of gods saw Śiva seated along with Pārvatī.

## \|\| 6.30.19 \|\|

*vasaṃtaṃ madhyadeśe ca yathendutārakāvṛtam \|*  
*amūlyaratnanirmāṇacitrasiṃhāsanasthitam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Śiva was in the midst of his attendants like the moon surrounded by stars. He was seated in a variegated throne set with valuable gems.

## \|\| 6.30.20 \|\|

*kirīṭinaṃ kuṃḍalinaṃ ratnamālāvibhūṣitam \|*  
*bhasmoddhūlitasarvāṅgaṃ bibhrataṃ kelipaṃkajam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. He had a crown on his head, earrings in his ears. He was embellished with gem necklaces. Ashes were smeared all over his body. He held a toy lotus.

## \|\| 6.30.21 \|\|

*purato gītanṛtyaśca paśyaṃtaṃ sasmitaṃ mudā \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. He was smilingly watching the song and dance going on in front of him.

## \|\| 6.30.22 \|\|

*śāṃtaṃ prasannamanasamumākāṃtaṃ mahollasam \|*  
*devyā pradatta tāmbūlaṃ bhuktavaṃtaṃ suvāsitam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. He was calm and delighted in the mind. He was highly brilliant. He was chewing the fragrant betel leaves offered by the goddess.

## \|\| 6.30.23 \|\|

*gaṇaiśca parayā bhaktyā sevitaṃ śvetacāmaraiḥ \|*  
*stūyamānaṃ ca siddhaiśca bhaktinamrātmakaṃdharaiḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. He was attended upon by Gaṇas with white chowries and eulogised by Siddhas with stooping shoulders with great devotion.

## \|\| 6.30.24-25 \|\|

*guṇātītaṃ pareśānaṃ tridevajanakaṃ vibhum \|*  
*nirvikalpaṃ nirākāraṃ sākāraṃ svecchayā śivam \|\| 24 \|\|*

*amāyamajamādyañca māyādhīśaṃ parātparam \|*  
*prakṛteḥ puruṣasyāpi paramaṃ svaprabhuṃ sadā \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. The great lord Śiva, the progenitor of the three deities, the lord beyond the reach of attributes, who assumes and discords his forms as he pleases and is invariable, who is free from illusion, unborn, the primordial being, the lord of illusion, greater than the greatest and greater than the Prakṛti and Puruṣa.

## \|\| 6.30.26 \|\|

*evaṃ viśiṣṭaṃ taṃ dṛṣṭvā paripūrṇatamaṃ samam \|*  
*viṣṇurbrahmā tuṣṭuvatuḥ praṇamya sukṛtāṃjalī \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. On seeing Śiva of perfect features, Viṣṇu and Brahmā eulogised him together after bowing to him with palms joined in reverence.

## \|\| 6.30.27 \|\|

*viṣṇuvidhī ūcatuḥ \|*  
*devadeva mahādeva parabrahmākhileśvara \|*  
*triguṇātīta nirvyagra tridevajanaka prabho \|\| 27 \|\|*

Viṣṇu and Brahmā said:—

27\. O lord Śiva, lord of the gods, O supreme Brahman, lord of all. O quiet one that is beyond the three attributes, O lord progenitor of the three deities.

## \|\| 6.30.28 \|\|

*vayaṃ te śaraṇāpannā rakṣasmāndukhitānvibho \|*  
*śaṃkhacūḍārditānkliṣṭānsannāthānparameśvara \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. We have sought refuge in you. O lord, save us who are distressed. O lord Śiva, we are harassed by Śaṅkhacūḍa and so dejected and well nigh exhausted. Save us.

## \|\| 6.30.29 \|\|

*ayaṃ yo'dhiṣṭhito loko goloka iti sa smṛtaḥ \|*  
*adhiṣṭhātā tasya vibhuḥ kṛṣṇo'yaṃ tvadadhiṣṭhitaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. The region that is adjacent to this place is called Goloka, Lord Kṛṣṇa is its presiding deity.

## \|\| 6.30.30 \|\|

*pārṣadapravarastasya sudāmā daivayaṃtritaḥ \|*  
*rādhāśapto babhūvātha śaṃkhacūḍaśca dānavaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. One of his leading attendants and comrades, Sudāmā, cursed by Rādhā and led by fate, has become the Dānava Śaṅkhacūḍa.

## \|\| 6.30.31 \|\|

*tena nissāritāḥ śaṃbho pīḍyamānāḥ samaṃtataḥ \|*  
*hṛtādhikārastridaśā vicaraṃti mahītale \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. O Śiva, the gods divested of all powers ousted and harassed by him roam over the Earth now.

## \|\| 6.30.32 \|\|

*tvāṃ vinā na sa vadhyaśca sarveṣāṃ tridivaukasām \|*  
*taṃ ghātaya maheśāna lokānāṃ sukhamāvaha \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Except by you he cannot be killed by any one of the gods. Please kill him and render the worlds happy.

## \|\| 6.30.33 \|\|

*tvameva nirguṇassatyo'naṃto'naṃtaparākramaḥ \|*  
*saguṇaśca sanniveśaḥ prakṛteḥ puruṣātparaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. You alone are devoid as well as possessed of attributes, truthful, of infinite valour, embedded in the good and greater than Prakṛti and Puruṣa.

## \|\| 6.30.34 \|\|

*rajasā sṛṣṭisamaye tvaṃ brahmā sṛṣṭikṛtprabho \|*  
*sattvena pālane viṣṇustribhuvāvana kārakaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. At creation, O lord, you are Brahmā, the creator through Rajas. O protector of the three worlds, in the activity of protection through Sattva you are Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 6.30.35 \|\|

*tamasā pralaye rudro jagatsaṃhārakārakaḥ \|*  
*nistraiguṇye śivākhyātasturyyo jyotiḥ svarūpakaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. In dissolution through Tamas you are Rudra the annihilator of the universe. In the state free from the three attributes you are Śiva the fourth one, of the form of brilliance.

## \|\| 6.30.36 \|\|

*tvaṃ dīkṣayā ca goloke tvaṃ gavāṃ paripālakaḥ \|*  
*tvadgośālāmadhyagaśca kṛṣṇaḥ krīḍatyaharniśam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. At your behest, Kṛṣṇa the protector, goes to Goloka. Stationed in the middle of your cowshed he sports day and night.

## \|\| 6.30.37 \|\|

*tvaṃ sarvakāraṇaṃ svāmī vidhi viṣṇvīśvaraḥ param \|*  
*nirvikārī sadā sākṣī paramātmā pareśvaraḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. You are the cause of all. You are the lord of all. You are Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva. You are free from aberrations. You are the constant witness. You are the supreme soul, the great Īśvara.

## \|\| 6.30.38 \|\|

*dīnānāthasahāyī ca dīnānāṃ pratipālakaḥ \|*  
*dīnabaṃdhustrilokeśaśśaraṇāgatavatsalaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. You are the redeemer of the distressed and the poor, the protector and the kinsman of the distressed, the lord of the worlds. You are favourably disposed to those who seek refuge in you.

## \|\| 6.30.39 \|\|

*asmānuddhara gaurīśa prasīda parameśvaraḥ \|*  
*tvadadhīnā vayaṃ nātha yadicchasi tathā kuru \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. O lord of Pārvatī, uplift us. O lord Śiva, be pleased. O lord, we are subservient to you. You do as you please, O lord.

## \|\| 6.30.40 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityuktvā tau surau vyāsa harirbrahmā ca vai tadā \|*  
*virematuḥ śivaṃ natvā karau baddhvā vinītakau \|\| 40 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

40\. After saying this, O Vyāsa, those two deities, Viṣṇu and Brahmā bowed to Śiva and stopped. They joined their palms in reverence and stood humbly.

## Chapter 31 - Śiva’s advice to Viṣṇu and Brahmā

## \|\| 6.31.1 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*athākarṇya vacaśśaṃbhurharividhyossudīnayoḥ \|*  
*uvāca vihasanvāṇyā meghanādagabhīrayā \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

1\. On hearing these words of the distressed Viṣṇu and Brahmā, Śiva laughingly spoke in the rumbling tone of the cloud.

## \|\| 6.31.2 \|\|

*śiva uvāca \|*  
*he hare vatsa he brahmaṃstyajataṃ sarvaśo bhayam \|*  
*śaṃkhacūḍodbhavaṃ bhadraṃ sambhaviṣyatyasaṃśayam \|\| 2 \|\|*

Śiva said:—

2\. “O dear Viṣṇu, O Brahmā, cast off your fear from all sides. Certainly something good will result from the activities of Śaṅkhacūḍa.

## \|\| 6.31.3 \|\|

*śaṃkhacūḍasya vṛttāṃtaṃ sarvaṃ jānāmi tattvataḥ \|*  
*kṛṣṇabhaktasya gopasya sudāmnaśca purā prabho \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. I know all the details of his activities factually as well as those of Sudāmā the cowherd devotee of Kṛṣṇa.

## \|\| 6.31.4 \|\|

*madājñayā hṛṣīkeśo kṛṣṇarūpaṃ vidhāya ca \|*  
*gośālāyāṃ sthito ramye goloke madadhiṣṭhite \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. At my bidding Viṣṇu has assumed the form of Kṛṣṇa and is stationed in the cowshed in the beautiful Goloka presided over by me.

## \|\| 6.31.5 \|\|

*svataṃtrohamiti svaṃ sa mohaṃ matvā gataḥ purā \|*  
*krīḍāssamakarodbahvīssvairavartīva mohitaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Considering himself independent under a delusion he indulged in many kinds of sportive dalliance like a deluded licentious person.

## \|\| 6.31.6 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā mohamatyugraṃ tasyāhaṃ māyayā svayā \|*  
*teṣāṃ saṃhṛtya sadbuddhiṃ śāpaṃ dāpitavān kila \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. On seeing his excessive delusion as a result of my deceptive art I suppressed their virtuous intellect and made them suffer curse.

## \|\| 6.31.7 \|\|

*itthaṃ kṛtvā svalīlāṃ tāṃ māyāṃ saṃhṛtavānaham \|*  
*jñānayuktāstadā te tu muktamohāssubuddhayaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Having thus performed my sport, I suppressed the illusion. Regaining knowledge they got rid of delusion and became well-intentioned.

## \|\| 6.31.8 \|\|

*samīpamāgatāste me dīnībhūya praṇamya mām \|*  
*akurvansunutiṃ bhaktyā karau baddhvā vinamrakāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. They came near me in a piteous plight. After bowing to me they eulogised me devoutly and humbly with palms joined in reverence.

## \|\| 6.31.9 \|\|

*vṛttāṃtamavadansarvaṃ lajjākulitamānasāḥ \|*  
*ūcurmatpurato dīnā rakṣarakṣeti vai giraḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Overwhelmed by shame they told me all the details. Dejected, they lamented before me saying the words “Save us, O save us.”

## \|\| 6.31.10 \|\|

*tadā tvahaṃ bhavasteṣāṃ saṃtuṣṭaḥ proktavān vacaḥ \|*  
*bhayaṃ tyajata he kṛṣṇa yūyaṃ sarve madājñayā \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Then I, becoming delighted, told them these words, Kṛṣṇa, you forget your fear at my behest.

## \|\| 6.31.11 \|\|

*rakṣako'haṃ sadā prītyā subhadraṃ vo bhaviṣyati \|*  
*madicchayā'khilaṃ jātamidaṃ sarvaṃ na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. I am the protector, always infused with love. Good will befall you. All this has happened at my will. There is no doubt in it.

## \|\| 6.31.12 \|\|

*svasthānaṃ gaccha tvaṃ sārddhaṃ rādhayā pārṣadena ca \|*  
*dānavastu bhavetsoyaṃ bhārate'tra na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Go to your abode along with Rādhā and your comrade. He will become a Dānava here in Bhārata, certainly.

## \|\| 6.31.13-14 \|\|

*śāpoddhāraṃ kariṣye'haṃ yuvayossamaye khalu \|*  
*maduktamiti saṃdhārya śirasā rādhayā saha \|\| 13 \|\|*

*śrīkṛṣṇo'modadatyaṃtaṃ svasthānamagamatsudhīḥ \|*  
*nyaṣṭhātāṃ sabhayaṃ tatra madārādhanatatparau \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. At the proper time I shall redeem you from the curse”. What I told thus Śrīkṛṣṇa and Rādhā accepted readily. Śrīkṛṣṇa the intelligent rejoiced and returned to his abode. There they engaged themselves in propitiating me and bidding their time.

## \|\| 6.31.15 \|\|

*matvākhilaṃ madadhīnamasvatantraṃ nijaṃ ca vai \|*  
*sa sudāmā'bhavadrādhāśāpato dānaveśvaraḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Realising that everything is subject to my control and his will is not independent, Sudāmā became the lord of Dānavas as a result of the curse of Rādhā.

## \|\| 6.31.16 \|\|

*śaṅkhacūḍābhidho devadrohī dharmavicakṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*kliśnāti subalātkṛtsnaṃ sadā devagaṇaṃ kudhīḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The virtuous demon Śaṅkhacūḍa distresses and harasses the gods always with his might. He is evil-minded to this extent.

## \|\| 6.31.17 \|\|

*manmāyāmohitassotiduṣṭamaṃtrisahā yavān \|*  
*tadbhayaṃ tyajatāśveva mayi śāstari vai sati \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. He has been deluded by my deception and hence he seeks the help of evil ministers. But myself being the chastiser of the wicked you can get rid of his fear quickly”.

## \|\| 6.31.18 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityūcivāñśivo yāvaddharibrahmapuraḥ kathām \|*  
*abhavattāvadanyacca caritaṃ tanmune śṛṇu \|\| 18 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

18\. O sage, by the time Śiva completed this expatiation in front of Viṣṇu and Brahmā, another event happened there. Listen to it.

## \|\| 6.31.19 \|\|

*tasminnevāṃtare kṛṣṇo rādhayā pārṣadaiḥ saha \|*  
*sadgopairāyayau śaṃbhumanukūlayituṃ prabhum \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. In the meantime Kṛṣṇa came there along with Rādhā and his attendant cowherds in order to propitiate Lord Śiva.

## \|\| 6.31.20 \|\|

*prabhuṃ praṇamya sadbhaktyā militvā harimādarāt \|*  
*saṃmato vidhinā prītyā saṃtasthau śivaśāsanāt \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Devoutly bowing to the lord, meeting Viṣṇu with respect and honoured by Brahmā with love he stood there awaiting Śiva’s behest.

## \|\| 6.31.21 \|\|

*tataḥ śaṃbhuṃ punarnatvā tuṣṭāva vihitāñjaliḥ \|*  
*śrīkṛṣṇo mohanirmukto jñātvā tattvaṃ śivasya hi \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Then he bowed again to Śiva with palms joined in reverence. Realising the principle of śiva and getting rid of his delusion Kṛṣṇa eulogised Śiva.

## \|\| 6.31.22 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*devadeva mahādeva parabrahma satāṃgate \|*  
*kṣamasva cāparādhaṃ me prasīda parameśvara \|\| 22 \|\|*

Lord Kṛṣṇa said:—

22\. O supreme God, lord of gods, Supreme Brahman and the goal of the good, forgive me my guilt. O supreme god, be pleased.

## \|\| 6.31.23 \|\|

*tvattaḥ śarva ca sarvaṃ ca tvayi sarvaṃ maheśvara \|*  
*sarvaṃ tvaṃ nikhilādhīśa prasīda parameśvara \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. O Śiva, everything originates from you. O supreme lord, everything merges in you. O lord of all, you are everything. O supreme lord, be pleased.

## \|\| 6.31.24 \|\|

*tvaṃ jyotiḥ paramaṃ sākṣātsarvavyāpī sanātanaḥ \|*  
*tvayā nāthena gaurīśa sanāthāssakalā vayam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. You are the greatest splendour. You are the eternal being directly pervading everything. O lord of Gaurī, with you as leader, we are well-guided.

## \|\| 6.31.25-26 \|\|

*sarvopari nijaṃ matvā viharanmohamāśritaḥ \|*  
*tatphalaṃ prāptavānasmi śāpaṃ prāptassavāmakaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*pārṣadapravaro yo me sudāmā nāma gopakaḥ \|*  
*sa rādhāśāpataḥ svāmindānavīṃ yonimāśritaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. Considering myself above all, I sported about, under the delusion. I reaped the fruit thereof. He who went astray was cursed. O lord, my leading comrade Sudāmā the cowherd is born as a Dānava.

## \|\| 6.31.27 \|\|

*asmānuddhara durggeśa prasīda parameśvara \|*  
*śāpoddhāraṃ kuruṣvādya pāhi naśśaraṇāgatān \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. O lord of Pārvatī, uplift us. O supreme lord, be pleased. Please redeem us from the curse. Save us who have sought refuge in you.

## \|\| 6.31.28 \|\|

*ityuktvā virarāmaiva śrīkṛṣṇo rādhayā saha \|*  
*prasanno'bhūcchivastatra śaraṇāgatavatsalaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. After saying this, Lord Kṛṣṇa, accompanied by Rādhā, stopped. Śiva was delighted thereat, Śiva who is favourably disposed to those who seek refuge in him.

## \|\| 6.31.29 \|\|

*śrīśiva uvāca \|*  
*he kṛṣṇa gopikānātha bhayaṃ tyaja sukhī bhava \|*  
*mayānugṛhṇatā tāta sarvamācaritaṃ tvidam \|\| 29 \|\|*

Lord Śiva said:—

29\. “O Kṛṣṇa, O lord of cowherdesses leave off your fear. Be happy. O dear, all this has been brought about by me with blessing in disguise.

## \|\| 6.31.30 \|\|

*saṃbhaviṣyati te bhadraṃ gaccha svasthānamuttamam \|*  
*sthātavyaṃ svādhikāre ca sāvadhānatayā sadā \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Good will befall you. Go back to your excellent abode. You shall be cautious and guarded in your position of authority.

## \|\| 6.31.31 \|\|

*viharasva yathākāmaṃ māṃ vijñāya parātparam \|*  
*svakāryaṃ kuru nirvyagraṃ rādhayā pārṣadaiḥ khalu \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Sport about as you please after realising me the greater than the greatest. Accompanied by Rādhā and your comrades carry out your task unexasperated and unfluttered.

## \|\| 6.31.32 \|\|

*vārāhapravare kalpe taruṇyā rādhayā saha \|*  
*śāpaprabhāvaṃ bhuktvā vai punarāyāsyati svakam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. In the excellent Vārāha Kalpa, you shall undergo the effect of the curse along with the young damsel Rādhā and then attain your region.

## \|\| 6.31.33 \|\|

*sudāmā pārṣado yo hi tava kṛṣṇa priyapriyaḥ \|*  
*dānavīṃ yonimāśrityedānīṃ kliśnāti vai jagat \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. O Kṛṣṇa, your comrade, the most beloved Sudāmā is born of a Dānava now and he harasses the universe.

## \|\| 6.31.34 \|\|

*śāpaprabhāvādrādhāyā devaśatruśca dānavaḥ \|*  
*śaṅkhacūḍābhidhasso'ti daityapakṣī suraduhaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. He has become a Dānava, an enemy of the gods, named Śaṅkhacūḍa as a result of the power of Rādhā’s curse. He hates and belongs to the party of Daityas.

## \|\| 6.31.35 \|\|

*tena nissāritā devāssendrā nityaṃ prapīḍitāḥ \|*  
*hṛtādhikārā vikṛtāssarve yātā diśo daśa \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Divested of their powers, ousted and harassed by him for ever, the demoralized gods including Indra have fled to the ten directions.

## \|\| 6.31.36 \|\|

*brahmācyutau tadarthe hī hāgatau śaraṇaṃ mama \|*  
*teṣāṃ kleśavinirmokṣaṃ kariṣye nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. It is for their sake that Brahmā and Viṣṇu have come here and sought refuge in me. There is no doubt in this that I will relieve them of their distress.”

## \|\| 6.31.37 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityuktvā śaṃkaraḥ kṛṣṇaṃ punaḥ provāca sādaram \|*  
*hariṃ vidhiṃ samābhāṣya vacanaṃ kleśanāśanam \|\| 37 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

37\. After saying this, he addressed Kṛṣṇa again eagerly after consoling Viṣṇu and Brahmā with words that quelled their agony.

## \|\| 6.31.38 \|\|

*śiva uvāca \|*  
*he hare he vidhe prītyā mamedaṃ vacanaṃ śṛṇu \|*  
*gacchataṃ tvaritaṃ tātau devānaṃdāya nirbhayam \|\| 38 \|\|*

Śiva said:—

38\. “O Viṣṇu, O Brahmā, lovingly listen to my words. O dear ones, go quickly for the pleasure of the gods. Be fearless.

## \|\| 6.31.39 \|\|

*kailāsavāsinaṃ rudraṃ madrūpaṃ pūrṇamuttamam \|*  
*devakāryārthamudbhūtaṃ pṛthagākṛtidhāriṇam \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Go to Rudra, resident of Kailāsa, who has my excellent and perfect form. He has manifested himself for the task of the gods with a separate form and features.

## \|\| 6.31.40 \|\|

*etadarthe hi madrūpaḥ paripūrṇatamaḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*kailāse bhaktavaśatassaṃtiṣṭhati girau hare \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. O Viṣṇu, it is for this purpose that the lord assuming my form fully and perfectly stays on the mountain Kailāsa favouring the devotees by being subservient to them.

## \|\| 6.31.41 \|\|

*mattastvatto na bhedo'sti yuvayossevya eva saḥ \|*  
*carācarāṇāṃ sarveṣāṃ surādīnāṃ ca sarvadā \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. There is no difference in him from us both. He shall be served by you two and all living beings—mobile and immobile as well as the gods and others always.

## \|\| 6.31.42 \|\|

*āvayobhedakartā yassa naro narakaṃ vrajet \|*  
*ihāpi prāpnuyātkṛṣṭaṃ putrapautravivarjitaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. He who differentiates between us falls into hell. In this life too he will attain stress and be devoid of sons and grandsons.

## \|\| 6.31.43 \|\|

*ityuktavaṃtaṃ durgeśaṃ praṇamya ca muhurmuhuḥ \|*  
*rādhayā sahitaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ svasthānaṃ sagaṇo yayau \|\| 43 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

43\. After bowing again and again to the lord of Pārvatī who had spoken thus, Kṛṣṇa returned to his abode accompanied by Rādhā.

## \|\| 6.31.44 \|\|

*harirbrahmā ca tau vyāsa sānandau gatasādhvasau \|*  
*muhurmuhuḥ praṇamyeśaṃ vaikuṃṭhaṃ yayaturdrutam \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. O Vyāsa, Viṣṇu and Brahmā became delighted and relieved of fear. After bowing again and again to Śiva they hastened to Vaikuṇṭha.

## \|\| 6.31.45 \|\|

*tatrāgatyākhilaṃ vṛttaṃ devebhyo vinivedya tau \|*  
*tānādāya brahmaviṣṇū kailāsaṃ yayaturgirim \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Having come there and mentioning everything to the gods, Brahmā and Viṣṇu went to Kailāsa taking the gods with them.

## \|\| 6.31.46-47 \|\|

*tatra dṛṣṭvā maheśānaṃ pārvatīvallabhaṃ prabhum \|*  
*dīnarakṣāttadehaṃ ca saguṇaṃ devanāyakam \|\| 46 \|\|*

*tuṣṭuvuḥ pūrvavatsarve bhaktyā gadgadayā girā \|*  
*karau baddhvā nataskaṃdhā vinayena samanvitāḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

46-47. On seeing lord Śiva there, the lord and husband of Pārvatī, who had taken a body for protecting the distressed, the lord of the gods possessed of attributes, they eulogised him as before with devotion and choking words. They joined their palms in reverence humbly and with drooping shoulders.

## \|\| 6.31.48 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*devadeva mahādeva girijānātha śaṃkara \|*  
*vayaṃ tvāṃ śaraṇāpannā rakṣa devānbhayākulān \|\| 48 \|\|*

The gods said:—

48\. O great god, lord of the gods, O Śiva, the lord of Pārvatī, we seek refuge in you. Please save the terrified gods.

## \|\| 6.31.49 \|\|

*śaṃkhacūḍadānavendraṃ jahi devaniṣūdanam \|*  
*tena viklāvitā devāḥ saṃgrāme ca parājitāḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Please slay Saṅkhacūḍa the king of Asura and the destroyer of the gods. The gods have been defeated and harassed by him.

## \|\| 6.31.50 \|\|

*hṛtādhikārāḥ kutale vicaraṃti yathā narāḥ \|*  
*devaloko hi durdṛśyasteṣāmāsīcca tadbhayāt \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Like men they are roaming on the earth divested of their powers. Their region the Devaloka has become very dreary to look at due to fear.

## \|\| 6.31.51 \|\|

*dīnoddhara kṛpāsindho devānuddhara saṃkaṭāt \|*  
*śakraṃ bhayānmaheśānahatvā taṃ dānavādhipam \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. O uplifter of the distressed, O ocean of mercy, redeem the gods, from this exigency. O great lord, save Indra from fright by killing that ruler of Dānavas.

## \|\| 6.31.52 \|\|

*iti śrutvā vacaśśaṃbhurdevānāṃ bhaktavatsalaḥ \|*  
*uvāca vihasan vāṇyā meghanādagabhīrayā \|\| 52 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

52\. “On hearing the words of the gods, Śiva favourably disposed to his devotees spoke to them laughingly in the rumbling tone of the cloud.

## \|\| 6.31.53 \|\|

*śrīśaṃkara uvāca \|*  
*he hare he vidhe devāḥ svasthānaṃ gacchata dhuvam \|*  
*śaṃkhacūḍaṃ vadhiṣyāmi sagaṇaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

Lord Śiva said:—

53\. O Viṣṇu, O Brahmā, O Gods, return to your own abodes by all means. I shall kill Śaṅkhacūḍa along with his followers and attendants. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 6.31.54 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya maheśasya vacaḥ pīyūṣasaṃnibham \|*  
*te sarve pramudā hyāsannaṣṭaṃ matvā ca dānavam \|\| 54 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

54\. On hearing the words of lord Śiva sweet as nectar they were excessively delighted considering the Dānava already killed.

## \|\| 6.31.55 \|\|

*harirjagāma vaikuṃṭhaṃ satyaloke vidhistadā \|*  
*praṇipatya maheśaṃ ca surādyāḥ svapadaṃ yayuḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. After bowing to lord Śiva, Viṣṇu went to Vaikuṇṭha and Brahmā to Satyaloka. The god and others went to their own abodes.

## Chapter 32 - The Emissary is sent

## \|\| 6.32.1 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*atheśāno mahārudro duṣṭakālassatāṃgatiḥ \|*  
*śaṃkhacūḍavadhaṃ citte niścikāya surecchayā \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

1\. Then lord Śiva, Death to the wicked, goal of the good, decided in his mind to slay Śaṅkhacūḍa in accordance with the wishes of the gods.

## \|\| 6.32.2 \|\|

*dūtaṃ kṛtvā citrarathaṃ gaṃdharveśvaramīpsitam \|*  
*śīghraṃ prasthāpayāmāsa śaṃkhacūḍāṃtike mudā \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. He made his friend the lord of Gandharvas his messenger and sent him in a wonderful chariot hurriedly to Śaṅkhacūḍa joyously.

## \|\| 6.32.3 \|\|

*sarveśvarājñayā dūto yayau tannagaraṃ ca saḥ \|*  
*mahendranagarotkṛṣṭaṃ kuberabhavanādhikam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. At the bidding of lord Śiva, the emissary went to the city of the Asura which was superior to Indra’s Amarāvatī and Kubera’s Palace.

## \|\| 6.32.4 \|\|

*gatvā dadarśa tanmadhye śaṃkhacūḍālayaṃ varam \|*  
*rājitaṃ dvādaśairdvārairdvārapālasamanvitam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Reaching there, he saw the excellent abode of śaṅkhacūḍa in the middle; it shone with its twelve entrance doors with gatekeepers in each.

## \|\| 6.32.5 \|\|

*sa dṛṣṭvā puṣpadantastu varaṃ dvāraṃ dadarśa saḥ \|*  
*kathayāmāsa vṛttāṃtaṃ dvārapālāya nirbhayaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Puspadanta (Puṣpadanta?) saw the main excellent entrance. Fearlessly he informed the gatekeeper.

## \|\| 6.32.6 \|\|

*atikramya ca taddvāraṃ jagāmābhyaṃtare mudā \|*  
*atīva sundaraṃ ramyaṃ vistīrṇaṃ samalaṃkṛtam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Passing beyond that door he joyously went in. It was spacious, exquisitely fine and richly decorated.

## \|\| 6.32.7 \|\|

*sa gatvā śaṃkhacūḍaṃ taṃ dadarśa danujādhipam \|*  
*vīramaṃḍala madhyasthaṃ ratnasiṃhāsanasthitam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Going in he saw Śaṅkhacūḍa, the ruler of Dānavas, seated on a gem-set throne in the midst of heroic warriors.

## \|\| 6.32.8 \|\|

*dānavendraiḥ parivṛtaṃ sevitaṃ ca trikoṭibhiḥ \|*  
*śataḥ koṭibhiranyaiśca bhramadbhiśśastrapāṇibhiḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. He was surrounded by leading Dānavas and served by three crores of attendants and guarded by another hundred crores of well armed soldiers moving to and fro.

## \|\| 6.32.9 \|\|

*evaṃbhūtaṃ ca taṃ dṛṣṭvā puṣpadaṃtassavismayaḥ \|*  
*uvāca raṇavṛttāṃtaṃ yaduktaṃ śaṃkareṇa ca \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Seeing him, Puṣpadanta was struck with wonder. He gave the message of war as conveyed by Śiva.

## \|\| 6.32.10 \|\|

*puṣpadaṃta uvāca \|*  
*rājendra śivadūto'haṃ puṣpadaṃtābhidhaḥ prabho \|*  
*yaduktaṃ śaṃkareṇaiva tacchṛṇu tvaṃ bravīmi te \|\| 10 \|\|*

Puṣpadanta said:—

10\. O great king, O lord, I am the Emissary of Śiva named Puṣpadanta. Please listen to what is mentioned by Śiva himself. I am telling you the same.

## \|\| 6.32.11 \|\|

*śiva uvāca \|*  
*rājyaṃ dehi ca devānāmadhikāraṃ hi sāṃpratam \|*  
*nocetkuru raṇaṃ sārddhaṃ pareṇa ca mayā satām \|\| 11 \|\|*

Śiva said:—

11\. Now, give back their kingdom to the gods and their authority. If not, fight with me, the greatest of the good warriors.

## \|\| 6.32.12 \|\|

*devā māṃ śaraṇāpannā deveśaṃ śaṃkaraṃ satām \|*  
*ahaṃ kruddho mahārudrastvāṃ vadhiṣyāmyasaṃśayam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The gods have sought refuge in me, the lord of the gods and the benefactor of the good. I the infuriated will certainly slay you.

## \|\| 6.32.13 \|\|

*haro'smi sarvadevebhyo hyabhayaṃ dattavānaham \|*  
*khaladaṃḍadharo'haṃ vai śaraṇāgatavatsalaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. I am Śiva, the destroyer. I have granted protection to all the gods. I am the holder of the chastising rod for the wicked and favourably disposed to those who seek refuge in me.

## \|\| 6.32.14 \|\|

*rājyaṃ dāsyasi kiṃ vā tvaṃ kariṣyasi raṇaṃ ca kim \|*  
*tattvaṃ brūhi dvayorekaṃ dānavendra vicārya vai \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. O lord of Dānavas, consider and let me know one of the two alternatives specifically, whether you will return the kingdom or fight.

## \|\| 6.32.15 \|\|

*puṣpadaṃta uvāca \|*  
*ityuktaṃ yanmaheśena tubhyaṃ tanme niveditam \|*  
*vitathaṃ śaṃbhuvākyaṃ na kadāpi danujādhipa \|\| 15 \|\|*

Puṣpadanta said:

15\. O lord of Dānavas, what has been stated by Śiva has been conveyed to you. Śiva’s words have never gone in vain.

## \|\| 6.32.16 \|\|

*ahaṃ svasvāminaṃ gaṃtumicchāmi tvaritaṃ haram \|*  
*gatvā vakṣyāmi kiṃ śaṃbhostathā tvaṃ vada māmiha \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. I wish to return to my lord Śiva immediately. After going back what shall I tell Śiva, you clearly let me know.

## \|\| 6.32.17 \|\|

*\|\| sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*itthaṃ ca puṣpadaṃtasya śivadūtasya satpateḥ \|*  
*ākarṇya vacanaṃ rājā hasitvā tamuvāca saḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

17\. On hearing these words of Puṣpadanta who was the emissary of lord Śiva, the king laughed, then spoke to him.

## \|\| 6.32.18 \|\|

*śaṃkhacūḍa uvāca \|*  
*rājyaṃ dāsye na devebhyo vīrabhogyā vasuṃdharā \|*  
*raṇaṃ dāsyāmi te rudra devānāṃ pakṣapātine \|\| 18 \|\|*

Śaṅkhacūḍa said:—

18\. I will never return the kingdom to the god. The earth shall be enjoyed by heroic warriors. O Śiva, I shall fight with you who are a partisan of the gods.

## \|\| 6.32.19 \|\|

*yasyopari prayāyī syātsa vīro bhuvena'dhamaḥ \|*  
*ataḥ pūrvamahaṃ rudra tvāṃ gamiṣyāmyasaṃśayam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The hero who allows another to supercede him is the basest in the world. Hence O Śiva I shall certainly march towards you just now.

## \|\| 6.32.20 \|\|

*prabhāta āgamiṣyāmi vīrayātrā vicārataḥ \|*  
*tvaṃ gacchācakṣva rudrāya hīdṛśaṃ vacanaṃ mama \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. I reach there in the morning in the course of my victorious campaign. O messenger, go and tell all this to Siva.

## \|\| 6.32.21 \|\|

*iti śrutvā śaṃkhacūḍavacanaṃ suprahasya saḥ \|*  
*uvāca dānavendraṃ sa śaṃbhudūtastu garvitam \|\| 21 \|\|*

Samtkumāra said:—

21\. On hearing these words of Śaṅkhacūḍa, the emissary of Śiva laughed aloud and then spoke haughtily to the lord of the Asuras.

## \|\| 6.32.22 \|\|

*anyeṣāmapi rājendra gaṇānāṃ śaṃkarasya ca \|*  
*na sthātuṃ saṃmukhe yogyaḥ kiṃ punastasya saṃmukham \|\| 22 \|\|*

Puṣpadanta said:—

22\. O Great king, you cannot face the Gaṇas of Śiva. Then how can you face lord Śiva himself?

## \|\| 6.32.23 \|\|

*sa tvaṃ dehi ca devānāmadhikārāṇi sarvaśaḥ \|*  
*tvamare gaccha pātālaṃ yadi jīvitumicchasi \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. So return their positions of authority to the gods entirely. Move immediately to Pātāla if you wish to live.

## \|\| 6.32.24 \|\|

*sāmānyamamaraṃ taṃ no viddhi dānavasattama \|*  
*śaṃkaraḥ paramātmā hi sarveṣāmīśvareśvaraḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. O excellent Dānava, do not regard Śiva an ordinary deity. He is indeed the great soul, the lord of the lord of all.

## \|\| 6.32.25 \|\|

*indrādyāssakalā devā yasyājñāvartinassadā \|*  
*saprajāpatayassiddhā munayaścāpyahīśvarāḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Indra and other gods abide by his commands. The Siddhas, the patriarchs, the sages and the serpent lords all follow suit.

## \|\| 6.32.26 \|\|

*harervidheśca sa svāmī nirguṇassaguṇassa hi \|*  
*yasya bhrūbhaṃgamātreṇa sarveṣāṃ pralayo bhavet \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. He is the overlord of Viṣṇu and Brahmā. He is both possessed and devoid of attributes. By a mere twitch of his knitted eyebrow everything is dissolved.

## \|\| 6.32.27 \|\|

*śivasya pūrṇarūpaśca lokasaṃhārakārakaḥ \|*  
*satāṃ gatirduṣṭahaṃtā nirvikāraḥ parātparaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Śiva is the perfect form of gods, the cause of the annihilation of the worlds, the goal of the good, the destroyer of the wicked. He is free from aberrations. He is greater than the greatest.

## \|\| 6.32.28 \|\|

*brahmaṇodhipatisso'pi harerapi maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*avamānyā na vai tasya śāsanā dānavarṣabha \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. He is the overlord of Brahmā. He is lord Śiva even into Viṣṇu. O excellent Dānava, his behest should never be slighted.

## \|\| 6.32.29 \|\|

*kiṃ bahūktena rājendra manasā saṃvicārya ca \|*  
*rudraṃ viddhi maheśānaṃ paraṃ brahma cidātmakam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Of what avail is an unnecessary digression, O great king. Ponder deeply. Know him to be great lord, the great Brahman, the knowledge-formed.

## \|\| 6.32.30 \|\|

*dehi rājyaṃ hi devānāmadhikārāṃśca sarvaśaḥ \|*  
*evaṃ te kuśalaṃ tāta bhaviṣyatyanyathā bhayam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Return their kingdoms to the gods as well as their positions of authority. O dear, thus you will fare well. Otherwise, terror will strike you.

## \|\| 6.32.31 \|\|

*santkumāra uvāca \|*  
*iti śrutvā dānaveṃdraḥ śaṃkhacūḍaḥ pratāpavān \|*  
*uvāca śivadūtaṃ taṃ bhavitavyavimohitaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

31\. On hearing this, the valorous king of the Dānavas, deluded by his fate spoke to the emissary of Śiva thus.

## \|\| 6.32.32 \|\|

*śaṃkhacūḍa uvāca \|*  
*svato rājyaṃ na dāsyāmi nādhikārān viniścayāt \|*  
*vinā yuddhaṃ maheśena satyametadbravīmyaham \|\| 32 \|\|*

Śaṅkhacūḍa said:—

32\. I shall neither give up kingdom nor the positions of authority, without a fight with him. This is certain. I tell you the truth.

## \|\| 6.32.33 \|\|

*kālādhīnaṃ jagatsarvaṃ vijñeyaṃ sacarācaram \|*  
*kālādbhavati sarvaṃ hi vinaśyati ca kālataḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The entire universe whether mobile or immobile is subject to the vagaries of time. Everything originates in time and everything merges into time.

## \|\| 6.32.34 \|\|

*tvaṃ gaccha śaṃkaraṃ rudraṃ mayoktaṃ vada tattvata \|*  
*sa ca yuktaṃ karotvevaṃ bahuvārtāṃ kuruṣva no \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Go and tell Śiva exactly what I have said to you. Let him do what is proper. Do not talk much.

## \|\| 6.32.35 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityuktvā śivadūto'sau jagāma svāminaṃ nijam \|*  
*yathārthaṃ kathayāmāsa puṣpadaṃtaśca sanmune \|\| 35 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

35\. O good sage, Puṣpadanta the emissary of Śiva when thus addressed by the Asura returned to lord Śiva and told him everything duly.

## Chapter 33 - March of The Victorious Lord Śiva

## \|\| 6.33.1 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*tasya tadvākyamākarṇya surarāṭ tataḥ \|*  
*sakrodhaḥ prāha giriśo vīrabhadrādikāngaṇān \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

1\. On hearing those words of the emissary, the infuriated emperor of the gods, Śiva spoke to Vīrabhadra and other Gaṇas.

Śiva said.

## \|\| 6.33.2-3 \|\|

*rudra uvāca \|*  
*he vīrabhadra he naṃdinkṣetrapālaṣṭabhairavāḥ \|*  
*sarve gaṇāśca sannaddhāssāyudhā balaśālinaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*kumārābhyāṃ sahaivādya nirgacchaṃtu mamājñayā \|*  
*svasenayā bhadrakālī nirgacchatu raṇāya ca \|*  
*śaṃkhacūḍavadhārthāya nirgacchāmyadya satvaram \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. “O Vīrabhadra, O Nandin, O eight Bhairavas,\[1\] the frontier guards, let the Gaṇas start along with my sons. at my bidding. Let those strong ones be ready and fully equipped with weapons. Let Bhadrakālī start with her army for the war. I start just now for slaying Śaṅkhacūḍa”.

## \|\| 6.33.4 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityājñāpya maheśāno niryayau sainyasaṃyutaḥ \|*  
*sarve vīragaṇāstasyānu yayussaṃpraharṣitāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

4\. Having ordered thus, lord Śiva started along with his army. His delighted heroic Gaṇas followed him.

## \|\| 6.33.5 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare skaṃdagaṇeśau sarvasainyapau \|*  
*yataturmuditau naddhau sāyudhau ca śivāṃtike \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. In the meantime Kārttikeya and Gaṇeśa, the overall generals of the army, came near Śiva joyously, fully equipped with weapons and ready for war.

## \|\| 6.33.6-9 \|\|

*vīrabhadraśca nandī ca mahākālassubhadrakaḥ \|*  
*viśālākṣaśca bāṇaśca piṃgalākṣo vikaṃpanaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*virūpo vikṛtiścaiva maṇibhadraśca bāṣkalaḥ \|*  
*kapilākhyo dīrghadaṃṣdro vikarastāmralocanaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*kālaṃkaro balībhadraḥ kālajihvaḥ kuṭīcaraḥ \|*  
*balonmatto raṇaślāghyo durjayo durgamastathā \|\| 8 \|\|*

*ityādayo gaṇeśānāssainyānāṃ patayo varāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ ca gaṇanāṃ vacmi sāvadhānatayā śṛṇu \|\| 9 \|\|*

6-9. The leading chiefs of the Gaṇas were Vīrabhadra, Nandin, Mahākāla, Subhadraka, Viśālākṣa, Bāṇa, Piṅgalākṣa, Vikampana, Virūpa, Vikṛti, Maṇibhadra, Bāṣkala, Kapila Dīrghadaṃṣṭra, Vikara, Tāmralocana, Kālaṅkara, Balībhadra, Kālajihva, Kuṭīcara, Balonmatta, Raṇaślāghya, Durjaya, Durgama and others. I shall enumerate the number of Gaṇas they had. Listen attentively.

## \|\| 6.33.10 \|\|

*śaṃkhakarṇaḥ koṭigaṇairyutaḥ paravimardakaḥ \|*  
*daśabhiḥ kekarākṣaśca vikṛto'ṣṭābhireva ca \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Śaṅkhakarṇa the suppressor of enemies went, accompanied by a crore Gaṇas; Kekarākṣa went with ten crores and Vikṛta with eight crores.

## \|\| 6.33.11 \|\|

*catuṣṣaṣṭyā viśākhaśca navabhiḥ pāriyātrikaḥ \|*  
*ṣaḍbhissarvāntakaḥ śrīmāṃsta thaiva vikṛtānanaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Viśākha with sixty four crores; Pāriyātrika with nine crores; Sarvāntaka with six crores and the glorious Vikṛtānana too with six crores.

## \|\| 6.33.12 \|\|

*jālako hi dvādaśabhiḥ koṭibhirgaṇapuṃgavaḥ \|*  
*saptabhissamadaḥ śrīmāndundubho'ṣṭābhireva ca \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The chief of Gaṇas, Jālaka went with twelve crores; the glorious Samada seven and Dundubha with eight crores.

## \|\| 6.33.13 \|\|

*paṃcabhiśca karālākṣaḥ ṣaḍbhissaṃdārako varaḥ \|*  
*koṭikoṭibhireveha kaṃdukaḥ kuṃḍakastathā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Karālākṣa went with five crores; the excellent Sandāraka with six crores; Kunduka and Kuṇḍaka each went with crores of Gaṇas.

## \|\| 6.33.14 \|\|

*viṣṭaṃbho'ṣṭābhireveha gaṇapassarvasa ttamaḥ \|*  
*pippalaśca sahasreṇa saṃnādaśca tathāvidhaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The leader of Gaṇas, the most excellent of all, Viṣṭambha, went with eight crores Pippala and Sannāda went with a thousand crores.

## \|\| 6.33.15 \|\|

*āveśanastathāṣṭābhistvaṣṭabhiścandratāpanaḥ \|*  
*mahākeśaḥ sahasreṇa koṭīnāṃ gaṇapo vṛtaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Āveśana went with eight crores; Candratāpana with eight crores; Mahākeśa the chief of Gaṇas with a thousand crores.

## \|\| 6.33.16 \|\|

*kuṃḍī dvādaśabhirvīrastathā parvatakaśśubhaḥ \|*  
*kālaśca kālakaścaiva mahākālaśśatena vai \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The heroic Kuṇḍin and the auspicious Parvataka went with twelve crores each; Kāla, Kālaka and Mahākāla with a hundred crores each.

## \|\| 6.33.17 \|\|

*agnikaśśata koṭyā ca koṭyāgnimukha eva ca \|*  
*ādityo hyarddhakoṭyā ca tathā caivaṃ ghanāvahaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Agnika went with a hundred crores, Agnimukha with a crore, Āditya and Ghanāvaha with half a crore.

## \|\| 6.33.18 \|\|

*sanāhaśca śatenaiva kumudaḥ koṭibhistathā \|*  
*amoghaḥ kokilaścaiva śatakoṭyā sumaṃtrakaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Sannāha and Kumuda went with a hundred crores each; Amogha, Kokila and Sumantraka with a hundred crores each.

## \|\| 6.33.19 \|\|

*kākapādaḥ koṭiṣaṣṭyā ṣaṣṭyā saṃtānakastathā \|*  
*mahābalaśca navabhiḥ pañcabhirmadhupiṃgala \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Kākapāda and Santānaka went with sixty crores each: Mahābala with nine crores and Madhu Piṅgala with five crores.

## \|\| 6.33.20 \|\|

*nīlo navatyā deveśaḥ pūrṇabhadrastathaiva ca \|*  
*koṭīnāṃ caiva saptānāṃ caturvaktro mahābalaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Nīla, Deveśa and Pūrṇabhadra each went with ninety crores; the powerful Caturvaktra with seven crores.

## \|\| 6.33.21 \|\|

*koṭikoṭisahasrāṇāṃ śatairviṃśatibhistathā \|*  
*tatrājagmustathā vīrāste sarve saṃgarotsave \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. With thousands, hundreds and twenties of crores many heroes came there to take part in that festival of War.

## \|\| 6.33.22 \|\|

*bhūtakoṭisahasreṇa pramathairkoṭibhi stribhiḥ \|*  
*vīrabhadraścatuṣṣaṣṭyā lomajānāṃ trikoṭibhiḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Vīrabhadra came there with a thousand crores of Bhūtas, three crores of Pramathas and sixty-four crores of Lomajas.

## \|\| 6.33.23 \|\|

*kāṣṭhārūḍhaścatuḥṣaṣṭyā sukeśo vṛṣabhastathā \|*  
*virūpākṣaśca bhagavāṃścatuṣṣaṣṭyā sanātanaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Kāṣṭhārūḍha with sixty four crores and Sukeśa and Vṛṣabha too similarly. The honourable Virūpākṣa and Sanātana went with sixty-four crores.

## \|\| 6.33.24-26 \|\|

*tālaketuḥ ṣaḍāsyaśca paṃcāsyaśca pratāpavān \|*  
*saṃvartakastathā caitro laṃkulīśassvayaṃ prabhuḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*lokāṃtakaśca dīptātmā tathā daityāṃtakaḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*devo bhṛṅgīriṭiḥ śrīmāndevadevapriyastathā \|\| 25 \|\|*

*aśanirbhānukaścaiva catuḥ ṣaṣṭyā sahasraśaḥ \|*  
*kaṃkālaḥ kālakaḥ kālo nandī sarvāntakastathā \|\| 26 \|\|*

24-26. Tālaketu, Ṣaḍāsya, the valorous Pañcāsya, Samvartaka, Caitra, Laṅkulīśa Svayamprabhu, Lokāntaka, Dīptātman, lord Daityāntaka, lord Bhṛṅgīriṭi, the glorious Devadevapriya, Aśani, Bhānuka, Kaṅkāla, Kālaka, Kāla, Nandin and Sarvāntaka each went with sixty-four crores.

## \|\| 6.33.27 \|\|

*ete cānye ca gaṇapā asaṃkhyātā mahābalāḥ \|*  
*yuddhārthaṃ niryayuḥ prītyā śaṃkhacūḍena nirbhayāḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. These and other leading Gaṇas, powerful and innumerable started lovingly to fight fearlessly with Śaṅkhacūḍa.

## \|\| 6.33.28 \|\|

*sarve sahasrahastāśca jaṭāmukuṭadhāriṇaḥ \|*  
*candrarekhāvataṃsāśca nīlakaṃṭhāstrilocanāḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. All of them had thousand arms, matted hair for their crowns, and crescent moon for embellishment. They had blue necks and three eyes.

## \|\| 6.33.29 \|\|

*rudrākṣābharaṇāssarve tathā sadbhasmadhāriṇaḥ \|*  
*hārakuṃḍalakeyūramukuṭādyairalaṃkṛtāḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. They wore Rudrākṣas as ornaments. They had smeared their bodies with fine Bhasma. They were decorated with necklaces, earrings, bracelets, coronets and other ornaments.

## \|\| 6.33.30 \|\|

*brahmendraviṣṇusaṃkāśā aṇimādiguṇairvṛtāḥ \|*  
*sūryakoṭipratīkāśāḥ pravīṇā yuddhakarmaṇi \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. They resembled Brahmā, Indra and Viṣṇu. They had the attributes of Aṇimā etc. They were as refulgent as a crore suns. They were efficient in warfare.

## \|\| 6.33.31 \|\|

*pṛthivīcāriṇaḥ kecitkecitpātālacāriṇaḥ \|*  
*kecidvyomacarāḥ kecitsaptasvargacarā mune \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. O sage, some of them were the residents of the earth; some of the Pātāla, some of the sky and some of the seven heavens.

## \|\| 6.33.32 \|\|

*kiṃ bahūktena devarṣe sarvalokanivāsinaḥ \|*  
*yayuśśivagaṇāssarve yuddhārthaṃ dānavaissaha \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. O celestial sage, why shall I dilate? All the Śivagaṇas, residents of different regions went to fight with the Dānavas.
