## \|\| 6.33.33-35 \|\|

*aṣṭau ca bhairavā raudrā rudrā ścaikādaśāśu ye \|*  
*vasavo'ṣṭau vāsavaścādityā dvādaśa te drutam \|\| 33 \|\|*

*hutāśanaśca candraśca viśvakarmāśvinau ca tau \|*  
*kuberaśca yamaścaiva nirṛtirnalakūbaraḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*vāyuśca varuṇaścaiva budhaśca maṃgalaśca vai \|*  
*grahāścānye maheśena kāmadevaśca vīryavān \|\| 35 \|\|*

33-35. The eight Bhairavas\[5\] the terrible eleven Rudras,\[6\] the eight Vasus,\[7\] the twelve Ādityas, Indra, the fire god, the moon, Viśvakarman, the Aśvins, Kubera, Yama, Nirṛti, Nalakūbara, Vāyu, Varuṇa, Budha, Maṅgala, the other planets and the valorous Kāmadeva went with lord Śiva.

## \|\| 6.33.36-37 \|\|

*ugradaṃṣṭraścogradaṇḍaḥ koraṭaḥ koṭabhastathā \|*  
*svayaṃ śatabhujā devī bhadrakālī maheśvarī \|\| 36 \|\|*

*ratnendrasāranirmāṇavimānopari saṃsthitā\|\| \|*  
*raktavastraparīdhānā raktamālyānulepanā \|\| 37 \|\|*

36-37. Ugradaṇḍa, Ugradaṃṣṭra, Koraṭa and Koṭabha too went. The great goddess Bhadrakālī herself with hundred arms was seated in an aerial chariot studded with gems. She was wearing a red cloth and a red garland. She had smeared red unguents over her body.

## \|\| 6.33.38 \|\|

*nṛtyaṃtī ca hasaṃtī ca gāyaṃtī susvaraṃ mudā \|*  
*abhayaṃ dadatī svebhyo bhayaṃ cāribhya eva sā \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. She was dancing, laughing and singing in a sweet voice joyously. She was offering protection to her own people and striking terror to the enemies.

## \|\| 6.33.39-44 \|\|

*bibhratī vikaṭāṃ jihvāṃ sulolāṃ yojanāyatām \|*  
*śaṃkhacakragadāpadmakhaṅgacarmadhanuśśarān \|\| 39 \|\|*

*kharparaṃ vartulākāraṃ gaṃbhīraṃ yojanāyatam \|*  
*triśūlaṃ gaganasparśiṃ śaktiṃ ca yojanāyatām \|\| 40 \|\|*

*mudgaraṃ musalaṃ vaktraṃ khaṅgaṃ phalakamulbaṇam \|*  
*vaiṣṇavāstraṃ vāruṇāstraṃ vāyavyaṃ nāgapāśakam \|\| 41 \|\|*

*nārāyaṇāstraṃ gāṃdharvaṃ brahmāstraṃ gāruḍaṃ tathā \|*  
*pārjanyaṃ ca pāśupataṃ jṛṃbhaṇāstraṃ ca pārvatam \|\| 42 \|\|*

*mahāvīraṃ ca sauraṃ ca kālakālaṃ mahānalam \|*  
*maheśvarāstraṃ yāmyaṃ ca daṃḍaṃ saṃmohanaṃ tathā \|\| 43 \|\|*

*samarthamastrakaṃ divyaṃ divyāstraṃ śatakaṃ param \|*  
*bibhratī ca karaissarvairanyānyapi ca sā tadā \|\| 44 \|\|*

39-44. Her tongue was a yojana long and terrible. She bore conch, discus, mace, lotus, sword, leather shield, bows, arrows, skull of circular shape, a yojana in width and majestic in appearance, a trident that touched the sky, a yojana long spear, iron club, threshing rod, thunderbolt, sword, a thick shield, the miraculous weapons of Viṣṇu, Varuṇa, Vāyu, Nārāyaṇa, Gandharva, Brahmā, Garuḍa, Parjanya, Paśupati, Parvata, and Maheśvara, Nāgapāśa, Jṛṃbhaṇāstra, the Mahāvīra, the Saura, the Kālakāla and the Mahānala weapons, the staff of Yama, the Sammohana, the divine weapon called Samartha. Many such and other divine weapons she held in her hands.

## \|\| 6.33.45 \|\|

*āgatya tasthau sā tatra yoginīnāṃ trikoṭibhiḥ \|*  
*sārddhaṃ ca ḍākinīnāṃ vai vikaṭānāṃ trikoṭibhiḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. She came and stood there with three crores of Yoginīs and three crores of terrible Ḍākinīs.

## \|\| 6.33.46 \|\|

*bhūtapretapiśācāśca kūṣmāṇḍā brahmarākṣasāḥ \|*  
*vetālā rākṣasāścaiva yakṣāścaiva sakinnarāḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Bhūtas, Pretas, Piśācas, Kūṣmāṇḍas, Brahmarākṣasas, Vetālas, Yakṣas, Kinnaras and Rākṣasas too came there.

## \|\| 6.33.47 \|\|

*taścaivābhivṛtaḥ skaṃdaḥ praṇamya candraśekharam \|*  
*pituḥ pārśve sahāyo yaḥ samuvāsa tadājñayā \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Skanda was surrounded by these all. He bowed to Śiva and at his bidding stayed near his father to assist him.

## \|\| 6.33.48 \|\|

*atha śambhussamānīya svasainyaṃ sakalaṃ tadā \|*  
*yuddhārthamagamadrudraśśaṃṅkhacūḍena nirbhayaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. The fearless, fierce Śiva gathered his armies and went to fight Śaṅkhacūḍa.

## \|\| 6.33.49 \|\|

*candrabhāgānadītīre vaṭamūle manohare \|*  
*tatra tasthau mahādevo devanistā rahetave \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. The great god stationed himself at the foot of a beautiful Banyan tree on the banks of the river Candrabhāgā,

\[9\] for the emancipation of the gods.

## Chapter 34 - The March of Śaṅkhacūḍa

## \|\| 6.34.1 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*vidhitāta mahābuddhe mune jīva ciraṃ samāḥ \|*  
*kathitaṃ sumahaccitraṃ caritaṃ candramaulinaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:—

1\. O dear son of Brahmā, O sage of great intellect, live long for many years. You have narrated the great story of the mooncrested lord.

## \|\| 6.34.2 \|\|

*śivadūte gate tatra śaṅkhacūḍaśca dānavaḥ \|*  
*kiṃ cakāra pratāpī sa tattvaṃ vada suvistaram \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. When Śiva’s emissary had departed, what did the valorous Dānava, Śaṅkhacūḍa do? Please mention that in detail.

## \|\| 6.34.3 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*atha dūte gate tatra śaṃkhacūḍaḥ pratāpavān \|*  
*uvāca tulasīṃ vārtāṃ gatvābhyaṃtarameva tām \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

3\. When the messenger returned, the valorous Śaṅkhacūḍa went in and told his wife Tulasī all the details.

## \|\| 6.34.4 \|\|

*śaṅkhacūḍa uvāca \|*  
*śambhudūtamukhāddevi yuddhāyāhaṃ samudyataḥ \|*  
*tena gacchāmyahaṃ yoddhuṃ śāsanaṃ kuru me dhruvam \|\| 4 \|\|*

Śaṅkhacūḍa said:—

4\. O dear lady, infuriated by the words of Śiva’s messenger I have prepared for a war. Hence I am going to fight. You carry out my directions.

## \|\| 6.34.5 \|\|

*ityevamuktvā sa jñānī nānābodhanataḥ priyām \|*  
*krīḍāṃ cakāra harṣeṇa tamanādṛtya śaṃkaram \|\| 5 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

5\. After saying this and slighting Śiva, that demon professing to be wise advised his wife in various ways and sported with her with delight.

## \|\| 6.34.6 \|\|

*tau dampatī cikrīḍāte nimagnau sukhasāgare \|*  
*nānākāmakalābhiśca niśi cāṭuśutairapi \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Throughout that night, the couple indulged in sexual dalliance. Uttering coaxing and cajoling words, practising various erotic arts, they immersed themselves in the ocean of happiness.

## \|\| 6.34.7 \|\|

*brāhme muhūrta utthāya prātaḥkṛtyaṃ vidhāya ca \|*  
*nityakāryaṃ ca kṛtvādau dadau dānamanaṃtakam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. He got up in the Brāhma Muhūrta, and finished his daily routine in the morning. He then performed the offering of charitable gifts.

## \|\| 6.34.8-9 \|\|

*putraṃ kṛtvā ca rājendraṃ sarveṣu dāna veṣu ca \|*  
*putre samarpya bhāryāṃ ca sa rājyaṃ sarvasaṃpadam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*priyāmāśvāsayāmāsa sa rājā rudatīṃ punaḥ \|*  
*niṣedhatīṃ ca gamanaṃ nānā vārtāṃ prakathya ca \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. He crowned his son as the lord of Dānavas. He entrusted his wife, his kingdom and his riches to the care of his son. When his wife cried and dissuaded him from going to the war he consoled her by various words of appeasement.

## \|\| 6.34.10 \|\|

*nijasenāpatiṃ vīraṃ samāhūya samādṛtaḥ \|*  
*ādideśa sa sanaddhassaṃgrāmaṃ kartu'mudyataḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. He called his general and ordered him to be ready for the war.

## \|\| 6.34.11 \|\|

*śaṃkhacūḍa uvāca \|*  
*adya senāpate vīrāssarve samaraśālinaḥ \|*  
*saṃnaddhākhilakarmāṇo nirgacchaṃtu raṇāya ca \|\| 11 \|\|*

Śaṅkhacūḍa said:—

11\. O general, let the heroic warriors start for the war. Let them be ready for action; they have been trained well for the war.

## \|\| 6.34.12 \|\|

*daityāśca dānavāḥ śūrā ṣaḍaśītirudā yudhāḥ \|*  
*kaṃkānāṃ balināṃ śīghraṃ senā niryāṃtu nirbhayāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Let the heroic Dānavas and Daityas, the armies of the powerful Kaṅkas of eighty-six divisions well-equipped in arms set out fearlessly.

## \|\| 6.34.13 \|\|

*pañcāśadasurāṇāṃ hi nirgacchaṃtu kulāni vai \|*  
*koṭivīryāṇi yuddhārthaṃ śambhunā devapakṣiṇā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Let the fifty families of Asuras, having the heroism and prowess of a crore set out to fight with Śiva, the partisan of the gods.

## \|\| 6.34.14 \|\|

*saṃnaddhāni ca dhaumrāṇāṃ kulāni ca śataṃ drutam \|*  
*nirgacchaṃtu raṇārthaṃ hi śambhunā mama śāsanāt \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. At my bidding, let the hundred armed families of Dhaumras speedily set out to fight with Śiva.

## \|\| 6.34.15 \|\|

*kālakeyāśca mauryāśca daurhṛdāḥ kālakāstathā \|*  
*sajjā niryāntu yuddhāya rudreṇa mama śāsanāt \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. At my behest, let the Kālakeyas Mauryas, Dauhṛdas and the Kālakas set out ready for the fight with Śiva.

## \|\| 6.34.16 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityājñāpyāsurapatirdānavendro mahābalaḥ \|*  
*nirjagāma mahāsainyaḥ sahasraibahubhirvṛtaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

16\. After ordering thus, the powerful lord of Asuras and the Emperor of the Dānavas set out surrounded by thousands of warriors and great armies.

## \|\| 6.34.17 \|\|

*tasya senāpatiścaiva yuddhaśāstraviśāradaḥ \|*  
*mahāratho mahāvīro rathināṃ pravaro raṇe \|\| 17 \|\|*

1 7. His general was an expert in the science and technique of warfare. He was the best of charioteers a great hero and skilled in warfare.

## \|\| 6.34.18 \|\|

*trilakṣākṣauhiṇīyukto māṃḍalyaṃ ca cakāra ha \|*  
*bahirbabhūva śibirādraṇe vīrabhayaṅkaraḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. He had three hundred thousand Akṣauhiṇī armies. He performed the rites of auspicious beginning and came out of the camp. He was terrible to the watching heroes.

## \|\| 6.34.19 \|\|

*ratnendraṃ sāranirmāṇaṃ vimānamabhiruhya saḥ \|*  
*guruvargaṃ puraskṛtya raṇārthaṃ prayayau kila\|\| \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Mounting on an aerial chariot of exquisite build and inlaid with gems, and making obeisance to the elders and preceptors he set out for the battle.

## \|\| 6.34.20-21 \|\|

*puṣpabhadrānadītīre yatrākṣayavaṭaḥ śubhaḥ \|*  
*siddhāśrame ca siddhānāṃ siddhikṣetraṃ susiddhidam \|\| 20 \|\|*

*kapilasya tataḥ sthānaṃ puṇyakṣetre ca bhārate \|*  
*paścimodadhipūrve ca malayasya hi paścime \|\| 21 \|\|*

20-21. In the holy land of Bhārata, to the east of the western ocean and to the west of Malaya\[3\] mountain, on the banks of river Puṣpabhadrā\[4\] there is a hermitage of Kapila\[5\] with an auspicious holy Banyan tree. It is called Siddhāśrama. It is the place where holy men achieve the result of their action,

## \|\| 6.34.22 \|\|

*śrīśailottarabhāge ca gaṃdhamādanadakṣiṇe \|*  
*paṃcayojanavistīrṇaṃ dairghye śataguṇastathā \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. It is to the north of Śrīśaila\[7\] and to the south of Gaṇḍhamādana. It is five Yojanas in width and a hundred times as much in length.

## \|\| 6.34.23 \|\|

*śuddhasphaṭikasaṃkāśā bhārate ca supuṇyadā \|*  
*puṣpabhadrā nadī ramyā jalapūrṇā sarasvatī \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. The river Puṣpabhadrā is very beautiful and full of transparent water. It confers merits on everyone in Bhārata, like the river Sarasvatī.

## \|\| 6.34.24 \|\|

*lavaṇodadhipriyā bhāryā śaśvatsaubhāgyasaṃ yutā \|*  
*sarasvatīsaṃśritā ca nirgatā sā himālayāt \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. It starts from Himālaya, has its confluence with Sarasvatī. It is the beloved of the briny sea and blessess people with good fortune.

## \|\| 6.34.25 \|\|

*gomaṃtaṃ vāmataḥ kṛtvā praviṣṭā paścimodadhau \|*  
*tatra gatvā śaṃkhacūḍaḥ śiva senāṃ dadarśa ha \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. It enters the western ocean where Gomanta is on its left. Śaṅkhacūḍa went there and saw the army of Śiva.

## Chapter 35 - The conversation between Śiva and the emissary of Śaṅkhacūḍa

## \|\| 6.35.1 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*tatra sthitvā dānavendro mahāntaṃ dānaveśvaram \|*  
*dūtaṃ kṛtvā mahāvijñaṃ preṣayāmāsa śaṃkaram \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

1\. Stationing himself there, the lord of Dānavas sent a leading Dānava of great knowledge as his emissary to Śiva.

## \|\| 6.35.2 \|\|

*sa tatra gatvā dūtaśca candrabhālaṃ dadarśa ha \|*  
*vaṭamūle samāsīnaṃ sūryakoṭisamaprabham \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The emissary went there and saw the moon-crested lord Śiva, of the refulgence of a crore suns, seated at the root of the Banyan tree.

## \|\| 6.35.3 \|\|

*kṛtvā yogāsanaṃ dṛṣṭyā mudrāyuktaṃ ca sasmitam \|*  
*śuddhasphaṭikasaṃkāśaṃ jvalaṃtaṃ brahmatejasa \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. He saw him sitting in a yogic pose, showing the mystic gesture with his eyes, with a smiling face and body as pure as crystal and blazing with transcendent splendour.

## \|\| 6.35.4-7 \|\|

*triśūlapaṭṭiśadharaṃ vyāghracarmāṃbarāvṛtam \|*  
*bhaktamṛtyuharaṃ śāṃtaṃ gaurīkāntaṃ trilocanam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*tapasāṃ phaladātāraṃ karttāraṃ sarvasaṃpadām \|*  
*āśutoṣaṃ prasannāsya bhaktānugrahakārakam \|\| 5 \|\|*

*viśvanāthaṃ viśvabījaṃ viśvarūpaṃ ca viśvajam \|*  
*viśvaṃbharaṃ viśvakaraṃ viśvasaṃhārakāraṇam \|\| 6 \|\|*

*kāraṇaṃ kāraṇānāṃ ca narakārṇavatāraṇam \|*  
*jñānapradaṃ jñānabījaṃ jñānānandaṃ sanātanam \|\| 7 \|\|*

4-7. Śiva held the trident and the iron club. He was clad in the hide of the tiger. The emissary saw the three-eyed lord of Pārvatī, the enlivener of the life of the devotees, the quiet Śiva, the dispenser of the fruits of penance, the creator of riches, quick in being propitiated, eager to bless the devotees and beaming with pleasure in his face. He saw the lord of the universe, the seed of the universe, identical with the universe and of universal form, born of all, lord of all, creator of all, the cause of the annihilation of the universe, the cause of causes, the one who enables devotees to cross the ocean of hell, the bestower of knowledge, the seed of knowledge, knowlege-bliss and eternal.

## \|\| 6.35.8 \|\|

*avaruhya rathād dūtastaṃ dṛṣṭvā dānaveśvaraḥ \|*  
*śaṃkaraṃ sakumāraṃ ca śirasā praṇanāma saḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. On seeing him, the messenger, the leader of Dānavas, descended from his chariot and bowed to him as well as to Kumāra.

## \|\| 6.35.9 \|\|

*vāmato bhadrakālī ca skaṃdaṃ tatpurataḥ sthitam \|*  
*lokāśiṣaṃ dadau tasmai kālī skaṃdaśca śaṃkaraḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. He saw Bhadrakālī to his left and Kārttikeya standing before him. Kālī, Kārttikeya and Śiva offered him the conventional benediction.

## \|\| 6.35.10 \|\|

*athāsau śaṃkhacūḍasya dūtaḥ paramaśāstravit \|*  
*uvāca śaṃkaraṃ natvā karau baddhvā śubhaṃ vacaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. This emissary of Śaṅkhacūḍa, had full knowledge of the sacred texts. He joined his palms in reverence and bowing to him spoke the auspicious words.

## \|\| 6.35.11 \|\|

*\|\| dūta uvāca \|*  
*śaṃkhacūḍasya dūto'haṃ tvatsakāśamihāgataḥ \|*  
*vartate te kimicchādya tattvaṃ brūhi maheśvara \|\| 11 \|\|*

The Emissary said:—

11\. “O lord, I am the emissary of Śaṅkhacūḍa and have come to you. What is it that you desire? Please tell me.”

## \|\| 6.35.12 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*iti śrutvā ca vacanaṃ śaṃkhacūḍasya śaṃkaraḥ \|*  
*prasannātmā mahādevo bhagavāṃstamuvāca ha \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. On hearing these words of Śaṅkhacūḍa, lord Śiva became delighted and spoke.

## \|\| 6.35.13 \|\|

*mahādeva uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu dūta mahāprājña vaco mama sukhāvaham \|*  
*kathanīyamidaṃ tasmai nirvivādaṃ vicārya ca \|\| 13 \|\|*

Lord Śiva said:—

13\. O messenger of great intellect, listen to my words conducive to happiness. After pondering over this, without disputation, this shall be mentioned to him.

## \|\| 6.35.14 \|\|

*vidhātā jagatāṃ brahmā pitā dharmasya dharmavit \|*  
*marīcistasya putraśca kaśyapastatsutaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Brahmā is the creator of the worlds and father of Dharma. He knows virtue. Marīci is his son. Kaśyapa is Marīci’s son.

## \|\| 6.35.15 \|\|

*dakṣaḥ prītyā dadau tasmai nijakanyāstrayodaśa \|*  
*tāsvekā ca danussādhvī tatsaubhāgyavivarddhinī \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Dakṣa gave him his thirteen daughters, with pleasure. Among them the chaste lady Danu increased his fortune to a great extent.

## \|\| 6.35.16 \|\|

*catvāraste danoḥ putrā dānavāstejasolbaṇāḥ \|*  
*teṣveko vipracittistu mahābalaparākramaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Danu gave birth to four sons called Dānavas. They were vigorous and powerful. Vipracitti of great strength and valour was one of them.

## \|\| 6.35.17 \|\|

*tatputro dhārmiko daṃbho dānavendro mahāmatiḥ \|*  
*tasya tvaṃ tanayaḥ śreṣṭho dharmātmā dānaveśvaraḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. His son, the virtuous Dambha of great intellect was the ruler of Dānavas. You are his excellent son, a pious soul, and the lord of Dānavas.

## \|\| 6.35.18 \|\|

*purā tvaṃ pāṣardo gopo gopeṣveva ca dhārmikaḥ \|*  
*adhunā rādhikāśāpājjātastvaṃ dānaveśvaraḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. In previous birth you were a cowherd and an attendant of Kṛṣṇa. Among the cowherds you were virtuous. As a result of Rādhā’s curse, you are born as Dānava and have become the king of Dānavas.

## \|\| 6.35.19 \|\|

*dānavīṃ yonimāyātastattvato na hi dānavaḥ \|*  
*nijavṛtaṃ purā jñātvā devavairaṃ tyajādhunā \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. You are casually born as a Dānava. You are really no Dānava. Realising your previous birth you leave off your inimical attitude to the gods.

## \|\| 6.35.20 \|\|

*drohaṃ na kuru taissārddhaṃ svapadaṃ bhuṃkṣva sādaram \|*  
*nādhikaṃ savikāraṃ ca kuru rājyaṃ vicārya ca \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Don’t be malicious towards them. You can enjoy your kingdom zealously. Do not try to expand your kingdom nor spoil it.

## \|\| 6.35.21 \|\|

*dehi rājyaṃ ca devānāṃ matprītiṃ rakṣa dānava \|*  
*nijarājye sukhaṃ tiṣṭha tiṣṭhaṃtu svapade surāḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. O Dānava, return their kingdom to the gods. Maintain my affection. Stay in your kingdom happily. Let the gods stay in their region.

## \|\| 6.35.22 \|\|

*alaṃ bhūtavirodhena devadroheṇa kiṃ punaḥ \|*  
*kulīnāśśuddhakarmāṇaḥ sarve kaśyapavaṃśajāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Do not offend people. Don’t be malicious to the gods. The descendants of Kaśyapa are noble and indulge in pure activities.

## \|\| 6.35.23 \|\|

*yāni kāni ca pāpāni brahmahatyā dikāni ca \|*  
*jñātidrohajapāpasya kalāṃ nārhaṃti ṣoḍaśīm \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Whatever sin is there in the world, even including that of slaughter of a brahmin, does not merit even a sixteenth part of the sin accruing from the offence towards kinsmen.

## \|\| 6.35.24 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityādibahuvārttāṃ ca śrutismṛtiparāṃ śubhām \|*  
*provāca śaṃkarastasmai bodhayan jñānamuttamam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. These and many such words of advice, auspiciously based on injunctions of Śruti and Smṛti, Śiva said to him enlightening him in an excellent manner.

## \|\| 6.35.25 \|\|

*śikṣitaśśaṃkhacūḍena sa dūtastarkavittama \|*  
*uvāca vacanaṃ namro bhavitavyavimohitaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The emissary who had been well instructed by Śaṅkhacūḍa who knew his duties well but who had been deluded by destiny spoke these words humbly.

## \|\| 6.35.26 \|\|

*dūta uvāca \|*  
*tvayā yatkathitaṃ deva nānyathā tattathā vacaḥ \|*  
*tathyaṃ kiṃcidyathārthaṃ ca śrūyatāṃ me nivedanam \|\| 26 \|\|*

The messenger said:—

26\. O lord, what has been narrated by you is true. It cannot be otherwise. But let my submission based on certain factual elements be heard.

## \|\| 6.35.27 \|\|

*jñātidrohe mahatpāpaṃ tvayoktamadhunā ca yat \|*  
*tatkimīśāsurāṇāṃ ca na surāṇāṃ vada prabho \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. O lord Śiva, verily a great sin has been cited as the result of offence to kinsmen by you now. But does it concern only Asuras and not the gods? Please tell me.

## \|\| 6.35.28 \|\|

*sarveṣāmiti cettadvai tadā vacmi vicārya ca \|*  
*nirṇayaṃ brūhi tatrādya kuru saṃdehabhaṃjanam \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. If it applies to all alike, I shall consider it and let you know. Please tell me your decision at the outset and clear my doubts.

## \|\| 6.35.29 \|\|

*madhukaiṭabhayordaityavarayoḥ pralayārṇave \|*  
*śiraśchedaṃ cakārāsau kasmāccakrī maheśvara \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. O lord Śiva, why did the discus-bearing lord Viṣṇu sever the heads of Madhu and Kaiṭabha the excellent Daityas in the ocean of dissolution?

## \|\| 6.35.30 \|\|

*tripuraissaha saṃyuddhaṃ bhasmatvakaraṇaṃ kutaḥ \|*  
*bhavāñcakāra giriśa surapakṣīti viśrutam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Your Majesty too, O Śiva, is famous as a partisan of the gods. Why did you fight with the Tripuras and reduce them to ashes?

## \|\| 6.35.31 \|\|

*gṛhītvā tasya sarvasvaṃ kutaḥ prasthāpito baliḥ \|*  
*sutalādi samuddhartuṃ taddvāre ca gadādharaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. After divesting him of every thing why was Bali packed off to Sutala and other regions? Did Viṣṇu go to his threshold as his uplifter?

## \|\| 6.35.32 \|\|

*sabhrātṛko hiraṇyākṣaḥ kathaṃ devaiśca hiṃsitaḥ \|*  
*śuṃbhādayo'surāścaiva kathaṃ devairnipātitāḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Why was Hiraṇyākṣa\[4\] harassed by the gods along with his brother? Why were Śumbha and other Asuras subjected to fall by the gods?

## \|\| 6.35.33 \|\|

*purā samudramathane pīyūṣaṃ bhakṣitaṃ suraiḥ \|*  
*kleśabhājo vayaṃ tatra te sarve phalabhoginaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Formerly when the ocean was churned, the nectar was drunk off by the gods. All the strain and stress was ours but the gods reaped the fruit of our endeavour.

## \|\| 6.35.34 \|\|

*krīḍābhāṃḍamidaṃ viśvaṃ kālasya paramātmanaḥ \|*  
*sa dadāti yadā yasmai tasyai tasyaiśvaryaṃ bhave ttadā \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. The entire universe is but an object of sport of Kāla the supreme soul. Whomsoever and whensoever he pleases to bestow the riches he atttains them.

## \|\| 6.35.35 \|\|

*devadānavayorvairaṃ śaśvanaimittikaṃ sadā \|*  
*parājayo jayasteṣāṃ kālādhīnaḥ krameṇa ca \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. The enmity of the gods and the Dānavas is perpetual and sparked off due to some reason or other. By turns, subject to the whims of Kāla they enjoy victory or defeat.

## \|\| 6.35.36 \|\|

*tavānayorvirodhe ca gamanaṃ niṣphalaṃ bhavet \|*  
*samasaṃbaṃdhināṃ tadvai rocate neśvarasya te \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Interference on your part in the dispute between the two is futile. This does not behove you, the lord who are equally in touch with both.

## \|\| 6.35.37 \|\|

*surāsurāṇāṃ sarveṣāmīśvarasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*iyaṃ te rahitā lajjā sparddhāsmābhissahādhunā \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Your rivalry to us is excessively shameful since you are lord unto the gods as well as to the Asuras. You are the supreme soul.

## \|\| 6.35.38 \|\|

*yatodhikā caiva kīrtirhāniścaiva parājaye \|*  
*tavaitadviparītaṃ ca manasā saṃvicārya tām \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. In the event of your victory your fame is not enhanced. In the event of your defeat you suffer a great loss. Let this disadvantage be pondered over.

## \|\| 6.35.39 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityetadvacanaṃ śrutvā saṃprahasya trilocanaḥ \|*  
*yathocitaṃ ca madhuramuvāca dānaveśvaram \|\| 39 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

39\. On hearing these words, the three-eyed lord laughed and spoke sweetly to the leading Dānava what seemed proper.

## \|\| 6.35.40 \|\|

*maheśa uvāca \|*  
*vayaṃ bhaktaparādhīnā na svataṃtrāḥ kadāpi hi \|*  
*tadicchayā tatkarmāṇo na kasyāpi ca pakṣiṇaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

Lord Śiva said:—

40\. We are subservient to our devotees. We are never independent. We carry out their tasks at their wish. We are not the partisans of any one in particular.

## \|\| 6.35.41 \|\|

*purā vidhiprārthanayā yuddhamādau harerapi \|*  
*madhukaiṭabhayordetyavarayoḥ pralayārṇave \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Formerly the fight of Viṣṇu with the excellent Daityas Madhu and Kaiṭabha in the ocean of dissolution was due to the prior request of Brahmā.

## \|\| 6.35.42 \|\|

*devaprārthanayā tena hiraṇyakaśipoḥ purā \|*  
*prahrādārthaṃ vadho'kāri bhaktānāṃ hitakāriṇā \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. For the sake of Prahlāda, at the request of gods, Hiraṇyakaśipu was slain by him acting in the interest of his devotees.

## \|\| 6.35.43 \|\|

*tripuraissaha saṃyuddhaṃ bhasmatvakaraṇaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*devaprārthanayākāri mayāpi ca purā śrutam \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Formerly I fought with the Tripuras and reduced them to ashes, only at the request of the gods. It is well known.

## \|\| 6.35.44 \|\|

*sarveśvaryāssarvamāturdevaprārthanayā purā \|*  
*āsīcchuṃbhādibhiryuddhaṃ vadhasteṣāṃ tayā kṛtaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Formerly Pārvatī, the Mother of all, the goddess of all, fought with Śumbha and others and killed them only at the request of the gods.

## \|\| 6.35.45 \|\|

*adyāpi tridaśāssarve brahmāṇaṃ śaraṇaṃ yayuḥ \|*  
*sa sadevo harirmāṃ ca devaśśaraṇamāgataḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Even today, the gods have sought refuge in Brahmā. And he along with the gods and the lord Viṣṇu has sought refuge in me.

## \|\| 6.35.46 \|\|

*haribrahmādikānāṃ ca prārthanāvaśatopyaham \|*  
*surāṇāmīśvaro dūta yuddhārthamagamaṃ khalu \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. O Emissary, paying heed to the request of Viṣṇu, Brahmā and others, I, though lord of all, have come here in the battle of the gods.

## \|\| 6.35.47 \|\|

*pārṣadapravarastvaṃ hi kṛṣṇasya ca mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*ye ye hatāśca daiteyā nahi kepi tvayā samāḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Really you are the foremost of the comrades of Kṛṣṇa, the great soul. Those Daityas who had been formerly killed are not on a par with you.

## \|\| 6.35.48 \|\|

*kā lajjā mahatī rājan mama yuddhe tvayā saha \|*  
*devakāryārthamīśohaṃ vinayena ca preṣitaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. What is there excessively shameful in my fight with you, O king? I the lord have been urged humbly to carry out the task of the gods.

## \|\| 6.35.49 \|\|

*gaccha tvaṃ śaṃkhacūḍe vai kathanīyaṃ ca me vacaḥ \|*  
*sa ca yuktaṃ karotvatra surakāryaṃ karomyaham \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Go to Śaṅkhacūḍa and tell him what I have said. Let him do what is proper. I shall carry out the taṣk of the gods.

## \|\| 6.35.50 \|\|

*ityuktvā śaṃkarastatra virarāma maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*uttasthau śaṃkhacūḍasya dūto'gacchattadaṃtikam \|\| 50 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

50\. On saying this, Śiva the great god, stopped. The emissary stood up and returned to Śaṅkhacñḍa.

## Chapter 36 - Mutual fight

## \|\| 6.36.1 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*sa dūtastatra gatvā ca śivavākyaṃ jagāda ha \|*  
*savistaraṃ yathārthaṃ ca niścayaṃ tasya tattvataḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

1\. The emissary returned and mentioned the words of Śiva, in detail and truthfully. He conveyed his decision as it was.

## \|\| 6.36.2 \|\|

*tacchutvā śaṃkhacūḍo'sau dānavendraḥ pratāpavān \|*  
*aṃgīcakāra suprītyā raṇameva sa dānavaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. On hearing that, the valorous Dānava Śaṅkhacūḍa accepted lovingly the alternative of a fight.

## \|\| 6.36.3 \|\|

*samāruroha yānaṃ ca sahāmātyaiśca satvaraḥ \|*  
*ādideśa svasainyaṃ ca yuddhārthaṃ śaṃkareṇa ca \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Hurriedly he got into his vehicle along with his ministers. He commanded his army against Śiva.

## \|\| 6.36.4 \|\|

*śivassvasainyaṃ devāṃśca prerayāmāsa satvaraḥ \|*  
*svayamapyakhileśopi sannaddhobhūcca līlayā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Śiva too hastened to urge his army and the gods. The lord of all was ready himself with his sport.

## \|\| 6.36.5 \|\|

*yuddhāraṃbho babhūvāśu nedurvādyāni bhūriśaḥ \|*  
*kolāhalaśca saṃjāto vīraśabdastathaiva ca \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The musical instruments formally announced the beginning of war. There was a great tumult along with the shouts of the heroes.

## \|\| 6.36.6 \|\|

*devadānavayoryuddhaṃ sparamabhūnmune \|*  
*dharmato yuyudhe tatra devadānavayorgaṇaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. O sage, the mutual fight between the gods and the Dānavas ensued. Both the hosts of the gods and the Dānavas fought righteously.

## \|\| 6.36.7 \|\|

*svayaṃ mahendro yuyudhe sārdhaṃ ca vṛṣaparvaṇā \|*  
*bhāskaro yuyudhe vipracittinā saha dharmataḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Mahendra fought with Vṛṣaparvan. Bhāskara fought with Vipracitti.

## \|\| 6.36.8 \|\|

*daṃbhena saha viṣṇuśca cakāra paramaṃ raṇam \|*  
*kālāsureṇa kālaśca gokarṇena hutāśanaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Viṣṇu fought a great battle with Dambha, Kala with the Asura Kāla and the firegod fought with Gokarṇa.

## \|\| 6.36.9 \|\|

*kuberaḥ kālakeyena viśvakarmā mayena ca \|*  
*bhayaṃkareṇa mṛtyuśca saṃhāreṇa yamastathā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Kubera fought with Kālakeya and Viśvakarman with Maya. Mṛtyu fought with Bhayaṃkara and Yama with Saṃhāra.

## \|\| 6.36.10 \|\|

*kālambikena varuṇaścaṃcalena samīraṇaḥ \|*  
*budhaśca ghaṭapṛṣṭhena raktākṣeṇa śanaiścaraḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Varuṇa fought with Kālambika, the wind god with Cañcala. Mercury with Ghaṭapṛṣṭha and Śanaiścara with Raktākṣa.

## \|\| 6.36.11 \|\|

*jayanto ratnasāreṇa vasavo varcasāṃ gaṇaiḥ \|*  
*aśvinau dīptimadbhyāṃ ca dhūmreṇa nalakūbaraḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Jayanta fought with Ratnasāra; the Vasus with the groups of Varcas’s; the Aśvins with the two Dīptimants and Nalakūbara with Dhūmbra.

## \|\| 6.36.12 \|\|

*dhuraṃdhareṇa dharmaśca gaṇakākṣeṇa maṃgalaḥ \|*  
*śobhākareṇa vaiśvānaḥ pipiṭena ca manmathaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Dharma fought with Dhurandhara; Maṅgala with Gaṇakākṣa; Vaiśvana with Śobhākara and Manmatha with Pipiṭa.

## \|\| 6.36.13-14 \|\|

*gokāmukhena cūrṇena khaḍganāmnā'sureṇa ca \|*  
*dhūmreṇa saṃhalenāpi viśvena ca pratāpinā \|\| 13 \|\|*

*palāśena dvādaśā'rkā yuyudhurdharmataḥ pare \|*  
*asurairamarāssārddhaṃ śivasāhāyyaśālinaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. The twelve sun gods fought with the Asuras—Gokāmukha, Cūrṇa, Khaḍga, Dhūmra, Samhala, the valorous Viśva and Palāśa. The other gods assisting Śiva fought righteously with the other Asuras.

## \|\| 6.36.15 \|\|

*ekādaśa mahārudrāścaikādaśabhayaṃkaraiḥ \|*  
*asurairyuyudhurvīrairmaihābalaparākramaiḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The eleven Mahārudras fought with the eleven terrible Asuras of great power and valour.

## \|\| 6.36.16 \|\|

*mahāmaṇiśca yuyudhe cogracaṃḍādibhissaha \|*  
*rāhuṇā saha candraśca jīvaḥ śukreṇa dharmataḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Mahāmaṇi fought with Ugracaṇḍa and others. The god Moon fought with Rāhu and Jīva fought with Śukra.

## \|\| 6.36.17 \|\|

*nandīśvarādayassarve dānavapravaraissaha \|*  
*yuyudhuśca mahāyuddhe noktā vistarataḥ pṛthak \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Nandīśvara and the rest fought with leading Dānavas in the great battle. This is not being explained separately.

## \|\| 6.36.18 \|\|

*vaṭamūle tadā śaṃbhustasthau kālyāḥ sutena ca \|*  
*sarve ca yuyudhussainyasamūhāssatataṃ mune \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. O sage, then Śiva stayed at the foot of the Banyan tree along with Kālī and his son. The hosts of the two armies fought continuously against each other.

## \|\| 6.36.19 \|\|

*ratnasiṃhāsane ramye koṭidānavasaṃyutaḥ \|*  
*uvāsa śaṃkhacūḍaśca ratnabhūṣaṇabhūṣitaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Decorated with gemset ornaments, Śaṅkhcūḍa sat on his gemset throne of great beauty attended upon by a crore Dānavas.

## \|\| 6.36.20 \|\|

*mahāyuddho babhūvātha devāsuravimardanaḥ \|*  
*nānāyudhāni divyāni calaṃtisma mahāmṛdhe \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Then ensued a great war in which both gods and Asuras were crushed. In that great war many divine and miraculous weapons were hurled.

## \|\| 6.36.21-22 \|\|

*gadarṣṭipaṭṭiśāścakrabhuśuṃḍiprāsamudgarāḥ \|*  
*nistriṃśabhallaparighāḥ śaktyunmukhaparaśvadhāḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*śaratomarakhaḍgāśca śataghnyaśca sahasraśaḥ \|*  
*bhiṃdipālādayaścānye vīrahasteṣu śobhitāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. Maces, long and short swords, Paṭṭiśas, Bhuśuṇḍis, Mudgaras (different kinds of iron clubs), javelins, spears, Parighas, Śaktis, axes, arrows, Tomaras, Śataghnīs, and other weapons shone in the hands of the heroes.

## \|\| 6.36.23 \|\|

*śirāṃsi cicchiduścaibhirvīrāstatra maho tsavāḥ \|*  
*vīrāṇāmubhayoścaiva sainyayorgarjato raṇe \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Using these weapons, the heroes severed the heads of each other. It was a jubilant occasion for the roaring heroes of the armies.

## \|\| 6.36.24 \|\|

*gajāsturaṃgā bahavaḥ syandanāśca padātayaḥ \|*  
*sārohavāhā vividhāstatrāsan suvikhaṃḍitāḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Elephants, horses, chariots and foot soldiers along with their drivers and riders were hit and split up.

## \|\| 6.36.25 \|\|

*nikṛttabāhūrukarakaṭikarṇayugāṃghrayaḥ \|*  
*saṃchinnadhvajabāṇāsitanutra varabhūṣaṇāḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The arms, thighs, hands, hips, ears and feet were cut off. The banners, arrows, swords, coats of mail and excellent ornaments were slit and split.

## \|\| 6.36.26 \|\|

*samuddhatakirīṭaiśca śirobhissaha kuṃḍalaiḥ \|*  
*saṃraṃbhanaṣṭairāstīrṇā babhau bhūḥ karabhorubhiḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The earth shone with heads divested of coronets but with earrings retained, strewn about and with thighs resembling trunks of elephants broken off during the tussle.

## \|\| 6.36.27 \|\|

*mahābhujaissābharaṇaissaṃchinnaissāyudhaistathā \|*  
*aṃgairanyaiśca sahasā paṭalairvā sasāraghaiḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Severed arms with the ornaments and weapons still retained and other limbs too were lying scattered about like honeycombs.

## \|\| 6.36.28 \|\|

*mṛdhe bhaṭāḥ pradhāvaṃtaḥ kabaṃdhān svaśirokṣibhiḥ \|*  
*paśyaṃtastatra cotpeturudyatāyudhasadbhujaiḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. The soldiers running in the battle field saw several headless bodies that jumped with many weapons lifted in their hands.

## \|\| 6.36.29 \|\|

*valgaṃto'titarāṃ vīrā yuyudhuśca parasparam \|*  
*śastrāstrairvividhaistatra mahābalaparākramāḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. With different kinds of miraculous and ordinary weapons and missiles, the heroes of great strength and valour fought one another shouting and leaping.

## \|\| 6.36.30 \|\|

*kecitsvarṇamukhairbāṇairvinihatya bhaṭānmṛdhe \|*  
*vyanadan vīrasannādaṃ satoyā iva toyadāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Some heroes killed the soldiers with their arrows fitted with goden tips and roared like water-laden rumbling clouds.

## \|\| 6.36.31 \|\|

*sarvataśśarakūṭena vīrassarathasārathim \|*  
*vīraṃ saṃchādayāmāsa prāvṛṭsūryamivāṃbudaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. One hero fully encompassed another hero as well as his chariot and charioteer, by discharging heaps of arrows like the rainy season covering up the sun under the clouds.

## \|\| 6.36.32 \|\|

*anyonyamabhisaṃsṛtya yuyudhurdvandvayodhinaḥ \|*  
*āhvayaṃto viśaṃto'gre kṣipaṃto marmabhirmithaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Fighters of duel rushed against one another, challenging, thrusting and diving in at the vulnerable points.

## \|\| 6.36.33 \|\|

*sarvato vīrasaṃghāśca nānābāhudhvajāyudhāḥ \|*  
*vyadṛśyaṃta mahāsaṃkhye kurvaṃtaḥ siṃhasaṃravam \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Everywhere groups of heroes were seen in that

terrible war roaring like lions with various weapons displayed in their hands.

## \|\| 6.36.34 \|\|

*mahāravānsvaśaṃkhāṃśca vidadhmurvai pṛthak pṛthak \|*  
*valganaṃ cakrire tatra mahāvīrāḥ praharṣitāḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. The heroes in their joy shouted and leapt blowing on their conches of loud sound severally.

## \|\| 6.36.35 \|\|

*evaṃ cirataraṃ kālaṃ devadānavayormahat \|*  
*babhūva yuddhaṃ vikaṭaṃ karālaṃ vīraharṣadam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Thus for a long time the great combat between the gods and Dānavas continued, terrible and tumultuous but delightful to the heroes.

## \|\| 6.36.36 \|\|

*mahāprabhośca līleyaṃ śaṃkarasya parātmanaḥ \|*  
*yayā samīhitaṃ sarvaṃ sadevāsuramānuṣam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Such was the divine sport of the great lord Śiva, the great soul. Everyone including the gods, Asuras and human beings was deluded by it.

## Chapter 37 - Śaṅkhacūḍa fights with the full contingent of his army

## \|\| 6.37.1 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*tadā devagaṇāssarve dānavaiśca parājitāḥ \|*  
*dudruvurbhayabhītāśca śastrāstrakṣatavigrahāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

1\. Then the gods were defeated by the Dānavas. Their bodies were wounded by weapons and missiles. Terrified, they took to flight.

## \|\| 6.37.2 \|\|

*te parāvṛtya viśveśaṃ śaṃkaraṃ śaraṇaṃ yayuḥ \|*  
*trāhi trāhīti sarveśetyū curvihvalayā girā \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Returning to Śiva, the lord of the universe, they sought refuge in him. In agitated words they cried “O Lord of all, save, O save us.”

## \|\| 6.37.3 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā parājayaṃ teṣāṃ devādīnāṃ sa śaṃkaraḥ \|*  
*sabhayaṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā kopamuccaiścakāra ha \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. On seeing the defeat of the gods and others and on hearing their cries of fear, Śiva was greatly infuriated.

## \|\| 6.37.4 \|\|

*nirīkṣya sa kṛpādṛṣṭyā devebhyaścābhayaṃ dadau \|*  
*balaṃ ca svagaṇānāṃ vai varddhayāmāsa tejasā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. He glanced at the gods sympathetically and assured them of his protection. With his brilliance he enhanced the strength of his Gaṇas.

## \|\| 6.37.5 \|\|

*śivājñaptastadā skando dānavānāṃ gaṇaissaha \|*  
*yuyudhe nirbhayassaṃkhye mahāvīro harātmajaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Commanded by śiva, the great hero Kārttikeya, son of Śiva fought fearlessly with the hosts of Dānavas in the battle.

## \|\| 6.37.6 \|\|

*kṛtvā krodhaṃ vīraśabdaṃ devo yastārakāṃtakaḥ \|*  
*akṣauhiṇīnāṃ śatakaṃ samare sa jaghāna ha \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Shouting angrily and roaring like a hero, the lord, the slayer of Tāraka killed a hundred Akṣauhiṇīs in the battle.

## \|\| 6.37.7 \|\|

*rudhiraṃ pātayāmāsa kālī kamalalocanā \|*  
*teṣāṃ śirāṃsi saṃchidya babhakṣa sahasā ca sā \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Clipping off their heads, Kālī with eyes like a red lotus, drank off the blood and devoured the flesh rapidly.

## \|\| 6.37.8 \|\|

*papau raktāni teṣāṃ ca dānavānāṃ samaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*yuddhaṃ cakāra vividhaṃ suradānavabhīṣaṇam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. She fought in diverse ways terrifying both the gods and the Dānavas. She drank the blood of the Dānavas all round.

## \|\| 6.37.9 \|\|

*śatalakṣaṃ gajendrāṇāṃ śatalakṣaṃ nṛṇāṃ tathā \|*  
*samādāyaikahastena mukhe cikṣepa līlayā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Seizing ten million elephants and an equal number of men with a single hand she playfully thrust them into her mouth.

## \|\| 6.37.10 \|\|

*kabaṃdhānāṃ sahasraṃ ca sannanarta raṇe bahu \|*  
*mahān kolāhalo jātaḥ klībānāṃ ca bhayaṃkaraḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Many thousands of headless bodies danced in the battle field. There was a great tumult that terrified the cowards.

## \|\| 6.37.11 \|\|

*punaḥ skaṃdaḥ prakupyoccaiḥ śaravarṣāñcakāra ha \|*  
*pātayāmāsa kṣayataḥ koṭiśo'suranāyakān \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Again Kārttikeya became furiously angry and showered volleys of arrows. He struck crores of leaders of the Asuras within a trice.

## \|\| 6.37.12 \|\|

*dānavāḥ śarajālena skandasya kṣatavigrahāḥ \|*  
*bhītāḥ pradudruvussarve śeṣā maraṇatastadā \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The Dānavas wounded in their bodies by the numerous arrows of Kārttikeya fled in fright. Those who remained were killed.

## \|\| 6.37.13 \|\|

*vṛṣaparvā vipracittirdaṃḍaścāpi vikaṃpanaḥ \|*  
*skaṃdena yuyudhussārddhaṃ tena sarve krameṇa ca \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Vṛṣaparvan, Vipracitti, Daṇḍa, and Vikampana fought with Kārttikeya by turns.

## \|\| 6.37.14 \|\|

*mahāmārī ca yuyudhe na babhūva parāṅmukhī \|*  
*babhūvuste kṣatāṃgāśca skaṃdaśaktiprapīḍitāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Mahāmāri also fought. She was never routed. All of them afflicted by Kārttikeya’s spear were wounded.

## \|\| 6.37.15 \|\|

*mahāmārīskaṃdayośca vijayobhūttadā mune \|*  
*nedurduṃdubhayassvarge puṣpavṛṣṭiḥ papāta ha \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. O sage, Mahāmārī and Skanda won the battle. Big wardrums were sounded in the heaven. Showers of flowers fell down.

## \|\| 6.37.16-17 \|\|

*skaṃdasya samaraṃ dṛṣṭvā mahāraudraṃ tamadbhutam \|*  
*dānavānāṃ kṣayakaraṃ yathāprakṛtikalpakam \|\| 16 \|\|*

*mahāmārīkṛtaṃ taccopadravaṃ kṣayahetukam \|*  
*cukopātīva sahasā sanaddhobhūtsvayaṃ tadā \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. On seeing the wonderfully terrible fight of Kārttikeya that caused wastage in the rank and file of the Dānavas like natural disasters, as well as the harassment and havoc wrought by Mahāmāri, Śaṅkhacūḍa became furious and himself got ready for the battle.

## \|\| 6.37.18-19 \|\|

*varaṃ vimānamāruhya nānāśastrāstrasaṃyutam \|*  
*abhayaṃ sarvavīrāṇāṃ nānāratnaparicchadam \|\| 18 \|\|*

*mahāvīraiśśaṃkhacūḍo jagāma rathamadhyataḥ \|*  
*dhanurvikṛṣya karṇāntaṃ cakāra śaravarṣaṇam \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. He got into his excellent aerial chariot that contained different weapons and missiles, that was set in diamond and that encouraged and emboldened the heroes. Śaṅkhacūḍa drew the string of the bow upto his ear and discharged volleys of arrows from his seat in the middle of the chariot. He was accompanied by many heroes.

## \|\| 6.37.20 \|\|

*tasya sā śaravṛṣṭiśca durnivāryyā bhayaṃkarī \|*  
*mahāghorāṃdhakāraśca vadhasthāne babhūva ha \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. His volley of arrows was terrifying. It could not be withstood. A terrible darkness spread in the battlefield.

## \|\| 6.37.21 \|\|

*devāḥ pradudruvuḥ sarve ye'nye nandīśvarādayaḥ \|*  
*eka eva kārttikeyastasthau samaramūrddhani \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. The gods Nandīśvara and others fled. Only Kārttikeya stayed behind in the battle field.

## \|\| 6.37.22 \|\|

*parvatānāṃ ca sarpāṇāṃ nāgānāṃ śākhināṃ tathā \|*  
*rājā cakāra vṛṣṭiṃ ca durnivāryā bhayaṃkarīm \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The king of Dānavas showered mountains, serpents, pythons and trees so terrifyingly that it could not be withstood.

## \|\| 6.37.23 \|\|

*taddṛṣṭyā prahataḥ skando babhūva śivanandanaḥ \|*  
*nīhāreṇa ca sāṃdreṇa saṃvṛtau bhāskarau yathā \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Oppressed by that shower Kārttikeya, the son of Śiva, looked like the sun enveloped by thick sheets of frost.

## \|\| 6.37.24 \|\|

*nānāvidhāṃ svamāyāṃ ca cakāra mayadarśitām \|*  
*tāṃ nāvidan surāḥ kepi gaṇāśca munisattama \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. He exhibited many types of illusions in the manner indicated by Maya. O excellent sage, none of the gods or Gaṇas understood it.

## \|\| 6.37.25 \|\|

*tadaiva śaṅkhacūḍaśca mahāmāyī mahābalaḥ \|*  
*śareṇaikena divyena dhanuściccheda tasya vai \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. At the same time, the powerful Śaṅkhacūḍa of great illusion split his bow with a divine arrow.

## \|\| 6.37.26 \|\|

*babhaṃja tadrathaṃ divyaṃ ciccheda rathapīḍakān \|*  
*mayūraṃ jarjarībhūtaṃ divyāstreṇa cakāra saḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. He split his divine chariot and the horses pulling it. With a divine missile he shattered the peacock too.

## \|\| 6.37.27 \|\|

*śaktiṃ cikṣepa sūryābhāṃ tasya vakṣasi ghātinīm \|*  
*mūrcchāmavāpa sahasā tatprahāreṇa sa kṣaṇam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. The Dānava hurled his spear as refulgent as the sun fatally on his chest whereat he fell unconscious by the force of the blow.

## \|\| 6.37.28 \|\|

*punaśca cetanāṃ prāpya kārtikaḥ paravīrahā \|*  
*ratnendrasāranirmāṇamāruroha svavāhanam \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Regaining consciousness, Kārttikeya the destroyer of heroic enemies, mounted his vehicle of sturdy build, set with gems.

## \|\| 6.37.29 \|\|

*smṛtvā pādau maheśasya sāmbikasya ca ṣaṇmukhaḥ \|*  
*śastrāstrāṇi gṛhītvaiva cakāra raṇamulbaṇam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Remembering the feat of lord Śiva accompanied by Pārvatī, and taking up weapons and missiles, the sixfaced deity fought terrifically.

## \|\| 6.37.30 \|\|

*sarppāṃśca parvatāṃścaiva vṛkṣāṃśca prastarāṃstathā \|*  
*sarvāṃściccheda kopena divyā streṇa śivātmajaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. With his divine missiles, the son of Śiva split the serpents, mountains, trees and rocks, everything furiously.

## \|\| 6.37.31 \|\|

*vahniṃ nivārayāmāsa pārjanyena śareṇa ha \|*  
*rathaṃ dhanuśca ciccheda śaṃkhacūḍasya līlayā \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. He prevented a conflagration by the missile of cloud. He split the chariot and the bow of Śaṅkhacūḍa playfully.

## \|\| 6.37.32 \|\|

*sannāhaṃ sarvavāhāṃśca kirīṭaṃ mukuṭojjvalam \|*  
*vīraśabdaṃ cakārāsau jagarja ca punaḥ punaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. He split his armour, coronet and the vehicles. He roared like a hero and shouted again and again.

## \|\| 6.37.33 \|\|

*cikṣepa śaktiṃ sūryābhāṃ dānavendrasya vakṣasi \|\| \|*  
*tatprahāreṇa saṃprāpa mūrcchāṃ dīrghatamena ca \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. He hurled his spear refulgent like the sun at the chest of the lord of Dānavas. At the blow he fell unconscious.

## \|\| 6.37.34 \|\|

*muhūrtamātraṃ tatkleśaṃ vinīya sa mahābalaḥ \|*  
*cetanāṃ prāpya cottasthau jagarja harivarca saḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. That powerful Asura got rid of the affliction in a Muhūrta and regained consciousness. With a leonine vigour he got up and roared.

## \|\| 6.37.35 \|\|

*śaktyā jaghāna taṃ cāpi kārtikeyaṃ mahābalam \|*  
*sa papāta mahīpṛṣṭhe'moghāṃ kurvanvidhipradām \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. He bit Kārttikeya of great strength with his spear. Not making that spear, a gift of Brahmā, futile, Kārttikeya fell on the ground.

## \|\| 6.37.36 \|\|

*kālī gṛhītvā taṃ kroḍe nināya śivasannidhau \|*  
*jñānena taṃ śivaścāpi jīvayāmāsa līlayā \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Taking him on her lap Kālī brought him near Śiva. By his divine sport and perfect wisdom Śiva enlivened him.

## \|\| 6.37.37 \|\|

*dadau balamanaṃtaṃ ca samuttasthau pratāpavān \|*  
*gamanāya matiṃ cakre punastatra śivātmajaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Śiva gave him infinite strength. As a result of that the valorous Kārttikeya stood up and felt inclined to go to the battlefield.

## \|\| 6.37.38 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare vīro vīrabhadro mahābalaḥ \|*  
*śaṃkhacūḍena yuyudhe samare balaśālinā \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. In the meantime the heroic Vīrabhadra of great strength fought with the powerful Śaṅkhacūḍa in the battle.

## \|\| 6.37.39 \|\|

*vavarṣa samare'strāṇi yāniyāni ca dānavaḥ \|*  
*ciccheda līlayā vīrastānitāni nijaiśśaraiḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Whatever arrows were discharged by the Dānava in the battle were split playfully by Vīrabhadra by means of his own arrows.

## \|\| 6.37.40 \|\|

*divyānyastrāṇi śataśo mumuce dānaveśvaraḥ \|*  
*tāni ciccheda taṃ bāṇairvīrabhadraḥ pratāpavān \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. The lord of Dānavas discharged hundreds of divine missiles. The valorous Vīrabhadra split all of them by means of his arrows.

## \|\| 6.37.41 \|\|

*athātīva cukopoccaiśśaṃkhacūḍaḥ pratāpavān \|*  
*śaktyā jaghānorasi taṃ sa cakaṃpe papāta kau \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. The valorous Śaṅkhacñḍa became infuriated and hit him on the grounds.

## \|\| 6.37.42 \|\|

*kṣaṇena cetanāṃ prāpya samuttasthau gaṇeśvaraḥ \|*  
*jagrāha ca dhanurbhūyo vīrabhadro gaṇāgraṇīḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Regaining consciouness in a trice the leader of the Gaṇas, Vīrabhadra caught hold of his bow again.

## \|\| 6.37.43 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare kālī jagāma samaraṃ punaḥ \|*  
*bhakṣituṃ dānavān svāṃśca rakṣituṃ kārtikecchayā \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. In the meantime Kālī went to the battle ground again at the request of Kārttikeya to devour the Dānavas and to protect her own people.

## \|\| 6.37.44 \|\|

*vīrāstāmanujagmuśca te ca nandīśvarādayaḥ \|*  
*sarve devāśca gaṃdharvā yakṣā rakṣāṃsi pannagāḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Nandīśvara and other heroes, the gods, Gandharvas, Yakṣas, Rākṣasas and serpents followed her.

## \|\| 6.37.45 \|\|

*vādyabhāṃḍāśca bahuśaśśataśo madhuvāhakāḥ \|*  
*punaḥ samudyatāścāsan vīrā ubhayato'khilāḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Drum-bearers and wine-carriers accompanied them in hundreds. Heroic warriors on either side were active again.

## Chapter 38 - Kālī fights

## \|\| 6.38.1 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*sā ca gatvā hi saṃgrāmaṃ siṃhanādaṃ cakāra ha \|*  
*devyāśca tena nādena mūrcchāmāpuśca dānavāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

1\. Going to the battle ground, the goddess Kālī roared like a lion. On hearing that the Dānavas fainted.

## \|\| 6.38.2 \|\|

*aṭṭāṭṭahāsamaśivaṃ cakāra ca punaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*tadā papau ca mādhvīkaṃ nanarta raṇamūrddhani \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. She laughed boisterously again and again boding ill to the Asuras. She drank the distilled grapewine and danced on the battle ground.

## \|\| 6.38.3 \|\|

*ugradaṃṣṭrā cogradaṃḍā koṭavī ca papau madhu \|*  
*anyāśca devyastatrājau nanṛturmadhu saṃpapuḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The manifestations of Durgā viz—Ugradaṃṣṭrā (one with fierce fangs) Ugradaṇḍā (one with fierce baton) and Kotavī (the naked) danced on the battle ground and drank wine.

## \|\| 6.38.4 \|\|

*mahān kolāhalo jāto gaṇadevadale tadā \|*  
*jahṛṣurbahugarjaṃtassarve suragaṇādayaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. There was great tumult on the side of the Gaṇas and the gods. All the gods and the Gaṇas roared and rejoiced.

## \|\| 6.38.5 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā kālīṃ śaṃkhacūḍaśśīghramājau samāyayau \|*  
*dānavāśca bhayaṃ prāptā rājā tebhyo'bhayaṃ dadau \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. On seeing Kālī, Śaṅkhacūḍa hastened to the battle ground. The Dānavas were frightened but the king Śaṅkhacūḍa assured them of protection.

## \|\| 6.38.6 \|\|

*kālī cikṣepa vahniṃ ca pralayāgniśikhopamam \|*  
*rājā jaghāna taṃ śīghraṃ vaiṣṇavāṃkitalīlayā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Kālī hurled fire as fierce as the flame of dissolution which the king put out sportively by means of Vaiṣṇava missiles.

## \|\| 6.38.7 \|\|

*nārāyaṇāstraṃ sā devī cikṣepa taduparyaram \|*  
*vṛddhiṃ jagāma tacchastraṃ dṛṣṭvā vāmaṃ ca dānavam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Immediately the goddess hurled the Nārāyaṇa missile at him. The missile developed its power on seeing the Dānava Śaṅkhacūḍa.

## \|\| 6.38.8 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā śaṃkhacūḍaśca pralayāgniśikhopamam \|*  
*papāta daṃḍavadbhūmau praṇanāma punaḥpunaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. On realising it as fierce as the flame of fire of dissolution, the Dānava Śaṅkhacūḍa fell flat on the ground and bowed again and again.

## \|\| 6.38.9 \|\|

*nivṛttiṃ prāpa tacchstraṃ dṛṣṭvā namraṃ ca dānavam \|*  
*brahmāstramatha sā devī cikṣepa maṃtrapūrvakam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. On seeing the Dānava humbled the missile turned away. Then the goddess hurled the Brahmā missile with due invocation through the mantra.

## \|\| 6.38.10 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā prajjvalaṃtaṃ ca praṇamya bhuvi saṃsthitaḥ \|*  
*brahmāstreṇa dānavendro vinivāraṃ cakāra ha \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. On seeing the missile blazing he bowed and fell on the ground. The leader of the Dānavas thus prevented the Brahmā missile from attacking him.

## \|\| 6.38.11 \|\|

*atha kruddho dānavendro dhanurākṛṣya raṃhasā \|*  
*cikṣepa divyānyastrāṇi devyai vai maṃtrapūrvakam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Then the infuriated leader of the Dānavas drew the bow violently and discharged divine missiles at the goddess with due invocation through the mantras.

## \|\| 6.38.12 \|\|

*āhāraṃ samare cakre prasārya mukhamāyatam \|*  
*jagarja sāṭṭahāsaṃ ca dānavā bhayamāyayuḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Opening the mouth very wide she swallowed the missiles and roared with a boisterous laugh. The Dānavas were terrified.

## \|\| 6.38.13 \|\|

*kālyai cikṣepa śaktiṃ sa śatayojanamāyatām \|*  
*devī divyāstrajālena śatakhaṃḍaṃ cakāra sā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. He then hurled a Śakti, a hundred Yojanas long at Kālī. By means of divine missiles she broke it into a hundred pieces.

## \|\| 6.38.14 \|\|

*sa ca vaiṣṇavamastraṃ ca cikṣepa caṃḍikopari \|*  
*māheśvareṇa kālī ca vinivāraṃ cakāra sā \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. He hurled the Vaiṣṇava missile on Kālī. She blocked it with the Māheśvara missile.

## \|\| 6.38.15 \|\|

*evaṃ cirataraṃ yuddhamanyonyaṃ saṃbabhūva ha \|*  
*prekṣakā abhavansarve devāśca dānavā api \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Thus the mutual combat went on for a long time. All the gods and Dānavas stood as mere onlookers.

## \|\| 6.38.16 \|\|

*atha kuddhā mahādevī kālī kālasamā raṇe \|*  
*jagrāha mantrapūtaṃ ca śaraṃ pāśupataṃ ruṣā \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Then the infuriated goddess Kālī, as fierce as the god of death on the battleground, took up angrily the Pāśupata arrow sanctified by mantras.

## \|\| 6.38.17 \|\|

*kṣepātpūrvaṃ tanniṣeddhuṃ vāgbabhūvāśarīriṇī \|*  
*na kṣipāstramidaṃ devi śaṃkhacūḍāya vai ruṣā \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. In order to prevent it from being hurled, an unembodied celestial voice said—“0 goddess, do not hurl this missile angrily at Śaṇkhacūḍa.”

## \|\| 6.38.18 \|\|

*mṛtyuḥ pāśupatānnāstyamoghādapi ca caṃḍike \|*  
*śaṃkhacūḍasya vīrasyopāyamanyaṃ vicāraya \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. “O Caṇḍikā, death of this Dānava will not take place even through the never failing Pāsupata missile. Think of some other means for slaying this warrior Śaṅkhacūḍa.”

## \|\| 6.38.19 \|\|

*ityākarṇya bhadrakālī na cikṣepa tadastrakam \|*  
*śatalakṣaṃ dānavānāṃ jaghāsa līlayā kṣudhā \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. On hearing this, Bhadrakālī did not hurl the missile. Sportively she devoured ten million Dānavas as if in hunger.

## \|\| 6.38.20 \|\|

*attuṃ jagāma vegena śaṃkhacūḍaṃ bhayaṃkarī \|*  
*divyāstreṇa ca raudreṇa vārayāmāsa dānavaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. The terrible goddess rushed at Śaṅkhacūḍa to devour him. The Dānava prevented her by means of the divine missile of Rudra.

## \|\| 6.38.21 \|\|

*atha kruddho dānavendraḥ khaḍgaṃ cikṣepa satvaram \|*  
*grīṣmasūryopamaṃ tīkṣṇadhāramatyaṃtabhīkaram \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Then the infuriated leader of the Dānavas hurled a sword, as fierce as the summer sun, with sharp and terrific edge.

## \|\| 6.38.22 \|\|

*sā kālī taṃ samālokyāyāṃtaṃ prajvalitaṃ ruṣā \|*  
*prasārya mukhamāhāraṃ cakre tasya ca paśyataḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. On seeing the blazing sword approaching, Kālī furiously opened her mouth and swallowed it even as Śaṅkhacūḍa stood watching.

## \|\| 6.38.23 \|\|

*divyānyastrāṇi cānyāni ciccheda dānaveśvaraḥ \|*  
*prāptāni pūrvataścakre śatakhaṃḍāni tāni ca \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. The lord of Dānavas hurled many divine missiles but before they reached her she broke them into hundreds of pieces.

## \|\| 6.38.24 \|\|

*punarattuṃ mahādevī vegatastaṃ jagāma ha \|*  
*sarvasiddheśvaraḥ śrīmānaṃtardhānaṃ cakāra saḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Again the great goddess rushed at him in order to devour him. But that glorious Dānava, leader of all Siddhas vanished from sight.

## \|\| 6.38.25 \|\|

*vegena muṣṭinā kālī tamadṛṣṭvā ca dānavam \|*  
*babhaṃja ca rathaṃ tasya jaghāna kila sārathim \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Thus unable to see him, Kālī who rushed with great velocity crushed his chariot and killed the charioteer with her fist.

## \|\| 6.38.26 \|\|

*athāgatya drutaṃ māyī cakraṃ cikṣepa vegataḥ \|*  
*bhadrakālyai śaṃkhacūḍaḥ pralayāgniśikho pamam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Then Śaṅkhacūḍa, an expert in using deception returned quickly and forcefully hurled the wheel blazing like the flame of fire of dissolution, at Bhadrakāli.

## \|\| 6.38.27 \|\|

*sā devī taṃ tadā cakraṃ vāmahastena līlayā \|*  
*jagrāha svamukhenaivāhāraṃ cakre ruṣā drutam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. The goddess sportively caught hold of the wheel with her left hand and immediately swallowed it.

## \|\| 6.38.28 \|\|

*muṣṭyā jaghāna taṃ devī mahākopena vegataḥ \|*  
*babhrāma dānavendropi kṣaṇaṃ mūrcchāmavāpa saḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. The goddess then hit him with her fist forcefully and angrily. The king of Dānavas whirled round and fainted for a short while.

## \|\| 6.38.29 \|\|

*kṣaṇena cetanāṃ prāpya sa cottasthau pratāpavān \|*  
*na cakre bāhu yuddhaṃ ca mātṛbuddhyā tayā saha \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Immediately the Dānava regained consciousness and got up valorously. He did not fight her with his arms by the thought that she was a woman like his mother.

## \|\| 6.38.30 \|\|

*gṛhītvā dānavaṃ devī bhrāmayitvā punaḥpunaḥ \|*  
*ūrddhvaṃ ca prāpayāmāsa mahākopena vegataḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. The goddess seized the Dānava, whirled him again and again and tossed him up with great anger and velocity.

## \|\| 6.38.31 \|\|

*utpapāta ca vegena śaṃkhacūḍaḥ pratāpavān \|*  
*nipatya ca samuttasthā praṇamya bhadrakālikām \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. The valorous Śaṅkhacūḍa fell down after being tossed up very high. He got up and bowed down to Bhadrakālī.

## \|\| 6.38.32 \|\|

*ratnendrasāranirmāṇavimānaṃ sumano haram \|*  
*āruroha sa hṛṣṭātmā na bhrāntopi mahāraṇe \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Highly delighted thereafter, he got into a beautiful aerial chariot of exquisite workmanship set with gems and did not lose the balance of his mind in the battlefield.

## \|\| 6.38.33 \|\|

*dānavānāṃ hi kṣatajaṃ sā papau kālikā kṣudhā \|*  
*etasminnaṃtare tatra vāgvabhūvāśarīriṇī \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Hungrily Kālī drank the blood of the Dānavas. In the meantime an unembodied celestial voice said:

## \|\| 6.38.34 \|\|

*lakṣaṃ ca dānavendrāṇāmavaśiṣṭaṃ raṇe'dhunā \|*  
*uddhataṃ guñjatāṃ sārddhaṃ tatastvaṃ bhuṃkṣva ceśvari \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. O goddess, a hundred thousand haughty leading Dānavas have been left out in the battle still roaring. Devour them quickly.

## \|\| 6.38.35 \|\|

*saṃgrāme dānavendraṃ ca haṃtuṃ na kuru mānasam \|*  
*avadhyoyaṃ śaṃkhacūḍastava devīti niścayam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Do not think of slaying the king of Dānavas. O goddess, Śaṅkhacūḍa cannot be killed by you. It is certain.

## \|\| 6.38.36-37 \|\|

*tacchutvā vacanaṃ devī niḥsṛtaṃ vyomamaṃḍalāt \|*  
*dānavānāṃ bahūnāṃ ca māṃsaṃ ca rudhiraṃ tathā \|\| 36 \|\|*

*bhuktvā pītvā bhadrakālī śaṃkarāṃtikamāyayau \|*  
*uvāca raṇavṛttāṃtaṃ paurvāparyeṇa sakramam \|\| 37 \|\|*

36-37. On hearing these words from the firmament, Bhadrakālī drank the blood and devoured the flesh of many Dānavas and went near Śiva. She then narrated to him the events of the war in the proper order.

## Chapter 39 - The annihilation of the army of Śaṅkhacūḍa

## \|\| 6.39.1 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*śrutvā kālyuktamīśāno kiṃ cakāra kimuktavān \|*  
*tattvaṃ vada mahāprājña paraṃ kautūhalaṃ mama \|\| 1 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:—

1\. O intelligent one, on hearing the narrative of Kālī what did Śiva say? What did he do? Please narrate to me. I am eager to know it.

## \|\| 6.39.2 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*kālyuktaṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā śaṃkaraḥ parameśvaraḥ \|*  
*mahālīlākaraśśaṃbhurjahāsāśvāsayañca tām \|\| 2 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

2\. On hearing the words of Kālī, lord Śiva, the actor of great divine sports, laughed. Śiva consoled her.

## \|\| 6.39.3 \|\|

*vyomavāṇīṃ samākarṇya tattvajñānaviśāradaḥ \|*  
*yayau svayaṃ ca samare svagaṇaissaha śaṃkaraḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. On hearing the celestial voice, Śiva, an expert in the knowledge of principles, went himself to the battle along with his Gaṇas.

## \|\| 6.39.4 \|\|

*mahāvṛṣabhamārūḍho vīrabhadrādisaṃyutaḥ \|*  
*bhairavaiḥ kṣetrapālaiśca svasamānaissamanvitaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. He was seated on his great bull and surrounded by Vīrabhadra and others, the Bhairavas and the Kṣetrapālas all equal in valour to him.

## \|\| 6.39.5 \|\|

*raṇaṃ prāpto maheśaśca vīrarūpaṃ vidhāya ca \|*  
*virarājādhikaṃ tatra rudro mūrta ivāṃtakaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Assuming a heroic form, lord Śiva entered the battle ground. There Śiva shone well as the embodied form of the annihilator.

## \|\| 6.39.6 \|\|

*śaṃkhacūḍaśśivaṃ dṛṣṭvā vimānādavaruhya saḥ \|*  
*nanāma parayā bhaktyā śirasā daṃḍavadbhuvi \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. On seeing Śiva, Śaṅkhacūḍa got down from the aerial chariot, bowed with great devotion and fell flat on the ground.

## \|\| 6.39.7 \|\|

*taṃ praṇamya tu yogena vimānamāruroha saḥ \|*  
*tūrṇaṃ cakāra sannāhaṃ dhanurjagrāha seṣukam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. After bowing to him he immediately got into his chariot. He speedily prepared for the fight and seized the bow and the arrows.

## \|\| 6.39.8 \|\|

*śivadānavayoryuddhaṃ śatamabdaṃ babhūva ha \|*  
*bāṇavarṣamivograṃ tadvarṣatormoghayostadā \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The fight between Śiva and the Dānava went on for a hundred years and they showered arrows fiercely like clouds pouring down incessantly.

## \|\| 6.39.9 \|\|

*śaṃkhacūḍo mahāvīraśśarāṃścikṣepa dāruṇān \|*  
*ciccheda śaṃkarastānvai līlayā svaśarotkaraiḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The heroic Śaṅkhacūḍa discharged terrible arrows playfully. Śiva split all of them by means of his arrows.

## \|\| 6.39.10 \|\|

*tadaṃgeṣu ca śastroghaistāḍayāmāsa kopataḥ \|*  
*mahārudro virūpākṣo duṣṭadaṇḍassatāṃ gati \|\| 10 \|\|*

1 0. Mahārudra, the odd-eyed Śiva, the punisher of the wicked and the goal of the good, angrily hit his limbs with various weapons.

## \|\| 6.39.11 \|\|

*dānavo niśitaṃ khaḍgaṃ carma cādāya vegavān \|*  
*vṛṣaṃ jaghāna śirasi śivasya varavāhanam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Taking up his sharp sword and the leather shield the Dānava rushed at the sacred bull of Śiva and hit it on its head.

## \|\| 6.39.12 \|\|

*tāḍite vāhane rudrastaṃ kṣurapreṇa līlayā \|*  
*khaḍgaṃ ciccheda tasyāśu carma cāpi mahojjvalam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. When his bull was hit, Śiva sportively cut off the sword and the shining shield by means of his Kṣurapra.

## \|\| 6.39.13 \|\|

*chinne'sau carmaṇi tadā śaktiṃ cikṣepa so'suraḥ \|*  
*dvidhā cakre svabāṇena harastāṃ saṃmukhāgatām \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. When the shield was split, the Asura hurled his spear. Śiva split it into two with his arrow as it came before him.

## \|\| 6.39.14 \|\|

*kopādhmātaśśaṃkhacūḍaścakraṃ cikṣepa dānavaḥ \|*  
*muṣṭipātena taccāpyacūrṇayatsahasā haraḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The infuriated Dānava, Śaṅkhacūḍa hurled a discus. Immediately Śiva smashed it into pieces with his fist.

## \|\| 6.39.15 \|\|

*gadāmāvidhya tarasā saṃcikṣepa haraṃ prati \|*  
*śaṃbhunā sāpi sahasā bhinnā bhasmatvamāgatā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. He hurled his club with force at Śiva. Rapidly split by Śiva, the club was reduced to ashes.

## \|\| 6.39.16 \|\|

*tataḥ paraśumādāya hastena dānaveśvaraḥ \|*  
*dhāvati sma haraṃ vegācchaṃkhacūḍaḥ krudhākulaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Then seizing an axe with his hand, the infuriated king of Dānavas, Śaṅkhacūḍa rushed at Śiva.

## \|\| 6.39.17 \|\|

*samāhṛtya svabāṇaughairapātayata śaṃkaraḥ \|*  
*drutaṃ paraśuhastaṃ taṃ bhūtale līlayāsuram \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. By the volley of his arrows Śiva sportively struck the Asura with axe in his hand.

## \|\| 6.39.18 \|\|

*tataḥ kṣaṇena saṃprāpya saṃjñāmāruhya sadratham \|*  
*dhṛtadivyāyudhaśaro babhau vyāpyākhilaṃ nabhaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The Dānava quickly regained consciousness and got into his excellent chariot. With divine weapons and arrows he encompassed the whole sky and shone.

## \|\| 6.39.19 \|\|

*āyāṃtaṃ taṃ nirīkṣyaiva ḍamarudhvani mādarāt \|*  
*cakāra jyāravaṃ cāpi dhanuṣo dussahaṃ hara \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. On seeing him coming on, Śiva sounded his Ḍamaru enthusiastically and twanged the bowstring, the noise whereof was unbearable.

## \|\| 6.39.20 \|\|

*pūrayāmāsa kakubhaḥ śṛṃganādena ca prabhuḥ \|*  
*svayaṃ jagarja giriśastrāsayannasurāṃstadā \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. The lord filled all the quarters with the sound of his horn. Śiva himself roared then, frightening the Asuras.

## \|\| 6.39.21 \|\|

*tyājitebha mahāgarvairmahānādairvṛṣeśvaraḥ \|*  
*pūrayāmāsa sahasā khaṃ gāṃ vasudiśastathā \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. The lordly bull then bellowed putting the haughty trumpeting elephants to shame. The deep roar filled the sky, the earth and the eight quarters.

## \|\| 6.39.22 \|\|

*mahākālassamutpatyā tāḍayadgāṃ tathā nabhaḥ \|*  
*karābhyāṃ tanninādena kṣiptā āsanpurāravāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. With his hands the fierce lord Śiva clapped the earth and the sky. All the previous shouts and roars were surpassed by that sound.

## \|\| 6.39.23 \|\|

*aṭṭāṭṭahāsamaśivaṃ kṣetrapālaścakāra ha \|*  
*bhairavo'pi mahānādaṃ sa cakāra mahāhave \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. The Kṣetrapāla produced a boisterous laughing sound boding ill to the Asuras. In that great battle Bhairava too roared.

## \|\| 6.39.24 \|\|

*mahākolāhalo jāto raṇamadhye bhayaṃkaraḥ \|*  
*vīraśabdo babhūvātha gaṇamadhye samaṃtataḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. There was a terrific tumult in the midst of that battle. All round amongst the Gaṇas, the shouts of heroes rose up.

## \|\| 6.39.25 \|\|

*saṃtresurdānavāssarve taiśśabdairbhayadaiḥ kharaiḥ \|*  
*cukopātīva tacchrutvā dānavendro mahābalaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The Dānavas were frightened by those harsh and terrible sounds. On hearing them the powerful king of Dānavas became very furious.

## \|\| 6.39.26 \|\|

*tiṣṭhatiṣṭheti duṣṭātmanvyājahāra yadā haraḥ \|*  
*devairgaṇaiśca taiḥ śīghramuktaṃ jaya jayeti ca \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. When Śiva shouted “O wicked one, stay by. Stay by”, the gods and the Gaṇas rapidly shouted “victory, Victory”.

## \|\| 6.39.27 \|\|

*athāgatya sa daṃbhasya tanayassupratāpavān \|*  
*śaktiṃ cikṣepa rudrāya jvālāmālātibhīṣaṇām \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Then coming again the valorous son of Dambha hurled at Rudra his spear terrible with shooting flames.

## \|\| 6.39.28 \|\|

*vahnikūṭaprabhā yāṃtī kṣetrapālena satvaram \|*  
*nirastāgatya sājau vai mukhotpannamaholkayā \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. While it came on, blazing brilliantly like a great conflagration in the battleground, it was immediately suppressed by Kṣeṭrapāla by means of the meteor springing from his mouth.

## \|\| 6.39.29 \|\|

*punaḥ pravavṛte yuddhaṃ śivadānavayormahat \|*  
*cakaṃpe dharaṇī dyauśca sanagābdhijalāśayā \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Again the great battle between Śiva and the Dānava was resumed. The heaven and the earth including all mountains, oceans and rivers shook and trembled.

## \|\| 6.39.30 \|\|

*dāṃbhimuktāccharāñśaṃbhuśśarāṃstatprahitānsa ca \|*  
*sahasraśaśśarairugraiściccheda śataśastadā \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Śiva split up the arrows discharged by the son of Dambha by means of hundred and thousands of his fierce arrows. Similarly the arrows of Śiva were split up by the Dānava.

## \|\| 6.39.31 \|\|

*tataśśaṃbhustriśūlena saṃkuddhastaṃ jaghāna ha \|*  
*tatprahāramasahyāśu kau papāta sa mūrcchitaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Then the infuriated Śiva hit him with his trident. Unable to bear that blow he fell unconscious on the ground.

## \|\| 6.39.32 \|\|

*tataḥ kṣaṇena saṃprāpa saṃjñāṃ sa ca tadāsuraḥ \|*  
*ājaghāna śarai rudraṃ tānsarvānāttakārmukaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. The Asura regained consciousness rapidly. He seized his bow and hit Rudra and all others by means of his arrows.

## \|\| 6.39.33 \|\|

*bāhūnāgayutaṃ kṛtvā chādayāmāsa śaṃkaram \|*  
*cakrāyutena sahasā śaṃkhacūḍaḥ pratāpavān \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The valorous Saṅkhacūḍa assumed ten thousand arms by means of magic and rapidly enveloped Śiva by means of ten thousand discuses.

## \|\| 6.39.34 \|\|

*tato durgāpatiḥ kruddho rudro durgārtināśanaḥ \|*  
*tāni cakrāṇi ciccheda svaśarairuttamai drutam \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Then Śiva, the infuriated consort of Durgā, the destroyer of all insurmountable distress split the discuses rapidly by means of his excellent arrows.

## \|\| 6.39.35 \|\|

*tato vegena sahasā gadāmādāya dānavaḥ \|*  
*abhyadhāvata vai haṃtuṃ bahusenāvṛto haram \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Then the Dānava seized his mace and accompanied by a huge army rushed at Śiva with the intention to kill him.

## \|\| 6.39.36 \|\|

*gadāṃ ciccheda tasyāśvāpatataḥ so'sinā haraḥ \|*  
*śitadhāreṇa saṃkruddho duṣṭagarvāpahārakaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. The infuriated Śiva, the destroyer of the pride of the wicked split the mace of the Dānava rushing headlong by means of a sharp-edged sword.

## \|\| 6.39.37 \|\|

*chinnāyāṃ svagadāyāṃ ca cukopātīva dānavaḥ \|*  
*śūlaṃ jagrāha tejasvī pareṣāṃ dussahaṃ jvalat \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. When the mace was split, the Dānava became very furious. The brilliant Dānava took up a spear that blazed unbearable to the enemies.

## \|\| 6.39.38 \|\|

*sudarśanaṃ śūlahastamāyāṃte dānaveśvaram \|*  
*svatriśūlena vivyādha hṛdi taṃ vegato haraḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. By means of his trident śiva hit the comely king of Dānavas rapidly in the chest even as he approached with the spear in his hand.

## \|\| 6.39.39 \|\|

*triśūlabhinnahṛdayānniṣkrāṃtaḥ puruṣaḥ paraḥ \|*  
*tiṣṭhatiṣṭheti covāca śaṃkhacūḍasya vīryavān \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. From the chest of Śaṅkhacūḍa pierced by the trident, a valorous huge being came out and said “Stand by, Stand by”.

## \|\| 6.39.40 \|\|

*niṣkrāmato hi tasyāśu prahasya svanavattataḥ \|*  
*ciccheda ca śiro bhīma masināso'patadbhuvi \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Laughing noisily Śiva severed the terrible head of the being that was coming out, by means of a sword. He fell on the ground.

## \|\| 6.39.41 \|\|

*tataḥ kālīṃ cakhādograṃ daṃṣṭrākṣuṇṇaśirodharān \|*  
*asurāṃstān bahūn krodhāt prasārya svamukhaṃ tadā \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Then spreading her mouth wide open Kālī furiously devoured innumerable Asuras whose heads were crushed by her fierce fangs.

## \|\| 6.39.42 \|\|

*kṣetrapālaścakhādānyānbahūndaityānkrudhākulaḥ \|*  
*kecinneśurbhairavāstracchinnā bhinnāstathāpare \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. The excited and infuriated Kṣetrapāla devoured many other Daityas. Some were killed struck down by Bhairava’s missiles. Others were wounded.

## \|\| 6.39.43 \|\|

*vīrabhadro'parāndhīmānbahūn krodhādanāśayat \|*  
*nandīśvaro jaghānānyānbahūnamaramardakān \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Vīrabhadra furiously destroyed many other heroes. Nandīśvara killed many other demons.

## \|\| 6.39.44 \|\|

*evaṃ bahugaṇā vīrāstadā saṃnahya kopataḥ \|*  
*vyanāśayanbahūndaityānasurān deva mardakān \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Thus the other Gaṇas, readily prepared and furiously heroic, destroyed many Daityas, Asuras and suppressors of the gods.

## \|\| 6.39.45 \|\|

*itthaṃ bahutaraṃ tatra tasya sainyaṃ nanāśa tat \|*  
*vidrutāścāpare vīrā bahavo bhayakātarāḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Thus a major portion of his army was destroyed there. Many other soldiers, cowardly and terrified, fled.

## Chapter 40 - Śaṅkhacūḍa is slain

## \|\| 6.40.1 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*svabalaṃ nihataṃ dṛṣṭvā mukhyaṃ bahutaraṃ tataḥ \|*  
*tathā vīrān prāṇasamān cukopātīva dānavaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

1\. On seeing the important and major portion of his army killed, including heroes as dear to him as his life, the Dānava became very furious.

## \|\| 6.40.2 \|\|

*uvāca vacanaṃ śaṃbhuṃ tiṣṭhāmyājau sthiro bhava \|*  
*kimetairnihatairmedya saṃmukhe samaraṃ kuru \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. He spoke to Śiva. “I am here standing ready. Be steady in the battle. What is it to me, if these are killed? Fight me standing face to face”.

## \|\| 6.40.3 \|\|

*ityuktvā dānavendrosau sannaddhassamare mune \|*  
*agacchanniścayaṃ kṛtvā'bhimukhaṃ śaṃkarasya ca \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. O sage, after saying this and resolving resolutely the king of Dānavas stood ready facing Śiva.

## \|\| 6.40.4 \|\|

*divyānyastrāṇi cikṣepa mahārudrāya dānavaḥ \|*  
*cakāra śaravṛṣṭiñca toyavṛṣṭiṃ yathā ghanaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The Dānava hurled divine missiles at him and showered arrows like the cloud pouring rain.

## \|\| 6.40.5 \|\|

*māyāścakāra vividhā adṛśyā bhayadarśitāḥ \|*  
*apratarkyāḥ suragaṇairnikhilairapiḥ sattamaiḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. He exhibited various kinds of deceptive measures invisible and inscrutable to all the excellent gods and Gaṇas and terrifying as well.

## \|\| 6.40.6 \|\|

*tā dṛṣṭvā śaṃkarastatra cikṣe pāstraṃ ca līlayā \|*  
*māheśvaraṃ mahādivyaṃ sarvamāyāvināśanam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. On seeing that, Śiva sportively discharged thereat the excessively divine Māheśvara missiles that destroy all illusions.

## \|\| 6.40.7 \|\|

*tejasā tasya tanmāyā naṣṭāścāsan drutaṃ tadā \|*  
*divyānyastrāṇi tānyeva nistejāṃsyabhavannapi \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. All the illusions, were quelled rapidly by its brilliance. Though they were divine missiles they became divested of their brilliance.

## \|\| 6.40.8 \|\|

*atha yuddhe maheśānastadvadhāya mahābalaḥ \|*  
*śūlaṃ jagrāha sahasā durnivāryaṃ sutejasām \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Then in the battle, the powerful lord Śiva suddenly seized his trident which could not be withstood even by brilliant persons, in order to slay him.

## \|\| 6.40.9 \|\|

*tadaiva tanniṣeddhuṃ ca vāgbabhūvāśarīriṇī \|*  
*kṣipa śūlaṃ na cedānīṃ prārthanāṃ śṛṇu śaṃkara \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. In order to prevent him then, an unembodied celestial voice said—“O Śiva, do not hurl the trident now. Please listen to this request.

## \|\| 6.40.10 \|\|

*sarvathā tvaṃ samartho hi kṣaṇād brahmāṇḍanāśane \|*  
*kimekadānavasyeśa śaṅkhacūḍasya sāṃpratam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. O Śiva, by all means, you are competent to destroy the entire universe in a trice. What doubt then in regard to a single Dānava Śaṅkhacūḍa?

## \|\| 6.40.11 \|\|

*tathāpi vedamaryādā na nāśyā svāminā tvayā \|*  
*tāṃ śṛṇuṣva mahādeva saphalaṃ kuru satyataḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Still, the limit imposed by the Vedas should not be disregarded by you, the lord. O great god, listen to that. Make it truthful and fruitful.

## \|\| 6.40.12-13 \|\|

*yāvadasya kare'tyugraṃ kavacaṃ paramaṃ hareḥ \|*  
*yāvatsatītvamastyeva satyā asya hi yoṣitaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*tāvadasya jarāmṛtyuśśaṃkhacūḍasya śaṃkara \|*  
*nāstītyavitathaṃ nātha vidhehi brahmaṇo vacaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. O lord Śiva, it has been mentioned by Brahmā, that, as long as he wears the armour of Viṣṇu and as long as his wife maintains the marital fidelity, Śaṅkhacūḍa has neither death nor old age. Please make those words truthful.’

## \|\| 6.40.14 \|\|

*ityākarṇya nabhovāṇīṃ tathetyukte hare tadā \|*  
*harecchayāgato viṣṇustaṃ dideśa satāṃ gatiḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. On hearing this celestial voice, Śiva said “So be it”. Viṣṇu came there at the wish of Śiva. Śiva, who is the goal of the good, commanded him.

## \|\| 6.40.15 \|\|

*vṛddhabrāhmaṇaveṣeṇa viṣṇurmāyāvināṃ varaḥ \|*  
*śaṅkhacūḍopakaṃṭhaṃ ca gatvovāca sa taṃ tadā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Then, in the guise of an old brahmin, Viṣṇu, the foremost of those who wield magic, approached Śaṅkhacūḍa and told him.

## \|\| 6.40.16-17 \|\|

*vṛddhabrāhmaṇa uvāca \|*  
*dehi bhikṣāṃ dānavendra mahyaṃ prāptāya sāṃpratam \|\| 16 \|\|*

*nedānīṃ kathayiṣyāmi prakaṭaṃ dīnavatsalam \|*  
*paścāttvāṃ kathayiṣyāmi punassatyaṃ kariṣyasi \|\| 17 \|\|*

The aged brahmin said:—

16-17. “O lord of Dānavas, give me the alms for

which I have come to you. I shall not say openly what I wish to have from you who are favourably disposed to the distressed. I shall tell you when you have promised me first.

## \|\| 6.40.18 \|\|

*omityuvāca rājendraḥ prasannavadanekṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*kavacārthī janaścāhamityuvāceti sacchalāt \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. With face and eyes indicating pleasure the king replied affirmatively. Then the deceptive Viṣṇu in the form of a brahmin said—“I am the suppliant for your armour.”

## \|\| 6.40.19 \|\|

*tacchrutvā dānavendrosau brahmaṇyaḥ satyavāgvibhuḥ \|*  
*taddadau kavacaṃ divyaṃ viprāya prāṇasaṃmatam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. On hearing that, the lord of Dānavas, a well wisher of the brahmins and of truthful word handed over the divine armour, his vital breath, to the brahmin.

## \|\| 6.40.20 \|\|

*māyāyetthaṃ tu kavacaṃ tasmājjagrāha vai hariḥ \|*  
*śaṅkhacūḍasya rūpeṇa jagāma tulasīṃ prati \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Viṣṇu thus snatched off his armour by means of deception. Then in the guise of Śaṅkhacūḍa Viṣṇu approached Tulasī.

## \|\| 6.40.21 \|\|

*gatvā tatra haristasyā yonau māyāviśāradaḥ \|*  
*vīryādhānaṃ cakārāśu devakāryārthamīśvaraḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Lord Viṣṇu, an expert in wielding magic went there and deposited his semen in her vaginal passage for the protection of gods.

## \|\| 6.40.22 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare śaṃbhumīrayan svavacaḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*śaṃkhacūḍavadhārthāya śūlaṃ jagrāha prajvalat \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. In the meantime the lord of Dānavas approached Śiva without the armour. He took up his trident that blazed to slay Śaṅkhacūḍa.

## \|\| 6.40.23 \|\|

*tacchūlaṃ vijayaṃ nāma śaṅkarasya paramātmanaḥ \|*  
*sañcakāśe diśassarvā rodasī saṃprakāśayan \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. That trident, named Vijaya, of Śiva, the great Ātman, shone illuminating heaven and earth.

## \|\| 6.40.24 \|\|

*koṭimadhyāhnamārtaṃḍapralayāgniśikhopamam \|*  
*durnivāryaṃ ca durddharṣamavyarthaṃ vairighātakam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. It was as refulgent as a crore midday suns and as fierce as the shooting flame of fire at the time of dissolution. It could neither be prevented nor withstood. It was never ineffective in destroying enemies.

## \|\| 6.40.25 \|\|

*tejasāṃ cakramatyugraṃ sarvaśastrāstrasāyakam \|*  
*surāsurāṇāṃ sarveṣāṃ dussahaṃ ca bhayaṃkaram \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. It had a fierce halo all round. It was the best of all weapons and missiles. It was unbearable to gods and Asuras. It was terrible to all.

## \|\| 6.40.26 \|\|

*saṃhartuṃ sarvabrahmāḍamavalaṃbya ca līlayā \|*  
*saṃsthitaṃ paramaṃ tatra ekatrībhūya vijvalat \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. In order to annihilate the whole cosmos sportively all brilliance had converged into it.

## \|\| 6.40.27 \|\|

*dhanussahasraṃ dīrgheṇa prasthena śatahastakam \|*  
*jīvabrahmāsvarūpaṃ ca nityarūpamanirmitam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. It was a thousand Dhanus in length and a hundred Hastas in width. It was in the form of individual as well as universal soul. It was eternal and uncreated.

## \|\| 6.40.28 \|\|

*vibhramad vyomni tacchūlaṃ śaṃkha cūḍopari kṣaṇāt \|*  
*cakāra bhasma tacchīghraṃ nipatya śivaśāsanāt \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. That trident whirling round over the head of Śaṅkhacūḍa for a while fell on the head of the Dānava at the behest of Śiva and reduced him to ashes.

## \|\| 6.40.29 \|\|

*atha śūlaṃ maheśasya drutamāvṛtya śaṃkarama \|*  
*yayau vihāyasā vipramanoyāyi svakāryakṛt \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. O brahmin, then it rapidly returned to Śiva and having finished its work went away by the aerial path with the speed of the mind.

## \|\| 6.40.30 \|\|

*nedurduṃdubhayassvarge jagurgaṃdharvakinnarāḥ \|*  
*tuṣṭuvurmunayo devā nanṛtuścāpsarogaṇāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. The Dundubhis were sounded in the heaven. Gandharvas and Kinnaras sang. The sages and the gods eulogised and the celestial damsels danced.

## \|\| 6.40.31 \|\|

*babhūva puṣpavṛṣṭiśca śivasyopari saṃtatam \|*  
*praśaśaṃsa harirbrahmā śakrādyā munayastathā \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. A continuous shower of flowers fell over Śiva. Viṣṇu, Brahmā, Indra, other gods and sages praised him.

## \|\| 6.40.32 \|\|

*śaṃkhacūḍo dānavendraḥ śivasya kṛpayā tadā \|*  
*śāpa mukto babhūvātha pūrvarūpamavāpa ha \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Saṅkhacūḍa the king of Dānavas was released from his curse by the favour of Śiva. He regained his original form.

## \|\| 6.40.33 \|\|

*asthibhiśśaṃkhacūḍasya śaṃkhajātirbabhūva ha \|*  
*praśastaṃ śaṃkhatoyaṃ ca sarveṣāṃ śaṃkaraṃ vinā \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. All the conches in the world are formed of the bones of Śaṅkhacūḍa. Except for Śiva, the holy water from the conch is sacred for every one.

## \|\| 6.40.34 \|\|

*viśeṣeṇa harerlakṣmyāḥ śaṃkhatoyaṃ mahāpriyam \|*  
*saṃbaṃdhināṃ ca tasyāpi na harasya mahāmune \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. O great sage, particularly to Viṣṇu and Lakṣmī the water from the conch is pleasant. To all persons connected with Viṣṇu it is so but not to Siva.

## \|\| 6.40.35 \|\|

*tamitthaṃ śaṃkaro hatvā śivalokaṃ jagāma saḥ \|*  
*suprahṛṣṭo vṛṣārūḍhaḥ somaskandagaṇairvṛtaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. After slaying him thus, Śiva went to Śivaloka seated on his bull, joyously, accompanied by Pārvatī, Kārttikeya and the Gaṇas.

## \|\| 6.40.36 \|\|

*harirjagāma vaikuṃṭhaṃ kṛṣṇassvavastho babhūva ha \|*  
*surāssvaviṣayaṃ prāpuḥ paramānandasaṃyutāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Viṣṇu went to Vaikuṇṭha. Kṛṣṇa became complacent. The gods went to their abodes with great delight.

## \|\| 6.40.37 \|\|

*jagatsvāsthyamatīvāpa sarvanirvighnamāpakam \|*  
*nirmalaṃ cābhavadvyoma kṣitissarvā sumaṃgalā \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. The universe regained normalcy. The whole earth was freed of obstacles. The sky was pure. The whole world became auspicious.

## \|\| 6.40.38 \|\|

*iti proktaṃ maheśasya caritaṃ pramudāvaham \|*  
*sarvaduḥkhaharaṃ śrīdaṃ sarvakāmaprapūrakam \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Thus I have narrated to you the delightful story of lord Śiva that removes all misery, yields wealth and fulfils cherished desires.

## \|\| 6.40.39 \|\|

*dhanyaṃ yaśasyamāyuṣyaṃ sarvavighnanivāraṇam \|*  
*bhuktidaṃ muktidaṃ caiva sarvakāmaphalapradam \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. It is conducive to prosperity and longevity. It prevents all obstacles. It yields worldly pleasure and salvation. It confers the fruits of all cherished desires.

## \|\| 6.40.40-41 \|\|

*ya idaṃ śṛṇuyānnityaṃ caritaṃ śaśimaulinaḥ \|*  
*śrāvayedvā paṭhedvāpi pāṭhayedvā sudhīrnaraḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*dhanaṃ dhānyaṃ sutaṃ saukhyaṃ labhetātra na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*sarvānkāmānavāpnoti śivabhaktiṃ viśeṣataḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

40-41. The intelligent man who hears or narrates the story of the moon-crested lord, or reads or teaches it shall undoubtedly derive wealth, grains, progeny, happiness, all desires and particularly devotion to Śiva.

## \|\| 6.40.42 \|\|

*idamākhyānamatulaṃ sarvopadravanāśanam \|*  
*paramajñānajananaṃ śivabhaktivivarddhanam \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. This narrative is unequalled. It destroys all torments. It generates great knowledge. It increases devotion to Śiva.

## \|\| 6.40.43 \|\|

*brāhmaṇo brahmavarcasvī kṣatriyo vijayī bhavet \|*  
*dhanāḍhyo vaiśyajaśśūdraśśṛṇvan sattamatāmiyāt \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. The brahmin listener attains brahminical splendour; the Kṣatriya becomes a conqueror; the Vaiśya rich and the Śūdra the most excellent of men.

## Chapter 41 - The curse of Tulasī

## \|\| 6.41.1 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*nārāyaṇaśca bhagavān vīryādhānaṃ cakāra ha \|*  
*tulasyāḥ kena yatnena yonau tadvaktumarhasi \|\| 1 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:—

1\. How did the lord Nārāyaṇa manage to deposit his semen in the vaginal passage of Tulasī? Please narrate the same.

## \|\| 6.41.2 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*nārāyaṇo hi devānāṃ kāryakartā satāṃ gatiḥ \|*  
*śaṃkhacūḍasya rūpeṇa reme tadramayā saha \|\| 2 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—
