## \|\| 6.50.22 \|\|

*udyadānaṃdasaṃdoha romāṃcācitavigrahaḥ \|*  
*praṇanāma mudā śaṃbhumaṃbho janayano dvijaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The brahmin bowed to Śiva with his eyes blooming like a lotus with pleasure and his body excited with horripilation by the surging waves of joy.

## \|\| 6.50.23 \|\|

*tuṣṭāvāṣṭatanuṃ tuṣṭaḥ praphullanayanācalaḥ \|*  
*maulāvaṃjalimādhāya vadañjayajayeti ca \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. With the palms raised and joined on the head in reverence and repeating “Victory, Victory”, the delighted sage eulogised the eight-formed Śiva with the blooming eyes.

## \|\| 6.50.24 \|\|

*bhārgava uvāca \|*  
*tvaṃ bhābhirābhirabhibhūya tamassamastamastaṃ nayasyabhimatāni niśācarāṇām \|*  
*dedīpyase divamaṇe gagane hitāya lokatrayasya jagadīśvara tannamaste \|\| 24 \|\|*

Bhārgava said:—

24\. O lord of the universe, Obeisance to you. O jewel of heaven, you shine brilliantly in the firmament for the benefit of the three worlds. With these lustrous rays you subdue all darkness and the desires of the Asuras.

## \|\| 6.50.25 \|\|

*loke'tivelamativelamahāmahobhirnirbhāsi kau ca gagane'khilalokanetraḥ \|*  
*vidrāvitākhilatamāssutamo himāṃśo pīyūṣa pūraparipūritaḥ tannamaste \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. O eye of the world, you shine in heaven, on the earth and in the sky, brilliantly lit by your excessive refulgence. You have driven away darkness. You are filled by the nectar of the moon. Obeisance to you.

## \|\| 6.50.26 \|\|

*tvaṃ pāvane pathi sadāgatirapyupāsyaḥ kastvāṃ vinā bhuvanajīvana jīvatīha \|*  
*stabdhaprabhaṃjanavivarddhi tasarvajaṃtoḥ saṃtoṣitā hi kulasarvagaḥ vai namaste \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. You are the wind, the goal in the holy path. You are worthy of being adored. O enlivener of the worlds, who can live here without you? O all-pervasive, benumber of storms, nourisher of creatures, delighter of the race of serpents, obeisance to you.

## \|\| 6.50.27 \|\|

*viśvekapāvaka na tāvakapāvakaikaśakterṛte mṛtavatāmṛtadivyakāryam \|*  
*prāṇiṣyado jagadaho jagadaṃtarātmaṃstvaṃ pāvakaḥ pratipadaṃ śamado namaste \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. O sole purifier of the universe, O protector of those who bow to you, O wielder of the power of fire, you are the fire, bestowing calmness at every step. Obeisance to you.

## \|\| 6.50.28 \|\|

*pānīyarūpa parameśa jagatpavitra citravicitrasucaritrakaro'si nūnam \|*  
*viśvaṃ pavitramamalaṃ kila viśvanātha pānīyagāhanata etadato nato'smi \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. O water-formed one, O great Īśa, the whole universe is holy. Really you make it variegated. O lord of the universe, this universe is free from dirt by diving into the water. Hence I bow to you.

## \|\| 6.50.29 \|\|

*ākāśarūpabahiraṃtarutāvakāśadānādvikasvaramiheśvara viśvametat \|*  
*tvattassadā sadaya saṃśvasiti svabhāvātsaṃkocameti bhakto'smi natastatastvām \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. O sky-formed one, because you give space within and without, that this universe evolves and expands; O merciful one, it always breathes in you and naturally merges in you Hence I bow to you.

## \|\| 6.50.30 \|\|

*viśvaṃbharātmaka bibharṣi vibhotra viśvaṃ ko viśvanātha bhavato'nyatamastamoriḥ \|*  
*sa tvaṃ vināśaya tamo tama cāhibhūṣastavyātparaḥ paraparaṃ praṇatastatastvām \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. O earth-formed one, O lord, you support and hold the universe. O lord of the universe, who else can be the enemy of darkness? You of this nature destroy my darkness. O you having serpents for ornaments, you are beyond all that deserve eulogy. Hence I bow to you. You are greater than the greatest.

## \|\| 6.50.31 \|\|

*ātmasvarūpa tava rūpaparaṃparābhirābhistataṃ hara carācararūpametat \|*  
*sarvāṃtarātmanilayapratirūparūpa nityaṃ nato'smi paramātmajano'ṣṭamūrte \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. O soul-formed one, O Śiva, this universe of the mobiles and immobiles is pervaded by these series of your forms. O eight-formed lord, having the form of the immanent soul, I always bow to you.

## \|\| 6.50.32 \|\|

*ityaṣṭamūrtibhirimābhirabaṃdhabaṃdho yuktau karoṣi khalu viśvajanīnamūrtte \|*  
*etattataṃ suvitataṃ praṇatapraṇīta sarvārthasārthaparamārtha tato nato'smi \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. O kinsman of those devoid of kinsmen, O you of the form of universe, equipped with the eight forms, you make all expand. O lord, you make all objects available to those who bow to you. Hence I bow to you.

## \|\| 6.50.33 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*aṣṭamūrtyaṣṭakenetthaṃ pariṣṭutyeti bhārgavaḥ \|*  
*bhargaṃ bhūmimilanmauliḥ praṇanāma punaḥpunaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

33\. Eulogising the eight formed Śiva by reciting the eight verses, Bhārgava touched the ground with his head and bowed again and again.

## \|\| 6.50.34-35 \|\|

*iti stuto mahādevo bhārgaveṇātitejasā \|*  
*utthāya bhūmerbāhubhyāṃ dhṛtvā taṃ praṇataṃ dvijam \|\| 34 \|\|*

*uvāca ślakṣṇayā vācā meghanādagabhīrayā \|*  
*suprītyā daśanajyotsnā pradyotitadiṃgataraḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

34-35. When he was eulogised by Bhārgava of great brilliance, the great god stood up and lifted the brahmin from the ground where he was bowing to him. Holding him up, the lord spoke in a rumbling voice like that of the cloud but gentle in effect, illuminating the quarters with the moonlight-brilliance of his teeth.

## \|\| 6.50.36-38 \|\|

*mahādeva uvāca \|*  
*vipravarya kave tāta mama bhakto'si pāvanaḥ \|*  
*anenātyugratapasā svajanyācaritena ca \|\| 36 \|\|*

*liṃgasthāpanapuṇyena liṃgasyārādhanena ca \|*  
*dattacittopahāreṇa śucinā niścalena ca \|\| 37 \|\|*

*avimuktamahākṣetrapavitrācaraṇena ca \|*  
*tvāṃ sutābhyāṃ prapaśyāmi tavādeyaṃ na kiṃcana \|\| 38 \|\|*

The great lord said:—

36-38. O excellent brahmin, O Bhārgava, O dear, you are my faithful devotee. By your severe penance in this life, by the merit of installing my phallic image, and the adoration of it, by the offerings made with concentrated devotion, your unshaken purity and holy conduct in this Avimuktakṣetra, I see you as my other two sons. There is nothing which cannot be given to you.

## \|\| 6.50.39 \|\|

*anenaiva śarīreṇa mamodaradarīgataḥ \|*  
*madvarendriyamārgeṇa putrajanmatvameṣyasi \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. With this body you shall enter the cavity of my belly and you will be born as my son through my excellent organ—the penis.

## \|\| 6.50.40 \|\|

*yacchāmyahaṃ varaṃ te'dya duṣprāpyaṃ pārṣadairapi \|*  
*harerhiraṇyagarbhācca prāyaśohaṃ jugopa yam \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. I am giving you now the boon inaccessible to even my attendants and which I have kept away even from Viṣṇu and Brahmā usually.

## \|\| 6.50.41-42 \|\|

*mṛtasaṃjīvanī nāma vidyā yā mama nirmalā \|*  
*tapobalena mahatā mayaiva parinirmitā \|\| 41 \|\|*

*tvāṃ tāṃ tu prāpayāmyadya maṃtrarūpāṃ mahāśuce \|*  
*yogyatā te'sti vidyāyāstasyāśśuci taponidhe \|\| 42 \|\|*

41-42. O pure one, O pure sage, I am giving unto you the lore in the form of Mantra, which is called Mṛtasañjīvanī. It is pure and it has been formulated by me alone through the power of the penance. You have the capacity to receive that lore.

## \|\| 6.50.43 \|\|

*yaṃyamuddiśya niyatametāmāvartayiṣyasi \|*  
*vidyāṃ vidyeśvaraśreṣṭhaṃ satyaṃ prāṇi ṣyati dhuvam \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Whoever he may be if you were to repeat this mantra in respect of anyone he will truly return to life. This lore is the most excellent one.

## \|\| 6.50.44 \|\|

*atyarkamatyagniṃ ca te tejo vyomni ca tārakam \|*  
*dedīpyamānaṃ bhavitā grahāṇāṃ pravaro bhava \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Your brilliant stellar lustre will excel the sun and fire. You will become the foremost of the planets.

## \|\| 6.50.45 \|\|

*api ca tvāṃ kariṣyaṃti yātrāṃ nāryo naro'pi vā \|*  
*teṣāṃ tvaddṛṣṭipātena sarvakāryaṃ praṇaśyati \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. If any man or woman were to proceed on a journey in your direction, their work will perish by your glance.

## \|\| 6.50.46 \|\|

*tavodaye bhaviṣyaṃti vivāhādīni suvrata \|*  
*sarvāṇi dharmakāryāṇi phalavaṃti nṛṇāmiha \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. O you of good rites, all virtuous actions like marriage etc. when performed while you rise shall be beneficent to those people.

## \|\| 6.50.47 \|\|

*sarvāśca tithayo nandāstava saṃyogataśśubhāḥ \|*  
*tava bhaktā bhaviṣyaṃti bahuśukrā bahu prajāḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. All the Nandā tithis are auspicious by your conjunction. Your devotees will be prolific in progeny and profuse in the production of semen.

## \|\| 6.50.48 \|\|

*tvayedaṃ sthāpitaṃ liṃgaṃ śukreśamiti saṃjñitam \|*  
*ye'rcayiṣyaṃti bhanujāsteṣāṃ siddhirbhaviṣyati \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. The phallic image installed by you is called Śukreśa. Those who worship it shall achieve success.

## \|\| 6.50.49-50 \|\|

*āvarṣaṃ pratighasrāṃ ye naktavrataparāyaṇāḥ \|*  
*tvaddine śukrakūpe ye kṛtasarvodakakriyāḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

*śukreśamarcayiṣyaṃti śṛṇu teṣāṃ tu yatphalam \|*  
*abaṃdhyaśukrāste martyāḥ putravaṃto'tiretasaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

49-50. Those who perform Vratas for every night throughout the year and offer water oblations in the Śukra well on your day and worship Śukresa shall derive these fruits. They will have semen unfailing and profuse in secretion. They will have sons.

## \|\| 6.50.51 \|\|

*puṃstvasaubhāgyasaṃpannā bhaviṣyaṃti na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*upetavidyāste sarve janāssyuḥ sukhabhāginaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. They will have the good fortune of manliness. There is no doubt. Those people will have good learning and enjoy happiness.

## \|\| 6.50.52 \|\|

*iti dattvā varāndevastatra liṃge layaṃ yayau \|*  
*bhārgavo'pi nijaṃ dhāma prāpa saṃtuṣṭamānasaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. After granting him boons, the lord vanished in the phallic image. The delighted Bhārgava too returned to his abode.

## \|\| 6.50.53 \|\|

*iti te kathitaṃ vyāsa yathā prāptā tapobalāt \|*  
*mṛtyuṃjayābhidhā vidyā kimanyacchrotumicchasi \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Thus O Vyāsa, I have narrated how the Mṛtyuñjaya lore was acquired by Śukra through power of penance. What else do you wish to hear?

## Chapter 51 - The story of Ūṣā

## \|\| 6.51.1-2 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*sanatkumāra sarvajña śrāvitā sukathādbhutā \|*  
*bhavatānugrahātprītyā śabhvanugrahanirbharā \|\| 1 \|\|*

*idānīṃ śrotumicchāmi caritaṃ śaśimaulinaḥ \|*  
*gāṇapatyaṃ dadau prītyā yathā bāṇāsurāya vai \|\| 2 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:—

1-2. O omniscient Sanatkumāra, a wonderfully excellent

story has been narrated with love and blessings by you. It is full of Śiva’s benediction. I wish to know more of the story of the moon-crested lord wherein he gave the Asura Bāṇa the position of the chieftain of his Gaṇas.

## \|\| 6.51.3 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu vyāsādarāttāṃ vai kathāṃ śaṃbhoḥ parātmanaḥ \|*  
*gāṇapatyaṃ yathā prītyā dadau bāṇā surāya hi \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

3\. O Vyāsa, listen with reverence to the story of Śiva, the great Ātman wherein it is explained how he bestowed the chieftainship of his Gaṇas on the Asura Bāṇa.

## \|\| 6.51.4 \|\|

*atraiva sucaritraṃ ca śaṃkarasya mahāprabhoḥ \|*  
*kṛṣṇena samaropyatra śaṃbhorbāṇānugṛhṇataḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Here is the good story of Śiva, the great lord. Here too is the story of Śiva’s fight with Kṛṣṇa when the former blessed Bāṇa.

## \|\| 6.51.5 \|\|

*atrānurūpaṃ śṛṇu me śivalīlānvitaṃ param \|*  
*itihāsaṃ mahāpuṇyaṃ manaḥśrotrasukhāvaham \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Listen from me the most befitting and the highly meritorious legend of the sports of Śiva. It is pleasing to the mind and to the ears.

## \|\| 6.51.6 \|\|

*brahmaputro marīciryo munirāsīnmahāmatiḥ \|*  
*mānasassarvaputreṣu jyeṣṭhaḥ śreṣṭhaḥ prajāpatiḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Marīci, the sage of great intellect, was the mentally created eldest son of Brahmā. He was a Prajāpati too.

## \|\| 6.51.7 \|\|

*tasya putro mahātmāsītkaśyapo munisattamaḥ \|*  
*sṛṣṭipravṛddhako'tyaṃtaṃ piturbhakto vidherapi \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. His son Kaśyapa was a noble soul. He was the most excellent of all sages. He made the creation flourish well. He was devoted to his father and to Brahmā.

## \|\| 6.51.8 \|\|

*svasya trayodaśamitādakṣakanyā ssuśīlikāḥ \|*  
*kaśyapasya munervyāsa patnyaścāsanpativratāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. O Vyāsa, thirteen daughters of Dakṣa were his wives. They were of good conduct and very faithful to their husband, the sage Kaśyapa.

## \|\| 6.51.9 \|\|

*tatra jyeṣṭhā ditiścāsīddaityāstattanayāssmṛtāḥ \|*  
*anyāsāṃ ca sutā jātā devādyāssacarācarāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The eldest of the wives was Diti. The Daityas were her sons. The gods and others including the mobile and immobile beings were born to others.

## \|\| 6.51.10 \|\|

*jyeṣṭhāyāḥ prathamau putrau diteścāstāṃ mahābalau \|*  
*hiraṇyakaśipurjyeṣṭho hiraṇyākṣo'nujastataḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The eldest Diti had the heroic sons Hiraṇyakaśipu the elder and Hiraṇyākṣa the younger.

## \|\| 6.51.11 \|\|

*hiraṇyakaśipoḥ putrāścatvāro daityasattamāḥ \|*  
*hrādānuhrādasaṃhrādā prahrādaścetyanukramāt \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Hiraṇyakaśipu had four sons. They were in order Hrāda, Anuhrāda, Saṃhrāda and Prahlāda.

## \|\| 6.51.12 \|\|

*prahrādastatra hi mahānviṣṇubhakto jitendriyaḥ \|*  
*yaṃ nāśituṃ na śaktāste'bhavandaityāśca kepi ha \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Prahlāda was a great devotee of Viṣṇu. He had full control of his sense-organs. The Daityas were unable to destroy him.

## \|\| 6.51.13 \|\|

*virocanaḥ sutastasya mahā dātṛvaro'bhavat \|*  
*śakrāya svaśiro yo'dādyācamānāya viprataḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. His son Virocana was the most excellent of donors. He gave even his head to Indra who requested for the same in the guise of a brahmin.

## \|\| 6.51.14 \|\|

*tasya putro baliścāsīnmahādānī śivapriyaḥ \|*  
*yena vāmanarūpāya haraye'dāyi medinī \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. His son was Bali who was a favourite of Śiva and a liberal donor. The earth was given by him to Viṣṇu who assumed the form of a dwarf.

## \|\| 6.51.15 \|\|

*tasyaurasaḥ suto bāṇaśśivabhakto babhūva ha \|*  
*mānyo vadānyo dhīmāṃśca satyasaṃdhassa hasradaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. His son Bāṇa became a devotee of Śiva. He was highly respected and intelligent. He was truthful and a liberal donor making thousands of charitable gifts.

## \|\| 6.51.16 \|\|

*śoṇitākhye pure sthitvā sa rājyamakarotpurā \|*  
*trailokyaṃ ca balāñjjitvā tannāthānasureśvaraḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Staying in the Śoṇita town he ruled over the three worlds after defeating several rulers forcefully.

## \|\| 6.51.17 \|\|

*tasya bāṇāsurasyaiva śivabhaktasya cāmarāḥ \|*  
*śaṃkarasya prasādena kiṃkarā iva te'bhavan \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. As a result of the grace of Śiva, the gods became the virtual servants of Bāṇa, the devotee of Śiva.

## \|\| 6.51.18-19 \|\|

*tasya rājye'marānhitvā nābhavanduḥkhitāḥ prajāḥ \|*  
*sāpatnyāduḥkhitāste hi paradharmapravartinaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*sahasrabāhuvādyena sa kadācinmahāsuraḥ \|*  
*tāṃḍavena hi nṛtyenātoṣayattaṃ maheśvaram \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. They were distressed by his enmity although he practised high virtues. In accompaniment of the instrumental music played by his thousand arms, by means of the Tāṇḍava dance he propitiated Śiva.

## \|\| 6.51.20 \|\|

*tena nṛtyena saṃtuṣṭassuprasanno babhūva ha \|*  
*dadarśa kṛpayā dṛṣṭyā śaṃkaro bhaktavatsalaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Śiva favourably disposed to his devotees was highly delighted and satisfied by his dance and he glanced at him with sympathetic eyes.

## \|\| 6.51.21 \|\|

*bhagavānsarvalokeśśaśaraṇyo bhaktakāmadaḥ \|*  
*vareṇa cchaṃdayāmāsa bāleyaṃ taṃ mahāsuram \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. The lord of the worlds, worthy of being sought refuge in, the bestower of the desires of the devotees asked the great demon, the son of Bali, to choose a boon he liked.

## \|\| 6.51.22 \|\|

*śaṃkara uvāca \|*  
*bāleyaḥ sa mahādaityo bāṇo bhaktavarassudhīḥ \|*  
*praṇamya śaṃkaraṃ bhaktyā nunāva parameśvaram \|\| 22 \|\|*

Śiva said:—

22\. The great Daitya Bāṇa, son of Bali, the foremost among the devotees and highly intelligent, bowed to lord Śiva with devotion and eulogised him.

## \|\| 6.51.23-24 \|\|

*bāṇāsura uvāca \|*  
*devadeva mahādeva śaraṇāgatavatsala \|*  
*saṃtuṣṭo'si maheśāna mamopari vibho yadi \|\| 23 \|\|*

*madrakṣako bhava sadā madupasthaḥ purādhipaḥ \|*  
*sarvathā prītikṛnme hi sasutassagaṇaḥ prabho \|\| 24 \|\|*

The Asura Bāṇa said:—

23-24. O great god, lord of the gods, favourably disposed to those who seek refuge in you, O great Śiva, if you are pleased with me, be my guardian for ever. Be present with me as the lord of my city along with your sons and Gaṇas. O lord, be delightful to me in every respect.

## \|\| 6.51.25-26 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*baliputrassa vai bāṇo mohitaśśivamāyayā \|*  
*muktipradaṃ maheśānaṃ durārādhyamapi dhruvam \|\| 25 \|\|*

*sa bhaktavatsalaḥ śaṃbhurdattvā tasmai varāṃśca tān \|*  
*tatrovāsa tathā prītyā sagaṇassasutaḥ prabhuḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

25-26. Bāṇa son of Bali, deluded by Śiva’s deception, did not request anything else from lord Śiva who would have bestowed even salvation if asked though he is hard to please. Śiva, who is favourably disposed to his devotees, granted boons to him and stayed there lovingly along with his sons and his Gaṇas.

## \|\| 6.51.27 \|\|

*sa kadācidbāṇapure cakre devāsuraissaha \|*  
*nadītīre haraḥ krīḍāṃ ramye śoṇitakāhvaye \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Once Śiva performed divine sports in Śoṇita, the beautiful city of Bāṇa, in the company of the gods and Asuras, on the banks of a river.

## \|\| 6.51.28 \|\|

*nanṛturjahasuścāpi gaṃdharvāsarasastathā \|*  
*jeyuḥ praṇemurmunaya ānarcustuṣṭuvuśca tam \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. The Gandharvas and the celestial damsels danced and laughed. The sages performed Japas, bowed to, worshipped and eulogised him.

## \|\| 6.51.29 \|\|

*vavalguḥ prathamāssarve ṛṣayo juhuvustathā \|*  
*āyayuḥ siddhasaṃghāśca dṛdṛśuśśāṃkarī ratim \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. The Pramathas jumped and shouted; the sages performed sacrifices. The groups of Siddhas came and saw the divine sport of Śiva.

## \|\| 6.51.30 \|\|

*kutarkikā vineśuśca mlecchāśca paripaṃthinaḥ \|*  
*mātarobhimukhāstasthurvineśuśca vibhīṣikā \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Mlecchas,\[2\] adversaries and evil-intentioned wranglers perished. The mothers (Brāhmi etc.) sat facing him. The terrifying imps perished.

## \|\| 6.51.31 \|\|

*rudrasadbhāvabhaktānāṃ bhavadoṣāśca vistṛtāḥ \|*  
*tasmindṛṣṭe prajāssarvāḥ suprītiṃ paramāṃ yayuḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. The worldly faults of those who had the good conception of devotion to Śiva were forgotten.

## \|\| 6.51.32 \|\|

*vavalgurmunayassiddhāḥ strīṇāṃ dṛṣṭvā viceṣṭitam \|*  
*pupuṣuścāpi ṛtavassvaprabhāvaṃ tu tatra ca \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. The sages and the Siddhas leapt and bounced on seeing the activities of the women. The seasons displayed their power and nourished it.

## \|\| 6.51.33 \|\|

*vavurvātāśca mṛdavaḥ puṣpakesaradhūsarāḥ \|*  
*cukūjuḥ pakṣisaṃghāśca śākhināṃ madhulampaṭāḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Gentle winds blew wafting the grey pollen dust. The flocks of birds eager after honey chirped on the trees.

## \|\| 6.51.34 \|\|

*puṣpabhārāvanaddhānāṃ rāraṭyeraṃśca kokilāḥ \|*  
*madhuraṃ kāmajananaṃ vaneṣūpavaneṣu ca \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. The cuckoo cooed sweetly in the forests and parks, generating love, on the branches heavily laden with flowers.

## \|\| 6.51.35 \|\|

*tataḥ krīḍāvihāre tu matto bālenduśekharaḥ \|*  
*anirjitena kāmena dṛṣṭāḥ provāca nandinam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Then being glanced at by Kāma who was not vanquished, the crescent-crested lord Śiva highly indulgent in sports spoke to Nandin.

## \|\| 6.51.36 \|\|

*candraśekhara uvāca \|*  
*vāmāmānaya gaurīṃ tvaṃ kailāsātkṛtamaṃḍanām \|*  
*śīghramasmādvanādgatvā hyuktvā'kṛṣṇāmihānaya \|\| 36 \|\|*

The crescent-crested Śiva said:—

36\. Go quickly from this forest and tell the dark-complexioned Pārvatī everything and bring her here from Kailāsa after she has bedecked herself.

## \|\| 6.51.37 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*sa tatheti pratijñāya gatvā tatrāha pārvatīm \|*  
*supraṇamya raho dūtaśśaṃkarasya kṛtāṃjaliḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

37\. “So be it” answered the secret messenger of Śiva who started on journey. Reaching there, with palms joined in reverence he bowed to Pārvatī and said.

## \|\| 6.51.38 \|\|

*\|\| nandīśvara uvāca \|*  
*draṣṭumicchati devi tvāṃ devadevo maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*svavallabhāṃ rūpakṛtāṃ mayoktaṃ tannideśataḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

Nandīśvara said:—

38\. “O goddess, the great lord of the gods wishes to see you, his beloved, well-dressed. It is at his bidding that I say this”.

## \|\| 6.51.39 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*tatastadvacanādgaurī maṃḍanaṃ kartumādarāt \|*  
*udyatābhūnmuniśreṣṭha pativrataparāyaṇā \|\| 39 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

39\. O excellent sage, then, at his importunity, Pārvatī, devoted to her husband, began to bedeck herself ardently.

## \|\| 6.51.40 \|\|

*āgacchāmi prabhuṃ gaccha vada taṃ tvaṃ mamājñayā \|*  
*ājagāma tato naṃdī rudrāsannaṃ manogatiḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. “I am coming. You return and so inform the lord at my bidding”. The Nandin approached Śiva with the velocity of mind.

## \|\| 6.51.41 \|\|

*punarāha tato rudro nandinaṃ paravibhramaḥ \|*  
*punargaccha tatastāta kṣipramā naya pārvatīm \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Śiva who was extremely agitated told Nandin again. “Dear, go again and fetch Pārvatī from there”.

## \|\| 6.51.42 \|\|

*bāḍhamuktvā sa tāṃ gatvā gaurīmāha sulocanām \|*  
*draṣṭumicchati te bhartā kṛtaveṣāṃ manoramām \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. “Yes, sir”, said he. He went to Pārvatī of sweet appearance and said: “Your lord wishes to see you beautifully and gorgeously dressed.

## \|\| 6.51.43 \|\|

*śaṃkaro bahudhā devi vihartuṃ saṃpratīkṣate \|*  
*evaṃ patau sukāmārte gamyatāṃ girinaṃdini \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. O goddess, Śiva is eagerly waiting for various sports. O daughter of the mountain, please go since the lord is distressed with passion”.

## \|\| 6.51.44-46 \|\|

*ksarobhissamagrābhiranyonyamabhimaṃtritam \|*  
*labdhabhāvo yathā sadyaḥ pārvatyā darśanotsukaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

*ayaṃ pinākī kāmāriḥ vṛṇuyādyāṃ nitaṃbinīm \|*  
*sarvāsāṃ divyanārīṇāṃ rājñī bhavati vai dhuvam \|\| 45 \|\|*

*vīkṣaṇaṃ gaurirūpeṇa krīḍayenmanmathairgaṇaiḥ \|*  
*kāmo'yaṃ haṃti kāmārimūcuranyonyamādatāḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

44-46. All the celestial damsels told one another—“Since lord Śiva is very eager to see Pārvatī being passionate, the lady whom this enemy of Kāma may woo will certainly be the queen of celestial damsels. She may sport with lord Śiva in the form of Pārvatī accompanied by the Gaṇas of Kāma. Kāma is indeed victorious over his foe.

## \|\| 6.51.47 \|\|

*spraṣṭuṃ śaknoti yā kācidṛte dākṣāyaṇī striyam \|*  
*sā gacchettatra niśśaṃkaṃ mohayetpārvatīpatim \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. If any lady, save Pārvatī, is able to touch Śiva, let her go there unhesitatingly and fascinate him.

## \|\| 6.51.48 \|\|

*kūṣmāṃḍatanayā tatra śaṃkaraṃ spraṣṭumutsahe \|*  
*ahaṃ gaurīsurūpeṇa citralekhā vaco'bravīt \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. The daughter of Kumbhāṇḍa. Citralekhā said—“I desire to attract Śiva in the form of Pārvatī.

## \|\| 6.51.49 \|\|

*citralekhovāca \|*  
*yadadhānmohinīrūpaṃ keśavo moha necchayā \|*  
*purā tadvaiṣṇavaṃ yogamāśritya paramārthataḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Just as Viṣṇu, by taking recourse to his yogic powers assumed the form of Enchantress (Mohinī)”.

## \|\| 6.51.50 \|\|

*urvaśyāśca tato dṛṣṭvā rūpasya parivartanam \|*  
*kālīrūpaṃ ghṛtācī tu viśvācī cāṃḍikaṃ vapuḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. On seeing the change of form of Urvaśī, Ghṛtācī adopted the form of Kālī and Viśvācī that of Caṇḍikā.

## \|\| 6.51.51 \|\|

*sāvitrirūpaṃ raṃbhā ca gāyatraṃ menakā tathā \|*  
*sahajanyā jayārūpaṃ vaijayaṃ puṃjikasthalī \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Rambhā assumed the form of Sāvitrī, Menakā that of Gāyatrī; Sahajanyā that of Jayā and Puñjikasthalī that of Vijayā.

## \|\| 6.51.52 \|\|

*mātṝṇāmapyanuktānāmanuktāścāpsarovarāḥ \|*  
*ratnādrūpāṇi tāścakrussvavidyāsaṃyutā anu \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. The unnamed celestial damsels assumed the forms of unnamed mothers with effort by employing their art.

## \|\| 6.51.53 \|\|

*tatastāsāṃ tu rūpāṇi dṛṣṭvā kuṃbhāṃ ḍanaṃdinī \|*  
*vaiṣṇavādātmayogācca vijñātārthā vyaḍaṃbayat \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. On seeing their forms, the daughter of Kumbhāṇḍa, taking recourse to the Vaiṣṇava and her own Yoga, knew everything and emulated the same.

## \|\| 6.51.54 \|\|

*ūṣā bāṇāsurasutā divyayogaviśāradā \|*  
*cakāra rūpaṃ pārvatyā divyamatyadbhutaṃ śubham \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Ūṣā, daughter of the Asura Bāṇa efficient in divine Yoga, assumed the wonderfully auspicious and divine form of Pārvatī.

## \|\| 6.51.55 \|\|

*mahāraktābjasaṃkāśaṃ caraṇaṃ coktamaprabham \|*  
*divyalakṣaṇasaṃyuktaṃ mano'bhīṣṭārthadāyakam \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Her feet were of excellent lustre. They shone like the great red lotus. They had all the divine characteristics bestowing every desired object.

## \|\| 6.51.56 \|\|

*tasyā ramaṇasaṃkalpaṃ vijñāya girijā tataḥ \|*  
*uvāca sarvavijñānā sarvāntaryāminī śivā \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Knowing that she wanted to indulge in love-sport with Śiva, the omniscient and omnipresent Pārvatī spoke.

Pārvatī said—

## \|\| 6.51.57-59 \|\|

*girijovāca \|*  
*yato mama svarūpaṃ vai dhṛtabhūṣe sakhi tvayā \|*  
*sakāmatvena samaye saṃprāpte sati mānini \|\| 57 \|\|*

*asmiṃstu kārtike māsi ṛtudharmāstu mādhave \|*  
*dvādaśyāṃ śuklapakṣe tu yastu ghore niśāgame \|\| 58 \|\|*

*kṛtopavāsāṃ tvāṃ bhoktā suptāmaṃtaḥpure naraḥ \|*  
*sa te bharttā kṛto devaistena sārddhaṃ ramiṣyasi \|\| 59 \|\|*

57-59. O friend Ūṣā, chaste and honourable lady since you have adopted my form out of passion, so you will have the monthly course in the appropriate time in the Kārttika month. On the twelfth day in the bright half of Vaiśākha, you will undertake a fast. During the night while you are asleep in the harem, a man will come there and enjoy you. He has been made your husband by the gods. You will sport with him.

## \|\| 6.51.60 \|\|

*ābālyādviṣṇubhaktāsi yato'niśamataṃdritā \|*  
*evamastviti sā prāha manasā lajjitānanā \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. This is because you have been devoted to Viṣṇu ever since childhood without sinking into lethargy. She then mumbled to herself. “Let it be so” and was very bashful.

## \|\| 6.51.61 \|\|

*atha sā pārvatī devī kṛtakautukamaṇḍanā \|*  
*rudrasaṃnidhimāgatya cikrīḍe tena śaṃbhunā \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Then the goddess Pārvatī bedecked herself zealously and went to Śiva. She then sported with him.

## \|\| 6.51.62 \|\|

*tato ratāṃte bhagavānrudraścādarśanaṃ yayau \|*  
*sadāraḥ sagaṇaścāpi sahito daivatairmune \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. O sage, at the end of the dalliance Lord Śiva vanished from the place accompanied by his wife, the Gaṇas and the gods.

## Chapter 52 - The story of Ūṣā (2)

## \|\| 6.52.2-3 \|\|

*purā bāṇāsuro nāma daivadoṣācca garvitaḥ \|*  
*kṛtvā tāṃḍavanṛtyaṃ ca toṣayāmāsa śaṃkaram \|\| 2 \|\|*

*jñātvā saṃtuṣṭamanasaṃ pārvatīvallabhaṃ śivam \|*  
*uvāca cāsuro bāṇo nataskandhaḥ kṛtāṃjaliḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

l. Listen to another story of Śiva the great soul which bestows the highest pleasure and wherein his endearment to his devotees can be seen.

2-3. Formerly the Asura Bāṇa had pleased Śiva by performing the Tāṇḍava dance. By adverse fate he became haughty. On realising that Śiva, the lover of Pārvatī, was delighted in mind, the Asura Bāṇa joined his palms in reverence, bent his shoulders and spoke.

## \|\| 6.52.4 \|\|

*bāṇa uvāca \|*  
*devadeva mahādeva sarvadevaśiromaṇe \|*  
*tvatprasādādbalī cāhaṃ śṛṇu me paramaṃ vacaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

Bāṇa said:—

4\. O great god, lord of the gods and crest-jewel of all the gods, I am very strong, thanks to your favour.

## \|\| 6.52.5 \|\|

*dossahasraṃ tvayā dattaṃ paraṃ bhārāya me'bhavet \|*  
*trilokyāṃ pratiyoddhāraṃ na labhe tvadṛte samam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. A thousand hands have been given to me by you. They are only a burden to me, since except you I do not find any match to oppose me having an equal strength.

## \|\| 6.52.6 \|\|

*he deva kimanenāpi sahasreṇa karomyaham \|*  
*bāhūnāṃ giritulyānāṃ vinā yuddhaṃ vṛṣadhvaja \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. O bull-bannered lord, what can I do with these thousand mountain-like hands without a fight.

## \|\| 6.52.7 \|\|

*kaḍūṃtyā nibhṛtaidoṃrbhiryuyutsurdiggajānaham \|*  
*purāṇyācūrṇayannadrīnbhītāstepi pradudruvuḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. When my hands itch for war I desire to fight the elephants of the quarters. By hitting the cities and mountains I reduced them to powder. Being frightened they fled away.

## \|\| 6.52.8 \|\|

*mayā yamaḥ kṛto yoddhā vahniśca kṛtako mahān \|*  
*varuṇaścāpi gopālo gavāṃ pālayitā tathā \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Yama has been made a combatant with me and the great fire-god too, similarly. Varuṇa has been made a cowherd looking after my cows.

## \|\| 6.52.9 \|\|

*gajādhyakṣaḥ kuberastu sairandhrī cāpi nirṛtiḥ \|*  
*jitaścākhaṃḍalo loke karadāyī sadā kṛtaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Kubera has been made the in-charge of couches, Nirṛti a chaperon. Indra has been defeated and forced to pay tribute.

## \|\| 6.52.10-11 \|\|

*yuddhasyāgamanaṃ brūhi yatraite bāhavo mama \|*  
*śatruhastaprayuktaśca śastrāstrairjarjarīkṛtāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*pataṃtu śatruhastādvā pātayantu sahasradhā \|*  
*etanmanorathaṃ me hi pūrṇaṃ kuru maheśvara \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. Please suggest a fight unto me wherein my hands may fall shattered by the weapons hurled by the enemy or cause him to fall in thousand pieces. O lord Śiva, please fulfil this desire of mine.

## \|\| 6.52.12 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*tacchrutvā kupito rudrastvaṭṭahāsaṃ mahādbhutam \|*  
*kṛtvā'bravīnmahāmanyurbhaktabādhā'pahārakaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

12\. Becoming furious on hearing that, Śiva laughed boisterously and in a wonderful manner; Śiva the remover of the distress of devotees became very angry and said.

Śiva said—

## \|\| 6.52.13 \|\|

*rudra uvāca \|*  
*dhigdhiktvāṃ sarvato garvinsarvadaityakulādhama \|*  
*baliputrasya bhaktasya nocitaṃ vaca īdṛśam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Fie upon you, O haughty base Daitya, such a talk as this does not behove the son of Bali and a devotee.

## \|\| 6.52.14 \|\|

*darpasyāsya praśamanaṃ lapsyase cāśu dāruṇam \|*  
*mahāyuddhamakasmādvai balinā matsamena hi \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Very soon, you will meet a terrible challenge to your bluff by fighting a great battle against person equal to me in strength. The battle will be sudden.

## \|\| 6.52.15 \|\|

*tatra te girisaṃkāśā bāhavo'nalakāṣṭhavat \|*  
*chinnā bhūmau patiṣyaṃti śastrāstraiḥ kadalīkṛtāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Therein your mountain-like hands will be cut off by weapons and missiles. They will fall off like reeds or stumps of plantain trees.

## \|\| 6.52.16-18 \|\|

*yadeṣa mānuṣaśiro mayūrasahito dhvajaḥ \|*  
*vidyate tava duṣṭātmaṃstasya syātpatanaṃ yadā \|\| 16 \|\|*

*sthāpitasyāyudhāgāre vinā vātakṛtaṃ bhayam \|*  
*tadā yuddhaṃ mahāghoraṃ saṃprāptamiti cetasi \|\| 17 \|\|*

*nidhāya ghoraṃ saṃgrāmaṃ gacchethāḥ sarvasainyavān \|*  
*sāṃprataṃ gaccha tadveśma yatastadvidyate śivaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

16-18. “O wicked soul, when this flagstaff of yours, with the emblem of a peacock with a human head, which is installed in your armoury, falls without being blown off by a gust of wind, you can decide within your mind that a terrible battle is at hand. Go to that terrible war accompanied by all your generals. Now return to your abode where Śiva is present.

## \|\| 6.52.19 \|\|

*tathā tānsvamahotpātāṃstatra draṣṭāsi durmate \|*  
*ityuktvā virarāmātha garvahṛdbhaktavatsalaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. O wicked one, you will see the great evil portents.” After saying this, the lord who is favourably disposed to the devotees and is the dispeller of pride stopped.

## \|\| 6.52.20 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*tacchrutvā rudramabhyarcya divyairajaṃlikuḍmalaiḥ \|*  
*praṇamya ca mahādevaṃ bāṇaśca svagṛhaṃ gataḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

20\. After hearing that, Bāṇa worshiped Śiva with palms joined in reverence in the form of buds and bowed to lord Śiva. He then went to his abode.

## \|\| 6.52.21 \|\|

*kuṃbhāṇḍāya yathāvṛttaṃ pṛṣṭaḥ provāca harṣitaḥ \|*  
*paryaikṣiṣṭāsuro bāṇastaṃ yogaṃ hyutsukassadā \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. On being asked, the delighted Asura mentioned everything to Kumbhāṇḍa in the manner it had happened. The Asura Bāṇa awaited the particular conjunction of circumstances eagerly.

## \|\| 6.52.22 \|\|

*atha daivātkadācitsa svayaṃ bhagnaṃ dhvajaṃ ca tam \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā tatrāsuro bāṇo hṛṣṭo yuddhāya niryayau \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Once, by chance he saw the flagstaff broken and fallen. On seeing it, he was delighted and he set out for war.

## \|\| 6.52.23-24 \|\|

*sa svasainyaṃ samāhūya saṃyuktaḥ sāṣṭabhirgaṇaiḥ \|*  
*iṣṭiṃ sāṃgrāmikāṃ kṛtvā dṛṣṭvā sāṃgrāmikaṃ madhu \|\| 23 \|\|*

*kakubhāṃ maṃgalaṃ sarvaṃ saṃprekṣya prasthito'bhavat \|*  
*mahotsāho mahāvīro baliputro mahārathaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. He called together his entire army. He was accompanied by his eight lieutenants. He performed the sacrifice for success in war. He surveyed the wine\[1\] prepared for use in the course of war. He observed the auspicious signs in the quarters and set off. He, the son of Bali, the heroic warrior capable of fighting with ten thousand persons, was very enthusiastic.

## \|\| 6.52.25-26 \|\|

*iti hṛtkamale kṛtvā kaḥ kasmādāgamiṣyati \|*  
*yoddhā raṇapriyo yastu nānāśastrāstrapāragaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*yastu bāhusahasraṃ me chinattvanalakāṣṭhavat \|*  
*tathā śastrairmahātīkṣṇaiścchinadmi śataśastviha \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. He thought within himself—“Who can be that warrior fond of battle, a master of the art of using weapons and missiles who will cut off my thousand hands like reeds or whom I shall cut into hundred pieces?”

## \|\| 6.52.27-28 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare kālaḥ saṃprāptaśśaṃkareṇa hi \|*  
*yatra sā bāṇaduhitā sujātā kṛtamaṃgalā \|\| 27 \|\|*

*mādhavaṃ mādhave māsi pūjayitvā mahāniśi \|*  
*suptā cāṃtaḥ pure gupte strībhāvamupalaṃbhitā \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. In the meantime, in the month of Vaiśākha after her monthly course, the daughter of Bāṇa had her auspicious bath and auspicious rites after worshipping lord Śiva. At night she lay asleep in the well-guarded harem. It was then that Kāma entered the place with lord Śiva.

## \|\| 6.52.29-30 \|\|

*gauryā saṃpreṣitenāpi vyākṛṣṭā divyamāyayā \|*  
*kṛṣṇātmajātmajenātha rudaṃtī sā hyanāthavat \|\| 29 \|\|*

*sa cāpi tāṃ balādbhuktvā pārvatyāḥ sakhibhiḥ punaḥ \|*  
*nītastu divyayogena dvārakāṃ nimiṣāṃtarāt \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. She was seized by Kṛṣṇa’s grandson\[3\] sent by Pārvatī of divine Māyā. She began to cry helplessly. He enjoyed her forcibly. Within a moment he was carried to Dvārakā by Pārvatī’s attendants by means of their divine Yogic power.

## \|\| 6.52.31 \|\|

*mṛditā sā tadotthāya rudaṃtī vividhā giraḥ \|*  
*sakhībhyaḥ kathayitvā tu dehatyāge kṛtakṣaṇā \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Rubbed and squeezed thus, she got up crying. She mumbled various words to her female attendants. She even decided to give up her life.

## \|\| 6.52.32 \|\|

*sakhyā kṛtātmano doṣaṃ sā vyāsa smāritā punaḥ \|*  
*sarvaṃ tatpūrvavṛttāṃtaṃ tato dṛṣṭvā ca sā bhavat \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. O Vyāsa, she was then reminded by her friend of the fault she had committed previously. She then came to realise the entire incident that had occurred formerly.

## \|\| 6.52.33 \|\|

*abravīccitralekhāṃ ca tato madhurayā girā \|*  
*ūṣā bāṇasya tanayā kuṃbhāṃḍatanayāṃ mune \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. O sage, Ūṣā, daughter of Bāṇa, spoke sweetly to Citralekhā, daughter of Kumbhāṇḍa.

## \|\| 6.52.34 \|\|

*ūṣovāca \|*  
*sakhi yadyeṣa me bhartā pārvatyā vihitaḥ purā \|*  
*kenopāyena te guptaḥ prāpyate vidhivanmayā \|\| 34 \|\|*

Ūṣā said:—

34\. “Dear friend, if he is the person ordained as my husband by Pārvatī, how can I obtain him duly?

## \|\| 6.52.35 \|\|

*kasminkule sa vā jāto mama yena hṛtaṃ manaḥ \|*  
*ityuṣāvacanaṃ śrutvā sakhī provāca tāṃ tadā \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. In what family is he born who has fascinated my mind thus?” On hearing the words of Ūṣā, the friend told her then.

## \|\| 6.52.36 \|\|

*citralekhovāca \|*  
*tvayā svapne ca yo dṛṣṭaḥ puruṣo devi taṃ katham \|*  
*ahaṃ saṃmānayiṣyāmi na vijñātastu yo mama \|\| 36 \|\|*

Citralekhā said:—

36\. “O gentle lady, how shall I bring that man who was seen by you in the dream and whom I do not know.”

## \|\| 6.52.37 \|\|

*daityakanyā tadukte tu rāgāṃdhā maraṇotsukā \|*  
*rakṣitā ca tayā sakhyā prathame divase tataḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Thus said by her, the daughter of the Daitya blinded by passion was ready to end her life. She was saved thus by her friend on the first day.

## \|\| 6.52.38 \|\|

*punaḥ provāca soṣā vai citralekhā mahāmatiḥ \|*  
*kuṃbhāṃḍasya sutā bāṇatanayāṃ munisattama \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. O excellent sage, again that daughter of Kumbhāṇḍa, Citralekhā, of great intellect spoke to Ūṣā the daughter of Bāṇa.

## \|\| 6.52.39 \|\|

*citralekhovāca \|*  
*vyasanaṃ te'pakarṣāmi trilokyāṃ yadi bhāṣyate \|*  
*samāneṣye naraṃ yaste manohartā tamādiśa \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. I can dispel your grief if such a man could be anywhere in the three worlds. I shall bring him who has captivated your mind. Please mention the details of his features.

## \|\| 6.52.40 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityuktvā vastrapuṭake devāndaityāṃśca dānavān \|*  
*gandharvasiddhanāgāṃśca yakṣādīṃśca tathālikhat \|\| 40 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

40\. After saying this, she painted all the gods on a canvas together with the Daityas, Dānavas, Gandharvas, Siddhas, Nāgas, Yakṣas and others.

## \|\| 6.52.41 \|\|

*tathā narāṃsteṣu vṛṣṇīñśūramānakaduṃdubhim \|*  
*vyalikhadrāmakṛṣṇau ca pradyumnaṃ narasattamam \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Similarly she painted men, the Vṛṣṇis among them, the heroic Ānakadundubhi, Balarāma, Kṛṣṇa and Pradyumna the excellent among men.

## \|\| 6.52.42 \|\|

*aniruddhaṃ vilikhitaṃ prādyumniṃ vīkṣya lajjitā \|*  
*āsīdavāṅmukhī coṣā hṛdaye harṣapūritā \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. On seeing Aniruddha the son of Pradyumna painted, she became bashful. Ūṣā’s heart was filled with delight. She stood with downcast face.

Ūṣā said—

## \|\| 6.52.43 \|\|

*ūṣā provāca cauro'sau mayā prāptastu yo niśi \|*  
*puruṣaḥ sakhi yenāśu cetoratnaṃ hṛtaṃ mama \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. “O, this is the thief who has stolen my heart. This is the man whom I secured in the night.

## \|\| 6.52.44 \|\|

*yasya saṃsparśanādeva mohitāhaṃ tathābhavam \|*  
*tamahaṃ jñātumicchāmi vada sarvaṃ ca bhāmini \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. By his very contact I became fascinated. I wish to know about him. O beautiful woman, mention everything to me.

## \|\| 6.52.45 \|\|

*kasyāyamanvaye jāto nāma kiṃ cāsya vidyate \|*  
*ityuktā sābravīnnāma yoginī tasya cānvayam \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. In whose family is he born? What is his name? On being thus asked by her, the lady, expert in yogic practice, mentioned the name of the family.

## \|\| 6.52.46 \|\|

*sarvamākarṇya sā tasya kulādi munisattama \|*  
*utsukā bāṇatanayā babhāṣe sā tu kāminī \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. O excellent sage, on hearing about his family, tḥe eager and passionate daughter of Bāṇa said.

Ūṣā said—

## \|\| 6.52.47-48 \|\|

*ūṣovāca \|*  
*upāyaṃ racaya prītyā tatprāptyai sakhi tatkṣaṇāt \|*  
*yenopāyena taṃ kāṃtaṃ labheyaṃ prāṇavallabham \|\| 47 \|\|*

*yaṃ vināhaṃ kṣaṇaṃ naikaṃ sakhi jīvitumutsahe \|*  
*tamānayeha sadyatnātsukhinīṃ kuru māṃ sakhi \|\| 48 \|\|*

47-48. O my friend, ascertain some means lovingly so that I shall regain my beloved husband in a trice. Without him, my friend, I am not at all eager to live even for a moment. Please bring him here strenuously. O my friend, make me happy.

## \|\| 6.52.49 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityuktā sā tathā bāṇātmajayā maṃtrikanyakā \|*  
*vismitābhūnmuniśreṣṭha suvicāraparā'bhavat \|\| 49 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

49\. On being thus requested by the daughter of Bāṇa, O excellent sage, the daughter of the minister was surprised and began to think seriously.

## \|\| 6.52.50 \|\|

*tatassakhīṃ samābhāṣya citralekhā manojavā \|*  
*buddhvā taṃ kṛṣṇapautraṃ sā dvārakāṃ gaṃtumudyatā \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Then taking leave of her friend, and knowing him to be the grandson of Kṛṣṇa, Citralekhā got ready to go to Dvārakā with the velocity of the mind.

## \|\| 6.52.51-53 \|\|

*jyeṣṭhakṛṣṇacaturdaśyāṃ tṛtīye tu gate'hani \|*  
*āprabhātānmuhūrte tu saṃprāptā dvārakāṃ purīm \|\| 51 \|\|*

*ekena kṣaṇamātreṇa nabhasā divyayoginī \|*  
*tataścāṃtaḥpurodyāne prādyumnirdadṛśe tayā \|\| 52 \|\|*

*krīḍannārījanaissārddhaṃ prapibanmādhavī madhu \|*  
*sarvāṃgasundaraḥ śyāmaḥ susmito navayauvanaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

51-53. When the third day after the fourteenth day in the dark half of the month of Jyeṣṭha elapsed, a Muhūrta before the dawn, she reached the city of Dvārakā within a moment by the aerial path because she was a Yoginī. Then in the park of the harem the son of Pradyumna was seen by her playing with women and drinking wine. He was dark-complexioned but beautiful in every limb, smiling and in the prime of youth.

## \|\| 6.52.54-55 \|\|

*tataḥ khaṭvāṃ samārūḍhamaṃdhakārapaṭena sā \|*  
*ācchādayitvā yogena tāmasena ca mādhavam \|\| 54 \|\|*

*tatassā mūrdhni tāṃ khaṭvāṃ gṛhītvā nimiṣāṃtarāt \|*  
*saṃprāptā śoṇitapuraṃ yatra sā bāṇanaṃdinī \|\| 55 \|\|*

54-55. When he lay on the cot she encompassed him with the shroud of darkness by employing her Tāmasa Yoga. Thereafter she carried the cot on her head and within a moment reached the city of śoṇita where the daughter of Bāṇa eagerly awaited her.

## \|\| 6.52.56 \|\|

*kāmārtā vividhānbhāvāñcakāronmattamānasā \|*  
*ānītamatha taṃ dṛṣṭvā tadā bhītā ca sābhavat \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Passionate that she was, she made various mad pranks displaying her emotions. On seeing that he was actually brought she became frightened too.

## \|\| 6.52.57 \|\|

*aṃtaḥpure sugupte ca nave tasminsamāgame \|*  
*yāvatkrīḍitumārabdhaṃ tāvajjñātaṃ ca tatkṣaṇāt \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. When they began their sexual dalliance in that fresh contact in the well-guarded harem, it became known to all in a moment.

## \|\| 6.52.58-59 \|\|

*aṃtaḥpuradvāragatairvetrajarjarapāṇibhiḥ \|*  
*iṃgitairanumānaiśca kanyādauḥśīlyamācaran \|\| 58 \|\|*

*sa cāpi dṛṣṭastaistatra naro divyavapurdharaḥ \|*  
*taruṇo darśanīyastu sāhasī samarapriyaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

58-59. The man with a divine body who carried on illegitimate affairs with a virgin was found out by the persons appointed at the doorway to the harem with cane-sticks in their old and emaciated hands, by means of gestures and inferences. They understood that he was a young man, very comely in features, daring and fond of battle.

## \|\| 6.52.60 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā sarvamācakhyurbāṇāya balisūnave \|*  
*puruṣāste mahāvīrāḥ kanyāntaḥpurarakṣakāḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. On seeing him, the heroic men who guarded the harem went and told Bāṇa, son of Bali, everything.

## \|\| 6.52.61 \|\|

*dvārapālā ūcuḥ \|*  
*deva kaścinna jānīte guptaścāṃtaḥpure balāt \|*  
*sa kastu tava kanyāṃ vai svayaṃgrāhādadharṣayat \|\| 61 \|\|*

The gatekeepers said:—

61\. O lord, no one knows how this was done. Indra has entered your harem in secret and forcibly. He has outraged the modesty of your daughter by seizing her himself.

## \|\| 6.52.62 \|\|

*dānavendra mahābāho paśyapaśyainamatra ca \|*  
*yadyuktaṃ syāttatkuruṣva na duṣṭā vayamityuta \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. O lord of Dānavas, of great arms, see, see him here. Do whatever is proper. We are not at fault.

## \|\| 6.52.63 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*teṣāṃ tadvacanaṃ śrutvā dānavendro mahābalaḥ \|*  
*vismitobhūnmuniśreṣṭha kanyāyāḥ śrutadūṣaṇaḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

63\. O excellent sage, on hearing their words, on hearing of the defilement of his daughter, the lord of Dānavas of great strength, became surprised.

## Chapter 53 - The dalliance of Ūṣā and Aniruddha

## \|\| 6.53.1 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*atha bāṇāsuraḥ kruddhastatra gatvā dadarśa tam \|*  
*divyalīlāttavapuṣaṃ prathame vayasi sthitam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

1\. The infuriated Asura Bāṇa went there and saw Aniruddha who was in the fresh years of youth and who seemed to have been born especially for divine sports.

## \|\| 6.53.2 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā vismitaṃ vākyaṃ kiṃ kāraṇamathābravīt \|*  
*bāṇaḥ krodha parītātmā yudhi śauṃḍo hasanniva \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The infuriated Bāṇa, very efficient in war, was a bit surprised on seeing him and wondered why he had done like that and therefore said mockingly.

## \|\| 6.53.3 \|\|

*aho manuṣyo rūpāḍhyassāhasī dhairyavāniti \|*  
*koyamāgatakālaśca duṣṭabhāgyo vimūḍhadhīḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. “Oh this man is really handsome, bold and daring. Who can this unfortunate deluded person be? His death is imminent.

## \|\| 6.53.4 \|\|

*yena me kulacāritraṃ dūṣitaṃ duhitā hitā \|*  
*taṃ mārayadhvaṃ kupitāśśīghraṃ śastraissudāruṇaiḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. O angry ones, with terrible weapons immediately kill the fellow who has outraged the traditional purity of my family and defiled my dear daughter.

## \|\| 6.53.5 \|\|

*durācāraṃ ca taṃ baddhvā ghore kārā gṛhe tataḥ \|*  
*rakṣadhvaṃ vikaṭe vīrā bahukālaṃ viśeṣataḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. O heroic ones, bind the terrible fellow of evil conduct. Put him in a frightful prison for a long time”.

## \|\| 6.53.6 \|\|

*na jāne koyamabhayaḥ ko vā ghoraparākramaḥ \|*  
*vicāryeti mahābuddhissaṃ digdho'bhūccharāsuraḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. After saying this, the Asura Bāṇa thought within himself intelligently. “It is not known who this fearless fellow is. Certainly he is a man of terrible exploit”. Thinking thus Bāṇa hesitated to act.

## \|\| 6.53.7 \|\|

*tato daityena sainyaṃ tu daśasāhasrakaṃ śanaiḥ \|*  
*vadhāya tasya vīrasya vyādiṣṭaṃ pāpabuddhinā \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Then gradually the evil-minded Daitya ordered ten thousand men from his army for slaying him.

## \|\| 6.53.8 \|\|

*tadādiṣṭāstu te vīrāḥ sarvatontaḥpuraṃ drutam \|*  
*chādayāmāsuratyugrāśchiṃdi bhiṃdīti vādinaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Commanded by him those heroic terrible fellows encircled the harem saying. “Cut him, pierce him”.

## \|\| 6.53.9-10 \|\|

*śatrusainyaṃ tato dṛṣṭvā garjamānaḥ sa yādavaḥ \|*  
*aṃtaḥpuraṃ dvāragataṃ parighaṃ gṛhya cātulam \|\| 9 \|\|*

*niṣkrāṃto bhavanāttasmādvajrahasta ivāṃtakaḥ \|*  
*tena tānkiṃkarān hatvā punaścāṃtaḥpuraṃ yayau \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. On seeing the army of the enemy, Aniruddha the scion of the Yādava family, roared. He seized the big iron club from the harem-gate and came out of the apartment like the god of death armed with thunderbolt. With that iron club he killed the servants and returned to the harem.

## \|\| 6.53.11 \|\|

*evaṃ daśasahasrāṇi sainyāni munisattama \|*  
*jaghāna roṣaraktākṣo varddhitaśśivatejasā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. O excellent sage, thus Aniruddha strengthened by Śiva’s splendour, with eyes turned red by anger, killed all the ten thousand men of the army.

## \|\| 6.53.12-14 \|\|

*lakṣe hate'tha yodhānāṃ tato bāṇāsuro ruṣā \|*  
*kubhāṃḍaṃ sa gṛhītvā tu yuddhe śauṃḍaṃ samāhvayat \|\| 12 \|\|*

*aniruddhaṃ mahābuddhiṃ dvandvayuddhe mahā have \|*  
*prādyumniṃ rakṣitaṃ śaivatejasā prajvalattanum \|\| 13 \|\|*

*tato daśasahasrāṇi turagāṇāṃ rathottamān \|*  
*yuddhaprāptena khaḍgena daityendrasya jaghāna saḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

12-14. With the sword captured in the course of the battle he killed ten thousands of horses and charioteers of the lord of Daityas. When a hundred thousand soldiers had been killed, the Asura Bāṇa furiously entered the fray taking with him Kumbhāṇḍa, expert in war. He then challenged Aniruddha for a duel in the course of that war—Aniruddha the highly intelligent son of Pradyumna, of refulgent body and protected by Śiva’s brilliance.

## \|\| 6.53.15 \|\|

*tadvadhāya tataśśaktiṃ kālavaiśvānaropamām \|*  
*aniruddho gṛhītvā tāṃ tayā taṃ nijaghāna hi \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Aniruddha then seized a spear blazing like the fire of death, for killing him and hit him with that.

## \|\| 6.53.16 \|\|

*rathopasthe tato bāṇastena śaktyāhato dṛḍham \|*  
*sa sāśvastatkṣaṇaṃ vīrastatraivāṃtaradhīyata \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Bāṇa was hit with the spear even as he was seated in a chariot. In a trice the heroic demon vanished along with his horse.

## \|\| 6.53.17 \|\|

*tasmiṃstvadarśanaṃ prāpte prādyumniraparājitam \|*  
*ālokya kakubhassarvāstasthau giririvācalaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. When he vanished, Aniruddha, the unvanquished son of Pradyumna, stood steady like a mountain observing all the quarters.

## \|\| 6.53.18 \|\|

*adṛśyamānastu tadā kūṭayodhassa dānavaḥ \|*  
*nānāśastrasahasraistaṃ jaghāna hi punaḥ punaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Remaining invisible, that Dānava Bāṇa, practising deceptive fight, hit him again and again with thousands of weapons.

## \|\| 6.53.19 \|\|

*chadmanāṃ nāgapāśaistaṃ babaṃdha sa mahābalaḥ \|*  
*baliputro mahāvīraśśivabhaktaśśarāsuraḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. That powerful son of Bali, the heroic devotee of Śiva, the Asura Bāṇa deceitfully bound him with Serpent-nooses.

## \|\| 6.53.20 \|\|

*taṃ baddhvā paṃjarāṃtaḥsthaṃ kṛtvā yuddhādupāramat \|*  
*uvāca bāṇaḥ saṃkuddhassūtaputraṃ mahābalam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. After binding him and putting him in a cage he stopped the battle. The infuriated Bāṇa then spoke to the very powerful son of the charioteer.

## \|\| 6.53.21 \|\|

*bāṇāsura uvāca \|*  
*sūtaputra śiraśchiṃdhi puruṣasyāsya vai laghu \|*  
*yena me dūṣitaṃ pūtaṃ balādduṣṭena satkulam \|\| 21 \|\|*

The Asura Bāṇa said:—

21\. O son of the charioteer, cut off the head of this wicked fellow who has defiled my family.

## \|\| 6.53.22 \|\|

*chitvā tu sarvagātrāṇi rākṣasebhyaḥ prayaccha bhoḥ \|*  
*athāsya raktamāṃsāni kravyādā api bhuṃjatām \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. After chopping off the limbs, give them to the Rākṣasas. Or let the beasts of prey swallow his flesh and blood.

## \|\| 6.53.23 \|\|

*agādhe tṛṇasaṃkīrṇe kūpe pātakinaṃ jahi \|*  
*kiṃ bahūktyā sūtaputra māraṇīyo hi sarvathā \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Or kill this sinner and put him in a grassy well. O son of the charioteer, what more shall I say? By all means he must be slain.

## \|\| 6.53.24 \|\|

*sanatku māra uvāca \|*  
*tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā dharmabuddhirniśācaraḥ \|*  
*kuṃbhāṃḍastvabravīdvākyaṃ bāṇaṃ sanmaṃtrisattamam \|\| 24 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

24\. On hearing his words, the Asura Kumbhāṇḍa, the most excellent of the ministers and righteous in thought, spoke to Bāṇa.

## \|\| 6.53.25 \|\|

*kuṃbhāṃḍa uvāca \|*  
*naitatkartuṃ samucitaṃ karma deva vicāryatām \|*  
*asminhate hato hyātmā bhavediti matirmama \|\| 25 \|\|*

Kumbhāṇḍa said:—

25\. O lord, this is not a proper thing to do. Please consider. I think by killing him we will be killing ourselves.

## \|\| 6.53.26 \|\|

*ayaṃ tu dṛśyate deva tulyo viṣṇoḥ parākramaiḥ \|*  
*vardhitaścandra cūḍasya tvadduṣṭasya sutecasā \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. O lord, he seems to be equal to Viṣṇu in exploits. His strength has been increased by the brilliance of the moon-crested lord, your favourite.

## \|\| 6.53.27 \|\|

*atha candralalāṭasya sāhasena samatsvayam \|*  
*imāmavasthāṃ prāptosi pauruṣe saṃvyavasthitaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Moreover, in daring he is equal to the moon-crested lord; though he is reduced to this plight he maintains his manliness.

## \|\| 6.53.28 \|\|

*ayaṃ śivaprasādādvai kṛṣṇapautro mahābalaḥ \|*  
*asmāṃstṛṇopamān vetti daṣṭopi bhujagairbalāt \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. It is by the grace of Śiva that he, the grandson of Kṛṣṇa, considers us insignificant as the blades of grass. Although he is bitten by serpents cruelly he is still very strong.

## \|\| 6.53.29 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*etadvākyaṃ tu bāṇāya kathayitvā sa dānavaḥ \|*  
*aniruddhamuvācedaṃ rājanītividuttamaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

29\. After saying thus to Bāṇa, the Dānava, the most excellent among statesmen, spoke to Aniruddha.

## \|\| 6.53.30 \|\|

*kuṃbhāṃḍa uvāca \|*  
*kosi kasyāsi re vīra satyaṃ vada mamāgrataḥ \|*  
*kena vā tvamihānīto durācāra narādhama \|\| 30 \|\|*

Kumbhāṇḍa said:—

30\. “O hero, who are you? Whose son are you? Tell us the truth. O meanest of men, of evil conduct, by whom have you been brought here?

## \|\| 6.53.31 \|\|

*daityendraṃ stuhi vīraṃ tvaṃ namaskuru kṛtājaliḥ \|*  
*jitosmīti vaco dīnaṃ kathayitvā punaḥpunaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Repeat piteously ‘I am vanquished’. Eulogise the heroic lord of the Daityas. Join your palms in reverence and bow to him.

## \|\| 6.53.32 \|\|

*evaṃ kṛte tu mokṣassyādanyathā baṃdhanādi ca \|*  
*tacchrutvā vacanaṃ tasya prativākyamuvāca saḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. If you do like this, you may get release. Otherwise this captivity and tortures will continue”. On hearing this Aniruddha replied.

## \|\| 6.53.33 \|\|

*aniruddha uvāca \|*  
*daityā'dhamasakhe kararpiḍopajīvaka \|*  
*niśācara durācāra śatrudharmaṃ na vetsi bhoḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

Aniruddha said:—

33\. O friend of the basest of Daityas, O you that sustain yourself with the balls of rice offered in the hands, O demon of evil conduct, you do not know the laws of adversaries.

## \|\| 6.53.34 \|\|

*dainyaṃ palāyanaṃ cātha śūrasya maraṇādhikam \|*  
*viruddhaṃ copaśalyaṃ ca bhavediti matirmama \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. I think that for the valorous person humble supplications and running away from the battlefield are worse than death. These are adverse and painful to him like a dart.

## \|\| 6.53.35 \|\|

*kṣatriyasya raṇe śreyo maraṇaṃ sanmukhe sadā \|*  
*na vīramānino bhūmau dīnasyeva kṛtāṃjaliḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. For a Kṣatriya, death while fighting face to face with the enemy is commendable rather than joining the palms in reverence like a man in humble condition professing to be valorous.

## \|\| 6.53.36 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityādi vīravākyāni bahūni sa jagāda tam \|*  
*tadākarṇya sabāṇo'sau vismito'bhūccukopa ca \|\| 36 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

36\. These and many other heroic words he uttered, on hearing which Bāṇa was surprised and angry too.

## \|\| 6.53.37 \|\|

*tadovāca nabhovāṇī bāṇasyāśvāsanāya hi \|*  
*śṛṇvatāṃ sarvavīrāṇāmaniruddhasya maṃtriṇaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Then a celestial voice was heard for the pacification of Bāṇa which all the heroes, Aniruddha and the minister, stood listening to.

## \|\| 6.53.38 \|\|

*vyomavāṇyuvāca \|*  
*bho bho bāṇa mahāvīra na krodhaṃ kartumarhasi \|*  
*baliputrosi sumate śivabhakta vicāryatām \|\| 38 \|\|*

The celestial voice said:—

38\. “O Bāṇa, O great hero, you shall not be angry. “O devotee of Śiva, O intelligent one, you are the son of Bali. Ponder over this.

## \|\| 6.53.39 \|\|

*śivassarveśvarassākṣī karmaṇāṃ parameśvaraḥ \|*  
*tadadhīnamidaṃ sarvaṃ jagadvai sacarācaram \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Śiva, the lord of all, the supreme lord, is the witness of all activities. This entire universe including the mobile and immobile beings is subservient to him.

## \|\| 6.53.40 \|\|

*sa eva kartā bhartā ca saṃhartā jagatāṃ sadā \|*  
*rajassattvatamodhārī vidhiviṣṇuharātmakaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. He alone is the creator, maintainer and the destroyer of the worlds, always taking up the attributes of Rajas, Sattva and Tamas in the form of Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva.

## \|\| 6.53.41 \|\|

*sarvasyāṃtargataḥ svāmī prerakassarvataḥ paraḥ \|*  
*nirvikāryavyayo nityo māyādhīśopi nirguṇaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. The lord is omnipresent. He is the inducer, greater than all. He is free from aberrations, unchanging, eternal, the lord of illusion and devoid of attributes.

## \|\| 6.53.42 \|\|

*tasyecchayā'balo jñeyo balī bali varātmaja \|*  
*iti vijñāya manasi svastho bhava mahāmate \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Even a weak person becomes strong, thanks to his will, O excellent son of Bali. O intelligent one, realise this in your mind, be normal and complacent.

## \|\| 6.53.43 \|\|

*garvāpahārī bhagavānnā nālīlāviśāradaḥ \|*  
*nāśayiṣyati te garvamidānīṃ bhaktavatsalaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. The lord who quells pride, who is an expert in various sports and who is favourably disposed to his devotees will destroy your arrogance.”

## \|\| 6.53.44 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityābhāṣya nabhovāṇī virarāma mahāmune \|*  
*bāṇāsurastadvacanādaniruddhaṃ na jaghnivān \|\| 44 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

44\. O great sage, having spoken thus, the celestial voice stopped. On hearing these words the Asura Bāṇa did not kill Aniruddha.

## \|\| 6.53.45 \|\|

*kiṃ tu svāntaḥpuraṃ gatvā papau pānamanuttamam \|*  
*madvākyaṃ ca visasmāra vijahāra viruddhadhīḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Then he went to his harem and drank excellent beverages. His intellect was adversely affected, he forgot those words and began to sport.

## \|\| 6.53.46 \|\|

*tatoniruddho baddhastu nāgabhogairviṣolbaṇaiḥ \|*  
*priyayā'tṛptacetāstu durgāṃ sasmāra tatkṣaṇāt \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Aniruddha was bound by serpentine bodies emitting poison powerfully. His passion for his beloved had not been satiated fully. He remembered Durgā then.

## \|\| 6.53.47 \|\|

*aniruddha uvāca \|*  
*śaraṇye devi baddhosmi dahyamānastu pannagaiḥ \|*  
*āgaccha me kuru trāṇaṃ yaśode caṃḍaroṣiṇi \|\| 47 \|\|*

Aniruddha said:—

47\. O goddess, you are worthy of being resorted to. I have been bound by serpents. O goddess bestowing fame, O goddess of fierce fury, come and save me.

## \|\| 6.53.48 \|\|

*śivabhakte mahādevi sṛṣṭisthityaṃtakāriṇī \|*  
*tvāṃ vinā rakṣako nānyastasmādrakṣa śive hi mām \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. O great goddess, devotee of Śiva, O cause of creation, sustenance and dissolution, there is no other saviour except you. O Śivā, save me.

## \|\| 6.53.49 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*tenetthaṃ toṣitā tatra kālī bhinnāṃjanaprabhā \|*  
*jyeṣṭhakṛṣṇacaturdaśyāṃ saṃprāptāsīnmahāniśi \|\| 49 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

49\. Propitiated by him, Kālī, lustrous like the split collyrium, arrived there in the dark night of the fourteenth day in the dark half of the month Jyeṣṭha.

## \|\| 6.53.50-51 \|\|

*gurubhirmuṣṭinirghātairdārayāmāsa paṃjaram \|*  
*śarāṃstānbhasmasātkṛtvā sarparūpānbhayānakān \|\| 50 \|\|*

*mocayitvā niruddhaṃ tu tataścāṃtaḥpuraṃ tataḥ \|*  
*praveśayitvā durgā tu tatraivādarśanaṃ gatā \|\| 51 \|\|*

50-51. With the heavy blows of her fists she broke the cage. She reduced the serpentine arrows to ashes. She released Aniruddha and let him enter the harem and then vanished from the scene.

## \|\| 6.53.52 \|\|

*itthaṃ devyāḥ prasādāttu śivaśaktermunīśvara \|*  
*kṛcchramuktoniruddhobhūtsukhī caiva gatavyathaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. O great sage, thus, thanks to the grace of the goddess—the Energy of Śiva, Aniruddha got rid of the difficulty, became free from pain and obtained happiness.

## \|\| 6.53.53 \|\|

*atha labdhajayo bhūtvāniruddhaśśivaśaktitaḥ \|*  
*prādyumnirbāṇatanayāṃ priyāṃ prāpya mumoda ca \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Securing success by means of Śiva’s Energy, Aniruddha the son of Pradyumna gained access to his beloved, the daughter of Bāṇa and rejoiced.

## \|\| 6.53.54 \|\|

*pūrvaṃvadvijahārāsau tayā svapriyayā sukhī \|*  
*pītapānassuraktākṣassa bāṇasutayā tataḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. In the company of his beloved—the daughter of Bāṇa, he carried on dalliance and was happy drinking the beverages till his eyes became red.

## Chapter 54 - The fight among Bāṇa, Śiva, Kṛṣṇa and others

## \|\| 6.54.1 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*aniruddhe hṛtai pautre kṛṣṇasya munisattama \|*  
*kuṃbhāṃḍasutayā kṛṣṇaḥ kimakārṣīddhi tadvada \|\| 1 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:—

1\. O excellent sage, when Aniruddha the grandson of Kṛṣṇa was abducted by the daughter of Kumbhāṇḍa what did Kṛṣṇa do? Please narrate it to me.

## \|\| 6.54.2 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*tato gate'niruddhe tu tatstrīṇāṃ rodanasvanam \|*  
*śrutvā ca vyathitaḥ kṛṣṇo babhūva munisattama \|\| 2 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

2\. O excellent sage, on hearing the woeful cries of his women when Aniruddha had gone off suddenly, Kṛṣṇa too became vexed.

## \|\| 6.54.3 \|\|

*apaśyatāṃ cāniruddhaṃ tadbaṃdhūnāṃ harestathā \|*  
*catvāro vārṣikā māsā vyatīyuranuśocatām \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The four months of the rainy season thus went by when his relatives and Viṣṇu could not see Aniruddha and so they bewailed.

## \|\| 6.54.4 \|\|

*nāradāttadupākarṇya vārtāṃ baddhasya karma ca \|*  
*āsansuvyathitāssarve vṛṣṇayaḥ kṛṣṇadevatāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. On hearing from Nārada about the imprisonment and activities of Aniruddha the Vṛṣṇis, followers of Kṛṣṇa, became dejected.

## \|\| 6.54.5 \|\|

*kṛṣṇastadvṛttamakhilaṃ śrutvā yuddhāya cādarāt \|*  
*jagāma śoṇitapuraṃ tārkṣyamāhūya tatkṣaṇāt \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. On hearing everything, Kṛṣṇa immediately called Garuḍa and went to the city of Śoṇita eagerly for fighting.

## \|\| 6.54.6 \|\|

*pradyumno yuyudhānaśca gatassāṃbotha sāraṇaḥ \|*  
*naṃdopanaṃdabhadrādyā rāmakṛṣṇānuvartinaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Pradyumna, Yuyudhāna, Sāmba, Sāraṇa, Nanda, Upananda, Bhadra and others following Rāma and Kṛṣṇa went there.

## \|\| 6.54.7 \|\|

*akṣauhiṇībhirdvādaśabhissametāsarvato diśam \|*  
*rurudhurbāṇanagaraṃ samaṃtātsātvatarṣabhāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. They were accompanied by twelve Akṣauhiṇīs. They, the chief of Sātvatas laid a siege all round the city of Bāṇa.

## \|\| 6.54.8 \|\|

*bhajyamānapurodyānaprākārāṭṭālagopuram \|*  
*vīkṣyamāṇo ruṣāviṣṭastulyasainyobhiniryayau \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. On seeing the parks, fortresses, ceilings and minarets of the city thus broken, Bāṇa became infuriated and set forth with an equal number of armies.

## \|\| 6.54.9 \|\|

*bāṇārthe bhagavān rudrassasutaḥ pramathairvṛtaḥ \|*  
*āruhya nandivṛṣabhaṃ yuddhaṃ karttuṃ samāyayau \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. In order to help Bāṇa, lord Rudra accompanied by his son and the Pramathas rode on the bull Nandin and arrived there to fight.

## \|\| 6.54.10 \|\|

*āsītsutumulaṃ yuddhamadbhutaṃ lomaharṣaṇam \|*  
*kṛṣṇādikānāṃ taistatra rudrādyairbāṇarakṣakaiḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. A tumultuous fight, wonderfully causing horripilation ensued between Kṛṣṇa and his followers on the one hand and the supporters of Bāṇa, Rudra etc. on the other.

## \|\| 6.54.11 \|\|

*kṛṣṇaśaṃkarayorāsītpradyumnaguhayorapi \|*  
*kūṣmāṃḍakūpakarṇābhyāṃ balena saha saṃyugaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The fight was between Kṛṣṇa and Śiva; Pradyumna and Kārttikeya; Kumbhāṇḍaka and Kūpakarṇa, Bala and Saṃyuga.

## \|\| 6.54.12 \|\|

*sāṃbasya bāṇaputreṇa bāṇena saha sātyakeḥ \|*  
*nandinā garuḍasyāpi pareṣāṃ ca parairapi \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Sāmba fought with Bāṇa’s son; Sātyaki with Bāṇa; Garuḍa with Nandin and groups of one side fought with the groups of the other.

## \|\| 6.54.13 \|\|

*brahmādayassurādhīśā munayaḥ siddhacāraṇāḥ \|*  
*gaṃdharvā'psaraso yānairvimānairdraṣṭumāgaman \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Brahmā and other gods, sages, Siddhas, Cāraṇas, Gandharvas and celestial damsels came there in aerial chariots to witness the affray.

## \|\| 6.54.14 \|\|

*pramathairvividhākārai revatyaṃtaiḥ sudāruṇam \|*  
*yuddhaṃ babhūva viprendra teṣāṃ ca yaduvaṃśinām \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. O best of brahmins, a terrible fight ensued between the members of the Yadu family with the groups of Pramathas ending with “Revatīs”.

## \|\| 6.54.15 \|\|

*bhrātrā rāmeṇa sahitaḥ pradyumnena ca dhīmatā \|*  
*kṛṣṇaścakāra samaramatulaṃ pramathaissaha \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Kṛṣṇa, his brother Rāma and the intelligent Pradyumna, fought an unequalled fight with the Pramathas.

## \|\| 6.54.16-17 \|\|

*tatrāgninā'bhavadyuddhaṃ yamena varuṇena ca \|*  
*vimukhena tripādena jvareṇa ca guhena ca \|\| 16 \|\|*

*pramathairvividhākāraisteṣāmanyaṃ tadāruṇam \|*  
*yuddhaṃ babhūva vikaṭaṃ vṛṣṇīnāṃ romaharṣaṇam \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. The fight continued with Agni, Yama, Varuṇa, Vimukha, Tripāda, Jvara and Kārttikeya and groups of Pramathas with the Vṛṣṇis. It was terrible and frightful causing horripilation.

## \|\| 6.54.18 \|\|

*vibhīṣikābhirbahvībhiḥ koṭarībhiḥ padepade \|*  
*nirllajjābhiśca nārībhiḥ prabalābhiradūrataḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. There was fight with the shameless women too, several groups of terrifying Koṭarīs at every step, not far from one another.

## \|\| 6.54.19 \|\|

*śaṃkarānucarāñśaurirbhūtapramathaguhyakān \|*  
*drāvayāmāsa tīkṣṇāgraiḥ śaraiḥ śārṅgadhanuścyutaiḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Kṛṣṇa routed the Bhūtas, Pramathas and Guhyakas, the followers of Śiva with sharp-pointed arrows discharged from his bow.

## \|\| 6.54.20 \|\|

*evaṃ pradyumnapramukhā vīrā yuddhamahotsavāḥ \|*  
*cakruryuddhaṃ mahāghoraṃ śatrusainyaṃ vināśayan \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. The heroes Pradyumna and others jubilant over the war destroyed the armies of the enemies and fought terribly.

## \|\| 6.54.21 \|\|

*viśīryamāṇaṃ svabalaṃ dṛṣṭvā rudrotyamarṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*krodhaṃ cakāra sumahannanāda ca maholbaṇam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. On seeing his army being scattered, Śiva became highly infuriated and roared terribly.

## \|\| 6.54.22 \|\|

*tacchrutvā śaṃkaragaṇā vineduryuyudhuśca te \|*  
*mardayanpratiyoddhāraṃ varddhitāśśaṃbhutejasā \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. On hearing that, Śiva’s Gaṇas too shouted and fought. They suppressed the opponents with their strength increased by Śiva’s brilliance.

## \|\| 6.54.23 \|\|

*pṛthagvidhāni cāyuktaṃ śārṅgāstrāṇi pinākine \|*  
*pratyakṣaiśśamayāmāsa śūlapāṇiravismitaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Kṛṣṇa discharged separate types of missiles from his bow towards the trident-bearing lord Śiva who without showing any dismay quelled them directly.

## \|\| 6.54.24 \|\|

*brahmāstrasya ca brahmāstraṃ vāyavyasya ca pārvatam \|*  
*āgneyasya ca pārjanyaṃ naijaṃ nārāyaṇasya ca \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. They discharged Brahmā-missile in counter to Brahmā missile; the mountain-missile to the wind-missile; the cloud-missile to the fire-missile and Śiva-missile to the Nārāyaṇa missile.

## \|\| 6.54.25 \|\|

*kṛṣṇasainyaṃ vidudrāva prativīreṇa nirjitam \|*  
*na tasthau samare vyāsa pūrṇarudrasutejasā \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Defeated by the opponents, the army of Kṛṣṇa fled, O Vyāsa; it could not face the full refulgence of Śiva.

## \|\| 6.54.26 \|\|

*vidrāvite svasainye tu śrīkṛṣṇaśca paraṃtapaḥ \|*  
*svaṃ jvaraṃ śītalākhyaṃ hi vyasṛjaddāruṇaṃ mune \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. O sage, when his army was routed, lord Kṛṣṇa, the scorcher of enemies, discharged terrible fever missile named ‘cold’.

## \|\| 6.54.27 \|\|

*vidrāvite kṛṣṇasainye kṛṣṇasya śītalajvaraḥ \|*  
*abhyapadyata taṃ rudraṃ mune daśadiśo dahan \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. O sage, when the army of Kṛṣṇa was routed, the cold fever missile of Kṛṣṇa rushed at Rudra blazing the ten quarters.

## \|\| 6.54.28 \|\|

*maheśvarotha' taṃ dṛṣṭvāyāṃtaṃ svaṃ visṛjajjvaram \|*  
*māheśvaro vaiṣṇavaśca yuyudhāte jvarāvubhau \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. On seeing that coming, lord Śiva discharged his own fever missile. The two fever missiles fought each other.

## \|\| 6.54.29 \|\|

*vaiṣṇavo'tha samākradanmāheśvarabalārditaḥ \|*  
*alabdhvā bhayamanyatra tuṣṭāva vṛṣabhadhvajam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Oppressed by the fever missile of lord Śiva, the fever missile of Śiva cried aloud. Unable to secure succour elsewhere, it eulogised the bull-bannered lord.

## \|\| 6.54.30 \|\|

*atha prasanno bhagavānviṣṇujvaranuto haraḥ \|*  
*viṣṇuśītajvaraṃ prāha śaraṇāgatavatsalaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. The delighted lord Śiva, favourably disposed to those who seek refuge, eulogised by Viṣṇu’s fever missile, spoke to the cold fever missile of Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 6.54.31 \|\|

*maheśvara uvāca \|*  
*śītajvara prasanno'haṃ vyetu te majjvarādbhayam \|*  
*yo nau smarati saṃvādaṃ tasya na syājjvarādbhayam \|\| 31 \|\|*

Lord Śiva said:—

31\. “O cold fever, I am delighted. Leave off your fear from my fever. There is no fear from fever to him who remembers this anecdote.

## \|\| 6.54.32 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityukto rudramānamya gato nārāyaṇajvaraḥ \|*  
*taṃ dṛṣṭvā caritaṃ kṛṣṇo visismāya bhayānvitaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

32\. Thus advised, the fever missile of Viṣṇu went away after bowing to Śiva. On seeing that activity, Kṛṣṇa was surprised and dismayed.

## \|\| 6.54.33 \|\|

*skanda pradyumnabāṇaughairardyamāno'tha kopitaḥ \|*  
*jaghāna śaktyā pradyumnaṃ daityasaṃghātyamarṣaṇaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. When attacked by the arrows of Pradyumna, the infuriated Kārttikeya, the slayer of Daityas, hit Pradyumna with his spear.

## \|\| 6.54.34 \|\|

*skaṃdaprāptihatastatra pradyumnaḥ prabalopi hi \|*  
*asṛgvimuṃcangātrebhyo balenāpākramadraṇāt \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. When hit by Kārttikeya’s spear, Pradyumna, though very strong, shed blood from his limbs and fled from the battle ground.

## \|\| 6.54.35 \|\|

*kuṃbhāṃḍakūpakarṇābhyāṃ nānāstraiśca samāhataḥ \|*  
*dudrāva balabhadropi na tasthepi raṇe balī \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Hit with various missiles by Kumbhāṇḍa and Kūpakarṇa, Balabhadra though strong did not stay there. He fled from the battle-field.

## \|\| 6.54.36 \|\|

*kṛtvā sahasraṃ kāyānāṃ pītvā toyaṃ mahārṇavāt \|*  
*garuḍo nāśayatyarthā''vartairmeghārṇavāṃbubhiḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Garuḍa, took up a thousand bodies and drank up the water from the great sea. He then began to work havoc by showering the sea-waters through Āvarta clouds.

## \|\| 6.54.37 \|\|

*atha kruddho maheśasya vāhano vṛṣabho balī \|*  
*vegena mahatāraṃ vai śṛṃgābhyāṃ nijaghāna tam \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Then the infuriated bull, the powerful vehicle of lord Śiva, hit him with great force by means of his horns.

## \|\| 6.54.38 \|\|

*śṛṃgaghātaviśīrṇāṃgo garuḍo'tīva vismitaḥ \|*  
*vidudrāva raṇāttūrṇaṃ vihāya ca janārdanam \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. When his limbs were shattered by the blows of his horns, Garuḍa was dismayed. He forsook Viṣṇu and fled from the battle ground immediately.

## \|\| 6.54.39 \|\|

*evaṃ jāte caritraṃ tu bhagavāndevakīsutaḥ \|*  
*uvāca sārathiṃ śīghraṃ rudratejotivismitaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. When the situation was like this, lord Kṛṣṇa, dismayed by Śiva’s refulgence spoke to the charioteer suddenly.

## \|\| 6.54.40 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*he sūta śṛṇu madvākyaṃ rathaṃ me vāhaya drutam \|*  
*mahādevasamīpastho yathā syāṃ gadituṃ vacaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

Lord Kṛṣṇa said:—

40\. O charioteer, listen to my words. Drive the chariot immediately to lord Śiva so that I shall speak to him.

## \|\| 6.54.41 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityukto hariṇā sūto dārukassvaguṇāgraṇīḥ \|*  
*drutaṃ taṃ vāhayāmāsa rathaṃ rudrasamīpataḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

41\. Thus commanded by Viṣṇu, the charioteer Dāruka, the foremost of persons of good qualities, drove the chariot immediately to lord Śiva.

## \|\| 6.54.42 \|\|

*atha vijñāpayāmāsa nato bhūtvā kṛtāṃjaliḥ \|*  
*śrīkṛṣṇaḥ śaṃkaraṃ bhaktyā prapanno bhaktavatsalam \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Lord Kṛṣṇa resorted to Śiva, favourably disposed to his devotees, bowed to him with devotion with palms joined in reverence and submitted as follows.

## \|\| 6.54.43 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*devadeva mahādeva śaraṇāgatavatsala \|*  
*namāmi tvā'naṃtaśaktiṃ sarvātmānaṃ pareśvaram \|\| 43 \|\|*

Lord Kṛṣṇa said:—

43\. O lord Śiva, lord of the gods, favourably disposed to those who seek refuge in you, I bow to you the great lord, the soul of all and of infinite power.

## \|\| 6.54.44 \|\|

*viśvotpattisthānanāśahetuṃ sajjñapti mātrakam \|*  
*brahmaliṃgaṃ paraṃ śāṃtaṃ kevalaṃ parameśvaram \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. I bow to you, the cause of the origin, sustenance and dissolution of the universe, the sole form of perfect knowledge, the symbol of Brahman, the highly quiescent, the supreme lord.

## \|\| 6.54.45-46 \|\|

*kālo daivaṃ karma jīvassvabhāvo dravyameva ca \|*  
*kṣetraṃ ca prāṇa ātmā ca vikārastatsamūhakaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

*bījarohapravāhastu tvanmāyaiṣā jagatprabho \|*  
*tannibaṃdhaṃ prapadyeha tvāmahaṃ parameśvaram \|\| 46 \|\|*

45-46. The time, the divinity, the activity, the individual soul, the nature, the solid objects, the vital airs, the soul, the groups of created beings, the series of seeds and sprouts everything is your illusion, O lord of the universe. I resort to you the cause of those things, the great lord.

## \|\| 6.54.47 \|\|

*nānā bhāvairlīlayaiva svīkṛtairnirjarādikān \|*  
*nūnaṃ bibhaṣiṃ lokeśo haṃsyunmārgānsvabhāvataḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. By the different forms assumed by you sportively, you, the lord of the worlds, support the gods and others and destroy those who go astray.

## \|\| 6.54.48 \|\|

*tvaṃ hi brahma paraṃ jyotirgūḍhaṃ brahmaṇi vāṅmaye \|*  
*yaṃ paśyaṃtyamalātmānamākāśamiva kevalam \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. You are the Brahman, the great light that is hidden in the Śabda Brahman which the purified souls see like the sole firmament.

## \|\| 6.54.49 \|\|

*tvameva cādyaḥ puruṣo'dvitīyasturya ātmadṛk \|*  
*īśo heturahetuśca savikāraḥ pratīyase \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. You are the primordial Puruṣa without a second. You are the fourth being, the vision of the soul. You appear as undergoing change though you are the lord, the cause without another cause unto you.

## \|\| 6.54.50 \|\|

*svamāyayā sarvaguṇaprasiddhyai bhagavanprabho \|*  
*sarvānvitaḥ prabhinnaśca sarvatastvaṃ maheśvara \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. O lord, for the manifestation of all the attributes, you appear different through your illusion, O supreme lord.

## \|\| 6.54.51 \|\|

*yathaiva sūryo'pihitaśchāyārūpāṇi ca prabho \|*  
*svacchāyayā saṃcakāsti hyayaṃ paramadṛgbhavān \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. O lord, just as the unconcealed sun illuminates many of his reflections by his brilliance, so you too do, being the great illuminating light.

## \|\| 6.54.52 \|\|

*guṇenāpihitopi tvaṃ guṇe va guṇān vibho \|*  
*svapradīpaścakāssi tvaṃ bhūman giriśa śaṃkara \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. O great one, O self-illuminated lord Śiva, you brighten the attributes by means of the attribute itself, though you are not encompassed by the attribute.

## \|\| 6.54.53 \|\|

*tvanmāyāmohitadhiyaḥ putradāragṛhādiṣu \|*  
*unmajjaṃti nimajjaṃti prasaktā vṛjinārṇave \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. People whose intellects are deluded by your illusion become attached to sons, wives, abodes etc. and sink and float in the ocean of sin.

## \|\| 6.54.54 \|\|

*daivadattamimaṃ labdhvā nṛlokamajitendriyaḥ \|*  
*yo nādriyeta tvatpādau sa śocyo hyātmavaṃcakaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. After deriving this divinely bestowed human habitation, if a person does not control his sense-organs and respect your feet he is to be pitied. He deceives his own self.

## \|\| 6.54.55 \|\|

*tvadājñayāhaṃ bhagavānbāṇadośchettumāgataḥ \|*  
*tvayaiva śapto bāṇo'yaṃ garvito garvahāriṇā \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. O lord, it is at your bidding that I have come here to cut off the hands of Bāṇa. This haughty Bāṇa was cursed by you who are the destroyer of haughtiness.

## \|\| 6.54.56 \|\|

*nivarttasva raṇā ddeva tvacchāpo na vṛthā bhavet \|*  
*ājñāṃ dehi prabho me tvaṃ bāṇasya bhujakṛṃtane \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. O lord, please return from the battle-ground. Let not your curse go in vain. O lord, command me to cut off the hands of Bāṇa.

## \|\| 6.54.57 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya vacaśśaṃbhuḥ śrīkṛṣṇasya munīśvara \|*  
*pratyuvāca prasannātmā kṛṣṇastutyā maheśvaraḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

57\. O great sage, on hearing these words of lord Kṛṣṇa, Śiva the supreme lord who was propitiated by Kṛṣṇa’s eulogy, replied:—

## \|\| 6.54.58 \|\|

*maheśvara uvāca \|*  
*satyamuktaṃ tvayā tāta mayā śapto hi daityarāṭ \|*  
*madājñayā bhavānprāpto bāṇadodaṃḍakṛṃtane \|\| 58 \|\|*

Lord Śiva said:—

58\. O dear, what you say is true; the lord of the Daityas has been cursed by me. It is at my bidding that you have come here to cut off the hands of Bāṇa.

## \|\| 6.54.59 \|\|

*kiṃ karomi ramānātha bhaktādhīnassadā hare \|*  
*paśyato me kathaṃ vīra syādbāṇabhujakṛṃtanam \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. O lord of Lakṣmī, what can I do? O Viṣnu, I am subservient to my devotees always. How can there be the chopping of Bāṇa’s arms while I am watching?

## \|\| 6.54.60 \|\|

*atastvaṃ jṛṃbhaṇāstreṇa māṃ jaṃbhaya madājñayā \|*  
*tatastvaṃ kuru kāryaṃ svaṃ yatheṣṭaṃ ca sukhī bhava \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Hence at my bidding make me benumbed by means of your Jṛṃbhaṇa missile. Thereafter you can do as you please and be happy.

## \|\| 6.54.61 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityuktaśśaṃkareṇātha śārṅgapāṇistu vismitaḥ \|*  
*svaraṇasthānamāgatya mumoda sa munīśvaraḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

61\. O great sage, thus urged by Śiva, lord Kṛṣṇa was surprised. He returned to the battlefield and rejoiced.

## \|\| 6.54.62 \|\|

*jṛṃbhaṇāstraṃ mumocātha saṃdhāya dhanuṣi drutam \|*  
*pinākapāṇaye vyāsa nānāstrakuśalo hariḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. O Vyāsa, Viṣnu an expert in the use of various missiles fixed the Jṛmbhaṇa missile to the bow and discharged it at Śiva.

## \|\| 6.54.63 \|\|

*mohayitvā tu giriśaṃ jṛṃbhaṇāstreṇa jṛṃbhitam \|*  
*bāṇasya pṛtanāṃ śaurirjaghānāsigadarṣṭibhiḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. After enchanting Śiva, and making him benumbed by means of the Jṛmbhaṇa missile, Viṣṇu slew the army of Bāṇa by means of swords, daggers and clubs.

## Chapter 55 - The chopping of Bāna’s arms and his humiliation

## \|\| 6.55.1 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*sanatkumāra sarvajña brahmaputra namostu te \|*  
*adbhuteyaṃ kathā tāta śrāvitā me tvayā mune \|\| 1 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:—

1\. O dear sage, Sanatkumāra, O omniscient son of Brahmā, obeisance be to you. A wonderful story has been narrated to me by you.

## \|\| 6.55.2 \|\|

*jṛṃbhite jṛṃbhaṇāstreṇa hariṇā samare hare \|*  
*hate bāṇabale bāṇaḥ kimakārṣīcca tadvada \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. When Śiva was made to yawn and lie flat by Viṣṇu through the Jṛmbhaṇa missile, in the course of the war and when the army of Bāṇa was slain, what did Bāṇa do? Please narrate.

## \|\| 6.55.3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya vacastasya vyāsasyāmitatejasaḥ \|*  
*pratyuvāca prasannātmā brahmaputro munīśvaraḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sūta said:—

3\. On hearing these words of Vyāsa of immeasurable refulgence, the great sage, the delighted son of Brahmā, replied.

## \|\| 6.55.4 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu vyāsa mahāprājña kathāṃ ca paramādbhutām \|*  
*kṛṣṇaśaṃkarayostāta lokalīlānusāriṇoḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

4\. O Vyāsa of great intellect, listen to the highly wonderful story of Kṛṣṇa and Śiva who indulge in sports in accordance with the worldly conventions.

## \|\| 6.55.5 \|\|

*śayite līlayā rudre saputre sagaṇe sati \|*  
*bāṇo vinirgato yuddhaṃ kartuṃ kṛṣṇena daityarāṭ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. When Śiva sportively lay flat on the ground along with his sons and Gaṇas, Bāṇa the king of Daityas came out to fight with Kṛṣṇa.

## \|\| 6.55.6 \|\|

*kuṃbhāṃḍasaṃgṛhītāśvo nānāśastrāstradhṛk tataḥ \|*  
*cakāra yuddhamatulaṃ baliputro mahābalaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. With the horses mobilised by Kumbhāṇḍa, and holding various weapons and missiles, the powerful son of Bali performed an incomparable fight.

## \|\| 6.55.7 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā nijabalaṃ naṣṭaṃ sa daityendro'tyamarṣitaḥ \|*  
*cakāra yuddhamatulaṃ bali putro mahābalaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. On seeing his army destroyed, the lord of the Daityas became infuriated. The powerful son of Bali fought an incomparable battle.

## \|\| 6.55.8 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇopi mahāvīro giriśāptamahābalaḥ \|*  
*uccairjagarja tatrājau bāṇaṃ matvā tṛṇopamam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Lord Kṛṣṇa the great hero with additional strength derived from Śiva roared loudly in the battlefield considering Bāṇa as insignificant as a blade of grass.

## \|\| 6.55.9 \|\|

*dhanuṣṭaṃkārayāmāsa śārṅgākhyaṃ nijamadbhutam \|*  
*trāsayanbāṇasainyaṃ tadavaśiṣṭaṃ munīśvara \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. O great sage, he made the twanging sound on his wonderful bow called Śārṅga and frightened what little remained of Bāṇa’s army.

## \|\| 6.55.10 \|\|

*tena nādena mahatā dhanuṣṭaṃkārajena hi \|*  
*dyāvābhūmyoraṃtaraṃ vai vyāptamāsīdanaṃtaram \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The intervening space between heaven and Earth was filled with the great sound originating from the twang on his bow.

## \|\| 6.55.11 \|\|

*cikṣepa vividhānbāṇānbāṇāya kupito hariḥ \|*  
*karṇāntaṃ tadvikṛṣyātha tīkṣṇānāśīviṣopamān \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Drawing the string of his bow upto the ear, the infuriated Viṣṇu discharged sharp arrows, as furious as serpents, on Bāṇa.

## \|\| 6.55.12 \|\|

*āyātāṃstānnirīkṣyā'tha sa bāṇo balinandanaḥ \|*  
*aprāptāneva ciccheda svaśaraissvadhanuścyutaiḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. On seeing the arrows coming, Bāṇa the son of Bali, split them even before they reached him, by means of arrows discharged from his bow.

## \|\| 6.55.13 \|\|

*punarjagarja sa vibhurbāṇo vairigaṇārdanaḥ \|*  
*tatrasurvṛṣṇayassarve kṛṣṇātmāno vicetasaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Lord Bāṇa, suppressor of enemies roared again. The Vṛṣṇis thinking of Kṛṣṇa were afraid and dejected.

## \|\| 6.55.14 \|\|

*smṛtvā śivapadāmbhojaṃ cikṣepa nijasāyakān \|*
