*sa kṛṣṇāyātiśūrāya mahāgarvo balessutaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Thinking upon the lotus-like feet of Śiva, the haughty son of Bali discharged his arrows at Krṣṇa the most valorous.

## \|\| 6.55.15 \|\|

*kṛṣṇopi tānasaṃprāptānacchinatsaśarairdrutam \|*  
*smṛtvā śivapadāmbhojamamarāri mahābalaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Thinking upon the lotus-like feet of Śiva, the powerful destroyer of Asuras, Kṛṣṇa split them before they reached him by means of his own arrows.

## \|\| 6.55.16 \|\|

*rāmādayo vṛṣṇayaśca svaṃsvaṃ yoddhāramāhave \|*  
*nijaghnurbalinassarve kṛtvā krodhaṃ samākulāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Rāma and other Vṛṣṇis, the powerful ones agitated by anger, slew their respective opponents.

## \|\| 6.55.17 \|\|

*itthaṃ cirataraṃ tatra balinośca dvayorapi \|*  
*babhūva tumulaṃ yuddhaṃ śṛṇvatāṃ vismayāvaham \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Thus the tumultuous fight between the two strong armies went on for a long time aggravating the wonder of the spectators.

## \|\| 6.55.18 \|\|

*tasminnavasare tatra krodhaṃ kṛtvā'tipakṣirāṭ \|*  
*bāṇāsurabalaṃ sarvaṃ pakṣāghātairamardayat \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. In the meantime the infuriated king of birds suppressed the army of Bāṇa striking all with his wings.

## \|\| 6.55.19 \|\|

*marditaṃ svabalaṃ dṛṣṭvā mardayaṃtaṃ ca taṃ balī \|*  
*cukopāti baleḥ putraḥ śaivarāḍ ditijeśvaraḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Seeing his army routed and himself oppressed, Bāṇa, the powerful lord of Daityas, son of Bali, foremost among Śiva’s devotees, was infuriated.

## \|\| 6.55.20 \|\|

*smṛtvā śivapadāmbhojaṃ sahasrabhujavāndrutam \|*  
*mahatparākramaṃ cakre vairiṇāṃ dussahaṃ sa vai \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Thinking upon the lotus-like feet of Śiva, the thousand-armed Bāṇa displayed his valour unbearable to his enemies.

## \|\| 6.55.21 \|\|

*cikṣepa yugapadbāṇānamitāṃstatra vīrahā \|*  
*kṛṣṇādisarvayaduṣu garuḍe ca pṛthakpṛthak \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. The destroyer of heroes discharged simultaneously an unlimited number of arrows on Garuḍa, Kṛṣṇa and Yadus separately.

## \|\| 6.55.22 \|\|

*jaghānaikena garuḍaṃ kṛṣṇamekena pattriṇā \|*  
*balamekena ca mune parānapi tathā balī \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. O sage, he hit Garuḍa with an arrow, Kṛṣṇa with another, Bala with a third. The powerful hero hit others too.

## \|\| 6.55.23 \|\|

*tataḥ kṛṣṇo mahāvīryo viṣṇurūpassurārihā \|*  
*cukopātiraṇe tasmiñjagarja ca maheśvaraḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Then Kṛṣṇa the great lord, of great valour, of the form of Viṣṇu, the destroyer of demons, became angry and roared in the course of the battle.

## \|\| 6.55.24 \|\|

*jaghāna bāṇaṃ tarasā śārṅganissṛtasaccharaiḥ \|*  
*ati tadbalamatyugraṃ yugapatsmṛtaśaṃkaraḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Thinking upon Śiva he hit Bāṇa and his terrible army simultaneously with the good arrows discharged with force from his bow.

## \|\| 6.55.25 \|\|

*ciccheda taddhanuśśīghraṃ chatrādikamanā kulaḥ \|*  
*hayāṃśca pātayāmāsa hatvā tānsvaśarairhariḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Viṣṇu split his bow and umbrella as well as other things. Without being excited he killed and felled his horses by means of his arrows.

## \|\| 6.55.26 \|\|

*bāṇo'pi ca mahāvīro jagarjāti prakupya ha \|*  
*kṛṣṇaṃ jaghāna gadayā so'pataddharaṇītale \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Bāṇa the great hero roared furiously. He hit Kṛṣṇa with his iron club and Kṛṣṇa fell on the ground.

## \|\| 6.55.27 \|\|

*utthāyāraṃ tataḥ kṛṣṇo yuyudhe tena śatruṇā \|*  
*śivabhaktena devarṣe lokalīlā'nusārataḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. O celestial sage, Kṛṣṇa got up immediately and fought with Bāṇa, the great devotee of Śiva. It was to keep up the worldly sport that he fought thus.

## \|\| 6.55.28 \|\|

*evaṃ dvayościraṃ kāla babhūva sumahānraṇaḥ \|*  
*śivarūpo hariḥ kṛṣṇaḥ sa ca śaivottamo balī \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. A great battle went on for a long time between Kṛṣṇa who was Viṣṇu or Śiva himself and that strong Asura who was the most excellent devotee of Śiva.

## \|\| 6.55.29 \|\|

*kṛṣṇo'tha kṛtvā samaraṃ ciraṃ bāṇena vīryavān \|*  
*śivā''jñayā prāptabalaścukopāti munīśvaraḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. O great sage, the powerful Kṛṣṇa fought for a long time with Bāṇa. Deriving strength at the instance of Śiva he became furious.

## \|\| 6.55.30 \|\|

*tatassudarśanenāśu kṛṣṇo bāṇabhujānbahūn \|*  
*ciccheda bhagavāñśaṃbhu śāsanātparavīrahā \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. At the bidding of Śiva, lord Kṛṣṇa, the destroyer of heroic enemies, chopped off several arms of Bāṇa by means of Sudarśana.

## \|\| 6.55.31 \|\|

*avaśiṣṭā bhujāstasya catvāro'tīva sundarāḥ \|*  
*gatavyatho babhūvāśu śaṃkarasya prasādataḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Only his four beautiful arms were left. Thanks to the grace of Śiva, the demon too was freed from pain.

## \|\| 6.55.32 \|\|

*gatasmṛtiryadā bāṇa śiraśchettuṃ samudyataḥ \|*  
*kṛṣṇo vīratvamāpannastadā rudrassamutthitaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Forgetting himself, Kṛṣṇa who assumed a great prowess, attempted to cut off the head of Bāṇa. Then Śiva got up.

## \|\| 6.55.33 \|\|

*rudra uvāca \|*  
*bhagavandevakīputra yadājñaptaṃ mayā purā \|*  
*tatkṛtaṃ ca tvayā vipra madājñākāriṇā sadā \|\| 33 \|\|*

Śiva said:—

33\. O lord, son of Devakī, O Viṣṇu, what was ordained by me formerly has been accomplished by you who always follow my dictates.

## \|\| 6.55.34 \|\|

*mā bāṇasya śiraśchiṃdhi saṃharasva sudarśanam \|*  
*madājñayā cakramidaṃ syānmoghaṃ majjane sadā \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Do not cut off the head of Bāṇa. Withdraw your weapon Sudarśana. At my bidding the discus shall always be rendered ineffective with regard to my people.

## \|\| 6.55.35 \|\|

*dattaṃ mayā purā tubhyamanivāryaṃ raṇe tava \|*  
*cakraṃ jayaṃ ca govinda nivartasva raṇāttataḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. O Viṣṇu, this unfailing discus and victory in battle were formerly bestowed on you by me. Hence you withdraw from the battleground.

## \|\| 6.55.36 \|\|

*dadhīce rāvaṇe vīre tārakādipureṣvapi \|*  
*vinā madājñāṃ lakṣmīśa rathāṅgaṃ nāmucaḥ purā \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. O lord of Lakṣmī, you did not hurl this discus at Dadhīca, Rāvaṇa, Tāraka, Tripuras and others without my consent.

## \|\| 6.55.37 \|\|

*tvaṃ tu yogīśvarasssākṣātparamātmā janārdana \|*  
*vicāryatāṃ svamanasā sarvabhūtahite rataḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. You are a great Yogin, the supreme soul and the exciter of men. Hence you ponder over this yourself. You are engaged in the welfare of all living beings.

## \|\| 6.55.38 \|\|

*varamasya mayā dattaṃ na mṛtyurbhayamasti vai \|*  
*tanme vacassadā satyaṃ parituṣṭosmyahaṃ tava \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. I have granted him a boon that he will not fear death. These words of mine shall remain true for ever. I am pleased with you.

## \|\| 6.55.39 \|\|

*purā'yaṃ garvito matto yuddhaṃ dehīti me'bravīt \|*  
*bhujānkaṇḍūyamānastu vismṛtātmagatirhare \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. O Viṣṇu, sometime back he became haughty enough to say “Give me battle” while he scratched his arms and forgot his goal.

## \|\| 6.55.40 \|\|

*tadāhamaśapaṃ taṃ vai bhujacchettā''gamiṣyati \|*  
*acireṇātikālena gatagarvo bhaviṣyasi \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Then I cursed him—“Ere long, the person will arrive and cut off your arms. You shall be cured of your haughtiness”.

## \|\| 6.55.41 \|\|

*madājñayā hariḥ prāpto bhujacchettā tavā'tha vai \|*  
*nivartasva raṇādgaccha svagṛhaṃ savadhūvaraḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. (Turning to Baṇa) At my bidding Viṣṇu has cut off your arms. Now withdraw from the battlefield. Go back to your abode along with the married couple.

## \|\| 6.55.42 \|\|

*ityuktaḥ sa tayomaitrīṃ kārayitvā maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*tamamujñāpya sagaṇaḥ saputraḥ svālayaṃ yayau \|\| 42 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

42\. Saying this and uniting them in friendship, lord Śiva returned to his abode along with his sons and Gaṇas.

## \|\| 6.55.43 \|\|

*\|\| sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya vacaśśaṃbhossaṃhṛtya ca sudarśanam \|*  
*akṣatāṃgastu vijayī tatkṛṣṇoṃtaḥpuraṃ yayau \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. On hearing the words of Śiva, Kṛṣṇa withdrew Sudarśana. With his body unwounded, the victorious Kṛṣṇa entered into the harem.

## \|\| 6.55.44 \|\|

*aniruddhaṃ samāśvāsya sahitaṃ bhāryayā punaḥ \|*  
*jagrāha ratnasaṃghātaṃ bāṇadattamanekaśaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. He consoled Aniruddha and his wife. He accepted the jewels given in plenty by Bāṇa.

## \|\| 6.55.45 \|\|

*tatsakhīṃ citralekhāṃ ca gṛhītvā parayoginīm \|*  
*prasanno'bhūttataḥ kṛṣṇaḥ kṛtakāryaḥ śivājñayā \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. They took Ūṣā’s friend Citralekhā the great Yoginī also with them. Kṛṣṇa who accomplished his task at the bidding of Śiva was immensely pleased.

## \|\| 6.55.46 \|\|

*hṛdā praṇamya giriśamāmaṃtrya ca balestutam \|*  
*parivārasametastu jagāma svapurīṃ hariḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. After mentally bowing to Śiva, Viṣṇu took leave of Bāṇa and returned to his city along with his followers.

## \|\| 6.55.47 \|\|

*pathi jitvā ca varuṇaṃ viruddhaṃ tamanekadhā \|*  
*dvārakāṃ ca purīṃ prāptassamutsavasamanvitaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. On the way he conquered Varuṇa who had opposed him in various ways. After reaching Dvārakā he celebrated the event jubilantly.

## \|\| 6.55.48 \|\|

*visarjayitvā garuḍaṃ sakhīnvīkṣyopahasya ca \|*  
*dvārakāyāṃ tato dṛṣṭvā kāmacārī cacāra ha \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. After reaching Dvārakā he dismissed Garuḍa. Seeing his friends and joking with them he roamed about as he pleased.

## Chapter 56 - Bāṇāsura attains the position of Śiva’s Gaṇa

## \|\| 6.56.1 \|\|

*\|\| nārada uvāca \|*  
*kṛṣṇe gate dvārakāyāma niruddhena bhāryayā \|*  
*akārṣītkiṃ tato bāṇastattvaṃ vada mahāmune \|\| 1 \|\|*

Nārada said:—

1\. O great sage, when Kṛṣṇa left for Dvārakā along with Aniruddha and his wife, what did Bāṇa do? Please narrate the same to me.

## \|\| 6.56.2 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*kṛṣṇe gate dvārakāyāmaniruddhena bhāryayā \|*  
*duḥkhito'bhūttato bāṇassvājñānaṃ saṃsmaranhṛdā \|\| 2 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

2\. When Kṛṣṇa left for Dvārakā with Aniruddha and his wife, Bāṇa was distressed thinking on his previous ignorance.

## \|\| 6.56.3 \|\|

*tato nandīśivagaṇo bāṇaṃ provāca duḥkhitam \|*  
*daityaṃ śoṇitadigdhāṃgamanutā pasamanvitam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Then Nandin, a gaṇa of Śiva, spoke to the grief-stricken Daitya Bāṇa whose limbs were smeared with blood and who repented repeatedly.

## \|\| 6.56.4 \|\|

*\|\| nandīśvara uvāca \|*  
*bāṇa śaṃkarasadbhakta mānutāpaṃ kuruṣva bhoḥ \|*  
*bhaktānukaṃpī śaṃbhurvai bhaktavatsalanāmadhṛk \|\| 4 \|\|*

Nandiśvara said:—

4\. O Bāṇa, devotee of Śiva, do not repent. Śiva is compassionate towards his devotees. Hence he is called Bhaktavatsala (i.e. favourably disposed to the devotees).

## \|\| 6.56.5 \|\|

*tadicchayā ca yajjātaṃ tajjātamiti cetasā \|*  
*manyasva bhaktaśārdūla śivaṃ smara punaḥpunaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. O foremost among devotees, whatever has happened, has happened at his will. Consider this and remember Śiva again and again.

## \|\| 6.56.6 \|\|

*mana ādye samādhāya kuru nityaṃ maho tsavam \|*  
*bhaktānukaṃpanaścā'sya śaṃkarasya punaḥpunaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Fixing your mind in the primordial being, Śiva who is compassionate towards the devotees, you celebrate his festival again and again.

## \|\| 6.56.7 \|\|

*nandivākyāttato bāṇo dviṣā śīrṣakamātrakaḥ \|*  
*śivasthānaṃ jagāmāśu dhṛtvā dhairyaṃ mahāmanāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. At the suggestion of Nandin, Bāṇa who had been like Rāhu unto his enemies immediately went to Śiva’s temple with lofty mind and great courage.

## \|\| 6.56.8 \|\|

*gatvā tatra prabhuṃ natvā rurodātīva vihvalaḥ \|*  
*gatagarvavrajo bāṇaḥ premākulitamānasaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. After going there he bowed to the lord and lamented in great agitation. Bāṇa who had been divested of his haughtiness became overwhelmed with love and devotion.

## \|\| 6.56.9-10 \|\|

*saṃstuvanvividhaiḥ stotrai ssaṃnamannutitastathā \|*  
*yathocitaṃ pādaghātaṃ kurvanvikṣepayankarān \|\| 9 \|\|*

*nanarta tāṃḍavaṃ mukhyaṃ pratyālīḍhādiśobhitam \|*  
*sthānakairvividhākārairālīḍhapramukhairapi \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. He eulogised him with various hymns, He bowed to the lord in the course of his worship. With proper steps and gestures of hands he performed the Tāṇḍava dance assuming various poses and postures—Pratyālīdha, Sthānaka, Ālīḍha being the chief among them.

## \|\| 6.56.11-14 \|\|

*sukhavādasahasrāṇi bhrūkṣepasahitānyapi \|*  
*śiraḥkampasahasrāṇi prāptānīkaḥ sahasraśaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*vārīśca vividhākārā darśayitvā śanaiśśanaḥ \|*  
*tathā śoṇitadhārābhissiñcayitvā mahītalam \|\| 12 \|\|*

*rudraṃ prasādayāmāsa śūlinaṃ candra śekharam \|*  
*bāṇāsuro mahābhakto vismṛtātmagatirnataḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*tato nṛtyaṃ mahatkṛtvā bhagavānbhaktavatsalaḥ \|*  
*uvāca bāṇaṃ saṃhṛṣṭo nṛtya gītapriyo haraḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

11-14. He produced thousands of gestures through his mouth. He knit and bent his brows and shook his head in various ways. He kept thousands of attendants in rows. He showed various gestures gradually. Much of his blood was shed on the ground. By all these means be propitiated the trident-bearing moon-crested lord. Bāṇāsura the great devotee of Śiva forgot himself and his activities in the course of his worship. Śiva who is fond of dance and music and is favourably disposed to his devotees spoke to Bāṇa.

## \|\| 6.56.15 \|\|

*rudra uvāca \|*  
*bāṇa tāta baleḥ putra saṃtuṣṭo nartanena te \|*  
*varaṃ gṛhāṇa daityendra yatte manasi vartate \|\| 15 \|\|*

Śiva said:—

15\. “Dear Bāṇa, son of Bali, I am delighted by your dance. O lord of Daityas, you choose the boon whatever be in your mind”.

## \|\| 6.56.16-20 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya vacaśśaṃmbhordaityendreṇa tadā mune \|*  
*bāṇena saṃvṛṇīto'bhūdvarastu vraṇaropaṇe \|\| 16 \|\|*

*bāhuyuddhasya coddha ttirgāṇapatyamathākṣayam \|*  
*uṣāputrasya rājyaṃ tu tasmiñśoṇitakāhvaye \|\| 17 \|\|*

*nirvairatā ca vibudhairviṣṇunā ca viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*na punardaityatā duṣṭā rajasā tamasā yutā \|\| 18 \|\|*

*śaṃbhubhaktirviśeṣeṇa nirvikārā sadā mune \|*  
*śivabhakteṣu ca sneho dayā sarveṣu jaṃtuṣu \|\| 19 \|\|*

*kṛtvā varāñśaṃbhorbaliputro mahā'suraḥ \|*  
*premṇā'śrunayano rudraṃ tuṣṭāva sukṛtāṃjaliḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

16-20. O sage, on hearing the words of śiva, Bāṇa the lord of Daityas asked for the healing of wounds, the skill in duels, everlasting position of Gaṇahood, the kingship for Uṣā’s (Ūṣā’s?) son at the city of Śoṇita, absence of enmity with the gods and Viṣṇu in particular, absence of rebirth as a Daitya defiled by the attributes Rajas and Tamas, special devotion to Śiva without any aberration for ever, friendship with the devotees of Śiva and kindness to all living beings. After requesting for these boons, the son of Bali, the great Asura joined his palms in reverence and eulogised Śiva with tears of love in his eyes.

## \|\| 6.56.21 \|\|

*bāṇa uvāca \|*  
*devadeva mahādeva śaraṇā gatavatsala \|*  
*tvāṃ namāmi maheśāna dīnabandho dayānidhe \|\| 21 \|\|*

Bāṇa said:—

21\. O great lord, lord of the gods, favourably disposed to those who seek refuge in you, O great lord, I bow to you, O kinsman of the distressed, O storehouse of mercy.

## \|\| 6.56.22 \|\|

*kṛtā mayi kṛpātīva kṛpāsāgara śaṃkara \|*  
*garvopahāritassarvaḥ prasannena mama prabho \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. O Śiva, O ocean of sympathy, you have taken pity on me. O lord, being delighted with me you have removed my arrogance.

## \|\| 6.56.23 \|\|

*tvaṃ brahma paramātmā hi sarvavyāpyakhileśvaraḥ \|*  
*brahmāṃḍatanurugreśo virāṭ sarvānvitaḥ paraḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. You are Brahman, the great soul, the all-pervading lord. \_ Your body is the whole cosmos. You are Ugra, Īśa, Virāṭ, the great, accompanied by everything.

## \|\| 6.56.24 \|\|

*nābhirnabho'gnirvadanamaṃbu reto diśaḥ śrutiḥ \|*  
*dyauśśīrṣamaṃghrirurvī te manaścandrastava prabho \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. O lord, your navel is the sky, mouth is the fire, semen is the water, ear the quarters, head the heaven, foot the earth and mind the moon.

## \|\| 6.56.25 \|\|

*dṛgarko jaṭharaṃ vārddhirbhujeṃdro dhiṣaṇā vidhiḥ \|*  
*prajāpatirvisargaśca dharmo hi hṛdayaṃ tava \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Your eye is the sun, the stomach the ocean, the arm Indra, and the intellect Brahmā. Your excretion is Prajāpati and your heart is Dharma.

## \|\| 6.56.26 \|\|

*romāṇyauṣadhayo nātha keśā jalamucastava \|*  
*guṇāstrayastrinetrāṇi sarvātmā puruṣo bhavān \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. O lord, your hairs are the herbs and plants, your tresses the clouds, your eyes the three attributes. You are the Puruṣa, the soul of all.

## \|\| 6.56.27 \|\|

*brāhmaṇaṃ te mukhaṃ prāhurbāhuṃ kṣatriyameva ca \|*  
*ūrujaṃ vaiśyamāhuste pādajaṃ śūdrameva ca \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. They call Brāhmaṇa your mouth, Kṣatriya your arms, Vaiśya your thighs and Śūdra your feet.

## \|\| 6.56.28 \|\|

*tvameva sarvadopāsyassarvairjīvairmaheśvara \|*  
*tvāṃ bhajanparamāṃ muktiṃ labhate puruṣo dhruvam \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. O lord Śiva, you alone deserve to be adored by all living beings. A person worshipping you certainly derives liberation.

## \|\| 6.56.29 \|\|

*yastvāṃ visṛjate martya ātmānaṃ priyamīśvaram \|*  
*viparyayendriyārthārthaṃ viṣamattyamṛtaṃ tyajan \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. O lord, the man who forsakes you, the favourite Ātman, for the adverse objects of sense, swallows poison forsaking nectar.

## \|\| 6.56.30 \|\|

*viṣṇurbrahmā'tha vibudhā munayaścāmalāśayāḥ \|*  
*sarvātmanā prapannāstvāṃ śaṃkaraṃ priyamīśvaram \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Viṣṇu, Brahmā, the gods and the sages of pure mind, in every respect resort to you, the favourite lord.

## \|\| 6.56.31 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityuktvā baliputrastu virarāma śarāsuraḥ \|*  
*premapraphullitāṃgaśca praṇamya sa maheśvaram \|\| 31 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

31\. After saying this, the Asura Bāṇa, son of Bali stopped with all the limbs blooming with love and bowed to lord Śiva.

## \|\| 6.56.32 \|\|

*iti śrutvā svabhaktasya bāṇasya bhagavānbhavaḥ \|*  
*sarvaṃ labhiṣyasītyuktvā tatraivāṃtaradhīyata \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. On hearing the request of his devotee Bāṇa, lord Śiva said “You will get everything” and vanished there itself.

## \|\| 6.56.33 \|\|

*tataśśaṃbhoḥ prasādena mahākālatvamāgataḥ \|*  
*rudrasyānucaro bāṇo mahāpramudito'bhavat \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Then through the grace of Śiva, Bāṇa attained the immortality of the eternal time and becoming one of the attendants of Śiva he rejoiced much.

## \|\| 6.56.34 \|\|

*iti kila śaranāmnaḥ śaṃkarasyāpi vṛttaṃ sakalaguru janānāṃ sadgurośśūlapāṇeḥ \|*  
*kathitamiha variṣṭhaṃ śrotraramyairvacobhissakalabhuvanamadhye krīḍamānasya nityam \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Thus I have narrated by means of words pleasing to the ears, the excellent story of the trident-bearing lord Śiva, who is the preceptor of the preceptors and who sports about always in the middle of the worlds. His story includes his activities in relation to Bāṇa.

## Chapter 57 - Gajāsura is slain

## \|\| 6.57.1 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu vyāsa mahāpremṇā caritaṃ śaśimaulinaḥ \|*  
*yathā'vadhīttriśūlena dānavendraṃ gajāsuram \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

1\. O Vyāsa, listen with great devotion to the story of moon-crested lord, how he killed Gajāsura, the lord of Dānavas, by means of his trident.

## \|\| 6.57.2 \|\|

*dānave nihate devyā samare mahiṣāsure \|*  
*devānāṃ ca hitārthāya purā devāḥ sukhaṃ yayuḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Formerly when the Asura Mahiṣa was killed in battle by the goddess for the welfare of the gods, they became very happy.

## \|\| 6.57.3-4 \|\|

*tasya putro mahāvīro munīśvara gajāsuraḥ \|*  
*piturvadhaṃ hi saṃsmṛtya kṛtaṃ devyā surārthanāt \|\| 3 \|\|*

*sa tadvairamanusmṛtya taporthaṃ gatavānvane \|*  
*samuddiśya vidhiṃ prītyā tatāpa paramaṃ tapaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. O great sage, his son the great hero Gajāsura could not forget the slaying of his father by the goddess at the request of the gods and hence remembered that enmity. He therefore went to the forest for undertaking penance. Interestingly he performed penance meditating on Brahma.

## \|\| 6.57.5 \|\|

*avadhyohaṃ bhaviṣyāmi strīpuṃsaiḥ kāmanirjitaḥ \|*  
*saṃvicāryeti manasā'bhūttaporatamānasaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. “I shall not be killed by men or women overwhelmed by lust.” Thinking thus in his mind he directed his attention to austerities.

## \|\| 6.57.6 \|\|

*sa tepe himavaddroṇyāṃ tapaḥ paramadāru ṇam \|*  
*ūrddhvabāhurnabhodṛṣṭiḥ pādāṃguṣṭhāśritāvaniḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. He performed a severe penance in a valley on the Himālaya mountain. He kept his arms lifted. He fixed his eyes at the sky. He stood on the ground on the two big toes.

## \|\| 6.57.7 \|\|

*jaṭābhāraissa vai reje pralayārka ivāṃśubhiḥ \|*  
*mahiṣāsuraputro'sau gajāsura udāradhīḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. With plenty of matted tresses of hair the benevolent Gajāsura, the son of Mahiṣa shone with his refulgence like the sun at the time of dissolution.

## \|\| 6.57.8 \|\|

*tasya mūrdhnaḥ samudbhūtassadhūmognistapomayaḥ \|*  
*tiryagūrdhvamadholokāstāpayanviṣvagīritaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The fire in the form of penance originating from his head filled with smoke spread all round to the worlds above, below and on the sides scorching them.

## \|\| 6.57.9 \|\|

*cukṣubhurnadyudanvaṃtaścāgnermūrddhasamudbhavāt \|*  
*nipetussagrahāstārā jajvaluśca diśo daśa \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The rivers and the seas were agitated by the fire originating from his head. The stars fell along with the planets. The ten quarters blazed.

## \|\| 6.57.10 \|\|

*tena taptāsturāssarve divaṃ tyaktvā savāsavāḥ \|*  
*brahmalokaṃ yayurvijñāpayāmāsuścacāla bhūḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The gods scorched by the fire left heaven and went to Brahma’s world along with Indra and submitted to him. The earth quaked.

## \|\| 6.57.11 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*vidhe gajāsuratapastaptā vayamathākulāḥ \|*  
*na śaknumo divi sthātumataste śaraṇaṃ gatāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

The gods said:—

11\. O Brahmā, we are agitated on being scorched by the penance of Gajāsura. We are unable to stay in heaven. Hence we seek refuge in you.

## \|\| 6.57.12 \|\|

*vidhehyupaśamaṃ tasya cānyāñjīvayituṃ kṛpā \|*  
*lokā naṃkṣyatyanyathā hi satyaṃsatyaṃ bruvāmahe \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Make it subside and find out a merciful remedy to enliven others. Otherwise the worlds will perish. Truth. It is the truth that we speak.

## \|\| 6.57.13 \|\|

*iti vijñāpito devairvāsavādyaissa ātmabhūḥ \|*  
*bhṛgudakṣādibhirbrahmā yayau daityavarāśramam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Thus informed by the gods including Indra and others the selfborn deity Brahmā went to the hermitage of the excellent Daitya along with Bhṛgu,\[2\] Dakṣa and others.

## \|\| 6.57.14 \|\|

*tapaṃtaṃ tapasā lokā nyathā'bhrāpihitaṃ divi \|*  
*vilakṣya vismitaḥ prāha vihasansṛṣṭikārakaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. On seeing him scorching the heaven and the worlds by his penance, the surprised creator laughed and said.

## \|\| 6.57.15 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*uttiṣṭhottiṣṭha daityendra tapassiddhosi māhiṣe \|*  
*prāpto'haṃ varadastāta varaṃ vṛṇu yathepsitam \|\| 15 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

15\. “O lord of Daityas, stand up, stand up. O son of Mahiṣa, you have achieved perfection in penance. O dear one, I, the granter of boons, have come. Choose your boon as you wish.”

## \|\| 6.57.16 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*utthāyotthāya daityendra īkṣamāṇo dṛśā vibhum \|*  
*girā gadgadayā prīto'gṛṇāddevaṃ sa māhiṣiḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

16\. Getting up in a hurry, the son of Mahiṣa, the lord of Daityas glanced at the lord and praised him lovingly with choking words.

## \|\| 6.57.17-18 \|\|

*gajāsura uvāca \|*  
*namaste devadeveśa yadi dāsyasi me varam \|*  
*avadhyo'haṃ bhaveyaṃ vai strīpuṃsaiḥ kāmanirjitaiḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*mahābalo mahāvīryo'jeyo devādibhissadā \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ lokapālānāṃ nikhilarddhisubhugvibho \|\| 18 \|\|*

Gajāsura said:—

17-18. O lord, O lord of the gods, if you are going to grant me a boon let me be immune from death by men or women overwhelmed by lust. Let me be very powerful, valorous and invincible to the gods, the guardians of the worlds and others for ever. Let me enjoy all prosperities.

## \|\| 6.57.19 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ vṛtaśśatadhṛtirdānavena sa tena vai \|*  
*prādāttattapasā prīto varaṃ tasya sudurlabham \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Thus requested by the Dānava, Brahmā who was delighted by his penance granted him the rare boon.

## \|\| 6.57.20 \|\|

*evaṃ labdhavaro daityo māhiṣiśca gajāsuraḥ \|*  
*suprasannamanāsso'tha svadhāma pratyapadyata \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Securing the boons thus, the Daitya Gajāsura the son of Mahiṣa, returned to his abode with a happy mind.

## \|\| 6.57.21-22 \|\|

*sa vijitya diśassarvā lokāṃśca trīnmahāsuraḥ \|*  
*devāsuramanuṣyendrāngaṃdharvagaruḍoragān \|\| 21 \|\|*

*ityādīnnikhilāñjitvā vaśamānīya viśvajit \|*  
*jahāra lokapālānāṃ sthānāni saha tejasā \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. The great Asura conquered all the quarters, the three worlds, the gods, Asuras, human beings, kings, Gandharvas, Garuḍa, serpents and others. He made them subservient to him. He became the conqueror of the universe. He usurped the places of the guardians of the worlds and took away their glory.

## \|\| 6.57.23 \|\|

*devodyānaśriyā juṣṭamadhyāste sma triviṣṭapam \|*  
*mahendrabhavanaṃ sākṣānnirmitaṃ viśvakarmaṇā \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. He occupied heaven\[6\] possessing the glory of the celestial garden and the palace of lord Indra built by Viśvakarman.

## \|\| 6.57.24 \|\|

*tasminmahendrasya gṛhe mahābalo mahāmanā nirjitaloka ekarāṭ \|*  
*reme'bhivaṃdyāṃghriyugaḥ surādibhiḥ pratāpitairūrjitacaṃḍaśāsanaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. The powerful Daitya of a lofty mind who reigned as the sole ruler after conquering all the worlds sported in the palace of lord Indra. The gods and others who were overwhelmed by his power worshipped the pair of his feet. He exercised a stern and fierce authority.

## \|\| 6.57.25 \|\|

*sa itthaṃ nirjitakakubekarāḍ viṣayānpriyān \|*  
*yathopajoṣaṃ bhuṃjāno nātṛpyadajitendriyaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Thus conquering the quarters and reigning as the supreme overlord he enjoyed pleasures to the maximum extent. Since he had not conquered his senses he was never satiated in his enjoyment of pleasures.

## \|\| 6.57.26 \|\|

*evamaiśvaryamattasya dṛptasyocchāstravartinaḥ \|*  
*kāle vyatīte mahati pāpabuddhirabhūttataḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. He was haughty, puffed up with prosperity. He slighted and transgressed the injunctions of the sacred scriptures. After the lapse of some time he became evil-minded.

## \|\| 6.57.27 \|\|

*mahiṣāsuraputro'sau saṃcikleśa dvijānvarān \|*  
*tāpasānnitarāṃ pṛthvyāṃ dānavassukhamardanaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. The Dānava, the suppressor of the gods, the son of Mahiṣāsura harassed the excellent brahmins and the sages on the earth very much.

## \|\| 6.57.28 \|\|

*surānnarāṃśca pramathānsarvāñcikleśa durmatiḥ \|*  
*dharmānvitānviśeṣeṇa pūrvavairamanusmaran \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. The wicked Daitya harassed the gods, the human beings, and all the Pramathas. He tortured all righteous people particularly recollecting the previous enmity.

## \|\| 6.57.29 \|\|

*ekasminsamaye tāta dānavo'sau mahābalaḥ \|*  
*agacchadrājadhānīṃ va śaṃkarasya gajāsuraḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. O dear, once this Dānava of great strength, Gajāsura came to the capital city of Śiva.

## \|\| 6.57.30 \|\|

*samāgate'surendre hi mahānkalakalo mune \|*  
*trātatrāteti tatrāsīdānaṃdanavāsinām \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. O sage, when the lord of Asuras came there,

there was a great tumult among the residents of Ānandavana, They shouted “Protect, Protect.”

## \|\| 6.57.31-32 \|\|

*mahiṣā'suraputro'sau yadā puryāṃ samāgataḥ \|*  
*pramathanpramathānsarvānnijavīryamadoddhataḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*tasminnavasare devāśśakrādyāstatparājitāḥ \|*  
*śivasya śaraṇaṃ jagmurnatvā tuṣṭuvurādarāt \|\| 32 \|\|*

31-32. When this son of Mahiṣāsura haughty of his valour entered the city suppressing the Pramathas, Indra and other gods previously vanquished by him sought refuge in Śiva. After bowing to him they eulogised him with a great respect.

## \|\| 6.57.33 \|\|

*nyavedayandānavasya tasya kāśyāṃ samāgamam \|*  
*kleśādhikyaṃ tatratyānāṃ tannāthānāṃ viśeṣataḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. They mentioned to him the arrival of the Dānava at Kāśī, the height of distress of the people there, especially of the rulers.

## \|\| 6.57.34 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*devadeva mahādeva tava puryāṃ gatosuraḥ \|*  
*kaṣṭaṃ datte tvajjanānāṃ taṃ jahi tvaṃ kṛpānidhe \|\| 34 \|\|*

The gods said:—

34\. O great gods, O lord of gods, the Asura has gone to your city. He is inflicting pain on your people. O storehouse of benignity, please slay him.

## \|\| 6.57.35 \|\|

*yatrayatra dharāyāṃ ca caraṇaṃ pramiṇoti hi \|*  
*acalāṃ sacalāṃ tatra karoti nija bhārataḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Wherever he sets foot on the earth he shakes the ground there by his great weight.

## \|\| 6.57.36 \|\|

*ūruvegena taravaḥ pataṃti śikharaissaha \|*  
*yasya dordaṃḍaghātena cūrṇā syuśca śiloccayāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. By his great velocity trees fall down with roots and branches. Hit by his brawny arms, big mountains are reduced to powder.

## \|\| 6.57.37 \|\|

*yasya maulijasaṃgharṣādghanā vyoma tyajaṃtyapi \|*  
*nīlimānaṃ na cādyāpi jahyustatkeśasaṃgajam \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. The clouds leave the sky hit by his head. Still they do not lose their blueness due to the contact with his hair.

## \|\| 6.57.38 \|\|

*yasya viśvāsasaṃbhārairuttaraṃgā mahābdhayaḥ \|*  
*nadyopyamandakallolā bhavaṃti timibhissaha \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. When he breathes out, the mighty oceans surge up with their billows. Even the rivers are filled with waves as though with whales.

## \|\| 6.57.39 \|\|

*yojanānāṃ sahasrāṇi nava yasya samucchrayaḥ \|*  
*tāvāneva hi vistārastanormāyāvino'sya hi \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. His height is nine thousand Yojanas. The girth of this Asura who wields Māyā is also of that proportion.

## \|\| 6.57.40 \|\|

*yannetrayoḥ piṃgalimā tathā taralimā punaḥ \|*  
*vidyutāḥ nohyate'dyāpi so'yaṃ smā''yāti satvaram \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. The tawny colour and the tremulousness of his eyes is not borne even by the lightning. Thus he has come there all of a sudden.

## \|\| 6.57.41 \|\|

*yāṃ yāṃ diśaṃ samabhyeti soyaṃ dussaha dānavaḥ \|*  
*avadhyo'haṃ bhavāmīti strīpuṃsaiḥ kāmanirjitaiḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Whichever quarter he approaches, the Dānava is unbearably oppressive. “I am not to be killed by men or women overwhelmed by lust” he shouts.

## \|\| 6.57.42 \|\|

*ityevaṃ ceṣṭitaṃ tasya dānavasya niveditam \|*  
*rakṣasva bhaktāndeveśa kāśīrakṣaṇatatpara \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. O lord of the gods, we have thus mentioned humbly the activities of that Dānava. Please protect your devotees, O lord, desirous of protecting Kāśī.

## \|\| 6.57.43 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*iti saṃprārthito devairbhaktarakṣaṇatatparaḥ \|*  
*tatrā''jagāma soraṃ tadvadhakāmanayā haraḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

43\. Thus requested by the goss, Śiva desirous of protecting the devotees came there quickly with the desire of slaying him.

## \|\| 6.57.44 \|\|

*āgataṃ taṃ samālokya śaṃkaraṃ bhaktavatsalam \|*  
*triśūlahastaṃ garjaṃtaṃ jagarja sa gajāsuraḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. On seeing that Śiva, favourably disposed to his devotees, had come roaring with the trident in his hand, Gajāsura too roared.

## \|\| 6.57.45 \|\|

*tatastayormahānāsītsamaro dāruṇo'dbhutaḥ \|*  
*nānāstraśastrasaṃpātairvīrārāvaṃ prakurvatoḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. A wonderfully terrible and great battle was fought between them roaring heroically and hitting with various weapons and missiles.

## \|\| 6.57.46 \|\|

*gajāsurotitejasvī mahābalaparākramaḥ \|*  
*vivyādha giriśaṃ bāṇaistīkṣṇairdānavaghātinam \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. The brilliant Gajāsura of great strength and valour pierced śiva, the slayer of the Dānavas, with sharp arrows.

## \|\| 6.57.47 \|\|

*atha rudro raudratanuḥ svaśarairatidāruṇaiḥ \|*  
*taccharāṃścicchide tūrṇamaprāptāṃstilaśo mune \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. O sage, Śiva who assumed a terrible body, split with his terrible arrows, the arrows of the Daitya to small pieces like gingelly seeds, even before they reached him.

## \|\| 6.57.48 \|\|

*tato gajāsuraḥ kuddho'bhyadhāvattaṃ maheśvaram \|*  
*khaḍgahastaḥ pragarjyoccairhatosītyadya vai mayā \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Then the infuriated Gajāsura rushed at the lord Śiva roaring loudly with a sword in hand “You are slain now by me.”

## \|\| 6.57.49 \|\|

*tatastriśūlahetistamāyāṃtaṃ daityapuṃgavam \|*  
*vijñāyāvadhyamanyena śūlenābhijaghāna tam \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Then the lord armed with the trident, realising that the leading Daitya who was rushing at him could not be killed by anything else or any one else, hit him with his trident.

## \|\| 6.57.50 \|\|

*protastena triśūlena sa ca daityo gajāsuraḥ \|*  
*chatrīkṛtamivātmānaṃ manyamānā jagau haram \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. When the trident pierced through his body, the Daitya Gajāsura thought that he was raised up like an umbrella. He then sang the glory of Śiva.

## \|\| 6.57.51 \|\|

*gajāsura uvāca \|*  
*devadeva mahādeva tava bhakto'smi sarvathā \|*  
*jāne tvāṃ tridiveśānaṃ triśūlinsmarahāriṇam \|\| 51 \|\|*

Gajāsura said:—

51\. O great lord, lord of the gods, I am in every respect your devotee. O trident-bearing lord, I know you as the lord of heaven and destroyer of Kāma.

## \|\| 6.57.52 \|\|

*tava haste mama vadho mahāśreyaskaro mataḥ \|*  
*aṃdhakāre maheśāna tripurāṃtaka sarvaga \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. O enemy of Andhaka, O great lord, O slayer of Tripuras, O omnipresent, my death at your hands is conducive to my great glory.

## \|\| 6.57.53 \|\|

*kiṃcidvijñaptumicchāmi tacchṛṇuṣva kṛpākara \|*  
*satyaṃ bravīmi nāsatyaṃ mṛtyuṃjaya vicāraya \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. I desire to submit something. O merciful lord, please listen to it. O conqueror of death, I am speaking the truth, not a lie. Please ponder.

## \|\| 6.57.54 \|\|

*tvameko jagatāṃ vaṃdyo viśvasyopari saṃsthitaḥ \|*  
*kālena sarvairmartavyaṃ śreyase mṛtyurīdṛśaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. You are the only person deserving the worship of the worlds. You stand high above the universe. Everyone should consider a death like this conducive to glory in due course.

## \|\| 6.57.55 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya vacastasya śaṃkaraḥ karuṇānidhiḥ \|*  
*prahasya pratyuvāceśo māhiṣeyaṃ gajāsuram \|\| 55 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

words, lord Śiva, the storehouse replied to Gajāsura, the son of

55\. On hearing his of mercy, laughed and Mahiṣa.

## \|\| 6.57.56 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*mahāparākramanidhe dānavottama sanmate \|*  
*gajāsura prasannosmi svānakūlaṃ varaṃ vṛṇu \|\| 56 \|\|*

Lord Śiva said:—

56\. O Gajāsura, O excellent Dānava, O depository of great valour, O well-intentioned one, I am delighted. Choose the boon favourable to you.

## \|\| 6.57.57 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya maheśasya vacanaṃ varadasya hi \|*  
*pratyuvāca prasannātmā dānavendro gajāsuraḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

57\. On hearing the words of lord Śiva, the granter of boons, the lord of Dānavas, the delighted Gajāsura replied.

## \|\| 6.57.58 \|\|

*gajāsura uvāca \|*  
*yadi prasanno digvāsastadā dityaṃ vasāna me \|*  
*imāṃ kṛttiṃ maheśāna tvattriśūlāgnipāvitām \|\| 58 \|\|*

Gajāsura said:—

58\. O nude one, if you are delighted, O lord Śiva, wear this hide of mine sanctified by the fire of your trident.

## \|\| 6.57.59 \|\|

*svapramāṇāṃ sukhasparśāṃ raṇāṃgaṇapaṇīkṛtām \|*  
*darśanīyāṃ mahādivyāṃ sarvadaiva sukhāvahām \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. It is of your size, it is gentle to the touch, it has been kept as a stake in the battlefield, it is worth seeing, it is of divine nature and it is always pleasing.

## \|\| 6.57.60 \|\|

*iṣṭagaṃdhissadaivāstu sadaivāstvatikomalā \|*  
*sadaiva nirmalā cāstu sadaivāstvatimaṃḍanām \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Let it ever emit an agreeable smell, let it be soft for ever, let it be ever free from dirt, let it be your best ornament always.

## \|\| 6.57.61 \|\|

*mahātaponalajvālāṃ prāpyāpi suciraṃ vibho \|*  
*na dagdhā kṛttireṣā me puṇyagaṃdhanidhestataḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. O lord, even after being scorched by the flames of the fire of penance for a long time, this hide was not burnt, hence it is the storehouse of holy fragrance.

## \|\| 6.57.62 \|\|

*yadi puṇyavatī naiṣā mama kṛtti digaṃbara \|*  
*tadā tvadaṃgasaṃgosyāḥ kathaṃ jāto raṇāṃgaṇe \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. O nude one, if my hide is not meritorious how did it get into contact with your limbs in the battlefield?

## \|\| 6.57.63 \|\|

*anyaṃ ca me varaṃ dehi yadi tuṣṭo'si śaṃkara \|*  
*nāmāstu kṛttivāsāste prārabhyādyatanaṃ dinam \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. O Śiva, if you are satisfied, please grant me another boon. Beginning from today let your name be Kṛttivāsas (one clad in elephant-hide).

## \|\| 6.57.64 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*śrutveti sa vacastasya śaṃkaro bhaktavatsalaḥ \|*  
*tathetyuvāca suprīto mahiṣāsurajaṃ ca tam \|\| 64 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

64\. On hearing his words, Śiva who is favourably disposed to his devotees, was pleased and replied to Gajāsura, the son of Mahiṣa “Let it be so”.

## \|\| 6.57.65 \|\|

*punaḥ provāca prītātmā dānavaṃ taṃ gajāsuram \|*  
*bhaktapriyo maheśāno bhaktinirmalamānasam \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Lord Śiva, the favourite of his devotees, becoming delighted spoke again to the Dānava Gajāsura whose mind had been purified by devotion.

## \|\| 6.57.66 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*idaṃ puṇyaṃ śarīraṃ te kṣetre'sminmuktisādhane \|*  
*mama liṃgaṃ bhavatvatra sarveṣāṃ muktidāyakam \|\| 66 \|\|*

Lord Śiva said:—

66\. “In this holy place, a means to the achievement of liberation, let your meritorious body become phallic image yielding liberation to all.

## \|\| 6.57.67 \|\|

*kṛttivāseśvaraṃ nāma mahāpātakanāśanam \|*  
*sarveṣāmeva liṃgānāṃ śirobhūtaṃ vimuktidam \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. It will be the foremost of all phallic images yielding salvation, destroying great sins and named “Kṛttivāseśvara”.

## \|\| 6.57.68 \|\|

*kathayitveti deveśastatkṛtiṃ parigṛhya ca \|*  
*gajāsurasya mahatīṃ prāvṛṇoddhi digaṃbaraḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

68\. After saying this Śiva, the lord of the gods, accepted the hide of Gajāsura and wore it.

## \|\| 6.57.69 \|\|

*mahāmahotsavo jātastasminnahni munīśvara \|*  
*harṣamāpurjanāssarve kāśīsthāḥ pramathāstathā \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. O great sage, there was a great jubilation on that day. All the people staying at Kāśī and the Pramathas were delighted.

## \|\| 6.57.70 \|\|

*hari brahmādayo devā harṣanirbharamānasāḥ \|*  
*tuṣṭuvustaṃ maheśānaṃ natvā sāṃjalayastataḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Viṣṇu, Brahmā and other gods were delighted in their minds. With palms joined in reverence they bowed to lord Śiva and eulogised him.

## \|\| 6.57.71 \|\|

*hate tasmindānaveśe māhiṣe hi gajāsure \|*  
*svasthānaṃ bhejire devā jagatsvāsthyamavāpa ca \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. When Gajāsura the lord of the Dānavas, and the son of Mahiṣa was killed, the gods returned to their original place and the universe attained normalcy.

## \|\| 6.57.72 \|\|

*ityuktaṃ caritaṃ śaṃbhorbhaktavātsalyasūcakam \|*  
*svargyaṃ yaśasyamāyuṣyaṃ dhanadhānyapravarddhanam \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. Thus I have narrated to you the story of Śiva which shows his affection to his devotees, which is conducive to the attainment of heaven, fame and longevity and which increases wealth and food-grains.

## \|\| 6.57.73 \|\|

*ya idaṃ śṛṇuyātprītyā śrāvayedvā śucivrataḥ \|*  
*sa bhuktvā ca mahāsaukhyaṃ labhetāṃte paraṃ sukham \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. He who listens to this with devotion, or narrates this observing pure rites, enjoys great happiness and attains salvation, the greatest bliss hereafter.

## Chapter 58 - Dundubhinirhrāda is slain

## \|\| 6.58.1 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu vyāsa pravakṣyāmi caritaṃ śaśimaulinaḥ \|*  
*yathā duṃdubhinirhrādamavadhīdditijaṃ haraḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

1\. O Vyāsa, listen. I shall narrate the story of the moon-crested lord Śiva how he slew the Daitya Dundubhinirhrāda.

## \|\| 6.58.2 \|\|

*hiraṇyākṣe hate daitye ditiputre mahābale \|*  
*viṣṇudevena kālena prāpa dukhaṃ pahadditiḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. When the Daitya Hiraṇyākṣa, son ofDiti, of great strength was killed by Viṣṇu, Diti remained griefstricken for a long time.

## \|\| 6.58.3 \|\|

*daityo duṃdubhinirhrādo duṣṭaḥ prahlādamātulaḥ \|*  
*sāṃtvayāmāsa tāṃ vāgbhirduḥkhitāṃ devaduḥkhadaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The wicked Daitya named Dundubhinirhrāda, the uncle of Prahlāda, the oppressor of the gods, consoled the dejected mother with the words.

## \|\| 6.58.4 \|\|

*atha daityassa māyāvī ditimāśvāsya daityarāṭ \|*  
*devāḥ kathaṃ sujeyāḥ syurityupāyamarcitayat \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. After consoling Diti, the king of Daityas, an expert in using Māyā began to think of the ways and means of conquering the gods easily.

## \|\| 6.58.5 \|\|

*devaiśca ghātito vīro hiraṇyākṣo mahāsuraḥ \|*  
*viṣṇunā ca saha bhrātrā sacchalairdetyavairibhiḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. “The great Asura Hiraṇyākṣa along with his brother has been killed through Viṣṇu by the gods, the enemies of Daityas, employing deceitful means.

## \|\| 6.58.6 \|\|

*kiṃbalāśca kimāhārā kimādhārā hi nirjarāḥ \|*  
*mayā kathaṃ sujeyāssyurityupāyamaciṃtayat \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. What is the strength of the gods? What is their diet? What is their support? How can the gods be easily vanquished by me?” Thinking like this he tried to find out the ways and means.

## \|\| 6.58.7 \|\|

*vicārya bahuśo daityastattvaṃ vijñāya niścitam \|*  
*avaśyamagrajanmāno hetavo'tra vicārataḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Thinking deeply in diverse ways the Daitya came to the conclusion that the brāhmaṇas were the cause of the trouble.

## \|\| 6.58.8 \|\|

*brāhmaṇānhaṃtumasakṛdanvadhāvata vai tataḥ \|*  
*daityo dundubhinirhrādo devavairī mahākhalaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The Daitya Dundubhinirhrāda, the most wicked enemy of the gods, ran after the brahmins to kill them.

## \|\| 6.58.9 \|\|

*yataḥ kratubhujo devāḥ kratavo vedasaṃbhavāḥ \|*  
*te vedā brāhmaṇādhārāstato devabalaṃ dvijāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Since the gods maintain themselves on sacrifices, sacrifices are born of the Vedas and the Vedas are the custody of the brāhmaṇas, so the brāhmaṇas constitute the strength of the gods.

## \|\| 6.58.10 \|\|

*niścitaṃ brāhmaṇādhārāssarve vedāssavāsavāḥ \|*  
*gīrvāṇā brāhmaṇabalā nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Certainly the gods including Indra are supported by the brāhmaṇas. The gods gain their strength from the brāhmaṇas. There is no doubt about this.

## \|\| 6.58.11 \|\|

*brāhmaṇā yadi naṣṭāssyurvedā naṣṭāstatastvayam \|*  
*atasteṣu praṇaṣṭeṣu vinaṣṭāḥ satataṃ surāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. If the brāhmaṇas are destroyed the Vedas will perish. If they are destroyed the gods will also perish.

## \|\| 6.58.12-13 \|\|

*yajñeṣu nāśaṃ gacchatsu hatāhārāstatassurāḥ \|*  
*nirbalāssukhajayyāḥ syurnirjiteṣu sureṣvatha \|\| 12 \|\|*

*ahameva bhaviṣyāmi mānyastrijagatīpatiḥ \|*  
*ahariṣyāmi devā nāmakṣayāssarvasaṃpadaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. If the sacrifices are destroyed, the gods will lose their food. They will grow weaker and be easily conquered. When the gods are conquered I shall become the sole honourable lord of the three worlds. I shall then confiscate the everlasting riches of the gods.

## \|\| 6.58.14 \|\|

*nirvekṣyāmi sukhānyeva rājye nihatakaṃṭake \|*  
*iti niścitya durbuddhiḥ punaściṃtitavānkhalaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. I shall enjoy happiness in my kingdom freed of thorns.” After thinking like this the wicked Daitya thought again.

## \|\| 6.58.15 \|\|

*dvijāḥ kva saṃti bhūyāṃso brahmatejotibṛṃhitā \|*  
*śrutyadhyanasaṃpannāstapobalasamanvitāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. “Where are these brāhmaṇas in plenty—the brāhmaṇas strengthened by the splendour of the Brahman, well versed in the study of the Vedas and possessing the strength of penance?

## \|\| 6.58.16 \|\|

*bhūyasāṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ tu sthānaṃ vārāṇasī khalu \|*  
*tāmādāvupasaṃhṛtya yāyāṃ tīrthāṃtaraṃ tataḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. It is Vārāṇasī indeed that is the place of many brāhmaṇas. I shall finish that first and then go to other holy centres.

## \|\| 6.58.17 \|\|

*yatra yatra hi tīrtheṣu yatra yatrāśrameṣu ca \|*  
*saṃti sarve'grajanmānaste mayādyāssamaṃtataḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. In holy centres or hermitages wherever these brāhmaṇas live they shall be devoured by me.”

## \|\| 6.58.18 \|\|

*iti duṃdubhinirhrādo matiṃ kṛtvā kulocitām \|*  
*prāpyāpi kāśīṃ durvṛtto māyāvī nyavadhīddvijān \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. After thinking thus in accordance with the nature of his race, Dundubhinirhrāda went to Kāśī and he, the wicked wielder of Māyas, killed the brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 6.58.19 \|\|

*samitkuśānsamādātuṃ yatra yāṃti dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*araṇye tatra tānsarvānsa bhakṣayati durmatiḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. When the excellent brāhmaṇas went to the forest to fetch sacrificial twigs and the Darbha grass, the wicked Dānava used to eat them there.

## \|\| 6.58.20 \|\|

*yathā ko'pi na vettyevaṃ tathā'cchanno'bhavatpunaḥ \|*  
*vane vanecaro bhūtvā yādorūpo jalāśaye \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. After that he used to lie hidden so that nobody could detect him. In the forest he used to roam about like a forest-dweller and in the waters he used to take the form of an aquatic animal.

## \|\| 6.58.21-22 \|\|

*adṛśyarūpī māyāvī devānāmapyagocaraḥ \|*  
*divā dhyānaparastiṣṭhenmunivanmunimadhyagaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*praveśamuṭajānāṃ ca nirgamaṃ hi vilokayan \|*  
*yāminyāṃ vyāghrarūpeṇābhakṣayadbrāhmaṇānbahūn \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. He was invisible in form. He wielded the art of deception. He could not be seen even by the gods. During the day he stood in the midst of sages engaged in meditation but observing the ingress and egress of persons in the hut. But at night he took the form of a tiger and ate many of them.

## \|\| 6.58.23 \|\|

*niśśaṃkambhakṣayatyevaṃ na tyajatyapi kīkaśam \|*  
*itthaṃ nipātitāstena viprā duṣṭena bhūriśaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. He used to eat unhesitatingly never leaving even a bone behind. Thus many brāhmaṇas were annihilated by him in this way.

## \|\| 6.58.24 \|\|

*ekadā śivarātrau tu bhaktastveko nijoṭaje \|*  
*saparyāṃ devadevasya kṛtvā dhyānasthito'bhavat \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Once on the Śivarātri day a certain devotee performed the worship of Śiva, the lord of the gods and was engaged in meditation in his own hut.

## \|\| 6.58.25 \|\|

*sa ca duṃdubhinirhrādo daityendro baladarpitaḥ \|*  
*vyāghrarūpaṃ samāsthāya tamādātuṃ matiṃ dadhe \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The lord of Daityas Dundubhinirhrāda, proud of his strength, assumed the form of a tiger and wanted to seize him.

## \|\| 6.58.26 \|\|

*taṃ bhaktaṃ dhyānamāpannaṃ dṛḍhacittaṃ śivekṣaṇe \|*  
*kṛtāstramantravinyāsaṃ taṃ krāṃtumaśakanna saḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. As the devotee was in meditation with a mind concentrated on Śiva and as he had fixed the Astramantra, the Daitya could not attack him.

## \|\| 6.58.27 \|\|

*atha sarvaṃ gataśśambhurjñātvā tasyāśayaṃ haraḥ \|*  
*daityasya duṣṭarūpasya vadhāya vidadhe dhiyam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Śiva, the omnipresent lord, knew his evil intention and decided to slay the Daitya.

## \|\| 6.58.28 \|\|

*yāvadāditsati vyāghrastāvadāvirabhūddharaḥ \|*  
*jagadrakṣāmaṇistryakṣo bhaktarakṣaṇadakṣadhīḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. While the Daitya in the form of the tiger was about to snatch the devotee, Śiva appeared before him. The three-eyed lord Śiva is very keen in intellect in saving the devotees, nay in protecting the universe.

## \|\| 6.58.29 \|\|

*rudramāyāṃtamālokya tadbhaktārcitaliṃgataḥ \|*  
*daityastenaiva rūpeṇa vavṛdhe bhūdharopamaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. On seeing Śiva coming out of the phallic image worshipped by the devotee, the Daitya in the form of a tiger increased in size like a big mountain.

## \|\| 6.58.30 \|\|

*sāvajñamatha sarvajñaṃ yāvatpaśyati dānavaḥ \|*  
*tāvadāyātamādāya kakṣāyaṃtre nyapīḍayat \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. The Dānava glanced with a contemptuous look at Śiva but the lord caught him and pressed him under his armpit.

## \|\| 6.58.31 \|\|

*paṃcāsyastvatha paṃcāsyaṃ muṣṭyā mūrddhanyatāḍayata \|*  
*bhaktavatsalanāmāsau vajrādapi kaṭhorayā \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. The five-faced lord favourably disposd to his devotees hit the tiger on its head with his fist harder than thunderbolt.

## \|\| 6.58.32 \|\|

*sa tena muṣṭighātena kakṣāniṣpeṣaṇena ca \|*  
*atyārtamāraṭadvyāghro rodasīṃ pūrayanmṛtaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. By the blow of the fist and the pressure at the armpit the tiger groaned aloud in great distress filling heaven and earth with the sound and died.

## \|\| 6.58.33 \|\|

*tena nādena mahatā saṃpravepitamānasāḥ \|*  
*tapodhanāssamājagmurniśi śabdānusārataḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Agitated in their minds by the loud sound, the ascetics came there in the night itself following the track of the sound.

## \|\| 6.58.34 \|\|

*atreśvaraṃ samālokya kakṣīkṛtamṛgeśvaram \|*  
*tuṣṭuvuḥ praṇatāssarve śarvaṃ jayajayākṣaraiḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. On seeing the lord there with the lord of the beasts in his armpit they bowed to him. They eulogised him with the words of “Victory, Victory.”

## \|\| 6.58.35 \|\|

*brāhmaṇā ūcuḥ \|*  
*paritrātāḥ paritrātāḥ pratyūhāddāruṇāditaḥ \|*  
*anugrahaṃ kuruṣveśa tiṣṭhātraiva jagadguro \|\| 35 \|\|*

The brahmins said:—

35\. We are saved, O, we are saved from this terrible obstacle. O lord, please bless us. O preceptor of the universe stay here alone.

## \|\| 6.58.36 \|\|

*anenaiva svarūpeṇa vyāghreśa iti nāmataḥ \|*  
*kuru rakṣāṃ mahādeva jyeṣṭhasthānasya sarvadā \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. O great lord, in this self-same form in the name of the lord of the tiger offer protection. Let this place remain sacred always.

## \|\| 6.58.37 \|\|

*anyebhyo hyupasargebhyo rakṣa nastīrthavāsinaḥ \|*  
*duṣṭānaṣṭāsya gaurīśa bhaktebhyo dehi cābhayam \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Save us the dwellers in this holy centre from other mishaps too. O lord of Pārvatī, leaving the wicked ones offer fearlessness to your devotees.

## \|\| 6.58.38 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya vacasteṣāṃ bhaktānāṃ candraśekharaḥ \|*  
*tathetyuktvā punaḥ prāha sa bhaktānbhaktavatsalaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

38\. On hearing the words of the devotees, the moon-crested lord who is favourably disposed to the devotees said affirmatively and told the devotees again.

## \|\| 6.58.39 \|\|

*maheśvara uvāca \|*  
*yo māmanena rūpeṇa drakṣyati śraddhayātra vai \|*  
*tasyopasargasaṃdhānaṃ pātayiṣyāmyasaṃśayam \|\| 39 \|\|*

Lord Śiva said:—

39\. “If any one sees me here in this form with faith, I will undoubtedly remove his torments and mishaps.

## \|\| 6.58.40 \|\|

*maccaritramidaṃ śrutvā smṛtvā liṃgamidaṃ hṛdi \|*  
*saṃgrāme praviśanmartyo jayamāpnotyasaṃśayam \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. After hearing this story of mine and after remembering my phallic image in the heart if a man enters the battlefield he will certainly win.

## \|\| 6.58.41 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare devāssamājagmussavāsavāḥ \|*  
*jayeti śabdaṃ kurvaṃto mahotsavapurassaram \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. In the meantime the gods came there along with Indra shouting slogans of victory jubilantly.”

## \|\| 6.58.42 \|\|

*praṇamya śaṃkaraṃ premṇā sarve sāṃjalayassurāḥ \|*  
*nataskaṃdhāḥ suvāgbhiste tuṣṭuvurbhaktavatsalam \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. After bowing to Śiva with love, the gods joined their palms in reverence, drooped their shoulders and eulogised lord Śiva who is favourably disposed to his devotees.

## \|\| 6.58.43 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*jaya śaṃkara deveśa praṇatārtihara prabho \|*  
*etadduṃdubhinirhrādavadhāttrātā vayaṃ surāḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

The gods said:—

43\. O lord Śiva, lord of the gods, remover of the distress of your devotees, be victorious. We the gods have been saved by killing this demon.

## \|\| 6.58.44 \|\|

*sadā rakṣā prakartavyā bhaktānāṃ bhaktavatsala \|*  
*vadhyāḥ khalāśca deveśa tvayā sarveśvara prabho \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. O fond of devotees, you shall protect them always. O lord of the gods, wicked men shall be slain by you, O lord of all.

## \|\| 6.58.45 \|\|

*ityākarṇya vacasteṣāṃ surāṇāṃ parameśvaraḥ \|*  
*tathetyuktvā prasannātmā tasmiṃlliṃge layaṃ yayau \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. On hearing these words of the gods, lord Śiva became delighted. After saying ‘yes’ he merged into the phallic image.

## \|\| 6.58.46 \|\|

*savismayāstato devāssvaṃsvaṃ dhāma yayurmudā \|*  
*te'pi viprā mahāharṣātpunaryātā yathāgatam \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. The gods, thus surprised returned to their respective abodes and rejoiced. The brahmins too in great delight returned the way they came.

## \|\| 6.58.47-48 \|\|

*idaṃ caritraṃ parama vyāghreśvarasamudbhavam \|*  
*śṛṇuyācchrāvayedvāpi paṭhedvā pāṭhayettathā \|\| 47 \|\|*

*sarvānkāmānavāpnoti narassvamanasesitān \|*  
*paratra labhate mokṣaṃ sarvaduḥkhavivarjitaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

47-48. He who reads this sacred narrative about the origin of the lord of the tiger, hears, narrates or teaches this shall obtain all desires. After death he will attain salvation becoming free of all miseries.

## \|\| 6.58.49 \|\|

*idamākhyānamatulaṃ śivalīlā mṛtākṣaram \|*  
*svargyaṃ yaśasyamāyuṣyaṃ putrapautrapravarddhanam \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. This narrative is incomparable as it contains the nectar-like words of the divine sports of Śiva. It is conducive to the attainment of heaven, fame and longevity. It increases sons and grandsons.

## \|\| 6.58.50 \|\|

*paraṃ bhaktipradaṃ dhanyaṃ śivaprītikaraṃ śivam \|*  
*paramajñānadaṃ ramyaṃ vikāraharaṇaṃ param \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. It yields great devotion and bliss. It is auspicious and increases the pleasure of Śiva. It yields supreme know ledge. It is beautiful and removes all aberrations.

## Chapter 59 - Vidala and Utpala are slain

## \|\| 6.59.1 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu vyāsa susaṃprītyā caritaṃ parameśituḥ \|*  
*yathāvadhītsvapriyayā daityamuddiśya saṃjñayā \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

1\. O Vyāsa, listen with pleasure to the story of the great lord how he killed through his beloved a Daitya whom he indicated by a sign.

## \|\| 6.59.2 \|\|

*āstāṃ purā mahādaityo vidalotpalasaṃjñakau \|*  
*apuṃvadhyau mahāvīrau sudṛptau varato vidheḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Formerly there were two great Daityas—Vidala and Utpala. They were great heroes, puffed up by the boon from Brahmā that they could not be slain by a man.

## \|\| 6.59.3 \|\|

*tṛṇīkṛtatrijagatī puruṣābhyāṃ svadorba lāt \|*  
*tābhyāṃ sarve surā brahman daityābhyāṃ nirjitā raṇe \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. O Brahmin, the gods had been defeated in the battle by the two Daityas who by the strength of their arms considered the people of the three worlds as insignificant as the blade of grass.

## \|\| 6.59.4 \|\|

*tābhyāṃ parājitā devā vidheste śaraṇaṃ gatāḥ \|*  
*natvā taṃ vidhivatsarve kathayāmāsurādarāta \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Defeated by them, the gods sought refuge in Brahmā. After bowing to him duly they submitted to him respectfully.

## \|\| 6.59.5-6 \|\|

*iti brahmā hyavocattān devyā vadhyau ca tau dhruvam \|*  
*dhairyyaṃ kuruta saṃsmṛtya saśivaṃ śivamādarāt \|\| 5 \|\|*

*bhaktavatsalanāmāsau saśivaśśaṃkaraśśivaḥ \|*  
*śaṃ kariṣyatyadīrgheṇa kālena parameśvaraḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. On hearing their account Brahmā said. “They will surely be slain by the goddess. Be bold. Remember Śiva and Pārvatī respectfully. Śiva is auspicious, benevolent favourably disposed to his devotees. The supreme god will bring about welfare ere long.”

## \|\| 6.59.7 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*ityuktvā tāṃstato brahmā tūṣṇīmāsīcchivaṃ smaran \|*  
*tepi devā mudaṃ prāpya svaṃsvaṃ dhāma yayustadā \|\| 7 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:—

7\. After saying this, Brahmā kept quiet remembering Śiva. The gods too returned to their respective abodes rejoicingly.

## \|\| 6.59.8 \|\|

*atha nāradadevarṣiśśivapreraṇayā tadā \|*  
*gatvā tadīyabhavanaṃ śivāsauṃdaryamājagau \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Then at the behest of Śiva, the celestial sage Nārada went to the abode of the Daityas and sang the glory of the beauty of Pārvatī.

## \|\| 6.59.9 \|\|

*śrutvā tadvacanaṃ daityāvāstāṃ māyāvimohitau \|*  
*devīṃ parijihīrṣū tau viṣameṣu prapīḍitau \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. On hearing his words the two Daityas were deluded by deception. Afflicted by the god of lust they desired to abduct the goddess.

## \|\| 6.59.10 \|\|

*vicārayāmāsatustau kadā kutra śivā ca sā \|*  
*bhaviṣyati vidheḥ prāptodayānnāviti sarvadā \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. They thought to themselves where and when they would obtain Pārvatī at the rise of their good fortune.

## \|\| 6.59.11-12 \|\|

*ekasminsamaye śaṃbhurvijahāra sulīlayā \|*  
*kautukenaiva cikrīḍe śivā kandukalīlayā \|\| 11 \|\|*

*sakhībhissaha suprītyā kautukācchivasannidhau \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. Once Śiva was engaged in sports. Pārvatī too was playing with a ball along with her friends in the presence of Śiva.

## \|\| 6.59.13 \|\|

*udaṃcaṃtyaṃcadaṃgānāṃ lāghavaṃ paritanvatī \|*  
*niśvāsāmodamuditabhramarākulitekṣaṇā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. At times she looked up. At times she displayed the lightness of limbs. At times when she took deep breaths, bees hovered round her enticed by the fragrance. At times the bees made her eyes agitated.

## \|\| 6.59.14 \|\|

*bhraśyaddhammillasanmālyasvapurīkṛtabhūmikā \|*  
*svidyatkapolapatrālīsravadaṃbukaṇojjvalā \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Flowers from her tresses fell on the ground in front of her. Her cheeks were perspiring. Drops of sweat dripping from the paintings on her cheek brightened up.

## \|\| 6.59.15 \|\|

*sphuṭaccolāṃśukapathatiryadaṃgaprabhāvṛtā \|*  
*ullasatkaṃdukāsphālātiśroṇitakarāmbujā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The lustre of her body spread all round through the partings of her gown. By exerting her too much in beating the ball her red hand became redder than the red lotus.

## \|\| 6.59.16-17 \|\|

*kaṃdukānugasaddṛṣṭinartitabhrūlatāṃcalā \|*  
*mṛḍānī kila khelaṃtī dadṛśe jagadambikā \|\| 16 \|\|*

*aṃtarikṣacarābhyāṃ ca ditijābhyāṃ kaṭā kṣitā \|*  
*kroḍīkṛtābhyāmiva vai samupasthitamṛtyunā \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. When the ball bounced, her eyes too followed it making the brows to dance thereby. As the goddess mother of the universe was playing, she was seen by the Daityas who were going by the aerial path. They were, as it were, held in the lap by the imminent death.

## \|\| 6.59.18 \|\|

*vidalotpalasaṃjñābhyāṃ dṛptābhyāṃ varato vidheḥ \|*  
*tṛṇīkṛtatrijagatī puruṣābhyāṃ svadorbalāt \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. They were the Daityas Vidala and Uptala who had become haughty by the boon of Brahmā and by the might of their arms thought the people of the three worlds as insignificant as the blades of grass.

## \|\| 6.59.19 \|\|

*devīṃ tāṃ saṃjihīrṣaṃtau viṣameṣu prapīḍitau \|*  
*diva utteratuḥ kṣipraṃ māyāṃ svīkṛtya śāṃbarīm \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Desirous of abducting the goddess as they were tormented by the god of lust, they descended from the sky quickly after adapting the Śāmbarī magic skill.

## \|\| 6.59.20 \|\|

*dhṛtvā pāriṣadīṃ māyāmāyātāvaṃbikāṃtikam \|*  
*tāvatyaṃtaṃ sudurvṛttāvaticaṃcalamānasau \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. The two wicked ones of fickle mind approached Pārvatī in the guise of Śiva’s attendants.

## \|\| 6.59.21 \|\|

*atha duṣṭanihaṃtrā vai sāvajñena hareṇa tau \|*  
*vijñātau ca kṣaṇādāstāṃ cāṃcalyāllocanodbhavāt \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. By the excessive tremulousness of their eyes they were in a trice recognized by Śiva, the chastiser of and contemptuous towards the wicked.

## \|\| 6.59.22 \|\|

*kaṭākṣitātha devena durgā durgatighātinī \|*  
*daityāvimāmiti gaṇau neti sarvasvarūpiṇā \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The lord shot a significant glance at Pārvatī the destroyer of miseries denoting that they were Daityas and not Gaṇas. They could assume any form.

## \|\| 6.59.23 \|\|

*atha sā netrasaṃjñāṃ svasvāminastāṃ bubodha ha \|*  
*mahākautukinastāta śaṃkarasya pareśituḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. O dear, she understood the sign of the eyes of her lord Śiva, the great lord who indulges in fancies.

## \|\| 6.59.24 \|\|

*tato vijñāya saṃjñāṃ tāṃ sarvajñārddhaśarīriṇī \|*  
*tenaiva kaṃdukenātha yugapannirjaghāna tau \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Realising the significant glance, the goddess, the sharer of half the body of Śiva hit both of them simultaneously with the ball.

## \|\| 6.59.25 \|\|

*mahābalau mahādevyā kaṃdukena samāhatau \|*  
*paribhramya paribhramya tau duṣṭau vinipetatuḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The powerful wicked Daityas hit by the ball whirled and whirled and fell on the ground.

## \|\| 6.59.26-27 \|\|

*vṛntādiva phale pakve tālenānilalolite \|*  
*daṃbholinā parihate śṛṃge iva mahāgireḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*tau nipātya mahādaityāvakāryakaraṇodyatau \|*  
*tataḥ pariṇatiṃ yāto liṃgarūpeṇa kaṃdukaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. After making the two Daityas fall like two ripe fruits from the palmyra tree when shaken by the wind, or like the two peaks of a great mountain struck by the thunderbolt, as they had attempted to do an evil action, the ball changed itself into the phallic image.

## \|\| 6.59.28 \|\|

*kaṃdukeśvarasaṃjñāṃ ca talliṃgamabhavattadā \|*  
*jyeṣṭheśvarasamīpe tu sarvaduṣṭanivāraṇam \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. That phallic image came to be known as Kandukeśvara. It is very near Jyeṣṭheśvara. It removes all the wicked things.

## \|\| 6.59.29 \|\|

*etasminneva samaye haribrahmādayassurāḥ \|*  
*śivāvirbhāvamājñāya ṛṣayaśca samāyayuḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. At the same time, knowing the manifestation of Śiva, Viṣṇu. Brahmā, other gods and the sages came there.

## \|\| 6.59.30 \|\|

*atha sarve surāśśambhorvarānprāpya tadājñayā \|*  
*svadhāmāni yayuḥ prītāstathā kāśīnivāsinaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Then all the gods received boons from Śiva and at his bidding returned to their respective abodes delightedly. So were the residents of Kāśī blessed with the boons.

## \|\| 6.59.31 \|\|

*sāṃbikaṃ śaṃkaraṃ dṛṣṭvā kṛtāṃjalipuṭāśca te \|*  
*praṇamya tuṣṭuvurbhaktyā vāgbhiriṣṭābhirādarāt \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. On seeing Śiva with Pārvatī they bowed to him with palms joined in reverence and eulogised him with devotion and pleasing words.

## \|\| 6.59.32 \|\|

*sāṃbiko'pi śivo vyāsa krīḍitvā suvihāravit \|*  
*jagāma svālayaṃ prītassagaṇo bhaktavatsalaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. O Vyāsa, Śiva and Pārvatī too, went delightedly to their abode. The lord favourably disposed to his devotees, an expert in divine sports, had already had his game.

## \|\| 6.59.33 \|\|

*kaṃdukeśvaraliṃgaṃ ca kāśyāṃ duṣṭanibarhaṇam \|*  
*bhuktimuktipradaṃ sarvakāmadaṃ sarvadā satām \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The Kandukeśvara phallic image at Kāśī destroys the wicked, yields worldly pleasures and salvation. Upon the good it bestows desires always.

## \|\| 6.59.34 \|\|

*idamākhyānamatulaṃ śṛṇuyādyo mudānvitaḥ \|*  
*śrāvayedvā paṭhedyaśca tasya duḥkhabhayaṃ kutaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Where is the cause of fear to him who hears this incomparable narrative with joy, narrates or reads it?

## \|\| 6.59.35 \|\|

*iha sarvasukhaṃ bhuktvā nānāvidhamanuttamam \|*  
*paratra labhate divyāṃ gatiṃ vai devadurlabhām \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. He enjoys pleasures of various kinds and of excellent nature. Hereafter he attains the divine goal inaccessible even to the gods.

## \|\| 6.59.36 \|\|

*iti taṃ varṇitaṃ tāta caritaṃ paramādbhutam \|*  
*śivayorbhaktavātsalyasūcakaṃ śivadaṃ satām \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. O dear, I have thus narrated to you the wonderful story of Śiva and Pārvatī. It indicates their favouritism to the devotees. It bestows welfare to the good.

## \|\| 6.59.37 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityuktvāmaṃtrya taṃ vyāsaṃ tannuto madvarātmajaḥ \|*  
*yayau vihāyasā kāśīṃ caritaṃ śaśimaulinaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

37\. After narrating the story of the moon-crested lord, my excellent son, Sanatkumāra took leave of Vyāsa. Duly honoured by him he then went to Kāśī by the aerial path.

## \|\| 6.59.38 \|\|

*yuddhakhaṃḍamidaṃ proktaṃ mayā te munisattama \|*  
*raudrīyasaṃhitāmadhye sarvakāmaphalapradam \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Thus the section called “Yuddha” has been narrated to you, O excellent sage. In the Compendium called Rudra, it bestows all cherished desires.

## \|\| 6.59.39 \|\|

*iyaṃ hi saṃhitā raudrī sampūrṇā varṇitā mayā \|*  
*sadāśivapriyatarā bhuktimuktiphalapradā \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Thus the whole of Rudrasaṃhitā has been explained by me. It is pleasing to Śiva always. It yields enjoyment here and liberation hereafter.

## \|\| 6.59.40 \|\|

*imāṃ yaśca paṭhennityaṃ śatrubādhānivārikām \|*  
*sarvānkāmānavāpnoti tato muktiṃ labheta nā \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. The man who reads this Saṃhitā that wards off harassment from enemies shall attain all desires. Thereafter he shall attain liberation.

## \|\| 6.59.41 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*iti brahmasutaśśrutvā pitrā śivayaśaḥ param \|*  
*śatanāmāpya śaṃbhośca kṛtārtho'bhūcchivānugaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

Sūta said:—

41\. Thus Brahmā’s son Nārada heard from his father the great glory of Śiva. Śatanāmā too was satisfied and became a follower of Śiva.

## \|\| 6.59.42 \|\|

*brahmanāradasamvādaḥ sampūrṇaḥ kathito mayā \|*  
*śivassarvapradhāno hi kiṃ bhūyaśśrotumicchasi \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. I have completely narrated the conversation between Brahmā and Nārada. Śiva is the most important of all deities. What else do you wish to hear about him?
